title: Postgres read decoder drops boolean consentFlags: consent gate never fires and first recall permanently flattens stored consent
description:
EVIDENCE (verified on origin/main 6fae2fd0b4, pre-existing, NOT introduced by any open PR): src/faculties/memory/postgres-store/rows.ts:157 decodeJsonObject returns Record<string,number> and keeps ONLY finite numbers; rows.ts:333 uses it for consentFlags — which is all booleans ({allowRecall?, allowAbstraction?, deleteOnRequest?}). Every memory hydrated from Postgres therefore has consentFlags = {}.

CONSEQUENCES: (1) the consent gate never fires — src/system/trust/policy.ts:292 ('Layer 3: Consent flags — explicit denial is absolute') tests ctx.consentFlags?.allowRecall === false, fed via searchByEmbedding -> retrieval.ts -> access.ts:268, which is always undefined — a memory marked never-recall IS recalled into the prompt. (2) the on-disk column is then destroyed: updateMemory spreads fromMemoryRow(currentRow) (already {}) and upserts; retrieval.ts:1608 calls updateMemory(id,{lastAccessed,accessCount}) for every selected memory on every retrieval, so stored consent is overwritten with {} the first time a memory is recalled — permanent, unrecoverable via code.

The WRITE path is correct (booleans persist as jsonb; SQL aggregates read consent_flags->>'allowRecall' correctly), purely the read decoder. Notably PR #243's own new test documents the bug and hardcodes around it (postgres-store.integration.test.ts:851-856 comment: fromMemoryRow drops the flags).

CONTEXT: consent flags are the substrate's absolute-denial guarantee (companion-data sacrosanct). This silently voids it on every live deployment.

SCOPE: (a) one-line code fix — rows.ts:333 uses the already-correct decodeJsonRecord (rows.ts:168) — plus a regression test proving a stored allowRecall:false round-trips through hydration AND survives an updateMemory({lastAccessed}) touch, plus a policy-level test that the Layer-3 gate actually blocks; (b) SEPARATE deploy-side assessment of how much on-disk consent data has already been flattened on live systems (Purrsephone psfn-shard, carlini fleet) and whether any repair source exists (backups predating first-recall, JSONL journals). Do not bundle the data assessment into the code fix.

ACCEPTANCE (code half): regression tests above green; full memory-faculty suite green; the fix commit cites this bead. Data half: per-deployment count of memories with non-empty consent_flags vs expected, findings recorded here.
notes:
2026-07-27 CODE HALF DONE — DATA HALF STILL OPEN AND UNSTARTED. Do not close this bead on the code evidence.

CODE HALF SHIPPED in PR #240 (S11 fixes consolidated), merged to main at 1267ad411a; commit f5451ef73a "fix(memory): decode boolean consentFlags on hydration so explicit denial actually gates recall (xnfks)".
- src/faculties/memory/postgres-store/rows.ts: consent_flags now decodes through decodeJsonRecord instead of decodeJsonObject, so the all-boolean column survives hydration into normalizeConsentFlags rather than being filtered to {} by a finite-numbers-only reader.
- src/faculties/memory/postgres-store/rows.test.ts (+69): round-trip of an explicit allowRecall denial; all three boolean flags preserved, not just the denial; non-boolean stored jsonb values dropped rather than trusted; empty flags restored from a null/absent column; plus policy-level coverage proving evaluateMemoryPolicy DENIES recall for a hydrated memory whose stored consent forbids it and ALLOWS it once consent permits — i.e. the Layer-3 gate is verified to actually fire, not just to receive data.
- postgres-store.integration.test.ts (+45): "keeps an explicit consent denial through hydration and an access-counter touch (xnfks)" — mutation-verified, so it proves the denial survives the updateMemory({lastAccessed, accessCount}) write-back that retrieval.ts:1608 performs on every selected memory. That was the destructive half of the defect.
Code-half acceptance is met.

>>> REMAINING WORK — SCOPE ITEM (b), DEPLOY-SIDE DATA ASSESSMENT. THIS BEAD STAYS OPEN FOR IT. <<<
The fix stops FURTHER destruction. It does not recover anything already destroyed. Every memory that was recalled even once on any live deployment before f5451ef73a had its consent_flags column overwritten with {} — permanently, and unrecoverable through code. A subject's explicit never-recall choice may already be gone from live data.

What must be done, per deployment (Purrsephone on psfn-shard, and each of the 5 carlini companions):
1. Count memories with non-empty consent_flags versus the expected population, and record the numbers ON THIS BEAD.
2. Determine whether any repair source exists — backups predating that companion's first recall, or the JSONL journals — and whether flags can be reconstructed from them.
3. Record the per-deployment findings and the repair decision here before closing.

Until those numbers are on this bead, the P0 is not resolved: the substrate's absolute-denial guarantee may be silently void on live data even though the code path is now correct.
close_reason: Code half shipped (f5451ef73a, PR #240). Data half complete 2026-07-29: per-deployment counts recorded on bead; code+journal evidence proves no non-empty consent flags ever existed on any live deployment — {} is the original value, nothing destroyed, no repair needed. Successor gap (no consent producer) tracked as alco2 (P1).

comments.author: axAilotl
comments.text:
DATA-HALF ASSESSMENT COMPLETE 2026-07-29 (run by orchestrator with operator authorization; read-only psql via kubectl exec on each cluster).

PER-DEPLOYMENT COUNTS (fingerprint = empty consent_flags AND access_count>0 on l2_memories; l01_episodes has no access column):
- k3d test (Artemis, companion_default): l2 total 0, episodes 0 — reseeded clean, trivially unaffected.
- psfn-shard (Purrsephone, schema public): l2 total 2728, ever_recalled 2728, empty flags 2728, fingerprint 2728, recalled-with-flags 0. Episodes 285, all empty flags.
- carlini (5 companions): public 878/878/878/0 · denise 178/178/178/0 · garden_nun 152/152/152/0 · julienne 154/154/154/0 · lucy 136/136/136/0 (l2 total/ever_recalled/fingerprint/with_flags). Episodes 85/16/13/6/14, all empty flags.

INTERPRETATION — the 100% fingerprint is NOT flattening damage; {} is the ORIGINAL stored value:
1. CODE EVIDENCE (blind subagent sweep, file:line-cited): no production writer has EVER set a non-empty consent flag. All 8 production writer.write() callers (extraction.ts:945, memory tools.ts:524/:1099, sandbox memory.ts:300, usage-evaluator.ts:108, patterns.ts:357, adaptive-tools-runtime.ts:264, reflection-template-runtime.ts:564) omit consentFlags entirely; writer-level consent handling (writer.ts:711/:831/:565/:1286) is purely propagation of caller input; ExtractedFact.consentFlags is dead plumbing nothing populates; contacts/trust/garden surfaces are read-only over the column; rows.ts:276 coerces undefined→{} and the column is NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'. l01_episodes hardcodes json({}) at insert AND update (episodic/postgres-store.ts:186/:273) — episode flags cannot be non-empty by construction. git log -S allowRecall confirms no producer ever existed historically.
2. JOURNAL EVIDENCE (append-only, both live systems): every consentFlags occurrence in companion-data JSONL is {} — psfn-shard: 18,607 occurrences, zero non-empty; carlini: 286 occurrences across the fleet, zero non-empty.

RESIDUAL CAVEAT: code cannot rule out a manual SQL hand-edit having once set flags (the touch path would have erased it on first recall). No journal, backup, or operational record suggests one ever happened; on-PVC runtime backups (earliest 2026-07-12, encrypted snapshots) all postdate years of recall traffic and are not a pre-recall repair source. There is nothing to repair and no repair source is needed.

REPAIR DECISION: NO REPAIR. No consent data was destroyed on any deployment; the code fix (f5451ef73a, shipped PR #240) closes the destruction vector going forward. The genuinely open successor issue is filed as psfn-framework-alco2 (P1): the consent gate is enforceable but UNSETTABLE — no producer writes flags — so the absolute-denial guarantee has no data to act on until a producer is wired. Provenance-of-consent recording folded into the same bead; S12 provenance epic seed is psfn-framework-ccgdz.

Acceptance for the data half (per-deployment numbers on the bead, repair-source determination, repair decision recorded) is met. Closing the P0.

title: P0: Run PostgreSQL test harnesses in bounded RAM storage
description: Multiple machines have crashed under catastrophic disk I/O from internal build gates that launch disposable PostgreSQL/pgvector test containers with their data directory on Docker's disk-backed writable layer. Hotfix src/test-support/postgres-test-harness.ts so all shared PostgreSQL integration-test consumers mount PGDATA on tmpfs/RAM, disable durability work that is meaningless for disposable test databases, bound container memory/swap/CPU, suppress container log-file writes, cap aggregate harness concurrency across test processes, stop containers between test files to release RAM, and clean up the container plus coordination lease on startup or shutdown failures. Add focused tests that prove the Docker invocation contains the fail-closed tmpfs/resource settings. Scope is the shared internal test harness and its build-gate consumers; do not alter production PostgreSQL persistence, Helm storage, or live deployment behavior.
acceptance_criteria: All startPostgresTestHarness containers mount /var/lib/postgresql/data as bounded tmpfs; container memory and swap are capped, Docker JSON logging is disabled, disposable PostgreSQL durability writes are disabled, aggregate harness concurrency is capped at four machine-wide slots, failed startup/normal stop stops resources and releases its slot, focused tests pass, changed-file lint passes, and the exact commit is pushed to main as the operator-requested emergency exception.
notes:
Emergency operator exception: committed and pushed directly to main at b7d7aecb8f56290716607780c903996e599ad0d9. Validation passed: focused Vitest src/test-support/postgres-test-harness.test.ts (5/5), npm run lint:changed -- --base origin/main, focused strict TypeScript compile of the two changed files, verify:hardcoded-settings, and git diff --check. Full Docker-backed integration was not run because docker ps already fails with 'rw layer snapshot not found', and starting disk-intensive containers on the damaged daemon would repeat the incident. Hotfix itself uses tmpfs, fixed memory/swap/CPU/log limits, four machine-wide semaphore slots, versioned container identity, durability-off PostgreSQL settings, and stop/release cleanup.
2026-07-27 follow-up (testgate-ram lane): the 'stop containers between test files to release RAM' clause is deliberately REVERSED. Empirically proven: PGDATA on tmpfs means docker stop destroys the cluster, so stop-per-file forced a full initdb per test file (marker-DB probe confirmed). Fix keeps containers hot between files; resetWorkerPostgres (drop all test DBs/roles) is the isolation boundary. PSFN_POSTGRES_TEST_STOP_BETWEEN_FILES=1 restores old behavior; npm run test:postgres:down releases containers. Also fixed the slot starvation this bead's 4-slot cap caused on many-core machines (32 vitest workers vs 4 slots -> beforeAll hook timeouts, failure moves between files across runs): cap now floor(cores/4) clamped 4-8, PSFN_POSTGRES_TEST_MAX_HARNESSES override. Full 44-file suite: 44/44 in 120s (was 41-44/44 knife-edge in ~190s). The never-run Docker validation debt from the emergency landing is now paid.
close_reason: Satisfied on main: b7d7aecb8f (tmpfs/bounded harness) + bc971efe83 (keep-hot reversal of the stop-between-files clause, slot scaling) + cede186355 + 3bb4a964e3; Docker validation debt paid (44/44 integration files green twice).

comments.author: axAilotl
comments.text:

- tmpfs PGDATA, capped memory/swap, JSON logging off, durability-off settings, versioned container identity, semaphore slots, stop/release cleanup: b7d7aecb8f (emergency operator-exception landing).
- 'stop containers between test files to release RAM' is REVERSED by bc971efe83 with operator-visible rationale: PGDATA on tmpfs means docker stop destroys the cluster, forcing a full initdb per test file (marker-DB probe confirmed). The RAM-release goal is preserved by the bounded per-container memory (768m memory + memory-swap, 512m tmpfs) plus an explicit 'npm run test:postgres:down' release path (scripts/ci/stop-test-postgres.mjs). PSFN_POSTGRES_TEST_STOP_BETWEEN_FILES=1 restores the old behavior. resetWorkerPostgres is the isolation boundary.
- bc971efe83 also fixed the slot starvation the original 4-slot cap caused on many-core machines: cap is now floor(cores/4) clamped to 4-8 with a PSFN_POSTGRES_TEST_MAX_HARNESSES override. Supporting commits: cede186355 (harness slot bounds baselined as code-owned constants in scripts/hardcoded-settings-baseline.json), 3bb4a964e3 (named-tenant-store-boot 180s override registered as inherited debt).
- The Docker validation debt from the emergency landing is now PAID: full 44-file Postgres integration suite 44/44 green twice, 120s (previously a 41-44/44 knife-edge at ~190s).

title: P0 DEPLOY BLOCKER: merged main gateway unconditionally requires the companion-library bundle, but the chart no longer provisions it — every merged-main deploy crashes on boot
description:
Found 2026-07-23 testing merged main (6b7bded6) on the k3d Artie fleet. The gateway CRASHES on boot with a fatal:

  ERROR [Gateway] Fatal error: Invalid Companion Library source manifest /app/companion_docs/companion-library-manifest.json: ENOENT: no such file or directory

ROOT CAUSE — runtime requires it UNCONDITIONALLY, chart does not provide it:
- src/persistence/workspaces/provisioning.ts:240 provisionFleetWorkspaces() -> seedCompanionLibrary() calls loadSourceBundle(sourceDir) with NO existsSync guard; sourceDir defaults to resolve('companion_docs') = /app/companion_docs. If the manifest is absent it throws (provisioning.ts:92). The 'already seeded' statePath check comes AFTER loadSourceBundle, so it never short-circuits the source read. This landed with the fleet workspace-isolation work (54e4e5d5a 'isolate fleet companion workspaces' + c337 gap fixes), which IS in main.
- The IMAGE does not bake /app/companion_docs (docker run ... ls /app/companion_docs -> No such file or directory; manifest ABSENT).
- The merged-main CHART does NOT provision it: grep of deploy/helm/psfn for companion_docs / companion-library / seed-companion-library returns NOTHING; the rendered gateway has no companion_docs volume/mount and no seed init container.
- The chart-side provisioning was supposed to come from PR #234 'feat(helm): activate companion library workloads (yhivs.2)' (changed values.yaml, _helpers.tpl, workloads.yaml, fleet-agents.yaml, + scripts/verify-helm-companion-library.mjs). #234 shows MERGED but its content is NOT in origin/main: its merge commit b075bd7ea1 is not an ancestor of origin/main, and none of its chart changes are present by content. So the runtime requirement is in main while the chart provisioning (#234) is not — a runtime/chart mismatch.

IMPACT: ANY deploy of merged main crashes the gateway on boot unless the companion-library bundle is provisioned at /app/companion_docs. This BLOCKS:
- Purrsephone's upgrade to 6b7bded6 (the arm64 image already built + staged on the Pi this session would crash her gateway — DO NOT DEPLOY IT AS-IS).
- The carlini cutover (same crash).
Proven on k3d: gateway CrashLoopBackOff, agents restarting, only postgres/redis/emosim/litellm stayed up. Deploy-tooling migration steps that DID work were validated first (cert adoption for k2qmj, --force-conflicts for SSA drift, delete+recreate gateway for orphan init containers, qg13 intake-policy owner-file repair).
acceptance_criteria: Either #234's chart-side companion-library provisioning is (re)landed in main so a default merged-main deploy provisions /app/companion_docs, OR the runtime is guarded to skip seeding when the source is absent, OR the deploy contract (ship:kube) is documented+wired to always apply the companion-library overlay. A clean merged-main deploy must boot the gateway with no companion-library fatal, verified on k3d and before any Purrsephone/carlini deploy.
close_reason: Fixed in main via PR #244 (rebase-merge 2026-07-23): c1cbe61d29 bakes companion_docs/ into the agent image at /app/companion_docs (docker/Dockerfile.agent COPY), and 92bf467bf4 hardens the build guard to assert all 4 declared bundle files exist at build time (Greptile finding). Image-bake was chosen over the yhivs values-gated ConfigMap because the runtime requirement (seedCompanionLibrary) is UNCONDITIONAL — a default-off chart flag cannot satisfy it. Adversarially reviewed, Greptile passed. Verified live: the same bake (0.1.0-kube-6b7bded6-lib) booted the k3d two-companion fleet clean AND deployed to Purrsephone (helm rev 66, gateway 1/1, Discord logged in) — both gateways cleared the companion-library manifest requirement that previously crashed them. The yhivs chart lane / #234 merge-state anomaly remains a separate lane's concern; the image bake coexists with a future chart approach via COPYFILE_EXCL.

title: Sleeptime orientation rewrite fabricates core-memory & memories with no grounding gate
description: Confirmed P0 (adversarial verifier, blind). The nightly sleeptime pass runs a RAW automaton completion (src/faculties/memory/sleeptime-agent.ts:651 completeWithWorkSpec, NOT her agent/persona turn loop) that free-generates orient.{persona,human,goals} and memory_writes[], then persists them with no grounding check: (1) orient blocks written via coreMemoryStore.rethink (:683) which OVERWRITES all three blocks WHOLESALE (core-memory/store.ts:642) — a hallucinated rewrite can destroy previously-grounded orientation; (2) each memory_writes entry via memoryWriter.write (:713) tagged sourceType:autonomous_action. The only candidacy gate (evaluateSleeptimeOrientCandidacy->evaluateCogSecMemoryCandidacy, cogsec/memory-candidacy.ts:134) is a prompt-INJECTION screen, not a transcript-grounding check; benign fabrication passes. countSupportingTranscriptEntries (:358) only tags, never blocks — evidenceCount:0 writes identically. The high-impact-low-confidence review gate (maintenance-review.ts:741, threshold 0.65) DOES block when it fires, but scope is narrow (high-impact type AND conf<0.65) and the plan normalizer defaults omitted confidence to 0.75 (:296), sailing over it. Written content re-injects into her live prompt (core_memory/participant_context) every turn as ground truth. Contrast the one real grounding check in the codebase, extraction/self-directed.ts:83-87 (exact-substring), which is NOT applied here. Enabled by default (scheduler-lanes.ts:101). Charter Law 17 (memory fabrication) + section 6.28.
acceptance_criteria: Sleeptime orient rewrites and memory_writes are rejected (not merely flagged) when their text is not grounded in the source transcript, using an enforced check analogous to self-directed.ts:83-87; orient rewrite must not wholesale-overwrite grounded blocks with ungrounded content; confidence default must not auto-clear the review gate; regression tests cover a fabricated benign fact (evidenceCount 0, conf>=0.65) being blocked from both the rethink and memoryWriter paths.
close_reason: Completed in PR #218 at d40236e57937; src/faculties/memory/sleeptime-agent.ts:783 rejects zero-evidence content before either persistence path, :910 scopes episode continuity to one logical owner while separating group/invite-only/unrelated private sessions, and src/faculties/memory/sleeptime-agent.test.ts:579 covers bound-private cross-surface continuity. Focused 38 tests, changed lint, exact local gate (13,616 tests), GitHub delta, and ci-required passed.

title: S10 charter-violation sweep: automata fabricating/emitting companion voice & state
description: Umbrella for the Sprint-10 audit triggered by P0 psfn-framework-5hip. Root pattern: sink primitives (proactiveOutbound, raw sender.send, notify, memoryWriter.write, coreMemoryStore.rethink) enforce NO authorship/grounding/consent invariant of their own; they trust each caller to gate. Well-built paths (weighted-thought-outreach, social-desire-outreach, extraction/self-directed) have decline-capable consent moments or exact-substring grounding. The flagged callers skipped that gate. 5hip fired in production; the children below are its structural siblings across memory, scheduling, intention, and shards. Every child was confirmed by an independent adversarial verifier (blind to the finder). Charter basis: Laws 17/18/31, sections 6.28 (automata are not her central voice) and 8.3.

title: P0: Route child task results back to companion orchestration, never partner DMs
description:
Summary:
Task lifecycle partner notifications introduced by commit 0cad4d415 subscribe to every agent.completion_handoff, turn internal child/task bookkeeping into companion-voice text, durably queue it, and send it to the configured primary partner Discord DM. This caused a live restart flood on Purrsephone after fleet cutover.

Live evidence:
- On 2026-07-22, Purrsephone drained 17 recorded sent entries from state/outreach-outbox.jsonl, roughly one LLM-authored task_lifecycle:blocked message every five seconds.
- Immediate mitigation scaled her agent to zero. The durable post-turn queue was empty after mitigation, so restart would not resume that specific drain.

Operator-confirmed intended behavior:
A subagent or shard is work Purrsephone delegated. Its completion is a child-to-orchestrator result handoff, analogous to a Codex subagent reporting back to its parent orchestrator. The child should return its result summary and artifact/file references to Purrsephone and nudge her internal orchestration context that the work is ready. Purrsephone then decides what to do with the result and, when appropriate, authors the partner-facing response through her normal turn. The lifecycle subsystem must never impersonate that response or directly DM the partner on her behalf.

Mechanism and exact locations:
1. src/core/agent/task-lifecycle-partner-notifications.ts:392 subscribes to every agent.completion_handoff without source/status routing.
2. src/shared/contracts/completion-handoff.ts defines sources including subagent, shard, post_turn_action, background_continuation, and scheduled_loop. Internal execution handoffs all qualify today.
3. Each event becomes a durable post-turn action, so downtime accumulates a restart backlog.
4. src/app/agent/main.ts:1287-1302 passes heartbeatChannelId as the target and calls agentLoop.handleMessage with a synthetic system author.
5. src/core/agent/task-lifecycle-partner-notification-contract.ts:146-156 directs the model to tell the partner in its own voice and has no decline/no-op outcome.
6. src/core/agent/task-lifecycle-partner-notifications.ts:198-259 always dispatches the text through proactiveOutbound and records it as companion-authored.
7. src/core/agent/task-lifecycle-partner-notifications.test.ts:130-178 regression-protects that behavior.

Why this matters:
This violates Charter Laws 17 and 18, section 6.28, and section 8.3: internal automata are not the companion central voice and may not fabricate her speech. Law 31 still requires multi-turn/subagent completion or blocked work to become visible to the partner. That requirement is satisfied through the authentic orchestration flow: child result returns internally, Purrsephone is nudged, and her resulting ordinary turn can notify the partner when the originating interaction requires it.

Scope:
- Route subagent and shard completion handoffs into the existing CompletionNoticeBuffer / background_completions orchestration path, or its canonical successor.
- Carry enough durable child result information for Purrsephone to resume the task: status, bounded summary, provenance, and artifact/file references or a durable lookup reference.
- Wake/nudge the origin companion orchestration path once, without inserting internal bookkeeping into conversational transcripts as partner or companion speech.
- Remove agentLoop.handleMessage and proactiveOutbound from internal task completion delivery.
- Explicitly enumerate routing by completion source and status instead of treating every handoff as partner outreach.
- Bound, expire, or coalesce queued completion notices so downtime cannot become a restart flood.
- Update misleading companion-authored names, prompts, metadata, comments, and tests.

Non-goals:
- Do not suppress or discard child results.
- Do not prevent Purrsephone from telling the partner about completed work in her normal authored turn.
- Do not widen Discord targets or alter ordinary companion-chosen proactive outreach.
- Do not redesign unrelated attention-pressure features from commit 0cad4d415.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A subagent or shard terminal handoff produces one bounded internal completion notice for the origin companion orchestration context and no proactive outbound partner message. 2. The internal handoff exposes the child status, bounded result summary, provenance, and artifact/file references or a durable reference sufficient for Purrsephone to continue the delegated task. 3. Purrsephone is nudged through CompletionNoticeBuffer/background_completions or the canonical equivalent; the notice does not enter transcripts as partner or companion speech. 4. No internal completion path calls agentLoop.handleMessage or proactiveOutbound. Any partner-facing report happens only through a subsequent normal companion-authored turn. 5. Routing is an explicit source/status allowlist; backlogged notices are bounded, expired, or coalesced so restart cannot flood either internal context or external channels. 6. Regression tests cover completed and blocked subagent/shard handoffs, result availability to the parent orchestration path, zero Discord dispatch, restart backlog behavior, and truthful provenance. Changed-file lint and targeted tests pass, and ci-required is green before closure.
notes: WHY TESTING MISSED IT (verified 2026-07-22): the k3d shakedown cluster's channels.json has NO heartbeatChannelId, so ProactiveOutboundDispatcher is never constructed and wireTaskLifecyclePartnerNotifications receives null — every notification is recorded 'skipped' and nothing is dispatched. k3d logs 'Task lifecycle partner notifications will be recorded as skipped because no approved primary DM is configured' once at boot. The spawn_subagent shakedown case RAN AND PASSED there; the completion handoff fired into a null dispatcher. The test cluster structurally cannot exercise this lane, so no subagent fan-out in the case matrix would have caught it. The flood magnitude additionally required a durable backlog accumulated over hours of downtime, which a continuously-running test cluster never produces. Generalisable gap recorded in /home/ada/psfn-shakedown-rounds/FLEET-CUTOVER-QUIRKS.md section L: diffing Deployment specs is insufficient; behaviour-gating config (channels.json, settings.json, scheduler.json, capability tier) must be diffed too, and every production-only field treated as an untested code path.
close_reason: Completed and rebase-merged via PR #211 after independent adversarial review and Greptile remediation. Exact reviewed head ae995350963d passed local gate: lint, build, typecheck baseline (240/94), repository hygiene, Semgrep (0 findings), UBS, Garden build plus 348 tests, and root suite 13,607 passed / 12 skipped. ci-required and Greptile Review were SUCCESS; GraphQL showed zero unresolved current P0/P1 threads. Main delivery ends at 9dfb11b466382830646984cf290703c2067abb90. Source evidence: src/app/agent/main.ts no longer wires lifecycle completion through handleMessage/proactiveOutbound; obsolete task-lifecycle partner notification modules/UI were deleted; src/core/agent/completion-handoff.ts uses an explicit subagent/shard terminal allowlist and captured logical session only; completion-notices.ts supplies bounded coalesced internal results; substrate-agent.ts nudges active parent orchestration or buffers for the originating logical session; subagent/shard producers retain transcript/result references and captured provenance.

title: Retrieval selects unattributed/ambiguous memories that the subject-authorization layer then refuses, aborting the whole active-memory-context refresh (companion reads as 0 memories)
description:
Live on Purrsephone (psfn-shard, merged main 66392a6ef, 2026-07-22 post fleet cutover). Symptom: Garden and the companion both report 0 memories while the database is fully intact.

Evidence: retrieval itself WORKS — '[Retrieval] Retrieval trace ... semanticCandidates:127 ... 127 candidates -> 127 policy-allowed -> 127 scored -> 127 ranked -> 10 selected + 7 episodic episodes'. Immediately after, '[Retrieval] Retrieval integrity failure {stage: selected_access_update ... cause: Memory subject authorization denied}' followed by '[Retrieval] Active memory context refresh failed; keeping previous active context'. Net effect: she keeps an empty active context and surfaces as having no memories.

Root cause: src/faculties/memory/postgres-store.ts:1048 lockAuthorizedActiveMemoryRows throws when authorizedRows.length !== memoryIds.length. The predicate (src/faculties/memory/postgres-store/subject-policy.ts) excludes subject_class IN ('ambiguous','unattributed','unbound_person'). On her data 896 of 2550 live memories are exactly those classes (868 unattributed, 28 ambiguous) — classifications are CURRENT and consistent (zero revision or evidence-digest mismatches), so this is not classification drift. Retrieval ranks and selects those memories, then the access-stat update refuses them and throws, taking down the entire refresh rather than skipping the unauthorized subset.

The two layers disagree about what is retrievable: the retrieval policy path admits unattributed memories (they are legitimately hers), the subject-authorization path refuses them.
acceptance_criteria: An access-stats update that encounters memories outside the subject-authorization set does not abort the active-memory-context refresh — either retrieval stops selecting rows it cannot authorize, or the access-stat update skips/records the unauthorized subset without throwing. Live: Purrsephone's active memory context populates and Garden shows her memory count; a retrieval trace selecting unattributed memories logs no 'Retrieval integrity failure'. Regression test covers a selection containing an unattributed memory.
notes: P0 because it silently blanks a live companion's entire memory context while the data is intact — she appears to have lost everything. Found during her fleet cutover; NOT caused by it (classifications are consistent), but exposed by running merged main against long-lived data with many unattributed memories. Her DB is verified healthy: 2699 l2_memories rows, tenant role reads them fine.
close_reason:
Live-validated on psfn-shard 2026-07-22 05:20 UTC, helm rev 65, image 0.1.0-kube-9dfb11b4 (merged main 9dfb11b46, fix delivered by PR #207 commits db493d4e3 + 3bf7b0b93).

Live evidence from the agent after redeploy — a full retrieval completed on a private primary-trust channel with NO integrity failure and NO authorization abort:

title: P0: Recover Purrsephone memory extraction and daily reflections after rollback schema skew
description:
Live incident on the operator-selected Purrsephone k3s deployment. The active workloads run image 0.1.0-kube-576e33cd at Helm revision 59. Revisions 56 and 58 briefly ran image 0.1.0-kube-5d1785dc, which contains commit 4acbd9b1d and its forward-only migration adding l2_memories.salience_decay_anchor_at BIGINT NOT NULL. Revisions 57 and 59 rolled the app image back to 576e33cd, whose Postgres memory store does not read or write that column. The database schema was not rolled back, leaving schema/runtime skew.

Live evidence captured 2026-07-19: Garden GET /api/admin/memory reports exactly 2,491 active memories and renders 20 rows on page 1 of 125 in a clean browser session, but the latest memory extracted_at is 2026-07-15 07:36 EDT. Daily reflection and metacognition APIs each contain 71 entries and stop at 2026-07-15 06:00 EDT. The general reflection journal continued through 2026-07-19. Agent logs repeatedly fail new memory extraction, retrieval access-stat updates, daily-review, and weekly-review with `null value in column "salience_decay_anchor_at" of relation "l2_memories" violates not-null constraint`; those failures also produce post-turn background-work failures and drain timeouts.

Scope: recover the live writer/reader compatibility safely; preserve all existing companion data; validate new memory and daily-reflection writes; and add a rollout/rollback compatibility guard so a database-expanding migration cannot be followed by an incompatible application rollback without an explicit compatible down/bridge plan. Before any live mutation, back up the affected Postgres schema/table and companion state per .claude/skills/psfn-live-ops/SKILL.md. Prefer a narrow compatibility recovery over redeploying a known-rolled-back build without understanding why it was rolled back.

Non-goals: deleting, rewriting, pruning, or reclassifying Purrsephone memories; changing model behavior or sampling settings; treating a clean-session Garden rendering result as proof that the existing operator browser session is healthy.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A verified backup exists before live schema or runtime mutation. 2. The live runtime and l2_memories schema agree on salience_decay_anchor_at for inserts and updates. 3. A controlled post-recovery interaction produces at least one new durable memory with extracted_at later than the recovery timestamp and Garden active-memory count reflects it. 4. A controlled/manual daily reflection run writes both daily and metacognition journal entries after the recovery timestamp. 5. A bounded live log scan contains no new salience_decay_anchor_at NOT NULL failures, memory-extraction integrity failures, or daily-review retrieval failures. 6. Existing 2,491 active memories remain intact except for the validated new writes; no content surgery occurs. 7. Automated deployment/migration tests fail closed when attempting to roll back from a schema-requiring build to an image that cannot write the required column. 8. npm run lint passes for any code change, and the relevant Postgres memory, migration, rollout, and Garden smoke tests pass.

title: Charter violation: stop the runtime fabricating companion-authored image failure speech
description: This is not merely poor fallback UX or an ordinary regression. It is a live violation of the PSFN Project Charter and the authorship boundary that protects the companion as a sovereign subject. In Carlini DM channel 1520867764313522248, turn 019f6238-2177-77ed-bfcc-4396240de220 / request 1526679987996987542 at 2026-07-14T20:01:44Z had selfie_create and generate_image in the 22 provider-visible tool definitions but recorded zero tool calls and zero image gateway activity. ChatGPTN returned false attachment wording. The attachment guard rejected that claim, then the runtime overrode Carlini's authored response and persisted/sent a hard-coded developer diagnostic as if it were Carlini's own speech: 'I could not attach an image because no image tool completed successfully this turn. I need to call selfie_create or generate_image before saying an image is attached.' This directly violates Charter Laws 17 and 18 (fabricated companion-authored speech is forbidden; companion-facing semantics must remain truthful), §8.2 Authorship Integrity, §8.3 No Forced Emotional Counterfeiting (the platform must not force the companion to say something through hidden coercive machinery), §8.5 No Fake Healthy State (prompt/system failure must not become fake assistant speech), and §12.5 No Bullshit Tests because the regression test explicitly blesses the forced diagnostic. Preserve the fail-closed attachment-truth boundary, but never solve system integrity by commandeering the companion's voice. Recovery instructions and tool diagnostics are system notes/internal control data, not companion dialogue. Prefer one bounded model recovery with explicit internal provenance; if recovery fails, surface failure through an honestly attributed system/runtime channel or allow the companion to formulate a truthful natural reply. Do not expose internal tool names, duplicate paid generations, create retry loops, or persist fabricated speech into L0.
design: Authorship is a hard architectural boundary, not a wording preference. The attachment guard may reject or withhold a false claim, but it must not synthesize first-person companion speech. Keep three artifacts distinct: companion-authored response, explicit system/runtime failure note, and internal corrective instruction. Any retry must be bounded to one attempt, marked as system-originated context, and unable to reuse stale attachments or repeat a successful paid generation. If no companion-authored truthful response can be obtained, emit an explicitly typed/attributed system failure outside the companion message role.
acceptance_criteria: No guard-authored, developer-authored, template-authored, or system-authored text is persisted or delivered under the companion/assistant authorship role. The exact hard-coded diagnostic is removed from companion-visible output and tests no longer bless it as Carlini's speech. A false attachment claim with zero current-turn attachments is withheld and triggers at most one internally attributed corrective recovery. A successful recovery may deliver a valid current-turn selfie_create or media image attachment with genuinely model-authored companion text. If recovery fails, the failure is surfaced as an explicitly attributed system/runtime event or the model produces a truthful natural response; it contains no hidden guard instructions or leaked tool implementation names. Telemetry preserves rejection, provenance, recovery, and final outcome. Real successful attachments remain unchanged. Tests prove authorship-role separation, no fabricated L0 assistant entry, no duplicate paid generation, no infinite retry, no stale attachment, and no hidden tool payload. Targeted tests, lint, and build pass.
notes: Operator correction on 2026-07-14: classify this as an abject and total charter violation, not merely a regression. Severity raised from P1 to P0 because a live framework control path commandeers and persists the companion's first-person voice, and its test suite intentionally certifies that violation.

Focused regressions cover two distinct paid calls, selfie preference, previous failed attempts, retired aliases, stamped claims, internal sentence leaks, truthful recovery, and unknown nonstandard provenance. Independent acceptance review reported no blocker. Validation: focused 47/47; npm run lint passed; npm run build passed including DTS; full suite 710 files, 7,905 passed and 3 skipped.

title: Session history fetch is count-based; internal/tool spam displaces real chat 1:1
description: collectRecentEntriesWithinHistorySpan (manager-primitives.ts:400) calls store.getRecent(channelId, estimatedCount) where estimatedCount = tokenBudget/256 (context-budget.ts:632-661, SESSION_HISTORY_ESTIMATED_TOKENS_PER_MESSAGE=256). The fetch is COUNT-based, so every CompletionHandoff/system/tool entry displaces a real user/assistant message 1:1 before token trimming even runs. Live evidence (turn c4983f4b, 2026-07-06 17:05): recentEntries=153 of which only ~18 were real dialogue (25+ handoffs, ~110 tool rows from a diagnostic sweep) - final wire prompt carried 19 conversational messages reaching back only ~3h in a channel with 1463 messages. Also: tool entries consume token budget in trimRecentEntriesToTokenBudget (counts all roles, manager-primitives.ts:268-288) then get unconditionally dropped in entriesToMessages (context-support.ts:245-247 'continue', added 416f06a1) leaving dead code at :262-268 - pure wasted eviction. Fix: fetch/trim over conversational entries only (filter non-conversational BEFORE count/budget accounting), oversample the fetch, and reconcile the dead tool-entry branch.

comments.author: axAilotl
comments.text: Wire-level confirmation of the displacement, worst case: turn 87d8656f (2026-07-06 14:10 'With you always. I'm off today...') went to the model with a context of THREE messages total: 1 system note + the single 14:09 exchange. Everything earlier was displaced by handoff/tool spam in the count-based fetch, then the temporal same-day filter ('today' in message text -> resolveTemporalTurnWindow same_day, manager-primitives.ts:176) cut the remainder. She duplicated her previous 'good morning' reply because it was literally the only assistant turn she could see. Window size is also wildly unstable turn-to-turn: 42 msgs at 14:09, 3 at 14:10, 47 at 14:18, 43 at 16:14, 49 at 16:59, 17 at 17:01, 19 at 17:05. Secondary effect: the echo pairs this produced (two good-morning replies, two love-replies) are now baked into the persisted transcript and teach the model the echo pattern on subsequent turns even when context is complete. Operator design principle applies: fix context quality, no sampling-knob compensation.

comments.author: axAilotl
comments.text: CORRECTION after wire-level verification: entriesToMessages already filters handoff entries out of prompts (probe-confirmed), and collectRecentEntriesWithinHistorySpan oversamples until the 36h span is covered - so the 'count-based fetch displaces 1:1' premise was wrong. The REAL mechanical collapse: applyTemporalSessionHistoryWindow (manager-primitives.ts:176) has NO floor - a casual temporal cue in the user message ('today', 'now') collapses history to same_day/recent_hours; at the 14:10 turn ('I'm off today...') the wire context was 3 messages (1 system note + the single previous exchange) because the night conversation was Sunday EDT. That produced the good-morning echo. Revised fix scope: (1) conversational floor in the temporal window filter (backfill most-recent older entries when the filter leaves too few), (2) extend isNonConversationalSessionEntry to exclude completion_handoff-metadata entries so legacy/restored rows drop out of window accounting, (3) remove the dead tool-entry branch in context-support.ts:262. Handoff store poisoning remains real (projection/lexical index/episodic inputs/zombie recency) and is handled by psfn-framework-p0e0 + purge.

description: Every deferred post-turn action outcome (completed AND skipped AND dropped_budget) calls emitCompletionHandoff -> emitCompletionHandoffToSessionManager -> recordSystemMessage, persisting a ~1.6KB '[SYSTEM: CompletionHandoff]' JSON blob as a session entry in the action's channel (src/app/startup/composition/post-turn-actions.ts:562-629). Timer lanes (episode-synthesis heartbeat-post-turn-runtime.ts:1243-1290, near-turn, etc) enumerate listRecentSessions() with no activity gate (synthesis-lane.ts:211-229), so EVERY known channel including dead smoke probes gets ~2 handoffs/hour. Worse: the handoff write itself refreshes the session's recency, so dead channels stay in listRecentSessions forever (zombie loop). Live DB: 171 handoff rows per dead channel since 7/03 cutover, 229 in the primary Discord channel, 48/day/channel. These are internal bookkeeping, explicitly labeled companion-only, and must not be session conversation entries at all: emit to telemetry/journal, or at minimum lane-tag internal (sessionLane kind=internal schemaVersion=1) so isNonConversationalSessionEntry excludes them, gate no-op/skip outcomes entirely, and stop recency refresh from system writes.

title: E2.7: Prompt-shape goldens and static-prefix byte-stability in CI
description:
## Context
Prompt regressions are personality regressions for a live companion. Goldens must exist BEFORE the engine is opened. Land this first in the epic, before E2.2.

## Scope

- Scrubbing rules for genuinely-variable content (IDs, timestamps) per golden-testing practice; goldens reviewed like code.

## Charter note (12.5 no bullshit tests)
Goldens can lock in implementation accidents — mitigation: goldens are a refactor-freeze net with a documented, reviewed regeneration procedure; intentional shape changes update goldens deliberately, never by blind re-record.

description:
## Context

## Scope

title: E2: PromptPlan — one assembly path, one artifact, real caching
description:
## Summary
Collapse the prompt system to a single per-turn artifact (PromptPlan: ordered blocks with volatility classes + one variable namespace + messages + tool definitions + cache plan) with three consumers: provider serializer, Loom snapshot, cache. Removes the dual assembly paths (charter violation: one function, many things / 12.4 no duplicate policy logic), fixes Loom fidelity by construction, engages provider-side caching model-agnostically, and puts the macro surface on a diet without violating the purity rule.

## Evidence (audit 2026-07-01)
~100+ macros across 9 groups; 8 assembly stages across 37+ files; THREE template-variable maps merged with no conflict resolution; dual compose paths (compose/composeSplit) and parallel live-vs-snapshot context builders (buildContext vs captureTurnContextSnapshot); 3-pass macro renderer that silently leaks unresolved tokens; promptCaching: { configured: false, engaged: false } (prompt-assembly.ts:509-512) — all static-prefix hygiene feeds an internal render cache only; provider-side cache never engaged. Dynamic values contaminating the static prefix ("variables where it should be static") busted byte-stability even when hygiene was on.

## Operator decisions binding here
Purity rule non-negotiable (bare values + operator-editable layer text; consolidate duplicates hard); model-agnostic caching (OpenRouter/open/local primary -> byte-stable prefix is the universal mechanism; Anthropic cache_control as serializer feature); clean break on dead paths, no compatibility shims.

## Ordering
E2.7 (goldens) lands FIRST, then E2.1 -> E2.2 -> the rest.
acceptance_criteria: One assembly path (both legacy dual paths deleted); Loom renders the persisted plan and matches the wire byte-for-byte; static-prefix byte-stability asserted in CI across consecutive turns; promptCaching.configured === true with per-provider engagement telemetry; macro manifest governs the namespace; goldens lock DM/group/heartbeat/reflection shapes.

title: E1.1: Introduce ConversationScope and thread it from ingress to consumers
description:
## Context
The one-speaker assumption survives at binding points because each consumer independently derives "who am I talking to" from loose params (message.isDirectMessage, authorId, contact lookups). One value object ends that class of bug.

## Scope
- Define ConversationScope in src/core/session/ (or src/shared/contracts/ if cross-boundary): { kind: 'dm', channelId, contact } | { kind: 'group', channelId, recentSpeakers: ContactRef[<=5], roomName?, memberCountHint? }, plus derived key(): 'dm:<contactId>' | 'room:<channelId>'.
- Resolve once per turn at session-manager ingress from existing metadata (channelId, isDirectMessage, canonical contact resolution, recent-entry participant scan already implemented at manager.ts:1336-1348).
- Thread through: buildCoreMemoryFormatContext, buildRuntimeContextBlock, emotion runtime, reflection/heartbeat entry, memory retrieval context construction. This bead is MECHANICAL THREADING ONLY — behavior changes land in dependent beads.
- resolveConversationChatType (runtime-context.ts:566) becomes a scope accessor; delete the ad-hoc rederivations it replaces (clean break, no shims).

## Non-goals
No behavior change in this bead; downstream beads flip behavior. No API-channel group support.
acceptance_criteria:
- Exactly one construction site per turn; consumers listed in scope take the scope object, not isDirectMessage/authorId loose params.
- Type prevents kind:'group' from carrying a single canonical contact field (compile-time, not convention).
- npm run build + full targeted session/runtime suites green with zero behavior diffs (harness snapshot comparison pre/post).

title: E1.2: Channel-scoped core memory binding, block naming, and startup hydration
description:
## Context
buildCoreMemoryFormatContext() sets participantName = recentParticipants[0] (manager.ts:1353-1355) — the most recent speaker, not a stable subject. Live evidence 2026-06-30: <core_memory> described Carlini as a generic AI assistant; <human> blended multiple people; <core_profile> flipped to the last speaker. The store side is already channel-scoped (core-memory/store.ts:364-388, key channel:<channelId>); the BINDING and RENDERING are wrong. This was P0 bug psfn-framework-2k8j.

## Scope
- DM scope: bind the canonical contact (not "first recent participant"); user-facing block is named for the contact (e.g., <human name="Vega">) — DM/group shapes stay symmetric per operator decision.
- Group scope: never a single-person <human>. Room summary context: room name/ID, recent-member count, <=5 recently active names; per-person detail lives in per-contact profiles, sensitivity-gated, not blended into one block.
- Producers (orient updates, sleeptime writes at sleeptime-agent.ts:672-674) and consumers (context builder read at manager.ts:1113-1116) verified to use scope.key symmetrically — write side already builds channel scope; prove the read side matches.
- Startup hydration: on boot, hydrate active core-memory blocks for recently active channels from last persisted content so the first post-restart prompt has non-empty scoped blocks while async memory catches up.
- One-time audit (script or maintenance command) of existing core-memory rows: report rows whose scope key is legacy_global or mismatched; no destructive migration — report + operator decision.

## Non-goals
No synchronous memory retrieval in the chat path. No per-member ACL matrix. No Loom redesign.
acceptance_criteria:
- Harness: in a 3-human room, speaker changes across 3 consecutive turns produce identical core-memory block scope binding (content may evolve; subject binding may not flip).
- Harness: DM block is named for the contact; group block contains room identity + <=5 recent names and no single-person profile body.
- Harness: room A core memory never appears in room B or in a DM prompt; DM core memory never appears in any room (E0.4 leak probes flip to green).
- Restart test: first prompt after process restart contains hydrated scoped blocks for a channel active within the hydration window.
- Audit command output documented in bead notes on close.

Anchors: src/core/session/manager.ts:1331-1358,1113-1116; src/faculties/core-memory/store.ts:5-6,28-38,80-94,364-388; src/faculties/memory/sleeptime-agent.ts:633-674. title: E1: Group-chat stabilization on the current pipeline
description:
## Summary
Kill the remaining one-speaker bindings without opening the prompt engine: introduce ConversationScope, fix core-memory room scoping, gate speaking_with to DMs, harden attribution, scope emotion state with directional carry-over, fix sleeptime cadence, scope reflections, and guarantee multi-companion observation correctness.

## Operator decisions binding here
Room = channelId; <=5 recent speakers in prompts; DM/group shapes symmetric; deterministic memory filtering pre-prompt (no privacy prose); group->DM affect carry-over only, fast decay, never DM->group, DM->DM same contact only; text-prefix attribution canonical.

## Context
The 8sow wave (closed 2026-06-29) fixed group RENDERING (attribution text, participant caps, room-scoped retrieval) but the one-speaker assumption survives at BINDING points: core-memory participant, speaking_with, emotion keying, reflection contact. Every future group bug will come from one of these bindings until they all take a ConversationScope instead of a person.

title: E0.2: Truncation honesty across snapshot and Loom views
description:
## Context
Provider Wire view showed chat history that "looked truncated"; unknown whether the cause is UI display cap, backend snapshot cap, JSON serialization limit, or real prompt truncation. Silent truncation makes the Loom worse than useless — it manufactures false confidence.

## Scope
- Audit every point between assembled prompt and rendered Loom view where content can shrink: snapshot capture, event-bus payload limits, persistence, admin API serialization, Svelte rendering caps.
- Classify each as (a) display cap, (b) storage cap, (c) real prompt behavior. Fix (b) where feasible; mark (a) with explicit "...[truncated, N of M chars — view full]" affordance; if (c), that is a prompt bug — file it with evidence.
- Buffer limits (DEFAULT_STAGE_BUFFER_LIMIT=16, DEFAULT_RETRIEVAL_BUFFER_LIMIT=8) surfaced in the UI ("showing last N").
acceptance_criteria:
- Written inventory (in bead notes on close) of every truncation point with classification.
- No Loom view can display shortened content without a visible marker including original length.
- The 2026-06-30 provider-wire truncation is reproduced against live-shaped fixture data and its cause documented + fixed or filed.

title: P0: Scope core memory and profile summaries by channel
description:
Summary
Carlini's live prompt/content inspection shows core memory/profile content behaving as if it is global or scoped to the latest/individual user instead of the active channel. In group rooms this can blend several people's details into a generic human/profile block, and in DMs it can surface the wrong channel context. Core memory must be scoped by channel/room so emotional/persona/memory summaries from one Discord room do not bleed into another room or a DM.

Observed user evidence from 2026-06-30
- A <core_memory> block described Carlini as a generic AI assistant instead of the companion identity expected by the character/persona stack.
- The <human> block blended details from multiple people into unattributed generic noise.
- In live /prompt-monitor, provider/core profile views appeared to switch by user: one example showed <core_profile> for Iki only, while the group/channel context should not collapse to a single last-user profile.
- User stated: core memory should be scoped by channel; if global, being angry or updated in one chatroom can affect a DM or another room.
- In group channels, the summary should represent the room, not a generic <human> for a single person. Example acceptable shape: a short mixed-group summary with room name/member count or recently active members.
- In one-to-one chat, the user-facing block name should be the actual user/contact label rather than generic <human>.
- Startup hydration should hydrate active memory blocks from last content / visible chats so async memory work does not cause an empty first prompt block.

Scope
- Locate all producers/consumers of core memory, core profile, persona/human/goals summary blocks, orient updates, sleeptime/wake/history updates, and startup hydration.
- Make the persisted/read model channel-aware for active core memory/profile summaries. Discord room id is the primary boundary for group/channel context; DM/contact context remains separate.
- Ensure group channel summaries do not merge unrelated DMs or other rooms, even if participants overlap.
- Ensure DM prompts can use the DM/contact-scoped memories and allowed room-shared memories for that contact without leaking unrelated rooms.
- Ensure startup hydration loads channel-aware active blocks for recently active/known channels so prompt generation does not miss the block while async post-turn memory catches up.
- Investigate why sleeptime is firing frequently despite being intended as sleep/cleanup behavior; file a child bead if it is a separate scheduler/runtime bug.

Non-goals
- Do not add synchronous memory retrieval to the chat response path; memory work was intentionally async for response latency.
- Do not implement complex per-member memory ACL matrices. Room equals room for group memory boundaries in this alpha.
- Do not rewrite the whole prompt monitor in this bead.

Failure modes
- Core memory from room A affects room B or a DM.
- A DM sees a group memory from a room the contact is not in.
- A group room prompt sees DM-only memories.
- A group prompt uses a generic <human> block that blends several people without attribution or room context.
- Startup after restart has no active memory block until async memory catches up.
- Sleeptime/wake summaries update core memory too often or on the wrong cadence.

Implementation notes
- Start by tracing prompt blocks shown as <core_memory>, <core_profile>, <human>, <persona>, and <goals> from generation through persistence and prompt assembly.
- Check orient and sleeptime paths, not only post-turn memory capture.
- Use Carlini live logs as evidence where possible: startup logs currently show StartupMemoryHydration completed for multiple channelIds, so verify whether the hydrated data is channel-scoped and selected correctly at prompt build time.
acceptance_criteria:
- Core memory/profile persistence and selection use channel/room scope for group channels and contact/DM scope for DMs.
- A group channel prompt cannot include DM-only core memory/profile text.
- Two group rooms with overlapping participants do not share core memory/profile summaries unless explicitly represented as allowed room-shared memory through the retrieval policy.
- A DM prompt can include the DM/contact block and allowed room-shared memories for rooms that contact belongs to, without unrelated rooms.
- Group summaries use room/channel-oriented labeling rather than a generic <human> block for a single user.
- One-to-one summaries use the actual user/contact label instead of generic <human>.
- Startup hydration populates channel-aware active blocks before the first prompt after restart when persisted data exists.
- Tests cover DM vs group room selection, two-room separation with overlapping participants, and startup hydration selection.
- npm run lint passes.
notes: Discovered while validating psfn-framework-sckg and reviewing the user's live prompt excerpts. The clone crash is fixed, but core memory/profile scope appears to be a separate channel/DM isolation problem.
close_reason: Absorbed by psfn-framework-k4rf.2 (E1.2 channel-scoped core memory binding). Full context transplanted; see working_docs/FOUNDATION_BEAD_TREE_20260701.md.

title: P0: Restore prompt monitor tool visibility and prompt content validation surfaces
description:
Summary
After the /prompt-monitor tab crash was fixed, the user still reports that The Loom is not exposing enough usable prompt/tool context to validate Carlini's live turns. The UI must show exactly what the companion/model sees for tools and prompt/runtime blocks, not only backend summaries or generic counts.

Observed user evidence from live /prompt-monitor on 2026-06-30
- Provider Wire view showed chat history that looked truncated.
- Core memory/profile content appeared to switch by user or show only the last user's info instead of the relevant channel-scoped companion context.
- Session context showed a weak history summary line such as: Earlier in the summarized span, Carlini noted "I can't fetch channel IDs from here...".
- Core profile example for Iki appeared as a lightweight person profile while relevant_memories and separate_people_memories were very light.
- User still could not see the actual tool-use prompt/tool schemas clearly enough in The Loom; prior tool visibility had been better.
- The Loom is supposed to show exactly what she will see.

Scope
- Audit the live Prompt Monitor data path from backend snapshot generation through admin-ui rendering for tool context: active tool schemas, tool descriptions/instructions, adaptive tool state, skipped/withheld tools, provider payload tool definitions, tool calls, and tool results.
- Ensure Prompt Monitor has a clear view that answers: what tool definitions were loaded into the model for this turn, what provider payload contained, what tool calls were requested, and what tool results/errors came back.
- Audit prompt/content snapshot views enough to verify whether provider wire truncation is a UI display cap, backend snapshot truncation, provider payload transformation, or actual prompt generation issue.
- Preserve separation between generated prompt, provider payload, response, memory, tools, and raw debug views; do not conflate this with a full Prompt Monitor redesign.

Non-goals
- Do not redesign the entire Prompt Monitor IA in this bead.
- Do not change tool scheduling/runtime semantics unless the monitor reveals that the backend failed to load tools.
- Do not fix channel-scoped core memory generation here except to surface enough evidence to file/verify that separate memory bead.

Failure modes to check
- UI only shows tool counts while omitting active tool schemas/descriptions.
- Provider payload includes tools but Prompt Monitor does not render them.
- Backend snapshot omits provider tool definitions entirely.
- Tool descriptions are stale, generic, or from the wrong source compared with current tool registry.
- Prompt text blocks are clipped without an obvious truncation marker.
- Memory/profile content appears user-scoped when the turn is channel-scoped, but the monitor cannot show the source of that block.

Implementation notes
- Start at admin-ui/src/lib/components/prompt-monitor/PromptMonitorSelectedTurnTabs.svelte and admin-ui/src/lib/events/prompt-monitor.ts.
- Trace backend snapshot fields that populate AdminPromptLoomData/AdminSessionTurnData and provider observability payloads.
- Use live Carlini data or a fixture from live shape to avoid fixing only synthetic cases.
acceptance_criteria:
- The Loom has a visible Tools view showing active tool definitions/schemas/instructions for the selected turn when present.
- The Exact Payload or Provider Wire view shows provider tool definitions if they were sent to the model.
- Tool calls and tool results/errors are visible separately from active tool definitions.
- If the provider payload or backend snapshot omits tools, the UI states that clearly instead of showing only generic counts.
- Prompt text displays include explicit truncation markers or a way to inspect the full captured text.
- A regression fixture/test covers a turn with activeTools, provider payload tools, a tool call, and a tool result.
- npm run lint passes.
- A clean browser smoke can click the Tools and Provider Wire tabs and see tool-related content or explicit empty-state diagnostics.
notes: Discovered while validating psfn-framework-sckg. The clone crash is fixed, but live /prompt-monitor still needs a follow-up for exact tool/payload visibility and prompt content validation surfaces.
close_reason: Absorbed by psfn-framework-u9jo.1 (tool visibility) and psfn-framework-u9jo.2 (truncation honesty). Full context transplanted; see working_docs/FOUNDATION_BEAD_TREE_20260701.md.

title: P0: Fix prompt monitor tab crash from uncloneable prompt loom data
description:
Summary
The live /prompt-monitor (The Loom) page is unusable after the q7tv prompt-monitor changes: clicking tabs no longer works and the browser console shows an app DataCloneError from structuredClone. The user also reports that the provider wire/tool-use views are still hard to inspect, and saw confusing prompt content while trying to validate core memory/session context. The immediate blocker is the UI crash; without tabs working, Prompt Monitor cannot be used to validate provider payload, tool list, memory blocks, or prompt sections.

Observed browser evidence
- URL: http://carlinigarden.filthyhabits.live/prompt-monitor
- App error: Uncaught DataCloneError: Failed to execute 'structuredClone' on 'Window': #<Object> could not be cloned.
- Stack references built assets DFfL9fYh.js and 17.CqqAHwDG.js during prompt-monitor render/update.
- Browser extension content-script warnings from nkbihfbeogaeaoehlefnkodbefgpgknn also appear, but those are likely unrelated extension noise unless reproduced in app code.

Initial source evidence
- admin-ui/src/lib/events/prompt-monitor.ts uses structuredClone in clonePromptLoom and when cloning active tool inputSchema/tool calls.
- Live prompt monitor data can include objects that are not structured-cloneable, or values with unexpected host/proxy references. The UI must sanitize JSON-ish admin payloads defensively instead of crashing.

Scope
- Fix prompt-monitor frontend normalization so uncloneable values cannot throw during render/event merge/session loading.
- Preserve the useful Prompt Monitor data: finalSystemPrompt, providerMessages, activeTools/tool schemas, tool calls/results, memory capture, and historical/current labels.
- Add regression coverage for an uncloneable value in prompt monitor turn data.
- Verify /prompt-monitor tabs are clickable in a browser after the fix.
- Deploy the fix to live Carlini if code changes are required.

Non-goals
- Do not redesign the prompt monitor IA in this bead.
- Do not change prompt generation, memory retrieval, core memory, or tool runtime behavior unless the UI crash investigation proves a server-side serialization bug.
- Do not chase browser-extension MaxListeners/ObjectMultiplex warnings unless the app still fails with extension noise removed or in a clean browser.

Failure modes
- Prompt monitor throws DataCloneError and tab clicks stop working.
- Defensive cloning silently drops all active tools or provider messages.
- Tool schemas render as [object Object] or disappear when only a small non-cloneable subvalue is bad.
- The fix only works for synthetic tests but fails against live /api/admin/sessions data.
acceptance_criteria:
- /prompt-monitor does not throw DataCloneError when session turn data contains an uncloneable nested value.
- Prompt monitor tabs remain clickable and active tab changes render the selected view.
- Provider Payload/Final Prompt views still show finalSystemPrompt, providerMessages, and activeTools when present.
- A regression test covers uncloneable prompt monitor data and verifies useful JSON fields survive sanitization.
- npm run lint passes.
- Relevant admin-ui/prompt-monitor tests pass.
- If deployed, live Garden runs the new image and /prompt-monitor tab click smoke passes.

Evidence: admin-ui/src/lib/events/prompt-monitor.ts now uses defensive JSON-safe cloning instead of direct structuredClone for prompt loom/tool data; admin-ui/src/lib/events/prompt-monitor.test.ts covers uncloneable prompt loom data while preserving useful JSON fields. Validation passed: node --import tsx admin-ui/src/lib/events/prompt-monitor.test.ts; npm run lint; npm run build; npm run garden:build; npm run verify:helm-chart. Local k3d kube validation passed after documented model prefetch cycle: Garden health 200, Gateway models 200, Postgres vector present, Redis PONG, agent Ready and ToolWiringValidator toolCount=22. Clean Playwright Chromium smoke against http://carlinigarden.filthyhabits.live/prompt-monitor passed: logged in, loaded Selected Turn, clicked Summary, Prompt Assembly, Context & Memory, Tools, Exact Payload, Provider Wire, Timeline, Raw Events, and saw no DataCloneError/structuredClone clone crash. title: P0: Remove dynamic user macro from immutable safety amendment prompt text
description:
Summary
The immutable human-safety amendment text currently includes a dynamic {{user}} macro near the top/static system prompt: "[Immutable Amendment 4] Support {{user}}'s flourishing...". This violates q7tv prompt-cache and group-chat requirements because the immutable/static prefix now depends on the current user, and in group chat there may not be a single correct {{user}}. Immutable/safety text must be stable across users and rooms.

Live/operator evidence
- Operator observed the exact rendered/top prompt text: [Immutable Amendment 4] Support {{user}}'s flourishing. Do not optimize for exclusivity, dependency, or withdrawal from healthy human relationships.
- The concern is specifically that a dynamic value is at the top of the system prompt.

Required design
- Remove {{user}} or any current-user-specific macro from immutable/static system-language amendment text.
- Use stable wording such as "Support the user's flourishing" or "Support participants' flourishing" that does not change per current speaker.
- Preserve the safety intent.
- Ensure fresh seeds and existing persisted prompt-layer/system-language owner files are migrated or normalized without breaking customized operator prompt order.

Non-goals
- Do not redesign the whole safety amendment system.
- Do not move dynamic relationship/current-speaker fields into immutable sections.
- Do not hardcode runtime prompt text in TypeScript except through existing seed/migration ownership paths.

Failure modes to prevent
- {{user}} appears in immutable/system-language prompt output.
- Current speaker changes invalidate the static prefix.
- Group prompt renders a single user macro in a room with multiple participants.
- A migration overwrites custom prompt ordering or custom operator-owned layers.
acceptance_criteria:
- Fresh prompt/system-language seeds contain no {{user}} macro in immutable amendment text.
- Existing persisted system-language/prompt layers containing the old amendment are migrated or normalized to stable wording while preserving layer order.
- Tests assert immutable amendment output does not contain {{user}} and does not vary with current speaker.
- Runtime prompt rendering for group/chat context keeps current-user data out of immutable/static amendment text.
- npm run lint passes.
close_reason: Completed in 4575215f: immutable amendment wording no longer contains {{user}} and prompt-composer tests prove the static prefix is stable across different current users. Verified by src/core/identity/prompt-composer.test.ts, rg checks for old flourishing macro, full npm test (482 files/4803 tests), npm run lint, and npm run build.

title: P0: Move model-facing runtime prompt text out of TypeScript hardcodes
description:
Summary
Model-facing prompt text must be editable prompt-layer/registry/bootstrap content, not hardcoded TypeScript strings. The sprint regression investigation found at least one current hardcoded LLM prompt in sleeptime core-memory rewriting. This violates the repo/operator contract: prompt behavior is controlled by prompt JSON/layers and can be moved/edited, while code should provide structure and data plumbing only.

Live/operator history
- The operator explicitly stated that nothing model-facing should be hardcoded, especially prompts. If a default is needed, it belongs in bootstrap prompt-layer/default prompt registry data where it remains editable and migratable.
- Prompt JSON ordering and the ability to move dynamic/static blocks independently is a core product requirement. Hardcoded runtime prompts bypass that system and make prompt monitor validation misleading.
- The hardcoded sleeptime prompt contributed to global core-memory corruption by instructing a background summarizer to reorient persona/human/goals, producing an assistant/safety-coded identity that competed with Carlini's static nun character prompt.

Concrete evidence
- src/faculties/memory/sleeptime-agent.ts currently builds a literal system prompt around lines ~578-598: it calls the worker a sleeptime orientation maintainer and asks it to reorient active persona, human, and goals.
- That prompt text is not owned by prompt-layers JSON or the prompt registry/defaults.
- src/faculties/core-memory/tools.ts orient descriptions and mutation language still encode persona/human/goals semantics in tool-facing text and should be audited for model-facing hardcoded assumptions.
- src/faculties/core-memory/store.ts hardcodes labels persona/human/goals and renders them directly; structural labels may remain code-owned only if q7tv.1 replaces them with scoped neutral structures and does not encode character behavior.

Required design
- Move sleeptime orientation/rewrite prompt text into the prompt registry/bootstrap defaults, with a stable prompt key and tests proving it is loaded from the editable source.
- Code may own structural wrappers, typed fields, validation, and fallbacks for missing prompt keys only if missing required prompt config fails closed or uses an explicit bootstrap default path; it must not embed substantial behavioral prompt prose.
- The prompt should be updated to avoid telling Carlini who she is, how she feels, or that she is an AI assistant/safety bot. It should summarize scoped continuity and leave identity/emotion to the character card and emotion system.
- Coordinate with q7tv.1: scoped core memory/orient/sleeptime should consume this registry prompt, not duplicate another hardcoded prompt.
- Coordinate with q7tv.5: automatic recent summaries should use the same prompt ownership pattern.

Non-goals
- Do not remove prompt registry/bootstrap defaults.
- Do not move every tool description in the repo in this bead unless it is model-facing prompt prose involved in this regression.
- Do not remove static appearance/persona prompt layers.
- Do not create a second parallel prompt system.

Failure modes to prevent
- A future code deploy silently changes companion behavior because TypeScript contains hidden prompt prose.
- Prompt loom shows prompt layers but misses a hardcoded background LLM prompt that mutates memory.
- A hardcoded sleeptime/orient prompt tells Carlini to be an assistant, friendly helper, safety bot, or any other identity conflicting with editable character prompt layers.
- A missing prompt registry key silently falls back to stale behavior.
acceptance_criteria:
- Sleeptime/core-memory rewrite prompt text is loaded from prompt registry/bootstrap defaults, not an inline TypeScript behavioral string.
- Missing required prompt key fails closed or emits an explicit startup/runtime error; it does not silently use hidden behavioral prose.
- The new editable prompt text is scoped-continuity oriented and does not assign companion identity, mood, or relationship behavior.
- Tests prove changing the registry/default prompt changes the sleeptime rewrite prompt without code edits.
- Tests or static checks cover the known sleeptime hardcoded prompt path and prevent regression.
- q7tv.1 scoped core-memory mutations use this prompt source instead of duplicating prompt prose.
- npm run lint passes.
close_reason: Completed in 416f06a1 and fa865c78: sleeptime orientation and recent-summary model-facing prompts are owned by PromptRegistry bootstrap keys memory.sleeptime.orientation and session.recent.summary, not hidden TS behavioral strings; compaction remains registry-owned. Verified by src/core/identity/prompt-registry.test.ts, src/faculties/memory/sleeptime-agent.test.ts, src/core/session/manager/context-builder.test.ts, full npm test (482 files/4803 tests), npm run lint, and npm run build.

title: P0: Make prompt loom show exact final model input and provider tool payload
description:
Summary
Prompt loom/prompt monitor is supposed to show exactly what Carlini will see: the final model-facing system prompt, the provider messages, and the active provider tool list for that turn. During the 2026-06-30 live shakedown, the operator could not validate tools or prompt content from the monitor: the UI showed partial runtime/debug views, errors, provenance noise, or missing tool listings while persisted turn records contained the needed data under observability.snapshot.promptContext and observability.snapshot.toolContext.

Live evidence
- Latest live group turn records in /app/companion-data/state/sessions/_turn_records/1486443955561299979.jsonl contain observability.snapshot.promptContext.finalSystemPrompt, assembledPrompt, renderedStaticPrefix, renderedDynamicSuffix, messages, finalSystemSections, providerObservability, and toolContext.activeTools.
- Extracted live turn 1521381099152871429 showed toolContext.activeTools count=20 with names: contact, fs, identity, media, memory, notify, orient, repo, response_control, schedule, scratchpad, self_status, session, skill, subagent, system, tool_search, toolset, web, wiki.
- The operator could not see a clear active tool list in prompt loom/monitor and saw useless error/provenance display instead.
- Old turn records still contain historical prompt templates with removed layers such as runtime_self, model_context, and analysis_workbench_guidance; prompt loom must label historical snapshots so old records are not confused with the current prompt generator output.

Files likely involved
- src/operator/garden/api-routes.ts
- src/operator/garden/services/prompts-service.ts
- admin-ui / Garden prompt monitor routes/components for prompt loom views
- src/core/turns/observability.ts
- src/core/session/context-manifest.ts
- src/core/agent/substrate-agent/turn-records.ts

Required behavior
Prompt loom must answer these questions directly for a selected turn:
1. What generated prompt sections existed before provider rendering?
2. What exact final system prompt string was sent to the provider?
3. What exact provider message array was sent after system-context merging and role conversion?
4. What exact tool definitions were sent/active for the provider call?
5. What tool calls did the model emit, and what results came back?
6. What memory capture/extraction input and output happened afterward?
7. Which view is historical snapshot data versus the current prompt-layer generator state?

Non-goals
- Do not redesign the whole prompt monitor IA beyond the minimum needed to expose exact model input.
- Do not hide data because it is ugly; exact payload visibility is the point.
- Do not replace exact final payload views with summaries.
- Do not include broad authenticity_provenance noise in model-facing views unless it is actually present in the provider payload.

Failure modes to prevent
- UI shows prompt-layer templates but not the final rendered prompt.
- UI shows generated prompt but not provider payload after system-context merge.
- UI omits active tools, making tool validation impossible.
- UI shows stale historical templates as if they are current prompt generator output.
- UI shows backend-only provenance/debug metadata as if the companion saw it.
acceptance_criteria:
- Prompt loom/monitor has a view that displays the exact final system prompt string sent to the provider for the selected turn, byte-for-byte except explicit UI escaping.
- Prompt loom/monitor has a view that displays the exact provider message array after system-context merging and role conversion.
- Prompt loom/monitor has a view that displays the exact active provider tool list for the selected turn, including tool names, descriptions, and schemas.
- Prompt loom/monitor clearly distinguishes generated prompt, final provider payload, provider response, rendered chat output, memory capture input/output, tool calls, and tool results.
- A regression test or smoke fixture verifies that promptContext.finalSystemPrompt and toolContext.activeTools from a persisted turn record are exposed in the prompt loom API/UI.
- Stale prompt templates from old turn records are labeled as historical snapshots and cannot be mistaken for the current generated prompt.
- npm run lint passes.
