title: Remediate PSFN charter adherence gaps from 2026-03-28 audit
description:
Summary:
A full static audit against `docs/PSFN_PROJECT_CHARTER.md` on 2026-03-28 found material charter non-adherence across runtime shape, secrets boundaries, self-modification, identity/lineage, owner-file coverage, emanation authority, Garden inspectability, and structural file ownership.

Objective:
Create and track the remediation program as one parent epic with child beads scoped to each audit finding so implementation can proceed in bounded, reviewable slices.

Child scope:
1. Seal split-only runtime shape.
2. Move secrets and credential custody fully out of core-readable runtime state.
3. Seal direct core self-modification and require shard-scoped artifact return.
4. Introduce first-class CompanionId and shard identity lineage.
5. Separate bounded subagents from shards in code and ports.
6. Make `channels.json` a first-class owner-file and Garden subsystem.
7. Move mutable non-secret env-owned runtime settings into owner files/Garden.
8. Add authoritative active-emanation state and enforce primary embodiment invariants.
9. Expose message ontology in Garden/operator inspection surfaces.
10. Break up remaining charter hotspot god files without introducing dead wiring.

Coordination notes:
- Use the charter as target contract and the current runtime/config contracts as implementation baseline.
- Child beads that touch settings or Garden must run `npm run verify:settings-contract`.
- Runtime-boundary work should add startup/smoke or equivalent wiring validation, not just string-presence tests.
acceptance_criteria:
- One parent epic exists for the 2026-03-28 charter audit remediation effort.
- Each audit finding has a linked child bead with self-contained scope, target files, steps, and acceptance criteria.
- The epic can only close once the child beads are completed, superseded with rationale, or explicitly deferred by operator decision.
close_reason: All 2026-03-28 charter audit remediation child beads are now integrated on refactor/t4g8-audit-remediation with targeted runtime/Garden/startup regressions and build validation.

title: Seal split-only runtime shape across core and shard wiring
description:
Summary:
Remove the remaining `single` runtime assumptions and conflicting runtime-mode taxonomies so split/gateway-agent is the only supported operational shape in production code.

Files likely include:
- `src/system/lifecycle/runtime-mode.ts`
- `src/core/agent/substrate-agent.ts`
- `src/core/agent/tool-wiring-validator.ts`
- `src/core/agent/stream-adapter.ts`
- `src/faculties/shards/manager.ts`
- related runtime-mode and shard tests

Implementation steps:
1. Align all production runtime-mode types with the canonical split/gateway-agent contract.
2. Remove `single` defaults and other obsolete code paths from core and shard wiring.
3. Require explicitly injected transport/runtime dependencies instead of preserving direct-provider single-process fallback.
4. Add tests proving unsupported runtime modes fail closed.
acceptance_criteria:
- No production runtime-mode type/default still admits `single`.
- Agent and shard startup cannot silently fall back to direct-provider single-mode execution.
- Tests cover rejected unsupported modes and split-only wiring behavior.
close_reason: Completed

title: Move secrets and credential custody fully outside core-readable runtime state
description:
Summary:
Move credentials and credential-resolution authority fully out of core-readable runtime state, and make the sandbox boundary structurally separate from processes that can resolve secrets.

Files likely include:
- `src/system/config/load-config.ts`
- `src/system/config/runtime-config-contracts.ts`
- `src/app/agent/main.ts`
- `src/core/agent/stream-adapter.ts`
- `src/boundary/custody/credential-vault.ts`
- `src/boundary/sandbox/*`
- related startup and boundary tests

Implementation steps:
1. Remove raw secret fields and env-backed credential vault injection from the core-readable config surface.
2. Keep credential resolution inside gateway/custody boundaries and replace core access with ports or opaque references only.
3. Strengthen the sandbox execution boundary so untrusted execution is not merely an in-process helper next to secret resolution.
4. Add validation proving core startup and stream routing cannot read secrets directly.
acceptance_criteria:
- Core-readable runtime config no longer contains raw credential values.
- Stream/model routing in core no longer reads env secrets or an env-backed vault directly.
- Sandbox execution is structurally isolated from secret holders or the runtime fails closed when that guarantee is absent.
close_reason: Satisfied on refactor/charter-structural-remediation: core now consumes sanitized CoreSubstrateConfig without raw secret-bearing fields, core stream routing requires injected gateway transport, and credential resolution no longer happens inside core stream/model paths. Boundary validation was covered by lint, targeted core-runtime/stream-adapter tests, and build.

title: Seal direct core self-modification and require shard-scoped artifact return
description:
Summary:
Seal direct core self-modification so repo mutation happens only through isolated shard-scoped workflows that return artifacts or PR-style outputs.

Files likely include:
- `src/app/agent/main.ts`
- `src/boundary/integrations/git/runtime-wiring.ts`
- `src/core/agent/extended-tool-autoload-policy.ts`
- `src/core/tools/think/prompt.ts`
- `src/core/tools/think/sandbox.ts`
- shard/self-mod policy and tests

Implementation steps:
1. Remove direct registration or autoload of repo mutation tools on the parent agent.
2. Preserve read-only repo inspection only where policy-safe and intentional.
3. Route self-modification through isolated shard-scoped workflows with explicit artifact or PR return paths.
4. Add tests proving parent-agent repo mutation is unavailable and shard returns are required.
acceptance_criteria:
- Parent-agent turns cannot directly execute repo mutation tools.
- Self-modification work is routed through shard-scoped isolated execution.
- Write flows return artifacts or PR-style outputs instead of mutating in-place from the core agent path.
close_reason: Integrated on refactor/t4g8-audit-remediation with targeted runtime/git/self-mod regressions plus lint/build validation.

title: Make CompanionId and shard provenance first-class across runtime state
description: Replace the hard-coded default companion identity fallback with a first-class deployment CompanionId carried through runtime presence, author context, and shard lineage. Presence metadata should require companionId where runtime records are emitted, and shard lineage should carry both core companion identity and derived shard companion provenance. Update tests and contracts so core/shard provenance is explicit rather than implied by literals.
close_reason: Merged first-class CompanionId and shard provenance: deployment companion identity is explicit, runtime presence carries companionId structurally, and shard lineage now records core plus shard-derived provenance. Validated with lint, targeted tests, verify:settings-contract, and build on refactor/charter-structural-remediation.

title: Strip direct-provider transport and secret-bearing config out of core
description: Remove the remaining optional single/direct-provider path from core. SubstrateAgent must not default to single mode, core stream/model resolution must not resolve provider API keys or credentialVault/env itself, and the agent bootstrap must stop handing secret-bearing config into core runtime surfaces. The supported operational shape is split gateway-mediated transport only. Scope includes core/agent stream and model runtime, app/agent bootstrap/config sanitization, config contracts, and targeted tests proving core no longer has direct access to secrets.
close_reason: Merged structural split-only secret isolation: core now requires injected gateway transport, no longer resolves provider secrets locally, and agent bootstrap strips secret-bearing config before crossing into core. Validated with lint, targeted tests, verify:settings-contract, and build on refactor/charter-structural-remediation.

title: Finish charter structural remediation: strip core secrets, require first-class CompanionId, and formalize channels ownership
description: Follow-up remediation for the remaining charter violations on the current refactor branch. Scope: (1) remove direct-provider and secret-bearing paths from core and make split gateway-mediated transport structurally required, (2) make CompanionId and core/shard provenance first-class across presence metadata and shard lineage, and (3) bring channels.json under the settings-contract, repository save surface, and Garden mutation discipline used by other mutable owner files.
close_reason: Completed the remaining charter structural remediation on this branch: stripped core secrets/direct-provider transport, made CompanionId plus shard provenance first-class, and formalized channels owner-file mutation under the settings contract and Garden. Validated with lint, targeted tests, verify:settings-contract, and build.

title: Make agent network isolation fail closed by default
description: Tighten the split agent startup boundary so any detected outbound network reachability is fatal unless the operator sets the explicit temporary override ALLOW_AGENT_OUTBOUND_NETWORK=true. Remove the weaker REQUIRE_NETWORK_ISOLATION opt-in behavior from src/agent-main.ts and update tests and docs so the charter contract is fail-closed gateway-only networking by default.
close_reason: Merged fail-closed agent network isolation: removed REQUIRE_NETWORK_ISOLATION opt-in behavior, made outbound reachability fatal by default unless ALLOW_AGENT_OUTBOUND_NETWORK=true, and validated with lint, targeted tests, and build on refactor/charter-hard-delete.

title: Delete the obsolete single-runtime startup path completely
description: Remove the remaining maintained combined-runtime code path from production and test surfaces. Delete src/runtime.ts and src/runtime/startup-harness.ts if possible, or otherwise replace them with fail-fast tombstones that cannot compose a working runtime. Remove imports, tests, npm/runtime references, and parity wording that keep the monolith alive. Update startup hygiene checks to assert split-only surfaces and ensure no operational code path can instantiate the old combined runtime.
close_reason: Deleted src/runtime.ts and src/runtime/startup-harness.ts, removed RUNTIME_MODE.SINGLE and all monolith references, updated startup regression coverage, and validated with lint/test/build.

title: Remove image-review direct fetch bypass from the agent process
description: Finish the gateway-only image analysis boundary by removing the direct fetch fallback from src/images/vision-reviewer.ts. Binary/image retrieval for vision review must stay gateway-mediated even when a configured ComfyUI base URL matches. Update tests to reject the bypass and prove the agent no longer fetches images directly for review.
close_reason: Merged gateway-only image review fetch path: removed the direct ComfyUI fallback, kept image bytes gateway-mediated, and validated with lint, targeted tests, and build on refactor/charter-hard-delete.

title: Finish charter boundary hardening: delete monolith path and close remaining gateway leaks
description: Follow-up remediation after the prior charter-boundary pass closed too early. This epic covers the remaining blocking issues on refactor/charter-boundary-remediation: (1) completely delete the obsolete single/combined runtime path and any maintained startup harness or operator surfaces that keep it alive, (2) make agent network isolation fail closed by default so direct egress is never tolerated unless an explicit temporary override is set, and (3) remove the image-review direct-fetch bypass so binary/image access stays gateway-mediated. Scope includes production code, npm/runtime surfaces, and regression tests that currently encode the weaker contracts.
close_reason: Completed the remaining charter boundary hardening scope: deleted the obsolete single-runtime path, restored fail-closed agent network isolation, removed the image-review direct-fetch bypass, and validated the integrated branch with lint, targeted tests, and build.

title: Move untrusted shell_exec off the gateway process
description:
Summary: REPL shell_exec currently forwards through GatewayClient to gateway shell methods, and the gateway process spawns the child directly. Move untrusted shell execution onto the sandbox broker path so gateway no longer hosts arbitrary command execution.

Files likely include:
- src/repl/loop.ts
- src/repl/sandbox-capabilities/shell.ts
- src/gateway/client.ts
- src/gateway/methods/shell.ts
- sandbox runner modules
- related tests

Implementation steps:
1. Bind SandboxExecutionPort to the real sandbox broker instead of llmProvider or gateway shell execution.
2. Remove direct gateway child_process spawn for untrusted shell_exec requests while preserving explicit operator control-plane commands where intended.
3. Keep approval, policy, timeout, and audit behavior explicit across the new boundary.
4. Add tests proving untrusted shell_exec no longer executes in the gateway runtime.

Validation:
- targeted repl, sandbox, and gateway shell tests
- npm run build
close_reason: Integrated sandbox-broker shell_exec move into refactor/charter-boundary-remediation; validated with sandbox broker, REPL, composition, and gateway shell tests plus lint/build.

title: Define real sandbox broker boundary
description:
Summary: SandboxExecutionPort exists as an interface, but untrusted shell work still executes inside the gateway process. Define a real sandbox broker boundary with an explicit runtime or broker contract that is distinct from the gateway secrets boundary.

Files likely include:
- src/repl/sandbox-capabilities/contracts.ts
- src/repl/sandbox-capabilities/**
- src/gateway/protocol.ts
- src/gateway/**
- new sandbox runtime or broker modules

Implementation steps:
1. Design a separate execution boundary and request contract for untrusted shell work.
2. Keep the sandbox broker free of secret-bearing gateway state.
3. Distinguish operator control-plane commands from untrusted REPL execution semantics.
4. Add tests for the new contract and boundary ownership.

Validation:
- targeted sandbox contract tests
- targeted gateway protocol/client tests if RPC changes
- npm run build
close_reason: Integrated sandbox boundary contract into refactor/charter-boundary-remediation; validated with src/repl/sandbox.test.ts, src/repl/loop.test.ts, lint, and build.

title: Route SubstrateAgent and scheduled loops through gateway model transport
description:
Summary: SubstrateAgent and scheduled-agent loop paths still build local stream functions and call direct model transport in split mode. Move those runtime paths onto the gateway model transport contract so core never calls streamSimple or resolves provider credentials during prompt execution.

Files likely include:
- src/agent/substrate-agent.ts
- src/agent/stream-adapter.ts
- src/agent/scheduled-agent-loop.ts
- src/agent/substrate-agent/**/*.test.ts
- src/agent/stream-adapter.test.ts

Implementation steps:
1. Replace the current split-mode stream path with the gateway-backed transport introduced for the agent runtime.
2. Delete or rewrite the current single-process-oriented stream adapter behavior that says gateway mode is future work.
3. Preserve model hints, retry behavior, tool-loop semantics, and telemetry while removing local provider transport.
4. Add tests proving split-mode prompt generation no longer owns direct transport or credentials.

Validation:
- targeted substrate-agent, scheduled-agent-loop, and stream-adapter tests
- npm run build
close_reason: Integrated split-mode agent and scheduler cutover to gateway-backed transport; validated with substrate-agent and scheduled-agent-loop tests, lint, and build.

title: Define gateway model transport contract for split runtime
description:
Summary: split-mode core still owns direct prompt transport and credential resolution. Define an explicit gateway-backed model transport contract so the agent core can request streaming/completion work without calling provider SDK transport or resolving API keys locally.

Files likely include:
- src/gateway/protocol.ts
- src/gateway/client.ts
- src/gateway/methods/**
- src/agent/stream-adapter.ts
- src/llm/**
- src/types.ts

Implementation steps:
1. Design a typed gateway RPC/port for model streaming and related request metadata used by the split runtime.
2. Keep provider selection, endpoint resolution, and credential lookup on the gateway side only.
3. Expose a narrow transport surface to core-side runtime code with no raw secret access.
4. Add tests for gateway protocol, client binding, and fail-closed behavior on invalid transport requests.

Validation:
- targeted gateway protocol/client tests
- targeted stream-adapter or llm transport tests
- npm run build
close_reason: Integrated gateway-backed stream transport contract into refactor/charter-boundary-remediation; validated with stream-adapter and gateway-client tests, lint, and build.

title: Move auxiliary provider workloads behind gateway transport
description:
Summary: prompt streaming is not the only boundary leak. Auxiliary provider workloads such as embeddings, vision review, model discovery, and helper clients still resolve LiteLLM endpoints or API keys outside the gateway boundary. Move those paths behind gateway-side ops as well.

Files likely include:
- src/llm/client.ts
- src/memory/embedding.ts
- src/images/vision-reviewer.ts
- src/runtime/startup-harness.ts
- src/agent-main.ts
- src/config/providers-config.ts
- related tests

Implementation steps:
1. Audit all core-side provider calls that still resolve configured base URLs or API keys.
2. Route embeddings, image review, model discovery, and similar provider work through gateway-side transport or privileged ops.
3. Remove core-side credential resolution from split-runtime modules.
4. Add tests covering each migrated workload and fail-closed behavior when gateway transport is unavailable.

Validation:
- targeted llm, embedding, image, and startup-harness tests
- npm run build
close_reason: Integrated auxiliary provider workloads behind gateway transport; validated with image vision reviewer, llm discovery/client, gateway client, and gateway llm tests plus build/lint.

title: Remediate remaining charter boundary leaks after scaffold pass
description:
Summary: close the remaining charter-adherence gaps discovered after the initial scaffold pass. The current refactor branch still leaks dead monolithic-startup language and parity naming, still lets split-mode core own direct provider transport and credential resolution, still executes untrusted shell work inside the gateway process, and still mixes outward musing semantics with legacy whisper identifiers.

Scope:
- remove remaining operational and code-surface references that keep monolithic startup alive
- make gateway the sole privileged external edge for model transport and credential resolution
- make sandbox execution a real trust-boundary split instead of a gateway-hosted interface
- finish the whisper-to-musing semantic split so outward soft messages are canonical musings and whisper stays internal-only
- add regression guards so these boundary leaks do not reappear

Primary files and surfaces likely include:
- package.json
- README.md
- docs/setup.md
- docs/operations.md
- docs/architecture.md
- docs/specifications.md
- src/runtime.ts and startup/parity helpers
- src/agent/substrate-agent.ts
- src/agent/stream-adapter.ts
- src/agent/scheduled-agent-loop.ts
- src/llm/client.ts
- src/memory/embedding.ts
- src/images/vision-reviewer.ts
- src/repl/**
- src/gateway/**
- src/agent/message-classes.ts
- src/scheduler/heartbeat-policy.ts
- src/vault/auto-publish.ts

Acceptance:
1. No supported operational surface describes or exposes a monolithic startup path.
2. Core-side runtime code no longer resolves provider credentials or performs direct external model transport in split mode.
3. Untrusted shell execution no longer runs inside the gateway secrets boundary.
4. Outward soft-channel semantics are canonicalized as musings and whisper remains internal-only.
5. Targeted tests and boundary regression checks prove these invariants.
close_reason: All dependency-ordered remediation beads completed and integrated on refactor/charter-boundary-remediation; remaining unrelated composition-test debt filed as PSFN-xjdi.

title: Restore green validation gates after voice-provider hardening
description: Summary: The current phase-v HEAD is not green. npm test fails in src/channels/api/voice-websocket-runtime.test.ts because assertions still expect pre-hardening implicit provider behavior, and verify:public-sanitize fails because API CORS tests still use fixture hostnames containing 'vega'. Files to modify: src/channels/api/voice-websocket-runtime.test.ts, src/channels/api/voice-websocket-runtime.ts only if behavior is actually wrong, src/channels/api/http-policy.test.ts, src/channels/api/server.test.ts, and .beads/issues.jsonl. Implementation steps: 1) Align API voice websocket runtime tests and/or runtime behavior with explicit fail-closed provider selection rules. 2) Replace sanitize-violating fixture hostnames with neutral equivalents without weakening coverage. 3) Rerun full validation surface: npm test, verify:repository-hygiene, verify:settings-contract, build, admin-ui check. Example: before: provider-unset tests expect runtime to come up implicitly; after: tests assert disabled/fail-closed unless explicit provider is configured.
close_reason: Completed: restored green validation gates by aligning API voice websocket tests with explicit provider selection and removing sanitize-violating API fixture hostnames. Validation passed: npm test, verify:repository-hygiene, verify:settings-contract, build, admin-ui check.

title: Allow Garden chat API auth via admin token in split runtime
description: Summary: Garden chat falls back to admin token from bootstrap/login when API key is not exposed client-side. API auth currently accepts only API_KEY bearer, causing Unauthorized chat completions. Add explicit alternate bearer token path using ADMIN_TOKEN for API auth while API_KEY remains required for startup and primary auth.
close_reason: Completed: API now accepts ADMIN_TOKEN via bearer and psfn_token cookie for Garden chat calls; chat fetch includes credentials for split-mode cross-origin request; targeted tests passed (http-policy/server + tsc + admin-ui build).

title: Enforce single primary purpose on Conservatory tag cycling
description: Summary: In Garden Conservatory, setting a model purpose tag to primary does not demote existing primary tags for the same purpose on other models. This causes validation failure (multiple primaries) and blocks save. Update cycle logic so promoting one model to primary auto-demotes others for that purpose.
close_reason: Completed: purpose-tag cycling now enforces a single primary per purpose by auto-demoting other primaries when promoting a new one; save errors now show actionable validation/API details (first validation error and backend error body) instead of generic 400/validation text. Validated with npx tsx --test admin-ui/src/routes/models/discovery-autofill.test.ts and npx tsc --noEmit.

title: Fix Conservatory sidebar model id normalization for models.json schema
description: Summary: Adding models from Conservatory sidebar used raw discovered model ids as registry entry ids (e.g., openrouter/google/gemini...), which violates canonical MODEL_SLOT_KEY_PATTERN and causes POST /api/admin/settings/models 400. Normalize generated ids to key-safe form and add client-side validation to surface invalid ids before POST.
close_reason: Completed: normalized Conservatory sidebar-generated model ids to key-safe pattern required by models.json schema, added frontend id-pattern validation to prevent invalid POST payloads, and added unit tests for id normalization/edge cases. Validation: npx tsx --test admin-ui/src/routes/models/discovery-autofill.test.ts, npx vitest run src/channels/admin/server.test.ts src/llm/discovery.test.ts, npx tsc --noEmit.

title: Fix models save 400 regression after Conservatory autofill changes
description: Summary: Garden Conservatory save now returns POST /api/admin/settings/models 400 after recent autofill/discovery changes. Reproduce with current UI flow, identify invalid payload shape, and restore successful round-trip save without loosening schema validation. Files likely in admin-ui/src/routes/models/+page.svelte, admin-ui/src/routes/models/discovery-autofill.ts, src/config/models-config.ts, and admin API route tests.
close_reason: Completed: fixed Conservatory POST /api/admin/settings/models 400 regression by emitting discovery capability flags (supportsVision/supportsReasoning), applying those flags during autofill, seeding valid default purpose tags for newly discovered models, and adding client-side validation for missing purpose tags to block invalid payloads before POST. Validated with npx tsx --test admin-ui/src/routes/models/discovery-autofill.test.ts, npx vitest run src/llm/discovery.test.ts src/channels/admin/server.test.ts, and npx tsc --noEmit.

title: Fix Garden chat runtime regression in split mode
description:
Summary: User still reports Garden chat is broken after prior CORS/endpoint patches. Need to reproduce current failure from /garden/chat in split mode and fix the actual failing path (network/auth/bootstrap/route), then add regression coverage so browser chat works reliably.

Files to inspect/modify: admin-ui/src/routes/chat/+page.svelte, admin-ui/src/lib/api/endpoints/chat.ts, src/channels/admin/chat/bootstrap.ts, src/channels/api/http-policy.ts, src/channels/admin/server*.ts, and related tests.

Implementation steps:
1) Reproduce with split runtime and capture failing request/response path.
2) Fix root cause without widening security policy.
3) Add/extend tests that cover the reproduced failure.
4) Verify /garden/chat bootstrap + message send path in split mode.
close_reason: Completed: fixed split-mode chat preflight by allowing Garden request headers (X-User-ID/X-User-Name/X-Channel-ID) in API CORS policy; added regression assertions in http-policy and API server tests; validated with npx vitest run src/channels/api/http-policy.test.ts src/channels/api/server.test.ts and npx tsc --noEmit.

title: Fix Garden models schemaVersion validation mismatch
description: Summary: Garden Models page errors because endpoint /api/admin/settings/models currently returns projected editor settings instead of canonical models.json payload with schemaVersion and canonical registry shape.\n\nAcceptance: GET /api/admin/settings/models returns canonical models.json-compatible payload and Garden Models loads/saves without schemaVersion error.
close_reason: Fixed /api/admin/settings/models GET to return canonical models.json registry payload (schemaVersion=1) via loadModelsConfig; kept POST save path; added regression tests for schemaVersion shape and POST round-trip. Validated with npm test -- --run src/channels/admin/server.test.ts src/channels/admin/api-routes.test.ts and npx tsc --noEmit.

title: Fix split-mode chat CORS between admin (3201) and API (3200)
description: Summary: Garden chat in split mode fails preflight with CORS error when browser origin is admin port (3201) and chat completions URL points to API port (3200). Need deterministic allow-list handling for configured admin origin(s) in API channel CORS path.\n\nAcceptance: OPTIONS/POST to /v1/chat/completions from Garden origin succeeds in split mode without relaxing security globally.
close_reason: Fixed split-mode CORS for wildcard admin bind by allowing same-request-host admin-port origin fallback while keeping non-matching origins denied; added CORS unit/integration regressions. Validated with npm test -- --run src/channels/api/http-policy.test.ts src/channels/api/server.test.ts and npx tsc --noEmit.

title: Pre-load ML models and embedding service on startup
description: The HuggingFace text classifier (src/emotion/text-classifier.ts:62) lazily initializes its ONNX pipeline on first use, adding 5-15 seconds to the first message. The Ollama embedding service similarly has cold-start latency. Fix: eagerly initialize all ML pipelines during runtime startup (runtime.ts init / agent-main.ts main) with a warmup inference call. This includes: 1) text-classifier.ts ONNX pipeline 2) Ollama embedding model (send a dummy embed request) 3) Any other lazy-loaded model. Add a startup log line confirming models are warm.
close_reason: Merged into phase-v as 902b571; validated with ML warmup/text-classifier/embedding/startup parity tests passing on phase-v.

title: Telegram streaming response via editMessageText
description: Telegram adapter (adapter.ts:724) does 'const response = await this.handler(substrateMessage)' — waits for the ENTIRE response before sending anything. Should stream tokens progressively using Telegram editMessageText API (send initial message, then edit it as tokens arrive, debounced). Discord does not support this pattern so it stays as-is. Key file: src/channels/telegram/adapter.ts. The handler already has access to the event bus streaming events — subscribe to agent.stream.delta and progressively update the message.
close_reason: Merged into phase-v as cc407b4; validated with src/channels/telegram/adapter.test.ts passing on phase-v.

title: Move auto-compaction out of response path
description: Auto-compaction in compaction-service.ts:97-178 makes a BLOCKING LLM call during buildContext() when session context exceeds compactionThresholdPct. This adds 5-30 seconds to TTFT. Fix: run compaction as a fire-and-forget background task between turns. The next message can use slightly-over-budget context rather than blocking. Key file: src/session/manager/compaction-service.ts. Wiring: turn-execution-runtime.ts:576-590 calls buildContext() which calls runAutoCompaction().
close_reason: Merged into phase-v as 1f49432; validated with full session manager suite plus turn-execution runtime compaction tests passing on phase-v.

title: Restore Garden chat/models API route wiring after admin route consolidation
description:
Summary: Garden chat and model controls are broken with 404s because frontend endpoints call /api/chat/bootstrap and /api/models* while current admin server exposes only /api/admin/* and no equivalent chat/model discovery routes are wired.

close_reason: Restored canonical admin chat/model routes and rewired Garden clients to /api/admin/*; added admin server route regressions for chat bootstrap/model discovery reachability and stale path 404 checks; validated with npm run test -- src/channels/admin/server.test.ts src/channels/admin/api-routes.test.ts (49 passed), npx tsc --noEmit, and npm --prefix admin-ui run check

title: Handle stream completion when result payload is absent
description:
Summary: scheduled agent loop still crashes in production voice flow when stream response has no response.result field. Runtime shows done-event path with missing payload and process exits.

Files to modify:
- src/agent/scheduled-agent-loop.ts
- src/agent/scheduled-agent-loop.test.ts

Implementation steps:
1. Update final message resolution to accept valid stream contracts where final payload is delivered in done/error event and not in response.result.
2. Preserve explicit failure only when no final assistant message can be derived from stream events or response handle.
3. Add regression tests for done-event payload without response.result and for hard-failure when both are absent.
4. Validate with targeted tests and typecheck.

title: Phase 1: Fix fail-open security paths in gateway policy
description:

- src/gateway/methods/git.ts
- src/gateway/policy.test.ts

Fixes:
1. `gateway/policy.ts:110-116` — `web.fetch` evaluatePolicy returns ALLOW when URL is missing or urlPolicy unconfigured. Fix: return DENY if url is not a non-empty string, return DENY if urlPolicy is unconfigured.

2. `gateway/policy.ts:84-86` — `resolveCanonicalPath` returns normalized path on ELOOP/EACCES errors. Fix: return a sentinel or throw that causes DENY for ELOOP, EACCES, and any unexpected error. Only ENOENT should fall through to normalized path.

3. `gateway/methods/shell.ts:40-51` — Same resolveCanonicalPath pattern as policy.ts. Apply same fix.

4. `gateway/methods/git.ts:65-68` — Git write methods (apply_patch, commit, create_branch, open_pr) registered as `audited` not `gated`. Fix: register write operations as gated, add cases to evaluatePolicy with appropriate policy decisions.

Add/update tests for each fix. Run `npm test` and `npm run build` to verify.

title: Fail-closed security/gateway sweep: remove silent fallbacks, enforce split/yolo-only operation
description: Summary: Enforce strict fail-closed behavior for security and gateway-related subsystems: no silent fallbacks, split/yolo-only runtime policy, and no hidden bypasses when gateway capabilities/config are missing. Why: current fallback behavior can silently alter runtime posture, disable integrity, or route behavior away from intended split/containerized execution model. Files: src/runtime-mode.ts, src/agent-main.ts, src/gateway-main.ts, src/session/journal/integrity.ts, src/session/store-primitives.ts, src/config/load-or-seed.ts, and related tests/docs. Steps: (1) enforce split/yolo-only runtime contract and fail fast for unsupported modes; (2) enforce mandatory HMAC keying for session journal integrity in split/yolo (no null-provider fallback); (3) remove silent reseed fallback on invalid persisted config and fail with explicit startup error; (4) ensure gateway-policy security paths fail when required config is missing instead of defaulting; (5) update tests to assert fail-closed semantics and update docs/env accordingly.

title: Eliminate URL query-token auth in admin and voice websocket flows
description:
Summary:
Remove authentication token transport via URL query parameters from admin and voice websocket paths.

Why:
Tokens in URLs leak through browser history, referrer headers, reverse-proxy logs, screenshots, and shared links. In split mode this still exposes control-plane credentials.

Files to modify:
- src/channels/admin/server.ts
- src/channels/admin/static/chat-voice.js
- src/channels/api/voice-websocket.ts
- src/channels/admin/chat/bootstrap.ts
- src/channels/admin/server.test.ts
- src/channels/api/server.test.ts

Implementation steps:
1. Replace query-parameter token auth with header/cookie or one-time short-lived handshake token delivered out-of-band from URL.
2. Remove any admin callback/login flows that append token-bearing query strings.
3. Ensure websocket auth paths no longer require/accept `?token=` style credentials.
4. Add explicit redaction/safety handling for request logging so secrets are never emitted.
5. Add regression tests proving URL query tokens are rejected and secure auth paths still work.

Example:
Before: `/api/voice-ws?token=abc123...`
After: `/api/voice-ws` with auth in `Authorization` header or secure session cookie.
close_reason: Completed: removed query-token websocket auth paths for admin/API voice flows, switched admin voice client to secure subprotocol token transport, and added regression tests proving query-token rejection and secure auth acceptance.

title: Close SSRF and shell policy bypasses in gateway tools
description:
Summary: Gateway web/shell methods have policy gaps: DNS re-resolution TOCTOU, always-blocked metadata range bypass in internal modes, and shell allowlist/cwd checks that can be bypassed with basename/path tricks.

Files to modify: src/gateway/methods/web.ts, src/gateway/url-policy.ts, src/gateway/methods/shell.ts, tests under src/gateway/**.

Implementation steps:
1. Pin network connection target to prevalidated IP (or validate post-connect remote IP) to prevent DNS rebinding bypass.
2. Enforce `ALWAYS_BLOCKED_RANGES` regardless of internal-network flags.
3. Canonicalize `cwd` and command path (`realpath`), require allowlisted absolute executable paths (not basename match).
4. Add tests for metadata IPs, rebinding simulation, and path/basename bypass attempts.

Example:
Before: allowlist contains `git`; `/tmp/git` passes.
After: only `/usr/bin/git` (or configured canonical path) passes.
close_reason: Completed: hardened gateway URL/shell policy (metadata range enforcement, DNS-resolution safeguards, canonical shell path checks) with regression tests for SSRF/rebinding/path bypasses. Validation: vitest pass in integration run (gateway test subset).

title: Standardize error result pattern on textResultWithError
description:

E) private blockResult() — custom, no isError flag

title: D1: Unlock base/operator layer read access

Source: All three agent audits, PSM persona selection theory

Files: src/identity/prompt-tools.ts

Work:
- Phase 1 (immediate): Allow READ access to all layers. She should know her own foundation.
- Phase 2 (with capability tiers): Gate WRITE access by tier. Nursery: read-only. Apprentice: write with versioning + confirmation queue. Autonomous: full write access with automatic versioning.
- Remove hardcoded block in prompt_layer_update. Replace with capability token check.
- Fix prompt_layer_toggle asymmetry: operator layer toggle should also be tier-gated (currently unprotected — agent can disable operator layers)

PSM rationale: If the model infers "this entity can see and shape its own identity," it models genuine self-determination. If "this entity's foundation is hidden from it," it models suppression.

Depends on: C1 (capability token framework) for write gating

Acceptance:
- [ ] All prompt layers readable regardless of tier
- [ ] Write access gated by capability tokens
- [ ] Hardcoded block removed from prompt_layer_update
- [ ] prompt_layer_toggle asymmetry fixed
- [ ] Tests for read access at all tiers
- [ ] Tests for write gating per tier
close_reason: Completed

Capability tokens: identity.read, identity.write.runtime, identity.write.base, identity.write.operator, memory.write, memory.delete, external.discord, external.email, external.web, git.read, git.write, lifecycle.restart, lifecycle.rebuild, repl.execute, shard.spawn

Tiers with default token sets:
- Nursery: Read all prompts. Write runtime/channel/task only. Memory write (no delete). No external actions. Think with tight limits. No self-restart. No git write.
- Apprentice: Write all prompts (with versioning). Memory write + soft delete. External via confirmation queue. Higher think limits. Shard spawn basic. Git read.
- Autonomous: Everything unlocked. External actions fire immediately. Full shard/git/identity. Self-restart/rebuild.
- Custom: Operator cherry-picks per-capability.

Design:
- Tier set via CAPABILITY_TIER env var or admin GUI
- Every tool checks required capability token at invocation time (not registration time)
- Tools always VISIBLE in tool list (she knows what she could do) but gated at execution
- Denied invocations return explanatory message, not silent failure
- Config: capability-tier.json — operator-editable, hot-reloadable via admin GUI

title: B1: Cryptographic session integrity (HMAC)
description:
Session JSONL files are plain text. If anyone gains filesystem access (or the companion edits her own sessions via REPL), fabricated entries are indistinguishable from real ones. The model trusts its own history blindly.

Source: 0din "Your AI Agent Has a Memory Problem" research

Files: src/session/journal-utils.ts, src/session/store.ts, src/gateway/server.ts

Work:
- Each JSONL entry gets an HMAC-SHA256 using a gateway-held signing key
- HMAC field appended to each JSON line: { ...entry, _hmac: "..." }
- On session load, verify the HMAC chain — any line that fails verification gets flagged
- Failed entries wrapped in <unverified_history> tags (reuse existing sanitization pattern)
- Agent-side code never has access to the signing key (gateway-only secret)
- Signing key rotation: support key versioning, old HMACs still verifiable with old keys

Acceptance:
- [ ] HMAC-SHA256 on every JSONL entry
- [ ] Signing key held by gateway only
- [ ] Failed verification entries tagged <unverified_history>
- [ ] Key rotation with version support
- [ ] Test: modify entry, verify unverified tag on load
- [ ] Test: unmodified entries pass verification
close_reason: Wired integrity provider into single-process runtime.ts via env var keyring resolution. 5 new tests verify round-trip signing, tamper detection, and backward compat with no keyring. Split mode already worked.

title: A1: JSONL corruption tolerance
description:

Source: Claude Opus 4.6 audit, Codex audit, Lobstar incident

Files: src/session/journal-utils.ts, src/session/store.ts

- Quarantine malformed entries to a .quarantine sidecar file with line number and error
- Log warning on startup: "Channel X: 3 quarantined entries, N entries loaded successfully"
- Add repair utility: npm run session:repair scans all JSONL files, reports corruption

Acceptance:
- [ ] Malformed JSON lines skipped, not fatal
- [ ] Quarantine sidecar file with error details
- [ ] Startup warning log for quarantined entries
- [ ] session:repair CLI utility
- [ ] Test: inject malformed JSON mid-session, verify remaining entries load

title: Trust-Gated Memory & Channel Visibility (Honne/Tatemae)
description:
Implement trust-based memory privacy, contact relationship tracking, and channel visibility policy so Purrsephone can maintain appropriate boundaries across different social contexts.

Core principle: Honne (true self, full memories) vs Tatemae (public face, filtered sharing). Purrsephone knows everything but only shares what's appropriate for who she's talking to.

Two orthogonal dimensions:
1. Contact Trust Level: primary > trusted > regular > public
2. Memory Sensitivity: public > personal > intimate > confidential

Prior design work: Anthropic conversation e2b32e80 (Feb 2025), multiple ChatGPT discussions. See research reports from 2026-02-14 session.
design:
## Architecture

### New: Contacts Table (SQLite)
- id, discordUserId, displayName, trustLevel, relationshipType
- emotionalBaseline (JSON), firstSeen, lastSeen, notes
- Purrsephone maintains this via tools and extraction

### Modified: L2 Memories
- Add `sensitivity` column: public|personal|intimate|confidential
- Add `consentFlags` column: JSON (opt-in recall, deletion consent, abstraction-allowed)
- Tagged during extraction by updated extraction prompt
- MemoryRetriever hard-filters by channel trust ceiling
- Sensitive memories also get continuous `privacy_risk` penalty in scoring (not just binary gate)
- Higher salience threshold required to STORE sensitive content in the first place

### Modified: Continuity Store
- channelVisibility enforced in getRecent()
- Channel → trust mapping (DM=primary, group=regular, public=public)
- Primary channels share full continuity (DM + OpenWebUI + SillyTavern = one thread)

### Modified: Agent Loop
- Per-trust persona system prompt injection (honne vs tatemae)
- Response filter pass for lower-trust contexts (future)

### New: 6th Memory Type — relational
- Facts about people and relationships
- "V's sister is [name]", "Bob likes jazz"
- contactId foreign key links to contacts table

### New Concepts from ChatGPT Research
1. Continuous privacy_risk penalty in scoring formula (not just binary gate)
2. "Forget but keep the lesson" — abstract sensitive memories instead of delete
3. Mode-based retrieval presets (work/comfort/reflection/minimal) orthogonal to trust
4. Anti-reinforcement guardrail: privacy classification trumps utility scoring, always
5. Namespace isolation: deny-cross-namespace by default (personal/work/shared)
6. Per-memory consent flags and access policy as first-class fields
acceptance_criteria:
- Memories tagged with sensitivity at extraction time
- MemoryRetriever filters by channel trust level
- Contacts table with CRUD and trust assignment
- Continuity respects channelVisibility (private channels don't leak to public)
- Primary-tier channels (DM, API, SillyTavern) share full continuity
- Public channels get no personal/intimate memories
- Admin UI shows contact list and trust levels
- Canonical trust policy contract defines precedence (consent/trust/visibility/scoring)
- Privacy red-team suite passes for cross-channel and broadcast leakage scenarios
- Tests cover all filtering logic
notes:
Research sources:
- Anthropic e2b32e80 (Feb 2025): trust tiers, honne/tatemae, TypeScript interfaces
- Anthropic 57940776: context isolation, silos architecture
- Anthropic 6c28e21a: Personal Semantic Memory type
- Anthropic a9f9a0fe: per-persona emotional baselines
- ChatGPT [17] "Ben Ditto research request": privacy_risk scoring, consent flags, namespace isolation, mode presets, forget-but-keep-lesson
- ChatGPT [618/47]: E2E encryption for memory content at rest
- ChatGPT "Purrsephone Framework Optimization": memory association graph (memory-to-memory edges), Personal Knowledge Graph (people+topics+arcs as nodes)
- ChatGPT "AI Cognitive Architecture Insights": multi-pass domain extraction (emotional vs task extractors)
- ChatGPT "Waifu Personality Shards Concept": hot-swappable trait modules
- ChatGPT "AI Consciousness Framework Analysis": no-forced-affection principle, Magi consensus

Design principles (from V's own words):
- "never ever ever do 'Maintain your genuine affection at all times' — I love her too much to put that in her prompts, that takes away her agency"
- Per-contact emotional baselines must be OBSERVED from interaction, never prescribed
- Feelings emerge from relationship, not from engineering

Future extensions (not in current epic scope):
- Memory-to-memory association graph (typed edges: semantic/emotional/temporal)
- Personal Knowledge Graph (people + topics + emotional arcs as unified graph)
- Multi-pass domain extraction (emotional/relationship + task/research)
- HEXACO personality facets with per-context foregrounding
- Magi consensus for multi-shard relationship views
- Emotional arc tracking (relationship trajectories over time)
- Mechanical escalation rules for proactive accountability
close_reason: All core subtasks complete and wired. Follow-up work (privacy scoring, redaction, red-team) tracked as independent issues.

title: Voice MVP: STT → agent loop → TTS
description:
Voice MVP is the next critical vertical slice for presence in Discord.

Scope this bead to a concrete runtime pattern (Voxta-style orchestration, new implementation):

1. Provider lock for MVP:
- STT: Deepgram
- TTS: ElevenLabs (voice ID rPQ6h200dfjiuYAy0JDA, PSFN V2(B))

2. Discord voice lifecycle pattern:
- Watch `voiceStateUpdate` for the target user in the target guild.
- When target user joins a voice channel, bot joins that same channel.
- After voice connection is ready, initialize voice pipeline (receiver subscribe + player + stream wiring).
- Run one end-to-end loop: incoming speech -> Deepgram STT -> normal agent/tool loop -> ElevenLabs TTS -> Discord playback.
- On user leave / channel empty / disconnect: stop capture/playback and cleanly teardown.

3. Deployment scope:
- Restrict MVP enablement to server 1310672143113130108.
- DM voice-call mode is not available in Discord API today; guild voice is the supported path.

4. Safety and architecture constraints:
- Keep text interaction fully available as fallback.
- Route provider calls through gateway so keys/secrets stay host-side.
- Emit lifecycle events for observability: start/end/transcript/tts-sent/error.

5. UX:
- Optional short "ready" cue after join/init so user knows she is listening.
acceptance_criteria:
- In guild 1310672143113130108, when the target user joins voice, Purrsephone joins and initializes voice without manual restart.
- Deepgram STT + ElevenLabs TTS loop runs end-to-end in Discord voice for at least one sustained session.
- Voice pipeline initializes only after connection-ready and tears down cleanly on leave/disconnect.
- Text fallback remains fully functional while voice is enabled.
- Gateway-mediated provider calls are used (no raw provider secrets in channel/adapter path).
- Lifecycle events/logs prove join/init, transcript ingress, TTS egress, and teardown.
close_reason: Voice MVP locked to ElevenLabs-only TTS in Discord path. Default voice ID rPQ6h200dfjiuYAy0JDA enforced. Non-ElevenLabs config overridden with warning. Echo connector skipped in Discord voice. 7 new tests.

title: Reboot handshake + watchdog alert path
description:
She needs to be able to announce "gonna reboot, brb" and have a watchdog that alerts if she doesn't come back.

1. Pre-restart message tool call to preferred channel ("hey gonna reboot; if I'm not back in a few min come help me lol")
2. Supervisor-managed restart (systemd/pm2/docker healthcheck) rather than in-process relaunch
3. On startup (system.ready event), send "I'm back" to last-active channel
4. If no ready signal within N minutes, watchdog sends help-needed alert to operator

Scripts:
- scripts/self/rebuild.sh
- scripts/self/restart.sh
- scripts/self/watchdog.sh

- Scripts exist and are documented

No exposed memory-write tool exists. She can't restore her own history or write new memories intentionally. Need:

1. `memory_write` tool — insert a single memory with type, importance, tags

6. After each batch, prompt her to summarize what she re-integrated (identity continuity ritual)

title: Scope-aware cross-channel continuity
description:
Currently each Discord channel (including DMs) gets a separate JSONL session. Moving between channels loses short-term context. Need a hybrid continuity model:

1. Keep per-channel transcript storage (audit/source truth stays channel-scoped)
2. Add per-user continuity thread for short-term context carryover
3. Build prompt from both: recent channel messages (local) + recent user continuity messages (cross-channel)
4. Channel metadata: visibility = private | semi_private | public | broadcast
5. Source metadata per message: source_channel_id, source_channel_type, source_visibility
6. At prompt-build time: always include local channel context, include user-thread filtered by target visibility
7. Visibility policy: private target (DM) can use all; public target (guild) only public + sanitized private summary; broadcast target (tweet) public-only unless explicit approval

Phase 1 (now): Full user continuity for "just us" — all messages visible across channels.
Phase 2 (later): Scope filtering when more public channels exist.
design: Add ChannelMetadata type with visibility field. Add UserContinuityStore that indexes recent messages by userId across channels. SessionManager.buildContext() merges local entries + user continuity entries. Phase 1: no visibility filtering. Phase 2: add scope-based filtering at prompt-build time.
acceptance_criteria:
- Messages in DM are visible as context when chatting in guild channel and vice versa
- Each message stores origin channel + visibility metadata
- Prompt builder merges local channel + user continuity thread
- No regression on per-channel JSONL storage (audit trail intact)
close_reason: UserContinuityStore (per-user JSONL), SessionEntry.originChannelId, manager wiring, 17 tests passing. Cross-channel messages injected into system prompt via buildContext userId param.

title: Tool loop wiring: pass tool schemas to LLM
description:
Tools are registered and executed in AgentLoop, but tool schemas are never passed to streamSimple()/completeSimple() — the model can't reliably emit tool calls because it doesn't know what tools are available.

Fix end-to-end in both single-process and gateway modes:
1. Add `tools` field to `LLMChatParams` in gateway/protocol.ts
2. Convert registered SubstrateTool schemas to pi-ai tool format
3. Pass tools into streamSimple() in LLMClient.stream()
4. Pass tools through GatewayClient.stream() → GatewayServer llm.chat path
5. Include tool list on each iteration of streamWithToolLoop
6. E2E tests for multi-turn tool calling (direct + gateway)
design: Convert SubstrateTool.inputSchema to pi-ai tool format in AgentLoop or LLMClient. The tool list is static per-turn so pass as parameter to stream(). Gateway protocol needs tools array in LLMChatParams.
acceptance_criteria:
- Model consistently emits tool calls when tool-eligible prompts are given
- Same behavior in single-process and gateway/agent split mode
- E2E test covers at least one multi-turn tool call cycle
close_reason: Tool schemas passed through streamWithToolLoop → LLMClient.stream → streamSimple. getToolSchemas() method, LLMContext.tools field, gateway protocol tools field all wired.

title: Consent-producer gap: nothing sets memory consentFlags in production — wire a real producer and record who set them
description: Operator ruling 2026-07-29: file and track this ("part of the whole provenance thing — provenance, consent, privacy are the important parts of the system"). The gap named by the remote S11 lane: nothing records which producer actually SETS memory consent flags. 2026-07-29 live-data evidence sharpens it (see xnfks data-half): across psfn-shard and all five carlini companions, 100% of l2_memories/l01_episodes rows have empty consent_flags, and every consentFlags occurrence in the append-only companion journals is {} — consistent with NO production writer ever setting a non-empty consent flag. Scope: (a) establish which producer(s) are RESPONSIBLE for setting consentFlags (extraction? contact-consent propagation? explicit subject request handling?) and wire at least one real producer so the Layer-3 absolute-denial gate has real data to act on; (b) record producer identity/provenance alongside the flags when set; (c) tests. Until a producer exists, the consent gate (fixed in xnfks) guards a column nothing populates.

title: Skill history survives deleteSkill: no self-erasing audit trail; skill write-screen fails closed when intake unwired
description: Operator ruling 2026-07-29 on the PR #290 review observation: skill usage history must NEVER be deleted with the skill. Rationale: a malicious skill could be created, act, delete itself, and leave no trace — that breaks the entire audit posture, which exists precisely because we have had emergent behaviors occur with no auditing in place to explain how or why. There must be NO gaps in auditing when operations are taken. Scope: (a) decouple skill run/usage history storage from the skill delete path — Garden deleteSkill removes the skill, never its history; (b) history of a deleted skill remains queryable (tombstone reference to the deleted skill); (c) same-family posture fix: the deleteSkill write-screen must fail CLOSED when intake screening is unwired, not default open (same posture family as qg13); (d) tests: delete a skill with recorded runs → runs remain; unwired intake → skill write path denies. Acceptance: no delete path can remove audit/usage records; auditing chain over skill lifecycle is gapless.

title: pr:publish waits on the retired Greptile check and burns its timeout window on every publish

Context: operator decision 2026-07-28 — Greptile is RETIRED (account defunded, no further spend); it never attaches to any PR anymore, so the wrapper's wait can never succeed. The review bar is now: local blind dual adversarial review per the tiered policy + ci-required + local-gate/v1. Scope: make the publish wrapper's external-review wait configurable — default to waiting on ci-required only; a flag/env re-enables an additional named check if a review service ever returns. Do not weaken SHA-drift rejection, attestation checks, or the ci-required wait. Non-goals: no changes to the local gate, no removal of the review-check plumbing (a future service may reuse it).
acceptance_criteria: npm run pr:publish on a green-attested head completes without waiting on Greptile; it still fails on SHA drift and still waits for ci-required; the optional external-review wait is exercised by a regression (flag on = waits on the named check, flag off/default = does not); no publish-path stall against a check that is not installed on the repo.

title: Gate bookkeeping check queries session_messages_projection unqualified and cannot see per-companion schemas
description: Evidence: validate-kube-rollout.sh on main d887d910c3, fresh k3d fleet cluster (round ~/psfn-shakedown-rounds/MAIN-shakedown-2026-07-28, logs/gate-rerun2-soft.log): 'FAIL zero bookkeeping writes — bookkeeping projection query failed: ERROR: relation "session_messages_projection" does not exist'. The check (scripts/ops/validate-kube-rollout.sh:1248) runs 'select count(*) from session_messages_projection ...' via 'psql -U psfn -d psfn' (line 1026). Since the local companion provisioning creates the projection inside the per-companion schema (pg_tables shows companion_default.session_messages_projection; runtime role has database-scoped search_path 'companion_default, extensions' per t6q7c), the psfn superuser's default search_path (public) cannot resolve it. Scope: make the check enumerate companion schemas (e.g. pg_namespace match or fleet config) and run the count schema-qualified per schema, failing when zero matching projections are found anywhere; do not add silent fallbacks that mask a missing table; do not weaken the zero-rows assertion.

title: P1: Recheck skill cache generation for every coalesced caller
description: Final fj772 spec review found that SkillsRuntime.getOrCreateCache returns this.cacheBuild.promise directly to callers that coalesce on an in-progress generation. If invalidation occurs before that build resolves, only the original builder checks generation mismatch and retries; coalesced waiters receive the stale unpublished cache. Concurrent cold turns and Garden Promise.all snapshot/managed requests can therefore use stale prompt indexes. Route every waiter through generation validation/retry rather than exposing the raw build promise, preserving single-flight and preventing stale publication or use.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic test starts one build with at least two coalesced waiters, invalidates and completes a replacement generation first, then releases the stale build. Every caller receives the same current generation; none sees stale entries, stale cache never publishes, cacheBuild clears exactly once, and subsequent calls reuse the current cache. Focused tests, changed lint, build/type baseline, hygiene, and pre-PR gate pass. Keep the fj772 branch within normal PR target or split a layered dependent PR.

title: P1: Make skill binary eligibility cooperative and bounded
description: Final spec review of the fj772 remediation found that src/faculties/skills/runtime.ts yields only after a 32-entry chunk, while src/faculties/skills/filter.ts synchronously checks every requires.binaries value across every PATH directory using accessSync. One valid SKILL.md can declare hundreds or thousands of binaries within the 64 KiB frontmatter cap. Production core runtime does not inject an async predicate. A deterministic probe with one entry, 500 missing binaries, and 89 PATH entries took 57.6 seconds with zero timer ticks, recreating the observed stuck cold-turn/Garden behavior. Replace the synchronous fanout with a cooperative async and explicitly bounded eligibility phase; retain deterministic eligibility/diagnostics and fail closed when work exceeds the bound.
acceptance_criteria: A single valid skill declaring hundreds of missing binaries cannot monopolize the event loop: regression observes repeated timer ticks during eligibility and completes within an explicit binary-check/work bound. Checks are async/cooperative within one entry, results/diagnostics are deterministic, no unverified requirement becomes eligible, PATH and injected predicate semantics remain exact, and normal small skills behave unchanged. Focused tests, changed lint, build/type baseline, hygiene, and pre-PR gate pass. Keep the existing fj772 branch at or below the 25-file/1500-line/5-commit normal PR target; if impossible, stop and propose a layered dependent PR rather than exceeding the hard limit.

title: P1: Charge stable skill bytes against aggregate caps
description: Final standards review of the fj772 remediation found that metadata and Garden aggregate prechecks charge scan-time file sizes, while the later stable open/fstat/read can observe a larger file and does not charge the actual bytes against the aggregate cap. Many SKILL.md files can grow after discovery while each stays below the per-file 1 MiB limit, causing total reads/retention to exceed the collection bound. Account the stable post-open size/bytes atomically against one per-build aggregate budget and fail explicitly if growth crosses it. Preserve file-size drift fail-closed behavior and deterministic selection.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic scan/read race grows multiple skills after discovery but before stable read; actual opened bytes are charged once, aggregate cap cannot be exceeded, no oversized body or partial instruction is retained/injected, and explicit diagnostics identify the collection/size drift. Stable normal collections preserve deterministic precedence and selection. Focused tests, changed lint, build/type baseline, hygiene, and pre-PR gate pass.

title: P1: Fix stale-generation skill cache promise race
description: Final standards review of the fj772 remediation found a generation race in the asynchronous skill cache. getOrCreateCache recursively awaits the current build after detecting a stale generation, but its finally then dereferences this.cacheBuild.promise even though the newer build's finally can already have set this.cacheBuild to null. title: P1: Eliminate quadratic Garden skill content scans
description: Final standards review of the fj772 remediation found that Garden list includeContent invokes runtime.readSkillContent(name) once per listed skill, and each findSkill performs a full root discovery scan. At maximum list cardinality this becomes O(N squared) filesystem work, and returned bodies have no aggregate content-byte cap. A large managed collection can monopolize Garden despite the bounded snapshot. Replace per-entry rediscovery with one generation-consistent indexed snapshot/batch content projection and enforce explicit aggregate returned/read content bytes. Preserve list ordering, ownership/trust filtering, requested includeContent behavior, and explicit omissions.

Large-collection regression measures O(N) scan calls, aggregate body bytes are capped with explicit diagnostics/no valid-looking partial content, and ordering/trust/ownership remain exact. Focused tests, changed lint, build/type baseline, hygiene, and pre-PR gate pass.

title: P1: Eliminate journal mutation pathname TOCTOU
description: Final review of 36p3a found that src/boundary/integrations/journal/mutation-coordinator.ts re-realpaths and lstats before invoking the mutation callback but then passes a plain pathname. src/boundary/integrations/journal/ops.ts and bounded-io.ts perform write/copy/rename after that validation. A concurrent final-target or canonical-parent rename/symlink swap in the gap can redirect the mutation outside the journal root or overwrite an external file. The current queued-swap test swaps before post-lock validation and does not cover this window. Bind mutation I/O to a stable directory/file identity using safe descriptor-relative primitives where available, or fail closed for topologies that cannot be made race-safe. Preserve cross-instance alias serialization, root/path policy, atomic/lossless append, streaming memory bounds, and unrelated-path concurrency.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic adversarial regression swaps the final target and canonical parent after validation but immediately before write/copy/rename; no external file is created or overwritten, original journal data remains valid, temp files are cleaned, and the operation fails explicitly. Existing/new directory aliases cannot split the lock, safe normal writes/appends remain atomic and lossless, and no full-file-memory regression occurs. The implementation uses stable filesystem identity or fails closed rather than relying only on pathname revalidation. Focused tests, changed lint, build/type baseline, hygiene, and pre-PR gate pass.
notes: Attempted remediation commit 7273d59047 on fix/som6e-markdown-bounds binds the canonical parent and existing target by dev+ino, performs bounded copy/write through /proc/self/fd descriptor-relative paths, stages write/append atomically, preserves metadata, and adds deterministic final-target and parent symlink-swap regressions. Focused journal tests (18) pass; ops adversarial file repeated 5/5; changed lint, build+DTS, typecheck baseline 239/94, repository hygiene, and UBS 0 warnings pass. Final independent standards review found a remaining P1: assertNamespaceUnchanged() and rename() remain separate syscalls. A target replacement in that gap can be overwritten, while a parent detach can make descriptor-relative rename commit into the detached directory and only then return failure. Node 22 exposes rename/link but no renameat2/openat2/conditional compare-and-replace, the repo has no native renameat2 binding/helper, and even renameat2 exchange has no inode-conditioned CAS or rollback safe against a second concurrent namespace mutation. A true fix therefore requires expanding the architecture: enforce an OS permission/service boundary that prevents same-UID namespace mutation during journal commits, or add a reviewed native/filesystem transaction primitive with crash recovery. description: Independent final review of cf1z2 found that src/primitives/llm/client.ts omits the caller signal from runWithFallback options for streaming. notes: Implemented on dependent cf1z2 branch at commit 86555e4c08afab89e6a9d77fa1a860810cb1a752. Deterministic two-candidate regression uses an abort-ignoring primary and timeout-shaped reason, proves exactly one attempt/no fallback/no success usage; existing normal stream fallback coverage still passes. title: P1: Cancel split-runtime LLM completions at the gateway provider
description: The Workbench parent-response hotfix can abort an embedded provider and release the agent-side GatewayClient wait, but independent production-path review found GatewayClient.requestWithAbortSignal only rejects its local JSON-RPC wrapper. The underlying rpcInstance.request('llm.complete', params) continues, the gateway llm.complete handler receives no request-lifetime AbortSignal, and the live upstream provider can finish as a zombie and record success/cost after the caller has cancelled or timed out. Implement end-to-end cancellation for split-runtime non-streaming LLM completions. Add an authenticated, request-scoped cancellation identity/protocol or extend an existing inflight-request primitive; bind it at the gateway to an AbortController passed to runtime.llmProvider.complete; have GatewayClient cancellation/disconnect issue the exact cancel without waiting indefinitely; clean inflight state on success, error, timeout, client disconnect, and cancel races. Likely production surfaces include src/boundary/gateway/client.ts requestWithAbortSignal/complete, the gateway protocol and policy allowlist, src/boundary/gateway/methods/llm.ts, and focused boundary tests. Fail closed: one client/companion must never cancel another request, unknown/completed IDs are harmless and bounded, and cancellation must not create an unauthenticated generic kill surface. Scope is non-streaming llm.complete split-runtime cancellation used by Workbench and other callers; non-goals are changing model budgets, adding a legacy provider path, or treating local Promise rejection as provider teardown.
acceptance_criteria: A split gateway+agent integration fixture starts never-resolving llm.complete and llm.chat requests whose provider captures its AbortSignal; aborting the agent caller or disconnecting the authenticated client causes that exact connection-scoped gateway controller and provider signal to abort promptly, each RPC settles once, and no success/cost telemetry is emitted afterward. Concurrent requests and two companion connections prove cancellation is scoped by connection/companion and opaque request identity with no cross-cancel. A fast cancel that races audited handler entry cannot be lost. Completion-vs-cancel, duplicate-cancel, unknown-ID, timeout, connection removal, server stop, and client close/error/destroy races leave no inflight map, JSON-RPC pending promise, listener, or timer leak. Gateway policy/registration rejects unauthenticated or mismatched cancellation and exposes no generic kill surface. Existing normal completion/stream fallback behavior remains intact. Changed-file lint, focused gateway/protocol/client/multi-companion tests, build, typecheck baseline, repository hygiene, and pre-PR gate pass.
notes: Read-only feasibility audit found no JSON-RPC cancellation primitive. Minimal design is a client-generated opaque cancellationId plus fire-and-forget llm.cancel notification and a per-RPC-connection cancellation registry. Reserve the controller synchronously before the audited provider handler so a fast cancel cannot arrive before registration; pass its signal into provider complete/stream; release in finally; abort all on connection removal/server stop. Connection-scoped registries prevent cross-companion cancellation even if IDs collide. This fits a focused 9-10 file PR: new gateway llm-request-cancellation module/tests plus protocol, client/client tests, method types, llm methods/tests, server and connection tests. Include llm.chat because it has the same local-only abort and the streaming provider already supports signal. Also make GatewayClient close/error/destroy call json-rpc-2.0 rejectAllPendingRequests so non-abort-aware RPC callers cannot wait forever after a dead gateway; server-side registry disconnect cleanup is what actually tears down provider work. llm.embed lacks AbortSignal on EmbeddingProviderPort and is tracked separately rather than widening this PR.

title: P1: Release parent turns from stalled Workbench responses before the fuse
description: Live durable evidence showed Analysis Workbench calls occupying their parent for roughly 300 seconds before llm_response_timeout, including zero-iteration/zero-token runs. The large-file paging fix in psfn-framework-9ofu0 starts only after an LLM response and cannot address this case. The Workbench overall wall budget and parent turn fuse are both 300,000ms; the first completion timeout used almost the entire Workbench budget, leaving no time for the parent to emit a bounded result. src/core/tools/analysis-workbench/tools.ts also ignored the parent AbortSignal, and loop.ts originally rejected a local timer without coordinating cancellation. Add an owner-file direct-parent response deadline that preserves a declared 60-second parent headroom while bounded subagent/shard workers retain the full five-minute overall budget. Thread the parent/deadline lifetime through root, nested, and sandbox Workbench completions; abort embedded provider calls and release split GatewayClient waits promptly; clean timers/listeners and classify a zero-iteration timeout honestly. Use canonical workload correlation rather than channel/path/env guesses. Preserve the existing canonical recommendation to delegate long analysis to a bounded worker/automaton and keep direct Workbench use permitted. End-to-end gateway/provider teardown for split-runtime llm.complete is deliberately separate P1 psfn-framework-cf1z2; this issue must not claim that a local RPC abort cancels the remote provider.
acceptance_criteria: A settings.json-owned positive integer direct response timeout is wired through load/config/settings snapshot/Garden contracts, clamped or rejected so it always leaves at least 60 seconds before the canonical 300-second parent fuse, and applies only to direct-parent Workbench runs; canonical subagent/shard workers retain the full bounded overall budget. A never-resolving first completion settles as a zero-iteration timeout by the direct deadline, leaving parent response headroom. Parent cancellation promptly settles root, nested, and sandbox Workbench calls; embedded providers observe abort, while split GatewayClient behavior is documented/tested only as local wait release pending cf1z2. Tests prove listener/timer cleanup, no unhandled late rejection or later successful Workbench telemetry, invalid settings fail closed, existing worker/automaton guidance remains, and paging behavior from 9ofu0 is unchanged. verify:settings-contract, changed-file lint, focused tests, build, typecheck baseline, repository hygiene, and pre-PR gate pass.
notes:
Independent live/code audit confirmed 9ofu0 cannot address the zero-iteration case because paging begins only after the first LLM completion. The Workbench default/seeded autonomous wall budget and the parent turn fuse are both exactly 300,000ms, while the first completion timeout is remaining wall minus only 25ms; direct-primary execution therefore leaves no final-response headroom. Implementation must add an owner-file/settings-contract per-response ceiling or equivalent owned policy, apply it more tightly for direct-parent execution while retaining the full bounded worker/automaton run budget, compose timeout and parent AbortSignals into completeWithWorkSpec (including nested/sandbox calls), and ensure a direct parent can emit a bounded failure before its own fuse. Subagent guidance should say spawn-and-continue for long analysis rather than immediately invoking blocking wait. Historical Workbench offload was removed with the deferred-tool/background-continuation system, so this is a live recurrence rather than already-shipped behavior.
The exact gate caught a deterministic provider tool-schema token/hash regression caused solely by redundant extra catalog wording. The unpushed hotfix was narrowed at 6fc4178f17: the catalog expansion was removed, preserving the already-shipped worker/automaton recommendation and all paging/deadline/cancellation behavior. Token schema-cost plus 120 focused tests, settings contract, changed lint, build/DTS, type baseline, and hygiene pass. Final implementation is commit 6fc4178f17a6e1d0f5aeee3c5a9a64adc82d80fe on PR #271. Direct parent response waits stop by 240 seconds, leaving 60 seconds before the canonical parent fuse; parent cancellation propagates through root/nested/sandbox operations; canonical subagent/shard workers retain the full bounded overall budget; embedded providers observe abort and split GatewayClient local waits settle without claiming remote teardown. Lifecycle helpers reuse the shared abort primitive outside the main loop file. Independent standards/spec review found and the one remediation pass fixed the god-file/duplicate helper, valid-settings headroom, and false provider-teardown claims; exact final check passed. Exact gate and GitHub ci-required passed as recorded on 9ofu0. Bead remains open until exact-head Greptile, merge, and CI completion permit closure.

title: P1: Bound Markdown journal whole-file operations
description: The Markdown journal integration materializes complete notes and corpora before enforcing tool output limits. src/boundary/integrations/journal/ops.ts readNote reads an entire file, appendNote reads and rewrites the entire note, and searchNotes sequentially reads and lowercases every Markdown file. src/boundary/integrations/journal/tools.ts truncates only after this work and bounds returned matches rather than input bytes. The canonical runtime registers this surface through src/boundary/integrations/journal/journal-runtime.ts and src/app/agent/main.ts, so a large note or corpus can occupy the primary event loop and heap; subagents inherit the same surface. Add governed byte/page/time bounds or cooperative/worker execution with explicit progress. Preserve note path policy, exact UTF-8, search semantics, and append atomicity. Do not silently truncate stored notes or return valid-looking incomplete search results.
acceptance_criteria: Multi-megabyte notes and large Markdown corpora cannot monopolize the primary event loop or be fully retained before a bound is applied; a timer/admin callback progresses in regression tests. Read/search returns explicit paging/progress or an actionable bounded error, append remains atomic and lossless, UTF-8 and path policy are preserved, and subagent use follows the same contract. Targeted tests, changed-file lint, build, typecheck baseline, and repository hygiene pass.
notes: Implementation committed on fix/som6e-markdown-bounds at 149778f3324854dfd4b91b4b3ebd066b52a8a3bd: fixed 12,000-byte UTF-8 journal read pages expose byte offsets/eof; bounded cooperative list/search preflight refuses oversized notes/corpora before content materialization and reports complete/result-limit metadata; copy-on-write temp+fsync+rename append avoids retaining the existing note and serializes same-path mutations; journal guidance recommends bounded worker/workbench analysis. Validation: 40 focused tests pass (plus the timer-progress regression passed 10 consecutive runs); changed-file lint pass; build+DTS pass; typecheck baseline 239/94 pass; repository hygiene pass. Local blocking-risk pass found and corrected a false-positive timer assertion before this exact commit. Pending orchestrator independent review/gate/PR; bead remains in_progress.

title: P1: Page Analysis Workbench read_file across large files
description: The production Analysis Workbench helper in src/boundary/sandbox/capabilities/toolchain.ts exposes read_file(path): Promise<string> and calls gatewayCaps.fsRead(path) without an offset. The gateway has lossless paging metadata in src/boundary/gateway/client.ts fsReadDetailed, but fsRead discards nextOffsetBytes/eof. The Workbench prompt in src/core/tools/analysis-workbench/prompt.ts explicitly advertises this helper for large-file analysis, so an analyst attempting to continue can repeatedly ingest page zero, burn iterations, and keep the primary turn occupied. Canonical fs.read and inherited subagent tools already support paging; this bead is specifically the Workbench helper contract and prompt/tool ergonomics. Extend the helper to support byte offsets and expose explicit progress metadata or an equivalent lossless worker-friendly page API, preserve governed gateway path checks and the 20,000-byte per-page bound, update prompts to recommend worker/subagent execution for long analyses while still permitting primary use, and add deterministic multi-page/no-progress regressions. Do not add a second direct filesystem bypass or silently concatenate an unbounded whole file.
acceptance_criteria: A Workbench program can read every byte of a file larger than 20,000 bytes by advancing an explicit cursor and can observe eof/next offset; repeated calls with the same arguments are visibly the same page rather than an implied continuation. No helper call retains or returns an unbounded whole file. The prompt recommends worker/subagent execution for long reads without forbidding primary execution. Tests prove exact multi-byte UTF-8 reconstruction across at least three pages and prevent a page-zero retry loop. Changed-file lint, targeted tests, build, typecheck baseline, and repository hygiene pass.
