title: P1: Cast atomic episode repoint timestamp as TIMESTAMPTZ
description: Live agent logs show every scheduled memory.sleeptime.run action retrying and then exhausting because PostgreSQL rejects repointThreadMembers with: column updated_at is of type timestamp with time zone but expression is of type text. In src/faculties/memory/episodic/postgres-store.ts around the atomic l01_episodes UPDATE, parameter $3 is explicitly typed as text inside to_jsonb($3::text), so PostgreSQL binds the same parameter as text when updated_at = $3. This breaks sleeptime episode/thread consolidation every five minutes and can prevent durable memory maintenance from completing. Fix the SQL type contract without splitting the atomic multi-row update. Audit the same store and repository for repeated-parameter SQL where a JSON/text cast can force an incompatible typed-column assignment. Add a real PostgreSQL integration regression that exercises repointThreadMembers (not only the in-memory query fake) and proves thread_id, episode_json.threadId, episode_json.updatedAt, and TIMESTAMPTZ updated_at change atomically. Scope: the concrete parameter-typing defect and exact same-pattern recurrences. Non-goals: changing sleeptime cadence, retry policy, episode semantics, or live schema.
acceptance_criteria: repointThreadMembers succeeds against the real PostgreSQL schema; all selected canonical members atomically receive the target thread and one consistent updated timestamp in both JSON and TIMESTAMPTZ columns; an injected/failed statement leaves all members unchanged; no same-pattern incompatible parameter reuse remains in the audited store; focused unit/integration tests, changed-file lint, build, pre-PR gate, exact-head CI, and a post-deploy live log window pass.
notes: Exact pre-PR gate passed at c2e1cc0221dbb7e911685bb6fafbf0bdf8a9f9c4 with 14,006 tests plus lint, build, type baseline, repository hygiene, Semgrep, and UBS. Independent SQL review found no sibling typed-placeholder recurrence and confirmed transactional rollback/success coverage. Branch remains unpushed/unpublished/open and must rebase onto final current main before publication. Live closure additionally requires a post-deploy completed sleeptime arc with zero TIMESTAMPTZ/text errors.

title: P1: Move startup L0 tombstone priming off the primary event loop
description: SessionStore construction still calls primeChannelIndexFromDisk synchronously in src/persistence/sessions/store.ts (constructor around lines 399-410; implementation around lines 576-614). For every indexed logical session it fingerprints each archive, calls scanArchiveMetadata across every L0 JSONL byte, and, when tombstone or quarantine evidence exists, calls readTurnTombstoneAuthorityFromChain on the primary event loop. Large or numerous owner journals can therefore make the agent/gateway unresponsive before bounded background-work recovery begins, even after psfn-framework-r2534 removes ensureChannelFullyLoaded from per-candidate recovery. Replace startup authority priming with bounded metadata/index validation and asynchronous or off-primary canonical tombstone verification. Preserve HMAC/CogSec fail-closed behavior: the unsigned channel index must never authorize unredaction, malformed/changing evidence must not be accepted, and no message bodies may be retained on the primary heap. Scope is SessionStore constructor/startup priming. Non-goals are TurnRecord enumeration, deleting history, or weakening redaction semantics.
acceptance_criteria: A fixture with multiple large and segmented L0 journals proves SessionStore construction does not synchronously parse O(total L0 bytes) or call full/matching journal scans on the primary thread; a heartbeat/admin callback advances within a declared startup budget; active signed redact/restore state remains exact; stale/unsigned index, malformed evidence, and concurrent mutation fail closed; retained startup state has a declared bound; targeted session/startup tests, changed-file lint, build, typecheck baseline, pre-PR gate, and exact-head CI pass.

title: P1: Bound SessionStore startup archive priming off the primary loop
description: The r2534 recovery audit found a separate startup recurrence outside per-candidate handoff eligibility. SessionStore construction calls primeChannelIndexFromDisk; for every indexed archive, src/persistence/sessions/store.ts around line 590 synchronously calls scanArchiveMetadata and may synchronously read authenticated turn-tombstone authority. This content-free scan still reads O(all L0 archive bytes) on the primary event loop before the agent can serve, so a large mature workspace can recreate the unresponsive startup state even after TurnRecord recovery moves to a child. Move all-archive metadata/tombstone priming to a cancellable asynchronous or worker-owned bounded path, or make startup use only cryptographically safe indexed evidence and lazily establish authority off-primary. Preserve HMAC/CogSec fail-closed semantics: an unsigned or stale channel index must not authorize unredaction. Scope is SessionStore constructor/startup priming across all L0 archives. Non-goals: per-candidate recovery eligibility in r2534, general bounded journal seek rows in og6cf, deleting history, or weakening redaction.
acceptance_criteria: A fixture with many archives and multi-megabyte L0 rows constructs/starts SessionStore without synchronously reading O(total bytes) on the primary loop; a timer/admin readiness callback advances within a measured budget while cancellable background priming proceeds. Active redact/restore state remains authoritative, unsigned/stale index data cannot authorize unredaction, and malformed/changing evidence fails closed. Cancellation closes descriptors/workers and startup readiness states the priming contract truthfully. Targeted constructor/index/tombstone tests, changed-file lint, build, typecheck baseline, pre-PR gate, and exact-head CI pass.

title: P1: Bound failed startup handoff retry state
description: Independent review of u7hvk found that recoverHistoricalBackgroundWorkHandoffs defers every enqueue failure into BackgroundWorkHandoffRecovery.pending, an uncapped process-local Map keyed by source/session/TurnID. During a transient Postgres outage, one entry is retained for every historical handoff, restoring O(history) primary RSS. Bound this outage path without dropping durable TurnRecords: use bounded durable/external retry state or a fail-closed capacity latch that preserves restart/rescan recovery and avoids a tight full-history retry loop. Deterministic semantic handoff corruption must never enter this retry index; u7hvk is separately validating fingerprints in the worker, but this lane must keep the retry store safe even if invalid input reaches it. Non-goals: increasing an arbitrary heap cap, silently discarding handoffs, or weakening idempotency/eligibility fences.
acceptance_criteria: A fixture with recoverable handoffs far above the declared retry capacity plus a sustained enqueue outage proves primary retained state remains bounded, no durable source row is deleted or silently marked recovered, and scheduler ticks do not repeatedly rescan the full archive; recovery resumes honestly after the backing store is available or after the documented restart/rescan path; deterministic semantic poison is rejected once and never rotates forever; fairness and exact source eligibility remain intact; targeted background-work/session tests, changed-file lint, build, typecheck baseline, pre-PR gate, and exact-head CI pass.
notes:
Implemented as a stacked follow-up on u7hvk base 4ac6427a2cf36a969698b4b23fac59e8aebdb0f8. Exact clean head af42a72ebb577856627bd5f2f10f3539b10a6bbc (2 commits, 14 files, +708/-103; each commit within hard budget). The process-local retry index now shares the existing 32-item recovery batch as a fail-closed capacity bound. Capacity exhaustion stops and closes the startup snapshot at item 33, latches later ticks onto bounded pending recovery only, and permits exactly one fresh durable rescan after the batch drains. Durable TurnRecords are never deleted or marked recovered. Full canonical live/retry rows retain complete semantic fingerprint validation. Startup uses a separate explicitly worker-validated content-free projection parser because user/assistant content is intentionally stripped before IPC; all surviving identity/payload/job bindings are still recomputed, old-fat projection input is rejected, and the full worker validated the source-turn fingerprint before projection. Deterministic evidence poison is retired rather than rotated. Evidence error construction/classification, including bounded AggregateError contents and IPC reconstruction, is centralized in recovery-contract.ts. The complete state machine moved out of SubstrateAgent into handoff-recovery-runtime.ts; SubstrateAgent is net 72 lines smaller and SessionManager adds only a thin projection delegation. Adversarial production-shaped regression writes 96 valid durable rows, drives a sustained enqueue outage through the real child worker, proves capacity+1 termination, byte-identical archive preservation and every row still findable, drains the bounded batch, then proves a complete honest rescan. Exact-head validation: 7 focused files / 343 tests passed; changed-file lint passed for 14 files; npm run build passed; verify:typecheck-baseline passed at unchanged 240 errors across 94 files; verify:hardcoded-settings passed; verify:dependency-cycles passed with zero cycles; git diff --check clean. title: P1: Avoid full L0 owner loads during handoff recovery
description: Independent review of u7hvk found that SessionStore.streamRecoverableBackgroundWorkTurnRecords calls ensureChannelFullyLoaded for every candidate owner. That path synchronously reads, parses, verifies, caches, and retains the complete L0 journal chain on the primary event loop. Many candidates across large owner journals can therefore recreate the same main-channel stall and O(history) memory growth even though TurnRecord enumeration moved to a child process. Replace this with authoritative content-free owner/tombstone eligibility that is asynchronous or off-primary, bounded independently of message history, and fail-closed on missing, malformed, changing, or unverifiable journal evidence. Reuse the canonical tombstone-authority machinery rather than weakening unsigned-index or CogSec/HMAC rules. Non-goals: TurnRecord exact identity indexing, deleting L0 history, or changing redaction semantics.
acceptance_criteria: A multi-owner fixture with large L0 message rows proves startup recovery never calls full journal-chain load, never retains message bodies on the primary heap, and lets a timer/admin callback advance within a measured budget; authoritative active redact/restore actions still include or exclude candidates exactly and an unsigned/stale index cannot authorize unredaction; changing or malformed journal evidence fails closed; retained owner/tombstone state has a declared bound independent of total message bytes and candidate count; targeted persistence/recovery tests, changed-file lint, build, typecheck baseline, pre-PR gate, and exact-head CI pass.
notes:
Implementation committed on stacked branch fix/r2534-recovery-l0-authority at head 42310e2d65. Recovery no longer calls ensureChannelFullyLoaded per candidate. It captures each owner L0 generation, scans complete pinned archive descriptors in a child process using the canonical journal parser, returns only bounded tombstone actions plus HMAC predecessor evidence, re-verifies actions with SessionJournalRuntime, retries one changing generation then fails closed, and retains an 8-owner/4096-tombstone LRU independent of message bytes and candidate count. Limits: 32 MiB per L0 row, 256 KiB per authority action, 4096 actions, 2 MiB IPC result, 64 KiB scan chunks. Regression coverage includes nine 1 MiB owners with timer heartbeat and zero full journal reads/primary message retention; signed redact/restore across generations; stale unsigned index plus unsigned restore; malformed evidence; repeated mutation. Exact-head local validation: 164 tests passed across store.test.ts, store-bounded-reads.test.ts, and turn-records.test.ts; changed-file lint against 4ac6427a2c passed; npm run build passed; verify:typecheck-baseline passed at unchanged 240 errors/94 files; verify:hardcoded-settings passed; git diff --check passed. Independent two-axis review remains delegated to the parent before integration; no publish, close, pre-PR gate, or CI in this lane. Discovered constructor-time synchronous L0 scanning was filed separately as psfn-framework-5jx2v.
Verified P1 remediation committed at exact head 585467e494b2e2463875764f3e35d05e5f267e63. The authority worker now expands each supplied L0 root through the canonical hgw3 numbered sealed-segment contract, requires contiguous generations plus the active file, snapshots identity/size/mtime/ctime, scans physical files in exact sealed-to-active and logical-chain order, and revalidates the complete generation before returning. It holds exactly one descriptor regardless of chain length; scan stats expose that bound. SessionStore applies actions in captured chain order so signed redact/restore ordering remains correct. Regressions cover a signed redact in .00001 with an empty active file and a deliberately stale unsigned index, restore then redact ordering across sealed/active files, fail-closed numbered-generation gaps, and an 80-file chain that also passes under ulimit -n 64 with peak descriptor count 1. title: P1: Abort handoff recovery before scheduler shutdown drain
description: Independent review of u7hvk found that production shutdown cannot reach the new recovery AbortController while historical recovery is active. src/app/agent/control-plane.ts currently awaits scheduler.stop before the later durable-background-work stop step; src/core/scheduler/scheduler.ts drains its in-flight tick, while SubstrateAgent.stopBackgroundWork is the operation that aborts the recovery child. A long archive scan can therefore hold graceful shutdown until the Kubernetes forced-exit deadline instead of closing the worker descriptor, SQLite scratch database, and temporary directory promptly. Add an explicit abort-before-drain shutdown seam without weakening the later durable supervisor drain or restart preparation. Scope is shutdown ordering and lifecycle tests. Non-goals: changing scheduler tick semantics, skipping durable job drain, truncating history, or owner/tombstone eligibility.
acceptance_criteria: A production-shaped control-plane shutdown test starts an in-flight historical recovery, initiates shutdown, and proves the recovery AbortSignal fires before scheduler.stop waits for the tick; the child exits and descriptors/scratch state are cleaned within a measured bounded budget; the durable background supervisor still receives its normal stop/drain and shutdown remains retryable/fail-closed; targeted control-plane/scheduler/substrate tests, changed-file lint, build, pre-PR gate, and exact-head CI pass.

title: P1: Bound old-fat TurnRecord healing and make agent readiness semantic
description:
During the live rollout of the large-content and reconnect hotfixes, the primary companion process authenticated to the gateway and opened its Garden admin transport, then synchronously consumed multiple CPU cores and about 3.5 GiB RSS while resolving historical TurnRecords. Logs emitted more than 7,300 turn_record_recent_entry_heal_drop events and hundreds of turn_record_continuity_withheld events for old-fat/ref-missing records. The admin transport accepted TCP but its semantic /api/admin/__transport_probe__ request timed out for minutes; four other fleet agents answered in about 20 ms. Kubernetes nevertheless reported the affected agent Ready because the fleet agent probe is TCP-only. This reproduces the user-observed state where the companion appears alive/registered but cannot answer while repeatedly ingesting/healing large persisted content.

Likely mechanisms/files: src/persistence/sessions/store.ts resolveTurnRecordSessionRefs/getRecentTurnRecords and old-fat healing callbacks; callers that request or scan an unbounded TurnRecord window after startup/turn resume; src/operator/garden transport probe; deploy/helm/psfn fleet agent readiness probe and Helm render tests. Profile/trace the actual caller before changing algorithms. Bound work per event-loop turn or move bulk repair to an explicit background/maintenance lane; avoid logging thousands of individual expected heal drops when a bounded aggregate preserves evidence. Readiness must not become healthy merely because the admin TCP listener opened: require completed runtime initialization plus responsive semantic admin health and authenticated gateway state.

Scope: persisted TurnRecord resolution/healing performance and truthful agent readiness under very large historical sessions. Preserve all canonical durable data and redaction/CogSec fail-closed behavior. Non-goals: deleting/truncating partner history, bypassing source-reference validation, widening trust, or weakening Garden semantic readiness.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A regression fixture with thousands of old-fat/ref-missing TurnRecord entries cannot monopolize the primary event loop for minutes or grow memory without a defined bound; admin health remains responsive within the configured readiness budget while repair proceeds. 2. Healing/redaction results are behaviorally identical and no durable history is deleted or silently accepted. 3. Expected per-entry events are bounded/coalesced into truthful aggregate telemetry without losing total/drop provenance needed for diagnosis. 4. Agent readiness stays false until runtime initialization is complete, the semantic admin probe responds, and the gateway registration contract is healthy; a TCP-only listener is insufficient. 5. Tests cover startup/resume, a live inbound message during repair, disconnect/restart interaction, and multi-companion fail-closed routing. 6. Targeted performance/behavior tests, Helm render tests, changed-file lint, build, pre-PR gate, and exact-head CI pass; live validation shows the affected agent answers Garden and an inbound message without operator data deletion.
notes:
Live evidence: affected agent was TCP Ready but semantic admin timed out 20s, emitted 7,375 heal_drop plus hundreds of continuity_withheld events, and reached ~3.54 GiB RSS. Root cause was the first background-work supervisor tick requesting getRecentSourceTurnRecords(..., Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER) plus repeated archive scans. Hotfix branch fix/mo48w-turnrecord-healing is rebased onto origin/main 80b5eccd0bbbd6090a18b712f955c76c0ef880d3 and clean at exact head 67db1c9843804be9534ee66c4eb37776507be528. Commits: 47e8f6a81f bounded persistence primitives, structurally content-free tool-usage projection, recovery-fd cleanup, and V8 range fix; 76fb6b2cc7 streamed recovery, bounded source/usage consumers, exact content-free source identity path; 67db1c9843 semantic same-agent-SPIFFE readiness and Helm/cert contracts. Usage projection retains only toolName/outcome/isError; 2 MiB result regression proves no result/call metadata survives and legacy skip classification remains. Fault-injected segment discovery proves pinned active fd cleanup. Startup recovery fixture is 1,024 x 128 KiB and asserts one full record in flight per source. Readiness is 503 until system.ready after gateway identity; Kubernetes exec probe uses CA-validated exact same-agent SPIFFE on loopback health only and survives distinct cert/key renewal; non-health stays forbidden. Cert usages preserve digital signature/key encipherment/server auth and add client auth; recovery-chart digest/verifier updated. Pre-PR type regressions were fixed without baselining: websocket authorizePeer explicitly disables the health-only self-probe exception, and recovery snapshots use numeric fs.Stats before end-offset arithmetic. Exact-head validation: affected 3 files/68 tests passed; broader 7 files/184 tests passed on equivalent content; changed-file lint passed; verify:typecheck-baseline passed with unchanged 240 errors/94 files; npm run build passed; verify:hardcoded-settings, helm lint, and verify:helm-chart passed. No push/deploy/closure. Separate follow-up streams g5erq/bb28h/ylu4i remain out of this hotfix.
Published as PR #263 at exact head 67db1c9843804be9534ee66c4eb37776507be528 after full pre-PR gate passed: 13,960 tests plus lint, build, unchanged typecheck baseline, repository hygiene, Semgrep/UBS, supply-chain, Helm and Kubernetes deployment contracts. Awaiting exact-head ci-required and Greptile before merge/deploy.
PR #263 merged to main as 3bc1e8305b and deployed as exact pinned application image at Helm revision 42. Live acceptance: 9/9 Deployments Ready, 7/7 PSFN containers on the exact new tag, all five same-agent mTLS semantic probes returned HTTP 200 in 18-22 ms, Postgres/vector and authenticated Redis probes passed, and a controlled gateway-only bounce caused exactly five supervised agent restarts followed by 5/5 Ready and another 5/5 semantic 200 pass. Gateway had zero identify/auth failures and zero errors; agent logs had zero heal_drop and zero continuity_withheld flood. Per-agent RSS was 1.18-1.31 GiB after reconnect rather than the prior pathological primary near 3.54 GiB, and CPU startup ticks were peer-normal. The only live ERROR is the pre-existing named-schema ModelUsageStore migration defect already tracked by stmof. Generated deployment value/image tar artifacts were moved to trash after acceptance; source archive/source directory retained for provenance. Bead remains open while g5erq, u7hvk, and bu4zb hardening complete and until an actual inbound user channel turn is observed.
Follow-up live semantic check after continued hardening work: all 9 Deployments remained at desired Ready replicas and every one of the five companion-specific authenticated Garden probes returned HTTP 200 in 20-21 ms. No live mutation was made; the running hotfix remains responsive while later PRs are isolated.

title: Fix local shakedown companion database search_path
description: During exact-main k3d validation for PR #259/#258 at commit 248f2f7bc6, scripts/ops/setup-local-artemis-shakedown.sh completed database role provisioning but psfn-gateway crashlooped with ModelUsageStore schema migration failed: permission denied for schema public. PostgreSQL therefore searches the nonexistent same-name role schema and then public, where the role lacks CREATE, instead of companion_default. Update the local shakedown database provisioning/URL contract so the runtime role resolves companion-owned tables into companion_default and extension objects into extensions without granting broad public-schema privileges. Add regression coverage in scripts/ops/setup-local-artemis-shakedown.test.ts and, if appropriate, a local rollout assertion that catches a gateway crash before later health checks. A fresh scripts/ops/setup-local-artemis-shakedown.sh run reaches Ready gateway/agent/Garden without permission denied for schema public. 2. companion_default_runtime uses companion_default (and extensions as needed) through an explicit role/database or connection search_path contract. 3. The fix does not grant CREATE on public or broaden cross-companion access. 4. Tests assert the search_path/schema-isolation wiring and fail on the previous URL/role shape. 5. Targeted tests and changed-file lint pass.

title: Fix local Artemis app-secret construction for current kubectl
description:
Summary: scripts/ops/setup-local-artemis-shakedown.sh:create_local_app_secret currently passes both --from-env-file and --from-file to one 'kubectl create secret generic' invocation. Current kubectl rejects that combination with: 'from-env-file cannot be combined with from-file or from-literal', blocking the local Artemis shakedown before Helm deployment.

Files: scripts/ops/setup-local-artemis-shakedown.sh near create_local_app_secret (currently around lines 837-850); scripts/ops/setup-local-artemis-shakedown.test.ts in the existing bootstrap-script contract tests.

Concrete work: add a regression that rejects the incompatible mixed-input invocation and proves the generated psfn-app Secret still incorporates all scalar values from the mode-0600 env file plus the private-key bytes from FLEET_AUTH_ASSERTION_PRIVATE_KEY_FILE; implement a kubectl-compatible construction that does not print or interpolate secret values into logs/argv; retain cleanup of temporary secret material.

Why: the command currently fails deterministically on the installed kubectl, preventing the canonical local Artemis shakedown from creating psfn-app. The assertion private key is multiline and must remain byte-exact while scalar values retain env-file parsing semantics.

Scope: only the local Artemis shakedown app-secret construction and its existing test. Non-goals: deployment, Helm chart changes, general secret helpers, live-cluster mutation, or changes to postgres secret handling.
acceptance_criteria: The setup script no longer combines --from-env-file with --from-file/--from-literal in one kubectl command; psfn-app output includes all app env entries and a byte-exact FLEET_AUTH_ASSERTION_PRIVATE_KEY; no secret values are emitted to stdout/stderr or passed directly in command-line literals; temporary secret files retain restrictive permissions and are cleaned up; the targeted setup-local-artemis-shakedown test and changed-file lint pass.
notes: Implemented at commit 42d82e50fdd437e3a73e45215fc1af02ce4b4fcf and published as PR #260. create_local_app_secret now uses kubectl --from-env-file only, injects the byte-exact assertion key into JSON in-pipeline, and applies the complete Secret without exposing secret values. title: P1: Restore agent-to-gateway reconnect and truthful readiness after gateway replacement
description:
Summary: The live split-topology Purrsephone deployment became functionally unavailable after a controlled gateway rollout restart even though both gateway and agent pods stayed Kubernetes Ready with zero restarts. The replacement gateway restored Discord and received an operator message, but rejected it because the old agent never completed its supervised restart/re-registration. A manual agent rollout was required.

Observed evidence (2026-07-28): gateway Ready/Discord login at 05:59:59Z; no agent authentication followed. At 06:00:30Z a real inbound Discord message was rejected as companion_not_connected. The old agent pod remained Ready until manually restarted; the new agent authenticated at 06:02:04Z. This recurs the closed psfn-framework-imlb incident.

Verified source cause: src/app/agent/main.ts intentionally has no in-process GatewayClient reconnect. Its disconnect hook awaits mutable stopFn and only then exits with the restart-contract code so Kubernetes recreates the process and gateway.client.identify repopulates surface routing. The imlb fix covered a rejected stopFn, but not a never-settling promise. Any hung shutdown step prevents process.exit forever. Meanwhile deploy/helm/psfn agent readiness is a tcpSocket against the local admin listener, so it remains green while the gateway has no authenticated agent route. GatewayClient transport heartbeat bounds disconnect detection, but graceful shutdown after detection is unbounded.

Concrete work: retain the existing supervised-restart architecture. On gateway disconnect, immediately make readiness false/degraded, begin graceful shutdown, and arm a bounded force-exit deadline using the restart-contract exit code. Success, rejection, or timeout must all terminate so Kubernetes automatically recreates and re-identifies the agent. Add explicit disconnect/drain/deadline telemetry. Preserve fail-closed multi-companion routing during the gap. Audit every production GatewayClient owner and other connection-triggered shutdown path for the same unbounded-await pattern.

Likely files: src/app/agent/main.ts, a focused extracted lifecycle helper plus tests to avoid growing main, agent readiness/admin-health composition, deploy/helm/psfn agent probe contract/tests, and existing gateway disconnect tests.

Scope: split production agent/gateway disconnect recovery and truthful agent readiness. Non-goals: a second in-process reconnect abstraction, Discord credential/routing changes, owner-file changes, host systemd, or unrelated Garden readiness (tracked separately as psfn-framework-cwxqr).
design: Live/source audit narrowed the defect to a recurrence gap in closed bead psfn-framework-imlb (commits a2ea2efc25/dc62feb943). The architecture intentionally has no in-process GatewayClient reconnect: on disconnect the agent performs graceful shutdown, exits with the restart-contract code, and Kubernetes recreates it so gateway.client.identify repopulates every fail-closed surface. The current disconnect handler directly awaits mutable stopFn with no deadline. If any shutdown step hangs, process.exit is never reached; the local admin listener remains open, so the tcp readiness probe stays green while gateway routing has no registered agent. Default transport heartbeat detects a blackholed gateway in at most two 30s ticks, but thereafter graceful shutdown is unbounded. Fix direction: retain supervised restart (do not invent a parallel reconnecting client); run gateway-disconnect shutdown under the same 15s force-exit guarantee as signal/uncaught-exception shutdown, using the restart-contract exit code on success, failure, or deadline. Make readiness reflect authenticated gateway connectivity or otherwise turn false immediately on disconnect before graceful drain. Regression must cover a never-resolving stopFn and prove bounded forced exit/re-registration semantics. Audit result so far: GatewayClient.connectEndpoint startup retry is bounded; only src/app/agent/main.ts is a production GatewayClient.connectEndpoint owner; operator/gateway signal shutdown already use createSignalShutdownHandler force deadlines; session-integrity worker owns a separate reconnect-on-demand loop. Preserve fail-closed multi-companion routing.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A unit/integration test supplies a gateway disconnect plus a graceful stop promise that never settles and proves the restart-contract exit is forced within the configured bound. 2. Rejected and successful graceful stops also exit exactly once; concurrent/duplicate close+error events cannot create loops or double shutdown. 3. Agent readiness becomes false/degraded as soon as authenticated gateway connectivity is lost and becomes healthy only in a newly registered process. 4. A gateway-only replacement in k3s automatically causes the agent to restart, re-identify, and receive the next inbound channel message without operator intervention. 5. Multi-companion routing remains fail closed during the gap and never delivers to another companion. 6. Audit verifies all production GatewayClient owners and other connection-triggered shutdown paths; any distinct uncovered defect is fixed in scope or linked as discovered work. 7. Targeted lifecycle/gateway/Helm tests, changed-file lint, build, pre-PR gate, and exact-head CI pass.
notes:
Merged via PR #259 and deployed live in image revision 248f2f7bc6b09d077c42cca9bca2b2e9eb1040a3. Controlled gateway-only rollout on 2026-07-28 caused all five agent containers to restart under the supervisor and regain Kubernetes Ready in 44 seconds; replacement gateway logs recorded five ready transitions and no identify auth failures. This proves bounded exit/restart/re-identification. The next real inbound channel-message acceptance criterion is not yet observed, so the bead remains in progress. Semantic probing also found one restarted primary could monopolize its event loop in synchronous old-fat TurnRecord healing while TCP Ready; that distinct readiness/saturation defect is psfn-framework-mo48w.
Helm revision 42 controlled gateway-only bounce acceptance passed on 2026-07-28: gateway rollout completed, all five connected agent processes exited/restarted exactly once under supervision, all five regained Kubernetes and semantic same-agent readiness, and post-bounce mTLS probes returned HTTP 200 in 18-20 ms with zero identify/auth failures. This proves the reconnect/restart path. Bead stays open only for the explicit next-real-inbound-channel-message criterion; no synthetic user message was injected.
Follow-up read-only fleet check: gateway, Garden, and all five agents remain Ready; all five semantic companion probes returned HTTP 200 in 20-21 ms without a restart or config change. Actual inbound user-channel acceptance remains the only unobserved criterion.
close_reason: Worktree audit 2026-07-29: both commits on fix/8i8tt-gateway-recovery are patch-equivalent to main (git cherry '-' on all). Stale in_progress status only — agent-to-gateway reconnect/readiness work is live on main.

title: P1: Restore subagent Workbench large-file handoff across gateway
description:
Summary: Large-file processing is failing and monopolizing the primary conversation in the split agent/gateway topology. Bounded subagents cannot make their first model call because their work spec declares background_continuation while GatewayClient sends flat chat correlation; the serving LLMClient rejects it as foreground_chat before provider I/O. The subagent wait tool then wraps the blocked worker outcome as a successful tool result, so the primary turn can keep retrying until timeout. Direct fs reads are capped at the first 20,000 bytes without paging, and analysis_workbench is currently hard-removed from parent turns even though the operator wants worker use to be a recommendation rather than a prohibition.

Why it matters: live diagnosis on 2026-07-28 observed the same non-retryable lane mismatch on five of five subagent generations. A 94 KB Markdown attachment was ingested and its full parsed sidecar was saved, but Purrsephone spent several minutes repeatedly trying to process it in the primary channel. This is a broken core large-file analysis and responsiveness path, not a provider context-window or document parser failure.

Domain contract: subagents are bounded automata and remain part of the companion whole. They receive the shorter/truncated worker context plus an explicit task and file provenance, use their available Workbench/file tools, and return a bounded provenance-bearing result. Long Workbench jobs should preferentially run in an automaton so the primary remains conversational, while direct primary Workbench use remains allowed when chosen.

Evidence and source cause:
- src/faculties/subagents/work-spec.ts builds a background work spec with matching nested correlation, but the wrapper injects only workSpec into stream options.
- src/boundary/gateway/client.ts builds outbound flat usage correlation only from LLMContext.correlation, which is chat on the fresh worker turn.
- src/primitives/llm/work-spec-wire.ts deliberately drops nested workSpec.correlation because flat RPC correlation is the single transport channel.
- src/boundary/gateway/methods/llm.ts rebuilds correlation from flat params; src/primitives/llm/client.ts correctly fails closed on lane mismatch.
- src/faculties/subagents/tools.ts action=wait renders every terminal SubagentResult through textResult, including blocked/cancelled/budget_limited outcomes.
- src/core/agent/substrate-agent/tool-runtime-facade.ts hard-removes analysis_workbench from every non-worker parent turn.
- src/boundary/integrations/filesystem/tools.ts caps direct reads at 20,000 bytes with no cursor.
- Shell support exists as an extended tool but the live settings owner has shellExec.enabled=false, so the deployed agent correctly does not register bash/shell. Enabling live shell is outside this code fix.

Scope:
1. Make GatewayClient.stream use the same canonical context-plus-work-spec correlation resolution as the in-process LLMClient before projecting the single flat RPC correlation. Preserve companion-private stripping and keep nested correlation off the wire.
2. Add a split-topology regression proving a real subagent work spec reconciles through GatewayClient, the gateway handler, and a serving LLMClient and reaches provider I/O.
3. Make subagent action=wait return an error-bearing tool result for every non-completed terminal worker outcome while preserving the full outcome and partial/checkpoint payload. Keep completed waits and explicit cancel control calls successful. This lets the existing per-turn tool degradation breaker stop futile retries.
4. Permit analysis_workbench on normal parent turns when capability policy allows it. Retain maintenance/routine-intent constraints, but treat a parsed attachment or explicit large-evidence request as eligible. Update canonical guidance to prefer worker/automaton delegation for long analysis because direct primary execution can block conversation for minutes; do not forbid direct use.
5. Add bounded direct fs paging with an offset_bytes cursor. Each page remains capped at 20,000 bytes, returns the actual offset and next_offset_bytes/eof metadata, and supports lossless sequential reading including UTF-8 boundaries. Workbench full-file read behavior remains unchanged.
6. Update schemas, protocol/client/ops wiring, canonical tool contracts, and focused tests without adding a parallel file abstraction.

Non-goals: do not weaken Law 12.4 lane reconciliation; do not put nested work-spec correlation on the wire; do not raise document-ingest prompt/sidecar limits, the per-page fs cap, scratchpad limits, or model context limits; do not automatically enable live shell/broad bash policy; do not add a legacy fallback or second lane resolver; do not make a subagent a separate identity or give it the full parent context stack.
acceptance_criteria: A split-boundary regression reproduces background_continuation versus foreground_chat before the fix and, after the fix, reaches the mocked provider exactly once with reconciled background correlation; companion-private linkage remains stripped and interactive chat is unchanged. Subagent wait marks blocked, cancelled, and budget_limited results as isError while preserving their full structured payload; completed wait and explicit cancel remain successful, and the existing repeated-tool-failure guard recognizes failed waits. Parent large-file/parsed-attachment turns retain analysis_workbench when repl.execute is granted, routine non-large intent and maintenance policy stay bounded, worker turns retain it, and canonical guidance recommends automaton delegation without prohibiting direct use. fs.read accepts offset_bytes, returns offset_bytes/next_offset_bytes/eof, keeps every page at or below 20,000 bytes, reconstructs ASCII and multibyte UTF-8 files losslessly across sequential pages, rejects invalid offsets, and leaves Workbench unbounded internal read behavior unchanged. Targeted gateway, LLM, subagent, tool-runtime, filesystem, and contract tests pass; changed-file lint and build pass.
notes: Merged via PR #258 and deployed live in exact image revision 248f2f7bc6b09d077c42cca9bca2b2e9eb1040a3. Source commits on main: c1332d2423 regressions, 5136e49984 split-transport correlation, 1092fd5a4a completion work-spec correlation, 3c1a9f64a5 direct Workbench eligibility/guidance, 248f2f7bc6 lossless byte-cursor paging. Exact-head focused suite: 373 tests; pre-PR 13,936; ci-required and Greptile passed. Live fleet rolled out the image and all five agent pods authenticated; the subsequent synchronous TurnRecord-healing saturation is a distinct cause tracked by psfn-framework-mo48w.
close_reason: Completed, merged in PR #258, and live-deployed at 248f2f7bc6b09d077c42cca9bca2b2e9eb1040a3. Verified implementations in src/boundary/integrations/filesystem/tools.ts, src/boundary/gateway/client.ts, src/faculties/subagents/tools.ts, and src/core/agent/substrate-agent/tool-runtime-facade.ts; 373 focused tests, exact pre-PR gate, ci-required, and Greptile passed.

title: Admin UI still claims contact deletion is destructive and cannot display archived contacts
description:
Found during PR #249 (qgqw.1 archive-never-delete) triage 2026-07-28. The backend now archives per ratified R10.3, but admin-ui was untouched: the button still reads 'Delete Contact' and the confirm dialog still claims 'L2 memories will be orphaned (kept but unlinked). This cannot be undone.' — both now false. archivedAt is surfaced on no admin API response and grep -ri archiv admin-ui/src has zero hits, so archived contacts sit in the operator contact list indistinguishable from live ones. Combined with archive being irreversible (channel identities snapshotted+cleared; no unarchive API), an operator can silently strand a contact believing they deleted it.

Scope: (a) truthful copy on the action + dialog; (b) surface archivedAt in the relevant admin API responses; (c) archived contacts visually distinct (grayed/filtered per the original commit-message intent); (d) decide and implement unarchive or explicitly document irreversibility in the UI. Related policy question for the operator recorded on qgqw.1: no production hard-delete path remains, so consent deleteOnRequest erasure has no API route.

Acceptance: admin UI never claims destruction for archival; archived contacts identifiable; qgqw.1 acceptance unaffected.
notes: 2026-07-29 close-out sweep — KEPT OPEN, scope (a)(b)(c) delivered, (d) awaits an operator ruling. Landed via PR #297 (main 2128516951); review record in lane PR #287, commit 3ff4fa0db. DELIVERED: (a) truthful copy — the action is now 'Archive Contact' and the dialog is accurate (history/audit/memories are KEPT, live identities are released, a recreated id is a new person, not reversible from here); the false 'L2 memories will be orphaned... This cannot be undone' claim is gone. (b) archivedAt was already serialized on the wire and a regression was added proving it. (c) archived contacts are visually distinct — grayed with an 'Archived' pill, default-hidden behind a 'Show archived' toggle with a count badge, and the archive action is hidden for archived/primary contacts. So the core acceptance ('admin UI never claims destruction for archival; archived contacts identifiable; qgqw.1 acceptance unaffected') is met on main. STILL OPEN — OPERATOR RULING REQUIRED for scope item (d): unarchive was NOT implemented (#287 states the bead left it open and surfaces the question rather than deciding it). Should archived contacts be recoverable at all, and if so with what identity-namespace semantics — the released channel identities may by then belong to a NEW person, so a naive unarchive can resurrect a contact whose identities now resolve elsewhere. The current UI documents irreversibility ('not reversible from here') rather than offering recovery, which is the safe interim state. Close this bead once the operator rules unarchive in (with identity semantics) or explicitly rules it out. Validation per #287: contact-archive 7/7, lifecycle-coordinator 13/13, store 80 + contacts-service 12 + social-graph 5, memory subject branches 9, all green and reviewer-re-run; blind adversarial review (Opus) PASS, zero blocking findings. Integrator note carried from #287: svelte-check could not run in-lane (admin-ui deps not cached offline) — the Svelte diff was eye-verified by the reviewer and should be svelte-check'd once. Related: the consent-erasure ruling tracked on psfn-framework-qgqw.6.
close_reason: Acceptance (a)(b)(c) shipped on main via PR #297; (d) resolved by operator ruling 2026-07-29 — unarchive is IN with confirm-dialog semantics (Discord IDs never collide); implementation continues on a fresh bead.

comments.author: axAilotl
comments.text: OPERATOR RULING 2026-07-29 (scope item d): UNARCHIVE IS IN, simple semantics. Discord snowflake IDs are unique and never reused — collision probability in that domain is negligible, so the two-live-contacts-per-identity scenario is a non-issue; no collision-policy design work. Display names are irrelevant (resolution is by numeric ID only, so a name-squatter never inherits an archived contact). Required UX: restoring shows a confirm step — "restoring this contact: here is the old information, here is the new information — confirm" — and that is all. Wider archive doctrine restated: contacts are NEVER deleted in normal operations, only archived/tombstoned (reasons range from cogsec removal to people drifting away); deletion orphans memories and destroys the person-context behind them, which we've been burned by before. Archived contacts should carry intentionally reduced weight in search/retrieval (normal memory degradation otherwise), and the contacts page should have an Archived tab as the operational surface (cogsec sweeps of an archived contact's memories/chats happen from there when the removal was adversarial). Core acceptance of this bead shipped on main (PR #297); the ruling resolves (d). Closing; implementation of unarchive + archived tab + retrieval weighting filed as a fresh bead.

title: Diagnose Purrsephone large-file tool failures on psfn-shard
description:
Summary: Purrsephone on the LAN Raspberry Pi deployment psfn-shard is having trouble reading and processing large Markdown or text files, despite expected supported paths through Analyst Workbench, scratchpad loading, or delegated subagent analysis. The operator asked for live tool-use log inspection to distinguish a tool transport/read failure, context-window or prompt-budget exhaustion, a fixed line/byte limit on Markdown reads, or a failure in the Workbench/scratchpad/subagent routing.

Scope: use the authoritative k3s namespace and running agent/gateway workloads described in docs/operations.md; capture the affected tool calls and surrounding model/runtime diagnostics; identify the actual file operation, requested ranges, returned byte/line counts, truncation markers, model/provider context accounting, retry behavior, and whether Workbench, scratchpad, and subagent paths preserve or bypass the same limit. Build a red-capable replay or the closest deterministic trace-based feedback loop from a real failure and minimize by file size/range/path when safe. Compare the live behavior to the current source contracts and tests. Record timestamps, pod/image or commit identity, and evidence without copying private deployment values into tracked files.

Non-goals: do not mutate live owner files, persistence, pods, deployment configuration, or the host-systemd legacy tree; do not implement a fix until the cause is verified and implementation is separately authorized; do not copy private file content or deployment identifiers into tracked code/docs.
acceptance_criteria: A real affected live trace is identified and a deterministic red-capable replay is run when possible; the failing layer is classified with concrete evidence as tool I/O/range handling, Workbench/scratchpad/subagent routing, model/provider context budgeting, or another verified cause; relevant source locations and configured/runtime limits are named; private content is redacted; the bead notes contain the diagnosis, repro command/result, and a scoped recommended fix or explicit evidence/access blocker.
notes:
Diagnosis evidence (2026-07-28, read-only live inspection; no private document content or deployment identifiers recorded):

- Live authority: authoritative k3s agent/gateway workloads were running without restarts. The deployed image maps to commit 6b7bded6d46cf5ee1949c1186a2d9e593d48988c. The relevant source files are byte-unchanged at current HEAD.
- Affected trace: one 94,246-byte Markdown attachment at 2026-07-28 04:59Z. Ingest succeeded and saved both the original and a 94,226-byte parsed sidecar. No parse, quarantine, file-size, pod-crash, provider 400/413, or context-window error occurred.
- Prompt/file limits: document ingest intentionally injects only 24,000 parsed characters into the parent prompt and preserves up to 240,000 characters in the sidecar (src/faculties/file-ingest/document-ingest.ts:44-47,473-493). Direct fs.read is hard-capped at 20,000 bytes and has no offset/range cursor (src/boundary/integrations/filesystem/tools.ts:13,105-125,204-220), so repeated reads return the same prefix. fs.search may inspect up to 200,000 bytes per file but returns matches, not sequential content.
- Main-turn context: PostgreSQL model_usage_events shows 23 successful GLM chat calls in the incident window. Input grew from 11,391 to 49,888 tokens; the live model registry declares a 1,048,576-token context window. All calls succeeded. Context growth was inefficient but was below 5 percent of the configured window and was not the failure.
- Expected large-file route: parent chat policy deliberately removes analysis_workbench with reason analysis_workbench_worker_context_required and recommends delegation (src/core/agent/substrate-agent/tool-runtime-facade.ts:1090-1146). A bounded worker receives analysis_workbench. Its read_file calls gateway fs.read without maxBytes, and gateway readTextFile reads the full file when maxBytes is absent (src/boundary/sandbox/capabilities/toolchain.ts:63-82; src/boundary/integrations/filesystem/workspace-ops.ts:388-405). Thus the intended route is parent -> subagent/worker -> Workbench -> full sidecar.
- Confirmed root failure: every observed worker generation failed before provider I/O with LLMWorkSpec.lane background_continuation does not reconcile with admission lane foreground_chat for purpose background. The incident produced four identical failures (one initial plus three parallel); a later retry was identical, for five observed failures total.
- Source cause: buildSubagentWorkSpec stamps the background correlation and lane (src/faculties/subagents/work-spec.ts:56-79), but createSubagentWorkSpecProvider only injects workSpec into stream options (lines 96-110). GatewayClient.stream builds flat RPC correlation only from the fresh worker LLMContext, whose default remains chat (src/boundary/gateway/client.ts:696-716), while toWorkSpecWireParams deliberately drops the nested spec correlation (src/primitives/llm/work-spec-wire.ts:24-49). The gateway reconstructs foreground chat correlation and the serving LLMClient correctly fail-closes on the mismatch before provider I/O (src/primitives/llm/client.ts:651-675). Existing tests validate the builder locally and wire parsing separately, but no test exercises the split agent -> gateway -> serving-client path with a background subagent work spec.
- Scratchpad is not a document loader: prompt injection is capped at 8 entries, 240 characters each, and 1,600 total characters (src/core/agent/substrate-agent/runtime-context.ts:111-114,584-633). It can preserve excerpts or a working summary after analysis, not hold the source document.
- Tool-record nuance: spawn/wait tool invocations can be recorded as successful tool transport while the returned worker result is blocked; the asynchronous model failure is inside the result/log payload. This explains why aggregate tool-use counts alone look healthy.

Closest deterministic red feedback loop: the live fail-closed trace repeated with identical inputs and error five times, and the source projection deterministically yields background_continuation in the spec while the flat RPC correlation yields foreground_chat. A local Vitest replay was not run because this checkout has no node_modules and npx --no-install reports tsx missing; dependencies were not installed or live state mutated solely for diagnosis.

Recommended scoped fix: make GatewayClient.stream honor the LLMProviderStreamOptions.workSpec correlation and purpose when constructing the single flat outbound correlation, preserving companion-private stripping and keeping nested correlation off the wire. Add an end-to-end split-topology regression that builds a real subagent work spec from a parent chat correlation, sends it through GatewayClient and the gateway handler into a serving LLMClient, asserts the background lane reconciles, and asserts provider I/O is reached. Align the direct fs large-document handoff text with the worker-only Workbench policy so a parent is told to delegate to a bounded worker whose Workbench reads the sidecar, rather than implying the parent can call Workbench directly.
close_reason: Diagnosis completed with read-only live evidence on deployed commit 6b7bded6: the 94 KB Markdown ingest and full parsed sidecar succeeded; 23 main GLM calls succeeded at <=49,888 input tokens against a 1,048,576-token window; direct fs is intentionally prefix-capped at 20,000 bytes; Workbench is intentionally worker-only; all five observed subagent generations failed before provider I/O because GatewayClient.stream dropped the work-spec background correlation from the flat RPC channel, producing background_continuation vs foreground_chat lane mismatch. Source proof recorded in notes at src/faculties/subagents/work-spec.ts:56, src/boundary/gateway/client.ts:696, src/primitives/llm/work-spec-wire.ts:24, and src/primitives/llm/client.ts:651. Scoped implementation tracked in psfn-framework-m8v69.

title: ANN+filter recall test races the async HNSW index build and flakes ~20% even in isolation
description:
EVIDENCE: 'returns authorized rows even when the nearest neighbours are all unauthorized (ANN + filter)' (src/faculties/memory/postgres-store.integration.test.ts:1894, a27w.2) failed 1/5 isolated runs of the file on a quiet 32-core machine (worktree testgate-ram @ main cc7c99ddcf, 2026-07-27), and once in a full 44-file integration sweep. Failures are assertion mismatches on the returned id set, not timeouts or connection errors. 4/5 isolated runs pass.

MECHANISM (verified structurally, not just hypothesized): the test creates the store via createPostgresMemoryStoreFromPool(pool, 4) WITHOUT awaitAnnIndexBuild, and postgres-store.ts:225 fires startAnnIndexBuild() -> buildL2EmbeddingAnnIndexConcurrently in the background (cf96ef4a60 moved the build off the boot critical path). Whether the query at :1916 runs before the index exists (exact seq scan -> correct) or after (HNSW iterative scan -> approximate) is machine-load timing. With 300 crowding unauthorized rows the approximate path can miss some of the 5 far-away authorized rows. Note the sibling test at :1652 passes awaitAnnIndexBuild:true explicitly; this one cannot simply copy that without changing what it claims to test — it asserts recall THROUGH the ANN path.

CONTEXT: this reddens the local delivery gate's heavy phase with meaningful probability per run, i.e. it intermittently blocks every PR attestation on this machine. Ruled out: test-harness container reuse (each test gets a fresh database via withMemoryDatabase -> harness.createDatabase(); reproduced against both stop-per-file and keep-hot harness configs).

SCOPE: owned by the a27w lane — the fix is a semantics decision: either (a) the production invariant really is 'filtered ANN never misses authorized rows', in which case the store must make the iterative-scan path deterministic-recall (and the test should await the index build so it tests THAT path, plus pin hnsw.iterative_scan GUCs), or (b) recall-through-ANN is best-effort, in which case the test asserts too much. Do not paper over by deleting the test or blindly adding awaitAnnIndexBuild without deciding which invariant is intended. Do not touch the test harness — the race is inside the test's own database.

ACCEPTANCE: 20 consecutive runs of 'npx vitest run src/faculties/memory/postgres-store.integration.test.ts' green on a loaded many-core machine, AND the chosen invariant documented in the test comment. Related draft PR #243 re-lands a27w.4-.6 — same lane, coordinate.
notes:
2026-07-27 CORRECTION (A/B-verified, 8 runs/side + 3 interleaved pairs): the reproducible failure mechanism on this machine is NOT the HNSW build race and NOT assertion mismatches — it is tmpfs exhaustion: 'could not extend file: No space left on device'. postgres-test-harness pins PGDATA tmpfs at 512m and resetWorkerPostgres drops databases between FILES, so ~43 withMemoryDatabase databases accumulate within one run of this file; the ANN+filter test is last and heaviest (300-row bulk seed + HNSW build) so it is always the first casualty. Flake scales with test count: main 25% fail, +2 tests (a27w re-land branch) = 100% fail; running only the ANN block passes. The 'do not touch the test harness' scope line is WRONG for this mechanism — fix is a harness capacity bump (tmpfs 512m->1g + env override), then re-measure before any store-semantics decision. HNSW-race remains structurally plausible but unproven as a firing cause.
2026-07-27 HARNESS CAPACITY SHIPPED — NOT CLOSED. The 2026-07-27 correction on this bead was right, and the fix follows it.

SHIPPED in PR #240 (S11 fixes consolidated), merged to main at 1267ad411a; commit cbc274b59d "fix(testing): give the RAM-backed test postgres headroom for database-heavy files (yje3l)":
- src/test-support/postgres-test-harness.ts: PGDATA tmpfs raised 512m -> 1g with --memory / --memory-swap raised to match, plus a new PSFN_POSTGRES_TEST_TMPFS_SIZE env override with validation (rejects '1024', '1gb', '1.5g', 'large', '-1g' — Docker size syntax only).
- The container profile label was rotated to io.local-gate.test-postgres.profile=tmpfs-v2 so existing containers are recycled rather than silently reused at the old 512m size. That matters: without the rotation a warm machine would keep the old capacity and appear unfixed.
- src/test-support/postgres-test-harness.test.ts (+35) covers the default, the override, and the profile label.

The commit's own A/B measurement, interleaved on one quiet 32-core box, confirms the mechanism was capacity and not the HNSW race: main at 512m 6/8 green (both failures ENOSPC), the same file plus 2 more databases at 512m 0/8 green, the ANN block alone (3 dbs) green. Root cause as stated in the correction — resetWorkerPostgres is the isolation boundary between FILES, so all ~44 withMemoryDatabase databases in postgres-store.integration.test.ts accumulate on tmpfs within one run, and the last/heaviest test (ANN+filter, 300 crowding rows + HNSW build) simply absorbed the blame for a sizing limit.

POST-FIX MEASUREMENT: the previously-failing file measured 5/5 green.

>>> REMAINING BEFORE THIS BEAD CAN CLOSE — two items, both now UNBLOCKED: <<<
1. THE 20-RUN SOAK. Acceptance requires 20 consecutive green runs of `npx vitest run src/faculties/memory/postgres-store.integration.test.ts` on a LOADED many-core machine. 5/5 is encouraging, not sufficient — the original flake was ~20-25%, which 5 runs cannot distinguish from fixed. Run the full 20 under contention.
2. THE HNSW INVARIANT DECISION. Still owed, and the capacity fix does not answer it. The structural HNSW-build race remains plausible but unproven as a firing cause: the ANN+filter test at postgres-store.integration.test.ts:1894 constructs the store WITHOUT awaitAnnIndexBuild, so whether the query hits an exact seq scan (index absent) or an approximate HNSW iterative scan (index built) is still decided by machine timing. Decide which invariant is intended and document it in the test comment:
   (a) production really guarantees "filtered ANN never misses authorized rows" — then the store must make the iterative-scan path deterministic-recall, the test should await the index build so it exercises THAT path, and hnsw.iterative_scan GUCs must be pinned; or
   (b) recall-through-ANN is best-effort — then the test asserts too much and should be narrowed.
   Do not close by deleting the test or by blindly adding awaitAnnIndexBuild without making that call. If the 20-run soak is clean, that is evidence about capacity, not evidence that the invariant question is moot.
Owned by the a27w lane; coordinate with PR #243, which re-lands a27w.4-.6 and adds the 2 extra databases that took the 512m configuration to 0/8.

comments.author: axAilotl
comments.text: PR #303 landed the filtered-ANN scope-preservation code (appendMemoryScopeSqlPredicate before LIMIT, partial HNSW index + vector_dims guards, plus the predicate-drift reclamation remediation). This does NOT close yje3l: the flaky ANN+filter recall test rides queryAuthorizedMemorySubjects (subject-queries path), NOT the searchByEmbedding path that got the predicate; the store is still constructed without awaitAnnIndexBuild, so the HNSW-invariant decision (deterministic-recall vs best-effort) and the 20-run loaded-machine soak acceptance are untouched. 5 consecutive isolated file runs were green, consistent with the already-shipped tmpfs fix, but that is not the soak. Bead stays OPEN for its stated acceptance.

title: Intention post-turn appraisal throws every turn (getRecentMessages inside admitted turn) — kills conversational proactivity
description:
On the carlini fleet (92bf467b) EVERY turn logs:

```
WARN [PostTurnRuntime] Intention post-turn appraisal dispatch failed
  {error:"Error: SessionManager.getRecentMessages cannot run during an admitted turn owned by \"<ch>:session:...\"; use CapturedSessionReads or resolveForeignSessionForTurn(reason, channelId, operation)"}
```

## Root cause
`src/core/scheduler/post-turn-runtime.ts:559` — the intention post-turn appraisal's FIRST statement calls the mutable active-context API `runtimeOptions.sessionManager.getRecentMessages(resolvedSessionId, 12)`, which is fenced by the admitted-turn guard (`src/core/session/manager.ts:2121`, `assertNoCapturedSessionOwner` → throw at `src/core/session/manager/captured-session-owner.ts:120-131`). The appraisal runs INSIDE the turn's owner-bound `CapturedSessionReads` scope (`turn-execution-runtime.ts:470`, dispatched via `inferDeferredPostTurnActions` → `triggerIntentionPostTurnAppraisal` at `post-turn-runtime.ts:1532`, IIFE at `:540-557`). So line 559 throws every turn; caught/logged at `:776-781`.

## Proactivity impact (this is the "companions under-proactive" cause)
Line 559 is the first try statement, so on throw NOTHING downstream runs: `intentionAppraisal.evaluate` (`:644`) never executes → no concern/follow-up decisions → `onIntentionConcernDecision`/`createConcernFromDecision` (`intention/runtime-wiring.ts:216`) never fire → no active concerns formed from conversation; `onIntentionFollowUpDecision`/`pendingFollowUpStore.enqueue` (`runtime-wiring.ts:242`) never fire; pending follow-up resurfacing (`:743-757`) never runs; `agent.post_turn.actions.inferred` (`:771`) never emitted. The conversational "notice → form concern → later reach out" engine is dead on every turn. (The standalone socialDesire/weightedThought/icpAutonomy lanes fire independently and are unaffected.)

## Fix
Read recent messages through the owner-bound `CapturedSessionReads` instead of the mutable manager: `CapturedSessionReads.getRecentMessages(limit)` (`captured-session-owner.ts:246-248`) or `resolveForeignSessionForTurn(reason, channelId, operation)` (`:299-314`). The sibling `src/core/agent/background-work/post-turn-runtime.ts:261,328` already does it correctly via `sessionReads.getRecentMessagesAtOrBefore(...)`. The `CapturedSessionReads` handle must be threaded into `triggerIntentionPostTurnAppraisal` (currently only holds `runtimeOptions.sessionManager`). Needs rebuild + fleet redeploy.

## Guardrail note (why enabling the lanes now is safe)
Proactive outbound is fail-closed to Discord approved-primary-contact private DMs + rate-limited (`core/intention/proactive-outbound.ts:82,85,92,95`). Enabling socialDesire/weightedThoughtOutreach/icpAutonomy in scheduler.json (done 2026-07-24) gives lane-driven proactivity now; this bead restores the conversational-appraisal path.
close_reason: Fixed by the pmqm re-land, landed on main via PR #283 train (main head 3b4bc63469): post-turn appraisal now dispatches through the turn's owner-bound CapturedSessionReads instead of the guarded getRecentMessages path — the every-turn throw under an admitted persistent-channel turn is gone. Same defect as psfn-framework-pmqm (closed with landing evidence); this was the locally-filed twin.

title: vcyxv backup lane, now that it runs, fails on pg_dump 'permission denied for schema' — the gateway backup role lacks dump grants on companion schemas
description:
Surfaced 2026-07-23 deploying merged-main (6b7bded6-lib) to Purrsephone (helm rev 66) and on the k3d two-companion fleet. The vcyxv fix (writable /runtime/backups mount + watermark + lane arming) WORKS — no more EACCES, the lane now arms ('Fleet auth consistent backup lane armed {backupRootDir:/runtime/backups, catchUpDueAtBoot:true}') and executes. But the consistent-family pg_dump then fails:

  ERROR [FleetAuthBackupCycle] Scheduled fleet auth consistent backup failed: Consistent pg_dump failed for schema public: pg_dump: error: query failed: ERROR: permission denied for schema public ... LOCK TABLE public.active_concerns, ... public.l2_memories, ... IN ACCESS SHARE MODE

So the gateway's DB role (the login role the backup lane connects as) lacks SELECT/LOCK (ACCESS SHARE) on the tenant schema's tables. Reproduced on BOTH: Purrsephone (schema public) AND the k3d companion_carlini agent. Before vcyxv this was HIDDEN — the lane was EACCES-blocked at the mount and never reached pg_dump. vcyxv exposed a pre-existing grant gap.

Same root family as stmof (tenant role vs adopted-public search_path/ownership): the consistent-family backup needs the gateway backup role to have ACCESS SHARE / SELECT on every table in every companion schema it dumps. The tenancy provisioning (provision:postgres-tenancy) grants tenant runtime access but not the cross-schema backup-role SELECT/LOCK.

SEVERITY/SCOPE: NOT a data-loss emergency — the SEPARATE host off-node NAS lane (psfn-backup.sh) is healthy and backs up the live DB every 6h (verified this session, dump growing + pg_restore --list valid). The gateway consistent-family IN-CLUSTER backup is the affected lane; it errors every cycle but does not crash the companion. Matters for carlini (5 named schemas — fires per companion).
acceptance_criteria: The gateway backup role is granted the ACCESS SHARE / SELECT needed to pg_dump every companion schema it backs up (via provision:postgres-tenancy or the fleet-auth backup setup), OR the consistent-family backup connects as a role with those grants; a fleet-auth consistent backup artifact is produced without 'permission denied for schema' on Purrsephone (public) and the k3d named-schema fleet.

title: Gate test-harness Postgres containers leak on killed or failed runs: 181 orphaned local-gate-test-postgres containers drove machine load past 300 and cascaded gate flakes
description:
Evidence (2026-07-22 ~17:36): docker ps showed 181 running local-gate-test-postgres-* containers (postgres:16.8-alpine, pgvector/pgvector:0.8.2, postgres:16-alpine) with zero active vitest/gate processes on the machine — ages 17 minutes to 6 DAYS (73 at 4h, 30 at 2h, 18 at 2 days, 6 at 6 days). ~1056 postgres backend processes; load average peaked 329 (5-min). Effect: every gate heavy phase after midday flaked on a different timing-sensitive suite (shell-runner pre-fix, process-harness e2e, start-gateway-agent launcher, session-manager budgets, fleet-auth write-lock heartbeat, retrieval under load) — each failed/killed run leaked MORE containers, a positive feedback loop. Manual  of the name-filtered set recovered the machine (1-min load 329 -> 26).

Context: the real-Postgres test harness (src/test-support, postgres harness that starts dockerized instances per suite/worker) does not reap its containers when the parent run is SIGKILLed/killed mid-flight, and apparently sometimes not on ordinary failures either (2-day-old and 6-day-old orphans predate today). System: testing (the harness), affects every gate on every machine.

Scope: make container lifecycle crash-safe — e.g. docker run with --rm plus a label and a startup sweep (harness start: remove any local-gate-test-postgres-* container whose owning PID is dead), and/or an ownership lease file checked by the next gate run. The gate runner should also sweep before HEAVY phase. Non-goals: changing the per-suite container topology or postgres versions.

Acceptance criteria: (1) SIGKILL a running integration suite mid-flight -> zero local-gate-test containers remain after the next harness startup sweep (test or scripted repro); (2) normal pass/fail runs leave zero containers; (3) a gate run on a machine with pre-existing orphans removes dead-owner orphans before its heavy phase; (4) concurrent live runs' containers are never reaped (ownership check test).
close_reason: Superseded by iifp4 b7d7aecb8 + keep-hot follow-up, both on main: deterministic per-image/profile container names make orphan proliferation structurally impossible (reuse-by-name), machine-scaled slot cap with PID-owned dead-owner-reclaim locks (postgres-test-harness.ts:279-312), keep-hot bounded tmpfs containers released via test:postgres:down (scripts/ci/stop-test-postgres.mjs). PR #231 reaper closed unmerged as incompatible (would rm -f unlabeled live containers). Original acceptance-2 (zero containers after normal runs) deliberately superseded by documented keep-hot decision. Reconciliation verdict CLOSE 2026-07-28.

title: Activate companion-library seeding on every Fleet workload
description: After yhivs.1 lands the chart can render an exact psfn-companion-library ConfigMap behind companionLibrary.enabled. Complete parent yhivs by flipping the gate on for the supported fleet topology and wiring a reusable seed-companion-library init container plus companion-library emptyDir and companion-library-src ConfigMap volumes into gateway, Garden, and every generated Fleet agent Deployment. The init must use the applicable PSFN application image, copy dereferenced source files from a read-only /lib-src mount into /lib-dst, run before seed-runtime-files, and inherit the chart's restrictive container security context. The main gateway, Garden, and agent containers mount the populated emptyDir read-only at /app/companion_docs, which is the default path consumed by src/persistence/workspaces/provisioning.ts and required by gateway startup. When the value is explicitly false, render none of these workload fields or the ConfigMap. Extend scripts/verify-helm-chart.mjs to assert exact volume sources, init ordering/command/mount permissions/security context, and main-container mounts for gateway, Garden, and all Fleet agents; compare the enabled live-shaped render to the hand-patch contract recorded in parent yhivs. Update the recovery digest. Non-goals: editing library text, changing provisioning semantics, adding image-baked fallback content, non-Fleet topology expansion, or live deployment.
acceptance_criteria: The default Fleet render includes the chart-owned ConfigMap, companion-library and companion-library-src volumes, a seed-companion-library init before seed-runtime-files, and a read-only /app/companion_docs mount on gateway, Garden, and every Fleet agent; companionLibrary.enabled=false removes all of them; the init copy command dereferences ConfigMap links and fails on copy error; render verification covers exact topology and npm run verify:helm-chart plus changed-file lint pass; the activation merges through a PR with ci-required green.
close_reason: Closed obsolete/superseded, not shipped. This activation depends on yhivs.1's invalid empty ConfigMap design and would mount emptyDir over origin/main's image-baked /app/companion_docs, causing the init copy to fail before workloads start. PR #234 targeted the yhivs.1 feature branch (not main), failed ci-required, and its commits are not ancestors of origin/main. The current viable bundle is the o3wwr image bake (c1cbe61d29 + 92bf467bf4); any chart activation must be redesigned.

title: Stage the canonical companion-library bundle in the Helm chart
description: Parent yhivs requires the chart to own psfn-companion-library instead of relying on a hand-created ConfigMap. The canonical source is the four files under repo-root companion_docs/: companion-library-manifest.json, welcome.md, privacy-boundary-reference.md, and live_verification_checklist.md (about 46 KiB/678 lines total). Helm cannot read files outside its chart package, so add byte-identical packaged copies under a focused deploy/helm/psfn/files/companion_docs/ directory, a values-gated ConfigMap template named from the release as psfn-companion-library, and an initially disabled companionLibrary.enabled value/schema contract. Extend chart verification to render with the gate enabled and compare every ConfigMap key byte-for-byte to the canonical repo source, including the manifest hashes, while proving the default inactive render adds no ConfigMap. Update recovery-chart.sha256. This is an inactive tracer PR that packages the source without changing any workload. Keep within the normal 12-file/800-line target. Non-goals: init containers, pod volumes/mounts, changing companion-library content, runtime provisioning behavior, or live deployment.
acceptance_criteria: With companionLibrary.enabled=false the chart renders no companion-library ConfigMap or workload changes; with it true exactly one release-owned ConfigMap renders with the four canonical filenames and byte-identical contents; verification fails on packaged-source drift, missing/extra keys, malformed manifest, or stale recovery digest; npm run verify:helm-chart and changed-file lint pass; the inactive tracer merges through a PR with ci-required green.
notes: 2026-07-27: PR #233 closed as superseded — see PR comment for full empirical evidence (helmignore excludes overlays/ so the ConfigMap renders empty; emptyDir mount would shadow the o3wwr baked bundle at /app/companion_docs; default-on init cp fails and wedges rollout). If helm-side staging is still wanted it is a redesign against the o3wwr bake, not a rebase.
close_reason: Closed obsolete/superseded, not shipped. PR #233 was closed after empirical verification that .helmignore excludes its overlay bundle, so the ConfigMap renders empty; its mount would shadow the working image-baked /app/companion_docs bundle and its default-on init copy would wedge rollout. origin/main instead carries c1cbe61d29 + 92bf467bf4 (o3wwr), which bake and build-verify all declared companion-library files. Any future Helm staging needs a redesigned scope, not this acceptance contract.

title: P1: preserve captured live Helm values during self-update upgrades
description: The live Kubernetes self-update pipeline captures the release's user-supplied Helm values and passes them into DeployPipelineRunner.helmUpgrade, but createLiveDeployPipelineRunner in src/app/operator/kube-self-update-transport.ts around lines 346-370 ignores its liveValues parameter and invokes helm upgrade with only three image --set values. Helm upgrade does not preserve prior user values by default, so a self-update can silently reset fleet topology, storage, certificate, resource, and runtime configuration to chart defaults even though the pipeline explicitly captured the live values. src/system/lifecycle/kube-deploy-pipeline.ts around lines 601-617 proves the intended dataflow; src/app/operator/kube-self-update-transport.test.ts lacks an assertion that the captured object reaches Helm. Commit-history review, including the pending 6187t commit 9b5b89810d, found no implementation. Implement a secret-safe transport for the exact captured values (for example a protected temporary values file with deterministic cleanup) and keep explicit image overrides authoritative. Fail closed on serialization/write/cleanup errors as appropriate, avoid exposing values on the process command line or logs, and add focused tests that prove preservation and cleanup. Files likely include src/app/operator/kube-self-update-transport.ts and its test; touch pipeline contracts only if required. Non-goals: redesigning Helm value ownership, changing ship-kube-update.sh (which already writes and supplies a protected live-values file), deploying live, or bundling the unrelated 3u2en chart topology.
acceptance_criteria: A live self-update Helm upgrade consumes the exact values object returned by captureLiveValues without placing its contents directly in argv or logs; image repository/tag/reference overrides still win; temporary material is mode-restricted and removed on success and failure; malformed/unserializable values fail before live mutation; focused tests cover preservation, override order, cleanup, and failure; changed-file lint and targeted tests pass; the fix ships through a reviewable PR with ci-required green.
close_reason: Satisfied on main: 57465fcd75. helm upgrade now consumes the captured live values via a 0600 mkdtemp'd --values file (never argv/logs), image --set overrides still win, temp dir removed in finally on success and failure; 11/11 transport tests green.

title: P1: bootstrap the shared runtime subPath before workload mounts
description: PR #229 adds a governed Fleet shared-workspace mount backed by the runtime PVC subPath workspaces-shared in deploy/helm/psfn/templates/_helpers.tpl around line 386. Greptile review comment https://github.com/CGIC-AI/psfn-framework/pull/229#discussion_r3631537270 identified that, on a fresh runtime PVC, Kubernetes must resolve the subPath before seed-runtime-files can execute; because seed-runtime-files mounts that same subPath, it cannot be relied upon to create the directory. Independently verified from the rendered init ordering and helper mounts. Implement a fail-closed, least-privilege chart bootstrap that makes workspaces-shared exist before gateway, Garden, and Fleet-agent containers or seed-runtime-files mount it. Reuse an existing chart primitive if one actually runs before subPath resolution; otherwise add a focused init container that mounts the runtime PVC root at a private bootstrap path and creates only the required directory. Update scripts/verify-helm-chart.mjs to prove ordering, writable root bootstrap mount, mkdir command, and continued subPath mounts for all affected workloads. Keep the correction on PR #229 per the small-related-fix rule. Files in scope: deploy/helm/psfn/templates/_helpers.tpl, deploy/helm/psfn/templates/workloads.yaml, deploy/helm/psfn/templates/fleet-agents.yaml, scripts/verify-helm-chart.mjs, and deploy/helm/psfn/recovery-chart.sha256. Non-goals: companion-library topology, revision-decoupling tooling, unrelated runtime subPath redesign, or live deployment.
acceptance_criteria: A fresh Fleet render places a runtime-subPath bootstrap init before seed-runtime-files for gateway, Garden, and every Fleet agent; the bootstrap mounts the runtime PVC without subPath at a private path and creates workspaces-shared before any container requests that subPath; scripts/verify-helm-chart.mjs fails if the bootstrap is absent, ordered later, read-only, or omits the mkdir; npm run verify:helm-chart and npm run lint:changed -- --base origin/main pass; the correction is committed to PR #229 for exact-head revalidation.

Commit f478b36105 (PR #229, exact head a5e68a3622; ci-required SUCCESS) adds the first bootstrap-shared-workspace init to gateway, Garden, and every Fleet agent. deploy/helm/psfn/templates/_helpers.tpl:392 mounts the runtime PVC root at /bootstrap/runtime without subPath, writable, and creates only workspaces-shared; scripts/verify-helm-chart.mjs:164 asserts first-init ordering, writable root mount, exact mkdir, and ordering before seed-runtime-files.
