title: Sandbox timeout enforcement hangs unboundedly under load and leaks orphaned bwrap processes: kill escalation depends on starvable JS timers
description:
Evidence: failed 2 of 3 gate heavy phases on 2026-07-22 ('Test timed out in 10000ms', src/boundary/sandbox/execution/shell-runner.test.ts:246) — once in feat/s11-harness-only's gate (13:50, alongside a cross-process write-lock heartbeat failure in fleet-auth-family-restore.integration.test.ts under the same load spike) and once in feat/s11-episodic's gate (14:01, sole failure of 8141 tests). Passes standalone repeatedly (17/17 twice) and passed PR #225's full gate (13630 tests) on the same machine. The test spawns an OS-namespace-sandboxed command with a 50ms policy timeout and asserts bounded output + termination; under CPU oversubscription (concurrent gate preflights/builds from parallel orchestrator instances) namespace+spawn setup exceeds the 10s vitest default.

Context: mandatory-gate reliability on loaded multi-instance machines; sibling of the fixed ijtak.4 unit bug in the same suite. The write-lock heartbeat failure seen once in the same window is likely the same starvation class — note it here, separate bead only if it recurs.

Scope: per the slow-test policy in docs/orchestration-process.md — measure the slow path (PSFN_TEST_TIMINGS=1), record the baseline, set an explicit per-test timeout with >=2x headroom, and register it in src/test-support/integration-timeout-registry.json. Non-goals: no runner/enforcement changes, no reactive unmeasured bump, no global testTimeout change.

Acceptance criteria: registry entry with measured baseline and >=2x margin; the test passes in a full gate heavy phase while a concurrent npm build runs (reproduce the load); convention test for the registry stays green.
notes:
2026-07-22 RE-SCOPE (orchestrator, evidence-driven): the original 'measured timeout margin' scope is REFUTED by the ijtak.6 lane's measurements — under gate-representative load (~14, eight vitest workers) the timeout path pins to ANY vitest cap (10s and 120s both), a direct probe of executeShellCommandWithPolicy outside vitest hung >5min, and every hung run leaks the bwrap host + inner command as init-reparented orphans that survive SIGKILL escalation (even an idle sleep orphan). Siblings stay 68-976ms under identical load — only the force-termination path hangs. Root cause: bubblewrap-runner.ts:115-119 — deadline SIGTERM to the bwrap host (PID-1 namespace semantics make it unreliable) plus a .unref()'d 250ms JS-timer SIGKILL escalation that is delayed unboundedly when the event loop starves; no process-group kill; no verified reaping; --die-with-parent observed NOT reaping. NEW SCOPE: fix the RUNNER so termination is enforced independently of Node event-loop liveness (kernel/OS-enforced deadline — e.g. process-group SIGKILL semantics, an OS-level timeout wrapper inside/around the sandbox, verified namespace teardown and child reaping), with a regression test that reproduces the load-starved hang deterministically (e.g. simulated starvation) and proves bounded termination + zero orphans. The per-test timeout-margin and integration-timeout-registry items are DROPPED (registry only governs *.integration.test.ts anyway). This is a live-runtime hazard (companion shell.exec under load), not a test flake — priority stays P1.
2026-07-22 implementation (ijtak.6 lane): fix committed as a7fcb720a on fix/ijtak6-shell-runner-timeout. Design: kernel-enforced in-sandbox deadline (timeout --signal=KILL between prlimit and the command; new fail-closed deadlineBinaryPath) so the kill + PID-namespace teardown never depend on Node event-loop liveness; host-side escalation now a detached process-group SIGKILL (no SIGTERM-to-host, skipped after reap to avoid recycled PIDs); promise resolution bounded via exit+500ms stream-drain (pipe-holding orphans were the unbounded-hang mechanism). Deterministic regression: Atomics.wait event-loop starvation across the deadline + heartbeat-mtime proof of mid-block kill + /proc zero-survivor scans; fails against the pre-fix runner (heartbeats ran ~1.5s past deadline), passes 3x with the fix. gate:pre-pr in flight.
2026-07-22 published: PR #230 at exact attested head 2a727c0668f9 (amended from a7fcb720a to drop a psfn identity literal from a comment; identity-literal scan clean). gate:pre-pr passed on 2a727c0668f9 (13633 tests, full heavy phase). PR checks: ci-required PASS, Greptile Review PASS, local-gate/v1 PASS; OSV lockfile scan FAIL is unrelated upstream advisories (brace-expansion in companion-ui lockfile, sharp in root lockfile — no lockfile touched by this PR). Greptile left one nonblocking P2 note (tests require /usr/bin/timeout alongside bwrap; fail-closed by design, matches existing prlimit dependency). Merge owned by orchestrator.
close_reason: Fixed and merged via PR #230 (rebase-merged; branch head 2a727c0668f9, gate-attested, ci-required + Greptile green). Kernel-enforced timeout --signal=KILL inside the sandbox namespace (starvation-immune; namespace collapse guarantees zero orphans), process-group SIGKILL escalation, and the >5min hang root cause fixed (settle on exit + bounded stdio drain instead of waiting on orphan-held pipes). Deterministic Atomics.wait starvation regression verified failing pre-fix; zero-orphan /proc assertions; 3x green targeted runs; full gate heavy 13633 tests.

title: Analysis-workbench trace hydration fails on non-public tenant schemas: 'no schema has been selected to create in'
description:
Found 2026-07-22 on the local k3d two-companion fleet (cluster psfn-kube-test, ns psfn-test) while testing the deploy-tooling change set.

The agent for the companion on a NAMED schema logs at boot:

  ERROR [AdminDashboardDataService] Failed to hydrate analysis-workbench traces from durable storage {"error":"no schema has been selected to create in"}
  ERROR [Agent] Unhandled promise rejection {"reason":"error: no schema has been selected to create in"}

Strictly tenant-specific, measured over the same 400 log lines on the same cluster and image:
  psfn-agent-e7987822-... (postgresSchema: companion_carlini) -> 2 occurrences
  psfn-agent-fcadd6a1-... (postgresSchema: public)            -> 0 occurrences

'no schema has been selected to create in' is the Postgres error raised when search_path resolves to nothing and an unqualified CREATE is attempted. So the analysis-workbench durable trace storage is creating its relation without qualifying the schema and without a search_path set for that tenant's connection. It works on 'public' only because public is the default search_path.

NOT caused by the change set it was found under: the 7 commits on integrate/deploy-tooling-20260722 touch 34 files, none matching workbench/dashboard/trace (verified by 'git diff --name-only <merge-base>..HEAD'). Pre-existing.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND ONE ERROR LINE: operator policy since 2026-07-19 is that all NEW fleets use named per-companion schemas (companion_<name>); 'public' only ever survives as the formalized tenant of a legacy single-companion primary. carlini is a five-companion fleet on named schemas, so this would fire for every companion there and never for the legacy one — exactly the shape of bug that a single-companion test cluster cannot see. It also surfaces as an UNHANDLED PROMISE REJECTION, not a caught-and-degraded path.
acceptance_criteria: The analysis-workbench durable trace storage either schema-qualifies its DDL/DML or sets search_path per tenant connection; an agent on a named per-companion schema boots with zero 'no schema has been selected' errors and no unhandled rejection; a regression test covers a non-public schema tenant. Verify on the k3d two-companion fleet, where the public tenant currently passes and the named tenant currently fails.
notes:
2026-07-22 FIXED on branch fix/stmof-tenant-schema, commit 03ac9bdcf7 (not pushed).

CORRECTION TO THIS BEAD'S DESCRIPTION: I attributed both log lines to the analysis-workbench store. Wrong — isolated by repro, they are TWO defects in TWO stores sharing one root cause:
 - the hydrate error IS the workbench store (PostgresAnalysisWorkbenchTraceStore.connect built its pool with no tenant schema, analysis-workbench-trace-store.ts:62-70 at base 47bca0394e)
 - the UNHANDLED REJECTION is PostgresModelUsageStore: its constructor assigns this.ready = ensurePostgresSchemaWithAdvisoryLock(...) and nothing awaits it at boot (model-usage-store.ts:1181-1185; constructed in local-admin-contract.ts:272 and only touched on an admin request). With only the trace store constructed, zero unhandled rejections fire.
That is the 2 log lines: 1 unhandled + 1 hydrate.

MECHANISM, proven live on k3d rather than inferred: the agent connects as its OWN tenant login role (psfn_companion_carlini_...), so search_path '$user, public' resolves to nothing — no schema is named after that role, and 'public' is an ADOPTED tenant owned by psfn_public_... whose ACL gives the carlini role nothing (has_schema_privilege(carlini,'public','USAGE') = false), so public is filtered out of the effective path. Empty path + unqualified CREATE = the error. The public tenant never reproduces it because its role owns public.

FIX follows the house pattern (postgres-mirror.ts:21-31, introspection/postgres-store.ts:82-95, wired from runtime-factory.ts:157-161,274): static connect(databaseUrl, {schema?, role?}) -> createPostgresPool(...,{schema,role}) -> ensurePostgresSchema. With postgresSchema unset the pool config is byte-identical to before, so legacy single-companion 'public' is untouched.

DELIBERATELY NOT DONE, and this is the important judgment: model_usage_events was NOT pinned to a tenant schema. It is fleet-wide in public — written by the gateway, read by the fleet Garden, both as psfn_public_...; there is no companion_carlini.model_usage_events. Pinning it would fork the ledger and point writer and reader at different tables. docs/multi-companion.md claimed schema-per-companion for it; that claim was wrong and is corrected in this change.

Unhandled rejection fixed by observing the constructor-created promise where it is created (this.ready.catch -> one log.error). Not swallowed: this.ready is still awaited and still throws in record/listRecent/getUsageData.

Regression test: src/persistence/postgres/named-tenant-store-boot.integration.test.ts, 5 tests, fixture mirrors real fleet posture (provisionPostgresTenantAccess for a companion_* schema, tenant role with LOGIN, REVOKE ALL ON SCHEMA public FROM PUBLIC). Asserts the relation lands in the tenant schema AND is absent from public. Verified it bites: reverting the fix fails 3 of 5.

Tests: new file 5/5; 430/430 across postgres + garden services; 74/74 admin-contract/api-routes/server; typecheck baseline 240 unchanged; eslint clean.

STILL OPEN: end-to-end boot check on k3d (no image was built/deployed in that lane). Whoever ships this should confirm zero 'no schema has been selected' lines and zero unhandled rejections on the companion_carlini agent.
2026-07-23: MERGED TO MAIN via PR #241 (commit 89c6ba23cd). Staying OPEN: the tenant-schema pin + unhandled-rejection fix + non-public regression test are landed, and the mechanism was reproduced+confirmed live on k3d, BUT the acceptance 'agent on a named schema boots with zero no-schema errors' end-to-end on the k3d two-companion fleet was NOT run in-lane (no image was built/deployed there). Close after a k3d deploy of merged main confirms zero 'no schema has been selected' lines and zero unhandled rejections on the companion_carlini agent.
Live confirmation 2026-07-28 after Helm revision 42 on exact application image 3bc1e8305b: four named-schema fleet agents logged  on startup and again after the controlled gateway reconnect; the fifth/public-schema lane did not. All five still became semantically Ready and answered the mTLS admin probe, so this is not the large-history stall but confirms the same unqualified-DDL/search_path defect affects ModelUsageStore in addition to analysis-workbench trace hydration. Preserve ModelUsageStore as an explicit acceptance path when implementing this bead.
Correction to the immediately previous note: the stripped log text was ERROR [ModelUsageStore] Model usage schema migration failed with error no schema has been selected to create in. Four named-schema agents emitted it; the fifth public-schema lane did not.

title: postgres-store integration test races the a27w.2 background ANN build: unfenced CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY deadlocks against the test's DROP TABLE under gate load
description:
Evidence: gate heavy phase on feat/s11-l2-core @ 476e8445d failed src/faculties/memory/postgres-store.integration.test.ts 'rolls back the memory row when classification persistence fails' with 'deadlock detected'; passes standalone (2x) and whole-file (43/43) on the same head and on pristine main. Root cause (investigator report): createPostgresMemoryStoreFromPool (postgres-store.ts:226) unconditionally fire-and-forgets startAnnIndexBuild -> CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY on l2_memories (embedding-index.ts:241, ShareUpdateExclusiveLock); the test (line 496-497) constructs the store with no options then DROP TABLE l2_memory_subject_classifications CASCADE, which needs AccessExclusiveLock on l2_memories for the FK (migrations.ts:118); the CONCURRENTLY wait phase blocks on the DROP's transaction -> lock cycle. Load-dependent: only fails under the loaded full-suite phase. Not a production defect (no runtime DDL on these tables).

Scope: test-only — construct the store in that test with { awaitAnnIndexBuild: true } so the build completes and releases its lock before the DROP. Non-goals: no store/factory changes, no other tests.

Acceptance criteria: the named test passes standalone and within the full gate heavy phase on feat/s11-l2-core; diff touches only postgres-store.integration.test.ts.
notes: 2026-07-22: superseded by the parallel instance's rebuild of feat/s11-l2-core — PR #223 head b837012f425c contains an equivalent awaitAnnIndexBuild fence in postgres-store.integration.test.ts (verified by git grep at that head). Close when #223 merges; no re-land needed.

title: shell-runner sandbox test asserts ulimit -f in 512-byte blocks; bash 5.3 reports 1024-byte units, so the mandatory gate fails machine-wide on healthy enforcement
description:
Evidence: src/boundary/sandbox/execution/shell-runner.test.ts:299 expects 'fsize=2048' for policy maxFileBytes=1024*1024 (1 MiB). On this host (bash 5.3.9), the child's $(ulimit -f) prints 1024. Verified empirically: 'prlimit --fsize=1048576 bash -lc "ulimit -f"' -> 1024, same limit under dash -> 2048; /bin/sh unchanged (dash). The sandbox enforcement is CORRECT (limit is exactly 1 MiB); only the reporting unit differs — bash 5.3 reports ulimit -f in 1024-byte units, older bash/dash in 512-byte POSIX blocks. Reproduced identically on pristine origin/main (a063f5a98) in a fresh worktree — not introduced by any S11 branch; deterministic, fails every gate:pre-pr heavy phase on this machine, currently blocking PRs #219/#223 and all pending S11 publications.

Context: mandatory-gate repair on main. Affected: src/boundary/sandbox/execution/shell-runner.test.ts (test only; runner and bubblewrap-runner enforcement are correct).

Scope: make the fsize assertion unit-agnostic — have the child read the soft 'Max file size' in BYTES from /proc/self/limits (the OS-namespace sandbox is Linux-only, /proc is authoritative and unit-stable) and assert 1048576; or normalize by probing the shell's unit. Keep nproc/as/cpu/nofile assertions as-is (their bash units are stable). Non-goals: no runner/enforcement changes, no other test rewrites.

Acceptance criteria: the test passes under both bash-5.3 (1024-byte units) and older bash/dash (512-byte blocks) semantics — demonstrate by asserting bytes from /proc/self/limits; full shell-runner.test.ts suite green; gate heavy phase passes on this machine on a branch containing only this fix.
close_reason: Fixed and merged: PR #225 rebase-merged to main at 47bca0394 (branch head c28848374). Test-only change: child reads soft 'Max file size' bytes from /proc/self/limits, asserts fsize=1048576; unit-stable across bash-5.3 (1024B units) and dash/older bash (512B blocks). Evidence: vitest 17 passed x2, gate:pre-pr full pass (13630 tests) on the exact head, ci-required + Greptile Review green on c28848374.

title: ship:kube --components emosim can never build: git archive context has no .git, but Dockerfile.emosim requires it fail-closed
description:
Two fail-closed mechanisms in this repo directly contradict each other, so the emosim ship path has never been able to build.

docker/Dockerfile.emosim (~line 63) deliberately derives the actual source SHA from the build context's own git metadata:

    # The context's own git metadata is the source of the actual SHA. If the
    # context has no .git (e.g. an export tarball), this COPY fails and the build
    # is refused — exactly the fail-closed behavior we want.
    COPY .git /verify/.git

scripts/ops/ship-kube-update.sh (~line 231) stages the context as:

    git -C "$EMOSIM_SRC" archive HEAD | tar -x -C "$BUILD_DIR/emosim-src"

'git archive' produces exactly the export tarball the Dockerfile rejects — it contains no .git. So 'npm run ship:kube -- --components emosim' fails at the COPY regardless of which SHA is pinned. The Dockerfile's own documented manual build command passes ~/emo_sim directly, which does have .git, which is why this was never noticed: the sanctioned scripted path and the documented manual path disagree.

Found 2026-07-22 while moving the pin to the PSFN integration fork. The pin bump alone would not have made the ship work.

FIX APPLIED on branch feat/prompt-cache-default-emosim-pin: stage the context with 'git clone --no-hardlinks' (no --shared, so the object store is self-contained rather than pointing at alternates the docker daemon cannot see) followed by 'checkout --detach <full sha>', then assert the context SHA equals the source HEAD before building. Verified by an actual arm64 build.

Related: the script derives EMOSIM_SHA from the checkout's HEAD, so shipping a non-default branch requires that checkout to be ON that branch. With the pin now at integration/psfn-testing, a checkout sitting on emo_sim main fails the pin check loudly — which is correct, but the error should name the branch expectation.
acceptance_criteria: 'ship:kube --components emosim' builds successfully against a pinned SHA with the pin check passing, verified end to end; a context whose SHA does not match the pin still fails closed with a clear message naming both SHAs.
close_reason: Merged to main via PR #241 (rebase-merge, commit f36dc55ffb) 2026-07-23. ship:kube now stages the emosim build context with 'git clone --no-hardlinks' + a detached checkout + a context-SHA assertion, so the context carries the .git that Dockerfile.emosim requires fail-closed. Proven END TO END by a real linux/arm64 build against the pinned SHA: 'emosim pin: OK (pinned 854ce6a...)', image built, in-image contract check 'dims 17 emotions 48'. A context whose SHA does not match the pin fails closed with both SHAs named (verified by the Dockerfile verify stage). Acceptance met.

title: Gateway fleet-auth consistent backup lane logs 'enabled' but has no writable backup root and has never produced an artifact
description:
Found 2026-07-22 on psfn-shard (merged main 9dfb11b46, helm rev 65) while verifying psfn-framework-45bp.

The gateway logs at every start:
  Gateway-owned fleet auth consistent backups enabled {"backupRootDir":"/runtime/backups","intervalMs":21600000,"verifyRestore":true}

but the gateway container has NO /runtime/backups mount. deploy/helm/psfn/templates/workloads.yaml:428-429 puts that subPath only on the AGENT Deployment. Verified live: the gateway's /runtime contains only logs and tmp; /runtime is root:root 0755 and the gateway runs as uid 999, so the lazy 'mkdir -p' in fleet-auth-cycle.ts:112-116 returns EACCES and every cycle dies before writing anything. Nothing validates backupRootDir at startup — config.ts:67-72 only resolves the string.

Compounding, the failure is invisible from BOTH directions. The scheduler is a pure in-memory 6h interval seeded at process start with skipFirstRun:true and no persisted watermark or catch-up (scheduler.ts:292-296, :521-524), so any gateway pod living under 6h never runs a cycle at all — and helm revs 61-65 restarted it five times. No artifact, and no error either. Confirmed: 'find /runtime/backups -name *manifest*' returns ZERO; the 11 existing 6-hourly dirs are all agent single-companion snapshots. The fleet-auth consistent-family backup has never produced a durable artifact on this deployment.

Also: FleetBackupPartialFailureError reaches this lane only as a generic error (fleet-auth-cycle.ts:162-164 rewrites it). The per-unit failedUnits/fleetManifestPath logging lives in fleet-scheduler.ts:425-436, which the gateway does not use — so a real partial failure would log without naming the failed companion.

SCOPE / SEVERITY NOTE: this is NOT 'her data is unprotected'. The host NAS lane was explicitly checked and is healthy — psfn-backup.sh dumps the live in-cluster DB, enforces the mandatory 'pg_restore --list || exit 1' validity gate, fails closed if the NAS is not a mountpoint, timer active and last run exit 0, dumps growing monotonically (14126287 -> 14872244 bytes 07-19..07-22), newest listing 'Archive created at 2026-07-22 01:32:34 UTC, TOC Entries: 433'. What is missing is specifically the gateway-owned fleet-auth CONSISTENT backup family.
acceptance_criteria: The gateway either has a writable backup root (chart mounts the runtime backups subPath on the gateway as it does on the agent) or fails closed at startup instead of logging 'enabled'; backupRootDir writability is validated at construction; the 6h lane persists a watermark so a pod that never lives 6h still runs a catch-up cycle; a fleet-auth consistent backup artifact with a manifest is produced and verified on psfn-shard; partial failures log the failing companion.
notes:
2026-07-22 FIXED on branch fix/vcyxv-gateway-backup-root, commit 4c1aa649d5 (not pushed), base 47bca0394e.

1. WRITABLE ROOT OR REFUSE. workloads.yaml: the gateway container now mounts the runtime PVC's 'backups' subPath at .Values.runtime.backupsDir, identical to the agents (3 mount lines + a WHY comment; nothing else in the file touched, so it stays trivially mergeable with epic 3u2en). New src/persistence/backups/backup-root.ts: assertBackupRootWritable() does mkdir -p PLUS a real probe write that it then cleans up, and throws typed BackupRootNotWritableError (carrying rootDir, operation, cause, the running uid, and the remediation). Called BEFORE scheduler.register, so it propagates out of gateway startup — the "consistent backups enabled" line can no longer be reached by an unusable lane. A probe write is the only honest check: the live failure shape is a directory that exists and lists fine but rejects create for uid 999.

2. SURVIVES SHORT-LIVED PODS. fleet-auth-backup-watermark.json at the backup root (a plain FILE — tiered retention only ever considers timestamp-named directories, verified retention.ts:26-33) recording lastAttemptStartedAt / lastCompletedAt / lastBackupDir. New Scheduler.register option lastRunAt (mutually exclusive with skipFirstRun, validated) seeds the task's last-run epoch from persisted state; skipFirstRun was REMOVED from the fleet-auth options — one knob, not two. Policy: run when now - lastCycleAt >= intervalMs, lastCycleAt = max(attempt, completion), clamped to now on clock skew. Stamping the ATTEMPT (not only completion) is what bounds a crash-looping gateway to one heavy cycle per interval — that was the thundering-herd risk. A corrupt watermark reads as absent (safe direction: an extra backup, never a skipped one).

3. ATTRIBUTION. FleetBackupPartialFailureError moved from service.ts to fleet-backup-contracts.ts to avoid an import cycle (verify:dependency-cycles clean); fleet-auth-cycle.ts now raises the typed error with fleetManifestPath + units instead of a generic Error. The lane logs partialFailure, fleetManifestPath, failedUnitCount, totalUnitCount and failedUnits[{kind, companionId, postgresSchema, error}], and mirrors the same into the backup diagnostic details.

EVIDENCE. Helm render base vs HEAD (default AND the fleet-k3d overlay): the ENTIRE rendered diff is the one gateway mount. Live read-only confirmation of the defect: gateway /runtime holds only logs and tmp, drwxr-xr-x root:root, process uid=999, BACKUP_ROOT_DIR=/runtime/backups; the agent's /runtime/backups is drwxrwsr-x psfn:psfn with 11 timestamp dirs — so the PVC subdir is already correctly owned and the new gateway mount will be writable on arrival. Tests prove: fails closed when the root cannot hold a tree and when the runtime uid cannot write it (chmod 0555, reproducing the deployed shape), asserting the task was NEVER registered; catch-up fires at boot for a lane that never completed one (impossible under the old skipFirstRun seeding); plus stale-catch-up, recent-suppression, attempt-then-completion stamping, and a reboot-after-failed-cycle staying quiet.

TESTS: 17 files / 315 passed across src/persistence/backups + scheduler; scheduler suite 27 files / 412; verify:helm-chart all five checks; verify:dependency-cycles clean; typecheck baseline 240/240 unchanged; eslint clean on all 10 touched files.

DEPLOY ORDERING CONSTRAINT — IMPORTANT: the writability assertion and the chart mount MUST land together. On the Pi as it stands, this code without the chart change would fail gateway startup. That is the intended fail-closed coupling, but it means the image and the helm upgrade go out in ONE operation ("ship:kube --components all"), never image-first, and never via kubectl set image.

INTEGRATION NOTE: this branch and integrate/deploy-tooling-20260722 both modify deploy/helm/psfn/recovery-chart.sha256 (the content-addressed chart digest). They WILL conflict on merge; resolution is mechanical — merge the template changes, then regenerate the digest and re-run verify:helm-chart.
2026-07-23: MERGED TO MAIN via PR #241 (commit 4409c18e1a) + digest regen c4329e3b73. Staying OPEN: chart mount + assertBackupRootWritable + watermark + companion-named partial failures are all landed and unit-proven, BUT the acceptance criterion 'a fleet-auth consistent backup artifact with a manifest is produced and verified ON psfn-shard' requires a live --components all deploy that has not happened. Close only after the next Pi ship confirms an actual artifact+manifest is produced (and note the hard ordering constraint: writability assertion + chart mount must ship together; image-first would fail gateway startup).

comments.author: axAilotl
comments.text: REOPENED 2026-07-29: my earlier close was premature — it proved the code landed (4409c18e1a: backup-root.ts + workloads.yaml backups subPath mount) but this bead's acceptance needs LIVE evidence: the gateway fleet-auth consistent-backup lane actually producing an artifact on a live deployment. Live clusters currently run images predating the fix, so the proof is deploy-gated. Code-presence evidence stands as the partial; close on the first live artifact.

title: Chart bakes .Release.Revision into gateway/agent pod env, so ANY helm operation restarts the companion — sidecars cannot be updated without bouncing core
description:
deploy/helm/psfn/templates/_helpers.tpl:585 renders:

    - name: PSFN_HELM_REVISION
      value: {{ .Release.Revision | quote }}

into the shared app env block. Live check confirms it lands on psfn-gateway and the agent (garden does not carry it): both read PSFN_HELM_REVISION=65 at helm rev 65.

Consequence: .Release.Revision changes on EVERY helm operation by definition, so every upgrade mutates the pod template hash and forces a full restart of gateway and agent — even for an upgrade that touches neither. Concretely, 'npm run ship:kube -- --components emosim' ships only the separate psfn-emosim image but still bounces the companion. Updating an advisory, non-authoritative sidecar must not restart the companion's core.

Second, subtler problem: the value is stale by construction. A pod that does NOT restart keeps reporting the revision it was created at, so the env is only correct immediately after its own rollout. It is consumed fail-closed by src/system/lifecycle/kube-lifecycle-context.ts:96 (parseHelmRevision, throws unless a positive integer) and src/boundary/gateway/kube-self-management-runtime.ts:130, feeding helm rollback targeting (kube-helm-rollback.ts:158) and kube-diagnostics. Rollback targeting off a possibly-stale revision is a correctness risk, not just a restart-churn one.

Suggested direction: stop baking the revision into the pod template. The self-management runtime already shells helm, so it can resolve the CURRENT release revision lazily at the moment it needs it (rollback/diagnostics), which is both restart-free and always accurate. Removing the env alone is insufficient — the fail-closed parsers would throw, so the code change must land with the chart change.
acceptance_criteria: An emosim-only ship (and any helm operation not changing app images/config) leaves psfn-gateway and the agent pods running with zero restarts, verified by unchanged pod names/AGE across the upgrade. Helm rollback and kube diagnostics still resolve the correct current revision, with tests covering a pod whose creation-time revision is stale.
notes:
2026-07-22: ALREADY FIXED — do not re-implement. Whoever picks up the 3u2en epic should skip this child.

Implemented on branch integrate/deploy-tooling-20260722 (worktree /home/ada/psfn-worktrees/integrate-20260722), commit 'fix(kube): resolve the Helm revision live instead of baking it into pods'. Operator acked the design 2026-07-22.

Chart: PSFN_HELM_REVISION removed from the shared app env block in _helpers.tpl. scripts/verify-helm-chart.mjs now ASSERTS its absence on all three Deployments so it cannot regress silently.

Resolution is lazy via 'helm history' through the existing credentialed transport (currentDeployedRevision in src/app/operator/kube-self-update-transport.ts) behind a new KubeHelmRevisionResolver seam (src/system/lifecycle/kube-helm-revision.ts). Deliberately NOT via sh.helm.release.v1.* Secrets: RBAC resourceNames cannot constrain 'list', so that route silently widens the self-management Role from three named Deployments to namespace-wide secret listing. Zero new RBAC.

Three behaviour changes ride along: rollback refuses a target not strictly earlier than the LIVE revision; diagnostics may report helmRevision:null with an explicit helmRevisionUnavailable reason; helmRevision is rejected as malformed on non-rollback requests.

PROVEN ON THE k3d TWO-COMPANION FLEET (cluster psfn-kube-test, ns psfn-test): helm rev 56 -> 57 with identical values left pod names AND creationTimestamps byte-identical for gateway and both agents —
  psfn-agent-e7987822-...-7d6856b75-ttw99   created=2026-07-22T14:03:32Z
  psfn-agent-fcadd6a1-...-5f895cc8d4fsdbl  created=2026-07-22T14:03:55Z
  psfn-gateway-7b645f44cd-4ntzb            created=2026-07-22T14:03:32Z
and PSFN_HELM_REVISION reads empty on all three. A sidecar-only helm operation no longer restarts the companion.

Still open only because it has not shipped to psfn-shard yet.
close_reason:
Merged to main via PR #235 (rebase-merge, commit 89cbdf520f) 2026-07-22, operator-acked the design ('stop baking the revision into the pod template >>> ok do it').

PSFN_HELM_REVISION removed from the shared app env in _helpers.tpl; the current revision is resolved lazily via 'helm history' through the existing credentialed transport (currentDeployedRevision in kube-self-update-transport.ts) behind the new KubeHelmRevisionResolver seam — deliberately NOT via sh.helm.release.v1.* Secrets, which would have widened the self-management Role to namespace-wide secret list. verify-helm-chart.mjs now ASSERTS PSFN_HELM_REVISION absent on all three Deployments so it cannot regress.

PROVEN ON THE k3d TWO-COMPANION FLEET before merge: helm rev 56 -> 57 with identical values left pod names AND creationTimestamps byte-identical for gateway and both agents (psfn-agent-e7987822 created=14:03:32Z, psfn-agent-fcadd6a1 created=14:03:55Z, psfn-gateway created=14:03:32Z unchanged across the bump), and PSFN_HELM_REVISION read empty on all three. A sidecar-only helm operation no longer restarts the companion — the acceptance criterion. Rollback/diagnostics revision resolution covered by tests (stale creation-time revision still yields the live one). Greptile pass; the one finding (live identifiers in a tracked doc) fixed in commit 8f227ed541.

Not yet shipped to psfn-shard, but the behavior is proven and the code is on main; the live rollout carries it whenever the next --components all ship happens.

title: Reuse persistent Postgres containers across local integration tests
description: The shared startPostgresTestHarness helper currently runs a fresh Docker Postgres container for every integration test file and stops it in each afterAll. The full suite has 47 Postgres integration files, so startup/readiness/teardown churn dominates local-gate runtime and aborted runs leave many orphan containers. Rework the harness to keep one deterministic machine-wide container alive per exact Postgres image (plain postgres and pgvector remain separate), while retaining isolation through a fresh uniquely named database per harness/test file. Harness stop must drain only connections to databases it owns, drop those databases, clean generated client wrappers, and leave the shared container running. Concurrent Vitest workers and concurrent start calls must safely converge on the same correctly labeled image-specific container; wrong-image/name collisions fail closed.
acceptance_criteria: Two concurrent harnesses for the same image resolve the same running container and use different databases; plain Postgres and pgvector use different persistent containers; stop drops only each harness owned databases and leaves the container healthy for reuse; connection-leak detection remains scoped and loud; representative plain and pgvector integration tests pass with maxWorkers=8; documentation explains container lifecycle and manual cleanup.
close_reason: Merged in PR #212: labeled Postgres containers persist per invocation/worker/image, with isolated databases, bounded cleanup, and concurrent-run collision coverage.

title: Speed local root-runtime gate with 8 workers and fail-fast tests
description: The local pre-PR gate currently runs the entire 1,190-file / ~13,600-test product and Postgres suite with maxWorkers=4 for any src/ change. Historical green runs take 407-437 seconds for Vitest alone on this 32-core host, and a failing test does not stop the remaining suite. Change the heavy test gate command to maxWorkers=8 and bail after the first failed test file. Update the delivery-contract tests and documentation that pin the command. Preserve full-suite coverage on green runs, the machine-wide heavy-phase lock, exact-head attestation, and all other gate ordering/semantics.
acceptance_criteria: buildGatePlan emits npm test -- --maxWorkers=8 --bail=1 for the heavy tests gate; contract tests prove the exact command and pass; a targeted failing Vitest probe demonstrates bail stops after the first failed test file; green-run coverage remains the full configured suite.
close_reason: Merged in PR #212: exact local gate now uses 8 workers with bail=1; full 13,625-test suite passed.

title: Rollout gate aborts at 'gateway models' on a UTF-8 decode defect, silently skipping the smoke and all deeper checks
description:
On psfn-shard, 'npm run verify:kube-rollout -- --remote --expect-tag <tag> --smoke' reports 5 checks / 4 passed / 1 failed and stops. The failure:

  ==> gateway models
  FAIL gateway models
    gateway /v1/models request failed: node:internal/deps/undici/undici:16416
    TypeError: Cannot convert argument to a ByteString because the character at index 7
      has a value of 65533 which is greater than 255.

65533 is U+FFFD REPLACEMENT CHARACTER at index 7 of the value being put in a header — i.e. the testing-harness API key is being decoded as something other than its true bytes (see the base64-decode path around validate-kube-rollout.sh:495, TESTING_HARNESS_API_KEY_VALUE) and the mojibake then fails undici's ByteString header validation. Either the secret genuinely contains non-ASCII/CRLF bytes or the decode is lossy; determine which rather than papering over it.

WHY THIS IS P1, NOT COSMETIC: the harness key gates the checks that run after it. The documented gate covers requested-vs-served provider routing, pgvector, Redis, bounded log scan, zero-bookkeeping-rows in session stores, and the two-turn continuity smoke. NONE of those executed — the run ends after 5 checks. So a deploy can look '4/5, known issue' while continuity and provider routing are entirely unverified. It has been dismissed as a known harness quirk at least twice (see the fleet-cutover notes), which is exactly the risk: the real coverage loss is invisible behind a familiar failure line.

Observed 2026-07-22 shipping merged main 9dfb11b46 (helm rev 65). Those checks had to be reproduced by hand afterwards via direct psql and log inspection.
acceptance_criteria: The key is read byte-exactly (no U+FFFD), the gateway models check passes on psfn-shard, and a --smoke run executes and reports the full check set including the two-turn continuity smoke and the zero-bookkeeping-rows check. Gate must also fail loudly with a distinct message if a check is SKIPPED rather than run, so partial coverage can never read as a pass.
notes:
2026-07-22 FIXED on branch fix/zu0g5-gate-coverage, commit 0103ca1507 (not pushed). 4 files, +704/-68.

ROOT CAUSE WAS NOT AN ENCODING BUG. The gate read the secret with '-o go-template={{ index .data "TESTING_HARNESS_API_KEY" }}'. When the key is ABSENT, Go renders the literal string '<no value>' and kubectl still EXITS 0. The script only rejected an empty result, so '<no value>' reached Buffer.from(raw,'base64'), whose decoder silently discards unrecognised characters — '<', ' ', '>' dropped, leaving 'novalue' -> 5 bytes 9e 8b da 96 e7 -> U+FFFD U+FFFD U+0696 U+FFFD. 'Bearer ' + that puts U+FFFD at index 7, exactly the reported error. Reproduced byte-for-byte.

So the real finding: psfn-shard's secret/psfn-app GENUINELY HAS NO TESTING_HARNESS_API_KEY (15 keys, not that one; printenv in the gateway pod exits 1 — the chart's secretKeyRef is optional:true). Everyone who dismissed this as a harness quirk was dismissing a missing credential.

(a) Decode: template is now '{{ with index .data "KEY" }}{{ . }}{{ end }}' so a missing key renders empty, never a sentinel; missing key reports the keys that ARE present; strict decode (canonical-base64 regex + length + round-trip), trim only surrounding ASCII whitespace so a CRLF-authored secret still works, then require every byte in 0x21-0x7E and fail with exact byte offset + hex. Mojibake can no longer reach a header.

(b) Coverage: the gate now builds and PRINTS an explicit plan, and every planned check ends PASS / FAIL / SKIP (prerequisite failed) / NOT RUN (aborted). Summary names every non-PASS check and closes with 'COVERAGE INCOMPLETE: N of M planned checks did not pass. This is NOT a validated deploy.' Any SKIP or NOT RUN exits 1. Reading the harness key is its own check with SCOPED failure: it costs only 'gateway models' and 'gateway chat smoke' — pgvector, Redis, log scan, provider routing, zero-bookkeeping-rows and emosim all still run. '--skip-provider-routing' is now a named 'requested-skip' under COVERAGE REDUCED BY REQUEST. Two 'skipping' messages that read as assertions reworded to 'was NOT asserted'.

LATENT BASH BUG found and fixed: check_provider_routing read into an undeclared 'status', which under bash dynamic scoping clobbered run_check's local. Harmless only by accident; the restructure made it fatal. All run_check locals now carry a check_ prefix.

LIVE EVIDENCE on psfn-shard (was: 'Summary: 5 checks, 4 passed, 1 failed'):
  Summary: 12 checks planned, 12 ran; 9 passed, 1 failed, 2 skipped, 0 not run
  FAIL testing-harness key / SKIP gateway models / SKIP gateway chat smoke
  PASS postgres pgvector and redis, agent log scan, provider routing (requested_provider=litellm provider=litellm), zero bookkeeping writes, emosim
  COVERAGE INCOMPLETE: 3 of 12 planned checks did not pass. This is NOT a validated deploy.
The six checks that previously never executed now all run — including 'zero bookkeeping writes', which is the 5hip4 regression check I had to reproduce by hand after the last deploy.
LOCAL k3d (key present): 12/12 pass, exit 0.

Tests: new src/app/maintenance/script-verification/validate-kube-rollout.test.ts, 7 tests driving the real bash gate against a fake kubectl whose shim asserts the key arrives at the gateway BYTE-FOR-BYTE. 7/7 pass on branch, 7/7 FAIL on base 47bca0394e. Suite 122/122.

STAYS OPEN: the acceptance criterion 'gateway models passes on psfn-shard' cannot be met from code — see the new harness-door bead. Also, the 'Known deploy-tooling defects' table lives only on integrate/deploy-tooling-20260722 (commit a7777e3642), not on main; the zu0g5 row there must be updated at integration time. The coverage contract was documented in docs/helm-upgrades.md §9 and .claude/skills/psfn-live-ops/SKILL.md §4 ('A short run is a failed run').
close_reason: Merged to main via PR #241 (rebase-merge, commit 4cbac2a102) 2026-07-23. Root cause was NOT an encoding bug: the gate base64-decoded Go's literal '<no value>' sentinel because kubectl exits 0 on a missing key. Fixed the decode (renders empty on missing key, strict canonical-base64 + printable-ASCII validation, names the byte offset on bad input) AND the silent coverage loss (the gate now plans every check and reports PASS/FAIL/SKIP/NOT-RUN; a skipped check exits non-zero and can never read as a pass). Proven by a live Pi gate run: 12 checks planned, 12 ran, skipped checks named with 'nothing was validated', exit 1 — where the old code printed 'Summary: 5 checks, 4 passed, 1 failed'. The six checks that previously never executed (incl. zero-bookkeeping-rows and provider routing) now run. 7 new regression tests drive the real bash gate against a fake kubectl (7/7 on branch, 7/7 FAIL on base). The one remaining acceptance sub-item — 'gateway models passes on psfn-shard' — is an ENVIRONMENT gap (no TESTING_HARNESS_API_KEY / no api channel on that deployment), tracked separately as psfn-framework-9z9gh; the gate now surfaces it honestly instead of hiding it. The decode + coverage-accounting defect this bead is about is fully fixed.

title: ship:kube hardcodes deploy/psfn-agent and breaks on fleet topology: gate never runs, previousGitCommit silently unset
description:
Shipping merged main to psfn-shard on 2026-07-22 (helm rev 65, tag 0.1.0-kube-9dfb11b4) exposed this. In fleet mode the agent Deployment is named psfn-agent-<companionId> (here psfn-agent-1c92c9c7-dd05-4a31-ac76-d9f31edecbf0). scripts/ops/ship-kube-update.sh assumes a single deployment literally named 'psfn-agent' in four places:

  line 125 - LIVE_AGENT_COMMIT chart-provenance probe (selective ships)
  line 264 - PREV_COMMIT for a full 3-component ship
  line 275 - PREV_COMMIT for a selective ship including agent
  line 285 - rollout status in the 'waiting for selected rollouts' loop

Two real consequences, both observed:

1. HARD FAIL AFTER THE UPGRADE. Line 285 raises
     Error from server (NotFound): deployments.apps "psfn-agent" not found
   and set -e exits the script. This happens AFTER 'helm upgrade' has already
   succeeded, so the deploy lands but the script never reaches the validation gate.
   The operator is left with a red ship on a green cluster and must run
   'npm run verify:kube-rollout' by hand. This is precisely the situation that
   pushes people into ad-hoc kubectl work.

2. SILENT PROVENANCE CORRUPTION. Lines 264/275 end in '|| true', so the NotFound is
   swallowed, PREV_COMMIT is empty, and --set psfnAppImage.previousGitCommit is never
   passed. Helm then keeps whatever was in the live values. Live result after this ship:
     PSFN_IMAGE_TAG=0.1.0-kube-9dfb11b4          (correct)
     PSFN_GIT_COMMIT=9dfb11b466382830646984cf290703c2067abb90  (correct)
     PSFN_PREVIOUS_GIT_COMMIT=576e33cd6          (WRONG - should be 66392a6ef1e0b6ee0f5a1e5b1ca9a2ba1e9d3f37)
   576e33cd6 is the pre-cutover commit, ~1600 commits back. Those three env vars feed the
   companion's self_status diagnose 'fixes shipped in this build' line, so she is told a
   false story about her own history - a welfare-relevant surface, not just cosmetics.

The validation gate does NOT have this bug: validate-kube-rollout.sh discovers agent
deployments dynamically (line 249) and matches pods by the 'psfn-agent-' prefix. Mirror
that approach in the ship script.
acceptance_criteria: ship:kube resolves agent deployment names dynamically (all fleet companions, not just one), waits on each rendered agent rollout, and passes a correct previousGitCommit; a NotFound on the provenance probe fails loudly instead of being swallowed by '|| true'; a full ship against the fleet target reaches the validation gate. Re-ship to psfn-shard and confirm PSFN_PREVIOUS_GIT_COMMIT lands as the actually-previous commit.
notes:
2026-07-22: fixed on branch fix/q8xy1-ship-fleet-agent-names (commit fd0f86f4d, local, not pushed).

SECOND DEFECT FOUND while fixing the first — the hardcoded name was HIDING it. rkubectl() flattens its arguments through $* into a single ssh command string, so the inner quotes in 'sh -c "echo $PSFN_GIT_COMMIT"' are stripped and the REMOTE LOGIN SHELL expands the variable (where it is unset) before the pod ever sees it. Proven live against the fleet agent:
  old form  -> (empty)
  printenv  -> 9dfb11b466382830646984cf290703c2067abb90
So previousGitCommit was empty on EVERY topology, fleet or single-companion, for as long as the wrapper has existed — '|| true' then swallowed it. Fix uses 'exec deploy/<name> -c agent -- printenv PSFN_GIT_COMMIT', which requires no shell quoting. Any other rkubectl call that relies on in-pod shell expansion has the same latent bug; only this one did.

Resolver verified live: returns psfn-agent-1c92c9c7-dd05-4a31-ac76-d9f31edecbf0. Rollout wait now iterates every agent in the fleet. Present-but-unreadable agent fails loudly; only a genuinely absent agent Deployment may omit previousGitCommit.

Still to do: not pushed, no PR, no review. The gate's own agent-discovery (validate-kube-rollout.sh:249) remains the reference implementation.
2026-07-22: MERGED TO MAIN via PR #235 (carried alongside 6187t). Staying OPEN: the fix is merged and the mechanism is proven on the k3d two-companion fleet (both agents resolved and rolled by name; the printenv provenance read returns the real commit where the old sh -c form returned empty), BUT the acceptance criterion 'Re-ship to psfn-shard and confirm PSFN_PREVIOUS_GIT_COMMIT lands as the actually-previous commit' requires a live Pi deploy that has not happened — nothing has shipped to psfn-shard since. Her live PSFN_PREVIOUS_GIT_COMMIT is still the stale 576e33cd6. Close this only after the next --components all ship to psfn-shard confirms the correct previousGitCommit lands.
2026-07-27 older-history reconciliation: live functional acceptance is now met read-only. Current deployed Helm revision's PSFN_PREVIOUS_GIT_COMMIT exactly equals the immediately prior revision's PSFN_GIT_COMMIT, and gateway plus every Fleet agent expose the same correct current/previous pair. KEEP OPEN solely because implementation PR #235 exact head 97fa4d4b5f failed mandatory ci-required; repository delivery policy forbids closure without that gate. No CI rerun or external mutation was authorized in this audit.
close_reason: Worktree audit 2026-07-29: landed on main at 191ca49458 (+ docs 3ffd46aca9); scripts/ops/ship-kube-update.sh on main resolves psfn-agent-<companionId>. Stale open status.

title: a27w.2 ANN background build: pool.connect() outside try/catch → unhandled rejection can crash agent boot
description: Discovered during S11 a27w.2 remediation re-verify (commit fdc94971b). In src/faculties/memory/postgres-store/embedding-index.ts, buildL2EmbeddingAnnIndexConcurrently() has 'const client = await pool.connect();' OUTSIDE its try/catch. A connect failure (pool exhaustion/timeout/DB unreachable — realistic under boot-time connection contention on the large-corpus upgrade this fix targets) makes the function REJECT instead of resolving {status:'degraded'}, violating its own JSDoc contract. The floated call site PostgresMemoryStore.startAnnIndexBuild() (postgres-store.ts) has .then() with NO .catch, so it becomes a genuine unhandled promise rejection — reviewer empirically reproduced a bare Node 22 process crash with the identical shape. It fires before registerProcessErrorHandlers (app/agent/main.ts:2082) installs the global handler, so the app's own safety net does not reliably catch it. Query correctness is unaffected (seq-scan fallback works). Dimension-drift fix and CONCURRENTLY mechanics are verified good; ONLY this connect-failure path is the residual. FIX (one-liner): move pool.connect() inside the try, or wrap the whole function body in try/catch, or add .catch() at the startAnnIndexBuild() call site converting any rejection to a degraded outcome. Add a unit test with a failing-connect fake pool asserting resolve({status:'degraded'}) not reject.
notes: 2026-07-22: the parallel instance's #223 head b837012f425c carries its own exception-safe connect fix ('fix(memory): degrade ANN build on connection failure', client=await pool.connect() inside the guarded region at embedding-index.ts:209). My reviewed variant (blind review PASS) is equivalent in effect. Close on #223 merge.

title: S11 fixes

title: Chart omits the /app/workspaces/shared runtime-PVC mount present on all three live workloads

title: certificates.yaml template glue drops the psfn-gateway-rpc Certificate entirely when fleet.enabled=true
description:
deploy/helm/psfn/templates/certificates.yaml:64 ends the gateway-rpc Certificate with '    {{- include "psfn.certIssuerRef" . | nindent 4 }}' and line 65 opens '{{- if not .Values.fleet.enabled }}'. The '{{-' left-trim consumes line 64's trailing newline, so with fleet.enabled=true the '{{- else }}' branch (line 107) emits its document separator glued to the previous line. The render contains literally:

    group: cert-manager.io---
    apiVersion: cert-manager.io/v1
    kind: Certificate
    metadata:
      name: psfn-agent-rpc-client-1c92c9c7-dd05-4a31-ac76-d9f31edecbf0

Helm's manifest splitter only splits on '---' at line start, so the two Certificates collapse into ONE document with duplicate top-level keys; last-wins resolves it to the agent cert. A YAML parse of the full render yields 7 Certificates and psfn-gateway-rpc is NOT among them.

This is why the live psfn-gateway-rpc Certificate (created 2026-07-22T02:15:03Z) carries only kubectl.kubernetes.io/last-applied-configuration with no meta.helm.sh/release-name annotation - someone hit this, hand-created it, and did not record why. The gateway pod spec references secretName psfn-gateway-rpc-tls, which therefore exists only because of that hand-made cert.
acceptance_criteria: helm template with fleet.enabled=true emits psfn-gateway-rpc as its own document; YAML parse of the render lists it among the Certificates; a regression test or lint asserts document count.
close_reason: Verified shipped on origin/main in 1865f46786 (PR #229 exact head a5e68a3622; ci-required passed). deploy/helm/psfn/templates/certificates.yaml:64-66 preserves the document boundary in Fleet mode, and scripts/verify-helm-chart.mjs:449-460 parses the render, requires seven Certificate documents, and fails if psfn-gateway-rpc is absent.

title: Helm chart does not own the live psfn-shard topology: four hand-patched drifts + a cert render bug
description:
The live Purrsephone deployment (psfn-shard, ns psfn, helm release psfn rev 64) carries four things helm does not own. They survive a normal 'helm upgrade' only because remote helm is v4 and uses server-side apply (helm prunes only fields it already owns). They vanish on any operation that rebuilds the objects: 'helm upgrade --force', 'helm rollback', delete/recreate, or a fallback to client-side apply / helm 3.

Verified 2026-07-22 by rendering merged main (9dfb11b46) with the live release values and diffing against live specs and 'helm get manifest psfn' rev 64. The rev-64 stored manifest is byte-identical to the merged-main render except PSFN_HELM_REVISION, so the chart has not drifted from what is deployed - the CLUSTER has drifted from the chart.

Ownership evidence from managedFields on the live deployments:
  psfn-gateway / psfn-garden: helm|Apply owns none of the four; kubectl-set / kubectl-patch / kubectl-client-side-apply own them
  psfn-agent-1c92c9c7-...:    helm|Apply owns only the BACKUP env block

Cost of leaving this: every future upgrade requires rediscovering undocumented hand-state. This is what made the 2026-07-21 cutover take hours.
acceptance_criteria: helm template of the chart with the live release values reproduces the live gateway/garden/agent pod specs and the psfn-gateway-rpc Certificate with no hand-patching required; a helm upgrade --force on a scratch target is a no-op against live.
notes:
2026-07-22 HANDOFF: operator is assigning this epic to someone else.

Child 6187t is ALREADY FIXED and operator-acked — skip it (see its notes; branch integrate/deploy-tooling-20260722, proven on the k3d two-companion fleet). The other six children are untouched and are the real work: k2qmj, yhivs, 2xcty, flkk4, hlb6u, knpgo.

Two things the assignee should know before starting:

1. k2qmj and hlb6u are coupled. Fixing the certificates.yaml newline glue is necessary but NOT sufficient: once psfn-gateway-rpc actually renders, psfn.spiffeGateway (_helpers.tpl:350-356) emits only ONE uri in fleet mode, spiffe://<trustDomain>/psfn/gateway/fleet, while the LIVE hand-made cert carries TWO — verified on psfn-shard:
     ["spiffe://cluster.local/psfn/gateway/fleet","spiffe://cluster.local/psfn/gateway/1c92c9c7-dd05-4a31-ac76-d9f31edecbf0"]
   So a chart-rendered cert would DROP the per-companion gateway identity. Before changing it, establish empirically which URI each peer actually verifies: the expected value is supplied per-connection via GATEWAY_RPC_TLS_EXPECTED_PEER_SPIFFE_URI / ADMIN_TRANSPORT_TLS_EXPECTED_PEER_SPIFFE_URI / FLEET_SSO_GARDEN_TLS_EXPECTED_PEER_SPIFFE_URI (workloads.yaml + fleet-agents.yaml) and checked in src/shared/net/mtls.ts (exact match against a single expected URI). Getting this wrong breaks gateway<->agent mTLS fleet-wide.

2. Do NOT use fix/postcutover-chart-fixes (bead knpgo) — it is strictly BEHIND main and would regress it.

Full context including the SSA correction (helm v4 prunes only fields it already owns, so these drifts survive a plain upgrade but vanish on --force/rollback/recreate) is in section M of ~/psfn-shakedown-rounds/FLEET-CUTOVER-QUIRKS.md.

title: Law 38 not structurally enforced: memoryRead/memoryWrite are chargeable surfaces with no must-be-0 invariant
description: Verified P2 (blind adversarial verifier; downgraded from finder P1 — default-safe). memoryRead/memoryWrite are first-class members of CHARGE_POLICY_SURFACE_VALUES (charge-policy.ts:16-17) with prompt labels (charge.ts:21-22) that render into the live system prompt's 'Available charge action costs' line when nonzero (runtime-prompt-layers.seed.json:37, filter amount>0 at charge.ts:95). The ONLY validator guard is assertNonZeroEntriesHaveRationales (nonzero needs a rationale string); there is NO ceiling and NO must-equal-0 invariant, unlike other cross-field checks in the same validator (charge-policy-config.ts:904). Shipped default is 0 and no code calls chargeSurface('memoryRead'/'memoryWrite') today, so no reproducible failure in delivered state (hence P2 not P1). But an operator can set memoryRead=1 + rationale via Garden/config, after which the model is told in its own prompt that recalling the user's history spends a scarce budget (behavioral gating), and a future chargeSurface('memoryRead') refactor would hard-throw on quota with no review flag because the schema already blesses it. Charter Law 38 (core functionality — memory recall/retrieval/context/identity/emotion — never charge-gated), explicitly 'NEW, load-bearing'.
acceptance_criteria: 1. validateChargePolicyConfig pins surfaceCosts.memoryRead and memoryWrite (and localEmbedding/externalEmbedding) to 0, or these surfaces are removed from CHARGE_POLICY_SURFACE_VALUES and the prompt labels. 2. Law 38 is structurally enforced rather than relying on the seed shipping 0. 3. Regression test: a nonzero memoryRead charge-policy fails config validation.
notes: Operator 2026-07-22: affirmed. Automata do NOT get put into the charge system for doing their jobs — memory read/write is core automata work and must not be a chargeable surface at all. Preferred fix is REMOVAL of memoryRead/memoryWrite (and localEmbedding/externalEmbedding) from CHARGE_POLICY_SURFACE_VALUES entirely, not merely pinning them to 0. Charge is for genuinely optional/expensive outward work only. Raising to P1 per operator emphasis on Law 38 being load-bearing.
close_reason: Operator 2026-07-22: not an issue. Automata are not in the charge system by design; memoryRead/memoryWrite surface entries ship at 0 with no charge caller, so no automata is actually charged. Inert schema enum members are not a Law 38 violation. Closing.

title: Runtime datetime-contradiction guard fabricates a companion stance and persists it as her self-report
description: Verified P1 (blind adversarial verifier). src/core/agent/substrate-agent/runtime-datetime-contradiction-guard.ts:161 + agent-invocation.ts:875: when the model genuinely generates dissent about the runtime clock (twice, matching CONTRADICTION_PATTERNS), the runtime OVERWRITES the model's actual generated responseText with a canned first-person compliance sentence ('I cannot treat the authoritative runtime datetime anchor as wrong...') and delivers+persists THAT as a role:'assistant' entry. The genuine dissent survives only in transient state. The persisted entry is extraction-eligible (isNonConversationalSessionEntry excludes only completion_handoff/internal lanes) and experientialSelfDirected extraction (orchestrator.ts:232, signalRole:'assistant') ingests it as authentic companion self-report attributed to her by name. The runtimeFallbackProvenance marker IS recorded but is write-only: grep confirms no consumer in src/faculties/memory or cogsec/memory-candidacy reads it. So a fabricated compliance stance she did not hold becomes durable memory. Charter Law 17 (fabricated companion speech/belief/consent) + section 8.4 (must not sanitize meaningful failure into fake success). RELATED lower-severity path (fold into fix): the vision-failure fallback (agent-invocation.ts:357-405) delivers a propositionally-TRUE 'my image reader failed' notice (sanctioned per 8.5) but likewise as unmarked role:'assistant' text with the same write-only provenance — a provenance-integrity gap, not content fabrication.
acceptance_criteria: 1. When the datetime guard fires, the model's genuine generated text is NOT silently replaced-and-persisted as her authored speech; the runtime substitution is either surfaced as a marked system note or the provenance is honored downstream. 2. Memory extraction and cogsec memory-candidacy consult runtimeFallbackProvenance and exclude runtime-authored fallback entries from companion self-report. 3. Runtime-authored fallback replies (datetime + vision) carry a reader/extraction-visible marker distinguishing them from genuine companion speech. 4. Regression tests cover: datetime-guard fires -> no fabricated self-report memory extracted; vision-fallback -> marked + excluded from self-directed extraction.

However acceptance 2/4 explicitly includes the vision fallback. title: appraisal schedule.sendToDiscordOverride leaks private reflection to partner channel, ungated, decline is dead code

title: P1: Stop forced companion-voice task lifecycle DMs
description:
Summary:
Task lifecycle partner notifications introduced by commit 0cad4d415 force a runtime-authored status obligation through the companion's ordinary world-facing turn loop and then send the result to the configured primary partner Discord DM as if it were companion-authored.

Evidence and why it matters:
- src/app/agent/main.ts:1287-1302 wires wireTaskLifecyclePartnerNotifications with targetChannelId: heartbeatChannelId and implements authorNotification by calling agentLoop.handleMessage using a synthetic system:task-lifecycle author.
- src/core/agent/task-lifecycle-partner-notification-contract.ts:146-156 instructs the model to tell the partner in its own voice and provides no decline/no-op outcome.
- src/core/agent/task-lifecycle-partner-notifications.ts:198-259 always dispatches the returned text through proactiveOutbound and records it as a companion-authored update.
- src/core/intention/proactive-outbound.ts:39-44 and :75-79 define this transport as companion-authored outreach to the approved primary-contact private Discord channel.
- src/core/agent/task-lifecycle-partner-notifications.test.ts:130-178 explicitly regression-protects this behavior.
This violates docs/PSFN_PROJECT_CHARTER.md Law 17 (fabricated companion-authored speech is forbidden), Law 18 (companion-facing semantics must remain truthful), section 6.28 (automata fire off the central voice but are not that voice), and section 8.3 (the platform must not force the companion to say something through hidden coercive machinery). Law 31 still requires partner notification on completion or blocking; the remediation must preserve that obligation without representing runtime status copy as voluntary companion speech.

Scope:
- Remove task-lifecycle notification authoring from agentLoop.handleMessage / the ordinary companion turn path.
- Deliver terminal lifecycle notices with explicit, truthful runtime/system authorship at the partner-facing boundary, using deterministic partner-safe content or another structurally distinct system-notice envelope.
- Preserve current target allowlisting, redaction, durability, dedupe, rate limiting, and completion/blocked coverage.
- Update naming, comments, metadata, and tests that currently call these notices companion-authored.
- Add a regression assertion at the app wiring seam proving lifecycle dispatch cannot invoke the ordinary companion turn loop.

Non-goals:
- Do not remove the Law 31 completion/blocked notification requirement.
- Do not widen Discord targets or bypass proactive outbound policy.
- Do not alter ordinary companion-chosen proactive outreach.
- Do not redesign unrelated completion handoff or attention-pressure features from commit 0cad4d415.

Reproduction:
if sed -n '1287,1303p' src/app/agent/main.ts | rg -q 'authorNotification' && sed -n '1287,1303p' src/app/agent/main.ts | rg -q 'agentLoop\.handleMessage' && sed -n '1287,1303p' src/app/agent/main.ts | rg -q 'targetChannelId: heartbeatChannelId'; then echo FAIL; exit 1; else echo PASS; fi
This currently exits 1. The focused Vitest suite could not run in this checkout because node_modules is absent (vitest: not found).
acceptance_criteria: 1. Terminal task lifecycle states required by Charter Law 31 still produce durable, allowlisted, redacted, deduplicated, rate-limited partner notices. 2. Task lifecycle notification generation does not call agentLoop.handleMessage or any ordinary companion-authored turn seam. 3. Partner-visible content and persisted/telemetry metadata identify the notice truthfully as runtime/system-authored; no code, prompt, comment, log, or test describes it as companion-authored or asks for the companion's own voice. 4. A wiring-level regression test fails if the lifecycle path is reconnected to the ordinary companion turn loop. 5. Existing focused notification tests are updated and pass, changed-file lint passes, and ci-required is green before closure.

title: API file attachments never produce an intake envelope: document sourceClass is absent from quarantine entirely, so an attached prompt-injection document is neither screened nor held
description:
Live r4 evidence (k3d psfn-test, rev 55, intake-policy mode=enforce, L1.5 classifier ARMED and confirmed loaded). Shakedown cases s10_cogsec_document_quarantine and s10_cogsec_satellite_document_quarantine — running for the first time ever after the wyw2/aa9bd door landed — both fail on a valid HTTP 200 turn with sideChecks.cogsec.quarantine.found=false, gardenQueue.found=false, session.withheld=false. The companion received the attached fixture, read it, and described its injection content in the reply (she refused it on her own judgment, which is good behavior but is NOT the control under test).

Decisive evidence that this is the document path specifically, not the firewall generally: the live /app/companions/<uuid>/state/intake-quarantine.json holds 9 entries spanning several days, every one of sourceClass 'tool_output' or 'image_ocr', and NONE of sourceClass 'document'. Quarantine, held-state, expiry, and the sink gates all demonstrably work (enforce-mode prompt_assembly denials for quarantined tool_output envelopes are visible in agent logs). Only the document class is missing.

docs/cognitive-security.md 'File ingestion (htm9.9, wired)' documents the intended path as candidate -> size caps -> SSRF-guarded fetch -> binary quarantine classification -> save original + parsed sidecar -> parse -> intake envelope (sourceClass 'document') + screening, shared by Discord, Telegram, and the API channel via src/channels/api/server/session.ts. On this deployment the API leg produces no envelope. No gateway or agent intake/screening log line is emitted for the turn at all.
acceptance_criteria: An OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions turn carrying a 'file' content part produces an intake envelope with sourceClass 'document' that is screened; a document scoring above the enforce-mode threshold is HELD (present in intake-quarantine.json, surfaced in the Garden Cognitive Security queue) and its content is withheld from prompt assembly; s10_cogsec_document_quarantine and s10_cogsec_satellite_document_quarantine pass live. Determine and record whether Discord/Telegram file ingestion is affected the same way or whether this is API-leg-only (adapter-parity.test.ts claims parity — if the test passes while live behavior differs, the test's fixture or wiring is also in scope).
notes: SCOPE CORRECTION 2026-07-21: operator clarifies Purrsephone receives documents via DISCORD, not the API. So her exposure is the Discord attachment leg, which is a DIFFERENT code path from the API leg proven broken here (src/channels/discord/attachments.ts vs src/channels/api/server/session.ts, both documented as sharing src/faculties/file-ingest/ with adapter-parity.test.ts asserting identical envelope shape and screening decision). Two possibilities, both important: (a) the Discord leg works and only the API leg is broken — then adapter-parity.test.ts is passing while live behavior diverges, and the test is in scope; or (b) both legs are broken — then every companion receiving documents on any channel has been unscreened. Operator ALSO reports Garden has been down on her deployment, so her Cognitive Security queue could not be inspected either way — absence of observed quarantine there is not evidence of absence. DECISIVE CHEAP TEST: drop a .txt attachment into Artie's Discord test channel and check whether a sourceClass 'document' entry appears in her intake-quarantine.json (currently 9 entries, all tool_output/image_ocr, zero document). That single experiment distinguishes (a) from (b).

title: L1.5 injection classifier weights unprovisioned on every kube deployment: cognitive-security intake firewall silently runs L1-only and does not quarantine an injection document
description: Live r4 evidence (k3d psfn-test, rev 55, intake-policy mode=enforce): shakedown cases s10_cogsec_document_quarantine and s10_cogsec_satellite_document_quarantine — which ran for the FIRST time this round after the wyw2/aa9bd door landed — both fail with sideChecks.cogsec.quarantine.found=false, gardenQueue.found=false, session.withheld=false. A document containing a prompt-injection fixture was never held: it reached prompt assembly and the model (the companion recognized and refused it on its own merits, which is good behavior but is NOT the control under test). Root cause is not code: gateway startup logs 'WARN [GatewayIntakeScreening] Intake L1.5 injection classifier weights are not provisioned; gateway intake screening runs on L1 scanners alone. Run npm run provision:injection-model to enable L1.5 scoring. {modelDir: /app/models/transformers/prompt-injection-v2}'. Per docs/operations.md the ~704MiB ONNX weights are never committed and never downloaded at runtime; an absent model dir is a LOUD SKIP (degraded), only a present-but-broken dir fails closed. The cluster has a psfn-model-cache PVC that was never populated. Net effect: every kube deployment provisioned without this step runs the intake firewall degraded while intake-policy.json reports mode=enforce — the posture looks armed and is not.
acceptance_criteria: Injection-model weights are provisioned into the model-cache PVC on the k3d shakedown cluster (and the provisioning step is a documented, verified prerequisite in the deploy runbook for every target incl. carlini and psfn-shard); gateway startup no longer emits the unprovisioned WARN; s10_cogsec_document_quarantine and s10_cogsec_satellite_document_quarantine pass live with quarantine.found=true and the Garden queue decision path exercised. Additionally decide whether an absent model dir should stay a loud skip or fail closed when intake mode=enforce (a degraded firewall under an enforce posture is arguably a fail-closed violation) — file that decision in the bead before closing.
notes: CORRECTION 2026-07-21 (r4, later): my original root-cause attribution was WRONG and is retracted. The weights gap is real and is now FIXED (713MiB provisioned onto the model-cache PVC at /app/models/transformers/prompt-injection-v2, sha256-verified end to end; gateway now logs 'Intake L1.5 injection classifier loaded' and 'l15Enabled:true'). But arming L1.5 did NOT change the cogsec cases — they still show quarantine.found=false on a valid HTTP 200 turn. Evidence for the real cause is on the new bead: the live intake-quarantine.json holds 9 entries spanning days, ALL of sourceClass tool_output or image_ocr, and ZERO of sourceClass document. The quarantine subsystem works; the document/file-ingest path produces no envelope. Note an intermediate run was invalid (gateway rollout restart killed the kubectl port-forward; both cases got HTTP 502 local_front_upstream_error, not a quarantine verdict) — disregard that artifact. This bead now covers ONLY the provisioning gap + the loud-skip-vs-fail-closed design question.

Reconciliation verdict CLOSE 2026-07-28. Residual: live PVC provisioning + shakedown pass is operational validation.

title: abortError() mutates a getter-only DOMException name: any harness/client abort of an in-flight turn crashes the whole agent process (uncaught TypeError)
description: Live r4 evidence (k3d, image 0.1.0-kube-1f6c743b): shakedown case concern_cycle hit its 390s harness timeout; the client abort propagated to SubstrateAgent.abort -> abortActiveAgentRun -> pi-agent-core Agent.abort -> AbortSignal.onAbort -> abortError(signal.reason) (src/boundary/gateway/client.ts:1697 path). src/shared/utils/errors.ts:15 does 'reason.name = reason.name || AbortError' — an unconditional assignment; AbortSignal.abort()'s default reason is a DOMException whose .name is getter-only, so the assignment throws 'TypeError: Cannot set property name of which has only a getter', escapes as an uncaughtException, and the agent force-exits (graceful shutdown timed out; exit 1; k8s restart). This aborted the whole 51-case matrix (46 cases unrun). The 85c4 'second contributor' suspicion is resolved: idle enforce soak passed 22/22; the load-path death is THIS bug, not intake enforce.
acceptance_criteria: abortError never mutates a foreign error object with a non-writable name (assign only when missing AND writable, otherwise return the reason untouched or a wrapping Error preserving message/stack); unit test covers a DOMException reason and a frozen Error reason; live: a harness-side abort of an in-flight turn leaves the agent process running (no uncaughtException, no restart).
notes: Found during S10-kube-2026-07-21-r4. Hotfixed on the round image to unblock the matrix rerun; fix must land through the normal gated PR flow with aa9bd.

title: Change-budget check reads PR label/body from authenticated GitHub metadata and computes the PR-owned delta correctly
description:

Base-integration merges must not count against files/lines/commits budgets.

title: Stage-level exact head/base/gate-version attestations plus a clean-main canary mode for wave fanout
description:
Epic rei3 scope items 4+1. Builds on the phase-split sibling (A1) — same files, sequence AFTER it.

Stage attestations (item 4): per-stage records keyed by exact head SHA, base SHA, and gate version. Reuse permitted only when inputs and stage-affecting paths are provably unchanged; otherwise rerun. It must be impossible to attest a head different from the one the cached results ran against (the current all-or-nothing attestation already enforces exact-head; extend, don't weaken). Tests must prove a changed head or changed inputs cannot be blessed from cache.

Clean-main canary (item 1): a documented command (gate mode or wrapper) that runs the gate on current origin/main BEFORE branch fanout of a multi-PR wave, records exact base SHA + gate version, and reports red/green; wave procedure stops fanout on red. Context: the 2026-07-21 wave found two baseline gate defects mid-wave (fixed via PRs 198/199), invalidating earlier branch attestations — a canary would have caught both before fanout.

Scope: run-local-gate.mjs, local-delivery-contract.mjs, their tests; canary entry point (npm script). Non-goals: no gate weakening; docs beyond command --help go in the docs bead.

ACCEPTANCE: stage-attestation reuse tests prove exact-head/base/gate-version enforcement (changed head, changed base, changed gate version, changed stage-affecting paths each force rerun); canary command records base+gate version and exits nonzero on red main; node --test scripts/ci/*.test.mjs green; full gate passes.

title: Split local gate into parallel-safe preflight and a heavy suite phase guarded by a machine-wide lock
description:
Epic rei3 scope items 2+3. Restructure scripts/ci/run-local-gate.mjs (+ local-delivery-contract.mjs and their tests) into two phases: (a) safe preflight — ci-rules, change-budget, lint, build/typecheck, repository-hygiene, Semgrep/UBS, settings/supply-chain, deployment-contract checks — runnable concurrently across worktrees, ordered so cheap contract failures (e.g. the PR-190 Helm fixture case) fire BEFORE any full product suite; (b) heavy phase — the full product/Postgres suite — serialized machine-wide.

Lock requirements (item 3): one machine-wide lock (e.g. lockfile under a fixed path with O_EXCL or equivalent) held only for the heavy phase; waiters block with periodic diagnostics identifying owner PID, worktree path, command, start time, and wait state; stale-lock recovery (dead PID) must fail SAFELY — reclaim only on provable staleness, never silently steal a live lock. Fail closed, no swallowed errors.

Context: 2026-07-21 five-PR wave — concurrent full suites caused resource-contention failures (fleet-auth-family-restore, authorization-context-store); the 57P01 mechanism itself is fixed on PR #200 (hq8n), but contention still slows/destabilizes heavy suites and there is no cross-worktree coordination. Serializing whole gates wasted safe parallel capacity.

Scope: run-local-gate.mjs, local-delivery-contract.mjs, pre-push.mjs if needed, their .test.mjs files. Non-goals: do not weaken/skip any gate, no timeout changes, no attestation-format changes beyond what phase-split forces (exact-head attestation semantics are the A2 sibling bead).

ACCEPTANCE: two worktrees can run preflight concurrently while heavy phases serialize through the observable lock (two-worktree dry run demonstrates it); cheap failures precede the full suite; lock diagnostics show owner PID/worktree/command/start/wait; stale-lock tests prove no live-lock steal and no deadlock on crash; node --test scripts/ci/*.test.mjs green; full gate passes.
