title: P1: Make local PR-wave gating deterministic and fast
description:
Problem and evidence:
The 2026-07-21 five-PR local-gate wave for PRs 188, 189, 190, 191, and 195 took roughly three hours. Exact gates normally consumed 8-15 minutes each, and several complete runs were discarded. A clean-main canary was not run before branch fanout, so two baseline gate defects were found mid-wave and fixed through PRs 198 and 199, invalidating earlier branch attestations. Concurrent full suites on the shared host caused resource-contention failures in fleet-auth-family-restore and authorization-context-store. An unrelated deploy-fixes-integration worktree could start the same heavy suite because there is no machine-wide coordination lock. Serializing entire gates wasted safe parallel capacity, while parallelizing entire gates created false failures. PR 190 also ran the full 13k-test suite before a cheap Helm fixture contract failed. Change-budget exceptions required manually supplied environment variables even though the label and PR body already existed. PR 191 was pushed while draft and then marked ready, so the synchronize-triggered CI run skipped and the PR needed a close/reopen event.

Required implementation scope:
1. Add a clean-main gate canary at the start of a multi-PR wave. Record the exact base and gate version and stop branch fanout if main is red.
2. Split local gating into safe parallel preflight and a resource-heavy phase. Run CI rules, change budget, lint, build/typecheck, repository hygiene, Semgrep/UBS, settings/supply-chain checks, and deployment-contract checks before the full product/Postgres suite wherever dependency ordering permits.
3. Add a machine-wide lock around only the heavy full-suite phase so independent worktrees and sessions wait instead of contending. Lock diagnostics must identify owner PID, worktree, command, start time, and wait state; stale-lock recovery must fail safely.
4. Define exact-head/base/gate-version stage attestations. Reuse is allowed only when inputs and stage-affecting paths are provably unchanged; otherwise rerun. Never attest a different head from cached results.
5. Make change-budget validation obtain the PR label/body through authenticated GitHub metadata when available, with a clear offline input contract. Normal merges of current base must not appear as giant authored commits or require misleading exception prose; calculate the PR-owned delta correctly.
6. Fix publication ordering and remote triggers: mark a draft PR ready before pushing the attested head, ensure CI handles ready_for_review, and verify GitHub CI plus Greptile target the exact pushed SHA.
7. Add timing/diagnostic output for slow certification tests and define a margin policy so scope growth cannot silently consume a fixed timeout. Investigate splitting or optimizing fleet-auth-family-restore while retaining every assertion.
8. Reuse or prewarm dependencies across worktrees safely to avoid repeated npm ci cost without sharing mutable build/test outputs.
9. Update AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, and docs/orchestration-process.md with the canonical wave procedure: canary first, safe-preflight parallelism, heavy-phase lock, ready-before-push ordering, exact attestation rules, external-session coordination, and blocker handling.
10. Update scripts/ci/run-local-gate.mjs, scripts/ci/check-change-budget.mjs and tests, .github/workflows/ci.yml, and other focused gate modules needed to implement the contract.

Non-goals:
Do not weaken or skip mandatory gates, remove restore coverage, broaden global timeouts without evidence, rewrite shared PR history, change live deployments, or bundle unrelated product refactors.

Additional failure observed during final merge:
The repository permits only rebase merges, while the shared remote PR branches were deliberately updated with normal merge commits to avoid history rewriting. GitHub therefore reported PR #195 clean and mergeable but rebaseable=false, and refused the only allowed merge method after all checks passed. The workflow must detect repository merge-method policy before branch integration. For a rebase-only repository, do not accumulate normal merge commits on the final delivery branch. Define and document a non-destructive compatible path, such as validating conflict resolution on an integration worktree and publishing an exact-tree linear replacement branch/PR, or explicitly changing repository policy through a separately approved governance change. The process must preserve the remote producer branch without force-pushing and must link/close any superseded PR only after the replacement is merged.

External-review cost control:
The workflow must explicitly classify trusted delivery-only changes, such as a narrowly scoped CI permission correction with focused contract coverage, before opening a PR that triggers paid external review. Define the cheapest approved review path for that class, record when Greptile or another paid reviewer is mandatory, and provide a governed opt-out mechanism when it is not. Cost avoidance must never bypass required security review or mandatory CI; the classification and exception must be auditable. The 10-line PR-label permission hotfix triggered a paid Greptile review because the permission defect was not caught before the original PR merged, demonstrating both the need for endpoint-specific workflow contract tests and review-cost controls.
acceptance_criteria: A documented clean-main canary blocks PR-wave fanout on a red base. Two or more worktrees can run safe preflight concurrently, while attempts to enter the heavy suite serialize through one observable machine-wide lock without resource-contention failures. Cheap deployment/settings/security failures occur before the full product suite. Change-budget evaluation correctly handles normal main integration and obtains authorized exception metadata without ad hoc manual environment setup in the connected GitHub path. Ready-before-push and ready_for_review behavior reliably start CI and Greptile on the exact attested SHA. Exact-head/base/gate-version attestation reuse has tests proving it cannot bless a changed head or changed inputs. Slow-test timing and timeout-margin policy are enforced without reducing assertions. AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, and docs/orchestration-process.md describe the same canonical process and commands. Focused tests, npm run lint, and the full mandatory local gate pass; a two-worktree dry run demonstrates deterministic coordination. The wave preflight detects an incompatible rebase-only plus merge-commit branch strategy before work begins; the documented fallback preserves the original shared branch, proves exact tree equivalence, re-attests the linear head, links the replacement PR, and closes the superseded PR only after the replacement merges. Trusted delivery-only changes are classified before publication; tests prove the paid-review opt-out cannot apply to product, security-sensitive, or untrusted workflow changes, and the documented process records estimated/actual external-review cost.
close_reason: All 7 child beads closed. PR #203 (feat/rei3-gate-determinism, ec191c36b66e) — CI + Greptile green on the attested SHA. Acceptance demonstrated: two-worktree dry run serialized heavy phases through the machine lock with owner-naming waiter diagnostics (5m4s wait captured); cheap failures fire in preflight before the suite; canary mode implemented and its defect class proven live (main's README rewrite broke hygiene + two parity tests via the docs cheap path — fixed forward on the branch); stage attestations enforce exact head/base/gate-version with pass-only records; change-budget exception flowed from PR label/body without manual env in CI; prewarm cut fresh-worktree install to ~15s.

title: Correct the pinned UBS JavaScript skip categories in the local gate
description:
Summary: The mandatory local delivery gate in scripts/ci/local-delivery-contract.mjs invokes pinned UBS 5.3.5 with --skip-js=7 while its adjacent contract comment says ordinary JavaScript equality findings are intentionally delegated to typed lint. UBS 5.3.5 classifies loose equality/nullish comparisons as category 4, while category 7 is the overlapping JavaScript security scan. The mismatch leaves category 4 enabled and category 7 disabled, causing changed-file amplification to block every draft PR on unchanged main loose-null checks. PR #189 reproduced 33 findings (30 inherited, 3 fixture additions); PR #190 reproduced two inherited findings.

Why it matters: local-gate/v1 is mandatory before GitHub CI accepts a PR. The incorrect skip set makes the gate structurally impossible for otherwise green branches and disables the wrong UBS category.

Scope: correct the pinned UBS invocation to match the documented scanner-ownership contract, preserving Semgrep as the blocking security scanner and typed lint as the equality owner. Add or strengthen scripts/ci regression coverage so the exact intended skip categories cannot drift again. Verify with a tight UBS reproduction against known loose-null input before and after the fix, the CI-rule tests, mandatory npm run lint, and npm run gate:pre-pr on the gate-fix branch.

Non-goals: do not rewrite application loose-null comparisons, alter the pinned UBS version, weaken Semgrep, suppress unrelated UBS categories, or modify the five draft PR product diffs.
acceptance_criteria: The UBS command skips both ordinary equality category 4 and the deliberately overlapping JavaScript security category 7 (or an equivalently verified explicit set matching the documented ownership contract); a deterministic contract test asserts the exact arguments; the known loose-null reproduction fails with the old invocation and no longer blocks with the corrected invocation while non-skipped categories remain active; npm run test:ci-rules, npm run lint, and npm run gate:pre-pr pass on a clean exact head; the fix is pushed and merged to main before the five draft PR lanes resume.
close_reason: Merged via PR #198. Rebase commit 17671ebaf updates scripts/ci/local-delivery-contract.mjs:167 to pass UBS 5.3.5 --skip-js=4,7; scripts/ci/local-delivery-contract.test.mjs:206-220 asserts the exact normal and deletion-path argument vectors. Red/green reproduction: existing fake-postgres-contact-pool.ts exited 1 with 28 category-4 criticals under --skip-js=7 and exited 0 under --skip-js=4,7 while 12 non-skipped warnings remained active. Validation passed: npm run test:ci-rules (32/32), npm run lint, exact-head npm run gate:pre-pr at 8aed8f92e, ci-required, and Greptile Review.

title: intake-policy.json mode=enforce hangs the agent runtime after '[Lifecycle] Ready notification sent': admin port dies, liveness exit-137 crashloop; shadow mode is stable
description:
Evidence: On image 0.1.0-kube-ea1c89e34 (k3d fleet, both the Artemis and carlini agents), flipping the system-data intake-policy.json `mode` from "shadow" to "enforce" and restarting the agents hangs the agent runtime shortly after boot. Boot completes normally through:

  [Lifecycle] Ready notification sent

then the process emits no further log lines, admin port 10055 stops accepting connections, and kubelet liveness kills the container (exit 137) ~2 minutes later — repeating indefinitely (6+ restarts over ~25 minutes). Reverting `mode` to "shadow" (identical image, config, and everything else) leaves both agents stable through a 5-minute+ soak with zero restarts. So mode=enforce specifically deadlocks/hangs the agent runtime shortly after Ready.

The v2 intake-policy schema itself is sound — the v2 migration was completed 2026-07-20 and shadow mode runs clean; the fault is isolated to the enforce code path on the agent side.

Context: The layered screeners/classifiers are gateway-side, so the suspect is the agent-side enforce path — intake sink gating or screener wiring blocking the main loop after Ready. Suspect files: src/core/session/intake-sink-gating.ts and src/core/cogsec/intake/. Because enforce is a prerequisite for the CogSec/quarantine shakedown cases, this blocks enforce-mode operation on the fleet entirely (this round ran on shadow and excluded the enforce-requiring cases). Reference: /home/ada/psfn-shakedown-rounds/S10-kube-2026-07-21/ROUND.md "Intake-policy enforce hang" section.

Scope: Find and fix whatever the agent-side enforce path blocks/deadlocks on after Ready (likely a synchronous wait, unresolved promise, or gating dependency that only engages in enforce mode). Do not change the v2 schema (it is fine) and do not gut enforce gating to make the hang disappear — the enforce sink-gating must still gate consequential sinks once fixed.

Acceptance: Both fleet agents run stable under intake-policy.json mode=enforce on the k3d fleet — a 10-minute soak with zero liveness kills / exit 137 restarts and the admin port (10055) continuously accepting — plus a regression test covering agent boot + idle under enforce mode.

Found-by: Purrsephone (self-observation, S10-kube-2026-07-21 shakedown enforce-mode probe)
acceptance_criteria: Both fleet agents run stable under intake-policy.json mode=enforce on k3d — 10-min soak, zero liveness kills / exit-137 restarts, admin port 10055 continuously accepting — plus a regression test covering agent boot+idle under enforce.
notes: Starvation fix merged to main via PR #204. Acceptance remains the 10-minute live enforce soak on k3d (runbook §6); second contributor to the 2-min kill never excluded — treat a soak hang as a fresh finding.
close_reason: Live acceptance met on S10-kube-2026-07-21-r4: fix merged via PR #204 (chunked datamark, 64KiB threshold, 256KiB cap, regression tests in commit); k3d soak under intake-policy mode=enforce on image 0.1.0-kube-1f6c743b — 22/22 samples over 11 min, both fleet agents restarts:0 ready:true, liveness (admin port) green throughout, agent log confirms 'Intake sink gates wired across consequential sinks {mode:enforce}'. Original failure killed the runtime ~2 min post-Ready. Evidence: /home/ada/psfn-shakedown-rounds/S10-kube-2026-07-21-r4/logs/enforce-soak-r4.log. The 51-case matrix continues under enforce as extended load evidence.

comments.author: axAilotl
comments.text: Root-cause investigation (deep-reasoner, static): event-loop STARVATION, not deadlock. The only non-trivial enforce-exclusive CPU on the boot hot path is data-marking on prompt assembly: applyPromptAssemblySinkGate (intake-sink-gating.ts:104-121, enforce-only branch) -> renderMarkedContent -> interleaveDatamark (marking.ts:166-178) — an unbounded per-code-point 'out += char' loop over every marked persisted entry on every context assembly. Boot self-turn fires deterministically (scheduler lastRun=0 -> heartbeat due immediately after Ready). Persisted web_fetch/document/tool_output entries recorded under shadow get re-marked under enforce; large single-line bodies -> multi-second sync bursts back-to-back -> admin :10055 accept starved -> liveness 137. Shadow never enters this code (mode gate before marking). Alternative hypothesis B (latent consumer loop on datamark PUA marker \u{E1D5}\u{E2A7} in prompt text) not excluded; discriminating unit harness defined. Decisive live check if needed: stack sample of wedged pod (operator action). Fix lane starting: timed repro first, then bounded marking (size cap -> summary/truncation reduced form, chunked insertion, per-context work cap; never allow-through).

comments.author: axAilotl
comments.text: Fix implemented, reproduced, and dual-reviewed (Opus + Pi blind, both PASS, no blockers) — staged on fix/deployment-helm-ops (31b3ad205). Repro numbers: 4x1MiB persisted entries = 367-388ms per gate call under enforce vs 0.5-0.9ms shadow (old interleaveDatamark: per-code-point walk + string concat, effectively O(n^2)); after fix 1.7ms. Hypothesis B (consumer non-termination on the datamark marker) probed and ruled out. Fix: chunked stride interleaving (byte-identical below threshold — verified over 200k randomized inputs incl. surrogate/ZWJ cases), 64KiB reduced-and-marked threshold, 256KiB per-context cap; overflow always reduced-and-marked, never passed through unmarked; shadow byte-identical (reference-equal). Full suite green (persistence flakes isolated-pass). CAVEAT for closure: 367ms/4MiB does not arithmetically explain a 2-min liveness kill alone — plausible amplifier is repeated context builds (boot self-turn + heartbeat + crashloop re-pay), which the cap resolves, but a second contributor cannot be excluded from static analysis. Bead stays OPEN pending its acceptance criterion: 10-min enforce soak on k3d with admin :10055 continuously accepting — deploy-gated on the PR merging + operator go for the cluster flip.

title: Helm chart lacks per-agent Postgres DATABASE_URL: fleet agents need per-tenant DSN, forcing a carlini volume hand-patch and --force-conflicts on every upgrade
description:
Evidence: The Helm chart does not support per-agent Postgres DATABASE_URL. Each fleet agent needs its own tenant DSN (e.g. carlini → companion-carlini-url), but the chart renders a single shared postgres-database-url volume/secret key. On the S10-kube-2026-07-21 round the carlini agent's postgres-database-url volume is hand-patched to companion-carlini-url outside Helm. Reproduced this round: the rev-51 helm upgrade failed on a server-side-apply conflict over that hand-patched volume; the upgrade only completed with `helm upgrade --force-conflicts`, after which the carlini volume patch had to be re-applied by hand (documented drift, rev 52).

Context: This is a recurring, load-bearing manual step on every fleet upgrade — it forces --force-conflicts (which itself is dangerous, overriding field-manager ownership) and a post-upgrade re-patch, and any missed re-patch points the carlini agent at the wrong tenant database. Related chart area: the agent Deployment/StatefulSet postgres-database-url volume + secret wiring (helm chart values/templates for per-companion agents). Not a duplicate of 7rg5 (secret pruning on auth.existingSecret flip) — this is per-agent DSN selection.

Scope: Make the chart render each agent's postgres-database-url from a per-companion secret key/value so no hand-patch is needed and no --force-conflicts is required for a routine upgrade. Do not change the tenant DSNs themselves or the postgres secret contents.

Acceptance: A helm upgrade on the fleet cluster completes without --force-conflicts and without any post-upgrade volume hand-patch, with each agent (carlini included) mounting its own tenant DSN (carlini → companion-carlini-url); verify:helm-chart fixtures cover per-agent DB URL rendering.
acceptance_criteria: A fleet-cluster helm upgrade completes without --force-conflicts and without any post-upgrade volume hand-patch, each agent mounting its own tenant DSN (carlini → companion-carlini-url); verify:helm-chart fixtures cover per-agent DB URL rendering.
close_reason: Shipped on PR #204 (rebase-merged to main at 1f6c743ba); local gate attested b5ed55a95617, ci-required + Greptile green. wyw2 live acceptance (harness tier-conformance under the door) folds into the next shakedown round.

title: No headless Garden-admin path for the shakedown harness under fleet-auth: mTLS peer passes but per-request capability admission 403s, excluding ~11 tier-conformance cases
description:
Evidence: On the S10-kube-2026-07-21 fleet-mode round, the shakedown harness has no working path to reach Garden-admin endpoints. The fleet garden (:10054) requires (1) an mTLS SPIFFE peer and (2) a gateway-signed, single-use, per-request capability with audience operator:<companionId>. ADMIN_TOKEN is never consulted under fleet auth. Verified live: an mTLS handshake with the psfn-garden-admin-client-tls cert passes the peer gate, but the request 403s at admission because no per-request fleet capability is present (plain ADMIN_TOKEN over that cert is ignored).

Impact: ~11 harness cases could not run this round — tool-conformance, cogsec quarantine resolution, backup roundtrip, hub enrollments, and capability-matrix confirmations — all of which need an authenticated Garden-admin call. This is not a one-round gap: it blocks tier-conformance sweeps on every future fleet-mode round.

Context: Fleet-auth capability minting is gateway-side (audience operator:<companionId>, single-use). The harness runs out-of-band with cluster credentials but has no sanctioned way to mint or present these capabilities, and the legacy ADMIN_TOKEN door is closed in fleet mode by design. Related: fleet-auth admission (src/boundary/fleet-auth/garden-route-authorization.ts, garden-route-capabilities.ts), garden admission (src/operator/garden/), docs/shakedown.md.

Scope: Provide a sanctioned, auditable harness path to Garden-admin under fleet auth — e.g. harness-scoped capability minting using cluster credentials, or a narrowly-scoped garden admission mode for the testing-harness principal. Must not reopen a bearer-token bypass of fleet auth or weaken single-use/audience constraints for real principals. Document it in docs/shakedown.md.

Acceptance: A documented harness path (in docs/shakedown.md) lets the shakedown harness authenticate to the fleet garden and is exercised by a green tier-conformance sweep on a fleet-mode cluster (the ~11 previously-excluded cases run and pass/fail on merit, not on auth 403).
acceptance_criteria: A documented harness path in docs/shakedown.md lets the harness authenticate to the fleet garden and is exercised by a green tier-conformance sweep on a fleet cluster (the ~11 previously-excluded cases run on merit, not auth 403).
close_reason: Shipped on PR #204 (rebase-merged to main at 1f6c743ba); local gate attested b5ed55a95617, ci-required + Greptile green. wyw2 live acceptance (harness tier-conformance under the door) folds into the next shakedown round.

comments.author: axAilotl
comments.text: Design decided (deep-reasoner pass, 3 candidates evaluated): gateway-owned testing-harness Garden door on the fleet SSO proxy. Bearer TESTING_HARNESS_API_KEY at the gateway unified origin synthesizes a real FleetAuthorizationContext (principalId=testing-harness, provider=testing_harness) and reuses the EXISTING mint->verify->replay->proxy tail — gateway stays the sole capability signer; single-use/TTL/audience byte-identical for real principals. Two-key fail-closed enablement: gateway gardenAdmin.enabled + garden-side FleetAuthVerifierConfig testingHarness.enabled + the secret; anything absent = closed. Route/action allowlist enforced pre-sign; assurance capped at webauthn_uv, never break_glass. REJECTED: harness self-signing keypair (moves Ed25519 minting authority outside the gateway — the exact threat the architecture forecloses) and headless SSO reuse (real owner creds in test infra, can't clear webauthn_uv step-up). Implementation in flight on work/wyw2-harness-garden-door with two pre-coding verifications: (V1) whether approvals:['cogsec'] is enforced at route handlers beyond admission — if it needs live queue interaction, those cases stay gapped and get reported, no approval shim; (V2) enumerate the ~11 blocked cases to derive the allowlist; backup roundtrip may be non-Garden and out of scope.

title: Concern grooming has no rest-window reconciliation: ghost/malformed concerns are never purged and nothing reweights
description:
Evidence: src/core/intention/concern-grooming.ts:98-151 resolves stale concerns (expiresAt <= asOf) and cap overflow, with metrics intention.concern.groomed (:240-248), wired hourly via the generic backgroundMaintenance task (config/scheduler.seed.json:5, intervalMs 3600000) — not a rest-window pass. Grep for purge/ghost/reweight across concern-store-port.ts, concerns.ts, and postgres-adapters/concerns-adapter.ts returns nothing: grooming only marks resolved, never purges, reopens, or reweights. A ghost concern with a malformed or anomalous expiresAt (March-dated ghosts observed live) escapes the stale sweep and has no owning cleanup path. Validated 2026-07-21 from audit synthesis sections 7 and 11.E.

Context: rumination clearance is top of the operator priority stack — allow discomfort, prevent stacks that never end. rest-window.ts and rest-window-policy.ts currently contain no concern references.

Scope: explicit end-of-day concern reconciliation as a rest-window job: detect and purge ghost/malformed concerns (invalid, far-past, or anomalous dates; orphaned records), optionally reweight survivors by class severity, and emit reconciliation metrics distinct from intention.concern.groomed (opened/closed/reweighted/ghost-purged counts). Wire off rest-window policy, not the hourly backgroundMaintenance interval. Non-goals: no automatic concern creation without candidates; keep the existing hourly stale+cap grooming as-is.

Acceptance: reconciliation job runs in the rest window; a fixture with a March-dated ghost concern is purged; reconciliation metrics emitted; existing grooming tests stay green.
notes: Operator 2026-07-22: concerns and location work waits until after the public-flip line

title: pending-contact-approvals persists the full roster on every sighting, including lastSeenAt-only refreshes
description:
Evidence: src/core/contacts/pending-contact-approvals.ts:209-211 and :229-230 — both branches of recordSighting call persist(entries), including the updated-existing branch where only lastSeenAt refreshed with no new preview. Invoked per untracked-speaker message via src/core/contacts/tracking-gate.ts:100. Validated 2026-07-21 from audit synthesis (roster-class idle I/O, sections 2 and 10).

Context: this is the roster-class junk write the operator called out — idle should be idle; real-event L0 appends stay. Every untracked-speaker message rewrites the whole approval store even when nothing material changed.

Scope: gate persist() on a material-change diff — persist on new entry, status change, or new message preview; skip or debounce lastSeenAt-only refreshes. Do not change approval semantics, entry shape, or the tracking-gate contract.

Acceptance: unit test showing repeated sightings of an existing pending contact with no new preview cause zero (or one debounced) persist calls; existing contact-approval tests stay green.
close_reason: Shipped on main 5cfb5c89a: pending-contact-approvals.ts:216-218 gates persist on displayNameChanged||previewAdded; lastSeenAt-only sightings no longer rewrite roster; regression tests cover zero-persist on bare refresh and durable lastSeenAt on next material write. comments.author: axAilotl
comments.text:

title: No unified automata registry: 10+ independent timer/spawn mechanisms exist outside the Scheduler and Garden renders only the scheduler lane
description:
Evidence (spawn inventory, validated 2026-07-21): central Scheduler tick loop (src/core/scheduler/scheduler.ts:450, ~23 register() callers) plus independent mechanisms: BackgroundWorkSupervisor setInterval lease heartbeat (src/core/agent/background-work/supervisor.ts:808), PostTurnActionRuntime handler queue (src/core/agent/post-turn-action-runtime.ts:267 with handlers registered across scheduler-lanes.ts and notify-companion-candidate.ts), SubagentTaskRegistry (src/faculties/subagents/task-registry.ts:25), memory decay setInterval (src/faculties/memory/decay.ts:97), maintenance-review setTimeout (src/faculties/memory/maintenance-review.ts:892-918), cross-process lock heartbeat (src/persistence/sessions/cross-process-lock-heartbeat.ts:49), contact-lifecycle recovery (src/core/contacts/contact-lifecycle-recovery-runtime.ts:52), skills telemetry flush (src/faculties/skills/telemetry.ts:282), cert-manager sweep (src/app/cert-manager/main.ts:92), observer-sidecar drain (src/core/eval/observer-sidecar/queue.ts:240), inline-image retention (src/boundary/gateway/inline-image-retention.ts:168). ScheduledTask metadata (src/core/scheduler/types.ts:48-70) lacks charge-surface, concurrency-class, and max-LLM-calls fields. Garden renders only the scheduler lane (src/operator/garden/routes/scheduler-routes.ts:28). No test asserts no-unregistered-timers. The only cross-cutting enumeration is a doc table that rots (working_docs/prompt-audit-findings-20260714.md:231).

Context: operator states there is no current accurate flowchart of the evolved automata topology (audit synthesis sections 6 and 11.B). A machine-readable registry rendered by Garden is runtime truth; a wiki is not.

Scope: PARENT task — decompose into sub-beads before dispatch per the leaf-bead sizing rule: (1) manifest schema covering kind, trigger, pre-gate, charge surface, concurrency class, max LLM calls (extend ScheduledTask fields); (2) fold the non-scheduler spawners into registration; (3) Garden rendering of the full manifest alongside live state; (4) lint/test that fails on any setInterval/setTimeout/registerHandler spawn not declared in the manifest. Non-goal: do not change scheduling semantics or cadences in this work.

Acceptance: a machine-readable registry enumerates every background spawn mechanism above; Garden renders it; CI fails when a new timer is added without registration.

title: Companion reflection journal is readable via plain Garden admin routes; privacy break-glass has no journal resource kind
description:
Evidence: GET /api/admin/values/reflections/journal (src/operator/garden/api-routes.ts:1240-1253) returns reflectionJournal.listRecent entries verbatim; same pattern serves reflection metacognition, reflection daily, and values journal routes. src/shared/contracts/privacy-break-glass.ts:13 defines PrivacyBreakGlassResourceKind = 'memory' | 'profile' — no journal kind, no confirm/audit flow; garden-route-authorization.test.ts:50-69 shows journal routes get the same generic operator capability as every other admin route. Validated 2026-07-21 from READONLY_AUDIT_origin-main_SYNTHESIS_20260721.md section 11.A; the gap is worse than the audit claimed (protection is not even kubectl friction — it is an ordinary admin API read).

Context: the charter treats the companion private journal as a welfare feature after the attribution-confabulation incident; operator priority stack puts companion QoL first and privacy second. Knowing privacy is structural matters more than hoping the operator does not look.

Scope: route companion-private substrates (reflection journal, metacognition journal, whispers/private notes) through the existing privacy-break-glass contract by adding a resource kind (e.g. 'journal') requiring the same WebAuthn-UV confirmation + audit evidence the service already emits for memory/profile (src/operator/garden/services/privacy-break-glass-service.ts). Default is deny. Non-goals: do not remove journal store wiring; do not invent new auth machinery — reuse break-glass.

Acceptance: journal/metacognition/values-journal admin routes without break-glass confirmation return denied; a break-glass read emits an audit record; tests cover both the deny path and the audited break-glass path.
close_reason: Shipped on main a2d6a378a + 2978beb78: PrivacyBreakGlassResourceKind includes journal (privacy-break-glass.ts:13); four values/reflection read routes default-deny, disclose only under active break_glass assurance with memory_access audit evidence, 503 fail-closed when disclosure cannot be audited; deny + audited paths tested. title: Chart renders no Certificate for the gateway RPC serving cert — upgrade pruned the hand-era one, orphaning a stale-SPIFFE secret
description: Evidence: k3d rev-45 cutover 2026-07-21 — after upgrade, both fleet agents crashlooped exhausting 30 gateway-RPC websocket retries. Root cause: agents expect peer spiffe://cluster.local/psfn/gateway/fleet (chart env GATEWAY_RPC_TLS_EXPECTED_PEER_SPIFFE_URI), and the release manifest renders Certificates for CA, per-companion agent rpc-client/admin, garden, and gateway-sso-client — but NONE for the gateway RPC SERVER (secret psfn-gateway-rpc-tls). The pre-upgrade hand-era Certificate was pruned by the upgrade, leaving the secret orphaned with the old per-UUID URI spiffe://.../psfn/gateway/fcadd6a1-... → mTLS peer verification failed. Live remediation: hand-created Certificate psfn-gateway-rpc (issuer psfn-ca, secret psfn-gateway-rpc-tls, uris fleet + legacy per-UUID, full svc dnsNames), gateway+agents restarted. Scope: chart renders the gateway-rpc server Certificate with the fleet SPIFFE URI + svc dnsNames alongside the existing cert set; verify fixture asserts its presence and URI. Acceptance: helm template with the k3d overlay includes the gateway-rpc Certificate; fresh upgrade brings agents through RPC connect without hand-created certs.
close_reason: Premise stale: the gateway-rpc server Certificate is chart-owned on current origin/main (deploy/helm/psfn/templates/certificates.yaml, 'psfn-gateway-rpc'). Verified by rendering with the preserved live overlay (helm-values-live-rev50.yaml): Certificate present with secretName psfn-gateway-rpc-tls, issuer psfn-ca, uris [spiffe://cluster.local/psfn/gateway/fleet], full svc dnsNames — exactly the hand-created remediation shape. The rev-45 incident predated this landing. Residual gap (no regression coverage) closed by commit on work/dgf1-gateway-rpc-cert: verify-helm-chart.mjs now asserts presence/issuer/secret/URI/dnsNames in fleet mode; ships in the consolidated deployment-fixes PR.

title: main fails lint and four integration suites after red-CI admin-merges, blocking every branch's local gate attestation
description:
Evidence (all reproduced on pure origin/main @ 636655705, 2026-07-21):

1. Lint: 'npm run lint' fails — src/app/agent/main.ts:93 'buildShellExecPolicyConfig' is defined but never used (@typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars). Landed by a3711af62 (7ym.3). Zero call sites in src/ (shell exec policy is wired via src/boundary/gateway/bootstrap-input.ts, not agent main).
2. src/core/agent/arbiter/egress-lease-phase.integration.test.ts — 5/5 fail: "Shared schema runtime is missing the shared_schema_migrations ledger ... the gateway shared-schema migration authority has not run" thrown by assertSharedSchemaReady via PostgresSpeakingArbiterStore.connect (speaking-arbiter-store.ts:263). reservation-phase.integration.test.ts fails identically. Root cause: the kl7y read-only shared-schema conversion flipped the store from self-provisioning ensureSharedSchema to fail-closed assertSharedSchemaReady, but these consumer tests still hand it a fresh harness DB (src/test-support/postgres-test-harness.ts createDatabase provisions only the extension schema).
3. src/app/e2e/icp-certification/process-harness.integration.test.ts — 9/10 fail: 'error: relation "icp_autonomy_invalidation_fences" does not exist' (same class: migration authority never runs against the harness DB).
4. src/app/e2e/fleet-garden-cutover-certification.integration.test.ts — suite fails at load: 'Invalid companions config: companions[0].postgresRole must be a string, got undefined' (load-or-seed.ts:112); fixture predates the postgresRole requirement. gateway-persistence.integration.test.ts (fleet-auth) also red.

How it landed: PR #184 head dd3e54324 had ZERO commit statuses (no local-gate/v1 attestation) and red ci-required, and was admin-merged ~04:23Z 2026-07-21 alongside the kl7y content; the local gate (lint + full tests) never ran on the merged result. Verified PR #187 adds no changes under src/core/agent/arbiter/, src/test-support/, or src/app/e2e/ relative to current main, so merging #187 does not heal this.

Impact: scripts/ci/run-local-gate.mjs runs full lint+tests for any root_runtime change, so NO branch cut from current main can attest; ci-required then fails on every PR (currently blocking PR #186 and the lint-fix branch fix/lint-7ym3-dead-import).

Scope: fix the consumer tests/fixtures — run the shared-schema migration authority (privileged/superuser path, mirroring the pattern already used in src/persistence/postgres/speaking-arbiter-store.integration.test.ts) before connecting shared-schema stores in the arbiter phase suites and the ICP process harness; add postgresRole (and any other now-required fields) to the fleet-garden cert companions fixture; remove the dead import (already staged on fix/lint-7ym3-dead-import). Non-goals: do NOT weaken assertSharedSchemaReady or any runtime fail-closed readiness check; do not touch production provisioning; do not modify PR #187's pending verifier content.

Acceptance: from a clean checkout of the fix branch, 'npm run lint' passes and 'npx vitest run' is green for egress-lease-phase, reservation-phase, icp-certification/process-harness, fleet-garden-cutover-certification, and postgres/fleet-auth/gateway-persistence integration suites against a fresh harness DB; full 'npm test -- --maxWorkers=4' passes; 'npm run gate:pre-pr' attests the branch.

Secondary system: persistence.
notes:
2026-07-21 progress: all four suites repaired and green (arbiter provisioning via migration-authority bootstrap; ICP harness least-privilege tenant credentials; fleet-garden fixture postgresRole/topology). Fifth finding: gateway-persistence binds-replay test failed 2/2 full-suite gate runs (passes isolated) — root cause is RUNTIME, not test: hub-device-human-attachment-store attach leaked raw SQLSTATE 40001 to concurrent same-channel admits instead of the designed 'retry' disposition. Fixed with a single bounded re-run on 40001 (commit be74d5b5b), matching sibling stores' 40001 handling; verified 3x green. Fix PR publishing from branch fix/lint-7ym3-dead-import; same commits cherry-picked onto PR #186 branch.
2026-07-21 blocking review correction: PR #196 was merged before unresolved Greptile P1 discussion_r3619811083 was addressed. The bounded 40001 retry recursively calls attach() from catch before finally releases the failed transaction client; pool-wide simultaneous conflicts can exhaust all clients and deadlock retries. Hotfix must release before retry, add a deterministic pool-exhaustion regression, audit sibling SQLSTATE 40001 retry sites, run targeted tests plus mandatory npm run lint, and ship a follow-up PR.
2026-07-21 hotfix status: commit b4e192da8 on PR #197 moves the retry acquisition after finally releases the failed client and adds a deterministic release-before-reacquire regression. Pre-fix regression failed (released=false); post-fix unit test passes, 10 repeated runs pass, gateway-persistence integration 12/12 passes, npm run lint passes, npm run build passes, and Greptile Review passes with no threads. Merge remains blocked: npm run gate:pre-pr fails only on unchanged main-branch src/core/session/icp-recovery-response-metadata.ts TS18048, so GitHub delta/ci-required report missing local-gate/v1. No adjacent code was changed.
close_reason: Completed and shipped. PR #196 restored the lint/integration gate; follow-up PR #197 merged as f7cb1f137 after correcting the blocking serialization-retry deadlock. Evidence: src/persistence/postgres/fleet-auth/hub-device-human-attachment-store.ts:221-228 releases the failed transaction client in finally before retry acquisition; src/persistence/postgres/fleet-auth/hub-device-human-attachment-store.test.ts deterministically verifies release-before-reacquire. Validation: pre-fix regression failed; post-fix test passed 10 repeated runs, gateway-persistence integration 12/12, npm run lint, npm run build, and Greptile review passed.

title: Authority-floor init asserts exact mode 700 but fsGroup-managed volumes pin the setgid bit — init crashloops on k3d local-path
description: Evidence: first helm-owned k3d upgrade (rev 45) — prepare-fleet-auth-authority-floor init (shipped in PR #175) crashlooped silently (set -eu + failing test emits nothing). Empirical repro in a debug pod on the same claim with the same securityContext: chown ok, chmod 0700 ok (rc=0), stat still reports 999:999:2700 — the setgid bit persists on the fsGroup: 999 volume (k3d local-path), so the strict test "999:999:700" can never pass. Setgid-group-999 inheritance under a 0700 root is harmless. Live remediation: gateway deployment init command hand-patched to accept 700|2700 (case statement, with a diagnostic echo on mismatch — the silent set -eu failure cost debugging time). Scope: chart _helpers.tpl init must (a) tolerate the setgid bit (accept %a of 700 or 2700), (b) echo the observed stat on failure instead of dying silently; verify-helm-chart fixture updated to match. Non-goals: do not add FSETID capability; do not fight kubelet fsGroup semantics. Acceptance: helm upgrade on the k3d cluster brings the gateway through the floor init without the hand-patch; fixture asserts the tolerant test shape.
close_reason: Validated live on the S10-kube-2026-07-21 round. Same clean-main helm rev 52 upgrade (chart @ ea1c89e34): prepare-fleet-auth-authority-floor init container reached Completed with NO mode hand-patch (fsGroup setgid-bit issue no longer trips the exact-700 assertion). Evidence: /home/ada/psfn-shakedown-rounds/S10-kube-2026-07-21/ROUND.md ('Deployment outcome' section), logs/helm-upgrade.log.

title: P1: Make pre-tool hook policies match tool aliases
description: Greptile P1 security finding on PR #184 (feat/7ym-interception), src/boundary/gateway/pre-tool-hook.ts:332. The production pre-tool interception adapter always supplies aliases: [], even though registry evaluation supports matching hook policies by alias. A hook registered only for a retired or surface alias is silently skipped, so the tool call can execute without its intended policy check. Scope: resolve the canonical tool's registered aliases in the production adapter and pass the exact alias set into pre-tool hook registry evaluation; preserve fail-closed interception behavior and add focused coverage proving alias-only policies intercept the corresponding tool call. Non-goals: no redesign of the hook registry, tool naming, or unrelated gateway policy.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Production pre-tool interception supplies the registered aliases for the invoked tool instead of an unconditional empty list. 2. A policy registered only for a retired or surface alias matches and intercepts the canonical tool call. 3. Unknown or malformed alias metadata fails closed rather than silently bypassing policy. 4. Focused tests and npm run lint pass.
close_reason: Verified complete on main in 8e7715c312 (PR #209, exact head 0605e88b06; ci-required SUCCESS). src/boundary/gateway/pre-tool-hook.ts:314-347 makes resolveAliases required and passes resolved aliases into policy evaluation; src/core/agent/tool-surface/registry.ts supplies the canonical/retired-alias equivalence resolver and throws on malformed metadata; src/boundary/gateway/pre-tool-hook.test.ts:216-275 proves alias-only interception, canonical interception from an alias invocation, malformed-metadata fail-closed behavior, and the no-hooks fast path. Full acceptance is met.

title: helm upgrade prunes release-owned postgres/redis Secrets when values switch to auth.existingSecret — total credential outage
description: Evidence: k3d rev-45 upgrade 2026-07-21 — overlay set postgres.auth.existingSecret/redis.auth.existingSecret (required to stop the chart clobbering live creds with CHANGE_ME defaults), which removes the psfn-postgres/psfn-redis Secret objects from the manifest; helm then PRUNED the existing release-owned Secrets. Every workload referencing postgres-database-url failed FailedMount ('secret psfn-postgres not found'); postgres STS itself would fail on next pod recreation. Recovered live by extracting both Secrets from the rev-42 release manifest (helm get manifest --revision 42), stripping helm ownership metadata, kubectl apply — restored secrets are now cluster-owned and safe from future pruning. Scope options (pick one): (a) chart renders credential Secrets with helm.sh/resource-policy: keep so the flip orphans instead of deletes; (b) docs/helm-upgrades.md gains a mandatory pre-flip step: copy the live Secrets to unowned objects (or annotate resource-policy keep) BEFORE any upgrade that sets auth.existingSecret. The floor-PVC precedent (PR #175) argues for (a) on every chart-rendered credential Secret. Acceptance: an upgrade flipping create→existingSecret on a cluster with release-owned credential Secrets leaves the Secrets present and pods mounting them; regression fixture or documented gate proves it.
close_reason: Validated live on the S10-kube-2026-07-21 round. Same clean-main helm rev 52 upgrade (chart @ ea1c89e34) with auth.existingSecret set: psfn-postgres and psfn-redis Secrets present and mounted after the upgrade, no FailedMount, no credential outage. Evidence: /home/ada/psfn-shakedown-rounds/S10-kube-2026-07-21/ROUND.md ('Deployment outcome' section), logs/helm-upgrade.log.

title: Fleet-mode garden workload renders without companion-data mounts while the garden runtime requires per-companion owner files
description: Evidence: first helm-owned upgrade of the k3d shakedown cluster (rev 45, image 0.1.0-kube-c1c53364, 2026-07-21): chart-rendered psfn-garden crashlooped with 'Missing required JSON owner file at /app/companions/fcadd6a1-.../scheduler.json'. Every pre-upgrade garden ReplicaSet mounted companion-data=psfn-companion-data (+workspace, model-cache); the fleet-mode chart garden template renders only system-data/runtime/tls volumes — zero per-companion companion-data mounts — while the garden OperatorSurface config load reads each fleet companion's owner files from companionDataDir. Scope: chart garden template mounts every fleet.companions[].companionDataClaim at /app/companions/<companionId> (mirror the agent workload mapping); verify-helm-chart fixture asserting garden mounts per companion. Non-goals: no runtime changes to what garden reads. Acceptance: helm template with the k3d overlay renders garden with one companion-data mount per fleet entry at the canonical path; verify:helm-chart passes; a helm upgrade on the k3d cluster brings garden Ready without the hand-patch.

Clean-main helm rev 52 upgrade (chart @ ea1c89e34, fix c8c5da2c9): psfn-garden rolled out Ready with chart-rendered per-companion companion-data mounts — garden-companion-data-0 and garden-companion-data-1 verified on the live deploy object — with NO hand-patch. Evidence: /home/ada/psfn-shakedown-rounds/S10-kube-2026-07-21/ROUND.md ('Deployment outcome' section), logs/helm-upgrade.log.

title: OpenAI-compatible response model field reports the first fleet companion's UUID regardless of responder
description: Split from psfn-framework-vknn (the DECIDE half stays there). Evidence: S10-kube-2026-07-19 — Carlini's reply carried Artemis's UUID in the response model field. Root cause verified 2026-07-20 against origin/main: src/channels/api/chat-completions.ts:999,1036,1063 return this.modelName, a static boot label, on every response regardless of which companion produced it. Context: misleading identity signal on the Bearer surface; matters more once MC routing exists (vknn decision) but is wrong today even single-pinned — the label should reflect the actual responding companion. Scope: response assembly only — set the model field from the responding companion's identity at response time; do not add companion selection/routing (that is vknn's decision); do not change request-side model semantics. Acceptance: in a two-companion fleet, a Bearer chat completion answered by companion B carries B's identity in the model field (non-streaming and streaming paths + usage chunk); focused test covers both paths. Blocked-by relationship: none — fixable before the vknn decision.
notes: 2026-07-21 operator escalation to P1: 'a pretty bad bug in a system where you expect to talk to the right person' — identity-integrity class. Also vknn DECIDED same day: Bearer surface stays PINNED to the configured companion by default but gains an authenticated per-request SELECTOR. Fix this bug and implement the selector in one lane (same surface, src/channels/api/chat-completions.ts + gateway routing).
close_reason: Completed by origin/main commit 6c37fc2048f13f5c8fd65f3fa55d6299bcd10f5b. src/channels/api/server/chat-completions.ts now derives response model identity from the authenticated responding companion and fails closed if a stream changes companion; chat-completions.identity.test.ts covers non-streaming responses, streaming chunks/usage, and two-companion routing. The containing PR #194's immediate ci-required was red from the then-broken main baseline; follow-up PR #196 restored and passed the full local gate and ci-required with this commit present. The separate selector-policy mismatch remains open under vknn and does not invalidate this response-identity fix.

title: P1: Isolate concern-arc reconciliation failures during agent startup
description:
Summary: PR #167 introduced startup repair for persisted concern-resolution arcs, but current main commit 0433451c3 awaits reconcileConcernResolutionArcs directly in src/app/agent/core-runtime.ts:656-659. The unresolved PR review thread https://github.com/CGIC-AI/psfn-framework/pull/167#discussion_r3617781351 correctly identifies that a transient concern-store read failure, reflection-journal file read/write failure, disk-full append, or emotion-sink failure rejects buildAgentCoreRuntime; src/app/agent/core-bootstrap.ts:143 awaits that builder without isolation and src/app/agent/main.ts:2017-2019 treats the rejection as fatal and exits the agent. Concern state remains authoritative in Postgres and the arc journal is derivative repair state, so this reconciliation failure must be visible but not startup-fatal. Individual malformed JSONL lines are already skipped by readJsonLines and are not part of this defect.

Scope: add a focused agent-startup reconciliation boundary that invokes the real reconcileConcernResolutionArcs helper, catches failures, logs structured error context, and allows core-runtime construction to continue; wire core-runtime through it; add a regression using a failing concern store at that public seam.

Non-goals: do not weaken required live intention.concern.resolution_appraisal delivery, change arc persistence/idempotency, hide the error without logging, add a parallel journal, or redesign retry scheduling.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A concern-store, journal, emotion-sink, or recorder error during startup concern-arc reconciliation does not reject the startup reconciliation boundary or prevent subsequent core-runtime wiring. 2. The failure is logged exactly once with actionable error text. 3. Successful reconciliation still executes the real reconciler. 4. The live required appraisal delivery path remains unchanged. 5. Focused regression tests, npm run lint, npm run build, and git diff --check pass.
close_reason: Completed in merged PR #176: commits fa1937a7a and 7ed131118 add the isolated startup boundary in src/app/agent/concern-resolution-arc-startup.ts and wire it from src/app/agent/core-runtime.ts. Verified failure and success behavior in concern-resolution-arc-startup.test.ts; focused suite 22/22 passed, npm run lint passed, npm run build passed, repository contracts passed, and all PR test-shard failures matched origin/main exactly.

title: Make delivery local-first before GitHub PR/CI
description: Summary: Repair the delivery workflow so predictable validation runs locally before any branch is pushed or a GitHub PR is opened, then keep GitHub Actions as a small clean-environment/complementary gate plus Greptile. Why: on 2026-07-20 billing-blocked and later genuinely failing CI runs were merged; installed local scanners and repository gates were inconsistently invoked, failures were not returned to the owning agent, 58 PRs/reviews were created in one day, and the 12-file/800-line normal target amplified paid Greptile churn. Scope: add a repo-owned portable Git pre-push hook installed through an explicit setup command; add one deterministic pre-PR runner that validates the exact HEAD against the merge base, records an attestation tied to that HEAD, and is required by the documented gh PR-opening workflow; cover change-budget/diff integrity, CI-rule tests, lint, build, typecheck baseline, repository hygiene, full/proportional tests, Semgrep rule+diff scan, UBS, and path-sensitive specialist/security tools that have shipped wrappers; fail closed when dependencies, base refs, tools, or attestation are missing. Review and reconcile AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, and docs/orchestration-process.md so workers, orchestrators, reviewers, mergers, and failure feedback use one contract. Add portable documentation for installing and running the local gate and reproducing the internal UBS plus blind-review workflow on another machine. Change the normal PR target to 25 files/1,500 counted lines per operator direction while retaining a separately documented hard ceiling. Refactor .github/workflows/ci.yml so GitHub performs only checks that add value beyond the attested local pass (clean install/environment, exact-head verification, platform-sensitive or nonlocal checks) and aggregates them with Greptile completion before merge; preserve exact action pins, least privilege, timeouts, and fail-closed behavior. Files expected: package.json, focused scripts/tests under scripts/ci or scripts/git-hooks, a tracked hooks directory, .github/workflows/ci.yml and PR template, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, docs/orchestration-process.md, and one focused workflow/tooling document under docs/. Non-goals: no live deployment or runtime/PVC changes; no remediation of product regressions; no implementation of the separate open OSV/Trivy/zizmor scanner beads beyond invoking wrappers only if they exist; no unrelated agent-tooling refactor.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A clean clone can run one documented setup command that configures the repo-owned pre-push hook without overwriting unrelated hooks; pushing a PR branch fails before network transfer unless the exact HEAD passes the local pre-PR runner. 2. The pre-PR runner and tests fail closed on dirty/unexpected state, missing base/tool/dependency, gate failure, or stale/mismatched attestation; the documented gh PR-opening command refuses to open a PR without an exact-HEAD attestation. 3. Local coverage includes change budget/diff integrity, CI-rule tests, lint, build, typecheck baseline, repository hygiene, tests, Semgrep test+diff, UBS, and shipped path-sensitive specialist wrappers; outputs identify the failing gate and preserve logs. 4. AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, and docs/orchestration-process.md are reviewed for duplication/contradiction and describe the same local-first lifecycle, exact-head handoff, failure return path, merge prohibition, and 25-file/1,500-line normal target. 5. A repo doc lets another operator install prerequisites and reproduce local gates, UBS review, blind adversarial review prompts, synthesis, Greptile wait, and failure handback on another machine without private deployment data. 6. GitHub CI is reduced to complementary clean-environment/nonlocal checks, remains pinned/least-privilege/timeout-bounded, exposes a stable ci-required result, and cannot report success if any retained lane fails or the local attestation is absent/mismatched. 7. Focused script tests, actionlint, npm run lint, build, repository hygiene, Semgrep, and the full test suite pass; changes are committed, pushed, opened as one focused PR, Greptile is allowed to finish, and ci-required is observed without merging.
notes:
Operator follow-ups 2026-07-20: design must prevent looping/retrigger behavior and speed deployment. Hooks never invoke push/gh recursively; exact-head attestations are reusable; label/review events do not multiply paid runs; failure handback is bounded. A same-day 80-line PR incurred another Greptile charge, so routine small compatible beads must batch into one coherent PR toward the 25-file/1,500-line target instead of one bead per PR; tiny standalone PRs are reserved for urgent, independently releasable, or unsafe-to-batch work.
Implementation validated locally at exact head 2bbfc05917f464e0f2e3b2756e8ed2c79e1cc6b1 against base ce91c8eddb7b7ed8679623d5c73bfa9a1596e570. Full gate passed: lint, build, baselined typecheck, repository hygiene, Semgrep rules and changed-file scan (0 findings), pinned UBS 5.3.5 (0 critical), 1,170 Vitest files/13,385 tests passed with 6 skipped, supply-chain verification, actionlint 1.7.12, and zizmor 1.27.0 (no findings). A 32-worker local run exposed inherited Postgres/time-out instability; the four failing files passed 37/37 under a four-worker diagnostic, and the gate now caps full tests at four workers for portable reliability without skipping coverage.
Final publication head 040bdd7662ae10261c181deab46fed04b7f1f688 passed the complete exact-head local gate after correcting gh shell-alias argument forwarding. The actual alias path was probed locally and forwarded --probe to the publisher; the failed pre-publication attempt created no remote branch, PR, Actions run, or Greptile review.
Published PR #179 at https://github.com/CGIC-AI/psfn-framework/pull/179. Exact-head local-gate/v1 and Greptile Review are successful. One GitHub delta run (29794017157) remains in progress on its integrated clean-environment suite; it has not restarted. Local wrapper polling was intentionally interrupted at operator request without canceling the remote job. Bead remains in_progress and PR is not merged.

title: Deploy the new emo-sim social-desire stack to the fleet
description:
Summary:
Deploy the post-oth4 emo-sim architecture to the current k3s fleet. This replaces the old w05a shadow-experiment/carlini rollout premise. The deployable system is now: GoEmotions/VAD plus mood-free appraisal projection -> long-lived emo_sim temporal accumulator -> directed per-contact social pressure -> PSFN durable social desire -> companion consent -> quiet-hours/trust/cooldown/availability gates -> human outbound or ICP candidate. emo_sim remains advisory and must never send directly.

Authoritative inputs and pins:
- PSFN implementation is on main at 685304c352581cba96142420ddf422304f17bd61 or a later validated descendant; PRs #166, #168, and #170 delivered oth4.1-.4 and oth4.6.
- Maintained emo_sim testing/fork line is FoxEngine-ai/emo_sim integration/psfn-testing at exact commit 112cd60edecad08ae2c99df818e623cd6245b8b5, containing directed social need (2447d5f) and per-drive session configuration (e98ca35). Upstream PR acceptance is not a prerequisite; an exact later reviewed descendant may replace this pin.
- Live authority is deploy/helm/psfn in namespace psfn, not host systemd.

Scope and concrete surfaces:
1. Advance the repo-owned fail-closed emo_sim build pin in docker/Dockerfile.emosim and src/core/eval/observer-sidecar/emosim-build-pin.test.ts to the exact maintained commit selected for rollout; update docs/operations.md and deploy/helm/psfn/README.md with the pin and build invocation.
2. Wire src/core/eval/observer-sidecar/emosim-server-adapter.ts and its tests to the new session-create/API contract: physiological drives disabled or scale 0, social/stimulation retained, directed A->B social need preferred when configured with legacy global fallback, unknown capabilities rejected rather than silently dropped, and PSFN reads at 1 Hz maximum.
3. Build the emo_sim image from a clean checkout at the exact pin using docker/Dockerfile.emosim and scripts/ops/ship-kube-update.sh --components emosim (PSFN_EMOSIM_SRC points at that checkout). Pin the deployed image by immutable tag/digest; do not use latest or a branch ref.
4. Configure deploy/helm/psfn/templates/emosim.yaml and values/owner-file inputs for the current fleet: emosim.enabled=true, explicit requests/limits, PVC persistence, NetworkPolicy retained, adapter.kind=emosim_server, stable per-companion sessionLabel/agentName from companion overlays, and no cross-companion state blending.
5. Roll out through the repo-owned k3s/Helm path. Verify model/API contract, image pin, one stable session per companion, restart recovery/catch-up, directed dyad state, physiological-drive isolation, 1 Hz sampling, and no terminal/API privacy error spam. Use scripts/ops/validate-kube-rollout.sh and record read-only before/after owner-file hashes per docs/operations.md.
6. Prove the end-to-end policy boundary in deployment telemetry: emo_sim produces state/advisory pressure only; PSFN creates/coalesces durable desires; no outbound occurs without the companion consent moment; quiet hours, trust, cooldown, availability, tight rate budget, and ICP routing remain enforced. Negative-origin desires are allowed but use the same consent and cooling gates.
7. Record rollback to the previous exact image/config and confirm rollback does not discard the PVC/session state.

Non-goals:
- Re-running the obsolete two-week w05a experiment or concern-lifecycle correlation study.
- Reviving spawn-per-call emo_sim, random outreach timers, direct emo_sim messaging, or physiological hunger/thirst/sleep behavior.
- Adding dynamic cast membership unless deployment proves it is required; file that separately if observed.
- Editing host systemd or off-repo live configuration.

title: Fix final consent, retry, and settlement blockers in PR #170
description:

title: Normalize concurrent primary-embodiment handoff serialization failures
description: CI run 29726892628, job 88302039387, failed on 2026-07-20 in src/persistence/postgres/fleet-auth/gateway-persistence.integration.test.ts:1496-1504. Two concurrent handoff() calls at expectedGeneration=1 are contractually supposed to yield exactly one success and one PrimaryEmbodimentHandoffDeniedError with code stale_generation. Instead, the rejected call leaked a PostgreSQL DatabaseError with SQLSTATE 40001 (serialization_failure). The implementation in src/persistence/postgres/fleet-auth/primary-embodiment-store.ts:111-176 starts a SERIALIZABLE transaction and rethrows every query/commit error without bounded retry or domain normalization. This makes a core fleet-auth handoff nondeterministic under the exact concurrency it is designed to serialize and flakes the mandatory test shard. Scope: reproduce the concurrent path; inspect the stored procedure and transaction boundary; implement a bounded, fail-closed serialization strategy so a losing valid concurrent request deterministically observes the committed generation and returns stale_generation, while preserving decision replay, cross-companion isolation, audit atomicity, and single-winner behavior. Retry only recognized retryable PostgreSQL transaction failures, use a small explicit bound, roll back/reacquire a fresh transaction between attempts, and preserve the original failure when the bound is exhausted. Strengthen focused integration coverage by repeating or barrier-coordinating the race enough to prove the contract. Non-goals: do not weaken the assertion, accept raw 40001 as equivalent, add broad catch-and-retry behavior, change isolation level without proof, or alter unrelated fleet-auth semantics. Evidence: actual CI diff expected reason.code=stale_generation but received DatabaseError code=40001; no existing bead or open PR touching this file was found.
acceptance_criteria: 1. The concurrent primary-embodiment handoff test deterministically produces one fulfilled result and one PrimaryEmbodimentHandoffDeniedError(code=stale_generation), never a raw SQLSTATE 40001. 2. Retry/normalization applies only to explicitly recognized retryable PostgreSQL transaction errors, is bounded, opens a clean transaction per attempt, and preserves the original database error if exhausted. 3. Exactly one authority generation advance and one atomic audit outcome occur; decision replay, cross-companion isolation, human authority, and attachment-current behavior remain covered. 4. Focused Postgres integration tests repeat or coordinate the race and pass reliably across multiple runs. 5. npm run lint, targeted tests, build, repository hygiene, and CI pass. 6. The fix ships in a focused in-budget PR with coherent small commits and Greptile review.

title: Remediate IaC baseline and add pinned Trivy gates
description: Summary: Use Trivy only for the security surfaces not owned by OSV or Semgrep: Dockerfiles, rendered Helm/Kubernetes configuration, and immutable built container images. Pin Trivy v0.72.0 to ghcr.io/aquasecurity/trivy@sha256:c6e969c5662a546ad5de4a73c2a6b7a7c627f86d916903e175aa623af5b97ada; do not use aquasecurity/trivy-action or setup-trivy. Supply-chain context: the Trivy ecosystem suffered a March 2026 credential compromise affecting CLI/image/action releases, so verify the post-incident immutable release/digest and keep every invocation tokenless, with --disable-telemetry and --skip-version-check. Current reproduced baseline (2026-07-20): static configuration scanning reports 13 HIGH Kubernetes/Helm misconfigurations, primarily writable root filesystems and default/missing security contexts. The main deploy/helm/psfn chart cannot be scanned correctly through Trivy direct Helm rendering because required .Files.Get content is unavailable; render with the repo-authoritative Helm command and representative fail-closed values first, then scan the rendered YAML. Scope: capture each current finding with rule ID/path, remediate real high findings in focused changes, create a repo-owned Docker wrapper/config, run `trivy config` with explicit HIGH,CRITICAL severity and exit code 1 for Docker/Helm/Kubernetes changes, scan an exported built-image archive or exact remote image digest without mounting the Docker socket, and schedule periodic rescans because advisories appear after build time. Trivy vulnerability databases are mutable security feeds: document a narrow feed-refresh exception to immutable application pins or implement reviewed digest refreshes; never freeze a stale DB silently. Use --offline-scan for image analysis where appropriate, explicit scanner selection, and exact scoped/owned/expiring .trivyignore.yaml entries only after independent verification. Expected files include deployment hardening values/templates/tests, focused scripts/ci wrapper/tests, Trivy config/ignore only if justified, and pinned workflow changes. Non-goals: no npm/lockfile vulnerability scanning (OSV owns it), no live `trivy k8s` cluster scan or node-collector privileges, no Docker socket mount, no deployment, no autofix, no floating scanner/database aliases without a documented feed policy, and no blocking gate until the 13-high baseline is resolved or narrowly risk-accepted.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Every one of the 13 current HIGH IaC findings is recorded with ID/path and either fixed with focused Helm/Kubernetes/Docker tests or represented by an exact, justified, owned, expiring exception; broad path/rule suppression is forbidden. 2. Trivy v0.72.0 runs from the stated immutable linux/amd64 digest, verifies its version/provenance, uses no Trivy GitHub Action, disables telemetry/version checks, and receives no repository or registry credentials unless a separately reviewed private-image path requires them. 3. The authoritative Helm chart is rendered first with real Helm and representative required values/.Files content, then the rendered YAML is scanned; renderer failure, empty output, missing inputs, DB failure, or scanner error fails closed. 4. PR config scans select only Dockerfile/Helm/Kubernetes misconfiguration scanners with HIGH,CRITICAL and --exit-code 1; image scans consume an exported archive or exact digest without mounting the Docker socket. 5. Periodic image/config rescans use a documented fresh vulnerability-feed policy; mutable DB refresh is explicit and auditable rather than silently frozen or floating without bounds. 6. Wrapper/config tests cover clean and vulnerable manifests, render failure, scanner/DB failure, severity/exit-code handling, exact expiring ignores, and immutable image targeting. 7. Helm/Kubernetes verification, targeted deployment tests, actionlint, Trivy baseline/image proof, npm run lint for code changes, repository hygiene, and ci-required pass. 8. Remediation and scanner wiring are split into small reviewable commits/PRs within budgets, pushed, Greptile-reviewed, and rebase-merged before the Trivy result becomes required.
close_reason: Shipped on main 8e4f62e04 + 30919b92e + 7fd39fb7e + bf1e3b875: 11/13 HIGH cleared via security contexts + read-only rootfs; Trivy pinned digest sha256:c6e969c5 + 0.72.0 runtime-verified; remaining 2 HIGH (postgres/redis writable rootfs AVD-KSV-0014) are exact owned expiring exceptions (.trivyignore.yaml, 2026-10-20) with gate-enforced expiry; config+image workflows on PR+schedule+dispatch. Reconciliation verdict CLOSE 2026-07-28.

title: Fix dependency advisories and add pinned OSV-Scanner gate
description: Summary: Remediate the current npm vulnerability baseline, then add OSV-Scanner as the sole dependency-vulnerability owner for every committed npm lockfile. Pin OSV-Scanner v2.4.0 to ghcr.io/google/osv-scanner@sha256:bcb04b6bab5ab578898b3ff8b81b381e7961b1eac6aa87639b53aaea0d266003; do not use latest/stable tags or a floating Action. Current reproduced baseline (2026-07-20): the explicit three-lockfile scan found 588 root, 144 Garden, and 282 companion-UI packages and exited 1 for five affected packages/four advisory families: companion-ui vitest 4.0.18, GHSA-5xrq-8626-4rwp/CVSS 9.8, fixed 4.1.0; root adm-zip 0.5.18, GHSA-xcpc-8h2w-3j85/CVSS 7.5, fixed 0.6.0; admin-ui cookie 0.6.0, GHSA-pxg6-pf52-xh8x, fixed 0.7.0; and esbuild 0.27.7 in root plus companion-ui, GHSA-g7r4-m6w7-qqqr/CVSS 2.5, fixed 0.28.1. Scope: update manifests/lockfiles through the package manager in small focused commits, run affected tests/builds, create a repo-owned Docker wrapper/config, scan package-lock.json, admin-ui/package-lock.json, and companion-ui/package-lock.json explicitly, add PR and nightly execution with retained machine-readable output, and join ci-required only after the baseline is clean. OSV has no scan-time severity threshold: do not suppress critical/high advisories; any unavoidable accepted advisory requires exact ID, concrete reachability rationale, owner, and expiry in osv-scanner.toml. Record whether online OSV API lookup (which sends package names/versions, not source) or a maintained offline DB is authoritative. Expected files: the relevant package.json/package-lock.json files, a focused scripts/ci wrapper/test, OSV config only if justified, and pinned GitHub workflow changes. Non-goals: no Trivy npm/filesystem vulnerability scan, no automatic package-manager autofix, no unrelated dependency upgrade, no container/IaC scan, and no gate made required while known findings remain.
acceptance_criteria: 1. All four current advisory families are eliminated by exact dependency updates, or any non-critical/non-high exception is exact-ID, reasoned, owned, expiring, and tested; critical/high findings are not ignored. 2. OSV-Scanner v2.4.0 runs from the stated immutable linux/amd64 image digest with a read-only source mount and no floating registry/action reference. 3. The scan names all three lockfiles explicitly and fails closed on missing/unreadable lockfiles, invalid config, API/DB failure, or any non-ignored vulnerability; Trivy does not duplicate npm scanning. 4. PR execution and a nightly/manual full-inventory run retain actionable JSON/SARIF output, and the OSV result joins ci-required only after a clean baseline. 5. Wrapper/config tests cover clean, vulnerable, missing-lockfile, scanner-error, and exact-expiring-ignore behavior without network-dependent unit tests. 6. Targeted package tests/builds, actionlint, pinned-image/version verification, npm run lint, repository hygiene, and a real clean OSV scan pass. 7. Work is split into reviewable commits/PRs within the repository change budgets, committed, pushed, reviewed by Greptile, and rebase-merged.
notes: 2026-07-27 historical closure audit: KEEP OPEN. The implementation commits 9aa2a96be6 and cf0e05888d are on main, but the bead acceptance requires a real clean OSV scan and the gate is currently red. PR #212 itself had OSV lockfile scan FAILURE even though ci-required passed. Every scheduled main run visible for 2026-07-23 through 2026-07-27 failed; latest run 30257064772 at main b7d7aecb produced osv-scan.json with active advisories including SvelteKit GHSA-866w-xmhq-wj7x and GHSA-wqjv-9729-c5q2, PostCSS GHSA-6g55-p6wh-862q and GHSA-r28c-9q8g-f849, brace-expansion GHSA-3jxr-9vmj-r5cp and GHSA-mh99-v99m-4gvg, and sharp/libvips GHSA-f88m-g3jw-g9cj. The workflow is correctly failing closed and retaining JSON, but acceptance items 1, 4, and 6 are not met on current main. Remediate the current exact lockfile findings and obtain a green real OSV run before closure; do not close from the original advisory-family fixes alone.

title: Fix Node 24 sandbox child-process startup

Why: production images and new GitHub CI pin Node 24.13.1, so this is a broken production execution path, not merely CI configuration. Non-goals: no analysis-workbench behavior changes, no broader sandbox policy changes, no CI workflow changes, and no fallback shim.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A sandbox child process starts successfully under exact Node 24.13.1 without the invalid --no-experimental-fetch option. 2. title: Add GitHub CI gates and change-size rules
description: Summary: Add the repository's first GitHub Actions CI workflow so broad validation runs once on GitHub instead of being repeated in every local agent loop, and add machine-readable PR/commit size rules that stop contaminated or oversized changes such as PR #124 (907 files, 88,469 changed lines, 100 commits). Files: .github/workflows/, a focused script under scripts/ci/, package.json, AGENTS.md, and directly relevant tests/docs only. Scope: pull-request/push/manual CI with concurrency cancellation, least-privilege permissions, exact action SHA pins, explicit timeouts, dependency caching, parallel lint/build/hygiene/test shards, path-sensitive specialist checks, one stable ci-required aggregation job, and a deterministic change-budget checker with clear diagnostics. Update the repo agent contract so local iteration runs targeted checks while GitHub owns broad gates; agents must wait for ci-required before merge. Configure supported non-destructive GitHub repository settings where available. Non-goals: no live deployment, no automatic production CD, no edits to active feature work, no branch/ruleset claim that the current private-repo plan cannot enforce, and no floating action references.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Pull requests, pushes to main, and manual dispatch run a pinned, least-privilege, timeout-bounded GitHub Actions workflow with stale-run cancellation. 2. CI exposes one stable ci-required result covering change-budget, diff integrity, install, lint, build, repository hygiene, tests, and relevant conditional repository checks. 3. A tested deterministic script fails oversized PRs/commits with actionable output, ignores only explicitly documented generated/lockfile classes, and PR #124's shape would fail. 4. AGENTS.md describes small PR/commit targets, exception handling, the GitHub-green-before-merge rule, and a reduced targeted local loop without weakening fail-closed/security expectations. 5. actionlint/workflow validation, script tests, npm run lint, and relevant build/hygiene checks pass. 6. Changes are committed, pushed, and opened as a focused PR; the handoff records the GitHub plan limitation for mandatory branch rules.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #128 at 1f7cd8b00, cd4a4c506, and 4d9e71b19. GitHub run 29720511847 passed change budget, lint, build, repository contracts, all four test shards, and ci-required. Repo settings are SHA-pinned Actions and rebase-only merges; private-plan branch protection remains unavailable. PR #124's 907 files/88,469 lines/100 commits is covered by a regression and fails every hard PR budget.

title: Egress reply sender must be hardened before egressLease.enabled is ever wired true: dedupe, datamark, disclosure routing, draw refund
description: Evidence: jp36.5.1.3 adversarial review (2026-07-20), all four verified against work/jp36-5-1-3@e4fe8d2a (integrated feat/jp36-social-autonomy@ee50fa28). The autonomous send path ships INERT (EgressLeasePhaseSettings.enabled=false, no owner-file/Garden override — grep-confirmed not operator-reachable), which is the only reason these are not P1 blockers on the branch. Before any enablement: (1) DOUBLE-SEND on post-TTL re-drive — egress-lease-phase.ts:591 completes the lease AFTER sender.deliver; if completeLease throws post-send, the lease stays held, TTL reclaim re-grants, and the send-once fence (keyed on delivered/overridden) does not block a second deliver. The code comment claims the sender's outbound-reply guard suppresses duplicates but createAgentLoopEgressReplySender receives NO dedupe guard (OutboundReplyDeduper only feeds the normal reply pump) — the comment is a trap. (2) DISCLOSURE gap — generation runs on internal:egress-reply:<channelId> channelType terminal (unrestricted internal context) then delivers raw to the real room via gateway.discordSend, skipping the room-destination retrieval clamping a normal room reply gets; over-disclosure of private material into a group room not fully ruled out. (3) WEAK DATAMARK — egress-reply-sender.ts fences untrusted room text with ad-hoc BEGIN/END delimiters instead of wrapUntrustedContext + boundary-forgery neutralization (appraiser.ts:255 conventions); a crafted closing delimiter can inject instructions that become autonomous room speech. (4) POT LEAK — draw precedes acquire/send; decline/failure paths never refund (bounded, machine-lane only). Scope: wire the deduper into the egress sender, route generation through the destination-clamped path or apply the room ceiling to the synthetic context, use wrapUntrustedContext, add refund-or-tolerate decision + test, and the missing regression (complete-fails -> post-TTL re-drive -> single delivery). Non-goals: no changes to the lease store fence or breaker. Discovered-from: psfn-framework-jp36.5.1.3. ALSO reconcile: local selectSpeakLeastWinner vs the shared resolveUnlinkedPeerSpeakLeast primitive (obligation #3 divergence, defensible but undocumented).
acceptance_criteria: With enabled=true in a test harness: complete-fails -> post-TTL re-drive delivers exactly once; hostile room message with forged closing delimiter cannot alter the generated reply's instructions (wrapUntrustedContext + neutralization in place); generated reply context is clamped to the destination room's disclosure ceiling (test with private material admitted); draw refund-or-documented-tolerance with test; lint + arbiter suites green. This bead BLOCKS wiring any owner-file/Garden override for egressLease.enabled.
notes: Operator review 2026-07-21: confirmed this bead is correctly open and is the enablement gate for the socially-judged-proactivity stack — do not close without the four fixes and the post-TTL re-drive regression test. Addendum from the mirrors-and-letters design pass (epic h4fp): the new letters correspondence layer is bin-not-push and does NOT use this sender; if any future letters or proactive path reuses createAgentLoopEgressReplySender, this hardening is a hard prerequisite (dedupe wiring, destination-clamped disclosure, wrapUntrustedContext datamarking, draw refund). Reference: docs/mirrors-and-letters.md; working_docs/mirrors-letters-architecture-20260721.md.

The sender/phase suites cover forged delimiters, disclosure clamping, complete-failure plus post-TTL re-drive yielding one delivery, and refund outcomes. The enablement-gate acceptance is fully met while the phase remains default-off.
