title: Propagate terminal lifecycle delivery failure without falsifying worker outcomes
description:
Summary:
PR #111 remediation commit 940dc5a78 made lifecycle notification intake durable and fail-closed, but terminal worker paths still suppress the final failure when both lifecycle durability sinks are unavailable.

Verified evidence:
- src/faculties/subagents/faculty.ts: finishHandle catches emitCompletionHandoff failure, logs Terminal subagent lifecycle handoff failed without changing the task result, then resolves the successful result. The partner lifecycle event has no durable outbox or post-turn queue record and the caller receives no delivery-failure signal.
- src/faculties/shards/manager.ts: the completed shard path catches emitShardCompletionHandoff failure, logs it, and returns the result; the failed-shard path also catches failure-handoff delivery errors. These paths can therefore finish without the Charter Law 31 lifecycle record after both sinks fail.

Why it matters:
The completed work result must remain honest, but lifecycle delivery failure must not disappear. Converting successful worker execution into a false execution failure is also incorrect. The caller or a durable retry surface needs a structured, actionable delivery state.

Scope:
- Define a caller-visible and/or durable retry contract for terminal completion-handoff delivery failure in subagent and shard results.
- Preserve the true worker execution outcome separately from notification-delivery outcome.
- Ensure a failed lifecycle delivery is retryable or explicitly surfaced and cannot be logged then forgotten.
- Add regression tests for subagent completion, shard completion, and shard failure when the completion-handoff guard rejects because both durable sinks are unavailable.

Non-goals:
- Do not redesign normal task execution state.
- Do not claim exactly-once external transport; provider idempotency/receipt limitations remain a separate nonblocking transport constraint.
- Do not add raw worker output to partner-facing payloads.
acceptance_criteria: Terminal subagent and shard execution preserves its true outcome while a completion-handoff delivery failure is durably retryable or returned through a structured caller-visible status; no terminal delivery error is catch-and-log-only; regressions cover completed subagent, completed shard, and failed shard; npm run lint and targeted tests pass.
notes:
2026-07-20 orchestrator fix pass pushed dbbcbb962 on fix/3slc-terminal-lifecycle. Both confirmed defects fixed: (1) execute() now throws SubagentExecutionError carrying the full SubagentResult — Wyoming delegate no longer loses completionHandoff; (2) shard cleanup failure no longer wraps executionFailure in AggregateError — ShardExecutionError stays the thrown value with cleanup failures on Error.suppressed, and single-cleanup-error on the completed path no longer silently replaces the structured return. Regressions: execute()-failure structure preservation + shard cleanup suppression. 84/84 focused tests, npm run lint, npm run build, git diff --check green. Ready for PR.
Merged into bundle branch fix/orphan-bundle-20260720; DRAFT PR #173 (https://github.com/CGIC-AI/psfn-framework/pull/173) to main, awaiting operator review. One trivial import-block conflict in subagents/faculty.ts resolved (kept both imports). Validation: build/lint PASS, 363/363 touched unit tests pass. Stays in_progress until PR merges.

title: Recover missed L2 memories from intact L0 session ranges
description:
Summary: On the live Purrsephone shard, the July 15-19 rollback-writer/forward-schema incident left L0/session journals intact but advanced extraction markers while L2 writes failed on the required salience_decay_anchor_at column. Evidence: session_messages_projection contains 248/160/136/134/312 rows on July 15-19 UTC, while l2_memories contains 21 rows on July 15, zero on July 16-18, and 11 post-bridge rows on July 19. The expected 2,491 Garden-visible memories became 2,502 only from the 11 post-bridge writes; the missed interval is not backfilled.

Scope: add an authenticated, operator-only, bounded session-memory recovery path that reads canonical L0 entries for one logical session and an explicit message-id/timestamp range, chunks them under configured caps, invokes the normal memory extraction/write pipeline with direct-session semantics, preserves original channel/session/message provenance, and does not regress or falsely advance the normal live extraction marker. It must be resumable/idempotent, expose dry-run counts before mutation, audit every run, fail closed on malformed ranges/missing extractor/concurrent work, and report processed/failed/deferred spans without returning private transcript bodies. Use it to recover the live Purrsephone primary conversation interval for July 16-18 (and any failed tail on July 15/19), then verify resulting L2 rows and absence of constraint errors.

Why: L0 means the conversations are recoverable, but current crash-recovery extraction is not wired as an operator backfill and successful post-bridge markers can strand the historical gap. Restoring writer compatibility prevents new loss but does not recreate the derived memories that failed during the incident.

Non-goals: do not expose companion-data through the model-facing shell; do not classify direct messages as group rooms; do not reset/delete L0 or existing L2 rows; do not replay deployment smoke-test channels; do not bypass normal memory novelty, trust, consent, attribution, or audit logic.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A dry-run for one logical session and explicit bounded range returns message/chunk counts and provenance bounds without transcript bodies. 2. Live recovery uses the normal direct-session extraction/write path, with original L0 channel/session/message provenance and all normal novelty/trust/consent gates. 3. Backfill cannot regress or falsely advance the live extraction coverage marker, is bounded and resumable, and fails closed on invalid ranges, missing runtime dependencies, or concurrent extraction. 4. Focused tests cover dry-run, live success, failure/resume, idempotency/deduplication, marker non-regression, bounds, and auth/audit routing. 5. npm run lint and targeted tests pass. 6. The committed image is deployed to Purrsephone; the July 15-19 missed primary-session interval is recovered from L0, Garden-visible memory count increases only by accepted novel memories, and live logs show no memory constraint failures.

title: Subagent capability gate inherits the parent tier: child's advertised capabilities never constrain per-call authorization
description:
Evidence (dual blind review of psfn-framework-p0le, 2026-07-20, Pi finding I1, Opus convergent): SubagentFaculty.runHandle builds the child SubstrateAgent with sanitizeCoreSubstrateConfig(this.deps.config) (src/faculties/subagents/faculty.ts:~483-504) which preserves capabilityTier (runtime-config-contracts.ts:~481-496); faculty.ts never calls agentLoop.setCapabilityAccess (grep-confirmed), so resolveCapabilityAccess() falls back to resolveTierCapabilityTokens(parent tier) (substrate-agent.ts:~784-796). The subagent's advertised capabilities param (default ['general']) is used only for spawn-required-capability checks and memory-write policy — never for the per-call tool capability gate. Consequence: every capability-gated tool a parent tier grants is callable by its bounded children: notify send (external.discord at apprentice+ — partner-facing egress authored by a bounded child), system restart/rebuild (autonomous), schedule schedule_prompt (child enqueues prompts the parent autonomously executes later — self-injection vector, BOTH reviewers' strongest case), world control, fs/repo writes (git.write), session lifecycle actions, beads mutations, analysis_workbench/shell (repl.execute at nursery+).

Context: this is the mechanism behind the entire residual surface after c7d (memory) and p0le (identity/values/consent/trust/companion-content tools) closed their seams with per-tool policy maps. Scoping the child's capability access to its advertised tokens closes the class wholesale instead of tool-by-tool. Charter framing: bounded-ness and write-trust are different axes (6.11 as amended).

Scope: make the subagent loop's capability access derive from the spawn request's capabilities (intersected with the parent tier — a child must never exceed the parent), defaulting to a minimal read posture for ['general']; keep c7d/p0le tool governance as defense-in-depth on top. NOTE: tools mapped to NO_CAPABILITY_REQUIREMENT (selfie_create, generate_image) are NOT closed by this fix and are handled by the sibling per-tool disposition bead. Non-goals: no changes to parent-loop capability resolution; no new governance framework.

Acceptance criteria: a test proves a default-['general'] subagent of an autonomous-tier parent is denied notify send, system restart, schedule schedule_prompt, fs write, and beads create at the capability gate; a spawn requesting an explicit capability its parent tier grants still works; a spawn requesting a capability the parent lacks is denied; lint green.
notes:
2026-07-19 implementation checkpoint: pushed branch fix/iy3y-subagent-capability-gate at b4ee8cf1549b63f66ccd97a564c3504a5816071e. Focused capability/composition tests 52/52, npm run lint, npm run build, and git diff --check passed. Default general children receive parent-bounded read posture; explicit capability requests are intersected with one parent grant snapshot; over-parent requests reject before registration. No concrete implementation defect was confirmed before the operator stopped redundant same-model review lanes. Review budget is spent: do not run another review. Only apply a fix if a concrete acceptance failure is found during PR/CI; otherwise proceed to PR.

title: P1: Fence Redis session tails during purge
description: Summary: src/persistence/sessions/testing-session-purge.ts:127-208 removes JSONL journals, the channel index, and Postgres transcript rows but never invalidates the optional Redis session-tail projection. RedisSessionTailCache keeps each channel tail for seven days under a companion-scoped channel plus epoch key. After a purge, recreating the same session starts its journal at entry id 1 (SessionStore ensureChannelForWrite at store.ts:605-631). Before the queued new tail write lands, fetchSessionTailWindow can accept the surviving old tail because its maximum id satisfies expectedMinEntryId, and mergeAuthenticatedJournalWithSessionTail accepts old cache rows newer than the new journal maximum. Failure mode: purged transcript content can be resurrected into the first reused turn, violating deletion and privacy expectations. Why: this is an IMPORTANT data-resurrection defect found during PR #115 review at f360044e4. Scope: make purge aware of the configured companion-scoped tail port and fail closed if the current epoch cannot be bumped or invalidated before irreversible deletion; preserve rollback safety when the Redis fence succeeds but later filesystem or Postgres work fails; close the cache cleanly; add deterministic same-id reuse coverage and Redis-enabled composition coverage. Non-goals: no Redis key scans, no cross-companion deletion, and no weakening of journal authority or cache degradation rules.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Purging a session with sessionTailCache enabled advances or invalidates the exact companion-scoped channel epoch before journals become irreversibly unavailable. 2. Redis failure aborts the purge with journals and index intact and no Postgres deletion. 3. After successful purge, recreating the same session id cannot expose any pre-purge tail row during the first or later turn. 4. A different companion scope and a different channel remain untouched. 5. Regression tests cover the queued-write race, same-id reset to entry 1, and rollback after a successful fence. 6. Focused tests, npm run lint, npm run build, npm run verify:repository-hygiene, and git diff --check pass.
close_reason: Fixed in a6d0f6a4a on wave branch (PR #115): purge fences psfn:session-tail:<scope>:<channelKey>:e<digits> family with exact digit-suffix matching (redis-session-tail-cache.ts:210), rollback of journals+index on partial DEL failure before projection commit, configured-but-unreachable Redis fails closed (tested). Opus+Pi: no blockers; sibling/prefix collision inputs proven excluded.

title: P1: Scope session purge to companion roots and Postgres tenant
description: Summary: The new session purge CLI in src/app/maintenance/purge-testing-session.ts:86-92 bootstraps the runtime but resolves its default sessions directory from runtime.dataDir and creates Postgres session adapters without the configured tenant schema or role. In production load-config.ts:343 and :449 define dataDir as SYSTEM_DATA_DIR, while authoritative journals live under resolveConfiguredCompanionDataDir(config) via composition.ts:214-217. Canonical Postgres session composition at composition.ts:226-234 also passes config.postgresSchema and derivePostgresTenantRole(postgresSchema) for multi-companion agents. Failure mode: the documented default command cannot find a real split-root session; if an operator supplies --sessions-dir, it can remove companion journals and index while deleting or creating projection rows in public instead of the companion tenant schema, leaving searchable stale rows or touching a same-named public channel. Why: this is an IMPORTANT persistence-isolation and deletion-correctness defect found during PR #115 review at f360044e4. Scope: reuse or extract the canonical companion session composition for maintenance; resolve the default from companionDataDir; require persistenceBackend=postgres; preserve explicit safe overrides; pass and validate postgresSchema plus derived tenant role; add split-root and multi-schema coverage. Non-goals: no changes to session naming, no cross-companion bulk purge, no fallback to system data or public schema.
acceptance_criteria: 1. With distinct systemDataDir and companionDataDir, the CLI defaults to companionDataDir/state/sessions and never probes systemDataDir/state/sessions as authority. 2. In multiCompanion mode it fails closed without postgresSchema and uses the derived tenant role plus exact configured schema. 3. A two-schema integration test proves only the intended companion schema rows are deleted and public plus a sibling schema are unchanged; the command must not create public projection tables. 4. Projection failure restores journals and index. 5. Focused tests, npm run lint, npm run build, npm run verify:repository-hygiene, and git diff --check pass.
close_reason: Fixed in a6d0f6a4a on wave branch (PR #115): purge target resolution via canonical resolveSessionsDir + fleet-manifest --companion-id (new testing-session-purge-target.ts), companion schema pinned at connection startup (postgres.ts:108 libpq options, allowlist-validated), refusal precedes deletion, public-isolation integration fixture green against Docker Postgres. Opus+Pi blind reviews: no blockers.

title: memory_patch updates the stored record but retrieval never finds the patched text: embedding/lexical projection not refreshed on patch
description: FOUND BY: Artie (ARTEMIS) in Layer B guided walk, shakedown round S10-kube-2026-07-19, build da5c5c3c1 (k3d, single-companion, UUID identity). REPRO (her session api:session-mrsg1o1y-2993eb0e, persisted): create semantic memory 'shakedown probe s10r2 — cobalt thunderstamp 7749' → memory_patch edits text (append [PATCHED]) → fresh search for patched text returns NOTHING; delete then restore shows the PATCHED text, proving the underlying record updated. DB EVIDENCE (public.l2_memories): row 019f7ccb-61e8-742f-84c1-d7c84887cc20 text='shakedown probe s10r2 — cobalt thunderstamp 7749 [PATCHED]', embedding IS NOT NULL — record + vector present, retrieval still misses. HYPOTHESIS: patch path updates text without re-embedding (vector still encodes pre-patch text) and/or lexical projection not refreshed on patch; verify both semantic and lexical lanes in src/faculties/memory/retrieval.ts + the patch handler. This also plausibly explains the Layer A matrix memory_patch_delete_restore narration_without_execution/semantic failures. SCOPE: make patch re-embed + refresh lexical projection atomically with the text update (fail closed if embedding provider unavailable — no silent stale vector); add regression coverage. FUTURE HARNESS CASE: extend memory_patch_delete_restore to assert patched-text searchability in both lanes immediately after patch.
close_reason: Implemented and integrated: feat/ahxy-s10-shakedown-fixes @ f4ccde738 (origin-equal; bead branch work/ahxy-uf2h @ ea80fb87c). Root cause dual-lane: postgres-store updateMemory accepted text mutations reusing the stored embedding (stale vector), and the authorized lexical path used substring matching with no durable projection. Fix: store rejects text updates lacking a replacement embedding (fail closed — writer.patchMemory re-embeds BEFORE opening the transaction, provider failure leaves no text/audit/cache mutation); lexical search now queries a generated search_vector tsvector (migration adds STORED column + GIN index, backfills existing rows). Evidence: real-Postgres integration suite 26/26 (patched text retrievable via new embedding, old embedding misses, tsvector lexical hits, delete/restore preserves projections); focused suites 100/100; lint clean; UBS change-range clean. Dual blind adversarial review (Opus + Pi GLM@high) both PASS, zero blockers; both independently verified atomicity, all 14 updateMemory callers safe under the new invariant, and migration idempotence/backfill. One integration test initially failed on an invalid fixture sensitivity ('low' not in SensitivityLevel) — fixture corrected, no product change. Follow-ups filed: psfn-framework-970c (P2, dead Garden admin patch route, discovered-from uf2h). Nonblocking observations (handoff): in-memory test double lacks the new invariant; pre-existing lexical divergence on non-authorized searchByText; STORED-column migration implies one-time l2_memories table rewrite lock at rollout; raw-SQL text update in memory-participant-name-repair.ts:378 still bypasses re-embed (pre-existing class).

title: Enable sandboxed Bash and explicit large-document handoff
description:
Summary: Purrsephone's canonical model-facing shell tool is registered but every shell.exec call fails closed because src/boundary/sandbox/execution/shell-runner.ts has no OS-enforced filesystem confinement. This blocks the operator-requested CLI route for large document work. Separately, fs action=read hard-caps output at 20,000 bytes but its canonical guidance and truncated result do not clearly tell the companion to use analysis_workbench or a bounded subagent, which led to repeated invalid max_bytes calls and a lossy summary-only handoff.

Scope: implement an OS-enforced Linux namespace sandbox for shell.exec using an exact-pinned runtime dependency, preserving direct argv execution, executable allowlists, cwd bounds, curated empty environment, no network, time/output caps, and audit/approval. Enable the policy through repo-owned Helm wiring for the Purrsephone deployment path with Bash as the operator-authorized CLI. Keep fs bounded at 20,000 bytes and add explicit canonical/tool-result guidance that large documents belong in analysis_workbench or a bounded subagent, with provenance-bearing excerpts/results brought back before the worker is discarded. Add focused regressions for filesystem/network/env isolation, allowlists, bounds, and the fs handoff. Do not widen fs limits, bypass the gateway, expose peer/system/secret roots, or create an off-repo supervisor/config workaround.

Why: the operator explicitly prefers a governed CLI for flexible document inspection, while keeping the routine fs surface bounded. The current shell surface advertises execution but cannot execute anything, and the current fs failure mode encourages retries that can never validate.
design: Use Bubblewrap as the OS-mediated execution boundary because the live Linux/k3s kernel permits user and mount namespaces. Invoke bwrap directly without a host shell; unshare user/PID/IPC/UTS/cgroup/network, bind system executable/library roots read-only, bind the canonical Personal Workspace at /workspace, mount fresh proc/dev/tmp, clear the environment, apply process/address-space/file-size/CPU/open-file limits, and execute only a settings-owned allowlisted entry command. Validate executable and cwd policy before spawn and preserve fail-closed errors when bwrap or namespace setup fails. Own mutable policy in canonical settings.json with Garden advanced-settings exposure; keep it disabled by default, then enable bash/rg for Purrsephone through the authenticated Garden settings API. Keep fs at its 20 KB limit and explicitly route larger document analysis to analysis_workbench or a bounded subagent with path plus line/byte provenance.
acceptance_criteria: 1. shell action=exec can run allowlisted bash/rg commands inside an OS-enforced sandbox on Linux. 2. The Personal Workspace is the only writable persistent root; paths outside the approved read-only runtime roots and Personal Workspace are inaccessible, process secrets are absent, and network is unavailable. 3. Command allowlist, cwd containment, timeout, output cap, capability gate, confirmation/audit, and fail-closed behavior remain covered by tests. 4. Helm exposes explicit disabled-by-default shell policy values and can enable the bounded Purrsephone Bash/rg profile without private deployment data in tracked files. 5. fs remains capped at 20,000 bytes; its schema/canonical description and truncated read result explicitly direct large-document analysis to analysis_workbench or a bounded subagent and require provenance-bearing excerpts/results rather than summary-only reliance. 6. Focused tests, npm run verify:helm-chart, npm run build, and mandatory npm run lint pass. 7. The committed image is deployed to Purrsephone and a live probe proves bounded Bash document inspection plus outside-workspace/network denial.
notes: 2026-07-20 orchestration: PR #177 open (feat/jdwd-sandbox-shell, head 0e58292d1) — ready-for-review, awaits operator merge. Implemented per operator scope: direct shell tool + workbench shell_exec via one gateway bubblewrap path; shellExec.mountRepositoryReadOnly ro-binds PSFN_REPOSITORY_DIR at /repo (fails closed on system-data/companion-data/workspace overlap + helm validation); pinned analysis toolset (jq/file/zip/sqlite3/poppler/pandoc/python3/uv multi-arch) in Dockerfile.agent with runtime verifier probes; circuit breaker no longer counts non-zero exits as failures. Review gate: UBS clean; blind Opus + Pi xhigh — no P0/P1; two P2s remediated (0e58292d1) and re-verified FIXED. Gates: lint/build/settings-contract/hardcoded-settings/helm-chart/repo-hygiene PASS, ~2100 focused tests green, docker image built + verify:shell-sandbox-image PASS. Remaining: operator merge, live deploy + shellExec enable, AC7 live probe. NOTE: foundation commits also on feat/yijy-shared-garden-control-plane (cherry-picked) — reconcile whichever lands second.
close_reason: PR #177 merged to main — sandboxed shell (direct tool + workbench shell_exec via one bubblewrap path), repo ro-mount with data-root overlap guards, pinned analysis toolset + python/uv, circuit-breaker exit-code fix. Full dual-blind review gate passed. Live enable/probe (AC7) is operator-side.

title: Subagent tool injection leaves non-memory core-authoritative mutation surfaces ungoverned: orient, identity, north_star, journal, wiki, skill
description:
Evidence (dual blind review of psfn-framework-c7d, 2026-07-19, both reviewers independently or by omission consistent): BLOCKED_SUBAGENT_TOOL_NAMES (src/faculties/subagents/faculty.ts:~80-102) blocks the split memory_* tools, delete class, and spawn surfaces, and c7d's governance wraps only tool.name === 'memory' (faculty.ts:~1236). Every other parent-catalog tool passes into subagent loops verbatim (catalog seam: src/app/startup/composition/composition.ts:603 toolCatalogProvider → parent agentLoop.getToolCatalog). Reproducible from a DEFAULT-tier subagent (no memory.write capability, no elevation): (a) orient action=introspection_consent_set enabled=false → IntrospectionConsentStore.append mutates the single global consent policy (src/faculties/introspection/consent-store.ts:~200); (b) orient action=values_update → executeValuesUpdateAction rewrites the global ValuesJournalStore feeding the system prompt values layer; (c) orient action=create_concern → writes companion continuity concerns the scheduler acts on; (d) identity (prompt-tools.ts:~531) mutates global PromptLayerStore; north_star mutates NorthStarStore; (e) journal/wiki/skill/scratchpad mutate their stores ungoverned. The subagent's SubstrateAgent has no intakeSinkGate, so persona_mutation candidacy screens an empty envelope set and does not deny. This is PRE-EXISTING (predates c7d; c7d closed the canonical L2 memory seam only) but violates the same charter principle c7d/Law 37 protect: core remains authoritative for identity, values, consent, and trust truth.

Context: found during c7d review; c7d shipped with the memory seam closed and is not blocked by this. Charter 6.11 (as amended) + 6.13 give the governance vocabulary; the fix should extend the same bounded-ness vs write-trust split to non-memory core state.

Scope: decide per tool: hard-block from subagent contexts (add to BLOCKED_SUBAGENT_TOOL_NAMES) vs govern (stage mutations through fold-review like c7d's restricted memory writes) vs allow (genuinely task-scoped, e.g. scratchpad may stay). Must inventory legitimate lanes first — introspection/sleeptime subagents may legitimately need orient reads or consent-aware flows; do not break production lanes with a blanket block (that inventory is the first task). Wire an intakeSinkGate (or equivalent) decision for persona_mutation in subagent contexts instead of the current empty-envelope pass. Non-goals: no parallel governance framework — reuse c7d's memory-governance/fold-review pattern; no changes to the parent companion's own use of these tools.

Acceptance criteria: a default-tier subagent cannot mutate introspection consent, values journal, prompt layers, north star, or continuity concerns (test per tool proving deny/stage); legitimate lanes enumerated with their disposition documented in the bead on close; targeted vitest for the subagent tool-injection filter; npm run lint green.
close_reason: Shipped stacked on c7d (PR base feat/c7d-subagent-memory-governance): identity/north_star/canonical-contact hard-blocked; orient/journal/wiki/skill/vault governed via tool-governance.ts policy maps (reads pass, mutations denied fail-closed, omitted/unknown actions denied, audit subagent.tool.mutation.denied fails closed). Lane inventory proved introspection/sleeptime run as direct LLM calls (no tool loop) — deny correct everywhere, no elevation lanes needed. Dual blind review (Opus+Pi): zero blockers in scope; both verified action-space exhaustiveness, wrapper integrity, single injection seam. Residual pre-existing class filed: iy3y (P1 capability-gate parent-tier inheritance root cause), klx1 (P2 per-tool dispositions incl. NO_CAPABILITY_REQUIREMENT selfie/image, schedule self-injection, notify egress, fs bypass of file-backed journal/vault), gjkh (P2 shard parity). lint+build+96 files/1067 tests green. Commit 3fd87b72b.

title: P1: Exclude testing sessions from autonomous durable memory lanes
description: Summary: The 9c4k implementation guards temporal wake/refresher, near-turn maintenance, and episodic synthesis, but testing-marked sessions still enter production autonomous artifact writers. The concrete blocking path is src/faculties/memory/sleeptime-agent.ts:502-607: inference enumerates every recent non-internal session and execution rechecks only retirement, then runs sleep consolidation, arc formation, dream meaning, wiki updates, core-memory rewriting, and durable memory writes. The extraction orchestrator, emotion persistence, and contact-profile persistence also lack the testing-session gate, so artifacts survive the documented journal/index/transcript purge. Failure mode: an exercised test session still spends LLM calls and pollutes durable companion memory, identity/orientation, emotion, contacts, arcs, and wiki state, which directly contradicts 9c4k scope to exclude testing sessions from autonomous fan-outs and sensible artifact generation. Why: this is an IMPORTANT broken acceptance path and companion-memory integrity defect verified during PR #115 review at f360044e4. Scope: add fail-closed isTestingSessionId checks at both inference and execution boundaries for sleeptime and at the earliest safe entry plus pre-write defense for each covered durable lane; preserve ordinary production and experiential internal sessions; add explicit no-call/no-write tests. Where an artifact writer cannot be safely gated by session id, extend purge to remove only records with exact testing-session provenance. Non-goals: no broad memory deletion, no change to non-testing cadence, no API session-routing redesign, and no silent best-effort cleanup.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A testing-marked session never queues or executes sleeptime consolidation, arcs, dream meaning, wiki updates, orientation rewrites, or memory writes, including replay of a previously queued action. 2. Extraction, emotion, and contact-profile durable writes attributable to a testing session are rejected at deterministic lane boundaries or removed by exact provenance-scoped purge. 3. Ordinary sessions and approved experiential internal sessions remain behaviorally unchanged. 4. Tests exercise inference, execution/replay defense, and zero durable rows or artifacts after create, exercise, and purge. 5. No LLM provider call occurs for excluded testing sessions. 6. Focused tests, npm run lint, npm run build, npm run verify:repository-hygiene, and git diff --check pass.

Confirmed defect fixed: unified memory tool + split memory_write/patch source-context builders now stamp getRequestContext().sessionId into provenance, so MemoryWriter's testing fence fires on api:*:testing:* writes and the exact-scope purge (provenance_json->>'sessionId') can select the row. title: Repair Garden chat upstream routing on the live split deployment
description: Discovered during the 2026-07-19 Purrsephone recovery on the live split k3s deployment. A clean authenticated Garden session renders /memory and /journal correctly, but submitting the built-in /chat form requests /v1/chat/completions on the Garden surface and receives HTTP 404. The failed probe created no companion turn or persistence write. Direct authenticated gateway /v1/chat/completions requests succeed, proving the companion and gateway chat path are healthy and isolating the defect to Garden chat URL/upstream/auth routing. Inspect src/operator/garden/chat/, Garden server routing/proxy composition, and Helm service/base-URL wiring. Scope: make the built-in Garden chat use the supported gateway route in split mode and preserve its authentication boundary. Non-goals: changing model routing, redeploying an unrelated image, or weakening Garden/gateway authentication.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A clean authenticated Garden browser session can submit one /chat message and receives a nonempty assistant response. 2. The browser request reaches the supported gateway chat endpoint rather than a 404 Garden-local path. 3. The resulting turn appears exactly once in canonical turn/session records. 4. Wrong-path and unauthenticated requests remain rejected. 5. Focused Garden chat routing tests and one split-runtime browser E2E regression cover the live topology. 6. npm run lint and relevant build/tests pass.
notes:
LIVE VERIFICATION 2026-07-22 (psfn-shard, merged main 9dfb11b46 / image 0.1.0-kube-9dfb11b4 / helm rev 65, all app pods 1/1). NOT FIXED — bead stays OPEN.

Code: no fix exists on any ref. `git log --all --grep=71y1` => 0 commits; `git log --all --grep='chat upstream'|'chat proxy'` => 0. The defect path is unchanged in the deployed tree: src/operator/garden/chat/api-base-url.ts:95-97 returns RELATIVE_BASE_URL whenever no apiPort is configured, and :117-121 then returns the bare path, so src/operator/garden/chat/bootstrap.ts:33 CHAT_COMPLETIONS_PATH='/v1/chat/completions' is handed to the browser as a Garden-origin path. src/operator/garden/server-request-routing.ts:41-48 admits only /api, /health, /login, /_app — there is no /v1 route on the Garden surface, hence the 404.

Live confirmation of the missing input: the psfn-garden deployment env sets GATEWAY_OPERATOR_API_BASE_URL=http://psfn-gateway:10053/v1 but never sets API_BASE_URL (the only var api-base-url.ts reads). Chart likewise only defines GATEWAY_OPERATOR_API_BASE_URL (deploy/helm/psfn/templates/workloads.yaml:547) and PSFN_API_BASE_URL (:793).

Mitigating nuance, NOT a fix: the live deployment now runs fleet mode (ADMIN_TRANSPORT_MODE=network, Garden admin 10054 mTLS-only, browser reaches Garden through the gateway unified-origin fleet SSO router). On that path admin-ui/src/routes/chat/+page.svelte:165-176 normalizes to /v1/chat/completions and apiFetch prepends /companions/<uuid>/garden, producing /companions/<uuid>/garden/v1/chat/completions, which src/boundary/gateway/fleet-sso-router.ts:89,437,510,578-591 does handle. So Garden chat may work today by a different mechanism while the split-mode relative-URL defect is untouched. Not verified live: submitting a chat message would write a companion turn, and this pass was read-only. Gateway logs since the 05:16 UTC restart contain zero fleet-sso/garden/chat/completions entries — no live traffic evidence either way.

Acceptance status: (1)(2)(3) unverified live; (4) unchanged; (5) UNMET — no focused Garden chat routing test and no split-runtime browser E2E exists. src/operator/garden/chat/api-base-url.test.ts:19 ('returns relative base URL when no port is provided') currently asserts the buggy behavior as correct, so a fix must change that test. src/app/e2e/chat-cockpit-smoke.test.ts:26,51,88-93 is same-origin by construction (one createServer answers both /api/admin/chat/bootstrap and /v1/chat/completions) and is structurally blind to this defect.

NEXT STEP: either (a) make the Garden bootstrap resolve an absolute gateway chat URL from GATEWAY_OPERATOR_API_BASE_URL in split mode, or (b) decide fleet unified-origin is the only supported topology and make split-mode Garden chat fail loudly instead of emitting an unroutable relative path. Either way, add the routing test and a split-runtime E2E that runs Garden and gateway on distinct origins.

title: Restore model usage telemetry across rollback schema skew
description: Live Purrsephone k3s incident discovered while recovering memory/reflection persistence. Helm revisions 56/58 ran image 0.1.0-kube-5d1785dc and migrated public.model_usage_events to canonical accounting/attribution schema: legacy attribution columns became NOT NULL with the canonical 'unknown' sentinel, and event_fingerprint became required. Revisions 57/59 rolled the app back to 0.1.0-kube-576e33cd. That writer explicitly inserts SQL NULL for absent origin/turn/tool/charge/slot attribution columns and omits event_fingerprint, so Postgres rejects the row before defaults can apply. Live gateway logs continuously report failed model usage persistence for turn_id/tool_name; model_usage_events has 5,429 rows and max recorded_at_ms 1784123728175, showing telemetry stopped July 15 while turns continued.\n\nScope: preserve the forward schema constraints while admitting the known legacy writer shape through a narrowly named compatibility bridge; use canonical 'unknown' for blank/null attribution and a deterministic legacy fingerprint derived from event id; verify both embedding and chat usage writes; add migration/rollback certification so a forward schema followed by an older app writer remains insert-compatible. Back up live Postgres before mutation. Non-goals: relaxing accounting constraints globally, rewriting historical usage rows, redeploying the twice-rolled-back image, or changing model routing/pricing.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Verified live backup predates mutation. 2. The deployed 576e33cd writer can persist embedding and chat model_usage_events without NOT NULL/fingerprint errors. 3. Canonical NOT NULL, token-accounting, currency, accounting-version, and attribution-version constraints remain enabled. 4. Compatibility rows use 'unknown' only where the old writer supplied null/blank and use a deterministic legacy fingerprint. 5. Existing 5,429 rows are not rewritten or deleted. 6. A bounded post-repair log scan has zero new model_usage_events NOT NULL failures. 7. Repository migration and rollback-certification tests cover the old insert shape against the new schema. 8. npm run lint and targeted tests pass for code changes.
notes:
Recovery evidence (2026-07-19): the same verified pre-mutation backup covers public.model_usage_events. A narrowly bounded BEFORE INSERT bridge now activates only when event_fingerprint is missing/blank, normalizes only the rollback writer null/blank attribution fields, and derives legacy:rollback-writer:<event-id>. A rolled-back live guard probe proved malformed modern rows with a nonblank fingerprint still fail NOT NULL and leak zero rows. A real authenticated post-guard turn persisted both embedding and chat events through the legacy bridge. Rows rose from 5,429 to 5,440 with zero missing fingerprints and zero invalid accounting/attribution versions; bounded agent/gateway scans contain zero new usage persistence failures. Commit a260591cf implements the focused bridge at src/persistence/postgres/model-usage-rollback-migrations.ts:7 and exact embedding/chat plus modern fail-closed certification at src/persistence/postgres/model-usage-migration-certification.integration.test.ts:212. Validation: npm run lint passed; npm run build passed; targeted migration unit and real-Postgres certification suites passed.
2026-07-20 mainline reconciliation: clean forward-port PR #125 merged to main as b5e12c64be0a0a7c2ae640da84eafbc76537c77e. This is the production landing evidence for orphaned commit a260591cf; the contaminated yijy squash was not used. Revalidation on current main base: focused rollback bridge suite 75/75, lint, build, repository hygiene, UBS production scan, and diff-check passed.
close_reason: Restored rollback-era chat/embedding telemetry while retaining canonical constraints; live rows 5,429 to 5,440 with zero invalid fingerprints/versions, modern malformed writes still rejected, lint/build and targeted tests passed, commit a260591cf.

title: Garden SPA login loops back to the token gate in real browsers: client-side redirect to /login aborts the post-auth dashboard fetches despite healthy cookie auth
description:
EVIDENCE (shakedown round S10-kube-2026-07-19, k3d psfn-test, build 0.1.0-kube-da5c5c3c = origin/main da5c5c3c1):
1. POST /login with valid ADMIN_TOKEN → 302 + Set-Cookie psfn_token (HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict). curl GET /api/admin/dashboard with that cookie → 200. GET / with cookie + Accept: text/html → 200 SPA. Server-side cookie auth is fully healthy.
2. Real browser (Playwright chromium 148): load /, SPA client token gate renders; fill Admin Token + Sign in → form POST succeeds, redirect to /, SPA starts /api/admin/dashboard + /api/admin/settings fetches which are ABORTED by an immediate client-side navigation to /login; final state is the login form again. Login is impossible through the UI.
3. shakedown/harness/operator-ui-sweep.mjs: auth.ok=false 'Operator UI remained on the admin-token gate after attempted login', all 15 pages red on this build (artifacts in round dir).
4. Previously deployed build 0.1.0-kube-29981432 predates the aylm merge + mus2 fleet-Garden admission changes; suspect client auth-state check in admin-ui (candidates: mus2.10 companion switcher/fleet view, mus2.2 admission targets, aylm.9/upx0.9 cleanup) redirects when its auth probe fails despite valid HttpOnly cookie.
SCOPE: fix the SPA client auth check so a valid psfn_token cookie session survives; do not weaken server auth. Add the login round-trip to the Garden behavioral sweep expectations (it already catches this).
ACCEPTANCE: operator-ui-sweep auth.ok=true and 15/15 pages green against a build ≥ da5c5c3c1 on the k3d shakedown deployment; manual browser login lands on the dashboard.
close_reason: Implemented and integrated: feat/ahxy-s10-shakedown-fixes @ 6593bc941 (origin-equal). Root cause: admin-ui/src/lib/stores/auth.svelte.ts aborted its own session probe on companion-scope activation and resolved auth to false in catch/finally, bouncing valid HttpOnly cookie sessions to /login. Fix: auth resolves only on probe success or definitive 401/403; same-scope probes survive scope activation; aborts/5xx/network errors leave auth unresolved. Regression suite admin-ui/src/lib/stores/auth-session.test.ts 6/6 (verified to fail 3/6 against pre-fix code); full admin-ui suite 191/191; npm run lint clean; UBS scan exit 0 (flagged comparisons are window/AbortError string checks, false positives). Dual blind adversarial review (Opus + Pi GLM@high) both PASS, zero blockers; both traced init/probe/guard state machine and confirmed no unauth-as-authed path and no weakening of server auth. Live k3d operator-ui-sweep acceptance moves to the wave validation bead per process (implementation closure does not depend on live checks).

title: Generic wiki write action can forge runtime_derived artifact lineage, bypassing the legacy egress quarantine
description: Evidence: jp36.1.2.2 adversarial review (2026-07-19) confirmed the path reachable: PERSONAL_SCOPE_WRITE_GUARD only rejects shared-world scope, so the model can call the generic wiki write/import action (src/faculties/wiki/tools.ts buildUpsertInput, ~line 171) with model-controlled id/tags/body/source_class and create a project.<id> doc tagged psfn:personal-project whose artifact body contains "metadataLineage":"runtime_derived". parsePersonalProjectDocument -> parseMetadataLineage (src/faculties/wiki/personal-project-contracts.ts:113) returns it verbatim, so requestArtifactShare (src/faculties/wiki/personal-projects.ts:254-260) treats the forged artifact as egress-eligible and will broaden it to public. Context: fail-open for partner-data privacy; defeats the jp36.1.2.1 runtime-metadata-authority fix and the jp36.1.2.2 quarantine (both landed on feat/jp36-social-autonomy@<see branch>). This is the recorded remaining closure item on parent jp36.1.2 — the parent must not close until this is fixed. Scope: close the forge path at the write seam — the generic write/import action must not be able to create or mutate personal-project docs' runtime-owned fields (metadataLineage, sensitivity, shareState, intendedAudience) or must route project.<id>/psfn:personal-project docs through the runtime-authoritative project path. Non-goals: do not change project_add_artifact or project_share semantics (landed), do not rebuild the quarantine CLI. Discovered-from: jp36.1.2.2 review. Branch context: feat/jp36-social-autonomy.
acceptance_criteria: Regression test proving a generic wiki write/import of a project.<id> doc with metadataLineage:runtime_derived (and/or model-set sensitivity/shareState/intendedAudience on artifacts) is rejected fail-closed or persisted with lineage forced to legacy_unverified; requestArtifactShare cannot broaden such a doc beyond self; existing wiki write tests still green; npm run lint clean.
close_reason: Generic wiki write/import rejects reserved-namespace docs (project./wardrobe.look. prefixes + reserved tags) fail-closed via isReservedManagedWikiWrite using the store's own normalizeWikiDocumentId — creation AND mutation blocked; legitimate runtime paths untouched. work/jp36-1-2-3@c83a3f5c, review PASS (0 blockers; all six bypass vectors attempted and blocked). Integrated feat/jp36-social-autonomy@570e3622. Validation: 157 wiki tests, lint clean.

title: Repair live multi-companion fleet backup path and Postgres dump failures
description: Helm mount-layer fix landed after the original observation (95fc7b080 companion PVCs RO into gateway; f7a98dfd5/cde0462df/18a9e7349 always-fleet), and the pg_dump SIGSEGV was fixed by q9ra.2 (3995ac766, KRB5CCNAME). Remaining: (1) add a real-layout regression test proving the backup leader resolves and dumps every declared companion + the cluster unit against the actual chart-mounted always-fleet paths (fleet-scheduler.test.ts:159 currently uses synthetic fixtures); (2) run one live/operator-triggered fleet backup cycle on the current always-fleet deployment and confirm no FleetBackupPartialFailureError plus a passing restore verification.
acceptance_criteria: A live-equivalent six-unit multi-companion fixture completes one scheduled fleet cycle with every declared companion and the cluster unit successful; no companion tree is resolved outside its governed mounted root; every configured Postgres schema exports with fail-closed role/isolation checks; the generated manifests and hashes pass existing verification; a targeted restore verification succeeds; focused backup/Helm tests, npm run verify:backup-restore, npm run verify:helm-chart, npm run build, and mandatory npm run lint pass; sanitized live validation shows the next scheduled or operator-triggered cycle completes without FleetBackupPartialFailureError.
notes:
LIVE VERIFICATION 2026-07-22 (psfn-shard, merged main 9dfb11b46 / image 0.1.0-kube-9dfb11b4 / helm rev 65, fleet.enabled=true, 1 companion). BOTH REMAINING ITEMS UNMET — bead stays OPEN. A new blocking defect was found; see below.

Item (1) real-layout regression test: NOT DONE. `git log --all --grep=45bp` => 0 commits. No commit since 2026-07-19 under src/persistence/backups/ added such a test (5c1ce2663, a14d739a8, 0f8d0459c, 543e32cf3, c2896696a, ca4392975 are all other work). Coverage is still synthetic: src/persistence/backups/fleet-scheduler.test.ts:58,65,115,130-132,154,166-169,243-249 and fleet-auth-scheduler-options.test.ts:33,45,63,166 use '/runtime/companion-data/<id>', a path shape the chart never produces. The chart renders '<runtimeRoot>/companions/<uuid>' and '<runtimeRoot>/workspaces/personal/<uuid>' (deploy/helm/psfn/templates/fleet-agents.yaml:5-6); the live agent mounts companion-data at /app/companions/1c92c9c7-... with PSFN_RUNTIME_ROOT=/app. `grep -r '/app/companions' src/` => 0 hits. No backup test exercises the chart layout.

Item (2) one live fleet cycle without FleetBackupPartialFailureError: NOT DONE, and it CANNOT currently succeed on this deployment.

Live state of /runtime/backups (runtime PVC psfn-runtime, host /mnt/psfn-nvme/k3s-storage/pvc-7fc4ed36-..._psfn_psfn-runtime/backups): 11 dirs, 20260712T130321808Z through 20260721T200312670Z on a clean 6-hourly cadence. Every one contains exactly encrypted-backup.json + snapshot.tar.gz.enc (~390MB) — these are the AGENT's single-companion snapshots (the agent has PSFN_KUBERNETES_BACKUP_ENABLED=true and mounts runtime subPath 'backups' at /runtime/backups). `find /runtime/backups -maxdepth 2 -name '*manifest*'` => ZERO. No fleet-auth-backup-manifest.json and no fleet-backup-manifest.json has ever been produced on this deployment, consistent with the 2026-07-21 comment.

=== NEW BLOCKING DEFECT: the gateway-owned fleet backup lane has no writable backup root ===

The gateway logs at every start:
  01:17:03 INFO [Gateway] Gateway-owned fleet auth consistent backups enabled {"companionCount":1,"mode":"consistent-family","intervalMs":21600000,"backupRootDir":"/runtime/backups","verifyRestore":true,"encryption":"required","mirrorDir":"(none)"}
(src/app/gateway/main.ts:344, scheduler registered at :330 -> registerScheduledFleetAuthBackupTask, src/persistence/backups/service.ts:572 -> fleet-auth-cycle.ts:258.)

But the gateway container has NO /runtime/backups mount. deploy/helm/psfn/templates/workloads.yaml:428-429 ('- name: runtime / mountPath: {{ .Values.runtime.backupsDir }} / subPath: backups') appears ONLY inside the agent Deployment (starts :268). The gateway Deployment (:32-252) mounts the runtime PVC at logsDir and tempDir only. Verified live:
  kubectl -n psfn exec deploy/psfn-gateway -c gateway -- ls -la /runtime
  => only 'logs' and 'tmp'; /runtime is root:root 0755, and /runtime/backups does not exist.
  kubectl -n psfn exec deploy/psfn-gateway -c gateway -- sh -c 'id; mkdir -p /runtime/backups'
  => uid=999(psfn) gid=999(psfn); mkdir: cannot create directory '/runtime/backups': Permission denied
(gateway pod securityContext runAsUser/runAsGroup 999, runAsNonRoot true.)

The cycle mkdirs its root lazily at src/persistence/backups/fleet-auth-cycle.ts:112-116 (mkdirSync(options.backupRootDir, {recursive:true})), so every fleet-auth consistent-family cycle that fires will die on EACCES before writing anything. Nothing validates backupRootDir at startup — src/persistence/backups/config.ts:67-72 only resolves the string — so startup reports the lane 'enabled' while it is structurally incapable of producing an artifact.

Compounding: the scheduler is a pure in-memory interval with no persisted watermark. src/core/scheduler/scheduler.ts:292-296 seeds lastRun to process start, fleet-auth-cycle.ts:323 passes skipFirstRun: true by default, and the due check at scheduler.ts:521-524 is (now - lastRun >= intervalMs) with no catch-up. With intervalMs=21600000 (6h), any gateway pod that lives under 6h never runs a single cycle. The pod has restarted at helm revs 61-65 (2026-07-22 01:44/01:49/01:50/02:03/05:16 UTC), so no cycle has fired and no EACCES error appears in the logs either — the failure is currently invisible from both directions.

Also note the failure telemetry gap: FleetBackupPartialFailureError (service.ts:1007) reaches this lane only as a generic error — fleet-auth-cycle.ts:162-164 rewrites it to 'Fleet auth recovery packaging produced an incomplete fleet family'. The per-unit partialFailure/failedUnits/totalUnits/fleetManifestPath logging exists only in src/persistence/backups/fleet-scheduler.ts:425-436, which the gateway does not use. So even a real partial failure would log without naming the failed companion.

NEXT STEPS (in order): (a) add the runtime 'backups' subPath mount to the gateway Deployment in workloads.yaml, or move the fleet-auth lane to a workload that has it; (b) fail closed at gateway startup if backupRootDir is absent or unwritable instead of logging 'enabled'; (c) give the lane a persisted watermark (or wall-clock cadence) so restart churn cannot starve the 6h cycle; (d) route FleetBackupPartialFailureError through the per-unit logging path; (e) then run one operator-triggered cycle plus verify-backup-restore and add the chart-layout regression test.

Separately verified HEALTHY and out of scope for this bead: the host-side NAS lane. /usr/local/bin/psfn-backup.sh dumps the LIVE in-cluster DB (kubectl exec psfn-postgres-0 -- pg_dump -Fc), enforces the mandatory 'pg_restore --list || exit 1' gate, and refuses to run if the NAS is not a mountpoint. /etc/psfn-backup.env is 0600 root:root with all five keys. psfn-backup.timer active (next 2026-07-22 06:01:48 UTC); last service run exited 0/SUCCESS at 00:01:27 UTC. No frozen-DB trap: dumps grow monotonically across cycles (14126287 -> 14528892 -> 14794576 -> 14840854 -> 14849566 -> 14863994 -> 14872244 bytes, 07-19 22:43 through 07-22 01:32), and pg_restore --list on the newest reports 'Archive created at 2026-07-22 01:32:34 UTC, dbname: psfn, TOC Entries: 433' with 53 TABLE DATA entries against a live DB holding 16020 session_messages_projection rows.

title: Replace presence auto-follow with shared-satellite response arbitration
description:
Implement the target shared-device policy in docs/productivity-pack.md section 11.5. Current src/core/agent/perception/presence-follow.ts moves a companion emanation when fresh trusted partner presence is observed at another bound physical place, while src/shared/contracts/satellite-registry.ts models at most one companionId per satellite. That behavior conflicts with the accepted companion-rest boundary: entering a room is an observation, not a summons.

Replace the existing unconditional presence-follow path rather than adding a parallel arbitration path. Extend the governed shared-satellite contract to distinguish: (1) one Satellite Primary, (2) exact observation recipients with per-event scopes, and (3) an allowlist of Emanation Members permitted to speak or appear through the device. A designated Productivity Companion may receive minimum normalized presence/location metadata even when it is not primary, but observation delivery must not confer speech, movement, world-control, or historical room access.

Add deterministic primary-first response arbitration. Explicit partner address or an active conversation wins; otherwise the Satellite Primary receives a bounded response lease and may speak, decline, or return a deterministic no-op. Only after release or timeout may the next policy-eligible Emanation Member acquire the lease. Exactly one companion may hold speech authority at a time. Eligibility must respect availability, fatigue, quiet hours, companion rest/personal time, active conversation, and device policy before any model call. Audit observation delivery, lease acquisition, decline/no-op, timeout, release, and speech outcome. Never fabricate a companion choice.

Inspect and extend current satellite registry, settings ownership, SensorIngestPort/presence bridge, ICP availability/fatigue contracts, and presence-follow tests. Preserve fail-closed fleet privacy, exact partner identity, provenance, and the single-Productivity-Companion invariant.

Scope: shared satellite contracts/config, presence routing, response leasing, current follow behavior, and focused tests/docs needed to ship the accepted policy. Non-goals: Partner Affect Estimation, general Productivity Pack implementation, raw sensor broadcast, companion movement from presence alone, or a second competing follow implementation.
acceptance_criteria: A satellite can declare one primary, scoped observation recipients, and explicit Emanation Members through canonical owner-file configuration; malformed or unauthorized configurations fail closed. Presence metadata can reach an authorized non-primary Productivity Companion without granting emanation or movement. Presence alone never moves, wakes, or summons a companion. Explicit address/active conversation routing and primary-first response leasing deterministically select at most one speaker; primary decline/no-op, timeout, release, fatigue, rest, and denial paths are tested and audited. The shipped unconditional presence auto-follow path is removed or narrowed into the new policy, with no parallel path. Settings/config ownership and Garden exposure are wired as required. Targeted tests, npm run verify:settings-contract, npm run verify:repository-hygiene, npm run lint, and npm run build pass; the implementation is committed and pushed.

Shared-satellite policy per productivity-pack 11.5 shipped: satellites.json models one Satellite Primary, per-event-scoped Observation Recipients, Emanation Member allowlist, and a fleet-singleton Productivity Companion; presence/location observations are normalized to minimum scalars, endpoint-scope-authorized, delivered only to exact recipients, and confer no speech/movement/world-control/history. Deterministic single-holder response lease (explicit address → active conversation → Primary → next eligible) shared by voice and HTTP entry paths — synchronous acquire, expiry re-check on complete, no two speech holders; eligibility (availability, fatigue ledger read, quiet hours, rest, device policy) evaluated BEFORE any model call; a resting companion is skipped, never woken, no fabricated declines (system no-op is unattributed). Presence auto-follow, handoffToPlace seam, and presence-light-automation deleted. All lease/observation transitions audited (ids/scopes only). Dual blind review (Opus PASS / Pi FAIL): verified P1 blocker — resolver acked-and-dropped telemetry for disabled registry / non-shared satellites / non-observation scopes instead of falling through to generic api.telemetry.ingest delivery, breaking single-companion presence perception; remediation returns null at those three sites (spoof/auth/no-recipient drops stay []), with fallthrough regressions. title: Cross-process shard workload registry seam: make the exact-once grant path reachable in the deployed split gateway/agent topology
description: Evidence: 2h6q.3 implementation + both blind reviews (2026-07-18). The grant authority, workload registry, auto-clear fence, and composite production-composition test all landed in 2h6q.3 (work/2h6q-3-grant-production-wiring 454245b240), but the deployed split topology runs ShardManager/ShardWorkloadRegistry in the agent process (agent/main.ts:624) while the sole production gateway construction (gateway/main.ts:496 createGatewayServer) passes no shardApprovalWorkloads — so ShardApprovalGrantAuthority is never constructed there and shard-originated world-control dispatches DENY fail-closed (POLICY_DENIED) instead of routing to operator exact-once approval. Safe (the auto-clear bypass is closed in every topology; no security regression) but the positive path is unreachable where it matters. OPERATOR DECISION NEEDED on the seam shape: (a) an authenticated agent-to-gateway workload-registration RPC (registry hosted gateway-side, registrations pushed on launch/release, carrying the frozen derived access + ownerVersion/grantDigest so reference-identity semantics survive process boundaries — likely needs a digest-based rather than reference-based sameWorkload comparison across the wire, a contract change to mus2.7's tuple), or (b) host the grant evaluation agent-side behind a gateway-verified surface. Scope: chosen seam + composite test through the SPLIT topology (separate gateway/agent processes) proving shard request -> operator approval -> exactly-one execution -> replay/sibling/replacement denial. Non-goals: no TTL, no mask changes. Acceptance: split-topology composite green; fail-closed behavior preserved when the seam is absent/unhealthy; lint/build/diff-check.
notes: 2026-07-18 addendum from 2h6q.3 Pi review (N2): even with the grant authority wired, a REAL shard turn cannot reach the gateway world.control dispatch — the agent-side capability gate (gate.ts:113-152 via requirements.ts world control -> world.control) denies the tool call inside the agent because the derived grant masks world.control; the 2h6q.3 composite test bypasses this with an LLM double invoking worldOps directly. The seam design must therefore also decide the agent-side affordance: a masked-but-request-scoped-delegable token (world.control per SHARD_MASK_TEMPORARY_GRANT_DISPOSITIONS) should let the TOOL INVOCATION pass the agent gate into the gateway approval path (where the exact-once grant governs execution), while still gating actual execution. Without this, the exact-once chain is vacuous end-to-end in every topology.

description: Evidence: PR #107 operator review (P1 + standards P2). title: Break the contact authority snapshot circular import on main
description:
Summary: npm run verify:dependency-cycles fails on origin/main da5530e115 with one cycle outside config/dependency-cycle-baseline.json: src/core/contacts/postgres-adapter/contact-authority-snapshot.ts imports the PostgresContactStore type from src/core/contacts/postgres-adapter/store.ts, while store.ts imports installPostgresContactAuthoritySnapshotOperations from contact-authority-snapshot.ts. The snapshot module entered through commit a92cbefcb1 (feat(fleet-auth): complete lifecycle authority ceremonies). The regression was reproduced while validating psfn-framework-fe5d; the Productivity Pack document changes no TypeScript.

Concrete work: read both modules and the contact store port/contracts; extract the narrow structural store/dependency type into an acyclic focused module or change the installer interface so the snapshot implementation no longer imports its composing store. Preserve Postgres-only persistence, authority lifecycle behavior, transaction semantics, and fail-closed fleet-auth rules. Add or adjust focused tests for snapshot install/read/write behavior if the seam changes.

Why: dependency-cycle verification is a mandatory repository hygiene gate, and a composing module importing its child back through the concrete store erodes the ownership boundary.

Scope: remove this one newly detected cycle and validate its affected contacts/fleet-auth behavior. Non-goals: do not absorb the four baseline-matched cycles already recorded by the checker, do not widen persistence interfaces, and do not add the new cycle to the baseline.

Replaced the contact-authority snapshot module's type-only dependency on concrete store.ts with the existing acyclic PostgresContactOperationContext/PostgresContactStoreClass seam in operation-map.ts; runtime imports, SQL, prototype installation, and fail-closed behavior are unchanged. title: Cost analytics: fleet-wide aggregated cost page + fan-out service
description:
FIRST read the wave context file at /tmp/e5n1-context.md (shared substrate map, gates, rules).
DEPENDS on: chart primitives bead (Sparkline, StackedBars optional). Coordinate integration with the
previous-period bead if you need comparison totals at fleet scope (totals-per-window helper reuse).

Build the FLEET-level cost surface: aggregated budget metrics across ALL companions, with rows linking
through to each companion's view. Today the model-usage store is per-companion (companionId bound at
construction in persistence/runtime-factory.ts) and Garden's AdminModelUsageDataService queries a single
store — so this bead owns the fleet fan-out.

## What to build

1. Backend: a fleet model-usage service (new file
   src/operator/garden/services/fleet-model-usage-service.ts) that, given the fleet's companion roster
   (inspect how Garden/composition learns the companion list — fleet launcher manifests, composition.ts,
   or an existing fleet service; do NOT invent a new roster source), fans out getUsageData across each
   companion's store and merges: fleet totals (sum of ModelUsageTotals fields — token/cost/call sums are
   additive; averages like averageDurationMs must be recomputed from totalDurationMs/durationSamples,
   NOT averaged), a per-companion leaderboard breakdown (companionId → totals + provider:model top entry),
   and a per-day fleet timeSeries (sum across companions per bucket). Preserve the privacy rule
   EXACTLY: each per-companion query goes through the same aggregate-vs-operator_visible combination as
   AdminModelUsageDataService before merging. If the current composition wires only ONE store into
   Garden, do the minimal composition change to expose a store registry/factory to the service — touch
   composition.ts and transport-server.ts only as needed, and keep single-companion deployments working
   (fleet = 1 row).
2. Route: GET /api/admin/fleet-model-usage accepting the same range/timezone/sinceMs/untilMs params as
   the model-usage route (reuse the parser from routes/model-usage-query.ts — extract a shared helper if
   clean rather than copying). Response: { resolvedRange, totals, perCompanion: [...], timeSeries }.
3. Frontend: new route admin-ui/src/routes/fleet-costs/+page.svelte (+ endpoint module
   admin-ui/src/lib/api/endpoints/fleet-model-usage.ts). Page contents:
   - Range controls reusing ACCOUNTING_RANGE_OPTIONS semantics (week/month/quarter/year/custom; 'today'
     and 'all' also fine — mirror cockpit behavior for custom dates).
   - Headline fleet stat cards (spend, requests, tokens, cache hit rate — reuse UsageMetricCards
     derivation helpers if extractable, else the derived-metrics helpers directly).
   - Stacked or plain fleet usage-over-time bars (single series acceptable; per-companion stacking is a
     nice-to-have ONLY if the payload already carries it cheaply — otherwise per-companion is the table).
   - Per-companion leaderboard table: companion, calls, tokens (in/out), cache read, effective cost,
     % of fleet spend; sortable by each numeric column; each row links to the companion-scoped view.
     LINK TARGET: inspect how Garden routes scope to a companion today (the main dashboard is
     per-companion — find the mechanism: query param, path segment, or companion switcher state) and
     reuse it; if no scoping mechanism exists, link to /charge-budget?tab=token-usage&filter.companionId=
     <id> after verifying the cockpit honors that filter param end-to-end (query-state.ts supports
     filter.companionId — verify the backend applies it for the bound store or document the gap).
   - Nav entry in admin-ui/src/lib/nav.ts ('runtime' group near Charge / Budget, id 'fleet-costs',
     label 'Fleet Costs').

## Non-goals

- No cross-companion per-model breakdown (fleet by-model is cockpit scope, not fleet page).
- No charge-ledger fleet view.
- No new persistence — fan-out over existing stores only.
- No fleet previous-period deltas unless the helper reuse is trivial.

## Acceptance criteria

- Fleet endpoint returns merged totals that EQUAL the sum of per-companion queries (test this property
  with a two-companion fixture in a service unit test, including the averaging rule for durations).
- Privacy combination preserved per companion before merge (unit test with a companion_private fixture:
  totals include it, per-companion rows expose no private detail beyond what the existing service emits).
- Page renders cards, chart, sortable leaderboard; row links land on a working companion-scoped view (or
  the gap is documented in the handoff with a filed follow-up).
- Single-companion deployment renders correctly (one row).
- Gates: svelte-check zero new errors, admin-ui build, root lint, targeted backend tests.
acceptance_criteria: Fleet endpoint merged totals equal the sum of per-companion queries (two-companion fixture test); privacy combination preserved before merge; page renders cards, chart, sortable per-companion leaderboard with working links to companion-scoped view (or documented gap + follow-up); single-companion deployment renders; svelte-check zero new errors, admin-ui build, root lint, targeted backend tests.
notes: ARCH UPDATE (post-PR-107 merge): the fleet Garden foundation routes per-companion Garden admin traffic through admin transports — see src/operator/garden/fleet-transport-client.ts + fleet-garden-target-registry.ts (one target per companion, admin transport socket per companion). The fleet fan-out for this bead should be implemented as a Garden-side service that queries EACH companion's own /api/admin/model-usage through the fleet transport client (per-companion stores stay bound) and merges, rather than reaching across persistence directly. Roster source: FleetGardenTargetRegistry entries. Verify transport client's error semantics for an unreachable companion (fleet page must degrade per-companion, not fail closed wholesale).
close_reason: Implemented and integrated. Range 5a74977ade..b03996502c (29 files, +2540/-23): fleet fan-out service (client of each companion's per-companion Garden /api/admin/model-usage via fleet transport client — NOT direct multi-store aggregation) + /api/admin/fleet-model-usage route + /fleet-costs page (fleet totals, metrics, chart, sortable companion leaderboard, companion-scoped links). PRIVACY GATE HOLDS: parseModelUsageResponse projects ONLY totals/visibleTotals/topModel/timeSeries (recentEvents/expensiveEvents/byPurpose-detail/metadata die at JSON.parse); visibleTotals recomputed from operator_visible groups only; defense-in-depth companion_private marker tripwire fail-closes; privacy test proves JSON.stringify(result) lacks companion_private even with poisoned child response. SIGNED ROSTER: gateway-signed Ed25519 roster (sorted RFC-4122, <=256, models.read only), re-authorizes each companion; cross-companion/time-range substitution impossible without gateway key (exact child target round-trip validation, timingSafeEqual compare). FAIL-CLOSED: unreachable/errored companions surface as unavailable with exact coverage accounting, never fabricated or dropped. P1 DUAL BLIND REVIEW: Reviewer A PASS + Reviewer B PASS, both zero blocking; 4 src/operator/garden suite failures confirmed PRE-EXISTING (reproduced identically at base 5a74977ade). UBS 2 'critical' secret-comparison findings confirmed false positives (crypto.timingSafeEqual :359/:365, crypto.verify :1241). Integrated gates on feat/cost-analytics @ 50bb881915: admin-ui vitest 168/168, backend targeted vitest 49/49, svelte-check 0/0, admin-ui+root build clean, root lint clean, verify:hardcoded-settings pass. Branch pushed. Nonblocking observations in wave handoff (fleet timeSeries aggregate-includes-private-by-design comment suggestion, marker-tripwire DoS edge, generic-500 route error, spendShare sort label).

title: P1: Remediate PR #103 approval-v2 and Companion UI production wiring blockers
description:
Summary: Repair PR #103 at pinned failed head 1b751c846c58ee880afead6b8a0499570af0d0bd so the hub-fronted Companion UI can actually receive and render approval-v2 data, fleet snapshots preserve the complete redacted contract, roster/config code is production-wired, and all PR-introduced repository standards violations are removed.

Why: GitHub reports the branch mergeable, but independent validation proved the core acceptance path cannot work. docs/approval-envelope.md:117 explicitly says Hub capability forwarding is unimplemented; src/channels/api/server/fleet-auth-routes.ts:71 down-projects fleet approvals to the legacy six fields; companion-ui/src/lib/fleet-roster.ts has no production consumer; companionUi.canonicalContactId is accepted but inert; and verify:hardcoded-settings flags six PR-introduced limits in redaction.ts and companions-config.ts. The standards review also found a no-shim compatibility path, duplicated shared contracts/UUID validation, an oversized fleet-auth-routes.ts, speculative approval abstractions without projectors, and duplicated exactKeys logic. The spec review additionally found parentLabel falling back to opaque parentId, only the gateway/tool-access projector implemented, and partial 8ora registry/Garden integration.

Scope:
1. Implement end-to-end approval-v2 capability negotiation and forwarding across the Satellite Hub-facing path so a connected Companion UI advertising approvals.v2 receives the complete v2 approval.requested payload. Preserve exact legacy behavior only where the external protocol explicitly requires a version projection; remove any internal compatibility shim or retired alias that conflicts with the no-shim rule.
2. Make GET /v1/fleet-auth/approvals preserve the full redacted v2 fields: sourceSystem, attribution, action, scope, reason, grantMode, expiry, status, and terminal data required by the shared contract. Owner filtering remains server-derived and fail closed.
3. Wire FleetRosterClient into a real Companion UI runtime/store/bootstrap consumer, including companion roster labels used by approval attribution and active-companion routing. Resolve parentLabel from authorized roster data; do not fall back to an opaque ID as a user-facing label.
4. Give companionUi.canonicalContactId one authoritative runtime behavior or remove it from the owner contract, seed, docs, and tests. No inert mutable config.
5. Fix all six PR-introduced verify:hardcoded-settings violations by moving policy/tuning values to an existing canonical owner contract where genuinely mutable, or recording genuinely code-owned structural limits in scripts/hardcoded-settings-baseline.json with one-line notes. Do not weaken the verifier.
6. Consolidate duplicated approval/UI contracts, UUID validation, and exactKeys onto existing shared primitives. Split fleet-auth-routes.ts by focused route capability if needed; do not expand the god file.
7. Implement or remove speculative source projectors so every sourceSystem the PR claims as supported has a real registered projection path. Keep future/unimplemented source kinds out of production claims.
8. Complete 8ora production registry and Garden channel-config integration so companion-ui is not merely a type/profile special case. Preserve fail-closed channel activation, authenticated hub-device stamping, contact binding, privacy metadata, and schedule exclusion.
9. Add regression coverage for Hub v2 negotiation/forwarding, fleet snapshot completeness and isolation, production roster consumption/labels, config behavior, and shared validation boundaries.

Non-goals: do not implement shard TTL grant evaluation (mus2.7), new approval card UX beyond the existing mus2.9 contract, direct shard chat, or unrelated pre-existing full-suite failures. Do not weaken authentication, owner filtering, redaction, route authorization, repository hygiene, or settings ownership.

Validation baseline from failed review: root lint, Companion UI lint, both builds, settings contract, startup owner files, diff check, 211 root focused tests, and 167 Companion UI tests passed. Full root suite had 11 failures in unchanged/pre-existing areas. Repository hygiene was red partly from inherited findings and specifically from six PR-introduced hardcoded settings violations. The remediation must preserve the green gates and eliminate every in-diff hygiene failure.
acceptance_criteria: A Hub-fronted Companion UI advertising approvals.v2 receives a complete redacted v2 approval frame end to end; clients without the capability follow the explicitly supported wire-version behavior without internal legacy aliases; GET /v1/fleet-auth/approvals preserves all required v2 attribution/action/scope/reason/grant/source/expiry/status fields and remains owner-isolated; FleetRosterClient has a production consumer and authorized roster labels populate approval parentLabel without opaque-ID fallback; companionUi.canonicalContactId is either authoritatively used or fully removed; every claimed approval sourceSystem has a real projector or is removed from supported claims; companion-ui is integrated through canonical channel registry and Garden owner-file surfaces; duplicated contracts/UUID/exactKeys helpers are consolidated; fleet-auth route code remains focused; all PR-introduced hardcoded-setting violations are resolved without weakening verification; focused root and Companion UI tests pass; root and Companion UI lint/build pass; verify:settings-contract, verify:startup-owner-files, verify:repository-hygiene, and git diff --check pass; full root suite is run once and any unrelated failures are reported separately.
close_reason: Completed in 5b31ca3e63. Framework now negotiates approvals.v2 on the gateway WebSocket, emits companion-scoped complete v2 events, preserves the full owner-isolated fleet snapshot, consumes the roster in production, switches to the owning companion before decisions, refuses wrong-owner submission on switch failure, uses canonical roster labels, removes inert canonicalContactId config, consolidates shared guards/contracts, narrows claimed projectors, and baselines code-owned structural limits. Evidence: root lint/build pass; 154 focused gateway/approval tests pass; Companion UI lint/build and 169 tests pass (including failed-switch isolation); settings/startup/hardcoded/shared-guard checks pass; full suite 10 failed + 1 failed suite, 11,318 passed, 6 skipped, matching inherited failed-head areas; repository hygiene remains blocked only by inherited public-sanitize/identity/cycle findings.

title: Garden capability catalogue throws at module load: GET /api/admin/dashboard/analysis-workbench-traces registered but unclassified
description:
