title: P1: Gate managed skill writes through canonical CogSec intake policy
description:
Summary: Personal SKILL.md create/update is a durable prompt-bearing write and must use the canonical CogSec intake/envelope/sink-gate architecture. Do not add the parallel Hermes-shaped SkillsGuardPort proposed by psfn-framework-i72.2.

Evidence: src/faculties/skills/tools.ts:365-424 calls SkillStore.create/update directly and invalidates the runtime, so newly written instructions can enter later prompt indexes without CogSec screening or a sink verdict. src/shared/contracts/intake-envelope.ts:157-164 defines all consequential sinks but has no skill_write sink. src/app/agent/core-runtime.ts:258-269 documents and composes the shared gate for prompt, memory, wiki, persona, trust, and egress, but src/app/agent/core-runtime.ts:399-407 wires skills without that gate. Current skill tests prove filesystem/path behavior, not prompt-injection, exfiltration, destructive-command, persistence, or taint enforcement. Searches for skill injection, CogSec skill, and skill write found no separate tracking bead.

Why: A companion-authored skill is durable executable guidance loaded into future model context. Its content can be derived from untrusted chat, web, tool, subagent, or shard input; writing it without propagated IntakeEnvelope provenance creates a persistence path around the Cognition Intake Firewall. A bespoke regex guard would duplicate the L1 scanner and diverge from intake-policy.json authority.

Scope:
1. Extend the closed CogSec sink vocabulary and intake-policy owner contract with an explicit skill_write sink, including seed/default policy, strict validation, Garden exposure, and any explicit repo-owned owner-file migration needed for live alpha. Do not add a silent compatibility default.
2. Thread the existing IntakeSinkGate and active-turn IntakeEnvelope provenance through skills runtime/tool wiring. Before SkillStore.create or SkillStore.update, evaluate skill_write against every envelope that influenced the proposed content; one denied/quarantined envelope denies the write. Unscreened behavior must be explicit in intake-policy.json and fail closed in enforce mode for this prompt-bearing mutation.
3. Reuse the canonical L1/L1.5/L2/L3 screening and risk-label taxonomy where content screening is required. Do not create a SkillsGuardPort, second regex rule set, or skill-local quarantine model.
4. Preserve existing capability gating and Personal Workspace containment. Emit auditable CogSec sink decisions without logging raw skill content or secrets.
5. Add focused tests for direct clean create/update, injected prompt override, encoded/exfiltration/destructive/persistence patterns, quarantined upstream input, multi-envelope propagation, shadow versus enforce mode, unscreened fail-closed behavior, and no file/runtime invalidation after denial.

Files likely include src/shared/contracts/intake-envelope.ts, src/system/config/intake-policy-config.ts, config/intake-policy.seed.json, src/core/cogsec/intake/sink-gates.ts, src/app/agent/core-runtime.ts, src/faculties/skills/runtime-wiring.ts, src/faculties/skills/tools.ts, their tests, and the Garden intake-policy/settings contract surface.

Non-goals: no new standalone skill scanner or rules file; no autonomous skill suggestion event; no delete action expansion; no changes to deployment-provided builtin skills; no compatibility reader that silently accepts owner files missing the new sink.
acceptance_criteria: INTAKE_SINKS and intake-policy.json own a validated skill_write rule with no silent missing-field fallback; the existing CogSec gate and upstream envelope provenance reach skill create/update before filesystem mutation; enforce mode denies risky, quarantined, over-tier, and unscreened skill writes according to explicit policy while shadow mode audits without enforcement; denied writes leave no SKILL.md change and do not invalidate/reload the skills runtime; clean authorized personal-skill writes still work; audits contain decision/provenance but no raw skill content or secrets; Garden exposes the owner-file policy consistently; focused skills/CogSec/config tests pass; npm run verify:settings-contract, npm run verify:repository-hygiene, npm run lint, and npm run build pass.
close_reason: Implemented and integrated: feat/ahxy-s10-shakedown-fixes @ d00edd86a (origin-equal; bead branch work/ahxy-k6tm @ 037feadab = 7ca0b648b impl + remediation). skill_write joins the closed CogSec sink vocabulary with a schema-v2 intake-policy owner contract (strict validation, Garden exposure, explicit atomic dry-run/apply migration CLI migrate:intake-policy-owner, fail-closed boot on unmigrated v1, no compatibility fallback); the skills tool evaluates every async-local active-turn IntakeEnvelope plus canonical L1 screening before SkillStore.create/update — one denied/quarantined envelope denies with no file write, no runtime invalidation, no quarantine copy, audit carries ids/labels only; turn provenance moved from global state to AsyncLocalStorage (no cross-turn contamination, proven under overlapping turns). Dual blind review (Opus PASS / Pi FAIL) surfaced one verified P1 blocker: the fs tool could write SKILL.md into workspace/skills (path-only ALLOW, loader ingests any SKILL.md next prompt build), bypassing the gate. One remediation pass write-protects the managed skills root at the gateway fs boundary (protectedWritePaths in production bootstrap + per-companion fleet connection policies, canonical/symlink-alias closure, fs.write+fs.edit), with denial regressions incl. multi-companion scoping; re-verified 170/170 + integrated-branch 229/229; lint/build/settings-contract/hardcoded-settings/hygiene gates green. Rollout notes (handoff): operators MUST run migrate:intake-policy-owner before deploying schema-v2 (boot fails closed); seed ships shadow mode (gate observe-only until enforce); Garden operator skill routes intentionally unscreened (trusted tier — confirm posture); agent-side screening is L1-only like sibling sinks; structural note: gate lives at tool layer, SkillsRuntime/SkillStore write surfaces remain public (future in-process consumers must be screened).

title: Approval wire contract v2: carry shard attribution + grant-mode offer to the app
description:
UNBLOCKS companion-ui bead psfn-framework-mus2.9 (shard-attributed approval cards). Owner: backend/wire agent (NOT the app lane).

Current wire shape (companion-ui/src/lib/protocol/events.ts:264 ApprovalRequestedMessage and src/lib/stream/hub-stream.ts:470) carries only: id, title, requestedAt, expiresAt, redactedContext, status. mus2.9 must render parent/shard attribution + grant-mode but is forbidden from inventing them.

Add to the approval.requested payload (and the corresponding stream/relay projection):
- attribution: { parentLabel, parentId (opaque), shardLabel?, shardId? (opaque) } — server-resolved
- action: redacted action summary
- scope: redacted scope
- reason: redacted reason
- grantMode: { kind: 'once' } | { kind: 'ttl', ttlSeconds } — the exact server-offered mode
- sourceSystem: tag identifying the originating subsystem (shard | cogsec | tool-access | expensive-usage | ...)

Requirements: versioned/tolerant parse (old clients must not break), never trust client-supplied identity/scope/duration. This is the contract the app renders. Coordinate with psfn-framework-mus2.8 (fleet-scope approval snapshots) and mus2.3 (attribution through approval queues).
close_reason: Implemented on feat/wire-approvals-roster-channel (PR #103, commits 1458611d28+347537c51f): v2 fields (attribution/action/scope/reason/grantMode/sourceSystem) capability-gated on approvals.v2 at the SSE seam, exact v1 down-projection proven byte-identical for old clients, TTL emission throws, companion-ui framing/reducer parse v2 tolerantly with strictness preserved elsewhere. 66 companion-ui + 112 root tests green; blind dual review zero blockers. Unblocks mus2.9 — ApprovalStreamEntry now carries optional attribution/action/scope/reason/grantMode/sourceSystem for the card lane.

title: Companion-scope all direct Garden database access in the fleet Garden and audit the existing wiring
description:
Evidence: operator decision 2026-07-17 (PR #100 review follow-up): Garden services that already read/write the database directly KEEP that access — rerouting through agent transports was judged not worth the rework — but in the fleet-scoped Garden every database access must be scoped to the request's authenticated companion target. Direct-access services confirmed by grep: src/operator/garden/services/dashboard-service.ts, audit-history-service.ts, session-turn-observability.ts, contact-session-linker.ts, icp-autonomy-service.ts, group-memory-diagnostics-service.ts (persistence/store imports), plus types/local-admin-contract wiring. Operator: 'we definitely have to make sure that when a garden switch is between companion views in a multi-companion scenario that database writes are going to the right companion... the distinction of who is generating the request and then it routes the proper way.' Recorded as invariant 11 in docs/garden-control-plane.md and a dedicated verification bullet (added on the PR #100 branch).

Context: partner-data isolation in the consolidated Garden (docs/garden-control-plane.md). Today each Garden process is bound to one companion, so unscoped queries are implicitly correct; after consolidation an unscoped or process-global query becomes a cross-companion leak. Same defect class as an52.3's process-global tier. Secondary system: fleet-auth, persistence.

Scope: (1) AUDIT every direct database access path in src/operator/garden (services and routes) and classify: already companion-keyed (by schema, companion column, or store construction) vs unscoped/process-global; operator hopes it was wired properly — prove it with file:line findings. (2) For the fleet Garden, derive the companion key for every query from the immutable GardenRequestContext of the authenticated request, never from a cached selection or process-global state. (3) Regression coverage in multi-companion mode: interleaved requests for companion A and B on the same Garden process cannot read or write each other's rows, including WebSocket/event streams and audit writes. Non-goals: do not reroute existing direct reads through agent admin transports; do not change store schemas or move data; single-companion Garden behavior unchanged.

Acceptance: audit findings recorded on this bead with file:line classification for every direct-access service; every unscoped path is keyed by the request's companion target; a multi-companion regression proves A/B isolation for at least the dashboard, audit-history, and session observability services under interleaved requests; verification bullet in docs/garden-control-plane.md is satisfied by the test evidence.
notes: AUDIT (mus2.16, invariant 11): All Garden domain services constructed once-per-process in createInProcessGardenAdminContract (local-admin-contract.ts:203); companion scope captured AT CONSTRUCTION from config -> companionDataDir (fs root, mech c), config.companionId (companion_id column, mech b), or Postgres schema (mech a). No per-request companion discriminator exists because a process serves ONE companion. Route/handler files (routes/*, handlers/*, api-routes*) carry ZERO direct DB access -- all delegate to service interfaces (transport-routed). CLASSIFICATION: ALREADY-KEYED by construction: dashboard-service.ts(c+ports), audit-history-service.ts(c fs-path garden-audit-history.jsonl + scopeId=companionId @local-admin-contract.ts:242,245), session-turn-observability.ts(ports+per-companion eventBus), contact-session-linker.ts(c+contactStore), session-service.ts(c), contacts-service.ts, memory-service.ts, episodic-memory-service.ts, group-memory-diagnostics-service.ts(c watermark + fleetMemoryStore per-request subject), scheduler-service.ts(c), images-service.ts(c), drift-review-service.ts(c), intake-quarantine-service.ts(c), settings/skills(c owner-file), model-usage-service.ts(b companion_id col @model-usage-store.ts:1124-1147), charge-cost-reconciliation(b strict, rejects mismatched companionId @:35-36), identity/prompts/concern/graph-proposals/rooms/pending-contacts/diagnostics(ports). KEYED-BUT-RISK (shared schema + app-side filter): icp-autonomy-service.ts + IcpAdminProjectionStore(icp-admin-projection-store.ts:252 uses SHARED_SCHEMA 'shared', reads whole projection then .filter by localCompanionId captured at ctor @icp-autonomy-service.ts:89-114, +binding-equality assert @:73-74; sibling IcpInitiationCandidateStore is per-companion schema). TRUE UNSCOPED/PROCESS-GLOBAL: observer-eval-sidecar-service.ts -> PostgresObserverEvalSidecarStore (core/eval/observer-sidecar/persistence.ts:361-376) pool has NO schema + queries key on run_id/observation_id/sidecar_id, NO companion_id -- eval-owned deployment-global telemetry by design (persistence.ts:36); isolation rests on per-deployment databaseUrl. FLEET-SHARED BY DESIGN (not per-companion): places-service.ts(shared system config.dataDir registries), shared-workspace-service.ts(cross-companion sharedWorkspacePath), wiki-service.ts shared-world(systemDataDir + shared pgvector schema keyed by siteId). FIX: added dispatch-chokepoint guard gardenRequestCompanionScopeDenial (garden-companion-scope.ts) wired into dispatchAdminRoute (server-routes.ts) -- refuses any fleet request whose authenticated resource.companionId != the connection-bound dispatch companionId (fail closed), so a request for A can never reach A-vs-B service instances. NON-GOAL respected: no store schema changes (observer-eval-sidecar left as deployment-global by design; icp shared-schema app-side filter unchanged -- per-companion instancing + guard covers it). Regression: garden-companion-scope.test.ts (guard + dispatch wiring, handler-not-called on cross-companion), garden-db-companion-isolation.test.ts (A/B isolation for dashboard cached-reads+live-event-stream, audit-history durable writes+reads, session-turn observability event streams, all interleaved).
close_reason: Implemented at work/mus2-16-garden-db-scoping 7e69734ade, merged to feat/mus2-fleet-garden ad83d058bc (branch head 0cde212d01). Exhaustive direct-DB audit recorded on bead notes (all services companion-scoped by construction; routes have zero direct DB access; icp store SQL-scopes by companion_id; observer-eval-sidecar deployment-global by design, disclosed). Fail-closed companion-scope guard wired into dispatchAdminRoute as invariant-11 chokepoint. A/B interleaved isolation regressions for dashboard/audit-history/session-observability incl. event streams (13 tests). Gates: lint, build, diff-check, UBS clean. Review: Opus PASS (1x tier), zero blockers. Docs verification bullet satisfied by garden-db-companion-isolation.test.ts.

title: Restore the full npm test gate after fleet-auth fixture and install drift
description:
The final validation run for psfn-framework-yijy at d464982ff4 executed the full suite once, after all three design beads were integrated. The branch changes only Markdown/working_docs, but npm test is red: 28 test files failed, 975 passed, 1 skipped; 15 tests failed, 11,042 passed, 6 skipped.

Observed failure groups:
1. Twenty-four suites cannot import src/boundary/fleet-auth/webauthn-uv.ts because @simplewebauthn/server is absent from this checkout's node_modules, even though package.json and package-lock.json exactly pin 13.3.2. Start from npm ci and distinguish stale local installation state from a reproducible dependency/package problem; do not add a second or floating dependency declaration.
2. src/channels/api/agent-backend.test.ts fails because the exercised request reaches validation without an object authContext ("authContext must be an object"). Update the test/runtime contract at the correct boundary without relaxing fail-closed authentication.
3. All ten src/app/e2e/icp-certification/process-harness.integration.test.ts cases report an early child-agent exit. Re-evaluate after the exact WebAuthn dependency is installed; if the exit remains, capture and repair the earliest startup error rather than weakening the harness.
4. scripts/install-psfn-service-workspace.test.ts times out. Diagnose the blocking operation and retain the intended workspace isolation assertions; do not merely raise the timeout without evidence.
5. Three intake-quarantine-routes tests receive a second undefined argument from current routing calls. Align mocks/expectations with the live signature while preserving the tested quarantine and fail-closed behavior.

Why: a mandatory broad regression gate is red and the mixed local-install/fixture failures obscure whether current main is releasable.

Scope: reproduce from a clean exact install, repair only the confirmed dependency/startup/fixture causes above, and restore the full suite. Non-goals: no changes to the yijy design specifications, no loosening auth or quarantine validation, no floating pins, and no blanket timeout increases. Discovered during psfn-framework-yijy final validation.
acceptance_criteria: From a clean npm ci using the committed exact lockfile: targeted WebAuthn/fleet-auth import tests, src/channels/api/agent-backend.test.ts, src/app/e2e/icp-certification/process-harness.integration.test.ts, scripts/install-psfn-service-workspace.test.ts, and the intake-quarantine route tests pass; npm test passes in full; authentication and quarantine remain fail closed; npm run lint and npm run build pass.
notes: 2026-07-18 (mus2 remediation final sweep): src/app/e2e/icp-certification/process-harness.integration.test.ts fails identically on origin/main 4c007fb3df (ICP conversation cost breaker opens warning_closeout_reserve_only and blocks all models) — inherited, likely from the PR #105 support-fixture/charge fixture era. Also: full-suite parallel runs flake install-psfn-service x2, fleet-auth-family-restore, gateway-persistence (all pass in isolation); trusted-host-provider-recovery x2 remain env-bound (session pepper).
close_reason: Full npm test green on feat/test-gate-repairs-20260719 (11,658 passed / 0 failed, exit 0, clean npm ci). Group triage: (1) @simplewebauthn absence = stale local install, not reproducible from clean ci; (2) agent-backend authContext passes on current main; (3) icp process-harness 10/10 after fixture-identity repair (3b2de3760 — mock marker heuristic predated ARTEMIS/Mica rename in 89e0e1d918, not a privacy regression per Opus diagnosis); (4) install-psfn-service-workspace.test.ts premise dead — file deleted on main; (5) intake-quarantine fixed under 9fdw. Additional real causes repaired: UUID companion-id fixture drift across seven suites (1d5d9c000 + straggler — same identity contract as the deployment migration; /v1/models UUID id confirmed intended by both reviewers), appraisal time-bomb fixture made execution-relative. gateway-persistence integration 1-test fail under full-suite load passes standalone — load flake, noted in handoff.

title: Render and secure exactly one fleet Garden in Helm
description: Summary: Change deploy/helm/psfn values and workload/certificate/networkpolicy/ingress/validation templates so a fleet deployment has exactly one Garden Deployment/Service and fleet-scoped Garden workload identity, while N companion agents retain distinct canonical owner roots/admin endpoints. Garden reaches only registered agent admin targets and narrow gateway control routes; it does not mount writable companion PVCs or provider/database secrets. Gateway reaches only the single Garden. Why: k3s is live authority and consolidated design must reduce components without collapsing companion isolation or widening network credentials. Scope: exact pinned image/reference usage, SPIFFE/mTLS, readiness for every registered target, least-privilege policies, render/schema verification. Non-goals: live rollout, per-shard resources, dual topology, owner-file changes.
acceptance_criteria: Representative multi-companion Helm renders contain exactly one Garden Service/Deployment and zero shard Gardens; all agents remain separately addressed; Garden/gateway/agent network and certificate identities are least-privilege and target-bound; no companion data/provider/database credential is mounted into Garden; every target participates in readiness; missing/duplicate target validation fails closed; Helm verification, build, lint, UBS, and diff-check pass.
close_reason: Implemented by Codex at work/mus2-13-helm-fleet-garden aa92498ce9, merged to feat/mus2-fleet-garden. Fleet Helm renders exactly one Garden Deployment/Service (verify-helm-chart.mjs asserts 1/1/0-shard-gardens); per-companion agent Services/Deployments from deepCopy values with duplicate/UUID/claims/schema validation failing closed; Garden egress = registered agent-admin targets + gateway API + DNS only (no postgres/redis/companion-data; gateway cannot reach agent admin in fleet mode); exact per-companion agent admin server SPIFFE SANs (Garden pins exact identity; readiness exec probe mTLS-checks every registered target with checkServerIdentity); pinned images with latest/main rejection; GATEWAY_OPERATOR_API_BASE_URL ends /v1 matching the fixed client convention. title: Implement shard-scoped request and TTL grants without standing tier mutation
description: Summary: Add a focused src/system/capabilities/shard-approval-grants.ts and integrate it with approval-boundary/policy dispatch. Request mode consumes the exact queued operation once. Optional TTL mode remains disabled until an explicit canonical JSON owner, maximum duration, and offered-action policy are selected and wired through config ownership/Garden contracts; browser/env values are never authority. Bind every grant to parent companion, shard instance/workload generation, approval/grant ID, method/action, normalized scope, expiry, and revocation. Why: shards need human-approved exceptional actions without adding masked tokens to standing custom access or relying on autonomous-parent auto-clear. Scope: exact-once request grants; server-offered TTL only; fail-closed replay, sibling/replacement/parent use, widening, expiry, revocation, restart, clock uncertainty. The approved mask disposition must permit only explicitly delegable tokens; lifecycle, base/operator identity, and memory.delete remain nondelegable. Non-goals: tier derivation, UI, cross-shard delegation.
acceptance_criteria: All six masked tokens are tested: only operator-approved delegable tokens can receive temporary authority and every nondelegable token denies; request grants are exact-once and tuple-bound; TTL is unavailable without canonical policy and then enforces ceiling/scope/expiry/revocation/recovery; parent autonomous tier does not bypass shard fences; no tier/mask/owner widening occurs; audit contains no secrets; non-shard approvals regressions, settings-contract/hygiene gates if config changes, build, lint, UBS, and diff-check pass.

Gates: 64 focused at lane + 39 merged approval suites + 94 wider stack, lint, build, diff-check, UBS clean. Review: dual blind Opus PASS + Pi PASS, zero blockers. Nonblocking for future executor bead: sameWorkload requires stable frozen access object per generation; modify decisions fail closed on shard grants (exact-params contract); clockUncertain latch is an availability sharp edge.

title: Fleet-scope Companion UI approval snapshots, events, and decisions by stored owner

title: Recompute and enforce digest-equal shard grants at gateway backend admission
description: Summary: Extend strict per-authenticated-companion CapabilityAccess through src/boundary/gateway/capability-tier-resolver.ts, server.ts, methods/types.ts, protocol.ts, and methods/shard-backends.ts. Gateway admission retains existing shell allowlist, approval, and autonomous/custom restrictions, requires authoritative parent shard.spawn, derives via mus2.1, and compares its grant digest with the manager-bound launch digest; mismatch or owner-file churn denies before backend execution. acceptance_criteria: Tests prove authenticated companion access is used; custom without shard.spawn denies; valid custom derives exact mask; spoofed tier/tokens cannot widen; missing/malformed resolver fails POLICY_DENIED; manager/gateway equal digest passes and any owner-file mutation/digest mismatch denies before executor side effects; companion A/B isolation and existing shell/approval/backend-tier behavior remain; protocol compiles without caller capabilityTier; tests/build/lint/UBS/diff-check pass.

title: Implement canonical shard capability snapshot, denial-mask derivation, and grant digest
description: Summary: Add one capability-system primitive that atomically snapshots authoritative parent access, validates/canonicalizes its tokens, subtracts the approved shard denial mask, and returns immutable custom shard access plus a stable grant digest/version for cross-boundary equality. Files: add src/system/capabilities/shard-derivation.ts and tests, export through src/system/capabilities/index.ts, and deepen src/system/capabilities/access.ts/runtime.ts only as needed to obtain one coherent tier+token snapshot rather than independently refreshing getters. Extend the smallest SubstrateAgent/runtime-context access seam so an explicit custom access governs tool gates and prompt availability without a disk-backed CapabilityRuntime. Why: CapabilityAccess getters currently refresh independently, and manager/gateway recomputation during owner-file churn could widen a shard beyond its launch snapshot unless the launch request binds an exact digest. Scope: exact canonical token ordering/deduplication, unknown-token refusal, digest/version handshake contract, six-token mask and per-token grant disposition, immutable custom access. Non-goals: no ShardManager or gateway method wiring, no owner-file schema change, no new tier, no approval UI, no fallback to tier-name defaults.
acceptance_criteria: Tests cover all-token, partial, default, and custom parents; one atomic snapshot cannot mix file versions; unknown tokens fail closed; output equals the parent subset minus exactly the approved mask in canonical order; the digest is stable for equal grants and changes for any authority change; explicit custom access gates and advertises identical tokens; every masked token has an explicit temporary-grant eligibility decision; no owner-file/tier format changes; targeted tests, npm run build, npm run lint, UBS, and git diff --check pass.
notes: Implemented on work/mus2-1-capability-snapshot @ a5adfdae6f (pushed). New src/system/capabilities/shard-derivation.ts (+tests): canonical token validation/ordering, six-token denial mask + per-token temporary-grant dispositions (world.control approval-only/policy-gated TTL, other five nondelegable), atomic parent snapshot with content-stable ownerVersion, SHA-256 grantDigest over exposed payload contract, immutable custom access. CapabilityRuntime.snapshotOwnerGrant() single-read snapshot; SubstrateAgent.setCapabilityAccess() explicit-access seam wins over disk runtime; prompt tool guide now advertises from the resolved granted token set (was tier-name re-resolution, empty for custom). Gates: focused vitest suites green (31+94+128+206+61+8+44), lint clean, build ok, git diff --check clean. No owner-file/tier format changes; no manager/gateway wiring (mus2.4/.5).

title: Deepen Garden admission for immutable companion-bound fleet targets
description: Summary: Make every Garden admin request bind one immutable server-derived companion target and authorize it through Fleet Auth before proxying. title: Keep local k3d Garden localhost access alive across rollouts
description: The local Artemis k3d cluster does not publish Garden directly from its Docker load-balancer, so scripts/ops/setup-local-artemis-shakedown.sh intentionally provides localhost access with a background kubectl port-forward on PSFN_ARTEMIS_GARDEN_PORT (default 10154). Its current start_port_forward helper runs kubectl once and exits permanently when the selected Garden pod rolls. The live failure occurred after a pod sandbox disappeared: the log ended with 'failed to find sandbox ... lost connection', leaving the PID file stale and localhost:10154 refused. Add a focused repo-owned resilient port-forward runner, use it for both Garden and gateway forwards, validate the target service before starting, bind loopback only, reconnect after kubectl exits, avoid rapid retry loops, preserve logs/PID state, and ensure TERM/INT clean up the active kubectl child. Update local setup output/docs so the supported local ports are unambiguous: gateway 10153 and Garden 10154 by default; 10053/10054 are in-cluster service ports, not host listeners in k3d. Scope is local k3d operator access. Do not alter fleet Helm exposure semantics or create off-repo supervisor configuration.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic test proves the runner restarts kubectl after a simulated lost connection and terminates its active child on shutdown; setup-local-artemis-shakedown.sh uses the runner for gateway and Garden; localhost:10154 returns Garden /health 200 before and after forcibly terminating the underlying kubectl child; the listener is bound only to 127.0.0.1; docs distinguish local forwarded ports from in-cluster ports; npm run lint and relevant tests pass; changes are committed and pushed.
close_reason: Completed in commit 7788989960. Root cause: k3d publishes no host Garden port, and the intended setup-local-artemis-shakedown.sh localhost:10154 kubectl forward died permanently when its selected pod sandbox rolled. Added scripts/ops/keep-kube-port-forward.sh with loopback-only binding, service preflight, bounded retry, reconnection, and child cleanup; setup now launches it detached with setsid for both gateway and Garden; added deterministic lost-connection/cleanup regression coverage and clarified local 10153/10154 versus in-cluster 10053/10054 in the chart README. Evidence: localhost:10154 health 200; killed kubectl PID 3076112 and runner reconnected as PID 3077120 with health still 200; ss showed only 127.0.0.1:10154; regression test passed; bash -n passed; npm run lint passed; npm run build passed. Repository-hygiene progressed to the existing unrelated docs/helm-upgrades.md Carlini sanitizer finding.

title: Restore opt-in direct Garden access in Helm
description: Restore the prior direct Garden access mechanisms for the normal fleetAuth.enabled=false single-admin topology. SSO is not a generic security tier: it exists for shared multi-admin identity, one login across settings/companions, and authorization of gated backend data. Default non-SSO rendering should expose the ADMIN_TOKEN-authenticated Garden Ingress as before; ingress.garden.enabled lets an operator disable it. Add hostPorts.garden.enabled/port/hostIP/sourceCIDRs as the optional single-node alternative. Render the Garden Ingress only when fleet auth is off, update NetworkPolicy for whichever direct mechanism is selected, and retain a rollout strategy that cannot deadlock on a hostPort. With fleetAuth.enabled=true, suppress the separate Garden Ingress because Garden uses gateway mTLS/SSO in that topology, and reject an explicitly enabled Garden hostPort. Document both administration topologies without labeling ordinary ADMIN_TOKEN operation an insecure fallback. Non-goals: building another gateway proxy for non-SSO mode or forcing all operators onto SSO.
acceptance_criteria: Default fleetAuth.enabled=false rendering includes a Garden Ingress targeting the ADMIN_TOKEN-authenticated Garden service and no hostPort; ingress.garden.enabled=false removes that Ingress; hostPorts.garden.enabled=true renders the configured Garden hostPort/hostIP and optional sourceCIDR policy; fleetAuth.enabled=true renders only the gateway browser Ingress even though the non-SSO Garden Ingress default is true, and rejects a Garden hostPort; Helm verification covers these states; docs explain single-admin ADMIN_TOKEN versus multi-admin/multi-companion SSO; npm run lint, npm run build, and npm run verify:helm-chart pass; both default direct Ingress and disabled-direct-exposure paths are tested on the local cluster.
close_reason: Completed in commit 24bb6d6bb9 (included by integrated main dfcbcb2bed). deploy/helm/psfn/values.yaml:142 and :564 restore Garden hostPort configuration and the default non-SSO Garden Ingress; templates/ingress.yaml, networkpolicy.yaml, workloads.yaml, and validations.yaml implement topology-aware rendering and fail-closed SSO hostPort rejection; scripts/verify-helm-chart.mjs covers default, disabled, hostPort, NetworkPolicy, ADMIN_TOKEN, and SSO states; docs/helm-upgrades.md:139 and docs/operations.md document single-admin ADMIN_TOKEN versus shared SSO administration. Validation: targeted integrated-wave tests 53/53, npm run lint, npm run build, npm run verify:helm-chart, helm lint, local default Ingress health 200 with unauthenticated admin 401, internal-only flag test with port-forward health 200, and exact integrated-tip kube rollout 10/10 on Helm revision 35.

title: Gateway capabilityTierProvider is process-global, not per-authenticated-companion: fleet companions share one tier for approvals, eligibility, and shard backends
description:
Evidence: verified during an52.2 review (2026-07-16). The gateway constructs ONE CapabilityRuntime per process, rooted at a single fixed dir input.startupHydration.companionDataDir (src/boundary/gateway/privileged-core.ts:86-90); getTier() always reads that one captured filePath (src/system/capabilities/runtime.ts:29,40-43) with no companion argument. capabilityTierProvider closes over that single runtime (privileged-core.ts:215) and the SAME closure is handed to every per-connection method runtime (src/boundary/gateway/server.ts:535) and to the approval boundary (server.ts:420, consumed at approval-boundary.ts:224) and eligibility gate (privileged-core.ts:91-96). By decisive contrast, workspace and policy ARE resolved per-authenticated-companion in the same object (server.ts:670-682 resolveConnectionWorkspacePath, :685-706 resolveConnectionPolicyConfig, keyed on connectionStatuses.get(conn).companionId) — tier is not.

Impact: in the one-gateway/N-companion fleet topology, each companion has its own capability-tier.json (PER_COMPANION_OWNER_FILES, settings-contract.ts:63-64; per-member read at startup-owner-files.ts:327-329; proven by capability-tier-per-companion.test.ts), but the gateway hydrates only ONE companionDataDir (bootstrap-helpers.ts:189 -> layout.ts:422-425). So all connected companions share that single companion's tier for tier-gated decisions: autonomous-approval auto-clear (approval-boundary.ts:224), LLM/channel eligibility (privileged-core.ts:91-96), and shard-backend admission (shard-backends.ts:58-72). An honest apprentice companion B, in a fleet whose gateway-rooted tier is autonomous, is treated as autonomous. This is a capability-model limitation shared across three gates, NOT introduced by an52.2 (that branch is a net improvement — it closed the caller-declared-tier spoof) but surfaced by it.

Scope: key capabilityTierProvider on the authenticated connection's companion id in multi-companion mode — resolve a per-companion CapabilityRuntime from the connecting companion's own companionDataDir, mirroring resolveConnectionWorkspacePath / resolveConnectionPolicyConfig. Fix must cover ALL THREE consumers (approvals, eligibility, shard backends) since they share the closure; do not fix only shard backends. Fail closed when the authenticated companion or its tier file is unavailable. Non-goals: single-companion deployments are unaffected (one root = correct); do not change the tier owner-file format or the tier enum.

Acceptance: with a two-companion fleet (A autonomous, B apprentice) on one gateway, B's shard.backend.request, approval auto-clear, and eligibility decisions all resolve to apprentice (B is denied autonomous-only paths) while A is admitted; a multi-companion regression test proves the per-companion resolution for at least the shard-backend and approval gates; single-companion behavior is unchanged.
close_reason: Merged to main in 6ea436d01d (commits e147c43648 + 54c1c2352b, scaffolding cleanup d547040db5); pushed to origin. Fix: new GatewayCapabilityTierResolver keys the gateway capability tier on the authenticated connection's companion id in multi-companion mode, one CapabilityRuntime per fleet companion rooted at that companion's own companionDataDir (hot-reload preserved via file-fingerprint recheck), covering all three consumers: approval auto-clear (authenticatedCompanionId threaded through gate options), eligibility gate (resolveAccess(companionId)), shard-backend admission (connection-scoped zero-arg closure). Fail closed: resolveTier throws on missing/unknown companion or unreadable tier file; single-companion unchanged. Review gate: UBS clean on change range; Codex adversarial review (BLOCK, 2 claimed P1) + independent Opus verification: claim 1 CONFIRMED (LLM eligibility keyed on agent-supplied/strippable correlation.companionId, fail-open to gateway-root tier via resolveAccess(undefined) — real for token-gated purposes background/memory/import_processing) and remediated in 54c1c2352b: server-injected eligibilityCompanionId from runtime.authenticatedCompanionId() on llm.chat+llm.complete, out-of-band from correlation; new resolveAccessStrict throws in multi-companion when id absent, wired only to the gateway LLM client; lenient path retained for gateway-global plugin activation. Claim 2 REFUTED as blocker (pre-existing, out of range) and filed as psfn-framework-an52.5. Final scoped re-verification: CLEAR. Evidence: 2548 tests passed 0 failed across gateway/capabilities/llm/agent/startup areas incl. 4 adversarial eligibility regressions with real tier files and gateway root deliberately autonomous (fallback regression would flip deny->allow) + acceptance regression (fleet A autonomous admitted / B apprentice denied for shard backend, approval auto-clear, eligibility); npm run lint clean; tsc no new errors.

title: Shakedown harness cannot target a kube deployment: add kube transport, kube Postgres proofs, and settings-API tier flip
description:
Evidence: 65rk.1 scope/acceptance target "a locally bootstrapped runtime" only, but the operator decision (2026-07-16 design session) is that the next round tests ONLY the kube deployment, at all three capability tiers. The kube deployment exposes gateway API :10053 and Garden :10054 (deploy/helm/psfn values.yaml ports). capability-tier.json hot-reloads on mtime change (src/system/capabilities/runtime.ts:39-83) and is mutable live via PATCH /api/admin/settings with capabilityTier (src/operator/garden/routes/settings-routes.ts:127-145, settings-service.ts:299-312) — so a three-tier sweep needs zero redeploys, but on kube the flip must go through the settings API, not an owner-file edit on the PVC.

Context: extends the 65rk.1 probe library with a target abstraction (local vs kube). Kube target reaches gateway/Garden/Postgres via kubectl port-forward (or equivalent), and persisted-state proof queries run against the deployment's Postgres.

Scope: (1) target abstraction in the shared probe lib; (2) tier flip via settings API with hot-reload confirmation (re-read settings + observe granted-token change) and guaranteed revert to the pre-run tier on exit, including on abort/kill — extend 65rk.1's exit-trap requirement to the API path; (3) mutation cases scoped to the internal:shakedown channel convention. Non-goals: do not modify the Helm chart; do not add a kube bootstrap path (Artie's PVC persists and is never wiped); do not bypass the settings contract by writing owner files directly.

Acceptance: from a workstation with kubeconfig, the harness runs the three-tier sweep against the live kube deployment and emits per-tier run JSONs; after the run (and after a mid-run kill) the tier is provably restored by re-reading the settings API; no /mnt/ or hardcoded cluster literals in shakedown/harness.
notes:
Implemented on work/65rk5-kube-target @ efa5ce2813. Added PSFN_TARGET (local|kube) abstraction in shakedown/harness/lib/target.mjs — one fail-closed resolver for {chat base, Garden admin base, api key, admin token, Postgres}; kube points PSFN_API_BASE/PSFN_ADMIN_BASE at kubectl port-forwards (:10053/:10054), no hardcoded cluster literals. Kube tier flip goes through PATCH /api/admin/settings {capabilityTier} and confirms the hot-reload by re-reading editors.capabilities.tier from GET /api/admin/settings before that tier's cases run; an unconfirmed flip or HTTP error is a loud non-zero error (proved: 'flip not confirmed within Nms' and 'PATCH ... title: Unified settings save strips the mandatory backup.json encryption block, so Save Settings errors on every real deployment
description:
Evidence (found during PR #98 adversarial review; independently verified against origin/main and the server validator):

buildBackupSettingsPayload (admin-ui/src/routes/settings/settings-page-helpers.ts:713-722) returns ONLY six curated fields (intervalHours, maxRotatingBackups, maxWeeklyBackups, maxMonthlyBackups, mirrorDir, verifyRestore). It drops encryption, groupMode, and maxDailyBackups. Unlike its sibling buildCapabilitiesSettingsPayload (:724, spreads ...current), it takes no current-config argument, so there is nothing to preserve the untouched fields from.

In the unified owner-config save (SettingsPageController.svelte:1054-1056), the backup entry is nextJson = JSON.stringify(buildBackupPayload()) (6 fields) vs currentJson = tryPrettyPrint(backupJson) (the full loaded backup.json). These always differ, so planUnifiedOwnerConfigSaves marks backup hasPendingChange=true and always includes it in the write set (unless the operator has the backup Raw JSON editor dirty, which skips it).

Server rejects the stripped payload fail-closed: saveSubConfig('backup', nextJson) -> saveBackupConfig -> validateBackupConfig (src/system/config/backup-config.ts:143-147, 109-127) -> validateEncryptionConfig throws 'Invalid backup config: encryption must be an object' (:79) because encryption is required (config/backup.seed.json always carries it).

Repro: in Garden settings, change any single curated field (e.g. sessionHistoryBudgetPct), click Save Settings. settings.json commits, then the backup owner-file write throws; banner shows 'Runtime settings saved, but canonical config save failed: Invalid backup config: encryption must be an object'. Net: the headline single Save Settings action errors on any deployment whose backup.json has the mandatory encryption block (i.e. all of them), and the curated backup fields are unsaveable via the primary save. No silent data loss (server fails closed), but a partial commit: settings.json persisted, backup did not.

PRE-EXISTING, not introduced by PR #98: the backup entry construction and the nextJson!==currentJson filter are byte-identical on origin/main (SettingsPageController.svelte:885-905 there), present since garden-ux wave 1 (#95). Bead 9lxg only refactored the entry array into planUnifiedOwnerConfigSaves and added the skip/fail-closed/invariant layer; it neither introduced nor worsened this. Filing here so the wave epic owns the fix. NOTE this bites the operator's live Garden usage today.

Tests miss it because raw-editor-preservation.test.ts uses synthetic {owner, form:1} JSON and never round-trips the real buildBackupPayload against a real backup.json through validateBackupConfig.

Scope: buildBackupSettingsPayload must take the loaded backup owner config and spread it (...getBackupEditorConfig() or equivalent), overlaying only the six curated fields, exactly as buildCapabilitiesSettingsPayload / buildSchedulerPayload already do — preserving encryption, groupMode, and maxDailyBackups. Do NOT weaken the server-side validateBackupConfig encryption requirement. Do NOT change the 9lxg skip/fail-closed/invariant logic (it is correct).

Acceptance criteria: a client-side integration test that round-trips buildBackupPayload() output for a realistic backup.json (with encryption/groupMode/maxDailyBackups) through validateBackupConfig without throwing AND asserts the three non-curated blocks are preserved byte-for-byte; manual repro (change a curated field, Save Settings) succeeds with backup.json intact; existing settings suites stay green.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #99, merged to main at 3556f3faba (fix commits 4d47b59db5 + ac1fc21836). buildBackupSettingsPayload now spreads the loaded backup owner config (data.editors.backup, served from configStore.loadBackup) and overlays only the six curated fields, so encryption/groupMode/maxDailyBackups survive and validateBackupConfig passes. Review found and fixed a companion gap in the same PR: 'backup' added to the saveRawConfig reload list (SettingsPageController.svelte:1199) so a raw backup.json save refreshes data.editors.backup before the next unified save — without it the stale spread would silently revert just-saved hand edits (same clobber class as the wave blocker). Verified on PR tip: svelte-check 0/0, 36/36 settings tests incl. 2 new round-trip regressions.

comments.author: axAilotl

Two regression tests in raw-editor-preservation.test.ts pin the fix: non-curated blocks (encryption/groupMode/maxDailyBackups) preserved byte-for-byte, curated overlay, untouched form round-trips unchanged. Gates green: svelte-check 0/0, build, root lint, settings suites 36/36. Ready to close on merge. Not self-merged — own-authored, awaiting operator review per workflow.

title: Create canonical Helm fleet upgrade guide
description:

Required content:
- State the source-of-truth and values-capture rules before any upgrade.
- Record rollout ordering for welfare grant change b87ba13cbc: gateway before agents; gateway/agent skew safely falls back to pre-welfare FIFO behavior, preserving correctness while anti-starvation protection is temporarily inactive.
- Record the intentional Garden exposure change: the chart renders no direct Garden Ingress or hostPort in either fleetAuth state. With fleetAuth.enabled=false, operator web access after upgrade is kubectl port-forward to the Garden ClusterIP plus ADMIN_TOKEN. With fleetAuth.enabled=true, browser access is only through the authenticated gateway origin. Companion runtime is unaffected.
- Include preflight, exact image pinning, owner migration references, rollout sequence, validation, and rollback/recovery boundaries.
- Link the canonical guide prominently from README.md, docs/setup.md, docs/operations.md, and deploy/helm/psfn/README.md while leaving detailed subsystem procedures in their existing documents.

Non-goals: no chart/runtime changes and no fleet deployment.

It distinguishes fleetAuth-off port-forward + ADMIN_TOKEN access from fleetAuth-on gateway-origin access. 3. It links to detailed owner-migration and fleet-auth procedures rather than duplicating them. 4. README.md, docs/setup.md, docs/operations.md, and the Helm README link to it near their deployment/upgrade entrypoints. 5. npm run verify:repository-hygiene and markdown/link-relevant checks available in the repo pass; git diff --check passes.

The guide covers gateway-before-agent welfare rollout ordering at b87ba13cbc, safe FIFO skew behavior, fleetAuth-off Garden port-forward + ADMIN_TOKEN access, fleetAuth-on gateway-only browser authority, preflight, owner migration references, staged rollout, validation, and recovery boundaries. title: Pi host-side psfn-backup.sh has no retention: NFS share grows ~70GB/month; port GFS pruning to the off-node target
description: Evidence (live, 2026-07-16): /usr/local/bin/psfn-backup.sh on psfn-shard (NOT repo-tracked) runs 6-hourly via psfn-backup.timer, writing auto-kube-<ts> dirs to the dedicated NFS share (psfn_illmatic); 13 dirs / 6.8GB after ~3 days, ~577MB per snapshot, zero pruning — ~70GB/month unbounded. Operator sizing decision: generational policy 4 rotating / 7 daily / 4 weekly / 12 monthly ≈ 16GB steady state, giving 12-month cogsec-event recovery depth. Scope: add GFS pruning to the host script (or repo-track the script first — preferred, it is currently config drift), matching the in-app tier semantics in src/persistence/backups/retention.ts. DESTRUCTIVE-NEAR-BACKUPS: requires explicit operator approval before any live change; no recursive force-delete patterns (use per-dir moves or guarded deletes per the no-destructive-retries rule); prune ONLY auto-kube-* dirs selected by parsed timestamp; mandatory dry-run mode demonstrated first; never touch the frozen pre-cutover dirs on the OLD /mnt/ai share. Apply the same policy when carlini off-node backups land (bead psfn-framework-80rx). Acceptance: operator-approved pruning live on the Pi with a demonstrated dry-run log; NFS steady state bounded per policy; script repo-tracked or drift explicitly accepted by operator.
acceptance_criteria: dry-run shown and approved; pruning live; auto-kube dirs bounded to policy; frozen pre-cutover dirs untouched
notes:
EVIDENCE CORRECTION after reading the live script: psfn-backup.sh DOES prune (keeps 48h of 6-hourlies + 00:xx dailies for 7 days, deletes older) — growth is bounded (~15 dirs / ~9GB), NOT 70GB/month as first filed. The real defects: (1) hard 7-day ceiling — zero weekly/monthly generations, so no cogsec-event recovery depth; (2) prune uses recursive force-delete, contrary to the no-destructive-patterns-near-backups ops rule. Operator approved (2026-07-16): implement GFS 4 rotating / 7 daily / 4 weekly / 12 monthly with a hard invariant that the newest backup always survives; dry-run first. Old /mnt/ai frozen dirs are out of reach by construction (script only touches the psfn-illmatic share).
LIVE (2026-07-16 23:19 UTC): GFS retention deployed to psfn-shard. Old script preserved at /usr/local/bin/psfn-backup.sh.bak-20260716-pre-gfs. title: Show settings validation errors at the field; stop force-navigating to All Fields tab
description:
On curated-save validation failure the page teleports the operator to a different tab.

Evidence:
- saveSimple (SettingsPageController.svelte:944-960) and saveAdvanced (:962-977) call void jumpToSection('advanced-fields') on validation failure (:953, :970), switching the active tab to 'advanced' and scrolling, because applyValidationErrors (:458-494) opens sections there.
- The flash message gives no warning this navigation is about to happen (and per the feedback bead it vanishes in 4s).

Scope: surface validation errors on the field where they occurred, in the tab where the user initiated the save. applyValidationErrors already maps errors to field keys (validationErrorsByField); render those errors at the curated control for that key when one exists (SettingFieldLabel / the field wrapper), not only in the All Fields view. Only auto-navigate when the invalid field has no curated control anywhere, and make the message say that explicitly. Non-goals: do not change backend validation; do not remove the All Fields error display (keep it for fields with no curated control).
acceptance_criteria: Validation errors render inline at the curated field that failed, in the tab where save was pressed. jumpToSection('advanced-fields') is only called for fields with no curated control, and the user-facing message explains why. validationErrorsByField drives curated-field error display. npm run lint passes.
close_reason: Implemented on work/irzz-qq67-feedback (5afa7bae22), merged to feat/garden-ux-irzz at 2c49fe3bcb. Validation errors render inline at the failed curated field via SettingFieldLabel + SETTINGS_FIELD_ERRORS_CONTEXT accessor (validationErrorsByField drives display); jumpToSection('advanced-fields') fires only when an invalid field has no curated control anywhere (resolveValidationNavigation over CURATED_SETTINGS_FIELD_KEYS), with an explanatory notice naming the uncovered fields. Dual blind review (Opus+Pi) + UBS: zero verified blockers. Both reviewers noted nonblocking P2 (field on a non-active curated tab shows persistent banner naming the field but no tab-switch cue) — recorded in wave handoff, not beaded per wave rules. Validation: lint clean, svelte-check 0/0, tests pass.

title: Make settings save feedback persist until dismissed; clean up flash timers
description:
Save feedback self-destructs and leaks timers.

Evidence:
- flash() (SettingsPageController.svelte:637-641) clears saveMessage after 4000ms via setTimeout. flashRaw() (:643-650) does the same per raw editor.
- The setTimeout handles are never stored or cleared; onDestroy (:1074-1081) removes event listeners but not these timers.
- Success and failure messages get identical 4s lifetimes. A failed validation error disappears in 4 seconds while the dirty form remains, leaving no record of what failed.

Scope: errors persist inline near the save button until dismissed or the next save attempt; only success confirmations may auto-dismiss. Store timer handles and clear them on destroy and on each new flash. Keep the visual success/error styling (SettingsPageChrome.svelte:32-39) but drive it from persistent state. Non-goals: do not change the validation error grouping logic (fieldErrors/applyValidationErrors) beyond how the message is displayed.
acceptance_criteria: Save error messages persist until dismissed or a subsequent save; success messages may auto-dismiss. No setTimeout handles leak past component destroy. SettingsPageChrome reflects persistent feedback state. npm run lint passes.
close_reason: Implemented on work/irzz-qq67-feedback (5afa7bae22), merged to feat/garden-ux-irzz at 2c49fe3bcb. Save feedback is a timer-tracked persistent state machine: errors and success-with-skipped-files persist until dismissed or next save (Dismiss button), plain successes auto-dismiss (4s); saveFeedbackTimer + per-editor rawSaveTimers Map cleared on every new flash and onDestroy — no leaked handles (Pi verified: no other setTimeout/setInterval in settings components). SettingsPageChrome driven from persistent state. Dual blind review (Opus+Pi) + UBS: zero verified blockers, no remediation needed. Validation: lint clean, svelte-check 0/0, settings-feedback.test.ts 12/12.

title: Unify settings save model: one save action that routes each field to its owner file
description:
The settings page has three independent write paths with three dirty trackers and three buttons, and they reject each other.

Current state:
- "Save Curated Settings" (SettingsPageController.svelte:1211) -> saveSimple -> runtime payload.
- "Save All Settings" in All Fields tab (AdvancedSettingsMode.svelte:445) -> saveAdvanced -> canonical payload.
- Per-file "Save" buttons in Raw JSON (RawSettingsMode.svelte:59,103) -> saveRawConfig.
- Cross-contamination guard: ensureNoDirtyRawEditorsForGeneralSave (SettingsPageController.svelte:743-751) BLOCKS the general save if any raw editor is dirty, flashing "Unsaved raw editor changes in <files>" — but those raw editors are on a DIFFERENT tab the user cannot see from the curated tab.

Goal (operator direction): one save action that persists whatever is dirty on the page to the specific owner file each field belongs to. The saveSettingsContract orchestration (SettingsPageController.svelte:880-942) already routes runtime payload + per-owner-file saves (providers/scheduler/capabilities/backup) in one call — extend that pattern so a single save commits curated fields, advanced canonical fields, and provider registry together, eliminating the raw-editor-blocking guard as a rejection path. Keep raw JSON editors as an explicit advanced surface with their own clearly-scoped save (they edit owner files directly), but they must not silently block the primary save; surface cross-tab dirty state instead of rejecting.

Scope: consolidate saveSimple/saveAdvanced into one save path; make the primary action label reflect what it writes; surface per-tab dirty state (GardenTabBar already supports an optional count badge, currently unused). Preserve fail-closed validation and owner-file authority (no silent coercion of unknown keys). Non-goals: do not remove the raw JSON editors; do not change the backend owner-file contract.
acceptance_criteria: A single primary save action on the settings page persists curated + advanced + provider-registry changes to their correct owner files in one operation. The ensureNoDirtyRawEditorsForGeneralSave rejection path is removed or replaced with visible cross-tab dirty indication. Save button labels state what they write. Validation remains fail-closed. npm run lint and targeted admin-ui tests pass.
close_reason: Implemented on work/irzz-9lxg-save-model (056487e092 + 2275b6eaf3 + remediation 4a48ee93d6), merged to feat/garden-ux-irzz at 109bda0e89. Unified save routes curated+advanced+provider-registry through saveSettingsContract to owner files in one call; broad ensureNoDirtyRawEditorsForGeneralSave guard replaced: providers/scheduler/capabilities/backup skip-with-honest-note (form changes to skipped files reported NOT saved), settings.json overlap fails closed before any write (its payload IS settings.json so skip is impossible). Dual blind review (Opus+Pi) + UBS; verified blocker (staged settings.json hand-edit clobber under success banner) fixed and re-verified: conflict check precedes updateSettings and all saveSubConfig writes; write-surface==skip-set invariant enforced+tested. Validation: lint clean, svelte-check 0/0, raw-editor-preservation.test.ts 6/6.

title: fleet-restore integration tests fail on main: restore_control marker psql commands fail fast in three tests
description: Evidence: on main 2459be7b0a, 'vitest run src/persistence/backups/fleet-restore.integration.test.ts' fails 3/5 even in isolation, fast (<4s each, not timeouts): 'authenticates the exact durable marker inside schema rollback', 'authenticates query passwords with RFC3986 literal and percent decoding', 'restores exact companion/shared/group scopes and rolls back collisions and partial failures'. Error: 'Fleet restore database marker operation failed: Command failed: /tmp/psfn-postgres-clients-*/psql.mjs --no-password --no-psqlrc --quiet --tuples-only --no-align --set=ON_ERROR_STOP=1 --dbname postgres://...?sslcertmode=disable&require_auth=%21gss%2C%21sspi --command /* restore_marker_prepare */ ...' (thrown at fleet-restore-database-marker.ts:129 executeMarkerSql; also readTargetSchemaState fleet-restore.ts:976). The two passing tests in the same file use the same ephemeral Postgres, so the instance itself boots. Context: could be a real regression in the marker/psql shim path or an environment interaction (psql client shim under /tmp, WSL2 host ada). Related: fleet-auth-family-restore.integration.test.ts and welfare-grant-verifier.integration.test.ts pass in isolation but flake under full-suite load — treat as secondary evidence, not in scope to fix. Scope: root-cause the marker command failure (capture the underlying psql stderr — the wrapped error currently swallows it, which itself violates no-swallowed-errors if confirmed); fix code or test harness as evidence dictates; if purely environmental, document the requirement and make the failure message name it. Acceptance: the three tests pass on main on this machine in isolation AND under the full suite, or the closing comment proves an environment defect with the exact missing dependency named and the error message improved to say so.
acceptance_criteria: vitest run src/persistence/backups/fleet-restore.integration.test.ts passes 5/5 on main, or environment root cause proven and surfaced in the error message; lint passes
notes: Root cause: KRB5CCNAME=FILE:/dev/null in createSanitizedPostgresChildEnv makes libpq's krb5 ccache probe SIGSEGV (exit 139) in every psql/pg_dump child — proven by env bisection (unset/PGPASSFILE ok; FILE:/dev/null segfaults; MEMORY: ok). Production bug, not test-only: same helper drives real restore/backup subprocesses. Fix: MEMORY: ccache (unsupported types fail closed via KRB5_CC_UNKNOWN_TYPE, no ambient fallback) + executeMarkerSql errors now carry exit code/signal/stderr/stdout, credential-redacted (closes the swallowed-stderr violation that hid this). Validation: previously-failing 3 tests + full backups suite 70/70 (agent + orchestrator independently), green under full suite too; lint clean; UBS criticals all pre-existing false positives. Blind dual review (Opus+Pi): cannot-break, recommend merge. Commit 3995ac7669, merged to fix/q9ra-loose-ends-20260716, PR #94. Ready to close on merge.
close_reason: Completed in PR #94 (merge a1b2b86347): commit 3995ac7669 fixes KRB5CCNAME isolation in src/persistence/backups/postgres-connection.ts and restores marker error fidelity in fleet-restore-database-marker.ts; fleet restore/full backup tests and mandatory lint were recorded passing.

title: Complete trusted-host provider recovery when the current subject is unavailable
description: Summary: OPL1.5 requires ordinary provider replacement to prove both the current and new provider subjects. When the current subject is genuinely unavailable, only a distinct repo-owned trusted-host recovery ceremony may replace it. Implement that exact recovery path against the existing fleet-auth authority lifecycle and trusted-host authority floor primitives. The ceremony must pre-bind companion, principal, current provider identity/version, expected new stable provider subject, exact action, reason, expiry and one-time credential; require trusted-host provenance, explicit confirmation, matching new-subject OAuth proof, and strong user-verifying WebAuthn; atomically fence/tombstone the old provider authority and revoke its sessions/JIT grants/challenges before activating the new provider; advance the non-restored monotonic authority floor before restored/old authority can remain usable; record redacted allow/deny audit. Scope: focused boundary service, PostgreSQL transaction/store, repo-owned trusted-host CLI or existing ceremony composition, exact routing/startup wiring, migration/schema only if required, and adversarial tests. Reuse existing shared guards, lifecycle store, passkey/JIT coordinator, and recovery-floor contracts; do not create parallel auth/session abstractions. Non-goals: first-owner bootstrap, ordinary dual-subject provider add/relink/replace, restored account/binding/role reapproval (psfn-framework-v5st), privacy break-glass, or any legacy ADMIN_TOKEN/psfn_token recovery path.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Ordinary provider replace continues to require independently bound current- and new-subject OAuth proofs. 2. The recovery ceremony requires trusted-host provenance, an exact one-time pre-bound credential, explicit confirmation, expected new stable provider-subject OAuth proof, live origin/RP-valid user-verifying WebAuthn, exact companion/principal/current-provider version/action/reason/expiry, and atomic single use. 3. Success first fences/tombstones old provider authority and advances the non-restored monotonic authority floor, then revokes old sessions/JIT grants/challenges and activates only the exact new provider; failures roll back without partial authority. 4. Old/current/restored provider authority cannot authenticate or satisfy lifecycle/JIT after success; wrong/new subject, stale provider version, wrong companion/principal/action, missing proof, expired/replayed/concurrent ceremony, non-trusted ingress, or legacy token all deny. 5. Every allow/deny is durably redacted-audited with no OAuth codes, tokens, cookies, WebAuthn blobs, raw one-time credentials, or unnecessary stable provider identifiers. 6. Disposable PostgreSQL race/rollback/restore tests, focused route/CLI/startup tests, build, mandatory npm run lint, exact UBS v5.3.5 scan, and diff check pass. Worker commits and pushes its branch but leaves the bead open for orchestrator integration.
close_reason: Completed and integrated at feature commit 80f1e603 from implementation 60de23f9. The distinct trusted-host provider recovery ceremony binds exact current/new subject, principal, companion, current credential/floors, origin-valid UV WebAuthn and atomic single use; old authority is tombstoned/fenced before exact new activation, with redacted allow/deny audit and ordinary replace retaining dual proof. Worker validation: 29 focused, 2 recovery PostgreSQL, 22 lifecycle, 5 migration and 28 schema tests, build/DTS, mandatory lint, UBS and diff-check. Integration combined account-reapproval/provider schema migrated deterministically as versions 26/27; 79 tests, build/DTS, lint and diff-check passed.

title: Populate TurnRecord subsystem output refs from durable post-turn effects
description: Summary: The Loom read-side resolver added for psfn-framework-v83d.3 can resolve extractedMemoryIds, concernDeltaRefs, and contactDeltaRefs, but production TurnRecord construction still initializes all three arrays to [] in src/core/agent/substrate-agent/turn-records.ts:402-404 and no later code updates them. Concern candidates are held only in the process-local ConcernCandidateQueue pending array in src/core/intention/concern-candidates.ts:151-190, so a historical TurnRecord cannot currently point to the candidate it produced. Why: without durable ref population, Prompt Monitor subsystemOutputs is structurally correct but live production turns will show no memory/concern/contact outputs even when background extraction or appraisal created them. Scope: define and implement canonical, retry-safe ref recording for memory writes, concern candidate/applied concern outputs, and contact mutations produced from a source turn; keep TurnRecord slim and preserve source-turn provenance across asynchronous background work. Wire refs to the stores used by the Garden read-side resolver and add end-to-end tests from a completed turn through background effects to API turn detail. Non-goals: do not embed memory/concern/contact payloads in TurnRecord; do not add client-side store access; do not weaken subject authorization or expose contact notes/identities in Loom.
design: Prefer a durable source-turn-to-effect receipt/journal or an atomic append-only projection compatible with the background-work effect fence. Do not rewrite historical JSONL records in place. Define and validate one canonical ref grammar before teaching readers to parse prefixes.
acceptance_criteria: A production test completes a turn whose post-turn work writes one memory, one concern output, and one contact mutation, then getSessionTurnDetail returns resolved subsystemOutputs for all three; persisted TurnRecord contains only stable refs (no duplicated payload text); retry/replay does not duplicate refs or effects; deleted/unauthorized targets remain missing or fail closed according to the existing read policy; npm run lint passes.
notes: 2026-07-16 independent adversarial review findings to remediate before closure: (1) HIGH — durable concern candidates become prompt-facing before operator review, consume the active-concern cap, and cannot resume review after restart while the review queue remains process-local; preserve review semantics and restart recovery. (2) MEDIUM/HIGH — emotional contact-update failures are swallowed, allowing a committed mutation without its output ref; fail the effect/projection boundary observably. (3) MEDIUM — the append-only source-turn projection table can still be erased via TRUNCATE; the persistence guard must forbid that destructive path. (4) MEDIUM — Garden renders pending and effect_outcome_unknown projections as if no outputs were referenced; surface explicit non-success states without content leakage. (5) MEDIUM — prior memories relinked during mention-only contact handling are missing from output refs. title: P1: Persist append-only audit for mutated Hub assertion replay
description: Summary: Combined final review of OPL1.18 found that PostgresHubDeviceAssertionReplayStore records mutated same-jti denial only by updating mismatch counters/digests/timestamps on the ephemeral hub_device_assertion_replays row. Cleanup deletes that row after assertion expiry, the table is intentionally excluded from durable backup, and the evidence is not append-only. A forged/mutated replay denial can disappear after TTL plus skew, so the implementation does not provide durable security audit even though exact replay fencing remains correct. Why: replay enforcement state may be ephemeral, but security-denial evidence must be sanitized, append-only, least-privilege and retained/backed up under the fleet_auth audit authority. Scope: transactionally append one redacted mutated-replay denial event to authorization_audit_events or a dedicated append-only durable audit table in the same lock/transaction that increments the ephemeral mismatch counter; bind event to safe jti/digest/issuer/kid/audience/companion/device/session/enrollment context hashes, authority generation/epoch and occurred_at without raw assertion/provider token; deterministic behavior under concurrent duplicates/lost ACK; migrate privileges/indexes/backup/restore and retention semantics. Non-goals: retaining raw signed assertions, making exact byte-identical retries audit spam, removing ephemeral replay cleanup, accepting changed jti reuse, or building the live ingress consumer.
acceptance_criteria: A mutated same-jti replay transactionally denies and appends a sanitized immutable audit event before returning; if the audit append fails the denial still fails closed and no successful consume/result is returned. Cleanup/expiry of hub_device_assertion_replays leaves the durable event queryable and included in the supported fleet_auth backup/restore artifact. The audit table rejects UPDATE/DELETE for runtime, backup and public roles; only the bounded replay function/store can append exact event shape. Concurrent identical mutated attempts have deterministic bounded event semantics (one canonical event or explicitly keyed append set) and lost-ack retry cannot turn denial into allow or corrupt counters. Exact byte-identical retry remains idempotent and does not create denial audit. No raw compact assertion, signature, provider token, place text or caller-controlled actor string is stored; diagnostics are redacted. Migration upgrade/restore, least-privilege, expiry cleanup, concurrency and audit tests, backup verification, build, mandatory lint, exact UBS v5.3.5 and two blind P0/P1 reviews pass.

title: P1: Prevent backup-role replacement of companion authority lineage rows

Why: backup/restore credentials are powerful but cannot become an authorization ceremony; restored or fresh lineages must stay quarantined until the exact trusted-host SECURITY DEFINER reapproval path. title: P1: Route live lifecycle OAuth callbacks before terminal transaction consumption
description: Summary: Second blind post-remediation review of OPL1.5.2 found that beginLifecycleOAuth emits the same configured Discord callback URI as login, while the only production HTTP callback route unconditionally invokes completeCallback. completeCallback consumes the OAuth transaction before checking its kind and then rejects lifecycle transactions as non-login. completeLifecycleOAuthCallback has no production caller. The live gateway therefore cannot create verified evidence/proofs for binding add/remove, provider link/unlink/revoke, principal merge or other lifecycle mutations even though direct broker/store tests pass. Why: test-only proof production makes the lifecycle feature unreachable and creates destructive lost-ack behavior by burning the one transaction on the wrong handler. Scope: regression-first API/broker integration showing a real lifecycle begin -> Discord callback -> verified proof flow; implement kind-aware callback dispatch before any terminal consumption, or an explicitly distinct routed callback with exact redirect registration; preserve login behavior, CSRF/state/PKCE/session/action/actor/role/ceremony binding, one-use semantics, redacted errors, and deterministic replay/lost-ack receipts; wire a bounded authenticated production caller to the lifecycle completion result without widening route authority. Non-goals: direct-provider bypass, accepting caller-supplied evidence, compatibility fallback, changing provider custody, implementing contact/UI surfaces, or reusing consumed transactions.
acceptance_criteria: A failing regression first proves the production callback route consumes then rejects a lifecycle transaction on the exact 5b7b8291 code. After the fix, the single registered callback deterministically inspects transaction kind without consuming it and dispatches login versus lifecycle to exactly one terminal completion path (or a separately registered lifecycle callback proves equivalent isolation). A valid lifecycle transaction produces one verified, action/ceremony/role/actor/principal/session-bound proof reachable through authenticated gateway wiring; login remains unchanged. Wrong kind/path, stale state, PKCE mismatch, session/actor/action mismatch, replay, concurrent duplicate and lost-ack retry fail closed or return the exact prior redacted receipt without double consumption or duplicated mutation. No raw provider token/evidence is exposed. Focused live HTTP/broker/Postgres integration tests, build, mandatory lint, exact UBS v5.3.5 and two blind P0/P1 reviews pass.

Implementation evidence (2026-07-16, work/opl1-dnll-dut9-7-lifecycle-callback):
- Regression first: npm test -- --run src/persistence/postgres/fleet-auth/oauth-session-store.integration.test.ts -t "routes the live shared callback" failed on the live FleetAuthHttpRoutes/GatewayFleetAuthBroker/Postgres path with HTTP 400 oauth_transaction_kind_mismatch after the row had already become status=consumed, verified_provider=NULL, and completed_session_id=NULL.
- Fix: added read-only state/browser/epoch/purpose callback classification before terminal consumption; shared callback now dispatches login or lifecycle exactly once. Login retains the 303/session cookie flow. Lifecycle returns only the purpose-bound verified proof receipt, clears preauth, creates no session, and exposes no OAuth/session token.
- Production caller: POST /v1/fleet-auth/lifecycle/oauth requires one valid session cookie, exact Origin, opaque session-bound CSRF, bounded JSON, a lowercase RFC-4122 ceremony ID, and an allowed action/proof-role pair before creating the purpose-bound transaction.
- Final focused validation: 3 files / 33 tests passed for fleet-auth-routes.test.ts, fleet-auth-broker.test.ts, and oauth-session-store.integration.test.ts. The real Postgres test proves classification leaves the row pending, then the live callback consumes it once and writes exact Discord verified identity while completed_session_id remains NULL.

- Exact UBS: UBS Meta-Runner v5.3.5 with UBS_ENABLE_AUTO_UPDATE=0, --diff --format=jsonl --ci --no-auto-update scanned 8 modified files. High-severity heuristics reviewed: hardcoded-secret hits are test fixtures; host/header/cookie findings are guarded by exact canonical Host/TLS validation, validated return paths, opaque values, and Secure+HttpOnly+SameSite=Lax; no request-derived SQL, unbounded body, tainted sink, eval, or resource leak finding.
