title: P1: Make companion remove and re-add recoverable without restoring old authority
description: Summary: Blind final review of OPL1.5.2 remediation f6b9e5fb..5b7b8291 found that companion.remove writes a permanent non-restored companion authority-floor tombstone, while companion.readd only changes the durable companion row to lifecycle=quarantined and leaves restore_state=live. Both createGatewayAccountReapprovalAuthority in src/persistence/postgres/fleet-auth/gateway-persistence.ts and executeAccountReapproval SQL in reapproval-sql.ts reject the tombstone; SQL also rejects live/quarantined. The implemented remove -> readd path therefore reports allow/quarantined but the same CompanionId can never complete trusted-host reapproval or reactivate, leaving suspended contacts/roles permanently dead. Why: removal must prevent snapshot rollback from restoring old authority, but an explicit authenticated re-add ceremony must be able to establish a fresh generation/lineage for the same stable CompanionId without reviving prior bindings or grants. Scope: regression-first end-to-end lifecycle proof from remove through readd and trusted-host reapproval; define a fail-closed, crash-consistent transition that preserves the permanent floor for old generations yet admits only a newly authenticated authority generation; align sidecar projection, Postgres companion state, restore_state/lifecycle, reapproval checks, audit decision/resource versions and replay behavior; prove lost-ack idempotency and rollback cannot restore pre-remove contacts/roles. Non-goals: silently clearing tombstones, reusing old lineage/generation, automatically restoring suspended bindings/roles, changing CompanionId, compatibility fallback, or implementing contact mutation saga/UI.
acceptance_criteria: A regression first reproduces remove -> readd -> trusted-host reapproval permanent denial on the exact OPL1.5.2 code. After the fix, an authenticated same-CompanionId readd creates a distinct monotonic companion authority generation/lineage and reaches quarantined pending reapproval; one exact trusted-host reapproval atomically activates only that new generation. The permanent floor continues denying every pre-remove snapshot, session, contact binding and role grant; none reactivate without their own fresh authenticated ceremonies. Sidecar and PostgreSQL transitions are crash-consistent and replay/lost-ack idempotent; conflicting decision reuse, stale proof, stale version and rollback fail closed with redacted resource/version-complete audit. Focused lifecycle/restore/reapproval tests, backup verification where affected, build, mandatory lint, exact UBS v5.3.5 and two blind P0/P1 reviews pass.
notes:
Implementation evidence (commit 32700a69):
- Regression-first proof: the exact remove -> same CompanionId re-add -> trusted-host reapproval integration test initially failed in gateway-persistence.ts with "Account authority is permanently tombstoned by non-restored authority".
- Fix: permanent companion removal remains as a stable authority floor; re-add allocates a fresh HMAC-bound monotonic companion lineage, publishes a decision-bound pending floor marker before the database transition, and resumes exact lost-ack replays without clearing old authority. Dedicated companion reapproval activates only the exact current lineage. Old account bindings, grants, and sessions remain suspended and ordinary account reapproval remains denied.
- Crash/restore safety: startup reconciles only exact pending marker/database version tuples; mismatches fail closed. Backup schema v4 preserves a lineage only when it exactly matches the current non-restored floor; older/stale snapshots import quarantined without lineage. Backup-role direct activation and PUBLIC function execution are denied.
- Focused tests passed: authority-floor.test.ts, reapproval.test.ts, authority-lifecycle-store.integration.test.ts (38 tests); selected schema migration/backup/restore/reapproval tests (4 tests); final exact lineage/readd/reconcile/restore selection (4 tests).
- Gates passed: npm run verify:backup-restore; npm run build; npm run lint; git diff --check.
- UBS: exact v5.3.5 scan completed over all 20 changed TypeScript files with exit 0. Raw heuristic findings were reviewed (typed equality and PL/pgSQL/test-fixture patterns); no actionable finding remained. Scanner reported no request-derived SQL, tainted sinks, eval, unhandled async/resource-lifecycle issue, TODO, or debugger.
- Bead intentionally left in_progress for parent integration/review; not closed.
Single bounded post-review remediation (commit 4c7488a7):
- Regression A red proof on 32700a69: a real backup captured after successful remove -> readd -> companion reapproval, then restored with the same non-restored floor, imported the companion as quarantined and retained the old allow audit while clearing ceremonies. Exact replay of the old direct SECURITY DEFINER request incorrectly resolved success. Green fix locks and verifies current authority, active/live companion post-state, consumed exact ceremony, exact lineage/generation/version/readd tuple, authority lineage/generation/global epoch, restore checkpoint, and both companion floor projections before treating an immutable audit as an idempotency receipt. Audit context schema v2 now records authorityLineageId and restoreCheckpoint.
- Regression B red proof on 32700a69: the backup role could update fresh live/quarantined lineage to live/removed and then live/active; both statements resolved. Green guard treats every lineage-bearing non-active row as protected, rejects lifecycle/restore/tuple/version changes and the two-step activation, and admits only the exact still-quarantined monotonic re-add shape projected by the permanent floor. Direct active, tuple stripping, version mutation, restored-state drop, and combined removed/live variants all deny.
- Normal concurrent and sequential lost-ack replay plus remove/readd/reapprove remain green.
- Final focused test pass: authority-floor, reapproval, lifecycle integration, and schema/backup/restore integration; 4 files and 64 tests passed.
- Required gates passed: npm run verify:backup-restore, npm run build, npm run lint, git diff --check.
- Exact UBS v5.3.5: production remediation files scanned with exit 0, 0 critical and 0 warning. A four-file scan including large pre-existing integration fixtures reported only reviewed full-file heuristics (fixture credentials/status comparisons, guarded harness narrowing, fixture JSON parsing); no remediation finding was actionable.
- Bead remains in_progress for parent integration/review and is not closed.

title: P1: Enforce Hub-only signing keys and reject fixture seeds when fleet auth enables
description: Summary: Final review of already-remediated OPL1.18 found two release-blocking key-boundary defects. First, fleet-auth config validates broker assertion and Satellite Hub verifier rings independently but permits the same Ed25519 public key in both; the gateway-held broker private key could then forge Hub device assertions, violating Hub-only device authority. Second, config/fleet-auth.seed.json installs the canonical Hub fixture public key as active through 2099 while the matching private key is committed in hub-device-assertion.test.ts. The label replace-before-enable is not enforced, so a seed-derived configuration can enable fleet auth and accept repository-forgeable Hub assertions. Why: device/place identity must be signed only by Satellite Hub, with no broker/shared/test private material capable of satisfying production verifier trust. Scope: compute canonical SPKI fingerprints for every broker and Hub public key; reject any cross-ring equality/duplicate or unsafe issuer/key ownership before listen and again when resolving the broker private key; make seed/test-only verifier entries cryptographically or explicitly marked unusable in enabled production, while preserving deterministic fixtures through test-local config; add strict seed replacement validation, error messages and key rotation tests. Non-goals: change the Hub assertion format, generate live keys, store private keys, weaken fixture coverage, add compatibility fallback, or implement OPL1.9 attachment/UI. Files: src/system/config/fleet-auth-config.ts/tests, config/fleet-auth.seed.json, Hub assertion tests/fixtures only as needed, startup owner tests.
acceptance_criteria: Enabled config rejects any canonical Ed25519 public-key fingerprint appearing in both broker verifier and Hub verifier rings, regardless of PEM formatting, kid, issuer, status or rotation overlap; broker private-key resolution rechecks it cannot derive any trusted Hub key. Enabled production also rejects every repo-known fixture/test/replace-before-enable Hub key and seed-derived placeholder, while deterministic tests use explicit test-local config and remain valid. A tracked seed cannot be toggled to enabled without replacing unsafe broker/Hub keys and required secrets. Distinct active/retiring broker and Hub rotations remain valid; unknown/revoked/duplicate/fixture keys deny before listen with no fallback. Regression-first config/startup tests, settings contract, build, mandatory lint, exact UBS v5.3.5, and two independent blind final reviews have no unresolved P0/P1.
notes: Implementation commit 7df8fc36 on work/opl1-dnll-dut9-5-hub-key-boundary (pushed). Regression-first evidence: before fix, npm test -- --run src/system/config/fleet-auth-config.test.ts src/system/config/startup-owner-files.test.ts collected 18 tests and failed the four new boundary/startup assertions; after fix the same command passed 18/18. Implemented canonical SHA-256 SPKI fingerprint separation across every broker/Hub key and within-ring duplicate denial; production owner validation rejects replace-before-enable plus current tracked broker seed and canonical Hub fixture fingerprints even after rename/PEM reformat; gateway private-key resolution independently rejects any trusted Hub match; distinct active/retiring rotations remain valid. Updated Postgres gateway fixture to use separate Hub signing material. Gates: npm run verify:settings-contract PASS; npm run build PASS; npm run lint PASS. UBS exact v5.3.5: UBS_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1 /tmp/ultimate_bug_scanner-v5.3.5/ubs --diff --format=jsonl --no-auto-update . scanned all 5 diff files; aggregate exit 1 findings triaged as non-actionable heuristics (public SPKI fingerprint equality, public denylist hashes/pre-existing test credentials, unchanged integration narrowing lines, tracked-fixture JSON.parse); no unresolved P0/P1. Bead deliberately left in_progress for independent reviews/integration.

title: P1: Certify DNLL charge and skills owner migration for Helm upgrades
description: Summary: Charter review found that DNLL.8 and DNLL.9 correctly require charge-policy.json and skills.json under every companion-data config root, but the Helm compatibility path documents only scheduler/capability migration and explicitly refuses to migrate legacy system-root charge/skills. The runtime fails closed, yet there is no checkable old-release to new-release procedure proving these owner files reach every exact companion root without bootstrap.seedOwnerFiles masking the migration. Why: a legitimate production Helm upgrade from the former system-owned layout can fail startup or silently depend on seeding rather than preserving operator state. Scope: regression-first upgrade fixture representing an old release with only system-root charge-policy.json and skills.json; use or extend the existing exact migrate:system-owner-fleet path so it copies/validates each owner into every manifest companion root with provenance, collision/refusal and idempotency semantics; verify exact-image Helm rollout/startup for multiple companions; update repo-owned Helm/operations/setup guidance and chart verification. If automatic Helm compatibility is introduced instead, first extend the live-alpha boundary in docs/specifications.md with scope, validation and beta-removal criteria. Non-goals: env fallback authority, implicit shared charge/skills, bootstrap seeding as migration, legacy alternate readers, off-repo config, or changing DNLL runtime ownership. Likely files: scripts/system-owner-fleet migration/verification modules and tests, deploy/helm/psfn README/templates/hooks only if justified, startup owner tests, docs/operations.md/setup.md/specifications.md only as required.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic old-release fixture containing only system-root charge-policy.json and skills.json migrates through the supported repo command into every exact manifest companion config root, preserving valid bytes/provenance and refusing malformed input, partial fleet, collisions and ambiguous roots without fallback. Repeated identical migration is idempotent; changed reuse requires explicit safe disposition. bootstrap.seedOwnerFiles is disabled in the proof and cannot count as success. An exact-image multi-companion Helm upgrade/startup reads each companions distinct charge/skills owner and no system-root value remains authoritative. Rollback and operator procedure are repo-owned and checkable. Any automatic compatibility is first named in the live-alpha boundary. Regression-first script/startup/Helm tests, settings contract, repository hygiene/public sanitize where docs change, build, mandatory lint, exact UBS v5.3.5, and dual blind P0/P1 review pass.
notes:
Regression-first evidence (2026-07-16): after installing the lockfile-pinned dependencies in the isolated worktree, `node scripts/verify-helm-chart.mjs` reached the new old-release fixture. The exact-byte two-companion fleet fan-out, receipt/idempotency checks, exact-image Helm init commands, and startup owner preflight passed. The malformed source case then failed as intended because `npm run migrate:system-owner-fleet -- --apply --approve skills.json=<sha256>` exited 0, migrated `{"enabled":"not-a-boolean"}`, and retired the source instead of rejecting the canonical skills schema. Implementation must make this exact test pass before creating any receipt/destination.
Implementation and validation evidence (2026-07-16): the supported `migrate:system-owner-fleet` CLI now validates live system-root charge-policy.json and skills.json with their canonical runtime loaders before apply/dry-run can create migration state; scheduler remains excluded because its supported pre-bundled schema must be copied before the separate Helm scheduler migrator. Added focused `scripts/verify-helm-charge-skills-owner-upgrade.mjs` to the `verify:helm-chart` chain. It proves a deterministic old-release fixture with only charge/skills system-root owners: exact dry-run approvals and two manifest destinations; exact-byte fan-out/quarantine/receipt provenance; identical idempotent rerun; safe atomic distinct per-companion evolution; immutable digest-pinned agent/gateway/Garden images and init images; rendered Helm init for both companion roots with seedOwnerFiles=false; fleet startup-owner preflight; no authoritative system-root charge/skills; and no-state-change refusal for malformed charge and skills. Updated Helm/setup/operations runbooks with the fleet-before-release order and whole-fleet backup rollback boundary. Also removed two pre-existing tracked live-host aliases required for public sanitization (comments only). PASS: focused verifier; full npm run verify:helm-chart; 45 targeted migration/evolution/startup tests; npm run verify:settings-contract; npm run verify:public-sanitize; shared-type-guards; model-usage-capture; postgres-only; npm run build; mandatory npm run lint; git diff --check; UBS v5.3.5 exact binary (0 critical, 2 pre-existing JSON.parse warnings in the unrelated k3d E2E file scanned because its hostname comment changed). Review remediation evidence (2026-07-16, commit 6ad167e3): fixed all consolidated dual-blind P1s in one bounded commit atop 53ecadea. Migration plan/apply now requires every exact manifest companionDataDir to pre-exist; roots are pinned and identity-bound before receipt creation, and receipt recovery re-pins every root (including non-schema owners) before quarantine/staging writes. Missing-root regressions prove source preserved and zero receipt/quarantine/staging/destination mutation. Canonical charge/skills validation now runs inside the pinned migration primitive for new source bytes and receipt-bound live owners after source quarantine/completion; malformed recovery/current owners fail closed while valid atomic completed-owner evolution remains supported.

Added repo-owned, durable split snapshot/restore tooling: one cluster/system tree plus one companion/<id> tree per exact root, per-file manifests bound by SHA-256 in a durable family manifest, no exclusions/special files, all-artifact verification before first restore write, and no-overwrite restore only into pre-provisioned empty roots with discard-all-PVC guidance after a partial failure. title: Enforce explicit primary embodiment handoff across Companion UI devices
description: Summary: Preserve the Charter invariant that one companion has at most one primary embodied emanation even when multiple enrolled Companion UI displays authenticate or reconnect. Add a separate gateway-owned embodiment authority and explicit atomic handoff protocol over current enrolled device/session state. A stale/offline reconnect cannot steal primary presence; simultaneous handoffs serialize; ordinary remote text/audio/touch/interrupt input does not force handoff. User logout or switch detaches the human actor without destroying device identity or automatically moving embodiment. Device de-enrollment/revocation safely releases or invalidates its claim; guest/session changes do not elevate. Persist current primary/device generation, handoff decision/reason/time, monotonic version and audit without browser-authoritative place/device claims. Scope: focused embodiment port/store/protocol, Companion UI action/UI for explicit handoff if product-visible, revocation/reconnect integration, concurrency tests. Non-goals: defining consciousness, multi-companion shared embodiment, inferring primary from activity, human identity/device flattening, or letting OAuth alone select room.
acceptance_criteria: Two enrolled displays and two human sessions can attach, but authentication/reconnect alone never creates or changes primary embodiment. Exactly one current primary per companion exists; explicit authorized handoff is atomic, generation-bound and audited. Concurrent handoffs yield one winner; stale/offline reconnect and replay cannot steal primary. Ordinary text/audio/touch/interrupt and browser place/device claims never trigger handoff. Logout/user switch clears human only and preserves device identity/current primary according to explicit policy; device revocation/de-enrollment invalidates its claim safely without assigning another implicitly. Cross-companion and stale generation attempts deny. Regression-first Postgres/concurrency/reconnect/browser E2E, settings contract if touched, build, mandatory lint, exact UBS v5.3.5, and dual blind P0/P1 review pass.

description: Summary: Create a new authenticated end-user portal projection rather than reusing the loopback fleet-status payload. title: Implement exact trusted-host Garden recovery capability
description: Summary: Implement the distinct trusted-host recovery authorization path required when fleet mode disables legacy token recovery. Current config resolves a trusted-host secret and OAuth supports a recovery transaction kind, but Garden has no exact, expiring, single-use recovery capability. Add a gateway-owned request/revocation/consume boundary bound to exact companion, action, typed resource, reason digest, audience, issued/expiry time, current non-restored authority floor, and a repository-owned independently provisioned credential. Sign using the OPL1.6 capability protocol with a distinct recovery kind; consume atomically with exact retry semantics and structured redacted audit. Ordinary owner/admin/member/guest policy never includes recovery. Dedicated recovery endpoints accept only this kind; it cannot authorize routine Garden/WS/memory, grant roles, enroll/replace passkeys, satisfy privacy assurance, or fall back to legacy ADMIN_TOKEN/psfn_token. Credential revocation must defeat issued but unconsumed capability. Scope: gateway recovery store/boundary, capability compiler/schema extension, dedicated narrow Garden routes/verifier, revocation/consume tests and E2E. Non-goals: routine login, owner bootstrap/grant, passkey reenrollment/replacement owned by OPL1.10, non-subject disclosure, or generic emergency admin session.

Concurrent consume permits exactly one first execution; byte-identical transport retry returns the recorded result without redispatch, while mutation or cross-companion reuse denies. Revoking the independently provisioned credential or advancing the recovery authority floor wins over an issued but unconsumed request. Recovery capability works only on explicit dedicated endpoints and cannot access routine Garden/WS/memory, grant roles, enroll/replace passkeys, satisfy WebAuthn/privacy assurance, or mint a normal session. Audit records exact scope/outcome without credential material. Fleet mode never evaluates ADMIN_TOKEN/psfn_token for recovery; feature-off legacy behavior remains unchanged. Regression-first Postgres/race/E2E tests, build, mandatory lint, exact UBS v5.3.5, and dual blind P0/P1 review pass.

title: Make Garden services and audits request-bound and subject-aware
description: Summary: Carry immutable trusted AuthContext, ActorContext, linked decision, action/resource, subject relation, and authority/session versions explicitly from fleet admission through every high-risk Garden handler/service/audit call. Outer admission alone is insufficient because current singleton services receive no principal context, actor identity is caller-controlled or hard-coded, memory JIT keys to unsigned psfn_garden_session/browser UUID/shared bearer digest, and reusable shared-workspace role headers form a parallel authentication system. Refactor request/service contracts rather than storing current context in a mutable singleton closure, which would cross subjects under concurrency. Derive actor/contact/role only from verified context; body/query/header actor fields remain domain data or are rejected, never attribution. Member self/co-subject memory uses request-local contact authority; logout/role/session fencing invalidates JIT. Strong memory.jit.self remains fail-closed until OPL1.10, and all non-subject disclosure remains fail-closed until OPL1.15. Existing confirmation/contact-approval/CogSec workflow requirements remain additional conjunctive checks. Shared-workspace workflow identity stays separate and must be trusted, not browser reusable credential. Scope: route/service contracts, local admin contract, memory/contact/enrollment/session/settings/confirmation/CogSec/shared-workspace handlers, subject-authorized store, structured audit types/history, concurrency tests. Non-goals: implementing WebAuthn, privacy break-glass, or trusted-host recovery.
acceptance_criteria: Immutable request-bound AuthContext/ActorContext and linked decision enter every high-risk service and structured audit record; no mutable global/request-current context exists. Parallel principals cannot observe or mutate each others memory/contact/session/settings/workflow state. Two principals bound to different companions with identical relative paths/IDs cannot cross-read/write filesystem, shell cwd, images, Beads, attachments, or channel artifacts through path/query/body/header substitution; every service derives the exact connection-bound companion workspace and revocation terminates continued access. Browser actor/contact/role/companion/workspace claims never affect trusted attribution or root selection. Member self/co-subject safe memory works only with exact current subject proof; other-contact/private access, strong JIT before OPL1.10, and every non-subject reveal before OPL1.15 deny. title: P1: Prevent caller-controlled authorization correlation data from leaking secrets
description: Summary: The OPL1.5.1 final review found that src/boundary/gateway/fleet-authorization-context.ts accepts any 1-128 character control-free correlationId from unknown caller input, while src/persistence/postgres/fleet-auth/authorization-context-store.ts persists that value verbatim in authorization_audit_events. A caller can set correlationId equal to a session token, Discord evidence identifier, provider subject, or contact identifier and thereby bypass the intended redacted audit actor. Why: durable audit storage must never become a credential or identity-data exfiltration surface; this violates the Blocking Risk Standard and was discovered only after the original OPL1.5.1 one-remediation allowance was consumed. Scope: make authorization correlation gateway-authored or persist only a domain-separated cryptographic digest so unknown request input cannot choose raw audit bytes; preserve safe traceability across allow decisions, semantic denials, infrastructure denials, and post-commit authorization-floor denials; add regression-first adversarial coverage proving supplied secret and identity values never appear raw in the audit table. Non-goals: weaken or omit authorization audits, add speculative compatibility readers, redesign OPL1.6 request IDs, or change unrelated authorization semantics. Files: src/boundary/gateway/fleet-authorization-context.ts, src/persistence/postgres/fleet-auth/authorization-context-store.ts, their focused tests, and production composition only if required.
acceptance_criteria: Regression-first tests demonstrate that correlationId values equal to a session token, evidence identifier, provider subject, and contact identifier never appear raw in authorization_audit_events; stored correlation is gateway-generated or a domain-separated cryptographic digest and remains consistent enough for traceability; allow, ordinary deny, infrastructure-deny, and post-commit floor-deny paths all preserve redaction; malformed inputs fail closed; focused tests, build, npm run lint, exact UBS v5.3.5, and two independent blind final reviews have no unresolved P0/P1 finding.
close_reason: Completed and integrated in PR #97 (merge 4b48377575): commits a389cbe81b/4fdd7736da/d89e2dd4b5 key/redact caller-controlled authorization correlation data; current fleet authorization and audit code stores domain-separated digests, with regression coverage. Integration is an ancestor of the certified PR.

title: P1: Make deferred lifecycle restart preparation and exit ordering deterministic
description: Focused reproduction on 2026-07-16: src/core/tools/lifecycle.test.ts fails 6/43 tests and emits an unhandled process.exit(0). The local fixed-argv restart case times out; deferred restart/rebuild cases observe process.exit even when durable preparation fails or restart strategy/build validation should block execution. The shared asynchronous exit from src/core/tools/lifecycle.ts:997 can escape one test and contaminate later cases. Diagnose the real preparation/dispatch ordering, make completion awaitable and deterministic, and preserve fail-closed restart policy. Scope includes the lifecycle implementation and focused tests needed to prove ordering and cleanup. Non-goals: no arbitrary sleeps, swallowed preparation failures, optional shutdown dependencies, process-exit fallback, or weakened unsupported-strategy/build gates.
acceptance_criteria: All 43 lifecycle tests pass with zero unhandled errors; a local fixed-argv command settles before live transport destruction; deferred restart/rebuild cannot run, stop, or exit before durable preparation succeeds; unsupported strategy and failed build never exit; success exits exactly once only after required notifications/preparation; no arbitrary sleeps/casts/assertions/fallbacks; npm run lint and npm run build pass.
close_reason: Completed in commit b6e89df1. Root cause: executeDeferredRestart/executeDeferredRebuild returned after spawning detached setImmediate work, so post-turn handler completion did not fence notification, build, durable preparation, restart dispatch, final shutdown, or process.exit; later tests restored the exit spy while prior work remained active. Fix: deferred handlers now await the complete ordered sequence and propagate unexpected notifier/shutdown errors; expected build/preparation failures remain notified and fail closed. Tests now await handler completion directly with no lifecycle flush/sleeps, and the real fixed-argv command supplies its required explicit 1000ms timeout before transport destruction. Evidence: regression-first run after test tightening failed 4/43 with 2 unhandled exits; final npm test -- --run src/core/tools/lifecycle.test.ts passed 43/43 with zero unhandled errors; npm run lint passed; npm run build passed; git diff --check passed. Unsupported strategy, missing build command, build failure, and durable preparation failure tests all verify no stop/restart command/exit as applicable; success exits exactly once after preparation and notifications.

title: Complete OPL1.5 ceremonies after unified origin and strong assurance
description: Summary: Complete the final reachable OPL1.5 provider/contact/role ceremony composition after the per-companion authorization resolver, atomic lifecycle authority, durable contact bridge, unified trusted HTTPS origin, and OPL1.10 strong-assurance service are integrated. Wire first-owner bootstrap, ordinary first link, provider add/relink/replacement, current-subject-unavailable recovery, and restore reapproval through focused HTTP/domain composition without expanding gateway main, server, or broker god files. Reuse the OPL1.5 lifecycle state machine and OPL1.10 assurance; do not duplicate WebAuthn, role, or fencing policy. Require current companion/contact validation immediately before activation, exact provider+principal+companion+contact+role tuple binding, fresh database-clock expiry after all relevant locks, exact session rotation/fencing, and one structured redacted allow/deny audit contract carrying provider, companion, contact, role, ceremony, authority/binding/grant/session versions, policy version, and decision. First-owner SQL currently checks expiry using caller-supplied p_at before row-lock work; add lock-wait-past-expiry regression and use fresh database time before making this path reachable. Production must remain bootstrap-only/principalAuthenticationWired=false until every required resolver, assertion, operator-verification, and ceremony route is reachable. Files likely include src/channels/api/server/fleet-auth-routes.ts, focused route/composition modules, src/boundary/gateway/fleet-auth-broker.ts, src/persistence/postgres/fleet-auth/first-owner-sql.ts, reapproval.ts/reapproval-sql.ts, audit persistence/schema, gateway-persistence composition, and focused tests. Why: staged first-owner and restore mechanisms currently fail closed but are unreachable, non-login OAuth kinds reject, and activation does not yet recheck live companion-owned contact truth. Non-goals: implement OPL1.6 origin/signing, duplicate OPL1.10 WebAuthn/JIT policy, weaken first-login pending/no-role, turn contact trustLevel into operator role, allow approval/passkey enrollment alone to elevate, or expose direct agent fleet_auth access.
design: Compose existing authorities: OPL1.6 supplies trusted-origin and signed-hop context; OPL1.10 supplies user-verifying strong assurance and trusted-host confirmation; OPL1.5.1 supplies immutable per-companion authorization context; OPL1.5.2 supplies the sole atomic lifecycle/fencing state machine; OPL1.5.3 supplies current versioned contact truth and durable cross-process lifecycle. Route handlers parse and authenticate only, then call a focused ceremony service. Database transitions recheck current rows and fresh database time under deterministic locks. Denial audit is durably appended outside a rolled-back mutation transaction without converting denial into success. Unknown ceremony kinds and incomplete dependency composition reject.
acceptance_criteria: First-owner bootstrap is production-reachable only through matching OAuth stable subject, user-verifying OPL1.10 WebAuthn, explicit trusted-host confirmation, exact companion/contact/owner tuple, atomic single-use consume/audit, a fresh no-active-owner recheck, and fresh database-clock expiry after locks; mismatch, replay, concurrency, and lock-wait-past-expiry deny. Ordinary link/add/relink/replacement proves the initiating/current and new stable subjects, uses OPL1.10 for privileged principals, checks exact current contact/version/conflicts, rotates or fences sessions, and records approval; unavailable current authentication permits only an audited trusted-host recovery that fences old authority first. Restore reapproval checks the exact current companion-owned contact snapshot/version immediately before activation. Every allow and deny decision writes the structured redacted audit fields without secrets. Pending login, passkey enrollment alone, approval alone, restored state, newly attached subjects, username/header claims, stale versions, and unknown actions never grant authority. Disabled mode retains legacy behavior; enabled incomplete composition remains fail-closed. Focused route/domain/Postgres race/restore tests, production reachability tests, build, mandatory npm run lint, UBS, two blind reviews, and final seam review pass with no P0/P1 or Charter finding.
close_reason: Completed in PR #97 (merge 4b48377575): integration commit 687ae116fe makes first-owner, relink/replacement, and trusted-host recovery ceremonies production-reachable through unified origin and strong-assurance seams.

title: P1: Preserve fleet migration evidence across mutable owner evolution
description: Summary: Fix the cross-bead migration seam discovered after DNLL system-owner fan-out was composed with scheduler schema migration and Garden owner-file writes. Current behavior: src/persistence/system-owner-fleet-migration-execution.ts:54-72 calls verifyDestination for a completed receipt, so the live destination must forever retain the migration-time digest and hard-link identity. A later exact-root scheduler schema migration or legitimate atomic Garden edit replaces that mutable owner, and a receipt retry falsely reports tampering. Separately, src/system/config/scheduler-owner-migration.ts:108 publishes through writeJsonAtomic, which renames without the durable file/parent fsync contract used by receipt state. Why: this can block an otherwise valid migrated fleet on retry or lose the canonical scheduler owner across a power-loss window, violating fail-closed owner authority and Garden mutability. Scope: completed-receipt verification must require retired source absence, exact quarantine and retained staging evidence, plus a current destination that exists as a regular non-symlink file; incomplete receipts must keep exact bytes and identity checks. Publish the scheduler schema replacement through writeFileDurableAtomicSync or a focused durable JSON wrapper. Add the integrated pre-bundled scheduler fan-out -> schema migration -> startup preflight -> already_completed retry path; an atomic post-migration owner edit retry; in-place mutation of hard-linked evidence still denied; and deterministic durable-write/mixed-state regressions. Files: src/persistence/system-owner-fleet-migration-execution.ts:54-72, src/persistence/system-owner-fleet-migration-io.ts:228-260, src/persistence/system-owner-fleet-migration.test.ts, src/system/config/scheduler-owner-migration.ts:35-109, src/system/config/scheduler-owner-migration.test.ts, and focused shared fs test seams if needed. Non-goals: weaken incomplete receipt checks, allow missing/symlink destinations, add runtime fallback readers, infer roots from env, change Helm fleet scope, or broaden generic config writes.
acceptance_criteria: A legacy system-root pre-bundled scheduler can be receipt-fanned to every exact companion root, durably schema-migrated, pass startup owner preflight, and return already_completed on receipt retry. A legitimate atomic Garden-style owner replacement remains valid while quarantine/staging evidence stays exact. In-place mutation of hard-linked migration evidence, missing/symlink destination, changed quarantine, or reappeared retired source fails closed. Scheduler migration publication uses the durable atomic writer and mixed legacy/canonical state never changes bytes. Focused tests, npm run build, and npm run lint pass; UBS and two blind reviews have no unresolved P0/P1/Charter finding.

title: Fsync recovered source-quarantine rename before completion
description: Summary: The schema-v4 owner-file migration retry path can mark a file and receipt completed without making a previously performed source-to-quarantine rename durable. title: Fix tenant-role background-work startup mutating an explicitly provisioned schema
description: Summary: On top of s10mc.2.1, a fully provisioned multi-companion child passes assertPostgresTenantAccessProvisioned and then fails during PostgresBackgroundWorkStore.connect. src/persistence/postgres/background-work-store.ts:289-294 prepends CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS whenever options.schema is set, even when options.role is the explicitly provisioned least-privilege NOLOGIN tenant role. PostgreSQL still requires database CREATE privilege for that DDL, so production-correct tenant roles fail with "permission denied for database". Reproduction: after provisioning certification_companion_a with provisionPostgresTenantAccess, run the real ICP process boot test; the stack fails at background-work-store.ts:295 via ensurePostgresSchemaWithAdvisoryLock. Required fix: tenant-role startup must run only the in-schema migration chain under its advisory lock and must never create or repair the schema. Preserve schema-on-demand behavior only for legacy/non-tenant callers that pass a schema without a role. Add regression coverage proving a role with schema ownership and no database CREATE can connect/migrate the background-work store, and that a missing tenant schema is not auto-created. Scope: background-work store schema bootstrap decision and focused tests. Non-goals: granting CREATE on the database, weakening the tenant preflight, changing production provisioning, shared-schema ownership redesign, or live/Pi/SSH work.
design: Use the presence of an explicit role as the tenant-boundary signal already threaded by runtime-factory.ts. For role-bound schemas, omit the CREATE SCHEMA statement and run the existing migration list under the same advisory lock/search_path. Keep the prior CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS statement only for role-free schema callers.
acceptance_criteria: A provisioned tenant NOLOGIN role with no database CREATE privilege can start PostgresBackgroundWorkStore and use its migrations; the connect path issues no CREATE SCHEMA for role-bound schemas. A missing role-bound schema fails rather than being created or repaired. Existing role-free explicit-schema behavior remains covered. The real ICP certification boot test advances past background-work startup. Focused tests, full npm run lint, npm run build, and git diff --check pass. The fix is committed separately from the s10mc.8 evidence harness.
close_reason: Completed in 8c8a93a8. src/persistence/postgres/background-work-store.ts:289 omits CREATE SCHEMA for role-bound startup while retaining role-free explicit-schema setup; src/persistence/postgres/background-work-store.integration.test.ts:539 proves a tenant role without database CREATE can migrate a pre-provisioned schema and cannot auto-create a missing schema. title: Make owner-file migration bootstrap and partial copies crash-recoverable
description: Summary: The r11o owner-file migration still wedges permanently across documented crashes. system-owner-fleet-migration-io.ts rejects an incomplete receipt-owned temporary copy left by the explicit during_temporary_copy crash on every retry. system-owner-fleet-migration-execution.ts also creates exclusive quarantine/staging directories before the first durable receipt, so a crash in that window strands artifacts that every retry rejects as pre-existing conflicts. Introduce a durable bootstrap ownership state before any migration-owned directory creation and make partial-copy retry safe without trusting or deleting an unidentified replacement. Preserve all descriptor/inode/symlink/TOCTOU protections and exact-source retirement. Scope: receipt state model, directory bootstrap ordering/recovery, partial-copy continuation or safe supersession, cleanup/finalization, docs, and crash tests. Non-goals: weakening conflict denial, path-based check-then-delete, trusting prefix names, or silently cleaning unknown files.
design: Persist and fsync a bootstrap receipt/intent in the already-pinned trusted receipt directory before creating staging/quarantine leaves. Bind every later directory and temporary file to an unpredictable receipt-owned identifier and record its expected identity before relying on it. For an incomplete copy, either resume through the exact already-open/identity-matched object or durably supersede it with a new receipt-owned object while preserving the unidentified/old object for quarantine; never path-check then unlink a possibly replaced leaf. Recovery must distinguish owned partial state from external conflict using durable receipt data and pinned identities.
acceptance_criteria: A crash/restart at every boundary from durable bootstrap intent through quarantine/staging directory creation, mid-temporary-copy, fsync, publish, source quarantine, receipt update, and finalization either resumes to one correct completed migration or safely denies an identified external replacement. No crash before the first in-progress receipt can strand a directory that blocks retry. A partial receipt-owned temporary cannot wedge retry and is never mistaken for or deleted after replacement. Unknown/pre-existing artifacts still deny. Directory/source/destination/staging/receipt/quarantine identities remain pinned and rechecked; exact source inode/digest retirement and replacement preservation+deny remain intact. Adversarial crash/symlink/swap/replacement tests, build, and mandatory npm run lint pass.

title: Retire Discord evidence lifecycle on terminal authority reset
description: Summary: Successful fleet provider revocation deletes Discord evidence snapshots/lifecycle fences and reconciliation may delete fences globally, but DiscordEvidenceLifecycleCoordinator retains affected active entries and renewal timers. The next timer or Discord authority event mutates a missing durable fence; failEntry retries revocation, aggregates the second failure, and the default queueMicrotask background handler throws an uncaught exception that shuts down the gateway. Implement one serialized terminal-authority-reset path that cancels timers and removes affected or all local active entries whenever provider authority/fences are terminally removed. Represent expected external fence ownership loss as a typed terminal result that cleans local state without escalating to the fatal handler; unexpected persistence failures remain fatal. Scope: broker/provider-revoke coordination, lifecycle coordinator/store result contracts, reconciliation/reset integration as required, and regression tests. Non-goals: swallowing unknown database failures or weakening session/evidence revocation.
acceptance_criteria: Provider revocation atomically/deterministically fences durable authority and, through the coordinator serialization queue, cancels the exact principal/provider timer and removes local active/reauthentication state as appropriate. Global authority reset removes every affected active entry. A subsequent scheduled timer or Discord member/observer event is a no-op and cannot crash or restart the gateway. Expected missing/stale fence ownership returns a typed terminal outcome and clears local state; permission, connectivity, corruption, and other unexpected persistence failures still surface fatally. Concurrency tests cover revoke versus timer/event/renewal, duplicate reset, global reset, and rollback behavior. Focused tests, build, and mandatory npm run lint pass.
notes: Implemented in git commit 6dcbe137. Added serialized provider/global reset through the Discord lifecycle queue; typed applied/retired mutation outcomes across Postgres store, runtime, and coordinator; exact/all timer and retained evidence retirement; fatal propagation for unexpected errors; and focused renewal/event/reset/rollback/no-op coverage. Focused test command ran once: 34 passed, 2 Postgres integration tests failed from one missing isRfc4122Uuid import; corrected without rerun per instruction. npm run build passed. npm run lint ran once and exposed psfn-framework-78w8; its one-line correction is included in 6dcbe137, but lint was intentionally not rerun pending full integration lint. Keep open until integration validation.

The one focused run passed 34 tests; two Postgres cases failed only from a missing test import that was corrected, build passed, and the later integration lint passed. title: Bridge companion contact lifecycle to fleet authorization
description: Summary: Add the synchronous/durable cross-process lifecycle port that makes companion contact mutations fence gateway-owned fleet authorization before canonical contact state can diverge. Integrate src/core/contacts PostgreSQL merge, delete, Discord identity unlink, and relevant identity-conflict paths with an agent-to-gateway protocol bound to the authenticated CompanionId. The gateway validates the exact companion and calls the opl1.5 authority state machine; the agent persists a durable idempotent intent/result so crash recovery resumes or safely preserves over-fenced authority. Never let contact trustLevel become operator role, never let a caller choose another companion root, and never use usernames for identity. Scope: port/protocol, companion-side durable lifecycle ledger/outbox, gateway RPC handler, contact store wiring, startup/recovery, and adversarial crash/race tests. Non-goals: generic distributed transactions, direct agent access to fleet_auth, provider/WebAuthn ceremony UI, or cross-companion shared contacts.
design: Use a fail-closed saga: prepare an exact idempotent lifecycle intent in the companion schema, ask the gateway to fence/transition fleet authority, durably record the gateway decision, then commit the canonical contact mutation/finalization. Crashes before gateway acknowledgement retry the same request; crashes after fencing may leave authority safely over-fenced but must never leave stale access active. The gateway derives CompanionId from the authenticated agent connection and rejects payload mismatch. Recovery is bounded, observable, and does not invent success.
acceptance_criteria: Contact merge/delete and Discord identity unlink cannot complete while stale fleet bindings, roles, sessions, grants, challenges, or evidence remain usable. Each request is CompanionId-bound, idempotent, versioned, durable across agent/gateway restart, and replay/mutation safe; another companion cannot address or observe it. Crashes at every prepare/fence/contact-commit/finalize boundary recover deterministically or remain safely over-fenced with visible failure state. Duplicate delivery returns the recorded result; changed reuse denies. Contact trust/privacy/relationship state never grants a PSFN operator role. Production startup wires the bridge and its recovery worker without expanding composition god files. Focused RPC, Postgres, crash/race, build, and mandatory npm run lint pass.
notes: 2026-07-16 gap/threat audit: add an exact versioned companion-owned snapshot proving that one current contact owns a verified Discord subject; total verified-link counts are insufficient. Merge, delete, unlink, implicit duplicate-primary merge, verification, and restored-contact reapproval must use the durable authenticated bridge. Test crashes before/after each database commit, idempotent retry, mutated replay, stale assertions, deleted/reassigned/unverified contacts, and cross-companion contact-ID collisions. Partial failure remains visibly over-fenced/pending. The agent never accesses fleet_auth directly and the gateway derives CompanionId from the authenticated connection.

A recovered attachment already classified confidential/intimate, or one contested upward after its original response was persisted, can therefore leave the companion without the required HITL approval. title: Implement atomic companion binding and role authority lifecycle
description: Summary: Implement the gateway-owned fleet_auth state machine for per-companion contact bindings and base-role grants. Provide focused, typed transitions for initial ordinary binding after an owner exists, role grant/change/revoke, contact/provider unlink, binding conflict suspension, principal merge, contact merge/delete, companion removal, and restore/re-enable quarantine. Every transition must atomically fence affected browser sessions, JIT grants/challenges, Discord evidence, authn/authz versions, binding/grant versions, and the global authority epoch as appropriate, with immutable audit provenance. Historical Discord subjects remain globally unique/tombstoned and cannot move between principals. Scope: state-machine contracts, PostgreSQL transactions/procedures/migrations, bounded gateway persistence port, and adversarial race/restore tests. Non-goals: HTTP/Garden ceremony routes, WebAuthn verification, trusted-host user interface, unified HTTPS proxy, or agent-to-gateway contact transport.
design: Keep transition admission separate from mutation: callers must supply a gateway-internal verified lifecycle decision containing actor principal, exact target principal/provider/companion/contact/role, ceremony kind/id, current authority versions, reason digest, and timestamp. The store rechecks all durable state and versions under locks; caller claims never replace database authority. For contact merge/delete or provider loss, over-fencing is safer than partial reactivation. Unknown actions or impossible state transitions reject. Restored candidates remain quarantined and ordinary transitions cannot activate them.
acceptance_criteria: All named lifecycle transitions have one primary state-machine implementation and reject unknown or stale transitions. Mutations lock/recheck exact principal, provider subject, companion, contact, binding/grant versions, restore state, and authority generation; conflicts or concurrent changes deny. Provider/contact unlink, principal/contact merge/delete, companion removal, and role changes atomically suspend/revoke affected authority and fence sessions, grants, challenges, evidence, versions, and audit state. Provider tombstones remain permanent and cross-principal reuse denies. Restored rows cannot become live through ordinary transitions. No direct raw-pool escape or duplicate policy logic is exposed. Transaction/race/rollback/restore integration tests, build, and mandatory npm run lint pass.
notes:
2026-07-16 gap/threat audit: the lifecycle authority must also model exact multi-provider provenance and revoke, immutable principal source-to-canonical merge aliases with cycle rejection and unchanged historical provider ownership, companion removal/re-add reconciliation, and one structured allow/deny audit contract. Current revoke selects all subjects and mutates rows.at(0), which is unsafe once provider-add exists; browser sessions also lack exact provider-subject authentication provenance. Regression-first cases include current-subject substitution, exact multi-provider revoke, current+new callback binding, replay/concurrent replacement, stale approval/version, role/contact conflicts, principal merge with differing companion roles/contacts, and companion removal/re-add. Reuse existing provider-lifecycle fencing and permanent tombstones; no parallel policy or raw-pool escape.
2026-07-16 implementation evidence: Added migration v13 atomic_authority_lifecycle and one gateway-owned lifecycle state machine covering binding.activate; provider.add/relink/replace/unlink; role.grant/change/revoke; binding.conflict_suspend; contact.unlink/merge/delete; companion.remove/readd; and principal.merge. Admission now strictly validates discriminated decisions, actor/current target/source authn/authz/binding/grant/policy versions, authority generation/global epoch, a live exact-provider actor session, and consumed unexpired gateway OAuth callback rows that durably record the exact verified provider subject. Caller-computable proof digests are checksums only; missing/forged/mismatched callback evidence denies under a database lock, and unique decision/callback receipts prevent replay. Mutations lock/recheck durable authority, use the shared exact provider-revocation primitive and batched non-restored floor fencing, preserve permanent subject ownership, suspend source roles/bindings on immutable cycle-checked principal aliases, quarantine restore/re-add state, fence sessions/JIT/challenges/custody/Discord evidence, advance central versions/epoch, and persist redacted allow/deny audit provenance. Backup snapshot/restore v3 includes companion state, merge aliases, lifecycle audit/counters, with restored rows quarantined. No HTTP/Garden/WebAuthn/OPL1.6/contact-RPC scope was added and no raw pool is exposed.

title: Resolve per-companion fleet authorization context
description: Summary: Implement the production gateway-owned resolver that turns an authenticated fleet session plus exact companion target into a bounded per-companion authorization context. Read current fleet_auth principal, Discord provider subject, principal_contact_bindings, principal_role_grants, authority generation, global epoch, and session authn/authz versions through a focused persistence port. Require exactly one live active binding and base role for the requested companion; contact IDs are companion-local and must never resolve across companion schemas. Discord guild/channel/role evidence may only narrow a separately authorized room entry and can never create or widen a contact binding, PSFN role, trust level, memory authority, or device identity. Scope: resolver domain types, store queries, audit reason codes, production broker wiring, and focused integration tests. Non-goals: provider mutation ceremonies, WebAuthn, unified-origin proxying, Garden route matrix, or contact mutation transport.
design: Place policy in a focused boundary/domain service rather than the broker or gateway composition root. Return immutable AuthContext data containing principal, companion, contact, role, session/version/epoch provenance, and optional bounded evidence reference. Treat missing, multiple, pending, suspended, conflict, revoked, quarantined, stale, or restored authority as explicit deny states. The resolver must use database-consistent reads/locks appropriate to prevent authority from changing between decision and returned context; opl1.6 will bind this decision into a signed hop capability.
acceptance_criteria: An active current session resolves only its exact companion-local active/live contact binding and role, with current principal/provider/session authn+authz versions, authority generation, and global epoch. First login remains pending/no-role. Cross-companion contact-ID collisions, absent or multiple bindings/grants, pending/conflict/suspended/revoked/quarantined/restored rows, stale session or versions, provider tombstones, malformed inputs, and unknown companions deny with audited reason codes. Discord evidence cannot manufacture or widen PSFN authority. Production wiring reaches the resolver without expanding a god file. Focused unit/race/Postgres integration tests, build, and mandatory npm run lint pass.

Current session validation checks principal/global versions but does not join exact active provider, companion-local contact binding, base role, binding/policy versions, or require one unambiguous live binding. Production returns fleet_auth_principal_resolver_unavailable. Include structured allow/deny audit and keep subject contact distinct from operator role/trust. Regression-first cases: pending/quarantined/conflicting/ambiguous, stale session/generation/version, tombstoned provider, unknown action/companion, same contact ID across companions, wrong audience, spoofed headers, and Discord evidence widening attempts. Do not add migrations in this stream unless a review proves unavoidable; coordinate only the narrow gateway-persistence composition seam with .5.2.

title: SessionManager resolution changes meaning under ambient ALS scope and throws mid-turn far from the offending call site; replace with explicit captured-owner read contract
description:
EVIDENCE

From the blind two-reviewer gate (Opus 4.8 + Pi GLM-5.2, independent) on the psfn-framework-9syj.9 fix, commit dba8f2b88e on work/mmo9-postreview-9syj.9: the shipped hotfix wraps the entire handleMessageForTurn body in an AsyncLocalStorage scope (src/core/session/manager/captured-session-owner.ts) and intercepts inside SessionManager.resolveSessionChannelId (src/core/session/manager.ts:438-455). Under a captured owner, resolving the owner or its physical source returns the captured owner; resolving anything else throws "Captured session owner mismatch: active owner is X but nested work requested Y".

Reviewer-verified fragilities (all latent today — none produced a wrong-session read with real inputs, which is why 9syj.9 shipped):

1. The mismatch throw detonates mid-turn at the chokepoint, far from the offending call site (Pi finding M7; Opus concurred). Any future legitimate cross-session read inside a turn — sibling-companion peek, cross-session lookup — becomes a runtime landmine whose error names sessions the caller never touched.
2. withResolvedSessionOwner (manager.ts:432-437) discards sourceChannelId, so a future nested caller that re-resolves the physical source inside a direct buildContext/captureTurnSessionContext ingress hits the mismatch throw (Pi M3; Opus minor #2).
3. getActiveContextSession() (manager.ts:510) bypasses the guard entirely and returns the live mutable active context under a captured owner (Pi M4); it fails closed today only because the one caller (tools/focus.ts:86 fallback) happens to re-enter the guarded path downstream.
4. If the ALS context is ever lost across a queue/emitter/timer escape from the continuation, resolution silently reverts to mutable active-context behavior — the exact 9syj.9 bug re-emerges with no detection. The primary correctness mechanism is invisible in every function signature and unverifiable by the type system.
5. Ingress currently resolves the active context twice before the wrapper (turn-execution-runtime.ts:732 via buildTurnCorrelation, then :745), safe only because both reads are synchronous pre-await (Pi M1).

Operator decision 2026-07-15: the ambient interception is accepted as the P1 hotfix; a proper explicit design is required — one where wrong usage cannot break mid-process: it must fail at the offending call site (compile-time where possible), never as an ambient throw distant from the cause.

CONTEXT

resolveSessionChannelId is the universal session-resolution primitive; its semantics now depend on invisible dynamic scope established up the async tree. History proves both naive shapes fail: explicit-parameter threading missed re-resolving call sites twice (the 9syj.6 fix left five sites → 9syj.8/9syj.9), and ambient interception closes the enumeration hole at the cost of dynamic scoping. The proper design must keep the closure property (a missed call site must be impossible, not merely unlikely) while making intent explicit and locally visible.

SCOPE — required shape

1. Split the resolution surface into explicit verbs:
   a. Ingress resolution — resolves the current mutable active context. Called exactly once at turn admission and by true direct ingress. Refuses to run under an admitted-turn scope by throwing at ITS call site.
   b. An admitted-turn read facade that carries the captured owner as data (e.g. a CapturedSessionReads object constructed at admission, handed through the turn pipeline, and rehydrated for durable background jobs from payload.source.logicalSessionId), exposing the owner-bound operations: buildContext, captureTurnSessionContext, getRecentMessagesAtOrBefore, getRoleEnvelopeRefsForEntries, scheduleAutoCompactionBetweenTurns. Omitting the owner must be a compile error, not a runtime default.
2. Preserve the closure property: admitted-turn code must not be able to reach mutable resolution at all except through a named, auditable escape hatch (e.g. resolveForeignSessionForTurn(reason)) that is test-covered and grep-able.
3. AsyncLocalStorage may remain only as a secondary tripwire. If kept, context loss must fail closed (detected and thrown), never silently revert to mutable resolution.
4. Staged migration: every intermediate commit must be fully consistent — no state where some consumers use the facade while others still depend on ambient interception for correctness.
5. All 9syj.9 runtime guarantees hold throughout; its regression tests pass at every stage.

NON-GOALS

No session-routing redesign. No physical-source attribution changes. No relaxation of source-entry/privacy/durability fences. Do not remove active-context routing for new API/terminal ingress. No unrelated turn-pipeline refactors.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

1. General session resolution has no ambient behavior: no getCapturedSessionOwner read inside resolveSessionChannelId (or its successor); resolution semantics are fully determined by arguments.
2. Every 9syj.9 consumer path takes the captured owner explicitly; adding a new SessionManager read to the turn pipeline without an owner fails to compile rather than silently re-resolving or relying on ambient state.
3. True ingress resolves the active context exactly once at admission — a single call site; the double pre-await read at turn-execution-runtime.ts:732/:745 collapses to one.
4. A deliberate foreign-session read inside a turn works via the escape hatch and is covered by a test; an accidental foreign resolution fails at the offending call site with an error that names that site, not the chokepoint.
5. The 9syj.9 regression tests (foreground api:* race in turn-execution-runtime.test.ts; background mechanism test in manager.test.ts) pass unchanged or strengthened; terminal:* end-to-end race coverage exists (coordinate with the 9syj test-hardening bead — do not duplicate it).
6. Focused tests, npm run lint, npm run build, UBS on changed files, and git diff --check pass.
close_reason: Implemented and integrated: feat/ahxy-s10-shakedown-fixes @ 30a6e6c6f (origin-equal; bead branch work/ahxy-x6ig @ 6ce90df67 = ec556d95c impl + remediation). Explicit captured-owner read contract replaces the 9syj.9 ambient ALS interception: resolveSessionForIngress is the sole mutable admission resolver (called exactly once, refuses under an admitted scope at its own call site; the old double pre-await read collapsed to one); CapturedSessionReads carries the owner as data through the turn pipeline (owner-bound ops omit channelId — ownerless reads do not compile in the turn contracts); durable jobs rehydrate from payload.source; deliberate cross-session reads only via grep-able resolveForeignSessionForTurn(reason); ALS is a fail-closed tripwire (loss throws at the facade, never silent reversion). Dual blind review: BOTH reviewers FAIL with different mechanically-reproduced blockers — Opus: unguarded resolveSessionChannelId let background extraction attribute session A's facts to session B (silent 9syj.9 regression); Pi: unmigrated getRecentMessages in the dynamic-variables callback made every production turn throw at prompt assembly, hidden by mocked harnesses. One remediation (Opus implementer after Codex sandbox read-only flapping): callback contract threads the facade (incl. emotion/self-model reads), resolver is owner-aware fail-closed, session/focus tool handlers migrated to an owner-aware accessor, substrate-agent mock implements the ingress/facade contract (130/130, was 27/130 broken by the impl commit), four new real-SessionManager regressions all red-on-pre-fix. Evidence: 388/388 across 8 suites + 347/347 orchestrator re-run; lint clean; both 9syj.9 regressions preserved/strengthened. Handoff: escape-hatch reason is enforced-present but not yet emitted to an audit sink — wire when the first real caller lands.

title: P1: Pin fleet migration paths and retire the verified source inode
description: Summary: final DNLL review found migration containment/hash checks occur before later pathname-based ensure/link/open/unlink operations. Ancestor or receipt directory symlink swaps can redirect publication, receipt loading follows symlinks, and a source replacement between final hash and unlink can cause deletion of changed/unapproved data. Scope: pin and validate system/receipt/destination directories and file identities for the full operation using descriptor/inode-safe primitives; never follow symlinked receipt or ancestor components. Stage/publish inside migration-owned private directories under pinned destination handles. Retire the exact approved source by atomically moving it into a receipt-owned private quarantine, then re-verify inode/digest/size after the move before marking retired; on changed/replaced source, preserve data and deny. Receipt publication and verification must be durable under the pinned receipt directory. Add directory swap, receipt symlink, ancestor symlink, final-check-to-retirement replacement, and crash/retry tests. Non-goals: no pathname check-then-mutate, deletion of mismatched data, overwrite/merge, or dependence on cooperative external writers for correctness.
acceptance_criteria: Receipt, staging, destination publication, verification, and source retirement remain bound to the originally validated directories/inodes despite ancestor/path swaps. Any source content/inode replacement before retirement is preserved and denied; only the exact approved source is moved into durable receipt-owned quarantine and then recorded retired. Receipt/ancestor/leaf/temp symlinks and pre-existing conflicts deny without writes outside roots. Crash/retry remains deterministic across quarantine/receipt completion. Focused adversarial migration tests and npm run lint pass.

Exact approved sources are renamed into receipt-owned quarantine and reverified before durable retirement; symlink/path swap/replacement/crash regressions are in src/persistence/system-owner-fleet-migration.test.ts.
