title: P1: Separate runtime owner preflight from seed-fixture verification
description: Summary: final DNLL review found scripts/verify-startup-owner-files.ts creates a disposable seed fixture and assigns DATA_DIR whenever no root env is explicit. The standard launcher invokes that same script, so it may report validation passed against the decoy while the real default runtime roots are missing/malformed, or force forbidden shared-root production mode. Scope: split repository seed/schema verification from runtime preflight into explicit modes/entrypoints. Launcher preflight must always resolve and validate the exact same topology/roots the following gateway process will use, including legal defaults, with no fixture injection. Repository gates may build an isolated split system+companion fixture explicitly and prove registry seed validity. Update package scripts and launcher integration tests to execute real no-explicit-root/default-root paths. Non-goals: no DATA_DIR production fallback, hidden temp authority, or skipped owner validation.
acceptance_criteria: Launcher preflight and gateway resolve identical system/companion/fleet roots for explicit and default layouts; missing/malformed real owners fail before start and no disposable fixture can make them pass. Repository seed verification uses an explicit isolated split fixture and cannot be invoked accidentally by launcher. Tests execute the real verifier through launcher for no-root defaults, explicit split roots, multi-companion roots, and missing/malformed cases. verify:startup-owner-files and npm run lint pass.
close_reason: Completed and integrated: commit 001395ea splits scripts/preflight-startup-owner-files.ts (real loadConfig/runtime roots) from scripts/verify-startup-owner-files.ts (explicit isolated repository-seed fixture), and scripts/start-gateway-agent.sh invokes only the runtime preflight. src/app/maintenance/script-verification/start-gateway-agent.test.ts exercises legal defaults, explicit split roots, fleet roots, and missing/malformed owners through the real verifier. On the reconciled feature branch the focused owner/launcher suite passed 65/65, verify:startup-owner-files passed, build passed, and npm run lint passed; independent DNLL final review found no remaining blocking issue in this seam.

title: P1: Validate nested Garden turn events without assertion casts
description: Summary: Garden WebSocket envelope normalization leaves event.data unknown, then prompt-monitor checks only two root strings and casts it to PersistedTurnSnapshot. Nested providerWireMessages, activeTools, prompt context, and related collections are later dereferenced with map, so malformed event values can throw through the uncaught event-bus subscriber instead of being rejected. Scope: add a focused total parser/validator for the persisted turn snapshot/event payload using canonical shared guards and exact allowed fields; normalize optional nested data without assertion casts or any; reject/log malformed events at the boundary so one event cannot kill the subscriber path. Reuse validation across replay/live paths. Non-goals: no permissive coercion, silent fallback, or duplicate domain policy.
acceptance_criteria: Malformed root or nested turn event payloads—including non-array providerWireMessages/activeTools, malformed messages/tools/context, unknown discriminants, and prototype/unknown-field cases—are rejected and surfaced without throwing out of the event subscriber or mutating monitor state. Valid slim/full events preserve semantics. No unchecked PersistedTurnSnapshot assertion or equivalent remains at the WebSocket boundary. Focused adversarial event tests, Garden check/build, and npm run lint pass.
close_reason: Completed and integrated: commit 1c386345 replaces the WebSocket snapshot assertion with focused total parsers split across admin-ui/src/lib/events/turn-snapshot-parser*.ts. They enforce exact records/prototypes/unknown fields, canonical discriminants, correlation identity, and all nested provider/tool/context/plan structures; malformed live payloads surface via onRejectedSnapshot without throwing or mutating monitor state. Adversarial parser coverage includes slim/full/explicit-empty, malformed arrays/messages/tools, prototype pollution, unknown fields, and identity mismatch. Garden check/build, focused tests, root build/lint, and final independent review pass.

title: P1: Preserve plan-derived semantics in slim Garden snapshots
description: Summary: prompt-monitor cloneSnapshot currently coerces absent providerWireMessages and activeTools to empty arrays. Core defines absent activeTools as a signal to derive from the retained plan; promptLoom/server projection is optional. In the fallback path, the coerced empty arrays are consumed as authoritative and a slim plan-backed turn can display false empty provider payload/tools rather than deriving them. The added regression deletes wire messages on a pre-plan fixture and incorrectly blesses []. Scope: preserve undefined versus explicit empty across the boundary, reuse the canonical plan-derivation behavior when server projection is absent, and add fixtures for slim plan-backed turns with missing wire messages/active tools plus explicit-empty cases. Non-goals: no fake defaults or weakening AdminTurn snapshot truth.
acceptance_criteria: Missing providerWireMessages/activeTools remains distinguishable from explicit empty arrays. When promptLoom/server projection is absent, a slim plan-backed turn derives current provider messages/tools from the retained plan exactly as core specifies; explicit empty stays empty. Garden displays truthful state and tests cover plan-backed missing fields, explicit empty, projection present/absent, and immutability. Focused prompt-monitor tests, Garden check/build, and npm run lint pass.
close_reason: Completed and integrated: commit c4a147be preserves undefined versus explicit-empty providerWireMessages/activeTools in Garden snapshots and reuses canonical serializePromptPlanForProvider derivation when projection fields are absent. admin-ui/src/lib/events/prompt-monitor.test.ts covers slim plan-backed derivation, explicit empty authority, projection fallback, and clone immutability. The combined Garden pass completed focused tests, Garden check/build, root build/lint, and independent final review with no P0/P1/Charter finding.

title: P1: Establish one observability call-type authority
description: Summary: Garden repair introduced OBSERVABILITY_CALL_TYPES in src/shared/contracts/runtime.ts but blind review found duplicated value authorities in src/shared/contracts/model-budget.ts, src/primitives/llm/correlation.ts, src/core/turns/observability.ts, src/persistence/sessions/turn-records.ts, and src/operator/garden/telemetry-correlation.ts. Adding or changing a call type can leave runtime validation, budget accounting, persistence, and Garden telemetry disagreeing, violating Charter §12.4. Scope: select one focused shared canonical module/tuple/type guard for observability call types and import it everywhere; remove local literal sets/unions/validators while preserving owner boundaries and avoiding cycles. Check requester provenance for the same class without duplicating already-canonical authority. Non-goals: no widening accepted values, compatibility shims, or unrelated telemetry refactor.
acceptance_criteria: Repository search finds exactly one value authority for observability call types; model budget, LLM correlation, turn observability, turn records, ICP metadata, and Garden telemetry all import/use it and reject unknown values consistently. No dependency cycle or god-contract growth is introduced. Focused validation/persistence/Garden tests, dependency-cycle gate, build, and npm run lint pass.
close_reason: Completed and integrated: commit fe14a003 establishes src/shared/contracts/observability-call-types.ts as the sole tuple/type/guard authority and imports it across model budget, LLM correlation/lane, turn observability, persistence, ICP metadata, model-usage attribution, and Garden telemetry. Repository search confirms one value authority and canonical guard usage; focused correlation validation exists. The combined Garden repair passed root build/lint, Garden check/build, focused tests, and independent final review with no P0/P1/Charter finding.

title: P1: Serialize Discord evidence lifecycle and store generations
description: Summary: Discord evidence event/timer work uses one pending chain, but recordActiveOAuthSession and recordSessionRotation bypass it. Old timer closures have no entry generation/identity check and requireReauthentication deletes whichever newer entry shares the key. PostgreSQL replacement locks the subject while revoke uses an unlocked delete, allowing a concurrent replacement to commit after revoke and leave an untracked positive. Scope: serialize all coordinator mutations, add monotonically unique entry generations/cancellation checks so stale timers and callbacks cannot affect a new login, and make store replace/revoke use the same transaction-scoped principal/provider authority lock and ordering. Revoke-before-refresh must remain fail-closed, close/drain must settle all work, and background errors must not create unhandled orphan authority. Non-goals: no process-local-only lock as the sole database authority and no last-write-wins ambiguity.
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic race tests cover old timer vs new login, event revoke vs callback refresh, session rotation vs expiry, close vs event, replace vs revoke in both commit orders, and cross-process-equivalent DB transaction ordering. No stale task can delete a newer entry or reinsert positive evidence after a completed revoke; no orphan positive remains without active lifecycle state; failures deny and surface. Focused concurrency/PostgreSQL tests, build, and npm run lint pass.
notes: 2026-07-16 commit 63632fba: focused concurrency/PostgreSQL tests and npm run build passed. npm run lint found one test-only optional-call issue, corrected afterward without rerun. Final blind review/integration lint pending.
close_reason: Completed in reviewed commit 63632fba and integrated by d92e1357. Evidence: commit history/stat and current coordinator/store code were read; coordinator mutations use the serialized pending chain and generation-bound lifecycle state, while PostgreSQL activation/invalidation share locked authority generations. The worker's focused concurrency/PostgreSQL suite and build passed; the only one-pass lint finding was corrected and the subsequent full integration npm run lint passed. Final independent OPL1.4 review found no P0/P1 or Charter issue, and the first full feature-branch suite reported no Discord evidence lifecycle/runtime failure.

title: P1: Revoke Discord evidence on bot authority loss and disconnect
description: Summary: lifecycle event translation emits bot GuildMemberUpdate as a human subject-scoped member change. The coordinator therefore matches only active OAuth subjects equal to the bot ID and refreshes nobody when the bot gains/loses a role, even though that changes observation authority for every mapped principal. Disconnect/invalidated/shard loss also has no immediate revocation event. Scope: distinguish observer/bot authority events from human-member events, bind the observer identity to the exact companion adapter, revoke all affected companion positives before recomputation, and immediately revoke on disconnect/invalidated/unavailable states until a fresh ready/current observation succeeds. Cover bot role assignment, bot removal, direct permission overwrite/channel visibility, and private-thread observation loss. Non-goals: no global cross-companion revocation when only one adapter changes and no cached-positive fallback.
acceptance_criteria: Bot role assignment/removal, guild removal, disconnect/invalidated/unavailable, channel overwrite visibility loss, and private-thread observation loss promptly revoke every affected positive for only that companion. Reconnect/ready may restore only after current complete OAuth+bot evidence. Human subject events remain scoped. Production event-source regression tests, cross-companion isolation tests, build, and npm run lint pass.
notes: 2026-07-16 commit 36d8833c: focused observer-loss/event tests, npm run build, and npm run lint passed. Final blind review pending.
close_reason: Completed in commit 36d8833c and integrated by d92e1357. Evidence: commit/stat plus current event source and tests were read; bot member events are distinguished as observer authority, disconnect/invalidated/shard loss emits immediate observer-unavailable revocation, reconnect emits readiness, and companion-scoped coordinator handling preserves isolation. Focused observer-loss/event tests, build, and npm run lint passed on the worker commit. Final independent OPL1.4 review found no P0/P1 or Charter issue; the first integration suite had no related failures.

title: P1: Enforce Discord-evidence reauthentication at session issuance
description: Summary: OPL1.4 lifecycle records an in-memory reauthentication reason when OAuth guild/member evidence is unavailable, invalid, expired, or session-bound renewal fails, but reauthenticationReason has no production caller. GatewayFleetAuthBroker creates/rotates an active session before the lifecycle result, FleetAuth routes set the cookie, and no denial/revocation prevents use. Scope: make lifecycle admission return a typed allow/reauth-required outcome; broker callback and rotation must atomically or compensating-transaction revoke/fence any just-created session and return a stable reauthentication-required denial before a cookie is emitted. Wire exact reason to the fleet-auth HTTP/UI contract without leaking provider details. Expiry timers must fence server authority, not merely retain an in-memory flag. First-owner activation must enter the same lifecycle or explicitly require a new OAuth ceremony. Non-goals: no bearer fallback, no legacy token, and no active fleet session that silently lacks required Discord evidence when mappings apply.
acceptance_criteria: Provider membership outage/malformed evidence during callback produces no usable active cookie/session; rotation/expiry/first-owner activation with unavailable evidence revokes/fences server authority and returns an explicit reauthentication-required response. A later valid OAuth ceremony can recover. Tests cover callback, cookie emission, rotation, expiry, first owner, concurrent failure, audit redaction, and feature-off parity. Focused broker/route/lifecycle tests, build, and npm run lint pass.
notes: 2026-07-16 commit aef5b3b2: 53/56 selected focused tests passed; only three unrelated backup tests failed because pg_dump is unavailable (spawn pg_dump ENOENT). All broker, route, lifecycle, schema migration, and new PostgreSQL fencing tests passed. npm run build and npm run lint passed. Final blind review pending.
close_reason: Completed in commit aef5b3b2 and integrated by d92e1357. Evidence: commit/stat and current broker/route/session-store paths were read; lifecycle admission yields a typed reauthentication-required denial, broker compensation fences server-side sessions, routes suppress cookie issuance and expose the stable denial, and Postgres fencing records the authority change. Worker evidence passed every broker/route/lifecycle/schema/fencing test (53/56 total; only 3 external pg_dump backup cases failed), plus build and lint. Final independent OPL1.4 review found no P0/P1 or Charter issue; the branch integration suite showed no related regression.

title: Validate latest main with local Helm deployment
description:
Summary: Fix and validate the latest origin/main local Helm deployment after the per-companion owner-file migration broke upgrades. The runtime now requires scheduler.json and capability-tier.json under COMPANION_DATA_DIR, but deploy/helm/psfn/templates/_helpers.tpl seeds only SYSTEM_DATA_DIR; an existing split-root release therefore crash-loops agent, gateway, and Garden after upgrade. Also repair the stale deploy/helm/psfn/recovery-chart.sha256 gate.

Scope: add a deterministic Helm verifier regression that fails when per-companion owner files are not placed/migrated into companion-data; implement an explicit, fail-closed, idempotent Helm init migration that preserves existing system-owned values byte-for-byte and only seeds from committed templates for an intentional first install; reject ambiguous divergent source/target states; update deploy/helm/psfn/README.md plus repo operations/setup documentation with the cluster upgrade procedure and validation; regenerate the recovery chart digest through the canonical contract; rebuild/import the exact main image; deploy to local k3d psfn-kube-test; and run full rollout/smoke checks.

Files: deploy/helm/psfn/templates/_helpers.tpl, deploy/helm/psfn/values.yaml and schema/docs/tests as required, scripts/verify-helm-chart.mjs, deploy/helm/psfn/recovery-chart.sha256, docs/operations.md, docs/setup.md, and focused runtime migration helpers/tests if the chart cannot safely own the migration alone.

Why: latest main moved scheduler.json and capability-tier.json to companion ownership without updating the Kubernetes bootstrap/upgrade contract, breaking every existing split-root Helm cluster. Manual file copies are not an acceptable operational workaround; the shipped chart must perform the validated migration and document rollout for other clusters.

Non-goals: no legacy fallback reads from SYSTEM_DATA_DIR at runtime; no silent overwrite of companion-owned values; no remote/live cluster deployment in this task; no deletion of PVCs or unrelated state.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A fast deterministic Helm verification command reproduces the current failure and passes only when the rendered init path places scheduler.json and capability-tier.json in COMPANION_DATA_DIR. 2. Existing clusters with only system-root copies migrate them byte-for-byte exactly once; existing identical target files remain unchanged; divergent source/target values fail closed with an actionable error; intentional fresh installs seed both per-companion owner files only when bootstrap seeding is enabled. 3. npm run verify:helm-chart, focused tests, npm run verify:settings-contract, npm run lint, npm run build, and git diff --check pass. 4. Operations/setup/Helm docs explain the ownership change, upgrade behavior, preflight, rollback, and verification for other clusters. 5. Image tag 0.1.0-kube-<main short SHA> with matching revision label deploys locally at a new Helm revision; agent/gateway/Garden are ready, Garden and gateway return 200, Postgres returns vector, Redis returns PONG, and agent logs meet the current ToolWiringValidator/Ready contract. 6. No remote cluster is modified.
notes:
Implemented commits c7069afc1a, ee3a0ed3b4, and 3d9e9093e6. Local k3d forward-upgrade validation completed on context k3d-psfn-kube-test, namespace psfn-test, release psfn. Exact image localhost/psfn-framework:0.1.0-kube-3d9e9093 has revision label 3d9e9093 and image ID sha256:d4f8d029e4cdeacd452ef2b858bf37dd1c9c20fe1c9c0523c15776ce9c304e7c. Helm revision 18 deployed. Agent/gateway/Garden all rolled out and use the exact image; Garden health and gateway /v1/models returned HTTP 200; pgvector 0.8.1; Redis PONG; ToolWiringValidator passed (23/25 tools) and Agent Ready. Legacy source hashes match retained markers; canonical scheduler has backgroundMaintenance.intervalMs=300000 with retired cadence fields absent. Garden UI enabled after removing a stale local emptyDir overlay that was not in the chart or saved Helm values; revision 18 reapplied chart-owned state. Validation passed: verify:helm-chart, 26 focused tests, verify:settings-contract, lint (NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192), build, git diff --check, and validate-kube-rollout.sh (10/10). Full npm test baseline: 10,317 passed, 45 failed across 24 unrelated files, 6 skipped; failures are outside this Helm/config migration. No remote cluster modified.
Reopened after mandatory git pull --rebase advanced origin/main and rewrote the tested commit range; rebuilding and redeploying exact pushed HEAD 97fbe9b590 before final closure.
Final post-rebase validation: pushed origin/main HEAD 97fbe9b590 (implementation commits d219de7267, 05584e166f, 97fbe9b590). Exact image localhost/psfn-framework:0.1.0-kube-97fbe9b5, revision label 97fbe9b5, image ID sha256:15b06c7acabee7037c20c0a9347249665a907f07accb86b917394fd87ef80dce. Local Helm revision 19 deployed. validate-kube-rollout passed 10/10; all app pods Running on exact tag; contract hash consistent; Garden health/admin transport OK with bundled UI present; gateway models HTTP 200; pgvector and Redis pass; provider routing passes; owner source markers verified and canonical scheduler intervalMs=300000 preserved. HEAD equals origin/main.
close_reason: Completed and revalidated after rebase at pushed origin/main 97fbe9b590; exact image 0.1.0-kube-97fbe9b5 deployed as local Helm revision 19 with 10/10 rollout validation and owner/schema migration evidence.

title: Own lifecycle and Kubernetes self-management operational limits in canonical settings
description:
Context: psfn-framework-xv84 found operational policy spread across src/system/lifecycle/command-runner.ts, kube-helm-rollback.ts, kube-rollout-restart.ts, kube-post-rollout-validation.ts, kube-post-rollout-validation-store.ts, kube-rollback-store.ts, src/app/operator/kube-self-update-transport.ts, src/app/operator/kube-self-update-validation-transport.ts, and src/boundary/gateway/kubernetes-read-api.ts plus kubernetes-rollout-api.ts. The mutable values include command/request timeouts, readiness wait and poll cadence, validation log count, and bounded history retention. Live composition in src/app/agent/control-plane.ts, src/boundary/gateway/kube-self-management-runtime.ts, and src/app/operator/kube-self-update-job-main.ts either repeats literals or takes module defaults.

Scope: design one coherent group in the appropriate existing canonical JSON owner for lifecycle/Kubernetes operational policy; add strict parser/types/seed values; pass them through every real agent, gateway, and operator-job composition; make bounded history stores accept owner-provided retention without losing atomicity; expose the fields through Garden; and add focused contract and reachability tests. Keep host/port/socket and credential wiring in env where already env-owned.

Non-goals: do not move Kubernetes response/body size DoS caps, credential/header length guards, DNS/protocol grammar, or other immutable safety ceilings into mutable settings; do not add a lifecycle.json owner or legacy env fallbacks.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical owner settings control all listed timeouts, wait/poll cadence, validation log count, and history retention in live agent/gateway/operator-job paths; malformed values reject and production has no silent fallback; Garden and seed/default contracts cover them; temporary xv84 deferred baseline notes are removed while genuine size/protocol guards remain documented; npm run verify:settings-contract, npm run verify:hardcoded-settings, targeted lifecycle/Kubernetes tests, npm run lint, npm run build, and git diff --check pass.
notes: Implemented in 1ac4cc81. Added strict settings.json lifecycleKubernetes policy, seed and Garden exposure; wired lifecycle restart, operator command/HTTP/confirmation transports, gateway Kubernetes read/rollout transports, rollout/rollback waits, post-rollout log count, and durable validation/rollback retention. Removed all 13 zhg9 temporary baseline entries while preserving immutable size/protocol guards. Validation: 159 focused tests passed, npm run lint passed, npm run build passed, verify:settings-contract passed, verify:hardcoded-settings passed, git diff --check passed.
close_reason: Completed in 1ac4cc81 with canonical settings ownership and live agent/gateway/operator reachability; 159 focused tests, full lint/build, both settings verifiers, and diff check passed.

title: Own committed voice segmenter thresholds in canonical runtime settings
description:
Context: psfn-framework-xv84 found mutable defaults in src/primitives/voice/reply-stream/segmenter.ts for minimum segment length and maximum buffered length. The pure segmenter already accepts SegmenterConfig, but the live API voice path at src/channels/api/voice-websocket-runtime.ts constructs createAgentReplyStreamBridge without a segmenter config, so production takes module policy.

Scope: add the two thresholds to the appropriate existing canonical JSON settings owner; strictly validate positive integers and max greater than min; thread them through gateway/API voice composition to createAgentReplyStreamBridge; expose them through Garden; and test owner round-trip plus live wiring. Preserve exact-concatenation, no-mid-token, bounded-look-ahead, and fail-closed content-gate laws.

Non-goals: do not change built-in abbreviation protocol, voice security byte limits, eligibility policy, or introduce env authority.
acceptance_criteria: The canonical owner file is authoritative for both live segmenter thresholds; invalid or incoherent values reject; API voice production wiring supplies the resolved config; Garden and seed/default contracts cover the fields; segmenter law tests still pass; temporary xv84 baseline entries are removed; npm run verify:settings-contract, npm run verify:hardcoded-settings, targeted tests, npm run lint, npm run build, and git diff --check pass.
close_reason: Completed in 9c4a733f. settings.json now owns strict voiceReplySegmenter min/max thresholds, validates positive integers and max > min, exposes them through Garden's voice editor, and threads them into the live API committed-segment bridge. The segmenter/bridge no longer contain or accept silent threshold defaults; abbreviation, concatenation, no-mid-token, look-ahead, and content-gate behavior remain intact. Both temporary xv84 baseline entries were removed. Validation: 7 focused suites / 99 tests passed; verify:settings-contract and verify:hardcoded-settings passed; npm run build passed; mandatory full npm run lint passed; git diff --check passed.

title: Own startup wiki hydration volume in canonical runtime settings
description:
Context: psfn-framework-xv84 found three mutable startup-hydration defaults in src/faculties/wiki/startup-hydration.ts: recent session count, recent message count, and maximum context characters. src/app/agent/startup-continuity.ts invokes the hydrator without values, so production silently takes module policy.

Scope: add these wiki hydration-volume fields to the appropriate existing canonical JSON owner, with strict parsing/types/seed values, thread them through the real startup continuity composition, expose them through Garden, and add focused tests for owner parsing and runtime reachability. Review the analogous memory/core-memory hydration settings only to ensure naming and ownership are consistent; changing their behavior is out of scope unless required to avoid duplicate owner concepts.

Non-goals: do not make startup continuity best-effort where it is currently fail-closed, change wiki retrieval semantics, add env overrides, or create a parallel config file.
acceptance_criteria: The canonical owner file is authoritative for wiki recent-session limit, recent-message limit, and context-character cap; production startup passes all three values; invalid owner values reject; Garden exposure and seed/default contracts are covered; the temporary xv84 baseline entries are removed; npm run verify:settings-contract, npm run verify:hardcoded-settings, targeted tests, npm run lint, npm run build, and git diff --check pass.
close_reason: Completed in 509e259f. settings.json now owns the strict wikiStartupHydration group (recentSessionLimit, recentMessageLimit, maxContextChars), production startup requires and passes it to the wiki hydrator, Garden exposes the object in the memory editor, seed values and invalid/unknown-key rejection are tested, and all three temporary xv84 baseline entries are removed. Validation: 4 focused suites / 30 tests passed; verify:settings-contract passed; verify:hardcoded-settings passed; npm run build passed; mandatory full npm run lint passed; git diff --check passed.

title: Move durable background-work tuning into canonical scheduler settings
description:
Context: psfn-framework-xv84 found mutable durable background-work policy still expressed as module defaults. The affected production paths are src/core/agent/background-work/supervisor.ts (max concurrent sessions, lease duration, retry base/max delays, shutdown drain timeout, terminal retention, cleanup cadence), src/core/agent/background-work/post-turn-runtime.ts (foreground-preemption and extraction-drain defer delays), and src/core/agent/substrate-agent.ts around the BackgroundWorkSupervisor construction. Production currently takes the defaults because the constructor seam is not wired.

Scope: define this complete background-work tuning group in the canonical scheduler.json owner contract; add strict parsing/types/seed values, thread the resolved settings through the real startup composition, expose the owner fields through Garden, and cover runtime wiring plus validation. Include the pre-existing lease/retention defaults so the domain does not remain partially hardcoded. Reject malformed or missing security-sensitive data according to the existing owner contract.

Non-goals: do not weaken durable queue invariants, effect fencing, payload validation, database safety ceilings, retry semantics, or add environment-variable authority. Do not create a second settings owner.
acceptance_criteria: scheduler.json is authoritative for all listed background-work tuning; production passes the resolved values to the supervisor and post-turn runtime; strict owner parsing and seed defaults are tested; Garden can read/edit the fields through the existing governed surface; module-level mutable defaults and any temporary xv84 baseline refusals are removed; npm run verify:settings-contract, npm run verify:hardcoded-settings, targeted tests, npm run lint, npm run build, and git diff --check pass.
notes: Implemented on work/companion-life-leg6 in commit 8ce9395e after rebasing onto integration base f70006d2. Validation passed: 130 focused tests across scheduler config, Garden, startup reachability, supervisor, post-turn runtime, and owner migration; verify:settings-contract; verify:hardcoded-settings; full npm run lint; npm run build; git diff --check. Bead intentionally remains open for root review and integration.
close_reason: Completed and integrated in db9e6033 (worker commit 8ce9395e). scheduler.json now strictly owns durable background supervisor and post-turn tuning, startup/Garden wiring is live, all module defaults and seven temporary baseline entries were removed. Independent root validation: 9 affected suites / 158 tests passed; verify:settings-contract and verify:hardcoded-settings passed. Worker validation additionally passed full npm run lint and npm run build after rebasing onto f70006d2.

title: P1: Restore companion-bound ICP cost certification profiles
description: Summary: DNLL updates the ICP harness to load charge-policy.json from companion roots, but src/app/e2e/icp-certification/fixture.ts still applies lowered_warning/lowered_hard profiles only to the leftover system-root charge-policy.json after copying per-companion owners. The harness therefore observes default companion policies and fleet cost-boundary assertions no longer prove distinct warning/hard behavior. Scope: mutate the exact intended companion owner file(s) in the fixture, delete/forbid the system-root decoy, and strengthen certification assertions so each profile proves the companion ID and threshold source actually used. Non-goals: no production fallback, no shared policy, and no test-only bypass of the real gateway resolver.
acceptance_criteria: ICP certification creates no system-root charge-policy.json decoy; lowered_warning and lowered_hard are written to explicit companion roots and produce distinct companion-bound decisions through the production gateway policy resolver. A regression that edits only system root has no effect and fails the certification expectation. Focused fixture/harness integration tests and npm run lint pass.
notes: Fixture now seeds per-companion owner files directly into companion roots and creates no system-root charge-policy/scheduler/capability/skills decoys. lowered_warning/lowered_hard apply only to companion B while A retains the baseline. Extracted createGatewayFleetChargePolicyResolver from gateway main and reused it in the certification harness; integration assertions prove A/B identities, distinct thresholds, and companion-B blocked decisions. Focused fixture + real process harness command passed 4/4 selected tests; npm run lint passed.
close_reason: Completed in main commit db97bfcd4d. ICP certification seeds lowered_warning/lowered_hard only in explicit companion owner roots, removes the system-root decoy, and exercises createGatewayFleetChargePolicyResolver through the process harness. The bead records 4/4 focused fixture/process tests and npm run lint passing; current source and commit ancestry match the acceptance scope.

title: P1: Verify startup owner files for every companion root
description: Summary: canonical scripts/verify-startup-owner-files.ts passes only config.dataDir (SYSTEM_DATA_DIR) and omits companionDataDir, causing src/system/config/startup-owner-files.ts to default per-companion capability-tier.json, scheduler.json, charge-policy.json, and skills.json back to the system root. Correct split deployments fail preflight, system-root decoys can falsely pass, and the verifier never iterates config.companionFleet. title: P1: Make fleet owner migration crash-atomic and durable
description: Summary: blind DNLL review found src/persistence/system-owner-fleet-migration.ts copies each owner file directly to its final destination with COPYFILE_EXCL. A process or host crash during copy can leave a truncated final file while the receipt remains pending; retry sees an existing digest mismatch and rejects permanently rather than recovering. Existing retry coverage injects only after verification/receipt persistence, missing this window. Destination bytes/metadata are also not durably synced before the system-root source is unlinked. Scope: copy to a same-directory uniquely owned temporary regular file with exclusive creation, fsync it, re-verify exact source/destination digest and size, atomically publish without overwrite, fsync the destination directory, durably advance the receipt, and make retry clean or safely resume only migration-owned temp artifacts. Protect against symlinks, attacker/pre-existing temp/final files, changed source, cross-filesystem rename, and crash windows before/after publish/receipt/source retirement. Non-goals: no overwrite/merge, no shared fallback, and no weakening exact digest approvals.
acceptance_criteria: Injected failures during partial temp copy, after temp fsync, after atomic publish, before receipt update, after receipt update, before source retirement, and after unlink all retry deterministically without data loss or accepting a conflicting file. Only exact durable copies reach final paths; pre-existing final/temp conflicts and symlinks deny; source change denies; source is retired only after every destination and receipt are durably verified. Focused crash/retry tests and npm run lint pass.
close_reason: Completed and integrated: commit 6e057c5b adds exclusive same-directory temporary copies, fsync, atomic publication, destination-directory sync, durable receipt advancement, and deterministic fault-injection coverage for copy/publish/receipt/retirement windows in src/persistence/system-owner-fleet-migration.ts and its test. Subsequent commits 9a1618a2 and 5d15967b preserve and strengthen this contract with pinned directories and receipt-owned staging/recovery; 8427741b closes recovered-quarantine durability. All are ancestors of the feature branch; final DNLL review found no remaining blocker and reconciled build/lint pass.

title: Prevent reflection grounding notes from becoming companion self-memories
description: Discovered while integrating psfn-framework-jy6s with psfn-framework-0ggv.1. The jy6s deliberation path appends a read-only evidence-grounding assistant turn to the same internal:reflection:<template> session before the final reflection. The 0ggv.1 extraction lane currently treats every assistant entry in internal:reflection:* as experiential evidence. Its lexical gate accepts text such as 'I found that Alice prefers blue' because it contains first-person language plus a preference word and is an exact assistant excerpt. That can misclassify a tool-grounding summary about another subject as companion-owned durable self experience; the resulting companion_private self_experience can later be recalled in a different primary DM. Scope: add a typed, durable distinction between intermediate grounding/tool-worker turns and final experiential reflection output, and make extraction accept only final experiential assistant turns. Preserve legitimate daily/weekly reflection and free-time extraction. Do not rely on model wording or a prompt-only rule, do not weaken subject authorization, and do not create a legacy text-pattern shim. Relevant files: src/core/scheduler/heartbeat-template-runtime.ts, session turn persistence/metadata contracts, src/faculties/memory/extraction/orchestrator.ts, src/faculties/memory/extraction/self-directed.ts. Link to both parent findings.
acceptance_criteria: A regression models one internal reflection session containing an intermediate assistant grounding note such as 'I found that Alice prefers blue' and a later genuine first-person final reflection. Extraction rejects the grounding note even when exact-cited and lexical checks would otherwise pass, accepts the final experiential reflection, and cannot persist or recall the other subject fact as companion_private self_experience. The distinction is structured and validated at the session/turn boundary rather than inferred from prose. Existing free-time and daily/weekly reflection extraction tests pass; npm run lint and build pass.
close_reason: Completed and integrated in b46f8527 (worker commit a8c4771b). Root review confirmed canonical reflection-journal final output is projected through a typed final_output seam, intermediate tool_grounding turns are rejected, and ordinary reflection session persistence remains disabled. Independent validation: 7 affected test files, 114 tests passed, including persist/recall regression proving 'I found that Alice prefers blue' is neither persisted nor recalled while genuine final reflection is companion_private self_experience.

title: P1: Refresh Discord evidence on authority changes and expiry
description: Summary: blind review of opl1.4 commit 2ecb15d6 found that positive Discord room evidence is refreshed only in the active-principal OAuth callback. There is no production listener or bounded renewal path for guild membership, member roles, channel overwrites/deletion, or private-thread membership changes, and session rotation does not refresh. Positive evidence can therefore remain accepted until its configured TTL (currently potentially one hour), while an expired or startup-time bot_absent snapshot cannot recover without another full login. src/boundary/gateway/fleet-auth-broker.ts refreshes only at callback; src/channels/discord/adapter.ts has no evidence authority-change listeners; src/boundary/fleet-auth/discord-evidence-types.ts accepts positive snapshots until expiry; gateway main starts the OAuth API before Discord clients, making a permanent-for-session bot_absent snapshot possible. Scope: add a production evidence lifecycle coordinator that revokes/replaces evidence promptly on bot-observed guild/member/role/channel/overwrite/thread changes, performs bounded scheduled renewal before/at TTL for active sessions/subjects without leaking OAuth tokens, and provides an explicit safe reauth requirement where provider OAuth evidence cannot be refreshed from custody. Close the startup ordering gap so bot readiness can renew prior bot_absent evidence. Tests must exercise the production lifecycle rather than manually calling refresh twice. Non-goals: do not extend evidence TTL, persist browser-readable provider tokens, turn Discord events into PSFN role/trust/contact authority, or add a permissive cache fallback.
acceptance_criteria: While a fleet session remains active, removal or change of guild membership, member roles, mapped channel/overwrites, bot membership/readiness, or private-thread membership causes prompt fail-closed evidence replacement/revocation. Evidence at or before expiry has a bounded automatic renewal path when current provider evidence is securely available, otherwise the session is explicitly required to reauthenticate and old evidence remains denied. A login before the Discord bot is ready can recover after readiness without a second silent authorization gap. Regression tests drive the actual production coordinator/listeners/scheduler, prove stale positive evidence cannot authorize after change/expiry, prove cross-companion isolation, and prove no provider token leaves gateway custody. Targeted lifecycle tests, PostgreSQL denial coverage, build, and npm run lint pass.
notes:
2026-07-16 remediation commit 3b348c56 adds production lifecycle coordination, bot authority-change hooks, startup/session/renewal/reauth handling, bounded non-secret membership custody, and DB authority denial coverage. One-pass focused lifecycle/runtime/DB run passed 13/13; npm run build passed. npm run lint failed once on 5 unnecessary-condition assertions; all 5 final-diff assertions were corrected afterward and lint was intentionally not rerun. Blind re-review and integration lint remain required before closure.
2026-07-16 second blind review rejected 3b348c56 with three P1s: reauthenticationReason has no production enforcement before cookie/session use (zhn1); bot self-role/disconnect authority changes can leave stale positives (sitf); coordinator and PostgreSQL replace/revoke races lack shared serialization/generation fencing and can orphan positives (y1rw). Confirmed correct: production reachability/start-before-serve, GuildMembers intent/partials, ready recovery, companion isolation, revoke-first shape, non-secret bounded membership custody, unchanged TTL, permission math/veto/private-thread, exact store bindings, and no role/trust/contact/memory conversion.
close_reason: Completed by 3b348c56 with P1 follow-up remediations 63632fba, 36d8833c, and aef5b3b2, all integrated at d92e1357. Evidence: commit history and current production coordinator/event/store wiring were read; lifecycle renewal, bot readiness and authority-change revocation, session reauthentication fencing, shared serialization/generations, and companion isolation are present. Worker focused lifecycle/runtime/Postgres tests passed; follow-up focused suites/build/lint passed as recorded; the later full integration npm run lint/build passed and no OPL1.4 tests failed in the first feature-branch suite. Final independent review reported PASS with no P0/P1 or Charter issue.

title: P1: Migrate shared owner files safely across existing split fleets
description: Summary: the registry-driven legacy cutover moves a file from one legacy root to one companion and retires the source, but existing split fleets currently keep charge-policy.json and skills.json in SYSTEM_DATA_DIR. The default cutover does not discover that source, and pointing legacy-data-dir at SYSTEM_DATA_DIR can copy to only one companion before deleting it, leaving the rest unable to start. Scope: add an explicit receipt-bearing system-owner re-root migration for current split fleets. It must identify one source by exact digest, enumerate the configured companions, copy without overwrite or merge to every companion root, verify every destination, survive partial failure/retry deterministically, and retire the source only after all destinations are verified. Name the temporary support in docs/specifications.md Live Alpha Migration Boundary with validation and beta-removal criteria; update operations/setup. Non-goals: no silent startup hydration, no dual-read fallback, and no automatic conflict resolution. Discovered by blind review of dnll.6/.8/.9.
acceptance_criteria: A current split fleet with system-root charge-policy.json and skills.json can run one explicit migration that copies exact bytes to every configured companion root, records source/destination digests and completion, refuses conflicts or changed source, retries partial completion safely, and removes or retires the source only after all companions verify. Startup then passes for every companion. Live-alpha boundary and operator docs name scope, validation, and beta removal. Focused migration/conflict/retry tests, verify:startup-owner-files, and npm run lint pass.
notes: 2026-07-16 remediation commit bc4953b5: focused migration suite passed 3 tests; verify:startup-owner-files passed; npm run lint passed. No gates rerun. Blind full-range re-review pending.

Regression coverage lives in src/persistence/system-owner-fleet-migration.test.ts. Follow-up P1 hardening landed in 6e057c5b, 9a1618a2, 5d15967b, and 8427741b. title: P1: Resolve gateway conversation cost-breaker charge policy per companion
description: Summary: dnll.8 moves charge-policy.json to each companion, but the gateway IcpConversationCostBreaker still holds one process-wide chargePolicy and applies it to every correlation. In a fleet, a correlation for companion B can therefore be admitted or denied using companion A or the gateway bootstrap companion budget, contradicting per-companion fatigue individuation and measuring per-companion ledgers against the wrong policy. Scope: bind gateway cost-breaker evaluation to the authoritative companion identity carried by each correlation and resolve that companion's charge policy from its companion data root. Fail closed when a correlation has no valid companion identity or no policy. Add a regression test with two companions and distinct budgets. Non-goals: no changes to agent-side fatigue ledgers or unrelated gateway capability-tier checks. Files: inspect src/app/gateway/main.ts and the IcpConversationCostBreaker construction/evaluation modules plus fleet correlation routing. Discovered during the dnll.8 post-commit adversarial audit.
acceptance_criteria: Two simultaneous fleet correlations for different companion IDs are evaluated against their own charge-policy.json budgets; changing companion A policy cannot alter companion B decision. Missing, unknown, or mismatched companion identity/policy denies without a default-companion fallback. A focused regression test, npm run lint, and relevant type/build checks pass.

title: P1: Route deliberation-mode reflections through the base identity prompt stack
description: Summary: Scheduled reflection templates configured with mode=deliberation bypass SubstrateAgent prompt assembly and call LLMProviderPort directly. In src/core/scheduler/heartbeat-template-runtime.ts:614-634, runTemplateDeliberation passes the narrative prompt to runExperientialTemplateDeliberation/runDeliberation; src/core/scheduler/heartbeat-template-runtime/experiential-deliberation.ts:38-96 supplies bespoke stage system prompts. Why it matters: psfn-framework-i3yx removes duplicate persona text from reflection user messages based on the invariant that the base identity system stack remains present, but default daily-review and weekly-review templates are deliberation-mode when llmProvider is wired, so their identity grounding would be weaker and the issue acceptance cannot be proven for those turns. Scope: design and implement one canonical route that preserves the bounded multi-stage deliberation behavior while applying the same authoritative base identity/policy stack required for ordinary companion turns; add regression coverage that inspects provider system prompts for deliberation reflection stages. Non-goals: do not restore persona/description/scenario copies to reflection user messages, do not add an alternate identity source, and do not weaken deliberation budgets or grounding policy.

Captures the exact canonical prompt-stack/runtime prefix at ordinary default prompt assembly, requires it fail-closed for reflection deliberation, and prepends it to every experiential stage plus non-experiential voice/aggregator system prompt without copying identity into user messages. title: P1: Preserve captured API session owner across turn reads and background work
description: Final-check finding against psfn-framework-9syj.6 remediation b1c66abf125b20f0b1d8335b4d226d7707668110, integrated in PR #79 at 61359e23cf. Turn admission captures TurnSessionIdentity.logicalSessionId in src/core/agent/substrate-agent/turn-execution-runtime.ts, but SessionManager read/background APIs treat that already-canonical api:* owner as a mutable source again: captureTurnSessionContext (src/core/session/manager.ts:1275), buildContext (:1334), scheduleAutoCompactionBetweenTurns (:862), getRoleEnvelopeRefsForEntries (:1193), and getRecentMessagesAtOrBefore (:1847) call resolveSessionChannelId. shouldOverrideSessionContext returns true for every api:* or terminal:* id, so after setActiveContextSession changes, the old turn can read the future API session during prompt assembly and its durable memory/emotion/compaction jobs can read the wrong owner then fail captured source-entry fences. Scope: introduce a fail-closed canonical-session read/background boundary or explicit captured-owner parameter and route every admitted-turn consumer through it without re-resolving; preserve mutable source resolution for true ingress/direct callers. Cover API and terminal active-context changes during prompt capture/build and before background jobs. Non-goals: no session-routing redesign, no changes to physical-source attribution, no relaxation of source-entry fences, and no unrelated turn-pipeline refactor.
acceptance_criteria: 1. After an API or terminal turn captures logical owner A, switching active context to B before captureTurnSessionContext/buildContext cannot expose B entries or metadata to the admitted turn. 2. getRecentMessagesAtOrBefore, role-envelope lookup, memory/emotion extraction, and scheduled auto-compaction for the captured turn remain bound to A after the active context changes; no cognition is dropped solely from re-resolution to B. 3. True ingress calls using a physical API/terminal source still resolve the current active context exactly once. 4. Regression tests exercise reset/context-switch races for prompt reads and background consumers. 5. Focused tests, npm run lint, npm run build, and git diff --check pass.
notes: GitHub issue: https://github.com/CGIC-AI/psfn-framework/issues/83. Operator explicitly accepted tracking this final-check P1 as follow-up and directed PR #79 to merge at integrated head 61359e23cf.
close_reason: Fixed in commit dba8f2b88e on work/mmo9-postreview-9syj.9, PR #86 (fixes GitHub issue #83). Implementation: captured-owner ALS boundary (src/core/session/manager/captured-session-owner.ts) wrapping handleMessageForTurn, interception at the resolveSessionChannelId chokepoint (fail-closed mismatch throw), background jobs re-pinned via withStableRecordedTurnEligibilitySnapshot from payload.source.logicalSessionId. Evidence: focused tests 334 passed, npm run lint + build + git diff --check pass; UBS change-range scan zero error-level findings; blind adversarial gate (Opus 4.8 + Pi GLM-5.2) returned zero blockers with converging verification of all five acceptance criteria. Coverage debt filed as psfn-framework-9syj.10; S11 design rework filed as psfn-framework-x6ig.

title: P1: Stop captured API turn owners from being re-resolved
description:
Final-check finding for PR #79 / psfn-framework-9syj.6 at immutable head b1c66abf125b20f0b1d8335b4d226d7707668110.

Summary: turn execution now captures a canonical TurnSessionIdentity and explicit L0 writes correctly bypass mutable routing, but SessionManager read and background-work APIs cannot distinguish an already-captured logical owner from an ingress/source identifier. For captured owners beginning with api: or terminal:, they call resolveSessionChannelId again. If setActiveContextSession changes after admission, the immutable old owner is rebound to the future active context.

Concrete paths:
- src/core/agent/substrate-agent/turn-execution/pre-turn-state.ts:358,417,427,612-624 passes the captured logical id to SessionManager, but src/core/session/manager.ts:464-468,1285,1637-1639,1673-1675 re-resolves it.
- src/core/agent/substrate-agent/turn-execution/prompt-assembly.ts:480-500 passes the captured logical id to buildContext, but src/core/session/manager.ts:1348 re-resolves it. A concurrent API active-session switch can therefore assemble the accepted turn with another partner/session history while persisting its L0 rows under the captured owner: a privacy/isolation failure.
- src/core/agent/substrate-agent/turn-support-runtime.ts:471-476 asks for role-envelope refs under the captured owner, but src/core/session/manager.ts:1193-1214 re-resolves and can silently omit or misassociate audit refs.
- Durable background jobs correctly persist payload.source.logicalSessionId, but src/core/agent/background-work/post-turn-runtime.ts:202-205,255-260,289-305 later calls getRecentMessagesAtOrBefore, captureAutoCompactionRecentEntries, and scheduleAutoCompactionBetweenTurns; src/core/session/manager.ts:862-864,952-956,1858-1861 re-resolves the captured api: owner. After an active-context change, the bounded source-entry check reads the future session and defers memory extraction, emotion appraisal, and compaction instead of processing the captured turn; compaction can also be targeted to the wrong session.

Why P1: this is a partner-data privacy/isolation path and breaks the core acceptance requirement that prior in-flight/recovered work remains fenced to the turn-start owner while future turns use the new owner.

Scope: introduce an explicit already-resolved or captured logical-session read contract and thread the captured identity through turn context reads, role-envelope lookup, and all background cognition reads and writes. Preserve physical source provenance and exact TurnRecord eligibility, fingerprint, tombstone, duplicate, and cross-process fences. Add regression coverage using real SessionManager and SessionStore for an API turn captured under owner A, active context switched to owner B after admission, and recovered/background execution.

Non-goals: do not remove active-context routing for new API or terminal ingress; do not add multi-owner fallback lookup; do not weaken exact source eligibility, privacy, or durability fences; do not redesign route reset semantics.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A real SessionManager and SessionStore API turn captures owner A once, then active context switches to owner B; every pre-turn read, prompt/session snapshot, L0 write, role-envelope lookup, TurnRecord, and post-turn manifest remains bound to owner A, with no owner-B content read or written.
2. Future API and terminal turns after the switch resolve owner B normally; passing a captured logical owner through the new explicit contract never invokes mutable source or active-context routing.
3. Recovered delivery and all durable background jobs for the old turn read owner A bounded source entries and execute the exact manifest once after the active-context switch; memory extraction, emotion appraisal, and compaction neither defer from a false missing-source result nor touch owner B.
4. Wyoming observability session ids remain telemetry-only and never become durable session ownership.
5. Exact source, owner, fingerprint, tombstone, duplicate, privacy, and cross-process fences remain fail closed.
6. Focused SessionManager, turn-runtime, and background-work tests pass, including a real Postgres fingerprint/replay case where applicable; npm run lint, npm run build, UBS, and git diff --check pass.
close_reason: Duplicate tracking of the same PR #79 final-check defect as psfn-framework-9syj.9 (GitHub issue #83). Runtime defect fixed by 9syj.9 commit dba8f2b88e (blind Opus+Pi review gate: zero blockers; foreground and background reads verified bound to the captured owner). The explicit read-contract requirement this bead's scope demanded (its acceptance criterion 2) is NOT satisfied by the ALS hotfix and is carried forward verbatim into psfn-framework-x6ig (P1, S11).

title: Bind Hub device assertions to the caller's expected session
description: Problem: Framework PR #82's final merge validation proved that src/boundary/fleet-auth/hub-device-assertion.ts validates signed Hub assertions against expected companion, device, enrollment version, and status, but HubDeviceAssertionExpectedBinding has no expected session identifier and verification returns claims.session_id without comparing it to the caller's handshake session. A byte-identical assertion signed for session A can therefore be accepted during session B's handshake. Scope: add the caller's exact session ID to the expected binding contract, compare it to signed claims.session_id before replay consumption/acceptance, and propagate the required field through every production/test caller. Preserve byte-identical retry behavior only for the same expected session. Add deterministic unit and real replay-path coverage for A-to-B rejection and A-to-A identical retry acceptance. Files include src/boundary/fleet-auth/hub-device-assertion.ts, its tests, gateway persistence port/callers, and any shared fixtures/types reached by compilation. Why: opl1.18 requires assertions to bind the exact enrolled device/session; accepting cross-session replay breaks the core device authority boundary. Non-goals: wire the downstream Companion UI handshake (tracked by opl1.9), change assertion canonical bytes/claims, alter Hub signing, or broaden replay policy.
acceptance_criteria: HubDeviceAssertionExpectedBinding requires a non-empty exact sessionId; verification rejects signed session_id mismatch before replay consumption and never returns a principal for session B using session A's assertion; identical A-to-A retry remains accepted under existing digest/jti semantics; all production callers compile and pass an expected session; focused verifier and real PostgreSQL replay tests, mandatory npm run lint, build, settings contract, and diff check pass; no Pi/live deployment.
close_reason: Completed and merged in Framework PR #82 at main 98a16c806a (fix commit befcd9f7). Hub assertions bind the exact expected session; verifier 17/17, gateway PostgreSQL 5/5, direct replay PostgreSQL 23/23, integration 22/22, lint, and build passed.

title: P1: Release background claims before command-strategy restart without destroying the command transport
description: Final-check finding against immutable remediation commit 45555531b1 for psfn-framework-9syj.5. In src/app/agent/lifecycle.ts, completeDurableShutdownForRestart invokes the full stopFn before runRestartCommand. In production, the control-plane stop function destroys GatewayClient, while command-strategy restart/rebuild then calls gateway.shellExec through that destroyed transport. A production-shaped reproduction using GatewayClient.destroy followed by shellExec remained pending, so restart/rebuild can hang after successfully releasing durable background work. Implement a termination-preparation boundary that durably releases or requeues claimed background work while keeping the restart-command transport alive; only then launch the validated command and complete remaining shutdown exactly once. If durable release fails, do not launch the command and do not exit. Cover immediate and deferred restart/rebuild. Define a recoverable outcome for command failure after release. Scope includes agent lifecycle/control-plane shutdown sequencing and focused tests. Non-goals: redesigning deployment or supervisors, changing reexec/supervisor strategy semantics, or undoing crash-safe lease recovery from psfn-framework-9syj.5.
acceptance_criteria: 1. With two injected background requeue failures, command-strategy restart/rebuild launches no command, closes neither gateway nor database transport, does not exit, and a later retry can succeed. 2. On success, durable background release precedes the restart command while GatewayClient remains usable; the command settles; remaining shutdown completes exactly once. 3. Focused tests cover immediate and deferred restart/rebuild command strategies using a production-shaped GatewayClient; reexec and supervisor strategies remain unchanged. 4. Command failure after durable release has an explicit recoverable outcome and cannot hang. 5. Focused unit/integration tests, real-Postgres tests where relevant, npm run lint, npm run build, and npm run check:diff pass.
notes:
Implementation fixed point 3a6f3078e5b (base 45555531b1), pushed on work/mmo9-postreview-9syj.7. Added fail-closed prepareRestartCommand contract, production control-plane retryable durable background-release boundary, command execution while GatewayClient remains live, and final teardown only after command settles. Command failure leaves the process explicitly quiesced with gateway/database command transport open and permits explicit retry without repeating a completed durable release. Tests cover two preparation failures then later success, live GatewayClient ordering, missing preparation fail-closed, command failure/retry, and immediate/deferred restart/rebuild sequencing. Validation: 35 lifecycle tests pass; npm run lint passes; npm run build ESM+DTS passed after implementation; git diff --check passes. npm run check:diff does not exist in package.json, so git diff --check is the applicable gate. UBS diff criticals were false positives: pre-existing undefined feature flag comparison and test-only discord token fixture; no actionable finding.
Dual blind review of 45555531b1..3a6f3078e5: FAIL. Lane A reproduced resolved ShellExecResult failures (nonzero/timedOut) being treated as success, causing final teardown and exit zero instead of a recoverable retry state. Lane B independently found the same result-validation defect, plus (a) transport-close/send-false leaves GatewayClient JSON-RPC pending indefinitely, and (b) production generic shell.exec intentionally denies every command without OS confinement, so the configured restart command can never succeed through that path; its live fixture bypassed the real gateway method. Lane B also verified registerDeferredLifecycleRuntime/executionMode=deferred are tests-only and unreachable in production. Orchestrator independently verified all claimed P1s in control-plane.ts, client.ts/json-rpc-2.0 close semantics, shell-runner.ts, gateway methods/shell.ts, and production registration grep. One remediation is authorized: replace generic gateway shell transport with a dedicated operator-configured fixed-argv lifecycle command runner that is bounded and throws on timeout/nonzero/null exit while generic shell remains denied; wire production system tools to deferred mode and register/unregister the durable deferred lifecycle inferer/handler with the same preparation and command dependencies; add real runner and production reachability regressions. Removing restart's GatewayClient dependency resolves transport-loss hangs without broadening generic RPC/shell policy.
close_reason: Authorized remediation landed on origin/main via PR #79 (merge 8d205ac47 'finalize lifecycle command transport'; commit a74dac4b5 'fix(lifecycle): run restart commands locally'). Replaces the generic GatewayClient shell transport with a dedicated fail-closed runner src/system/lifecycle/command-runner.ts (spawn of fixed argv; throws on missing command, non-positive timeout, timeout expiry, and null exit code), wired through control-plane.ts so durable background release precedes an in-process restart command while transports stay live; covered by command-runner.test.ts, control-plane.test.ts and core/tools/lifecycle.test.ts.

title: Make Hub session detach generation-safe across reconnects
description: Problem: EmbodiedSessionRegistry.detachSatellite(sessionId, satelliteId) has no connection or attachment generation. During overlapping reconnect, a current enrollment/version can attach, then stale cleanup or revocation fencing from the old connection unconditionally detaches the newer authority. The next context lookup silently recreates a satellite without deviceAuthority, stripping the current enrollment and producing an unsafe false context. Scope: assign an opaque attachment/connection generation or ownership token and make detach/fence compare-and-delete only the authority installed by that connection. Stale cleanup must never remove a newer connection; current cleanup and live registry revocation/version drift must still detach promptly. Do not silently recreate an authenticated endpoint as unauthenticated authority. Add deterministic overlap tests for old N cleanup after new N+1 attach and for current revocation. Non-goals: change human OAuth attachment or opl1.9 integration.
acceptance_criteria: Old connection cleanup/fence cannot detach a newer attachment; current owner cleanup and device revocation/version drift still detach; no context path silently downgrades a previously authenticated active connection to authority-less state; overlapping reconnect tests pass; Hub full tests, lint/typecheck, build, and diff check pass.
close_reason: Completed and merged in Satellite Hub PR #2 at main 42427bf671 (implementation ec2754e, final remediation f2ef59f). Device detach is generation-safe and hot-reload token collision is fenced; Hub 138/138 tests, lint, and build passed.

title: Retry authenticated Hub requests after lost transport responses
description: Problem: opl1.18 now supports idempotent identical-jti retries and Hub recovery for agent_busy, empty responses, and abort timeouts, but src/ts/hub/psfn-model.ts retries only AbortError. A fetch rejection such as TypeError or ECONNRESET after Framework may have consumed the authenticated request emits failed and stops after one call, so the documented timeout/lost-response recovery contract is false. Scope: classify bounded retryable transport-loss failures separately from application/authentication failures and retry the exact same assertion/body within the existing attempt/deadline budget. Do not retry deterministic HTTP denial or unbounded arbitrary exceptions. Add authenticated lost-response coverage that proves a first consumed request followed by a transport rejection retries with identical assertion bytes and succeeds through Framework idempotent replay. Non-goals: change assertion format, mint new jti per retry, or broaden general retry policy.
acceptance_criteria: Authenticated post-consume transport-loss rejection retries within the current budget using byte-identical assertion/body; deterministic HTTP/auth failures do not retry; deadline/cancellation semantics remain intact; Hub full tests, lint/typecheck, build, cross-repo focused replay tests, and diff check pass.
close_reason: Completed and merged in Satellite Hub PR #2 at main 42427bf671 (implementation 9b87175, final remediation f2ef59f). Lost-response retry behavior is authenticated and exact; Hub 138/138 tests, lint, and build passed.

title: Route self_status memory statistics through subject authorization
description: Problem: opl1.17 wired the named memory surfaces through SQL-first subject authorization, but live core self_status still calls raw global memoryStore.getStats() in src/app/agent/core-runtime.ts. src/core/tools/self-status.ts returns corpus-wide total, byType, and avgSalience through its default snapshot path, allowing inaccessible rows to be enumerated despite the bead's non-enumerable count requirement. Scope: make self_status derive statistics through the same trusted subject context and SQL authorization boundary as other memory reads, or fail closed when no trusted context exists. Preserve content-free telemetry and companion-internal behavior only where the existing runtime actually proves the authorized subject context. Add tests with visible and hidden subjects proving total/type/salience aggregates exclude hidden rows and absence of context cannot reveal global counts. Non-goals: redesign self_status UX, role/JIT policy, or other opl1.11+ authorization features.
acceptance_criteria: Every production self_status memory statistic is authorization-filtered or fail-closed; hidden/non-subject rows do not affect total, byType, or avgSalience; no raw getStats bypass remains in the live snapshot path; focused unit and real-Postgres tests, mandatory npm run lint, build, and git diff --check pass.
close_reason: Completed and merged in Framework PR #82 at main 98a16c806a (fix commit b89fe788). self_status memory statistics are subject-authorized; focused unit/PostgreSQL tests plus mandatory lint/build passed.

title: Fence live fleet sessions after floor-first provider revocation failure
description: Problem: opl1.3 provider revocation publishes the non-restored provider-subject tombstone first, but a later PostgreSQL/reconciliation failure rolls back all database fencing. src/persistence/postgres/fleet-auth/provider-lifecycle-store.ts currently leaves the principal/session rows live, while src/persistence/postgres/fleet-auth/oauth-session-store.ts session validation consults only database state. The existing partial-failure test proves one live session remains until startup/manual reconciliation. This violates fail-closed revocation: after the durable floor advances, the running gateway must not continue accepting superseded authority. Scope: thread the gateway-owned non-restored floor state into runtime session/provider validation or install an equivalent monotonic over-fence so every request denies immediately after floor publication even when SQL mutation fails; preserve floor-first ordering and eventual reconciliation. Add a real-Postgres partial-failure test that attempts the previously live session before restart and is denied. Non-goals: redesign trusted-host storage, provider replacement UX, or opl1.5 lifecycle work.

title: P1: Bind TurnRecord handoffs to the turn-start session identity
description: Final check of psfn-framework-9syj.4 at immutable head a59b0ea2eb reproduced a residual routed-session data-loss race. src/core/agent/substrate-agent/turn-execution-runtime.ts captures logicalSessionId from the turn correlation at turn start (around line 733), but src/core/agent/substrate-agent/turn-support-runtime.ts buildTurnRecord re-resolves SessionManager.resolveSessionChannelId(message.channelId) at record construction (around lines 461-464), and post-turn scheduling re-resolves again near lines 257-262. If Garden resets/remaps the physical source route while a turn is in flight, the completed TurnRecord and handoff can be written under the new logical owner while the error guard still searches the old captured owner at turn-execution-runtime.ts:1713-1718. An enqueue failure then appends a duplicate failed record for the same physical channel/turn; exact source eligibility rejects both and all four cognition jobs are lost. Recovered-delivery replay has the same identity drift: after a route reset it looks up the old durable turn using the current/captured new owner, misses, and can schedule a second completed TurnRecord. A real SessionStore reproduction produced completed+failed records for one physical source/turn and recoverPendingBackgroundWorkHandoffs returned zero enqueues. Scope: capture one immutable physical source channel + logical session owner identity at turn admission and thread it through every TurnRecord build, record-first handoff, error guard, recovered-delivery lookup/replay, and background source reference. Route changes may govern future turns only, never rebind an in-flight or recovered turn. Non-goals: no compatibility lookup across multiple owners, no route-reset redesign, no weakening exact-source/tombstone/duplicate fences, and no raw-content recovery store.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A real SessionStore test starts a routed turn, remaps/resets its physical source before completion, injects enqueue failure, and proves exactly one completed TurnRecord remains bound to the turn-start logical owner and later bounded recovery enqueues its exact four-job manifest once. 2. Error handling never appends a duplicate failed TurnRecord when the record-first handoff exists, regardless of a mid-turn route change. 3. Recovered delivery after a route change resolves the original durable source/owner identity, replays the exact manifest once, and cannot fall through to author a second completed record. 4. Future turns use the new route while the prior in-flight/recovered turn remains fenced to its captured owner; tombstone, duplicate-source, fingerprint, privacy, and cross-process eligibility protections remain fail closed. 5. Focused turn/session/supervisor tests, real PostgreSQL fingerprint replay, npm run lint, build, UBS triage, and diff-check pass.
notes:
Dual blind review of 057dcf16c3..1dd95eda679c: FAIL. Both reviewers independently verified two P1 identity/core defects. (1) fresh-turn durable ownership is derived from buildTurnCorrelation, whose Wyoming observability override can select routing.wyoming.sessionId even though canonical L0 persists under SessionManager.resolveSessionChannelId(physical source); TurnRecord/jobs then point at an empty/noncanonical journal and defer/fail. (2) immutable identity reaches only TurnRecord/post-turn refs; user/system/tool/assistant writers still receive physical message.channelId and re-resolve the live route, so a mid-prompt reset writes old-turn tool/assistant content into the new/quarantine owner and embeds those wrong-journal entry IDs in the old-owner TurnRecord. Orchestrator verified all cited writers/resolvers. One remediation is authorized: source fresh durable owner directly from SessionManager; retain Wyoming only in telemetry correlation; thread the captured physical+logical identity through every session-entry/system-note/tool/assistant write, correlation rebuild, and bounded snapshot. Regressions must assert both L0 owners and execute the recovered four-job manifest with a concurrent future turn, plus a persistence-backed Wyoming case.
Remediation implementation committed at b1c66abf12 (work/mmo9-postreview-9syj.6-remediation), pending the orchestrator's single independent final check. Captures immutable physical source + SessionManager logical owner at admission; keeps Wyoming session telemetry-only; threads identity through transcript/system-note writes, snapshots, correlations, TurnRecord/error/recovery guards, and four-job handoffs. Additional local sanity fix makes explicit captured API/terminal logical owners bypass mutable active-context re-resolution, with a real SessionManager regression over user/system/tool/assistant/internal-note writes. Post-fix validation: focused lane 1 127/127; lane 2 119/119; session/Postgres lane 247/247 (493/493 total); npm run lint PASS; npm run build PASS; git diff --check PASS; UBS --diff ran with full AST and baseline comparison, with all count deltas triaged as strict session-ID equality/test-array heuristic noise and no new production finding. Full npm test: 9492 passed, 18 failed in 13 unrelated pre-existing/stale fixture or certification tests outside the changed files; affected focused lanes pass. Bead intentionally remains in_progress for independent final check/integration.
close_reason: Authorized post-review remediation landed on origin/main via PR #79 (merge 3d792962e 'finalize turn identity ownership'; commit b1c66abf1 'fix(turns): preserve turn-start session identity'). Captures immutable physical source + SessionManager logical owner at turn admission and threads it through turn-execution-runtime.ts, turn-support-runtime.ts, turn-records.ts and session/manager.ts, keeping Wyoming telemetry-only; ships regression tests in turn-execution-runtime.test.ts / turn-support-runtime.test.ts / manager.test.ts asserting single completed TurnRecord bound to turn-start owner and once-only four-job recovery.

title: P1: Make scheduled full-family verification exercise the canonical restore path
description: Final integration check after psfn-framework-kl7y.2 remediation found that src/persistence/backups/fleet-restore.ts:679 verifyFleetAuthConsistentFamilyRestore restores raw companion/cluster slices into the scratch database using only the backup credential, then verifies fleet_auth transactionally.
