title: Wire end-to-end voice-stream cancellation through the production gateway path (make barge-in actually cancel the model)
description:
EPIC-LEVEL / COMPOSITE gap surfaced by the mmo9.6.2 blind review (2026-07-15). mmo9.6.1 (cancellation identity + cancelTurn + provider-port signal) and mmo9.6.2 (WS interrupt frame bypass) are each correct in isolation and both PASSED per-bead review, but the COMPOSITE does NOT deliver barge-in in production.

Root cause (in a production-glue file neither bead owns): the production voice composition src/app/gateway/api-surface.ts:310-325 constructs createApiVoiceWebSocketRuntime with a handleAssistantTurn override that calls gateway.requestAgentVoiceStream(message, {signal}) — BYPASSING runAgentAssistantTurn (which is what the unit/e2e tests exercise). requestAgentVoiceStream (src/boundary/gateway/voice-stream-request.ts:170-205) mints a cancellationId into the routed message (so the agent turn IS addressable by cancelTurn) BUT only polls options.signal?.aborted inside the text-chunk loop (:178-183); during model generation it is blocked awaiting the voice.stream.end RPC (:191-199) with NO signal.addEventListener('abort') and NO sendCancel.

So when a WS interrupt fires handleInterrupt -> cancelInFlight -> state.abortController.abort (runtime.ts:355), the abort mirrors into the stage controller but neither rejects the in-flight JSON-RPC nor sends voice.stream.cancel. Result: local WS state is released (feels responsive, ack sent) but the AGENT KEEPS GENERATING until the end RPC resolves; the LLM stage locally hangs until the 45s llm budget times out; a follow-up barge-in turn queues behind the still-active uncancelled turn. This defeats mmo9.6's core stated goal (preemptive interrupts).

Scope: in requestAgentVoiceStream, attach an abort listener on options.signal for the WHOLE turn (not just the chunk-loop poll) that sends voice.stream.cancel / rejects the in-flight voice.stream.end RPC so the gateway aborts the agent turn (cancelTurn) and tears down the upstream provider stream during generation. Confirm the gateway voice.stream.cancel handler actually reaches SubstrateAgent.cancelTurn(cancellationId) + the provider-port cancel signal (mmo9.6.1's seam) so remote model+TTS generation stops, not just local state. This also subsumes mmo9.6.1's flagged split-process follow-up (an llm.chat.cancel-style reverse RPC) for the voice path.

Regression test: a PRODUCTION-composition test (voice-websocket-runtime.test.ts currently has ZERO interrupt/cancel coverage) that drives requestAgentVoiceStream, aborts mid-generation, and asserts voice.stream.cancel is sent + the agent turn is cancelled + no follow-up turn queues behind a still-active turn.

Non-goals: no new RPC redesign beyond the cancel path; do not touch mmo9.6.2's frame-bypass (correct) or mmo9.6.1's identity (correct).

Base: feat/mmo9-performance. This is the piece that makes 6.1+6.2 add up to working barge-in — a textbook epic-seam defect (both beads correct, composite broken, gap in an unowned glue file).
close_reason: Implemented on work/mmo9perf-mmo9.6.5 (f7192794e0..fe9a7dca4d), integrated to feat/mmo9-performance@51f1a4c0e4 (pushed; clean merge). THE COMPOSITE barge-in fix (closes the gap between 6.1+6.2 flagged by the 6.2 review). requestAgentVoiceStream (voice-stream-request.ts) now attaches a WHOLE-TURN abort listener that (a) sends voice.stream.cancel once (idempotent cancelSent guard), (b) rejects the in-flight reverse RPC via an abort-race so the await unblocks instead of hanging to the agent timeout; losing RPC .catch-guarded (no dangling); listener detached in finally on every exit path (no per-turn leak). Full chain verified: WS interrupt (6.2) -> abort -> voice.stream.cancel -> GatewayClient.handleVoiceStreamCancel aborts the same per-stream controller threaded into the model dispatch (handleVoiceStreamEnd) -> SubstrateAgent.cancelTurn(cancellationId) (6.1, identity-guarded, untouched) -> abort() -> provider-port cancel at the agent; the cancelled turn is released so the follow-up barge-in dispatches (not queued). Evidence at worker head: new production-composition test (real requestAgentVoiceStream <-> real GatewayClient over in-memory JSON-RPC bridge) FAILS pre-fix (hang->timeout, rejects 'timed out' not 'abort'), PASSES post-fix (voice.stream.cancel sent + dispatch signal aborted + cancellationId present + follow-up dispatches); 5 files 203 tests; integrated revalidation @51f1a4c0e4: 69 tests + lint clean. UBS range: no new critical/warning. Pi (GLM 5.2 @high) blind adversarial review: PASS, 0 blocking — traced remote-generation-stops in split topology, no abort-race promise leak/double-settle, idempotent cancel, listener cleanup on all paths, follow-up dispatch, benign json-rpc aborted log. Nonblocking (handoff): lost-cancel-frame on host<->agent partition = agent turn runs to completion (best-effort distributed cancel, acknowledged in code, not a regression); the agent's requestWithAbortSignal rejects local llm.chat but does NOT propagate a cancel to the gateway so an already-in-flight gateway->provider fetch isn't torn down (wasted tokens, no user-visible output — SAME split-process residual as 6.1's llm.chat.cancel follow-up; user-perceived barge-in works); timeoutRace setTimeout not cleared (pre-existing, bounded); new test proxies reservation-release via mock dispatch (cancel seam + follow-up faithfully exercised). Completes mmo9.6 barge-in end-to-end.

title: P1: Fail shutdown when safe background claims cannot be requeued
description: Source: independent review of PR #79 / psfn-framework-mmo9.3 at commit 5686ed21467ecf7c7624ffaba017428c2a662e73. src/core/agent/background-work/supervisor.ts:352-388 catches requeuePreBoundaryClaims failure, logs, and resolves stop(). src/app/agent/control-plane.ts:179-201 then proceeds to close PostgreSQL. A safe pre-boundary claim can remain leased and later exhaust its last attempt during expiry recovery, silently losing deferred cognition. Scope: make shutdown fail closed or retry boundedly until safe claims are durably released before database closure; preserve outcome-unknown treatment after the write boundary. Non-goals: no process supervisor/deployment changes or unlimited shutdown wait.
acceptance_criteria: 1. An injected requeuePreBoundaryClaims failure makes stop/shutdown observably fail and prevents database close, or succeeds through a bounded retry before close. 2. Pre-boundary claims are durably queued without consuming an attempt; started/applied receipts are never replayed. 3. A max-attempt pre-boundary claim cannot become retry_exhausted solely because graceful requeue failed silently. 4. Focused supervisor/control-plane and disposable-Postgres tests, npm run lint, build, and diff-check pass.
notes: Dual blind review of 057dcf16c3..882932e71d: FAIL. Both reviewers independently verified two P1 production-boundary gaps. (1) After both bounded requeue attempts fail, signal shutdown, immediate/deferred restart/rebuild, and gateway-disconnect owners still exit or launch restart; the abandoned maxAttempts=1 pre-boundary claim then expires and recoverExpired increments it to terminal retry_exhausted without any effect. (2) control-plane and signal outer promises cache the rejected shutdown forever, so the supervisor's deliberately resettable stop promise cannot be retried and the process remains partially shut down. Orchestrator verified every cited path in signal-shutdown.ts, lifecycle.ts, agent/main.ts, control-plane.ts, and background-work-store.ts. One remediation is authorized: routine termination/restart only proceeds after stop succeeds; outer shutdown owners reset failed attempts for a later deduplicated retry; lease-expiry recovery never consumes an attempt for pre-boundary/pending/applied claims, while started outcome-unknown stays terminal. Add behavioral signal/lifecycle/retry-owner tests and maxAttempts=1 real-PG crash recovery.
close_reason: Completed and integrated on feat/mmo9-background-supervisor at merge commit 3aef374caf (implementation 882932e71d, one remediation 45555531b1). Verified production shutdown now retries durable background release without poisoning later attempts; pre-boundary leases remain recoverable; signal, disconnect, and lifecycle paths do not exit after failed release. Evidence: 56 focused unit tests and 32 real-Postgres integration tests passed in remediation; final check passed 32/32 real-Postgres, npm run lint, npm run build, and git diff --check. Final check found a separate command-strategy transport-order P1, tracked self-contained as psfn-framework-9syj.7 per the bounded-loop rule. The final check's sole focused test failure was a stale source assertion that reproduced unchanged at base 057dcf16c3.

title: P1: Recover record-first background handoffs after live enqueue failures
description: Source: independent review of PR #79 / psfn-framework-mmo9.3 at commit 5686ed21467ecf7c7624ffaba017428c2a662e73. src/core/agent/substrate-agent/turn-execution/post-turn-scheduling.ts:352-357 durably records the TurnRecord before enqueue, but src/core/agent/substrate-agent.ts:1213-1226 scans recoverable handoffs only once at startup. If enqueue fails after that scan, the completed TurnRecord manifest has no queue rows and is not retried in the running process; ordinary non-ICP turns remain stranded until restart. Scope: provide bounded same-process recovery/retry for record-first handoffs, retaining atomic batch/fingerprint semantics and privacy/eligibility fences. Non-goals: no global unbounded per-tick history scan, second raw-content store, or compatibility path.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Injected enqueue failure after startup recovery records the canonical manifest, reports the failure, and causes a later bounded recovery attempt in the same process to enqueue the exact jobs once. 2. Duplicate recovery across concurrent ticks/supervisors is idempotent and fingerprint mismatches fail closed. 3. Recovery is bounded/indexed and does not scan all historical TurnRecords on every tick. 4. Tombstoned/duplicate/ineligible source turns never enqueue. 5. Focused turn/supervisor and disposable-Postgres tests, npm run lint, build, and diff-check pass.
notes: Dual blind review of 5686ed2146..3b4fff2fbc: Reviewer B PASS. Reviewer A FAIL with two P1 core acceptance defects, both independently verified by the orchestrator. (1) Route-split sessions: post-turn scheduling records the completed handoff under physical TurnRecord.channelId, but turn-execution error/recovered-delivery guards call SessionManager.hasRecordedTurn/findRecordedTurn, which resolve to the logical session before lookup. Enqueue failure therefore appends a second failed physical record with the same turnId; the exact-source eligibility gate sees duplicates and retires the pending handoff, losing all four cognition jobs. (2) BackgroundWorkHandoffRecovery.recover uses [...pending.values()].slice(0, limit), which exhausts the entire map iterator before slicing and makes each nominally bounded tick O(total outage backlog), violating AC3. One bounded remediation is authorized on work/mmo9-postreview-9syj.4-remediation: use exact physical+logical source lookup/guard through real SessionStore regression, and select only O(limit) pending entries with traversal-count coverage.
close_reason: Completed and pushed in merge commit 057dcf16c3 (fixed points 3b4fff2fbc and a59b0ea2eb): durable record-first handoff, atomic batch enqueue, canonical eligibility, bounded recovery, routed/reset coverage, and O(limit) pending traversal. Integration evidence: 185 focused unit tests passed; 31 real-Postgres background-work tests passed; npm run lint passed; npm run build passed; git diff --check passed. The final immutable-range check found a distinct turn-start route-identity defect, recorded as fresh P1 bead psfn-framework-9syj.6 per the bounded-loop contract.

title: P1: Strictly validate privacy-minimal compaction payloads
description: Source: independent review of PR #79 / psfn-framework-mmo9.3 at commit 5686ed21467ecf7c7624ffaba017428c2a662e73. src/core/agent/background-work/types.ts:307-373 accepts arbitrary finite adaptive-profile percentages and shallow-copies arbitrary modelSelection keys and value types. title: P1: Cross intention effect boundaries only adjacent to durable writes

title: P1: Stop renewing foreground leases after ownership loss
description: Source: independent review of PR #79 / psfn-framework-mmo9.3 at commit 5686ed21467ecf7c7624ffaba017428c2a662e73. The next heartbeat retries the same ID during that extension, sees it as unexpired, and renews it indefinitely; a wedged foreground turn can therefore permanently fence same-session memory/compaction. Scope: terminally remove/fence locally lost foreground leases while preserving one bounded durable quarantine and safe endForeground cleanup. Non-goals: no scheduler redesign, provider preemption, or lease-duration tuning.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Regression first: after one lease expires, two subsequent heartbeats cannot renew or extend it beyond the single quarantine window. 2. A second supervisor can claim same-session background work after that bounded window even if the first foreground operation ignores abort. 3. endForeground remains idempotent after local loss and cannot delete another owner lease. 4. Existing foreground isolation and disposable-Postgres suites pass, plus npm run lint, build, and diff-check.

Fixed point 80e5e711dd removes a locally lost foreground lease ID from the only renewal-ready set, so the store's observed-expiry extension remains exactly one quarantine window while managed state supports safe late endForeground. title: Sub-tick scheduling via adaptive next-wake
description: mmo9.5 child C (independent seam). ROOT CAUSE: scheduler.ts:347-425 + scheduler.seed.json:2 — start() arms one setInterval(tick, tickIntervalMs=60000); runTick(:408) is the ONLY due-ness evaluator, so every per-task intervalMs/runAt (incl. the executor's own intervalMs:Math.max(50,...) task @post-turn-actions.ts:1299 and rescheduleAt @:926-951) is checked only on the 60s edge — a job asking to run in 250ms waits up to 60s. The interval is a hard granularity FLOOR. CHANGE (no second scheduler — doc 9 / non-goal): scheduler.ts start()/runTick(): after each runTick compute nextWakeAt = min over tasks of (every: lastRun+intervalMs | wall-clock next | one-shot runAt), clamp to [minWakeMs~50ms, tickIntervalMs (stays coarse ceiling/safety net)], arm setTimeout. Add requestWake(atMs) to re-arm earlier when a near-term task is registered/updated. updateConfig/stop must clear the timer. OPTIONAL cross-file: post-turn-actions.ts rescheduleAt path (@926-951) calls scheduler.requestWake(rescheduleAt) so a 250ms defer is honored — this is the ONLY cross-file edit; can be deferred to keep C in one file (adaptive next-wake needs no executor change). AC: with tickIntervalMs:60000, a task/one-shot due in 250ms fires within a small tolerance of 250ms not at the 60s edge; periodic tasks still fire on cadence; no busy-loop (idle system arms a single timer at the true next due). Regression-first: scheduler.test.ts register one-shot runAt=now+250, fake timers, advance 300ms, assert fired (fails today, fires only at 60s); assert idle scheduler arms exactly one wake at next real boundary (no tight loop). Base: feat/mmo9-performance. Repo rules: fail closed, no swallowed errors, no real names.

title: Preemptable and reservable provider capacity at the model-call gate
description: mmo9.5 child A (hard core). Replace the single-boolean active slot with capacity-aware, preemption-capable admission; plumb a gate-owned cancel signal into the LLM transport; forward the supervisor per-job signal into background LLM calls; map preemption to the supervisor pre-boundary defer. ROOT CAUSE: model-call-gate.ts:25-168 ResourceQueue has one active:boolean per resourceKey; acquire() grants only when !active && pending empty; selectNextPendingIndex (:145) reorders WAITERS by lane priority but preemption is structurally impossible (gate holds only a release closure, no handle to cancel the running execute); caller signal (:74-90) only removes a WAITING acquire. So foreground voice waits behind an in-flight background extraction. NOTE resolveModelCallResourceKey (client.ts:517-531) returns a key ONLY for request_base_url/configured_litellm_proxy/litellm/local_endpoint; cloud providers return null and bypass the gate (already non-contended) — this defect bites shared-endpoint/local-substrate (Pi) deployments. CHANGES: model-call-gate.ts ResourceQueue gains capacity:number (default 1) + active:ActiveCall[] {runtimeClass, preemptController:AbortController, sequence}; run() passes execute a gate-owned preemptSignal; on acquire, grant immediately if active<capacity AND interactive-reservation invariant holds (keep >=1 slot free for foreground_chat unless acquirer IS foreground); else if acquirer higher-priority than lowest-priority active AND that lane is preemptable, abort that call's preemptController(PreemptError) and grant; else park (existing reorder). worker-lanes.ts: add preemptable:boolean to RuntimeLaneBudgetProfile (foreground_chat:false, post_turn_appraisal:false, background_continuation:true, maintenance_reflection:true — single home, Law 12.4). client.ts: thread gate preemptSignal through runWithModelCallGate(@584); complete path(@1058-1073) + stream path build transport signal = AbortSignal.any([options.signal, preemptSignal]) — MUST cover llm.stream path (mmo9.8 needs it; RE-VERIFY line numbers on the feat branch, ~35 hunks there). Capacity config goes in routing/model OWNER config (a provider property), NOT scheduler.seed.json (feat branch already edited it — conflict risk); default capacity 1 for local_endpoint/litellm shared keys (fail-closed). background-work/post-turn-runtime.ts: forward input.signal (currently unused) into extractor.maybeExtract / emotionRuntime.triggerEmotionAppraisal / sessionManager.scheduleAutoCompactionBetweenTurns; map a preemption-reason abort to BackgroundWorkDeferredError('foreground_active', delayMs) (defer, NO attempt consumed) not failOrRetry. SAFETY (load-bearing): for all four job classes the LLM call is BEFORE commitEffectBoundary, so aborting is always pre-boundary = supervisor-safe (receipt pending, abandonEffect drops it, job requeues revision-bumped, no duplicate write). Never preempt a non-preemptable lane; a test must assert an abort AFTER boundary crossing fails closed via outcome_unknown (no replay). AC: (i) capacity 1, in-flight background_continuation on key K aborted within budget when foreground_chat acquire on K arrives, foreground execute starts without waiting; (ii) capacity 2 + reserve-1, background holds one slot, foreground gets reserved slot with NO preemption; (iii) foreground_chat never itself preempted; (iv) preempted background job -> supervisor deferred, no attempt consumed, later resumes; (v) preemption telemetry {reason, resourceKey, preemptedRuntimeClass, waitedMs}. Regression-first: model-call-gate.test.ts fake execute blocking on a deferred — assert current code FAILS 'foreground starts before background completes' then passes; capacity/reservation test; streaming-path preemptSignal composition test; supervisor-integration preempt mid-extraction (pre-commitEffectBoundary) -> requeues cleanly no duplicate. OPEN RISK (verify, flag if true): ModelCallGate is per-LLMClient (client.ts:195); if each companion is a separate agent process, in-process gate can't coordinate two companions on the same endpoint (proxy-side concurrency limit is the cross-process control) — this bead fully solves multi-CHANNEL within one companion, not cross-process multi-companion. Base: feat/mmo9-performance. Repo rules: fail closed, no swallowed errors, no shims, no second budget system (Law 12.4), no real names.
close_reason: Implemented on work/mmo9perf-mmo9.5.1 (5686ed2146..52ca6fba7f) + one remediation (..98face9bfa), integrated to feat/mmo9-performance@97125b38a1 (pushed; delegated signal-compose merge with mmo9.6.1). Capacity-aware preemption-capable model-call gate: ResourceQueue{capacity, reservedForegroundSlots, active[]}; higher-priority foreground acquire preempts the lowest-priority PREEMPTABLE background call it strictly outranks (aborts its preemptController = ModelCallPreemptedError); gate provides execute a preemptSignal; foreground/post_turn_appraisal never preempted; config via ProviderRegistryEntry.capacity/reservedForegroundSlots (fail-closed). Preempt maps to supervisor BackgroundWorkDeferredError('foreground_active') pre-boundary defer (no attempt consumed). REVIEW FAIL@xhigh->remediated->verified: Pi found P1 — ModelCallPreemptedError flattened to -32603 across the gateway->agent JSON-RPC boundary (name lost), so preempted background job hit failOrRetry -> permanently failed after maxAttempts=5 (LOST cognition job in production split topology); in-process mock-transport tests missed it. Orchestrator confirmed against code. Remediation: dedicated GatewayErrors.MODEL_CALL_PREEMPTED=-32018, mapped in exposeModelCallGateBlocks (both llm.chat+llm.complete), reconstructed on GatewayClient (both complete+stream via modelCallPreemptedErrorFromRpc) so .name+instanceof hold across the wire -> defers correctly; new real-boundary regression test (JSON round-trip -> production mapping -> executePostTurnBackgroundWork asserts deferred not failed). INTEGRATION SEAM: 5.1 preempt signal + 6.1 caller-cancellation signal both thread the stream path; delegated merge composed both (composeTransportSignal(options?.signal, preemptSignal), adopted options-object signature across LLMProviderPort/LLMClient/transport/GatewayClient) and caught a LATENT trap in stream-adapter.ts (auto-merged clean but would have dropped caller cancellation in both topologies via undefined options.signal) — fixed + both-signal regression test added. Evidence: 5.1 remediation 190+17+3; merge validation 366 (306 6.1-cancellation suite + 59 5.1-preemption suite + 1 compose test) + lint + build/DTS + diff-check clean. title: Separate TTS first-byte budget from playback budget
description: mmo9.6 child 4/4 (independent seam; shares src/channels/discord/voice-turn-runtime.ts with mmo9.6.3 — different functions, expect small textual merge; also touches primitives/voice/policy/reliability.ts + websocket runtime.ts — grep VoiceRuntimeStage usages before editing the union). Root cause: one budget spans request-to-first-byte AND playback-duration, and retry has no 'cancel prior attempt first' guarantee. Discord: speakVoiceText (:464) wraps the ENTIRE synth+playback (playWithTtsConnector->playTtsSession->playReadableAudio, awaits entersState(Idle,120s)) in a single stage-tts budget (reliability.ts:18: 25s timeout, maxRetries 1) — a reply whose playback exceeds 25s trips the timeout and RETRIES the whole synth+playback while the first playback is not guaranteed cancelled => double-speak. WebSocket: streamPlayback (runtime.ts:459) budgets only synthesizeStream (session open) under stage-tts; the first audible chunk arrives lazily in the unbudgeted for-await loop => NO first-byte budget at all. Scope: add a tts_first_byte stage (short, retry-safe) to VoiceRuntimeStage/DEFAULT_VOICE_RELIABILITY_BUDGETS (reliability.ts:4,:14); keep tts/output as long non-retryable playback. Discord: split speakVoiceText/playWithTtsConnector (:434-529) — budget synth-request->first chunk under tts_first_byte; playback under output with maxRetries 0; on first-byte retry, assertActiveVoiceTurn + cancel prior turn.ttsSession BEFORE re-synth (use existing voice.tts.first-byte events :513,:566 as the budget boundary). WebSocket: streamPlayback (runtime.ts:459) wrap the FIRST for-await chunk (:469) in tts_first_byte, keep per-chunk output. GATED sub-task (only with new incremental-MP3 decoder-boundary tests): remove the one-chunk look-ahead in connectors/tts/elevenlabs-stream.ts:85 (responseBodyToAudioChunks holds 'pending' and yields the previous chunk, delaying first audible byte by one network read). title: Preemptive WebSocket voice control frames
description: mmo9.6 child 2/4. DEPENDS ON mmo9.6.1 (interrupt must reach the model via cancellationId, not just cancel local playback). Root cause: primitives/voice/transports/websocket/server.ts:165 drainFrameQueue processes ALL frames strictly serially (processingFrames flag + await fireHook('onFrame') per frame), so an 'interrupt' frame queues behind a session.end frame whose onFrame is still awaiting the full model+TTS pipeline (runtime.ts:287 handleSessionEnd awaits onAssistantTurn then streamPlayback). The interrupt handler (runtime.ts:351 handleInterrupt) is correct but never runs until the in-flight frame resolves — control-plane and data-plane share one FIFO. Scope: route control frames (interrupt, ping) out of the data-plane FIFO so they dispatch synchronously on receipt (server.ts drainFrameQueue/handleMessage:68), bypassing frameQueue, while keeping session.start/audio.chunk/session.end ordered. Ensure handleInterrupt drives the mmo9.6.1 cancellationId so the MODEL turn (not just local playback) aborts; confirm handleSessionEnd's onAssistantTurn signal (runtime.ts:317) reaches the agent via .6.1. AC: test enqueues session.end (long model) then interrupt; assert interrupt is handled BEFORE end resolves and the model/TTS abort fires (criterion: stops remote model/TTS generation, not merely local playback). Base: feat/mmo9-performance. Repo rules: fail closed, no swallowed errors, no real names.
close_reason: Implemented on work/mmo9perf-mmo9.6.2 (68d505dfc3..0b6a71f291), integrated to feat/mmo9-performance@50f5a9ef86 (pushed; clean merge). Control-frame classifier (interrupt, ping) splits handleMessage: control frames dispatch synchronously via fireHook on receipt, bypassing the data-plane frameQueue + its backpressure ceiling; session.start/audio.chunk/session.end stay strictly ordered through drainFrameQueue. So an interrupt runs concurrently with a blocked in-flight session.end instead of queuing behind the full model+TTS pipeline. Evidence at worker head: websocket 24 (server 10 incl. interrupt+ping-ahead-of-blocked-session.end + saturated-queue, runtime 8, serializer 6) + gateway client + substrate-agent 181 (6.1 seam intact); integrated revalidation @50f5a9ef86: 24 WS tests pass. UBS range: 1 new listener-imbalance warning = TEST-ONLY (once:true mock in runtime.test.ts, self-cleans; production server.ts adds no listeners). Pi (GLM 5.2 @high) blind adversarial review: PASS, 0 blocking — traced ordering integrity (all 5 frame types accounted, data frames still FIFO, control bypass safe), interrupt-during-session.start no-ops (SESSION_NOT_FOUND), interrupt-mid-session.end idempotent (no double-cancel/free), no 6.1 identity-clobber reintroduced (control path never touches activeTurnCancellationId), no new swallowed error. IMPORTANT COMPOSITE FINDING (-> fix bead mmo9.6.5): 6.2's frame bypass is a NECESSARY PREREQUISITE for barge-in but does NOT by itself deliver production remote-model cancellation — the production voice composition (api-surface.ts requestAgentVoiceStream) mints a cancellationId but only polls signal.aborted in the chunk loop and does NOT observe the abort during the voice.stream.end generation RPC, so a WS interrupt releases local state (feels responsive) while the agent keeps generating. Neither 6.1 nor 6.2 per-bead review could flag this as blocking (each bead correct in its own scope; gap in an unowned glue file). Tracked as mmo9.6.5 (P1). [--force: mmo9.6.2 was created with an inverted 'blocks 6.1' dep.]

title: End-to-end voice turn-cancellation identity (keystone)
description: mmo9.6 child 1/4 (KEYSTONE — land first; mmo9.6.2 and mmo9.8 depend on it). Mint one cancellationId at transport ingress and thread it transport->gateway->agent model->TTS, with a real abort keyed to it at each layer, closing the cancel-after-dispatch gap. Root cause: SubstrateAgent.abort() (substrate-agent.ts ~:1097) works and is exercised by API text (chat-completions.ts:294) but NO voice path threads a turn identity to it. MessageHandler (channels/backplane/types.ts:4) has no signal param; Discord handleVoiceUtterance wraps handler(message) but the signal only unblocks the local Promise.race, not the agent turn (uncancellable model calls). Gateway handleVoiceStreamCancel (client.ts:1248) only sets cancelled=true/deletes state AFTER handleVoiceStreamEnd (client.ts:1219->dispatchHandleMessage:1120, no signal) already dispatched the model. Scope: add turn-cancellation registry + cancelTurn(cancellationId) (identity-guarded over abort()) on SubstrateAgent; extend MessageHandler to carry {signal,cancellationId}; add cancellationId to SubstrateMessage.routing (survives serializeMessage:242); VoiceStreamState gains cancellationId+AbortController; handleVoiceStreamEnd threads signal into dispatchHandleMessage; handleVoiceStreamCancel aborts the controller / calls cancelTurn instead of only deleting state; voice-stream-request.ts carries cancellationId. Abort order on barge-in: model turn first, then TTS session, then transport state. cancelTurn(id) aborts IFF active turn id matches (a stale late cancel must NOT kill the next turn — critical for mmo9.8 rapid segment turns). VERIFY FIRST (open risk): whether inner Agent.abort() (substrate-agent.ts:514 inner Agent) truly cancels the upstream provider HTTP stream mid-generation or only stops local consumption; if only local, .1 grows to thread a provider-port cancel signal. AC: unit test dispatches a voice turn, cancels AFTER model dispatch, asserts (a) inner provider stream receives abort, (b) cancelTurn fires for that id and no other, (c) a late stale-id cancel does NOT abort a newer turn; cancellation observed at gateway state + agent turn + TTS session. Regression-first: failing tests proving today's Discord handler(message) and gateway dispatchHandleMessage ignore cancellation. Keep identity transport-agnostic (mmo9.8 reuses it); do NOT rename voice.stream.* RPCs (that's mmo9.8). Base: feat/mmo9-performance. Repo rules: fail closed, no swallowed errors, no shims, no real names in tests.
close_reason: Implemented on work/mmo9perf-mmo9.6.1 (5686ed2146..72df813d50) + one remediation (..1aefcecb22), integrated to feat/mmo9-performance@68d505dfc3 (pushed). End-to-end voice turn-cancellation identity (keystone). REVIEW FAIL->remediated->verified: Pi found a P1 (activeTurnCancellationId single field clobbered to null by a concurrent ordinary turn via runShared -> voice barge-in silent no-op in production topology); orchestrator confirmed against code; remediation = guarded identity claim (claim only when carrying an id AND slot null, clear only own claim) + concurrency regression test (fails pre-fix not_active, passes post-fix signaled). Verify-first: inner Agent.abort() was local-only -> threaded provider-port cancel signal end-to-end. Integrated revalidation @68d505dfc3: 351 tests + lint + build/DTS clean. UBS: no new findings. Cogsec untouched. Nonblocking (handoff): split-process upstream provider-fetch not torn down (user-perceived interrupt works, wasted tokens only, needs llm.chat.cancel reverse RPC); two-concurrent-voice-turns identity race deferred to mmo9.8 activeRun-binding. [--force: mmo9.6.2 dep was created inverted as 'blocks 6.1'; 6.1 is genuinely complete.] Keystone for mmo9.6.2 + mmo9.8.

title: Turn-record userMessage/assistantMessage frozen copies ignore CogSec tombstones
description: Discovered during eb14 remediation (2026-07-15). TurnRecord.userMessage.content (and by symmetry assistantMessage.content) is a frozen verbatim copy of partner/companion text persisted on the turn record at write time (turn-records.ts ~363, sessionEntryId + content). A CogSec tombstone of the backing L0 entry does not scrub it: the eb14 wave gated recentEntries (9ree/hgw3.10), plan.messages (9ree), memory candidates (jsi9), and capturedWirePayload (eb14), but the top-level userMessage/assistantMessage fields are served ungated by every turn-record read exit — consumers include introspection source.ts (reads userMessage/assistantMessage), Garden session views (buildTurnData), and telemetry sanitizers. Same partner-data retention class as eb14. The eb14 remediation deliberately did not expand scope (its withhold key now USES userMessage.sessionEntryId, so the plumbing to resolve the entry's L0 state at read time already exists — likely a small symmetric gate). Coordinate with ervg (cross-channel continuity) so the family lands coherently. Non-goals: wirebody (eb14, done), continuity surfaces (ervg).
acceptance_criteria: A CogSec tombstone of the L0 entry backing userMessage (or assistantMessage) results in the frozen copy no longer being served verbatim from any turn-record read exit or Garden/introspection surface (masked with the redaction marker, consistent with the 9ree convention); live text byte-identical; heal/telemetry consistent with hgw3.10; regression test: append turn, tombstone the current-turn partner entry, assert userMessage.content serves the marker not plaintext across getRecentTurnRecords/findTurnRecord/Garden session views; sessions + garden + introspection suites green.
close_reason: Implemented and integrated: feat/ahxy-s10-shakedown-fixes @ abf73d02b (origin-equal; bead branch work/ahxy-ervg-sm9l @ ad20e27d3, shared with ervg). TurnRecord userMessage/assistantMessage frozen copies now masked symmetrically with the eb14 capturedWirePayload convention at every turn-record read exit — all five SessionStore read methods route through resolveTurnRecordSessionRefs (store.ts:1283-1453), covering introspection listCandidates, Garden buildTurnData, and telemetry sanitizers. sessionEntryId is stamped for all L0-persisted turns (turn-records.ts:376,385); null only for deliberately non-persisted turns with no L0 row to tombstone. Evidence: changed suites 158/158 locally incl. 'serves redaction notices through introspection, Garden buildTurnData, and every store read exit'; lint/build/hygiene gates green; UBS change-range clean. Dual blind adversarial review (Opus + Pi GLM@high) both PASS, zero blockers. Known bounded residual (handoff, pre-existing vintage): records written before the sessionEntryId plumbing cannot be re-resolved; their recentEntries/plan.messages copies ARE gated.

title: P1: Close fleet-auth authority and reapproval bypasses
description: Sources: psfn-framework-opl1.2.3, opl1.2.4, and opl1.2.5; discovered during independent validation of PR #78 at feat/opl1-fleet-sso@fa336f2910. Verified failures: schema.ts rejects five direct PostgreSQL attributes but permits membership/SET ROLE into arbitrary predefined or external powerful roles and leaves inheritance/expiry/connection/database-owner posture unspecified; the runtime role has full DML on authority_state and reapproval trusts that mutable database copy; reapproval-sql.ts ignores trusted_host_ceremonies.exact_scope, so a ceremony for a lower role can promote a quarantined owner grant, and compares expiry to caller-controlled p_at; migrations v4 backfills history but post-migration restore can insert history-only provider ownership without updating provider_subject_registry, allowing later reassignment; fleet-auth-config.ts compares lexical URL host/port/path while libpq routing query overrides can redirect one credential; reapproval.ts swallows rollback failure. Scope: deny all role memberships/SET ROLE targets and enforce a documented exact safe login posture; remove ordinary runtime authority_state mutation while retaining bounded coordinator reconciliation; bind reapproval to exact principal/provider/companion/contact/binding/grant/role/current lineage+generation+checkpoint and database time; register every appended immutable history row; reject connection-routing overrides before identity comparison; surface rollback failure. Non-goals: OAuth/UI/passkey enrollment, backup filesystem/restore orchestration (sibling fix beads), production/Pi, or speculative refactors. Current working tree with regression-first draft: feat/opl1-fleet-sso worktree based fa336f2910.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Every fleet role rejects SUPERUSER/CREATEROLE/CREATEDB/REPLICATION/BYPASSRLS, any direct or transitive membership/SET ROLE target including predefined server roles, target database ownership, unsafe inheritance, expired credentials, and unbounded/unusable connection posture before schema/data work; valid dedicated roles pass. 2. Runtime SQL has SELECT-only authority_state access and cannot rewrite/delete the current floor projection; startup/restore coordinator reconciliation remains bounded and green. 3. Reapproval uses database time for expiry and requires exact JSON scope binding principal, provider subject, companion/contact, binding ID, grant ID, role, authority lineage/generation/restore checkpoint; wrong-role, stale, backdated-expiry, replay, and direct-SQL attempts deny with no mutation. 4. Restored/appended history-only provider evidence permanently registers its original principal and rejects reassignment. 5. Fleet database URLs reject query parameters that can override host/hostaddr/port/dbname/user/service or authentication target before same-database comparison. 6. Rollback errors are surfaced or aggregated, never swallowed. 7. Disposable-PG and config regressions, focused tests, npm run lint, build, settings contract, and diff check pass.
notes: Dual blind review of fa336f2910..23a14ec541: FAIL. Both reviewers independently reproduced account reapproval accepting a ceremony that expired while waiting on row locks because v_now is captured before locking. Reviewer A additionally reproduced v4-to-v5 migration installing the history trigger without backfilling history appended after v4, allowing an existing subject binding to be permanently reassigned; orchestrator verified the migration lacks a backfill. One bounded remediation assigned on fix/opl1-security-authority-remediation; no successive inline cycle after final check.
close_reason: Integrated and pushed on feat/opl1-fleet-sso at 5c610f2ae865fbe82b70b87b1ccf3b40d51a7a44 (implementation 23a14ec541 plus bounded remediation 0c716cf157). Source evidence: schema.ts enforces safe login/topology and SELECT-only authority_state; reapproval-sql.ts exact scope and fresh post-lock DB expiry before mutation; migrations.ts v5 locked/conflict-denying history backfill before trigger; fleet-auth-config.ts rejects libpq routing/auth overrides; reapproval.ts aggregates rollback failures. Dual blind review findings remediated; final check PASS. Integrated validation: 44/44 focused tests including 31 disposable-PostgreSQL integration tests, npm run lint, npm run build/DTS, npm run verify:settings-contract, git diff --check; clean HEAD equals live origin.

title: P1: Make fleet-auth family restore rollback-safe and restore tenant access
description: Source: psfn-framework-opl1.2.1, discovered during independent validation of PR #78 at feat/opl1-fleet-sso@fa336f2910. Observed failures: restoreFleetAuthConsistentFamily in src/persistence/backups/fleet-restore.ts commits each companion/shared pg_restore separately and only then restores fleet_auth, so a later failure strands earlier schemas and a retry collides. Dumps/restores use --no-owner --no-privileges with the backup role, and no post-restore ownership/grant step makes restored schemas usable by their intended companion runtime roles. src/persistence/backups/fleet-auth-restore.ts also uses ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING across durable/audit imports, silently discarding conflicting rows rather than proving an identical/monotonic merge. Scope: use the repo's existing restore marker/rollback primitives or an equivalent bounded family transaction so late failures leave zero residual family state and retry is safe; carry a strict manifest mapping from restored schemas to validated target runtime roles and re-establish exact ownership/grants without granting fleet_auth; replace silent conflict drops with explicit identical/monotonic merge or a fail-closed error. Non-goals: filesystem backup coverage (sibling fix bead), new auth routes, prod/Pi, or widening companion access to fleet_auth. Current base feat/opl1-fleet-sso@fa336f2910; owned work branch fix/opl1-restore-atomic.
acceptance_criteria: 1. All dump scopes, target identities, target role mappings, and complete family integrity are verified before mutation. 2. A failure during the second schema restore or fleet_auth import rolls back/removes every schema/database marker created by the family and leaves both non-restored floors safe; retry from the same family succeeds. 3. After successful restore each companion runtime role can use only its mapped schema and shared access contract, while companion roles still have zero fleet_auth access; ownership/grants are exact and fail closed on unknown/missing roles. 4. Conflicting durable/audit rows are accepted only when explicitly identical or monotonically newer; incompatible conflicts abort instead of ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING. 5. Real PostgreSQL regressions prove late-failure cleanup, retry, companion-role access, isolation, and conflict denial; focused tests, npm run lint, build, and diff check pass.
notes: Dual blind review of fa336f2910..674b34518d: FAIL. Reviewer A reproduced runtime DDL ownership failure after restore, fleet-wide runtime role mapping that breaks tenant isolation, and a concurrent same-family restore race where a stale loser can drop the winner schemas. Reviewer B independently reproduced the production role-mapping/isolation defect and URI username versus effective ?user= divergence. Orchestrator verified all three committed source paths. One bounded remediation assigned on fix/opl1-restore-atomic-remediation; no successive inline cycle after final check.
close_reason: Integrated and pushed at feat/opl1-fleet-sso@1e03b2b233 after fixed point 674b34518d, dual blind review, one remediation d942415b3c, and final integration reconciliation. Evidence: canonical restore now preflights exact manifest schema/access identities, authenticates per-schema owners, serializes with a database advisory lock, cleans prepared families and retries safely, restores exact companion/shared grants and isolation, rejects routed owner credentials and incompatible durable/audit conflicts, and leaves fleet_auth inaccessible to companion roles. Integrated focused unit tests passed 22/22; real PostgreSQL family restore passed 1/1 and fleet-auth schema suite passed 22/22; npm run lint, npm run build, npm run verify:settings-contract, npm run verify:backup-restore, and git diff --check passed. Final-check residuals were routed—not hidden—to fresh P1 children psfn-framework-kl7y.4 (shared DDL migration authority) and psfn-framework-kl7y.5 (scheduled verifier canonical path), per docs/orchestration-process.md.

The replacement in src/persistence/backups/fleet-auth-coordinator.ts and fleet-auth-cycle.ts currently packages only companion/shared database dumps, fleet_auth JSON, and fleet-auth.json. This creates real recovery data loss while reporting healthy encrypted backups. Also, verifyRestore only verifies hashes/pg_restore TOC and sets manifestVerified=true without performing a scratch full-family restore. Scope: make the single gateway-owned fleet-auth lane preserve the canonical filesystem/workspace/system/Helm recovery coverage in the same authenticated encrypted family while keeping all database artifacts on the one exported snapshot and using only the dedicated backup/restore credential; make verifyRestore exercise a real scratch full-family restore. Reuse existing backup capture/contents primitives rather than a parallel format. Feature-off behavior stays byte-identical. Non-goals: OAuth/session product routes, auth policy, production deployment, Pi access, or companion POSTGRES_DATABASE_URL fallback. Current implementation branch/base: feat/opl1-fleet-sso@fa336f2910; owned work branch fix/opl1-backup-coverage.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Enabled fleet-auth produces exactly one gateway-owned encrypted family containing every companion database schema, shared schema, fleet_auth snapshot, fleet-auth.json, each companion data/session/journal/card slice, each personal workspace, governed shared workspace, system owner-file snapshot, and configured Kubernetes/Helm recovery artifact. 2. No companion/agent database credential or second/sequential dump is used; all database artifacts retain one exported PostgreSQL snapshot identity. 3. verifyRestore performs a real isolated scratch restore of the complete family and fails the cycle before publication on any database, filesystem, manifest, identity, or floor-preservation mismatch; success diagnostics distinguish actual restore verification. 4. Feature-off scheduled backups remain unchanged. 5. Regression tests prove coverage parity and detect a tampered/missing filesystem member and a restore-only failure; focused tests, npm run lint, build, and diff check pass.

title: Cross-channel continuity content ignores CogSec redaction on every persisted surface: wirebody.system, continuityEntries, Loom continuity views
description: Discovered during eb14 dual blind review (Opus reviewer, line-verified + mechanical repro; Pi independently confirmed the wirebody gating family). Cross-channel continuity entries (context-builder.ts:298 xmlElement('text', entry.content) -> body.system at :1072; persisted sessionContext.continuityEntries at :638) carry verbatim partner content from OTHER channels' journals with real L0 ids, but: (1) they are never plan.messages, so eb14's wire-body gate cannot key on them; (2) the origin channel's L0 state is unreadable from the consuming store's resolver (the exact reason 9ree excluded continuityEntries from the diet); (3) the un-gated continuityEntries surface renders in Loom continuityProvenance views independent of the wirebody. Concrete leak: partner message M in channel A -> turn T in channel B embeds M via continuity -> CogSec tombstone of M in channel A -> Loom read of T serves M verbatim from BOTH body.system and continuityEntries. Scope: one coherent cross-channel redaction propagation design covering all continuity-persisting surfaces (wirebody.system withhold key, continuityEntries gating, Loom views) — likely needs an origin-channel L0 resolution seam or a tombstone-fanout index; coordinate with the 9ree/hgw3.10 heal/telemetry conventions. Non-goals: same-channel gating (eb14), memory-store redaction (jsi9, shipped). Related: eb14 carve-out documented in that bead's close evidence.
acceptance_criteria: A CogSec tombstone applied in the origin channel results in the affected continuity content no longer being served verbatim from any persisted turn-record surface of any OTHER channel (wirebody.system, sessionContext.continuityEntries, Loom continuity/raw-wire views) — masked/withheld with telemetry; cross-channel resolution failures heal loudly rather than serving stale plaintext or breaking channel reads; regression test spans two channels (tombstone in A, assert gated reads in B); lint + sessions + garden suites green.
close_reason: Implemented and integrated: feat/ahxy-s10-shakedown-fixes @ abf73d02b (origin-equal; bead branch work/ahxy-ervg-sm9l @ ad20e27d3, shared with sm9l). Design: origin-channel L0 resolver seam (over tombstone-fanout) — continuity provenance records immutable source L0 entry IDs (continuity-provenance.ts); a shared bounded fail-closed resolver (continuity-redaction.ts, one range read per source channel, capped by the 20-entry continuity index) resolves origin-channel L0 state for BOTH the live getMerged path and every persisted surface (wirebody.system, sessionContext.continuityEntries, Loom continuity/provenance and orientation views, provider wire messages). Missing refs, tombstones, resolver errors, identity mismatches (5-field check), and forged non_persistent attestations all withhold with the standard redaction notice + heal-withhold telemetry (ids/reasons only, no content). Wired live: composition.ts createSessionComposition captures the production SessionStore getEntriesInRange. Evidence: manager.test drives the exact leak repro (tombstone in channel A scrubs M from channel B turn T's systemPrompt and every persisted surface) through real SessionStore/SessionManager/applyCogSecTombstones; 158/158 changed suites; gates green. Dual blind review (Opus + Pi) both PASS, zero blockers. Rollout notes (handoff): legacy continuity rows without sourceEntryId render as redaction placeholders until the window rolls (~20 appends/user) — consider one-time backfill by (channelId, role, timestamp); one withheld entry blanks the whole orientation/wire-body view for that turn (deliberate fail-closed over-redaction).

title: CogSec redaction must reach _shared/wirebodies: tombstoned partner content persists in capturedWirePayload and renders in Loom
description: Reclassified P1 by operator review of the wave-20260715 handoff (PR #77). The 80f6 wire capture persists the COMPLETE provider request body (system prompt, memories, partner messages) content-addressed under _shared/wirebodies/<sha>.json, resolves it unconditionally on turn-record reads (turn-record-shared-store resolveSerialized via turn-records.ts read compose chain), and renders it in the Loom 'Raw Wire Body' panel. The 9ree/hgw3.10 redaction propagation gates recentEntries and plan.messages only — a partner message tombstoned/redacted in L0 AFTER capture remains verbatim in capturedWirePayload.body and is served to the Garden. This is partner-data redaction/retention risk (Blocking Risk Standard: partner-data privacy), not report-only. Context: content-addressed dedup means one wirebody file may be shared across turns, so per-turn redaction is non-trivial (re-intern rewritten body vs dangle-and-heal); the read path currently fails closed on dangling refs (whole-channel), so naive deletion breaks Garden reads — the fix must handle refs (heal-on-absent for wirebodies, or rewrite+re-ref). Discovered-from: psfn-framework-80f6 (capture, Pi review observation #2/#4) and psfn-framework-hgw3.10 (which closed the sibling recentEntries surface). Non-goals: GC/retention policy (separate concern, coordinate), MoA turns (no capture).
acceptance_criteria: A CogSec tombstone/redaction applied to an L0 entry whose content appears in a captured wirebody results in that content no longer being served from any turn-record read or Loom surface (masked, healed, or rewritten — never verbatim); dangling/rewritten wirebody refs do not break whole-channel reads (heal path with telemetry, consistent with hgw3.10 semantics); regression test: capture a turn, tombstone a partner entry in L0, assert the Loom raw-wire view and getRecentTurnRecords no longer return the tombstoned plaintext; existing wirebody byte-identity tests updated to reflect the gated contract; lint + sessions suite green.
close_reason: Implemented @ e5f54ba6ab + remediation f79bf1a737 on fix/eb14-wirebody-cogsec, squash-merged to main @ 5656dcf2b2 (PR #80, agent-pair validated+merged). Read-time whole-body withhold ({withheld:'cogsec-redaction'} + safe metadata) at the SessionStore boundary on the union of three signals from the existing single L0 range read: plan.messages provenance suppression, current-turn partner entry (userMessage.sessionEntryId — structurally excluded from plan.messages per prompt-assembly.ts:499 guard) redacted/absent, and any window redaction/heal-drop; empty-plan bypass removed; sidecar files never touched (shared refs + fail-closed dangling semantics intact); telemetry turn_record_wire_body_withheld. Review gate (P1 dual blind + UBS clean): BOTH reviewers FAILed the first cut with different verified blockers — Pi: current-turn exclusion gap (confirmed at every line; original test used production-impossible shape); Opus: cross-channel continuity leak in body.system (line-verified + repro). Single remediation fixed the current-turn gap with production-shape regressions; continuity carved out per orchestrator ruling to P1 psfn-framework-ervg (all three continuity surfaces coherently — identical content leaks independently via un-gated continuityEntries) with docstrings corrected to claim exactly what is gated. Also discovered → P1 psfn-framework-sm9l (frozen userMessage/assistantMessage copies ignore tombstones). Final gates: 496 sessions+garden tests, 8/8 regression file incl. current-turn-tombstone→withheld, lint, build, validator-confirmed on the PR.

title: Fail queued durable extraction closed when shutdown begins
description: Final Standards review of u5bv.8 range cd0c8b9b6c..017b518eda reproduced a shutdown race that can mark a durable snapshot covered without writing it. MemoryExtractor.trackExtraction serializes bounded B behind existing same-session work at src/faculties/memory/extraction.ts:454-491. If BackgroundWorkSupervisor shutdown times out and MemoryExtractor.stop flips acceptingExtractions before B's chained run starts, the extraction orchestrator skips fact writes at src/faculties/memory/extraction/orchestrator.ts:476 but resolves normally. maybeExtract then advances B coverage and the effect receipt completes. Scope: distinguish not-started/draining from successfully consumed; queued durable work must either finish its exact snapshot or fail/defer so the job and receipt remain retryable. Non-goals: no forced process hang, no receipt deletion after a possibly committed effect, no weakening graceful shutdown timeouts.

title: Keep kube operator credentials out of the agent approval path
description: Final Spec review of x5rt.4 range 2128dca325..4035e2df64 reproduced an operator-boundary bypass in the one allowed remediation. src/operator/garden/api-routes.ts forwards the browser's ADMIN_TOKEN Authorization/Cookie through the agent-hosted Garden admin transport; src/app/agent/admin-surface.ts wires src/app/startup/support/gateway-operator-confirmation-client.ts so the agent process relays that credential to the gateway operator endpoint. Even though ADMIN_TOKEN is absent from the agent environment, the less-trusted agent can capture and replay the credential, then resolve its own kube mutation. Scope: move the credential-bearing gateway confirmation call into the independently authenticated Garden operator process, which already owns ADMIN_TOKEN, while keeping companion/agent RPC resolution denied for operator-only kube entries. Remove credential forwarding, operator endpoint client authority, related env, and related network access from the agent. Preserve the separate gateway ADMIN_TOKEN endpoint, exact resolver identity audit, ServiceAccount token rotation, and executed-but-result-audit-failed semantics delivered by x5rt.4. Files: src/operator/garden/operator-surface.ts and/or transport proxy boundary, src/operator/garden/api-routes.ts, src/app/agent/admin-surface.ts, src/app/startup/support/gateway-operator-confirmation-client.ts, src/channels/api/server.ts, deployment Helm/network policy and verification tests. Non-goals: no broad SSO redesign, no shared admin token in agent env, no off-repo proxy, no enabling production kube mutations, no live deployment.
design: The operator process must originate the gateway operator confirmation request only after its own authenticated Garden HTTP boundary succeeds. Credential bytes must not traverse the agent process or its admin transport. Agent-local confirmation listing may remain sanitized, but operator-only resolution must route directly from operator to gateway using repo-owned endpoint configuration and existing ADMIN_TOKEN ownership. The gateway continues to bind resolver {kind:operator,id:garden-admin}; normal agent RPC supplies companion identity and is rejected for resolutionAuthority=operator.

An authenticated Garden operator can resolve an operator-only kube confirmation through a direct operator-to-gateway path; unauthenticated, agent-RPC, and cross-companion attempts fail closed and leave the entry pending. 3. title: Make fleet-auth lifecycle witness transitions monotonic across replicas
description: Fresh final review of opl1.2 combined range 5d1785dcb1..464be9d9cd reproduced a lost disable-to-re-enable transition across gateway replicas. FleetAuthLifecycleWitnessStore.prepareEnable at src/persistence/postgres/fleet-auth/lifecycle-witness.ts:93-109 releases its file lock before floor/DB reconciliation; recordEnabled at :112-123 later overwrites the witness unconditionally. initializeGatewayFleetAuthPersistence spans prepare, floor open, database reconcile, and record across src/persistence/postgres/fleet-auth/gateway-persistence.ts:243-256. Race: enabled replica A prepares with no transition; feature-off replica B records disabled; stale A records enabled; the next enable sees enabled and skips checkpoint/epoch fencing, so old sessions survive. Scope: make lifecycle transitions monotonic and replica-safe through the complete startup publish boundary. Non-goals: no global singleton gateway assumption, no long-held filesystem lock across network I/O, no feature-off state for never-enabled installs, and no loss of ordinary same-generation restart sessions.
design: Use a versioned transition token/CAS or equivalent two-phase witness protocol. prepareEnable returns the exact witness version it observed. recordEnabled may publish only if that version and phase remain unchanged; a concurrent disabled transition wins, stale startup must fail before listen, and its next retry consumes the disable transition through the non-restored floor. All writes remain durable/atomic and lineage-bound.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Deterministic two-replica interleaving A prepare-enabled, B record-disabled, A stale publish cannot erase disabled; A rejects before listen and the next enable advances restore checkpoint/auth epoch and clears ephemerals. 2. Simultaneous enabled restarts converge idempotently without revoking valid sessions or corrupting the witness. 3. Repeated disable calls and crash at every prepare/floor/DB/publish boundary over-fence or recover; no transition is lost. 4. Never-enabled feature-off remains state-free; lineage mismatch/missing floor fails closed. 5. Focused lifecycle/unit plus disposable-Postgres startup races, npm run lint, build/DTS, and diff check pass.

Deterministic unit and disposable-Postgres coverage includes simultaneous ordinary restarts, exact prepare→disable→stale-publish refusal, next-retry epoch/checkpoint/session fencing, repeated disable idempotence, never-enabled read-only state-free behavior, lineage/missing-floor failure, and crashes before/after DB reconciliation. title: Treat empty bounded post-turn snapshots as authoritative
description: Final review of immutable u5bv.4 range fa2fdde0a4..cd0c8b9b6c reproduced the original cross-turn redaction race through an empty-snapshot fallback. SessionStore.withStableTurnRecordEligibilitySnapshot at src/persistence/sessions/store.ts:1164-1219 accepts an empty content snapshot when requiredTurnIds contains the canonical source TurnID, locks that source, rechecks empty equals empty, and invokes the effect. The memory handler passes that authoritative empty array through src/core/agent/background-work/post-turn-runtime.ts:168-192 and src/faculties/memory/extraction.ts:287-296. runExtractionOrchestration at src/faculties/memory/extraction/orchestrator.ts:282-289 treats recoveredEntries.length === 0 as though no snapshot was supplied, rereads current live history, and consumes TurnIDs that were never fenced. Scenario: B has an empty or missing bounded history while live A/C appear; redaction of A/C completes during extraction and stale content can be durably written. Scope: distinguish no snapshot from an authoritative empty snapshot across post-turn handlers and fail/defer closed when required bounded history is missing. Non-goals: no live fallback for a durable job, no process-local dedupe, and no weakening of source or consumed-record eligibility.
design: Represent snapshot presence explicitly rather than overloading array length. When a durable handler supplies recoveredEntries, an empty array is authoritative: either the operation deterministically skips with no sink write or raises the existing source-not-ready/source-missing classification. Any fallback live read is permitted only for legacy foreground call sites that did not supply a snapshot at all.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Canonical source B plus authoritative empty bounded snapshot and live A/C never invokes getRecentMessages, consumes A/C, or writes a durable effect. 2. Undefined snapshot retains the intentionally supported foreground behavior, while [] is never reinterpreted as undefined anywhere in memory extraction, emotion appraisal, or compaction. 3. Missing/reduced history during a durable job deterministically skips, defers, or fails closed with an operator-visible reason and preserves retry semantics. 4. Non-empty snapshots remain exact under lock and redaction/tombstone races still defer or reject. 5. Focused orchestrator/post-turn/session and disposable-Postgres race tests, npm run lint, npm run build/DTS, and git diff --check pass.

title: Project bounded post-turn snapshots through ICP delivery status
description: Final review of immutable u5bv.4 range fa2fdde0a4..cd0c8b9b6c reproduced durable ingestion of failed or undelivered ICP assistant output. createIcpDeliveryProjectionStore in src/core/session/manager/icp-delivery-projection-store.ts:89-128 filters getRecent and getEntriesInRange but forwards getEntriesBefore directly to the raw journal. The new bounded memory path calls SessionManager.getRecentMessagesAtOrBefore at src/core/session/manager.ts:1785-1799, which uses that unprojected method. Bounded compaction at src/core/session/manager.ts:932-943 calls this.store.getEntriesBefore directly. Scenario: turn A persists a pending assistant response, delivery fails, later successful turn B snapshots history; ordinary getRecent hides A while bounded memory and compaction include it, allowing partner-private unsent content into durable memories or summaries. Scope: apply the canonical ICP delivery projection to every bounded ordinary extraction, emotion, and compaction read before the consumed TurnID set is derived and fenced. Raw journal access remains only for explicit restart-safe delivery recovery. Non-goals: do not delete failed delivery records, change retry semantics, or weaken exact TurnRecord fencing.
design: Extend the shared delivery projection primitive rather than duplicating status logic. getEntriesBefore and any bounded compaction adapter must filter pending, failed, and suppressed ICP assistant entries identically to getRecent, while delivered entries remain visible. The projected snapshot itself defines the exact consumed TurnIDs acquired by u5bv.4.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Failed, pending, and suppressed ICP assistant A followed by successful B is absent from memory extraction, emotion appraisal, and auto-compaction inputs and cannot produce a durable sink row or summary. 2. Delivered A remains included with identical ordering, limits, compaction-boundary behavior, room-window gating, and non-ICP behavior. 3. All bounded SessionStore read methods used by ordinary context/extraction/compaction honor the canonical delivery projection; raw access is named and limited to delivery recovery. 4. Snapshot lock sets are derived after projection and still re-read/revalidate exact entries under lock. 5. Focused ICP projection, post-turn, session manager, real-Postgres race tests, npm run lint, npm run build/DTS, and git diff --check pass.
notes: Implemented in commit 777b382107 on isolated branch fix/u5bv-icp-projected-snapshots. Canonical ICP delivery projection now implements paged getEntriesBefore with bounded-order/limit backfill, failed/pending/suppressed exclusion, delivered visibility, and fail-closed page progress. CompactionBoundaryStore now owns bounded getEntriesBefore, and source-bounded auto-compaction reads it instead of the raw journal. Real post-turn SessionManager coverage proves memory, emotion, and durable compaction summary inputs exclude failed ICP A while retaining successful B. Disposable-Postgres race proves projection happens before consumed TurnID fence derivation (failed A fence remains free while B is held), exact projected entries are reread after fences, and a concurrent failed-to-delivered status change aborts before a second durable sink write. Regression controls cover delivered/non-ICP order and limits, compaction-summary boundary behavior, and source-id plus room-window floors. Validation: 145 affected tests across projection, post-turn, ICP restart, room-window, SessionManager, stale-window, and full Postgres background-work integration; npm run lint PASS; npm run build/DTS PASS; git diff --check PASS; focused UBS production scan exit 0.
