title: Make multi-write post-turn effects retry-safe
description: Final review of immutable mmo9.3 range 5d1785dcb1..fa2fdde0a4 reproduced duplicate durable effects after an ordinary post-write exception. src/core/agent/background-work/post-turn-runtime.ts:147-156 wraps an entire handler in one receipt; memory extraction performs multiple fact writes at src/faculties/memory/extraction/orchestrator.ts:682-799. src/core/agent/background-work/supervisor.ts:574-600 deletes the started receipt whenever the operation throws, and :470-477 schedules a generic retry. A real supervisor plus Postgres job store and durable sink wrote the same logical effect twice: first execution wrote then threw, receipt was removed, retry repeated the write and succeeded. MemoryExtractor also launches contact-profile/emotional persistence after maybeExtract returns at orchestrator.ts:860-880, extraction.ts:853-918, runtime-helpers.ts:269-292, and profile-synthesis.ts:288-295, allowing the outer receipt/fence to become applied and release while durable children remain in flight. Scope: give every durable child write an idempotent/transactional boundary that survives exceptions and keep the job receipt/fence open until all durable children settle. Non-goals: no swallowing handler errors, no blanket terminal failure for safely retryable pre-effect work, no reliance on process-local dedupe, and no detaching durable writes from job lifecycle.
design: Use stable per-logical-effect idempotency keys and sink-level atomic insert/upsert or per-child durable receipts. Never delete evidence that an effect may have occurred merely because the enclosing operation threw. Convert detached profile/emotional writes into awaited job-owned work or separately durable child jobs with their own receipts and eligibility fences. The parent job may become applied only when every owned durable child is applied; ambiguous children quarantine, while proven unapplied children can retry.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Failure injected after the first durable child write but before parent completion produces exactly one logical sink row across retry and restart; no started/ambiguous receipt is deleted into a duplicate-capable state. 2. Multi-fact memory extraction, emotion/reflection/compaction, profile synthesis, and any other multi-write handler use stable per-effect idempotency or one atomic transaction. 3. No durable child remains detached after the parent receipt is applied or its TurnRecord eligibility fence is released; shutdown waits/requeues or persists the child independently. 4. Pre-write exceptions remain retryable, post-write unknown outcomes fail closed, and fully applied receipts short-circuit duplicates. 5. Real-Postgres crash/exception/retry tests, focused handler tests, mandatory npm run lint, npm run build/DTS, and git diff --check pass.
close_reason: Implemented on work/mmo9-u5bv.6 (dfa9a0c7e2..69f1d81b6f), integrated to feat/mmo9-background-supervisor@e41f818086 (pushed; orchestrator resolved a post-turn-runtime.ts conflict with u5bv.10 snapshot-limit wiring, keeping both the interval sizing and the boundary-fence semantics). Three coupled fixes: (1) abandonEffect deletes ONLY a pending receipt — a boundary-crossed 'started' receipt survives, so a post-write exception fails closed as outcome_unknown on retry instead of replaying (closes the reproduced duplicate); (2) memory extraction crosses its durable boundary at the FIRST real durable write via a threaded non-crossing pre-write fence (input.effects.assertOwned), not at handler entry, so pre-write transient failures stay retryable; (3) detached contact-profile/emotional children now awaited inside the effect-guarded region (each self-swallows best-effort failure). Evidence at worker head: background-work integration 26/26; combined focused+integration 314 + 309 pass (extraction, writer, contacts incl. postgres-adapter, post-turn-runtime 14, supervisor 11) incl. new real-supervisor+PG+durable-sink exactly-once-across-retry test, store-level abandon-never-deletes-started, orchestrator await-ordering; integrated revalidation @e41f818086: 143 background-work+extraction tests + lint + build/DTS + diff-check clean. UBS range scan: no new critical/warning. Pi (GLM 5.2 @high) blind adversarial review: PASS, 0 blocking — traced every receipt-mutating path (no path deletes/downgrades a started receipt), confirmed every durable write from maybeExtract crosses the boundary first, detached children run post-cross so a retry cannot re-enter them. Nonblocking (handoff only): retry_exhausted vs effect_outcome_unknown reason-code labeling on max_attempts=1 (no duplicate); beginEffect same-owner+revision 'execute' resume is a latent footgun if a future handler calls effects.run twice per claim (pre-existing from u5bv.5); multi-fact partial-write fail-closed (1..k persist, k+1..N not retried) = accepted AC2 fail-closed design; scheduleProfileRefresh coalescing widens receipt-open window (no duplicate).

title: Requeue pre-effect jobs safely during graceful shutdown
description: Final review of immutable mmo9.3 range 5d1785dcb1..fa2fdde0a4 reproduced loss of work that had not crossed any side-effect boundary. src/core/agent/background-work/supervisor.ts:554-576 writes an effects.run started receipt before provider/compute begins. Supervisor stop at :330-347 waits five seconds but does not release or requeue claims; production closes stores at src/app/agent/control-plane.ts:172-202 and src/app/agent/main.ts:889-892. On restart src/persistence/postgres/background-work-store.ts:1164-1204 converts every expired job with a started receipt into terminal effect_outcome_unknown, even when sinkWrites=0. Scope: distinguish safely cancelable/pre-effect work from genuinely outcome-ambiguous work, and make graceful stop durably requeue or release only the former before closing stores. Preserve fail-closed handling once any externally durable effect may have occurred. Non-goals: no process-wide kill semantics, no assuming provider cancellation proves an external side effect absent, no infinite shutdown wait, and no weakening multi-replica lease ownership.
design: Introduce an explicit durable phase boundary rather than treating handler entry as effect entry. A job canceled before that boundary can be returned to pending/retry state under its claim token during graceful shutdown; a job at or beyond the boundary retains outcome-unknown quarantine unless an idempotent receipt proves completion. Supervisor stop must coordinate active AbortSignals, bounded drain, and claim release/requeue before Postgres close. Recovery must classify from the durable phase, not merely receipt existence.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A real-Postgres graceful-shutdown race with a blocked provider/compute step and zero sink writes stops within the configured bound, durably requeues the job, and a new supervisor completes it exactly once. 2. A crash or shutdown after crossing the possible-effect boundary remains fail closed as effect_outcome_unknown unless an applied receipt proves completion. 3. Shutdown never releases a claim while the old worker can still cross the effect boundary; cancellation and ownership checks are ordered and tested. 4. Multi-replica claim recovery, lease expiry, bounded quarantine/crash recovery, and normal drain behavior remain correct. 5. Focused unit and disposable Postgres tests, mandatory npm run lint, npm run build/DTS, and git diff --check pass.
close_reason: Implemented on work/mmo9-u5bv.5 (1c5cc05db3..38d37c4b4b), integrated to feat/mmo9-background-supervisor@dfa9a0c7e2 (pushed). Introduced explicit durable phase boundary in the background-work effect model: beginEffect writes a 'pending' receipt (run entered, no external write attempted = requeue-safe); handler pre-write fence promotes to 'started' via new commitEffectBoundary, then 'applied'. supervisor.stop aborts per-claim AbortSignal, bounded-drains, then durably requeues only pre-boundary claims (no started/applied receipt) under their claim token via requeuePreBoundaryClaims (per-session serialized; revision bump fences in-flight workers); boundary-crossed claims left for fail-closed lease-expiry recovery. recoverExpired discards 'pending' receipts and classifies from durable phase (only 'started' -> effect_outcome_unknown). Migration adds 'pending' state (backward-safe for existing started/applied rows). No faculty/handler code changed. Evidence at worker head: supervisor.test.ts(11)+post-turn-runtime.test.ts(14)+background-work-store.integration.test.ts real-PG(23, incl. graceful-shutdown-requeue exactly-once race + pre/post-boundary discrimination)+runtime-factory(4)+substrate/turn-support/scheduler(129); lint/build(DTS)/diff-check clean. Integrated revalidation @dfa9a0c7e2: 49 background-work tests + lint clean. UBS range scan: no new critical/warning vs base. Pi (GLM 5.2 @high) blind adversarial review: PASS, 0 blocking — verified the safety invariant airtight (transaction-scoped pg_advisory_xact_lock + revision/owner fencing: requeue<=>no write, write<=>requeue skipped). Nonblocking observations (handoff only): concurrent cross-during-stop path argued-correct but not execution-tested; assertOwned/assertEffectAllowed type carries no write-boundary meaning (future-handler footgun); recoverExpired two-statement autocommit; wide-shutdown lock latency. Unblocks u5bv.6.

title: Fence every TurnRecord consumed by a post-turn effect
description: Final review of immutable mmo9.3 range 5d1785dcb1..fa2fdde0a4 reproduced a stale-source write across turns. src/persistence/postgres/turn-record-eligibility-fence.ts:14-20 keys the advisory fence by logicalSessionId plus the durable job source turnId, and src/core/agent/background-work/post-turn-runtime.ts:133-142 holds only that source fence. Memory extraction reads the whole recent session window at src/faculties/memory/extraction/orchestrator.ts:285-292 and writes derived facts at :682-799; emotion and compaction handlers also consume multi-turn windows. Concrete failure: older turn A contains content later redacted; newer turn B schedules extraction; B holds only its own fence while redaction of A completes under a different key; B then persists A-derived content. Scope: make every TurnRecord whose content can influence a durable post-turn effect participate in the same eligibility serialization/recheck as that effect, using stable lock ordering and bounded consumed sets or an equally strong source-only design. Preserve canonical fingerprint, duplicate, tombstone, restore, and queue ownership checks inside the effect boundary. Non-goals: no broad extraction redesign, no weakening redaction, no content-bearing diagnostics, and no unbounded session-wide lock.
design: At the point the handler forms its bounded input snapshot, identify the exact consumed TurnIDs. Serialize with TurnRecord redact/restore/tombstone writers for every consumed ID in deterministic order, then re-read/revalidate the snapshot while fenced and keep the fence through the effect receipt/sink boundary. If a handler cannot enumerate exact consumed records, fail closed or narrow it to an enumerable source; never assume the durable job source TurnID covers the whole recent window. Audit lock ordering against foreground/session fences and prove no reverse acquisition.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A deterministic real-Postgres race with turn A in the recent window and source turn B proves redaction/restore of A cannot complete while a B effect can still consume A; after redaction wins, B rechecks and performs no A-derived write. 2. Memory, emotion, reflection/compaction, and every other multi-turn post-turn handler enumerate and fence all content-bearing TurnIDs or are explicitly source-only with tests. 3. Duplicate TurnRecords, source tombstones, sibling-store redactions, and restore remain exact and fail closed. 4. Advisory locks acquire in stable order with bounded cardinality; cross-session work remains concurrent and no deadlock/reverse-order path is found. 5. Focused unit and disposable Postgres races, mandatory npm run lint, npm run build/DTS, and git diff --check pass.
notes:
Implemented in cd0c8b9b6c on isolated range fa2fdde0a4..cd0c8b9b6c. Class-6 TOCTOU fix: bounded exact session snapshots enumerate every consumed TurnID, acquire deduplicated Postgres advisory fences in canonical order, re-read exact content under lock, revalidate physical-source ownership/tombstone/duplicate eligibility, and hold all fences through effect receipt and durable sink. Memory, emotion, and auto-compaction now consume their exact source-bounded snapshots; the sole production intention hook was audited source-only because it consumes only the canonical source message/response pair. Lock audit found eligibility outer, queue-effect/session-tail/filesystem locks inner, no reverse acquisition; 512 unique-TurnID cap fails closed. Deterministic disposable-Postgres race proves A redaction wins over B stale capture with no stale sink write, restore blocks through the consuming effect, reverse-order overlap completes, unrelated sessions remain concurrent, and duplicate TurnRecords fail closed. Validation: 122 tests across Postgres integration/supervisor/turn execution; 247 focused post-turn/session/memory/wiring tests; 3 emotion-scoping tests; npm run lint; npm run build including DTS; git diff --check. Sibling beads u5bv.5 and u5bv.6 untouched. No Pi or production access.
2026-07-15 fresh final review of fa2fdde0a4..cd0c8b9b6c verified two residual P1 interactions after implementation/lint/build passed: bounded getEntriesBefore/compaction reads bypass the ICP delivery projection, and authoritative empty recoveredEntries falls back to live unfenced history. No second inline remediation was started. Fresh children psfn-framework-u5bv.7 and .8 own the verified leftovers; .4 remains isolated pending integration into the mmo9.3 candidate.
close_reason: Implemented and integrated into the mmo9 candidate at cd0c8b9b6c. Exact bounded consumed-TurnID fencing, deterministic multi-lock ordering, under-lock snapshot/physical TurnRecord revalidation, 512-key fail-closed cap, and source-only intention audit shipped on the integration branch. Validation passed: 372 focused unit/disposable-Postgres tests, npm run lint, build/DTS, and diff check. Fresh final review found two separate cross-module interactions; per the bounded process they are fully tracked as psfn-framework-u5bv.7 (ICP delivery projection) and .8 (empty-snapshot fallback), so the u5bv/mmo9 candidate remains unshipped until those children plus .5/.6 and a combined final check complete.

title: Add versioned owner-file migration preflight to Kubernetes rollouts
description: The first live rollout of merged 5d1785dcb1 failed closed twice before application readiness because existing canonical owner files predated newly mandatory schema fields. /app/system-data/scheduler.json lacked scheduler.icpAutonomy; after an atomic disabled-default migration, /app/system-data/charge-policy.json lacked companion_social, companionSocialContinuation, icpCostBreaker, and fatigue.socialRegulation. A merge-missing-defaults one-shot allowed the new image to start, but rollback to the prior image then correctly rejected the new icpCostBreaker key until only the newly added fields were removed again. This demonstrates that required owner-schema changes currently have no versioned deploy preflight or reversible cutover contract. Scope: design and implement an explicit alpha migration lane for canonical JSON owner files used by scripts/ops/ship-kube-update.sh and live Kubernetes deployment; include dry-run, exact old/new schema recognition, operator-value preservation, atomic writes, audit evidence, forward validation by the target image, and rollback compatibility/snapshot restoration. Add the temporary support to the named live alpha migration boundary in docs/specifications.md with beta-removal criteria before enabling it. Files likely include focused scripts/ops migration modules/tests, config validators/seed metadata, ship/validate scripts, and specifications/operations docs only where contractually required. Non-goals: no generic recursive seed merge, no silent startup fallback, no overwriting existing operator values, no acceptance of unknown/malformed keys, no parallel config roots, and no automatic production mutation without an explicit approved release step.
design: Use a small versioned migration registry keyed by owner file and exact from/to schema fingerprint, not ad hoc default merging. Each migration declares preconditions, additions/removals/transforms, invariant checks, and reverse/restore strategy. The ship preflight runs target-image validation against a read-only snapshot, emits a content-safe plan, requires the existing deployment authorization boundary, then performs an atomic in-volume transaction and records before/after digests without values. If Helm rollout fails, rollback restores the exact pre-migration owner bytes before starting the old image. Unknown source shapes or operator-modified migration fields fail closed for manual review.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Fixtures matching the pre-5d1785 live scheduler and charge-policy shapes migrate to the target schemas while preserving every pre-existing JSON value, including custom run-charge quotas; only declared fields are added. 2. Forward migration is atomic, fsyncs file+directory, emits only file/version/digests/changed paths, and target validators accept the result; malformed/unknown/already-modified shapes fail without changing bytes. 3. A forced Helm failure restores exact pre-migration bytes before old pods restart, and the prior validators accept them; successful rollout retains the new schema. 4. ship-kube-update integrates the preflight without remote git resets or off-repo authoritative config, and validate-kube-rollout verifies the expected schema/version. 5. docs/specifications.md names the temporary alpha boundary, validation, and beta-removal criteria. 6. Focused migration/ship tests, verify:settings-contract where applicable, verify:helm-chart, mandatory npm run lint, npm run build, and git diff --check pass.
close_reason: Duplicate of existing psfn-framework-m82u. The full 2026-07-15 scheduler/charge-policy rollout and rollback incident, versioned registry design, target-image preflight, exact-byte rollback, custom-value preservation, alpha-boundary requirement, and acceptance criteria were merged into m82u; relation to 5vhi added.

title: Wire the audit opaque-ID HMAC dependency into the Kubernetes agent
description: Live rollout of merged framework commit 5d1785dcb1 failed after successful scheduler/charge-policy owner migrations: psfn-agent initialized, then src/operator/garden/local-admin-contract.ts failed closed because Garden audit history opaque IDs required key material. The first candidate f7d924e9 wired the gateway root GATEWAY_SESSION_HMAC_KEY into the agent; independent security review correctly rejected that because src/boundary/gateway/companion-auth.ts can use the root keyring to mint arbitrary companion/role proofs. The agent already receives a distinct role-bound GATEWAY_SESSION_INTEGRITY_AUTH_TOKEN in Helm and from the scrubbed split launcher. Scope: derive a dedicated Garden audit opaque-ID keyring from that worker proof with a one-way domain-separated transform, remove the gateway root from the agent, preserve fail-closed validation, and prove both rendered Helm and env-i split-launch boundaries. Relevant files: src/operator/garden/audit-opaque-id-keyring.ts, src/operator/garden/local-admin-contract.ts, deploy/helm/psfn/templates/workloads.yaml, scripts/verify-helm-chart.mjs, and focused script-verification tests. Non-goals: do not expose or copy the gateway root, add a parallel live secret lifecycle, weaken audit key requirements, change gateway proof verification, move audit history ownership, or redesign the session-integrity RPC.
design: Treat the already-delegated internal_session_integrity proof as pseudorandom input material, not as the audit key itself. Validate the canonical version.hex64 proof shape; HMAC the proof digest under the fixed psfn-garden-audit-opaque-id-key-v1 domain plus key version; expose the result only as an AuditOpaqueIdKeyring to the Garden audit service. Local admin construction consumes config.gatewaySessionIntegrityAuthToken, which agent-mode config already requires and sanitizes from public admin config. Kubernetes keeps GATEWAY_SESSION_HMAC_KEY only in gateway; agent keeps its existing GATEWAY_SESSION_INTEGRITY_AUTH_TOKEN Secret reference, and Garden gets neither. npm run split already derives/passes the worker proof through its env-i allowlist; the regression executes a real derivation probe inside that scrubbed child and proves the root is absent. Rotating the worker proof intentionally changes opaque IDs while preserving the underlying audit records.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Parsed rendered Helm container env shows GATEWAY_SESSION_HMAC_KEY exactly in gateway and absent from agent/Garden; agent retains only its role-bound GATEWAY_SESSION_INTEGRITY_AUTH_TOKEN dependency. 2. A stable known-vector test proves domain-separated audit-key derivation; absent/malformed proofs fail closed, and a proof minted with the derived audit key is rejected by the gateway root keyring. 3. A real env-i split-launch regression proves the scrubbed agent receives the worker proof, never receives the gateway root, and can derive the expected audit keyring. 4. In-process Garden server/API and audit-history suites pass with the scoped derivation; no literal production secret, fallback to root, new secret owner path, or Garden exposure is introduced. 5. helm lint, parsed rendered-manifest test, npm run verify:helm-chart including provenance, mandatory npm run lint, npm run build including DTS, targeted tests, and git diff --check pass. 6. After merge, an exact-image rollout to the operator-directed local k3d cluster reaches Ready for agent/gateway/Garden; Garden health and authenticated audit-history API pass without audit-key startup errors; rendered live env still keeps the root gateway-only. Production rollout is explicitly out of scope after the operator directed that psfn-shard receive no further deployment testing.
notes:
Live red at 5d1785dcb1 / Helm rev58: agent completed core initialization then failed with Session HMAC keyring is required for Garden audit history opaque IDs; live was restored to old image at Helm rev59. Initial f7d924e9 regression proved the missing dependency but incorrectly mounted the gateway proof-signing root into agent. Remediation RED evidence: parsed rendered Helm failed because agent had GATEWAY_SESSION_HMAC_KEY; the env-i split child could not construct an audit keyring from its actual scoped environment. Green remediation commit 2ab9bdc91a derives a separate audit key from the existing worker proof and removes the root mount, so chart contents/recovery digest return to the origin/main baseline. Immutable review range: 5d1785dcb12c59e064c4a0b57028164523e7e9f5..2ab9bdc91a; bounded remediation commit: f7d924e9a1400387011b62531e2e333ddce7c9ab..2ab9bdc91a. Evidence: derivation unit 6/6; combined audit/Helm/launcher suites 63/63; Garden server 21/21; Garden API 47/47; helm lint; verify:helm-chart including recovery digest and selective-rollout provenance; mandatory lint; build ESM+DTS; diff-check. Exact live rollout remains pending after merge.
2026-07-15 operator scope correction: stop all psfn-shard deployment work and use the local cluster. PR #71 merged as 2128dca32506c716aa80d9a4b176d81eb692db49. Exact native-amd64 image localhost/psfn-framework:0.1.0-kube-2128dca3 rolled out only to local k3d context k3d-psfn-kube-test, Helm psfn-test revision 14. title: Fence TurnRecord eligibility through content-consuming background effects
description: Final independent review of the frozen mmo9.3 candidate at d7179bd1d0 reproduced a privacy-relevant TOCTOU race. src/core/agent/background-work/post-turn-runtime.ts requireCanonicalTurnRecord() checks source eligibility/tombstone state once before raw TurnRecord rehydration, then later effect fencing checks only queue-claim ownership. A concurrent tombstone or uniqueness revocation after rehydration can therefore allow raw user/assistant content to reach intention effects; src/core/intention/runtime-wiring.ts passes assistant content to src/core/intention/postgres-adapters/intention-record-adapter.ts, which can persist a private excerpt. Scope: make canonical source eligibility authoritative through every content-consuming/durable effect boundary for all four mmo9.3 job kinds, coordinated with tombstone/uniqueness writes and queue ownership. title: Fence same-session foreground ownership through background side-effect boundaries
description: Final independent review of the frozen mmo9.3 candidate at d7179bd1d0 reproduced three fail-open interleavings in the durable BackgroundWorkSupervisor. (1) src/persistence/postgres/background-work-store.ts beginForeground() takes a per-session advisory lock but claimNext() does not, so replica B can claim while replica A foreground acquisition is in flight; the foreground commit then leaves the already-running claim untouched. (2) src/core/agent/background-work/supervisor.ts executeClaim() checks foreground state only once; effects.assertOwned() checks queue ownership but not foreground leases, so a foreground turn arriving before the side-effect boundary can overlap a background durable effect. (3) foreground renewal loss is only logged by ensureHeartbeat(); ForegroundWorkLease exposes no ownership-loss signal, so after lease expiry another replica can claim while the original foreground turn is still local. Scope: make the per-session foreground fence authoritative across acquisition, claim, every content/durable side-effect boundary, renewal loss, defer/retry, and cross-replica operation; preserve cross-session concurrency and the existing record-first handoff. Likely files: src/persistence/postgres/background-work-store.ts and its integration tests; src/core/agent/background-work/supervisor.ts, types/ports, and tests. Non-goals: no provider preemption or reserved capacity, no sub-tick scheduler/cadence work from mmo9.5, no broad supervisor rewrite, and no change to the four handler semantics.
design: Use one durable session-serialization/ownership contract shared by foreground acquisition, background claim, and effect fencing. A background claim must not cross a durable effect boundary unless it can prove both queue-claim ownership and absence of a current same-session foreground lease. Foreground lease renewal loss must become an observable ownership-loss signal to the local turn/supervisor rather than a log-only condition. Safe pre-effect work should durably defer and resume under the same idempotency key; already-committed effects must not be duplicated. Keep telemetry content-free and fail closed on store/check errors.

A deterministic supervisor test lets a claim pass its initial check, begins foreground work before effects.assertOwned, and proves the background effect does not run; the same idempotency key durably defers and resumes exactly once after foreground release. 3. A forced renewForeground ownership-loss/expiry test proves the original local foreground lease receives a loss signal and no second replica can execute a same-session background effect while that foreground work remains active. 4. Cross-session claims remain concurrent; retry deadlines/idempotency/effect receipts and shutdown behavior remain correct. 5. Focused supervisor/store tests, disposable real-Postgres integration, touched SubstrateAgent tests, mandatory npm run lint, npm run build, and git diff --check pass.
notes: Implemented one authoritative per-session Postgres advisory fence across foreground begin/renew/end, background claim, and effect receipt start. claimNext uses try-lock session selection so an in-flight same-session foreground acquisition cannot be crossed while unrelated sessions remain claimable. ForegroundWorkLease now exposes an AbortSignal. Renewal loss aborts the exact request-owned active agent run and observed expiry leaves a bounded durable quarantine; a crashed owner recovers after that bounded window. title: Fence passkey revocation across fleet-auth restore
description:
## Summary
Correct the canonical Fleet SSO decision so an old fleet_auth backup cannot resurrect a revoked or replaced WebAuthn passkey. Current gap: opl1.2 persists passkey_credentials in the restorable artifact, but its authority_generation covers provider/link/tombstone/contact binding/role and global_auth_epoch invalidates only session/grant/challenge/evidence state. opl1.1 restore design and AC14, the opl1 parent restore prose, opl1.10 strong JIT/passkey replacement, and opl1.12 restore certification omit passkey credentials and their revocation history from the non-restored monotonic fence.

## Rationale
Concrete P1 failure: back up with passkey A active; A is stolen; trusted-host recovery revokes A and enrolls B; restore the old artifact; exact legitimate account/binding/role reapproval later makes restored A registered again unless credential authority is independent. A can then satisfy user-verifying strong JIT or trusted-ingress opl1.15 privacy break-glass. An auth epoch bump is insufficient because resurrected A can mint new current-epoch sessions and grants. This is partner-data/privacy exposure and account-recovery rollback, so old A must remain denied even after legitimate account authority is reapproved.

## Alternatives Considered
1. Rely on global_auth_epoch: rejected because it invalidates existing ephemeral authority but does not make restored credential A revoked when A authenticates again. 2. Let exact account/binding/role reapproval also promote restored passkeys: rejected because it conflates independent account and credential ceremonies and recreates the exploit. 3. Merge restored passkey rows into the current fleet_auth table: rejected because a restorable table cannot be the monotonic authority that decides which side wins. 4. Keep the authoritative current verifier and lifecycle ledger in a non-restored PasskeyAuthorityFloor, quarantine every restored row, and require a distinct exact current credential ceremony when no exact current verifier survives: selected because current B/tombstones remain authoritative while restored A cannot return.

## Scope and Non-goals
Update the canonical parent and every affected child design/acceptance field so current passkey authority is monotonic outside restorable state and restored passkeys fail closed. No code. Preserve accepted provider/role/Discord/privacy decisions, gateway-only authority, safe first-owner bootstrap, current-plus-new provider authentication, the ban on enabled legacy recovery tokens, and all opl1.19/.19.2/.19.3 decisions. Do not create a reusable recovery token or weaken user-verifying WebAuthn requirements.
design: Use a trusted-host-owned non-restored monotonic `PasskeyAuthorityFloor`/credential-revocation registry integrated with `TrustedHostAuthorityFloor`. It is the sole authoritative source for current credential identity/fingerprint, public-key verifier and RP/principal/expected-provider binding, generation/status, counter/backup signals, and revocation/replacement tombstones; authenticator private material is never stored. Any `fleet_auth.passkey_credentials` row is a non-authoritative projection/import candidate. Enrollment, compromise, revocation, replacement, and recovery advance/bind the floor before an old credential can remain usable; failure over-fences. Restore/disable-to-re-enable advances the account restore checkpoint and auth epoch while preserving the current credential floor, quarantines every restored passkey, and merges restored credential history without replacing or rolling back later entries. Account/binding/role reapproval does not promote passkeys. Current replacement B remains usable only through an exact non-restored credential/floor match. If current verifier state is missing, unavailable, or inconsistent, passkey authentication and strong assurance deny until a separate expected-provider one-time trusted-host nonce plus matching OAuth and live WebAuthn origin/RP/user-verification registration creates a new generation. Replacement atomically tombstones the prior credential, revokes superseded sessions/grants/challenges, advances generation, and audits. Restored or tombstoned A can never become current.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Canonical fields explicitly bind passkey credentials and revocation/replacement history to a non-restored monotonic `PasskeyAuthorityFloor`; global auth epoch is not claimed sufficient. 2. Every restored passkey is quarantined and cannot authenticate, step up, mint JIT, or satisfy opl1.15 privacy assurance; account/binding/role reapproval never promotes it. 3. Backup with A→trusted-host revoke/replace A with B→restore old backup→reapprove account/binding/role→attempt A denies before and after reapproval. Restored rows/history cannot erase current B or current tombstones. B works only from an exact current non-restored floor entry; missing/unavailable/mismatched verifier state fails closed. 4. Distinct re-enrollment/recovery requires expected stable provider subject, trusted-host one-time nonce, matching OAuth, live origin/RP/user-verification validation, atomic consume/generation/audit, and revocation of superseded sessions/grants/challenges; the new generation never reactivates A. 5. opl1 parent/.1/.2/.10/.12 design and acceptance agree, threat certification includes the exact sequence and JIT/privacy assertions, graph cycles remain empty, .2 stays blocked by .1, targeted lint is zero, and fresh final P0/P1 review is CLEAN.

Preservation/scope: no opl1.19, opl1.19.2, or opl1.19.3 field was changed; no code or git file was changed; no bead was closed; no lower-priority observation was added.

Validation evidence: `bd dep cycles --json` = []; psfn-framework-opl1.2 is blocked by exactly psfn-framework-opl1.1; targeted `bd lint` over opl1/.1/.2/.10/.12/.20/.20.1 reports total 0; semantic scan confirms every affected record names PasskeyAuthorityFloor, restored-passkey quarantine, account-reapproval separation, old-A JIT/privacy denial, and the current-B/missing-verifier branch.

title: Make member-specific deny a PSFN hard veto for Discord administrators
description:
## Summary
Resolve the final ambiguity between Discord ADMINISTRATOR semantics and PSFN room-evidence policy. Discord normally lets ADMINISTRATOR bypass channel overwrites, but PSFN treats an explicit member-specific channel deny as a hard evidence veto even for an administrator. When that veto is absent, current ADMINISTRATOR may otherwise contribute to proven Discord visibility and private-thread moderator evidence. It never creates or widens PSFN role, trust, contact binding, memory access, or other authority.

## Rationale
The previous opl1.1 and opl1.4 wording simultaneously said member-specific deny always denies and ADMINISTRATOR may satisfy visibility according to Discord semantics. In the combined case, those statements choose opposite outcomes. Leaving that ambiguity could expose a companion room despite an explicit per-member veto. Separating the native Discord calculation from PSFN final evidence preserves useful administrator visibility/moderator signals while keeping the stricter PSFN denial boundary fail closed.

## Scope
Update tracker decision fields in opl1.1, opl1.4, the opl1.12 certification fixtures, and exact equivalent opl1 wording. Persist or expose the native Discord result, explicit member-specific-deny veto, and final PSFN evidence result separately. Require a combined ADMINISTRATOR plus member-specific deny => deny regression alongside ordinary administrator and ordinary member-deny fixtures. Preserve every opl1.19.1 and opl1.19.2 authority, bootstrap, recovery, privacy, restore, and no-fallback decision.

## Non-goals
No product code, live Discord change, OAuth-scope change, removal of ADMINISTRATOR from all visibility evidence, PSFN role redesign, reopening other fleet-auth decisions, or unrelated editorial cleanup. Do not close opl1.19.3, opl1.19.2, opl1.19.1, opl1.19, or opl1.1 until one fresh independent P0/P1 review accepts the frozen candidate.

## Alternatives Considered
1. Mirror Discord exactly and let ADMINISTRATOR bypass the member overwrite: rejected because PSFN deliberately treats the explicit member-specific deny as a stricter operator safety veto. 2. Ignore ADMINISTRATOR entirely: rejected because current administrator status remains valid Discord visibility and private-thread moderator evidence when no PSFN hard veto exists. 3. Clarify only the certification test: rejected because canonical decision and implementation beads would remain internally contradictory even if one fixture happened to choose deny.
design: Treat Discord's native effective-permission calculation as an input to PSFN evidence, not the final PSFN admission decision. Preserve the native Discord result, then apply an explicit PSFN member-specific-channel-deny hard veto before producing the final evidence result. If the veto is absent, current Discord ADMINISTRATOR may contribute to visibility and private-thread moderator evidence according to Discord semantics. It never creates or widens PSFN role, trust, contact binding, memory access, or other authority. Require the three-way executable fixture matrix: ordinary ADMINISTRATOR positive evidence, ordinary member-specific deny, and ADMINISTRATOR plus member-specific deny => deny.
acceptance_criteria: 1. opl1.1 and opl1.4 explicitly state member-specific deny is a PSFN hard veto even when the principal has Discord ADMINISTRATOR. 2. ADMINISTRATOR may otherwise affect proven Discord visibility/private-thread moderator evidence but never PSFN role/trust/memory. 3. Certification requires an ADMINISTRATOR plus member-specific deny yields deny fixture, alongside ordinary administrator and member-deny cases. 4. Search finds no contradictory fallback across opl1, bd lint is clean, dependency cycles are empty, and a fresh final P0/P1 review is CLEAN before opl1.1 closes.
notes:
Frozen tracker-only decision candidate prepared 2026-07-15 for one fresh independent P0/P1 review. No product code, lint, build, git commit, or PR is part of this remediation lane. Do not close opl1.19.3, opl1.19.2, opl1.19.1, opl1.19, or opl1.1 until that review is CLEAN.

Exact changed fields:
- psfn-framework-opl1.1: design and acceptance_criteria. The canonical DiscordEvidenceSnapshot now separates native Discord permission result, member-specific-deny veto, and final PSFN evidence result; the design, threat matrix, and executable acceptance matrix state ADMINISTRATOR plus member-specific deny => deny.
- psfn-framework-opl1.4: description, design, and acceptance_criteria. A member-specific channel deny is an explicit PSFN hard veto even for ADMINISTRATOR; absent that veto, current ADMINISTRATOR may contribute only to Discord visibility/private-thread moderator evidence. Persistence and tests distinguish the native result, veto bit, and final result.
- psfn-framework-opl1.12: design and acceptance_criteria. Deterministic certification requires ordinary ADMINISTRATOR positive evidence, ordinary member-specific denial, and combined ADMINISTRATOR plus member-specific deny => deny fixtures.
- psfn-framework-opl1.19.2: description and acceptance_criteria received only the equivalent hard-veto clarification; an appended note records that opl1.19.2's no-fallback decision is unchanged.

Preserved decisions: every opl1.19.1 gateway-only broker, recovery, first-owner bootstrap, provider replacement, privacy, durable-restore, assertion, credential-separation, and feature-off decision remains unchanged. opl1.19.2's complete-current-bot-evidence and no-PSFN-fallback decision remains unchanged. No configured role, PSFN role, or other authority can substitute for missing/unknown/expired Discord evidence or override any denial.

Canonical opl1 through opl1.18 had zero occurrences of the old active forms: 'Discord ADMINISTRATOR can satisfy', 'Discord ADMINISTRATOR may satisfy Discord visibility', 'Discord ADMINISTRATOR affects only', 'permissionInputs/result', 'absent private-thread membership', 'deny or require explicit PSFN authorization', and 'bot-observed overwrites or explicit configured role rules'. title: Remove the last Discord visibility fallback from fleet SSO
description:
## Summary
The fresh final review of opl1.19.1 found one remaining P1 contradiction in psfn-framework-opl1.4 description. That field said channel evidence could use bot-observed overwrites or explicit configured role rules, and that unproven private-thread visibility could deny or require explicit PSFN authorization. Those phrases create a fallback where configured PSFN authority can admit someone despite missing Discord overwrite evidence or private-thread membership.

## Rationale
The stale phrases conflict with opl1.4 own adversarial correction and acceptance plus canonical opl1.1. Configured mappings may only narrow a complete current bot-observed Discord effective-permission result. A member-specific deny, missing or unknown overwrite input, expired evidence, absent bot observation, and a private thread with neither explicit current membership nor current MANAGE_THREADS must deny deterministically. Under the subsequent psfn-framework-opl1.19.3 clarification, Discord ADMINISTRATOR may otherwise contribute to Discord visibility and private-thread moderator evidence, but a member-specific channel deny remains a PSFN hard veto even for ADMINISTRATOR; it never grants PSFN authority. Leaving contradictory prose gives an implementer two incompatible security contracts and risks a fail-open room-access path.

## Scope
Correct opl1.4 description, design, and acceptance so the evidence prerequisite, deny cases, private-thread rule, and Discord ADMINISTRATOR boundary are unambiguous. Search the complete opl1 graph across description, design, acceptance, and notes for equivalent stale fallback wording. ## Alternatives Considered

Permit an explicit PSFN role or configured Discord-role rule to substitute for incomplete bot evidence: rejected because it converts narrowing policy into a fail-open visibility authority. 3. title: Make gateway notification receipts transport-truthful
description: Summary: The 343f notification-ack change counts ready/healthy gateway connections, but GatewayRpcConnection.send returns whether the transport accepted the frame. GatewayServer.notifyAll currently ignores that result and increments anyway; notifyChannelMessage multi-companion routing also returns 1 unconditionally. A socket can close after health refresh but before send, so Discord receives forwarded_to_agent and suppresses its error even though no agent received the turn. Relevant files: src/boundary/gateway/server.ts notifyAll/notifyOne/notifyChannelMessage; src/boundary/gateway/transport.ts GatewayRpcConnection and NDJSON/WebSocket implementations; src/boundary/gateway/channel-surfaces.ts; server/channel tests. Important transport nuance: WebSocket send false means closed/not-open/rejected. Node net.Socket.write false means backpressure after the frame was accepted, not rejection, so do not treat NDJSON backpressure as message loss. Define an unambiguous accepted-versus-rejected send contract or normalize implementations so the receipt count means frame accepted for delivery. Scope: single and multi-companion notification paths only, deterministic close-race tests, preserve exact companion routing and current health checks. Why: otherwise a broken core Discord path loses partner turns while emitting a false success acknowledgement. Non-goals: end-to-end agent processing acknowledgement, retry/queue redesign, Satellite Hub diagnosis, provider fallback, or changes to blocked_by_policy/authored/noReply semantics.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A single-companion ready/healthy connection whose transport rejects the frame yields recipient count zero and the Discord boundary emits no forwarded_to_agent acknowledgement. 2. A multi-companion exact route whose selected connection rejects the frame likewise fails closed without rerouting or broadcasting. 3. An NDJSON socket write that returns false solely for backpressure still counts as accepted because Node already queued the frame; a destroyed socket does not. WebSocket closed/not-open/send-throw does not count. 4. Successful single- and multi-companion sends count exact accepted recipients and preserve existing routing, policy suppression, authored response, malformed empty, and no-reply behavior. 5. Focused transport/server/channel regression tests, mandatory npm run lint, npm run build, and git diff --check pass. 6. Fresh independent final P0/P1 check is CLEAN before merge.

GatewayServer now increments notification recipient counts only when the exact GatewayRpcConnection accepts the frame; multi-companion rejection returns zero without rerouting. GatewayRpcConnection.send documents accepted-versus-rejected semantics. NdjsonConnection treats net.Socket.write(false) as accepted backpressure while destroyed/write-throw returns false; WebSocket closed/not-open/send-throw remains rejected. Regressions cover NDJSON backpressure/destroyed, WebSocket throw/closed, single-companion close race, exact multi-companion rejection/no reroute, and exact success counts. title: Resolve final fleet SSO authority and bootstrap contradictions
description:
Correct the six residual P1 contradictions from the final psfn-framework-opl1.1 decision review. Update the canonical bead fields, not product code.

1. Gateway ownership: remove every opl1.3 allowance for an operator-side broker. OAuth exchange, session authority, fleet_auth DML and all secret/private signing/pepper resolution belong only to the unified HTTPS gateway's dedicated fleet-auth broker; the per-companion operator is a verifier/proxy.
2. Recovery credential: remove admin-token break-glass wording from opl1 parent and opl1.3. In enabled mode legacy ADMIN_TOKEN/psfn_token is never recovery. Use only the independently provisioned trusted-ingress recovery credential defined by .1/.7/.10.
3. First-owner bootstrap: specify a fail-closed trusted-host ceremony that pre-binds a one-time nonce to the expected stable provider subject, companion, intended contact binding and initial owner grant. Require matching OAuth plus UV WebAuthn, explicit local operator confirmation, atomic consume/audit, and no existing active owner. Subsequent owner grants use ordinary privileged policy; the ceremony cannot be replayed after an owner exists.
4. Provider replacement: remove where-possible ambiguity. Ordinary link/replacement must authenticate current and new identities; inability to authenticate current forces the trusted-host recovery ceremony, never approval-only relink.
5. Privacy grants: update opl1.11 summary/design/acceptance so routine JIT grants are only self/co-subject. Every non-subject owner/admin reveal is exclusively opl1.15 privacy break-glass with trusted ingress and UV WebAuthn.
6. Durable restore fencing: define a concrete authoritative rule. After restore or re-enable, all restored durable provider links, contact bindings and role grants are quarantined/suspended until trusted-host reapproval against current companion/contact state; tombstone/revocation authority must be monotonic outside the restored snapshot or re-established by that ceremony. Regression: backup, revoke/unlink, restore old backup, fresh OAuth login remains denied.

Update opl1.1 acceptance/threat matrix and children .2/.3/.5/.11/.12 as necessary. Search the whole opl1 epic for stale contradictory phrases. Keep .17/.18 blocking graph and all previously accepted decisions unchanged. Record exact changed bead fields and run bd dep cycles.

## Rationale
These are authentication, account-recovery, durable-authorization, and non-subject privacy boundaries. Leaving any downstream bead ambiguous can produce an operator-side secret holder, first-user self-elevation, approval-only account takeover, routine owner privacy access, or authority resurrection from an old backup. Correcting the tracker contract before code is cheaper and safer than reconciling divergent implementations.

## Alternatives Considered
1. Treat later adversarial-correction paragraphs as sufficient while retaining contradictory summaries: rejected because workers and tests may implement the earlier allowance. 2. Keep legacy ADMIN_TOKEN as emergency recovery in enabled mode: rejected because it bypasses principal assurance and creates a reusable owner credential. 3. Let operator approval substitute for current-provider authentication: rejected as account-takeover authority. 4. Rely only on an auth-epoch bump after restore: rejected because epochs fence ephemeral state but do not prevent restored provider links, tombstones, bindings, or roles from becoming durable authority. 5. Permit routine owner exceptions for private data: rejected; opl1.15 is the only non-subject disclosure path.
design: This is a fresh decision-remediation lane under the bounded orchestration process. Prefer one canonical statement per authority boundary and make downstream acceptance executable. Do not hide contradictions with vague reconcile or where possible language.
acceptance_criteria:
1. No opl1 bead permits operator-side OAuth/session/fleet_auth broker authority; gateway-only ownership is explicit.
2. No enabled-mode bead calls ADMIN_TOKEN or psfn_token break-glass; independent recovery credential and feature-off token parity are unambiguous.
3. A complete first-owner bootstrap ceremony binds provider subject, companion, contact and owner grant, requires OAuth+UV WebAuthn+trusted-host one-time confirmation, denies when an owner already exists, and is replay/audit tested.
4. Provider replacement authenticates current+new identities or must use trusted-host recovery; approval-only fallback is impossible.
5. Routine memory JIT is self/co-subject only; all owner/admin non-subject disclosure points solely to opl1.15 privacy break-glass.
6. Restored durable links/bindings/roles stay suspended until current trusted-host reapproval or a specified non-restored monotonic revocation source proves currency; old-backup fresh-login resurrection denies.
7. Parent/child descriptions, designs, acceptance and threat tests agree; bd dep cycles is empty.
8. A fresh independent P0/P1 review is CLEAN; no code, lint or PR is required.

title: Define and ship Satellite Hub authoritative device/location assertions for fleet SSO
description:
Background: opl1.9 can remove routine pasted credentials from Companion UI only if the authoritative Satellite Hub protocol separates an enrolled device/location principal from the logged-in human principal. Current Companion UI hello fields are browser-supplied requests; changing mirrored client types in psfn-framework cannot make them authoritative. The Satellite Hub server/protocol is a separate codebase and must issue a verifiable assertion before the framework can safely bind room/place identity.

Scope:
- In the Satellite Hub source of truth, define a versioned authenticated assertion containing Hub issuer, stable enrolled device ID, enrollment version/assurance, optional server-owned place binding, audience/companion, issued/expiry time, nonce/jti, and key ID; human principal/session attachment is a separate optional field proven by the fleet broker.
- Reject browser-authoritative device/place/contact/companion/channel fields. Bind WebSocket/session establishment to enrolled device credentials and the exact audience; support device revocation, key rotation, shared-display user switch, offline/reconnect, and replay protection.
- Publish/update the protocol contract consumed by psfn-framework opl1.9, with deterministic cross-repo fixtures and sanitized diagnostics.
- Record the authoritative Satellite Hub issue/commit/PR here when created; this bead is the framework-side dependency anchor.

Why: OAuth proves a human provider subject, not which physical room endpoint is speaking. Without a Hub-issued assertion, a browser can spoof location/device identity and inherit the wrong companion context.

Non-goals: implement Discord OAuth or PSFN role/memory authorization in the Hub; merge human and device identities; store OAuth tokens in the Hub; change live off-repo configuration.

Adversarial correction: choose an asymmetric Hub assertion protocol and a concrete verifier trust boundary. Satellite Hub signs with an Ed25519 private key it alone owns; fleet-auth strict config carries a versioned allowlisted Hub issuer/public-key ring and rotation/revocation state. Bind the assertion to the exact audience, companion and enrolled device/session; PSFN owns atomic replay consumption. Never share an HMAC or PSFN broker signing key with the Hub.
design:
Use a signed, short-lived, audience-bound server assertion over the existing enrolled device channel. Keep device registry and place binding authoritative in the Hub. PSFN validates issuer/kid/signature/audience/companion/expiry/jti and treats all raw browser hello fields as untrusted requests. Human logout revokes only the attachment/session; device de-enrollment revokes device assertions independently.

Use a Hub-specific Ed25519 issuer/key ring distinct from fleet broker request keys. Cross-repo fixtures define canonical bytes and claims. title: Build versioned memory-subject classification projection for fleet privacy
description:
Background: opl1.1 establishes that subject identity is intrinsic to a memory and is not equivalent to source speaker, routed contact, room participant, or viewer. opl1.11/.13/.14 cannot enforce subject-scoped Garden and profile privacy safely with the current optional contactId/subjectContactId fields alone. Missing/ambiguous classification must hide data, and filtering must occur in SQL/query primitives before counts, snippets, embeddings, exports, prompt previews, or bulk mutations are constructed. Existing subjectContactId/routedContactId graph work (ybzz/ipw1) is useful evidence but does not provide this privacy projection.

Scope:
- Define the shared versioned MemorySubjectClassification contract from opl1.1: single_contact, multiple_contacts, shared_room, companion_private, unbound_person, unattributed, ambiguous; define evidence provenance/precedence and viewer relation separately.
- Add companion-schema Postgres projection tables: one classification row per memory plus zero-or-more subject-contact rows, tenant-safe keys, classifier version, evidence digest, timestamps, and fail-closed status.
- Classify new memory writes transactionally with the source write. Build an idempotent, resumable, bounded backfill for existing memories that records ambiguity rather than guessing; coordinate with ipw1/27ut instead of duplicating provenance derivation. Missing/stale/version-mismatched rows remain hidden during enforcement.
- Add one authorization-aware memory query primitive used beneath list/detail/search/count/embedding/snippet/export/prompt-preview/bulk/update paths so unauthorized rows cannot leak through metadata or counts. `ContactProfileArtifact.contactId` maps to single_contact but remains separately gated by opl1.14.
- Expose only content-free backfill/classification counts, versions, reason classes, and timings.

Why: a view-layer redaction after a broad query leaks existence/count/snippet/embedding information and cannot safely authorize bulk operations. A canonical projection is the prerequisite for all subject-scoped fleet privacy children.

Non-goals: OAuth/session/JIT grant issuance (opl1.3/.7/.10/.11), holistic reflection/multi-admin policy (opl1.16), changing graph proposal semantics, or treating every contact-associated memory as proven self-subject.

Adversarial correction: transactionality applies to the full subject-evidence lifecycle, not only new writes. Every update to text, provenance, contactId, provenanceRefs, embedding or other subject evidence; repair/backfill/restore; and contact merge/delete must recompute or invalidate the projection in the same transaction. The projection records a memory revision and evidence digest. A failure or stale grant leaves the row hidden, never at the prior classification.
design:
Extend the canonical memory Postgres schema and existing provenance/subject primitives. Classification is strict and versioned; viewer authorization consumes it but does not mutate it. Use a single deep query-policy port that composes tenant, trust/privacy, subject, action, assurance, and grant predicates in SQL. Backfill under advisory locking with checkpoints and deterministic evidence hashes. Unknown/missing/contradictory evidence maps to ambiguous/unattributed and denies.

Add a monotonic memory authorization revision (or equivalent immutable content/evidence version) to the projection. The update store and all maintenance/restore/contact lifecycle ports must call one transactional classifier/invalidation primitive. Authorization/JIT checks compare current revision, classifier version and evidence digest; no post-commit async window may expose stale classification.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Strict shared types cover all seven subject classes, evidence provenance, classifier version, memory revision/evidence digest and separate viewer relation; unknown values reject.
2. Companion-schema projection tables, constraints, indexes and backfill checkpoints are tenant-safe; disposable Postgres proves cross-schema isolation.
3. New memory creation classifies atomically and retry is idempotent.
4. Every subject-affecting update (including text, provenance, contactId, provenanceRefs and embedding), repair, backfill, restore, contact merge/delete recomputes or invalidates in the same transaction. Failure/stale/missing versions hide.
5. Historical backfill is bounded/resumable, reuses canonical provenance resolution and records ambiguity rather than guessing.
6. One authorization-aware SQL primitive filters list/detail/search/count/snippet/embedding/export/prompt/bulk/update before construction; inaccessible IDs/counts are non-enumerable and bulk is atomic.
7. Grants/queries bind current memory revision, classifier version and evidence digest or re-evaluate on use; mutation invalidates old grants immediately.
8. Tests cover all classes, mutation races, restore, contact lifecycle, subject/routed conflicts and failure injection.
9. Telemetry contains only counts/versions/reasons/timings; migration/backup compatibility, build, mandatory lint and diff check pass.
close_reason: Completed and integrated: 8102d555 added the strict seven-class versioned memory-subject contract, tenant-safe projection/schema, transactional classification, bounded resumable backfill, contact-lifecycle invalidation and restore support; 944ff97c added the deep authorization-aware store/query boundary and bound runtime call sites, integrated at 73ad5943. Current source verified in src/shared/contracts/memory-subject.ts, src/faculties/memory/postgres-store/subject-queries.ts, src/faculties/memory/postgres-store/subject-backfill.ts, src/faculties/memory/postgres-store.ts, and src/core/contacts/postgres-adapter/memory-subject-lifecycle.ts: missing/stale/invalidated classifications fail closed, authorization filters before count/content construction, writes bind revision/version/evidence digest, and contact changes invalidate transactionally. Validation: current contract/classifier/policy/authorized-store/Postgres/restore suite 47/47 passed; full build/DTS and mandatory repository lint passed at feature head 0e144688.

title: Validate old landmark retrieval under the operator-owned memory matrix
description:
Background: PR #65 (merge 35dab6cca38e4e89a9052f7ef9e0f9fcbb523dfd; implementation d1051422bc plus bounded remediation b010655553) shipped the settings-owned seven-type memory decay/retrieval matrix from psfn-framework-m14v. Local tests prove the exact defaults, a two-year-old high-valence emotional memory outranking a fresh low-relevance candidate, bounded lexical pagination, live settings propagation, retained-context caps, and shard task priors. What remains is the operator-visible deployed proof required by m14v acceptance criterion 7.

Scope:
- Deploy an immutable build containing merge 35dab6cca38e4e89a9052f7ef9e0f9fcbb523dfd through the repo-owned deployment path to one explicitly approved companion.
- Record the canonical settings.json memoryRetrievalPolicy in effect, redacting unrelated/private values. Use the shipped defaults unless the operator explicitly approves a tuning change.
- Identify or create a consent-safe old emotional landmark at least 180 days old in a controlled fixture/companion dataset, with strong contextual relevance and a fresh low-relevance competing memory. Do not copy partner message content into logs or bead notes.
- Run repeatable contextually on-point turns through the normal live active-context path, not a direct store/search helper, and inspect content-free retrieval telemetry plus the rendered-memory provenance necessary to prove which memory won.
- Run a casual control turn and a task-context control turn to confirm procedural down-weighting/boosting and reflection/procedural caps remain bounded in the deployed path.
- Record immutable deployment provenance, timestamps, sanitized setup, turn count, selected memory IDs/types/ages/scores, policy fingerprint, and operator conclusion.

Why: local conformance tests cannot prove that the deployed owner file, reload path, Postgres corpus, prompt assembly, and real provider turn all compose correctly. This validation is deliberately separate so the shipped code bead can close without claiming live evidence.

Non-goals: no fleet-wide rollout or tuning; no weakening privacy/trust filters or dedup thresholds; no synthetic backdating of production partner memories; no off-repo runtime overrides; no new compatibility path; no broad retrieval redesign.
acceptance_criteria: 1. The tested deployment identifies an immutable build containing merge 35dab6cca38e4e89a9052f7ef9e0f9fcbb523dfd and records the active memoryRetrievalPolicy fingerprint/defaults without secrets or partner content. 2. Through the normal live turn path, an old (at least 180-day) high-valence, strongly relevant emotional landmark is selected and rendered ahead of a fresh low-relevance competitor in at least two repeatable contextually on-point trials; evidence records only sanitized IDs/types/ages/scores and content-free telemetry. 3. A casual control does not inappropriately load task-shaped procedural memory, while a deterministic task-context control demonstrates the procedural task prior; no turn renders more than two reflections or two procedurals after retained-context merge. 4. Privacy/trust gating and dedup remain unchanged: an intentionally ineligible fixture is not selected and no private content appears in telemetry or notes. 5. The operator records a pass/fail conclusion before any fleet-wide tuning. If behavior fails, capture the evidence and create one self-contained discovered-from remediation bead rather than tuning blindly.
notes:
2026-07-21 triage: Keep open as an operator-owned live validation. No completion commit or sanitized live evidence is recorded for the required old-landmark trials, casual/task controls, privacy gating, and pass/fail conclusion; source implementation alone cannot satisfy this bead.
2026-07-22 read-only live check on psfn-shard (merged main 9dfb11b46 / image 0.1.0-kube-9dfb11b4 / helm rev 65, deployed 05:16 UTC). Bead stays OPEN.

AC1 PARTIALLY VERIFIED: merge 35dab6cca38e4e89a9052f7ef9e0f9fcbb523dfd is an ancestor of the deployed commit 9dfb11b46 (git merge-base --is-ancestor -> true). Active policy is the shipped default set: no memoryRetrievalPolicy override exists anywhere under the system-data or companion roots on the live pod (grep -rl returns nothing), so the runtime resolves createDefaultMemoryRetrievalPolicy() at src/system/config/load-config.ts:489.

CLEARS THE 2026-07-21 k3d BLOCKER: unlike the k3d fleet, this host does have an aged corpus. public.l2_memories holds 2670 live (non-deleted) rows, oldest extracted_at 2024-12-25, newest 2026-07-22, of which 444 are >= 180 days old (semantic 227 / emotional 160 / relational 48 / procedural 9).

NEW STRUCTURAL BLOCKER FOUND (read-only SQL, 2026-07-22): the aged cohort carries no valence signal at all. Grouping live rows on age >= 180d: aged n=444 with nonzero emotional_valence = 0 and max(abs(valence)) = 0.000; non-aged n=2226 with nonzero valence = 1719 and max(abs(valence)) = 1.000. The oldest row with nonzero valence is 158.1 days old, i.e. the valence signal only begins well inside the 180-day boundary. Because resolveMemorySalienceFloor() scales the salience floor by absolute valence (src/system/config/memory-retrieval-policy.ts:536-549), the precise mechanism AC2 asks to prove -- an old HIGH-VALENCE emotional landmark outranking a fresh low-relevance competitor -- cannot be exercised against the organic production corpus, because no row is simultaneously >= 180 days old and non-zero valence.

AC2-AC5 NOT VERIFIED. Separately, observability.retrievals was empty on all three post-reboot turns; the channel itself does work (191 turn-record lines across history carry non-empty retrievals), so scored evidence requires deliberately on-point probe turns rather than passive observation. Passive observation also cannot satisfy AC2's "fresh low-relevance competitor" comparison or AC3's casual/task-context controls.

NEXT STEP to close: per this bead's own scope, stand up the old landmark in a controlled fixture/companion dataset with valence populated (the non-goals forbid backdating the live partner's production memories), paired with a fresh low-relevance competitor and an intentionally ineligible fixture for AC4. Then run >= 2 contextually on-point trials plus a casual control and a deterministic task-context control through the normal live turn path, and capture observability.retrievals sanitized IDs/types/ages/scores.

title: Validate bounded parent-turn continuation on psfn-shard
description:

This is the deployment/provenance and controlled-outage proof split from the implementation bead so the shipped code can land without silently claiming live evidence that has not been collected.

The 2026-07-14/15 outage held the single active agent slot while a session.search.summary continuation ran for 394875ms and the parent accumulated repeated toolUse completions without a terminal assistant message. PR #61 adds a five-minute wall-clock fuse, a 36-prompt-entry cap, typed failure persistence, and AbortSignal propagation through the live session-summary path. title: Acknowledge API cancellation only after proven active-run abort
description: Verified P1 from the bounded final check of mmo9.2 range 57c28d86f6..718ff78439. In src/channels/api/agent-backend.ts abortActiveTurn casts the companion pipeline to a void abort method, invokes it, and unconditionally returns true. SubstrateAgent.abort in src/core/agent/substrate-agent.ts delegates to the pi agent, whose abort can be a no-op before activeRun exists during pre-prompt work. cancelActiveRequest then returns cancelled true and emits cancellationOutcome acknowledged even though retrieval, compaction, provider, or tool work may continue. This recreates the exact false-acknowledgment telemetry defect the remediation intended to remove and can leave expensive work alive after client disconnect or timeout. Scope: establish a typed cancellation result from the canonical agent loop that proves whether an active parent run was signaled or already terminal; thread it through SubstrateAgent and AgentApiBackend; emit acknowledged only for a proven abort, and a truthful non-success outcome for no active run or failure; preserve FIFO lease release, timeout handling, direct-completion AbortController behavior, and voice cancellation semantics. Add deterministic tests for cancellation during pre-prompt, active pi run, already-finished/no-active request, thrown abort, and timeout. Non-goals: relaxing single-active-prompt, a new cancellation framework, cancelling unrelated channels, voice redesign, or provider-specific workarounds.
acceptance_criteria: API cancellation returns cancelled true and emits acknowledged only when the active underlying parent/provider run was actually signaled; a pre-prompt or absent-run no-op returns cancelled false with a non-success outcome and never an acknowledgment; thrown abort is logged and reported failed; active provider and tool work observe the abort signal and settle; channel lease and activeRequests cleanup remain deterministic; focused API, substrate-agent, and pi-agent cancellation tests, npm run build, mandatory npm run lint, and git diff --check pass.

Direct model completions retain per-request controllers and internal vision/continuation timeouts retain intentional unscoped aborts. title: Record toolcall_start as provider first output
description: Verified P1 from the bounded final check of mmo9.2 range 57c28d86f6..718ff78439. In src/primitives/llm/client.ts around the streaming event switch, provider-first output is marked for nonempty text_delta, thinking_delta, nonempty toolcall_delta, or toolcall_end, but pi-ai toolcall_start is ignored even though it already carries the provider-emitted tool identity and name. A tool-first stream can therefore report provider_first_token late when argument fragments arrive, or miss it until toolcall_end when arguments are empty, violating the foreground timeline acceptance that text, thinking, and tool output all define substantive first output. Scope: mark the first valid toolcall_start as output kind tool at the provider boundary, exactly once per physical attempt; preserve text/thinking behavior, fallback accounting, and the rule that a terminal-only done event never fabricates first output. Add deterministic stream tests for toolcall_start followed by delayed args, empty args/end, duplicate start/delta/end, and terminal-only output. title: Prevent stale contact upserts from clobbering concurrent high-tier trust
description: Verified P1 from the one final check of z7qe/suaf at commit 8888f24730. src/core/contacts/postgres-adapter/crud-operations.ts reads the target row and computes nextTrustLevel, then later writes trust_level unconditionally. If an operator-authorized setTrustLevel promotion to trusted or primary commits after the upsert read but before its UPDATE, the stale resolver/profile upsert overwrites the new high-tier value (the deterministic fake-pool schedule produced before=regular, after=public, stored=public). This remains possible even though commit 8888f24730 preserves contacts that were already high-tier at the initial read. It can silently undo an operator trust decision and make ICP policy reject an otherwise canonical peer. Scope: make generic contact upsert concurrency-safe for trust without serializing unrelated profile fields unnecessarily; use a row lock, conditional trust write, CAS/retry, or equivalent Postgres-safe mechanism so a stale generic write never changes trust after a concurrent high-tier mutation. Extend FakePostgresPool only as needed to model the exact post-read/pre-update schedule, and add a real Postgres integration regression if the existing harness supports it. Preserve explicit operator setTrustLevel promotion and demotion, configured-primary rules, unknown-speaker public creation, and low-tier upsert behavior when no concurrent trust mutation occurs. Non-goals: no trust-tier redesign, no global transaction refactor, no weakening actor authorization, and no unrelated fake-pool rollback work.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic regression interleaves generic resolveChannelIdentity or resolveUserId/upsert with operator setTrustLevel after the target read and proves trusted and primary cannot be overwritten; the production SQL path provides the same atomic guarantee under real Postgres concurrency; explicit operator high-tier promotion/demotion still works; unseen external identities remain public; focused contact/privacy/ICP policy tests pass; npm run lint passes.
close_reason: Completed and merged in PR #58 (merge be93ac6d83, implementation 05f26a853e plus remediation a00c4dd8e9). Generic and explicit trust mutations now CAS on trust_level plus durable trust_version; trust and audit commit on one transaction; existing contacts cannot gain primary through unbound or conflicting proposed identities; merge and configured-owner writers advance the version. Validation: 277 contact tests, 108 focused adapter/store/migration tests, 8 real PostgreSQL concurrency tests, 12/12 real ABA/audit stress executions, 17 privacy regressions, 7 real PostgreSQL ICP tests, build, mandatory lint, and diff-check passed. The retired store correctly required manual authority for every mutation touching a high tier, minted unknown speakers at public, and kept primary trust sticky. Preserve low-tier public and regular drift, approved propose_trust behavior, configured primary identity promotion, and explicit operator-admin mutation paths. Non-goals: no trust-model redesign, no Garden workflow change, no generic contact hydration refactor, and no unrelated audit-parity work.

title: Validate provider prompt-cache engagement and cache-read pricing on one companion before fleet rollout
description:
Background: psfn-framework-2z12.1 implementation is shipped on canonical origin/main in squash commit 84c0089e (implementation 1fa353ea). config/models.seed.json now ships promptCaching.enabled=true; src/core/agent/substrate-agent/turn-execution/prompt-assembly.ts applies the owner-file policy, records promptCaching observability, and emits prompt.cache.prefix_instability when the static prefix changes. The shipped seed does not rewrite already-deployed system-owned models.json files, so operational validation must be performed separately from implementation closure.

Scope: on one explicitly approved, non-PSFN-Pi companion deployment, verify the deployed canonical models.json owner file has modelRegistry.promptCaching.enabled=true (retention/scope left at shipped defaults unless the operator specifies otherwise); run a representative multi-turn soak with stable system-prompt inputs; inspect prompt-cache observability/telemetry for engagement, byte-stable static prefixes, and absence of unexpected prompt.cache.prefix_instability events; then inspect authoritative provider usage/billing data for cache-read token accounting and cache-read pricing. Record deployment identity without secrets, observation window, representative turn count, provider/model route, telemetry evidence, usage evidence, and response-behavior comparison.

Why: code and tests prove the mechanism and fail-closed behavior, but only an operational soak can prove the existing owner file was enabled and the selected provider route actually bills cache reads. This evidence must not hold the shipped implementation bead open.

Non-goals: code changes, prompt restructuring, changing response behavior, broad fleet rollout, SSH, PSFN-Pi access, SQLite work, weakening fail-closed provider capability checks, or treating models.seed.json as authority for an already-deployed models.json.
acceptance_criteria: On one operator-approved non-PSFN-Pi companion: (1) the deployed canonical models.json owner file is evidenced with modelRegistry.promptCaching.enabled=true and secrets redacted; (2) a representative multi-turn soak records promptCaching.engaged=true for the intended provider/model route; (3) prefix-stability evidence shows the static region is byte-stable turn-to-turn, with every instability event explained or zero unexpected prompt.cache.prefix_instability events; (4) authoritative provider usage/billing evidence shows non-zero cache-read tokens charged at the provider cache-read rate; (5) sampled responses show no behavior regression; (6) evidence includes deployment identity, observation window, turn count, provider/model, telemetry extracts, pricing/usage extracts, and operator conclusion before any fleet-wide rollout.
notes:
2026-07-22 live check on psfn-shard (merged main 9dfb11b46, image 0.1.0-kube-9dfb11b4, helm rev 65). NOT validated — leaving open, but with new evidence:

1. promptCaching is ABSENT from her live /app/system-data/models.json (grep for 'promptCaching' returns nothing). This is exactly the condition this bead predicted: the shipped config/models.seed.json promptCaching.enabled=true does NOT rewrite an already-deployed system-owned models.json. The PSFN-side policy is therefore OFF on this companion and prompt-assembly's owner-file policy path is not being exercised.

2. Despite that, model_usage_events already records substantial cache activity: 5929 events, cache_read_tokens sum = 3,827,815, cache_write_tokens sum = 0. Reads without any writes indicates PROVIDER-SIDE IMPLICIT caching (e.g. automatic prefix caching), not PSFN-directed caching. So any cache-read pricing measured today reflects implicit provider behaviour and must not be mistaken for validation of the 2z12.1 feature.

To actually close this: enable promptCaching in her models.json owner file (Garden POST /api/admin/settings/models or the owner-file path), restart to pick it up, then confirm (a) prompt.cache.prefix_instability telemetry is quiet, (b) cache_write_tokens becomes non-zero, and (c) cache-read cost columns (provider_cache_read_cost_usd vs estimated_/effective_) reconcile. Until then the feature is unexercised on the only live companion.
