title: Implement the minimal shared-world wiki caretaker proposal and operator-review flow
description: W5 foundations are shipped on feat/multi-companion: ac389e5b/3df117e0 provide durable shared-schema companion presence, co-presence context/events, and heartbeat refresh; 53033de6 plus 451835ea/f912d85d provide personal vs shared_world site-scoped retrieval and shared projection; 5b542520 plus 3d07ebf5 provide virtual world.move through CompanionPresenceTurnPort. The remaining privacy-critical W5 scope is the minimal caretaker flow. Current src/faculties/wiki/store.ts correctly rejects direct companion shared_world writes and operator maintenance imports use filterPersonalFactProposals, but no durable companion proposal queue, dedup/review state, Garden approve/reject flow, or independent bounded cleanup process owns shared-world writes. Scope: (1) companions may submit shared-world proposals only, carrying actor, source, site scope, provenance, and content digest; (2) run deterministic personal-fact rejection before durable queueing and again before apply; (3) deduplicate equivalent/pending/applied proposals; (4) expose an operator Garden list/inspect/approve/reject surface; (5) only approved proposals may write through the caretaker-authorized shared-world store/projector; (6) run bounded deterministic cleanup/reprojection independently of companion turns, with an LLM call only behind an explicit cheap changed-content gate if genuinely required. Non-goals: no cross-cluster sync, no direct companion shared_world write, no personal-memory import, and no full caretaker rebalancing/rewrite architecture (future design psfn-framework-s10d5 remains separate).
design: Add a focused shared-world proposal store/state machine rather than widening WikiStore authority: pending -> approved|rejected, with a unique digest/site key and audited idempotent apply marker. Keep deterministic personal-fact filtering in one reusable guard invoked both before persistence and inside the approval transaction. Garden endpoints call an operator-authorized service; only that service can invoke the existing caretaker-authorized shared-world writer. Use bounded batches, advisory/row locking, and revision-aware reprojection so retries and concurrent approvals remain exactly once.
acceptance_criteria: A companion-authored valid world fact becomes a durable pending proposal and does not appear in shared retrieval before approval. An operator approval applies exactly one shared_world document/projection with actor/provenance/revision audit data; failure injected between approval and projection resumes without duplicate writes. Rejection remains durable and prevents identical re-proposal. Equivalent concurrent proposals deduplicate deterministically. A proposal containing personal facts, personal-memory provenance, invalid site scope, or companion-private content is rejected before any shared write and remains absent from projection/retrieval. A two-companion toaster end-to-end script proves a fact proposed by A is invisible to B before approval and readable by B at the matching site after approval, while personal wiki data never crosses; logs include redacted proposal ID, state transitions, site, digest, revision, batch counts, and rejection class, never proposal content. Background cleanup/reprojection is bounded and runs only on changed approved content. Focused state-machine/filter/dedup unit tests, Garden authorization tests, disposable real-Postgres shared-projection integration, multi-companion retrieval tests, npm run lint, npm run build, and git diff --check pass.
notes:
Plan-space polish pass 1: tightened the authority/state-machine boundary, concurrent/exactly-once and failure-resume cases, privacy-safe diagnostics, and comprehensive unit/Garden/Postgres/two-agent E2E coverage; no scope removed.
Plan-space polish pass 2: rechecked parent/child boundaries, duplicate search, priority, non-goals, and validation separation; graph is coherent and no further change was required.
Plan-space polish pass 3: final one-bead-at-a-time stability read found the scope self-contained, acceptance testable, logging privacy-safe, and no feature loss or graph repair needed.

title: Finish W2 tenant boundary: flagship and shard schema adoption with fail-closed Postgres isolation
description: Current feat/multi-companion evidence: merges ee375e39/459594ab implement schema-pinned pools, per-schema migrations, and the shared schema; 75abf583 implements per-companion and group backup artifacts. The remaining W2 implementation is not shipped. There is no public-to-companion flagship cutover helper, shard execution derives a companion ID but does not derive/thread a distinct Postgres schema, and src/persistence/postgres.ts still pins tenant search_path to <tenant>,public. That public fallback can silently read/write a legacy public tenant table when a companion migration is incomplete, while a shared database role can access peer schemas. This bead completes the tenancy boundary before any live cutover. Scope: (1) add a dry-run-first, resumable/idempotent flagship adoption helper that inventories public objects, copies/verifies them into the configured companion schema, records checksums/counts and rollback metadata, and never runs implicitly at startup; (2) derive a validated collision-free shard schema from the parent companion identity plus shard identity and thread it through shard pools, migrations, backups, and cleanup; (3) move shared extensions into an explicit extension schema or otherwise make them resolvable without retaining public in tenant search_path; (4) provision least-privilege per-companion/shard database roles and grants so cross-schema reads/writes fail closed; (5) preserve the flag-off single-companion path deliberately. Non-goals: do not perform a live flagship cutover, touch SQLite, change column tenancy, or merge/deploy this branch. The real flagship restore/workspace rehearsal remains psfn-framework-g44z and must pass before an operator authorizes live apply.
design: Keep planning and mutation separate: a pure inventory/planner produces an auditable manifest, and an explicit executor consumes that manifest under transactions and advisory locking. Reuse the canonical Postgres schema validator/quoting path rather than interpolating identifiers. Derive shard schema names through one shared tenancy helper used by pools, migrations, backup, and restore. Provision tenant roles/grants as an explicit deployment/migration artifact, with extension lookup isolated from tenant object lookup. Tests should use disposable real Postgres instances and emit schema, role, object-count, checksum, resume, and rollback diagnostics without row contents or secrets.
acceptance_criteria: A dry-run fixture over a populated legacy public schema produces a deterministic adoption plan; apply into a disposable database copies every required table/sequence/view with matching row counts/checksums, is safe to resume after injected interruption, and preserves rollback evidence. Two companion schemas plus one derived shard schema run migrations and concurrent writes without collisions. Tenant and shard search_path values do not include public; deliberately omitting a tenant table fails instead of falling through to a public table. Per-companion/shard roles cannot select or mutate peer schemas, while explicitly shared-world access remains limited to approved grants. Per-schema backup and restore tests cover the adopted flagship and shard slices. title: Verify shipped required-tool empty-argument recovery in a safe non-Pi runtime
description: The fail-closed implementation for literal '{}' tool arguments is already shipped on this branch via merge 7243616b (implementation a186538c): src/primitives/llm/empty-tool-argument-retry.ts detects required-schema calls with empty args, retries the same completion at most twice, and returns the final corrupt response for downstream schema rejection; src/primitives/llm/client-response-helpers.ts classifies a literal two-byte '{}' as provider_emitted_empty. Original bead psfn-framework-mihm must close because implementation is complete. This child owns only the important residual runtime verification that a production-wired request cannot dispatch a corrupt required-action tool call. Run against Artemis/local runtime or another safe controlled non-Pi environment using a deterministic provider fixture/replay that emits literal '{}' for a required-action tool before a valid retry. Confirm telemetry/usage records the retry and no corrupt call reaches dispatch. Scope includes correcting only wiring defects that prevent the already-shipped behavior from operating. Non-goals: no PSFN-Pi or other live host, no SSH, no OpenRouter/provider routing changes, no broad malformed-tool-call reprompt work (tracked separately by psfn-framework-b0yl.3), no optional-action redesign, and no repeated review loop.
acceptance_criteria: In a safe non-Pi runtime, a deterministic required-action tool completion that first emits literal '{}' is retried and then succeeds without dispatching the corrupt call; an exhaustion case rejects before tool dispatch; runtime telemetry or persisted model-usage evidence records provider_emitted_empty and the retry count; targeted tests, npm run lint, and the relevant local runtime smoke pass; the evidence is recorded in the close reason.
notes:
2026-07-22 adjudication (repo audit at merged main 9dfb11b46). Bead stays OPEN.

Scope note first: this bead requires "a safe non-Pi runtime". psfn-shard IS the Pi, so no live evidence from that host is admissible here regardless of what it shows. This adjudication therefore looked only at the repo's fixture/replay lane, which is what the bead sanctions.

IMPLEMENTATION IS SHIPPED AND WIRED: merge 7243616b (impl a186538c) is an ancestor of 9dfb11b46. retryCompletionOnCorruptEmptyToolArgs is wired into the real request path at src/primitives/llm/client.ts:1225 (stream) and :1863 (complete), with MAX_EMPTY_TOOL_ARGS_COMPLETION_RETRIES = 2 (empty-tool-argument-retry.ts:20) and the retry count persisted into model-usage metadata as emptyArgsRetries (client.ts:1428,1466,1503,1553,1748,1795,1825,1849).

BUT THE ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA ARE NOT MET. Verified gaps:

1. "exhaustion case rejects before tool dispatch" -- NOT covered. The only exhaustion test, client.test.ts:1552 'fails closed after exhausting retries: returns the corrupt-empty response as-is', asserts the OPPOSITE at :1567-1569: expect(response.toolCalls).toEqual([{ id: 'call-journal', name: 'journal', input: {} }]). The client deliberately returns the corrupt call so downstream AJV rejects it. The actual rejection lives at src/core/agent/tool-call-scheduler.ts:399-403, and no test in the repo joins the two halves.

2. "without dispatching the corrupt call" -- NOT asserted anywhere. There is no dispatcher or tool.execute spy in client.test.ts; non-dispatch is inferred from the return value, not proven.

3. "telemetry or persisted model-usage evidence records provider_emitted_empty AND the retry count" -- only half. The retry count is asserted in persisted usage metadata. provider_emitted_empty is NEVER persisted: it exists only as a field value inside a log.warn in logEmptyToolArgumentProvenance (empty-tool-argument-retry.ts:48) that no test observes, and it is absent from recordUsage metadata entirely. It is asserted only as a pure-function return in tool-argument-provenance.test.ts:29-30.

4. The literal two-byte '{}' wire case is exercised only by the pure classifier. The client-level fixture (client.test.ts:1472-1483 doneWithToolCall) emits arguments: {} on the done event and never streams a literal '{}' fragment, so argumentFragmentBytes stays 0 on the wired path.

5. The complete() wiring at client.ts:1863 has zero coverage -- no completeSimple mock in client.test.ts returns a tool call at all.

6. No recorded smoke/validation artifact exists anywhere (docs/, scripts/, *.md searched for provider_emitted_empty / emptyArgsRetries / empty-tool-args). No commit message claims runtime verification. No relevant npm smoke target exists.

Incidental finding worth keeping: both call sites pass onRetriesResolved: () => {} (client.ts:1232 and :1872), discarding the helper's resolved retry count. The persisted number comes from the per-attempt attemptIndex instead, so today's value happens to be correct, but the helper's own summary is consumed by nothing.

NEXT STEP to close: in the local/dev fixture lane, add a test that drives a fake-provider request through the dispatcher and asserts tool.execute is never called for the corrupt call in BOTH the recovery and exhaustion cases; stream a real literal two-byte '{}' fragment end-to-end; surface provider_emitted_empty into telemetry or model-usage so it is assertable from the wired path; cover the complete() wiring; then record the run output (targeted tests + npm run lint) as the close evidence.

title: Validate fleet workspace isolation and flagship restore before live cutover
description:
Summary:
After the c337 implementation and its repository-hygiene prerequisite are integrated into the immutable deployment revision, validate the Personal/Shared Workspace boundary and a real flagship backup/restore rehearsal in the live multi-companion topology. This is a validation/cutover gate, not unfinished c337 implementation, and must not block or reopen psfn-framework-c337 once its bounded local implementation gates pass.

Why:
Local unit/integration tests prove the code contract but cannot prove that the existing shared workspace PVC was migrated without loss, that every deployed agent/Garden receives the intended resolved root, or that a real flagship snapshot restores into disposable destinations. Audit psfn-framework-3ajb reproduced the current leak: all five agents use WORKSPACE_PATH=/app/workspace, and Denise, Garden Nun, and Lucy selfie_create outputs from Discord channel 1486443955561299979 are visible in Carlini Garden.

Scope:
- Require a pushed deployment revision containing c337 and repository-hygiene remediation commit a81cdd49 (or an equivalent reviewed descendant) before validation.
- Back up the existing shared workspace/PVC before migration. Assign artifacts only where ownership/provenance is proven; quarantine ambiguous ownership for operator review.
- Deploy through repo-owned Kubernetes/Helm wiring and record the immutable source/image revision.
- Verify each companion agent and Garden resolves its own Personal Workspace and cannot read/write peer journal, wiki, managed-skill, module, inbound-attachment, generated-image, download, or artifact sentinels through normal surfaces.
- Reuse Discord channel 1486443955561299979 and the Denise/Garden Nun/Lucy reproduction corpus to prove those images are absent from Carlini Garden while retained in the correct personal workspace or explicit operator quarantine.
- Verify the governed Shared Companion Workspace remains separately contained and companion access is approved-revision read-only.
- Restore a real flagship snapshot into disposable PostgreSQL schemas/database and fresh filesystem destinations, verify companion/system/shared scope and manifests, then remove only the disposable rehearsal resources.
- Record failures as new implementation/fix beads; do not silently patch during validation.

Non-goals:
- Do not move/delete live data without a verified backup and explicit cutover authority.
- Do not expose private media, secrets, or raw personal content in logs or bead notes.
- Do not treat a gallery-only filter as workspace isolation.
- Do not make SQLite/provider changes or invent off-repo runtime configuration.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The deployed immutable source/image revision is recorded and contains c337 plus a81cdd49 or an explicitly evidenced equivalent hygiene remediation.
2. Pre-migration backup and restoreability are verified; ambiguous legacy files remain losslessly quarantined for operator review.
3. Every deployed agent and Garden reports a distinct canonical Personal Workspace, and synthetic cross-companion read/write checks for personal files, inbound attachments, and generated images fail closed.
4. Denise, Garden Nun, and Lucy images from channel 1486443955561299979 are not visible in Carlini Garden and remain available only in their proven owner workspace or quarantine; no private paths/content are written to tracker notes.
5. The Shared Companion Workspace exposes only approved, revision-matched read-only artifacts to companions and never auto-loads skills/modules/prompt/wiki/memory.
6. A real flagship snapshot restores successfully into disposable Postgres and filesystem destinations with companion/cluster scope verified and the original live state untouched.
7. Close evidence records revision ancestry, backup identifier, migration/quarantine counts, cross-visibility results, restore verification, rollback/cutover outcome, and any follow-up bead IDs.
notes:
2026-07-21 triage: Keep open as an operator-owned live cutover validation. No recorded live evidence satisfies the required workspace isolation probes, quarantine ownership check, disposable flagship restore, and rollback/cutover conclusion; implementation presence alone is insufficient.
LIVE RE-CHECK 2026-07-22 (read-only). Still NOT met — no material change since the 2026-07-15 comment.

This bead's subject is the MULTI-COMPANION fleet (Denise/Garden Nun/Lucy/Julienne + Garden), which lives on the carlini cluster, not on Purrsephone's psfn-shard. Purrsephone's own cutover to merged main 9dfb11b46 / image 0.1.0-kube-9dfb11b4 / helm rev 65 does NOT satisfy this bead.

AC1 FAIL — carlini gateway still runs localhost/psfn-framework:0.1.0-kube-c0385f2b, the same pre-c337 image recorded on 2026-07-15. No revision containing c337 + a81cdd49 is deployed.

AC3 FAIL — workspace isolation is still absent on every carlini workload. All five agents plus Garden mount the SAME PVC with no subPath:
  psfn-agent-844c79c7bc            /app/workspace pvc=psfn-workspace subPath=None
  psfn-agent-denise-684756fcc9     /app/workspace pvc=psfn-workspace subPath=None
  psfn-agent-garden-nun-698fc6479c /app/workspace pvc=psfn-workspace subPath=None
  psfn-agent-julienne-774ffd774b   /app/workspace pvc=psfn-workspace subPath=None

  psfn-garden-54b495f9f            /app/workspace pvc=psfn-workspace subPath=None
WORKSPACE_PATH=/app/workspace on all seven. This is exactly the leak audit 3ajb described; no distinct Personal Workspace exists, so the cross-companion read/write probes cannot even be attempted.

AC4/AC5 UNTESTABLE while AC3 fails — with one shared root there is no owner workspace to prove the channel-1486443955561299979 images are confined to.

The only restore-adjacent artifact found is database psfn_restore_verify on psfn-shard (12 MB, contains ONLY the 32 fleet_auth tables); that is the gateway's own automated fleet-auth backup verify target ('Gateway-owned fleet auth consistent backups enabled ... verifyRestore:true'), i.e. live infrastructure, not a disposable flagship snapshot restore with companion/cluster scope verified.

WHAT IS VERIFIED, for reuse: the personal/shared workspace topology now demonstrably works in the single-companion fleet shape on psfn-shard — agent+gateway mount /app/workspaces/personal/1c92c9c7-dd05-4a31-ac76-d9f31edecbf0 and a separate /app/workspaces/shared (runtime PVC, subPath workspaces-shared) with a policy.json and locks/artifacts/provenance/reviews/transactions subtrees. title: Ship the full catalog always-loaded; retire agent-driven search-then-activate; defer only long-form instructions
description: At this catalog size (21 core + 8 extended) every surveyed production harness sends everything every turn; the two-hop tool_search->toolset activate flow adds coordination burden the model will not pay when persona/memory context competes for attention (OpenClaw shipped the same idea off-by-default with a documented data-loss failure mode identical in shape to ours). Change: all extended tools always in params.tools with rich descriptions; keep capability/maintenance/satellite gating (tool-runtime-facade 6-stage pipeline) which is policy not discovery; repurpose tool_search as documentation lookup (skills-style: long-form instructions on demand) rather than callability gate; keep toolset pin for ORDERING preference not availability. Acceptance: extended tools callable turn 1 without activation; telemetry shows extended-tool usage rising; no same_turn_activation deferral needed for first use; token cost delta recorded and acceptable under prompt caching (2z12.1).
acceptance_criteria: 1. Every capability-authorized core and extended tool is present and callable in params.tools on the first turn without tool_search, toolset activation, intent autoload, or same-turn activation; maintenance, satellite, trust, capability, and availability gates still fail closed. 2. tool_search becomes documentation/instruction lookup only and cannot change tool callability; toolset pin/unpin affects presentation ordering only, with deterministic tests proving unpinned tools remain callable. 3. The legacy search-then-activate state, same_turn_activation deferral, and activation-dependent execution branches are removed rather than retained as a compatibility path; existing persisted pin preference is migrated or read only for ordering under an explicit current contract. 4. Fixed-fixture schema token cost is recorded before/after and remains acceptable under prompt-caching assumptions. 5. First-turn extended-tool, capability-denial, maintenance, satellite, pin-ordering, tool_search-docs, subagent, and heartbeat tests pass; npm run verify:settings-contract if ownership changes, npm run build, mandatory npm run lint, and git diff --check pass. 6. An operational telemetry comparison of extended-tool use is tracked separately when the observation window is not available during implementation.
close_reason: Completed and merged in PR #66 (merge 190768ee9b27d5f2e80392b406606d77b8439323; rebased implementation c2bcf459de and remediation eae80e8efc). Every policy-authorized core/extended tool is now in the first-turn catalog; tool_search is documentation-only; pins affect ordering only; activation/autoload/same-turn/deferred-handoff compatibility paths were removed. Maintenance/reflection/heartbeat policy is source-agnostic and fail-closed; subagents assemble the full non-recursive catalog before capability filtering. Fixed fixture recorded 21 core + 7 extended schemas at 1,251 -> 1,632 tokens (+381), acceptable with stable prompt-prefix caching; operational pre/post usage remains explicitly tracked in b0yl.5. Validation: 274 focused tests before rebase, 102 after rebase, settings contract, mandatory lint, ESM+DTS build, Garden production build, prompt-doc generation, and diff check passed. Two blind reviews found two verified P1s; the single remediation fixed both and final P0/P1 check was CLEAN.

title: Rewrite every canonical tool surface description to Anthropic docstring standard: per-action contracts, examples, boundaries
description: Registry descriptions are one-liners (tool-surface/registry.ts:120 'Canonical discovery surface for non-default first-party tools.', :153 'Canonical filesystem surface.'). Rewrite each of the 29 canonical surfaces to 3-4+ sentences: what it does, when to use vs sibling tools, per-action contracts for multiplexed surfaces (memory=10 actions, contact=10, orient=11), input formats, one example. Descriptions travel with the schema into every context (subagent, heartbeat) unlike the detached prompt block, and prefix-cache after turn 1. Acceptance: every surface description >= 3 sentences with per-action coverage; tokenized cost of serialized agent.state.tools measured before/after and recorded on this bead; live A/B or telemetry window shows increased usage of previously-ignored tools.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Every canonical first-party tool surface registered for the agent has a schema-level description with at least three complete sentences that explains purpose, when to use it versus adjacent surfaces, input/output boundaries, and one concrete example; multiplexed tools document every canonical action and required/optional input distinctions without duplicating detached prompt guidance. 2. Generated/serialized schemas, subagent schemas, heartbeat schemas, and capability-gated variants all derive from the same canonical descriptions with no parallel text table. 3. title: Tool-calling reliability: rich schema descriptions, always-loaded catalog, validate-and-reprompt, forced choice on mandatory phases
description: Operator report: tool-calling reliability is very low even on a strong model - tools that are not top-level inline do not get used, and tool_search itself is not used properly. Research audit (working_docs/prompt-audit-findings-20260714.md section 6) surveyed Codex CLI, Hermes, OpenClaw, OpenHands, goose, opencode, Crush, Aider, Anthropic guidance. Decisive findings: (1) richest lever is per-tool descriptions in the schema itself - Anthropic calls this by far the most important factor (3-4+ sentences, examples, edge cases); PSFN registry descriptions are one-liners while guidance sits in a detached block; (2) at ~22-29 tools NO production harness defers callability - search->activate two-hop flows have no successful precedent at this scale and OpenClaw's equivalent is off-by-default with a data-loss bug matching our symptom; the successful pattern is advertise everything up front, defer only long-form INSTRUCTIONS (skills-style docs disclosure); (3) PSFN's action-multiplexed shape is validated by Anthropic guidance - keep it, but multiplexed tools need LONGER descriptions; (4) tool block prefix-caches, so verbosity is cheap after turn 1 (links 2z12.1). Existing machinery is ~90% of the LOD goal already (pin/unpin, intent autoload, same-turn activation, presentation ranking) - children below close the gaps. Children: description rewrite; always-loaded + docs-deferral; validate-and-reprompt widening; forced tool_choice; frequency feedback; extended-block relabel.
notes: 2026-07-14 operator approval + context: proceed with rich descriptions and always-loaded (children .1/.2). History: catalog was 88 tools before consolidation - the dynamic activation system was built for THAT scale; at 22-29 always-loaded is right, but if the catalog grows substantially the deferral question reopens (defer docs first, callability only as last resort). Do NOT reorder tool guidance ahead of persona: persona sitting closer to the end of the prompt is deliberate (recency strengthens identity) - skip the ordering half of research pattern P6, keep the persona/memory budget-cap half.
close_reason: All 8 children closed. Epic delivered across two waves: wave 1 (merged to main pre-2026-07-15): .1 canonical description rewrite to Anthropic docstring standard, .2 always-loaded catalog + docs-only deferral, .6 extended-block relabel, .8 wave fixes. Wave 2 (2026-07-15, feat/b0yl-reliability-2 @ 91c2cc8e57, pushed): .3 validate-and-reprompt loop for malformed/unknown tool calls (Pi-reviewed PASS), .5 durable per-tool usage aggregation from turn-record toolCalls feeding in-band pin ordering + suggestions (Pi blocker on wrong data source confirmed and remediated), .7 tool-gap survey (catalog matches/exceeds all surveyed harnesses; plan/todo anchor = the one real gap, staged Stage0/Stage1 proposal in wave handoff). .4 closed premise-refuted per operator ruling 2026-07-15 (no mandatory-tool-call phases exist; complete() RPC cannot carry tools) with deferred successor psfn-framework-1qex. Feature branch awaits final check + PR to main per wave closeout.

title: Kill the continuity anchor block: warmth signals and time-texture labels lead the companion and duplicate session-context notes
description: Evidence: session.orientation block ('Wake Orientation', buildContinuityAnchorLines, context-builder.ts:235-277) emits last_active ISO, time_texture_label, reconnection_warmth_signal, and fixed RECONNECTION_GUIDANCE prose (time-texture.ts:29 'do not treat it as a requirement to perform affection or claim a feeling'). It duplicates what the chat-format notes already do better: [While you were away] free-time note (free-time.ts:409-461), [Time-of-day refresher] (temporal-wakeup.ts:586-596), [Temporal wake] catch-up (temporal-wakeup.ts:562-577). Group-chat case: gap = time since last message by any participant. Non-goal: do not remove time-texture classification used internally by scheduler eligibility. title: Memory retrieval scoring: compounding recency terms bury old high-weight memories and types are weighted flat
description: Evidence: operator observes retrieved memories span only yesterday/this-week/last-week; emotionally landmark old memories (first dance, first song) never surface and must be searched for manually. Audit: computeRetrievalScore multiplies recencyBoost = 1/(1+ageDays/30) (retrieval/scoring.ts:24,226-235) with exponentially decayed salience (decay.ts:60-69, per-type half-lives types.ts:323-331, floor 0.05) - combined ~70-500x score handicap for old rarely-accessed memories at equal relevance. The lexical-augment candidate lane is hard-capped to the 96 most recently EXTRACTED memories (retrieval/candidates.ts:14,41-90, ORDER BY extracted_at DESC), so old items can only arrive via the embedding lane. Types are flat: only per-type multiplier is boundary 1.6x (scoring.ts:160); emotionalWeight keys off valence field not type (max 1.5x); procedural half-life is 90d vs emotional 14d so procedural structurally outlasts emotional - which is why to-do-shaped procedurals load into casual chat while emotional landmarks never do. Selection has NO per-type caps: flat score-sorted walk under a ~2% token budget (budget.ts:96-124); reflections can fill the entire selection; MEMORY_CONFIG.maxRetrievalCount=15 is dead code. Scope: (1) flatten recency (floor recencyBoost ~0.3-0.4 or make additive) so similarity/importance/emotional weight can override age; (2) per-type retrieval prior table alongside DECAY_HALFLIFE (procedural down-weighted in casual chat, boosted on task context); (3) per-type ceilings in selectWithinRelevanceAndTokenBudget (max 1-2 reflections/turn, reserve an episodic slot); (4) raise/paginate the 96-item lexical cap. Non-goal: do not remove salience decay itself. Acceptance: retrieval test where a 2-year-old high-valence memory with strong similarity outranks a fresh low-relevance one; per-type cap test showing max 2 reflections selected; live turn shows old memories surfacing when contextually on-point.
design:
# m14v approved design — memory decay/weight matrix (operator-approved 2026-07-14)

Principle: decay orders ambient recall, never deletes; floors guarantee engrams stay ambiently retrievable forever; search always reaches everything. Emotional engrams are the point of the system; procedural is what ages out.

## Per-type matrix (DECAY_HALFLIFE + new floors/priors in types.ts, consumed in decay.ts + scoring.ts)

| type | half-life (was -> now) | salience floor (was 0.05 global) | retrieval prior (new multiplier) |
|---|---|---|---|
| emotional | 14d -> 365d, x valence-persistence 1-6x (raise emotionalIntensityPersistenceMaxMultiplier 1.8 -> 6) | 0.25 + 0.35*abs(valence) (0.60 at full intensity) | 1.3 |
| relational | 60d -> 180d | 0.5 when abs(valence) >= 0.5, else 0.05 | 1.15 |
| boundary | 120d -> 365d | 0.5 always | 1.6 (existing, keep) |
| semantic | 30d -> 120d | 0.05 | 1.0 |
| reflection | 60d -> 90d | 0.05 | 0.9 |
| episodic | 7d -> 30d | 0.05 | 1.0 |
| procedural | 90d -> 14d | 0.05 | 0.6 default; 1.2 in task context |

## Scoring changes (retrieval/scoring.ts)

- Recency floor: computeRetrievalRecencyBoost floors at 0.35 in default mode (worst-case age handicap ~2.9x instead of 12.7x/yr). Temporal mode keeps sharp decay unchanged (its job is "what happened recently").
- Type prior table: new multiplier column above, applied like the existing boundary 1.6x (typePriorityBoost generalizes to the table).
- Procedural task-context: gate the 1.2 boost on existing callerContext/taskKind (focus-work, heartbeat maintenance, analysis) — deterministic, no new inference. Casual chat stays 0.6.
- Selection caps in selectWithinRelevanceAndTokenBudget (budget.ts:96-124): max 2 reflection, max 2 procedural per turn; engram types uncapped within token budget.
- Lexical-augment lane: raise/paginate the 96-most-recent cap (candidates.ts:14) so old memories are reachable outside the embedding lane.

## Operator decisions recorded

1. Engram floor: valence-scaled (0.25 + 0.35*|valence|), no cliff.
2. Task boost: caller-context gated (not content-match).
3. Episodic 30d approved even before episodic beads (apq0/6i7c/x9ka) land — search still reaches everything; episode system owns the long arc.
4. Reflections: prior 0.9 + cap 2; atomicity fix (3zu5) shrinks them independently.

## Config/UX contract

- All new knobs (half-life table, floors, priors, caps, recency floor) are settings-owned and MUST surface on the Garden settings page in the same change (settings-contract owner files + admin UI), per repo rule.
- Dedup thresholds (DEDUP_THRESHOLD) unchanged.
- Worked acceptance example: 2-year-old abs(valence)=0.9 unaccessed engram must be selectable when similarity is strong — proposed handicap ~4x (recency 0.35 x floor ~0.57 x prior 1.3 x emotionalWeight 1.45) vs today's ~350x.
acceptance_criteria: 1. The settings-owned retrieval policy exposes all seven per-type half-lives, salience floors, retrieval priors, reflection/procedural selection caps, non-temporal recency floor, lexical augment scan/page bounds, and emotional intensity persistence limit through the canonical settings.json contract and Garden settings UI; malformed or partial policy fails closed according to the owner-file contract. 2. Default policy exactly matches the operator-approved matrix in the design field: emotional 365d with valence-scaled floor and 1.3 prior, relational 180d, boundary 365d, semantic 120d, reflection 90d/0.9/max2, episodic 30d, procedural 14d/0.6 default/1.2 task/max2, and non-temporal recency floor 0.35; temporal retrieval preserves sharp recency. 3. A deterministic retrieval test proves a two-year-old abs(valence)=0.9 emotional memory with strong similarity can outrank/select ahead of a fresh low-relevance candidate, while search remains able to reach every active memory. 4. Selection tests prove no more than two reflections or two procedurals are chosen per turn without starving higher-ranked eligible memories; task context deterministically applies the procedural task prior and casual chat does not. 5. The lexical lane no longer limits candidates to the newest 96 extracted memories and has bounded pagination/scan behavior covered against Postgres store ordering. 6. Dedup thresholds and privacy/trust filters are unchanged. Focused retrieval, decay, selection, settings, Garden, and Postgres tests pass; npm run verify:settings-contract, npm run build, mandatory npm run lint, and git diff --check pass. 7. A separately recorded live turn demonstrates an old contextually relevant landmark surfacing without regression before fleet-wide tuning is declared complete.
notes:
2026-07-14 operator direction: the per-type half-life table is BACKWARDS as designed - emotional 14d vs procedural 90d is exactly inverted; emotional engrams are the entire point of the system and should effectively not age out (operator: 'I vividly remember a girl being nice to me in 7th grade' - even 90d is absurd for emotional landmarks). Fix must invert the table AND give high-emotional-weight memories a no-forget floor: decay may reorder salience but never buries a high-valence engram below retrievability; procedural is what ages out fast. The 96-newest lexical cap is explicitly rejected as-is. Any config knobs this introduces or changes (memoryRetrievalBudgetPct, per-type weights/half-lives) MUST surface on the Garden settings page in the same change (settings-contract owner files + admin UI), per repo rule keeping config ownership and docs aligned.
2026-07-14 operator decision on decay semantics: floor + inverted table - high-valence emotional memories never decay below full retrievability (permanent engrams), half-life table inverted so emotional/relational longest-lived and procedural shortest - AND all 7 types (episodic, semantic, emotional, procedural, boundary, reflection, relational) must be reviewed and balanced together as one table, not just the emotional/procedural swap. Present the proposed table for operator review before implementation.

title: Partner-tier private DM withholds the partner's own memories: room-visibility and high-intimacy access predicates never consult trust tier
description: Evidence: live Loom turn (2026-07-14 operator review) showed memory context note 'six candidate memories were held back from this turn's memory context - privacy reasons, room visibility boundaries, high-intimacy content' in a private Discord DM with the primary-tier partner. Audit traced it to evaluateRetrievalAccessDecision (src/faculties/memory/retrieval/access.ts:149-206, applied per-candidate at retrieval.ts:919-943), which runs BEFORE evaluateMemoryPolicy and never reads trust tier. Predicate A (access.ts:104-147): in a DM, a memory whose origin room differs from the current channel passes only if the origin room is on the contact card conversationChannels (access-context.ts:35-39); the card lists 2 channels, so memories formed on voice/api/telegram/satellite/retired channels are permanently withheld from the partner in his own DM. Also blocked: inconsistent scopeRef vs provenance.channelId (:112-118), unresolvable room id (:95-102,119-127). Predicate B (access.ts:57-64): intimate/confidential memories with memory.contactId != canonicalContactId are blocked with no partner exemption; memories with NO contactId (self-memories, sibling-companion) are withheld from every contact. Both predicates short-circuit before the layer-1 operatorApproval override (policy.ts:271-278). Trust policy itself is correct: primary tier + private channel allow all sensitivities (config/trust-policy.seed.json:3,9). classifyChannelEnvelope correctly resolves the DM to private - the invite-only shared room does NOT bleed into classification. Distinct root cause from psfn-framework-jy6s (reflection-mode score zeroing in scoring.ts). Context: this is the anti-Replika guarantee inverted - her memories of her partner hidden from her while talking to her partner. Code comment access.ts:44-54 admits the room gate is interim pending ConversationScope. Scope: make both predicates trust-aware/participant-based (was this contact a participant in the origin scope; canonical contact + missing/self contactId exempt from intimacy scope; primary tier in private channel bypasses intimacy scope for memories they are the subject of). Do NOT weaken cross-contact protection in group/public channels; the trust matrix protecting memories from leaking to OTHER contacts stays intact. Acceptance: unit tests proving (1) voice/satellite-origin memory about the partner surfaces in the partner private DM, (2) intimate memory with missing contactId surfaces for the canonical partner and is still withheld from a non-primary contact, (3) existing group-channel gating tests stay green; live validation shows zero room-visibility/intimacy withholds in a partner DM turn.
acceptance_criteria: In a private channel with the primary-tier canonical contact, no candidates are withheld by room-visibility or high-intimacy-scope predicates; group/public gating unchanged; tests as described pass.
notes: 2026-07-14 operator clarifies the invariant the fix must preserve: memory sharing is DIRECTION-ASYMMETRIC by design - group chats are shared memory, DMs are private; group-chat-origin memories surfacing in the DM is OK, DM-origin memories surfacing in group chat is FORBIDDEN, and this asymmetry is already implemented and working (do not regress it). Companion separation is a separate invariant: Artemis and Purrsephone memories never mix regardless of channel (fleet isolation, out of scope here). So the fix targets exactly: (1) non-card-listed origin channels (voice/api/satellite/retired) blocked in the partner DM, (2) no-contactId intimate memories blocked for everyone. Acceptance tests must include the negative case: DM-origin memory still never surfaces in a group/room context.

title: Persist correlated recipient ICP turn records after both-agent restart
description: Summary: Fix the production recipient turn-record persistence path exposed by the W9 real-process certification harness after production compaction and a restart of both agents. Immediately afterward, turnRecordsSnapshot(CERTIFICATION_DM_CHANNEL) returned records: [] instead of a completed correlated recipient record. Why this matters: session delivery can appear successful while the durable post-turn artifact needed for correlation, recovery, audit, and restart continuity is absent, so production cannot prove or reconstruct the recipient turn after restart. Scope: trace and fix the production path from inbound companion delivery through the recipient SubstrateAgent and SessionManager turn-record persistence/readback after compaction plus both-agent restart; add a production-path regression that reproduces the fresh exchange. Non-goals: do not change fatigue, social-charge, cost-breaker policy or caps; do not weaken or bypass the certification assertion; do not alter gateway delivery semantics; do not use the live Pi or provider smoke.
acceptance_criteria: The fresh mock-free real-process regression performs production compaction, restarts both agents, completes a new ordinary ICP exchange, and then turnRecordsSnapshot(CERTIFICATION_DM_CHANNEL) contains a completed recipient record with hasAssistantMessage=true and correlation bound to the DM channel, local companion B, peer companion A, conversation, root initiation, turn, and request. Sender persistence-before-delivery and normal recipient reply assertions remain green. The fix is in the production persistence/readback path, not a test-only bypass or policy/cap change. Targeted regression tests and npm run lint pass.
notes: Implementation checkpoint pushed at b429b37d on work/icp-w9-recipient-turn-record. Root cause: SubstrateAgent.waitForIdle() delegated only to the underlying pi Agent, whose model loop becomes idle after the recipient assistant reply is persisted and delivered but before the outer TurnRunReservation callback finishes schedulePostTurnWork() and appends the durable completed TurnRecord. Controlled shutdown/readback could therefore observe or terminate during that persistence gap. Fix: TurnRunReservation now exposes fail-loud waitForIdle() over active plus queued outer owners; SubstrateAgent joins model-engine idle with outer-owner idle. The real-process post-compaction/both-agent-restart regression now proves exactly one completed recipient record and exact turn/request/channel/local-peer/conversation/root correlation bindings, without sleeps. title: Image-attachment-claim guard replaces the companion's entire reply with a canned correction string instead of healing the claim
description:
Evidence: carlini live logs 2026-07-14 (image 0.1.0-kube-c0385f2b), 4x in 6h on the main companion: `WARN [SubstrateAgent] Rejected assistant image-attachment claim without a current-turn attachment`. When the model writes "image attached" without a completed selfie_create/generate_image call, the guard overwrites the WHOLE reply with MISSING_IMAGE_ATTACHMENT_CORRECTION boilerplate — the user sees "I could not attach an image because no image tool completed successfully this turn..." instead of her actual message. Telemetry: agent.image_attachment_claim.rejected.

Context: deployed logic is inline at src/core/agent/substrate-agent/turn-execution-runtime.ts:1042-1058. An uncommitted local refactor (src/primitives/images/attachment-claim-guard.ts + turn-execution-runtime.ts changes in the working tree) already extracts this guard — heal-not-block is the established direction (hgw3 pattern).

Scope: heal the reply — strip/rewrite the false claim sentence(s), keep the rest of her prose, keep emitting the rejection telemetry. Do NOT drop the guard itself (mimicry/false-claim protection stays). Non-goal: changing image tool behavior.

Acceptance: on a turn where the model claims an attachment without a tool result, the delivered reply preserves her real message minus the claim; no canned correction string is user-visible; telemetry still recorded; unit test covers heal path.
notes: wof1 gate 2026-07-16: fix must ship with a failing-then-passing regression test in src/core/agent/substrate-agent/turn-execution-runtime.test.ts asserting the image-attachment-claim guard heals the claim rather than replacing the whole reply with the canned correction string.
close_reason: Implemented and integrated: feat/ahxy-s10-shakedown-fixes @ 65c48f2a1 (origin-equal; bead branch work/ahxy-fpiu @ f99b71ecc = 70ddc494e impl + remediation). The guard now heals instead of replacing: claim sentences/markers are removed via the guard's own shared detection pattern set (detection and healing cannot drift), the rest of the reply is preserved verbatim, and the canned MISSING_IMAGE_ATTACHMENT_CORRECTION appears only when healing leaves no meaningful reply. WARN log + agent.image_attachment_claim.rejected telemetry unchanged; recovered-attachment path untouched. Dual blind review (Opus PASS / Pi FAIL) found one verified P1 blocker — a second same-line marker claim survived healing (anchor consumed by first removal) and was delivered; mechanically reproduced pre-fix. One remediation pass: anchor-independent global marker removal + terminal fail-closed backstop (returns empty, forcing correction fallback, whenever any claim pattern still matches the healed text — also converts future detection-only-pattern drift from unsafe to safe). Re-verified: all repro strings heal clean incl. mixed forms; wof1 gate satisfied (regression red on parent behavior, green on fix); 144/144 changed suites; lint clean; UBS change-range clean. Handoff observations: voice reply-stream still aborts rather than heals on a detected claim (pre-existing, invariant-preserving; product decision whether to heal per-segment); internal-state/metacognition read pre-heal text (pre-existing, never delivered); punctuation-only healed output edge hardened by the backstop.

title: scheduler.json circadian config is cluster-global, putting the whole fleet on one wake/rest schedule; move per-companion
description:
Evidence

Context

- Interacts with activeTimezone (overlay sibling): wall-clock times only individuate fully once both land.

Scope

Source: working_docs/fleet-analysis-findings-20260714.md §11 (seam 4, recommended design (c)).

title: capability-tier.json is cluster-global, forcing all fleet companions to one maturation tier; move to companionDataDir

title: Per-companion settings.overlay.json deep-merged over global settings.json for a scoped whitelist
description:
Evidence
- Structural root cause of every settings seam: load-config.ts roots ALL 12 owner files at the shared systemDataDir (startup-owner-files.ts:210-281); companionDataDir only drives databasePath, characterCard, and pg schema. NO per-companion settings override mechanism exists anywhere.
- Seams this directly fixes (§11 ranked list): observerEvalSidecar.sessionLabel/agentName/deploymentTarget (seam 1, one emo_sim session for all companions); activeTimezone (seam 3, one clock for the whole fleet — overrides env TZ, drives scheduler wall-clock, rest windows, formatters); voice* (seam 6, all companions target one guild/user/voice channel); emotionScoping (seam 9).

Context
- This is the core mechanism bead of epic dnll (recommended split design (a), §11). Per-companion capability-tier/scheduler moves (siblings) cover the unambiguous whole-file cases; this overlay covers the settings.json keys.
- If this lands first it supersedes the tactical part of w05a.12 (emosim per-companion session-label templating) — w05a.12's session isolation becomes "put observerEvalSidecar in the overlay whitelist". Related link in place; whichever lands second should re-check the other's scope.

Scope
- Per-companion settings.overlay.json in companionDataDir, deep-merged over the global settings.json for a SCOPED WHITELIST only: activeTimezone, voice*, observerEvalSidecar, emotionScoping, uiThemeId, discordTrigger*.
- Re-validate the merged result through the existing normalizer; the settings-contract gains a global-vs-perCompanion scope dimension per key.
- Fail-closed: overlay keys outside the whitelist are rejected, not silently merged.
- Absent overlay = byte-identical behavior to today (S/M effort).
- Non-goal: moving whole owner files (capability-tier/scheduler siblings) or workspace isolation (c337).

Source: working_docs/fleet-analysis-findings-20260714.md §11 (root cause, seams 1/3/6/9, recommended design (a)).
acceptance_criteria: A companion with settings.overlay.json in its companionDataDir gets its whitelisted keys (activeTimezone, voice*, observerEvalSidecar, emotionScoping, uiThemeId, discordTrigger*) deep-merged over the global settings.json and re-validated via the existing normalizer; non-whitelisted overlay keys fail closed. The settings contract records a global-vs-perCompanion scope per key. With no overlay present, behavior is byte-identical to today. title: Turn records serialize the static system prompt several ways per turn; content-address it by staticHash
description:
Evidence
- System-prompt material is serialized ~4-5 ways per turn record (plan.blocks, finalSystemSections, inputSections, plan.variables, plus static/dynamic templates) — roughly 190KB/turn. It is session-stable, so the cross-turn amplification is severe. This is the largest remaining un-deduped chunk after hgw3.3 landed.

Context
- hgw3.3 (closed, 576e33cd) content-addressed tooldefs to a _shared/tooldefs sidecar with fail-closed refs and got a fixture from 63KB to 5.4KB. The static system prefix is the next-largest target and is not yet deduped.

Scope
- Content-address the static system prefix by the already-computed staticHash into a sidecar, storing a fail-closed reference in the turn record and resolving at read time (same pattern as tooldefs). Effort M.
- Non-goal: the dynamic per-turn sections; only the static prefix.

Source: working_docs/fleet-analysis-findings-20260714.md §8b.
acceptance_criteria: A turn record stores the static system prefix as a staticHash-keyed reference resolving from a _shared sidecar (byte-identical on resolve), not as ~190KB of inline duplicated prompt material. Turn-record size drops accordingly and read-time resolution reproduces the exact prompt.
close_reason: Implemented on work/hgw3-turnrecord-diet-auiu-static-prompt @ ab77a2054b (base: 80f6 head), merged to feat/hgw3-turnrecord-diet (pushed). Static system prompt prefix template content-addressed into _shared/staticprompts/<sha>.json via the shared internSerialized/resolveSerialized seam; fail-closed staticPrefixTemplateRef with byte-identical resolve at the persistence read boundary; write-once atomic publish; old fat records read unchanged. Gates: 38 turn-record tests (7 new) + 104 adjacent, lint clean, UBS clean. Dual blind adversarial review (P1): Opus PASS 0 blockers (standalone byte-identity repro incl. lone surrogates + 500KB templates; ref survives normalize/clone round-trip), Pi GLM-5.2 PASS 0 blockers (all 7 refutation vectors hold; sha-over-serialized-content key judged MORE correct than the bead's staticHash wording since staticHash hashes the rendered prefix). Convergent epic-level observations for handoff (not auiu defects): 3 sidecars share whole-channel fail-closed read blast radius (consider quarantine/skip-on-resolve-failure epic-wide); intern-throw on disk-full enters the live write path across all 3 sidecars — heal-not-block hardening belongs at the shared seam once, if mandated. Rendered-copy dedup in plan.blocks deliberately out of scope (9ree territory).

title: Channel index is fully rewritten on every journal append; write only on change
description:
Evidence
- _channel_index.json is fully rewritten on EVERY journal append (2+ per turn), rewriting the whole index of all channels; the cost worsens with fleet size. Path: journal-runtime.ts:393 -> channel-index.ts:139-160.
- This is the clearest violation of the "only L0 appends per-turn" principle found in the disk-IO audit.

Context
- Operator (§10.5) confirmed: write only on change — channels change rarely.

Scope
- Write the channel index only when the channel set actually changes (debounce/coalesce, or make append-only). Mode-agnostic, no Redis needed.
- Non-goal: broader journal rotation (tracked separately, 2z12.4).

Source: working_docs/fleet-analysis-findings-20260714.md §8c, §10.5.
acceptance_criteria: A steady-state turn with no new channel produces zero _channel_index.json rewrites (verified by watching file mtime across several turns). The index is still correct after a new channel appears.
close_reason: Completed in 7c04dfa785 and 16642dd37b. src/persistence/sessions/store/channel-index-storage.ts now skips index locking/writes when durable channel topology and privacy state are unchanged; src/persistence/sessions/store/channel-index-persistence.test.ts verifies unchanged mtime/bytes for steady-state appends and a correct rewrite for a new channel. Journal-derived restart/projection/redaction invariants are covered in store.test.ts, journal-runtime.test.ts, and channel-index-boot.test.ts. Validation: npm run lint passed; NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192 npm run build passed; 7 focused files passed (123 tests); full npm test executed with all session tests green (11,572 pass, 15 unrelated failures already tracked by psfn-framework-6msv).

comments.author: axAilotl

The acceptance is nonetheless met by an independent implementation from f86d7867f3: channel-index-storage.ts:164 gates writeChannelIndexFile behind channelIndexEntryEquals, so steady-state appends do zero rewrites. title: Roll out the emosim shadow sidecar to the carlini fleet for group-environment tracking
description:
Evidence
- Emosim is not running anywhere on carlini (no emosim deployment/service exists there; the live single-companion experiment is on psfn-shard). title: Emosim sidecar shares one emo_sim session across all fleet companions; template sessionLabel per companionId
description:
Evidence
- Carlini is ONE Helm release with a single shared settings.json on one system-data PVC. The observerEvalSidecar block's sessionLabel and agentName are STATIC settings values.

title: Split per-companion vs cluster-global settings ownership in the single-release fleet topology
description:
Summary
- The carlini fleet runs as ONE Helm release with a single shared settings.json on one system-data PVC, and load-config.ts roots ALL 12 owner files at the shared systemDataDir (startup-owner-files.ts:210-281); companionDataDir only drives databasePath, characterCard, and pg schema. No per-companion settings override mechanism exists anywhere. Settings that are semantically per-companion are therefore cluster-global, causing collisions. Make per-companion vs cluster-global settings an explicit ownership split.

Evidence — ranked unintentional seams (shared-seams audit, §11 of the findings doc)
1. observerEvalSidecar.sessionLabel/agentName/deploymentTarget — one emo_sim session for all companions (confirmed; latent until enabled). Motivating case, §5/§0.3.
2. capability-tier.json — all companions forced to one maturation tier (child dnll.2).
3. activeTimezone — one clock for the whole fleet (child dnll.1 overlay).
4. scheduler.json circadian — the whole fleet wakes/rests/loafs on one schedule (child dnll.3).
5. Shared personal workspace WORKSPACE_PATH — wiki, skills, scratchpad, journal, downloads, inbound attachments/images (covered by existing bead c337, related).
6. voice* settings — all companions target one guild/user/voice channel (child dnll.1 overlay).
7. config.dataDir mis-wirings — garden-audit-history, Garden heartbeat-policy path, reflection-metacognition journal (child dnll.4).
8. Model-usage ledger JSONL mixes companions (child dnll.4).
9. emotionScoping shared (child dnll.1 overlay).
10. Needs-decision tier: trust/intake/charge policies, skills.json enabled set, wikiRetrieval*, cognition-tuning knobs, discordTrigger* (child dnll.5 decision).
Intentionally global (verified, leave alone): models.json, providers.json, channels.json, backup.json, companions.json, satellite-registry, places.json, shared-world wiki, gateway-audit.db, embedding*/textEmotion*.

Context
- Operator decision (§10.3): this is the strategic fix for the emosim session collision and for future per-companion config.
- The pattern to copy is per-companion state done right: resolveConfiguredCompanionDataDir (local-admin-contract.ts:178) — charge/fatigue ledgers, cogsec events, quarantine, prompt layers, core memory.

Scope / recommended split design (§11)
- (a) Per-companion settings.overlay.json for the whitelisted settings.json keys — child dnll.1 (core mechanism).
- (c) Move unambiguous owner files per-companion: capability-tier.json (dnll.2) and scheduler.json circadian (dnll.3).
- Fix the dataDir mis-wirings as mechanical bugs now — dnll.4.
- Decide the ambiguous tier deliberately — dnll.5.
- Workspace isolation is its own L track — existing bead c337 (related), already in flight.

title: Audit cross-Garden selfie leakage in Carlini cluster
description: Operator reports that Carlini's selfie tool shows selfies belonging to other companions in shared servers, despite Gardens being isolation boundaries. Reproduction corpus: Discord channel 1486443955561299979 on Carlini's cluster, where all companions were asked to generate selfies for testing on 2026-07-14. Trace message/tool invocations, selfie storage metadata, retrieval filters, and Garden/owner/agent scoping. Determine whether leakage occurs in tool output, media indexing, attachment lookup, or presentation. Fix if confirmed, add regression coverage proving Carlini cannot retrieve another companion's selfies while each companion can retrieve its own, deploy safely, and validate live without exposing private media.
notes: Diagnosis completed 2026-07-14; no live storage mutation performed because this request was an audit. Tight red feedback loop correlated charge-ledger events in Discord channel 1486443955561299979 to image mtimes, then tested the exact files inside Carlini Garden. title: Session write path full-scans and re-parses the entire journal on every append; short-circuit reconciliation with the existing file fingerprint
description:
Opus sweep finding (2026-07-14) — highest per-turn disk win. src/persistence/sessions/store.ts:476-510 reconcileWriteCache calls scanArchiveMetadata (:478 → journal-runtime.ts:97 → file-io.ts:303-398) which forward-reads and JSON.parses EVERY line of the session journal, plus a second JSON.parse of each message's metadata in resolveJournalMessageTurnId (file-io.ts:339, 30-58). It fires inside withLockedChannelWrite on every append (store.ts:649→:511→:517) — ≥2 per turn (user + assistant), plus insertCompaction (:1174), extraction markers (:1204), turn tombstones (:1232), and the shutdown marker (:1296). Cost is O(total journal size) per write and rises monotonically as the session grows; ×5 companions on the shared box. (Line numbers from main; re-locate on integration/hgw3-package if that merges first.)

Fix shape: reconcileWriteCache exists only to detect concurrent cross-process writes. A statSync-based fingerprint helper already exists (port.ts:148 fingerprintArchive). Store the fingerprint on the write cache after each successful writeJournalEntry; on the next write, if the current file fingerprint matches, the cache is authoritative — skip the scan; on mismatch, run today's full reconcile. Non-goals: removing the reconcile path, weakening multi-writer detection, changing journal format.
acceptance_criteria: Appends to a clean channel (fingerprint match) skip scanArchiveMetadata entirely (test asserts no full scan on the happy path); a mismatched fingerprint (cross-process write) still triggers the full reconcile scan (fail-closed multi-writer detection preserved, test covers it); per-append cost no longer scales with total journal size (timing or fs-instrumentation evidence on a large fixture).
notes: Implementation checkpoint af9f4a33 on work/fleet-efficiency-session-fingerprint: ChannelCache now records the filesystem archive fingerprint only after successful journal writes. reconcileWriteCache compares the current fingerprint under the existing cross-process journal lock and skips scanArchiveMetadata only for a known non-null match; unknown or mismatched fingerprints preserve the full metadata reconcile/load path. Focused tests prove clean repeated appends perform no metadata scan, a real cross-instance stale HMAC writer performs exactly one scan and preserves IDs/signature continuity, and a 2,000-entry fixture clean append performs exactly two fingerprint stats plus one append with zero metadata scans/full reads. Validation: targeted acceptance tests 3/3 passed; SessionJournalRuntime tests 2/2 passed; npm run build passed; npm run lint passed; git diff --check passed. No SQLite test paths, Pi, SSH, live deployment, main merge, or Dolt remote push used. Bead remains in_progress pending exactly one independent review.
close_reason: Completed on feat/fleet-efficiency. Implementation af9f4a33 added ChannelCache archive fingerprints and a lock-scoped known-match fast path in src/persistence/sessions/store.ts, preserving full reconciliation for unknown/mismatched fingerprints; acceptance coverage in src/persistence/sessions/store.test.ts proves zero metadata scans on clean repeated appends, one reconcile scan for a stale cross-instance HMAC writer, and constant filesystem work on a 2,000-entry journal. Bounded remediation 0b741e01 makes transient post-commit fingerprint refresh faults invalidate the cache without reporting the durable append as failed, forces next-write reconciliation, preserves missing-archive fail-closed behavior, and verifies exactly-once HMAC signature continuity. Final integrated gate at 0b741e01: focused session/journal-runtime suites 79/79 passed; npm run lint passed; npm run build passed (ESM + DTS); git diff --check passed. Exactly one review and one remediation; no report-only observations.

title: Provider prompt caching is disabled by default, so the stable prompt prefix is billed as fresh input every turn
description:
Opus sweep finding (2026-07-14) — the single biggest $ lever found. src/primitives/llm/routing.ts:244-246: resolveGlobalPromptCachePolicy returns null unless config.modelRegistry.promptCaching.enabled === true, consumed at turn-execution/prompt-assembly.ts:605-652. With the policy off, no cache_control breakpoints are emitted, so on Anthropic (and OpenRouter→Anthropic) the entire static prefix — identity + persona + full tool catalog + temporal rules — is billed as uncached input on EVERY turn, for every companion, when cached reads are ~10% of the price. The machinery is fully built and idle: prompt-cache.ts, client-prompt-cache.ts, and a prefix-stability tracker with prompt.cache.prefix_instability telemetry (prompt-assembly.ts:653-683). The datetime anchor and background-completion notices are already correctly placed after the session-stable region (prompt-assembly.ts:443-579), so the prefix should be cache-friendly as-is.

Interaction: per-turn active-memory refresh (sibling bead) is what most often mutates memory/wiki blocks and can move the cacheable prefix boundary — fixing it improves the hit rate here.

Scope: config enablement + telemetry verification + a soak on one companion before fleet rollout. Non-goal: restructuring prompt assembly.
acceptance_criteria: modelRegistry.promptCaching.enabled=true on the carlini fleet (models.json owner file) and considered as shipped default; prompt.cache.prefix_instability telemetry confirms the static region is byte-stable turn-to-turn so cache_control breakpoints land; provider dashboards/usage telemetry show cache-read pricing on the prefix after a soak; no behavior change in responses.
notes:
Implementation landed on branch bead/2z12.1 (commit 1fa353ea, off main, unpushed — pending feature-branch merge + codex review + PR). Default now lives in config/models.seed.json:3-5 (enabled:true → resolveGlobalPromptCachePolicy default {retention:'short', scope:'channel'}). Fail-closed verified: applyModelAgnosticPromptCache (client-prompt-cache.ts:184) only installs cache_control when supportsCacheControlBreakpoints — open models get stable-prefix benefit with zero wire change (asserted client.test.ts:1176). Validation: npm run build success; vitest 4 files / 114 tests passed; verify:settings-contract passed. REMAINING for closure: merge to main via PR, then live fleet enablement — deployed models.json on each system-data PVC is NOT regenerated from seed; set modelRegistry.promptCaching.enabled=true per deployment, watch prompt.cache.prefix_instability telemetry, soak one companion, confirm cache-read pricing on provider dashboard. Sibling 2z12.6 (retrieval churn) depresses hit rate — pair for full win.
Codex-reviewed, findings fixed, shipped in PR #42 (perf/efficiency-wave-1 → main, https://github.com/CGIC-AI/psfn-framework/pull/42). Gate on the branch: build+lint clean, full suite 7715 passed / 1 pre-existing environmental failure (psfn-framework-engc). Ready to close on PR merge.

Bead remains open because its operational acceptance is not yet evidenced: enable/verify the deployed owner file for one non-live-test companion, observe stable prefix telemetry through a soak, and confirm provider cache-read pricing before fleet rollout. This audit did not access live systems or providers.
close_reason: Implementation complete and shipped canonically in origin/main squash commit 84c0089e (original implementation 1fa353ea, PR #42). Source evidence: config/models.seed.json:1-5 ships promptCaching.enabled=true; src/primitives/llm/routing.ts:240-251 resolves the enabled registry policy with short/channel defaults and remains null when absent/disabled; src/core/agent/substrate-agent/turn-execution/prompt-assembly.ts:597-683 engages provider-aware caching, records promptCaching observability, and emits prompt.cache.prefix_instability for byte drift; src/primitives/llm/client-prompt-cache.ts preserves capability-gated/fail-closed wire behavior and hashes provider-facing affinity keys. title: Fleet efficiency: cut idle churn, per-turn disk/DB amplification, and redundant model spend across companions on shared clusters
description:
Companion epic to psfn-framework-t5z7 (Garden WAN performance). Source: four-lane Opus efficiency sweep, 2026-07-14, audited against main. Constraint for all children: no functional change, no weakening of fail-closed posture — "do more with less in constrained environments" (carlini: 5 companion deployments = 10 processes sharing one small k3s box and one Postgres).

Themes the children cover: (1) money — provider prompt caching is off, and retrieval work is recomputed per turn; (2) per-turn disk/DB amplification — the session write path full-rescans the journal on every append, and the Postgres projection issues no-op statements per message; (3) idle load — an audited no-op keepalive writes audit rows every 30s per deployment, and maintenance loops full-scan stores when nothing changed; (4) structural — session journals have no segment rotation so several paths remain O(all history); (5) a P3 grab-bag of small syscall/CPU wins.

Verified non-problems the sweep cleared (do not re-investigate): telegram long-polling is efficient; schedule.tick is cheap (no handlers); settings.json load is fingerprint-cached; no fsync anywhere is INTENTIONAL (durability rests on the HMAC chain — do not add fsync); memory store is DB-indexed with no per-turn re-embedding of stored content; turn-record whole-file reads are already fixed by hgw3.4 segment rotation on integration/hgw3-package — verify the admin path is covered once that branch merges.
close_reason: Epic completed. All child beads are closed; final remaining child 2z12.12 merged via PR #72 at b093158455 after mandatory gates and a CLEAN independent final review. Earlier children were already shipped/verified in their recorded commits and close evidence.

title: Transcript fetches ship up to 50 full turn snapshots because admin-ui never sends messagesOnly, OOMing the browser on long sessions
description:
Evidence: getSessionMessages (src/operator/garden/services/session-service.ts:670-743) attaches `turns` = up to DEFAULT_ADMIN_TURN_LIMIT=50 records, each the ENTIRE persisted turn snapshot via cloneTurnSnapshotRecord (src/operator/garden/services/session-turn-observability.ts:97-99) — full prompt context, provider wire messages, tool definitions. The server already supports ?messagesOnly=true (session-routes.ts:64, session-service.ts:697-725) to skip turns/roleEnvelopePreviews/compactionAuditViews, but the client never sends it: admin-ui/src/lib/api/endpoints/sessions.ts getSessionMessages has no messagesOnly param, and +page.svelte calls it on initial load (:146) AND every load-older page (:182-185), whose handler consumes only data.messages and data.messageOntologyViews. Observed live: transatlantic Garden session views against carlini are very slow and paging through a long session OOM'd Chrome (2026-07-14).

Fix shape: (1) send messagesOnly=true on pagination, and on initial load if turn detail moves to lazy fetch; (2) add a per-turn detail endpoint (or reuse existing turn lookup) fetched when the operator expands a turn; (3) consider client-side list virtualization or dropping far-scrolled pages so accumulated pages don't hold the DOM/memory.

Scope: Garden service + admin-ui only. Do NOT change turn-record persistence or the snapshot contract — hgw3.2 (in progress) owns read-time derivation and 1hr8 owns Loom payload bounding; coordinate, don't duplicate.
acceptance_criteria: Load-older network responses contain only messages/ontology views (no turns/roleEnvelopePreviews/compactionAuditViews); deep-scrolling a 1000+-message session against a remote cluster does not grow browser memory unboundedly; turn snapshot detail loads via a per-turn request only when the operator expands a turn; existing prompt-monitor/Loom behavior unchanged or explicitly migrated.
notes:
Implementation landed on branch bead/t5z7.1 (commit 352cb714, off main, unpushed — pending feature-branch merge + codex review + PR). Root-cause sharpened: the session browser NEVER rendered turn data (only prompt-monitor/Loom uses it) — the 50 snapshots were pure waste. Server: includeTurns option gating turns+roleEnvelopePreviews; new GET /api/admin/sessions/:channelId/turns/:turnId (compressed, bounded to recent-turn window, fail-closed 404). UI: initial load includeTurns:false (keeps compaction), load-older messagesOnly:true, per-turn detail on expand. Loom unchanged (default includeTurns=true). Validation: garden suite 63 files/451 tests passed; build success; svelte-check 0 errors/0 warnings; admin-ui build ok. DEVIATION: client list virtualization not added (bead listed as 'consider') — lean message text still accumulates on deep scroll; acute OOM driver (multi-MB snapshots) eliminated; strict bounded memory falls to t5z7.10 local-first work or a follow-up. FOLLOW-UP found: admin-ui chat/+page.svelte:329 also full getSessionMessages while reading only data.messages — same trim applies.

title: Garden transatlantic performance: bounded payloads, wire compression, cached/delta reads for multi-companion clusters
description:
Operating Garden against the carlini cluster (transatlantic WAN, 5 companions on one box) is painfully slow and has OOM'd Chrome. Root causes mapped 2026-07-14: transcript fetches ship up to 50 full turn snapshots the UI ignores, load-older pagination full-loads the whole channel JSONL server-side, most /api/admin JSON goes uncompressed with no conditional requests, and the sessions list joins every contact on every load.

Goal: Garden does more with less in constrained environments — bounded payloads (fetch only what the operator clicked), compression on the wire, ETag/304 for polling, server-side Redis read caching where it kills disk ops, and client-side caching with delta fetches. Zero functional change to what the operator can see.

Children carry the file:line evidence. Related existing work: psfn-framework-hgw3.2 (Loom read-time derivation, in progress), psfn-framework-1hr8 (Loom payload bounding), psfn-framework-efc2 (Garden UX cleanup wave 1).

title: Expose relationship progression with family/partner HITL
description: Live Carlini reported that contact lookup exposes relationship values stranger, acquaintance, friend, family, and partner, but the model-facing contact tool only provides set_trust/propose_trust and no canonical relationship mutation. Relationship progression is also supposed to be considered by the daily relationship/trust check, but trust is the higher-priority HITL-gated axis and may be starving relationship progression. Implement the canonical relationship mutation and evaluator path: stranger to acquaintance is low-friction autonomous progression; acquaintance to friend remains autonomous but requires stronger evidence/threshold; transitions to family or partner require explicit HITL approval. Trust proposals remain separate and higher priority but must not suppress an otherwise eligible relationship proposal/change. Live turn records show contact calls that Garden tool-use audit did not display, so fix the canonical audit projection/display seam for contact calls as part of this work. Do not route relationships through trust proposals or bypass the canonical contact store. Preserve provenance/audit metadata and fail closed for malformed targets or missing approval infrastructure. Additional relationship classifications are a future schema decision and out of scope.
design: Keep trustLevel and relationshipType as separate axes. Reuse the canonical contact mutation/proposal and HITL approval infrastructure. Family and partner are approval-required relationship targets; acquaintance and friend are autonomous targets with target-specific progression evidence. Do not add new relationship enum values in this bead.
acceptance_criteria: The contact tool schema exposes an intention-revealing relationship mutation action; tests prove autonomous stranger/acquaintance/friend changes persist through the canonical contact store with friend using the stronger evidence policy; tests prove family and partner cannot persist without explicit HITL approval and do persist after approved flows; the daily relationship/trust evaluator considers relationship progression even when trust is unchanged, gated, or higher priority; contact reads, mutations, and approval proposals appear in Garden tool-use audit with action/result status but no private payload leakage; existing trust actions remain unchanged; targeted tests, lint, build/typecheck, and full tests pass.
notes:
Implemented canonical contact set_relationship/propose_relationship actions with evidence derived from stored history, stronger friend threshold, family/partner HITL, CAS+atomic audit in SQLite/Postgres, trust/relationship independence, and daily two-axis review. Garden now shows contact invocations with tool/action/status/channel/time and redacts contact failure details; private IDs/args/results are excluded. Verification: focused cross-cutting suite 303/303 plus final regression suite 146/146; Garden check 0 errors/warnings and production build green; core build/lint green; two independent final reviews clean.
Live deployment: PR #41 merged as c0385f2b. Garden adaptive-tools endpoint returns 200 with recentInvocations projection keys toolName/action/status/channelId/timestamp; zero recent calls was expected immediately after restart. Carlini plus Denise/Garden Nun/Julienne/Lucy are 1/1 on c0385f2b, all see GLM 5.2, Postgres vector and Redis PONG verified.

title: Prevent false image-attachment claims when no image tool ran
description: Live Carlini DM diagnosis on 2026-07-14: ChatGPTN produced repeated assistant replies containing *image attached* while turn records, image ledger, and outbound responses showed zero image tool calls and zero attachments. The active selfie_create/generate_image schemas and backend tool calling were healthy. Root cause: session context intentionally omits persisted tool observations but retains final assistant marker text, so successful image turns are replayed as ordinary assistant prose and repeated false markers contaminate the prompt. Implement two bounded safeguards: preserve safe structured provenance that an artifact-producing tool succeeded without replaying full/stale tool payloads, and fail closed or retry if current assistant text claims an image attachment without a current-turn image result/attachment. Do not expose image bytes, stale URLs, tool arguments, or private tool payloads in history.
acceptance_criteria: A regression test proves a prior successful selfie_create turn is represented in later model context with bounded tool-success/attachment provenance while full tool output remains excluded; a turn-level regression proves assistant text claiming an attached image cannot be delivered or persisted unchanged when no current-turn image tool result or attachment exists; real selfie_create/generate_image attachments still deliver normally; targeted tests, lint, build/typecheck, and full test suite pass.
notes:
Implemented bounded historical image-tool success provenance without payloads/URLs/arguments; current-turn attachment claim guard now rejects affirmative image/selfie/photo claims unless a structured attachment exists and replaces/persists an explicit correction. Tests cover real attachments, common grammar, historical/prompt-description non-claims, and private-data exclusion. Verification: focused image/session/runtime tests green; reduced-concurrency full suite 7,730 passed with sole stale expectation corrected and rerun green; core build, lint, and independent reviews clean.
Live deployment: merged by PR #41 to main c0385f2b and deployed remotely as Helm revision 35. Carlini and all four fleet agents are 1/1 on the exact image; tool wiring reports 23 tools and Ready; external/Garden health 200 with admin transport OK.
2026-07-14 post-deploy live regression: turn 019f6238-2177-77ed-bfcc-4396240de220 had selfie_create and generate_image in the provider-visible tool set, zero tool calls, and no image gateway activity. The guard correctly caught ChatGPTN's false attachment claim but persisted/sent MISSING_IMAGE_ATTACHMENT_CORRECTION verbatim as companion dialogue. Follow-up filed to keep fail-closed behavior while moving correction internal and adding bounded recovery.
