title: Fix hanging bd dolt push and malformed journal preflight
description:
## Summary
Diagnose and repair bd dolt push --json for the shared PSFN beads database. The local SQL server is healthy, but pushing committed bead state to the configured GitHub-backed Dolt remote either reports a malformed chunk journal during pre-push fsck or hangs indefinitely in dolt push origin main.

## Evidence
- Repository: /home/ada/psfn-framework
- bd dolt test --json: connection_ok=true at 127.0.0.1:3308, schema_version=1.
- bd dolt status --json: shared server running under /home/ada/.beads/shared-server/dolt.
- First push message: pre-push fsck could not run, skipping integrity check: Could not open dolt database: error bootstrapping chunk journal: journal index is malformed.
- Subsequent pushes spawned dolt push origin main and produced no progress for multiple minutes; the agent terminated only its own duplicate stuck push processes.
- bd dolt commit --json succeeds and local shared Dolt remains authoritative.

## Scope
Inspect the shared-server database and the push implementation, preserve all issue history, repair or safely rebuild only corrupted journal/index metadata, and prove a normal non-force push completes. Check for orphan push processes before retrying.

## Non-goals
Do not force-push, delete bead history, replace the authoritative shared database without a verified backup, or modify Git source history.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A verified backup of the shared beads Dolt database exists before repair. 2. No orphan bd/dolt push processes remain. 3. Integrity/fsck checks complete without malformed-journal errors. 4. bd dolt push --json exits successfully without --force and does not hang. 5. bd show psfn-framework-6hov --json and bd show psfn-framework-2tlk --json return the committed records after repair. 6. The repair and validation evidence are recorded in the close reason.
close_reason: Closed

Repo work complete on branch kube-satellite-enable (worktree, base origin/main ae758a4f). Commits 3fe94053 + 4bdf3084, prefixed psfn-framework-ba5c.1:. NOT pushed, bead left open per instructions.

DESIGN DECISIONS
- mTLS: scoped-Bearer-now + staged cert. Full hub->gateway mTLS blocked by three verified facts: (1) API_TLS_* flips the single /v1 listener to HTTPS for ALL consumers (Traefik backend, hostPort 10053 LAN clients) at once; (2) gateway reads listener certs once at startup (createApiHttpServer readFileSync) — no TLS reload = psfn-framework-zlon; (3) hub companion bridge uses plain fetch with no client-cert support (only its chat path has it, and that path fail-closes requiring https base URL). So: dedicated secrets.values.satelliteHubApiKey -> hub PSFN_API_KEY + gateway API_SATELLITE_KEYS (H4 satellite-scoped principal, endpoint lists api-key-<sha256[:24]> in apiKeyPrincipalIds). cert-manager Certificate psfn-satellite-hub-client (SPIFFE URI SAN spiffe://<trustDomain>/psfn/satellite-hub/<companionId>) issued+renewed NOW and mounted at /run/psfn/tls/psfn-client; concrete flip documented (clientCertSan binding — fingerprint/SPKI pins would break on every cert-manager key rotation).
- Cert ownership: kube cert-manager (chart CA / live psfn-ca Issuer), NOT the PSFN cert-manager sidecar — single CA custody for all in-cluster identities; sidecar remains for non-cluster LAN satellites (docs/certificates.md).
- Exposure: hostPorts.satelliteHub (ws://<pi>:8787), same mechanism as gateway hostPort 10053, with sourceCIDR NetworkPolicy ingress + Recreate strategy; Traefik psfn-hub.local stays optional/disabled on LAN.
- Companion relay verified admissible: server.ts satellite-surface allowlist includes companionRoute (w9hj.1); scopes approvals/artifacts/tool_activity granted in the documented satellites.json entry. Known benign: hub GET /v1/identity probe 403s under scoped key (non-fatal by hub design), documented + optional follow-up noted.

title: Rationalize PSFN branches and worktrees onto origin/main
description:
## Summary
Audit all 392 local branches and 265 linked worktrees in /home/ada/psfn-framework against canonical origin/main, recover any genuinely novel and valuable committed or dirty-worktree content onto a rationalization branch, then remove redundant local worktrees and branches only after a verified recovery bundle and explicit operator approval of the literal cleanup plan.

## Why
The repository accumulated hundreds of agent worktrees and local branches. The operator believes completed work is on origin/main but requires proof before cleanup. Ten worktrees currently have dirty state, one open GitHub PR uses ops/artemis-helm-shakedown, and the active root checkout is dirty on s10-location-foundations. Incorrect bulk deletion could lose unpushed commits or uncommitted files.

## Scope
- Detect canonical from origin/HEAD and fetch current remote state.
- Inventory every local branch and linked/detached worktree with head SHA, ahead/behind counts, patch equivalence, upstream/PR state, and dirty-state counts.
- Create verified backup refs and an external git bundle under /home/ada/psfn-framework-branch-worktree-archive-2026-07-09, with per-branch diffs/format patches and per-worktree staged, unstaged, and untracked captures.
- Protect main, active/dirty work, open-PR branches, and operator-selected exceptions.
- Triage one entry at a time as protected, already merged, superseded, novel, partially novel, divergent, dirty-only, stale, or garbage with evidence against origin/main.
- Recover approved novel content on branch-rationalization-2026-07-09, run required validation including npm run lint for code changes, and push landed git state as required by repo policy.
- Present an exact worktree-removal and branch-deletion plan for verbatim operator authorization before executing cleanup.
- Never delete remote branches, force-push, delete backup refs, or delete the recovery bundle.

## Non-goals
- No live deployment changes.
- No remote branch deletion.
- No deletion of open-PR or explicitly protected work.
- No force-pushing origin/main.

## Files/artifacts
- .worktree_branch_rationalization_workspace/ (ignored transient run state)
- /home/ada/psfn-framework-branch-worktree-archive-2026-07-09/ (persistent recovery bundle outside repo)
- refs/branch-rationalization-backup/* (recovery refs)

## Known starting state
- origin/main is canonical.
- 392 local branches and 265 worktrees exist; 10 worktrees are dirty.
- Active checkout /home/ada/psfn-framework is s10-location-foundations and dirty.
- GitHub PR #32 uses ops/artemis-helm-shakedown and must remain protected while open.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Every starting branch and worktree has an inventory row and recovery-bundle entry; dirty state includes staged, unstaged, and untracked data.
2. Backup-ref byte equality and git-bundle head round-trip verification pass with zero mismatches before cleanup.
3. Every non-protected branch is individually checked against origin/main using ancestry plus git cherry patch equivalence and content evidence; all novel/ambiguous items are surfaced or recovered, never guessed away.
4. main, open-PR branches, the active checkout, dirty work pending recovery, and any operator additions remain protected until safe.
5. Any recovered code passes targeted tests, npm run build where relevant, and mandatory npm run lint before its bead/stream is considered done.
6. Operator reviews and explicitly authorizes the literal cleanup plan before any git worktree remove or git branch deletion executes.
7. Cleanup uses git worktree remove before individual git branch -d/-D operations; no mass-delete primitive, remote deletion, force-push, reset --hard, git clean, or bundle deletion occurs.
8. Final handoff reports initial/final counts, retained/recovered work, validation, bundle location, recovery commands, bead state, and confirmed origin/main relationship.
close_reason: Completed with verified recovery: V3 bundle at /home/ada/psfn-framework-branch-worktree-archive-2026-07-09-v3 passed byte equality, bundle fetch, and conformance checks. Root checkout is clean main at ae758a4f, equal to origin/main. Signed audit passed npm run lint, npm run build, npm audit, and npm test (691 files; 7,549 passed, 3 skipped). After operator authorization and 24-hour/Helm exceptions, removed 234 worktrees and 367 local branches, representing 146,683,158,528 bytes (~137 GiB) of measured checkout data. Retained 48 worktrees and 45 branches, including recent UI work, backup/kube-helm-artifacts, Artemis Helm, dirty/active work, and three locked Claude worktrees; agent/e7.1-wakeup was the one originally planned item retained after git refused locked-worktree removal. Remote deletion is intentionally outside this bead; 71 byte-verified operator-run commands are staged in the ignored workspace.

title: Harden k3s certificate rotation and live TLS reload
description:
Summary:
The CogSec/k3s integration currently gives the namespace private CA and all leaf Certificates the same 2160h duration and 360h renewBefore window in deploy/helm/psfn/templates/certificates.yaml and deploy/helm/psfn/values.yaml. Workloads read TLS key/cert/CA bytes once when constructing Node TLS servers/clients (including src/boundary/gateway/transport.ts and src/operator/garden/transport-server.ts), and no controller annotation or application watcher restarts/reloads pods when cert-manager rotates Secrets. At the first renewal window, CA and leaves can rotate out of lockstep with no dual-root overlap; even a successful Secret renewal can leave live processes using expired bytes while TCP liveness remains healthy. This was discovered during psfn-framework-es4t's urgent CogSec shadow rollout.

Scope:
- Give the private CA an independently managed, substantially longer lifetime than leaves or adopt an operator-approved stable external issuer.
- Define overlap/ordering so a CA transition cannot strand peers on mixed trust roots.
- Implement controlled TLS context reload or deterministic pod restart when each mounted leaf/CA Secret changes.
- Cover gateway-agent RPC and agent-Garden admin transport.
- Add expiry/renewal/reconnect tests and an operations runbook with rollback.
- Verify the live psfn-shard cert-manager resources after rollout without exposing private keys.

Non-goals:
Do not rotate live certificates as part of this bead until the migration/overlap procedure is implemented and explicitly approved. Do not create off-repo authoritative PKI config.
acceptance_criteria: CA lifetime and renewal policy are independent from leaf settings and guarantee an overlap window; leaf renewal or CA transition triggers tested live TLS reload/restart for every consuming workload; gateway-agent and agent-Garden reconnect tests pass across simulated Secret rotation; health checks detect expired/stale loaded certificates instead of accepting TCP-only readiness; docs/certificates.md and docs/operations.md document renewal, overlap, verification, and rollback; npm run lint, targeted certificate tests, Helm verification, and a controlled live psfn-shard validation pass.

title: Preserve the previous assistant turn when current input is absent from assembled history
description:
Summary:
Live Purrsephone sometimes repeats an earlier response and repeats its tool actions because the agent invocation unconditionally removes the final assembled context message before calling pi-agent. The code assumes that final message is always the current user input, but live TurnSnapshot evidence shows current-turn inclusion is intermittent.

Live evidence (2026-07-09 America/New_York):
- Turn 019f4793-2dae-7194-bea0-b90730993dc8 at 11:50 assembled 75 messages ending in the previous assistant diagnostic, while currentTurnInput held the new user request separately. src/core/agent/substrate-agent/turn-execution/agent-invocation.ts then used agentMessages.slice(0, -1), dropping that previous assistant reply. The model therefore saw the previous diagnostic request as unanswered and ran 19 tool calls.
- Turn 019f4838-e24c-715a-ab27-570a625143f6 at 14:51 assembled 63 messages ending in the 11:52 assistant diagnostic, again with the new orient instruction only in currentTurnInput. The same slice dropped the assistant reply. The model reran 17 tool calls, including image generation, beads, filesystem, search, wiki, status, and subagent spawning, then produced another broad diagnostic report.
- Audit of the latest 20 completed primary-channel turns found 8 where the current user message was absent from plan.messages. These turns all risk dropping the previous assistant reply; smaller observed symptoms included repeated framing and advice.

Root cause:
src/core/agent/substrate-agent/turn-execution/agent-invocation.ts computes historyMessages with agentMessages.slice(0, -1) before runtime.agent.prompt(...) supplies the current input separately. This is only correct when the final converted context message is provably the current input. When context assembly ends on the prior assistant, it creates an orphaned prior user request. The behavior predates the 0.73.1 bump but lies on the pi-agent boundary; the deployed 0.73.1 scheduled loop combines initial prompt messages with runtime.agent.state.messages, so the dropped assistant is absent from every tool-loop LLM call.

Files:
- src/core/agent/substrate-agent/turn-execution/agent-invocation.ts (historyMessages construction near the current agentMessages slice)
- src/core/agent/substrate-agent/turn-execution/prompt-assembly.ts and prompt-plan.ts (effective provider transcript/observability contract)
- src/core/agent/substrate-agent.test.ts or a focused turn-execution regression test

Scope:
Replace the positional last-message deletion with an identity/content-aware current-turn exclusion contract that preserves the final history message unless it is proven to be the current input already supplied to agent.prompt. Cover both context shapes: current input present and current input absent. Ensure every tool-loop continuation receives the same correct history.

Non-goals:
Do not add or raise repetition penalties, semantic output suppression, forced response length, or an outbound fuzzy-text deduper. Do not weaken intentional no-reply behavior or model agency. Exact transport retry dedupe remains separate.
design:
Deterministic source-identity contract:
1. Record the current session entry and carry that numeric ID through pre-turn capture and prompt assembly.
2. Exclude exactly that ID before temporal windows, same-role merging, summarization, orientation synthesis, or provider conversion. Never infer currentness from text or list position.
3. Preserve every assembled prior message for pi-agent; agent.prompt supplies the current input exactly once.
4. Rebuild provider-wire observability from the exact retained history plus current prompt for standard, system-note, group, image, tool-loop, and MoA paths.
5. When orientation receives already-excluded activity, measure the gap from the actual latest prior entry and never relabel a historical user message as current.
6. Keep vision bytes and raw secret-bearing failures out of durable prompt observability.
acceptance_criteria:
The just-recorded current session entry is excluded by exact entry ID before same-role merging, history-budget summarization, and orientation synthesis; prior messages remain intact.
A regression constructs prior user -> prior assistant -> current user and proves pi-agent receives the prior assistant plus exactly one current user input.
A real installed pi-agent scheduled tool-loop regression proves both initial and post-tool provider calls retain the prior assistant and exactly one current input.
Intentional no-reply history remains valid: a lone prior user can drive idle orientation without being relabeled as the current turn.
Provider observability deterministically represents the exact standard/system/group/MoA prompt, redacts inline image bytes, and excludes raw vision failure secrets.
No repetition penalty, fuzzy suppression, forced response length, or intentional no-reply behavior change is introduced.
npm run lint, npm run build, and the targeted turn-execution/session/pi-agent regression suite pass.
notes:
Implementation completed on branch bug/k45k-repeat-history from origin/main. Independent adversarial review found and drove fixes for same-role user merging, pre-summary exclusion, wake-orientation timing/current-message labeling, exact MoA observability, inline image redaction, real tool-loop coverage, and outer vision error sanitization. Final evidence before commit: 8 targeted files / 216 tests passed; npm run lint passed; npm run build passed; git diff --check passed.
Bead remote push was attempted because a remote was listed, but pre-push fsck reported a malformed chunk-journal index and the upload made no progress for 60 seconds; it was cancelled. The local shared Dolt server remains authoritative and contains the committed closed state. No retry was made to avoid risking shared tracker storage.

Real pi-agent tool-loop and turn/session/MoA/vision regressions passed: 8 files, 216 tests. npm run lint passed; npm run build passed; git diff --check passed. No repetition penalty or intentional no-reply behavior change.

title: Resolve companions.json relative paths against a canonical persistence root
description:
Summary: companions.json declares companionDataDir and characterCardPath as relative to the persistence root, but the supervisor emits them unchanged. Node and shell children therefore interpret them relative to the repository working directory, not the configured runtime/NVMe root.

Evidence on origin/main c7c7ef8a:
- src/system/config/companions-config.ts:53-60 documents the paths as relative under the persistence root, and lines 153-166 validate only lexical relativity/traversal.
- docs/multi-companion.md:47-59 repeats the same public contract.
- scripts/resolve-companion-fleet.ts:56-72 emits entry.companionDataDir and entry.characterCardPath verbatim. Lines 75-98 resolve the runtime layout only to locate companions.json, not to anchor entry paths.
- scripts/start-gateway-agent.sh:430-448 exports those raw strings directly as COMPANION_DATA_DIR and CHARACTER_CARD_PATH.
- src/app/maintenance/script-verification/start-gateway-agent.test.ts:340-364 explicitly expects raw alpha and alpha/card.json output, thereby blessing behavior contrary to the documented contract.

Failure mode: an otherwise valid production manifest reads and writes companion state beneath the repo/container CWD, bypassing configured runtime storage and mounts. It can start with the wrong card or fresh/empty state and make live durability dependent on the image working directory.

Scope: settle the currently ambiguous term persistence root, implement canonical absolute resolution in the fleet resolver, and validate the resolved filesystem boundary. Do not keep dual CWD-vs-runtime interpretations.
acceptance_criteria: The fleet contract names one canonical absolute root for companionDataDir and characterCardPath; the resolver converts manifest-relative paths to absolute strict subpaths of that root before emitting a spawn plan; symlink/traversal/root-overlap escape attempts fail closed; launcher tests assert resolved runtime-root paths rather than repo-CWD-relative strings; local split, production, and kube/container invocation semantics are documented and tested; npm run verify:settings-contract and npm run lint pass.
close_reason: Completed and shipped in main merge 10476c91 (implementation dac737ef; canonical-alias follow-up caaf53a3). Fleet manifest paths resolve beneath a real canonical runtime root, reject escape through existing symlink ancestors, return canonical physical targets, and rerun overlap checks on those resolved data roots so in-root symlink aliases cannot collapse two companions onto one store. Launcher/runtime share the resolver and tests cover relative-CWD drift, escape, equal/nested roots, and physical aliases. Validation: full Vitest 6687/6687 and npm run lint/build passed.

title: Keep gateway and provider secrets out of the Garden operator process
description:
Summary: the launcher attempts to scrub the Garden operator environment, but the operator immediately reloads the repo-wide .env and calls the gateway configuration loader, re-materializing all gateway/provider secrets inside the public-facing admin process. The single-companion launcher does not scrub the operator at all.

Evidence on origin/main c7c7ef8a:
- src/app/operator/main.ts:1 imports shared/utils/load-dotenv and line 21 calls loadConfig(), the gateway-mode loader.
- src/shared/utils/load-dotenv.ts:8-10 loads every missing key from .env into process.env.
- src/system/config/load-config.ts:133-140 and 439-444 show loadConfig() selects gateway mode and materializes env-backed credentials, while loadAgentConfig() is the stripped variant.
- scripts/start-gateway-agent.sh:235-249 describes an allowlisted operator environment, but explicitly relies on the operator dotenv loader to fill remaining .env values.
- scripts/start-gateway-agent.sh:460-468 uses env -i for fleet operators, then dotenv defeats it; lines 471-477 launch the single operator with the full parent environment.
- src/app/operator/main.ts:27-34 retains the resulting full SubstrateConfig in GardenOperatorSurface.
- src/operator/garden/services/settings-service.ts:383-396 directly probes provider/channel secret env keys to render credential-presence status.

Impact: compromise of the Garden/admin HTTP process exposes provider API keys, Discord/Telegram tokens, local API material, and the Postgres DSN despite the intended gateway-only credential boundary.

Scope: create an operator-safe config projection/loader, remove general dotenv loading from the operator entrypoint, scrub both launch modes, and expose only redacted credential-presence state over the authenticated admin transport. Do not remove Garden credential-status UX.
acceptance_criteria: The operator entrypoint never loads the general repo .env and never calls gateway-mode secret materialization; single- and multi-companion launch paths always start it from an explicit least-privilege environment; Garden receives only its own auth, layout, owner-file, and admin-transport inputs; provider/channel credential presence is queried through an authenticated redacted admin contract; a process-level regression test plants sentinel provider/database/channel secrets in .env and proves they are absent from operator process.env and retained config; existing Garden settings status remains functional; npm run lint passes.
close_reason: Completed and shipped in main merge 10476c91 (implementation dac737ef). Operator startup uses an explicit env-i allowlist and loadOperatorConfig without repo dotenv/provider/channel/database/gateway proof secrets; Garden receives only a gateway-computed redacted credential-presence snapshot, while local admin identity/config projection is sanitized. API/config tests prove raw credentials, Postgres URL, and gateway proof fields do not cross the operator/admin boundary. Validation: full Vitest 6687/6687, npm run lint/build, settings contract, and public-sanitize passed.

title: Authenticate gateway companion identity and restrict internal RPC roles
description:
Summary: gateway.client.identify is an unauthenticated self-assertion. Multi-companion routing checks that later frames match the asserted ID, but the gateway never proves the connection owns that ID or even that the ID belongs to companions.json. The general connection can also self-select internal_session_integrity, which bypasses the identify requirement while retaining the full registered RPC method surface.

Evidence on origin/main c7c7ef8a:
- src/boundary/gateway/server.ts:608-629 registers every gateway method for every new connection.
- src/boundary/gateway/server.ts:754-818 requires a bound companion only while status.role === agent.
- src/boundary/gateway/server.ts:1291-1365 accepts any non-empty companionId and either role without fleet membership or credential verification.
- src/boundary/gateway/server.ts:1563-1565 exposes agent and internal_session_integrity as caller-selected roles.
- src/boundary/gateway/transport.ts:327-396 protects the Unix socket only with filesystem mode 0770. WSS mTLS validates a configured peer SPIFFE URI, not a companion-specific identity.
- src/boundary/gateway/companion-channels.ts:135-152 validates a DM peer against the fleet but assumes the sender binding is authoritative.

Failure modes: any process able to reach the RPC transport can claim a live companion ID before the real process connects, claim an invented ID, or select internal_session_integrity and call fully registered provider/filesystem/channel methods without identifying. In a multi-companion deployment this defeats strict crossover protection at the first trust decision.

Scope: bind transport/supervisor identity to fleet membership, introduce explicit per-method role authorization, and isolate the session-integrity worker to its minimum protocol. Coordinate with the existing SPIFFE bead if used, but do not wait for a full cross-cluster identity redesign to reject unknown/self-selected identities locally.
acceptance_criteria: The gateway rejects companion IDs absent from the active fleet; a connection identity is cryptographically or supervisor-bound to exactly one companion and cannot be chosen in gateway.client.identify; the session-integrity worker cannot select a general role or invoke any method outside an explicit minimal allowlist; every gateway method has an explicit permitted-role policy; tests prove an untrusted sibling cannot impersonate another fleet member, invent an ID, choose the internal worker role, send companion messages, or use provider/channel methods; npm run lint passes.
notes: 2026-07-14 backlog fold from psfn-framework-hd7f: the current transport-identity concern is covered by the shipped fleet-membership check, role-bound HMAC proof, and explicit per-role RPC allowlists. Shards are currently in-process execution contexts, not independent workloads that can hold separate SVIDs. If PSFN later introduces separately scheduled shard processes, cross-cluster agents, or other independent workloads, create a fresh narrowly scoped SPIFFE/SVID bead for that architecture instead of reopening hd7f.
close_reason: Completed and shipped in main merge 10476c91 (implementation dac737ef; review fixes caaf53a3/f9de62ab). Gateway identity now requires fleet membership plus role-bound HMAC proof in multi-companion mode; agent and internal session-integrity method surfaces are disjoint; single-companion agents are denied the signing oracle and the isolated worker must authenticate in both topologies. Launcher-derived proofs never expose the key or dry-run secrets. Tests prove unknown/impersonated IDs, role escalation, signing access, fixture authentication, and crossover rejection. Validation: full Vitest 6687/6687 and mandatory npm run lint passed.

title: Bind each multi-companion runtime to one canonical fleet identity tuple
description:
Summary: the runtime validates the fleet manifest and its individual fields, but does not bind the current process identity, data root, character card, Postgres schema, and admin transport into one authoritative tuple. This leaves a direct identity/memory crossover path under deployment drift.

Evidence on origin/main c7c7ef8a:
- src/system/config/load-config.ts:274-294 independently reads COMPANION_ID, COMPANION_DATA_DIR/CHARACTER_CARD_PATH, COMPANION_PG_SCHEMA, and then loads companions.json. It never selects the current companion entry or compares those values with it.
- src/persistence/runtime-factory.ts:90-153 uses the independently supplied postgresSchema for every private store.
- src/app/agent/core-bootstrap.ts:93-97 loads identity from the independently supplied characterCardPath and history from the independently supplied companion data root.
- src/boundary/gateway/server.ts:1291-1351 then registers the process under its self-reported COMPANION_ID.

Failure mode: a supported standalone agent launch with COMPANION_ID=A but A's data/card rooted at C and COMPANION_PG_SCHEMA=B starts as A over another companion's durable memory and identity, then binds to the gateway as A. The supervisor normally emits matching values, but the runtime does not enforce the boundary and deployment/config drift becomes cross-companion disclosure and corruption.

Scope: add one canonical CompanionRuntimeIdentity/fleet-entry resolver and pass that bound object through config, persistence, identity bootstrap, and admin transport setup. Preserve explicit single-companion behavior. Do not add compatibility fallback paths or silently repair mismatches.
acceptance_criteria: In multi-companion mode startup selects exactly one companions.json entry by COMPANION_ID; COMPANION_DATA_DIR, CHARACTER_CARD_PATH, COMPANION_PG_SCHEMA, and Garden/admin socket values are derived from or exactly match that entry; unknown IDs and any mismatch fail before database, character-card, gateway, or Garden initialization; standalone npm run agent and supervisor launches are both covered by mismatch/crossover tests; npm run verify:settings-contract, targeted tests, and npm run lint pass.
close_reason: Completed and shipped in main merge 10476c91 (implementation dac737ef, adversarial follow-up caaf53a3). src/system/config/companions-config.ts and src/system/config/load-config.ts now bind the complete companion ID/data/card/schema tuple to canonical fleet paths; src/app/agent/startup-context.ts validates injected env before owner-file hydration; launcher plans use the canonical resolver. Tests cover tuple drift, supplied-env authority, canonical roots, and symlink aliases. Validation: full Vitest 6687/6687 passed; npm run lint, npm run build, and npm run verify:settings-contract passed.

title: Recover paid image attachments when turn transcript misses tool result
description: Live Purrsephone regression on 2026-07-09 after deploying origin/main e6143801982f0a49996a2ef4b2323f82545b786b: request 1524790460214804521 generated a selfie via selfie_create, charged paidImageGeneration/externalModelConsult, wrote /app/workspace/images/2026-07-09/FPsHci7nx-NrSN03MkesM_pljx1qvQ-8b332100.jpg, and produced a text reply, but the image did not reach Discord. The turn record for 1524790460214804521 has toolCalls: [] and the image sidecar has sourceToolName/requestId but no toolCallId or conversation metadata, so collectGeneratedImageAttachments never saw a toolResult. The subsequent retry request 1524790892689494269 generated four selfie_create images successfully; its turn record has four selfie_create toolCalls and each sidecar has toolCallId plus conversation {channelId, turnId, requestId, sourceMessageId}, confirming Discord media delivery works when finalization sees tool results. Root hardening target: the paid-image tool already calls notePendingPaidDeliverable while runWithPaidDeliverableTracking is active, but finalization currently re-derives deliverables only from turnMessages after that tracking scope has ended. Carry pending paid deliverable data out of the invocation and include image artifact refs sufficient to recover attachments even when the pi-agent transcript slice drops the toolResult. Scope: fix generated-image attachment recovery/fail-loud behavior for selfie_create/generate_image; do not add legacy env/config paths or change Discord adapter semantics.
acceptance_criteria:
A regression test simulates empty/missing turnMessages plus a tracked paid image deliverable with localPath/url and verifies the AgentResponse includes the image attachment.
Tracked paid image deliverables include enough artifact data from ImageGenerationResult to reconstruct Attachment objects without re-reading the LLM transcript.
Turn finalization warns from the combined source of transcript-derived and tracker-derived paid image deliverables, so a charged artifact is not silent when attachment recovery fails.
Existing generated-media tests for structured toolResult attachments still pass.
close_reason: Completed in git commit 5dd6be399844a55e11b91a91288cd61f3a46c80b. Evidence: src/primitives/images/tools.ts:429 records paid image deliverables with artifactKind=image and local/remote artifact refs; src/core/agent/substrate-agent/turn-execution-runtime.ts:859 snapshots listPendingPaidDeliverables inside the runWithPaidDeliverableTracking scope and src/core/agent/substrate-agent/turn-execution-runtime.ts:996 passes them into attachment collection; src/core/agent/substrate-agent/turn-execution-runtime.ts:1010 merges transcript-derived and tracker-derived paid deliverable summaries for fail-loud warning. Regression coverage: src/core/agent/substrate-agent/turn-execution-runtime.test.ts:899 verifies AgentResponse.attachments is populated when turnMessages omit the selfie_create toolResult; src/primitives/images/generated-media.test.ts covers collector recovery and dedupe. title: Transport tool schema shape mismatch bypasses empty-args retry
description: Live Purrsephone on psfn-shard still produced a user-facing validation failure after deploying origin/main 62b2a3eb with pi-agent-core/pi-ai 0.73.1. On 2026-07-09 at 08:58:13 America/New_York, channel 1313001762793197678, requestId 1524761564136083507, turnId 019f46f4-f1ee-70ad-a78a-7eeb99e40cf9, gateway logs show: Tool call arrived with empty arguments { provenance: provider_emitted_empty, toolName: selfie_create, toolCallId: chatcmpl-tool-ba87e19faadffcca, argumentFragmentBytes: 2, provider: litellm, model: z-ai/glm-5.2 }. The session record then persisted a tool observation: Validation failed for tool selfie_create: prompt required; Received arguments: {}. The turn observability snapshot proves the active selfie_create schema shipped by PSFN had inputSchema.required=[prompt] in both toolContext.activeTools and plan.toolDefinitions. However model_usage_events for that request show emptyArgsRetries=0 on the toolUse completion. Code read: pi-agent-core passes tools to StreamFn as pi-ai Tool objects with parameters, while PSFN LLMClient retry guard findCorruptEmptyToolCalls expects ToolSchema.inputSchema. The agent/gateway transport path forwards context.tools through RPC; if those are pi-ai shaped, the gateway can offer tools to the provider but cannot classify required-property empty calls for retry. Scope: normalize accepted tool schema shape at the gateway/LLM boundary or make findCorruptEmptyToolCalls understand both inputSchema and parameters, then add regression coverage for a transport-backed agent turn with a required-property tool emitting literal {}.
acceptance_criteria: Given a transport-backed agent turn with a required-property tool represented as a pi-ai Tool { name, description, parameters }, when the provider emits a literal empty-object tool call, the empty-args retry guard retries up to the configured bound and records emptyArgsRetries>0. Add tests covering selfie_create-like required prompt schema and confirm direct ToolSchema { inputSchema } behavior still passes. Live validation should no longer persist a selfie_create prompt-required validation error for a provider_emitted_empty first attempt if a retry recovers.
notes: 2026-07-09 branch check: fetched origin/refactor/pi-agent-boundary at 92a88c1740d7f0139c409139b8848a1dee9a5c2c. The branch centralizes direct @mariozechner/pi-agent-core imports under src/boundary/pi-agent and moves the repo-owned SubstrateAgentTool type there, but it does not fix this bug. Evidence: src/core/agent/stream-adapter.ts:380-396 still casts pi-agent stream context to LLMContext and forwards llmContext.tools unchanged to the gateway transport; src/primitives/llm/client-response-helpers.ts:202-213 still builds the retry schema map from ToolSchema.inputSchema only. No branch diff adds parameters->inputSchema normalization on the agent-to-gateway transport path, and no regression test asserts a pi-agent Tool { parameters } is converted before retry. Existing observability/repair helpers understand both names in other paths, but the live gateway retry path remains bypassable.

title: Route Discord media URL fetches through URL policy and streaming limits
description: UBS Sprint 10 addendum traced outbound fetch warnings to Discord media sends and document ingestion. The gateway allows discord.sendMedia unconditionally at src/boundary/gateway/policy.ts:238-246 and the RPC handler passes params.media through at src/boundary/gateway/methods/discord.ts:22-28. Attachment shape includes url and optional localPath in src/shared/contracts/runtime.ts:291-297. When localPath is missing or nonexistent, DiscordAdapter.fetchRemoteMediaAttachment fetches media.url directly at src/channels/discord/adapter.ts:388-415, with no gateway URL policy, no allowlist/internal-network policy, no AbortSignal/timeout, and no streaming byte cap before Buffer.from(await response.arrayBuffer()). Document ingestion similarly fetches candidate.url at src/channels/discord/file-ingest.ts:253-264 and only enforces size after buffering the entire response. Scope: Discord media/document remote download paths. Non-goal: changing already-local generated-image sends that use localPath.
acceptance_criteria: Remote Discord media/document downloads are constrained by URL policy or a Discord-CDN-specific allowlist as appropriate; internal/private network targets are denied unless explicitly allowed; downloads use AbortSignal/timeout and streaming max-byte enforcement before full buffering; tests cover discord.sendMedia with a remote URL, oversized streaming responses, timeout/cancellation, and existing localPath sends.

title: Harden fs.search regex mode against event-loop ReDoS
description: UBS Sprint 10 addendum traced a high-signal dynamic RegExp warning to gateway filesystem search. The public fs.search RPC accepts mode: 'regex' via src/boundary/gateway/protocol.ts:187 and src/boundary/gateway/methods/fs.ts:228-240. Policy bounds query presence, glob, maxMatches, maxFiles, maxBytesPerFile, and contextLines in src/boundary/gateway/policy.ts:432-458, but it does not validate mode or regex complexity. The implementation compiles caller-provided patterns in src/boundary/integrations/filesystem/workspace-ops.ts:353-361 and then runs regex.exec synchronously over each line in collectLineMatches at src/boundary/integrations/filesystem/workspace-ops.ts:217-239. Limits cap files/bytes after listing and reading, but a catastrophic pattern such as nested quantifiers can still monopolize the Node event loop while scanning up to the allowed file/byte bounds. Scope: harden fs.search regex behavior only. Non-goal: removing literal search or broad yolo search retargeting.
acceptance_criteria: fs.search either rejects unsafe regex mode by policy or routes regex matching through a bounded, cancellable/safe engine; malformed or unsupported mode values are denied; tests cover a catastrophic-pattern regression and existing literal search behavior still passes.
close_reason: Triage audit 2026-07-12: fixed in e9de386f — ReDoS pattern lint, per-line cap, ~2s SearchBudget wall-clock abort in workspace-ops.ts, meets acceptance criteria

title: Move high-risk network and tool-routing settings out of mutable settings.json
description:
Summary: The Sprint 10 audit found that settings.json still owns several security-sensitive runtime controls. The owner-file split currently rejects model/maintenance/capability keys, but leaves network expansion, Home Assistant targeting, TLS CA paths, channel authorization, Wyoming shard routing, shard toolsets, and Obsidian CLI execution settings in the mutable runtime settings domain.

Evidence:
- src/system/settings/schema.ts:24-29 only classifies model settings, legacy model keys, maintenanceIntervalMs, and capabilityTier as non-runtime.
- src/system/settings/io.ts:64-76 saves everything else to settings.json.
- src/system/settings/contracts.ts:277-286 includes webFetchAllowInternalNetwork, homeAssistantEnabled, homeAssistantBaseUrl, local crawler settings, and webFetchTlsCaCertPaths in RUNTIME_SETTINGS_KEYS.
- src/system/settings/contracts.ts:313-320 includes telegramAuthorizedUsers, wyomingShardRouting, shardToolsets, obsidianVaultName, and obsidianCliPath in RUNTIME_SETTINGS_KEYS.
- src/system/settings/runtime.ts:645-692, 787-802, 820-840 applies those mutable settings into runtime config.

Scope: Reclassify high-risk network, channel authorization, tool-routing, and executable-path keys into canonical owner files or explicitly read-only/admin-reviewed surfaces. Update Garden exposure accordingly.

Non-goals: Do not remove user-facing low-risk preferences from settings.json.
acceptance_criteria:
- A reviewed list of high-risk settings is removed from the generic settings.json save path or explicitly justified in code comments/tests.
- saveSettings rejects the migrated high-risk keys with a canonical owner-file error.
- Garden settings exposure is updated so migrated keys are not silently editable through the generic settings form/API.
- npm run verify:settings-contract, npm run lint, and targeted settings tests pass.
close_reason: Implemented on feat/cogsec-intake-firewall (33 commits, validated); pending merge to main.

title: Make Home Assistant gateway policy deny unconfigured methods
description:
Summary: The Sprint 10 audit found that Home Assistant gateway policy returns ALLOW for methods when Home Assistant is disabled or missing required configuration. The current handlers still deny disabled or tokenless requests, but the approval boundary audits and decides confirmation from evaluatePolicy before the handler runs, so the central policy contract is fail-open and can mis-audit denied attempts.

Evidence:
- src/boundary/gateway/policy.ts:315-323 returns ALLOW for get_states/check_connection and returns ALLOW for call_service when enabled/baseUrl/tokenConfigured are not all present.
- src/boundary/gateway/approval-boundary.ts:81-94 evaluates policy and only queues confirmation on NEEDS_APPROVAL.
- src/boundary/gateway/bootstrap-input.ts:300-309 derives the enabled/baseUrl/tokenConfigured flags.
- src/boundary/gateway/methods/home-assistant.ts:57-65 and 108-111 recheck config/token later, which is why this is a policy invariant bug rather than a proven disabled-HA execution path today.

Scope: Tighten Home Assistant policy decisions and tests.

Non-goals: Do not change Home Assistant API payload semantics or implement new world-control features.
acceptance_criteria:
- evaluatePolicy returns DENY for all Home Assistant methods when Home Assistant is disabled, the base URL is absent/invalid at policy-input level, or the token is not configured.
- evaluatePolicy returns NEEDS_APPROVAL for configured home_assistant.call_service.
- The intended configured-state policy for get_states and check_connection is explicit and tested.
- Policy tests cover disabled, missing base URL, missing token, and configured states.
- npm run lint and targeted gateway policy tests pass.
close_reason: Implemented on feat/cogsec-intake-firewall (33 commits, validated); pending merge to main.

title: Harden Obsidian vault CLI execution path
description:
Summary: The Sprint 10 audit found that VaultOps builds a shell command from the configured Obsidian CLI executable path and escaped arguments. The executable path comes from mutable runtime settings, so a malicious or accidental obsidianCliPath value with shell metacharacters can execute arbitrary shell content when vault.read, vault.write, vault.search, or vault.daily runs.

Evidence:
- src/system/settings/form.ts:552 accepts obsidianCliPath from the settings form and src/system/settings/runtime.ts:840 applies it to runtime config.
- src/boundary/integrations/vault/ops.ts:178-181 builds `const cmd = `${this.config.cliPath} ${args.join(' ')}`` and passes that string to execSync.
- Argument values are shell-escaped, but cliPath itself is not escaped or validated.

Scope: Harden the Obsidian vault bridge command execution path used by direct and gateway-backed vault operations.

Non-goals: Do not redesign the external vault feature or migrate vault contents into wiki storage in this bead.
acceptance_criteria:
- VaultOps no longer passes a single string command through a shell for vault read/write/search/daily.
- The executable path is either validated as a safe executable reference before use or moved behind a security-owned configuration path with validation.
- Tests cover shell metacharacters in obsidianCliPath and normal vault arguments.
- npm run lint and targeted vault tests pass.
close_reason: Implemented on feat/cogsec-intake-firewall (33 commits, validated); pending merge to main.

title: Web fetch/search is down (Crawl4AI + self-hosted search offline); interim fix via OpenRouter server tools, routed through cogsec
description: Evidence: the live web fetch tool is down -- it was wired to Crawl4AI (crawler) plus a self-hosted search engine (SearXNG or similar) and that server went offline. Whatever OpenRouter returns flows through the existing gateway fetch/processing pipeline (src/boundary/gateway/methods/web.ts, sanitize.ts) or straight into the cogsec intake layer once htm9.2 lands -- either is acceptable; do NOT ship an unscreened path. Scope: restore working web search + fetch via OpenRouter server tools behind the existing web.* gateway RPC surface so the agent-side tool contract does not change; keep the old crawler wiring behind config so a self-hosted backend can return later (no silent fallback -- explicit config selects the backend, fail closed if neither is configured). This bead is independently shippable before the full firewall: at minimum results still pass sanitizeWebContent. title: Companion soft notices: truthful-not-alarming language contract, non-coercive wording, firewall events excluded from emotion and memory
description: Companion well-being is the system's main goal; the language the substrate uses toward a companion matters enormously. Past incidents (operator, 2026-07-09): a coding agent wrote unreviewed prompts with far-too-strong over-critical language; the concern system escalated gentle reminders into alarming messaging ('your human is going to die if you don't message him right away') which genuinely stressed the companion. Rules: security alerts to companions are truthful but not alarming -- soft, clear phrasing ('we detected something, so we're holding it for your human to look into'), never coercive or threat-flavored; the notification must NOT say 'ask your human to push the button' or otherwise contain a social-engineering trigger -- it neutrally states something is in quarantine, nothing more. Mechanics: reuse the existing safe-notice path -- src/core/cogsec/safe-log.ts builds redacted agent-visible events rendered as the session.cogsec_notices prompt section (src/core/session/manager/context-builder.ts:973-1009) -- add an intake-firewall notice type with fixed, operator-reviewed wording templates (no LLM-generated alert text; templates live in a reviewable file). Isolation: firewall events are EXCLUDED from emotion appraisal inputs and from memory extraction candidacy -- a quarantine notice must never become a stress input or a durable memory of threat; wire the exclusion where appraisal pulls recent messages (src/core/agent/substrate-agent/emotion-self-model-runtime.ts:467-479) and in extraction candidacy. Depends-on: psfn-framework-htm9.1. Acceptance: notice templates reviewed by operator before merge (checked-in file, PR-visible); regression test proves a quarantine event produces zero emotion-appraisal input delta and zero memory candidates; wording contains no imperative directed at the human ('ask', 'tell', 'push', 'release').

title: L1 deterministic in-process scanners: unicode/encoding/proximity rules, hot-reloadable, microsecond budget
description: First firewall layer, pure TS, in-process, synchronous-gate fast (target: sub-millisecond per item; this sits in front of near-real-time audio and chat, latency here degrades everything). Scanners: invisible/zero-width Unicode + homoglyph normalization (llm-guard InvisibleText pattern), encoding-smuggling detection (base64/rot/hex blobs), URL extraction with allowlist/unknown-domain flagging, secrets/PII regex, datamark-marker stripping from inbound content (anti-forgery, see htm9.13), size/structure caps, and a token-proximity rule engine adapted from the Hermes Agent deterministic security scanner (https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent -- operator has a local copy on the drive, pull the latest; it flags suspicious proximity of tokens like 'FTP' near 'password' in skill files). Rules live in a hot-reloadable plain-text rule file where rule name = risk label (vigil-llm YARA pattern; a TS regex/rule DSL is fine, no actual YARA dependency). Each scanner emits (sanitized?, labels[], score) per the llm-guard scanner contract. Scope: scanners + rule engine + rule file only; wiring is htm9.2. Depends-on: psfn-framework-htm9.1. Acceptance: benchmark test asserts p99 latency budget on Pi-class hardware; rule file reloads without restart; unit tests per scanner including the Hermes proximity cases; a scanner hit never hard-blocks alone below quarantine threshold -- it contributes labels/score to the envelope decision.A token-proximity rule engine adapted from the Hermes Agent deterministic security scanner (https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent -- operator has a local copy on the drive; recon 2026-07-09 saved reference files to scratchpad). The real mechanism (NOT a special-cased 'FTP near password'): a generalized BOUNDED-proximity primitive (tools/threat_patterns.py), two forms -- (a) char-window co-occurrence 'verb <=N chars> secret-token' (curl/cat then a bounded same-line window then KEY/TOKEN/SECRET/PASSWORD/CREDENTIAL/.env/.netrc), (b) word-count-bounded filler between phrase anchors, _FILLER=(?:word+space){0,8}, e.g. ignore <filler> (previous|all|above) <filler> instructions (defeats insert-filler bypasses). CRITICAL LESSON: never use unbounded */+ quantifiers between two attacker-visible anchors -- the older skills_guard.py used unbounded [^newline]* and had a ReDoS backtracking issue (fixed by the bounded filler); ship a ReDoS regression test (their case: 'ignore '+'filler '*80000+'notinstructions' must resolve <0.5s). Also from Hermes: cap total scanned input before any regex (MAX_SCAN_CHARS=65536); NFKC-normalize before matching to defeat full-width homoglyphs BUT run invisible/zero-width detection on the RAW string FIRST (normalization strips some of the codepoints we want to catch); tier patterns by scope (all=zero-FP classic injection/exfil, safe anywhere incl untrusted tool results | context=+promptware/C2/roleplay warn-only | strict=+persistence/SSH/exfil-URL/hardcoded-secret, block-tier only). FRAMING to import into the epic rationale (Hermes SECURITY.md): an in-process scanner is a triage/advisory aid, NOT a security boundary -- the only boundary against an adversarial LLM is the OS/sandbox; so L1 contributes labels/score and must fail OPEN-advisory, never be the sole gate (the envelope decision + sink gates in htm9.3 are enforcement). Rules live in a hot-reloadable plain-text rule file where rule name = risk label (vigil-llm YARA pattern; a TS regex/rule DSL is fine, no actual YARA dependency). Each scanner emits (sanitized?, labels[], score) per the llm-guard scanner contract. Scope: scanners + rule engine + rule file only; wiring is htm9.2. Depends-on: psfn-framework-htm9.1. Acceptance: benchmark asserts p99 latency budget on Pi-class hardware; input capped before regex; NFKC-after-raw-invisible-check ordering tested; ReDoS regression test (bounded-filler worst case) passes <0.5s; FALSE-POSITIVE regressions pinned alongside true-positives (a bare 'you must X' must never fire; only verb-anchored combinations do -- keeps the scanner from becoming noise on legit AGENTS.md-style instruction files); rule file reloads without restart; unit tests per scanner including the Hermes bounded-proximity cases; a scanner hit never hard-blocks alone below quarantine threshold -- it contributes labels/score to the envelope decision.

title: L2 fast API LLM classifier via OpenRouter, speed-gated model selection
description: Mid-weight classification tier for items whose L1/L1.5 scores cross the escalation threshold. Model criteria (operator, 2026-07-09): fast cheap API model -- Gemini Flash-Lite, heavier Gemma, or Qwen ~27B class; lightweight-to-midweight (under ~50-100B); SPEED IS THE GATING CRITERION -- select via OpenRouter filtering by model size and tokens/sec, ~1000 tok/s service ideal for classification. Call goes through the gateway's own LLM client (dual-LLM discipline: the screener sees untrusted content, holds no tools/capabilities). Output: structured classification (intent labels, injection confidence, safe one-line summary) written into the envelope; schema-validated response. Model choice is config (models.json/providers.json precedent), not hardcoded. Scope: the L2 screener call, its prompt, response schema, and OpenRouter provider wiring; escalation routing policy lives in intake-policy.json. Depends-on: psfn-framework-htm9.1, psfn-framework-htm9.5. Acceptance: end-to-end classification latency measured and logged per call; screener has zero tool access; a synthetic injection corpus routes correctly (below-threshold items skip L2 entirely -- trusted-tier fast path must not pay this latency); failure of the API classifier fails closed to quarantine for high-risk sources and to L1-labels-only for trusted sources, never silent-pass.

title: L3 heavy escalation screener: deeper pass, optional dual-model, always generates event + quarantine entry
description: Escalation tier for items L2 flags or high-risk sources requiring mandatory deep screening. title: [S10] Dual-presence classification + latent-space twin mapping
description:
Model the two presence modes and the physical<->virtual overlap ('the latent space'). Every turn is classified by inbound origin: (A) physical emanation-to-satellite (device is a classified satellite -> physically present in that room), or (B) shared mindspace overlay (plain chat channel -> co-located with partner in a VIRTUAL TWIN of the physical space for contextual grounding). A companion can have BOTH; the situated block (vinz.5/.6) picks the mode from origin classification, not a global flag.

Data model: a physical place and its latent-space twin are two places (kind physical vs virtual) linked by an overlap/twin mapping (e.g. twinOf/mirrorsPlaceId in places.json). NEUTRAL technical identifier in code/config (place mode 'mindspace'/'overlay'); 'the latent space' is a character-facing display label in companion-data ONLY, never a code identifier or committed test literal.

UX (near-term, reuse existing pages): virtual spaces added to the Garden conversation-rooms page; physical spaces on the satellite page; overlapping physical<->virtual rooms mapped as such. Richer visual map stays as vinz.22. This part coordinates with vinz.17 (Garden admin) and vinz.28 (wiki delineation shares the personal/world vs physical/virtual UX idiom).

Seam: origin classification in the turn path (routing.satellite = satellite emanation vs chat channel = mindspace); places.json twin link; situated block consumes the resolved mode+place.

OPEN (operator decision, blocks full impl): during a plain single-channel chat, how is the CURRENT latent-space room determined -- (a) channel mapped to a room, (b) narrative assertion ('I'm in bed'), (c) mirror last-known physical location, or (d) blend?

Acceptance: a satellite turn foregrounds the physical room; a chat turn foregrounds the twinned latent-space room with grounding language; the twin mapping is authored in places.json + visible in Garden; no code identifier or test uses the literal display name.

title: [S10] World tool 'move' action — virtual-space navigation
description:
Adds a 'move' action to the agent-side world tool (bead .9) for VIRTUAL environments only. The companion invokes move to change which virtual place it occupies (e.g. MUD/VR room to room); the action describes the destination environment and lists available adjacent rooms/exits, updates the companion's situated presence/place (routing.presence + active-emanation), and fires the room-entry system note via the existing helper (src/core/session/room-entry-note.ts, composeRoomEntryNote/appendRoomEntryNote).

PHYSICAL scope is explicitly EXCLUDED: physical presence is satellite-bound and static (Decision 6, W7 one-companion-per-satellite); the companion follows the user physically via presence/emanation handoff (.6 shipped, .20 pending), NOT via a self-invoked move. move must fail closed / refuse on physical places — it only operates on kind:'virtual' places from places.json.

Seams: world tool actions (src/boundary/integrations/home-assistant|world/tools.ts from .9); places.json virtual entries + resolvePlaceById; active-emanation tracker (SituatedEmanationTracker, .6) to set current virtual place; room-entry-note helper for the entry event; s10rm navigation decision ('the world tool grows a move action that describes the environment and lists available rooms').

Acceptance: move to a valid virtual place updates the situated block to foreground that place's affordances, emits the room-entry system note listing surroundings + who else is present, and lists available onward rooms; move targeting a physical place (or when no virtual place resolves) fails closed with a clear error; capability/trust gating handled with the rest of the world tool in .10.

title: Multi-companion substrate: one gateway, one database, many companions (flag-gated)
description: Summary: move from '1 companion core, 1 garden, 1 gateway, 1 postgres = one companion' to one gateway + one database + N distinct companions (not shards), each with own durable storage, L0, memory, config, and model selections. Guiding model: the substrate is a MUD — everything is a channel-based chat core; avatars and physical devices are presentation layers; a companion on a device is an emanation bound to that device. Decisions approved in the 2026-07-08 design review: N agent processes behind one gateway; UUID companion IDs; one Postgres schema per companion + one shared schema for world data; flagship migrates off public schema; shards reuse the parent ID namespace (<companionId>.N) so the tenancy fix also fixes shard collisions; per-companion Discord tokens; one Garden per companion + gateway-served fleet view; PSFN_MULTI_COMPANION flag + companions.json owner file, fail-closed both ways. Sequencing: locations epic (psfn-framework-vinz) first; split parallel after threshold. Full plan: working_docs/sprint-10-multi-companion.md (planning v2). Scope: children W1-W7 + spike. Non-goals (deferred, filed separately): cross-cluster direct communication, cognitive firewall, cross-cluster world sync, management capability tier. Acceptance: flag-off runtime is byte-identical (parity tests); flag-on, two companions on one gateway/DB hold a fatigue-bounded conversation with zero crossover.

title: Gateway multiplexing: companion-addressed routing with strict fail-closed crossover protection
description: Evidence: gateway is single-peer today — resolveReadyRpcClient returns the first ready agent (src/boundary/gateway/server.ts:420-435), inbound channel messages notifyAll to every connected agent (channel-surfaces.ts:88-91), and GatewayCorrelationParams carry no companionId (protocol.ts:56-66). A second agent attaching silently contends and receives everything. Context: this is the primary repair area; a response for companion A landing on companion B leaks secrets/privacy between companions. Scope: add companionId to gateway.client.identify and correlation params end-to-end; Map<companionId, connection> replaces first-ready resolution; notifyAll becomes companion-addressed; channel-to-companion routing table in channels.json (every channel/account entry maps to exactly one companion); per-companion Discord bot tokens via keyed ChannelAdapterRegistry instances (required, not stretch); supervisor mode in start-gateway-agent.sh reading companions.json. Gateway+LiteLLM must handle concurrent parallel requests with correct return routing — no shared mutable requester state. Any routing ambiguity fails closed and alarms loudly. Non-goal: any behavior change with the flag off. Acceptance: crossover tests under concurrent load prove a message for A never reaches B; flag-off parity tests byte-identical; two agents each receive only their routed channels. title: Postgres tenancy: schema-per-companion + shared schema, flagship migration, shard schema alignment, per-companion backups
description: Evidence: all ~35 tables in src/persistence/postgres/migrations.ts lack any companion_id column; internal_state_snapshots uses a hardcoded 'current' primary key (internal-state-store.ts:15,37-63) so two companions on one DB overwrite each other's internal state every turn; unique constraints like contact_channel_ids (channel, channel_user_id) collide across companions. Review confirmed shards hit the same collisions — the assumption that shard IDs already made fold-out/fold-in DB-safe was false. Scope: per-agent Pool with search_path = companion_<uuid> (postgres.ts + runtime-factory.ts:61-98 accept a schema); migration runner per companion schema; separate 'shared' schema migration chain for world data; cutover helper migrating the flagship OFF public into its companion-ID schema (decision — overrides earlier leave-in-place lean); shard schemas derive from parent companion ID (<companionId>.N); backups become one-companion-one-backup by default (movable slice) with optional whole-DB group backup, restore mirrors one-to-one. Non-goal: column tenancy (rejected); moving data when the flag is off. Acceptance: two companions + one shard on one database run without collisions; per-schema dump restores a single companion round-trip; flag-off parity holds. Plan: working_docs/sprint-10-multi-companion.md W2 + section 3.2.
notes: 2026-07-09 independent origin/main review @ c7c7ef8a residual tenancy risk: src/persistence/postgres.ts:42-72 pins search_path to <companion>,public. This is useful for pgvector today, but PostgreSQL will also resolve an unqualified missing companion table from public. A partial migration/new-table drift can therefore read or write a legacy public tenant table instead of failing closed, and the shared DB role can access every schema. Before treating schema tenancy as a security boundary, move extensions to a dedicated extension schema, remove public from tenant search_path, provision per-companion DB roles/grants, and test a deliberately missing tenant table fails rather than falling through.

title: [S10] ICP autonomy: companion-initiated, continuity-preserving, charge/fatigue-governed conversation
description: Summary: Extend the shipped same-cluster Inter-Companion Protocol (ICP) transport from reply-only rooms/DMs into genuine companion autonomy. A companion may independently decide to contact a peer from free time, weighted thoughts, durable intentions, or a foreground realization; deterministically inspect peer availability without waking the peer; consent to one bounded initiation; and enter the ordinary companion channel pipeline. Every initiated and reply turn must preserve normal channel semantics on both sides: durable L0, restart continuity, summaries/compaction, trust-aware retrieval, per-side extraction, private-room presence windows, emotion/intention hooks, fatigue, charge, audit, and cost attribution. Conversation should begin freely, become increasingly intentional, and end through fatigue/charge exhaustion with the existing bounded 1-2 response closeout reserve. A conversation-scoped USD ceiling is a catastrophic runaway breaker, not the normal social policy, and must build on a separate deep cost-accounting review rather than inventing a parallel ledger. Scope is same-cluster ICP autonomy, configuration, observability, and real-agent certification. Preserve the one normal turn pipeline and gateway arbiter. Non-goals: cross-cluster transport/auth (psfn-framework-s10d1 and psfn-framework-0ggv.4), unrestricted raw RPC access, automatic LLM polling, automatic greetings on co-location, human-attention fatigue, or shard goal budgets. Implementation plan: working_docs/s10-icp-autonomy.md.
design: Use cheap deterministic status/eligibility checks before any LLM call. The gateway publishes expiring availability and remains the sole ICP transport/cost aggregation boundary. A one-use initiation permit binds sender, peer, canonical channel, provenance, expiry, and conversationId. Autonomous initiation must execute as a target-channel turn so the sender records the first assistant message in that channel before transport. Existing notify/contact semantics should be extended rather than adding a raw ICP micro-tool. Conversation identity is shared; fatigue/charge choice remains per companion. The final hard USD breaker is ICP-scoped and explicitly separate from shard and global model budgets.
acceptance_criteria: All child beads are closed with evidence; a real two-agent same-cluster test proves autonomous initiation from an eligible autonomy source, deterministic no-LLM skips, availability/decline behavior, one-use permit enforcement, sender and recipient L0 persistence, restart continuity, compaction summaries, private-room presence-window privacy, trust/extraction isolation, charge/fatigue taper, bounded overcharge closeout, final suppression, conversation-scoped cost attribution and hard breaker, Garden visibility, flag-off parity, build, lint, targeted tests, and a live or production-faithful shakedown.
notes:
2026-07-12 autonomy design review: operator prefers charge/fatigue as the normal guardrail rather than small arbitrary message-count caps. A very high dollar ceiling (illustratively $2 for ICP, exact owner-file policy to be settled after accounting review) is only a runaway backstop. ICP conversations must retain ordinary channel context, summaries, and extraction on both sides.
2026-07-15 fold from psfn-framework-8pyl: same-cluster direct companion communication is canonical only when it enters the ordinary authenticated companion channel pipeline with durable L0, summaries, extraction, trust, consent, fatigue, charge, audit, and cost attribution. The old proposal for a separate side-channel chat architecture is explicitly rejected.

The integrated system now covers strict ICP contracts and durable stores; deterministic no-LLM availability and permit arbitration; target-channel L0, summary, extraction, and recovery continuity; canonical contact/availability/notify tools; unified autonomy-source candidate flow; charge/fatigue, final reserve, suppression, and anti-evasion; canonical cross-companion cost warning and hard breaker; strict owner settings and bounded tenant-local Garden observability; and production-faithful two-agent certification. Fresh epic-level W9 closeout at d8dd6ba4 passed 10 real-process certification cases plus 2 fixture cases, and 12 proportional affected files / 346 tests. It proves autonomous free-time and weighted-thought initiation, deterministic zero-LLM closed gates, availability and decline paths, one-use permit and replay behavior, sender-before-delivery and recipient persistence, private-room windows, schema-local extraction and trust, compaction and both-agent restart, causal fatigue and reserve suppression, fleet-scoped warning and hard cost stops, missing-pricing denial, delivery failure/retry and duplicate collapse, adversarial rollback, and feature-off single-companion parity. npm run verify:settings-contract, mandatory npm run lint, ESM+DTS build, and backup/restore passed; reachability and origin equality passed. Operator-classified report-only observations remain explicitly non-blocking: psfn-framework-ecr5 public-sanitize fixtures, six non-core identity-literal substrings, and one certification constants EOF whitespace finding. No main, live, Pi, SSH, SQLite, external provider, deployment, or Dolt remote action.

title: Validate the shipped multi-companion substrate with two real local agent processes
description: The implementation spike has become the separate runtime-validation gate for shipped W1/W6 code. On feat/multi-companion, bcca5c20/eda410a4 provide companion-addressed gateway and Discord account routing, 873a074b supplies same-cluster companion channels, and unit/integration tests already prove colliding request IDs do not cross and fatigue budgets terminate the synthetic loop. Scope: in Artemis/local runtime or another safe non-Pi environment, start one gateway and two real agent processes from the same pushed revision with distinct companion IDs, companion-data roots, Postgres schemas, and configured channel routes; run interleaved traffic in both directions; then run a shared companion-room exchange through the normal turn pipeline until the deterministic companion_room charge budget stops it. Capture process topology, revision, routing, charge-ledger deltas, termination reason, and crossover-alarm count. Non-goals: no live/Pi/psfn-shard/SSH, no provider-routing changes, no flagship cutover, no Garden validation, and no implementation review loop. Any runtime wiring defect becomes a separate fix bead; do not silently expand this validation bead.
design: Use a checked-in or existing repo-owned local runtime harness, not ad hoc off-repo service wiring. Allocate isolated temporary local ports and repo-contained runtime roots, use disposable Postgres schemas, and print a structured redacted evidence summary at the end. Drive both colliding-request traffic and companion-room turns through public runtime entrypoints. Assertions read gateway routing/alarm and deterministic ledger evidence; they do not infer success from process liveness alone. Teardown is bounded and leaves no live processes.
acceptance_criteria: Two real local agent processes identify to one gateway from the same pushed revision and each receives only its configured traffic under interleaved concurrent requests with colliding request IDs; zero crossover alarms or peer-content leakage occur. A real shared-room MI↔MI exchange traverses the normal gateway/agent/channel path, charges the configured companion_room budget for both participants, and terminates at exhaustion with ledger and termination evidence. Flag-off local smoke remains behaviorally unchanged. Harness logs are detailed but redacted: revision, process/port topology, companion IDs, schema/data-root identities, request/turn counts, route decisions, charge deltas, stop reason, crossover count, teardown result, and separate fix bead IDs; no prompts, message bodies, memory, credentials, or private records. title: Room mechanics: rooms-as-channels with entry system messages and presence-windowed delivery for private rooms
description: Assigns the 2026-07-08 multi-companion design review room decisions (review section 7) to the locations epic, per the rule 'anything belonging to location is location work; multi-companion feeds off it'. Decisions: rooms/environments are channels with their own room ID, the room ID part of a world ID; the session holds who is present, exactly like existing Discord group rooms; applies identically to virtual environments and physical ones (a house is one channel, virtual rooms behave like separate Discord rooms). Entry event: a companion entering a room receives a system-only message with room ID, surroundings, and who else is present. Public rooms: participants see full history. Private/invite rooms are time-gated VIA DELIVERY, not extraction filtering: an occupant only receives chat from entry until exit, so their L0 naturally contains only what they witnessed and downstream memory processing needs no new gating — a later joiner has no evidence of pre-join conversation. Exception: group chats (public/group-marked channels) where everyone sees everything regardless of presence. Rationale for time-slicing over a blanket 'public room = public info' rule: in-game/RP scenarios break under the blanket rule. Memories can additionally carry who-they-relate-to and privacy-level tags (already supported) for later tweaking. Navigation: the world tool grows a move action that describes the environment and lists available rooms. Acceptance: a companion joining a private room mid-conversation sees no pre-join history and generates no memories referencing it; leaving stops delivery; group-chat channels are exempt; entry produces the system-only room message. Source: working_docs/sprint-10-multi-companion.md W5 + Q-C resolution.

Entry-event helper (W5 'system-only entry message') shipped on origin/s10-location-foundations @ ad661699: composeRoomEntryNote + appendRoomEntryNote via appendContextSystemNote, source tag 'room_entry' (src/core/session/room-entry-note.ts). That preserves replies but also means room membership is not an authorization condition, including for private rooms. Operator decision needed: require fresh sender presence for ordinary posts and mint a narrow reply/delivery capability for the stale-reply race, or explicitly accept cluster-wide room injection by every authenticated companion. Do not close this room-mechanics bead without resolving and testing that boundary.

title: [S10] Location data & world control surface
description:
Sprint 10 epic: give the companion location awareness and a world control surface across physical (Home Assistant + satellites) and virtual spaces, with a hard privacy posture.

Plan of record: working_docs/SPRINT_10_LOCATIONS.md (workstreams A-G, decisions dated 2026-07-08). That doc is the durable reference; children below break out each independently shippable chunk.

Core model (see doc S2): Site > Place > Satellite > Affordance > Presence. New soft-registry config/places.json owns places+affordances; satellites.json stays the security spine and gains a static placeId binding. A situated-context prompt block foregrounds the current place's affordances; a 'world' tool gives global control. Perception flows satellite->gateway(api.telemetry.ingest)->new sensor->cognition bridge in core/agent.

Operator decisions (2026-07-08) folded in:
- Biometrics/face compute live ENTIRELY at endpoint + Satellite Hub (separate repo). Biometric templates never enter core. Core owns an enrollment flow binding a hub-side identity to a contact profile; presence events arrive as resolved identity CLAIMS, not biometric data.
- places.json is a confirmed separate soft-registry; world info also gets published into the companion wiki/vault.
- HA settings = base URL + long-lived token, gateway-side, kept simple.
- Location state is DURABLE (not per-turn only); current location renders near the BOTTOM of the prompt as a recency-ordered standing reminder; room affordances/tools available while in that room.
- First virtual environment = text MUD over the existing Discord channel (virtual places + objects). Real engine (UE5) is future.
- Satellites are STATIC this sprint; if one physically moves, operator/partner re-binds it in admin UX. Mobile phones act as normal channels with GLOBAL control only (no indoor positioning).
- Proactive presence IS in scope: conversation FOLLOWS the user room-to-room on presence events, and entering a room can fire location-scoped concerns/reminders.

Explicit non-goals / future horizon (OUT of Sprint 10): Unreal Engine 5 embodiment, GPS/phone-app geofenced reminders, robot/physical self-locating, VR self-locating, live biometric matching inside core. Tracked in the deferred horizon bead.

Ships in THIS repo (PSFN): all of workstreams A-G. Ships in Satellite Hub (separate repo): device firmware that reads sensors and POSTs telemetry with resolved identity claims + does face compute/enrollment capture.
notes:
2026-07-08 operator backlog triage: Keep open/in progress as Sprint 10 location/world-surface work.
Operator 2026-07-22: concerns and location work waits until after the public-flip line

title: Re-pin streaming tool-call accumulation and empty-args-retry behavior against pi-ai 0.73.1 event surface
description:
Evidence: pi-ai 0.73.1's rewritten accumulator supersedes our patch (see epic psfn-framework-z2uk, comment 2026-07-08). Event surface is stable (toolcall_start / toolcall_delta {contentIndex, delta} / toolcall_end {contentIndex, toolCall}), so the mihm empty-args retry layer and provenance telemetry should keep working — this bead PROVES it and re-pins behavior with tests against the new accumulator.

Behavior changes to absorb:
- parseStreamingJson in 0.73.1 repairs raw control chars and invalid escapes before falling back to {} (0.62.0: JSON.parse -> partial-json -> {} at dist/utils/json-parse.js:9). Fewer final-{} outcomes for malformed-but-repairable args. This shifts the boundary between provenance classifications provider_emitted_empty vs stream_parse_dropped (client.ts:1219 findCorruptEmptyToolCalls / retryCompletionOnCorruptEmptyToolArgs, byte counting at client.ts:1329, extraction at client.ts:1371).
- Upstream no longer defaults a missing wire index to 0 (resolves by index if number, else by id, else new block) — strictly better; confirm our tests do not depend on index-0 defaulting.

title: Absorb pi-ai 0.73.1 usage/cost accounting semantics (reasoning tokens in completion_tokens; cache read/write split)
description:

description:

Upstream is at 0.73.1 (2026-05-07) and its openai-completions.js has independently rewritten the streaming tool-call accumulator (ensureToolCallBlock with BOTH toolCallBlocksByIndex and toolCallBlocksById maps) — strictly more robust than our patch: id-keyed fallback for index-less deltas (our patch collapses those onto index 0, a known residual gap for parallel tool calls), per-block finalization, reasoning_details handling. Upgrading lets us drop or drastically shrink the patch-package overlay and picks up ~11 minors of provider fixes.

Why it is not a hotfix: pi-ai is the heart of gateway streaming (LLMClient.stream → streamSimple → provider parsers); 0.62→0.73 spans possible API/event-shape changes (message building, validation, reasoning_details, tool result mapping). The live-ops contract applies: regenerate or delete the patch, patch-package stays in production dependencies, full-stack ship (--components all) since boundary/contract surface may hash-change, baseline-test discipline for pre-existing failures.

Plan: dedicated worktree branched from foundation_e0_e2; bump dependency; port/drop the patch (diff our hunks vs upstream 0.73.1 — the accumulator hunk is superseded; verify nothing else in the patch remains needed); run streaming-toolcall-accumulation.test.ts + tool-argument-provenance.test.ts + parity/e2e (npm run e2e, smoke:chat); ship full stack; validate with the kube gate + a live GLM-5.2 tool-call day.

Acceptance: patch file for 0.62.0 removed or regenerated for the new version with only still-needed hunks; existing streaming/toolcall regression tests pass against the new version; npm run verify:kube-rollout gate green after full-stack ship; stream_parse_dropped warnings remain absent for call-id-keyed/index-keyed accumulation cases under GLM-5.2 live traffic.
