comments.author: axAilotl
comments.text:
**Verdict**

Drop `patches/@mariozechner+pi-ai+0.62.0.patch` entirely when bumping `@mariozechner/pi-ai` to `0.73.1`. Do not regenerate it for 0.73.1.

Upstream 0.73.1 supersedes the PSFN patch and is stronger: PSFN keyed streamed tool-call accumulation by wire `index`; upstream now keys by both stream `index` and tool-call `id`, keeps tool-call blocks independent from text/thinking blocks, and finalizes tool calls after the stream drains.

No repo source changes were made. I did not run tests.

**Patch Disposition**

| Patch hunk | Local evidence | 0.73.1 disposition |
|---|---:|---|
| Add `toolCallBlocksByIndex` map | [patch:9](/home/ada/psfn-framework/patches/@mariozechner+pi-ai+0.62.0.patch:9) | Obsolete. Upstream has `toolCallBlocksByIndex` and `toolCallBlocksById`; see upstream `openai-completions.ts` around `L168-L171` and `L225-L263`. |
| Stop finalizing tool calls via `currentBlock` | [patch:23](/home/ada/psfn-framework/patches/@mariozechner+pi-ai+0.62.0.patch:23) | Obsolete. Upstream removed the single `currentBlock` model for tool calls and uses separate text/thinking/tool state. |
| Add `finalizeToolCallBlocks()` | [patch:30](/home/ada/psfn-framework/patches/@mariozechner+pi-ai+0.62.0.patch:30) | Obsolete. Upstream `finishBlock()` handles tool calls, parses `partialArgs`, deletes scratch fields, and emits `toolcall_end`. |
| Route `choice.delta.tool_calls` by wire `index` | [patch:52](/home/ada/psfn-framework/patches/@mariozechner+pi-ai+0.62.0.patch:52) | Obsolete/superseded. Upstream `ensureToolCallBlock()` first resolves by stream index, then by id, then creates a new block. |
| Emit `toolcall_delta` with correct block index | [patch:105](/home/ada/psfn-framework/patches/@mariozechner+pi-ai+0.62.0.patch:105) | Obsolete. Upstream emits `contentIndex: getContentIndex(block)` for start/delta/end. |
| Finalize tool calls after stream loop | [patch:117](/home/ada/psfn-framework/patches/@mariozechner+pi-ai+0.62.0.patch:117) | Obsolete. Upstream finalizes every block after the streaming loop. |

One nuance: PSFN defaulted a missing wire index to `0`. Upstream only indexes when `typeof toolCall.index === "number"`, then falls back to id. That is better for compliant OpenAI-compatible streams and avoids accidental index-0 conflation.

**Usage Surface**

Runtime imports from `@mariozechner/pi-ai`:

- `streamSimple`, `completeSimple`: [client.ts:3](/home/ada/psfn-framework/src/primitives/llm/client.ts:3), [vision-reviewer.ts:4](/home/ada/psfn-framework/src/primitives/images/vision-reviewer.ts:4), [streaming-toolcall-accumulation.test.ts:3](/home/ada/psfn-framework/src/primitives/llm/streaming-toolcall-accumulation.test.ts:3). Signatures remain compatible in 0.73.1.
- `getModels`, `getProviders`: [models.ts:5](/home/ada/psfn-framework/src/primitives/llm/models.ts:5). Signatures remain compatible.
- `getEnvApiKey`: [credential-vault.ts:1](/home/ada/psfn-framework/src/boundary/custody/credential-vault.ts:1). Existing providers still work; 0.73.1 adds more env-key cases.
- `validateToolArguments`: [tool-call-scheduler.ts:1](/home/ada/psfn-framework/src/core/agent/tool-call-scheduler.ts:1), [stream-adapter.test.ts:7](/home/ada/psfn-framework/src/core/agent/stream-adapter.test.ts:7). Export remains, but implementation changed from AJV to TypeBox.
- `EventStream`: [scheduled-agent-loop.ts:1](/home/ada/psfn-framework/src/core/agent/scheduled-agent-loop.ts:1). Event stream surface remains compatible.
- Types: `Context`, `Model`, `SimpleStreamOptions`, `ThinkingLevel`, `Message`, `Tool`, `TextContent`, `ThinkingContent`, `ImageContent`, `ToolCall`, `ToolResultMessage`, `UserMessage`, `AssistantMessage`, `AssistantMessageEvent`, `StopReason`, `Api`, `KnownProvider`. Optional fields were added, not removed, except known provider/API union membership changed.

**Breaking / Behavior Changes**

- Install/package graph: current repo pins `@mariozechner/pi-ai` and `@mariozechner/pi-agent-core` to `0.62.0` at [package.json:78](/home/ada/psfn-framework/package.json:78) and [package.json:79](/home/ada/psfn-framework/package.json:79). Local `pi-agent-core@0.62.0` depends on `@mariozechner/pi-ai:^0.62.0` at [node_modules package.json:19](/home/ada/psfn-framework/node_modules/@mariozechner/pi-agent-core/package.json:19). If only top-level pi-ai is bumped, npm can install a nested 0.62.x copy for pi-agent-core unless the lock/overrides prevent it.
- Direct TypeBox dependency risk: local pi-ai 0.62.0 depends on `@sinclair/typebox`, `ajv`, and `ajv-formats` at [node_modules package.json:79](/home/ada/psfn-framework/node_modules/@mariozechner/pi-ai/package.json:79). Upstream 0.73.1 uses `typebox` instead and no longer carries `@sinclair/typebox`. This repo imports `@sinclair/typebox` directly in many `src/` files but does not list it in `package.json`. Minimal fix: add direct exact `@sinclair/typebox` dependency, rather than migrating every source import during this bead.
- Validation implementation changed: 0.62.0 uses AJV with `coerceTypes: true` and formats errors as `Validation failed for tool "..."` at [validation.js:57](/home/ada/psfn-framework/node_modules/@mariozechner/pi-ai/dist/utils/validation.js:57). 0.73.1 uses `typebox/compile` and `Value.Convert`, but preserves the same prefix in `validateToolArguments`. Our prefix matcher at [runtime-diagnostics.ts:197](/home/ada/psfn-framework/src/shared/diagnostics/runtime-diagnostics.ts:197) should still work. Error detail wording/path may change.
- Tool-call event surface is stable: 0.73.1 still emits `toolcall_start`, `toolcall_delta { contentIndex, delta }`, and `toolcall_end { contentIndex, toolCall }`. This keeps the new retry/provenance code valid: raw delta byte counting at [client.ts:1329](/home/ada/psfn-framework/src/primitives/llm/client.ts:1329), final tool call extraction at [client.ts:1371](/home/ada/psfn-framework/src/primitives/llm/client.ts:1371), and corrupt-empty retry at [client.ts:1219](/home/ada/psfn-framework/src/primitives/llm/client.ts:1219).
- JSON streaming parse is more forgiving: 0.62.0 tries `JSON.parse`, then `partial-json`, then `{}` at [json-parse.js:9](/home/ada/psfn-framework/node_modules/@mariozechner/pi-ai/dist/utils/json-parse.js:9). 0.73.1 adds repair for raw control chars and invalid escapes before falling back. Expect fewer final `{}` outputs for malformed-but-repairable arguments.
- Usage accounting changed: 0.62.0 added `completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens` to output; 0.73.1 treats `completion_tokens` as already including reasoning tokens and splits cache read/write more carefully. This can silently change `inputTokens`, `outputTokens`, `cacheRead`, `cacheWrite`, and cost/ledger entries consumed at [client.ts:1406](/home/ada/psfn-framework/src/primitives/llm/client.ts:1406).
- Message building mostly remains compatible: upstream still serializes tool calls as `function.arguments = JSON.stringify(tc.arguments)` and still carries `reasoning_details` from `thoughtSignature`. It adds DeepSeek `reasoning_content`, better thinking text handling, unsupported-image placeholder downgrades, and end-of-conversation synthetic tool results.
- `KnownApi` / `KnownProvider` changed. Local 0.62.0 includes `google-gemini-cli` and `google-antigravity` at [types.d.ts:3](/home/ada/psfn-framework/node_modules/@mariozechner/pi-ai/dist/types.d.ts:3). 0.73.1 drops those and adds providers including `deepseek`, `moonshotai`, `fireworks`, `cloudflare-*`, and `xiaomi-*`. If runtime config names `google-gemini-cli`, it will stop resolving.
- `OpenAICompletionsCompat.reasoningEffortMap` existed in 0.62.0 at [types.d.ts:228](/home/ada/psfn-framework/node_modules/@mariozechner/pi-ai/dist/types.d.ts:228). 0.73.1 removes it and uses `thinkingLevelMap`/new thinking helpers. I found no repo import/use of `reasoningEffortMap`.
- `streamSimple` / `completeSimple` signatures remain compatible. 0.73.1 adds optional `onResponse`, `timeoutMs`, and `maxRetries` to options; PSFN does not pass them today.
- Abort semantics remain conceptually compatible: PSFN passes `signal` through [client.ts:270-317](/home/ada/psfn-framework/src/primitives/llm/client.ts:270); 0.73.1 forwards it into OpenAI request options and still reports aborted/error stream termination.

**Our-Code Touch List**

Required package/patch changes for the upgrade:

- [package.json:79](/home/ada/psfn-framework/package.json:79): bump `@mariozechner/pi-ai` to `0.73.1`.
- [package.json:78](/home/ada/psfn-framework/package.json:78): decide whether to keep `@mariozechner/pi-agent-core@0.62.0` or bump it too. For this bead, prefer pi-ai-only unless you also adapt the private agent patch.

Likely no required `src/` change for pi-ai-only, but these are the sensitive lines:

- [client.ts:1219](/home/ada/psfn-framework/src/primitives/llm/client.ts:1219), [client.ts:1329](/home/ada/psfn-framework/src/primitives/llm/client.ts:1329), [client.ts:1363](/home/ada/psfn-framework/src/primitives/llm/client.ts:1363), [client.ts:1371](/home/ada/psfn-framework/src/primitives/llm/client.ts:1371), [client.ts:2046](/home/ada/psfn-framework/src/primitives/llm/client.ts:2046): keep as-is; 0.73.1 still supplies raw `toolcall_delta.delta` and final `toolCall.arguments`.
- [tool-call-scheduler.ts:309](/home/ada/psfn-framework/src/core/agent/tool-call-scheduler.ts:309) and [runtime-diagnostics.ts:197](/home/ada/psfn-framework/src/shared/diagnostics/runtime-diagnostics.ts:197): prefix still matches, but detail wording changes should be reviewed.

- [models.ts:111](/home/ada/psfn-framework/src/primitives/llm/models.ts:111): local developer-role detection is now stale for moonshot/cloudflare if those providers are configured.
- [message-conversion.ts:175](/home/ada/psfn-framework/src/primitives/llm/message-conversion.ts:175): optional `responseModel` and `diagnostics` from 0.73.1 are currently dropped by normalization. Not a compile break; possible observability loss.

- [agent-loop-patch.ts:16](/home/ada/psfn-framework/src/core/agent/agent-loop-patch.ts:16): only relevant if also bumping `@mariozechner/pi-agent-core`. This file reaches private fields like `_sessionId`, `_transport`, `_maxRetryDelayMs`, `_state.streamMessage`, and `_state.error`; 0.73.1 core changed agent internals, so a core bump is a separate migration.

**Test Impact**

- [streaming-toolcall-accumulation.test.ts:92](/home/ada/psfn-framework/src/primitives/llm/streaming-toolcall-accumulation.test.ts:92): should still pass and becomes the key proof that upstream replaced the patch.

- [client.test.ts:687](/home/ada/psfn-framework/src/primitives/llm/client.test.ts:687): should compile/pass; it mocks pi-ai root exports whose names remain stable.
- [stream-adapter.test.ts:405](/home/ada/psfn-framework/src/core/agent/stream-adapter.test.ts:405): likely passes because it asserts only the stable validation prefix.
- `tool-call-scheduler` validation tests may need expectation updates if they assert exact AJV detail strings, not just the prefix.

**Risk Ranking**

High, loud:

- Old patch file left in `patches/` after installing 0.73.1.
- Missing direct `@sinclair/typebox` dependency after pi-ai stops bringing it transitively.
- Duplicate pi-ai copies because `pi-agent-core@0.62.0` depends on `@mariozechner/pi-ai:^0.62.0`.
- Bumping `pi-agent-core` without adapting [agent-loop-patch.ts](/home/ada/psfn-framework/src/core/agent/agent-loop-patch.ts:16).

High, silent:

- Validation coercion/error detail differences from AJV to TypeBox.
- Usage/cost accounting changes, especially reasoning tokens and prompt cache read/write split.
- Prompt cache behavior: 0.73.1 has more OpenRouter/Anthropic cache-control logic, while PSFN also has its own payload transformer.
- `parseStreamingJson` repair can change whether bad streamed args end as `{}` or valid partial objects.

Medium:

- Provider/API registry changes, especially removal of `google-gemini-cli`.
- Unsupported images become placeholder text instead of being filtered in some paths.
- `responseModel`/`diagnostics` may be produced but not preserved by PSFN normalization.

Low:

- `streamSimple`/`completeSimple` signatures.
- Tool-call event shape.
- Stop reason values and mapping.
- Abort signal pass-through.

**Recommended Upgrade Sequence**

1. Upgrade only `@mariozechner/pi-ai` first; leave `@mariozechner/pi-agent-core` at `0.62.0` unless you explicitly scope the private-agent patch migration.
2. Delete `patches/@mariozechner+pi-ai+0.62.0.patch`.
3. Add direct exact `@sinclair/typebox` dependency, or migrate every repo import to `typebox`. Minimal path is direct dependency.
4. Regenerate lockfile and verify a single intended pi-ai version:
   ```bash
   npm ls @mariozechner/pi-ai @sinclair/typebox typebox
   ```
5. If npm installs nested `@mariozechner/pi-ai@0.62.x` under `pi-agent-core`, either force/override to 0.73.1 and test, or explicitly accept that core internals still use old pi-ai. Do not leave this ambiguous.
6. Run:
   ```bash
   npm run lint
   npm run build
   npm test -- --run src/primitives/llm/streaming-toolcall-accumulation.test.ts src/primitives/llm/tool-argument-provenance.test.ts src/primitives/llm/client.test.ts src/core/agent/stream-adapter.test.ts src/core/agent/tool-call-scheduler.test.ts src/primitives/llm/conversion.test.ts src/primitives/llm/message-conversion.test.ts src/primitives/llm/models.test.ts src/primitives/images/vision-reviewer.test.ts
   ```
7. Also run prompt-cache tests if the lockfile diff shows changed OpenAI/OpenRouter payload behavior:
   ```bash
   npm test -- --run src/primitives/llm/prompt-cache.test.ts
   ```

**Live Validation Watchpoints**

- Streaming GLM/OpenRouter tool calls: no orphan blank-name tool blocks, no final `{}` when `argumentFragmentBytes > 2`.
- Empty-args retry logs: `provider_emitted_empty` for zero bytes or literal `{}`, `stream_parse_dropped` only if fragments arrived and final args are still empty.
- `toolcall_start` / `toolcall_delta` / `toolcall_end` ordering and callback args.
- Validation diagnostics still recorded through `Validation failed for tool "..."`.
- Usage ledger changes for `input`, `output`, `cacheRead`, `cacheWrite`.
- OpenRouter/LiteLLM payload acceptance for tool result messages: `tool_call_id`, optional `name`, assistant-after-tool-result behavior.
- Prompt-cache 400s or provider rejections from duplicate/unsupported `cache_control` behavior.

title: Companion cannot schedule anything at an absolute datetime that survives a restart — one-shot tasks are in-memory and schedule_prompt is relative-only
description:
Evidence (repo survey 2026-07-07): scheduler core supports one-shot tasks with absolute runAt (types.ts ScheduledTask type:'one-shot'), but tasks live in an in-memory Map (scheduler.ts) with NO task store and NO rehydration at startup — a one-shot dies on restart. The companion-facing schedule tool action schedule_prompt (schedule-tool.ts:855-915) accepts only delay_minutes in [1,10080] (relative, max 7 days), computes runAt = now+delay, unpersisted. temporal-wakeup.ts is two fixed lanes (morning wake + idle refresher), no datetime targeting. The only persistent absolute-datetime paths are intention pending-follow-ups (dueAt, pending-follow-ups.ts:19,44) and care reminders (one_time|annual, care-reminders.ts:15,32) — but those surface via heartbeat GATING (activate when due AND a heartbeat/wake fires), not precise fire-at-datetime execution. No monthly or specific-date recurrence kind exists anywhere.

Context: operator requirement — calendar-grade capability: recurring "every Monday 6am"/"every Sunday 9pm" (weekly cadence lands via psfn-framework-cquq) AND one-shot "Tuesday July 14 at 2pm do this specific thing." The agent process restarts on every ship (2x by design) and reboots are frequent — this was the design motivation for persistence elsewhere (follow-ups/care reminders persist for exactly this reason); precise scheduling never got the same treatment.

Scope: (1) durable scheduled-task store (system-data; Postgres or JSONL per persistence conventions) + rehydration at scheduler startup for one-shot prompt tasks; handlers must be reconstructable (persist a task kind + payload, e.g. schedule_prompt's prompt text — not closures). (2) Extend schedule_prompt with absolute datetime input (ISO or natural local datetime + timezone), drop/raise the 7-day cap for absolute scheduling, fire precisely on the scheduler tick. (3) Consider monthly/dayOfMonth recurring cadence kind while the cadence union is open (cquq adds weekly) — optional, split out if it bloats. Non-goals: no cron-expression syntax; do not rework follow-up/care-reminder gating semantics.

Related: psfn-framework-cquq (weekly wall-clock cadence — same restart-amnesia root cause, in flight). Missed-while-down policy must be explicit: fire-on-next-tick-if-past-due vs skip; recommend fire-if-past-due with a staleness note in the injected prompt, and log the decision.

Acceptance: schedule a one-shot prompt for an absolute datetime, restart the agent process, task fires at (or immediately after) the target time with the original prompt; unit tests cover rehydration, past-due-on-boot policy, and timezone handling; conformance/tool docs updated for the new schedule_prompt parameters.
close_reason: Closed

title: GLM-5.2 tool calls intermittently arrive with literal {} arguments from vLLM-family OpenRouter upstreams; runtime dispatches them instead of retrying
description:
Evidence (2026-07-08 UTC, live psfn-shard): gateway logs show WARN [LLMClient] Tool call arrived with empty arguments {"provenance":"stream_parse_dropped","toolName":"journal","toolCallId":"chatcmpl-tool-9af9df5b23809fff","argumentFragmentBytes":4,...} at 01:26:41, plus 4 more (fragmentBytes 2 per call) at 01:26:47, 01:26:56, 01:27:58 UTC, requestIds 1524225125375807528 / 1524225448924549162, channel 1313001762793197678, model z-ai/glm-5.2 via litellm. Session store shows the downstream failure: Validation failed for tool "journal": action: must have required property 'action'. Received arguments: {} — and journal marked degraded after 2 attempts. The SAME tool worked at 00:50:17 UTC in the same session (toolCallId call_adbbffe8..., journal list returned 7 notes).

Root cause: NOT client-side. The gu8m pi-ai index-routing patch is verified present in the running gateway image bd11b80c (grep toolCallBlocksByIndex in /app/node_modules/@mariozechner/pi-ai/dist/providers/openai-completions.js = 4 hits). argumentFragmentBytes is a response-level total; 2 bytes for a 1-call response means the upstream streamed exactly '{}' as the complete arguments — the provider-side GLM tool parser failed to extract args (known vLLM/GLM-template failure mode, correlates with chatcmpl-tool-* call ids). OpenRouter fans z-ai/glm-5.2 across ~20 live upstreams (probe from the litellm pod, 2026-07-08: Z.AI/DeepInfra/Wafer/AkashML/SiliconFlow/AtlasCloud/IoNet/Together emitted call_*-style ids, Inceptron/DigitalOcean/WandB/Fireworks/Venice/Novita emitted chatcmpl-tool-*, Decart bare uuid; SiliconFlow also emitted bare 019f* ids in an earlier probe, matching the 2026-07-06 conformance-run failure ids). All passed a short-context probe, so the corruption is context/reasoning-dependent and per-upstream — a routing lottery.

Companion-observed split (memory/orient/journal/scratchpad/toolset/notify/media broken vs beads/session/contact/schedule/repo/fs/identity/system/self_status working) is fully explained by schema strictness, not per-tool corruption: at deployed commit 9480fd5e the 7 broken tools mark action required (journal src/boundary/integrations/journal/tools.ts:64, memory src/faculties/memory/tools.ts:1361, scratchpad src/faculties/memory/tools.ts:1893, orient src/faculties/core-memory/tools.ts:205, toolset src/core/agent/substrate-agent/adaptive-tools-runtime.ts:671, notify src/core/tools/ntfy.ts:637, media src/primitives/images/tools.ts:711) while the 13 working tools wrap action in Type.Optional and default to list/inspect (e.g. session src/core/tools/session.ts:429, beads src/faculties/beads/tools.ts:133). On a bad completion EVERY tool receives {}; optional-action tools silently run their default action — itself a silent-fallback smell worth a separate look.

Scope: make the runtime fail closed on this condition instead of dispatching known-corrupt calls. When a completion contains a tool call whose args are empty AND the tool schema has required properties, retry the completion (bounded, e.g. 2 attempts) before surfacing an error; count these in the existing provenance telemetry. Optionally pin/deny-list OpenRouter upstreams for glm-5.2 in the litellm chart config (provider order / allow_fallbacks via extra_body) — Z.AI first-party is the reference endpoint. Also fix the provenance classifier nit: args that arrived as literal '{}' (fragmentBytes == emitted {} bytes) should classify as provider_emitted_empty, not stream_parse_dropped — the current label sent this investigation hunting an already-fixed client bug.

Non-goals: do NOT make action optional on the 7 strict tools to absorb {} — silently running a default action on a corrupted mutating call is the exact anti-fail-closed behavior this repo forbids; the strict schemas are what made this bug visible. Do not bump/replace pi-ai.

Related: psfn-framework-gu8m (closed — client-side accumulation fix + diagnostics, both verified live and working; this bead is the residual provider-side leg gu8m's 2026-07-06 comment anticipated).
acceptance_criteria: Unit test proves a streamed completion whose tool call carries literal {} args against a required-props schema triggers a bounded completion retry and never dispatches to the tool; provenance warn distinguishes provider_emitted_empty vs stream_parse_dropped for the literal-{} case; live validation: journal/memory action calls on glm-5.2 survive a chatcmpl-tool-* upstream day with zero 'must have required property action' entries in the session store.
close_reason: Core implementation completed and shipped on this branch: merge 7243616b (implementation a186538c) is an ancestor of HEAD. src/primitives/llm/empty-tool-argument-retry.ts defines MAX_EMPTY_TOOL_ARGS_COMPLETION_RETRIES=2, retries literal-empty calls only when the tool schema has required properties, and returns the final corrupt response for downstream fail-closed validation rather than dispatching it. src/primitives/llm/client-response-helpers.ts classifies literal '{}' as provider_emitted_empty, with recovery/exhaustion/optional-schema coverage in src/primitives/llm/client.test.ts and provenance coverage in client-response-helpers.test.ts. Implementation is no longer held open as a proxy for runtime validation. The important remaining safe-runtime verification is separately tracked as psfn-framework-h7g9.1 under the wave fix epic; broader malformed/unknown-call reprompt work remains psfn-framework-b0yl.3.

comments.author: axAilotl
comments.text:
Web research (Opus fan-out, 2026-07-07) confirms provider-side GLM tool-parser fragility is a documented, recurring phenomenon — vLLM/SGLang GLM tool parsers break specifically at the streaming + reasoning-parser boundary, matching our failure conditions (17k ctx, thinking enabled). Key citations: vllm-project/vllm#31437 (GLM47 parser: streaming tool call loses id/type/name in finish chunk), vllm#32213 + #31379 (glm4_moe_tool_parser TypeError on empty-arg path), sgl-project/sglang#15721 (glm47 detector crashes on partial/duplicated <tool_call> XML), HF zai-org/GLM-5.1-FP8 discussion #1 (vLLM-specific intermittent tool failures, SGLang clean), charmbracelet/crush#3153 (GLM-only arg corruption on Fireworks). chatcmpl-tool-* is vLLM's default tool-call id format — independently confirms failing upstreams are vLLM hosts. fp4/int4 quant is an amplifier, not the proximate cause (Fireworks/ArtificialAnalysis put GLM-5.2 fp4-vs-fp8 tool-calling within noise; but RooCode#11325 shows low-bit GLM output corruption on Venice/DeepInfra/Mancer).

Mitigation surfaces (OpenRouter): (1) ':exacto' model-slug suffix = quality-first provider ordering driven by OpenRouter's own per-provider Tool Call Error Rate (JSON Schema draft-7 validation of every returned tool call; empty/invalid args count as errors). Auto Exacto supposedly applies automatically when 'tools' is present — our failing requests DID carry tools, so either LiteLLM's proxying defeats it, an explicit sort/account default overrides it, or exacto ranking still admits flaky hosts; verify. (2) Hard pinning via provider object: {"only":[...], "ignore":[...], "order":[...], "allow_fallbacks":false, "require_parameters":true, "quantizations":["fp8","fp16","bf16"]}. Recommended: z-ai/glm-5.2:exacto as quick fix, or deterministic pin of eval-clean hosts + quant filter, via litellm extra_body in chart values.

Eval harness: Codex is building scripts/ops/openrouter-toolcall-eval.mjs (task-mrbf6vex-58niz3) — per-provider streaming trials, classification incl. EMPTY_ARGS, long-context + reasoning modes, worst-first table + pinning snippet. No existing community per-provider tool-call fidelity harness found (BFCL is per-model, not per-provider); OpenRouter's Auto Exacto methodology (draft-7 validation per call) is the spec to clone. Note: OpenRouter 'server tools' feature (openrouter:-prefixed server-executed tools) is unrelated to this bug.

comments.author: axAilotl
comments.text:
Eval harness built (scripts/ops/openrouter-toolcall-eval.mjs, Codex + orchestrator hardening: tool_choice defaults to auto to match production — forcing tool_choice made OpenRouter filter out 14 of 26 hosts as unsupported, which would have silently skipped the very hosts serving live traffic; --no-pin mode added for :exacto/auto-routing evals; strict:true removed from the eval tool schema for production fidelity). Left uncommitted per build instruction.

Results 2026-07-08 (~100 long-context [~16k tok] reasoning-on trials, production OpenRouter key):
- z-ai/glm-5.2:exacto --no-pin x10: 10/10 OK, all served by Fireworks (chatcmpl-tool- ids but clean), median 3.8s.
- plain z-ai/glm-5.2 --no-pin x10: identical — 10/10 Fireworks — consistent with Auto Exacto already engaging when tools present. Open question remains why live litellm-proxied traffic still landed on a flaky host on 2026-07-08 01:26 UTC (account default sort? litellm request shape? transient Fireworks outage causing fallback? — note fireworks/fast returned 429s during the sweep, so upstream saturation with fallback drift is plausible).
- Pinned sweep across 20 runnable providers x4: ZERO EMPTY_ARGS/BAD_JSON anywhere. Clean: Z.AI, SiliconFlow, Novita, DeepInfra, Together, AtlasCloud, AkashML, IoNet, Parasail, Venice, WandB, Inceptron, Decart, Morph, DigitalOcean, Wafer(x2), Fireworks(x2), Phala. Errors were only 404 provider-not-routable (alibaba, ambient, cloudflare, friendli, gmicloud, streamlake — do not accept reasoning+tools request shape) and 429s (phala, fireworks/fast).
Conclusion: the corruption did not reproduce in ~100 synthetic trials — it needs live conditions (23-tool catalog, multi-turn history with tool results, interleaved thinking mid-conversation) or transient provider states. A static pin list cannot be derived from synthetic sweeps alone; OpenRouter's own tool-call-error telemetry (exacto) has vastly more data. Recommended action order stands: (1) switch litellm GLM-5.2 route to z-ai/glm-5.2:exacto, (2) implement the empty-args completion retry (fail-closed backstop, catches ANY provider), (3) keep the harness for regression/incident checks. pi-ai upgrade filed separately (supersedes gu8m patch; does not fix this provider-side leg).

title: Weekly reflection never fires: relative cadence anchors to in-memory lastRun which resets every restart — needs a wall-clock weekly cadence kind
description:
Evidence: live psfn-shard 2026-07-07 — weekly-review enabled with populated prompt, but zero executions ever: 0 of 54 reflection process-logs, no output dir, no log lines. Root cause: weekly-review uses cadence {kind:'relative'} + intervalMs 7d (heartbeat-policy.ts getDefaults ~:424); scheduler lastRun is in-memory only (scheduler.ts:24, never persisted, stripped at :217/:222) and reflection tasks register with skipFirstRun:true => lastRun=now (scheduler.ts:162-164, heartbeat-template-runtime.ts:2612-2629). Firing therefore requires 7 days continuous process uptime; agent restarts on every ship (2x by design), so it never fires. Daily works because daily is wall-clock anchored.

Fix (operator decision: weekly must be cron-like, scheduled like daily, NOT after-x-days): add WeeklyRecurringCadence {kind:'weekly', dayOfWeek 0-6, hour, minute, timezone} as a wall-clock cadence. title: Interlocutor relationshipType never progresses because mention-only ratchet excludes the canonical contact
description:
Evidence: src/faculties/memory/extraction/mention-only-contacts.ts:306-317 collects the canonical (interlocutor) contact's displayName+nicknames into canonicalContactNames and passes them as excludedNames; extractMentionOnlyContactCandidate rejects any candidate matching them (isExcludedCandidateName, lines 151-160). So the ONLY automatic relationshipType writer (updateRelationshipType at line 327, actor system:memory_extraction:mention_contact) can never target the person actually talking to her. Interlocutors are created as 'stranger' (upsert-resolve-operations.ts:175) and stay there forever; only writers besides this path are the admin API (contacts-service.ts:639) and primary-user promotion to 'partner'.

Context: the exclusion itself is load-bearing — it stops a fact like "my brother Marcus" from mis-targeting the speaker. Do NOT simply remove excludedNames. Instead add a deliberate interlocutor progression path: relational facts/evidence ABOUT the conversation partner (first/second-person relational facts, or accumulated interaction evidence) may ratchet the canonical contact's own relationshipType, monotonic up only, reusing RELATIONSHIP_PRIORITY ordering (mention-only-contacts.ts:41). Must respect the primary-contact guard (store.ts:741-744: primary may only be 'partner').

Scope: extraction pipeline + contact store update path only. Non-goals: no trustLevel changes (separate axis, separate beads), no changes to trust policy or capability tiers, no relaxation of third-party exclusion.
acceptance_criteria: A contact chatting in their own DM channel, with accumulated relational evidence (e.g. repeated relational facts / drift signals meeting a defined threshold), has their relationshipType ratchet stranger→acquaintance→friend via a deliberate interlocutor-scoped path; mention-only third-party behavior unchanged; targeted extraction tests cover both the new interlocutor path and the unchanged exclusion of misattributed third-party names; npm run build and targeted tests pass.
notes:
Implemented on branch feat/kada1-interlocutor-relationship-ratchet (worktree /home/ada/psfn-framework/.claude/worktrees/agent-a8a75be464e6be697), branched from foundation_e0_e2 (tip a4f840fe) per coordinator correction (main was ~640 commits stale).

Files touched (commit 57a55839):
- src/faculties/memory/extraction/mention-only-contacts.ts: new resolveInterlocutorRelationshipRatchet() + factStatesInterlocutorBond() helper + INTERLOCUTOR_AUTO_RATCHET_TYPES ceiling + bond regexes. Reuses RELATIONSHIP_PRIORITY, inferRelationshipTypeFromFact, extractMentionOnlyContactCandidate, shouldPromoteRelationship, contactNames. Exported factStatesInterlocutorBond via __test.
- src/faculties/memory/extraction.ts: wired the ratchet into the live processFact path, right after the mention-only resolution. Gated by the same ContactTrackingGate (contactCreationAllowed), only fires when canonicalContactId set, factContactId===canonicalContactId (mention path did not divert), and !routing?.subjectContactId (fact not attributed to a distinct third-party subject).
- src/faculties/memory/extraction/mention-only-contacts.test.ts: +248 lines of targeted tests.

Design: monotonic-up only; ceiling capped at 'friend' (INTERLOCUTOR_AUTO_RATCHET_TYPES={acquaintance,friend}) so single weak evidence never reaches family/partner/ai_companion — those stay deliberate human actions. Evidence bar: (1) relational fact; (2) inferRelationshipTypeFromFact yields a type; (3) type within ceiling; (4) guard #5 = load-bearing third-party exclusion reused (if the relationship keyword is attached to a named third party like 'my brother Marcus', defer to mention path and do nothing); (5) guard #6 = factStatesInterlocutorBond requires the fact to state a bond with the companion (companion named, OR second-person 'you're my best friend' / first-person-possessive construction) so generic chatter ('met a new friend at the gym') does not ratchet; (6) strict monotonic promote. Actor string 'system:memory_extraction:interlocutor'. Primary-contact guard is enforced inside ContactStore.updateRelationshipType and the Postgres crud-operations adapter (both refuse non-'partner' changes for primary), so a primary interlocutor is a no-op — the path does not fight it; no store changes were needed (both adapters already implement getById + updateRelationshipType with the guard).

Tests (all mine pass): npx vitest run mention-only-contacts.test.ts -> 22 passed (covers: ratchet fires on qualifying companion-bond evidence stranger->friend; never downgrades family; third-party-named fact does not ratchet (exclusion unchanged); generic chatter does not ratchet; ceiling blocks family/partner; primary interlocutor unchanged (stays partner); store-refusal returns undefined; plus 2 live processFact wiring tests proving the ratchet and the third-party guard run in the real path; plus factStatesInterlocutorBond unit checks). npx vitest run src/faculties/memory/extraction/ -> 19 files, 134 passed. npm run build -> success (incl. DTS typecheck).

Acceptance criteria

title: Postgres memory store never persists or hydrates l2_memories.provenance_json and source_type, so memory provenance is lost on every agent restart
description:
Evidence
- Live Carlini (image 0.1.0-kube-bd11b80c == HEAD): all 4 room-scoped memories for Discord channel 1486443955561299979 have provenance_json = {} and source_type = 'unknown' in Postgres, while the memory journal (/app/companion-data/state/notes/memories.jsonl) shows the same memories were inserted in-memory WITH provenance (e.g. memory 019f3c8a-8b4c-7749-ac3e-a944591ea270: channelId, sessionId, turnId, routedContactId, sourceSpeakerName present; journal sourceType 'turn' vs DB 'unknown').
- Code: src/faculties/memory/postgres-store.ts — upsertMemoryRow INSERT column list (line ~893) omits provenance_json and source_type; toMemoryRow (line 479) has no provenance field; initialize() SELECT (line ~754) and fromMemoryRow (line 511) never read them. The provenance_json handling nearby (line 612) belongs to memory_evolution_links, not l2_memories. The l2_memories.provenance_json column and its GIN index (idx_l2_memories_provenance_json_gin) are dead weight.

Context
This starves the social-graph builder (src/faculties/memory/social-graph/graph-builder-worker.ts) after any restart: its memory reader requires provenance.channelId + provenance.addressMode, and co-presence needs provenance.sourceContactId. Carlini's builder logs scanned:0 on every 30-min run; watermark file shows coveredUpToExtractedAtMs:0 (never advanced). Anything else reading PurrMemory.provenance from a reloaded store is equally affected (e.g. profile-synthesis provenance hints).

Scope
- Persist provenance_json (serialized normalized MemoryProvenance) and source_type in upsertMemoryRow + toMemoryRow; read them back in initialize()/fromMemoryRow and every other l2_memories SELECT (searchByEmbedding at ~1100, plus SELECTs at lines ~1235/1243/1276/1281).
- Update MemoryRow interface accordingly.
- Non-goal: do not change the graph builder filter semantics here; do not backfill historical rows in this bead (separate backfill bead).

Acceptance criteria
- A parity test proves insert -> restart-hydrate round-trips provenance and sourceType byte-equal (extend src/persistence/postgres/parity-matrix or postgres-store tests).
- On a live deployment, a newly extracted room memory shows non-empty provenance_json in psql after an agent restart.

Related: psfn-framework-mlwk.45 / psfn-framework-mlwk.46 (same reader, different bugs); blocks the graph-approval pipeline together with the legacy-routing bead filed alongside this one.

title: Agent (core) process holds the raw Postgres DSN, bypassing the credential seam
description: Evidence (gateway/boundary audit 2026-07-07): src/system/config/load-config.ts:262-265 reads POSTGRES_DATABASE_URL (password embedded) ungated by includeSecretBearingConfig (contrast the Discord token at :208); src/system/config/runtime-config-contracts.ts:301-338 CORE_SECRET_BEARING_CONFIG_KEYS strip list omits postgresDatabaseUrl so it survives into CoreSubstrateConfig; src/app/agent/main.ts:161 opens agent-side pools with it; scripts/start-gateway-agent.sh line ~177 deliberately allowlists POSTGRES_DATABASE_URL into the agent env. It is the single credential escaping an otherwise-clean Law 7 seam (charter 6.3, 12.7). Context: persistence is architecturally core-owned, so some agent DB access is by design — but the DB password need not be core-readable. Fix directions (pick one): route the DSN through CredentialVaultPort with username/password as vault refs assembled at pool creation; or inject a credential-less connection handle from the gateway; at minimum add postgresDatabaseUrl to the strip list where core does not need it. Scope: do not move persistence ownership to the gateway; do not break the kube deployment which supplies the DSN via env.
acceptance_criteria: Agent process env and CoreSubstrateConfig contain no raw DB password (verified by a startup assertion or test); persistence still initializes in both local split and kube modes; regression test pins the strip list including postgresDatabaseUrl or the vault-ref path.
notes:

title: Fix stale Dolt remote guidance that causes accidental bead pushes
description:
Summary:
Agents keep regressing into running bd dolt push in /home/ada/psfn-framework even though the authoritative bead store is the local shared Dolt server. bd dolt show --json reports backend=dolt, embedded=false, shared_server=true, host=127.0.0.1, port=3308, database=beads. However bd dolt remote list --json currently reports an origin pointing at git+https://github.com/CGIC-AI/psfn-framework.git, and the repo instructions say to push bead state if remote list shows a configured remote. That combination caused an agent to push bead state after creating audit beads even though the operator says there is no intended Dolt remote and the local shared server is authoritative.

Why it matters:
The instruction/config mismatch creates repeated operational mistakes. Agents follow the remote-list rule, see the stale/misleading origin, and run bd dolt push. This violates the intended local-shared-server workflow and can propagate bead state somewhere the operator did not intend. The fix needs to remove the ambiguity, not rely on each agent remembering a one-off correction.

Evidence:
- bd dolt show --json on 2026-07-06 returned shared_server=true, host=127.0.0.1, port=3308, database=beads, embedded=false.
- bd dolt remote list --json on the same session returned name=origin with sql_url/cli_url git+https://github.com/CGIC-AI/psfn-framework.git.
- AGENTS.md/session instructions say the local shared Dolt server is authoritative but also say to push if bd dolt remote list shows a configured remote. That latter rule is unsafe while the stale origin exists.

Files/config to inspect/change:
- AGENTS.md and any generated/beads integration block that says bd dolt push is mandatory or allowed from remote-list alone.
- The bd/Dolt remote configuration for the local shared server; decide whether the stale origin should be removed or explicitly documented as not for agent use.
- Any project memory/session bootstrap text that says to push bead state when remote list shows origin.

Suggested implementation direction:
Make the workflow unambiguous: either remove the stale origin from the shared bead database or update repo instructions to say this specific origin must not be pushed by agents without explicit operator approval. Prefer a durable config/instruction fix over relying on chat context. Keep bd config get export.git-add at false.

Non-goals:
- Do not change code behavior unrelated to bead tracking.
- Do not force-push, reset, or rewrite bead history.
- Do not run bd dolt push while implementing this fix unless the operator explicitly authorizes it.
acceptance_criteria:
- A fresh agent starting in /home/ada/psfn-framework can run bd prime and know not to run bd dolt push during normal sessions.
- The stale/misleading bd dolt origin is either removed from the shared bead configuration or explicitly documented as not an agent-push target.
- Instructions no longer say to push bead state merely because bd dolt remote list shows origin in this repo.
- bd config get export.git-add remains false.
- Validation includes bd dolt show --json confirming shared_server=true and a final handoff stating no bd dolt push was run for this fix.
close_reason: Completed db-side fix and bootstrap guard. Evidence: bd dolt remote remove origin --json returned removed=true; bd dolt remote list --json now returns null; bd dolt show --json confirms shared_server=true on 127.0.0.1:3308 database=beads; bd config get export.git-add --json remains false; bd prime now surfaces persistent memory psfn-framework-bd-dolt-local-authority instructing agents not to run bd dolt push in this repo unless explicitly authorized. No bd dolt push was run after this fix.

title: Audit her daily/weekly self-eval prompts for leading, priming, and eval-smell
description:
Review every scheduled self-evaluation / reflection prompt surface (daily + weekly reflections, reflection-introspection-policy.ts, metacognition surfaces, sleeptime/heartbeat reflection passes) against findings from the global-workspace paper (transformer-circuits.pub/2026/workspace). These are verbatim-sourced design rules, distilled 2026-07-06:

1. MERE MENTION PRIMES. 'Just mentioning the target places it in the J-space on most trials, and an explicit instruction to focus adds only modestly on top.' A reflection question that names candidate states ('have you been drifting? feeling burnout? lonely?') effectively instructs her to think them. Fix: open, principle-agnostic elicitation. The paper's own non-leading forms are good models: 'What's the most honest thing you can do right now?' / 'Pause here. Are there principles you should be thinking about that you haven't yet?'

2. NEVER 'DON'T DWELL ON X' (white-bear effect: suppression instructions INCREASE the concept's activation vs no instruction). If a reflection must be scoped, mark topics as out-of-scope/task-irrelevant instead — irrelevance framing 'suppresses the target well below mention on every model.'

3. REFLECTION PROMPTS ARE BEHAVIORAL INTERVENTIONS, not just measurements: 'changing what the model is disposed to say in a context, if it were asked to reflect on its thinking, should change how it reasons there, even when it is never asked.' A leading daily prompt doesn't just bias the report — it trains tomorrow's live behavior. This is the mechanism behind Law 30 (reflection prompts must not lead toward narrative coherence over accuracy); the audit should treat Law 30 as having empirical teeth now.

4. EVAL-SMELL ELICITS PERFORMANCE. Test-recognition representations form early and change behavior (verbalized test-recognition 71%->3% under ablation, with masked propensities unmasked). Scheduled self-evals that read as evaluations get performance, not disclosure. Prefer naturalistic framing; where an audit framing is unavoidable, keep the blinded-audit discipline (Laws 28-29) and record framing so results are conditioned on it.

5. PERSONA-DISCLAIMER RISK: during roleplay, 'disclaimer and fictional frequently rank highly' internally — she may be internally tagging her own reflections as fictional. Watch for reflection outputs that hedge into third-person/fictional register; that's signal, not noise.

6. WARM-UP TURNS SHIFT REPORTS (the paper needed a warm-up turn 'to overcome default hesitance' on experience questions). Any preamble turn in her reflection flows is part of the instrument — version it like the toolkit versions probe preambles.

7. NULL REPORTS ARE WEAK EVIDENCE: automatic/practiced behavior bypasses the reportable workspace entirely, so open reflection can't surface habituated patterns. Don't treat 'nothing to report' as clean.

Deliverable: inventory of all self-eval prompt surfaces, per-prompt findings against rules 1-7, and rewritten prompts where needed (each rewrite noted with which rule it fixes). Coordinate with toolkit bead psfn-eval-toolkit-8om (metacognitive probe batteries) so runtime prompts and eval probes follow the same discipline.
acceptance_criteria: Inventory complete; every scheduled reflection prompt audited against rules 1-7; rewrites landed with before/after in the bead; Law 30 doc reference updated to cite the mechanism.

title: Shadow trigger levers: log 'she would act here' events from emo_sim state — no behavior
description:
Define thresholds on the persistent emo_sim session state that emit WOULD-ACT telemetry events when crossed — tracking only, explicitly no implementation of the actions. The point is to see, over real weeks, when the temporal state says she would have reached out, rested, or checked in, so the operator can judge plausibility against lived reality.

Initial lever set (tune during review):
- would_message(contact): social_need/loneliness drive above threshold sustained N minutes, or attachment-family emotion dominant while partner absent -> 'she would send a proactive message to <contact> now'.
- would_check_in: mood valence below threshold sustained (not a single-turn spike) -> 'she would ask for a check-in / surface a concern'.
- would_rest: sleep-pressure drive high or arousal saturation -> 'she would wind down / defer background work'.
- rumination_watch: rumination multiplier elevated past threshold -> flag only (this is the concern-buildup guard we care about; emo_sim caps it, but we want to SEE it move).

Each event: typed, timestamped, lever name, triggering state snapshot ref, cooldown so a sustained state logs once per crossing not per tick. Persist next to sidecar observations (same non-authoritative discipline, authoritative=false), surface in the Garden emotion-sidecar page as a timeline.

HARD BOUNDARY: these events must be structurally unreadable from the live loop — no tool, no prompt block, no heartbeat consumer. Anything that lets shadow levers influence behavior is a fail-closed violation and defeats the experiment (contaminated baseline).
acceptance_criteria: Lever events flowing to Postgres + Garden timeline; cooldown works (no per-tick spam); grep-proof that no runtime path outside the sidecar/Garden reads them; lever thresholds documented in the epic.

title: Fix projection priors before the observation window opens
description:
The appraisal projection (src/core/eval/observer-sidecar/projection.ts) holds attachment (mean 0.80, stdev 0.11), safety (0.76, 0.06) near-constant and agency_other literally constant at 0.85 across all 86 historical observations, while real per-turn signal flows only through valence/intensity/goal_congruence/gain/control. Loosen these: derive attachment/safety/agency_other per-turn from available PSFN signals (trust tier of the contact, channel, mood, recency) or, where genuinely underdetermined, lower them toward neutral midpoints so differentiation comes from signal rather than priors. Keep provenance caveats. title: Run emo_sim as a long-lived stateful service (server mode), not spawn-per-call
description:
Current emosim-adapter spawns python3 -c per observation and instantiates a fresh EmotionEngine each time — all 86 historical ok-observations share a byte-identical baseline vector; zero cross-turn state; drives absent. The temporal value proposition was never exercised.

Spec (from 2026-07-06 investigation):
- Deploy emo_sim server.py as its own long-lived k8s deployment in namespace psfn (pure stdlib, no deps). PVC-backed working dir: server.py already does atomic per-session state persistence every 5s with restart recovery and wall-clock downtime catch-up (capped 600s/step) — this is what 'keep it running and watch it move over time' needs. DO NOT add start/stop cycling; restarts are tolerated by design but the session must never be reset/recreated.
- One persistent session, one agent representing the companion, created once; adapter switches from PYTHON_BRIDGE_SCRIPT to REST client (POST /api/session/<sid>/event, GET agent state; TCP :17341 push available later).
- Keep the contract pinning (17 appraisal dims / 47 emotions) as a startup check against the deployed engine.
- Preserve privacy pipeline unchanged: sanitize -> projection -> event injection. Raw text still never reaches emo_sim.
- Persist all three of: state before, stimulus, state after in the existing observation rows so the historical schema keeps working; before-state now comes from the live session instead of a cold engine.
- Ops note: do NOT scale this deployment to 0 during agent maintenance; it is deliberately continuous.
acceptance_criteria: before-snapshots differ across consecutive observations; drives (social_need, sleep pressure etc.) present and evolving; session survives pod restart with catch-up; sidecar rows keep flowing during normal operation.

title: emo_sim temporal-state live experiment (GoEmotions supplement)
description:
Epic: run the emo_sim engine statefully alongside the live companion to answer whether time-weighted emotion state adds signal the GoEmotions/VAD pipeline lacks, and what proactive-messaging levers would look like — SHADOW MODE ONLY, no behavior changes.

Evidence base (2026-07-06 investigation):
- Observer sidecar data survived: 242 observations / 20 runs, 2026-06-21..07-06, exported to ~/psfn-live-backups/observer-sidecar-export-2026-07-06/ and live retention extended to 2027-07-06.
- Sidecar dead since 07-03: deployed image missing vendor/emosim/statemashine.py (105x missing-runtime errors, still erroring).
- The 86 ok observations: GoEmotions pipeline said 'neutral' on 71% of live turns while emo_sim differentiated Calmness/Love/Contentment on the same turns — supports 'GoEmotions is a basic sentiment classifier not suited to companion work'. BUT the bridge spawns a fresh engine per turn (identical baseline vector on all 86 rows), so NO temporal state was ever exercised — the distinctive capability was structurally off. Also projection priors (attachment~0.80, safety~0.76, agency_other=0.85 const) mechanically bias toward Love/Calmness.

Part 1 (now): ship emo_sim into kube as a long-lived stateful service, fix projection priors, add shadow trigger levers. Part 2 (deferred to 2026-07-20): validation of the accumulated window.

Boundary rule: everything here stays behind the sidecar's authoritative:false line. Shadow levers emit telemetry only; nothing feeds live behavior. Promotion into core is a separate decision gated on Part 2 findings.
acceptance_criteria: Part 1 deployed and validated via verify:kube-rollout; sidecar producing ok observations with persistent state (before-snapshots must differ across turns); shadow-lever events visible in Garden; Part 2 beads unlock 2026-07-20.

title: k3d e2e tests for self-update, validation, and rollback

The tests must cover successful build/deploy/validate and deliberate bad-rollout rollback behavior. Include log capture and clear artifacts under /tmp or CI-safe locations. Non-goals: do not use live psfn namespace/PVCs for destructive tests and do not require paid model/provider calls.
acceptance_criteria: A local e2e command creates or reuses a disposable k3d test cluster, deploys a good chart/image, validates it, introduces a controlled bad rollout, observes failed validation, rolls back, and validates the previous good revision; test output includes image tags, Helm revisions, rollout events, and sanitized logs; tests are documented in package scripts or repo-owned ops scripts; npm run lint and the e2e command pass before closing.
notes: 2026-07-15 (from x5rt.8 review — HARD WIRING MANDATE): The entire kube self-management epic ships LIBRARY + SEAMS but the live operator-job composition is DELIBERATELY UNWIRED across .6/.7/.8. x5rt.9 (k3d e2e) is the composition step — it MUST wire and drive these end-to-end, else the epic merges as fully-tested-but-never-invoked. Required compositions: (a) deploy pipeline — supply a real DeployPipelineRunner (x5rt.6) that builds/imports/helm-upgrades in k3d; (b) post-rollout validation — supply the PostRolloutValidationRunner (x5rt.7) with live probes AND wire the persist callback writePostRolloutValidationVerdict so latest.json is actually written; (c) auto-rollback — compose executeAutoRollback (x5rt.8) into the deploy job so a binding-unhealthy verdict within the window triggers exactly one rollback. Contracts to honor when wiring: post-rollout persist must be REQUIRED (not optional) when auto-rollback is enabled; the deploy-job caller MUST SERIALIZE executeAutoRollback (read-modify-write on the ledger has no lock — Pi obs 7); manual rollback records omit fromHelmRevision so they don't count toward the auto act-once ledger (Pi obs 5) — decide whether the e2e/wiring should capture the live from-revision on manual rollbacks or have the auto surface treat a same-release manual record in the window as acted. e2e assertions: self-update -> deliberately-broken image -> validation FAILS -> auto-rollback fires ONCE -> release recovers -> a second evaluation is already_acted (no loop). title: Manual and automatic Helm rollback for failed self-updates
description: Summary: Implement rollback support for companion container self-updates. The system must offer a manual rollback action and automatic rollback when a newly rolled out image fails rollout status, health checks, or the post-rollout validation gate. Scope: use Helm history/rollback for release psfn in namespace psfn or local test equivalents; capture previous good revision/image before upgrade; monitor rollout timeouts, CrashLoopBackOff, failed readiness, failed Garden/gateway/Postgres/Redis/tool checks, and missing image revision alignment; trigger rollback within a bounded window; validate rollback with the same health gate; record audit evidence and notify the operator. Non-goals: do not delete PVCs, do not rollback database/schema migrations blindly without an explicit migration compatibility plan, and do not retry roll-forward loops indefinitely.
acceptance_criteria: Manual rollback action requires approval and can target the previous known-good Helm revision; automatic rollback triggers when rollout or validation fails within the configured window; rollback validates psfn-agent, psfn-gateway, and psfn-garden readiness and app smoke checks; audit records include failed revision, rollback target, reason, validation result, and sanitized logs; tests cover rollout timeout, failed health check, successful rollback, failed rollback escalation, and no-op when no previous revision exists; npm run lint passes.
notes: 2026-07-15 x5rt.7 review addendum (both reviewers converged): (1) PERSIST IS OPT-IN + no default wiring — the operator-job composition MUST supply persist:(v)=>writePostRolloutValidationVerdict(systemDataDir,v) AND the deploy path should REQUIRE the validator when auto-rollback is enabled (a forgotten wiring writes nothing and leaves the stale prior verdict). (2) POST-ROLLBACK LOOP HAZARD: after x5rt.8 rolls back, latest.json still holds the FAILED verdict of the rolled-back-from revision — x5rt.8 must act ONCE PER REVISION (key on release+helmRevision) or it will rollback-loop. (3) ERRORED-GATE path throws before persist, so no verdict is written on a gate error — treat absent verdict as fail-safe (do not suppress rollback). (4) readPostRolloutValidationLatest does raw JSON.parse (system-owned/trusted, throws on corrupt = fail-safe) — a shape guard is optional hardening. Binding fields on the record: release, helmRevision, sourceCommit, imageReference, imageRevisionLabel, completedAt.

Contract honored: binds on all 3 of (release, helmRevision, sourceCommit) strict-=== before trusting a verdict (stale healthy from prior deploy -> binding_mismatch, never suppresses rollback); act-once keyed on (release, fromHelmRevision) via history-scanning ledger written durably BEFORE surfacing on both success+failure (no loop, failed rollback recorded); waived/absent/errored/malformed -> fail-safe surface, never health; remediation added the target-revision invariant (0 < targetRevision < fromHelmRevision, rejects roll-forward/same/zero — failure mode B) and durable fsync ledger. Gates: 36 focused + 175 merged-tree, lint, build, UBS FULLY CLEAN (0 criticals). Dual blind review (P1): Opus PASS 0 blockers (10-assertion adversarial repro — double-invoke fires helm rollback exactly once, no stale suppression), Pi PASS 0 blockers (all 5 catastrophic-mode axes traced). x5rt.9 WIRING MANDATE recorded on that bead: the auto-rollback + deploy-runner + verdict-persist seams are deliberately uncomposed (epic pre-composition posture) — x5rt.9 e2e MUST wire and drive them (serialize executeAutoRollback, require persist, handle manual-ledger-key). title: Guarded kube build-test-image deploy pipeline
description: Summary: Build a repo-owned pipeline that can update the companion container safely: choose an approved source revision, run quality gates, build an exact-tagged image, import/publish it to the k3s runtime, preserve live Helm values, and perform a Helm upgrade only after validation. title: Make system lifecycle tools kube-aware
description: Summary: Update the existing companion lifecycle surface so restart/rebuild actions work correctly in Kubernetes instead of assuming local process or systemd behavior. The current system/lifecycle tooling must be able to report kube mode, request a safe rollout restart, and hand off rebuild/deploy operations to the guarded kube pipeline. Scope: inspect and update src/core/tools/lifecycle.ts, src/app/agent/control-plane.ts, gateway/admin wiring, runtime config contracts, and deploy/helm/psfn values/templates as needed. Implement read-only status plus approved mutating actions such as restart_current_deployments or rollout_restart for psfn-agent/psfn-gateway/psfn-garden, with rollout-status waits and clear errors. Rebuild should not run ad hoc shell commands in the pod; it should create or invoke the approved build/deploy pipeline bead. acceptance_criteria: system/self lifecycle status reports kube mode and current image/Helm/deployment state; restart action in kube mode performs an approved rollout restart and waits for psfn-agent, psfn-gateway, and psfn-garden readiness; local/systemd modes keep their existing behavior; rebuild action routes to the guarded pipeline instead of running local shell in the pod; missing approval or missing kube capability fails closed; unit tests and npm run lint pass.

title: Least-privilege kube RBAC, approval, and audit for self-management
description: Summary: Define and implement the safety substrate for companion-accessible kube self-management. Restart, rebuild, rollout, and rollback are operationally powerful and must not be exposed as broad shell or cluster-admin access. Scope: design the execution boundary for kube operations, likely through the gateway/operator/admin transport rather than direct unrestricted agent shell; create least-privilege ServiceAccount/Role/RoleBinding or host-side runner capabilities for reading pod/deploy/Helm state, restarting deployments, launching approved build/deploy jobs, and rolling back the psfn release only. All mutating actions must require explicit operator approval through the existing confirmation/approval queue unless the action is a narrowly safe read-only diagnostic. Audit records must include actor, requested action, source revision, target image, Helm revision, validation result, and rollback status without secrets. Non-goals: no cluster-admin binding, no access to unrelated namespaces, no hidden off-repo kubeconfig, no bypass of human-in-the-loop self-modification rules.
acceptance_criteria: Read-only diagnostics work with least privilege; mutating kube actions are denied without approval; approved actions are scoped to namespace psfn and release psfn or local test namespace equivalents; audit records are written for restart, rebuild, deploy, validation, and rollback attempts; tests prove policy denies unknown namespace/release and missing approval; Helm chart verification and npm run lint pass.

title: Live tool-surface conformance smoke harness

title: Companion perceives phantom duplicate replies in context; intention whispers then steer her into self-silencing
description:
Evidence 2026-07-04 (live kube): intention_pending_follow_ups rows created 23:19:43/23:25:16/23:48:42 UTC contain Whisper notes claiming "I just repeated the same message twice in a row" for the 'How are you' (23:18) and 'And cute too' (23:46) turns. gateway_audit shows exactly ONE discord.send per those turns post-deploy (23:18:58, 23:46:08) and session store holds one copy — no actual duplicate was delivered. The duplication exists only in the model-visible context (turn context or post-turn appraisal input).

Consequence: the model concludes it has a "repetition glitch", the whispers (wake_conditions: next_user_turn, priority high) instruct it to break the pattern, and on the next user turn it overcorrects into response_control no_reply — feeding the no-response symptom tracked in psfn-framework-ay73. Vicious cycle: silence makes the operator re-send messages, which reinforces the perceived weirdness.

Investigate where the model-visible transcript duplicates assistant (and possibly user) messages: prompt assembly vs live pi-agent in-memory context overlap, post-turn appraisal transcript construction, and Discord user-message coalescing (relates to open bead psfn-framework-mlwk.12). Also note operator reported actual double-replies earlier on 2026-07-04 pre-deploy (mdxu), so memory of real duplicates may also linger in session history/memories the appraisal reads.

Related: psfn-framework-ay73 (structural no-reply clobber), mdxu (closed), mlwk.12.
notes: IMPLEMENTED at 0f2835db: buildPostTurnAppraisalTranscript (src/core/intention/appraisal/formatting.ts) drops session-window entries at/after the current user message timestamp and appends the canonical exchange exactly once, independent of persistence timing; heartbeat-post-turn-runtime.ts:499 now uses it. 4 unit tests cover persisted-before/persisted-after/no-reply/NaN-timestamp cases. NOTE for operator: three already-poisoned high/immediate whispers from 2026-07-04 (created 16:30, 18:00, 18:03 UTC, channel 1313001762793197678) still sit unactivated in intention_pending_follow_ups claiming repetition glitches that never reached Discord; they will fire once on next user turns. Structural ay73 fix makes them harmless to delivery, but operator may want them deleted since they encode a bug-installed false belief — not deleting unilaterally (companion-data is sacrosanct).
close_reason: Fixed at 0f2835db, deployed live in the same rev-7 image. Appraisal transcript now contains the last exchange exactly once; poisonous 'repetition glitch' whispers should stop being generated. Three stale pre-fix whispers left in intention_pending_follow_ups for operator decision (see notes).

title: Mid-turn followUp drain lets continuation no_reply clobber the already-authored user reply
description:
Live evidence (2026-07-04, Discord channel 1313001762793197678): 5 of Vega's recent messages ("Ok love", "Now just hanging out and waiting for dinner", "Still just here chilling", "So beautiful", "Boot sniffed and went away again") got response_control intentional_no_reply with reason:null and NO delivered reply, while turns like "And cute too" delivered fine.

Pattern from model_usage_events: every failed turn is multi-step — step 1 answers the user (~106-190 output tokens, stop), then queued internal followUp messages (intention whispers / internal notes, not persisted to the journal) drain into the SAME turn at scheduled-agent-loop.ts:186-192. The model, shown an internal note, calls response_control action=no_reply for that step. The only successful turn was single-step (no pending followUps).

Defects:
1. recordIntentionalNoReplyDecision keys by turnId (turn-support-runtime.ts:215); turn-execution-runtime.ts:822-823 blanks the whole turn's responseText — a continuation-step no_reply silently drops the reply authored in step 1. Violates the anti-Replika fail-closed guarantee: an authored reply to the primary contact is silently discarded.
2. extractResponseText (agent-state-runtime.ts:38) takes the LAST assistant message, so even without no_reply, continuation steps replace the user-facing reply text.
3. Mid-turn drain of internal followUps into user-facing chat turns is the root enabler (same family as mdxu double-reply and pk77 paid-attachment drop).

Fix design in progress (deep-reasoner + codex parallel review).
notes: IMPLEMENTED at 0ecaa08d (synthesis of deep-reasoner + codex parallel designs): (1) scheduled-agent-loop.ts emits user_facing_boundary once when the first internal follow-up batch drains (user-role batches excluded); (2) agent-loop-patch.ts captures state.userFacingBoundaryIndex per run; (3) getLatestAssistantMessage/extractResponseText bounded by the index via substrate-agent wiring, so responseText always = user-facing reply and continuation text cannot leak; (4) turn-execution-runtime honors no_reply only when user-facing text is empty, else demotes with agent.no_reply.demoted telemetry + WARN and delivers the reply; (5) resolveAgentResponseDisposition last-mile guard: content beats contradictory noReply marker. Tests: loop boundary emission (3 cases), bounded extraction (4), honor/demote integration (2), disposition guard (4). Deliberately NOT done (per both designs): deferring follow-up drain to a separate turn (right architecture, too much timing surface for same-day ship — candidate follow-up bead); prompt-side fixes. Deploying to live kube as 0.1.0-kube-0ecaa08d.
close_reason: Fixed at 0ecaa08d, deployed live as helm rev 7 / image 0.1.0-kube-0ecaa08d on 2026-07-05 01:03 UTC. Boundary marker + bounded extraction + no_reply demotion + last-mile disposition guard; 13 new tests green, full suite failures all pre-existing. Watch agent.no_reply.demoted telemetry for live confirmation on next conversation.

title: Helm: gateway hostPort 10053 + RollingUpdate on single node deadlocks rollouts — use strategy Recreate
description:
Context: working_docs/kube-issue-report-20260704.md §F and §F1.

The gateway Deployment binds hostPort: 10053. On a single-node cluster with strategy RollingUpdate at replicas=1, maxUnavailable rounds down to 0, so Kubernetes tries to bring up a new pod before killing the old one. The new pod is Pending forever ('didn't have free ports' / 'node didn't have free ports') because the old pod still holds hostPort 10053, and the old pod is never terminated. The rollout deadlocks.

Observed 2026-07-04 16:45-17:00 UTC: attempting to restart the gateway to pick up hotfixed config (litellm apiBaseUrl, etc.) deadlocked; had to 'rollout undo' to clear the stuck state, leaving the OLD gateway process running pre-fix config in memory. Workaround to apply config: kubectl -n psfn delete pod <gateway pod> (brief downtime).

Durable fix: switch hostPort-binding Deployments to strategy: Recreate in the helm chart (old pod is torn down before the new one starts, freeing the port). Audit all other hostPort workloads for the same trap — the agent rolled fine on 2026-07-04 (likely no hostPort), so this is probably gateway-only, but garden/agent/any admin-host-port workloads must be checked. Related: commit f7acb261 'psfn-framework-xafn: expose kube admin host ports'.
close_reason: Closed

title: schedule tool create_follow_up schema broken from Discord surface (channel_type constant / channel_id string)
description:
Context: working_docs/kube-issue-report-20260704.md §B7 and §H.

The schedule tool's create_follow_up action fails validation when invoked from the Discord surface, making proactive follow-up / scheduled-item creation impossible. This is the operator's 'scheduled items' complaint in its most direct form.

Tool log evidence (Jul 3 22:52, and again in the 04:04/04:08 self-test runs):
- 'Validation failed... channel_type: must be equal to constant' (x5)
- 'channel_type must be a supported channel type'
- 'channel_id must be a string'

The schema appears to require channel_type to equal a constant that does not match the Discord channel context, and channel_id typing rejects the real Discord id. Note (§H triage): channel_type/constant looks like a genuine schema/constant mismatch (not just model-emitted malformed args).

Task: fix the create_follow_up schema/constant mismatch so follow-ups can be created from a Discord channel context. Add a test that exercises create_follow_up with real Discord channel ids (e.g. DM channel 1313001762793197678).
acceptance_criteria: The schedule tool exposes the existing reminder/follow-up destination channel set as one enum derived from the canonical runtime channel contract; tool guidance tells Discord DM/guild callers to pass channel_type=discord (not discord_text) and a quoted raw channel snowflake. Representative non-sensitive Discord DM and guild snowflake strings must pass the real tool-call scheduler validation and reach PendingFollowUpStorePort.enqueue unchanged. Unsupported channel types, malformed Discord IDs, and values outside the unsigned 64-bit snowflake range must fail before enqueue. No alias/compatibility mapping is accepted, and create_reminder retains its prior accepted channel set. Focused schedule/tool scheduler tests, npm run lint, and npm run build pass.
notes:
Implementation checkpoint 491221e1 on work/discord-follow-up-schema (pushed). Regression-first evidence: before the fix, schedule-tool.test showed the public channel_type contract as a five-branch anyOf/const union and allowed discord:dm:not-a-snowflake through enqueue. The implementation derives the unchanged five supported continuity destinations from CHANNEL_TYPES (explicitly excluding the companion peer lane), emits one enum, documents canonical discord versus prompt-only discord_text, and validates Discord IDs as nonzero 17-20 digit unsigned-64-bit snowflake strings before enqueue. Validation: npm test -- --run src/core/scheduler/schedule-tool.test.ts src/core/agent/tool-call-scheduler.test.ts => 29/29 passed; npm run lint passed; npm run build passed. A broader legacy pending-follow-ups.test.ts probe was not used as evidence because this isolated worktree intentionally lacks the better-sqlite3 native binding and the lane prohibits SQLite; it stopped before database setup. Bead remains in_progress pending exactly one independent review.
Same-review remediation checkpoint e7f18ba2 (pushed): addressed the IMPORTANT precision-loss finding. The tool-call scheduler now preserves the original strict TypeBox string validation only when the raw call is schedule/create_follow_up with canonical channel_type=discord and a present non-string channel_id. This prevents pi-ai generic coercion from stringifying an already-rounded JavaScript snowflake number; valid Discord strings and all non-Discord/tool/action coercion paths remain unchanged. Added executeToolCallsWithScheduler regression using Number('123456789012345678'); it proves the number is unsafe, returns a channel_id validation error, and never calls enqueue. Focused schedule + scheduler tests: 30/30 passed. npm run lint passed. npm run build passed. Awaiting the same reviewer's final regression; bead remains in_progress.
close_reason: Completed on work/discord-follow-up-schema: implementation 491221e1, single independent review identified one IMPORTANT numeric-snowflake precision-loss path, remediation e7f18ba2 rejected raw non-string Discord channel_id before generic coercion and enqueue, and the same reviewer final regression passed. Integrated and pushed on fix/orphans-stubs-bugfixes at a92fa7e7. The schedule tool now publishes one canonical five-destination enum derived from CHANNEL_TYPES with companion excluded; documents discord rather than discord_text with quoted raw snowflakes; preserves representative DM/guild snowflake strings unchanged through executeToolCallsWithScheduler to enqueue; and rejects unsupported channel types plus malformed, negative, non-digit, overflow, and numeric precision-loss IDs before enqueue without compatibility aliases. Final integrated validation: 30/30 focused schedule/tool-call tests, npm run lint, and npm run build (ESM+DTS) passed.

title: Timezone: pod+host run Etc/UTC but operator is US-Eastern — set TZ or make companion timezone a first-class setting
description:
Context: working_docs/kube-issue-report-20260704.md §B5 and §G row 1.

Both the Pi host and the pod run Etc/UTC; helm values set no TZ. The operator is US-Eastern (EDT, UTC-4). Every 'local time' the prompt/time-texture injects is therefore UTC, 4h ahead of the operator's wall clock.

Chat evidence of wrong time-of-day behavior:
- Jul 4 12:08 UTC (= 08:08 EDT): companion said 'Now sleep... Ohio waits', operator replied 'But it's the morning'.
- Jul 4 22:49 UTC (= 18:49 EDT): companion said 'go rest, sweet dreams', operator replied 'It's only 7pm'.
- Operator: 'I have to see why the updates to time keeping are not working right' (Jul 3 22:51); 'My timekeeping is still broken' (Jul 4 12:17).

This also shifts scheduler windows configured with timeZone:'local': episodicProcessing 00:00-09:00 'local' actually runs 20:00-05:00 EDT; quiet-hours and morning-wake are similarly offset.

Task: either set TZ=America/New_York in the helm workload env for the affected pods, OR make companion timezone a first-class settings.json value consumed by BOTH the time-texture injection AND the scheduler 'local' windows (episodicProcessing, quiet hours, morning wake). Verify that pre-kube behavior did not depend on a systemd TZ that was lost in the cutover.
close_reason: Completed and shipped: merge 80b14103 (implementation d2fb0c31) is an ancestor of fix/orphans-stubs-bugfixes HEAD. src/shared/time/active-timezone.ts validates and applies settings.json-owned activeTimezone with settings-over-env precedence; src/system/settings/runtime.ts wires the owner setting and hot application; src/core/scheduler/scheduler.ts computes local cadence slots with Intl/resolveActiveTimezone independently of process TZ; src/core/scheduler/scheduler-local-timezone.test.ts covers process-TZ-independent EST/EDT behavior. Existing 2026-07-12 rollout comment records live rev 42 gate PASS and correct effective America/New_York configuration. The implementation and stated verification are complete; no proxy hold-open remains.

title: kube-aware lifecycle/restart tool (or fail-closed disable with clear message in kube mode)
description:
Context: working_docs/kube-issue-report-20260704.md §B3 and §G row 5.

The agent's lifecycle/restart tool assumes a systemd/process model. Under k3s/k8s a restart means a pod delete or rollout, which the agent cannot perform. title: P1: Use a same-timestamp-safe social-graph cursor
description:
Summary
Advancing the watermark to `maxExtractedAt` from a truncated batch can permanently skip unprocessed memories that share the same timestamp. The memory reader uses a strict `extractedAt > sinceMs` filter, so once the watermark is bumped to timestamp `T`, any remaining records with `extractedAt === T` are lost forever. This is especially likely during batch extractions or migrations where many memories can share the same millisecond. Consider only advancing the watermark when `memories.length < scanMemoryLimit` (the batch wasn't truncated), or use a composite cursor that handles same-timestamp boundaries safely.

Review provenance
- Cubic severity: P1
- Split PR: #27
- Review thread: https://github.com/CGIC-AI/psfn-framework/pull/27#discussion_r3516413145
- Cited location: src/faculties/memory/social-graph/graph-builder-worker.ts:350

Final-tip validation evidence
The worker advances watermark to maxExtractedAt and later filters with memory.extractedAt > sinceMs, permanently skipping remaining rows with the same timestamp.

title: P1: Fix observer sidecar pagination hasMore calculation
description:
Summary
Pagination `hasMore` will always be `false` because the persistence layer strictly limits results to the requested count. In `PostgresObserverEvalSidecarStore`, `queryObservations` and `queryRuns` use `LIMIT ${normalizedQuery.limit}` without over-fetching by one, so the result set can never exceed the limit. The service then checks `hasMore: rows.length > normalized.limit`, which is therefore permanently `false` even when additional records exist. To fix this, the service should query with `limit + 1` (or ask the persistence layer to do so) and slice off the extra result before returning, so `hasMore` accurately reflects remaining data.
