title: Temporal wake-up: scheduled morning system note + idle time-of-day refresher
description:
## Problem

Datetime anchors, elapsed-time summaries, and time-texture classification (short_gap / long_workday / overnight / multiple_days — src/core/scheduler/time-texture.ts) all exist, but the companion still resumes overnight conversations in the previous night's frame. Nothing pushes the temporal context forward; the passive anchors are demonstrably not enough.

## Scope

Two lanes, both with system-note semantics (charter 6.17): explicit runtime→companion messages, never attributed to the partner. Anything the operator did not type into the text box must never read as partner speech.

1. Scheduled morning wake — default 08:00 local, config-owned (habit-derived timing is a follow-up bead). Injects a system note establishing the new day: date/time, elapsed time since the last exchange, and yesterday's catch-up summary produced by the existing shared summarization service (no bespoke summarizer). The note is context, not a script: the companion responds however she wants under the charter — maybe good morning, maybe something else, maybe nothing outward. The point is to move her headspace into the new day, not to force behavior.
2. Idle time-of-day refresher — after a long same-day gap (config threshold), refresh the temporal frame using the existing time-texture classes so afternoon does not feel like the morning conversation's continuation.

Constraints:
- Wake events must NOT reset elapsed-time-since-last-partner-message tracking or ambient-presence idle accounting. They are refreshers, not partner activity.
- Any outward message the companion chooses to send from a wake event rides the existing proactive-outbound policy gates and rate limits. Blocked outward delivery must not block the internal frame update.
- Quiet hours respected for outward delivery.
- All times/thresholds in scheduler.json.

## Non-goals

- Habit-derived wake-window estimation (follow-up bead).
- Sensor-driven wake detection (future, SensorIngestPort).
acceptance_criteria:
1. Overnight resume: first partner message of the new day is answered in the correct day frame (simulated-clock E2E test).
2. Wake notes are explicit system notes in the message ontology; attribution tests prove they can never render as partner speech.
3. Elapsed-time-since-partner-message and ambient idle accounting unaffected by wake events (test).
4. Outward messages from wake events pass proactive-outbound policy and rate limiting; blocked delivery does not block the internal frame update.
5. Catch-up summary produced by the shared summarization service; no new summarizer.
6. Times/thresholds owned by scheduler.json.
notes: 2026-07-02: implemented on agent/e7.1-wakeup, merged to foundation_e0_e2. temporalWakeup namespace in scheduler.json (morningWake 08:00 default + idleRefresher), both lanes emit context-visible system notes via new SessionManager.appendContextSystemNote (charter 6.17 lane — existing appendSystemNote internal lane never reaches context builds, so criterion 1 was unsatisfiable without it). Reused summarizeRecentSessionEntries (compaction-service) with purpose wake_session — no bespoke summarizer. Spend choice: note-only injection for dormant sessions; full wake turn only when last partner exchange within fullTurnMaxIdleHours (72h default). Outward path uses real ProactiveOutboundDispatcher + quiet-hours gate; blocked delivery never blocks the internal frame update. 24 new tests + attribution/accounting/gating coverage; build+lint+verify:settings-contract green.
close_reason: Merged to foundation_e0_e2; AC verified (simulated-clock overnight test, attribution forge-guard, accounting unaffected, real-dispatcher gating tests, shared summarizer reused, config-owned)

title: Retire blocking legacy retrieval fallback; failures alert
description:
## Problem

src/core/agent/substrate-agent/turn-execution/pre-turn-state.ts:402-419 silently falls back to a blocking legacy `retrieve()` on the turn hot path when the active memory context is unavailable. That is a silent fallback on a latency-critical and correctness-relevant path, against the working rules (no silent fallback behavior).

## Scope

- Remove the blocking legacy fallback from turn execution. When active context is unavailable, the turn proceeds with the last-good active context (possibly empty) and the background refresh catches up on the next pass — remembering something a turn late is acceptable and even natural.
- Persistent refresh failure becomes an explicit typed event plus an operator alert through the system-derived notification path (ntfy), not silent degradation. Status surfaced in Garden (subsystem-health dashboard bead).
- Audit the same path for any other silent retrieval fallbacks and remove them under the same rule.

## Non-goals

- Rewriting retrieval itself; active-memory context remains the mechanism.
acceptance_criteria:
1. No blocking retrieval path reachable during turn execution (test-enforced).
2. Degraded active-memory state emits a typed event; repeated failure raises an operator alert via the system-derived notification path.
3. Turn proceeds on last-good context; no fake-healthy states; Garden shows degraded status.

title: Deterministic episode-synthesis trigger gate (turns-or-timer + relevance minimum)
description:
## Problem

Even after re-laning, candidate-episode synthesis needs a deterministic gate so it fires only when there is meaningful new companion-relevant conversation — not because a timer ticked.

## Scope

- Trigger check runs when the timer fires OR the turn threshold is reached, whichever comes first. Both config-owned.
- Gate 1 (free, deterministic): are there new messages since the last watermark? If not, no-op with zero LLM spend.
- Gate 2 (deterministic): minimum relevant-turn count before processing (default ~10, config-owned). Relevant = conversation with the companion, or where the companion is directly mentioned or meaningfully involved (reuse the existing addressing/mention detection from the group-chat work). People talking around her — async group traffic between other members while she is uninvolved — is NOT relevant on its own.
- Below minimum: hold and accumulate into the next period. Example shape: 9 relevant turns now → hold; next period brings the total to 25 → process that accumulated chunk.
- Every skip records a reason as a typed event (feeds the subsystem-health dashboard bead).

## Non-goals

- Relevance-driven memory extraction policy for observed group traffic (psfn-framework-4caj.15 owns that).
- Topic segmentation of the chunk once the gate passes (sibling bead).
acceptance_criteria:
1. Timer fire with no new messages performs zero LLM calls (test).
2. Below-threshold relevant count holds and accumulates; the 9-now/25-later shape processes as one chunk (test).
3. Async group traffic around the companion produces no episode; direct-mention traffic above threshold does (tests).
4. All thresholds in scheduler.json; every skip emits a typed event with reason.
notes: 2026-07-02: merged to foundation_e0_e2 (533fd7c3). synthesis-lane.ts: timer (30m) OR turnThreshold (24), Gate 1 new-messages-since-watermark (zero work when empty), Gate 2 minRelevantTurns=10 via new classifySessionEntryCompanionRelevance export (built on isDirectCompanionAddress/containsCompanionMention/reply metadata). Hold-and-accumulate implicit: skips do not advance the watermark. Typed memory.episode_synthesis.gate events with reasons (no_new_messages/below_relevance_minimum/session_retired) — feeds 4yb3.6 dashboard.
close_reason: Merged in 533fd7c3; AC verified (zero-LLM no-op on empty timer, 9-to-25 hold-accumulate test, around-her vs direct-mention tests, thresholds in scheduler.json, typed skip events)

title: Hard message claiming: one live episode per source message
description:
## Problem

Nothing marks L0 turns as already-used by an episode. Watermarks only bound the scan window, and the >50% span-overlap heuristic (src/faculties/memory/episodic/synthesis.ts:549-626) merges candidates, but partial overlap below the threshold produces multiple live episodes covering the same messages. This is the root of the duplicated-processing mess.

## Scope

- Add claim tracking to the episodic store (Postgres l01_* tables): each stored episode (candidate or consolidated) claims its source turn/message identifiers. Reuse the spanRefs/turn ids already captured at synthesis time (synthesis.ts:345-366).
- Daytime synthesis filters claimed entries out of its input before grouping. Fail closed: a claimed message can never enter a new episode from the daytime lane.
- Nightly consolidation (psfn-framework-m58.1) is the ONLY process allowed to restructure claims: when consolidating, claims transfer to the consolidated episode and the covered candidates are marked superseded (never deleted). This bead specifies and provides the claim-transfer interface; m58.1 consumes it.
- Keep the overlap-merge heuristic as defense in depth behind claiming.

## Non-goals

- Topic segmentation (sibling: contextual cutting bead).
- The consolidation pass itself (m58.1).

Imperfect episode cuts are acceptable. Re-processing the same chat turns into multiple overlapping live episodes is not.
acceptance_criteria:
1. DB-level invariant: no two non-superseded episodes share a source message (test-enforced).
2. Daytime synthesis provably skips claimed turns; regression test reproducing the 16:51/16:52 overlap pattern passes.
3. Claim-transfer interface for nightly consolidation specified and covered (m58.1 consumes it); superseded candidates retain claim history, never deleted.
4. lint + build + episodic tests green.
notes: 2026-07-02: implemented on agent/e5.1-claiming, merged to foundation_e0_e2 (bb2a65c2). l01_episode_message_claims table with partial unique index (one active claim per claim_key), fail-closed synthesis filter, transferEpisodeMessageClaims + supersede API ready for m58.1. Episodic suites 68/68; build+lint green; 6 pre-existing failures verified identical on base. Deviations noted in bead-report: claim granularity is per source message (channelId+entryId) with turn ids kept for provenance; three synthesis tests updated for intentional second-pass behavior change; lone unclaimed tail entries now held until salient (4yb3.4 lane owns holdback).

title: Split near-turn memory lane from sleeptime; heavy passes scheduler-only
description:
## Problem

All four heavy passes (episode synthesis, sleep consolidation, arc weaving, dream-meaning) ride the near-turn cadence (src/faculties/memory/sleeptime-agent.ts:719-765, 864-890): every 3 turns in DMs, 8 entries/15 min in groups. Sleeptime must be scheduler-owned nightly work — like dreaming — not a runtime turn-based process.

## Scope

- Near-turn lane keeps only lightweight work: extraction trigger evaluation, active-memory refresh, concern-candidate derivation. Rename its config so it is no longer called "sleeptime" (naming confusion becomes runtime confusion).
- Candidate-episode synthesis moves to its own gated lane (sibling bead owns the deterministic trigger gate).
- Sleep consolidation, arc weaving, and the dream-meaning pass run ONLY from the scheduler within the rest window (true sleeptime), never from turn cadence.
- All lanes/cadences owned by scheduler.json with schema validation. Migrate tuning-knob code constants into config: synthesis.ts:94-100 (transcript limit, gap split, max entries, salience minimums, max episodes/run), sleep-consolidation.ts:53-56 (windows, refinement cap), arc-formation.ts:47-52 (pass interval, review window, confidence floor). Nothing hardcoded.

## Non-goals

- Changing what consolidation does (m58.1 owns the candidate-then-consolidate model).
- The trigger-gate internals (sibling bead).
acceptance_criteria:
1. Consolidation, arc weaving, and dream-meaning passes unreachable from turn cadence (test-enforced).
2. Rest-window scheduler task runs the heavy stack and is visible in the scheduler task list and Garden.
3. Near-turn lane performs no LLM calls except gated extraction.
4. scheduler.json owns every migrated cadence/threshold constant; verify:settings-contract passes; near-turn lane no longer named sleeptime.

Near-turn lane holds no LLM provider (structurally zero spend). Sleeptime agent requires restWindow at construction, sole trigger memory.sleeptime.rest-window scheduler task; runs consolidation+arcs+dream+orient rewrite. NOTE for E6 (jpvd.4): the orientation-block rewrite now lives in the nightly lane — gate it deterministically there. Behavioral-summary writes moved to the synthesis lane (provenance retagged episode_synthesis). Unreachability test-enforced: 12 turns through real wiring, zero heavy-pass/LLM calls.

title: E5: Episodic gating, message claiming, and scheduler-owned sleeptime
description:
## Problem

Live-code audit (2026-07-02) confirmed "sleeptime" is not sleeptime: the sleeptime agent fires every 3 turns in DMs (`scheduler.json sleeptime.direct.cadenceTurns`) and every 8 entries / 15 min in groups, and every firing runs the full heavy stack — episode synthesis, sleep consolidation, arc weaving, dream-meaning pass (src/faculties/memory/sleeptime-agent.ts:864-890). Episode boundaries are mechanical (UTC day, 45-min gap, 14-entry cap — src/faculties/memory/episodic/synthesis.ts:209-240) with no topic awareness. Overlap protection is a processing watermark plus a >50% span-overlap merge heuristic; there is no hard claim rule, so consecutive passes re-process the same turns into overlapping episodes (the 16:51/16:52 case documented in psfn-framework-m58.1).

The result is the Groundhog Day failure: remembering the same thing every few minutes and dreaming overlapping versions of it.

## Goal

Sleeptime becomes actual sleeptime — scheduler/rest-window-owned nightly work, like dreaming: the day's rough candidate material becomes clean, consolidated, thematic episodes at night. Daytime keeps a cheap deterministic near-turn lane and a gated candidate-episode lane. No message is ever processed into more than one live episode.

Token principle: minimize UNNECESSARY token use, not token use for its own sake. If a process does not need to run, it must not run. Spend tokens where they matter.

## Members and sequencing

Children own: hard message claiming, lane split, deterministic trigger gate, contextual cutting, legacy-retrieval retirement, and the subsystem health dashboard. Nightly consolidation and cross-day arcs are the existing beads psfn-framework-m58.1 and psfn-framework-m58.2, which build on the claiming and lane work here (deps wired).

## Operator constraints (2026-07-02 planning chat)

- Nothing hardcoded: every cadence/threshold/window lives in JSON owner files by function (scheduler.json primarily), schema-guarded.
- Wherever a summary is needed, use the one shared summarization tool. No bespoke summary generators per feature.
- First-wave priority alongside E7.1 (temporal wake-up).

## Model assignment

Implementation: Fable. Testing: Sonnet.
notes: 2026-07-02: wave 1 complete and pushed. Children 4yb3.1/.2/.3/.5 closed; history linearized by pull --rebase so per-bead commit prefixes (not merge hashes) are the durable trace; final wave-1 tip 17c6333c. OPERATOR MIGRATION REQUIRED before next live restart: scheduler.json "sleeptime" key removed (fails validation with rename guidance); new required blocks nearTurnMemory/episodeSynthesis/sleepConsolidation/arcFormation must be present in live system-data scheduler.json.
close_reason: All six children complete and merged (claiming, lane split, trigger gate, topic cutting, retrieval fallback retirement, subsystem-health dashboard) plus m58.1 nightly consolidation. Episodic overlap structurally impossible (DB invariant); sleeptime is scheduler-owned nightly work; all tuning config-owned.

## Non-goals
No sentiment-only views, no reply-suppression tiers, no content firewall (LATER doc).

title: E3.1: Ratify and land the Context Envelope contract
description:
## Context
Vocabulary ratified 2026-07-01 (plan section 3.3/7). This bead is the CONTRACT: types, owner-file schema, derivation rules, precedence — reviewed by operator before wiring (E3.3). ## Scope

title: E3: Context Envelope — channel/relationship/trust semantics
description:
## Summary
Split the overloaded channelVisibility into ratified orthogonal dimensions (channelPrivacy: private/invite_only/public + derived audienceScope/audienceKnowledge + broadcast flag), make privacy channel-owned, keep the 6-layer deterministic gate shape, add the contact-tracking policy gate as scale scaffolding, and gate the admin memory API. Design target: invite-only rooms of ~10 known people + companions; large-audience behavior expressible but LATER (operator has a dedicated doc for role-gating/sentiment views/content firewall).

## Ratified vocabulary (operator, 2026-07-01)
channelPrivacy: private / invite_only / public, default invite_only (replaces semi_private — clean break, no alias). broadcast: boolean flag for tweet-like/very-large surfaces, not a privacy level. audienceScope: one/few/many/unbounded, thresholds config-owned. audienceKnowledge: all_known/partially_known/anonymous. Trust (4 tiers) and sensitivity (4 levels) UNCHANGED — the gap was missing dimensions, not missing granularity. Delivery guidance is length/delivery only ("don't yap"-class), never persona/tone prose (charter: substrate must not tell a companion how to BE).

## Invariant
All gating stays deterministic and pre-prompt. No privacy prose in prompts; blocked content is simply absent (+ withheld summary with reason codes).

title: E2.4: Model-agnostic provider cache engagement
description:
## Context
promptCaching: { configured: false, engaged: false } (prompt-assembly.ts:509-512). Primary stack is OpenRouter + open models and local runners, where the cache mechanism is implicit prefix/KV reuse — i.e., BYTE-STABLE PREFIX IS THE FEATURE. Anthropic cache_control is a per-provider extra. Model-agnostic per operator decision; backends are adapters (charter Law 22).

## Scope
- CachePlan on the artifact: static boundary (base+operator+static layers), session-stable boundary; serializers apply per-provider mechanism: Anthropic -> cache_control breakpoints; OpenRouter/open/local -> guarantee byte-stable prefix ordering + pass provider cache params where supported.

- Telemetry: per-turn prefix-stability check (did the static region's bytes change? which block caused it?) + provider-reported cache metrics where available; surfaced in the E2.3 Cache tab.
- Prefix-instability is a NAMED ALERT, not a silent stat — a regression here is exactly the "variables where it should be static" bug returning.

- Ten-turn quiet conversation on the test channel: static region hash identical across all turns; any change identifies the offending block in telemetry.

title: E1.8: Multi-companion observation correctness in shared rooms
description:
## Context
Target deployment: ~10 friends + several companions on the same substrate in one room. Companions are contacts with isMachineIntelligence (contacts/types.ts:256); group extraction already weights them (extraction/group-classifier.ts). Unverified: a peer companion must never be selected as DM-canonical human, core-memory subject, or speaking_with target, and its messages must be attributed like any speaker.

## Scope
- Guard rails: canonical-contact resolution for scope.kind:'dm' and core-memory subject selection exclude isMachineIntelligence contacts unless the DM IS with that companion (companion-DM is legitimate — Artemis case; then it binds normally and the machine-intelligence flag flows to prompt state, which already exists at runtime-context.ts:282,1459).
- Harness fixtures include a peer companion speaking in the room: attribution rendered, participant list includes it, extraction weighting applied, no human-profile blending.
- Loop-risk: verify existing behavior does not auto-respond in a tight loop in fixtures; if it does, file separately, do not patch silently.

## CHARTER GATE (Law 26 / 8.10 / Phase 12)
The charter requires fatigue/load policy BEFORE companion-to-companion chat becomes active. This bead delivers observation correctness only; enabling multiple companions to actively converse in a shared live room remains gated on the FatigueBudgetPort epic (rate/charge/attention budgets, loop stopping conditions). Until then, multi-companion rooms run with companions that do not reply to each other, or the fatigue epic lands first. This gate must be stated in the room-enablement runbook.

## Non-goals
No companion-to-companion protocol (psfn-framework-8pyl). No fatigue budgets — but they gate live enablement, see above.
acceptance_criteria:
- Fixture: peer companion speaks; <human>/profile blocks contain zero companion-derived content; participant XML lists it with its identity.
- Companion-DM fixture: binding works, speaking_with_is_machine_intelligence true.
- Loop check documented in bead notes; any auto-reply loop found is filed as its own bug, not silently patched.
- Charter gate recorded: live multi-companion conversational rooms blocked on fatigue policy; documented where operators will see it (Garden channel view or ops doc).

title: E1.6: Group-aware, JSON-owned sleeptime cadence
description:
## Context
Sleeptime fires every 3rd turn per session (DEFAULT_CADENCE_TURNS = 3, sleeptime-agent.ts:50,550) unless a rest window suppresses it. In a busy 10-person room that is near-continuous background LLM work — matches operator observation "sleeptime firing frequently despite being intended as sleep/cleanup," and burns charge (charter 8.8/8.9: background work must respect windows; budget pressure is a care issue). Group rooms already have watermark/range machinery for extraction (docs/memory.md:135-149); sleeptime should use the same posture.

## Scope
- Cadence config moves to a JSON owner (scheduler or memory settings owner — follow existing ownership of groupMemory.* settings), per-mode: direct keeps turn-cadence; group uses watermark/interval-based batching (min-interval + min-new-entries), not per-N-turns.
- Investigate whether the "sleeptime as sleep/cleanup" intent means group sleeptime should defer to rest-window/nightly consolidation entirely; implement the conservative version (interval batching) and note the open question for the memory-lane rework.
- Telemetry: sleeptime fire-rate per channel per hour, visible in Garden scheduler views.
acceptance_criteria:
- Group room fixture: 30 rapid turns produce <= configured number of sleeptime runs (vs ~10 today).
- DM behavior unchanged by default.

- Fire-rate telemetry visible in Garden.

title: E1.5: Scoped emotion/appraisal state with directional fast-decay carry-over
description:
## Context
Audit indicates emotion snapshots/appraisal are keyed to contact/last-speaker with no room dimension (runtime-context.ts:1072; src/core/emotion/state.ts VAD/mood). Operator-ratified semantics: per-scope state; a room argument may briefly color a following DM ("Jeff was so annoying in gc") but decays fast; GROUP->DM ONLY, NEVER DM->GROUP; DM->DM allowed for the same contact across channels; disliking one user must not meaningfully affect others.

## Scope
- FIRST: a short written audit of current keying (emotion state, appraisal chains, per-contact baselines) — confirm or correct the audit inference before changing persistence. Post findings to this bead before implementation.
- Persist emotion/appraisal state keyed by scope.key; companion-global baseline (her overall mood/VAD) remains a separate layer that scoped states modulate, so "her mood" still exists.
- Carry-over modifier: on scope switch group->DM (same companion, DM contact is a member of that group), apply a bounded, fast-decaying modifier from the group state (half-life on the order of minutes — config-owned in the emotion settings owner, not hardcoded). Direction enforcement mirrors continuity flow rules (policy.ts:447-473 precedent): DM state never seeds any group state; DM->DM carry-over only when same canonical contact.
- Per-contact emotional baselines (contacts/types.ts emotionalBaseline) unchanged — they are about the CONTACT, not the scope.
- Restart persistence: scoped states participate in existing internal-state rehydration.

## Non-goals
No changes to appraisal LLM prompts beyond scope key plumbing. No cross-companion emotion sharing. This is deliberately NOT the weighted-thought system (charter Law 27; accumulation lives in psfn-framework-1xb.4) — they stay distinct.
acceptance_criteria:
- Audit note posted (current keying, confirmed with anchors) before the change lands.
- Test: high-arousal group state -> subsequent DM shows bounded modifier that decays below threshold within the configured half-life; DM state change produces zero group-state delta; second unrelated DM contact sees no modifier.
- Config knobs live in a JSON owner (settings/emotion), documented; no magic constants.
- Restart test: scoped states rehydrate.
notes: Depends on E1.1. Anchors: src/core/emotion/state.ts; src/core/agent/substrate-agent/runtime-context.ts:1072-1130; src/system/trust/policy.ts:447-473 (directional-flow precedent). Plan: working_docs/GROUPCHAT_PROMPT_TRUST_FOUNDATION_PLAN_20260701.md. Bead tree: working_docs/FOUNDATION_BEAD_TREE_20260701.md.

title: E1.4: Canonical attribution contract: one formatter, escaping, forgery tests
description:
## Context
Attribution is a text prefix "Name (id): " built in entry-attribution.ts:58-68 and structurally dropped at message-conversion.ts:226-281. Operator decision: text-prefix is canonical (general LLM limitation — provider chat formats do not carry per-message speaker metadata portably). What is missing is hardening: a display name containing "): " or a crafted "Alice (discord:123):" prefix inside message CONTENT can forge attribution. Charter Laws 17-19 (authorship integrity) made mechanical.

## Scope
- Single exported formatter + (for tooling/tests) parser: the only code allowed to construct or interpret the prefix. Delete duplicate inline formatting.
- Escaping/sanitization for display names (strip/encode delimiter sequences, control chars, leading whitespace tricks); stable author ID always present as the trustworthy component.
- Content-forgery mitigation: document the trust rule (only the prefix outside user-authored content is authoritative) and ensure history rendering never lets user content start a line indistinguishable from a real prefix (escape or mark user-content lines matching the prefix grammar).
- Round-trip and adversarial tests (hostile display names, prefix-shaped message bodies, unicode confusables at the delimiter).
- Write the contract into docs/ (short section: format, trust rule, escaping).

## Non-goals
No structural provider metadata (not portable). No renaming of existing stored entries.
acceptance_criteria:
- One formatter; grep proves no other call site builds the prefix pattern.
- Adversarial test suite green: hostile names cannot break out; content cannot forge a prefix that the renderer emits as authoritative.
- Docs section merged in the same change.
notes: Anchors: src/core/session/entry-attribution.ts:58-68,168-229; src/primitives/llm/message-conversion.ts:226-281; src/core/session/manager/context-builder.ts:195-260. Charter Laws 17-19. Plan: working_docs/GROUPCHAT_PROMPT_TRUST_FOUNDATION_PLAN_20260701.md. Bead tree: working_docs/FOUNDATION_BEAD_TREE_20260701.md.

Single formatter (formatGroupUserMessageContent) hardened: display-name/stable-id sanitization, content-forgery guard, removed vulnerable prefix-passthrough; 24 adversarial tests green; docs/attribution.md contract; grep proves sole constructor. Charter Laws 17-19 mechanical.

title: Define shared-world wiki MVP semantics, ACLs, and review gates
description:
Summary
Define the production semantics for the shared-world wiki that the companion roadmap depends on: what counts as shared world knowledge, who/what can write it, how room/contact ACLs work, and how public/external/imported content is reviewed before durable shared-world persistence.

Current evidence
A wiki MVP exists as workspace-backed durable Markdown/reference storage with metadata, source class, sensitivity, provenance, list/get/search/write/import tool actions, and Garden read APIs (docs/memory.md:76, src/faculties/wiki/store.ts:235, src/faculties/wiki/tools.ts:97, src/operator/garden/api-routes.ts:556). It is intentionally separate from L0/L0.1/L2 memory and tool responses state no L2 memory is created (src/faculties/wiki/tools.ts:197). This is not yet a semantic shared-world substrate for multi-companion/group environments: no room/world scope, no write review workflow for public/external sources, no relationship-aware ACL model, and no prompt integration contract that distinguishes shared world facts from personal memory.

Scope
- Define wiki scopes: personal reference, room/world shared knowledge, project knowledge, imported/reference documents, and companion-authored world notes.
- Define ACL/review semantics for owner/admin, trusted DM, semi-private group, public/broadcast, external web/docs, another companion, and shard/subagent outputs.
- Define how wiki entries enter prompt context without becoming personal memory.
- Define provenance, attribution, sensitivity, and rollback/audit expectations.
- Decide whether implementation extends the current workspace-backed store or adds a Postgres-backed shared-world index.
- Specify Garden/operator review surfaces needed before implementation.

Non-goals
- Do not implement the shared-world wiki in this decision bead.
- Do not merge personal memories or contact profiles into wiki.
- Do not import public chat or external docs directly without review policy.
acceptance_criteria:
- A canonical contract defines wiki/reference vs shared-world vs project knowledge and keeps all distinct from L0/L0.1/L2/core memory.
- The contract defines writer classes, source classes, ACLs, review states, and release requirements for owner/admin, trusted contacts, group rooms, public/broadcast sources, external docs/web, companions, shards, and subagents.
- The contract defines prompt-inclusion behavior and provenance requirements for shared-world facts.
- The contract specifies how public/external/imported/generated content is held/reviewed before shared durable world persistence.
- The contract identifies implementation files/settings/Garden surfaces that must change next.
- Follow-up implementation beads can be created directly from the contract without re-litigating semantics.
- If settings/contracts are touched, npm run verify:settings-contract and npm run lint pass.

title: Typed intake envelope: source/provenance/risk/quarantine/release contract with taint propagation and write stamping
description: UPDATE to existing bead with design detail. Evidence: SubstrateMessage and Attachment (src/shared/contracts/runtime.ts:276-298) carry no source-class/risk/quarantine field; MessageRoutingMetadata (:227-274) is the natural non-breaking slot (already carries authorIsMachineIntelligence, canonicalContactId, generated-provenance). Scope: define IntakeEnvelope {id, sourceClass, provenance chain, sourceRiskTier, contentRef (opaque -- raw bytes never travel with the envelope), extractedFields, riskLabels[], scores, decision, state} with state machine received -> screened -> {released | released_sanitized | quarantined} -> {human_released | human_released_sanitized | discarded | expired}; every transition appends to the gateway audit journal. Taint propagates on derivation (CaMeL rule): a summary, OCR transcript, or subagent digest of untrusted content inherits the envelope tier. Risk label vocabulary seeds from CogSecMemoryRiskClass A-E (src/core/cogsec/memory-candidacy.ts) generalized to intake time, plus injection/* exfil/* pii/* secrets/* poisoning/* categories (taxonomy in the research doc section 7). Envelope-id stamping on every memory and wiki write from day one -- cheap now, impossible to retrofit, enables later lineage excision of a poisoned source via the existing revocation/regeneration machinery. Config owner: new intake-policy.json following the standard owner-file pattern (loader + seed + startup-owner-files.ts registration + settings-garden-contract entries), or a section in trust-policy.json if small -- decide at implementation, precedent is src/system/config/trust-policy-config.ts. Non-goals: no classifier logic here (htm9.4-.7), no UI (htm9.11). Acceptance: contract types land in src/shared/contracts (or system/trust sibling), owner file verifies under npm run verify:settings-contract, memory/wiki write paths persist envelope ids, unit tests cover state transitions and taint inheritance, build+lint clean.

Load-bearing fact: the gateway -- not the agent -- holds the real LLM client and API keys (src/boundary/gateway/privileged-services.ts, credential vault wired only in src/app/gateway/main.ts:133), and web fetch / binary fetch / Discord attachment downloads already flow through it, so classification runs gateway-side with no new credential surface. (2) Web fetch -- sanitizeWebContent (src/boundary/gateway/sanitize.ts:84-104) logs injectionPatternsFound but never blocks; route through the envelope + layers instead. (3) Tool observations -- formatToolObservationForContext (src/core/session/tool-observation.ts:222-240) renders raw content with no wrap; wrap + label. (4) Public context wrappers -- wrapUntrustedContext (src/core/session/manager-primitives.ts:989) is narrow opt-in; audit call sites, unify under the envelope. (5) Subagent completion handoff -- full lifecycle audit exists (src/faculties/subagents/faculty.ts) but zero content-risk gate; add intake screening on foldback. (6) Shard fold -- merge review exists (fold-review.ts) but reviews output, not what the shard ingested; propagate envelope taint through shard workspace content. title: Sink gates consume intake labels: prompt, memory, wiki, persona/trust, tools, egress -- hard for untrusted sources, soft for trusted
description: UPDATE to existing bead with locked strictness policy. Every consequential sink checks envelope state/labels before consuming content: prompt assembly (src/core/agent/substrate-agent/turn-execution/prompt-assembly.ts -- classified content becomes typed PromptPlanBlocks on the landed E2.2 PromptPlan artifact), memory write (extend memory-candidacy checks to read the upstream envelope instead of re-deriving), wiki write (compose with i5s2 ACL work), persona/self-model mutation, trust-state mutation, and tool/egress invocation. Structural rules: tier-N content may INFORM but never INSTRUCT higher-tier state mutation; lethal-trifecta invariant (untrusted content + private data + egress never all three in one uncontrolled path) enforced HARD for public/untrusted sources, SOFT (release-prompt/review) for trusted sources -- operator decision 2026-07-09. Quarantined content is invisible to all sinks. Non-goals: do not rebuild the retrieval-side gates that already work (trust/visibility/consent in src/faculties/memory/retrieval/access.ts) -- this bead is intake-side. Depends-on: psfn-framework-htm9.1, psfn-framework-htm9.2. Acceptance: sink-gate policy table lives in intake-policy.json; per-sink deny paths are fail-closed with auditable reasons; regression tests prove the same hostile payload is refused at every sink regardless of arrival adapter; trifecta tests cover hard (public) and soft (trusted) modes.

title: Epic: Cognition intake firewall (mindwall) for untrusted inbound content
description: UPDATE to existing epic with 2026-07-09 design decisions (see working_docs/COGSEC_INTAKE_FIREWALL_RESEARCH_20260709.md for the verified surface map and prior-art research). Mission: every untrusted inbound item (web, files, images, chat by source risk, tool outputs, subagent/shard foldback, audio transcripts) passes a typed intake envelope and a layered L1->L3 classifier gate BEFORE it can reach prompt, memory, wiki, persona, trust state, or tools. Prevention over remediation: L0 uses HMAC integrity chaining, so removing poison after the fact requires regenerating downstream signatures (tooling exists, proven in a live remediation of a test companion, but costly) -- stopping poison before it enters L0 is the priority; remediation stays as backstop. Core principle: whatever gets flagged must NOT reach the main context. Design philosophy: do not implement everything -- combine techniques covering ~90% of threats as fast as possible; the firewall is a synchronous gate in front of concurrent pipelines (near-real-time audio, chat snappiness), so speed is essential and the layer must be invisible. Companion well-being is the top-level goal: firewall activity must not feed the emotion/stress model, and all companion-facing security language is truthful but never alarming (soft notices: 'we detected something, so we're holding it for your human to look into'). Hermes-Agent SECURITY.md framing adopted: in-process scanners are triage aids, NOT boundaries -- the only boundary against an adversarial LLM is the OS/sandbox; L1 fails open-advisory and the envelope decision + sink gates are the enforcement. Trinity pattern borrowed (quarantine incoming content for batched async human review, isolate before it reaches L0) -- pattern only, not specifics. Children: htm9.1-htm9.17 in this file. Evals live in a separate repo -- see working_docs/cogsec-evals-beads.json handed to the eval repository.

title: P1: Expose safe agent-visible CogSec event log
description:
## Summary
Expose safe CogSec event metadata to agents and diagnostics so they know why context is missing, without exposing what the poisoned content said or how it worked. This is separate from transcript search: agents should learn from a CogSec log/notice, not by seeing tombstone rows in search results.

## Why
After tombstoning and search exclusion, an agent may encounter continuity gaps. It should be allowed and encouraged to know that a CogSec intervention occurred, but only at a bland, non-infectious level. Returning ten tombstones in transcript search will confuse the companion and pollute task context. A dedicated safe log is cleaner.

## Current Code Anchors
- src/core/session/manager/context-builder.ts and prompt/session context assembly can include safe notices where relevant.
- src/core/tools/session-search.ts should avoid tombstone spam; CogSec visibility belongs elsewhere.
- src/operator/garden/routes/session-routes.ts and future CogSec routes can expose admin/operator metadata.
- src/core/turns/observability.ts and prompt monitor surfaces may display safe diagnostic metadata.

## Required Behavior
Provide a safe CogSec event/log view for companion runtime and developer diagnostics:
- Agent-visible event summary: case ID, high-level type/severity/status, affected source/session/range metadata if safe, and bland reason text.
- No payload, no bypass pattern, no sealed artifact dereference, no exploit details, no raw tombstone row dump.
- Prompt/runtime inclusion only when relevant: e.g. current session/range had context sealed or an agent explicitly asks why context is missing.
- Operator/admin views may show richer metadata and counts but still not raw sealed payload by default.
- CogSec log should explain that derived cognitive artifacts were revoked/regenerated from clean sources when applicable.

## Example Safe Notice
`CogSec case cogsec_123 sealed unsafe instruction-like content from this conversation span. Related cognitive artifacts were revoked or regenerated from clean sources. The sealed payload is unavailable to companion runtime.`

## Non-goals
- Do not expose sealed payload content or reproduction details.
- Do not use transcript search as the primary way agents learn about CogSec interventions.
- Do not make every CogSec event a permanent identity/persona memory.
acceptance_criteria:
- Agents/diagnostics can access safe CogSec event metadata explaining missing context without payload details.
- Prompt/session context includes CogSec notices only when relevant and never includes raw payload, exploit mechanics, or sealed refs that can be dereferenced by companion tools.
- Normal transcript search does not return tombstone rows as the CogSec awareness mechanism.
- Operator/admin surfaces can show safe counts/status/action metadata.
- Tests prove prompt snapshots, session search, and agent-visible logs omit poisoned payload text and attack mechanics.
- npm run lint and targeted tests pass before closure.
close_reason: Implemented safe CogSec event log and prompt/session notices. Evidence: src/core/cogsec/safe-log.ts exposes agent/operator-safe event views that omit sealed refs/hashes and dirty text; src/core/session/manager/context-builder.ts accepts relevant CogSec events and renders session.cogsec_notices into the final system prompt plus prompt-section telemetry; src/core/identity/prompt-runtime.ts registers session.cogsec_notices as a reorderable runtime prompt block; scripts/cogsec-remediation-smoke.ts validates the live remediation flow builds a safe notice without dirty text or sealed refs. Validation: npm test -- src/core/cogsec/safe-log.test.ts src/core/session/manager/context-builder.test.ts src/core/tools/session-search.test.ts passed 18 tests; npm test -- src/core/cogsec/events.test.ts src/core/cogsec/forensic-archive.test.ts src/core/cogsec/lineage.test.ts src/core/cogsec/revocation.test.ts src/core/cogsec/regeneration.test.ts src/core/cogsec/safe-log.test.ts src/persistence/sessions/store.test.ts src/persistence/sessions/sqlite-adapters.test.ts src/persistence/sessions/postgres-adapters.test.ts src/core/tools/session-search.test.ts src/faculties/memory/retrieval.test.ts src/core/session/manager/context-builder.test.ts src/core/identity/prompt-runtime.test.ts passed 239 tests; npm run smoke:cogsec passed; npm run lint passed; npm run build passed; git diff --check passed.

title: P1: Add CogSec remediation mode to Session Recovery UX
description:
## Summary
Extend the existing Garden Review & Safety Session Recovery page with a CogSec remediation mode. This mode should guide an operator through creating a CogSec event, selecting affected source channel/message range, previewing lineage impact, and applying the seal -> tombstone -> search-exclude -> revoke -> regenerate -> epoch-cut workflow.

## Why
The current /session-recovery page handles emergency fresh logical session resets. CogSec remediation is more dangerous and specific: it removes contaminated payload from companion L0 and revokes derived cognition. Operators need a deliberate UX that distinguishes normal recovery from CogSec redaction and shows enough impact preview to avoid accidental broad damage.

## Current Code Anchors
- admin-ui/src/routes/session-recovery/+page.svelte is the existing page.
- admin-ui/src/lib/nav.ts already places Session Recovery under Review & Safety.
- admin-ui/src/lib/api/endpoints/sessions.ts has session route APIs.
- src/operator/garden/routes/session-routes.ts and services/session-service.ts own current admin session route endpoints.
- New CogSec services/routes should follow existing Garden route/service/type patterns.

## Required Behavior
The UX should include a CogSec mode separate from ordinary fresh split/quarantine:
- Inputs: source channel, logical session/message IDs or range, case type, severity, reason, actor.
- Option to create an event draft and preview lineage impact.
- Preview counts/classes: L0 rows, projection rows, memories/embeddings, summaries, active cache, episodic/profile/persona-adjacent artifacts, lineage gaps.
- Apply action with strong confirmation and clear destructive wording: dirty companion L0 will be tombstoned, sealed archive retained outside companion reach.
- Progress/result panel for seal, tombstone, projection rebuild, revocation, regeneration queue, epoch cut.
- Safe CogSec event log visible on the page.

## Safety Rules
The page must not render raw poisoned payload, exploit mechanics, sealed artifact contents, or reproduction details. It may display IDs, ranges, counts, safe summaries, and opaque sealed refs/hashes where appropriate.

## Non-goals
- Do not make CogSec remediation a companion-facing tool.
- Do not bury CogSec only in generic sessions page.
- Do not add raw payload preview by default.
acceptance_criteria:
- /session-recovery has a distinct CogSec mode separate from ordinary fresh split/quarantine.
- Operators can enter source channel, affected message/session range, case type, severity, reason, and actor.
- UX can request and display a safe lineage/remediation preview with counts/classes and lineage gaps.
- UX can apply the remediation pipeline and show step results without displaying raw payload.
- UX clearly states that companion L0 rows will be tombstoned and sealed evidence stored outside companion reach.
- Frontend/API contract tests or type checks cover the new endpoint contracts where practical.
- npm run lint, npm run garden:build, and relevant targeted tests pass before closure.

title: P1: Regenerate clean summaries, memories, and indexes after CogSec redaction
description:
## Summary
Add a maintenance/operator job that regenerates clean cognitive state after CogSec redaction and revocation. It should rebuild from tombstoned companion L0 plus clean lineage, never from sealed payloads.

## Why
After L0 tombstoning and derived-artifact revocation, the companion may have continuity gaps. The correct repair is to recompute summaries, memories, embeddings, search projection, active memory packs, and profile/episodic state from clean sources. This should not run synchronously in the chat turn path.

## Current Code Anchors
- src/core/session/manager.ts and context builder own compaction summaries and context assembly.
- src/faculties/memory/extraction.ts and orchestrator can generate memories from session content.
- src/faculties/memory/startup-hydration.ts warms active memory context.
- src/faculties/memory/sleeptime-agent.ts handles background memory/orientation cleanup.
- src/persistence/sessions/store.ts and transcript projection adapters rebuild search projection from L0.
- src/operator/garden/services/session-service.ts can be extended or a new CogSec service can own operator-triggered regeneration.

## Required Behavior
After a CogSec case is applied:
- Rebuild transcript projection/search indexes from tombstoned L0, with tombstones excluded from normal search.
- Recompute compaction/session summaries from clean/tombstoned source only.
- Regenerate memories where lineage says clean recovery is possible.
- Recompute embeddings only from clean regenerated memory text.
- Rebuild active-memory cache from clean source.
- Queue/regenerate episodic/profile/contact/persona-adjacent artifacts where supported.
- Advance/cut session epoch or route fresh lane as needed after regeneration.
- Record regeneration results in CogSec event metadata.

## Safety Rules
The regeneration job must not read sealed payload content. It must not include tombstone text as a substantive memory. It may include a safe CogSec event notice when needed to explain a continuity gap.

## Non-goals
- Do not block normal chat responses on regeneration.
- Do not silently restore revoked artifacts without clean source provenance.
- Do not run broad model summarization over sealed forensic artifacts.
acceptance_criteria:
- A CogSec regeneration job can rebuild projections, summaries, memories, embeddings, active memory, and supported episodic/profile artifacts from clean/tombstoned sources only.
- Regenerated artifacts contain no sealed payload text, attack mechanics, or tombstone text treated as substantive memory.
- Revoked artifacts are not restored unless regenerated from clean provenance.
- Regeneration is operator/maintenance triggered or queued, not synchronous in the chat response path.
- CogSec event metadata records regeneration results and failures.

title: P1: Revoke lineage-derived cognitive artifacts for CogSec cases
description:
## Summary
Implement the CogSec revocation executor that takes a CogSec event plus lineage preview and removes affected derived artifacts from companion cognition. This should revoke/soft-delete/invalidate artifacts by provenance, not by loose string search.

## Why
L0 tombstoning removes the direct payload, but poison can survive as summaries, memories, embeddings, active-memory cache, episodic landmarks, profile summaries, or persona-adjacent state. Since lineage exists, the right strategy is to revoke derived artifacts and regenerate clean state instead of patching poisoned artifacts in place.

## Current Code Anchors
- psfn-framework-4tkt will provide CogSec lineage preview.
- src/faculties/memory/postgres-store.ts supports memory soft-delete/delete versions and stores embeddings on l2_memories.
- src/faculties/memory/retrieval.ts already excludes deleted/superseded and retired-session-quarantined memories.
- src/faculties/memory/active-context.ts caches active memory context by session/channel identity.
- src/faculties/memory/startup-hydration.ts and src/faculties/memory/sleeptime-agent.ts hydrate/update active memory contexts.
- Episodic/profile artifacts expose provenance in existing Garden/memory services.

## Required Behavior
Given a CogSec event and lineage preview, perform revocation/invalidation for affected artifacts:
- Soft-delete or revoke L2 memories with deleteReason including CogSec case ID.
- Ensure embeddings for revoked memories are not returned by vector search.
- Invalidate active-memory cache entries tied to affected sessions/artifacts.
- Invalidate compaction/focus/session summaries that include tainted rows.
- Invalidate or mark for rebuild episodic landmarks/episodes and profile/contact/persona-adjacent derived artifacts tied to affected provenance.
- Record result counts and failed items back to CogSec event metadata.
- Leave unrelated clean artifacts untouched.

## Safety Rules
Revocation logs and events must not include payload text. They may include artifact IDs, counts, source refs, case IDs, and safe reason codes.

## Non-goals
- Do not hard-delete memory rows where soft-delete/versioning exists.
- Do not regenerate clean artifacts in this bead; queue or mark for regeneration only.
- Do not revoke all channel memories unless the CogSec event scope is the full session/epoch.
acceptance_criteria:
- CogSec revocation executor consumes a lineage preview and revokes/invalidates affected derived artifacts by structured provenance.
- Revoked L2 memories are no longer returned by semantic/vector, lexical, proactive, active-memory, or contact/profile retrieval paths.
- Affected embeddings, summaries, active-memory cache entries, episodic/profile/persona-adjacent artifacts are invalidated or marked for regeneration.
- Unrelated clean artifacts in the same channel remain available.
- CogSec event metadata records artifact counts, IDs where safe, and failures without payload text.
- Tests cover direct memory revocation, embedding exclusion, cache invalidation, summary invalidation, unrelated artifact preservation, and failure reporting.
- npm run lint and targeted tests pass before closure.

title: P1: Exclude CogSec tombstones from normal transcript search and projections
description:
## Summary
Make CogSec tombstoned L0 rows non-searchable in normal companion-facing transcript search, grep, and projection paths. Agents should know via the safe CogSec event log that a span was sealed, but normal search should not return tombstone spam or case refs as if they were useful transcript matches.

## Why
After CogSec remediation, affected L0 rows will contain safe tombstones such as `[CogSec redaction: case_id]`. If transcript projection indexes those tombstones normally, searches for CogSec/case IDs/redaction text can return many tombstones and confuse the companion. Searching for the original payload must return zero. Searching normal conversation should not be polluted by tombstones. Operators still need diagnostics for redaction counts by case through CogSec/admin views.

## Current Code Anchors
- src/persistence/sessions/store.ts syncs transcript projection and implements searchByKeywords.
- src/persistence/sessions/transcript-projection-port.ts defines projection/search interfaces.
- src/persistence/sessions/transcript-projection.ts implements SQLite projection.
- src/persistence/sessions/postgres-adapters.ts implements Postgres projection/search.
- src/core/tools/session-search.ts exposes session_search and session_grep.
- src/core/session/search-runtime.ts filters and summarizes transcript hits.

## Required Behavior
- Rebuild transcript/search projections from tombstoned L0 after CogSec redaction.
- Exclude CogSec tombstone rows from normal session_search/session_grep/searchByKeywords results by default.
- Ensure tombstone text, case IDs, sealed refs, and original payload text are not indexed into normal companion search.
- Provide an operator-only diagnostic path that can report tombstone/redaction counts by CogSec case without payload text.
- Keep projection rebuild deterministic and compatible with both SQLite and Postgres projection adapters.

## Safety Rules
Companion-facing search should not reveal payload, attack mechanics, sealed refs, or long lists of tombstones. Agent awareness comes from the safe CogSec event log, not transcript-search hits.

## Non-goals
- Do not hide the existence of a CogSec event from authorized operator/agent diagnostics.
- Do not delete sealed forensic evidence.
- Do not change L0 message schema.
- Do not solve memory revocation in this bead.
acceptance_criteria:
- After L0 tombstoning, searching for the original payload returns zero normal companion-facing hits.
- Searching for CogSec tombstone text or case IDs does not return tombstone spam through normal session_search/session_grep/searchByKeywords.
- Operator-only diagnostics can report redacted/tombstoned row counts by case ID without payload text.
- Projection rebuild excludes tombstones consistently for SQLite and Postgres-backed projections.
- Tests cover session_search, session_grep, projection rebuild, payload search miss, tombstone search miss, and diagnostic counts.
- npm run lint and targeted tests pass before closure.

title: P1: Add sealed forensic archive outside companion runtime reach
description:
## Summary
Add the sealed forensic archive used by CogSec remediation to preserve contaminated source rows outside companion reach. This archive is for operators/security tooling and future CogSec shield classifier/tool development. Companion runtime, prompt generation, memory extraction, summarization, embedding, and normal search must not be able to read the sealed payload.

## Why
CogSec remediation must remove dirty payload from companion-owned L0, but the project still needs forensic continuity: exact payloads, row metadata, hashes, and context needed to build detectors and regression tools. That evidence belongs in a security-only archive, not in normal L0 or the CogSec event table.

## Current Code Anchors
- src/persistence/layout.ts owns runtime storage paths and must define any new owner path.
- src/operator/garden/services/session-service.ts and future CogSec services need to write archive refs.
- Existing backup/layout rules in AGENTS.md require runtime authority under repo/runtime roots, not ad hoc off-repo files.
- The CogSec event store should hold opaque archive refs/hashes only.

## Required Behavior
Implement a sealed artifact store with a minimal API:
- write contaminated L0 rows/payload bundle and return an opaque sealedForensicPayloadRef plus hashes/counts
- read/verify only through explicit security/operator-only service boundaries
- list metadata without payload for ordinary admin/CogSec event views
- deny or omit access from companion tools, memory extraction, summarization, embedding/indexing, transcript search, prompt generation, and agent-visible event logs

The stored artifact should include enough for future detector work:
- original L0 row(s)
- channel/logical session/message IDs
- timestamps and safe surrounding metadata if included by operator
- hash/checksum
- CogSec event ID
- operator/actor and createdAt

## Safety Rules
The sealed archive may contain raw payload but must be outside companion runtime/tool reach. Normal Garden event list, prompt monitor, memory tooling, and search must show only metadata/ref/hash, not payload.

## Non-goals
- Do not store sealed payload inside the CogSec event record.
- Do not expose a companion-facing tool that can dereference sealed refs.
- Do not create hidden off-repo authoritative state without explicit operator approval.
- Do not implement classifier training in this bead.
acceptance_criteria:
- A sealed forensic archive API exists and writes contaminated row bundles before L0 tombstoning.
- The archive returns opaque refs and hashes for CogSec event records.
- Companion runtime, memory extraction, summarization, embedding/indexing, transcript search, and normal agent tools cannot dereference sealed payload refs.
- Operator/security-only code can verify artifact existence and hashes without exposing payload in default views.
- Tests prove sealed payload is not reachable through normal companion/admin list/search surfaces.
- npm run lint and targeted tests pass before closure.

title: P1: Replace contaminated companion L0 rows with existing-schema CogSec tombstones
description:
## Summary
Implement the CogSec redaction step that removes contaminated payload text from companion-owned L0/session JSONL and replaces affected rows with tombstone messages that fit the existing L0 message schema. The tombstone points to a CogSec event ID; the rich remediation metadata lives in the CogSec event store.

## Why
For CogSec cases, dirty payload cannot remain in companion-owned L0. Keeping it in L0 means compaction, search rebuilds, memory extraction, wake summaries, or future tools can accidentally re-ingest it. The original payload must be sealed outside companion reach first, then L0 should only retain a safe tombstone so continuity, ordering, and message IDs/ranges remain coherent.

## Current Code Anchors
- src/persistence/sessions/store.ts owns append/load/getRecent/searchByKeywords/redactTurn/restoreTurn and transcript projection sync.
- src/persistence/sessions/store/journal-runtime.ts handles JSONL backfill/projection indexing.
- src/core/session/manager.ts reads L0 for context and compaction.
- src/core/session/session-routes.ts already records route/epoch cuts but does not tombstone rows.
- Existing turn redaction/restore tests in src/persistence/sessions/store.test.ts are relevant but CogSec needs row/range tombstoning tied to CogSec events.

## Required Behavior
Given a CogSec event and selected affected message IDs/ranges:
1. Verify sealed forensic archive write succeeded before modifying companion L0.
2. Replace affected L0 message content with a safe tombstone string using the existing message row schema, for example `[CogSec redaction: cogsec_2026_0630_001]`.
3. Preserve safe structural fields needed for ordering/continuity: channelId/logical session, message ID, timestamp, role, and safe author metadata when safe.
4. Do not add new fields to the existing L0 message schema.
5. Ensure reload/backfill/compaction/context builder treat tombstones as ordinary safe redacted messages.
6. Record counts and affected IDs in the CogSec event store.

## Safety Rules
Tombstone content must not contain the original payload, exploit mechanism, bypass details, Unicode trick, or private poisoned text. The tombstone should reference only the CogSec event ID or safe public case label.

## Non-goals
- Do not hard-delete L0 rows without preserving sealed forensic records.
- Do not change the L0 message schema.
- Do not make tombstones visible as useful search results; search exclusion is a separate bead.
- Do not implement full derived-artifact revocation in this bead.
acceptance_criteria:
- A CogSec tombstone operation can replace selected companion-owned L0 message rows/ranges with existing-schema tombstone messages.
- Original contaminated row data is sealed successfully before companion L0 is modified.
- Tombstone rows preserve safe structural fields and reference the CogSec event ID without payload text.
- Session reload, getRecent/buildContext, and projection backfill continue to work with tombstoned rows.
- No new L0 message fields are required for tombstones.
- Tests prove payload text is absent from companion L0 after tombstoning and tombstone rows survive reload.
- npm run lint and targeted tests pass before closure.

title: P1: Add CogSec lineage preview for derived cognitive artifacts
description:
## Summary
Add a CogSec lineage preview service that uses existing provenance/lineage to answer: given a tainted source channel, logical session, and message range, which companion cognitive artifacts must be tombstoned, search-excluded, revoked, regenerated, or manually reviewed?

## Why
The operator clarified that lineage already exists well enough to regenerate memories. The missing workflow is a safe operator preview and execution input: show which artifacts will be affected without exposing the contaminated payload. This prevents remediation from becoming manual string hunting and lets later beads revoke/rebuild derived state systematically.

## Current Code Anchors
- src/core/session/manager.ts records L0 entries and compaction summaries.
- src/faculties/memory/extraction.ts and src/faculties/memory/extraction/orchestrator.ts write sourceRef/provenance.sessionId/provenanceRefs.
- src/faculties/memory/postgres-store.ts persists source_ref, provenance_refs, provenance_json, deleted_at/delete_reason, and embedding.
- src/faculties/memory/active-context.ts keys active memory by channel/session identity.
- Episodic memory Garden routes already expose provenanceRefs for episodes.
- src/persistence/sessions/transcript-projection-port.ts plus postgres/sqlite adapters own transcript/search projection rows.

## Required Behavior
Given a CogSec event draft with sourceChannelId, affected logical session IDs, and message IDs/ranges, return a typed remediation preview including:
- affected L0 message refs/ranges, without payload text
- transcript projection rows that should be rebuilt or excluded from search
- memory IDs linked by sourceRef/provenanceRefs/provenance_json/session IDs
- embedding-bearing memory rows that need invalidation/recompute
- compaction/focus/active-memory artifacts linked to affected sessions/ranges
- episodic/profile/contact/persona-adjacent derived artifacts where provenance supports it
- clean vs tainted vs uncertain classification and reason for each artifact
- lineage gaps that require manual review

## Safety Rules
Preview output must not include sealed payload text, exploit mechanics, or tombstoned content beyond safe metadata. IDs, timestamps, source refs, counts, and redacted snippets are fine only when they cannot reveal the poison.

## Non-goals
- Do not mutate artifacts in this bead; it only previews/remediation-plans.
- Do not add broad fuzzy text matching as the primary mechanism.
- Do not assume all artifacts in a channel are tainted unless the operator selected the full session/epoch.
- Do not expose raw L0 content for affected rows.

## Suggested Implementation Notes
- Put the service somewhere focused, such as src/core/cogsec/lineage.ts or src/faculties/memory/cogsec-lineage.ts.
- Reuse the structured sourceRef/session token parsing currently used by retired-session memory filtering.
- Return confidence/reason fields so later UX can distinguish deterministic lineage from manual-review gaps.
acceptance_criteria:
- A typed CogSec lineage preview API exists and accepts source channel/logical session/message range inputs.
- Preview returns affected L0 refs, transcript projection refs, memory IDs/embeddings, compaction/focus/active-memory artifacts, episodic/profile/persona-adjacent artifacts where available, and lineage gaps.
- Preview uses structured provenance/sourceRef/session IDs before any heuristic fallback.
- Preview never includes raw contaminated payload or attack mechanics.
- Tests cover direct memory provenance, logical-session scope, message-range scope, transcript projection refs, missing-provenance gaps, and no-mutation behavior.
- npm run lint and targeted tests pass before closure.

title: P1: Add CogSec event store and safe case metadata
description:
## Summary
Add a durable CogSec event/case store for cognitive-security interventions. This is the authority record for a remediation event. It tracks what was sealed, tombstoned, revoked, regenerated, and hidden from normal search without storing raw poisoned payload text in companion-accessible state.

## Why
The existing Session Recovery page can reset a source channel route, but CogSec remediation needs an explicit event record that agents/operators can inspect safely. The event tells the system why rows are tombstoned and why derived cognition was revoked. The raw payload belongs in a sealed forensic archive outside companion reach, not inside this event record.

## Current Code Anchors
- src/core/session/session-routes.ts stores source-channel route/quarantine state.
- src/core/session/manager.ts emits session.route.reset.
- src/operator/garden/services/session-service.ts and src/operator/garden/routes/session-routes.ts implement current Session Recovery API.
- admin-ui/src/routes/session-recovery/+page.svelte is the Review & Safety UX surface.
- src/persistence/layout.ts owns repo/runtime state paths.

## Required Behavior
Create a typed CogSec event model/store. The event store may have its own schema because it is not L0. It should capture:
- caseId / eventId
- type: prompt_injection | persona_poisoning | memory_poisoning | policy_drift | content_poisoning | unknown
- severity: low | medium | high | critical
- status: open | planned | applying | applied | failed | superseded
- sourceChannelId and affected logical session IDs
- affected L0 message IDs/ranges
- sealed forensic artifact refs and hashes, opaque only
- tombstoned L0 row count
- affected derived artifact IDs/counts: memories, summaries, embeddings, active-memory entries, episodic/profile/persona-adjacent artifacts
- actions requested/performed: seal, tombstone, search_exclude, revoke, regenerate, epoch_cut
- actor/operator
- timestamps
- safe agent-visible summary
- failure details that do not include payload text or attack mechanics

## Safety Rules
The event store must never contain raw poisoned payload, exploit text, bypass details, Unicode tricks, or reproducer steps. Agent-visible summary should say only that unsafe instruction-like/content-poisoning material was sealed and removed from active cognition. Sealed forensic refs are opaque and not dereferenceable by companion tools.

## Non-goals
- Do not modify existing L0 message schema.
- Do not store raw payload in the CogSec event JSON/table.
- Do not make the sealed forensic archive readable through this store.
- Do not replace SessionRouteStore; CogSec events may reference route resets and epoch cuts.

## Suggested Implementation Notes
- Add a focused module such as src/core/cogsec/events.ts or src/core/session/cogsec-events.ts.
- Add resolveCogSecEventsPath(...) in src/persistence/layout.ts if JSON-owned.
- Use strict parse/fail-closed behavior similar to SessionRouteStore.
- Emit events when a CogSec case is created/applied so Garden/prompt monitor can display safe metadata later.
acceptance_criteria:
- A typed CogSec event store exists in a focused module and persists under repo/runtime-owned state paths.
- Event records include case ID, type, severity, status, source channel, affected sessions/message ranges, sealed forensic refs/hashes, affected artifact IDs/counts, actions, actor, timestamps, safe summary, and result/failure details.
- Store parsing is strict and fails closed on unknown fields or unsupported schema versions.
- Event records never store raw payload text, bypass details, exploit mechanics, or reproducer steps.
- Agent/operator APIs can list safe CogSec event metadata without exposing sealed payloads.
- Tests cover create/read/persist/reload, malformed-state rejection, safe-summary constraints, and linking an event to a route/epoch cut.
- npm run lint and targeted tests pass before closure.

title: P1: CogSec redaction and cognitive revocation workflow
description:
## Summary
Enhance the emergency Session Recovery work from psfn-framework-ohi0 into a CogSec remediation workflow for content poisoning, prompt injection, persona poisoning, and memory poisoning. The existing session-route quarantine work is emergency containment: it can cut a source channel onto a fresh logical session and block retired-session context. This epic adds cognitive revocation: remove tainted payloads from companion-owned L0 and every companion cognitive surface while preserving a sealed forensic copy outside companion reach for future CogSec shield/classifier/tooling work.

## Correct Boundary
For normal recovery, old L0 can remain retained and labeled retired. For CogSec recovery, dirty payload must not remain in companion-owned L0. It must be extracted into a sealed forensic archive outside companion runtime/tool reach, then the companion L0 rows must be replaced with tombstones using the existing message schema.

The raw forensic record is preserved in the sealed CogSec archive, not in the companion's normal L0. Companion-facing history, transcript projection, search, memory extraction, embeddings, summaries, active memory packs, episodic/profile artifacts, and persona-adjacent state must only see tombstones/safe metadata.

## Current Code Anchors
- admin-ui/src/routes/session-recovery/+page.svelte provides the current Review & Safety emergency UI.
- src/core/session/session-routes.ts stores durable source-channel route/quarantine state.
- src/core/session/manager.ts resolves source channel -> active logical session and emits session.route.reset.
- src/faculties/memory/retrieval.ts filters retired-session memory with reason session_quarantine.blocked.
- src/faculties/memory/postgres-store.ts has memory sourceRef/provenanceRefs/provenance_json plus soft-delete/delete-version support.
- src/persistence/sessions/store.ts owns canonical JSONL, turn redaction/restore, transcript projection sync, and searchByKeywords.
- src/persistence/sessions/transcript-projection-port.ts plus postgres/sqlite adapters separate canonical archive from search projection.

## Required Product Shape
CogSec remediation should be an operator workflow:
1. Create a CogSec event/case.
2. Freeze or reject writes for the affected scope while remediation runs.
3. Extract affected dirty L0 rows into sealed forensic storage outside companion reach.
4. Replace affected companion L0 rows with existing-schema tombstone messages that point to the CogSec event ID.
5. Rebuild transcript/search projection from tombstoned L0, excluding tombstones from normal companion search.
6. Use existing lineage to revoke memories, summaries, embeddings, active-memory caches, episodic/profile artifacts, and persona-adjacent derived state.
7. Regenerate clean derived state from tombstoned L0 plus clean sources.
8. Cut or advance the session epoch/fresh lane as needed.
9. Expose safe CogSec event metadata to agents/operators so they know why context is missing, without exposing what/how.

## Non-goals
- Do not add fields to the existing L0 message schema. Tombstones must fit existing rows/content/metadata conventions.
- Do not leave dirty payload in companion-owned L0.
- Do not make CogSec tombstones normally searchable or return them as transcript-search spam.
- Do not expose raw payload, bypass details, exploit mechanics, Unicode tricks, or reproduction patterns to companion runtime, memory summarizers, embedding/indexing, normal search, or agent-facing logs.
- Do not invent a parallel memory system. Extend the existing session store, transcript projection, memory store, lineage/provenance, SessionRouteStore, and Garden service patterns.
- Do not rely on a broad LLM classifier as the first implementation step; start with deterministic operator-selected ranges and structured lineage.

## Child Work
Child beads cover CogSec event storage, sealed forensic archive, L0 tombstone replacement, search/projection exclusion, lineage-driven revocation, clean regeneration, Session Recovery UX, agent-visible safe CogSec log, memory candidacy gates, and persona conformance checks.
acceptance_criteria:
- CogSec workflow can remove dirty payload from companion-owned L0 and replace affected rows with existing-schema tombstones referencing a CogSec event.
- Raw contaminated rows are preserved only in a sealed forensic archive outside companion runtime/tool reach.
- Normal companion search/retrieval does not return payload text or tombstone spam after remediation.
- CogSec event metadata is agent/operator visible at a safe level: why context is missing, not what/how the payload worked.
- Derived cognitive artifacts are revoked or regenerated by lineage: memories, embeddings, summaries, active-memory cache, episodic/profile artifacts, and persona-adjacent state.
- Child beads are linked to this epic and are independently implementable with current repo file anchors.
- No child bead requires changing the existing L0 message schema or hard-deleting audit evidence without sealed forensic preservation.

title: P1: Add emergency session quarantine UX in Review & Safety
description:
## Summary
Add an operator-only emergency UX page under Garden's Review & Safety navigation for session quarantine / fresh logical session reset. This supports psfn-framework-0ybi and psfn-framework-hiwt.

## Why
The operator needs a break-glass surface for cases where live channel context is poisoned or dangerous. This is emergency use only and generally runs against normal continuity/charter expectations, but it is safer to excise dangerous prompt-visible context than to let harmful or poisoned context keep influencing the companion.

## Scope
- Add a Review & Safety nav item and page for emergency session quarantine/reset.
- Show source channels, active logical session IDs, retired/quarantined sessions, message counts, linked contacts when available, and route/quarantine audit metadata.
- Provide a deliberate reset/quarantine form requiring source channel, reason, and actor/operator identity where available.
- Call the Garden/admin API added for session routes/quarantine.
- Make the page clear that old L0 remains searchable/auditable and that this operation changes live context routing only.

## Non-goals
- Do not delete L0 history.
- Do not make this a normal chat control or model-facing companion tool.
- Do not bury the route state only inside the generic sessions page.
design: Implement after or alongside psfn-framework-0ybi/hiwt. Keep it operator/admin-only through existing Garden auth. Prefer extending the sessions admin service/endpoints rather than creating an unrelated runtime path.
acceptance_criteria:
- A Garden page exists under Review & Safety for emergency session quarantine/reset.
- The nav contains a Review & Safety item for the page.
- The page lists route state with physical source channel, active logical session, retired/quarantined sessions, and audit metadata.
- The page can trigger quarantine/reset through an authenticated admin API with source channel and reason.
- The UI text makes clear that old L0 is retained for audit/search and the operation changes live context routing.
- Focused frontend/API tests or type checks cover the new endpoint contract where practical.
- npm run lint and relevant targeted tests pass before closure.
