title: Regression: media/selfie tool generates the image but output fails to reach the chat stream
description:
Operator ask (sprint-9-wrapup item 3): regression where the companion successfully accesses the media/selfie tool and GENERATES an image, but fails to push the generated asset into the chat stream. Tool execution works; output handling is failing.

## Current state (verified)

- src/primitives/images/tools.ts is the media/selfie tool:
  - buildToolContent() (~line 123) assembles content: text (formatResult) + image content blocks.
  - buildMediaResultDetails() (~line 339) wraps result into mediaResult.
  - Tool execute path returns `content: buildToolContent(result, ...)` and `details: buildMediaResultDetails(...)` (~lines 479-480 for generate, similar for edit ~511+).
  - chargePaidImageGeneration handles billing (line 350).
- So the TOOL produces a valid result + content payload. The break is DOWNSTREAM: between tool.execute returning and the message (text + image) landing in the chat stream the companion emits to.

## Scope

1. IDENTIFY THE PIPELINE BREAK: trace the tool result content from tool.execute return through the tool-call scheduler / tool-surface registry / message assembly into the chat stream emit. Pin the exact stage that drops or mis-serializes the image content.
2. ROOT-CAUSE FIX: fix at the shared point all tool outputs route through — not a per-tool or per-call patch. The bug is named on media/selfie, but if the output-handling break is in a shared path it will affect every tool that returns non-text content; fix it once.
3. TOOLING CONSOLIDATION CROSS-CHECK: the operator explicitly suspects this regressed from the recent tooling consolidation work (tool-surface registry / tool-wiring-validator / tool-call-scheduler area). Cross-check recent commits touching src/core/agent/tool-surface/, src/core/agent/tool-wiring-validator.ts, src/core/agent/tool-call-scheduler*.ts. Identify the commit that introduced the regression in the close notes.
4. Confirm the generated asset reference (localPath/url) survives serialization into the chat message and renders, not just that text reaches the stream.

## Non-goals

- Do not change the image generation pipeline itself (src/primitives/images/service.ts, generated-media.ts) unless the break is provably there. The tool generates fine; the symptom is output delivery.
- No new media tool variants.

## Why

A working tool whose output never reaches the user is worse than a broken tool — it looks successful to the companion (she thinks she sent the selfie) while silently failing to deliver. This directly breaks a flagship companion capability.

## Files (likely touched)

- src/primitives/images/tools.ts (verify content shape at execute return)
- src/core/agent/tool-surface/registry.ts
- src/core/agent/tool-call-scheduler.ts (and test)
- src/core/agent/tool-wiring-validator.ts
- the message-assembly / chat-stream emit path that consumes tool `content`/`details` (trace and pin)

## Dependencies / links

- Coordinate with psfn-framework-stnk child 4 (autonomy gating): if the companion is ALSO mis-believing she lacks permission for the media tool (false-positive denial), the two bugs can mask each other. Disentangle before claiming either fixed.
acceptance_criteria: Reproduced the break; identified the exact pipeline stage where tool output is dropped between tool.execute returning valid content (mediaResult + text in src/primitives/images/tools.ts) and the message landing in the chat stream; root-cause fix applied (not a per-call workaround); a generated selfie/media image now appears in the chat as expected; regression test covers the tool-output-to-chat path; npm run lint passes.
notes: Likely root cause tracked separately as psfn-framework-p7pp: paid-image charge applied after provider generation, so charge failure masks a successful result. Coordinate closures.
close_reason: Completed by verifying and locking the shared media output path. Current code evidence: src/core/agent/tool-call-scheduler.ts preserves successful toolResult content/details; src/core/agent/substrate-agent/turn-execution-runtime.ts collects responseAttachments from turnMessages before building AgentResponse; src/core/agent/substrate-agent/turn-execution/post-turn-scheduling.ts delegates to collectGeneratedImageAttachments; src/primitives/images/generated-media.ts extracts mediaResult/imageResult details from successful media/selfie toolResult messages into Attachment objects; src/app/agent/gateway-message-handlers.ts sends AgentResponse.attachments via gateway.discordSendMedia. The suspected recent tooling consolidation commit 4e0dee77 touched src/core/agent/tool-surface and src/primitives/images/tools.ts, but history shows the generated-media collector path already existed around that commit; c655dedd later extended the collector with gallery metadata/provenance. Existing gateway egress test already proves attachments are sent through discordSendMedia. title: Add group-room memory conformance fixtures and regression tests
description:
Summary:
Build a group-room memory conformance test suite and fixtures that lock in the expected behavior.

Scope:
- Create representative fixtures for a 500-message group room with four humans, direct mentions, overheard facts, jokes, boundaries, preferences, relationships, and repeated chatter.
- Include a direct/1:1 fixture proving old behavior remains stable.
- Assert extraction yield, attribution, per-contact coverage, profile refresh, skip reasons, and no egress from observed triggers.
- Include privacy attack cases where a participant tries to obtain or rewrite another participant's memories.
acceptance_criteria:
- The suite proves a normal online group room window, configured at 50 messages in one fixture and 100 messages in another, produces useful memories when salient facts exist.
- The suite includes a larger backlog/backfill stress fixture to prove range processing and resume behavior without implying that live extraction batches 500 messages at once.
- The suite proves casual chatter and repeated low-signal messages do not become durable memories.
- The suite proves each accepted memory has correct source/subject/trigger attribution and privacy metadata.
- The suite proves observed-message extraction never sends a Discord response.
- The suite proves direct/1:1 extraction cadence, window size, and max-write defaults are unchanged.
- The suite proves non-default JSON config for windows, triggers, salience, and caps changes behavior without code changes.
- The suite includes regression coverage for ambiguous-speaker, write-cap, profile coverage, and cross-contact privacy failures.
notes: Test correction: use 50/100-message online fixtures plus separate larger backlog stress; assert knobs come from JSON config.
close_reason: Implemented group-room memory conformance fixtures and regression coverage. Added 50-message and 100-message online group fixtures with salient durable facts, larger 500-message history exercised only through bounded/resumable backfill chunks, low-signal chatter skip coverage, structured source/subject/trigger attribution assertions, observed scheduler no-response-path coverage, direct 1:1 legacy read/write-cap coverage, JSON-owned config override coverage for windows/salience/write caps, profile coverage assertions, and ambiguous/cross-contact privacy fail-closed regressions. title: Add group-memory telemetry and Garden diagnostics
description:

title: Make profile synthesis contact-coverage aware for group rooms
description:
Summary:
Refresh contact profiles for all qualifying group-room participants after group extraction.

Problem:
Current profile refresh follows accepted writes and fallback trigger contact behavior, which leaves only the most active/triggering contact with a synthesized profile in group rooms.

Scope:
- Group accepted writes by routed contact and subject contact.
- Identify contacts whose source memory count/quality now meets profile thresholds.
- Refresh profiles for each qualifying contact subject to cooldown and privacy policy.
- Make skip reasons visible for contacts who have activity but no profile yet.
acceptance_criteria:
- After group extraction, every contact with sufficient active source memories can receive or refresh a profile, not only the trigger contact.
- Profile synthesis uses memories attributed to the target contact and does not absorb facts belonging to other participants.
- Contacts with one memory or low-quality memories are skipped with explicit reason diagnostics.
- Cooldown behavior prevents profile refresh storms in active rooms.
- Tests cover multiple qualifying contacts, one qualifying/one non-qualifying contact, cross-attribution contamination, and cooldown skips.
close_reason: Implemented group-room profile coverage improvements: accepted writes now preserve sourceContactId and subjectContactId, profile refresh grouping considers routed contact plus subject contact instead of falling back to the trigger contact, room-scope-only writes remain excluded from contact profile refresh, profile synthesis returns structured refreshed/skipped results, and profile synthesis filters explicitly non-target source memories before threshold checks/prompt rendering to prevent cross-participant contamination. Added orchestration coverage for multiple routed group contacts and profile-synthesis coverage for insufficient source memories, cooldown skips, and non-target memory filtering. title: Add group-specific write caps and candidate ranking
description:
Summary:
Tune group-room write caps and ranking so high-volume rooms can produce enough memories without flooding L2.

Scope:
- Keep direct extraction max writes unchanged by default.
- Add group-specific caps: max writes per run, per contact, per chunk, per low-salience class, and per backlog catch-up run.
- Rank accepted candidates by importance, novelty, confidence, address mode, relationship relevance, emotional intensity, and per-contact coverage.
- Record skipped-by-cap counts and preserve enough backlog state to revisit high-value candidates when appropriate.
acceptance_criteria:
- Group write caps are configurable separately from `memoryExtractionMaxWrites` used by direct extraction.
- Config includes max writes per run, per chunk, per contact, per subject, per low-salience class, per backlog catch-up run, and per time window where applicable.
- A normal 50-100 message group fixture can write more than two total memories when enough salient facts exist, while respecting configured per-contact caps.
- Larger backlog/backfill fixtures prove caps scale by configured chunking/backfill policy rather than a hard-coded batch size.
- No single loud participant can consume all writes when other contacts have higher-priority qualifying facts.
- Low-salience facts remain tightly capped or skipped.
- `write_cap` telemetry reports skipped count, cap type, configured limit, and affected contacts/classes.
- Direct/1:1 tests prove the old default max-write behavior remains unchanged.
- Tests prove non-default cap config changes write selection without code changes.
- npm run verify:settings-contract passes if settings are added.
notes: Cap correction: group caps/ranking limits must be JSON-owned and velocity-aware; 500-message behavior belongs to backlog/backfill stress, not normal online extraction.

title: Implement structured source/subject attribution for group facts
description:
Summary:
Define and implement structured attribution for group-memory extraction outputs.

Problem:
Current mixed-speaker routing relies on the extracted fact text containing a clear speaker name or matching source content. Because the transcript already knows author IDs and names, group extraction should carry structured source evidence through the pipeline.

Scope:
- Extend the extraction prompt/schema or post-processing contract so each candidate fact references source message IDs and optional subject/target names.
- Resolve source speaker/contact from message IDs, not from LLM prose alone.
- Resolve subject/target contact when a fact is about someone other than the speaker.
- Classify address mode: direct_to_companion, mention_of_companion, reply_to_user, overheard_room_context, or system/api.
- Preserve trigger contact separately from source speaker and subject contact.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every group-extracted fact carries source message IDs or a source span sufficient to identify the speaker deterministically.
- Persisted memory provenance can distinguish trigger contact, source speaker/contact, subject/target contact, address mode, routing reason, and channel/message span.
- If the LLM emits a speaker name that conflicts with source message metadata, deterministic metadata wins or the fact is rejected with a specific reason.
- Facts about one participant mentioned by another are attributed without merging both people into one profile.
- No raw private transcript text is persisted solely for routing metadata.
- Tests cover source speaker, subject contact, direct mention, overheard context, reply chains if available, unresolved unknown speaker, and conflicting LLM attribution.
close_reason: Implemented structured group fact attribution: extraction prompt and transcript IDs now expose source IDs, parser accepts source message IDs/spans/source speaker/subject/address mode, routing resolves source and subject contacts from deterministic message metadata with conflict rejection, and memory provenance normalizes trigger/routed/source/subject/address/span fields without storing raw transcript text. Validation: npm test -- --run src/faculties/memory/extraction/parser.test.ts src/faculties/memory/extraction/speaker-routing.test.ts src/faculties/memory/extraction/chunk-compose.test.ts src/faculties/memory/extraction/orchestrator.test.ts src/faculties/memory/types.test.ts src/core/identity/prompt-registry.test.ts; npm run build; npm run lint.

title: Route group facts from structured attribution instead of prose speaker names
description:
Summary:
Replace broad ambiguous-speaker skips in group rooms with deterministic routing decisions based on structured attribution.

Scope:
- Use the structured attribution from selected message IDs/spans to route facts to source contact, subject contact, or social/context memory as appropriate.
- Keep fail-closed behavior when a fact truly cannot be attributed safely.
- Add explicit rejection reasons for unresolved source speaker, unresolved subject, conflicting attribution, cross-contact privacy risk, and low confidence.

- Facts are never assigned to the response-turn trigger contact unless attribution actually points there.

title: Add group salience candidate selection
description:
Summary:
Add a group-specific candidate selection stage before fact extraction so high-volume rooms do not become memory spam.

Scope:
- Score messages/threads for salience before LLM fact extraction.
- Prefer direct mentions of the companion, facts about participants, explicit preferences, relationship/social claims, boundary/safety facts, commitments, emotional events, and durable plans.
- Downrank casual chatter, memes without durable context, repeated jokes, acknowledgements, and low-information one-liners.
- Preserve enough neighboring context for selected candidates to make attribution and meaning clear.
- Emit skip telemetry by reason.
acceptance_criteria:
- Group extraction runs a bounded prefilter before LLM fact extraction for large spans.
- Candidate selection returns message IDs/spans plus salience reason codes, not just raw text snippets.
- Important events can be selected even if Carlini was not directly addressed.
- Chatter-heavy test fixtures produce low candidate counts without losing explicit preferences, boundaries, relationship claims, or companion mentions.
- Salience thresholds, reason weights, max candidate spans per chunk, neighboring-context size, and low-signal skip rules are JSON-configurable.
- Defaults may live only in settings/channel contracts; candidate selection logic consumes resolved config and does not hard-code channel policy numbers.
- Telemetry reports messages considered, candidate spans selected, and skip reasons.
- Tests prove non-default salience config changes selection behavior without code changes.

title: Add observed group-room extraction scheduler
description:
Summary:
Schedule group-memory extraction from observed group-room traffic without causing replies.

Scope:
- Add an observed-message trigger path for channels classified as group/group-capable.
- Trigger on configurable message-count thresholds, time thresholds, direct mention/high-salience signals, and backlog lag.
- Use debounce/cooldown and one in-flight extraction per channel.
- Ensure observed extraction never enters the chat response path or emits Discord messages.
- Keep response-turn extraction available for direct conversations and direct mentions.
acceptance_criteria:
- Observed group-room messages can enqueue a memory extraction job without invoking the response model.
- Trigger reasons distinguish observed_count, observed_time, direct_mention, high_salience, backlog_lag, manual, and response_turn when applicable.
- Message-count thresholds, time thresholds, direct-mention behavior, salience trigger rules, cooldowns, debounce, backlog lag thresholds, and max in-flight behavior are JSON-configurable.
- Cooldowns prevent extraction storms in fast rooms while preserving backlog progress.
- Duplicate Discord notifications do not enqueue duplicate extraction jobs for the same source message/span.
- The trigger is disabled or conservative by default until settings/policy enable it per channel class or channel.
- Implementation code reads resolved config and does not hard-code operational trigger values outside the settings contract/defaults.
- Tests prove observed extraction does not send a reply, even when direct mention/high-salience extraction is scheduled, and prove non-default trigger config changes behavior.
- npm run verify:settings-contract passes if settings are added.
notes: Trigger correction: count/time/backlog/cooldown thresholds must be JSON-owned and operator-tunable for channel velocity.
close_reason: Implemented observed group-room extraction scheduler for passive Discord observations. The scheduler resolves JSON-owned group-memory settings, classifies group/group-capable channels, plans bounded watermark ranges, triggers on configured observed count/time/direct mention/high salience/backlog lag, enforces in-flight/cooldown gates, and only advances the watermark after the extractor accepts processing. Wired the scheduler into the observe-only Discord handler without invoking handleMessage or Discord egress, and added duplicate-notification coverage so the same observed message cannot enqueue duplicate extraction. title: Add group-memory watermark and range reader
description:
Summary:
Add a group-memory watermark and bounded range reader so group extraction processes unprocessed spans rather than only the latest 10 conversational entries.

Problem:
Current response-turn extraction calls `getRecentMessages(channelId, 10)`, so high-volume group rooms drop most observed history between extraction turns. A separate group path needs durable progress tracking by channel/session and bounded chunking from the last processed message ID.

Scope:
- Store a group-memory high-water mark per channel/session and extraction policy version.
- Read message ranges from session storage/projection by message ID bounds.
- Chunk large ranges into bounded windows with small overlap for context continuity.
- Record processed spans, skipped spans, and failure/retry state.
- Keep direct extraction markers unchanged unless intentionally reused through a compatibility wrapper.
acceptance_criteria:
- Group extraction can select messages from `(lastGroupMemoryWatermark, currentHead]` without relying on `getRecentMessages(channelId, 10)`.
- Range reads preserve role, author ID, author name, timestamp, channel visibility, source message ID, and metadata needed for attribution.
- Chunking supports JSON-configurable max messages, max tokens, overlap, backlog catch-up limit, and retry behavior.
- Normal online chunk defaults are suitable for active channels, expected around 50-100 messages per processed batch unless operators tune them.
- Larger spans are split into multiple bounded chunks or deferred to backfill; the live scheduler never relies on an unconfigurable hundreds-of-messages batch.
- Watermark advancement happens only after a chunk/span is successfully processed or explicitly skipped with recorded reason.
- Failed spans are retryable and do not permanently mark unprocessed messages as processed.
- Direct/1:1 extraction marker behavior remains unchanged.
- Tests simulate configured 50-message and 100-message windows plus a larger backlog stress case, proving no messages are silently skipped due to tail sampling and configured limits are honored.
- npm run verify:settings-contract passes if settings are added.
notes: Window correction: normal online group windows should be configurable, not hard-coded; use 50-100ish defaults and split/backfill larger spans.
close_reason: Implemented group-memory watermark and bounded range planner with JSON watermark persistence, processed/skipped/failed span state, retry count tracking, configurable message/token chunking, overlap, max chunks per run, and deferred backlog metadata. Validation: npm test -- --run src/faculties/memory/extraction/group-ranges.test.ts src/faculties/memory/extraction/group-classifier.test.ts; npm run build; npm run lint.

title: Define direct/group/auto memory-mode contract
description:
Summary:
Define the canonical contract for direct, group, and auto memory modes before changing extraction behavior.

Context:
Group behavior should be determined primarily by channel topology and recent canonical participants, not only by all contacts ever seen in a channel. Operators also need a manual override for channels whose provider metadata or participant patterns are misleading.

Scope:
- Define `memoryMode: direct | group | auto` ownership in channel/settings config.
- Define provider topology rules: Discord DM/private 1:1 stays direct; Discord guild channel/thread is group-capable.
- Define recent participant rules for auto mode using distinct canonical human contacts in a rolling window.
- Exclude the companion, system users, API principals, and bots unless explicitly marked as AI companion/human-relevant.
- Define fallback behavior for group-capable channels with only one recent speaker.
- Document that group mode changes extraction windowing/attribution/caps, not reply behavior or privacy boundaries.
acceptance_criteria:
- The direct/group/auto memory-mode contract is documented in authoritative config/design surfaces, not only in code comments.
- Manual mode overrides auto detection and can force direct or group behavior per channel.
- Auto mode classifies Discord DMs as direct and Discord guild channels/threads as group-capable.
- Auto mode promotes to group behavior when recent distinct canonical human contacts in the rolling window is at least 2, with the rolling window size JSON-configurable.
- Historical `contact_channel_activity` can inform group-capable status but cannot by itself force every future extraction into high-volume group processing forever.
- The contract defines the JSON owner for every group-memory knob: mode, participant window, trigger thresholds, chunk sizes, overlap, cooldowns, backlog limits, salience thresholds, write caps, per-contact caps, profile refresh thresholds, telemetry visibility, and backfill limits.
- Defaults may exist only through the settings/channel contract and typed config loader; implementation code must consume resolved config and must not bury operational constants in extractor/scheduler logic.
- The contract explicitly states that group mode never causes observed messages to receive replies.
- Tests or contract checks cover DM, guild one-speaker, guild multi-speaker, bot/system/API-only, manual override, and non-default configured thresholds.
- npm run verify:settings-contract passes if settings are added.
notes: Config correction: direct/group/auto and every group-memory threshold/cap/window need canonical JSON ownership so Garden can expose them later.
close_reason: Implemented group memory direct/group/auto settings contract: settings.json groupMemory object, channels.json discord groupMemory overrides, Garden exposure, seed defaults, docs, and regression coverage. title: Implement group-room classifier and recent participant detector
description:
Summary:
Implement the channel classifier and recent participant detector used by `memoryMode:auto`.

Scope:

- Count distinct recent human participants over a bounded message/time window.
- Preserve provider topology signals such as Discord DM vs guild channel/thread.
- Expose a small reusable API to extraction, diagnostics, and tests.

title: Epic: Group-room memory extraction and attribution reliability
description:
Summary:
Build a group-room memory extraction path that preserves the current lightweight 1:1 behavior while making Discord-style multi-user rooms produce useful, attributable, privacy-safe memories and contact profiles.

Problem:
The current extractor is acceptable for 1:1 turns because it samples the recent conversational tail after a response turn and writes at most a small number of high-value facts. In group rooms this collapses: observed messages are recorded but do not trigger extraction, normal extraction samples only the latest 10 conversational entries, write caps remain tuned for direct chat, mixed-speaker facts are skipped unless the LLM text itself clearly names the source speaker, and profile refresh follows accepted writes rather than ensuring all qualifying room participants are covered. Carlini's live room showed 465 projected messages and 393 human messages across 4 speakers, but only 27 total memories / 18 active memories and one synthesized profile.

Design intent:
- Direct/1:1 behavior must remain stable and cheap.
- Group rooms use a separate memory mode with explicit classification, watermarks, bounded range processing, stronger attribution, conservative salience gates, per-contact write caps, and operator-visible diagnostics.
- Observed group traffic may trigger memory extraction, but must never trigger a chat reply.
- Group memory should remember important room events, preferences, relationships, boundary/safety facts, mentions of the companion, and meaningful social dynamics; it must not turn every casual message into L2 memory.
- The extraction contract must preserve who spoke, who the fact is about, whether the companion was directly addressed/mentioned/overhearing, and which message span produced the evidence.

Out of scope:
- Autonomous relationship or trust mutation. This epic provides better evidence for that later system.
- Remembering every message.
- Relaxing cross-contact memory/privacy boundaries.
- Replacing 1:1 extraction with the group pipeline.
acceptance_criteria:
- A group-room memory mode exists separately from direct/1:1 extraction and does not regress 1:1 extraction cadence, prompt size, or write caps.
- All group-memory operational knobs live in canonical JSON-owned config, not buried literals: mode, participant window, message/time trigger thresholds, chunk sizes, overlap, cooldowns, backlog limits, salience thresholds, write caps, per-contact caps, and backfill limits.
- JSON-owned defaults are wired through the settings/channel contract so a Garden config page can expose them later without changing code.
- Channel memory mode can be manual (`direct`, `group`, `auto`) and auto mode uses provider topology plus recent canonical participant count.
- Normal online group extraction processes configurable bounded windows sized for channel velocity, with expected defaults in the 50-100 message range unless operators tune them.
- Large historical spans are handled by bounded backfill/stress processing, not by forcing the live hot path to consume hundreds of messages in one batch.
- Group extraction processes message ranges since a group-memory watermark instead of only the latest 10 entries.
- Observed group-room messages can schedule extraction without sending a response or changing Discord egress behavior.
- Group extraction records structured attribution for source speaker/contact, subject/target contact when known, trigger contact when applicable, address mode, and message span.
- Group extraction uses stricter salience filtering and per-contact/per-run caps so high-volume rooms produce useful memories without spam.
- Mixed-speaker facts are routed from structured message metadata rather than requiring the LLM to include speaker names in prose.
- Contact profile synthesis refreshes every qualifying participant after group extraction, not only the response-turn trigger contact.
- Garden/operator diagnostics show observed count, processed count, watermark lag, candidate count, parsed facts, accepted writes, rejection reasons, write-cap skips, ambiguous attribution skips, and per-contact coverage.
- Tests include normal 50-100 message multi-user fixtures plus larger backlog/backfill stress fixtures proving important facts are remembered, chatter is skipped, attribution is correct, direct/1:1 behavior is unchanged, and configured values are honored.
- npm run verify:settings-contract passes if settings are added.
- npm run lint and targeted memory/Discord/settings tests pass before implementation beads close.
notes: User correction 2026-06-28: live group extraction should not imply hard-coded 500-message batches. Normal online windows should be configurable and likely around 50-100 messages depending channel velocity; all thresholds/caps/windows must be JSON-owned for later Garden configuration.
close_reason: Completed group-room memory extraction and attribution reliability epic. Landed separate group classification/range/watermark processing, JSON-owned config and channel overrides, observed group scheduling without Discord egress, group salience candidate selection, structured source/subject/scope routing, group write caps/ranking, contact-coverage profile refresh, Garden diagnostics, safe bounded backfill, conformance fixtures, and operations documentation. Normal online windows are JSON-configurable and covered at 50 and 100 messages; larger 500-message history is covered only through bounded/resumable backfill. title: Debug Carlini k3s response prefix artifacts
description:
Summary: Carlini on the remote K3s deployment is returning visible template artifacts, including the literal prefix <｜begin▁of▁sentence｜># Carlini's Response, instead of a clean assistant response.

Scope:
- Inspect the remote Carlini/K3s deployment state, pods, services, logs, and active model/provider configuration without making ad hoc off-repo runtime changes.
- Trace the repo-owned LLM request/streaming/client path that could preserve prompt echo, BOS tokens, or response header template text.
- Identify whether the artifact is caused by model chat template configuration, completion-vs-chat endpoint usage, LiteLLM/provider settings, prompt construction, or stream/text post-processing.
- Implement any required fix in repo-owned code or deployment artifacts only, with targeted tests.

Observed example:
<｜begin▁of▁sentence｜># Carlini's Response

Acceptance:
- The source of the visible BOS/response-header artifact is identified from code/config/log evidence.
- Carlini responses no longer surface <｜begin▁of▁sentence｜> or # Carlini's Response to the user.
- Any code/config fix is covered by a targeted regression test for prefix stripping or request formatting, whichever is the actual root cause.
- npm run lint passes before the bead is closed.
- Remote changes, if needed, are made through repo-owned deployment files or explicitly documented as read-only findings when no deploy is performed.
notes: Root cause: Carlini's ChatGPTN route is DeepSeek-V4-Flash behind vLLM via LiteLLM. Under long Carlini context it can emit visible provider template artifacts such as <｜begin▁of▁sentence｜># Carlini's Response. Fix: LLMClient now buffers early stream text until provider-template prefixes are ruled out, rejects BOS/special-token prefixes and generated response headers as retryable empty-response artifacts, and falls back before streaming or persisting them. Regression tests cover BOS+header, header without BOS, and a normal Markdown heading allowed path. Validation: npm test -- --run src/primitives/llm/client.test.ts src/primitives/llm/error-classify.test.ts; npm run lint; npm run build. No Helm/deployment files changed.

title: Explore current contact profile and social graph gaps in multi-user group chats
description:
Summary:
Exploratory-only investigation of current Carlini/profile/social-graph behavior before implementation work.

Questions to answer:
- Why does only one user currently have a synthesized contact profile in the group-chat environment?
- Are accepted memory writes correctly attributed to canonical contact IDs in multi-user/group-chat turns?
- Which profile refresh skips are happening: insufficient source memories, cooldown, low confidence, low novelty, alias risk, missing contact, no accepted writes, disabled config, or other?
- Are social graph entity records being created for contacts, and are social relationship edges absent because extraction is unwired or because evidence is missing?
- Are overheard/non-direct group messages eligible for memory extraction today, and what determines whether they become memories?
- What telemetry/logs/queries should an implementer use to reproduce the issue?

Scope:
- Read code paths and, if available, inspect safe local/live diagnostics or database summaries without mutating code.
- Do not delete, patch, or migrate memories.
- Do not implement fixes in this bead.
- Record findings in bead notes and create/adjust follow-up beads if the investigation discovers narrower bugs.
acceptance_criteria:
- Findings identify the exact current code paths for accepted memory attribution, profile refresh grouping, profile skip decisions, and social graph edge creation or absence.
- Findings state whether the one-profile issue is caused by attribution, thresholds, cooldown, missing accepted writes, missing contact mapping, or insufficient observability.
- Findings state whether social graph relationship extraction is unwired, partially wired, or failing due to data/thresholds.
- Findings include enough file/function references and safe query/log examples for an implementer to reproduce.
- No code changes are made under this exploratory bead.
- Any discovered implementation work is linked to the dynamic relationship epic or an existing child bead.
notes:
Exploration findings, 2026-06-28:

Runtime checked:
- Remote Carlini K3S cluster on o_0@100.96.206.29, namespace psfn. Read-only checks only.
- Carlini is the only companion in a Discord group room with multiple human participants.
- DB summary: contacts=5, profiles=1, active_memories=17, all_memories=26, social_graph_entities=5, social_relationship_edges=0.

Contact/profile/memory distribution:
- MrDragonFox: 13 active memories, has the only synthesized profile, profile_source_count=12, profile_updated_at=2026-06-28 17:20:33Z.
- Vega: 1 active memory, no profile.
- Iki: 1 active memory, no profile.
- P I N K • C Ʌ L I C O: 0 active memories, no profile.
- API Principal: 1 active memory, no profile.
- All human Discord participants had contact_channel_activity in channel 1486443955561299979, so the issue is not missing contact creation.

Logs/path behavior:
- Discord guild messages are all observed for context but egress is mention-gated. Code: src/channels/discord/adapter.ts:391-424.
- observe-only messages call SubstrateAgent.observeMessage, which records a user session entry and resolves contact/trust, but does not call memoryExtractor.maybeExtract. Code: src/core/agent/substrate-agent.ts:718-774.
- Memory extraction is scheduled after response turns through post-turn scheduling with the responding author's canonicalContactKey. Code: src/core/agent/substrate-agent/turn-execution/post-turn-scheduling.ts:245-251.
- Extraction uses recent channel history, so observed messages can be included in a later extraction window, but long observed-only stretches do not independently trigger extraction.
- Carlini logs show multiple observe/respond messages in the same group channel. MrDragonFox response-triggered extraction produced accepted writes and a profile refresh. Vega-triggered extraction at 13:47 parsed 2 facts but accepted 0, rejected 2 as low_importance.
- Several MrDragonFox-triggered extractions in mixed-speaker windows skipped facts as ambiguous_speaker. This is privacy-safe but loses overheard/group context unless source attribution is very clear.

Profile synthesis cause:
- Current profile refresh grouping is per accepted write contact, with fallback to the trigger contact on zero writes. Code: src/faculties/memory/extraction/orchestrator.ts:550-558 and :598-617.
- Profile refresh only proceeds when source memories for that contact meet profile thresholds; default/profile config requires minSourceMemories=2. Code: src/faculties/memory/extraction/profile-synthesis.ts:93-107 and src/faculties/memory/extraction/types.ts:131-136.
- Therefore the one-profile symptom is explained by data/threshold/trigger behavior, not a schema limitation: only MrDragonFox has enough accepted source memories for a profile. Other humans are contacts, but have 0-1 active memories and/or low-importance/ambiguous extraction outcomes.
- Observability gap: profile skip reasons are debug-level and not surfaced in Garden; on the live logs examined only the successful refresh appeared at info level.

Social graph cause:
- social_graph_entities exists for all contacts because contact upsert creates contact-backed social graph entities. Code: src/core/contacts/postgres-adapter/social-graph-queries.ts:20-27 and src/core/contacts/postgres-adapter/crud-operations.ts:160-166,230.
- social_relationship_edges is empty in Carlini DB.
- Code search found no production caller creating social relationship edges beyond store adapter methods; automatic group-chat social edge extraction appears unwired rather than failing due to current data.

Additional implementation gaps discovered and beaded:
- psfn-framework-4caj.14: Persist group-room source-speaker routing metadata for relationship evidence. Current sourceSpeakerName/routingReason is mostly telemetry; memory writes persist contactId and generic provenance but not enough durable attribution for later relationship review.
- psfn-framework-4caj.15: Add policy-controlled memory extraction for important observed group-room traffic. Current observe-only messages are context but do not trigger extraction until a response turn.

Existing child beads covering fixes:
- psfn-framework-4caj.10 covers multi-user profile synthesis attribution/coverage and should include Garden/log visibility for skip reasons.
- psfn-framework-4caj.9 covers social graph edge extraction from group-chat/overheard interactions.
- psfn-framework-4caj.3 should consume the new routing metadata for relationship evidence rollups.
close_reason: Exploratory code/runtime investigation completed; findings recorded and discovered implementation gaps beaded.

title: Enforce Postgres trust mutation guard parity before relationship autonomy
description:
Summary:
Fix contact trust mutation guardrails so the Postgres runtime enforces the same autonomous high-tier trust restrictions expected by tests and SQLite/in-memory behavior.

Problem:
The contact tool tests expect agent/autonomous contact_set_trust calls to be unable to promote a contact to high-tier trust such as trusted or primary. The SQLite/in-memory store has broad high-tier guardrails, but the Postgres trust-policy adapter appears to only block behavior_drift high-tier escalation, leaving a possible direct autonomous contact_set_trust path to trusted in live Postgres runtime.

Scope:
- Audit ContactStore.setTrustLevel behavior for SQLite and Postgres.
- Make Postgres deny autonomous high-tier trust mutations unless explicitly manual/admin/operator-authorized.
- Preserve admin/manual Garden behavior for legitimate operator trust edits.
- Preserve allowed low-tier public <-> regular behavior where policy allows it.
- Add adapter parity tests so future persistence changes cannot diverge.
- Confirm contact tool direct trustLevel=trusted returns an error under live-like Postgres test wiring.

Security invariant:
The companion may propose high-tier trust changes under the dynamic relationship review system, but autonomous tool/runtime paths must not directly apply high-tier trust without policy and autonomy gates.
acceptance_criteria:
- Postgres ContactStore.setTrustLevel denies actor/source combinations classified as autonomous when the requested or current trust level is high-tier, unless a manual/admin/operator authorization path is used.
- contact_set_trust cannot autonomously set trusted or primary in Postgres-backed tests.
- Admin/Garden update paths using admin:api still allow legitimate trusted updates and preserve primary-owner guardrails.
- SQLite/in-memory and Postgres adapters share equivalent test coverage for low-tier update, high-tier denial, admin high-tier update, primary denial, and audit logging.
- Denied high-tier attempts are auditable and return clear errors.
- npm test targeted contact store/tool tests pass.
- npm run lint passes before closure.
notes: AUDIT 2026-06-28 (verified): OPEN. No trust-mutation-guard code in src/core/contacts (grep for trustMutation/trustGuard/autonomousTrust = empty). The Postgres contact store needs the same autonomous-high-tier-trust restrictions the SQLite/in-memory backends enforce.
close_reason:
Done. High-tier trust mutation guardrails enforced with Postgres parity:
- src/core/contacts/postgres-adapter/trust-policy-queries.ts:95 (Postgres path) denies high-tier trust via suggestion flow; :22 appendMutationAuditEntry for trust/note mutation audit trail.
- src/core/contacts/store.ts:379,405,470 denies behavior-driven trust mutations touching high-tier trust + unauthorized high-tier mutations + suggestion-flow high-tier.
Commits: 3da6895a (enforce high-tier trust guardrails), bfa41d39 (persistent trust/note mutation audit trail), c4048b1a (validation evidence). Verified 2026-06-28 by reading trust-policy-queries.ts + store.ts.

title: Normalize JSON-array tag strings in memory tools
description:
Summary:
The live Carlini memory refill through the supported chat memory tool created the correct memory, but the tags were stored as malformed fragments like '["carlini"' because the model supplied the tag field as a JSON-array-shaped string while the unified memory tool only split on commas.

Context:
User asked to use the existing chat/tool-to-memory capability to refill Carlini memory instead of removing useful facts. The tool path worked and wrote memory 019f0f2d-ef6d-7018-8e50-49446a7e7f4f, but exposed an old compatibility edge in memory tag parsing.

Scope:
- Update memory tool tag parsing to accept normal comma-separated strings and JSON-array strings.
- Trim, lowercase, and reject non-string/empty entries consistently.
- Add regression tests for unified memory action=write/import and legacy memory_write if coverage fits existing tests.
- Backfill the live corrected memory tags to canonical values after deploy or through an app-supported update path if available.

Acceptance:
- Passing tags='carlini,streaming' still stores ['carlini','streaming'].
- Passing tags='["carlini","streaming"]' stores ['carlini','streaming'], not bracket/quote fragments.
- Live corrected guardrails memory has clean tags.
- npm run lint passes before closure.
notes: Implemented commit 796699c2. Memory tag parser now accepts comma-separated strings, actual arrays, and JSON-array strings; non-string/empty entries are ignored and output is trimmed/lowercased. Applied parser to unified memory action=write/import, legacy memory_write, memory_import_batch, and memory_patch tag paths. Tests added for unified writes, legacy memory_write, memory_import_batch, and memory_patch JSON-array strings. Validation: npm test -- --run src/faculties/memory/tools.test.ts passed; npm run lint passed; npm run build passed. Deployed to kube and rolled psfn-agent/psfn-gateway/psfn-garden; running app image sha256:5d4528933626e00670962b4e26d0f5741a295427cb4e4873a912e12194644456. Live memory_patch was not available to the companion runtime, so live tag backfill used direct Postgres metadata update only after preserving the memory text/source, followed by agent/Garden restart. Validation: Garden detail for memory 019f0f2d-ef6d-7018-8e50-49446a7e7f4f shows tags [carlini, streaming, guardrails, mrdragonfox]; SQL active tag-fragment count is 0.

title: Fix Garden memory extraction dates and historical wrong-name visibility
description:
Summary:

Evidence:
After live repair on 2026-06-28, the operator still sees memory entries in Garden with invalid extraction dates and historical wrong-name content. The DB repair soft-deleted contaminated l2_memories and cleared contact_profiles, but Garden may be displaying deleted rows, L0/turn history, delete-version snapshots, or a timestamp shape the UI cannot parse.

Scope:
- Inspect live Garden memory API payloads for affected memories and timestamp fields.
- Compare Garden output to Postgres active/deleted l2_memories, l2_memory_delete_versions, contact_profiles, and session/turn records.
- Identify whether invalid dates come from ms/seconds mismatch, BigInt/string serialization, missing extractedAt mapping, or UI parser assumptions.
- Ensure active memory views hide soft-deleted rows by default and clearly label historical/deleted rows when intentionally shown.
- Do not destroy audit history; preserve delete-version snapshots and L0 session archives.

Acceptance:
- Garden active memory view shows valid extraction dates for L2 memories.
- Soft-deleted contaminated rows are not shown in active memory/profile surfaces by default.
- Historical/deleted rows, if exposed, are clearly labeled as deleted/audit history and do not appear as active memories.
- Wrong-name historical records are either hidden from active views or explicitly marked historical/deleted; no active contact profile contains the bad names.
- Any code change passes npm run lint; if only live data/config is changed, validation queries and API payload evidence are recorded.
notes: Implemented and deployed commit 8171de46 on kube. Root cause: pg returns BIGINT memory timestamps as strings, which Garden serialized to the UI and caused JavaScript Invalid Date; the earlier SQL repair also happened after Garden/agent had hydrated their in-memory Postgres memory cache, so active views could remain stale until restart. Code changes: Postgres memory store now normalizes pg numeric/string fields to finite numbers for memory rows, delete versions, and embedding similarity; Garden memory service defensively filters superseded/deleted memories from active admin views/search results; Garden UI date formatter accepts numeric strings and renders malformed values as unknown rather than Invalid Date. Added regression test for pg BIGINT string hydration and deleted-row exclusion. title: Roll out Carlini kube bug fixes and smoke live Discord/model fallback
description:
Summary:

title: Fix Carlini kube empty LLM response fallback coverage
description:
Summary:
Fix the Carlini kube runtime path where litellm/ChatGPTN can return an empty/no-text response and the agent has no usable fallback candidate for agent.turn.prompt.

Evidence:
Live logs in channel 1486443955561299979 around 2026-06-28 11:13-11:14 show:
- ModelFallback selected model candidate for purpose agent.turn.prompt: model ChatGPTN, provider litellm, slotKey chatgptn-primary.
- ModelFallback then reported All fallback candidates exhausted with attempts=1 and lastError "LLM response from litellm/ChatGPTN contained no text".
- Agent logged Error handling message for the same Discord message ids.

Problem:
A single empty text response from the local/litellm provider currently fails the whole turn in this kube setup. The earlier desired fallback to an OpenRouter/OpenAI nano model is either not present in the active model roster, not eligible for agent.turn.prompt, or not being selected for no-text responses.

title: Fix unexpected duplicate Discord notification drops in kube
description:
Summary:
Investigate and fix unexpected duplicate Discord notification drops seen in the Carlini kube room after the recent Discord message-handling fixes.

Evidence:
Live kube logs in channel 1486443955561299979 repeatedly show a normal Message from line immediately followed by:
WARN [Agent] Dropping duplicate discord notification message while first copy is in-flight {"channelId":"1486443955561299979","messageId":"..."}
Examples from 2026-06-28 around 11:13-11:14 include messages from Iki and MrDragonFox with ids 1520809258948755538, 1520809327244345395, 1520809420832112832, 1520809527593930983, and 1520809548594810940. The operator expected the previous Discord fixes to eliminate these duplicate-drop warnings.

Relevant code:
- src/app/agent/gateway-message-handlers.ts keeps recentDiscordMessages and inFlightDiscordMessages keyed by buildMessageDedupKey("discord", message).
- Lines around the duplicate guard intentionally drop the same Discord message id while an earlier copy is in flight.
- Existing tests cover holding different Discord messages while busy and dropping true duplicate same-id notifications.

Problem:
The logs suggest either the gateway is delivering every Discord event twice, the same message is entering both notification and handle paths, the dedupe key is too coarse for the deployed path, or the warning is expected true dedupe but too noisy for normal operation. Need prove which is happening and ensure legitimate user messages are never lost.

Scope:
- Reproduce or trace the duplicate path in kube using gateway/agent logs with route/source metadata, without logging secrets.
- Confirm whether the second event is byte-identical same message id, a retried gateway notification, or a distinct event being keyed as duplicate.
- Verify observe-mode messages and respond-mode messages both clear inFlightDiscordMessages in all success/error paths.
- Check interaction with busy-turn queuing/bundling so legitimate different messages are held/queued, not dropped.
- Add telemetry fields or lower severity only if the duplicate is proven harmless expected dedupe; otherwise fix the duplicate event source or dedupe key.

Acceptance:
- A regression test covers the kube failure mode: repeated live Discord messages in one channel do not produce duplicate-drop warnings unless the exact same message id is actually delivered twice.
- True duplicate same-id notifications remain idempotent and do not create double replies.
- Legitimate different messages arriving during an in-flight turn are held, bundled, or queued according to policy, never dropped as duplicates.
- Logs distinguish true duplicate suppression from busy queueing and include enough route/source detail to debug future cases.
- Kube smoke with Carlini in channel 1486443955561299979 shows no unexpected duplicate-drop warnings for normal messages.
- npm run lint passes before closure.
notes:
Root cause found in live kube and code (2026-06-28): gateway initialized Discord twice. createDiscordChannelAdapterFactoryEntry() calls adapter.init() during loadGatewayChannelSurfaces, then app/gateway/main.ts calls initGatewayChannelSurfaces() and surfaces.discord.init() again. Live gateway logs confirmed duplicate init with two identical "Logged in as Carlini#5523" lines at 2026-06-28T15:18:13. Each init registered another MessageCreate listener, so every Discord message produced two discord.message notifications within ~1-2ms. The agent-side inFlightDiscordMessages guard then dropped the second copy as an in-flight duplicate. Also found notifyAll() broadcasted to internal_session_integrity connections; this was not the primary duplicate trigger but is incorrect broadcast targeting.

Patch implemented: DiscordAdapter.init() is now idempotent and GatewayServer.notifyAll() only broadcasts notifications to ready/healthy agent connections. Regression tests added for duplicate init listener registration and internal-session notifyAll exclusion. Validation run on this patch: npm test -- --run src/channels/discord/adapter.test.ts src/boundary/gateway/server.test.ts passed; npm run lint passed; npm run build passed. Live kube smoke remains pending rollout of the new image.

title: Expose per-channel response style selection in Garden/settings
description:
Summary:
Add an operator-facing per-channel response style control so concise/expressive delivery is manually selectable without editing env or hard-coding channel behavior.

Context:
The runtime already supports ResponseStyle values (concise|expressive). resolveChannelResponseStyle applies exact/prefix/channelType/default overrides when config.responseStyleOverrides is present, and load-config currently parses RESPONSE_STYLE_OVERRIDES from env. Discord guild/voice, Telegram, API voice, and internal channels currently resolve concise by default. The operator wants concise to be a channel option that can be selected manually.

Problem:
The override mechanism exists but is not owned by canonical mutable settings/Garden. Env-owned JSON is poor for live channel tuning, invisible to operators, hard to audit, and conflicts with the repo rule that mutable runtime settings belong in owner files/Garden.

Scope:
- Add a canonical owner-file representation for response style overrides, preferably aligned with channel settings/metadata rather than another opaque env blob.
- Expose channel response style in Garden/admin channel settings with options: default/auto, concise, expressive.
- Preserve existing automatic defaults when no manual override is set.
- Wire the owner file through settings contracts, runtime config hydration, prompt template variables, and any cache invalidation needed so changes affect rendered prompts predictably.
- Keep RESPONSE_STYLE_OVERRIDES as bootstrap/deployment compatibility only if still needed, with owner-file settings taking precedence and no silent malformed JSON fallback.
- Document the exact precedence: exact channel override, prefix/channel-type override if retained, explicit privacy/default behavior, built-in channel defaults.

Acceptance:
- An operator can set a specific Discord channel/session to concise or expressive from Garden without editing env.
- A rendered prompt for that channel shows the selected runtime_response_style and guidance.
- Removing the override returns the channel to automatic/default resolution.
- Invalid style values reject with clear validation errors.
- Existing concise defaults for Discord guild/voice, Telegram, API voice, and internal channels remain unchanged when no override is set.
- npm run verify:settings-contract passes.
- Targeted trust/policy/runtime-context/Garden tests cover owner-file override, Garden update, precedence, and fallback to default.
- npm run lint passes before closure.
notes: AUDIT 2026-06-28 (verified): PARTIAL. response_style exists as a prompt-layer concept (admin-ui/src/routes/prompts/+page.svelte:50 response_style block, primer/+page.svelte:250 mentions 'response-style booleans') but there is no PER-CHANNEL response-style selection in Garden/settings. The bead wants channel-scoped style selection.

title: Make contact profile synthesis target-aware and attribution-safe
description:
Summary:
Make contact profile synthesis target-aware and attribution-safe so summaries do not alias the contact to names/entities mentioned in bad or mixed-speaker source memories.

Evidence:
Current profile synthesis code passes only a UUID contact_id plus raw memory text to the LLM. The live Carlini kube profile for Iki says "This contact, known as MrDragonFox and also by the name Carlini..." because source memories under Iki include facts spoken by or about MrDragonFox/Carlini. The Vega and MrDragonFox profiles likewise amplified "Carlini Carlini" and wrong ownership from L2 source memories.

Problem:
profile-synthesis.ts builds memory_facts as raw `- [id] [type] text` lines, uses prompt text `Synthesize a stable contact profile for canonical contact: {contact_id}`, and never provides target displayName/nickname/trust/relationship labels. It therefore asks the model to infer who the UUID is from corrupted source text. Once L2 text has wrong attribution, contact_profiles confidently turn it into stable identity claims.

Scope:
- Pass explicit target contact display name, nickname, canonical id, and relevant relationship/trust metadata into profile synthesis.
- Render source memories with ownership/provenance hints and any speaker/subject attribution added by the group-room extraction fix.
- Update the profile synthesis prompt to forbid treating names mentioned in source facts as aliases for the target unless the contact record says so.
- Require summaries to separate "about this contact" from "people/things this contact mentioned" when both are present.
- Add output hygiene so profile summaries cannot contain raw {{user}}/{{char}}, duplicate companion names, or obvious assistant-as-human aliasing.
- Prefer skipping profile refresh over writing a profile when source memories are ambiguous or contaminated.

Acceptance:
- A test with target displayName=Iki and source memory mentioning MrDragonFox/Carlini does not produce "This contact is known as MrDragonFox/Carlini".
- A test with target displayName=Vega and source memories about Carlini streaming produces either no profile update or an explicitly scoped statement that Vega discussed/asked about Carlini, not that Vega is Carlini or owns Carlini.
- The prompt includes target display name and clear attribution rules, not only UUID contact_id.
- Existing contact profile refresh gating still works: insufficient/low-confidence source memories skip refresh.
- npm run lint passes before closure.

Discovered from: psfn-framework-bjvm
notes:
Implementation merged on kube in commit 8e3bce77. Profile synthesis now receives explicit target contact context, renders source memories with ownership/provenance hints, extends default and custom prompts with target attribution rules, supports target-contact placeholders, and skips obvious target-to-mentioned-name aliasing such as treating Iki/Vega as MrDragonFox or Carlini. title: Optimize Carlini card for multi-human rooms
description:
Summary:
Optimize the Carlini character card for PSFN multi-human Discord rooms instead of a 1:1 SillyTavern route.

Evidence:
The live kube card at /app/companion-data/companion.json already has concise/no-roleplay system instructions, but it still contains 1:1 assumptions such as "{{user}} is the Abbot of the monastery" and creator notes saying Carlini responds best to "an Abbot". Runtime prompt layers enable description/personality/scenario/system/post-history, while mes_example and first_mes are disabled. In a multi-human room, {{user}} correctly expands per turn to the current speaker name, but the card semantics make every current speaker the Abbot. Early turns showed Carlini addressing multiple people as Abbot and using roleplay/action style despite the newer system instructions.

Problem:
{{user}} is useful as a per-turn current speaker macro, but card text written for 1:1 roleplay turns it into a universal identity/relationship claim. The card also includes strong route/romance framing and lore assumptions that make sense for SillyTavern but should be narrower for a live group-room companion test.

Scope:
- Rewrite Carlini's live card fields so {{user}} means current speaker, not necessarily the Abbot.
- Make Abbot a specific role/contact relationship that only applies when the current speaker is actually the operator/Abbot or when context says the person is being addressed that way.
- Preserve the concise first-person/no-action-text style from the v1.1 card.
- Remove or soften route/romance/game framing that makes group-room participants all share one 1:1 relationship state.
- Keep mes_example and first_mes disabled unless deliberately re-enabled; if re-enabled, examples must match first-person short-line style and group-room semantics.
- Preserve useful character flavor: chaotic monastery livestreamer, gardening, gossip, bored easily, playful, but without universal Abbot assumptions.
- Apply through the repo/runtime-approved identity/card update path with history, not by ad hoc live file edits.

Acceptance:
- Rendered static prompt no longer states that every {{user}} is the Abbot.
- In a group-room smoke with at least two non-operator contacts, Carlini does not call each participant Abbot by default.
- Replies remain first-person, 1-2 short lines, and avoid action narration/asterisks/emojis in at least a short smoke sample.
- The card history records the update and the active card version is inspectable in Garden/admin surfaces.
- No provider secrets or unrelated runtime config are changed.

Discovered from: psfn-framework-bjvm
notes:
Existing response-length/style mechanisms checked after operator note:
- Discord text outbound chunks at MAX_DISCORD_LENGTH=2000 via src/channels/discord/adapter.ts splitMessage/sendReply; adapter exposes outbound.textChunkLimit=2000.
- Telegram text outbound chunks at TELEGRAM_TEXT_LIMIT=4096 via src/channels/telegram/adapter.ts splitMessage/sendTextInternal; streaming edits fail if a single edited message exceeds 4096.
- Discord/API voice paths validate TTS input length via validateTtsInputText, default maxTtsChars=3000, before synthesis. Gateway voice stream also chunks text for reverse RPC transport.
- Runtime response style already marks Discord guild/voice, Telegram, and API voice channels as concise and injects concise prompt guidance.
- I did not find a reusable assistant-output postprocessor that strips roleplay narration, asterisk actions, emotes, or emojis. Current controls appear prompt/style based plus transport/voice safety limits. If we need hard enforcement for Carlini, add or reuse a shared final-output sanitizer deliberately rather than hiding it in one transport.
Follow-up created from operator note: psfn-framework-w4tx tracks making concise/expressive manually selectable per channel through Garden/settings instead of env-only RESPONSE_STYLE_OVERRIDES.
Live Carlini card optimized through Garden admin identity field API, not an ad hoc companion.json overwrite. Applied updates to description, personality, scenario, system_prompt, post_history_instructions, creator_notes, first_mes, mes_example, and alternate_greetings. Garden identity reports active version=12, historyCount=11, and current scenario begins with multi-human wording: '{{char}} is in a monastery-adjacent Discord/community test environment with several human participants. The current speaker is {{user}}...' Validation: active scenario no longer contains '{{user}} is the Abbot'; system prompt says {{user}} is current speaker and forbids calling someone Abbot unless that specific contact/context says so. Live post-rollout replies in Discord were concise one-line spoken responses without roleplay narration, e.g. after MrDragonFox/Iki turns she replied in short first-person/personality-focused lines and did not call non-operator participants Abbot by default.
close_reason: Carlini live card updated through Garden identity API to group-room semantics and verified as active version 12.

title: Analyze Carlini card and contact profile summary failures
description:
Summary:
Analyze the Carlini test card and contact profile summary generation after the first multi-human kube room test, without changing code or live config.

Context:
The operator observed that Carlini's card is still too SillyTavern/1:1 oriented: {{user}} is treated as the Abbot, everyone gets addressed as Abbot in a multi-human room, and replies overuse roleplay narration/emotes. The updated card reduces narration and talkativeness. Separately, generated summaries from memory/contact profiles are distorted, likely due attribution and source-memory wording.

Scope:
- Inspect the live Carlini card/prompt-layer material enough to identify where Abbot/{{user}} assumptions enter runtime prompts.
- Compare the pasted v1.1 card shape against the observed failures.
- Inspect code that generates contact profile summaries from L2 memories.
- Identify whether summary corruption is caused by card text, memory extraction ownership, profile synthesis prompt, or source-memory hygiene.
- Record findings and follow-up bead recommendations. No code or live config changes.

Acceptance:
- Findings distinguish card/runtime prompt issues from contact profile synthesis issues.
- Relevant code paths and live artifacts are identified.
- Follow-up beads are updated or created with detailed acceptance if needed.
- No code or live config changes.
notes:
Analysis results (2026-06-28):

Card:
- The kube/live Carlini card already has concise response instructions: first-person only, 1-2 short lines, no roleplay narration/action text/asterisks/emojis. That reduces emotes, but the active card is only a partial version of the user-provided v1.1 card and still lacks the full alternate greetings/extensions/version fields from the pasted card.
- The remaining card problem is semantic, not just macro rendering. Runtime correctly resolves {{user}} per turn via buildPromptTemplateVariables/buildDynamicPromptTemplateVariables, so {{user}} is useful for multi-user rooms. However, the card text still says "{{user}} is the Abbot" and creator/scenario text frames the route as 1:1 romance with the Abbot. In a group room, that makes every current speaker inherit the Abbot role.
- Live prompt layers show message examples and first message disabled by default, so the emote/action leakage is not coming from active mes_example/first_mes layers. If it persists, likely sources are model inertia, legacy active prompt/cache, old card turns in history, or other runtime/context layers.
- The pasted v1.1 card is better for style control but still not optimized for group rooms because it keeps {{user}} as the Abbot. The fix should preserve {{user}} as current speaker while moving Abbot into explicit relationship/contact context.

Contact profile summaries:
- profile-synthesis.ts builds contact summaries from getMemoriesByContact(canonicalContactId), then sends raw memory.text lines plus only the UUID as {contact_id}; it does not pass display name, nickname, channel context, speaker, subject, or relationship metadata to the prompt.
- normalizeProfileSummary only whitespace-normalizes/truncates. It does not reject unresolved macros, duplicate names like "Carlini Carlini", or obviously cross-attributed facts.
- Retrieval later renders the profile as authoritative "Core profile for this person", so bad contact_profile rows poison future prompts.
- Live DB evidence shows the issue is downstream of L2 contamination: Iki profile used source memories about MrDragonFox/Carlini and concluded Iki is "known as MrDragonFox and also by the name Carlini"; Vega profile says "Carlini Carlini" and streaming guardrails; MrDragonFox profile includes a mixed "has a Carlini named Carlini" relationship.
- Root causes are layered: group-room extraction writes facts from a mixed recent window under the trigger contact; memory text hygiene allows bad macro/name artifacts through; profile synthesis is target-blind and consumes those rows verbatim.

Tracked follow-ups:
- psfn-framework-ro4k: optimize Carlini card for multi-human rooms.
- psfn-framework-gfl5: make contact profile synthesis target-aware and attribution-safe.
- Existing prerequisites remain psfn-framework-8it9 (group-room speaker ownership) and psfn-framework-0zd6 (macro/name hygiene). Repair/cleanup of existing rows remains psfn-framework-fq24 after fixes land.
close_reason: Analysis complete; card/profile root causes documented and follow-up beads filed

title: Harden memory text macro/name hygiene for {{user}} and {{char}}
description:
Summary:
Harden memory extraction/profile text against raw character-card macros and duplicate participant names in generated memory text.

Evidence:
In Carlini kube on 2026-06-28, L2 rows and contact profile summaries contained "Carlini Carlini". The active prompt registry was the default v1 memory.extraction prompt, which is singular-user oriented and uses "User" examples. src/faculties/memory/extraction/naming.ts normalizes generic "user", "assistant", and "companion" labels, but does not handle raw {{user}}/{{char}} tokens or adjacent duplicate participant names. profile-synthesis then consumes L2 memory text verbatim, amplifying bad text into contact_profiles.

Problem:
Character-card macros are useful in persona prompts, but durable memory text must not store literal {{user}}/{{char}} or artifacts of macro expansion such as duplicated companion names. Multi-human rooms make {{user}} especially unsafe because there is no single human participant.

Scope:
- Update the default memory.extraction prompt to use "human participant(s)" / "named speaker" language instead of singular "the user" framing.
- Add explicit extraction guidance forbidding raw {{user}}/{{char}} and requiring actual speaker/companion names when known.
- Add a durable-memory text hygiene gate that rejects or normalizes raw {{user}}, {{char}}, {{character}}, {{assistant}}, and adjacent duplicate resolved names before write/profile synthesis.
- Ensure profile synthesis does not emit or preserve raw macros or duplicate names from source memories.
- Add tests for macro tokens, possessives, duplicate companion names, and multi-human wording.

Acceptance:
- getDefaultPromptText(memory.extraction) no longer frames all memories as facts about "the user" in a way that conflicts with group rooms.
- normalize/name-hygiene tests cover "{{user}}", "{{char}}", "{{char}} {{char}}", "Carlini Carlini", and possessive forms.
- A parsed fact containing unresolved macros is either rewritten with known participant names or rejected with telemetry; it is not written to L2.
- Profile synthesis output is checked so contact_profiles cannot contain raw macros or adjacent duplicate participant names.
- npm run lint passes before closure.

notes:

title: Fix group-room memory extraction speaker ownership
description:
Summary:
Fix memory extraction ownership in multi-human Discord rooms so durable facts are assigned to the speaker or explicit subject, not blindly to the contact whose turn triggered extraction.

Evidence:
In Carlini kube on 2026-06-28, session 1486443955561299979 lines 56-66 included several speakers. MrDragonFox directly said: "ya i mean if we put her on twitch or yt live or ticktok we need also guardrails". The interval extraction triggered on Vega's later turn and wrote L2 memory 91502042-eae5-41fb-809c-8b351e7a9884 under Vega contact 2dee7909-7a8b-4255-8da1-77685eef5781 with text beginning "MrDragonFox believes...". That then fed the Vega contact profile.

Problem:
The extractor consumes a mixed recent window and passes one canonicalContactId through processFact for every accepted fact. In group channels this conflates extraction trigger contact with fact owner. Per-entry authorName exists in the transcript, but the parsed fact schema has no speaker/subject contact field and the writer cannot route fact ownership accurately.

Scope:
- Extend extraction output or orchestration metadata so each fact carries speaker/subject attribution when the transcript contains multiple human speakers.
- Route self-stated facts to the speaker's canonical contact, not the triggering contact.
- Preserve relational facts about third parties as relational facts with explicit subject/object wording and correct contact ownership.
- Keep current single-user/DM behavior unchanged.
- Make profile synthesis consume only facts owned by the target contact, plus explicitly related facts that are safe and labeled as about another person.
- Add telemetry/debug evidence for routed contact id, source speaker, and trigger contact id without logging secrets.

Acceptance:
- A test transcript with Vega and MrDragonFox proves MrDragonFox's statement is written to MrDragonFox's contact, even when extraction is triggered by Vega's later turn.
- A fact about Carlini spoken by one user does not create a profile paragraph claiming another user owns or believes it.
- Mixed-speaker extraction writes either separate correctly-owned facts or skips ambiguous facts; it never defaults ambiguous group-room facts to the trigger contact.
- Existing single-user extraction, mention-only contact logic, and contact profile refresh tests still pass.
- npm run lint passes before closure.

Group-room extraction now resolves the source speaker contact when possible, routes self-stated facts to that contact, skips ambiguous mixed-speaker facts instead of defaulting to the trigger contact, records routing metadata through processFact, and refreshes profiles by routed contact. notes: Findings 2026-06-28: Live Carlini kube memory issue is not only contact-key attribution. Evidence from Postgres l2_memories/contact_profiles and session JSONL shows: (1) active prompt registry is the default v1 memory.extraction prompt, which repeatedly says 'the user' and uses User examples; this is unsafe wording for multi-human Discord rooms. (2) Source lines 56-66 show MrDragonFox directly said 'if we put her on twitch or yt live or ticktok we need also guardrails'; extraction wrote it to Vega contact 2dee7909... as 'MrDragonFox believes that if Carlini Carlini...' because the extraction run was triggered on Vega's turn and used a mixed recent window. (3) The L2 row 91502042... and profile row for contact 2dee7909... contain 'Carlini Carlini', proving companion-name/macro/name duplication survives into profile synthesis. (4) naming.ts only normalizes generic user/assistant/companion labels, not raw {{user}}/{{char}} macros or adjacent duplicate companion names. (5) profile-synthesis consumes existing memory text verbatim, so once bad text lands in L2 it is amplified into contact_profiles. title: Kubernetes provider-routing shape for LiteLLM, direct endpoints, and billing metadata
description:
Summary:
Define the Kubernetes-era provider routing contract so LiteLLM remains a first-class routing and billing/usage integration option without making every deployment depend on localhost-only LiteLLM assumptions.

Context:
During Artie kube validation, the live Pi providers.json had LiteLLM enabled at http://127.0.0.1:4000/v1 and OpenRouter provider/source metadata. In Kubernetes, 127.0.0.1 inside gateway/agent pods is not the host LiteLLM service, so the shakedown needed direct OpenRouter routing from source metadata. The operator clarified that LiteLLM was originally introduced to support many providers and to provide provider/billing/usage data; kube should preserve that capability deliberately rather than treating LiteLLM as dead code.

Scope:
- Inventory current provider data flow across providers.json, models.json modelRegistry identity/source fields, LLM routing candidates, stream-adapter model resolution, usage/budget metadata, and any LiteLLM billing/provider discovery calls.
- Decide the Kubernetes contract for each provider route mode: in-cluster LiteLLM service, external LiteLLM endpoint, direct OpenRouter endpoint, and other direct OpenAI-compatible endpoints.
- Define Helm values and generated env/secrets shape for LiteLLM: enabled/disabled, service URL, api key ref, upstream provider key refs, and whether billing endpoints are enabled.
- Define how billing/usage/provider metadata is collected when the route is LiteLLM versus direct provider, including clear absence semantics for data not available on direct routes.
- Ensure no kube path assumes host-local 127.0.0.1 unless explicitly configured as an in-pod sidecar. Use Kubernetes service DNS or explicit external URLs.
- Document migration behavior for Pi/live provider files imported into kube so source metadata can route safely while preserving operator intent.

Files likely involved:
- charts/psfn/values.yaml and templates/secrets/configmaps/deployments if LiteLLM is charted or referenced
- src/primitives/llm/routing.ts
- src/primitives/llm/client.ts
