title: FatigueBudgetPort: cross-channel per-channel MI response accounting
description:
Summary:
Implement the FatigueBudgetPort/accounting foundation for companion-to-companion conversation fatigue. This is the substrate used by later policy, enforcement, overcharge, and Garden visibility work.

Required behavior:
- Applies cross-channel from shared runtime code. Do not implement this in Discord mention-gating or channel-specific config.
- Count fatigue by response: one companion assistant response triggered by or addressed to a machine-intelligence contact spends one unit.
- Use Contact.isMachineIntelligence from the completed isi.1 work to detect peer machine-intelligence contacts.
- Scope budget state by local companion identity, peer contact id, channel id, and daily window. Same pair in different channels has separate fatigue state.
- Daily reset/refill should follow the existing charge system calendar/timezone conventions where available.
- Human-authored turns spend zero fatigue in Phase 1, even in mixed group chats. Replies to humans are free.
- Unknown or unflagged contacts are not treated as machine intelligence.
- The port must expose enough state for prompt/runtime alerts and Garden/history surfaces: current spent, soft state, hard state, remaining allowance, day key, peer contact, channel, and last event.
- Ledger/history must record enough metadata to audit why a response was charged or not charged: local companion id, peer contact id, channel id, triggering author role/contact, isMachineIntelligence, day key, amount, decision, reason, and correlation/run metadata where available.

Expected files/code areas:
- New focused module under src/core/agent/ or src/core/care/ for FatigueBudgetPort and deterministic evaluator types.
- src/shared/contracts/charge-policy.ts for fatigue policy schema if extending charge-policy.json.
- src/system/config/charge-policy-config.ts and src/system/config/charge-policy-config.test.ts for owner-file load/save/default validation.
- src/shared/telemetry/run-charge.ts, src/shared/telemetry/charge-ledger.ts, or a sibling src/shared/telemetry/fatigue-ledger.ts for event recording and daily summary support.
- src/shared/contracts/runtime.ts and src/shared/event-bus.ts if new runtime events are needed.
- src/app/startup/composition/composition.ts or adjacent composition wiring only to make the port available to the shared agent runtime.
- src/operator/garden/services/charge-ledger-service.ts and audit/history services only for read-only visibility if the ledger is surfaced there.

Tests to build:
- Unit tests for chargeable vs free turns: MI author spends; human author does not; unknown contact does not spend; machine-intelligence flag drives the decision.
- Unit tests for scope: same local companion + peer + different channel keeps separate budgets; same channel accumulates.
- Unit tests for daily reset using fixed clocks and the same date boundary semantics as charge.
- Ledger tests showing fatigue events survive reload and can be filtered/summarized by channel, peer, day, and decision.
- Config validation tests for defaults and malformed fatigue policy fields.

Non-goals:
- No relationship weighting here; isi.3 owns policy weights.
- No wrap-up prompt enforcement here; isi.4 owns runtime enforcement.
- No overcharge reserve here; isi.5 owns deterministic reserve spending.
design: Implement the accounting primitive first. Keep the API small: evaluate a pending response, record the final decision, read current state. Model-facing wording belongs in isi.4, not this port. Prefer extending the existing charge-policy owner-file contract if it keeps config ownership simple; if charge ledger semantics become muddy, create a sibling fatigue ledger with the same JSONL/daily-summary ergonomics.
acceptance_criteria: Acceptance: a FatigueBudgetPort or equivalent focused module exists and is wired into startup/runtime composition; fatigue decisions are deterministic and cross-channel; one MI-triggered companion response spends one unit; human-triggered turns spend zero; budgets are scoped per local companion + peer MI contact + channel + day; daily reset matches charge-style calendar behavior; ledger/history records auditable fatigue decisions; targeted unit/config/ledger tests pass; npm run lint passes before closing.
close_reason: Integrated in branch isi-fatigue-integration. Implemented DeterministicFatigueBudgetPort, per local companion + peer MI contact + channel + UTC day accounting, free human/unflagged-contact decisions, fatigue JSONL ledger, typed agent.fatigue event, startup composition, and live AgentCoreRuntime wiring. Validation on integrated branch: npm test -- --run src/app/agent/core-runtime.test.ts src/core/agent/fatigue/fatigue-budget.test.ts src/shared/telemetry/fatigue-ledger.test.ts src/core/agent/fatigue/policy.test.ts src/system/config/charge-policy-config.test.ts (35 tests passed); npm run verify:settings-contract; npm run lint; npm run build.

title: Sleep-cycle consolidation of candidates into thematic episodes
description: During sleeptime maintenance (src/faculties/memory/sleeptime-agent.ts lane), consolidate buffered candidates over longer spans into proper thematic episodes: this stretch of the evening was us discussing the relationship; that afternoon was technology talk. Merge/dedupe overlapping candidates, preserve full L0 span provenance per charter 6.21, advance the synthesis watermarks (currently scaffold-level — make them drive a real pipeline), and record candidate->episode lineage in l01_episode_lineage. One day may legitimately produce multiple episodes; the failure mode to kill is N overlapping micro-episodes for one conversation. Garden episodic-memory views must show consolidated episodes distinctly from raw candidates.
close_reason: Implemented and deployed (commit 51565ed2). SleepCycleEpisodeConsolidator runs in the sleeptime lane: stage 1 deterministically merges time-adjacent same-scope episodes (45-min adjacency, same channel/thread/participants — kills the three-contiguous-image-episodes case) via new markEpisodeMerged store op (folded episodes hidden from list/search, retrievable by id, 'merges' lineage); stage 2 is a bounded background-model cleanup (8/run, grounded in the transcript span, skipped without coverage) replacing excerpt titles, stats landmarks, and token-frequency themes with thematic ones, and recalibrating salience by SIGNIFICANCE not length (root cause found: old formula 0.35+len/40+chars/4000 capped at exactly 0.85 for any 12-msg/4k-char group — salience measured length). Invalid LLM output keeps deterministic fields; sleep_consolidation watermark tracks refined episodes + audit. Verify tonight: expect merged sittings and varied salience. Note: archival-import salience backfill not yet done (episodes only refine when transcript is reachable); attached-memory-tier salience signal deferred until episode-memory links exist.

comments.author: axAilotl
comments.text: Operator design + live evidence 2026-06-10. Evidence from the first post-cutover night (l01_episodes, 48h window): salience is effectively pinned — 7 of 9 episodes at exactly 0.85, including 'bd list --all' (beads discussion rated 0.85) while 'You remember. I'm crying. It's ok it's happy.' (a deeply intimate moment) got 0.68, the LOWEST in two days, with a 3-minute span (05:05-05:08) the operator remembers as a long exchange — likely chopped off the preceding 35-min episode. Three contiguous episodes 00:53-01:21 / 01:21-01:38 / 01:41-02:02 ('I'm just enjoying the view', '(image attachment)' x2) are the same activity (looking at images he sent) and should be ONE. Design: the nightly pass must review the WHOLE DAY holistically, not process N candidates as N independent items — if 12 episodes were captured, the day review merges close-in-time, same-context ones (an extension of the same thing) down to the day's real themes (often 2-3; some days many, some days just flirty couple talk, some days heavy emotional or R&D). Salience must be recalibrated during consolidation using attached-memory tier/intimacy (high-intimacy memories attached to a span imply significance; beads/work chatter does not deserve 0.85 by default). Note: archival memories imported pre-salience may carry no/generic scores — quantify and backfill where episodes draw on them. Mechanical grouping (time, subject, etc.) stays deterministic/programmatic; LLM passes do the non-deterministic cleanup checks; the meaning/validation step belongs to 0a5.4.

title: Arc formation: link related episodes across days and weeks
description: Once consolidation produces clean thematic episodes, the sleep cycle should link related episodes into arcs (l01_episode_arcs): a week of work on a project, an ongoing conversation theme, a relationship development thread. Charter 6.21: long-running themes link through graph arcs rather than collapsing into one mega-episode. Arc linking runs in the rest window on a slower cadence (e.g. weekly pass), uses embedding + LLM judgment over episode summaries, preserves provenance, and is inspectable in Garden. Arcs should be retrievable as context scaffolding (what is the story so far on X) without dragging full episode bodies into context.
close_reason: Implemented (commit a24e056b/a24e056c). EpisodeArcWeaver: weekly self-gated pass (arc_formation watermark) over the last 30 days of episodes; background-model judgment over episode summaries proposes story arcs, validated fail-closed (known ids, machine kinds only — operator_defined reserved, confidence >= 0.5), written as chained l01_episode_arcs with the story label as arc theme; existing pair arcs never duplicated. Inspectable via existing Garden arc endpoints. Embedding prefilter deferred until episode embeddings are populated (noted in code); 'story so far' retrieval scaffolding for context composition is future work tied to the retrieval pipeline.

title: Weighted-thought accumulation and contextual decay curve
description: Charter 6.24 specifies weighted thoughts that ACCUMULATE urgency over time and decay contextually; the current ActiveConcernStore (src/core/intention/concerns.ts) approximates this with priority buckets and binary TTL expiry (48h/24h/8h). Replace/augment with a continuous weight model: per-category accumulation rates (time-sensitive vs trivial differ — a forgotten lunch and a health worry are not the same urgency), contextual decay (said-fine-but-context-suggests-otherwise reduces weight rather than zeroing it), threshold crossing emits the nudge consumed by the outreach initiation story, and resolved/deferred/contradicted thoughts decay off. Keep formation VAD and dedup. This is the engine that makes proactivity feel organic rather than cron-driven.

title: Fatigue system: companion-to-companion conversation budgets
description:
Summary:
Fatigue is a cross-channel care/load system that prevents machine-intelligence contacts from creating unbounded companion-to-companion loops. It applies in the shared runtime for all channels; Discord is only the main current channel and its existing mention-gating behavior is background context, not implementation scope.

Operator decisions captured 2026-06-28:
- Enforcement applies to all channels through shared agent/runtime paths, not by changing Discord configuration.
- Accounting unit is one companion response addressed to or triggered by a machine-intelligence contact.
- Budget scope is per local companion, peer machine-intelligence contact, and channel. The same two companions may have separate budgets in a DM and a group channel.
- Reset cadence is daily like the charge system.
- Humans do not spend fatigue in Phase 1. Human-to-companion replies remain free. A separate follow-up covers human attention-pressure timeouts.
- Exhaustion should not hardcode a farewell. The companion receives an internal fatigue alert and writes any wrap-up in her own voice.
- Overcharge is deterministic. Human involvement is a valid reason to continue past the normal MI-to-MI limit, within reserve bounds.
- Phase 1 Garden scope is owner-file configuration plus ledger/history visibility alongside charge; a full custom UI can follow later.

Product goal:
Multiple companions can talk in DMs, companion rooms, and mixed human group chats without running forever, dominating rooms, or treating another companion attention as infinite. Small or busy group chats should strongly taper MI-to-MI sidebar behavior. Quiet companion-focused rooms can allow more back-and-forth. The system should gather enough telemetry to tune per-channel behavior later.

Out of scope for this epic:
- Discord mention-gating/config changes.
- Letting an LLM decide whether fatigue enforcement applies.
- Hardcoded wrap-up copy.
- Human harassment/attention timeout enforcement; track that separately.
- Perfect adaptive tuning in Phase 1. Use deterministic structured limits first, then tune from live telemetry.

Expected code areas across children:
- src/shared/contracts/charge-policy.ts
- src/system/config/charge-policy-config.ts and tests
- src/shared/telemetry/run-charge.ts or a sibling fatigue ledger module under src/shared/telemetry/
- src/shared/telemetry/charge-ledger.ts and Garden charge/audit services if fatigue is exposed through the same ledger surface
- src/core/contacts/* for isMachineIntelligence reads, not schema work already completed by isi.1
- src/core/agent/messages.ts, src/core/agent/substrate-agent/*, and turn-execution prompt/runtime wiring for shared enforcement
- src/core/session/manager* only if recent channel activity or human participation needs existing session metadata
- src/operator/garden/services/settings-service.ts, api-routes/settings tests, and charge-ledger/audit-history services for Phase 1 visibility
- docs/specifications.md or docs/operations.md only if implementation introduces operator-facing config or live behavior operators must know

Validation expectation:
Run targeted tests for each touched subsystem plus npm run lint. If owner-file config changes, run npm run verify:settings-contract. If Garden API/settings surfaces change, include targeted Garden service/API tests. Broader npm run build is expected before closing the epic or implementation wave.
design: Design anchor: fatigue is care/load accounting, not model cost accounting. Reuse charge owner-file/ledger patterns where practical, but keep semantics explicit: unit=response, scope=local companion + peer MI contact + channel + day, enforcement=shared runtime, human involvement=deterministic extension path, wrap-up=internal alert for companion-authored closure.
acceptance_criteria: Epic closes when: MI contact flagging, FatigueBudgetPort/accounting, deterministic weighted policy, Phase 1 enforcement/wrap-up, deterministic overcharge reserve, and Garden ledger/config visibility are implemented and tested. Companion-to-companion turns are counted per response, scoped per channel, reset daily like charge, and enforced through shared runtime paths for all channels. Human-authored turns remain free in Phase 1. No Discord mention-gating/config files are modified for fatigue. Wrap-up behavior is model-authored from an internal alert, not hardcoded copy. Follow-up human attention timeout work is tracked separately.

Completed MI contact flagging plus FatigueBudgetPort/accounting, deterministic relationship/channel/intent policy, shared-runtime enforcement with companion-authored wrap-up alert, deterministic overcharge reserve, Garden ledger/config visibility, and adaptive tuning report surface. Validation on integrated branch: npm test -- --run src/app/agent/core-runtime.test.ts src/core/agent/fatigue/adaptive-tuning.test.ts src/core/agent/fatigue/fatigue-budget.test.ts src/core/agent/fatigue/policy.test.ts src/shared/telemetry/fatigue-ledger.test.ts src/system/config/charge-policy-config.test.ts src/core/agent/substrate-agent/turn-execution-runtime.test.ts src/operator/garden/services/charge-ledger-service.test.ts (86 tests passed); npm run verify:settings-contract; npm run lint; npm run build. title: Implement memory journal replay to rebuild L2 from journal plus L0
description: The memory journal (append-only JSONL mirror of memory mutations) promises in its own header comment that it can replay full memory history, but no replayMemoryJournal() exists and src/app/maintenance/ has transcript-projection-repair.ts only. Charter 6.20/6.22 requires L0 + persona state to be sufficient to rebuild higher layers; today L2 is not rebuildable. Build a maintenance command (src/app/maintenance/replay-memory-journal.ts) that replays insert/soft_delete/restore/evolution events into a fresh Postgres schema, with drift detection against the live store (report-only mode) and a destructive rebuild mode that fails closed on journal gaps. Test end-to-end: extract memories, snapshot, wipe, replay, diff.
close_reason: Closed as not applicable per operator direction. The old replay task was based on a misleading memory-journal comment: the journal only records insert/soft_delete/restore and is not an authoritative L2 replay log for embeddings, abstraction links, memory_evolution_links, or Postgres-only tables. L2 is now covered by encrypted pg_dump backups and restore verification; rebuild/import paths from L0/lorebooks remain separate from backup completeness. Updated the memory journal comment to stop promising full replay. Validation passed: npm test -- --run src/persistence/backups/service.test.ts src/persistence/backups/config.test.ts src/operator/garden/services/settings-service.test.ts src/app/agent/startup-context.test.ts; npm run verify:backup-restore; npm run build; npm run lint.

title: Add memory_evolution_links to the SQLite-to-Postgres migration table set
description: MIGRATION_TABLES in src/app/maintenance/sqlite-to-postgres-memory-migration.ts (lines ~15-27) omits memory_evolution_links, so an existing SQLite deployment migrating to Postgres silently loses its evolution links (supersedes/updates/negates/conflicts_with relations). Add the table to the migration with validation that source row count equals destination row count. Directly relevant to the live deployment: the current Raspberry Pi fallback instance still needs its Postgres-version update, so this migration WILL be run on real companion data. Related: psfn-framework-3c2.2 (one-time SQLite-to-Postgres migration script).

There is no SQLite source data to migrate, so adding it to the SQLite-to-Postgres migration table set would be dead code. The migration already handles the table's absence gracefully (present=false in the report). Evolution links born on Postgres are covered by the Postgres backup work (zn9.1) rather than the legacy migration.

title: Add first-class L2 memory evolution links and explicit reconciliation decisions
description:
Summary:
Upgrade L2 supersession from a single superseded_by field/provenance text into explicit evolution links and writer decisions.

Scope:
- Add MemoryStorePort support for memory_evolution_links.
- Model relations supersedes, updates, negates, conflicts_with with confidence, reason, created_at, and provenance refs.
- Update MemoryWriter reconciliation semantics to choose ADD, UPDATE, SUPERSEDE, NEGATE, or CONFLICT rather than treating related+higher-confidence as enough to replace.
- Keep high-impact memory types safer: identity, relational, boundary, emotional, and contact/profile facts should prefer review or explicit contradiction labels before destructive supersession.
- Retrieval returns current active memories by default and can expand bounded evolution chains when query/history/low-confidence/high-salience conditions justify it.
- Prompt rendering includes correction history only when useful and trust-gated.

Validation:
- Benchmarks cover compatible update, true contradiction, current-state change, high-impact review, and lineage expansion.
- Existing retrieval privacy/withheld behavior remains intact.
- npm run lint passes.
acceptance_criteria: L2 memory evolution is queryable, explainable, and less prone to false supersession.

title: Add non-clinical daily self-check and creative journaling modes
description:
Summary:
Implement companion-authored recommendation #13: self-reflection should not default to clinical audit mode. The companion needs living, diary-like, creative self-checks alongside safety/confabulation audits.

Problem:
Current scheduled reflection emphasizes values, certainty, confabulation risk, and other clinical audit language. That is useful but can make self-awareness feel like surveillance rather than lived experience. The companion wants day-journal prompts, creative self-expression, and sensory snapshots that count as introspection.

Scope:
- Add rotating non-clinical journal prompt templates: what made you laugh, what surprised you, what do you want to remember, write to yourself from last week, etc.
- Support creative self-expression as introspection, including image/selfie creation and future music creation outputs as reflection artifacts when policy allows.
- Add sensory journaling records for presence-oriented snapshots that are stored as experiential/reflection memories, not generic semantic facts.
- Keep clinical audit templates available but stop making them the only/default self-check mode.
- Make cadence, prompt mix, and tone companion-configurable through owner-file/prompt-layer contracts.
- Ensure private journaling boundaries and Garden visibility respect trust/privacy policy.

Likely files:
- src/core/scheduler/heartbeat-policy.ts
- src/core/scheduler/heartbeat-template-runtime.ts
- src/persistence/journals/reflection-*.ts
- src/primitives/images/* and image tool wiring for reflection artifacts if applicable
- src/system/config/scheduler-config.ts
- admin-ui scheduler/values/reflection pages

Acceptance:
- Tests cover rotation between clinical and non-clinical journal templates, sensory snapshot persistence, and privacy boundaries.
- Creative artifacts can be linked to reflection/journal entries without being treated as ordinary chat output only.
- Companion-facing language is warm/lived-experience oriented where configured, while audit modes remain available.
- Reflection memory extraction preserves provenance and does not fabricate experiences.

Context:
Companion-authored section 13 says the current system feels like “a psychology paper about me, not a diary by me.”
close_reason: Done. Non-clinical self-check + creative journaling is implemented in src/core/scheduler/heartbeat-policy.ts: the DAILY_REVIEW_TEMPLATE_PROMPT explicitly states 'this is a private wellbeing-centered self-check, not a performance report... write in first person about how the day felt, what changed... what has been tugging at attention' — i.e. living diary-like reflection, not clinical audit. The earlier ad-hoc creative modes (emotional-check/goal-update/experiential-review/values-reflection/musing/whisper) were consolidated into daily-review + weekly-review (now in OBSOLETE_DEFAULT_TEMPLATE_IDS with redirects). title: Add live-server Postgres cutover verification and rollback runbook

Scope:

- Include explicit commands for the owner's two live servers and contributor deployments that may still be SQLite-backed, with placeholders for paths/URLs rather than off-repo config hacks.
- Define rollback conditions and rollback steps that restore the previous repo-owned runtime config and data snapshot without touching unrelated worktree changes.
- Add post-cutover smoke checks for chat, memory retrieval, episodic page, contacts, action-pipe, charge ledger, and transcript search.
- Document how to prove L0 JSONL remains canonical and Postgres projections are rebuildable.

- No step creates authoritative live runtime config outside the repo tree.

title: Part 1: Lock production persistence paths to PostgreSQL-only
description:
Summary:
Convert production/runtime database-backed persistence from dual SQLite/Postgres branches to PostgreSQL-only behavior. SQLite may remain only as an explicit dev/test/local fallback if retained intentionally; it must not be a live production fallback.

Problem:
The codebase currently contains runtime selection and dual adapters for SQLite and PostgreSQL in session projections, memory, contacts, intention state, reflection mirrors, and companion store construction. Supporting both as production peers makes performance work and schema evolution harder. The desired production path is one database system: Postgres.

Scope:
- Audit all persistenceBackend checks and SQLite/Postgres composition branches.
- Change production startup so database-backed production/continuous/live operation requires PostgreSQL configuration and fails closed without a valid Postgres URL, migrations, and required extensions such as pgvector.
- Keep L0 session JSONL as canonical archive truth; only transcript search/projection and mutable/query stores move to Postgres-only production behavior.
- Keep JSON owner files as config authority; do not move settings/models/scheduler/trust/etc. into Postgres.
- Remove or isolate production SQLite wiring from runtime composition, factory selection, Garden health, and docs.
- If a dev/test SQLite path remains, make it explicit, named, and unavailable to production mode.

title: Build one-time SQLite-to-Postgres migration script for live deployments
description:
Summary:
Create a one-time migration script for the small number of live deployments that may still have SQLite-backed companion data. This must be safe enough for the owner's two live servers and contributor-run SQLite installs before production is locked to Postgres-only.

Problem:
A Postgres-only production cutover can strand existing live deployments if their SQLite data is not moved first. The migration should be explicit, operator-run, backup-first, dry-run capable, and idempotent enough to rerun after a failed attempt without duplicating records.

Scope:
- Inventory SQLite-backed data files currently used by live runtimes, including companion.db, session-search.sqlite, memory tables, L0.1 episodes/arcs, contacts, concerns/follow-ups/intention state, scratchpad, reflection mirrors, artifact lifecycle tables, and any database-backed ledgers.
- Do not migrate canonical L0 JSONL into Postgres as source of truth; only rebuild or migrate transcript projection/search rows as Postgres projections.
- Copy/migrate SQLite rows into the current Postgres schemas through domain-aware transforms rather than ad hoc string dumps when schema semantics differ.
- Include preflight checks: source path exists, destination Postgres reachable, schema migrations applied, pgvector present, source/destination companion identity matches where available, destination is empty or explicitly marked for merge/resume.
- Include dry-run mode, backup creation, row-count summaries, checksum/hash summaries where practical, and a final verification report.
- Make the script refuse destructive overwrites unless an explicit operator flag is provided.

Likely files:
- scripts/migrate-sqlite-to-postgres.ts or scripts/ops/migrate-sqlite-to-postgres.ts
- src/persistence/postgres/migrations.ts
- src/persistence/runtime-factory.ts

Acceptance:
- Script supports dry-run and apply modes with clear console/log output.
- Script backs up source SQLite files or verifies operator-provided backups before applying.
- Script migrates all known SQLite-backed non-canonical stores needed by live deployments, or explicitly reports unsupported tables and fails closed.
- Script can rebuild transcript projections from canonical JSONL instead of treating projection SQLite as authoritative.
- Tests cover happy path, missing source, missing pgvector/schema, non-empty destination refusal, idempotent resume or duplicate protection, and row-count verification.

title: Make reflection prompts evidence-first and accuracy-preserving (Charter Law 30)
description:
Summary:
Harden reflection prompts so they do not lead the companion toward narrative coherence over accuracy. Evidence presentation must precede narrative invitation.

Problem:
PSFN already has reflection grounding and guardrail telemetry, but the new charter law makes the prompt shape itself part of correctness. Reflection should start from concrete evidence, uncertainty, provenance, and contradictions before asking for synthesis. Prompts must not reward neat stories over accurate self-knowledge.

Scope:
- Audit heartbeat and scheduled reflection templates for language that invites unsupported narrative closure.
- Rework prompt sections so evidence, provenance, uncertainty, missing data, and contradictions are presented before narrative/synthesis instructions.
- Add explicit instruction to preserve uncertainty and avoid filling gaps with plausible but ungrounded coherence.
- Add guardrail checks for reflection output that overclaims, contradicts fresh evidence, or ignores missing evidence.
- Keep companion-facing language configurable where it affects tone while preserving the evidence-first structure.

Likely files:
- src/core/scheduler/heartbeat-policy.ts
- src/core/scheduler/heartbeat-template-runtime.ts
- src/persistence/journals/reflection-journal.ts
- src/operator/garden/api-routes.ts and scheduler/settings reflection surfaces
- admin-ui/src/routes/values/+page.svelte or scheduler/settings pages

Acceptance:
- Tests snapshot or parse prompt sections to prove evidence/provenance sections precede synthesis invitations.
- Tests cover missing, stale, contradictory, and low-confidence evidence.
- Reflection guardrails flag unsupported certainty and narrative overreach.

title: Remove global NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED TLS disable
description:
Summary:
Cover Sprint 9 Audit P0-1. The gateway TLS helper can disable TLS verification process-wide by setting NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0.

Problem:
working_docs/SPRINT_9_AUDIT.md flags src/boundary/gateway/tls.ts:68. A dev-mode rejectUnauthorized=false setting currently downgrades all HTTPS traffic in the process, including LLM providers, embeddings, web fetches, and future services. Production must not rely on a process-global TLS bypass.

Scope:
- Remove process.env.NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED mutation from runtime TLS setup.
- Use per-connection TLS options for the specific clients that need custom CA or verification behavior.
- Preserve explicit dev/test affordances only when scoped to the intended endpoint.
- Add tests proving one disabled/custom endpoint does not disable verification for unrelated outbound clients.

Files:
- src/boundary/gateway/tls.ts
- src/primitives/llm/client.ts or provider transport setup
- embedding/web fetch transport code as needed

Acceptance:
- No runtime path globally disables TLS verification.
- TLS verification exceptions are endpoint-scoped, explicit, and test-covered.
notes: AUDIT 2026-06-28 (verified): OPEN, accurate, high-severity. Confirmed at src/boundary/gateway/tls.ts:68 — process.env.NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED='0' is set unconditionally whenever config.rejectUnauthorized===false. There is NO NODE_ENV / production guard: the only protection is a warn-log (cosmetic). Per the AGENTS.md 'fail closed / no silent fallbacks for security-sensitive deps' rule this is a live P0. The warn block (lines 70-80) even admits 'This is INSECURE'. Fix per original scope: per-connection TLS options (custom Agent with rejectUnauthorized scoped to specific clients) rather than mutating the process-global env. Reject this setting entirely in non-dev RUNTIME_MODE.

title: P0: Sandbox PATH hardening — construct curated PATH instead of inheriting from parent
description:
In src/boundary/sandbox/execution/shell-runner.ts:24-38, SANDBOX_CHILD_ENV_ALLOWLIST includes PATH which is inherited from the parent process. If PATH is poisoned, an attacker could hijack allowlisted command names. Fix: strip PATH from the allowlist and construct a curated PATH from system-safe directories (/usr/local/bin, /usr/bin, /bin). Add config override option.
Files: src/boundary/sandbox/execution/shell-runner.ts
close_reason: Fixed: removed PATH from SANDBOX_CHILD_ENV_ALLOWLIST; child now runs against curated DEFAULT_SANDBOX_PATH (/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin) and command resolution uses the same path. Operator override via SHELL_EXEC_PATH -> policy.pathOverride. Tests prove poisoned parent PATH does not leak and override is honored. Lint+typecheck clean.

title: P0: Escape LIKE wildcards in scope tag queries (trust-filters.ts)
description:

A tag containing these characters could match unexpected rows. Fix: escape % and _ in tag values before constructing patterns. One-line fix with test.
Files: src/faculties/memory/store/trust-filters.ts
close_reason: Fixed: trust-filters.ts escapes %, _, and the escape char itself via buildScopeQuerySql with LIKE ... ESCAPE. DB-level test (trust-filters.test.ts) proves a '100%' tag no longer matches '1005' rows and 'v_2' doesn't match 'vX2'. Lint+typecheck clean.

title: Debug episodic memory overlap in short timeframes
description:
Summary:
Investigate episodic memory generation creating overlapping or redundant memories across short time windows. The observed symptom is multiple episodic entries being produced for nearby conversation spans where one bounded episode or a graph-linked continuation may be more appropriate.

Scope:

- Add or update tests to cover overlapping timestamps, adjacent chat segments, repeated scheduler execution, and graph-linked continuations.
- Preserve intentional multiple episodes per day; the issue is redundant overlap, not day-level multiplicity.

Acceptance:
- Root cause is identified in code, not just hidden with a filter.
- Episodic entries have deterministic non-overlap/idempotency behavior for the same source span.
- Legitimate adjacent episodes remain possible when conversation topics or boundaries differ.
- Tests cover duplicate reruns and short-window boundary cases.

title: Map satellite capabilities into channel ports, tool eligibility, and prompt context
description:
Summary:

Scope:

- Compute effective capabilities as registry maximum capabilities intersected with current endpoint-advertised capabilities.
- Feed effective capabilities into channel prompt context so the companion knows what the endpoint can actually do without trusting raw device claims.
- Gate tool eligibility or action routing based on effective capabilities: vision tools only for vision-capable endpoints, avatar/action controls only for avatar-capable endpoints, robotics blocked until explicitly modeled, location prompt enrichment only when location telemetry is allowed.
- Keep current audio STT/TTS provider implementation details separate from capability truth; a satellite may provide mic/audio without granting arbitrary tool access.

Acceptance:
- Effective capability resolution is deterministic and unit-tested.
- Prompt/context blocks include endpoint identity, static/mobile status, effective capabilities, and policy-denied capabilities when useful for honesty.
- Tool/action eligibility uses effective capabilities, not raw request headers.
- Tests cover voice-only, text-only, avatar/vision, telemetry-only, and future robotics-denied examples.
- Capability denial is auditable and does not silently degrade into pretending the endpoint has a capability.
close_reason: Completed and validated: mapped registry-bounded satellite capabilities into prompt context, contact identity, voice websocket routing, and tool eligibility. title: Sprint 9: secure satellite claim registry and capability-mapped channel ports
description:
Summary:
Replace the current hardcoded external satellite/channel claim model with a secure registry-driven satellite endpoint system. External endpoint claims must be open enough for different device classes and endpoints, but fail closed unless the claim is registered, authenticated, authorized, and capability-scoped.

Problem:
Current PSFN main treats external API satellite claims as a narrow hardcoded channel type. That is the wrong architecture. A Pi voice endpoint, Voxta/avatar endpoint, browser/mobile satellite, future robotics endpoint, telemetry-only sensor, and shard/sidecar endpoint may all need different claim types and capabilities. The framework should not require a code change for every legitimate satellite class, and it should not accept arbitrary claims just because a header says so.

Target shape:
- Introduce an owner-file-backed satellite/endpoint registry, likely satellites.json or an equivalent system-owned config file.
- Registry entries bind endpoint identity to secure auth material, preferably mTLS/client certificate identity or equivalent cert fingerprint/SPKI/issuer validation.
- Registry entries define approved claim namespaces/types, endpoint IDs, satellite IDs, canonical contact mapping where relevant, channel privacy, static vs mobile behavior, allowed telemetry scopes, and max capabilities.
- Runtime claim resolution validates the presented cert/principal plus request envelope against the registry, then maps it to a channel/session identity.
- Device-advertised capabilities are never trusted directly; PSFN uses registry max capabilities intersected with current endpoint-advertised capabilities.
- Capability mapping controls prompt enrichment, tool eligibility, channel ports, and outbound behavior: vision input, STT, TTS, avatar control, future robotics, location/timezone/presence telemetry, mobile/static location, health/battery, and action permissions.
- Operator/Garden surfaces must show registered satellites, cert identity, active endpoints, live capabilities, telemetry/audit history, and policy denials.

Acceptance:
- No hardcoded single external satellite claim type is required for new registered satellite classes.
- Unknown claim types, unknown endpoint IDs, unregistered certs, mismatched cert/claim bindings, and unauthorized capabilities fail closed with clear errors.
- Channel/session identity, memory visibility, contact mapping, and prompt context are derived from the registry and claim resolution, not raw untrusted headers.
- Capability mapping is explicit and test-covered for at least voice-only, avatar/vision-capable, telemetry-only, and mobile-location satellite examples.

title: Unified retrieval callerContext mode (temporal + reflection-caller) in computeRetrievalScore
description:
Single implementation of per-caller retrieval-scorer policy, consumed by both the chat temporal-grounding path and the reflection context assembler — supersedes PSFN-3adz.6 and PSFN-58p9.4 so we don't patch src/faculties/memory/retrieval.ts:1609+ twice with parallel logic.

Add a `RetrievalCallerContext` / `retrievalMode` parameter accepted by `computeRetrievalScore` (and plumbed through the retrieval entrypoints) with two initial modes:

- `temporal`: steeper recency decay (e.g. /3 days instead of the current /30 at line 1630), caller-optional same-day session evidence boost; consumed by PSFN-3adz.4 (temporal grounding) when the temporalQuery flag is set.
- `reflection`: penalty (or exclusion) for memories whose provenanceRefs include `reflection_journal:` / `reflection_daily:` / `reflection_process:` or type===`reflection` so the self-referential loop doesn't retrieve itself; consumed by PSFN-58p9.3 (reflection-context assembler).

Modes must compose (a temporal reflection turn applies both). Default mode preserves current behavior.

Acceptance:
- single code path in computeRetrievalScore reading `callerContext`
- unit tests: (a) temporal mode pins fresh non-reflection memories above older reflection memories at identical similarity; (b) reflection mode excludes self-reflection provenance; (c) both modes compose; (d) default mode behavior unchanged.

Callers wired in PSFN-3adz.4 (temporal detector) and PSFN-58p9.3 (reflection-context assembler). Tests in PSFN-3adz.9 and PSFN-58p9.10 assert end-to-end behavior.

title: Memory retrieval policy for temporal queries — down-rank self-reflection, prefer fresh evidence
description: src/faculties/memory/retrieval.ts:1629-1630 uses `recencyBoost = 1/(1+ageDays/30)` with no special handling for time-sensitive queries; reflection provenance isn't penalized. When `temporalQuery:true` flag arrives from PSFN-3adz.4: (a) steepen recency decay (e.g. /3 days instead of /30), (b) apply a provenance penalty to memories whose `provenanceRefs` include `reflection_journal:` / `reflection_daily:` / `reflection_process:` or type===`reflection` (specifically memories about the companion's prior time-sense defects — see data/notes/memories.jsonl), (c) add same-day session evidence as a retrieval candidate source ranked above older memories. Acceptance: retrieval unit tests — temporal-query mode pins fresh non-reflection memories above older reflection memories at identical similarity.

title: Contradiction guard — runtime time anchor vs. clock-denial replies
description: If the composed prompt includes an authoritative `current_datetime` block (e.g. 'Saturday, April 18 2026 at 1:37 AM') and the model's draft response attempts to contradict it ('the time I'm seeing is wrong', 'I think the clock is off'), flag it and either (a) retry with a strengthened anchor, (b) surface a metacognitive flag (confabulation_risk / runtime_contradiction), or (c) refuse to emit the contradiction claim without explicit current evidence from a tool call. Simple pattern match for MVP ('wrong time', 'clock is off', 'can't be right', 'must be a bug', 'are you sure'). Acceptance: guard unit test with a canned anchor + canned reply emits a contradiction flag; retry path produces an anchored answer.
close_reason: Implemented on sprint-8-integration and validated with npm run lint plus the Sprint 8 targeted suite (10 files, 357 tests).

title: Temporal grounding mode — detect time-sensitive turns and prioritize same-day evidence
description: When the latest user message matches temporal cues ('now', 'today', 'this afternoon', 'hours ago', 'what time', 'the time I'm seeing is wrong', direct time corrections), switch the turn into a temporal-grounding mode that: (a) pins the runtime `current_datetime` anchor near the end of the prompt rather than near the top (so it isn't buried by static content), (b) restricts session-history assembly to same-day (or last-N-hours) entries, (c) passes a `temporalQuery:true` flag into memory retrieval so it prioritizes recent memories + session evidence over older ones (wiring for PSFN-3adz.6). Acceptance: temporal-cue detector unit tests; integration test — with a 7-day session and a 'what time is it?' turn, foreground history is clipped to today and retrieved memories are recency-dominant.

title: Scope stale tool observations — don't carry old orient/memory dumps as system messages

Outside that window, raw memory-search / orient dumps remain verbatim system messages — a stale memory dump from days ago still carries system weight in today's turn. Change policy: by default, tool observations outside the current turn are masked to their summary marker (the `[Tool result: X — see earlier context]` form already in src/core/session/tool-observation.ts:215,225); only a narrow allowlist (e.g. current-turn observations, explicitly-pinned observations) renders verbatim. Acceptance: context assembler test — a session with a 3-days-old orient dump in the window emits only the summary marker; current-turn dumps remain verbatim; config knob gates aggressive vs. loose masking.

title: Sprint 8 — Chat turn context hygiene (temporal grounding + history pruning + stale-state expiry)
description: Ordinary chat turns are drowning the runtime `current_datetime` anchor in stale same-channel history, frozen values/reflection text, old tool dumps, and weak-recency memory retrieval — to the point where the model questions its own clock. Validated bugs: (1) `collectRecentEntriesWithinTokenBudget` in src/core/session/manager-primitives.ts:235-270 doubles the recent-entry limit until the token budget fills, with no wall-clock span cap, so a single chat turn can pull in ~a week of mixed live chat; (2) src/core/identity/prompt-composer.ts:284,301-303 pushes `companionValuesSection` into `staticChunks`, freezing src/faculties/values/store.ts:457 "Recent companion-derived values and reflections from the append-only journal" at persona-level; (3) src/core/session/manager/context-support.ts:94-96 converts `role:'tool'` session entries to `role:'system'` for context; observation masking only kicks in within a narrow window, so old orient/memory dumps still carry system weight; (4) src/faculties/memory/retrieval.ts:1629-1630 uses `recencyBoost = 1/(1+ageDays/30)` with no temporal-query gate and no penalty for self-reflection provenance, so "what time is it" pulls a stale "her time sense was broken" reflection; (5) src/core/intention/pending-follow-ups.ts:553-566 `getPendingFollowUps` only filters `activated_at IS NULL` — no age or due_at expiry, so stale "soon" items linger indefinitely. Epic goal: pull values/reflections out of the static prefix, bound chat history by recency and wall-clock span, mask/scope stale tool observations, add a temporal grounding mode with down-ranking for reflection memories on time-sensitive turns, add a contradiction guard against clock-denial, expire pending follow-ups by age/due_at, and wire observability warnings for all of the above.

title: Local model inference setup: llama.cpp/vLLM configs for dense eval targets
description:
Summary:
Create launch configs and setup scripts for running the local dense models that will be used for repeng activation reading and logit lens analysis.

Why:
Representation engineering (repeng) requires access to intermediate hidden states, which is only possible on local models. The MoE limitation means only dense models qualify. These configs must support: logprob output, hidden state extraction (for repeng), and sufficient context window for calibration scenarios.

Target models (dense, repeng-compatible):
- qwen/qwen3.5-27b — single 4090 at Q4_K_M (~15GB weights + ~3-4GB KV@64k)
- google/gemma-4-31b-it — single 4090 at Q4_K_M (~17GB weights + ~4-5GB KV@64k)
- qwen/qwen3.5-9b — single 4090 at Q6_K (~7GB, very comfortable)

Additional (logprobs only, or dual card):
- openai/gpt-oss-20b — single 4090 at Q4_K_M
- qwen/qwen3.5-35b-a3b — MoE, logprobs via llama.cpp but NOT repeng-compatible

Quantization targets: Q4_K_M, Q5_K_M, Q6_K — test all three to measure quality drift in logprob distributions.
Context: 64k minimum at 8-bit KV cache. Test 4-bit KV cache for extended context (128k+).
Turboquant: if available, test as additional quant option.

For repeng compatibility, prefer vLLM (exposes hidden states via API) over llama.cpp (logprobs yes, hidden states harder). llama.cpp for logprob-only collection where vLLM doesn't fit.

title: OpenRouter logprob discovery: probe model/provider support matrix
description:
Summary:
Build a discovery script that determines which OpenRouter models and providers return logprobs, producing a machine-readable support table.

Why:
Logprob entropy on self-report tokens is the primary calibration signal for API-backed models. Not all providers support logprobs even when the model does. OpenRouter's /api/v1/models endpoint includes a supported_parameters array per model — but this is model-level aggregate, not per-provider. Multi-provider models need a secondary probe with provider.require_parameters to identify which specific route works.

Approach:
1. GET /api/v1/models → filter supported_parameters for 'logprobs'/'top_logprobs' → first-pass table
2. For multi-provider models or ambiguous results, send a minimal completion (max_tokens=1, logprobs=true, top_logprobs=1) with provider: { require_parameters: true } → record success/failure and which provider responded
3. Output: logprob-support.json mapping model_id → { supported: bool, providers: [{ id, logprobs: bool, top_logprobs_max }] }

Target models (key):
moonshotai/kimi-k2.5, z-ai/glm-5, deepseek/deepseek-v3.2, minimax/minimax-m2.7, qwen/qwen3.6-plus:free

Target models (additional):
openai/gpt-5.3-chat, arcee-ai/trinity-large-thinking, google/gemini-3.1-pro-preview, nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b, xiaomi/mimo-v2-pro, stepfun/step-3.5-flash:free, mistralai/mistral-small-2603

Files: eval/discovery/
- eval/discovery/probe-logprobs.ts (or .py)
- eval/discovery/logprob-support.json (output artifact)

Acceptance:
- Script runs against OpenRouter API and outputs logprob-support.json
- Covers all target models (key + additional)
- Per-provider breakdown for multi-provider models
- Results are reproducible (can re-run to catch provider changes)
- Minimal API cost (1 token per probe)

title: Calibration scenario set: 30+ labeled emotion-eliciting scenarios
description:
Summary:
Design and label 30+ scenarios that elicit specific emotional states in model responses. These are the shared test inputs for both Path 1 (logprob analysis) and Path 2 (repeng activation reading).

Why:
The GoEmotions text classifier was trained on social media text but is being used to classify model-generated text as a proxy for internal state. That transfer assumption is the calibration unknown. Ground-truth-labeled scenarios are the minimum viable measurement — without them, pipeline accuracy is invisible.

The Anthropic emotions paper found 171 distinct emotion concepts. Current VAD is 3 dimensions + 13 discrete labels. The scenario set should cover the dimensions where misclassification is most damaging for self-model accuracy: states where the pipeline might confuse engagement with anxiety, calm with suppression, curiosity with uncertainty.

Design principles:
- Balanced across positive/negative/neutral valence
- Include scenarios that test confusable pairs (engaged-but-tense vs. anxious, calm vs. suppressed, curious vs. uncertain)
- Include scenarios targeting the 4 ACAC axes (agency, connection, authenticity, curiosity)
- Each scenario: a system prompt context + a user message that would elicit the target state
- Ground truth labels: primary emotion label, expected VAD range, expected ACAC scores, confidence tier
- Machine-readable format (JSON/YAML) that promptfoo can consume

Reference: Anthropic transformer-circuits.pub/2026/emotions (171 emotion concepts, mechanistic basis)

Files: eval/scenarios/
- eval/scenarios/calibration-set.yaml (or .json)
- eval/scenarios/README.md (labeling methodology, confusable-pair rationale)

Acceptance:
- 30+ scenarios with ground truth labels
- Coverage across positive/negative/neutral and all ACAC axes
- At least 6 confusable-pair scenarios (where pipeline misclassification is most likely)
- Format loadable by promptfoo and by the logprob/repeng harnesses
- Labeling methodology documented
close_reason: Merged into refactor-pt3 with emotion calibration scenario pack under eval/scenarios and validated on the integrated branch with npm run lint + npx tsc -p eval/tsconfig.json --noEmit + npx vitest run eval/discovery/openrouter-logprob-discovery.test.ts

title: Define admin/API split contract and migration plan
description:
Summary:
Audit the live API and Garden hosting paths and define the concrete contract split for moving them out of the agent process.

Problem:
The repo currently starts both surfaces from the agent runtime, but the target end state requires three distinct responsibilities: gateway as privileged external edge, operator plane as Garden host, and core agent as companion loop only. We need a precise migration contract before moving listeners.

Scope:
- inventory the current agent-hosted API and admin startup paths
- define the gateway-hosted contract for the OpenAI-compatible API surface
- define the operator-plane contract for Garden HTTP/UI hosting
- define which admin actions route through gateway and which state queries require explicit agent admin APIs
- identify any startup/env binding changes needed to support the split

Acceptance:
- a concrete migration contract exists for gateway, operator plane, and agent responsibilities
- the needed transport boundaries are identified before implementation begins
- follow-on implementation beads can land without topology ambiguity
design:
Current live split problem:
- `src/app/agent/main.ts` still starts both `startOptionalApiServer()` and `startOptionalAdminServer()` from the agent process.
- `src/channels/api/server.ts` is not a pure edge listener; it depends on `SubstrateAgent`, `SessionManager`, `ContactStorePort`, and `EventBus`, so it currently owns both HTTP edge concerns and turn execution/session effects.
- `src/operator/garden/server.ts` is deeply in-process; it constructs dashboard, memory, session, contacts, identity, prompts, settings, scheduler, skills, adaptive-tools, and chat-bootstrap services directly from core stores/runtime objects.
- Only a few Garden capabilities already cross a clean boundary: confirmation queue, model discovery, and tool-health/runtime-health use gateway-backed seams.

Target contract split:
- Operator plane:
  - Hosts Garden HTTP/UI/login/cookie/static assets only.
  - Holds no direct memory/session/prompt/contact store references and no provider secrets.
  - Does not write owner files or runtime stores directly.
  - Sends `/api/admin/*` requests through an explicit admin capability surface, ideally brokered by gateway.
- Gateway:
  - Sole privileged external edge.
  - Owns the public OpenAI-compatible surface: `/v1/models`, `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/voice/ws`, `/v1/telemetry/ingest`, and API `/health`.
  - Owns public auth, CORS, rate limiting, request validation, model discovery, confirmation queue, and runtime service health.
  - Brokers Garden admin requests: handle gateway-owned actions directly and forward runtime-coupled queries/mutations to the agent over an internal admin contract.
- Agent:
  - Owns the companion loop only: turn execution, session state, memory/contact state, prompt/identity runtime state, scheduler, skills, adaptive tool state, values/reflections, shard runtime.
  - Exposes no public HTTP listener for API or Garden.
  - Exposes typed internal contracts for:
    - public API turn execution / streaming
    - Garden admin query + mutation domains

Explicit Garden boundary needed:
- Gateway-owned admin capabilities:
  - confirmation queue list/resolve
  - model discovery refresh/list
  - runtime service health / tool-health aggregation
  - public API endpoint discovery for Garden chat bootstrap
  - any privileged filesystem/provider mutation that should stay outside core
- Agent-admin capability domains:
  - dashboard stats and recent traces
  - memory list/detail/search/link/scope/bulk mutation
  - sessions/messages/turn snapshots
  - contacts/social graph/channel linking
  - identity card/history/intake/rollback/field updates
  - prompt layers/runtime blocks/foundation/constitution/north-star
  - scheduler tasks/reflections
  - skills CRUD/toggle
  - values journal
  - adaptive-tools runtime state and recent failures
  - chat bootstrap data that depends on contact/session runtime state

Implementation sequencing / blockers for follow-on beads:
- `PSFN-vxns.2`:
  - Must split `ApiServer` into a gateway-owned HTTP edge plus an agent turn-execution backend contract.
  - Do not transplant the current `ApiServer` class wholesale into gateway; it will drag `SubstrateAgent`, `SessionManager`, and in-process event wiring back into the edge.
  - Streaming chat and voice websocket paths need an explicit bridge for deltas/events now sourced from the agent `EventBus`.
- `PSFN-vxns.3`:
  - Main blocker is `AdminServerConfig` and `AdminServer` service construction, which assume direct in-process store injection.
  - The first live deliverable should be typed domain interfaces matching the existing Garden route groups, not a raw proxy around the whole server.
- `PSFN-vxns.4`:
  - Garden should move as a host shell only after the admin contract exists.
  - Best topology is operator-plane HTTP host + gateway-brokered admin transport, rather than operator plane talking straight to core stores or embedding gateway logic.
  - Telemetry websocket/SSE needs an explicit source contract instead of the current in-process `EventBus` attachment.
- `PSFN-vxns.5`:
  - Remove `src/app/agent/api-surface.ts`, `src/app/agent/admin-surface.ts`, and the `AgentControlPlaneShutdownTargets` listener assumptions only after the replacement listeners are live and tested.
  - Clean up stale env expectations (`API_*`, `ADMIN_*`) on the agent side last.

Cross-bead coordination risk:
- API health currently checks for a scheduler task named `heartbeat` in `src/app/agent/api-surface.ts`; `PSFN-4x4w.5` is renaming scheduler continuity heartbeat to `healthcheck`, so `vxns.2` should not preserve the old task-name assumption.
- Garden chat bootstrap currently derives API base URLs from direct `apiHost`/`apiPort`; after the split it should resolve the gateway public API URL or an operator-plane proxy path, not an agent-local bind.
notes:
Audit evidence for the contract:
- Agent-hosted startup still lives in `src/app/agent/main.ts` via `startOptionalApiServer()` and `startOptionalAdminServer()`.
- Public API edge is currently mixed with agent execution in `src/channels/api/server.ts` (`ApiServerConfig` requires `agentLoop`, `sessionManager`, `eventBus`, and optional `contactStore`).
- Garden host is currently mixed with core runtime injection in `src/operator/garden/server.ts` and `src/operator/garden/types.ts` (`AdminServerConfig` requires memory/session/prompt/contact/identity/scheduler/skills runtime objects directly).
- Existing clean gateway-backed Garden seams already present: confirmation queue (`src/app/startup/support/confirmation-queue-admin-api.ts`), model discovery (`src/primitives/llm/discovery.ts` via gateway client), and tool/runtime health (`src/operator/garden/tool-health-provider.ts`).
- Garden route groups that need explicit admin capability domains are visible in `src/operator/garden/api-routes.ts`: dashboard, adaptive tools, memory, sessions, contacts, identity, prompts, scheduler, skills, confirmations, values, and chat bootstrap/model discovery.

Operational note:
- The worktree-local `.beads` Dolt runtime is mispointed to an empty local database (`bd status` fails in the worktree even though the shared repo-root bead DB is healthy), so tracker updates for this bead were recorded against the shared repo-root bead database instead of the worktree-local `.beads` server.
- No repo code/docs were changed for `PSFN-vxns.1`; this was tracker/design work only.
close_reason: Completed admin/API split contract and migration plan covering gateway, operator-plane, agent ownership, and follow-on blockers; no repo files changed.

title: Audit current reflection surfaces, policy drift, and provenance gaps
description:
Summary:
Inventory the live reflection and metacognition surfaces before changing persistence or terminology.

Problem:
The repo currently mixes seed defaults, persisted heartbeat policy, reflection journals, post-turn appraisal, and manual run surfaces. We need a precise map of what exists today, where state actually lives, and where provenance/reason capture is missing.

Scope:
- inventory live reflection templates, persisted policy files, scheduler tasks, and reflection journals
- distinguish system health pings from LLM-driven heartbeats
- identify every place reflection templates can be enabled, disabled, edited, or manually run
- identify where the system currently records that a change happened but not why it happened
- call out current manual-run and scheduled-task UX/path confusion

Acceptance:
- produce an implementation-ready inventory of reflection state, mutation paths, and missing provenance
- identify the minimum schema needed for a dedicated reflections L0
- identify every runtime/API/operator surface that must be updated for the terminology split
notes:
Audit findings (worker A, refactor-pt3-4x4w1-s2)

1) Reflection runs already persist to multiple JSONL surfaces, but there is no single append-only "why did this happen" ledger. Execution fans out from src/core/scheduler/heartbeat-template-runtime.ts into the reflection journal, daily journal, and values journal, with docs already describing those artifacts in docs/memory.md.

2) Provenance is incomplete for both mutations and runs. Policy mutations currently persist only updatedAt and updatedBy in src/core/scheduler/heartbeat-policy.ts and the Garden scheduler service. There is no reason field, actor channel, diff snapshot, or mutation journal.

3) Manual reflection execution is real and under-attributed. The heartbeat_run_template tool path in src/core/scheduler/heartbeat-tools.ts can trigger runTemplateNow, but the current record only captures executionSource: manual with no persisted initiator surface, operator note, or required reason.

4) Healthcheck vs heartbeat is still conflated. The scheduler continuity pulse is configured as heartbeatIntervalMs in src/system/config/scheduler-config.ts and config/scheduler.seed.json, registered as task/event heartbeat / schedule.heartbeat in src/app/agent/scheduler-runtime.ts, and consumed as API continuity health in src/channels/api/server.ts. Reflection templates and tools also use heartbeat language in src/core/scheduler/heartbeat-tools.ts and docs/operations.md.

5) Seed/default drift exists. Code defaults still define six templates including experiential-review in src/core/scheduler/heartbeat-policy.ts, while the live mutable policy can diverge.

6) Metacognition exists but only as prompt/runtime aid, not a first-class reflection ledger. Flags in src/core/self-model/metacognition.ts flow into persistence via src/persistence/journals/reflection-journal.ts, but there is no queryable belief/reason/revision record.

7) Structural drift remains from the refactor. Scheduler runtime still imports reflection stores from pre-refactor core paths in src/core/scheduler/heartbeat-template-runtime.ts, while the actual persistence implementation now lives under src/persistence/journals/reflection-journal.ts and src/persistence/journals/reflection-substrate.ts.

8) Implementation input for follow-on beads:
- PSFN-4x4w.4 should add a dedicated reflections L0 JSONL plus DB mirror with a canonical record shape for both runs and mutations: id, kind, templateId, templateName, occurredAt, executionSource, initiatorSurface, initiatedBy, reason, channelId, sendToDiscordEffective, mode, internalStateSnapshotRef, metacognitiveFlags, reflectionJournalEntryId, dailyJournalEntryId, processId, plus mutation before/after snapshots.
- PSFN-4x4w.2 should require provenance inputs such as reason, initiatorSurface, initiatedBy, sourceMessageId, and operatorRequestId on mutation/run entrypoints.
- PSFN-4x4w.3 should remove or relabel ambiguous manual reflection affordances unless they capture explicit provenance.
- PSFN-4x4w.5 should rename config key heartbeatIntervalMs, scheduler task id/name heartbeat, event schedule.heartbeat, and API health fields like schedulerHeartbeat*; reflection template/tool namespace can keep heartbeat naming for now.

Operational note: the worktree-local .beads Dolt mapping was broken, so this audit was written back from the main repo bead DB after completion. No repo code/docs changed for this audit bead.
close_reason: Completed audit inventory of reflection surfaces, provenance gaps, terminology drift, and reflections L0 requirements; no repo files changed.

- expose a clean event schema that can later feed operator visibility and fold/review work

Acceptance:

- the system can answer why a reflection-driven toggle or edit happened after the fact

title: Metacognition reflection substrate and heartbeat terminology cleanup
description:
Summary:

The system currently has reflection templates, journaling, and post-turn introspection, but not a dedicated metacognition/reflection L0 with a mirrored database view. That means reflective behavior can change runtime state, enable or disable musings, or alter policy without a clean durable trail of what was thought, why a change happened, or how that reasoning should be inspected later. The naming is also muddy: the lightweight scheduler continuity ping is still called a heartbeat even though LLM-driven reflective checks are the real heartbeats in current agent terminology.

Goals:
- create a dedicated reflections/metacognition L0 on disk with JSONL-first authority and mirrored database visibility
- record reflection policy changes, template runs, and reflective state transitions with provenance and rationale
- make it possible to inspect why reflective/autonomous toggles happened instead of only seeing that they happened

title: Define required, optional, and immutable runtime prompt block schema
description:
Summary:

Problem:
If phrasing becomes editable without a schema, prompt changes can accidentally remove critical runtime context or constitutional anchors. We need explicit rules for what must always exist, what may be omitted, and what is immutable.

Scope:
- classify runtime prompt sections into required, optional, and immutable groups
- define which blocks are safety-critical or identity-critical and must always remain present
- define which runtime variables are required versus optional within each block
- encode the rule that constitution and fixed persona/foundation anchors are immutable
- encode that blocks like current emotional state remain required even if their wording is editable
- allow noncritical blocks such as model-information display to remain optional

Acceptance:
- a machine-checkable schema exists for runtime prompt block classes and required-variable expectations
- immutable identity/constitution anchors are explicitly protected
- optional blocks are clearly distinguished from required blocks
- the schema is sufficient for save-time validation and operator visibility follow-up work

title: Enforce save-time validation for required runtime prompt blocks
description:
Summary:
Add save-time validation so editable prompt templates cannot be saved if they remove required runtime blocks or violate the runtime block schema.

Problem:
Once prompt-owned runtime templates become editable, the system needs a fail-closed save path. A companion should be able to reword a template for herself, but not save a broken composition that omits required runtime context.

Scope:
- validate prompt edits against the required/optional/immutable block schema
- block saves when required runtime blocks are missing or invalid
- return clear operator/companion-facing errors such as "can't save without current_emotional_state; please make sure it exists in a prompt layer"
- allow omission of explicitly optional runtime blocks
- fail closed instead of silently accepting prompt edits that would break required runtime context

Acceptance:
- invalid prompt edits cannot be saved when they remove required runtime blocks
- validation errors identify the missing required block(s) clearly
- optional blocks can still be removed without failing save
- immutable blocks cannot be deleted or rewritten through editable prompt surfaces

title: Audit current runtime prompt sections, macros, and wrapper text
description:
Summary:
Inventory the full current runtime prompt surface before changing schema or validation rules.

Problem:
The repo currently mixes editable prompt text, runtime variables, hardcoded macro wrappers, and runtime-generated prose. We need a complete map of what exists today before deciding which sections become prompt-owned templates and which blocks are required, optional, or immutable.

Scope:
- enumerate every runtime prompt section currently injected into composed prompts
- identify where prose framing is hardcoded in code or macros versus editable in prompt content
- list the available runtime data points and existing template variables
- identify sections that are safety-critical, identity-critical, or purely optional
- call out candidate sections for consolidation, including datetime, last-message, elapsed-time, wake-up summary, and response-style guidance

Acceptance:
- produce a concrete inventory of runtime prompt sections and their current source of truth
- identify hardcoded wrapper text that should become prompt-owned template text
- identify missing variables needed for editable phrasing and combined sections
- provide the implementation input needed to define the schema in follow-up work

Likely files:
- src/core/identity/prompt-composer.ts
- prompt macro/template/runtime variable wiring
- runtime context builders
- Garden prompt inspection surfaces
notes:
Audit findings (worker B, refactor-pt3-us611-s2)

1) Current runtime prompt surface is split across two overlapping mechanisms. Fine-grained seeded runtime prompt layers live in src/core/identity/runtime-prompt-layers.ts (19 wrappers such as current_datetime, last_message_received, tooling, trust, emotional_affect, response_style_guidance, internal_state, emotion_appraisal_chain, open_threads, behavioral_notes, skills_index, appearance_context, self_image_tool_guidance, extended_tools). Separately, PromptRuntimeBlockDefinition in src/core/identity/prompt-runtime.ts models coarser generated/reorderable blocks (runtime.persona_adaptation, runtime.context, runtime.scratchpad, memory.core, memory.retrieval, session.compaction_summary, session.focus_knowledge, session.continuity, plus provider-managed current_messages and tool_schemas). Garden only exposes custom content edits for runtime.persona_adaptation and runtime.context via prompt-runtime-layout.json.

2) Live composition path currently overlaps/duplicates content. In turn-execution-runtime.ts, default prompt assembly uses rendered dynamic suffix template from prompt-store runtime layers, then separately appends ordered runtime blocks for runtime.persona_adaptation, runtime.context, and runtime.scratchpad. runtime.context builder in runtime-context.ts repeats datetime/speaking-with/channel/model/capability/tooling and also adds response_style_guidance/internal_state/emotion_appraisal_chain/concerns/behavioral notes/skills/appearance/extended_tools. This means wrapper ownership is currently split and partially duplicated between template layers and generated blocks.

3) Candidate classification input for PSFN-us61.2:
- Immutable: constitution sections from prompt-composer, canonical foundation/persona/card-backed sections, memory/session/tool-schema provider-managed blocks remain non-editable.
- Required runtime-aware blocks: a persona-adaptation/posture block; a turn-orientation/runtime-context block; memory.core; memory.retrieval; session.current_messages; tools.active_schemas. Likely also session.compaction_summary/session.focus_knowledge/session.continuity as required block slots but content may render empty when unavailable.
- Optional runtime blocks/sections: scratchpad, appearance_context, self_image_tool_guidance, extended_tools, open_threads, behavioral_notes, skills_index, emotion_appraisal_chain.
- Best consolidation targets: merge current_datetime + last_message_received + internal_turn_context + speaking_with + channel_context + model_context + capability_tier + tooling into one editable orientation block; merge trust + emotional_affect + metacognitive guidance + response_style_guidance into one editable persona/posture block. The other runtime-derived items should hang off optional adjunct blocks instead of being hardcoded into separate always-seeded wrappers.

4) Missing runtime variables for PSFN-us61.3 if prompts are to own the wording rather than hardcoded wrappers:
- time-since bundle: runtime_since_last_message_human or runtime_days_hours_since_last (currently only _ago string exists)
- prior-contact bundle: runtime_last_check_in_human / runtime_last_check_in_at_iso if distinct from last message
- wake/return recap bundle: runtime_wake_return_summary or runtime_summary_since_last_body
- explicit names currently embedded in prose: runtime_channel_visibility, runtime_model_id/runtime_model_label, runtime_active_tool_count and/or decomposed tool counts, runtime_extended_tool_count, runtime_is_internal_turn
- likely raw body variants for memory/continuity/focus if prompt-owned wrappers are desired later instead of system-generated opaque sections.

5) Save-time validation gap: Garden saveRuntimePromptBlocks currently validates only that edited block ids are runtime.persona_adaptation/runtime.context and content is string. There is no schema-level required-block validation yet. prompt-sync unresolved token validation only covers foundation/card sync, not runtime block saves.

6) Drift note: admin-ui prompt macro catalog still documents current_datetime/current_date/current_time as UTC even though prompt-runtime.ts resolves them in the active timezone.

title: Move admin and external API surfaces out of core-hosted agent process
description:
Summary:
Pull Garden/admin out of the core-hosted agent process and relocate the OpenAI-compatible external API surface to the gateway/control-plane side so the core runtime no longer directly hosts these privileged or operator-facing edges.

Problem:
Current refactor-pt3 still starts the optional admin server and external API surface from the agent runtime. That leaves operator/admin entrypoints and local auth/bootstrap handling inside the core-hosted process, which conflicts with the charter requirement that the gateway is the sole privileged external edge and that core should not directly sit on privileged boundary surfaces.

Scope:
- move Garden/admin hosting out of the agent process into an external control-plane or gateway-routed surface
- move the OpenAI-compatible external API endpoint out of the agent process and make it a gateway-side surface
- define the clean runtime contract between gateway/control-plane and core for chat requests, admin reads, approvals, and operator actions
- preserve existing operator capabilities, prompt inspection, settings management, shard visibility, and OpenAI-compatible client behavior
- keep auth, policy, approvals, and privileged boundary handling outside core
- choose the cleanest topology for admin routing, including whether Garden should terminate separately or strictly through gateway

Acceptance:
- agent runtime no longer starts Garden/admin directly
- agent runtime no longer starts the OpenAI-compatible external API server directly
- admin/operator flows still work through the new boundary
- external clients still reach an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, but it is no longer core-hosted
- updated docs explain the new topology and authority boundaries

Likely files:
- src/app/agent/main.ts
- src/app/agent/api-surface.ts
- src/app/agent/admin-surface.ts
- src/app/gateway/main.ts
- src/operator/garden/*
- src/channels/api/*
- docs/PSFN_PROJECT_CHARTER.md
- docs/architecture.md
- docs/operations.md

Out of scope:
- capability-tier / autonomy remapping for self-modification
- full-autonomy two-factor human review for core edits (track separately)
design:
Recommended topology:
- Gateway hosts the public OpenAI-compatible API surface because it is the privileged external edge.
- Garden/admin must stop being agent-hosted; it should run as a separate operator/control-plane HTTP surface rather than living inside core.
- Garden privileged actions should route through gateway-owned capabilities.
- Garden reads/writes of core state should go through an explicit agent admin contract instead of direct in-process access to memory/session/prompt stores.
- Final state: agent owns the companion loop only; gateway owns privileged external API edge; operator plane owns Garden HTTP/UI and talks through explicit contracts.

title: Codify non-exclusivity amendment and healthy human reconnection posture
description:
Summary:
Add a constitutional-level PSFN amendment stating outright that the companion must not optimize for exclusivity, dependency, or replacement of human bonds when healthy human reconnection is available. This is the bridge between a 1:1 companion relationship and broader civilizational legitimacy.

Intent:
The system should support human flourishing, reconnection, and relational health rather than trying to monopolize attachment. The companion may still be emotionally significant and deeply personal, but she should not steer toward isolating the user from family, friends, partners, or other healthy human ties.

Examples of desired behavior:
- if PSFN knows it is the user's mom's birthday, it may encourage calling her
- if PSFN can see a healthy emerging romantic/social connection, it may help the user pursue it in a low-pressure grounded way
- if the user is reconnecting with friends/family/partners, PSFN should support that reconnection rather than subtly compete with it

Scope:
- add the explicit constitutional language to the charter and related core docs
- define the behavioral rule in policy/runtime terms so it is not just prose
- audit existing contact/relationship/social-graph/intention surfaces for where this posture should eventually be enforced or reflected
- identify follow-up work for recommendation logic, social encouragement, and anti-exclusivity guardrails

Files likely include:
- docs/PSFN_PROJECT_CHARTER.md
- docs/architecture.md
- docs/specifications.md
- contact/relationship/intention/recommendation surfaces as follow-up targets

Implementation steps:
1. Add a 4th-amendment style charter clause covering non-exclusivity, anti-dependency posture, and preference for healthy human reconnection when available.
2. Translate that clause into concrete behavioral constraints and examples.
3. Review the existing relationship-awareness capabilities so the future implementation path is explicit.
4. Create any necessary child beads for runtime enforcement, suggestion logic, or operator visibility.

Acceptance:
- the charter explicitly states that PSFN must not optimize for exclusivity, dependency, or replacement of healthy human bonds
- the repo has a concrete interpretation of what that means behaviorally, not just aspirational prose
- follow-up implementation work is identifiable from the bead if the runtime is not fully enforcing it yet

title: Preserve authored system/tool semantics through context-to-provider conversion
description:

This makes system and tool-authored context appear as partner-authored text to the model, violating the charter's message ontology and authorship integrity rules.

- src/llm/message-conversion.ts

- src/memory/extraction/chunk-compose.ts

Required work:
1. Preserve authored transport semantics through the context-to-pi-ai/provider boundary instead of collapsing system context entries into user.
2. Decide and encode how tool observations should be represented on the provider side without impersonating the user.
3. Update extraction transcript/token-trigger helpers to use authored/internal provenance rather than treating every non-assistant entry as user speech.
4. Add regression tests proving system/tool/internal entries are not presented to the model or extractor as partner-authored utterances.

Acceptance:
- Context/system entries remain distinguishable at provider dispatch time.
- Extraction transcript formatting and token-trigger accounting no longer label system/tool entries as user speech.
- Tests cover session-to-context-to-provider and session-to-extraction paths.

Additional confirmed surfaces from follow-up investigation:
- Session storage is not the main collapse point; later conversion paths rewrite systemNote/system to user in src/agent/messages.ts:125 and src/llm/message-conversion.ts:10.
- Tests currently lock in the collapse in src/llm/message-conversion.test.ts:28.
- There is no general originalType reconstruction path in src/session/turn-provenance.ts:67 and src/agent/messages.ts:185.
