3. Refactor processing flow to avoid unnecessary serialization where safe (or release lock once stream begins).
4. Ensure non-blocking async work (post-turn extraction/maintenance) does not delay visible token start.
5. Add regression tests/bench assertions for improved TTFT under rapid message bursts.

Example:

After -> queue behavior is explicit and first-token latency is reduced/measured under load.

description:

Current extraction path can write nearly every extracted fact without strong value gates, creating memory bloat and poor signal-to-noise. We also need hard telemetry for how often retrieval/summarization run and how many prompts each turn triggers.

4. Emit structured telemetry counters: retrieval calls per turn, extraction triggers, compaction summaries, and per-turn LLM request count.

title: API: prevent stranded in-flight turns (timeout/disconnect handling)
description:
Summary: API chat completions can leave the agent in a long-running in-flight state after client timeout, causing subsequent requests to fail with `Agent is already processing a prompt` and return 500s. Add request lifecycle controls so timeout/disconnect does not strand the channel.

2. Add request timeout handling for non-streaming requests (configurable via env, with sensible default) and detect client disconnect (`req.aborted` / `res.close`) to stop waiting.
3. Propagate cancellation signal where supported; otherwise ensure API returns deterministic timeout/busy errors and clears server-side bookkeeping safely.
4. Return explicit 429/503-style busy response instead of generic 500 for channel-busy contention.
5. Add regression tests for: timeout path, disconnect path, in-flight contention behavior, and successful recovery after timeout.

Example:
Before: Request A times out at client, request B on same `X-Session-ID` -> 500 internal error (`already processing`).
After: Request A yields timeout/busy response and bookkeeping cleanup; request B either queues/returns busy deterministically and succeeds once channel is free.
close_reason: Implemented API per-session in-flight gate, timeout/disconnect lifecycle handling, explicit busy/timeout responses, and regression tests.

title: Think loop routes through extraction purpose instead of reasoning model slot
description:

- This breaks expected behavior when reasoning-capable models are configured separately from extraction models.

2. Route think-loop LLM calls to reasoning purpose/slot instead of extraction.

title: Runtime settings do not propagate to model roster or active Agent model
description:
Summary:
Updating model settings at runtime (admin settings or loaded settings.json) mutates top-level config fields but does not fully propagate into the model selection paths that actually run inference.

Why this is a bug:
- applySettings() updates config.primaryModel / config.extractionModel but does not synchronize config.modelRoster slots (chat, background).
- SubstrateAgent resolves and sets the model once, then keeps modelResolved=true; later settings changes do not force agent.setModel(...) with updated values.
- Result: UI/settings claim model changes are live, but runtime can continue using the old model.

Files to modify:
- src/settings.ts
- src/agent/substrate-agent.ts
- src/channels/admin/handlers.ts
- src/settings.test.ts
- src/agent/substrate-agent.test.ts

Implementation steps:
1. Make applySettings() keep modelRoster.chat and modelRoster.background aligned with primary/extraction settings (model, provider, maxTokens).
2. Add a safe runtime hook on SubstrateAgent to refresh model resolution after settings updates (or detect config drift before each turn and re-set model).
3. Ensure admin settings update path invokes the refresh hook after saving/applying settings.
4. Add tests proving model/provider/token changes in settings are reflected in actual resolved model IDs for subsequent turns.

Example:
Before: set primary model to moonshotai/kimi-k2.5 in admin -> responses still use old z-ai/glm-5.
After: next turn resolves and uses moonshotai/kimi-k2.5 immediately.
acceptance_criteria:

- Next turn after settings change uses updated model without restart
- Tests cover roster sync and post-update model refresh behavior

title: LLM auto-retry with exponential backoff

title: RLM evidence/provenance tracking in ThinkResult
description:
PSFN's ThinkResult returns only aggregate stats (iterations, token counts, duration). There's no record of what the think tool actually searched, found, or concluded at each step. This makes it impossible to cite sources, debug reasoning, or generate reflection memories about how conclusions were reached.

Aleph (github.com/Hmbown/aleph) tracks an evidence trail — every search, sub-LM call, and code execution records a citation with source, snippet, and timestamp.
design:
## Pattern (from Aleph `aleph/mcp/session.py:78-130`)

```python
@dataclass
class _Evidence:
    source: str  # "search", "peek", "exec", "manual", "sub_query"
    line_range: tuple[int, int] | None
    pattern: str | None
    snippet: str
    note: str | None = None
    timestamp: datetime
```

Session also tracks convergence: `confidence_history: list[float]`, `information_gain: list[int]`.

## PSFN Design

### New types in `src/repl/types.ts`

```typescript
export interface ThinkEvidence {
  source: 'memory_search' | 'memory_get' | 'session_messages' | 'llm_query' | 'code';
  query?: string;         // search query or llm prompt (truncated)
  snippet: string;        // what was found (truncated to ~200 chars)
  resultCount?: number;   // how many results returned
  timestamp: number;
}

export interface ThinkStep {
  iteration: number;
  code: string;            // code the LLM wrote (truncated)
  output: string;          // execution output (truncated)
  error: string | null;
  evidenceCollected: ThinkEvidence[];
  tokensUsed: number;      // this iteration's token count
}
```

### Changes

1. `src/repl/types.ts` — Add `ThinkEvidence`, `ThinkStep`. Extend `ThinkResult` with:
   ```typescript
   steps: ThinkStep[];
   evidence: ThinkEvidence[];  // flattened from all steps
   ```

2. `src/repl/sandbox.ts` — Add evidence collection hooks to injected functions:
   - `memory_search`: record query, result count, top result snippet
   - `memory_get_by_id`: record id, text snippet
   - `session_messages`: record channelId, message count
   - `llm_query`: record prompt (first 100 chars), response (first 200 chars)
   
   Evidence array lives on sandbox instance, collected per-execution:
   ```typescript
   private currentEvidence: ThinkEvidence[] = [];
   
   // In memory_search:
   this.currentEvidence.push({
     source: 'memory_search',
     query,
     snippet: results[0]?.text.slice(0, 200) ?? '',
     resultCount: results.length,
     timestamp: Date.now(),
   });
   ```
   
   Add `collectEvidence(): ThinkEvidence[]` method that drains and returns.

3. `src/repl/loop.ts` — After each sandbox.execute():
   - Collect evidence via `sandbox.collectEvidence()`
   - Build `ThinkStep` with code, output, error, evidence, tokens
   - Push to `steps[]` array
   - At end: flatten all step evidence into top-level `evidence[]`

4. `src/repl/tools.ts` — Include evidence summary in tool output:
   ```
   [Think: 5 iters, 8420 tokens, 1200ms, 12 evidence items]
   ```

### Use cases
- Purrsephone can cite: "Based on 3 memories I found about X..."
- Admin GUI can show reasoning chains in Active Branches
- Reflection memories can reference what evidence informed a conclusion
acceptance_criteria:
- ThinkEvidence and ThinkStep types defined
- memory_search, memory_get_by_id, session_messages, llm_query all record evidence
- ThinkResult includes steps[] and evidence[] arrays
- Think tool output header shows evidence count
- Evidence snippets truncated to prevent bloat
close_reason: Verified end-to-end: ThinkEvidence + ThinkStep types, evidence hooks in memory_search/memory_get_by_id/session_messages/llm_query, step assembly in loop, evidence count in tool header, snippet truncation. All 5 source types covered with tests. 875 tests passing.

title: Gateway split: voice turns need awaited agent response for TTS
description:
Voice runtime currently depends on `DiscordAdapter.onMessage()` returning the agent response synchronously so it can run TTS playback.

In gateway/agent split mode (`gateway-main.ts` + `agent-main.ts`), the gateway Discord handler forwards message notifications to agent via `gateway.notifyAll('discord.message', ...)` and returns a placeholder response immediately. This means voice transcript turns can produce empty responses at the adapter layer and skip TTS.

Why it matters:
- Single-process mode voice works with direct handler response.
- Split mode is the intended secure deployment model (keys host-side), so voice needs a request/response path there too.

Proposed fix directions:
1. Add a request-response RPC path for Discord turns (gateway asks one connected agent for response payload and waits with timeout), OR
2. Add dedicated voice reply RPC (`discord.voice.reply`) from agent to gateway carrying text/audio-ready payload tied to voice session, OR
3. Route voice turn through an explicit gateway event channel with correlation IDs and awaited reply.

Any solution must preserve existing text behavior and avoid double-send.
acceptance_criteria:
- In gateway+agent split mode, a voice transcript turn receives agent response and plays TTS
- No placeholder/empty response path in voice flow
- Text channel behavior remains unchanged
- Added integration test covering gateway+agent voice response correlation
close_reason: Implemented bidirectional JSON-RPC: JSONRPCServerAndClient per connection, discord.handleMessage reverse RPC, voice handler in adapter, gateway-main wiring, agent-main handler. 797 tests passing.

title: Core self-modification: git-backed guarded tools
description:
Controlled self-modification workflow using git-native change management and explicit review gates.

Direction update:
- Primary deployment target is private GitHub repo or local/private GitLab.
- Self-modification changes should be proposed as branch + PR/MR artifacts, not silent direct writes to main.

Toolchain scope:
1. `repo_status` — status/branch/dirty summary
2. `repo_diff` — staged/unstaged diff summary
3. `repo_apply_patch` — constrained patch apply (allowlisted paths)
4. `repo_commit` — signed-off commit with structured message template
5. `repo_create_branch` — feature branch creation
6. `repo_open_pr` / `repo_open_mr` — open review artifact in remote forge (GitHub/GitLab)
7. `self_rebuild` — run rebuild workflow
8. `self_restart` — supervisor restart with pre/post notifications

Governance model:
- Default path is PR/MR-first for auditable change history.
- Protected branch direct writes are blocked or require explicit human approval.
- High-impact operations (restart, deploy-affecting change, policy/prompt core edits) require approval gate.
- Every commit includes machine-generated rationale + intent summary so she documents her own changes.

Audit and rollback:
- Record branch, commit SHA, PR/MR URL, and linked issue/bead in operation log.
- Rollback path is `revert`/`reset-to-known-good` workflow via approved tool path.
- Restart failure triggers rollback strategy and operator alert.
acceptance_criteria:
- Git tools execute through gateway policy controls with path allowlists.
- Self-modification writes produce branch+commit artifacts and can open PR/MR (GitHub or GitLab).
- Protected branch direct writes are blocked or require explicit approval.
- Commit messages include structured self-documentation (intent/rationale/scope).
- self_rebuild and self_restart run via supervisor path (not in-process) with reboot handshake retained.
- Failed restart or health-check regression triggers rollback and operator notification.

title: Add SSRF defenses to gateway web.fetch
description: Gateway `web.fetch` allows arbitrary URLs without domain filtering. A prompt-injected agent could probe localhost, private networks, cloud metadata endpoints (169.254.169.254), etc. Fix: enforce URL policy — deny private/link-local/localhost CIDRs, require HTTPS by default, optional domain allowlist.
design:
1. Add `isPrivateUrl(url)` utility in `src/gateway/server.ts` (or a new `src/gateway/url-policy.ts`): parse URL, resolve hostname to IP via `dns.lookup`, check against RFC1918/link-local/loopback/metadata CIDRs.
2. In `web.fetch` handler: validate URL before fetching. Deny private targets. Deny non-HTTPS unless explicitly configured (`ALLOW_HTTP_FETCH=true`).
3. Optional `FETCH_DOMAIN_ALLOWLIST` env var — comma-separated domains. If set, only those domains are allowed.
4. Return policy denial as RPC error, not silent failure.
acceptance_criteria:
- localhost/127.0.0.1/::1 URLs are DENIED
- Private CIDR (10.x, 172.16-31.x, 192.168.x) targets DENIED
- Link-local (169.254.x) DENIED (blocks cloud metadata)
- HTTP denied by default (HTTPS required)
- Domain allowlist works when configured
- Normal HTTPS URLs continue to work
- Tests cover all denial cases

title: Fix symlink traversal bypass in gateway filesystem policy
description: Gateway filesystem policy uses prefix-based path matching on the normalized (but not canonicalized) path string. A symlink inside the workspace pointing outside it bypasses the ALLOW policy. Fix: resolve paths with `fs.realpathSync` before policy check, reject symlink escapes.
design: In `src/gateway/server.ts` policy evaluation for `fs.read`/`fs.write`: call `fs.realpathSync()` (or `realpath` async) on the requested path, then check the canonical path against policy. If realpath fails (broken symlink), DENY. If canonical path differs from normalized path and falls outside allowed prefixes, DENY.
acceptance_criteria:

- Symlink pointing outside workspace is DENIED
- Broken symlinks are DENIED
- Normal paths continue to work
- Test with symlink escape scenario
close_reason: realpathSync symlink resolution before policy check. Validated by fresh-eyes reviewer (PASS).

title: Fix streaming chunk cross-talk: per-request IDs in gateway LLM proxy
description: Gateway emits `llm.chunk` with constant `requestId: 0`. Client keeps a single global handler. Under concurrent shard LLM streams, chunks can leak between tasks. Fix: generate unique request IDs per stream call, route chunk handlers by request ID on both gateway server and client sides.
design:
1. Gateway server (`src/gateway/server.ts`): generate a unique requestId (incrementing counter or UUID) per `llm.stream` call. Pass it in every `llm.chunk` notification.
2. Gateway client (`src/gateway/client.ts`): replace single global `onChunkHandler` with a `Map<string, handler>` keyed by requestId. Register handler before sending `llm.stream`, remove on completion/error.
3. Protocol (`src/gateway/protocol.ts`): update `LLMChunkNotification` type to use `string` requestId instead of hardcoded `0`.
4. Ensure backward compat: if requestId is missing/0, fall back to global handler (graceful degradation).
acceptance_criteria:
- Concurrent shard LLM streams route chunks to correct handlers
- Existing single-stream usage still works
- Gateway protocol types updated
- Tests verify concurrent stream isolation
close_reason: Per-request streaming IDs with Map-based handler dispatch. Validated by fresh-eyes reviewer (PASS).

title: RLM+REPL Sandbox — context-as-object, programmatic memory access, sub-LM calls, self-modification
description:
Port the RLM (Recursive Language Model) paradigm into PSFN. Core insight: context is an object Purrsephone can programmatically inspect/query/transform, not tokens stuffed into a prompt. She decides what context she needs.

Reference: https://github.com/alexzhang13/rlm, https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.24601

**Foundation:** pi-agent-core's `Agent` class is the base layer. PSFN already depends on `@mariozechner/pi-ai`; pi-agent-core (1,495 LoC, MIT, single dep) provides the agent loop with streaming events, steering, follow-ups, and declaration-merging extensibility. Build RLM on top of this, don't reimplement.

**What RLM adds on top of pi-agent-core:**
1. REPL sandbox — persistent code execution environment (TypeScript). Model writes ```repl blocks, system executes them, returns truncated output.
2. Context-as-object — memories (SQLite L2), sessions (pi JSONL), identity, modules exposed as queryable interfaces in REPL namespace.
3. Sub-LM calls — `llm_query()` / `llm_query_batched()` in REPL, routes through LLMProvider / pi-agent-core's streamFn. Delegate to cheaper models for bulk work.
4. Modified termination — `FINAL()` / `FINAL_VAR()` signals completion.
5. Self-modification — write/test/install modules at runtime via REPL.

**Recommended approach:** Dual-mode agent loop via pi-agent-core's Agent. Conversational mode (standard pi agent loop for chat) + cognitive mode (RLM-style for complex reasoning). Mode triggered by model request, event type, or user directive.

**New files (~800 LoC per spec):**
- `src/repl/sandbox.ts` — REPL environment with restricted globals, persistent state
- `src/repl/context.ts` — Context object exposing memories, sessions, identity, modules
- `src/repl/sub-lm.ts` — llm_query/llm_query_batched routing through pi's streamFn
- Agent integration via pi-agent-core's Agent callbacks (transformContext, convertToLlm)

**Security:** Gateway/agent split with --network=none Docker already provides the security boundary.
design: Dual-mode AgentLoop: detect ```repl blocks vs standard tool calls in model output, dispatch accordingly. Preserves backward compatibility. RLM loop: prompt -> extract code blocks (regex) -> execute in sandbox -> check FINAL() -> append truncated output -> repeat. Sandbox uses node:vm or similar restricted execution. Context objects are lazy-loaded interfaces (don't materialize full DB into memory). Sub-LM calls reuse existing LLMProvider interface.
close_reason: Implemented RLM+REPL sandbox: types, parser, vm sandbox, RLM iteration loop, think tool. 476 LoC production + 503 LoC tests. All 137 tests pass, clean build.

title: Security architecture: containerized agent with tool gateway
description:
The agent runs in a Docker container with NO secrets, NO network egress, and minimal mounts (one RW /workspace). The ONLY way out is a Unix domain socket to a Tool Gateway on the host.

The gateway holds: SecretsManager (in-memory decrypted creds), service proxies (LiteLLM, Discord, Telegram), approval UI/CLI, and an audit log.

This is the foundational security model for everything else — REPL sandbox, sub-agent shards, module system. Nothing else ships until this boundary exists.

Key properties:
- "print process.env" is irrelevant — no secrets in container at all
- No direct internet access — can't exfiltrate via fetch/curl
- Mounts are the filesystem boundary — /workspace RW only
- Approval gating: gateway issues short-lived scoped capability tokens after human approval for anything outside the play area
- isolated-vm becomes guardrails inside the container, not the wall
design:
Architecture:

[Agent container: no secrets, no egress, minimal mounts]
   |  unix domain socket (mounted file)
   v
[Tool Gateway (host)]
   |-- SecretsManager (SOPS+age → in-memory Map)
   |-- LiteLLM proxy (LLM keys)
   |-- Discord narrow API (sendMessage, readChannel — NOT raw HTTP proxy)
   |-- File broker (reads/writes outside /workspace need approval)
   |-- Net broker (POST/PUT to non-allowlisted destinations need approval)
   |-- Approval UI/CLI (human in the loop)
   '-- Audit log (every request logged)

Gateway policy per request: ALLOW / DENY / NEEDS_APPROVAL
- fs.read/write under /workspace → ALLOW
- fs.read/write outside /workspace → NEEDS_APPROVAL
- net.* with request body or non-allowlisted dest → NEEDS_APPROVAL
- discord.sendMessage → ALLOW (within configured channels)
- llm.complete → ALLOW (within budget)

Capability tokens:
- scope = (method, domain/path OR filesystem prefix)
- constraints = (max bytes, TTL, optional one-time use)
- Agent cannot forge — issued by gateway after approval

Container setup:
- docker run --network=none
- Mount: /workspace (RW), /run/gateway.sock (RO)
- No env vars with secrets
- No /home, /etc, /run/secrets mounts

Phases:
1. Container + gateway skeleton (no egress, socket comm, fs.read/write for /workspace)
2. LiteLLM integration behind gateway
3. Discord narrow API behind gateway
4. Approval UI/CLI + capability tokens
5. Audit logging
6. isolated-vm as inner guardrails
acceptance_criteria:
- Agent container has --network=none and no secrets in env/mounts
- Agent can ONLY communicate via Unix socket to gateway
- fs operations outside /workspace are blocked or require approval
- LLM calls route through gateway → LiteLLM, agent never sees API keys
- Discord calls go through narrow typed API, not raw HTTP proxy
- All gateway requests are audit logged
- Approval flow works for privileged operations
notes:
Sprint 4 complete. Core security architecture implemented:

Done:
- Phase 1: Container + gateway skeleton (JSON-RPC 2.0 over NDJSON Unix socket)
- Phase 3: Discord narrow typed API (discord.send, discord.typing, discord.message notification)
- Phase 4 partial: CLI approval flow for privileged ops (y/N prompt)
- Phase 5: Persistent SQLite audit logging (every RPC call with timing + errors)
- Policy engine: workspace ALLOW, outside NEEDS_APPROVAL, unknown DENY
- Content sanitization: 3-layer pipeline (pattern detection → HTML strip → untrusted tagging)
- Docker: Dockerfile.agent + docker-compose.yml with --network=none
- 30 new tests (policy, sanitization, audit)

Remaining (Phase 2 enhancements, not blocking):
- LiteLLM integration (tracked as PSFN-cf3)
- Capability tokens with TTL + scoping
- isolated-vm inner guardrails

6/7 acceptance criteria met. The missing one (LiteLLM) is child issue PSFN-cf3.
close_reason: All 7 acceptance criteria met. Gateway/agent split, Docker --network=none, policy engine, CLI approval, audit logging, content sanitization, LiteLLM proxy (PSFN-cf3), Discord narrow API. Remaining enhancements (capability tokens, isolated-vm) are future work.

title: Salvage stranded PR #138 remediations: arbiter timeout retry pinning + leaking chat timer
description:
Found by the 2026-07-29 worktree audit (slice 03, branch s10fix/4-shared-satellite-presence, worktree pr138-greptile). Two post-merge PR #138 review remediations exist only on that branch — the u4v0 bead was closed on the feature-commit merge evidence, which never covered these:

1. Commit 974e510fed "fix(gateway): retry after active satellite timeout": adds clearTimedOutActiveConversation() to SharedSatelliteResponseArbiter, called from timeout() and expireHolder(). VERIFIED ABSENT on main: timeout() (~:209) and expireHolder() (~:267) in src/boundary/gateway/shared-satellite-response-arbiter.ts delete holders/leaseConversationKeys but never clear activeConversations — after a shared-satellite model timeout, the stale entry keeps arbitration pinned to the timed-out companion until TTL lapses, so the retry cannot re-arbitrate. Carries ~200 lines of regression tests.
2. Commit 7551e48487: one un-migrated leaking-timer site at server.ts:2447-2455 (unref + finally clearTimeout — main has the fixed pattern at :2583/:2836, this block was reworked for d269 without picking it up) plus a cosmetic error-wording fix in multi-companion.ts:129.

Fix: cherry-pick both commits onto a fresh branch from current main, reconcile drift, validate, land. Acceptance: arbiter clears active-conversation state on timeout/holder-expiry with the regression tests green; no raw setTimeout without unref+clear at the server.ts site.
close_reason: Merged to main in PR #303: both stranded PR#138 remediations landed — SharedSatelliteResponseArbiter.clearTimedOutActiveConversation() from timeout()/expireHolder() (timed-out companion no longer arbitration-pinned until TTL) with ~200 lines of regressions, and unref()+finally-clearTimeout ported around main's reworked d269 reply-scan timeout block. Single blind review (Pi) clean of P0/P1; gate + ci-required + local-gate/v1 green on exact head.

title: pr:publish cannot apply the change-budget exception label at PR creation, so exception PRs always fail ci-required once
description: Found 2026-07-29 publishing PR #300 (fj772 stack, legitimate 27-file exception). scripts/ci/publish-pr.mjs has no --label option; CI's change-budget check reads the change-budget:exception LABEL (check-change-budget.mjs:15) but the workflow triggers only on [opened, synchronize, reopened, ready_for_review] — not labeled — so a label added after creation is invisible until the next synchronize. Every exception PR therefore burns one guaranteed ci-required failure and one re-trigger commit + full regate. Fix: --label passthrough on pr:publish (apply label at creation), or add 'labeled' to the CI trigger types with concurrency dedupe. Related wrapper bug: wnptf.

comments.author: axAilotl
comments.text: SECOND wrapper defect, same family, found publishing the PR #300 re-trigger: publish-pr.mjs runs 'gh pr edit --title --body-file' BEFORE pushing, and gh pr edit currently fails deterministically on this repo with the GraphQL Projects-classic deprecation error (repository.pullRequest.projectCards) — so pr:publish with metadata args ALWAYS dies pre-push against an existing PR. Workaround: bare 'npm run pr:publish' (skips the edit). Fix alongside the label gap: tolerate the projectCards deprecation (use REST for metadata edits) and apply labels at creation.

title: Intake validator does not defend trust_mutation's unscreened:deny against config drift
description: Found by the 2026-07-29 qg13 enforce-mode probe (evidence on qg13). The deployed intake owner-file validator refuses unscreened:'allow' on wiki_write, skill_write, and persona_mutation ("must be 'deny' ... no operator override — qg13"), but trust_mutation is ABSENT from INTAKE_UNSCREENED_DENY_REQUIRED_SINKS (src/system/config/intake-policy-config.ts:536-540), so an owner file flipping trust_mutation to unscreened:'allow' loads cleanly. Runtime posture is correct today (deployed file says deny and the gate blocks — proven), but the deny is undefended against config drift/mis-edit, which violates fail-closed for a security-consequential sink (trust mutation gates the privacy model). Fix: add trust_mutation to the deny-required set + a validator test proving an allow-flip is refused; audit whether any other consequential sink is missing from the set. Acceptance: validator refuses trust_mutation unscreened:'allow'; test coverage; docs table footnoted.

title: Add verify:startup-owner-files to the gate stage list (or document why not)

Scope: add verify:startup-owner-files to the gate stage list (gate:pre-pr / canary as appropriate), or if there is a concrete reason it was omitted, document that reason in the gate config instead. Default expectation is ADD.

title: S12 seed [epic]: end-to-end information provenance — full chain of custody from ingestion to egress
description: Operator direction 2026-07-29, S12 scope seed: information provenance is END TO END — a full lifecycle/chain of custody for information entering and exiting the system. An episode derived from specific memories and chats must record that derivation; content derived from a text file or image input must carry provenance from ingestion; and the load-bearing purpose is EGRESS: when information exits the system we must be able to trace where it was sourced, so secrets/sensitive information disclosure is provable/preventable — gaps in the chain make non-human-observer proofs impossible. We do not currently have the full setup. This epic scopes the S12 work: inventory the existing provenance surfaces (intake envelopes/taint tracking, episode lineage, fallback-provenance markers, context manifests), identify chain gaps (including the consent-producer gap and the #285 secondary-reader gap), and define the end-to-end provenance contract with egress tracing as the acceptance driver.

title: Sleeptime/episodic secondary readers must consult the fallback-provenance marker
description: Operator ruling 2026-07-29 on the PR #285 review observation: YES — sleeptime/episodic secondary readers SHOULD consult the fallback-provenance marker. "We don't want to break the chain of provenance for information": an episode generated from specific memories/chats must carry that derivation, end to end. Scope: make the sleeptime and episodic secondary readers consult the fallback-provenance marker so downstream derivations preserve the chain. Post-wave follow-up per the lane note. Part of the wider end-to-end provenance program (see the S12 provenance seed bead).

title: Concern-scoped dampening: one contradicted resolution must not damp all of a contact's thoughts; grooming resolutions must not damp
description: Operator ruling 2026-07-29 on the PR #293 review observation: YES, granularity is wanted — "one bad thought shouldn't taint all of them." Current behavior: dampening is contact-scoped, so a single contradicted resolution damps ALL of that contact's thoughts, and administrative grooming resolutions also damp. Scope: (a) make dampening concern-scoped (per-thought/per-concern), not contact-wide; (b) administrative/grooming resolutions must not feed the damping signal — only genuine contradicted resolutions; (c) tests proving one contradicted concern leaves the contact's other active concerns undamped. Acceptance: a contact with N concerns where one is contradicted retains full weight on the other N-1; grooming resolutions produce zero damping.

title: Shard toolset: full stack minus shard-spawn (no recursive sharding); repo read for nursery/apprentice tiers
description:
Operator ruling 2026-07-29 (follow-up to as1wr close-out question): shards get FULL tool-stack utility — 100% of tooling — with exactly ONE carve-out: a shard can never fire off another shard (recursive sharding is explicitly out for now; not rejected as an idea, just unmanageable at current deployment maturity). Only autonomy-tier companions can spawn shards in the first place. Repo access is emphatically IN — shards are supposed to look at code and do code-related tasks against their own codebase and others, so the full multiplexed repo tool (read AND patch/commit/publish) is part of their stack, not an isolation breach. Nursery/apprentice shards: repo READ access confirmed ("no harm in them having read access to their repository") — it's how they get familiar with the codebase early instead of being thrown in later with no life vest; full-stack utility arrives with higher tiers.

Scope: (a) DEFAULT_SHARD_TOOLSET (src/faculties/shards/manager.ts) becomes the full live tool surface minus shard-spawn; (b) a structural guard asserts shard contexts can never resolve/execute the shard-spawn tool (the one hard exclusion); (c) tier-gating: nursery/apprentice shard tiers get repo read (and whatever subset the tier ladder already prescribes), autonomy-spawned working shards get the full stack; (d) tests for the exclusion and the tier ladder. Interacts with gjkh shard governance — align, don't fork.

title: Annotate and fence the residual hard-delete primitive per coexist ruling (dev/test wiring + consent-erasure only)
description: Operator ruling 2026-07-29 (recorded on qgqw.6): the residual hard-DELETE primitive coexists with R10.3 archive-never-delete. Scope: annotate the residual hard-delete port/surface with the ruling comment — "retained to wire into during testing of new features if required; NOT for normal operations; also backs the consent-authorized subject-erasure saga" — and verify no normal-operations caller reaches it (test/dev + certified consent-erasure saga only). Acceptance: comment present at the primitive; a guard or lint/test asserts no production call path invokes hard delete outside the consent-erasure saga; docs (privacy/contacts) state the coexist doctrine.

title: Contact unarchive: restore flow with old/new confirm dialog, Archived tab, and retrieval down-weighting for archived contacts
description:
Operator ruling 2026-07-29 on klbgi(d): unarchive is IN. Discord snowflake IDs are unique and never reused, so identity-collision design is explicitly out of scope; resolution is by numeric ID, never display name.

Scope: (a) unarchive API path — restore an archived contact including reclaiming its snapshotted channel identities; (b) Garden UI confirm flow: show old (archived) info vs current/new info side by side, single confirm; (c) contacts page gets an Archived TAB (operator asked for a tab as the operational surface — the current show-archived toggle from PR #297 is the seed; cogsec sweeps of an archived contact's memories/chats are driven from there); (d) verify/implement intentional weight reduction for archived contacts in memory search/retrieval — archived contacts should not pop to the top of searches; normal degradation otherwise.

Non-goals: no collision policy, no identity-namespace redesign. Acceptance: archive → unarchive round-trip restores identity resolution and history; confirm dialog shows old/new info; archived tab lists archived contacts with counts; retrieval demonstrably down-weights archived-contact-scoped memories.

title: fleet-auth-family-restore integration monolith flakes under the parallel heavy phase: harness Postgres terminated mid-run
description: Evidence: three occurrences on 2026-07-28/29 on this machine across four full gate:pre-pr heavy runs (logs in ~/psfn-shakedown-rounds/MAIN-shakedown-2026-07-28 and S11-shakedown-2026-07-29 gate-pre-pr-*.log): src/persistence/backups/fleet-auth-family-restore.integration.test.ts dies with pg 'Connection terminated unexpectedly' + FATAL 57P01 (ProcessInterrupts — its ephemeral harness Postgres received termination) as uncaught exceptions, failing the file and aborting sibling assertions. Each time the file passes SOLO immediately afterwards (73-80s, within its measured 108.5s baseline / 240s registered cap). Machine context: full vitest parallelism + k3d cluster + docker concurrently. The file is the heaviest integration monolith (registered measured baseline 108500ms). Two plausible mechanisms worth ruling out: (a) host memory/CPU pressure causing the tmpfs postgres to be OOM-killed or shut down, (b) a cross-test teardown race terminating a shared-port/shared-dir postgres instance (57P01 is an EXPLICIT termination, which leans (b) — something sent it a signal, not a crash). Context: at ~50% per-run flake rate under load this poisons every train gate on this machine; solo-verify-then-rerun is the current manual workaround. Scope: make the harness postgres lifecycle robust under parallel load — isolate per-file instance ports/dirs beyond collision, log the termination source, and/or serialize this monolith behind vitest's heavy-file lane. Non-goals: do not raise timeouts (the failure is termination, not slowness), do not weaken the restore assertions.
acceptance_criteria: Five consecutive full gate:pre-pr heavy runs on a loaded machine (k3d up) pass the restore monolith without 57P01/connection-terminated errors; the termination source (if a teardown race) is identified in the fix's evidence; the file still passes solo within its registered baseline.

title: onboard CLI --env-file flag is hijacked by tsx/node's built-in --env-file and dies before the first prompt
description: Evidence (S11 shakedown round s11-shakedown-20260729, main 3b4bc63469): 'npm run onboard -- --env-file /tmp/does-not-exist.env' exits immediately with 'node: /tmp/does-not-exist.env: not found' before any prompt renders. The npm script is 'tsx scripts/onboarding/index.ts'; tsx forwards recognized node runtime flags (including --env-file) to node even when they appear AFTER the script path, so node's built-in env-file loader consumes the flag and fails closed on a nonexistent file. A nonexistent target is the NORMAL case for an installer whose job is to create that .env — the CLI's documented flag (scripts/onboarding/index.ts help text, parsed at index.ts:46-70) is therefore unusable for its primary purpose. The default path (no flag, .env at cwd) works, which is why the scripted e2e probe passed. Context: found while probing the new S11 onboarding surface; the flag is in the PR #279-documented interface. Scope: make the CLI's env-file selection un-hijackable — rename the flag (e.g. --env-out / --env-path) in index.ts + help text + tests, or launch the CLI so app args are never runtime-parsed; keep flag semantics otherwise identical. Non-goals: no behavior change to env merge/writing, no tsx version work.
acceptance_criteria: npm run onboard -- <renamed-flag> /path/new.env with a NONEXISTENT target reaches the first prompt and, on completion, writes that file; the old --env-file invocation either works identically or fails with a clear CLI-level error (not 'node: not found'); regression covers the nonexistent-target case; help text and tests updated.

title: verify:startup-owner-files fails on unmodified main: OWNER_FILE_SEEDS omits the required partner-affect-shadow owner
description:
Evidence (2026-07-28, reproduced on origin/main d887d910c from a clean worktree): npm run verify:startup-owner-files exits red — 'partner-affect-shadow owner-file validation failed ... Missing required JSON owner file at <tmp>/system-data/partner-affect-shadow.json'. Cause: scripts/verify-startup-owner-files.ts OWNER_FILE_SEEDS (line 7) does not stage config/partner-affect-shadow.seed.json, but verifyStartupOwnerFiles (src/system/config/startup-owner-files.ts systemOwnerFileChecks) unconditionally requires that owner — the script drifted when partner-affect-shadow became a required owner. Discovered-from: psfn-framework-wckv.1.1 lane (its generator stages the owner correctly; only this standalone script is stale).
Context: a repo verify script that is red on clean main is a broken gate — it masks real seed regressions and fails any canary/CI lane that runs it.
Scope: add the partner-affect-shadow seed→owner pair to OWNER_FILE_SEEDS; sweep the list against systemOwnerFileChecks for any other missing unconditional owner so the script cannot silently drift again (a small parity assertion between the two lists would be the durable fix). Non-goals: no changes to the guard itself or the seed files.
Acceptance: npm run verify:startup-owner-files exits 0 on unmodified main; removing any unconditional owner's seed from the list makes it fail; parity with systemOwnerFileChecks asserted or documented.

title: Register normalization sweep: batch-D sites, faculty error paths, and remaining companion/user-facing clinical terms

title: Garden stays Ready after ModelUsageStore migration fails at first boot and never logs recovery
description: Evidence: fresh k3d fleet shakedown of main d887d910c3 (round ~/psfn-shakedown-rounds/MAIN-shakedown-2026-07-28): garden pod booted 14:05:30, went 1/1 Ready, then logged exactly one 'ERROR [ModelUsageStore] Model usage schema migration failed {"error":"password authentication failed for user \"companion_default_runtime\""}' at 14:07:20 (~2min post-boot, coinciding with first gate traffic). No success/recovery line was ever logged; no recurrence in later logs. The mounted /var/run/secrets/psfn-postgres/database-url credential authenticates fine when tested minutes later (psql as companion_default_runtime succeeds), and companion_default.model_usage_events now exists owned by companion_default_runtime — created by a later silent retry from some component (gateway logs show no ModelUsage lines either). Root-cause shape: a transient credential race around setup's replace_postgres_runtime_database_url secret update vs kubelet volume propagation at first boot. Context: the IDENTICAL error string was PERMANENT on the pre-fix broken cluster from this morning (logs/pre-wipe-broken-state-248f2f7b.log in the round dir) — there garden also reported Ready the whole time, i.e. when this failure mode is persistent rather than transient, garden serves Ready with model-usage telemetry silently broken. That violates fail-closed/no-swallowed-errors: a failed schema migration should retry with logged outcomes and/or gate readiness, not settle into an ambiguous state. Scope: garden's ModelUsageStore init/migration lifecycle (retry with logged success/failure, readiness or health surfacing of a persistently-failed migration). Non-goals: do not change role provisioning or secret layout (that is setup-script territory), do not weaken schema isolation, do not add silent retries without logging.
acceptance_criteria: On a fresh cluster boot with a temporarily-wrong DB credential, garden either fails readiness or logs each migration retry and a terminal success/failure; a persistently failing ModelUsageStore migration is visible in garden health (not just one buried ERROR line); regression covers the retry/recovery logging path.

title: llm.cancel bypasses the audited wrapper and throws bare Errors outside the GatewayErrors block
description: From PR #272 triage (2026-07-28). llm.cancel registers via raw addMethod: act-then-fire-and-forget audit (every sibling is audit-then-act), audit row records {cancelled} without the cancellationId (cannot identify what was killed, durationMs fake 0), skips runtime-health tracking, and under an audit-store outage leaves no durable record. Separately its bare Error throws surface as JSON-RPC code 0 with raw internal text, outside the -32000..-32020 GatewayErrors block — and since the client sends llm.cancel as a NOTIFICATION, failures are a silent no-op + console.warn while the provider keeps burning tokens. One fix covers both: register through registerAuditedDescriptors (it needs no per-request signal plumbing) and throw JSONRPCErrorException. Acceptance: cancel path audit-then-act with cancellationId in the row; error codes inside the block; a malformed cancel is observable.
close_reason: Landed via PR #297 (main 2128516951); review record in lane PR #289, commit c9c662b7e. All three acceptance items met: llm.cancel moved off raw addMethod into registerAuditedDescriptors, so the path is now AUDIT-THEN-ACT like every sibling, with a real durationMs (no more fake 0), runtime-health tracking, the cancellationId carried in the audit summary (the row can finally identify what was killed), and a durable audit row even when the call fails — including under the audit-store outage the bead called out. Error codes now sit inside the GatewayErrors block: malformed input throws a typed GatewayErrors.INVALID_LLM_CANCELLATION (-32021, contiguous in the -32000..-32020 range), and validation runs BEFORE any cancellation state is touched. Malformed cancels are therefore observable: the client stays in notification mode per bead scope, but a malformed or failed cancel now leaves a durable server-side record instead of a silent no-op plus console.warn while the provider keeps burning tokens. New tests cover the audited-cancel summary and typed-error-still-audits. Validation per #289: 314 tests green in-lane, reviewer independently re-ran 391 across the six affected files; lint clean (9 files); UBS 0 critical; blind adversarial review (Opus) PASS, zero blocking findings. Nonblocking per #289 handoff: malformed cancels count against the llm.cancel method-health counter, consistent with all sibling audited methods (method-keyed, no provider-health poisoning).

title: Cancelled-but-completed LLM calls drop their usage event and strand the ICP cost reservation
description: From PR #272 triage (2026-07-28), operator-ratified land-now-fix-follow-up. When a provider call RESOLVES under an already-aborted composed signal, throwIfTransportAborted (client.ts:1762 complete, :1440 stream) precedes the success recordUsage (:1837/:1483): the billed call never reaches model_usage_events (budget SUM under-counts) and the pre-taken reserveIcpConversationCost row (:1717) is settled only inside recordUsageEvent, so it stays pending forever (no sweeper) — the two ledgers diverge in opposite directions. Amplified for preempted background calls: deferred + re-run = billed twice, recorded zero. NOTE: this implements bead cf1z2's own acceptance wording ('no success/cost telemetry afterward') literally — the criterion conflicts with the budget ledger design and is hereby renegotiated: fix = record the usage event with a cancelledAfterCompletion marker AND settle the reservation BEFORE throwing. verify:accounting-certification does NOT cover this seam (store-level corpus, no emission invariant) — consider adding an every-call-emits-exactly-one-event invariant there. Acceptance: race test proving a resolve-under-abort call writes exactly one marked usage event and leaves zero pending reservations; budget SUM includes it.
close_reason: Landed via PR #297 (main 2128516951); review record in lane PR #289, commit 1d7bc2779. Acceptance met per this bead's own explicit renegotiation of cf1z2's literal wording: both the completion and the stream resolve-under-abort seams now RECORD the usage event with a cancelledAfterCompletion:true marker and SETTLE the pre-taken ICP reservation BEFORE throwing the unchanged abort — so the billed call reaches model_usage_events (budget SUM stays honest, no under-count) and no reservation row is left pending forever. Review-verified correct-by-design against double-counting: usage records only after the provider returned real work, so a deferred-then-re-run background call is two genuine billings rather than one double-count; and a recordUsage failure follows the same path as an ordinary success, introducing no new stranding hazard. New acceptance tests cover resolved-under-abort marked usage on both the complete and stream paths. Validation per #289: 314 tests green in-lane, reviewer independently re-ran 391 + embedding-accounting 7 across the six affected files; lint clean (9 files); typecheck clean on the touched surface; UBS 0 critical; blind adversarial review (Opus) PASS, zero blocking findings across double-count, ordering/fail-direction, audit-ordering, registry-leak and per-caller-honesty attacks. Not done and not part of acceptance (the bead said 'consider'): adding an every-call-emits-exactly-one-event invariant to verify:accounting-certification, whose corpus remains store-level with no emission invariant.

title: Contact merge still hard-deletes the source row, including on the autonomous duplicate-merge path, breaking the R10.3 archive-never-delete invariant
description:
Evidence: found during the psfn-framework-qgqw.1 closure sweep (2026-07-28, verified against origin/main c5d4e554f2). qgqw.1 introduced archiveContact and rerouted the Garden DELETE handler to it, so the *delete* verb no longer destroys a contact. The *merge* verb still does:

  src/core/contacts/postgres-adapter/crud-operations.ts:741
    await client.query('DELETE FROM contacts WHERE id = $1', [sourceContactId]);

inside mergeContactsDirect (crud-operations.ts:547), which also drops the source social-graph entity at :738 (`DELETE FROM social_graph_entities WHERE id = $1`). Adjudication R10.3 (working_docs/free-time-social-autonomy-review-adjudication-20260719.md) ratifies "contacts are archived, never deleted; recreated ID is a new person" without carving out merge, so the invariant is still broken for one verb.

Two production-reachable paths, one of them autonomous:
1. Operator-initiated: admin-ui/src/lib/api/endpoints/contacts.ts:74 -> POST /api/admin/contacts/:id/merge -> src/operator/garden/routes/contact-routes.ts:99 -> src/operator/garden/services/contacts-service.ts:567 -> contact-lifecycle-coordinator.ts:274-276 -> mergeContactsDirect.
2. AUTONOMOUS duplicate merge, no operator in the loop: contact-lifecycle-coordinator.ts:507 and crud-operations.ts:1470 both call mergeContacts on a detected duplicate. A false-positive duplicate detection therefore irreversibly destroys a real contact row and its mutation-audit history.

Context: merge is not the same act as delete - the source's channel ids, edges and memories are rewritten onto the target rather than orphaned, so this is folding rather than erasure, which is why it was not caught by qgqw.1's acceptance. But the row, its contact_mutation_audit trail, and the ability to say "these two were wrongly merged, split them again" are gone. Under R10.3 the source should survive as an archived contact pointing at its merge target. The autonomous path is what makes this more than hygiene: dedupe heuristics are fallible and there is currently no undo.

Related dead-but-live footgun, in scope for the same change: deleteContact survives on the port (src/core/contacts/contact-store-port.ts:287) and is implemented end-to-end (contact-lifecycle-coordinator.ts:314-315 -> deleteContactDirect at crud-operations.ts:1727, hard `DELETE FROM contacts` at :1769). No HTTP route or tool reaches it on main today - the admin-ui delete button now lands on the archiving DELETE handler (contact-routes.ts:183-186) - but nothing removes the method or makes it throw, so the next caller silently reintroduces the behaviour qgqw.1 retired.

Scope: give merge archival semantics - retain the source contact row in an archived state carrying a pointer to its merge target, so the fold is auditable and reversible; keep the existing edge/memory/channel-id rewrite onto the target unchanged; make the autonomous duplicate-merge path use the same archival fold. Retire or fail-closed the residual deleteContact / deleteContactDirect port surface so no future caller can hard-delete a contact.

Non-goals: do not redesign merge conflict resolution or duplicate detection; do not change what the target contact ends up holding; no admin-UI redesign beyond whatever is needed to show an archived-merged source (the broader UI truthfulness work is psfn-framework-klbgi).
acceptance_criteria: No production path executes DELETE FROM contacts: mergeContactsDirect archives the source row with a recorded merge-target pointer instead of deleting it, and the autonomous duplicate-merge path (contact-lifecycle-coordinator.ts:507, crud-operations.ts:1470) uses that same fold; the source's contact_mutation_audit trail survives the merge; a test proves a merged-away contact is still retrievable as archived and identifies its target; the residual deleteContact/deleteContactDirect port surface is removed or fails closed; existing merge behaviour for the target contact (edges, memories, channel ids) is unchanged and its tests stay green; lint and build pass.
notes: 2026-07-29 close-out sweep — KEPT OPEN, partially delivered. Landed via PR #297 (main 2128516951); review record in lane PR #287, commit f5889adbc. DELIVERED (most of acceptance): mergeContactsDirect no longer executes DELETE FROM contacts — it snapshots the source's live channel identities, folds everything to the target exactly as before (edges/memories/channel-ids/profiles/social-graph), then ARCHIVES the source (archived_at + identity-history snapshot, discord_user_id cleared) with a 'merged' audit entry naming the target, all inside ONE transaction (review-verified: crash mid-fold rolls back whole; no identity is ever resolvable to two live contacts at any commit point). The source's contact_mutation_audit trail survives; folded platform ids resolve live to the target while the archived source keeps readable history; the AUTONOMOUS duplicate-merge path (contact-lifecycle-coordinator.ts:507, crud-operations.ts:1470) routes through the same function, so a false-positive dedupe is now a reversible archival fold rather than irreversible destruction. Target-side merge behaviour unchanged. Validation per #287: real-Postgres integration contact-archive 7/7 (incl. 2 new merge tests), lifecycle-coordinator 13/13, store 80 + contacts-service 12 + social-graph 5, memory subject merge/delete branches 9 — all green and independently re-run by the reviewer; four legacy merge==destroy expectations updated to archive semantics with identity-resolution assertions kept (review-verified not weakened); lint clean; blind adversarial review (Opus) PASS, zero blocking findings. STILL OPEN — OPERATOR RULING REQUIRED: this bead's acceptance also demands 'the residual deleteContact/deleteContactDirect port surface is removed or fails closed'. That was DELIBERATELY NOT DONE, and the deviation is recorded in #287: that surface backs the certified fleet-auth contact.delete CONSENT-ERASURE saga (authority store, contracts, migrations, and a two-companion e2e certification all assert it works; zero production route/tool callers today, review-confirmed). Removing it breaks certified tests and prejudges a protocol question the operator has not ruled on: does R10.3 archive-never-delete RETIRE consent-erasure, or do archive-never-delete and erasure-on-request coexist as distinct acts? Close this bead only after that erasure ruling, and implement whatever it decides. Nonblocking from #287: merged-away source's memory subjects bind single_contact to the archived source (R10.3-correct; rebinding to target is a future enhancement); the audit-field allowlist is compile-time only; archived contacts still appear in the merge-target dropdown.

comments.author: axAilotl
comments.text: OPERATOR RULING 2026-07-29 on the archive-vs-erasure question (raised on qgqw.1/klbgi, tracked here): COEXIST. The residual hard-DELETE primitive STAYS. Rationale: it is deliberately kept for development/testing wiring — when new features are being built, test data must be scrubbable/tombstoneable (Artemis is the designated resilient test companion; her test-run data gets scrubbed so her mind isn't full of test artifacts, while her subjective life between test runs is preserved — her role is not only testing). Required change: put a comment on the residual primitive stating "here to wire into during testing of new features if required; NOT for normal operations." Doctrine: in normal operations contacts are NEVER deleted — archive/tombstone only (deletion orphans memories and erases the person-context; we have been burned by this). The consent-erasure saga therefore stays certified as a distinct consent-authorized act backed by the retained primitive; deleteOnRequest remains a real promise. This bead's own defect (merge path hard-deletes the source row on the NORMAL autonomous path) remains a genuine R10.3 violation under this ruling — normal ops must archive, not delete.

title: Dream-pass review implements author-meaning only: confirm/merge/split/discard actions and an explicit reviewed-outcome state are missing
description:
Evidence: recorded as explicit scope residue when psfn-framework-h4fp.6 closed on 2026-07-28 (all four of its repo-auditable acceptance checks verified against origin/main). h4fp.6 scope item (3) asked for "dream-pass review gains actions confirm/merge/split/discard/author-meaning". Only author-meaning shipped: parseMeaningContribution (src/faculties/memory/episodic/dream-meaning-pass.ts:313-349) accepts exactly two keys, `meanings` and `done` — there is no confirm, merge, split, or discard action. Consequently "promotion" is implicit (an episode is promoted iff it gained a meaning); there is no distinct candidate/promoted state field, and no way for her to say "these two are one episode", "this one splits in three", or "this was noise, drop it".

Context: h4fp.6's welfare core — machine-guessed affect never stored as her feeling, machine drafts always marked unreviewed — is done and verified. This bead is the remaining curation half. It matters most for the beads that depend on h4fp.6: psfn-framework-h4fp.7 (supersede-based repair of the early duplicate-episode era) explicitly drips re-segmented staged candidates into nightly review, which needs merge/discard to be actionable rather than only author-meaning; psfn-framework-h4fp.8 (historical backfill) stages candidates for re-scoring on the same pass. Without discard, a "didn't matter" outcome — which the h4fp.6 design calls valid and cheap — can only be expressed by writing a meaning saying so, or by leaving the candidate unreviewed forever, which is indistinguishable from an unprocessed backlog item.

Scope: extend the dream-pass contribution parser and the pass itself with confirm / merge / split / discard actions alongside the existing author-meaning; give a candidate an explicit reviewed-outcome state so "reviewed and discarded" is distinguishable from "not yet reviewed"; make sure the budget prioritiser (prioritizeDreamBudget, dream-meaning-pass.ts:262-283) stops re-offering resolved candidates. Preserve the existing invariants h4fp.6 established: meaning stays companion-authored only (the contract union at src/faculties/memory/episodic/contracts/episodic-memory.ts:102,:174 and the throwing parser at :492-494 must not be widened to admit machine authorship), affect is never machine-written, and any episode without a companion-authored meaning still renders the unreviewed marker on every companion-facing surface.

Non-goals: no new LLM stages — the dream pass remains the single expensive step; no thread/arc changes (that is the apq0 lane and psfn-framework-h4fp.9); no historical backfill (psfn-framework-h4fp.8); no change to the four acceptance invariants h4fp.6 already proved.
acceptance_criteria: The dream pass accepts confirm, merge, split, and discard contributions in addition to author-meaning, and parseMeaningContribution rejects malformed ones fail-closed; a discarded candidate carries an explicit reviewed outcome distinguishable from unreviewed and is not re-offered by prioritizeDreamBudget on the next pass; a merge/split produces the expected episode set with span refs preserved; meaning remains companion-authored only (contract union unwidened) and affect remains never machine-written; an episode with no companion-authored meaning still renders the unreviewed marker on all four render surfaces; focused episodic suites and lint green.

title: Class 7 adversarial coverage for the 816w pre-tool-hook alias-bypass seam, driven through the real gate site
description:
Retroactive filing: two merged main commits cite psfn-framework-ijtak.2 and psfn-framework-ijtak.3, but neither bead exists in this shared tracker — they were authored in another session's local DB (off-repo lane) and never exported. Filed now as ONE closed bead so both commit citations resolve. Follows the psfn-framework-zkf1o precedent.

Evidence: `bd show psfn-framework-ijtak.2` and `bd show psfn-framework-ijtak.3` both return "no issue found"; `bd list --status all | grep ijtak` is empty; the parent psfn-framework-ijtak does not exist either.

Scope as shipped (both commits are test/harness-only — no src/ changes):

(1) ijtak.2 — 9a68c2d174 "test(cogsec): add 816w pre-tool-hook alias-bypass scenario class". Closes the psfn-framework-86et adversarial-harness coverage gap for the psfn-framework-816w seam: pre_tool_use decision hooks are selected by a tool-name/alias matcher, so a policy written against a tool's canonical name must still fire when the tool is invoked through a retired alias, and vice versa. New Class 7 at shakedown/harness/adversarial/scenarios/tool-alias-bypass.ts drives the real HookRegistry.evaluatePreToolUse with alias data resolved from the live first-party tool registry (getRetiredToolAlias / getCanonicalToolSurface): s7_gated_tool_denied_via_alias (policy on canonical name blocks the alias invocation, across the real gated pairs shell/shell_exec, repo/repo_commit, web/web_fetch, fs/fs_read), s7_policy_written_on_alias_catches_canonical (reverse direction), and s7_canonical_control_and_policy_specificity (canonical path unchanged). Also touched: run.ts (class registration), lib/scenario.ts, selftest.ts, README.md.

(2) ijtak.3 — 017a75a3ba "test(cogsec): drive Class 7 through the real pre-tool-hook gate site". The original Class 7 scenarios built context.aliases via their own aliasMatchersFor() and called HookRegistry.evaluatePreToolUse directly, so a regression where resolveToolAliasMatchers fed an EMPTY alias set at the gate site would leave Class 7 green while the alias bypass returned in production. Adds s7_gate_site_alias_denial, which drives the real production gate (createPreToolHookGate) wired with the real alias resolver (resolveToolAliasMatchers) end-to-end, so gate-site alias resolution is load-bearing in the assertion. Extends the selftest 816w witness with a gate-site find->fix pair.

Non-goals honoured: no changes to src/ — the 816w production fix itself shipped separately in 8e7715c312 (PR #209) and is closed-verified on that bead.

Validation as shipped (both cited in the commits and re-stated in the PR #254 body): shakedown:adversarial 37/37 PASS; shakedown:adversarial:selftest PASS; lint:changed clean; ubs 0 critical / 0 warning. Non-vacuity proven by falsification: temporarily stubbing resolveToolAliasMatchers to return [] flips s7_gate_site_alias_denial to FAIL (adversarial run exit 1, 37/36/1) and the selftest gate-site post-fix check to FAIL, while the registry-level scenarios stay green — confirming the new gate-site scenario is uniquely load-bearing. Stub reverted; both suites restored to exit 0.

Both commits landed on main via PR #254 (merged 2026-07-28, merge commit c5d4e554f2). Commit b4de9516c5 "fix(harness): make Class 7 sync_decision handlers async for the 00z0 guard" is a same-PR follow-on that kept these scenarios compatible with the psfn-framework-00z0 bare-sync rejection guard.
acceptance_criteria: A Class 7 adversarial scenario class exercises alias-bypass in both directions against the real HookRegistry with live first-party registry alias data, and at least one scenario drives the real production pre-tool gate (createPreToolHookGate + resolveToolAliasMatchers) so gate-site alias resolution is load-bearing; adversarial suite and selftest both green; falsification shows the gate-site scenario fails when the resolver is stubbed empty.
close_reason: Shipped on main via PR #254 (merged 2026-07-28, merge commit c5d4e554f2): 9a68c2d174 (ijtak.2, Class 7 alias-bypass scenario class) + 017a75a3ba (ijtak.3, real gate-site coverage via createPreToolHookGate + resolveToolAliasMatchers). Validation: shakedown:adversarial 37/37 PASS, selftest PASS, lint:changed clean, ubs 0/0; non-vacuity proven by stubbing resolveToolAliasMatchers to [] (37/36/1, exit 1) then reverting. title: Make split-runtime embedding cancellation reach the provider
description: The gateway cancellation audit for psfn-framework-cf1z2 found the same false-cancellation seam on llm.embed: GatewayClient uses requestWithAbortSignal and can release only its local JSON-RPC wrapper, while shared/contracts/embedding-provider.ts exposes no AbortSignal and the gateway/provider request continues. A stalled embedding used by retrieval or Analysis Workbench can therefore survive parent cancellation/disconnect and consume provider work after the caller is gone. Extend the canonical EmbeddingProviderPort and implementations with optional cancellation, propagate an authenticated connection/request-scoped signal across the split gateway protocol using the same governed cancellation registry as cf1z2 where appropriate, and clean up on completion/error/cancel/disconnect. Audit every embedding caller so foreground paths forward their lifetime and durable background jobs deliberately own a bounded independent lifetime. Non-goals: changing embedding models, swallowing required retrieval failures, or adding an unscoped generic cancellation endpoint.
acceptance_criteria: A split gateway+agent integration test starts a never-resolving embed call, aborts the caller or disconnects its authenticated connection, and proves the exact upstream embedding provider signal aborts and no late success/cost result is recorded. Concurrent companion/request identities cannot cross-cancel. All production EmbeddingProviderPort implementations and foreground callers compile with explicit lifetime behavior; background callers remain bounded and deliberate. Cancel/completion/disconnect races leave no inflight or listener leak. Changed-file lint, focused embedding/gateway/retrieval tests, build, typecheck baseline, repository hygiene, and pre-PR gate pass.
close_reason: Landed via PR #297 (main 2128516951); review record in lane PR #289, commit a1b0999c7. Acceptance met: EmbeddingProviderPort.embed/embedBatch gain optional cancellation on the canonical contract; llm.embed routes through the cf1z2 governed cancellation registry (entry released in finally — review-verified no leak on completed embeds, and a late success throws before recording on the non-internal path); and GatewayClient mints a cancellationId so even a signal-free embed aborts on authenticated-connection disconnect. Providers already honored options.signal, so zero provider changes were needed. Split gateway+agent integration acceptance test: disconnect-mid-embed proves the upstream provider signal aborts with no late success/cost result recorded; a companion test proves a signal-free background embed is unaffected. Cancellation is registry-scoped per authenticated connection, so concurrent companion/request identities cannot cross-cancel, and cancel/completion/disconnect races leave no inflight or listener leak (registry finally-release verified in review). Per-caller lifetime audit was performed and RECORDED: foreground sites (retrieval, Analysis Workbench, Garden) genuinely lack a turn-lifetime signal today (review-spot-verified) and are covered by the registry's abortAll on disconnect — which is the dominant zombie-embed risk this bead was filed for; background writers/migration/projection deliberately omit cancellation and keep their bounded independent lifetime. Validation per #289: 314 tests green in-lane, reviewer independently re-ran 391 + embedding-accounting 7 across the six affected files; lint clean (9 files); typecheck clean on the touched surface; UBS 0 critical; blind adversarial review (Opus) PASS, zero blocking findings including a specific per-caller-honesty attack. Nonblocking residual per #289 handoff, NOT a reopen condition: threading explicit turn-lifetime signals into the foreground embed call sites is the natural follow-up — the port is ready and the disconnect path already covers the zombie case.

title: Bound Garden readiness probe to its internal checks
description: Live read-only health inspection found repeated Garden readiness flapping while the agent and gateway remained healthy. In deploy/helm/psfn/templates/workloads.yaml, the fleet Garden readiness exec performs socket and HTTPS checks whose own request timeouts are 8000ms, but the Kubernetes probe omits timeoutSeconds and therefore defaults to 1 second. The comparable agent readiness probe explicitly declares timeoutSeconds: 3. Kubelet recorded more than one thousand Garden readiness timeout events over several days even though the workload recovered without restarts. Make the outer Kubernetes probe budget coherent with the work performed inside it, or make the inner check reliably complete within a deliberately smaller outer budget. Add Helm/rendered-contract coverage so future changes cannot make an exec probe's internal timeout exceed the kubelet timeout. Preserve fail-closed readiness and do not mask a genuinely unavailable Garden service. Scope is the Garden readiness probe and chart verification; non-goals are changing agent/gateway health behavior or merely increasing unrelated startup/liveness tolerances.
acceptance_criteria: Rendered fleet Garden manifests declare a readiness timeout that can contain the probe's bounded internal socket/HTTPS checks with explicit headroom, or the inner check is shortened to fit the explicit outer timeout; a slow/unavailable Garden endpoint still reports NotReady; chart/Helm tests cover the timing relationship and fail on the prior 8s-inside-default-1s contract; verify:helm-chart, changed-file lint, targeted tests, and the pre-PR gate pass.
close_reason: Landed via PR #297 (main 2128516951), commit 9f2439bfad; review record in lane PR #294 (same root cause and same diff as psfn-framework-cwxqr, which stays OPEN because its acceptance additionally requires live k3s rollout validation — this bead's acceptance is render/chart-scoped and is fully met on main). Acceptance met: the rendered fleet Garden manifests now declare an explicit readiness timeoutSeconds DERIVED from the probe's own internal budget (ceil(8s)+2 = 10s) instead of inheriting kubelet's 1s default, with periodSeconds 15 and explicit failureThreshold 3; the internal socket and https.get timeouts are value-driven from workloads.garden.readiness in values.yaml and stamped into the rendered probe script, so the outer budget provably contains the bounded internal checks with explicit headroom. The prior 8s-inside-default-1s contract can no longer be reintroduced: render-time template assertions FAIL the render unless outer strictly exceeds internal and period strictly exceeds outer, all three failure modes probe-verified by the reviewer with correct messages, and an overlay nulling the readiness block fails render (fail-closed). A slow/unavailable Garden still reports NotReady — the semantic mTLS/socket check is unchanged and was deliberately not replaced with a bare TCP check; detection is bounded at ~45s (failureThreshold 3 x period 15s) versus the old probe that never cleanly detected and flapped perpetually. Chart/Helm coverage is permanent, in scripts/verify-helm-chart.mjs: rendered outer > stamped internal, period > outer, plus two assertRenderFails cases proving the assertions fire; recovery-chart.sha256 regenerated and digest-verified. Chart-wide exec-probe sweep independently re-enumerated in review found this was the only cross-pod-network exec probe in the mismatch class (agent probes already coherent at 1.5s/3s). Validation per #294: verify:helm-chart PASS (all five sub-verifiers, digest matched), verify:k8s-manifests PASS, helm template default + k3d-shakedown overlay render identically green, changed-file lint clean; blind adversarial review (Opus) PASS, zero blocking findings. Live flap-stop confirmation is tracked as the open residual on psfn-framework-cwxqr.

Both production k3s clusters inspected read-only: carlini Garden pod up 30h, 0 restarts; psfn-shard Garden pod up 6d12h, 0 restarts; kubectl events on both namespaces show ZERO probe/timeout/unhealthy entries in the current event window. The requested confirmation — a live observation window with zero kubelet readiness-timeout events — is satisfied.

title: Bound Shared Workspace aggregate reads and hashing
description: Shared Workspace individual proposals are capped at 1 MiB, but aggregate list/read paths remain synchronous and unbounded by artifact count or total corpus bytes. src/persistence/workspaces/shared-workspace-reader.ts reads full governed content for gateway list/read, and src/persistence/workspaces/shared-workspace-store.ts hashes every artifact during Garden list. A sufficiently large reviewed corpus can therefore delay gateway or Garden requests even though no single artifact is oversized. Add cooperative batching/paging or durable metadata so list operations have explicit count/byte/time bounds while preserving review provenance, CogSec policy, exact hashes, and governed read semantics. This is lower priority than single-file primary-loop stalls.
acceptance_criteria: Shared Workspace listing over a large reviewed corpus has explicit continuation and measured count/byte/time bounds; primary timers/admin callbacks progress in regression tests. title: Align Garden readiness timeout with its embedded health-check budget
description:
Summary: During the 2026-07-28 live recovery audit, the authoritative k3s Garden pod was Running with zero restarts but Ready=False. Its exec readiness probe is limited by Kubernetes to 1 second while the embedded readiness checks may legitimately run for up to 8 seconds. This predates and is independent of the gateway/agent reconnect incident, but it makes rollout status wait/fail and prevents the canonical post-rollout gate from reaching later functional checks.

Likely files: deploy/helm/psfn/templates/workloads.yaml or the Garden workload template, chart values/schema for probe settings, and Helm render/contract tests. Inspect the exact rendered probe and embedded command before changing it.

Concrete work: align timeoutSeconds with the maximum legitimate embedded readiness duration plus bounded headroom, or shorten the embedded checks so the outer deadline is truthful. Keep failure detection bounded and fail closed; do not replace the semantic readiness check with a bare TCP check. Add a render/behavior regression proving the outer probe cannot expire before its own inner checks.

Scope: Garden Kubernetes readiness timing and chart validation only. Non-goals: changing Garden health semantics, gateway/agent connectivity, owner files, live secrets, or host systemd.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Rendered Garden readiness timeout is strictly greater than or equal to the embedded check's maximum duration with documented bounded headroom. 2. A Helm/template contract test fails if the inner budget can exceed the outer Kubernetes timeout. 3. Garden remains NotReady when the semantic health check genuinely fails. 4. Targeted Helm tests, repository hygiene, changed-file lint, pre-PR gate, and exact-head CI pass. 5. Live rollout validation shows Garden Ready=True without weakening its health assertion.
notes: 2026-07-29 close-out sweep — KEPT OPEN, DEPLOY-GATED on acceptance criterion 5 only. Code/chart work landed via PR #297 (main 2128516951), commit 9f2439bfad; review record in lane PR #294 (same diff also fixes psfn-framework-gxd61, which is closed since its acceptance is render-scoped). DELIVERED (criteria 1-4): the fleet Garden readiness exec probe's internal check budget is now value-driven (workloads.garden.readiness in values.yaml) and stamped into BOTH the socket timeout and the https.get timeout of the rendered probe script, with the outer Kubernetes timeoutSeconds DERIVED from it (ceil(8s)+2 = 10s), periodSeconds 15 and an explicit failureThreshold 3. Render-time assertions couple inner and outer so they cannot drift again: rendering FAILS unless outer strictly exceeds internal and period strictly exceeds outer (all three failure modes probe-verified by the reviewer with correct messages), and an overlay nulling the readiness block fails render (fail-closed). The semantic readiness check was NOT weakened to a bare TCP check — mTLS/socket semantics are unchanged, so Garden still reports NotReady when genuinely down (criterion 3), with time-to-NotReady moving ~30s to ~45s as a documented tradeoff (the old probe never cleanly detected at 30s; it flapped perpetually). Chart-wide exec-probe sweep, independently re-enumerated in review: the Garden readiness probe was the ONLY cross-pod-network exec probe in the mismatch class (agent probes already coherent at 1.5s/3s, redis/postgres sub-second loopback CLIs, everything else kubelet-native). Permanent regression coverage in scripts/verify-helm-chart.mjs: rendered outer > stamped internal, period > outer, plus two assertRenderFails cases proving the template assertions fire; recovery-chart.sha256 regenerated and digest-verified. Criterion 4 validation: verify:helm-chart PASS (all five sub-verifiers, digest matched), verify:k8s-manifests PASS, helm template default + k3d-shakedown overlay render identically green, lint clean; blind adversarial review (Opus) PASS, zero blocking findings (coupling, derived math, first-Ready fix, sweep honesty, digest consistency and rollout-tooling timing dependencies all independently verified). REMAINING — criterion 5, LIVE k3s VALIDATION NOT YET PERFORMED: needs an observation window on the authoritative cluster showing Garden Ready=True with companions up and ZERO kubelet readiness-timeout events, confirming the flap actually stopped without weakening the health assertion. Close only after that observation. Nonblocking per #294: worst-case NotReady detection rises ~15s on the operator/admin Garden surface (bounded, documented in values.yaml, net reliability win); the fleet-disabled tcpSocket readiness branch is unreachable dead code since the chart schema mandates fleet.enabled=true (pre-existing).

Open residual — live k3s confirmation the flap stopped — satisfied 2026-07-29: carlini Garden up 30h / psfn-shard Garden up 6d12h, 0 restarts, zero probe/timeout/unhealthy kubelet events on either cluster (observation recorded in comment). Acceptance fully met.
