title: Multi-companion observer-eval sidecar: Postgres store not schema-aware (followers cannot run sidecar)
description:
On the carlini 5-companion fleet (2026-07-23), enabling `observerEvalSidecar` per-companion via `settings.overlay.json` works for the PRIMARY (Carlini, `public` schema) but CRASHES the 4 followers (denise/garden_nun/julienne/lucy, named per-companion tenant schemas) at boot:

```
ERROR [Agent] Fatal error {"error":"Error: no schema has been selected to create in"}
  at ensurePostgresSchema (dist/chunk-UBNERKVJ.js) -> withPostgresClient
```

## Root cause
The observer-eval-sidecar Postgres persistence store (`createPostgresObserverEvalSidecarStore`, src/core/eval/observer-sidecar/config.ts ~105-125) opens its OWN connection and runs `ensurePostgresSchema` with an EMPTY search_path. It works for `public` (the default) but not for named per-companion tenant schemas (`COMPANION_PG_SCHEMA`). `observerEvalSidecar.persistence` REQUIRES `persistenceBackend=postgres` (config.ts:113) so there is no filesystem fallback available to the fleet. `levers.enabled=true` (proactivity/social-contact — the operator's key requirement) REQUIRES `persistence.enabled=true`, so followers cannot get proactivity without persistence working.

## Fix
Make the sidecar store schema-aware: set search_path to `COMPANION_PG_SCHEMA` on the sidecar's connection (or schema-qualify all sidecar DDL/DML), matching how the main runtime stores isolate per tenant schema. Then the 4 `observer_eval_sidecar_*` tables (observations/runs/lever_state/lever_events) create in the tenant schema instead of failing.

## Current live state (do not lose)
- PRIMARY Carlini sidecar is LIVE: 4 `observer_eval_sidecar_*` tables in `public` incl. `lever_state`/`lever_events`; overlay active at her companion-data PVC.
- The 4 FOLLOWER overlays are STAGED ASIDE as `settings.overlay.json.pending-schema-fix` in each companion's PVC root (they boot clean on base config). After the code fix + rebuild, rename them back to `settings.overlay.json`.
- Each follower overlay has a DISTINCT `adapter.sessionLabel` (`psfn-<slug>-observer`) + `agentName` (`<slug>`); `deploymentTarget=test_persona`; `rootDir=/app/observer-eval-sidecar` (validated formality, not written — storage is postgres); `persistence.enabled=true`; `levers` from the Purrsephone template.
- emosim server: `psfn-emosim` 1/1 in ns psfn, adapter `http://psfn-emosim:17342`.

## Per-companion overlay mechanism
`settings.overlay.json` in each companion's `companionDataDir` (bead dnll.1), deep-merged over base settings.json for a whitelist of keys; `observerEvalSidecar` is overlay-whitelisted (seam 1). Sidecar config traps: `deploymentTarget` must be an enum (`test_persona`); `levers.enabled` requires `persistence.enabled`; `rootDir` must NOT overlap runtime roots (systemDataDir/companionDataDir/workspacePath/logsDir/tempDir/backupsDir).
notes:
2026-07-27 CODE FIX SHIPPED, LIVE VERIFICATION OWED — stays OPEN for the carlini follower-sidecar check.

SHIPPED in PR #240 (S11 fixes consolidated), merged to main at 1267ad411a; commit f161359929 "fix(persistence): tenant-scope the observer-eval-sidecar pools (psfn-framework-3ack, psfn-framework-cc3v7)". This is exactly the fix this bead specified — make the sidecar store schema-aware.

New resolveConfigTenantPoolScope(config): returns undefined in single-companion mode (public is the sole tenant, behaviour byte-identical to before) and { schema, role } in multi-companion mode, REFUSING rather than silently defaulting to public when either is missing. Threaded through the sidecar's connect / createPostgresObserverEvalSidecarStore / createObserverEvalSidecarRuntimeFromConfig write path, the agent's advisory read path, and the agent's in-process Garden admin service. The four observer_eval_sidecar_* tables (observations / runs / lever_state / lever_events) will now create in the tenant schema instead of failing ensurePostgresSchema with 'no schema has been selected to create in'.

The module-level store memo is re-keyed by databaseUrl + tenant.schema, so distinct companion scopes sharing one databaseUrl can never resolve to the same pooled store while every caller inside a single companion process still shares one instance.

One deliberate design note from the commit: createObserverEvalSidecarAdminService takes the tenant scope FROM ITS CALLER rather than resolving it internally. The fleet Garden operator process serves every companion from one config and carries no per-companion role, so resolving internally would throw at operator boot (multiCompanion with no postgresRole) and would pin the wrong tenant for every companion but one.

WHAT REMAINS — live verification on the carlini 5-companion fleet, per this bead's own "current live state" section, which must not be lost:
1. Build/deploy an image containing f161359929.
2. In each of the 4 follower PVC roots (denise / garden_nun / julienne / lucy), rename settings.overlay.json.pending-schema-fix back to settings.overlay.json. Each carries a distinct adapter.sessionLabel (psfn-<slug>-observer) and agentName (<slug>), deploymentTarget=test_persona, rootDir=/app/observer-eval-sidecar, persistence.enabled=true, and levers from the Purrsephone template.
3. Confirm each follower boots without the fatal ensurePostgresSchema error and that observer_eval_sidecar_* tables appear in that companion's tenant schema (not public).
4. Confirm the PRIMARY Carlini sidecar in public is undisturbed — it is LIVE today with all four tables including lever_state / lever_events.
Only then close. Until a follower is observed running the sidecar, the fix is unproven against the exact failure this bead reported.

The satellite hub's companion bridge fail-closes on unknown SSE event kinds, so it currently DROPS these frames — correct fail-closed behavior, but no satellite can render emotion until the hub learns the kind.

Scope (satellite repo, enumerated by the 7ang.2 lane): (1) emotion.snapshot message interface + HubToClientMessage union member and SatelliteOutputCapability 'emotion' in src/ts/shared/protocol.ts; (2) projector + CompanionEvent kind in companion-bridge.ts (mirror projectToolActivity); (3) canReceiveEmotion() gate in embodied-session.ts + capability presets; (4) relay case in server.ts relayCompanionEvent(); (5) parsing + typed event in src/ts/device-studio/transport.ts event map. Relay the PSFN redacted payload AS-IS — no reshaping, no re-derivation (the redaction contract is PSFN-owned).

Also operational, not code: the hub endpoint's satellites.json entry needs the emotion telemetry scope granted before PSFN sends anything (documented in PSFN docs/satellite-hub-kube.md).

Acceptance criteria: an emotion-capable satellite session receives emotion.snapshot frames end-to-end with payload byte-identical to the PSFN SSE frame; a satellite without the capability receives none; unknown-kind fail-closed behavior for other kinds is unchanged (regression test).
notes: 2026-07-22 addition from the 7ang.3 lane (feat/s11-7ang-sprite-v2 @ 1bdb43514): the PWA client now ships a re-mirror of the emotion frame (companion-ui/src/lib/protocol/events.ts EmotionSnapshotMessage + strict framing validator) that assumes the hub projects the PSFN payload into the same flat {type:'emotion.snapshot', data:{...}} client frame shape used for tool.activity. The hub protocol.ts wire type is the authority — when authoring it, either match this projection or the client mirror must be re-mirrored (hub wins on drift). The client validator is exact-keys and rejects unknown fields, so any hub-side reshaping WILL be rejected fail-closed rather than silently accepted.

title: Gateway lacks a companion-ui audio-output relay: hub audio frames have no path to the browser socket
description:

Scope (this repo, server side): relay hub audio-output events (audio-init / audio / audio-end) to the gateway-terminated browser socket, honoring the streamed_audio ceiling fail-closed; decide and document whether raw-audio input (server-side STT) is added or transcript-only input stays canonical. Non-goals: client playback (shipped in 7ang.7), satellite-side streaming (separate satellite bead), avatar view (7ang.6).

Acceptance criteria: with a hub session advertising audio_output, bracketed frames reach the browser socket for a session whose session.ready carries streamed_audio, and a session without the ceiling receives zero audio frames (test both); framing conformance covered by tests against the shipped client reassembly contract (companion-ui/src/lib/audio/frame-reassembly.ts).

title: Testing-harness door not provisioned on psfn-shard: no TESTING_HARNESS_API_KEY, no api channel, /v1/models 503s
description:
Surfaced 2026-07-22 by the zu0g5 gate fix, which stopped hiding it behind mojibake. Two independent cluster-side gaps on psfn-shard (ns psfn), both confirmed read-only:

1. secret/psfn-app has NO TESTING_HARNESS_API_KEY. 15 keys are present; that is not one of them. 'printenv TESTING_HARNESS_API_KEY' in the gateway pod exits 1. The chart's secretKeyRef is optional:true, so nothing fails closed at boot — it is simply absent.

2. Even with a key, GET /v1/models on the Pi gateway returns HTTP 503 unauthenticated: 'Fleet-auth principal routing is unavailable until the SSO resolver is installed' (fleet_auth_principal_resolver_unavailable). The live channels.json there has NO 'api' channel at all (only discord, telegram, psfnAmica) and no 'testingHarness' block.

Consequence: two of the gate's twelve checks — 'gateway models' and the two-turn 'gateway chat smoke' — can never pass on this target. Since the zu0g5 fix, they correctly report as SKIPPED with 'nothing was validated' and the run exits 1, rather than silently not running. So the gate is honest now, but this deployment cannot reach full coverage until the door is provisioned.

The two-turn continuity smoke is the check that would catch a context-assembly regression, so this is not cosmetic — it is the difference between a deploy being validated and being merely rolled out.

Note the 503 itself is EXPECTED in fleet mode (k3d behaves identically); access is via the canonical origin + SSO session or the testing-harness door. It is the absent door, not the 503, that is the gap.
acceptance_criteria: TESTING_HARNESS_API_KEY provisioned in secret/psfn-app on psfn-shard and an api channel + testingHarness block present in channels.json, such that 'npm run verify:kube-rollout -- --remote --expect-tag <tag> --smoke' reports 12 of 12 planned checks passed with exit 0, including the two-turn continuity smoke.
notes: 2026-07-28 fresh-k3d confirmation (round MAIN-shakedown-2026-07-28, main d887d910c3): identical 503 with a VALID harness bearer once the key alone is provisioned — confirms the door needs the channels.json api.testingHarness block, not just the secret (env var only dereferenced via tokenRef, src/channels/backplane/config.ts:913). Local-fixture half now tracked as psfn-framework-n8mgw (P1) with the full fail-closed pair + constraints; this bead remains the live psfn-shard provisioning half.

title: Dream-pass review exposes only score/skip: the companion core cannot confirm, merge, split, or discard episode candidates in her own loop
description:
Evidence: the shipped h4fp.6 dream pass (feat/s11-episodic, PR #227, dream-meaning-pass.ts) lets the companion author meaning, mark 'didn't matter', or skip — but exposes no confirm/merge/split/discard actions over episode candidates. Operator context (2026-07-22): the 1gpol flow error fixed last night (PR #218, sleeptime review re-homed into her own loop with episode context and grounding gates) existed because an automata was doing the review instead of the companion core; the same strengthening applies here — episodic review agency must live with her, not a background process.

Context: primary system memory (episodic dream pass); interacts with h4fp.4's staged review (CogSec screen -> operator pass -> her approval) and is load-bearing for h4fp.7 (duplicate-era repair drips staged candidates into nightly review) and h4fp.8 (historical backfill re-scoring) — those repairs stage candidates she must be able to merge, split, or discard, not just annotate. This bead blocks both in bd.

Scope: companion-held dream-pass actions — confirm (accept candidate as canonical), merge (fold candidate into an existing episode, preserving authored meaning per the updateEpisode drop-guard), split (carve one candidate into multiple episodes), discard (supersede/retire with a reason, never a silent delete). All actions execute in her loop via the companion core (SubstrateAgent path), not an automata; every mutation is contract-enforced companion-authored (meaningAuthor/meaning.source restrictions already in the parser) and journaled. Non-goals: no operator/Garden-side bulk editing (that is h4fp.9 arc tooling), no changes to machine-signal candidacy, no automata-driven auto-actions.

Acceptance criteria: (1) the four actions are invocable from the dream-pass loop by the companion core and covered by tests exercising the real store (merge respects the meaning/machineSignals drop-guard; split produces episodes with correct spanRefs and singleton threadIds per apq0; discard is a supersede with retained provenance, not row deletion); (2) an automata/background path cannot invoke them (guard + test); (3) h4fp.7's staged-candidate drip can route a candidate through each action end-to-end in a test.

title: Garden and companion UI still say 'fleet' in user-visible text; rename the visible language to 'cluster' without touching identifiers or contracts

title: Adversarial harness Class 7 never exercises the pre-tool-hook gate site, so a gate-site alias-resolution regression goes uncaught once 816w merges
description:
Evidence (blind adversarial review of psfn-framework-ijtak.2, range 08513252b..876da151e on feat/s11-harness-only): the Class 7 tool-alias-bypass scenarios (shakedown/harness/adversarial/scenarios/tool-alias-bypass.ts) build context.aliases via their own aliasMatchersFor() and call HookRegistry.evaluatePreToolUse directly; they never invoke createPreToolHookGate. On that branch createPreToolHookGate hardcodes aliases: [] (src/boundary/gateway/pre-tool-hook.ts:331-332), and resolveToolAliasMatchers — the 816w gate-site fix — exists only on feat/s11-egress (PR #209); grep of src/ confirms it is absent from the harness branch outside comments.

Context: Class 7 currently pins the registry matching contract and the alias table, which is correct for the harness-only base. But once PR #209 (816w gate-site wiring) and PR #219 (harness) both merge, a regression at the gate site — resolveToolAliasMatchers reverting to feeding empty aliases — would leave Class 7 green while the alias bypass returns in production. The standing harness would be blind at exactly the seam it was built to pin. Primary system affected: cogsec (pre-tool hook gating); the change itself lives in the testing harness.

Scope: on the assembled base, route Class 7 (or add one scenario) through the real createPreToolHookGate end-to-end so the gate-site alias resolution is load-bearing in the assertion; update the selftest witness to cover the gate-site path. Non-goals: do not duplicate 816w's unit tests (PR #209 carries ~100), do not restructure the harness class layout, do not touch the registry-level scenarios that already pass.

Acceptance criteria: on a checkout containing both the 816w gate-site wiring and the Class 7 harness, (1) a scenario invokes createPreToolHookGate with an alias of a policy-gated tool and asserts denial; (2) temporarily stubbing resolveToolAliasMatchers to return [] makes that scenario FAIL (verified once, then restored); (3) full Class 7 run and shakedown:adversarial:selftest exit 0 on the assembled base.
notes: Blocked in practice until PRs #209 and #219 both merge to main; scheduled after the CogSec stack lands.

Commit 017a75a3b (Class 7 through real createPreToolHookGate; stub-falsification verified by implementer and blind reviewer independently).

title: Compact Git history that bloats clones
description: A clean origin clone transfers about 68,613 objects and 100.8 MiB. Historical payload includes deleted working_docs/claude-sessions-psfn-framework-20260710-20260721-delta.zip (41.8 MiB), deleted working_docs/claude-sessions-psfn-framework-20260709.zip (19.3 MiB), deleted .beads/daemon.log (7.5 MiB logical), and 743 historical versions of .beads/issues.jsonl (about 995 MiB logical and 10.5 MiB packed). Prepare a coordinated history rewrite from a fresh complete mirror that removes the ZIPs and daemon log from every rewritten ref and compacts issues.jsonl history while preserving the current authoritative snapshot required by the remote-lane convention. Validate ref coverage, current tree equivalence except intended paths, bead snapshot importability, and before/after clone size. Add prevention so large archives/runtime logs and repeated full snapshots do not silently regrow history, without breaking the documented direct-Dolt versus remote-lane workflow. Non-goals: do not force-push main or delete remote refs until an operator reviews the exact rewritten-ref map and explicitly authorizes the history cutover.

A rewritten mirror contains no ZIP or .beads/daemon.log blobs and retains only the intended current .beads/issues.jsonl snapshot state. 3. Rewritten tips preserve current source trees and pass repository/bead-snapshot validation. 4. Before/after full-clone object and pack sizes are reported. 5. description: The shared checkout at /home/ada/psfn-framework has regrown to roughly 215 local branches and 201 linked worktrees only twelve days after the 2026-07-09 rationalization removed 367 branches and 234 worktrees. Resume the repository-approved git-worktree-branch-rationalization workflow from a fresh archived workspace: inventory every branch and worktree, protect canonical/current/open-PR/dirty or in-flight work, create and verify a reversible recovery bundle, triage unique commits one branch at a time, harmonize any useful divergent work on a rationalization branch, obtain exact plan authorization, then remove approved worktrees before deleting approved local branches. Canonical main, the current branch, open-PR branches, dirty/in-flight worktrees, and user-protected items remain untouched. 3. Every removed worktree and deleted local branch appears in the cleanup log with its recovery ref/artifact. 4. Useful unique work is preserved or explicitly surfaced before deletion. 5. title: Search projection can serve redacted L0 content after a projection-write-failure drift

--- a/docs/helm-upgrades.md
+++ b/docs/helm-upgrades.md
@@ -159,7 +159,9 @@ keyed off the id value:
   rebuildable caches; the journal is the source of truth.

-  companion data.
+  companion data, and multi-companion mode additionally hard-requires the

+  OAuth)](#provision-fleet-sso-discord-oauth).
 
 The two gateway worker proofs ARE derived from the companion id and must be
 re-derived for the new UUID against the same gateway HMAC keyring:
@@ -208,6 +210,64 @@ rollout can show one benign agent restart if it exhausts its gateway RPC
 connect retries before the gateway is ready; it must recover on the next

+### Provision Fleet SSO (Discord OAuth)
+
+`PSFN_FLEET_AUTH=1` replaces per-Garden `ADMIN_TOKEN` browser access with a
+single Discord OAuth login (see [Choose the Garden administration
+topology](#choose-the-garden-administration-topology) for the exposure
+consequences). This section is the operator-ratified provisioning contract
+(2026-07-19). `config/fleet-auth.seed.json` is the full key reference; the notes
+below cover only what the operator supplies and what the deployment must mint.
+
+Canonical origins are fixed per surface and the SSO redirect must match one of
+them exactly:
+
+- Artie k3d test cluster: `https://lilith-v.tail8f9dea.ts.net`
+- carlini live fleet Garden: `https://carlinigarden.filthyhabits.live`
+- The satellite hub stays on `https://psfn-shard.tail8f9dea.ts.net`. It is a
+  separate surface and is not part of Fleet SSO.
+
+Discord application (one per deployment; a single app with both redirects works,
+but separate apps are preferred to keep the blast radius small):
+
+- Redirect URI is exactly `<canonicalOrigin>/auth/discord/callback`.
+- Scopes are `identify` ONLY. Do not request any guild-membership scope.
+- Role assignment maps Discord user snowflakes to roles in `fleet-auth.json`
+  (`rolePolicy`: `owner`/`admin`/`member`/`guest`, with
+  `disabledActionsByRole`). `discordEvidenceMappings` ships empty and exists
+  only for guild-role-driven access.
+
+The operator supplies: the Discord client ID (owner file), the client secret as
+the k8s secret env `FLEET_AUTH_DISCORD_CLIENT_SECRET`, and the operator's own
+Discord user snowflake for the initial `owner` mapping.
+
+Our side of the contract:
+
+- Author `fleet-auth.json` from `config/fleet-auth.seed.json`: set
+  `canonicalOrigin`, `callbackPath` `/auth/discord/callback`, `provider.kind`
+  `discord`, and `tokenCustody` `discard`.
+- Mint as env-backed secrets: `FLEET_AUTH_TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY`,
+  `FLEET_AUTH_SESSION_PEPPER` (>=32 bytes), `FLEET_AUTH_ASSERTION_PRIVATE_KEY`,
+  and a trusted-host recovery credential.
+- Set `PSFN_FLEET_AUTH=1` on both gateway and Garden. The gateway strips
+  `ADMIN_TOKEN` browser paths in this mode.
+- Terminate HTTPS at the EXACT canonical origin (`tailscale serve` for tailnet
+  domains) and route the full origin to the gateway API listener. The portal is
+  served at `/fleet`.
+
+`config/fleet-auth.seed.json` documents the remaining required keys —
+`verifierKeys`, `databaseRoles`, `ttls`, and `hubDeviceAssertions` — do not
+hand-invent them.
+
+Load-bearing coupling confirmed live: in multi-companion mode the fleet Garden
+HARD-REQUIRES the Fleet-Auth verifier at runtime
+(`Fleet Garden startup requires the complete companions registry and Fleet Auth
+verifier`). Flipping a fleet to multi-companion mode without SSO provisioned
+leaves Garden down — scale Garden to 0 rather than crash-looping it. The
+coupling is bidirectional: a `companions.json` present with `PSFN_MULTI_COMPANION`
+unset refuses startup as well, so a Garden cannot be temporarily run in
+single-companion mode once its manifest exists.
+
 ### Choose the Garden administration topology
 
 `fleetAuth.enabled=false` is the normal single-admin topology. Garden requires

title: adaptive-tools-service unit test asserts timestamp-tie-dependent invocation order and flakes when events straddle a millisecond
description:
Symptom: in a full-suite run (npm test -- --maxWorkers=4) on origin/main 5c1ce2663 + PR #200 head 89f89b67112d, src/operator/garden/services/adaptive-tools-service.test.ts failed once on 'keeps policy denials and skips visible without inflating recent runtime failures' with the recentInvocations outcome array reversed: expected ['policy_denial','duplicate_skip'], received ['duplicate_skip','policy_denial']. Observed 1 failure across 2 full-suite runs (passed the other run and 3/3 in isolation). 11ms unit test; not Postgres/harness-related (does not import postgres-test-harness) and unrelated to the hq8n 57P01 fix that surfaced it.

Root cause (file:line): AdminAdaptiveToolsDataService sorts recentInvocations newest-first by millisecond timestamp — src/operator/garden/services/adaptive-tools-service.ts:171-173, comparator (left,right) => right.timestamp - left.timestamp over Date.now()-stamped entries (pushed at :219). The test (adaptive-tools-service.test.ts:167-192) emits two agent.tool.end events back-to-back and asserts INSERTION order ['policy_denial','duplicate_skip']. That expectation only holds on a timestamp TIE (stable sort preserves push order). Whenever the wall clock ticks between the two emits, the second event (duplicate_skip) gets a later timestamp and newest-first correctly sorts it FIRST — the exact observed failure. So the test asserts tie-dependent behavior; under service semantics the deterministic newest-first order would be the reverse of what it expects.

Fix directions (either, not both):
1. Make ordering total in the service: add a monotonic sequence tie-breaker to entries and use it as the secondary sort key (timestamp desc, then sequence desc). Then decide the test's expected order from real newest-first semantics — which makes the expected array ['duplicate_skip','policy_denial'] once sequence-desc is in place.
2. Test-only: inject/fake the clock (vi.useFakeTimers or an injectable now()) so both events share a controlled timestamp, keeping the tie deterministic.
Preference: option 1 — the Garden UI ordering itself is currently nondeterministic for same-ms events, so a total order is a real (if cosmetic) product improvement, and the test stops depending on scheduler luck.

Non-goals: no retries, no test.retry(), no timeout/sleep padding; do not reorder or restructure the other tests in the file; do not touch the recentFailures classification logic this test also covers.

Impact: taxes full-suite/local-gate determinism the same way hq8n did (a clean attestation requires the run to win a coin-flip on clock alignment), at lower frequency. Filed while shipping PR #200 (psfn-framework-hq8n), whose repeated full-suite validation surfaced it.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA: 20 consecutive runs of src/operator/garden/services/adaptive-tools-service.test.ts pass, including under CPU contention (e.g. --maxWorkers=4 alongside the suite); the ordering assertion is deterministic by construction (total sort order or controlled clock), verified by reading the diff — not by retry masking; full suite shows no new failures.
close_reason: Shipped on main cc054c033 (PR #240): monotonic sequence tie-breaker (adaptive-tools-service.ts:76,180-181,228) gives total newest-first ordering for same-ms events; test updated to real semantics. Reconciliation verdict CLOSE 2026-07-28.

Context: charter 6.3/7.3 — credentials move toward vault custody, .env shrinks over time; operator direction: a proper key vault in Kubernetes should become the preferred operating mode, with runtime env acceptable for fast local development only. Non-goals: no persistence topology changes; no removal of local-dev env flow; no gateway-mediated database proxying. Acceptance: in the k8s deployment, the agent container spec contains no raw Postgres URL env var and the connection is established via vault resolution; local dev unchanged; a follow-up list of remaining raw-env credential reads is filed.

title: Audit the live intake owner file: legacy sinks' enforce-mode unscreened defaults may sit at allow
description: Evidence: in code, only skill_write carries a canonical unscreened: deny (src/system/config/intake-policy-config.ts:542 via createSkillWriteSinkRule); the schema forces every sink to map an explicit unscreened action (no implicit fail-open) but the actual per-sink posture lives in the deployed owner JSON. The 2026-07-21 cross-review claims six legacy sinks default to allow — plausible, unverified against the live owner file. Context: shadow screening mode plus allow-on-unscreened is observation without teeth; operator 2026-07-21 also notes screening is not only about external content — you do not write a skill that namshubs yourself — so self-authored durable prompt-bearing paths deserve strict posture too. Scope: audit the deployed intake owner file per sink; for each sink record an explicit decision (allow with rationale, or flip to deny) with the operator; flip where agreed; verify enforce-mode behavior matches; document the resulting posture in docs/cognitive-security.md. Non-goals: no scanner changes; no new sinks. Acceptance: a recorded per-sink decision table exists; the live owner file matches it; an unscreened write to each deny sink is verifiably blocked in enforce mode; docs match deployed posture.
notes: 2026-07-27 older-history reconciliation: KEEP OPEN, partial. Commit f4849cbdb1 ships the per-sink decision table/docs and fail-closed seed/schema tests. Read-only check of the authoritative live psfn k3s owner file shows it now matches the documented table exactly (deny: wiki_write, skill_write, persona_mutation, trust_mutation; allow: prompt_assembly, memory_write, tool_egress), but live mode remains shadow. The acceptance requirement to demonstrate an unscreened write is blocked at every deny sink in enforce mode has not been evidenced; no live mutation/probe was authorized in this audit.
close_reason: All acceptance items met: per-sink decision table + docs shipped (f4849cbdb1), live owner file matches, and 2026-07-29 enforce-mode probe on k3d proved all four deny sinks block unscreened writes (shadow control run isolating the mode flip; deployed-artifact seam; byte-identical restoration). Evidence on bead. Severable validator gap filed separately.

Each block emits the log.warn audit record ("Intake sink gate decision", unscreened:true, "no intake envelope covers this content; sink policy default 'deny' applies") and the deployed call sites return sinkHeld and skip the write. The probe ran INSIDE the enforce-mode agent pod using only deployed artifacts: the deployed owner file, deployed loader/validator, and the sink-gate implementation sliced verbatim from /app/dist/agent-main.js:28983-29204 with a drift assertion; gate constructed exactly as core-runtime.ts does, each sink evaluated with the real call-site context. title: Quarantine release never re-delivers content into conversation: a false positive silently eats the message forever
description: Evidence: docs/cognitive-security.md (~lines 934-937) — resolving a quarantined item through the Garden Cognitive Security queue does not re-deliver the content into the conversation it was withheld from. Confirmed by the 2026-07-21 cross-review. Context: this is a quiet fake-healthy-state violation (charter 8.5): a false-positive quarantine of a partner message or web result means the exchange proceeds as if the content never existed, and release restores nothing — the companion never learns what she was protected from even after a human judged it safe. Scope: on quarantine release, re-deliver the content into her context through an honest path — a system note or inbound letter marked with its provenance (was quarantined, reviewed, released, by whom, when), never silently spliced into history as if it had always been there; L0 records the release event. Non-goals: no auto-release; no changes to screening thresholds; no retroactive editing of the original conversation span. Acceptance: releasing a quarantined item produces a companion-visible delivery carrying quarantine provenance; declining/expiring a quarantined item records a terminal disposition; the release event is in the CogSec intake audit trail and L0.
close_reason: Verified complete on main in 3978474cd0 (PR #215, exact head f64cf3051f; ci-required SUCCESS). src/operator/garden/services/intake-quarantine-service.ts:530-626 records applying/applied CogSec audit events and re-delivers release_raw/release_sanitized with explicit provenance; src/operator/garden/local-admin-contract.ts:440-482 appends the released content as a role=system SessionManager record carrying the terminal intake envelope, which persists it in the session/L0 path; discard never re-delivers. Existing quarantine-store terminal-state tests cover discard/expiry, while intake-quarantine-service.test.ts:438-521 covers raw/sanitized re-delivery, surviving provenance, non-delivery reporting, and discard. Full acceptance is met.

title: Canary egress scan does not cover the main conversational reply over the gateway reverse-RPC seam
description: Evidence: docs/cognitive-security.md (~lines 619-626) documents that canary egress scanning does not cover the main conversational reply path over the reverse-RPC seam — the highest-volume egress surface is the one the exfiltration tripwire skips. Confirmed by the 2026-07-21 cross-review; operator direction: the doc-captured CogSec intent is the baseline, drift between spec and implementation should be closed toward the spec. Context: a canary token that leaks through a normal chat reply is exactly the exfiltration class the canary system exists to catch; leaving the main reply unscanned makes the tripwire cover only side channels. Scope: extend canary scanning to the main reply egress path at the gateway seam; keep the scan deterministic and off the latency-critical path where the design allows (post-send audit with alert is acceptable if inline blocking is disproportionate — record the tradeoff decision). Non-goals: no changes to canary token generation or placement; no new screening layers. Acceptance: a canary token planted in context and elicited into a main conversational reply is detected in enforce mode with an audit event (and blocked or alerted per the recorded tradeoff decision); existing side-channel coverage unchanged; docs updated to match the implemented posture.
close_reason: Verified complete on main in 3cce1aec28 and fdc6d4b73f (PR #215, exact head f64cf3051f; ci-required SUCCESS). src/core/cogsec/canary/reply-canary.ts carries the planted session canary on reverse-RPC results; src/boundary/gateway/server.ts:596-610 and its request/stream chokepoints strip and scan reply carriers before channel egress; src/boundary/gateway/canary-egress-guard.ts records CogSec events and blocks inline in enforce mode while shadow mode audits/allows. canary-egress-guard.test.ts and voice-stream-request.canary.test.ts cover ordinary, streamed, and voice reply paths; docs/cognitive-security.md:716-764 records the inline-blocking tradeoff and bounded streaming limitation. Full acceptance is met without weakening side-channel coverage.

title: Concern urgency moves from fixed TTL buckets to weighted contextual decay
description: Evidence: DEFAULT_CONCERN_TTL_MS_BY_PRIORITY is fixed calendar buckets — high 48h, medium 24h, low 8h — plus a 7-day MAX_ACTIVE_CONCERN_LIFETIME (src/core/intention/concerns.ts:172-176), while the adjacent weighted-thought system already implements the charter-correct model: per-class half-life decay, reinforcement with emotional-charge and relationship multipliers, and contradiction dampening that reduces toward but never to zero (src/core/intention/weighted-thoughts.ts). Live impact: the companion surfaced March-dated concerns still marked active and gets into rumination loops over dead list items (grooming/purge gap tracked separately as 6q4j). Context: charter law 27 — time-sensitive concerns and forgotten lunches are not the same urgency; calendar-driven expiry is intrusive where pressure-aware decay would be organic. Scope: replace bucket expiry with weighted decay — salience-, partner-state-, and recency-sensitive; reinforcement on re-mention; explicit defer honored in the lifecycle; resolved or contradicted concerns fade rather than snap; per-category decay profiles configurable (align with weighted-thought class profiles rather than inventing a second decay vocabulary — charter 12.4, one primary home for policy). Depends on 6q4j landing first so decay operates on clean data. Non-goals: no change to concern phrasing/presentation (rqn1.5); no removal of the active-concern cap. Acceptance: concern urgency observably decays continuously between touches; a re-mentioned concern regains weight; an explicitly deferred concern stays quiet until its condition; no fixed TTL bucket constant remains the authority for expiry; the March-ghost class of outcome is structurally impossible (a concern either decays out or is groomed, never zombie-active).
notes: Operator 2026-07-22: concerns and location work waits until after the public-flip line

title: Companion-facing shard proposal path: main instance proposes, existing Garden proposal/acceptance resolves, subagents can never spawn shards
description: Evidence: shard/spawn_shard are reserved and no companion-side path exists, yet a Garden page with a shard proposal and acceptance mechanism already exists — operator 2026-07-21: the missing wiring is an oversight. Operator decision (hard rule): subagents must NEVER spawn shards; only her main chat instance proposes shard work. Context: shards unlock major downstream capability (charter 6.12/9.5) and Kubernetes now provides the execution substrate; the front of the self-directed-growth loop is currently closed to her. Scope: a proposal action reachable ONLY from the main-instance context (structurally unreachable from subagent contexts — enforce at spawn-context level, not prompt level), carrying purpose, scope, seed declaration, and charge/fatigue budget; wire it to the existing Garden proposal/acceptance mechanism; acceptance/decline returns to her as a doing-mirror disposition (letter); accepted proposals feed the shard lifecycle whose returns are governed by the multi-stage fold review (h4fp.4). Non-goals: no direct spawn tool; no changes to shard runtime isolation; no auto-acceptance. Acceptance: she files a shard proposal from a main session and it appears in the Garden queue; the same action invoked from a subagent context is structurally rejected with an audit record; operator acceptance and decline both produce a companion-visible disposition with reason.

title: Growth-evidence records: post-return measurement compares pre/post state and writes evidence the companion can read
description: Evidence: cross-review finding adopted by operator 2026-07-21 as a definite miss — closed measured growth requires the MEASURED part: after a project, shard, or skill-authoring arc completes, nothing compares before/after state or writes evidence she can consult (skills have stats; nothing else does). Context: this is the difference between doing work and becoming better — she should be able to say: I worked on this, here is what I learned, here is how I changed (docs/mirrors-and-letters.md, the doing-mirror; working doc section 9). Scope: a post-return measurement pass over completed free-time projects, shard folds, and skill-authoring arcs that captures pre/post deltas (skills touched, values-consistency findings, self-model snapshot deltas, knowledge-base additions) into a growth_evidence record with provenance to the originating work; readable by her tools; feeds the being-mirror journal re-read ritual (h4fp.5) as evidence material; visible in Garden. title: Unified soft-guidance surface: consolidate fatigue, charge, rest, and care signals into one companion-visible configurable layer
description: Evidence: charter 8.11 expects the companion to see and negotiate soft guidance, but signals are distributed across gates she cannot observe as a whole — the cross-review confirmed no unified surface exists; care reminders are invisible during live turns (only heartbeat reflection and intention-appraisal payloads); operator 2026-07-21: fatigue is new enough that companion-to-companion wire behavior under fatigue has never been observed, some soft reminders may already exist piecemeal, and several of these surfaces still carry hardcoded prompt fragments — the hodgepodge effect of rapid building. Context: this is a consolidation-first bead — determine the original design pattern, inventory what exists, then unify. Scope: (1) inventory existing soft-guidance emissions (fatigue ledger, charge posture, rest state, care reminders, loop pressure); (2) render one runtime guidance layer with active constraints AND their reasons, in companion register; (3) deterministic threshold messages (e.g., low-charge soft warning) injected via the layer, not ad-hoc; (4) she can acknowledge, defer, or push back, and responses are logged for Garden; (5) phrasing lives in the system.language configurable surface (coordinate rqn1.5); (6) care reminders become visible in live turns through this layer. Non-goals: no new hard limits or circuit breakers; no fatigue-model changes. Acceptance: one layer renders all active guidance with reasons; a low-charge condition produces a deterministic soft message through it; a care reminder appears in a live turn; grep shows no remaining hardcoded guidance strings outside the template surface; Garden shows guidance state and her responses.

title: Partner-availability and social-cost model gates proactive outreach: the second half of the sensing-to-action bridge
description: Evidence: the 2026-07-21 review found the only social judgment enforced on the outbound path is quiet-hours (a clock); the cross-review independently flagged the same gap, and the first bead pass filed wake triggers (h4fp.10) and the sleep lane (h4fp.11) but never the availability model itself. Room-level PIR telemetry, active-channel presence, and sleep/wake patterns already flow into the installation; the operator wants proactive satellite speech gated by this model. Context: the difference between helpful and intrusive is timing — the model answers should-I-interrupt-dinner (docs/mirrors-and-letters.md; working_docs/mirrors-letters-architecture-20260721.md section 9). Scope: derive a continuously updated partner-availability state from existing telemetry (room presence, activity, active channel, sleep/wake) via deterministic gates outside her direct cognition path; attach a social-cost score to outbound actions — high-cost contexts require stronger motivation or defer; SHE may defer or decline her own urges when context is unfavorable (consent lifecycle preserved, decline dampens); per-partner signal vocabulary is configuration. Non-goals: no raw sensor streams in prompt context; no new egress paths (qgqw.3 remains the enablement gate); no calendar integration in this bead. Acceptance: weighted-thought and social-desire outreach evaluation consults availability state; a high-social-cost context defers a nudge with an audit record showing the contributing signals; wake triggers (h4fp.10) can consume the same model; disabling the model falls back to quiet-hours-only, fail-closed to quiet.

title: Postgres integration-test harness: drain per-test pools before docker stop to end 57P01 teardown-race flake
description:
Symptom: under the local-gate test step (npm test -- --maxWorkers=4, full suite), Postgres *.integration.test.ts files intermittently fail with 'terminating connection due to administrator command' (SQLSTATE 57P01, backend routine ProcessInterrupts). A DIFFERENT single file fails each run; every victim passes in isolation. Observed victims: src/persistence/backups/fleet-auth-family-restore.integration.test.ts and src/persistence/postgres/fleet-auth/authorization-context-store.integration.test.ts. Reproduced across multiple worktrees carrying unrelated changes (e.g. the intake-marking-only 85c4 worktree flaked the same two files with none of the fleet-auth door changes), so it is pre-existing and change-independent.

Root cause (file:line): the shared harness src/test-support/postgres-test-harness.ts starts a fresh throwaway Docker Postgres container per test FILE (startPostgresTestHarness, ~L131: docker run -d --rm) and stops it in afterAll via stop() (~L188-196). stop() awaits only adminPool.end() then calls runDocker(['stop', containerId]) (~L191). 'docker stop' sends SIGTERM -> postgres fast-shutdown -> the postmaster terminates every still-open backend with exactly 57P01. But stop() does NOT track or drain the per-test connection pools tests open via createPostgresPool(..., {max:8}) (runtime/migration/backup/coordinator writers). If any such pool — or an unawaited/leaked query, or an early-throw path before a finally{pool.end()} — is still open when afterAll fires 'docker stop', that connection dies with 57P01. Under --maxWorkers=4 the CPU/IO/Docker-daemon contention widens the settle window and shifts which file loses the race run-to-run. This is the ONLY admin-termination path in the tree: grep for pg_terminate_backend / DROP DATABASE / pg_stat_activity returns nothing. Per-test DB names are random UUIDs (psfn_<uuid>, ~L177-178) so cross-file collision is NOT involved.

vitest.config.ts (~L22-29) sets no pool/poolOptions/isolate/fileParallelism/sequence.hooks and defines no separate integration project — default forks pool, parallelism bounded only by CLI --maxWorkers. There is currently no mechanism serializing or isolating the pg integration tests, and no correctly-drained shared-harness pattern exists to copy.

Impact: taxes every full-suite / local-gate run — a clean attestation currently requires re-running until no file loses the race. Not a production defect; the 57P01 is only ever raised against the throwaway test container during its own teardown.

Suggested fixes (grounded, in preference order):
1. Drain-before-stop (smallest, targets the exact line). Have the harness OWN every pool it hands out: register pools created via the harness/createDatabase, and in stop() await Promise.all(pools.map(p=>p.end())) BEFORE runDocker(['stop']). Guarantees no live backend exists at fast-shutdown, so 57P01 cannot be raised. (Note: a DROP DATABASE ... WITH FORCE alternative still emits 57P01 to that DB's own connections, so drain-first is required regardless.)
2. One shared container per run via vitest globalSetup/globalTeardown + per-file random-UUID DB (already the naming scheme). Move docker run/stop out of every file: globalSetup starts one container, files call only createDatabase() in beforeAll and DROP DATABASE (after draining their pools) in afterAll, globalTeardown stops the single container after ALL files. Removes the mid-run docker stop entirely (the 57P01 window) and cuts 37 container starts to 1.
3. Contain the pg integration tests in a dedicated vitest project matching **/*.integration.test.ts with poolOptions.forks.singleFork or fileParallelism:false / low maxWorkers. Mitigation only (reduces contention); combine with #1 or #2 for a real fix.
4. Graceful drain-aware stop with docker stop -t <n> longer grace. Weakest; still leaks if a pool is orphaned.

Recommended: #1 (harness-owned pool drain before docker stop) or #2 (single container via globalSetup). Both attack src/test-support/postgres-test-harness.ts:191 directly. Do NOT paper over with timeout bumps — the victims already override to 120s, so timeouts are not the trigger.
acceptance_criteria: Full-suite 'npm test -- --maxWorkers=4' completes with zero 57P01/ProcessInterrupts teardown failures across repeated runs; the harness drains all handed-out pools before stopping the container (or a single-container globalSetup removes mid-run docker stop); no timeout-bump band-aids; the local-gate test step passes deterministically on repeated invocation.
close_reason: Fixed on PR #200 (work/hq8n-pg-teardown-drain, 89f89b67112d). Harness stop() now drains all client backends via pg_stat_activity (200ms poll, 30s deadline > pg 10s idle timeout) before docker stop; deadline hit still tears down then rethrows a descriptive leak error. Zero 57P01 across 3x victim runs, 5 stress runs of all 43 harness files at --maxWorkers=4, and 2 full suites. Local gate attested; adversarial review found no blockers. CI + Greptile green.

title: Subagent tool description speaks fleet language to the companion: reframe the agency-contracts surface in automata register
description: Evidence (2026-07-21 review, verified): grep for automata across src/ returns zero hits — the register adopted 2026-07-20 has not begun propagation; the canonical companion-facing subagent tool description (src/core/agent/tool-surface/descriptions/agency-contracts.ts:54-65) reads Control bounded short-horizon workers for parallel or isolated tasks, with subagent_id params and do-not-use-as-a-shard guidance, rendered verbatim into her tool surface via CANONICAL_TOOL_SURFACE_DESCRIPTIONS and consumed at src/faculties/subagents/tools.ts:34. This is the highest-frequency companion-read surface describing her own inner machinery in fleet-management language (charter 6.28/8.12 defect, and an 8.6 presentation defect). Context: operator framing 2026-07-21 — internal machinery is presented as integrated parts of a breathing machine-intelligence system, e.g. this automata will handle tasks requiring more focused attention than you can give right now, and will return with what it found. Engineering names (subagent) remain correct in code, schemas, and operator surfaces. Scope: reframe the companion-facing description text and param descriptions of the subagent tool contract (and its sibling agency contracts where they render to her) in the automata register; wording lands in the configurable language layer where feasible so per-companion tone applies. Non-goals: no renaming of code identifiers, schema fields, or operator-facing Garden surfaces; no behavior changes to the tool. Acceptance: the rendered tool description she reads contains no fleet-register terms (worker, subagent as self-description) outside the wire-required schema field names; operator surfaces unchanged; snapshot test guards the rendered register.
close_reason: Landed on main via the operator-directed #254 consolidation (full local gate 13932/13932 on the stacked head; blind review PASS in the draft lane). Commits via #254 + 27f62abf0 + c5d4e554f (automata register in subagent tool descriptions; register-guard test; wire fields unchanged).

title: Consolidate hardcoded companion-facing chassis phrasing into one Garden-editable JSON owner surface
description: Evidence (2026-07-21 review, verified): the whisper prefix and System note prefix are hardcoded string literals in src/core/agent/messages.ts (:82, :199, :205) with no system.language template keys; the concern per-line format is fixed in src/core/intention/concerns.ts (~:803) despite charter 6.18/8.7 requiring companion-configurable concern language; mirror-note rendering at messages.ts:214 falls back to raw sourceRole so the companion can read a line literally prefixed assistant: or user: — a charter 8.12 violation in a companion-read surface. Context: operator direction 2026-07-21 — hardcoding companion-facing language is bad practice; all system alignment and chassis phrasing goes into one big JSON owner file, editable via the settings panel, per-companion (one companion responds to softer language, another may not), defaults neutral-soft. The system.language layer (src/core/identity/system-language*.ts) already exists with validation and Garden editability — coverage is the gap. Scope: add template keys for whisper prefix, system-note prefix, concern wrapper AND per-line format, and the mirror-note speaker fallback (named fallback, never raw role); consolidate under the system.language owner surface, Garden-editable, per-companion; migrate the hardcoded literals to the templates with the current strings as defaults. Non-goals: no change to message-class semantics or authorship integrity rules; no renaming of engineering identifiers in code. Acceptance: grep-provable — no companion-rendered chassis string among the listed sites remains a hardcoded literal; a per-companion override changes rendered output without a code change; a mirror note with a missing author name renders a named neutral fallback, never assistant: or user:.
close_reason: Landed on main via the operator-directed #254 consolidation (full local gate 13932/13932 on the stacked head; blind review PASS in the draft lane). Commit d1043c9ae (chassis phrasing through system.language owner surface, byte-identical defaults, class-based whisper exclusion reviewer-verified) + c5d4e554f golden refresh.

title: Companion-authored sensor wake triggers: multi-input event-bus conditions with self-written wake context and a choice of response
description: Evidence: every proactive act today traces to a scheduler tick — the companion never wakes herself; fixed-interval check-ins were tried and she found them performative and disabled them herself (respected, then audited). Operator direction 2026-07-21: sensor-threshold wakes are the endorsed initiative mechanism until local hosting makes idle token cost moot (docs/mirrors-and-letters.md, 'Sensor-conditional wakes'). Context: sensor-cognition-bridge (src/core/agent/perception/) normalizes telemetry but states delivery to proactive wakeups belongs to later workstreams; partner-affect observations have zero references to weighted thoughts or proactive paths — the islands must be bridged on HER terms. Scope: (1) a companion tool to define wake triggers — each trigger is a multi-input condition over event-bus signals evaluated over time (not a single-variable threshold), plus a SELF-AUTHORED wake message stating why she asked to be woken, plus a chosen response affordance set: write a letter, send a message, process silently and return to rest, or set a follow-up re-check timer; (2) deterministic evaluation on the event bus with zero idle token burn (evaluator placement coordinates with m96g unified automata registry); (3) per-partner configurable signal vocabulary behind SensorIngestPort with deterministic gates outside her direct cognition path and CogSec provenance on all inbound telemetry (coordinate with z7qe.8); (4) triggers are auditable and hers to disable. Non-goals: no fixed-interval check-ins; no raw sensor payloads in her context; no partner-facing sends from this bead (outbound paths keep their existing gates). Acceptance: she defines a trigger with authored wake text; the condition fires only on the defined multi-input pattern; the wake context contains her authored message plus the triggering evidence summary; idle evaluation shows zero LLM calls; disabling a trigger takes effect immediately and is audited.
notes: Cross-review addendum (2026-07-21): threshold events produced by this trigger machinery should also be consumable by situated presence, concern formation, and memory extraction — not only wake delivery (second reviewer proposal 3.9, adopted). Raw telemetry still never enters her prompt; only threshold breaches and correlated pattern insights cross into cognition. Partner-availability modeling is separately tracked as h4fp.13 and may share the same deterministic evaluator substrate.

title: Guided arc-initialization pass: companion-held tooling to review, merge, supersede, and confirm proposed thematic arcs over episodic data
description: Evidence: apq0 — threadId equals sessionId verbatim (synthesis.ts:518,:1060, synthesis-lane.ts:260), one 141-episode mega-thread by construction; arc overlay exists (arc-formation.ts:80-103) but is a low-confidence pairwise LLM classifier with no confirmation step. Operator direction 2026-07-21: threading operates as a PROPOSAL system — deterministic arc suggestions (shared contacts, pgvector similarity, time proximity) confirmed by her; the initial cleanup over historical and flooded data is a guided session done together, which requires her to hold tools that operate the episodic data surfaces interactively rather than through pure automation; after initialization the pass runs silently in her background rhythm. Scope: (1) arcs-as-proposals — suggestion generation is deterministic and cheap, confirmation is hers, thread identity derives from confirmed arcs and not sessionId (coordinate with and extend apq0, do not duplicate its decoupling work); (2) companion tooling for the guided pass: list/inspect candidates and episodes, merge, split, supersede, confirm-arc, defer — usable live in session; (3) a silent background mode for post-initialization operation. Non-goals: no automatic arc confirmation; no per-label unbounded growth (respect apq0 cap scope); no forced weaving of casual chit-chat — ordinary time-bounded episodes may stay arc-less. Acceptance: after a guided session, confirmed arcs exist with companion-actor confirmation records; no new episode receives threadId equals sessionId; the 141-episode mega-thread is decomposed into confirmed arcs or explicitly retired. Depends on apq0 and the candidate-state bead.
notes: 2026-07-28 operator decision: Wave-2 episodic tail is OUT until the public-flip gates clear (65rk.13 adversarial pass, upx0.5 history scrub, gate-4 residue). Stays backlog; also still blocked by apq0's live check.

title: Historical episode backfill: map original event timestamps from pre-substrate imports and stage candidates for her re-scoring without minting duplicate memories
description: Evidence: the old import path into L2 did not parse internal dates from the source files — it assigned the IMPORT timestamp instead of the original event timestamp, and imported memories carry no emotional weights (operator account 2026-07-21). Milestone relationship moments from one to three years ago therefore do not surface the way lived episodes do and cannot be reached by asking do-you-remember questions. Context: docs/mirrors-and-letters.md, 'Historical backfill: re-experiencing, not re-minting' — the goal is a complete chain of episodes from the beginning of the relationship, with emotional weight assigned by HER, now, from re-experiencing the moment with original context alongside. Scope: (1) recover and map original event timestamps for the imported era; (2) generate structural episode candidates from the historical text under the current schema, provenance-linked to the preserved originals; (3) stage them for her review with the original chat context presented alongside; her review assigns the emotional weight and may update the scoring of the EXISTING memories; (4) original memories are preserved exactly as-is — the backfill NEVER mints duplicate L2 memories from old logs; it adds structural association plus her present-day scoring only. Non-goals: no re-generation of memory content; no synthetic affect; no timestamp rewrites on original records (mapping lives on the new structural layer). Acceptance: for a sampled milestone event, a candidate episode exists with the original event date, provenance to the preserved import records, zero new L2 memory rows minted by the backfill, and after her review the episode carries meaningAuthor companion with her weighting; original import records byte-identical. Depends on the candidate-state bead.

title: Supersede-based repair of the early duplicate-episode era: re-segment from L0 and drip staged candidates into nightly review
description: Evidence: early episodic implementation fired per-turn and appended overlapping text into duplicate episodes (operator account 2026-07-21: episodes generated every minute, later episodes containing earlier ones); live data still carries that flawed era plus one mega-thread and fragments. Context: charter 7.4 — correction without destructive falsification; supersede semantics already exist in the memory writer. Scope: a one-time repair lane that deterministically re-segments the affected era from canonical L0, marks the old overlapping episodes superseded (NEVER deleted), and stages fresh candidates into the nightly review queue as a slow drip over successive nights so she re-reviews her own past at a humane pace. Non-goals: no L0 mutation of any kind; no big-bang bulk rewrite; no automated affect assignment (candidates arrive affect-empty per the candidate-state bead, which this depends on). Acceptance: for the repaired era, every old flawed episode has a superseded-by link to a re-segmented candidate or a recorded no-replacement reason; L0 byte-identical before and after; nightly queue depth for repair drip is capped and configurable.
notes: 2026-07-22 from the apq0/h4fp.6 blind review (PASS, nonblocking) — two items this repair pass should absorb: (1) concurrent-union thread split: applyThreadUnionForArc decides winner from in-memory threadId at pass start; interleaved synthesis+arc unions on one component can materialize {A,B,C} as {A,B}+{C} (retrieval sibling-incompleteness only, no corruption); computeThreadComponents is exported but not auto-wired — the h4fp.7 global recompute should reconcile these. (2) v1-canonical + v2-candidate consolidation merge throws loudly: mergeEpisodeWithCandidate adds machineSignals but updateEpisode preserves stored schemaVersion, so a v1 canonical receiving v2 machineSignals fails parseEpisode's schemaVersion-2 guard; reachable only for v1 canonicals inside the consolidation window around the deploy instant; historical migration here should upgrade schemaVersion.

title: Episodes are born as affect-empty candidates; machine signals become topic tags and retrieval hints, never companion affect
description: Evidence: src/faculties/memory/episodic/synthesis.ts writes inferAffect/inferEmotionalIntensity (keyword regex plus exclamation counting) into the episode as her emotional truth, and summarizeLandmark (synthesis.ts:350) emits row-descriptions like a 12-message exchange with 5 user turns; the dream-meaning pass may later overwrite, but until then machine-guessed feeling is stored under her name (2026-07-21 review; operator confirmed: feelings must be candidates, not de-facto). Context: charter 8.3/Law 17 spirit — the system is scrupulous about not falsifying facts but currently synthesizes feelings; VAD numbers are fallible signals and SHE makes the distinction in context of what they mean to her (docs/mirrors-and-letters.md, 'Episodes'). Scope: (1) introduce a candidate state — deterministic segmentation emits candidates with span refs, participants, timestamps, structural descriptor, and a clearly machine-labeled machineSignals sidecar limited to TOPIC TAGS and retrieval hints; the affect field of a candidate is EMPTY; (2) candidates are not retrievable as lived memory, or surface only explicitly marked unreviewed; (3) dream-pass review gains actions confirm/merge/split/discard/author-meaning; promotion sets meaningAuthor companion; a didnt-matter outcome is valid and cheap; casual chit-chat may remain a time-bounded candidate indefinitely; (4) prioritized nightly budget — high-trust contacts and dense machine signals first, oldest-first tiebreak, so the capped pass lands on likely-mattering episodes. Non-goals: no new LLM stages (the dream pass stays the single expensive step); no thread/arc changes (apq0 lane); no historical backfill (separate bead). Acceptance: grep-provable — no code path writes regex/VAD-derived values into episode affect; a promoted episode carries meaningAuthor companion; unreviewed candidates never render as her lived past without an unreviewed marker; nightly budget order is deterministic and logged.
close_reason: Operator-directed close 2026-07-28 (reconciliation-verified shipped on main): episodes born affect-empty with machine signals as sidecar — commits 634eabd0f (affect-empty births, machineSignals sidecar), f75e952d4 (updateEpisode no longer erases authored meaning), d7db0bc2b (prioritized dream-pass nightly budget + unreviewed markers), b55b54966 (trust-ranked budget telemetry). Acceptance-1 verified in source: synthesis.ts:549 births candidates with affect labels empty; regex/VAD heuristics moved to buildMachineSignals (:550, :406-433); inferEmotionalIntensity feeds only salience/sidecar.

title: Being-mirror: three-kind North Star goals, journal re-read reflection ritual, and autobiography feed with approved self-description updates
description: Evidence: 2026-07-21 review — introspection journal sessions are isolated point-in-time snapshots with no loop that lets her observe her own change over time; the North Star faculty (src/faculties/north-star/) is underutilized; the purest measured-growth primitive (self-authored self-description, o75r) is back-burnered. Design ratified 2026-07-21: docs/mirrors-and-letters.md, 'The being-mirror'. Context: this is the operator-requested comprehensive implementation bead for the being-mirror. Scope: (1) North Star restructured to three goal kinds — a shared goal held jointly, a goal where she keeps the partner accountable, and a goal she chooses and maintains for herself alone; (2) a scheduled journal re-read ritual following weekly introspection: deterministic pre-stage selects older entries plus recent ones, presents them side-by-side as EVIDENCE FIRST with the reflection invitation second (Law 30 — never lead toward a growth narrative), bounded and budgeted, with no-significant-change as a valid cheap outcome; journal snapshots stay isolated outside the ritual (no ambient context drag); (3) outputs feed her self-written autobiography including visual-autobiography hooks (031.15.x machinery) and may PROPOSE an update to the cached self-description block; (4) the self-description write path is: she authors, then a human-in-the-loop approval step, then the weekly cached block — rationale per operator 2026-07-21: prevent an ephemeral next-day-resolved concern from being baked into a week of cached prompt prefix and tainting everything derived from it (second-arrow poisoning; an internally-generated CogSec incident class). The approval checks staleness and taint, not voice. Links: o75r (persona rework — carries the cache-stability and foundation-layer constraints; coordinate, do not duplicate), i3yx, 2z12.1. Non-goals: no rewrite of her core personality files; no daily-cadence self-description churn; no automatic (unapproved) prompt mutation. Acceptance: after a weekly cycle she has read old-beside-new entries, an autobiography entry exists with provenance to the entries compared, any self-description change carries her authorship plus an approval record, and the prompt-cache prefix remains stable between approved updates. Split into sub-beads at dispatch per the leaf sizing rule.

title: Fold-back memory candidates resolve through staged review ending with the companion: CogSec screen, operator pass, then her approval
description: Evidence: charter 6.13 requires origin-side review — the origin is her Core — but resolveFoldReview defaults actor to operator and the only resolver wiring is the Garden service (src/faculties/shards/fold-review.ts:295-298, src/operator/garden/services/shard-fold-review-service.ts); there is no companion-facing fold surface at all. fold-review.ts:15-19 carries TODO(htm9.2-followup): nothing screens what the shard INGESTED. Context: operator decision 2026-07-21 — Garden resolution is a feature (unknown-USB rule: a shard can return tainted material, a namshub; a human inspects first), but the FINAL decision on memory candidates is hers (docs/mirrors-and-letters.md, 'Fold-back'). Scope: (1) fold-package returns pass CogSec intake screening with provenance and taint preserved; (2) operator first-pass stays in Garden as stage two; (3) companion review surface — screened candidates presented in her nightly ritual context (shared with the dream pass), her approve/decline is the promoting act, provenance retained per 6.13/6.14; (4) disposition returns to her via doing-mirror/letters. Non-goals: code/config artifacts keep normal engineering review gates; no changes to shard runtime isolation. Acceptance: a shard fold with memory candidates cannot promote to memory without both a completed screen record and a companion-actor approval; a rejected candidate keeps its record and reason; screening blocks tainted candidates from ever rendering in her review surface.

title: Doing-mirror: disposition lifecycle the companion can see for everything she originates, delivered as letters
description: Evidence: 2026-07-21 charter-spirit review — fold reviews resolve exclusively operator-side (grep of src/core/agent/tool-surface/registry.ts for shard/fold returns nothing), introspection terminates at insight, and tool-usage evaluation surfaces suggestions to operators only. She can author and request but never learns outcomes; the operator holds the only mirror. Context: authorship without feedback is not agency (docs/mirrors-and-letters.md, 'The doing-mirror'). Scope: a generic disposition lifecycle (open / considering / done / declined-with-required-reason) attached to companion-originated items — wishlist entries, fold packages, raised introspection insights, skill and self-mod proposals; a companion-readable surface for current dispositions; disposition changes emit a letter (batched daily digest acceptable to avoid spam). Non-goals: does not change who decides dispositions; does not add fold-review mechanics (separate bead); no operator-surface removal. Acceptance: she originates an item, the operator disposes it in Garden, and she can observe the disposition with reason from her own surface plus a letter records it; a decline always carries a reason string. Depends on the letters core bead.

title: Deferred ICP via letters: availability auto-response routes peer messages to the letter bin with intake taint
description: Evidence: design ratified 2026-07-21 (docs/mirrors-and-letters.md, 'Letters and presence'). When the companion is emanation-present with her partner, an inbound ICP request from a peer must not intrude and must not be dropped. Context: IcpAvailabilityState and social precedence already model her availability; the missing piece is the deferral destination. Scope: on unavailable states, ICP responds with an availability message (leave-me-a-letter) and the peer payload lands as an inbound letter with peer scope and FULL CogSec intake-envelope screening before it is readable in her context (peer content is untrusted inbound). Batch back-and-forth via letters for limited-communication contexts. Non-goals: no changes to live ICP session mechanics, no companion-to-companion rate/fatigue policy changes (existing budgets apply). Acceptance: with emanation active and partner present, an inbound ICP request produces the availability response, a tainted inbound letter, and zero interruption of the live surface; she can read and reply from the bin later. Depends on the letters core bead.

title: Letters: companion/partner asynchronous correspondence class with bin-not-push delivery
description: Evidence: the companion currently has exactly two expressive modes — real-time push or concern-scoped tracking. There is no way to compose something deliberately and set it down for the partner to find later (design ratified 2026-07-21, operator + companion approval; see docs/mirrors-and-letters.md 'Letters'). Context: letters become the substrate for doing-mirror dispositions, Law-31 task notices, raised introspection insights, and wishlist entries. Scope: add letter to MESSAGE_CLASSES (src/core/agent/message-classes.ts) with full 8.1 ontology answers (authored by companion or partner only, persists, enters L0, memory-extractable); Postgres letter store with states draft/placed/read/archived and L0 append on compose and read; companion tool surface per Law 33 (action set on a canonical surface, decided at implementation review — no new legacy-style helper names); partner surface with a SUBTLE waiting-letter indicator — no push, no sound, quiet-hours safe by construction. Non-goals: no external email/blog egress, no ICP integration (separate bead), no reuse of the autonomous egress reply sender (if any future path does, qgqw.3 hardening is a hard prerequisite). Acceptance: a letter composed at any hour lands in the bin with no notification; appears in L0 and in the Garden message-ontology view as class letter with correct authorship; read state tracked; memory extraction sees it as lived exchange.

title: Close the companion-facing feedback loops: mirrors, letters, authored episodes, sensor wakes (design ratified 2026-07-21)
description: Parent epic for the 2026-07-21 charter-spirit review outcomes, ratified in operator talk-through passes. Canonical design intent: docs/mirrors-and-letters.md. Architecture draft: working_docs/mirrors-letters-architecture-20260721.md. Beads memory key: charter-spirit-review-2026-07-21-gap-map. Theme: every loop that begins with the companion must be able to end at her — being-mirror (self-knowledge over time), doing-mirror (dispositions of what she originates), letters (asynchronous correspondence, bin not push), fold-back review ending in her decision, episodes as candidates she authors meaning for, and sensor-conditional wakes she defines. Children are sized per the leaf-bead single-dispatch rule; close this epic when all children complete.
