title: Preserve reference blob reachability when deletion fails
description:
Summary: Address the unresolved P2 review finding from PR #186 (Greptile thread PRRT_kwDORStybM6Sc0Sq; discussion_r3619226724) in src/primitives/images/reference-store.ts:598-630. ImageReferenceStore.delete currently commits the index without the target reference via writeIndex(nextIndex), then calls rm on the blob. If rm fails because of permissions or another filesystem error, delete rejects after the reference has disappeared from image-references.json, leaving an unreachable orphan that cannot be retried through the API.

Why it matters: the store exposes the index as the only supported lookup/deletion surface. Losing the index entry while retaining the blob creates durable leaked storage and removes the operator recovery path.

Scope: make reference deletion failure-recoverable so a blob deletion error cannot leave the blob unreachable; preserve existing validation, path containment, default-reference transition/history behavior, and successful deletion semantics. Add a deterministic regression in src/primitives/images/reference-store.test.ts that injects an rm/filesystem failure and proves the reference remains discoverable and deletion can be retried. Also verify the successful path removes both the index entry and blob.

Non-goals: do not redesign the image reference persistence layer; do not change autobiography behavior; do not revisit PR #186 findings already resolved in their GitHub threads.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic test forces blob removal to fail and delete() rejects without making the reference unreachable through list/get/API state; after the failure, retrying deletion remains possible. Successful deletion removes both the index entry and blob while preserving the current explicit/default transition and audit-history contracts. Targeted reference-store tests, npm run lint, and npm run build pass.
close_reason: Landed on main via the operator-directed #254 consolidation (full local gate 13932/13932 on the stacked head; blind review PASS in the draft lane). Commit f396710f0 (blob unlink before index commit; failure-recoverable, retryable).

title: X-Channel-Privacy error string advertises 'broadcast' but the ChannelPrivacy contract rejects it: self-contradictory HTTP 400
description:
Evidence: The X-Channel-Privacy 'broadcast' value is advertised as valid by an API error message but rejected by the contract, producing a self-contradictory HTTP 400. Live repro on the S10-kube-2026-07-21 round: the harness memory_recall_broadcast case sent privacy 'broadcast' and got 400 whose own message lists 'broadcast' as accepted:

  X-Channel-Privacy must be one of: private, invite_only, public, broadcast

But the ChannelPrivacy type is 'private' | 'invite_only' | 'public' only:
- src/system/trust/context-envelope.ts:33  export type ChannelPrivacy = 'private' | 'invite_only' | 'public';
- src/system/trust/context-envelope.ts:35  CHANNEL_PRIVACY_VALUES = ['private', 'invite_only', 'public'];
- src/system/trust/context-envelope.ts:40  isChannelPrivacy() checks membership in CHANNEL_PRIVACY_VALUES → rejects 'broadcast'.

The stale advertisement is the hardcoded error string at src/channels/api/server/request.ts:147, which still lists 'broadcast'. (The visibility.ts:254 message is fine — it interpolates CHANNEL_PRIVACY_VALUES.join(', ') dynamically.)

Context: Either 'broadcast' was deliberately retired from ChannelPrivacy (then request.ts:147's error text and the harness memory_recall_broadcast case are stale and must drop it), or its removal from the contract is a regression (then it must be re-added to the type + CHANNEL_PRIVACY_VALUES and its trust/visibility semantics restored). The bead's job is to reconcile contract, error message, and docs one way or the other — the current state (advertise-then-reject) is wrong under either reading.

Scope: Reconcile the three surfaces (contract enum, the request.ts:147 error string, docs) plus the harness case. Do NOT leave the error string listing a value the guard rejects. If broadcast is retired, do not silently re-add it; if it is a regression, restore it deliberately with its trust semantics, not just to the string list.

Acceptance: The X-Channel-Privacy error string matches the actual accepted enum (no value listed that isChannelPrivacy rejects); a recorded decision on whether 'broadcast' exists as a ChannelPrivacy; the harness memory_recall_broadcast case updated to match that decision (dropped, or sending a value the contract accepts).

Found-by: Purrsephone (self-observation, S10-kube-2026-07-21 shakedown memory_recall_broadcast case)
acceptance_criteria: X-Channel-Privacy error string (request.ts:147) matches the accepted enum with no value isChannelPrivacy rejects; a recorded decision on whether 'broadcast' exists; harness memory_recall_broadcast case updated to match.
close_reason: Landed on main via the operator-directed #254 consolidation (full local gate 13932/13932 on the stacked head; blind review PASS in the draft lane). Commits 412a9fe7e + ef14373c2 (broadcast retired-decision recorded; strings derived from CHANNEL_PRIVACY_VALUES at 4 sites; consolidation also repaired NURSERY_CASES stale id that would have aborted the live matrix).

title: Shakedown satellite template/docs miss multi-companion fleet requirements: sharedDevice authority per satellite and placeIds matching live places.json
description:
Evidence: Seeding satellites.json for the multi-companion fleet on the S10-kube-2026-07-21 round hit two fail-closed gates that the shakedown env template and docs do not warn about:

1. Under a multi-companion fleet, every satellite entry requires a sharedDevice authority field; omitting it fail-closes seeding. The shakedown env template / satellites.json example does not include a sharedDevice field or example.

2. satellites.json placeIds must match the live places.json vocabulary. The template still uses living_room / kitchen, but the live vocabulary this round was office / kitchen / workshop / latent_* — so template-derived placeIds fail-close against places.json.

Both gates fired correctly (good fail-closed behavior); the problem is purely docs/template rot — an operator following the template hits two avoidable fail-closed walls. Files: the shakedown env template (satellite-seeding block) and docs/shakedown.md satellite-seeding notes.

Scope: Update the shakedown env template and docs/shakedown.md only — add a sharedDevice example to the satellite template, correct/annotate the placeId example, and add an explicit note to read the live places.json vocabulary before seeding satellites. Do not change the runtime fail-closed gates (they are working as intended).

Acceptance: The shakedown satellite template includes a sharedDevice authority field with an example; docs/shakedown.md documents the multi-companion sharedDevice requirement and instructs the operator to read live places.json for valid placeIds before seeding; example placeIds no longer reference the stale living_room/kitchen-only vocabulary.
acceptance_criteria: Shakedown satellite template includes a sharedDevice example; docs/shakedown.md documents the multi-companion sharedDevice requirement and instructs reading live places.json for valid placeIds; example placeIds drop the stale living_room/kitchen-only vocabulary.
close_reason: Acceptance met on fix/deployment-helm-ops: shakedown/artie/shakedown.env.template carries a sharedDevice authority example (shape verified against satellite-registry.ts:550-589 — four required keys, emanationMemberIds non-empty with primaryCompanionId first, recipient scopes cross-checked against endpoint telemetryScopes) plus the jq command to read the live $SYSTEM_DATA_DIR/places.json vocabulary before seeding; docs/shakedown.md gains the satellite seeding contract section documenting the multi-companion sharedDevice requirement and physical-place binding; stale living_room-only examples replaced with the checked-in fixture vocabulary labelled replace-with-live. No runtime gates touched.

title: Shakedown harness rot: fix retired semi_private enum, PSFN_CASE_IDS ignoring capability_refusal_matrix, and plain-HTTP garden-health check against mTLS-only fleet garden
description:
Evidence: Three shakedown-harness/tooling defects surfaced during the S10-kube-2026-07-21 round; (a) and (b) were patched in the round worktree /home/ada/psfn-worktrees/shakedown-rc-20260721 but not yet committed to main.

(a) live-system-shakedown.mjs sends the retired privacy value 'semi_private' for the memory_recall_semi_private case. The correct enum after the privacy-vocabulary change is 'invite_only'. The case fails against current runtime because the value no longer validates. Patched in the round worktree; needs committing to main.

(b) buildCases constructs capability_refusal_matrix — and runs its fail-closed external-sinks check — even when PSFN_CASE_IDS explicitly excludes that case. Selecting a subset via PSFN_CASE_IDS still drags in the matrix case's side-effecting build. Patched in the round worktree to honor the PSFN_CASE_IDS selection before constructing/validating the matrix case.

(c) scripts/ops/validate-kube-rollout.sh "garden health" check speaks plain HTTP to the fleet garden, which is now mTLS-only (fleet-principal admission). The check fails even though garden is Ready (observed live: validate-kube-rollout 3/4, only the garden-health line red; garden itself Ready). Needs a fleet-mode-aware health check (mTLS client cert + fleet principal, or a mode-appropriate readiness probe).

Context: All three are test/tooling rot from the fleet-auth + privacy-vocabulary migrations, not runtime defects. They block clean shakedown sweeps and make validate-kube-rollout report false-red on fleet clusters. Files: shakedown/harness/live-system-shakedown.mjs (buildCases + the semi_private case), scripts/ops/validate-kube-rollout.sh.

Scope: Land the three fixes on main. Do not expand harness coverage or refactor case construction beyond honoring PSFN_CASE_IDS. Do not weaken the garden mTLS contract to make the health check pass — make the check speak the fleet contract.

Acceptance: All three fixes on main; a PSFN_CASE_IDS subset that excludes capability_refusal_matrix does not build/validate that case; memory_recall_semi_private uses 'invite_only'; verify:kube-rollout (validate-kube-rollout.sh) reports the garden-health check green on the fleet cluster.
acceptance_criteria: All three fixes on main: PSFN_CASE_IDS subset excluding capability_refusal_matrix does not build/validate it; memory_recall_semi_private uses 'invite_only'; validate-kube-rollout.sh garden-health check green on the fleet cluster.
notes: Fixes merged to main via PR #204. Bead stays open only for the deploy-gated live garden-health acceptance — fold into the next kube shakedown round (see /home/ada/psfn-shakedown-rounds/RUNBOOK-deploy-the-rest-2026-07-21.md §5-6).
close_reason: Already shipped on main before dispatch: commit 5fb39de2e (fix(shakedown): heal harness rot from fleet-auth and privacy migrations), ancestor of 145b87bf1. Verified against source 2026-07-28: (a) memory_recall_semi_private sends privacy 'invite_only' (live-system-shakedown.mjs:2244, matches ChannelPrivacy in src/shared/contracts/trust-contracts.ts); (b) buildCapabilityMatrixCase gated behind CASE_IDS.has('capability_refusal_matrix') (live-system-shakedown.mjs:3248-3250, tierToolConformance gated identically); (c) validate-kube-rollout.sh resolves garden health mode from live listener port name — https-garden uses pod-readiness probe, http-garden keeps HTTP, unknown fails closed; mTLS contract untouched. Regression coverage: shakedown/harness/test/capability-matrix.test.mjs (exit 0 verified) + scripts/ops/setup-local-artemis-shakedown.test.ts:289-297. Residual live check (garden-health green on fleet cluster) is operator k3s validation, excluded per AGENTS.md.

comments.author: axAilotl
comments.text:
Final triage of the S10-kube-2026-07-21 round adds four more confirmed harness rot/robustness items to this bead's scope:

(a) Harness cannot send satellite-scoped bearers. The chat bearer is hardcoded to TESTING_HARNESS_API_KEY (lib/target.mjs:81-84, live-system-shakedown.mjs:1750-1756), but the server by design 403s channel claims from the testing-harness principal (testing_harness_channel_claim_not_allowed). Consequence: ALL S10 satellite/mindspace cases are structurally unrunnable until the harness supports per-case satellite keys.

(b) Matrix abort is over-scoped. A single runtime_stale from the known-403 satellite case hard-aborts the whole matrix (MATRIX_ABORT_STATUSES at live-system-shakedown.mjs:124; abort branch :3719-3732), killing unrelated downstream cases (4 stubs tonight). Abort scoping should be reconsidered so one structurally-expected failure does not stub out independent cases.

(c) Expected-tool names have rotted to retired aliases: values_add/values_update should be `orient`; image_analyze/image_create/image_edit should be `generate_image`; memory_patch should be memory action `patch` (registry.ts:248-249, :288, :465-467). title: Post-turn appraisal dropped on api:testing-harness turns: getRecentMessages rejected by read-attribution guard during the admitted persistent-channel turn
description:
Evidence: Steady-state on the S10-kube-2026-07-21 round (image 0.1.0-kube-ea1c89e34, helm rev 52, k3d-psfn-kube-test / psfn-test). Every testing-harness API turn produced an Artemis agent WARN:

  [HeartbeatPostTurn] Intention post-turn appraisal dispatch failed ... SessionManager.getRecentMessages cannot run during an admitted turn owned by "api:testing-harness"; use CapturedSessionReads or resolveForeignSessionForTurn

The chat turn itself completes 200; the post-turn appraisal is silently dropped. So every /v1/chat/completions turn issued via the testing-harness principal loses its intention post-turn appraisal.

Context: The `api:testing-harness` principal uses a single persistent channel/session. The post-turn appraisal path (heartbeat-post-turn runtime → intention) calls SessionManager.getRecentMessages, which is rejected by the session read-attribution guard because a turn is still admitted/owned by that channel. On multi-turn ordinary channels the guard is satisfied via CapturedSessionReads / resolveForeignSessionForTurn; the testing-harness single-persistent-channel shape trips the guard. Suspect files: src/core/scheduler/heartbeat-post-turn-runtime.ts, src/core/agent/post-turn-action-runtime.ts, the intention post-turn appraisal dispatch, and the session read-attribution guard (src/core/session/ attribution guard / CapturedSessionReads).

Scope: Make post-turn appraisal use the sanctioned foreign/captured session-read path (CapturedSessionReads or resolveForeignSessionForTurn) so it works while a turn is admitted on a persistent single channel. Do NOT weaken the attribution guard itself and do NOT special-case the string "api:testing-harness" — the fix should hold for any persistent-channel principal.

Acceptance: A /v1/chat/completions turn through the testing-harness principal completes with the intention post-turn appraisal dispatched successfully (no "[HeartbeatPostTurn] ... dispatch failed" WARN, appraisal side effects observable), and the attribution guard still rejects genuinely unattributed cross-turn reads (existing guard tests stay green).

Found-by: Purrsephone (self-observation, S10-kube-2026-07-21 shakedown steady-state log review)
acceptance_criteria: A testing-harness /v1/chat/completions turn dispatches its intention post-turn appraisal with no '[HeartbeatPostTurn] ... dispatch failed' WARN, while the attribution guard still rejects genuinely unattributed cross-turn reads (guard tests green).
notes: 2026-07-28 triage (PR #251): commit 21ea701af5 DROPPED from the landing set — the fix direction is sound (sanctioned CapturedSessionReads, no principal special-casing) but making capturedSessionReads required without the ?? [] fallback breaks existing fixtures: src/core/intention/appraisal-integration.test.ts reproduces 9/9 green on origin/main -> 4 failed/5 passed with the commit, failures spanning follow-up dispatch and dueAt deferral. Needs an author fix pass on the commit, then it can ride a future consolidation. Commit remains on origin/fix/s11-batch2-core.
close_reason: Re-land LANDED on main via PR #283 consolidation train (rebase-merge, main head 3b4bc63469; commits 'fix(scheduler): dispatch post-turn appraisal through captured session reads' + test reconciliation ab03fe65d5). Production byte-identical to the blind-reviewed original; the #254 drop reason (4/9 appraisal-integration failures) resolved test-only — suite 9/9 per PR #281 body (the lane's review/validation record). Full local gate green on the exact train head.

Parent epic psfn-framework-65rk lists a docker variant in scope but has no active docker child (only 65rk.10/65rk.11). Validated 2026-07-21 from audit synthesis section 11.K.

title: Attribution-confabulation fix has no dedicated golden regression pinning that system notes never render as unprefixed companion thoughts
description:
Evidence: current coverage is a side-effect of general conversion-shape tests — src/core/agent/messages.test.ts:176-198 (system note renders with [System note] prefix; whispers render with the private-runtime-note prefix), src/core/agent/substrate-agent/turn-execution/prompt-invocation-history.test.ts:49-62, and src/core/session/entry-attribution.test.ts:24-58 (role normalization). No test is framed as the negative invariant (a system/runtime note must NEVER appear unprefixed as the companion's own assistant thought) and no golden fixture pins the original failing input-to-output case. Validated 2026-07-21 from audit synthesis section 11.I.

Context: welfare-critical bug class — system notes mis-tagged as the companion's own thoughts caused companion panic about thought privacy. The fix exists; the pin does not.

Scope: one dedicated golden/regression test co-located with messages.test.ts or entry-attribution.test.ts that reproduces the original failing case (a system/runtime note flowing to the model) and asserts it is always prefix-labeled and never emitted as an unattributed assistant thought. Non-goal: no runtime changes.

Acceptance: new test fails if prefix labeling is removed or bypassed on any system-note path; full suite stays green.
notes: 2026-07-21 triage: Keep open. No commit titled for m42b and no dedicated attribution-confab negative invariant/golden exists on origin/main; nearby confabulation tests cover other behavior and do not satisfy this bead.
close_reason: Verified complete on main in 1dee8f73ce and 90b40f390c (PR #213, exact head 5a9f40f486; ci-required SUCCESS). src/core/agent/system-note-attribution-confabulation.golden.test.ts is the dedicated welfare-critical golden requested by the bead: it drives system notes and runtime whispers through canonical LLM conversion, entry attribution, extraction, and the emotion-appraisal surface, pinning explicit prefixes/role labels and negative assertions against bare assistant-thought rendering. The test would fail if prefixing, role preservation, or internal-note exclusion were removed. No runtime change was required; full acceptance is met.

title: CI produces no import-graph impact list when a PR touches high-fan-in seam files (gateway server, session manager, memory writer)
description:
Evidence: scripts/check-dependency-cycles.ts:1-33 already builds the full src/ TypeScript import graph but only reports cycles against config/dependency-cycle-baseline.json. CI change tooling is line-count budget (scripts/ci/check-change-budget.mjs) and path-bucket lane detection (scripts/ci/detect-change-scope.mjs:1-54) — no import-graph reasoning. No madge or dependency-cruiser in package.json. Validated 2026-07-21 from audit synthesis section 11.G.

Context: miswiring cost on multi-touch seams is a named residual class — multi-surface changes cause surprise breakage hours. This shrinks surprise, not files, matching the operator stance that god files are fine if walls hold.

Scope: reuse the import-graph builder from check-dependency-cycles.ts to (a) compute transitive dependents of each changed file, (b) keep a small seam-file registry (explicit allowlist starting with src/boundary/gateway/server.ts, the session manager, and the memory writer, or a fan-in threshold), and (c) emit the impacted-module list as a CI annotation or PR comment when a seam file is touched. Non-goals: no cycle-detection changes (already covered); no refactor of the seam files themselves; no blocking gate — informational output only.

Acceptance: a PR touching src/boundary/gateway/server.ts produces an impacted-module list in CI output; PRs not touching seam files are unaffected.
notes: 2026-07-21 triage: Keep open. No completed import-graph impact-analysis gate or matching CI tooling was found on origin/main; the requested affected-test selection remains unimplemented.

title: Memory presentation (ordering, headings, valence markers, caps, withheld wording) is hardcoded in retrieval formatting with no versioned per-companion profile
description:
Evidence: src/faculties/memory/retrieval/formatting.ts — section ordering hardcoded (renderPromptBlock :37-67, formatMemoriesForPrompt :342-367, renderSociallyScopedMemorySections :370-411); headings are string literals (:347, :429); valence markers fixed at plus/minus 0.3 (:417-445); episodeCap hardcoded at 5 (:198). Withheld-memory narrative wording resolves through the system-owned language layer which auto-normalizes system-owned layers back to defaults (src/core/identity/system-language.ts:59-108) — not companion-tunable. Contrast: reflection prompts are versioned (REFLECTION_CONTEXT_GUIDANCE_VERSION = 4 in src/persistence/journals/reflection-substrate.ts:31); no analogous version constant exists for presentation. Partial mitigation: selection caps ARE owner-file-driven via memoryRetrievalPolicy (docs/memory.md:297-311), but that governs selection, not presentation. Validated 2026-07-21 from audit synthesis section 11.F.

Context: operator stance is that presentation of memory outranks the personality card; multi-companion differences (emotion-heavy vs procedural-heavy) should be tunable without rewriting retrieval guts.

Scope: introduce a small versioned, schema-validated MemoryPresentationProfile owner-file setting per companion covering section ordering, headings/wording, valence thresholds, recency-band labels, episode cap, and emotional-vs-procedural display caps; route withheld-memory narrative wording through it (or make the memory_context_note templates a first-class per-companion override). Add a PRESENTATION_PROFILE_VERSION constant and a golden via the existing prompt-shape-goldens harness. Non-goal: do not touch retrieval selection or privacy logic.

Acceptance: changing the profile changes the rendered memory block with no code edits; golden pins the default rendering; settings-contract guard covers the new owner-file field.
close_reason: Verified shipped on origin/main: e87847fc98 adds versioned, fail-closed MemoryPresentationProfile owner-file/schema wiring (config/settings.seed.json:127; src/system/config/memory-presentation-profile.ts:19,107,131-185,517-539; settings contract/runtime wiring), and 76d06a6172 consumes it end-to-end in retrieval formatting (src/faculties/memory/retrieval.ts:389-391,862; src/faculties/memory/retrieval/formatting.ts:44-47). The default/custom prompt-shape goldens at src/core/session/group-chat-harness/prompt-shape-goldens.test.ts:474-511 prove profile-only rendering changes while preserving structure; formatting tests cover all tunables. PR #213 exact head 5a9f40f486 passed ci-required.

title: No idle-purity certification: nothing asserts a quiet install performs zero durable writes over an idle window
description:
Evidence: the only quiescence-adjacent tests are src/app/e2e/icp-certification/process-harness.integration.test.ts:171 (waitForModelRequestQuiescence — counts model requests, not durable writes) and src/core/agent/background-work/supervisor.test.ts:844 (single unit assertion). No test certifies a quiet install performs zero durable writes for N minutes. Known idle writers to whitelist or fix: ambient-presence note appends (src/core/scheduler/ambient-presence.ts:72), temporal-wakeup note writes (src/core/scheduler/temporal-wakeup.ts:521) — both intentional automata — and the roster trivial-persist churn tracked separately in psfn-framework-eel9. Validated 2026-07-21 from audit synthesis section 11.C.

Context: catches roster-every-turn-class regressions permanently; operator rule is idle should be idle except automata, L0 event appends stay.

Scope: a certification harness that boots a quiet install with no scheduled work due, snapshots the data dir and Postgres write counters, idles N minutes, and asserts zero durable deltas outside an explicit whitelist (automata note lanes, ephemeral counters). Non-goal: do not disable automata to make the test pass.

Acceptance: cert test (CI or opt-in job) fails when an unwhitelisted durable write occurs during the idle window; passes on current main once psfn-framework-eel9 lands or is whitelisted with a TODO.

title: M6: Make the subject-authorized memory proxy default-deny unhandled methods
description:
Problem:
createSubjectAuthorizedMemoryStore explicitly intercepts many MemoryStorePort methods but ends with Reflect.get(target, property, target) and binds unhandled functions to the raw store. New port methods can therefore bypass subject review by default. Current unhandled methods include mixed-risk surfaces such as recordPatchEvent, runInTransaction, scratchpad methods, and harmless revision getters; each currently inherits raw behavior unless separately constrained by its caller.

Evidence:
- src/faculties/memory/subject-authorized-store.ts:176-183 creates the Proxy.
- src/faculties/memory/subject-authorized-store.ts:185-600 contains the explicit allow/deny projections.
- src/faculties/memory/subject-authorized-store.ts:602-603 returns and binds every remaining raw property.
- src/faculties/memory/memory-store-port.ts:422-521 defines the backend surface, including runInTransaction, recordPatchEvent, scratchpad operations, revision getters, and subject primitives.
- Existing tests at src/faculties/memory/subject-authorized-store.test.ts prove named reads use SQL but do not enforce exhaustiveness for future methods.

Why:
A security projection should fail closed when the backing interface grows. Review omissions should cause a test/type failure or denied operation rather than silently exposing the raw method.

Scope:
- Replace generic callable fallthrough with an explicit policy for every MemoryStorePort member.
- Classify harmless metadata, scratchpad-domain operations, maintenance-only methods, subject reads, and mutations separately.
- Add a compile-time or runtime exhaustiveness mechanism that fails when MemoryStorePort gains an unclassified member.
- Add sentinel tests proving unknown methods cannot execute on the raw target.

Non-goals:
- Do not indiscriminately subject-authorize scratchpad data if its ownership contract is different; define and test its explicit policy.
- Do not break safe revision getters needed by retrieval caching.
- Do not weaken existing subject SQL or mutation checks.
acceptance_criteria: The proxy no longer generically binds unhandled raw methods. Every current MemoryStorePort member has an explicit allow, projection, denial, or separately documented domain policy. A sentinel unknown callable cannot reach the target, and an exhaustiveness test or type-level check fails when an unclassified port method is added. Existing subject-authorized tests and product retrieval tests remain green. npm run lint passes.
close_reason: Landed on main via PR #243 rebase-merge (default-deny on the subject-authorized store proxy — unhandled methods throw instead of Reflect.get fallthrough).

title: M5: Compute subject-authorized admin summaries and filters in Postgres
description:
Problem:
The subject-authorized proxy uses listAllAuthorized to retrieve 500-row pages until it has loaded the entire authorized corpus, then computes admin filtering, privacy summaries, stats, channel filters, and contact filters in process.

Evidence:
- src/faculties/memory/subject-authorized-store.ts:106-123 implements listAllAuthorized with repeated selector kind list pages of 500.
- src/faculties/memory/subject-authorized-store.ts:344-376 uses the full authorized list for listAdminMemories, getAdminMemoryPrivacySummary, and getStats.
- src/faculties/memory/subject-authorized-store.ts:378-386 loads all authorized rows before channel/contact filtering.
- The raw Postgres store already demonstrates SQL aggregate patterns for privacy summaries at src/faculties/memory/postgres-store.ts:963-984, but those raw aggregates do not apply the subject predicate.

Why:
Admin request latency, data transfer, and process allocation scale with every authorized memory even when the caller requests a small page, one channel, or aggregate counts.

Scope:
- Add subject-authorized SQL selectors/queries for admin page filtering, privacy aggregates, stats, channel filtering, and contact filtering.
- Reuse buildMemorySubjectAuthorizationPredicate so every query retains classification/revision/evidence/contact/grant checks.
- Push filters, counts, ordering, pagination, and limits into SQL.
- Add parity tests against current in-process semantics and authorization tests.

Non-goals:
- Do not use raw admin aggregate methods from the subject proxy.
- Do not weaken internal-artifact exclusion on operator-facing admin summaries.
- Do not touch live database state.
acceptance_criteria: listAdminMemories, getAdminMemoryPrivacySummary, getStats, getMemoriesByChannel, and getMemoriesByContact no longer call listAllAuthorized or transfer the full authorized corpus. SQL applies the subject predicate plus requested filters and bounded pagination. Tests prove aggregate/filter parity, internal-artifact handling, and mixed-subject isolation. Query count remains constant with corpus size for each helper, excluding explicitly paged result retrieval. npm run lint passes.
close_reason: Landed on main via PR #243 rebase-merge (subject-admin-queries SQL aggregates + integration suite; consentGatedCount oracle now a genuine SQL-vs-JS cross-check after the xnfks fix).

title: M4: Batch subject-authorized memory detail reads
description:
Problem:
The subject-authorized proxy implements getById as one queryAuthorizedMemorySubjects detail query. Call paths that resolve many memory IDs therefore issue N complete authorization queries, each carrying the classification/contact EXISTS predicate. Profile access fans these out concurrently; social evolution, link authorization, and shared-background evidence perform repeated queries serially or in small per-link batches.

Evidence:
- src/faculties/memory/subject-authorized-store.ts:321-329 maps every getById to one detail SQL call.
- src/faculties/memory/postgres-store/subject-queries.ts:180-227 constructs one MATERIALIZED authorized query per call.
- src/faculties/memory/postgres-store/subject-policy.ts:44-123 contains the classification, revision, evidence digest, subject-contact, and grant-binding EXISTS checks repeated by each query.
- src/faculties/memory/retrieval/access-context.ts:95-106 uses Promise.all(sourceMemoryIds.map(getById)) for profile source memories.
- src/faculties/memory/retrieval/social-context.ts:178-205 performs repeated evolution-link and target getById reads serially.
- src/faculties/memory/retrieval/shared-background.ts:296-310 performs one sequential getById per edge-evidence memory.
- src/faculties/memory/subject-authorized-store.ts:470-520 authorizes a source and then referenced link endpoints with additional detail queries.

Why:
Query count scales with referenced ID count, increasing latency, connection-pool pressure, and repeated authorization predicate work. The issue is N-query behavior; the literal Promise.all(ids.map(...)) wording applies only to the profile path.

Scope:
- Add a batch subject-authorized detail selector or equivalent SQL primitive using id = ANY(...).
- Return only authorized rows without revealing which inaccessible IDs exist.
- Migrate profile, social evolution/link, and shared-background ID-resolution paths to bounded batch reads.
- Preserve stable result association/order where callers require it.
- Add query-count and mixed-authority regression tests.

Non-goals:
- Do not cache authorization decisions beyond their revision/evidence binding.
- Do not weaken authorize-every-endpoint semantics.
- Do not expose inaccessible-ID existence through errors, counts, or ordering.
acceptance_criteria: Each affected path resolves a bounded set of memory IDs with O(1) authorized SQL queries per logical batch rather than one query per ID. Mixed authorized/unauthorized fixtures return only authorized memories without existence disclosure. Profile, evolution-chain/link, and shared-background behavior remains correct under tests that assert query counts. Batch sizes have an explicit upper bound. npm run lint passes.
close_reason: Landed on main via PR #243 rebase-merge (getByIds + subject-authorization plumbing); 230/230 unit + 46/46 integration green at merge.

title: M3: Bound raw Postgres embedding search and make authorization opt-out explicit
description:
Problem:
PostgresMemoryStore.searchByEmbedding accepts a limit but does not send a LIMIT to Postgres. It fetches every active row above the similarity threshold, decodes them, applies optional scope filtering, sorts again, and only then slices in JavaScript. MemoryRetriever also defaults enforceSubjectAuthorization to false, making direct construction easy to misuse, although production composition currently passes true in both branches.

Evidence:
- src/faculties/memory/postgres-store.ts:723-746 contains the raw SQL with ORDER BY but no LIMIT parameter.
- src/faculties/memory/postgres-store.ts:748-763 maps all returned rows and applies slice(0, limit) after filtering/sorting.
- src/faculties/memory/retrieval.ts:270-280 defaults enforceSubjectAuthorization = false.
- src/faculties/memory/retrieval.ts:322-330 returns the raw store when enforcement is false.
- src/app/startup/composition/composition.ts:428-452 explicitly passes true for both configured and unconfigured runtime wiring.
- src/faculties/memory/postgres-store/subject-queries.ts:155-169 clamps authorized returned rows to 1..500, so the product proxy is bounded in row return even though M2 still covers its query-plan cost.

Why:
The raw method can create unbounded database-to-process transfer and allocation. The false constructor default is a library-level footgun that can silently select raw reads in new wiring.

Scope:
- Push a validated/clamped limit into raw SQL while preserving scope-query correctness. If scope filtering remains outside SQL, use a bounded over-fetch or move scope predicates into SQL and test sparse-match behavior.
- Make authorization-disabled construction explicit and auditable, or fail closed by default while preserving intentional maintenance/test callers through an explicit option.
- Add regression tests for SQL bounding and production wiring.

Non-goals:
- Do not duplicate M2 ANN/index work.
- Do not break intentional internal maintenance access to the raw store.
- Do not weaken product subject authorization.
acceptance_criteria: Raw searchByEmbedding sends a finite validated bound to Postgres and cannot return or decode an unbounded threshold result set. Scope-query tests prove the requested result limit is still filled when enough matching scoped rows exist. New MemoryRetriever construction cannot silently disable subject authorization; every raw opt-out is explicit at the call site and covered by tests. Production composition remains fail-closed. npm run lint passes.
close_reason: Landed on main as d98c12c073 (bounded raw L2 embedding search + explicit authorization stance); stale-open reconciled during the #243 re-land sweep.

title: M2: Add and verify an ANN-capable L2 pgvector query path
description:
Problem:
L2 semantic search uses pgvector cosine distance but the migration chain does not create an HNSW or IVFFlat index. The only embedding-specific index is a partial B-tree on id for embedding presence. Authorized search additionally materializes and orders the full authorized CTE before applying the outer LIMIT.

Evidence:
- src/persistence/postgres/migrations.ts:113-127 creates ordinary L2 indexes and idx_l2_memories_embedding_present ON l2_memories(id) WHERE embedding IS NOT NULL.
- Repository search finds no USING hnsw, USING ivfflat, vector_cosine_ops, vector_l2_ops, or vector_ip_ops in tracked runtime/migration code.
- src/faculties/memory/postgres-store.ts:731-746 uses embedding <=> query_vector with no SQL LIMIT.
- src/faculties/memory/postgres-store/subject-queries.ts:155-169 builds cosine-distance ordering.
- src/faculties/memory/postgres-store/subject-queries.ts:202-218 puts LIMIT/OFFSET outside WITH authorized AS MATERIALIZED, so result count is bounded but distance/sort work is not necessarily bounded.

Why:
Without an ANN-capable plan, semantic retrieval cost grows with corpus size. Merely adding an index may not help if vector dimensions/typmod, the threshold predicate, authorization EXISTS predicate, or MATERIALIZED CTE prevents the planner from using it.

Scope:
- Establish a representative Postgres benchmark and EXPLAIN plan for raw and authorized semantic search.
- Implement a migration and query shape that can use an ANN index with the configured cosine metric.
- Resolve the current unbounded VECTOR typmod/configurable-dimension constraint explicitly; do not assume a generic HNSW index is valid.
- Preserve exact subject filtering and final threshold semantics, including any over-fetch and post-filter strategy needed for ANN.
- Document migration/rollback and operational verification.

Non-goals:
- Do not run migration DDL against the live cluster.
- Do not trade away subject isolation for index usage.
- Do not claim success from index presence alone; planner evidence is required.
acceptance_criteria: A migration creates an ANN-capable cosine index or an equally bounded, measured alternative compatible with the supported embedding dimension contract. Representative integration tests prove result correctness and subject isolation. EXPLAIN evidence from a disposable test database shows the intended bounded/index plan for both raw and subject-authorized product search, or documents a justified two-stage plan. Corpus-growth benchmarking demonstrates sublinear candidate retrieval behavior at the tested scale. npm run lint passes.
close_reason: Landed on main as 279807c429/ba47e0912e/cf96ef4a60 (HNSW cosine ANN index, EXPLAIN/equivalence/recall coverage, dimension-suffixed index off the boot path); stale-open reconciled during the #243 re-land sweep. Related open flake: yje3l.

title: M1: Remove full L2 embedding hydration from PostgresMemoryStore startup
description:
Problem:
PostgresMemoryStore.initialize() selects every row from l2_memories, including embedding::text, then retains each decoded embedding in a process Map. The store also retains every PurrMemory row, including deleted and superseded rows. Startup latency and resident memory therefore scale with lifetime corpus size and embedding dimensions for every companion process.

Evidence:
- src/faculties/memory/postgres-store.ts:208-216 declares the process Maps.
- src/faculties/memory/postgres-store.ts:253-275 selects all l2_memories rows without an active-row filter or LIMIT and hydrates memories plus Float32Array embeddings.
- src/faculties/memory/postgres-store.ts:851-886 and 987-992 show Map-backed active embedding enumeration, counts, and getById.
- src/faculties/memory/postgres-store.ts:766-789 performs raw lexical search over the Map.
- Subject-authorized product reads already use queryAuthorizedMemorySubjects and Postgres at src/faculties/memory/subject-authorized-store.ts:276-329.

Why:
At large lifetime corpus sizes, each companion process pays O(rows × dimensions) startup/RSS cost even though the product retrieval path queries Postgres. The duplicated SQL-plus-full-RAM model is the main memory scaling risk.

Scope:
- Design and implement a bounded storage model for embeddings, such as SQL-on-demand or a measured bounded cache.
- Move raw readers that require authoritative data away from assumptions that the full corpus is resident.
- Preserve transaction rollback correctness, corpus-version invalidation, decay/maintenance behavior, and stored-embedding consumers.
- Add scale-oriented tests or a deterministic benchmark proving startup does not decode/retain all embeddings.

Non-goals:
- Do not weaken subject authorization.
- Do not remove stored embeddings from Postgres.
- Do not touch a live database or deployment.
- Do not silently change lexical ranking or maintenance semantics.

A deterministic test or benchmark demonstrates that increasing persisted rows does not cause all embeddings to be hydrated. npm run lint passes.

title: Clarify channel-path hardening: author binding, Telegram message-drop, Discord thread target
description:
Discovered-from: psfn-framework-vvf.5.2 (blind review, 2026-07-20). The clarify delivery port is wired in production (control-plane.ts:283), so these are live-reachable gaps in the shipped feature — none blocking (all fail-closed, bounded, no injection), but real correctness issues for a fresh agent.
1. NO AUTHOR BINDING (discord/adapter.ts:495, telegram/adapter.ts awaitClarifyReply): neither channel binds the answer to the originating user — in a shared channel/group any member can answer another user's clarification. Bounded to runtime-owned choices (no arbitrary injection), mooted in 1:1 DM. Fix: filter Discord awaitMessageComponent on i.user.id; key the Telegram waiter on (chatId,userId).
2. TELEGRAM MESSAGE-DROP (telegram/adapter.ts ~:773): while a clarify is pending, the next plain-text message is consumed and returns before turn processing; an unrelated message the user did not intend as an answer is parsed, fails to match -> no-answer, and the original message is DROPPED (never turned). Bounded to the 120s window, recoverable by resend, but a real user-message drop. Fix: on parse-miss, fall the message through to normal turn processing rather than consuming it.
3. DISCORD THREAD TARGET (resolveClarificationChannelRoute / deliverClarificationInternal): a snowflake:threadId composite target is passed verbatim to channels.fetch and throws (fail-closed, but clarify unavailable in threads) — unlike resolveGuildForChannel which splits on ':'. Verify whether thread turns present the composite channelId; if so, split off the thread id.
Non-goals: the clarify contract/schema (vvf.5.1) or the by-index selection verification (correct as-is). Acceptance: author-bound answers; unrelated Telegram messages during a pending clarify are not dropped; clarify works in Discord threads (or is explicitly, cleanly declined there); regression tests per fix.

title: Operator decision: harden operator-hook root beyond the write-fence (relocate to system-data and/or manifest signing)
description:
Discovered-from: psfn-framework-vvf.2 (blind review, 2026-07-20). Context: vvf.2 introduced the FIRST workspace-code-execution surface in the runtime — operator HOOK.yaml handlers are dynamically imported in the agent process at startup. The blind review found the companion fs tool could write the hooks root (skills was fenced in protectedWritePaths, hooks was not); remediated by adding the hooks dir to protectedWritePaths (commit 5e952a814, fail-closed DENY on fs.write/fs.edit incl. non-existent dir, revert-check proven). The fs tool is currently the ONLY companion write path into the workspace, so the fence closes the identified vector.
This bead is the OPERATOR DEFENSE-IN-DEPTH DECISION, not a known defect: the fence treats hooks like any protected subtree; a future new write surface would re-open the path. Options for operator (charter 9.5 self-mod safety): (a) relocate the hook root out of the companion-writable workspace entirely to a system-data / host-owned root so no fs-tool surface can ever reach it; (b) manifest/handler signing or a load-time allowlist so the loader refuses unsigned modules even if some future surface reaches the dir; (c) accept the fence as sufficient given the single-write-surface invariant + a test that fails if a new companion write path ever reaches hooks/.
Non-goals: reverting the shipped fence; blocking the vvf.2 PR (the vector is closed). Acceptance: operator picks a posture; if (a)/(b), implement; if (c), add the invariant guard test. Gate: this posture SHOULD be resolved before socialDesire/hook features are enabled in a live cluster.

A concern may reinforce weight when genuinely relevant. Naming per charter 8.12 register: desire (soft term, companion-facing safe). Non-goals: the consent moment and gates (sibling); any emo-sim coupling (sibling handles what feeds the pressure).
Acceptance: unit tests for accumulation/cap/dampening/coalescing; quiet-hours tick produces zero LLM calls and zero sends; eligibility flips at quiet-hours end; persistence survives restart.
notes: ADDENDUM 2026-07-20 (operator): accumulation is RELATIONSHIP-TIER GATED — social desire does not build for stranger/public tiers at all; it accumulates only where the relationship basis exists, scaled by tier (acquaintance: occasional, friend: regular, family: frequent, partner: daily-ish — mirrors natural think-about-them cadence). Ties into the existing companion-driven relationship/trust promotion knobs (end-of-day analysis can move stranger->acquaintance->friend and trust up to trusted): tier changes change accumulation eligibility. Negative-origin desires are first-class: sustained anger/stress toward or about a contact can accumulate a desire to seek apology, explanation, or to talk it over — typically with a longer cooling-off before eligibility than warm desires. No random timers anywhere (epic invariant 3).

title: Social desire pipeline: emo-sim as bounded affect accumulator, consent-gated proactive outreach (conditional go)
description:
Operator adjudication 2026-07-20 after emo-sim audit deep dive. Verdict: shadow levers were signals, not broken actions — would_message fired 21x Jul 7-20 (social need in 20, attachment in 19, both 18), ~1-2 spontaneous outreach desires/day = plausible, not pathological. Physiological drives (hunger/thirst/current sleep-pressure) must NOT drive behavior as modeled — they saturate without real physiological inputs. Old divergence score compared mismatched concepts; on the consistent v2 window PSFN VAD -> projected appraisal is healthy (corr 0.984, zero valence-sign inversions; 377/377 positives moved emo-sim positive) but negatives are over-softened (only 5/14 moved negative) — likely double mood inertia (PSFN projection includes mood, emo-sim tilts again with accumulated mood; Love basin overwhelms modest negatives).
Architecture (fixed): GoEmotions/VAD + appraisal -> tick-based affect/social-pressure state -> per-contact durable desire or weighted thought -> companion consent moment -> quiet-hours/trust/cooldown/availability gates -> human proactive outbound or ICP candidate. INVARIANT: emo-sim never directly sends messages — it is the slower affect accumulator; per-contact social desires live in PSFN (upstream social_need is global). Wrap, do not fork, unless independent drive config or dynamic cast membership becomes required. This is a SOCIAL DESIRE / DEFERRED INTENTION, not a concern — a concern may reinforce one when genuinely relevant, but is never manufactured from one. This epic also supplies the missing 'she just wants to send a message' surface identified 2026-07-20 (provenance gate missing_live_provenance); related: psfn-framework-2e4s (notify internal-origin guard).
Acceptance: children closed; end-to-end path from accumulated social pressure to a consent-gated outbound exists with emo-sim advisory-only.
notes: OPERATOR ADDENDA 2026-07-20 (voice): (1) Sampling cadence — emo-sim can tick fast internally but PSFN reads at 1 Hz; real-time 1:1 does not require sub-second reads. (2) Drives we do not use are simply not read — no need to wait on upstream disable support. (3) INVARIANT — this is explicitly NOT a retention system: no random timers, no fire-after-X-and-reveal. Events derive only from classified felt state accumulating into desire; if nothing is felt, nothing fires. (4) Negative affect is a valid desire source, not only positive (charter 8.4 failure-is-valid-experience). (5) Upstream posture revised: emo_sim maintainer is a project contributor (also building realtime voice + Discord upgrades) — upstream-first PRs are the norm, fork only for genuinely divergent needs; emo-sim remains a swappable component. (6) Classifier posture: GoEmotions + VAD is the working interim; the long-term direction is the eval harness / activation-probing work (does the felt state match the words — logprob/internal-state introspection); emo-sim is a supplement in those cycles of proactive self-directed autonomy, not the destination.

   This is the system prompt for a separate call that generates HER first-person emotion appraisal chain-of-thought (comment: "You write the companion's private chain-of-emotion appraisal in her own continuous first-person voice"); per file comment, that generated appraisal text later feeds future prompts via runtime_emotion_appraisal_* macros. So this string is the *instruction* steering a generation whose *output* is what she later reads as her own voice — it is not itself literally rendered into her live context the way the sleeptime/reflection blocks are. Judgment call: charter 6.28 explicitly lists "appraisal" as an automata-register domain, so recommend still converting "classifier signals" -> "automata-derived signals" / "instrument readings" for consistency, but this is one layer removed from direct companion-read text (same category question as the memory.extraction / sleeptime.orientation system prompts — see item 9).

9. src/core/identity/prompt-registry.ts (CORE_PROMPT_SEEDS) — EXTRACTION_PROMPT_KEY (:49-117), COMPACTION_SUMMARY_PROMPT_KEY (:123), RECENT_SESSION_SUMMARY_PROMPT_KEY (:133-137), SESSION_SEARCH_SUMMARY_PROMPT_KEY (:144-148), PROFILE_SYNTHESIS_PROMPT_KEY (:155-177)
   These are system prompts for separate subsystem LLM calls (memory extraction, session/compaction summarization) whose *output* (not this literal prompt text) can end up folded into her context (e.g. a compaction summary becomes part of her session history). The prompt text itself uses "user"/"assistant" only in instructive negative examples (":88 Facts about the assistant/system/tools/platform...", ":84 raw character-card macros such as {{user}}... {{assistant}}") and is not something she reads as her own voice.
   KEEP (recommended): these are extraction/summarization-worker system prompts, not her prompt — same bucket as operator/engineering surfaces per the epic's own framing ("memory extraction... are all automata" describes the *concept* she should call these things when she talks about them, not a mandate to rewrite every internal worker's system prompt). Flagging for record only; no action recommended unless operator wants full-depth coverage.

10. src/core/agent/tool-surface/descriptions/operations-contracts.ts:17 (system tool purpose)
   "...under Kubernetes it also reports deployment mode and routes restart/rebuild through the approval-gated kube pipeline."
   Rendered into her tool description for `system`. "pipeline" here names a real external deployment mechanism (Kubernetes), not her own cognition/self — different from the "classifier labels describing her own emotions" case.
   KEEP (recommended): describes genuine infrastructure fact, not clinical self-description; low priority even if operator wants it softened.

title: Codify and auto-apply GitHub PR label taxonomy

Track the catalog and classification rules in focused files with unit tests. title: Add pinned zizmor GitHub Actions security gate
description: Summary: Add zizmor as the dedicated static-security owner for GitHub Actions workflows, local composite actions, and Dependabot configuration. Current reproduced offline baseline (2026-07-20): strict workflow collection initially reported seven artipacked findings because actions/checkout persisted credentials; PR #131 set persist-credentials:false on every checkout, after which `--offline --strict-collection --collect=workflows --format=github .` exited 0 for ci.yml and semgrep-full.yml. Scope: create a repo-owned Docker wrapper/config, run regular-persona strict collection on PRs (at least whenever .github/** or action definitions change), run a weekly/manual full online audit using only the default read-only GitHub token, emit direct GitHub annotations with enforceable exit status, and integrate the deterministic result into ci-required. Use --format=github for enforcement because zizmor SARIF intentionally exits 0 on findings; SARIF may be generated separately only as a retained report. Required permissions are contents:read only, checkout credentials remain non-persistent, and malformed/no-input collection fails closed. Expected files: focused scripts/ci wrapper and tests, zizmor.yml only for exact justified policy, and pinned workflow changes. Non-goals: no automatic fixes, no pedantic/auditor persona as a blocking default, no broad GitHub token permissions, no Semgrep rule duplication, no dependency or container vulnerability scanning, and no floating zizmor Action/image reference.
acceptance_criteria: 1. zizmor v1.27.0 runs from the stated immutable linux/amd64 image digest, verifies its runtime version, and records the image-metadata provenance caveat; no floating Action or tag is used. 2. A required regular-persona job uses strict collection and GitHub/plain output so findings produce nonzero status; malformed inputs, zero collected inputs, and scanner failures fail closed. 3. PR execution covers workflow/composite-action/Dependabot changes without producing a skipped ci-required dependency, and a weekly/manual full online audit runs with only contents:read/default GitHub token access. 4. The current workflow baseline is clean, every checkout keeps persist-credentials:false, and suppressions—if any—are exact, justified, owned, and expiring in zizmor.yml. 5. Wrapper/config tests cover clean input, an intentionally insecure workflow, malformed YAML, no inputs, and scanner failure; test assertions verify exit-code handling, not SARIF success semantics. 6. Pinned-image/version verification, actionlint, offline and online zizmor runs, npm run lint for code changes, repository hygiene, and ci-required pass. 7. The change ships as a focused in-budget PR, is reviewed by Greptile, pushed, and rebase-merged.

title: Regression-cover surface routing after gateway reconnect (2026-07-19 ready-but-unrouted incident)
description: FOUND S10-kube-2026-07-19 fleet SSO/Discord bring-up. title: Tool-outcome classifier reclassifies keyword-matching RETURNED failures as rejections, hiding real failures from runtime-failure telemetry
description:
Evidence (s10p2 seam review of psfn-framework-t9ur, 2026-07-20): src/core/tools/results.ts:211,214 + src/shared/contracts/tool-call-outcome.ts:40-53. A genuine runtime failure that RETURNS structured error details whose diagnostic text matches the invalid_input regex (invalid|required|missing|malformed|...) or the policy_blocked regex (forbidden|denied|blocked|...) is reclassified to validation_rejection / policy_denial and excluded from runtimeFailureCount (src/operator/garden/services/session-turn-observability.ts:449) and the usage-source failures counter. Scenario: a gateway tool that fails with 'Missing required field' or surfaces an upstream real 403 Forbidden as a returned result gets bucketed as a rejection/denial → invisible in the runtime-failure telemetry an operator uses to spot a broken tool.

Bounded (why IMPORTANT not BLOCKER, confirmed by the reviewer): thrown errors hard-set execution_failure (tool-call-scheduler.ts:432, correct); the dominant real-failure classes timeout/unavailable/rate-limited (results.ts:199-206) map to execution_failure correctly. Only RETURNING tools whose diagnostic text contains policy/validation keywords leak, and only into a display metric — no safety or decision path consumes the misclassified outcome. t9ur otherwise verified correct: strict execution_failure gating, exhaustive switches with no permissive default, claim-guard blocks false success claims.

Context: t9ur's contract is to distinguish skips/rejections from runtime failures; this is the inverse leak (a real failure hidden as a rejection) in its own classifier. Scope: classification of a RETURNED error must not downgrade to rejection/denial on diagnostic-text keyword match alone — require an explicit structured outcome signal from the tool (or a rejection/denial reason code) rather than regex-sniffing free-text error messages; real returned failures stay execution_failure. Non-goals: don't change the thrown-error or skip paths (correct). Acceptance: a returning tool failure with 'Missing required field'/'403 Forbidden' text counts in runtimeFailureCount; a genuine validation rejection (structured signal) still classifies as validation_rejection; targeted session-turn-observability + tool-outcome tests; lint green.

title: CogSec remediation preview accepts inverted entry-id ranges
description:
Summary
The Garden CogSec remediation admin service normalizes affected-message ranges without comparing startEntryId/endEntryId. An inverted range (endEntryId < startEntryId) is accepted by the preview/lineage path (which silently sorts min/max and returns results) but rejected by the apply/event path (which throws). This preview/apply asymmetry means an operator can preview a range that then fails to apply, and the preview gives no signal that the range is invalid.

Verified live (2026 audit pass of retired qs83.115):
- src/operator/garden/services/session-service.ts:378-415 normalizeCogSecRanges normalizes startEntryId and endEntryId independently via normalizeOptionalPositiveInteger but performs NO endEntryId >= startEntryId comparison. The only range validation is 'must include messageIds, startEntryId, or endEntryId'.
- Apply path already rejects inverted ranges: src/core/cogsec/events.ts:393-395 throws '${field}.endEntryId must be greater than or equal to startEntryId'.
- Preview path stays lenient: src/persistence/sessions/store.ts:1633-1637 getEntriesInRange sorts via Math.min/Math.max, so an inverted range still yields results in preview.

Scope
Reject endEntryId < startEntryId inside normalizeCogSecRanges (session-service.ts) BEFORE the range reaches preview or apply, so both paths agree. Mirror the existing events.ts guard text/shape for consistency. Apply to BOTH the per-range loop (affectedMessageRanges[i]) and the top-level input.startEntryId/input.endEntryId normalization.

Non-goals
- Do not change getEntriesInRange's min/max sort (it is a correct defensive lower-level primitive; the fix belongs at the admin normalization boundary).
- Do not change the events.ts apply guard (it is already correct).
- Do not touch unrelated CogSec admin normalization.
- Bead 114 (auto-compaction visibility classification) is explicitly out of scope and tracked separately.

Implementation notes
- Read src/operator/garden/services/session-service.ts:378-415 and src/core/cogsec/events.ts:387-395 before editing.
- Reuse the same comparison shape as events.ts for a consistent operator-facing error message.

Acceptance
- normalizeCogSecRanges throws on endEntryId < startEntryId for both the per-range and top-level cases.
- A regression test proves an inverted range is rejected at preview/draft build time (the path that previously accepted it).
- npm run lint passes; close reason names the commit and test evidence.
acceptance_criteria: normalizeCogSecRanges rejects endEntryId < startEntryId for both per-range and top-level inputs; a regression test covers the preview/draft path that previously accepted inverted ranges; npm run lint passes; close reason names commit + test evidence.
close_reason: Fixed in worktree commit 5c827de87 (branch fix/cubic-p2-cogsec-session). Added endEntryId >= startEntryId guard to normalizeCogSecRanges in src/operator/garden/services/session-service.ts for BOTH the per-range loop and the top-level input.startEntryId/input.endEntryId path, mirroring the existing events.ts:393-395 apply-path guard so preview and apply agree. Regression test 'rejects inverted CogSec affected-message ranges at preview time' (session-service.test.ts) covers both paths and passes. title: Fallback failure summary matches arbitrary lines containing 'failed '
description:
Summary
The emergency/fallback tool-failure summary rebuilds the full session summary source block and then stringly filters lines containing the substring 'failed '. Any conversation line that happens to contain 'failed ' (e.g. a user saying 'the deploy failed yesterday', or 'I failed to ...') is misclassified as a compressed tool failure and injected into the 'Earlier tool calls had compressed failures' summary. Only the [Compressed tool failures] aggregate lines should ever feed that summary.

Verified live (2026 audit pass of retired qs83.111):
- src/core/session/manager-primitives.ts:700-702:
    const failureBlock = buildSessionSummarySourceBlock({ entries, characterName })
      .split('\n').filter(line => line.includes('failed ')).slice(-2);
  buildSessionSummarySourceBlock emits a [Conversation excerpt] section (User:/Assistant:/Tool: lines) followed by an optional [Compressed tool failures] section whose lines are formatted as '${toolName} failed ${countText}; latest error: ...'. The substring filter grabs BOTH the real aggregate lines AND any conversation line that contains 'failed '.

Scope
Restrict the fallback failure summary to actual compressed-tool-failure aggregate lines only. Prefer deriving the aggregate lines directly rather than rebuilding the whole block and string-matching it, so the conversation excerpt can never leak into the failure summary. Keep the existing 'Earlier tool calls had compressed failures: ...' output shape and token-budgeting behavior.

Non-goals
- Do not change buildSessionSummarySourceBlock's output format (other callers depend on it).
- Do not change the [Compressed tool failures] aggregate formatting.
- Do not broaden to other summary paths.

Implementation notes
- Read src/core/session/manager-primitives.ts around the fallback failure summary (currently ~695-705) and buildSessionSummarySourceBlock (~585-625) which already builds the toolFailures map internally.
- The cleanest minimal fix exposes the formatted failure-aggregate lines without the conversation excerpt, so the caller no longer needs a substring filter.

Acceptance
- A regression test proves a conversation line containing the word 'failed' is NOT included in the fallback failure summary, while a real compressed tool failure still is.
- npm run lint passes; close reason names the commit and test evidence.
acceptance_criteria: Fallback failure summary is restricted to [Compressed tool failures] aggregate lines; a regression test covers a conversation line containing 'failed' (no real tool failure) not leaking into the summary, and a real tool failure still appearing; npm run lint passes; close reason names commit + test evidence.
close_reason: Fixed in worktree commit b25ad788a (branch fix/cubic-p2-cogsec-session). Extracted collectToolFailureAggregateLines in src/core/session/manager-primitives.ts (derives formatted failure-aggregate lines only from real isError tool observations) and used it in buildRecentSessionSummaryFallbackText, replacing the rebuild-block-and-substring-filter-'failed ' that leaked conversation/tool text containing 'failed' into the compressed-failure summary. buildSessionSummarySourceBlock output format unchanged (non-goal preserved). Regression tests in manager-primitives.test.ts: (1) 'does not misreport tool text containing "failed" as a compressed tool failure' — verified to FAIL on pre-fix code via stash (bug present) and PASS after fix; (2) 'includes a real compressed tool failure in the fallback failure summary' guards the real-failure path. Validation: 1389 tests passed across touched modules; npm run lint clean.

title: CogSec remediation smoke false-passes when keyword search backend is unavailable
description:
Summary
The CogSec remediation smoke script asserts that dirty L0 text returns zero keyword-search hits after revocation, but it never confirms that keyword search is actually working. SessionStore.searchByKeywords returns [] when no transcript search backend is configured, so the zero-hits assertion passes vacuously — the smoke reports a green pass even when the revocation produced no searchable state change at all (e.g. search silently unavailable or unindexed).

Verified live (2026 audit pass of retired qs83.113):
- scripts/cogsec-remediation-smoke.ts:192 only asserts (await sessionStore.searchByKeywords(DIRTY_L0_TEXT, 10)).length === 0.
- src/persistence/sessions/store.ts:1452-1467 searchByKeywords: 'if (!this.transcriptSearch) return [];' — empty result when the backend is absent, so the smoke's zero-hits assertion is satisfied trivially.

Scope
Make the smoke fail when the keyword search backend is unavailable or returns nothing for text that should be findable. Assert a known clean L0 message is searchable BEFORE the dirty-revocation zero-hits assertion, so a missing/unindexed search backend fails the smoke instead of false-passing it.

Non-goals
- Do not change SessionStore.searchByKeywords behavior (the [] return for absent backend is intentional fail-closed at the store level).
- Do not change production CogSec revocation code; this is a smoke/test-quality fix only.
- Do not add a new search backend or wiring.

Implementation notes
- Read scripts/cogsec-remediation-smoke.ts around the search assertion (currently ~190-200) and the fixture setup near the top of the run function.
- Append a clean L0 message in the fixture and assert searchByKeywords(CLEAN_L0_TEXT, ...) returns at least one hit before asserting dirty text has zero hits post-revocation.

Acceptance
- The smoke asserts a known clean L0 message is searchable before the dirty-zero-hits assertion.
- A regression check demonstrates the smoke fails (not false-passes) when the keyword search backend is absent.
- npm run lint passes; close reason names the commit and test evidence.
acceptance_criteria: CogSec remediation smoke asserts a known clean L0 message is searchable before the dirty-zero-hits assertion, so an unavailable/unindexed keyword search backend fails the smoke instead of false-passing; npm run lint passes; close reason names commit + test evidence.
close_reason: Fixed in worktree commit 6b9d32721 (branch fix/cubic-p2-cogsec-session). Added CLEAN_L0_TEXT sentinel + a pre-condition assertion in scripts/cogsec-remediation-smoke.ts that a known clean L0 message is searchable BEFORE the dirty-zero-hits assertion, so an unavailable/unindexed keyword search backend fails the smoke instead of false-passing. SessionStore.searchByKeywords unchanged (fail-closed [] return preserved). Demonstration: forcing transcriptSearch: null makes the smoke fail at the new guard ('keyword search backend unavailable... clean L0 text not searchable') instead of reporting [cogsec-smoke] passed; with the wired transcriptProjection backend the smoke passes end to end. npm run lint clean.

title: Garden admin memory-patch route is dead: AdminMemoryDataService never implements patchMemory so the endpoint always returns 400

title: Deferred memory extraction across a demotion boundary stamps the post-demotion epoch, making pre-demotion content auto-eligible to the demoted-public room
description: Evidence: jp36.6.4 review (2026-07-20). collectDisclosureMemorySources stamps sourceChannelEpoch = channelClassificationEpochAsOf(sourceChannelId, extractedAt) (src/faculties/memory/retrieval/active-context-refresh.ts). extractedAt is the memory FORMATION instant; a pre-demotion invite_only conversation whose memory is extracted AFTER demotion+restart (deferred sleeptime extraction) gets extractedAt > at -> stamped with the current epoch -> destinationEpochEligible passes -> auto-eligible to the now-public room, contrary to bible §9.3 (content admitted under epoch N must not auto-flow after widening). Mainline (extraction before demotion) is correctly fail-closed. Root cause: MemoryProvenance carries no source-conversation timestamp (only sourceMessageIds), so there is no better instant to stamp. Context: partner-data privacy; narrow window (requires demotion + restart + deferred extraction of older conversation content). Scope: thread a source-conversation timestamp through MemoryProvenance/extraction so the epoch as-of instant is the CONVERSATION time, not extraction time; stamp from it in collectDisclosureMemorySources. Non-goals: no changes to the pure epoch gate or the demotion flow. Discovered-from: psfn-framework-jp36.6.4. Branch: feat/jp36-social-autonomy.
acceptance_criteria: Regression test: memory of a pre-demotion conversation extracted after demotion+restart carries the pre-demotion epoch (or undefined) and is approval_required to the demoted channel; mainline extraction timing unchanged; lint + focused retrieval/disclosure suites green.

Commit 62fcd6402 (disclosure epoch anchored to conversation time, fail-closed legacy provenance). Follow-up candidate: earliest-instant straddle bound (PR #248 handoff).

description:

title: Distinguish skipped and rejected tool calls from runtime failures in turn telemetry
description: Follow-up from the completed 2026-07-18 Purrsephone turn-record audit. The operator observed many tool errors and was unsure whether Purrsephone had actually finished. All 47 error-marked calls are now classified from canonical session projections: 25 fs duplicate invocations were intentionally skipped because the same action/input had already succeeded in that turn; 10 fs calls and 1 memory call were dependency skips after an earlier sequential failure; 7 fs calls were argument validation rejections (four max_bytes above 20,000, two context_lines above 2, one missing action); 2 web calls were denied by runtime policy; 1 orient call supplied a non-string persona; and 1 wiki lookup requested a missing document. There were no filesystem runtime crashes or missing final assistant messages. The remaining product problem is observability/reporting: the compact TurnRecord exposes only isError, so expected duplicate/dependency skips are indistinguishable from execution failures and inflate operator error counts. Scope: add a bounded outcome taxonomy to tool-call observability and make operator/Garden projections distinguish executed failures, validation/policy denials, duplicate skips, and dependency skips. Preserve the existing safety behavior and the guarantee that skipped calls are not reported to the user as successful executions. Non-goals: weakening path/runtime policy, raising fs size limits without evidence, or treating invalid arguments as successes.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Tool-call observability records a stable outcome category for success, execution failure, argument validation rejection, policy denial, duplicate skip, and dependency skip while retaining backward-compatible isError derivation only where required. 2. TurnRecord and Garden/operator projections report duplicate/dependency skips separately from actual execution failures. 3. The exact audited duplicate and sequential-skip messages have regression coverage and do not inflate the runtime-failure count. 4. Validation and policy denials remain explicit, fail closed, and visible. 5. Final-response conformance tests prevent claiming execution success for a denied or skipped-only operation. 6. npm run lint and focused turn-record/tool-observability tests pass.
notes: Audit evidence: 43 completed turns, 16 tool-using turns, 206 tool calls, 47 error-marked calls, zero tool turns missing a final assistant response. Canonical projection mapping by call ordinal proved the complete 47-call classification in the description. The original suspected recurrent filesystem runtime fault has no supporting evidence; the remaining issue is outcome taxonomy and operator clarity.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #123 (fix/s10-shakedown-bugfix-p2). Six-outcome tool-call taxonomy across scheduler/TurnRecords/observations/persistence/audit/relay/Garden; runtime-failure count excludes rejections/denials/skips; final-response claim guard. Seam review: no blocker; IMPORTANT (returning-error keyword misclassification) filed separately; audit-only MINORs noted.

title: Define core partner affect estimation and refine Productivity Pack boundaries
description:
Create a production-facing core design document under docs/ for estimating a partner/operator affective support state from governed telemetry, and update docs/productivity-pack.md to reflect the clarified boundaries from the 2026-07-18 operator design follow-up.

The new core document must translate the supplied Sad Brains Detection draft into externally distributable architecture language without personal history, private companion identities, jokey wire messages, self-disparaging language, or diagnostic claims. Preserve the useful mechanism: deterministic multi-signal fusion against personal baselines; transparent weights; uncertainty and missingness; optional bounded model interpretation only after deterministic gating; a hysteretic support-posture state machine; separation of detection, response authority, and environmental actuation; mode-aware interaction/register policy; auditable consent and prospective preferences; fleet-scoped ICP summaries rather than raw feeds; revocation without coercive lock-in; and evaluation based on false positives, latency, usefulness, and recovery—not dependence.

Clarify that core PSFN owns the Partner Affect Estimate, state machine, provenance, privacy, support posture, and companion-facing context. Productivity Pack may contribute additional consented observations such as work cadence, routine completion, calendar shape, delivery/receipt summaries, and other personal-operations signals, but absence of the Pack must not disable core affect estimation. All signals are fallible observations, not medical evidence; the feature is non-diagnostic and must degrade to unknown.

Update docs/productivity-pack.md in two further areas. First, multi-companion satellites: local presence/sensor metadata may be broadcast as a scoped observation to the designated Productivity Companion even when another companion owns the satellite; companions must be explicitly whitelisted to emanate through a device; presence never summons a companion by itself; and when two companions become eligible to speak, the satellite primary gets the first bounded opportunity, with deterministic no-op/timeout handoff before another eligible companion may speak. Second, Thoth/knowledge ownership: Thoth continues to own general wiki/reference data, bulk ingestion, and the user-facing Obsidian reference corpus. PSFN imports only governed human-shape material into a partner dossier/relationship graph—identity, roles, relationships, preferences, routines, and relevant context—with provenance. Both sides use a simple Markdown plus YAML-frontmatter interchange; projections do not create dual authority.

Inspect current charter, emotion/self-model, ICP, satellite registry, presence, memory/wiki, and Productivity Pack contracts before writing. Cross-reference exact current seams and clearly label target behavior as unimplemented.

Scope: docs/productivity-pack.md plus one new production-facing docs design file. Non-goals: no runtime implementation, no medical classifier or diagnosis, no private deployment data, no new generic pack framework, no coercive Ulysses lockout, no changes to Thoth itself, and no CONTEXT.md/ADR.
acceptance_criteria: A new docs design file defines the core Partner Affect Estimate in externally distributable language; separates observation, estimate, posture, response, and actuation; specifies deterministic fusion, uncertainty, hysteresis, missingness, audit, consent/revocation, fleet/ICP privacy, non-diagnostic limits, and evaluation; distinguishes core signals from optional Pack-enriched signals. docs/productivity-pack.md specifies satellite observation broadcast, emanation allowlists, primary-first speaking arbitration, and Thoth versus PSFN human-shape authority with Markdown/YAML interchange. 1. Sparkline.svelte — tiny inline SVG line/area chart. Props: values: number[], width?, height?, stroke/fill via CSS currentColor-friendly classes, optional min/max padding, aria-label + visually-hidden value list for a11y. Must render sensibly for 0/1 points and all-zero series (flat line at baseline, not NaN). Used later for headline-card trends.
2. StackedBars.svelte — vertical stacked bar chart for time buckets. Props: buckets: Array<{ startMs: number; segments: Array<{ key: string; value: number }> }>, series: Array<{ key: string; label: string; colorClass: string }>, timezone, valueFormatter, optional onSelectBucket. Renders: proportional stacked segments (top-N series + automatic 'Other' merge handled by CALLER, not the component — keep it dumb), x-axis date labels (adaptive density: skip labels when crowded), y-axis gridlines with formatted ticks, HTML title tooltips per segment, keyboard-focusable bars with aria-labels, and a legend row with per-series toggle to show/hide that series. Pure SVG, viewBox-scaled so it is width-responsive.
3. TrendDelta.svelte — small "+10.1% vs prev period" pill. Props: current: number, previous: number, invertPolarity?: boolean (cost going UP is bad → red; cache-hit-rate going up is good → green; polarity flag decides), formatter. Handles previous===0 (render '—' not Infinity%) and null previous.
