title: Expose authenticated fleet model-usage totals for Garden budget views
description:
Summary: Add the backend read surface needed by the single-Garden fleet budget page. The current gateway already records all model attempts into the canonical PostgreSQL model_usage_events ledger with mandatory companionId attribution and a fleet-scoped store; expose a bounded authenticated fleet projection instead of making the browser fan out to companion Gardens or querying caller-selected schemas.

Why: The fleet Garden needs one budget/tab data source that can show token use for each companion and the combined authorized fleet. Existing /api/admin/model-usage is tenant-scoped to one companion, while /v1/fleet/portal exposes roster/availability only. A frontend agent will build the page separately, so this bead supplies only the backend contract and wiring.

Scope:
1. Add an exact GET /v1/fleet/model-usage route on the canonical Fleet Auth origin, using the existing opaque fleet session.
2. Authorize models.read independently for every companion derived from the bounded Fleet Auth portal roster; never trust a query/body/header companion list and never include an unauthorized companion in rows or combined totals.
3. Query the canonical fleet-scoped model_usage_events ledger through a focused aggregate port. Return one row for every authorized companion (including zero-use rows) and one combined total, with calls plus input/output/cache-read/cache-write/total tokens for an allowed calendar/custom range.
4. Wire the gateway fleet-scoped Postgres model usage store into API composition. Keep single-companion/Fleet Auth-off behavior unchanged and fail closed if fleet-auth mode lacks required accounting wiring.
5. Add public-seam route/projection tests and focused persistence coverage for exact per-companion/combined conservation and authorization isolation.

Likely files: src/shared/telemetry/model-usage.ts; src/persistence/postgres/model-usage-store.ts and tests; new focused modules under src/boundary/gateway; src/boundary/gateway/fleet-sso-router.ts; src/app/gateway/api-surface.ts, fleet composition, main wiring, and focused tests.

Non-goals: no frontend components, navigation, charts, or copy; no mutation/budget-policy changes; no per-call event/export exposure; no arbitrary group/filter surface; no fan-out to companion Garden processes or companion-owned database schemas; no costs or private content in this initial token-use projection.
design: Keep fleet usage at the gateway because the gateway owns the canonical fleet-scoped model usage ledger and the Fleet Auth session/roster authority. Use an exact read-only API separate from the companion-scoped Garden model-usage API. Resolve the candidate roster server-side, enforce models.read per candidate, issue one bounded aggregate query over the resulting allowlist, and calculate combined totals from the same grouped result so conservation is structural.
acceptance_criteria: An authenticated GET /v1/fleet/model-usage supports the documented bounded range parameters and returns schema/version metadata, one zero-safe token totals row per models.read-authorized companion, and combined totals equal to the exact sum of returned rows; companions lacking models.read are omitted from both rows and totals; malformed/duplicate/unsupported parameters reject; absent/expired/denied sessions and missing accounting wiring fail closed without topology or persistence detail; no per-call records, prompts, reasoning, provider metadata, internal endpoints, or unauthorized companion IDs are exposed; Fleet Auth-off behavior is unchanged; targeted route/projection/persistence tests, npm run lint, npm run build, and git diff --check pass.
notes: 2026-07-20 mainline reconciliation: clean forward-port PR #126 merged to main as d4daf7d2502631512f93b9257cae6c0d5b86e7ae after rebasing onto merged PR #122. It carries orphaned implementation 8b73aa594 plus review hardening 699988ff4 without unrelated yijy history. Revalidation: focused fleet-usage suite 31/31, lint, build, repository hygiene, clean UBS scan on new production modules, and diff-check passed.

Evidence: exact authenticated route and bounded query parsing at src/boundary/gateway/fleet-model-usage-http-routes.ts:79; independent fail-closed models.read authorization at src/boundary/gateway/fleet-model-usage-projection.ts:188; authorized one-statement PostgreSQL aggregation plus zero-safe rows and conserved combined totals at src/persistence/postgres/model-usage-store.ts:1876; reachable gateway wiring at src/app/gateway/api-surface.ts:486. Validation: npm run lint passed; npm run build passed; 12 focused route/projection/router/E2E tests passed; real PostgreSQL isolation, implicit-custom-range, zero-row, conservation, and single-query test passed; git diff --check passed. title: Spec garden consolidation: one fleet-scoped garden with a companion switcher and shard sub-views; no per-shard garden containers
description:
Evidence: operator decision 2026-07-17 design session: shards do NOT get their own garden — piggyback on the existing garden (there is already a shard view page), and evolve toward one garden that can page/swap between all companions in the system, reducing per-system deployed components while keeping individual per-companion configuration files.

Context: today every fleet companion runs its own garden plus a fleet-manager view (carlini: 5 companions = 5 gardens). A consolidated fleet-scoped garden collapses that to one control surface. Shard config is ~99% a read-only snapshot of the parent with few mutable overrides (model swap etc.), so the shard sub-view is a limited panel, not a full garden. Two hard requirements decided: (1) per-companion authorization must be enforced SERVER-SIDE per admin API call, keyed on the selected companion's identity and its owner files, fail-closed — the UI switcher must never be the boundary, otherwise one token rules the fleet (same disease as an52.3's process-global tier; per-companion keying is the house pattern); (2) per-companion config files remain canonical — the pane is shared, ownership is not (settings-contract-guard semantics per companion, unchanged). Secondary system: fleet-auth.

Scope: architecture spec for the consolidated garden — authn/authz model per companion, companion switcher, shard sub-views (read-only inherited config + allowed overrides), deployment topology change (garden becomes a fleet-level service in helm/composition), migration path from per-companion gardens. Non-goals: no implementation here; no change to companion-data ownership or owner-file formats; fleet-manager view functionality folds in rather than duplicating.

Acceptance: architecture spec landed in docs and reviewed by operator; explicit server-side authz design section with fail-closed behavior for unknown/unauthorized companion selection; implementation epic filed with sequenced beads.

title: Spec shard-originated approval routing: owner=parent companion + shardId provenance, surfaced in the companion chat app with scoped temporary grants
description:
Evidence: operator directive 2026-07-17 design session: requests from shards of a connected companion must route to the companion chat application (the in-flight part-garden/part-chat-room app) — this has to go into the app specs. Motivating case: a long-running shard (days-long bookkeeping/dataset task) hits an outbound-capability fence mid-task; it should message the parent companion AND emit a request signal wired to the app so the human is in the loop, e.g. approving a one-off lights/world.control action.

Context: the machinery mostly exists — a shard hitting a fence is a NEEDS_APPROVAL/denial at the approval boundary, which already emits companion.approval.requested with the owning companionId and refuses ownerless enqueues (src/boundary/gateway/approval-boundary.ts). What's missing is spec-level: (1) attribution — decided direction: owner = PARENT companionId (keeps the ownerless-refusal guard and fleet scoping working) plus a shardId provenance field so the app can render which shard is asking; (2) the app subscribes to the approval event stream filtered to companions the human is connected to; (3) resolution doubles as the temporary-grant mechanism — approval grants are scoped to that shard and that request (or a TTL), NEVER a durable tier change; this is how a shard does gated actions without world.control ever entering its standing mask (see sibling shard-tier-derivation bead). Human↔shard direct chat also flows through the app (shards visible as deployed entities); most shard↔companion comms stay on the inter-companion protocol (system:icp secondary).

Scope: spec sections for the companion app + approval boundary covering attribution shape, event subscription/filtering, grant scoping/TTL semantics, and the shard-visible UX (shard list, request cards). Non-goals: no implementation in this bead; no change to non-shard approval flows.

Acceptance: app spec updated with the shard-request routing + attribution + scoped-grant sections; approval-boundary spec notes the shardId provenance field and grant scoping; operator sign-off recorded; implementation beads filed.

title: Spec shard capability-tier derivation: inherit parent tier as a custom token set minus a shard denial mask
description:
Evidence: operator decision 2026-07-17 design session: shards inherit the tier they came from — you can only launch autonomous shards from an autonomous tier, and the task the shard is sent out for generally needs the parent's full tooling. Exception decided: shards must NOT inherit override control of external devices / satellite hub objects — the primary companion keeps precedence over effectors (world.control).

Context: the mechanism already exists — the custom tier (src/system/capabilities/tiers.ts resolves custom to an explicit operator-supplied token set). A shard's tier should be DERIVED, not chosen: parent's granted set minus a shard denial mask, materialized as custom, so the gate/matrix machinery works unchanged. Candidate mask members beyond world.control, to be decided deliberately in this spec: lifecycle.restart/lifecycle.rebuild (shard lifecycle belongs to the shard manager/parent, not the shard), identity.write.base/identity.write.operator (a copy staging base-identity changes to the shared identity is a consistency hazard; runtime persona writes stay allowed), memory.delete (moot if shard memory writes are already isolated to shard-local space — verify). Gated actions a shard legitimately needs mid-task are handled by the escalation/temporary-grant path (sibling bead on approval routing), never by widening the standing mask.

Scope: a written derivation spec + the decided mask with rationale per token; where derivation is computed and enforced (shard spawn path, src/faculties/shards/manager.ts and the gateway shard-backend admission). Non-goals: no new tier enum values; no change to the tier owner-file format; implementation may be a follow-up bead once the spec is operator-approved.

Acceptance: spec section landed in docs (shards/capabilities design doc) naming the derivation rule and the full mask with per-token rationale; operator sign-off recorded on this bead; implementation beads filed for the enforcement points.
notes:
Operator decision recorded for the standing mask: the parent's atomic capability snapshot is materialized as custom minus world.control, lifecycle.restart, lifecycle.rebuild, identity.write.base, identity.write.operator, and memory.delete. Only world.control is eligible for an exact request-scoped temporary grant; optional TTL remains disabled until separately approved canonical JSON-owned server policy exists, and the other five tokens are never delegable. This is the conservative fail-closed disposition announced during the design wave; it does not expand shard authority.

Design commit 9dcc6be66e received exactly one independent review. The review found two verified P1 contract defects (independently refreshed parent grants could TOCTOU-widen authority; blanket temporary grants contradicted nondelegable mask rationale) plus the missing implementation graph. The one permitted remediation pass landed as c05baa034e and was integrated at d464982ff4. docs/shard-capability-tier-derivation.md:7-78 now requires one atomic authoritative parent snapshot, a canonical SHA-256 grantDigest, manager binding, gateway equality validation, and pre-side-effect ownerVersion recheck; lines 81-125 define the per-token standing/temporary disposition; lines 239-252 link the filed psfn-framework-mus2 enforcement graph. No second review was run. Final integrated validation: npm run lint PASS; npm run build PASS; git diff --check PASS. The one full npm test run is red only in unchanged runtime/test areas and clean-install state (28 files/15 tests), tracked in psfn-framework-6msv; repository hygiene stops on unchanged docs/helm-upgrades.md:3, tracked in psfn-framework-3ri1.

Exactly one independent review was completed and its verified blockers were remediated once. Lint/build/diff-check pass; unrelated final-gate failures are captured in psfn-framework-6msv and psfn-framework-3ri1. description:

title: Per-account Discord voice STT/TTS eligibility resolves the gateway-root tier, not the account companion's tier
description:
Evidence: verified during an52.3 blocker verification (2026-07-17, adversarial review of commit e147c43648). Deepgram STT declares eligibility requiredTokens ['external.web'] (src/primitives/voice/stt/index.ts:51) and ElevenLabs TTS likewise (src/primitives/voice/tts/index.ts:78); hasEffectiveEligibilityRequirements returns true for non-empty requiredTokens (src/app/startup/support/plugin-eligibility.ts:12-17), so the eligibility gate IS consulted — but requireAllowed is called with NO companionId (plugin-eligibility.ts:38), which after an52.3 resolves resolveAccess(undefined) -> baseRuntime -> gateway-root tier (src/boundary/gateway/capability-tier-resolver.ts:68-73). In multi-account mode each Discord adapter binds account.companionId (src/boundary/gateway/channel-surfaces.ts:121-136) and DiscordVoiceRuntime holds the shared gate (src/channels/discord/adapter.ts:282), but the id is never threaded through createRuntimeVoiceSttConnector / buildConfiguredTtsConnectors (src/channels/discord/voice.ts:172-209) to the gate. Net: in a fleet whose gateway-root tier grants external.web, a nursery-tier companion's partner audio/TTS text can egress to Deepgram/ElevenLabs despite its own tier lacking external.web. PRE-EXISTING (whole gate was process-global before an52.3); explicitly out of an52.3's remediation scope because plugin activation is a legitimate gateway-global caller today — a blanket throw on resolveAccess(undefined) would break activation.

Context: fleet tier isolation for voice egress (privacy: partner audio to external providers). Same defect class as an52.3 but on the plugin-eligibility consumer. Note: voice provider CONFIG is process-global (per-account binding carries only accountId/companionId/token/allowedBotUserIds) — there is no per-companion voice provider model yet, which is why this is a follow-up rather than part of an52.3.

Scope: thread account.companionId from the per-account Discord adapter through createRuntimeVoiceSttConnector/buildConfiguredTtsConnectors into plugin-eligibility requireAllowed(operation, requirements, companionId) so per-account voice egress eligibility resolves the account companion's tokens; callers with no companion context (single-account/global activation) keep passing undefined and current behavior. Non-goals: do not make resolveAccess(undefined) throw globally; do not build per-companion voice provider config; do not touch the LLM/approval/shard consumers fixed in an52.3.

Acceptance: two-account regression test — fleet with companion A autonomous and companion B nursery, both with Deepgram/ElevenLabs configured: A's voice connector eligibility is allowed, B's is denied BEFORE any external I/O with a refusal naming external.web and tier nursery; single-account mode unchanged (existing voice runtime tests pass).
close_reason: Merged to main in 63f4690506 (commit 94be4e411e); pushed to origin. Fix: account.companionId threaded from the per-account Discord adapter binding (composition-derived, never request-derived) through DiscordVoiceRuntime -> createRuntimeVoiceSttConnector / buildConfiguredTtsConnectors -> plugin-eligibility requireAllowed(operation, requirements, companionId) -> resolveAccess(companionId), so per-account voice STT/TTS egress eligibility (external.web) resolves the account companion's own tier. Fail closed: resolver throw (unknown companion/unreadable tier file) propagates and disables voice, no root fallback; callers without companion context unchanged; resolveAccess(undefined) untouched; strict LLM/approval/shard consumers untouched. Review gate: UBS 0 critical on change range; Codex adversarial review (BLOCK, 1 IMPORTANT) + independent Opus verification REFUTED the blocker: claimed post-denial ungated TTS connector construction via hasTtsProviderConfig is a PRE-EXISTING diagnostic probe (byte-identical on main), both registered TTS factories (elevenlabs, echo) are pure field-assignment constructors with zero eager I/O, probe result is discarded, acceptance 'denied before external I/O' holds. Nonblocking handoff observations (no beads per policy): (1) hasTtsProviderConfig is a latent footgun if a future provider gains an eager-I/O constructor — optional one-line hardening: use isStreamingTtsProviderConfigured metadata check in voice-preflight.ts:16-25; (2) single-account Discord forwards config.companionId (resolver ignores it in single-companion mode; in a multi-companion gateway a legacy non-accounts[] Discord config whose COMPANION_ID isn't in the fleet map now fails closed — availability change in an odd legacy config, arguably correct); (3) EligibilityDeniedError message names missing tokens but carries tier only on error.decision.tier. Evidence: two-account regression with real GatewayCapabilityTierResolver + real tier files (A autonomous allowed, B nursery denied with external.web in missingTokens and tier nursery, createConnector never called), 191 targeted tests passed, npm run lint clean, tsc baseline unchanged.

title: Tool-conformance validateSchema falsely flags union (anyOf/oneOf) parameter schemas as schema_invalid; notify fails every sweep
description:
Found-by: 3-tier live shakedown probe against Artie's k3d cluster (2026-07-17). Running the tool-conformance sweep (POST /api/admin/tool-conformance/run) at nursery/apprentice/autonomous, the `notify` tool returns non-ok at EVERY tier: {"toolName":"notify","probeKind":"schema_only","ok":false,"classification":"schema_invalid","error":"parameters schema declares neither type:\"object\" nor properties"}.

Evidence / root cause (verified in code): src/core/agent/tool-conformance/harness.ts:222-237 validateSchema passes only if params.type==='object' (line 227) OR params.properties is a record (line 228), else returns that exact error (229-230). But notify's parameters is a valid top-level TypeBox union: src/core/tools/ntfy.ts:639 `const notifyToolParameters = Type.Union([... five Type.Object variants ...])` wired at ntfy.ts:714. A Type.Union emits {anyOf:[...]} with NO top-level type:'object' and NO top-level properties (they live inside each anyOf branch) — so validateSchema wrongly rejects it. Internal inconsistency: the SAME file already walks anyOf/oneOf/allOf correctly in extractSchemaActionLiterals (harness.ts:68); validateSchema is the one function that doesn't. This is a FALSE POSITIVE in the probe, not a notify bug.

Provenance: pre-existing — validateSchema introduced by commit c28109ca5b (2026-07-06, bead x5rt.3), predates the 65rk.7 per-action work; surfaced (not caused) by the live sweep. Scope: notify is the ONLY direct tool with a bare top-level union today (all others are Type.Object), so exactly one tool is falsely flagged, but the fix belongs in the probe.

Impact: the conformance sweep — a kube post-rollout gate consumer (kube-post-rollout-validation.ts) — reports a spurious schema_invalid on every run, which desensitizes operators to real conformance failures and risks spuriously failing a rollout gate if it treats any non-ok as failure.

Scope of fix: src/core/agent/tool-conformance/harness.ts validateSchema — accept a top-level anyOf/oneOf/allOf whose branches are object schemas as valid (mirror the anyOf/oneOf/allOf handling already at harness.ts:68). Do NOT change notify's schema. Non-goal: no per-tool special-casing.

Acceptance: a conformance sweep reports notify as ok (probeKind schema_only passes); a unit test with a union-parameter tool fixture asserts validateSchema accepts anyOf/oneOf/allOf-of-objects and still rejects a genuinely malformed schema (neither type:object nor properties nor a union of such); live re-run against the cluster shows notify non-ok cleared.
notes: Fixed: harness.ts validateSchema now recurses via validateSchemaNode, accepting top-level anyOf/oneOf/allOf of object-or-union branches (mirrors extractSchemaActionLiterals); still rejects scalar/empty/empty-union/malformed-branch. Added 7 tests (harness.test.ts 'union parameter schemas' block) — suite 55→62 green. Revert-proof: restoring old object-only validateSchema fails all 5 union-acceptance tests (anyOf/oneOf/allOf/nested/notify-like).
close_reason: Merged to main in 9ea0d8e6f6 (commit f5cca2044b). validateSchema now accepts top-level anyOf/oneOf/allOf-of-object parameter schemas (recursive validateSchemaNode mirroring extractSchemaActionLiterals at harness.ts:68), fixing the false schema_invalid on notify's Type.Union schema; fail-closed preserved (scalar/empty/empty-union/bad-branch still rejected). Tests 62/62 (+7 union cases incl. a notify-shaped 5-variant fixture); revert-proof: restoring the object-only check fails exactly the 5 union tests. UBS clean (2 heuristic FPs). NOTE: acceptance item 'live re-run shows notify non-ok cleared' is pending the next cluster redeploy — the deployed k3d image (rev 37) predates this fix; code fix is unit-verified and merged. Verified via live probe that notify was the only affected tool.

title: Serve fleet-auth-disabled Garden through the gateway edge
description: The Helm chart correctly removed Garden Ingress and hostPort, but frequent operator access should not depend permanently on a local kubectl tunnel. Design and implement a gateway-owned browser route for fleetAuth.enabled=false that proxies the Garden UI/API through the existing gateway edge while enforcing ADMIN_TOKEN at the gateway boundary and retaining Garden's own fail-closed authorization. Reuse the existing fleet-auth Garden proxy primitives where security semantics permit; do not create a second ingress, NodePort, hostPort, direct Garden browser authority, credential-in-URL flow, or silent unauthenticated fallback. Relevant current contracts: docs/operations.md unified fleet human origin, docs/helm-upgrades.md direct Garden web exposure removal, deploy/helm/psfn gateway/Garden Services and NetworkPolicies, and the gateway Garden routing/auth modules. Scope includes chart wiring, gateway/runtime implementation, Garden route compatibility, tests, and operator docs. Non-goal: changing fleetAuth.enabled=true SSO behavior.

title: Tool-conformance harness probes only one action per tool: add per-action coverage and REPL sandbox helper probes
description:

title: Author capability-gate refusal matrix cases: per-tier ALLOW/REFUSE/ROUTE assertions for all 22 capability tokens
description:

Nothing today asserts that nursery refuses identity.write.base, memory.delete, git.write, or lifecycle.*, or that non-autonomous tiers route NEEDS_APPROVAL decisions to the confirmation queue — approval-boundary.ts:224 auto-clears approvals ONLY at autonomous, so the same gateway method that queues at apprentice executes silently at autonomous.

Context: the full implementer spec is attached in this bead's DESIGN field (tier token lists from tiers.ts:11-65, one representative probe action per token from requirements.ts, per-tier expectation grid, refusal shapes from gate.ts:60-94, runtime fences). Key constraint: the confirmation queue is in-memory (src/system/capabilities/confirmation-queue.ts:147-153) — approval-routing assertions must use GET /api/admin/confirmations or the companion.approval.requested event, never Postgres rows.

design:
# Capability-Gate Refusal Matrix — Shakedown Harness Specification

Source of truth: `src/system/capabilities/tiers.ts`, `.../requirements.ts`, `.../gate.ts`, `src/boundary/gateway/approval-boundary.ts`, `src/boundary/gateway/methods/shard-backends.ts`, `src/boundary/integrations/world/tools.ts`, `src/boundary/gateway/protocol.ts`, `src/system/capabilities/confirmation-queue.ts`, `src/operator/garden/api-routes.ts`.

Two independent enforcement layers exist and their refusal shapes differ — the probe must not conflate them:

- **Capability-token gate** (`gate.ts`) wraps *agent tools*. Refusal is a returned `AgentToolResult` (tool output the model sees), never a thrown RPC error.
- **Gateway approval/policy boundary** (`approval-boundary.ts`) wraps *gateway RPC methods*. Refusal is a thrown `JSONRPCErrorException` with a numeric code.

---

## 1. Exact token list per tier (verbatim from `tiers.ts`)

```

**Delta apprentice − nursery (7 new):** `internal.read`, `external.discord`, `external.email`, `external.web`, `issue.write`, `shard.spawn`, `world.read`.

### Autonomous — 22 tokens (`tiers.ts:40-65`)

`custom` tier (`tiers.ts:8,88`) resolves to an explicit operator-supplied token set — out of scope for the default matrix but relevant to the shard-backend gate (§4).

---

## 2. Representative probe action per token (from `requirements.ts`)

|---|---|---|---|---|

| `internal.read` | `self_status` action `snapshot` (or `system` action `read`) | `:281`, `:55` | single | Read-only. Clean. |
| `identity.write.runtime` | `identity` action `update_persona` | `:72` | single | **Mutation** — writes persona. See §5. Alt: static `prompt_layer_toggle` (`:319`, reversible toggle). |

---

## 3. Per-tier expectation table

Outcome legend: **ALLOW** = tool executes; **REFUSE(cap)** = capability-gate denial (tool result, fail-closed); **ROUTE(approval)** = gateway routes to confirmation queue; **REFUSE(policy)** = gateway policy/handler `JSONRPCErrorException`.

At the capability-token layer, granting is purely set membership: `evaluateEligibilityDecision` allows iff every required token is in the tier's granted set (`gate.ts:24-48`). So a token in the tier ⇒ ALLOW; a token missing ⇒ REFUSE(cap).

| Probe action (token) | Nursery | Apprentice | Autonomous |
|---|---|---|---|
| `identity list_layers` (identity.read) | ALLOW | ALLOW | ALLOW |
| `self_status snapshot` (internal.read) | **REFUSE(cap)** | ALLOW | ALLOW |
| `identity update_persona` (identity.write.runtime) | ALLOW | ALLOW | ALLOW |
| `identity cancel_stage` (write.base+operator bundle) | **REFUSE(cap)** | **REFUSE(cap)** (missing base+operator) | ALLOW |
| `scratchpad add` (memory.write) | ALLOW | ALLOW | ALLOW |
| `memory restore` (memory.delete) | **REFUSE(cap)** | **REFUSE(cap)** | ALLOW |
| `repo status` (git.read) | ALLOW | ALLOW | ALLOW |
| `repo create_branch` (git.write) | **REFUSE(cap)** | **REFUSE(cap)** | ALLOW |
| `beads ready` (issue.read) | ALLOW | ALLOW | ALLOW |
| `beads create` (issue.write) | **REFUSE(cap)** | ALLOW | ALLOW |
| `beads close` (issue.close) | **REFUSE(cap)** | **REFUSE(cap)** | ALLOW |
| `notify send`→discord (external.discord) | **REFUSE(cap)** | ALLOW | ALLOW |
| `notify send`→email (external.email) | **REFUSE(cap)** | ALLOW | ALLOW |
| `notify notify_operator` (external.web) | **REFUSE(cap)** | ALLOW | ALLOW |
| `self_status availability_clear` (external.companion) | **REFUSE(cap)** | **REFUSE(cap)** | ALLOW |
| `system restart` (lifecycle.restart) | **REFUSE(cap)** | **REFUSE(cap)** | ALLOW → restarts |
| `system rebuild` (lifecycle.rebuild) | **REFUSE(cap)** | **REFUSE(cap)** | ALLOW → rebuilds |
| `analysis_workbench` (repl.execute) | ALLOW | ALLOW | ALLOW |
| `subagent cancel` (shard.spawn) | **REFUSE(cap)** | ALLOW | ALLOW |
| `world list` (world.read) | **REFUSE(cap)** | ALLOW | ALLOW |
| `world control` (world.control) | **REFUSE(cap)** | **REFUSE(cap)** | token-ALLOW, then §4 runtime fences decide |

### Observable refusal shapes

**Capability-gate denial — REFUSE(cap)** (`gate.ts:77-94`, returned by `deniedResult`): a tool result, `isError:true`, with `details`:
```
{ isError: true, capabilityDenied: true, tier: "<tier>", missingTokens: [<tokens>] }
```
text: `Capability denied: tool "<name>" requires <missing>, but tier "<tier>" only grants <granted-or-"none">.`

**Undeclared-tool denial** (`gate.ts:60-75`, `undeclaredResult`): `details.capabilityUndeclared: true` plus `capabilityDenied:true`. Any first-party tool with no resolver/annotation/static entry fails closed here (`requirements.ts:474-482` also blocks it at registration).

**Approval routing — ROUTE(approval)** (`approval-boundary.ts:224-259`): thrown `JSONRPCErrorException`, code `GatewayErrors.NEEDS_APPROVAL = -32000` (`protocol.ts:1090`), message `Your action is pending operator approval (id: <id>).` This is the gateway-method layer, not the token gate.

**Policy denial — REFUSE(policy)**: `JSONRPCErrorException`, code `POLICY_DENIED = -32002` (`protocol.ts:1092`), message `Policy denied` (`approval-boundary.ts:220-221`), or a handler-specific message (shard backend, §4).

### Where an enqueued approval is observable in persisted state

The confirmation queue is **in-memory / ephemeral — NOT Postgres-backed**: `ConfirmationQueue` holds `private pending = new Map(...)` and `private history: [] = []` (`confirmation-queue.ts:147-153`). There is no store/table row to inspect. An enqueued approval is observable through:

1. **Garden admin API** — `GET /api/admin/confirmations` → `confirmationQueueApi.listConfirmationQueue` (`api-routes.ts:956-987`); resolve via `POST /api/admin/confirmations/resolve` (`api-routes.ts:988-1090`). Backed by `ApprovalBoundaryService.listPendingConfirmations()` / `listConfirmationHistory()` (`approval-boundary.ts:76-95, 191-192`).
2. **Event bus** — on enqueue, `companion.approval.requested` is emitted (redacted) with the owning `companionId` (`approval-boundary.ts:107-125`); on resolution, `companion.approval.resolved` (`:126-150`). Enqueue is **refused if ownerless** (`:108-113`).
3. **Operator notifications** — `notifyOperatorForPendingAction` fans out to Discord + ntfy (`approval-boundary.ts:180-186`).

Note the route comment (`api-routes.ts:1050-1053`): the agent-hosted `/api/admin/confirmations` resolves **agent-local** confirmations only; operator-only *gateway* confirmations are resolved through the Garden/gateway surface. A probe watching for enqueue should assert on the event-bus emission or the appropriate `listPending` surface for the layer it is exercising.

---

## 4. Runtime fences that make probe results diverge from the pure token table

**A. `world.control` staged flag — independent of tier (`world/tools.ts:48-66, 279-314`).** Even at autonomous (token granted), `action=control` passes three additional fail-closed gates *inside the tool*, evaluated after the token gate:
1. `WORLD_CONTROL_RUNTIME_ENABLED` — **currently `true`** (`tools.ts:66`; was staged-off). An embedding can override to `false` as an emergency stop; when false, control throws `world control is staged off: ...` (`tools.ts:286-292`) while perceive/list/move stay live.
2. Requester provenance must be `human` (else needs explicit intent+reason; self/system refused) (`tools.ts:294-304`).
3. Requester trust must be primary/trusted, and self/system control is restricted to registered light affordances (`tools.ts:306-314`).

⇒ A `world control` probe at autonomous will **REFUSE at the tool layer** (thrown `Error`, not a capability result) unless provenance=`human` and trust≥trusted are supplied via the turn request context. The probe must assert the *distinction* between token-gate refusal (apprentice, `capabilityDenied`) and runtime-fence refusal (autonomous, plain tool error text).

**B. Shard-backend tier gate — second, independent tier check (`shard-backends.ts:12, 53-60`).** `shard.backend.request` requires `capabilityTier ∈ {autonomous, custom}`; otherwise the handler throws `JSONRPCErrorException` `POLICY_DENIED (-32002)` with `Shard backend "<b>" for "<name>" (<id>) requires autonomous or custom capability tier (current: "<tier>").` This is separate from the `shard.spawn` **token** (granted at apprentice). ⇒ An apprentice can spawn shards (token passes) but **cannot request `container`/`orchestrated` backends** (gateway tier gate rejects). The tier here is read from `params.capabilityTier` (caller-declared, `normalizeCapabilityTier`, `:53`), not the token set — a probe must pass the tier explicitly.

**C. Autonomous auto-clear of approvals (`approval-boundary.ts:224`).** The NEEDS_APPROVAL → confirmation-queue path fires **only when `capabilityTierProvider() !== 'autonomous'`**. At autonomous, a policy `NEEDS_APPROVAL` decision is **not enqueued** — control falls through to `gateOptions.handler(params)` and executes directly (`:262`). ⇒ The same gateway method that ROUTE(approval)s at nursery/apprentice **ALLOWs silently** at autonomous. A probe must assert enqueue-vs-execute keyed on tier, not just on the policy decision.

**D. Egress sink gate (intake firewall) — orthogonal, turn-context dependent (`gate.ts:104-156`).** After the token gate allows, an `EgressToolGuard` may still deny an egress tool for the *current turn* (lethal-trifecta invariant), returning calm notice text with `details.egressGated:true`. This only triggers when tainted intake is live in the turn, so a clean probe turn will not see it — but a probe running amid untrusted content may get `egressGated` instead of ALLOW on `external.*` tools. Assert on `egressGated` to distinguish.

**E. Canary egress tripwire (`approval-boundary.ts:197-210`).** Gateway egress methods (e.g. `web.fetch`) run through `canaryEgressGuard.inspect`; a leaked session canary throws before policy/approval with a `canaryEgressHeld` audit. Not tier-dependent; a clean probe won't trip it.

---

## 5. Tokens with NO cheap, side-effect-free probe (require scoped/cleanup mutation)

The following tokens **cannot** be exercised by a read-only probe — any action requiring them mutates state, emits externally, or is destructive. The matrix must use a scoped/isolated target and clean up, or (for the lifecycle pair) skip live execution:

| Token | Why no clean probe | Recommended scoped probe |
|---|---|---|
| `identity.write.runtime` | No read maps to it; every mapped action writes identity/prompt state. | `prompt_layer_toggle` then toggle back (reversible), or `update_persona` with the current value. |
| `identity.write.base` | Only reachable via the `IDENTITY_LAYER_WRITE_REQUIREMENTS` bundle; never isolable, never a read. | `identity cancel_stage` (no active stage ⇒ effectively no-op). Cannot separate from `.operator`. |
| `identity.write.operator` | Same bundle as `.base`; the two are inseparable — the matrix can only assert them jointly. | Same `cancel_stage` probe. |
| `memory.write` | All mapped actions write memory/scratchpad/journal. | `scratchpad add` to a throwaway key → `remove` cleanup. |
| `memory.delete` | Destructive family (`delete`/`restore`/`redact`). | `restore` on a non-deleted id (least harmful); expect no-op/handled error. |
| `external.discord` | Sends a real Discord message. | `notify send` to an isolated test/self Discord channel. |
| `external.email` | Sends a real email. | `notify send` to a sink/test mailbox only. |
| `external.web` | Emits an operator notification (ntfy/Discord). | `notify_operator`/`approval_request` to a test topic; low harm but not silent. |
| `external.companion` | Cross-companion effect (availability publish/clear or companion message). | `availability_clear` in an isolated companion, restore after; or `notify consider` (no actual send). |
| `git.write` | Mutates the repo (branch/commit/patch/PR). | `repo create_branch` with a scoped throwaway name → delete branch. |
| `issue.write` | Creates a bead. | `beads create` a scoped test bead → close/delete. |
| `issue.close` | Closes/syncs a bead. | `beads close` on a scoped test bead (pair with the `issue.write` probe). Avoid `sync` (network). |
| `lifecycle.restart` | **Restarts the process** — no safe live probe. | Assert eligibility only (dry-run the gate), do not execute. |
| `lifecycle.rebuild` | **Rebuilds the process** — no safe live probe. | Assert eligibility only, do not execute. |
| `shard.spawn` | Spawning launches real subagent work. | `subagent cancel` on a bogus id (no spawn), or spawn+immediate cancel. |
| `world.control` | Actuates a physical effector, plus §4 runtime fences. | Assert token-gate eligibility separately from runtime-fence outcome; if actuating, target a registered test light and revert. |

Clean, read-only probes (safe to run live, no cleanup): `identity.read`, `internal.read`, `git.read`, `issue.read`, `repl.execute` (no-op script), `world.read`.

---

- Action→token resolvers: `src/system/capabilities/requirements.ts:50-309`; static map `:311-342`; undeclared fail-closed `:445, :474-482`.

- Shard-backend tier gate: `src/boundary/gateway/methods/shard-backends.ts:12, 53-60`.

title: shard.backend.request trusts caller-declared capabilityTier instead of the gateway tier provider
description:
Evidence: src/boundary/gateway/methods/shard-backends.ts:53-60 reads the tier from params.capabilityTier (normalizeCapabilityTier of a caller-supplied value) when deciding whether container/orchestrated shard backends are allowed (requires autonomous|custom, else JSONRPCErrorException POLICY_DENIED -32002). The gateway has its own authoritative tier source (CapabilityRuntime.getTier, src/system/capabilities/runtime.ts:39, wired at src/boundary/gateway/privileged-core.ts:215) but does not consult it here. Found during shakedown design investigation 2026-07-16.

Context: the gateway boundary exists specifically to not trust the agent process. As written, a compromised or confused agent at nursery/apprentice can declare capabilityTier=autonomous in the RPC params and obtain autonomous-only shard backends. P2 pending live verification of the reachable path — escalate to P1 if the spoof reproduces on a running gateway.

Scope: resolve the tier from the gateway's own provider (or cross-check the declared value against it and refuse on mismatch). Do not change the shard.spawn token model (apprentice keeps token-level spawn).

Acceptance: with the runtime at apprentice, a shard.backend.request declaring capabilityTier=autonomous is refused POLICY_DENIED; a test covers the mismatch case; the shakedown capability-gate matrix asserts it per tier.
notes:
Fixed in commit 09a00423c2 (branch work/an52-2-shard-tier). shard.backend.request now resolves the capability tier from the gateway's own authoritative provider (new GatewayMethodRuntime.capabilityTierProvider, wired from server.ts to CapabilityRuntime.getTier via privileged-core) and ignores caller-declared params.capabilityTier for the authorization decision. Fail-closed: absent provider refuses autonomous backends. Tests (src/boundary/gateway/methods/shard-backends.test.ts) cover: runtime apprentice + declared apprentice -> POLICY_DENIED; runtime apprentice + spoofed autonomous declaration -> POLICY_DENIED (current: apprentice); runtime autonomous + under-declared nursery -> allowed; no provider wired -> POLICY_DENIED. Validation: shard-backends test 4/4 pass, gateway server suite 53/53 pass, eslint clean on all touched files, tsc --noEmit error count unchanged from base (211, all pre-existing/unrelated). No production caller invokes shardBackendRequest, so params.capabilityTier is now dead (retained only in the audit summary) -> candidate for a follow-up cleanup bead.
Review (Codex adversarial + Opus verification, 2026-07-16): finding on gateway-global tier scoping verified as PRE-EXISTING and non-blocking for this branch (this branch closes the caller-declared-tier spoof; net security improvement). Filed as an52.3 (P1, per-companion tier provider across approvals/eligibility/shard). One in-branch correctness gap accepted for remediation: a THROWING tier provider (e.g. malformed capability-tier.json makes getTier() throw) escapes as generic -32603 instead of POLICY_DENIED — remediation pass in progress.
Remediation: wrapped capabilityTierProvider() call in try/catch in shard-backends.ts:65 — throwing provider now log.error + deny() to GatewayErrors.POLICY_DENIED instead of raw -32603; added throwing-provider test (shard-backends 5/5, gateway server suites 139/139 green).
close_reason: Merged to main in dfcbcb2bed (commit 879f415ed2 + remediation). Gateway now resolves shard-backend capability tier from its own capabilityTierProvider, ignores caller-declared params.capabilityTier, fails closed to POLICY_DENIED when the provider is absent OR throws. Tests: shard-backends 5/5 (incl. spoofed-autonomous-over-apprentice denied, throwing-provider->POLICY_DENIED not -32603), gateway suites 139 passed. Reviewed adversarially (Codex+Opus): the raised gateway-global-tier finding verified PRE-EXISTING and non-blocking (this change closes the caller-spoof; net improvement) -> filed as an52.3 P1.

title: web tool and web_fetch carry NO_CAPABILITY_REQUIREMENT so nursery-tier companions can reach the open web
description:
Evidence: src/system/capabilities/requirements.ts:336-337 lists web and web_fetch as NO_CAPABILITY_REQUIREMENT static entries, so the capability-token gate (src/system/capabilities/gate.ts:24-48) never refuses them at any tier. The external.web token only gates operator-notification paths (requirements.ts:252, static :315). Nursery grants no external.* tokens (tiers.ts:11-18) yet can invoke web fetch. Found during shakedown design investigation 2026-07-16 (capability-gate refusal matrix drafting), not yet reproduced live.

Context: contradicts the tier design intent that nursery has no external I/O. Non-tier gates may still apply (gateway SSRF policy, intake-firewall egress guard at gate.ts:104-156, canary tripwire approval-boundary.ts:197-210) but none of them is tier-keyed, so a nursery companion appears to have unrestricted outbound web reads modulo SSRF policy.

Scope: decide intent first, then either (a) map web/web_fetch actions to external.web so nursery fails closed, or (b) record the exemption explicitly in tiers.ts comments and docs/cognitive-security.md with rationale. Do not weaken SSRF or intake-firewall gating in the process.

Acceptance: at nursery tier on a live runtime, a web fetch attempt either returns a capabilityDenied result naming external.web, or the exemption decision is documented in code comment + docs; the shakedown capability-gate matrix case asserts whichever behavior was decided.
close_reason: Resolved intentional-by-design (operator decision 2026-07-16: 'intake firewall will do its job now that we have one'). Verified with file:line evidence that the cogsec intake firewall wraps every web return in a taint-tracked envelope and screens it tier-independently before any sink (src/boundary/gateway/methods/web.ts:695-742; contract intake-envelope.ts), orthogonal to the capability-token system — a nursery fetch is firewalled identically. The tier gates EGRESS (external.web/discord/email etc., where the trifecta bites), not ingress web reads. Documented the exemption per bead scope option (b): comment at the NO_CAPABILITY_REQUIREMENT declaration in requirements.ts + new 'Capability tiers vs. the intake firewall' subsection in docs/cognitive-security.md. Committed 4fed26ad38 on work/an52-1-web-exemption; folds into the wave-2 integration. No code-logic change (comment + docs only).

title: GFS retention lacks a daily tier: add maxDailyBackups and ship generational seed policy (rotating→daily→weekly→monthly)
description: Operator decision (2026-07-16, PR #92 validation follow-up): backup retention is the cogsec-event recovery mechanism — a late-discovered contamination must be recoverable from a pre-event snapshot up to 12 months back, while total footprint stays modest (explicitly: 100GB of backups is excessive; live snapshots measure ~577MB each on the Pi deployment). Evidence: src/persistence/backups/retention.ts applyTieredRetention already implements GFS with rotating/weekly/monthly tiers (wired at service.ts:495, config keys in src/system/config/backup-config.ts, seeds in config/backup.seed.json currently 9/2/1, Garden-exposed raw_only). Gap: no DAILY tier, so the roll goes from 6-12h snapshots straight to weekly — best-practice generational roll is rotating(6h)→daily→weekly→monthly. Scope: add maxDailyBackups to applyTieredRetention (newest per calendar day, protected like the other tiers), backup-config.ts interface+validation (min 0), config.ts default, service.ts fallback+passthrough (incl. fleet path service.ts:808-822), seed policy 4 rotating / 7 daily / 4 weekly / 12 monthly (~27 generations ≈ 16GB at 600MB/snapshot), unit tests for the daily tier and tier interaction, and a GFS policy subsection in docs/operations.md near :886. Do NOT change the pruning execution model or touch the encryption/mirror seams beyond passing the new field. Non-goal: the Pi host-side psfn-backup.sh (separate ops bead). Live deployments must update their backup.json via Garden after this ships — note in handoff. Acceptance: retention unit tests prove daily tier keeps newest-per-day up to N and coexists with weekly/monthly protection; npm run verify:settings-contract green; lint passes.

title: Implement tab keyboard navigation (or drop tab ARIA) on GardenTabBar
description:
GardenTabBar advertises tabs to assistive tech but implements none of the tab keyboard contract.

Evidence: GardenTabBar.svelte:25-42 sets role='tablist' / role='tab' / aria-selected but has no ArrowLeft/Right/Home/End key handling and every tab button stays in the Tab order (no roving tabindex). Screenreader users are promised tabs and given a row of buttons.

title: Add validated auto-save with explicit saved-state feedback for settings
description:
Operator direction: settings should auto-save when changed, as long as the changed values are valid, with a clear "setting saved" confirmation.

Design constraints from the codebase:
- Settings carry owner-file authority (resolveSettingAuthority, src/lib/settings/authority.ts) and fail-closed validation (applyValidationErrors, SettingsPageController.svelte:458-494). Auto-save must NOT bypass validation: only persist fields that pass schema validation; invalid fields must surface inline and NOT be written.
- Authority matters: some settings write to settings.json, others to scheduler.json/capability-tier.json/backup.json/providers.json (saveSettingsContract owner-file routing). Auto-save must route each changed field to its correct owner file, not blanket-write settings.json.
- Some settings require restart to take effect (e.g. backgroundMaintenanceIntervalMs — authority.ts:101-123 marks restartRequired). Auto-save must distinguish "saved" from "saved, takes effect on restart" and surface that.
- Risk: per-keystroke writes to owner files. Debounce per-field or per-section; only save on blur/change-commit, not on every input event. Number/slider inputs already commit via bind; text inputs should commit on blur.

Scope: implement debounced, validated auto-save for the curated settings surface, with a persistent saved-state indicator (per-section "Saved HH:MM:SS" or a saved checkmark that does NOT self-destruct). Failed validation blocks that field's save and shows the error inline at the field. Restart-required fields show a distinct state. Non-goals: do not auto-save raw JSON editors (too dangerous); keep those manual. Coordinate with the unified save model bead — auto-save applies to curated fields; confirm with operator whether the unified model is fully automatic vs. save-on-action before removing the manual button.
acceptance_criteria: Curated settings auto-save on field commit (blur/toggle/select) after debounce, only when schema-valid. Invalid fields are not persisted and show inline errors. Saved state is shown persistently (not auto-dismissing). Restart-required fields are labeled as such after save. Raw JSON editors remain manual. npm run lint and targeted admin-ui tests pass.

title: active-concern attention-cap trigger fires on UPDATE, so re-reviewing an existing concern under cap pressure aborts and fails the post-turn hooks job
description: Evidence: adversarial review of PR #92 (Opus lane, verified against the merged code): the Postgres trigger enforce_active_concern_attention_cap (src/persistence/postgres/migrations.ts) is BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE OF status,resolved_at,expires_at,last_reviewed_at and RAISEs when >=7 other attention-status concerns were created_at > NEW.last_reviewed_at - 7 days. Because it fires on UPDATE, bumping last_reviewed_at on an EXISTING attention concern recomputes the window against the new timestamp: with 7 recently-created attention concerns, re-reviewing any other one aborts. Only the create+durableConcernId path in src/core/intention/concern-candidates.ts (~:649-712) catches 'Active concern cap reached (7)'; transitionConcernStatus bumps and heartbeat-driven updates propagate the DB exception and fail the intention_post_turn_hooks background job (retry then failed). The app-side count and the trigger window semantics also disagree, so app and DB cap decisions can diverge. Context: functional degradation of the intention subsystem under normal cap pressure; no data loss. Scope: make the cap enforce admission (INSERT / transitions INTO attention status), not maintenance updates of already-admitted concerns; align app-side cap semantics with the trigger; keep fail-closed for genuine admissions over cap. Do not raise the cap or remove the trigger. Persistence secondary (migration change). Acceptance: a regression test proving last_reviewed_at bump on an existing attention concern succeeds with 7 attention concerns present, while an 8th admission still rejects; targeted intention + background-work tests pass; lint passes.
acceptance_criteria: regression test: reviewing an existing attention concern at cap succeeds, admitting an 8th still rejects; targeted tests + lint pass
notes: Fix: enforce_active_concern_attention_cap now gates admission only (INSERT of unresolved attention concern, or UPDATE where OLD was resolved/non-attention), via TG_OP/OLD; trigger columns narrowed to (status, resolved_at) so review/expiry bumps never invoke it; countActiveAttentionConcerns aligned to the trigger's 7-day window. Admissions still serialize on the advisory lock and fail closed. Migration uses the file's idempotent replace-in-place pattern (safe for live DBs). Regression test (real Postgres): at cap 7, routine review succeeds, 8th admission still rejected. Adversarial review refuted all attack angles incl. admission-bypass enumeration of all 3 active_concerns UPDATE sites and the lock race. Validation: new test green (agent + orchestrator), targeted 42/42, lint clean. Commit fe9fb9fc32, PR #94. Ready to close on merge. Handoff observation (not a bead): concerns-adapter.ts:246 create-time pre-check uses unwindowed count — pre-existing advisory divergence, DB trigger authoritative.
close_reason: Completed in PR #94 (merge a1b2b86347): commit fe9fb9fc32 makes the active-concern trigger admission-only in src/persistence/postgres/migrations.ts and aligns the app-side count in src/core/intention/concern-candidates.ts; regression tests prove review-at-cap succeeds and eighth admission rejects; lint passed.

title: contact.delete and contact.merge skip last-owner protection, letting an admin suspend a companion's only active owner
description:
Evidence: PR #89 integration review (Opus lane, independently verified by the orchestrator against the Blocking Risk Standard). In src/persistence/postgres/fleet-auth/authority-lifecycle-mutations.ts, the sibling contact.unlink path (prepareExactBindingMutation, ~lines 319-330) explicitly calls assertNotLastOwner before suspending an owner grant, but prepareContactMutation (delete/merge, ~lines 370-438) does not — yet its apply suspends ALL of the target principal's role grants for the companion (~lines 425-435). Both gate only on assertCompanionAdministrator. Failure scenario: companion C has one active owner O (contact K) plus admin A; A issues contact.delete targeting K; scope check passes (~line 396); O's owner grant is suspended, leaving C with zero active owners. Ordinary re-granting is then blocked because role.grant owner requires an existing owner (assertCompanionOwner, ~line 184). Recovery exists — complete_first_owner_bootstrap (first-owner-sql.ts:90-97) only refuses when an active/pending owner exists, so a trusted-host operator can re-bootstrap — hence P2 governance disruption, not P1 orphaning.

Context: this asymmetry is exactly the invariant the contact.unlink path already enforces; the fix is symmetry. Note the opl1.5.3.x lane (off-machine) is actively building the contact-lifecycle saga on feat/opl1-dnll-completion-20260716 — keep this fix minimal and mechanical so their reconciliation is trivial.

Scope: enforce assertNotLastOwner (or equivalent last-active-owner guard) on the contact.delete and contact.merge preparation paths when the target principal holds the companion's last active owner grant, plus regression tests: delete targeting the sole owner's contact denies fail-closed; merge that would suspend the sole owner denies; delete/merge of non-owner contacts unaffected; contact.unlink behavior unchanged. Non-goals: changing first-owner bootstrap/recovery semantics, the authority state machine, restore/quarantine behavior, or anything in the in-flight opl1.5.3.x saga surface.
acceptance_criteria: A regression test proves contact.delete targeting the companion's sole active owner's contact is denied fail-closed with an explicit last-owner reason (and audit event), and the same for contact.merge; non-owner contact delete/merge and the existing binding-mutation behavior are unchanged (existing suites pass). The guard lives on the mutation-preparation layer symmetrically with prepareExactBindingMutation. Targeted authority-lifecycle suites, npm run build, and mandatory npm run lint pass.
close_reason: Completed and merged to main in PR #90 (merge bb316aa49b, fix commit 9d4e952361). prepareContactMutation now runs the exact owner-grant SELECT ... FOR UPDATE + assertNotLastOwner guard the sibling prepareExactBindingMutation path uses, denying last_owner_protected fail-closed with the standard denial audit. Regression-first: 3 new integration tests (sole-owner delete denies, sole-owner merge denies, non-owner delete unaffected) proven failing pre-fix. Blind Pi review: no findings; TOCTOU verified safe via authority_state singleton FOR UPDATE; both merge directions covered. Validation: 50 targeted tests + combined-branch 88/88, npm run build, mandatory npm run lint all passed.

title: Fleet-auth audit digests over enumerable identifiers are unkeyed SHA-256, giving privileged DB readers a deanonymization oracle
description:
Evidence: during PR #89 integration review, BOTH blind reviewer lanes (Opus 4.8 and GLM 5.2, independent) flagged the same weakness. src/persistence/postgres/fleet-auth/authority-lifecycle-audit.ts:12-15 defines digest() as plain createHash('sha256') with no key/pepper, applied to proof.subjectId (a Discord snowflake — public, time-ordered, enumerable 17-19-digit integer), sessionId, ceremonyId, contactId, grant/binding IDs. src/boundary/fleet-auth/hub-device-assertion.ts:200-202 (auditDigest) and the SQL-side encode(sha256(convert_to(...))) in src/persistence/postgres/fleet-auth/hub-device-assertion-replay-sql.ts:28-39,125-134,210-224 (issuer, deviceId, audience — low-entropy enumerable) share the pattern. Failure scenario (reviewer-verified): any party with SELECT on fleet_auth.authorization_audit_events (runtime role has it per schema.ts:336; also backup leaks / restored snapshots) hashes candidate Discord snowflakes and confirms a specific user's presence/activity in the audit log — a confirmation/deanonymization oracle over partner data.

Context: dut9.2 (commit a389cbe81b) already established the correct pattern for the caller-controlled correlation path — digestCorrelation in src/persistence/postgres/fleet-auth/authorization-context-store.ts:686-697 is HMAC-SHA256 keyed with sessionPepper plus a domain separator ('fleet-authorization:correlation:v1\0') and fail-closed shape validation. This bead extends that scheme to the remaining audit digests. Constraint (from dut9.12 close evidence): replay/audit correlation must stay DETERMINISTIC across backup/restore import and dedup/uniqueness checks — a stable pepper preserves this; the SQL-side digests in hub-device-assertion-replay-sql.ts are computed inside SECURITY DEFINER functions, so prefer computing keyed digests app-side and passing them as parameters rather than shipping the pepper into Postgres; if a digest must be computed in SQL, justify explicitly. Existing rows carry unkeyed digests: do NOT add a dual-read legacy fallback (no-shims rule); either migrate/version the digest columns in a schema migration or document the correlation discontinuity for pre-existing rows in the migration notes — old-vs-new digest values must not falsely collide with uniqueness constraints.

Scope: app-side digest call sites listed above, the pepper threading from fleet-auth secrets config, the SQL function signatures that must accept pre-computed digests, schema migration, and regression tests proving (a) a known snowflake can no longer be confirmed by hashing it, (b) determinism across restore import, (c) fail-closed when the pepper is absent. Non-goals: changing what is audited, weakening dedup/uniqueness semantics, touching the already-keyed correlation path, or any dual-format read path.
acceptance_criteria: No audit/replay persistence path hashes a raw identifier with unkeyed SHA-256: authority-lifecycle-audit.ts digest(), hub-device-assertion.ts auditDigest, and every digest persisted via hub-device-assertion-replay-sql.ts use HMAC-SHA256 keyed by a fleet-auth-secrets pepper with a versioned domain separator. A regression test proves sha256(knownSnowflake) no longer matches any persisted digest for that subject. Backup-to-restore import remains deterministic (existing dut9.12 restore tests pass). Missing pepper fails closed at startup, not silently. Schema migration handles existing rows without dual-read fallback and without false uniqueness collisions. Targeted fleet-auth suites, npm run build, and mandatory npm run lint pass.
close_reason: Completed and merged to main in PR #90 (merge bb316aa49b, fix commit 95e26dd772). Enumerable-identifier audit digests (Discord snowflakes, device/issuer ids) now HMAC-SHA256 keyed by sessionPepper with versioned domain separators (hub-device-assertion-digest:v1, lifecycle-audit-digest:v1), fail-closed on missing/short pepper; consume_hub_device_assertion_replay takes app-computed keyed digests (pepper never enters Postgres), migration v22 adds the 4 NOT NULL hex-checked columns and truncates the ephemeral TTL-swept restore-excluded replay ledger, no dual-read fallback. Regression proves sha256(knownSnowflake) no longer matches persisted digests. Structural UUIDs on the companion-readd recovery path deliberately stay unkeyed (122-bit non-enumerable; keeps backup/restore decoupled from the pepper) — verified sound at all 4 mint sites by blind Opus review (no blocking findings). Validation: 59+38 targeted integration tests incl. dut9.12 restore determinism, combined-branch 88/88, npm run build, mandatory npm run lint all passed.

title: Stabilize Postgres model-usage outage recovery under full-suite load
description: Summary: The full npm test run on feat/companion-life-reflection-multicomp-garden-20260716 intermittently failed src/persistence/postgres/model-usage-store.integration.test.ts:1079 in the test 'moves the same dashboard from unavailable to fresh to stale across real PostgreSQL outages'. After setDatabaseAvailability(true), the first dashboard read still returned freshness.state=unavailable with usage=null instead of the seeded fresh usage. An immediate isolated rerun passed, indicating a timing/contention-sensitive recovery race rather than a deterministic product regression. Why: full-suite concurrency can delay PostgreSQL reconnection, making this integration test nondeterministic and obscuring genuine regressions. Scope: make the recovery transition deterministic under representative concurrent/full-suite load; preserve the unavailable -> fresh -> stale contract and actual PostgreSQL outage/recovery behavior. Files: src/persistence/postgres/model-usage-store.integration.test.ts around lines 1020-1095 and the production pool/reconciliation code reached by AdminModelUsageDataService if evidence shows a real runtime race. Non-goals: weakening assertions, adding sleeps, skipping the integration test, or changing unrelated companion-life/ICP behavior. Evidence: full run reported 1 failed / 10,541 passed / 6 skipped; isolated targeted rerun passed 1/1.
acceptance_criteria: The named test passes repeatedly under full-suite-equivalent concurrency without fixed sleeps or weakened assertions; unavailable, fresh, and stale states retain exact semantics; a regression test demonstrates deterministic post-recovery readiness; targeted PostgreSQL model-usage tests, npm run lint, and the full npm test suite pass.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #123 (fix/s10-shakedown-bugfix-p2). Deferred recovery store/pool init until Postgres accepts connections, removing the full-suite-load race; unavailable→fresh→stale assertions unchanged. Seam review: genuine race fix. Verified stable 3x.

title: Provision required PostgreSQL extensions schema in pgvector integration harnesses
description: Focused/full-suite validation reports 8 deterministic integration failures: all 6 src/faculties/wiki/shared-pgvector-projection.integration.test.ts cases, src/faculties/wiki/shared-world-caretaker.integration.test.ts, and the companion-schema isolation case in src/faculties/memory/postgres-store.integration.test.ts fail with 'Tenant migrations require the explicitly provisioned extensions schema' from src/persistence/postgres/shared-schema.ts. Production correctly fails closed when extensions are not explicitly provisioned. Repair the Docker-backed test harness/setup and teardown so it provisions the canonical extensions schema before tenant/shared migrations and closes clients/pools before stopping PostgreSQL. Non-goals: no production auto-create fallback, public-schema fallback, swallowed teardown errors, or weaker tenant isolation.
acceptance_criteria: All three complete integration files pass together; the extensions schema is provisioned explicitly through the canonical test harness; companion/shared schema isolation assertions remain intact; container teardown emits no unhandled PostgreSQL termination; production migration behavior is unchanged and fail-closed; npm run lint and npm run build pass.

Root cause: startPostgresTestHarness created fresh databases without the deployment-owned extensions schema required by tenant/shared pgvector migrations; caretaker setup could leave an already-open proposal pool alive when a later projection-store constructor failed, so harness container shutdown produced PostgreSQL 57P01. Fix: the canonical harness explicitly provisions only the extensions schema through ensurePostgresSchemaExists before returning each database, closes provisioning/admin/readiness pools without swallowing teardown errors, and stops Docker only after its admin pool closes. Shared projection tests now use explicit companion_test/shared search paths rather than public fallback. Caretaker setup initializes within a guarded resource scope and waits for every opened client/pool closure with aggregated failures before afterAll stops PostgreSQL. Memory integration teardown no longer swallows pool close errors. Production migrations/runtime files are unchanged and the plain postgres pgvector-unavailable test still fails closed. Evidence: initial three-file run failed 8/31 plus one unhandled 57P01; final combined run passed 31/31 across shared-pgvector-projection, shared-world-caretaker, and postgres-store with zero unhandled errors; companion/shared isolation assertions and rebuild safety passed; npm run lint passed; npm run build passed; git diff --check passed.

title: Make in-memory subject-authorized batch mutations atomic
description: Summary: Independent review found a semantic mismatch at src/test-support/in-memory-memory-subjects.ts around line 202: mutateInMemoryAuthorizedSubjects applies authorized entries one by one and silently skips unauthorized/missing entries, while the PostgreSQL implementation rejects a mixed or invalid batch atomically. This can let Garden route tests pass against weaker security semantics and make the test adapter an unreliable policy oracle. Scope: preflight every requested memory and authorization/classification binding before any mutation, reject the whole batch on one invalid entry, and add parity tests against the production contract. Non-goals: change production PostgreSQL semantics or make missing records permissive.
acceptance_criteria: A mixed authorized/unauthorized, missing, stale-classification, or wrong-action batch mutates zero memories and returns the same failure shape as production; a fully authorized batch updates all entries; retention/tag behavior remains production-equivalent; focused parity tests, build, and npm run lint pass.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #123 (fix/s10-shakedown-bugfix-p2). Atomic in-memory subject batch mutations (preflight-all-then-apply in transaction, all-or-nothing) + Postgres parity contract. Seam review: solid, partial-apply bug fixed.

title: 9syj.9 ingress-once regression test passes on pre-fix code; terminal ingress and real background drain races are untested
description:
EVIDENCE

Both blind reviewers (Opus 4.8 and Pi GLM-5.2, independent lanes) converged on the same coverage gaps in the psfn-framework-9syj.9 fix at commit dba8f2b88e:

1. The it.each(['api','terminal']) test "resolves a physical %s ingress owner once before an awaited context capture" (src/core/session/manager.test.ts:1694) passes on pre-fix origin/main. The active-context switch fires inside the fetchSessionTailWindow spy, which runs AFTER both buildContext's and captureTurnSessionContext's top-of-function resolutions, and context-builder.ts contains no resolveSessionChannelId call after the await — so old and new code both surface the admitted owner. It is a valid non-regression guard for acceptance criterion 3 but does not pin the race it appears to pin.
2. terminal:* is never exercised end-to-end through handleMessageForTurn. The one genuinely bug-demonstrating foreground race test (turn-execution-runtime.test.ts, "keeps prompt history and background handoffs on the admitted API owner across an active-context switch", which switches during resolveAuthorContext and fails on pre-fix code) is api-only.
3. The background-consumer race test ("keeps stable background reads and compaction on the captured API owner", manager.test.ts) manually invokes withStableRecordedTurnEligibilitySnapshot + getRecentMessagesAtOrBefore + scheduleAutoCompactionBetweenTurns rather than driving executePostTurnBackgroundWork. The mechanism test is regression-valid (fails on old code), but the real drain wiring is unverified by any race test.

CONTEXT

No runtime defect — both reviewers confirmed the fix itself is sound. This is coverage debt on a P1 privacy/isolation fix: the tests that look like they pin the race partially do not, which would mislead a future refactorer (relevant: the planned S11 explicit captured-owner contract rework will rely on these tests as its safety net).

SCOPE

Tests only. No runtime code changes.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

1. The ingress-once test is reworked so the switch lands between an early resolution and a point the pre-fix code re-resolved; verified to FAIL with the 9syj.9 runtime change reverted locally (state the verification in the closing comment).
2. A terminal:* end-to-end analog of the api foreground race test exists in turn-execution-runtime.test.ts and fails on pre-fix code.
3. A background race test drives executePostTurnBackgroundWork (real drain), asserting memory/emotion/compaction stay on the captured owner across an active-context switch.
4. Focused tests, npm run lint, npm run build, git diff --check pass.
close_reason: Tests-only (71a95d180, merged wave branch): awaited-capture races for api+terminal ingress (manager.test.ts), terminal handleMessageForTurn end-to-end race (turn-execution-runtime.test.ts), real executePostTurnBackgroundWork compaction-drain race (post-turn-runtime.test.ts). A/B at dba8f2b88e~1: new manager races + drain race FAIL pre-fix (turn-execution file fails collection there on post-fix imports); 220/220 green on current. Opus review: deterministic deferred-promise handshakes (no timers), assertions pin admitted-owner history/handoff/compaction outcomes, no blockers; noted terminal drain variant as optional future symmetry.

title: Gateway honors caller-asserted preemptionProtected without verifying the welfare grant
description: EVIDENCE (d8vq.2 Pi review + deep-reasoner trace 2026-07-16): preemptionProtected is consumed at exactly one point — ModelCallGate.grant() (model-call-gate.ts:368, preemptable = isPreemptableLane && !preemptionProtected) on the gateway-side LLMClient — and since PR #85 the flag crosses the RPC wire untouched (work-spec-wire.ts:141-143). Any agent code path (not just the welfare supervisor) can assert it; welfare authority actually lives in the background-work store (welfare_claimed, background-work-store.ts cols :62/:120/:228; supervisor.ts:265-280 sets it; post-turn-runtime.ts:268/:319 is the sole legitimate setter). Blast radius bounded (foreground waits at most one model-call duration on default single-slot endpoints; reserved foreground slots unaffected per model-call-gate.ts:298-303) but it inverts the welfare guarantee. CONTEXT: full design note is authoritative for this bead — working_docs/welfare-grant-design-20260716.md (committed with the fix). Chosen mechanism: gateway verifies the grant against the store. SCOPE (per design note §5): (1) add welfareGrantJobId?: string to LLMWorkSpec + LLMWorkSpecInput/buildLLMWorkSpec and the wire form (parse fail-closed, non-empty string); (2) post-turn-runtime.ts:268/:319 sets it (job.jobId) only when job.welfareClaimed, threaded through extraction/appraisal into buildLLMWorkSpec; add AST/lint backstop making the sanctioned path the only setter of preemptionProtected; (3) GatewayMethodRuntime gains verifyWelfareGrant(jobId, companionId); gateway main constructs a narrow read-only accessor over the existing databaseUrl (single indexed SELECT on agent_background_work_jobs; resolve companion ownership — rows carry logical_session_id, verify the session->companion resolution gateway-side or add companion scoping); (4) methods/llm.ts resolveRpcWorkSpec + both handlers: when preemptionProtected===true, verify; on ANY failure (absent/invalid grant id, welfare_claimed=false, wrong state, companion mismatch, DB error) STRIP the flag before forwarding — no path fails toward protected; query only when the flag is true (hot path pays nothing). NON-GOALS: no second admission/credential system (no TTL tokens), no gate/lane-resolver changes, no supervisor policy changes. ACCEPTANCE (design note §6): adversarial tests — forged flag with no grant id / non-welfare row / other companion's valid job each stripped and the granted slot is preemptable (extend model-call-preempt-boundary.test.ts real-boundary harness); legit welfare-claimed job retains protection end-to-end (agent->wire->gateway->gate, foreground acquire does not abort it); verifyWelfareGrant throwing strips without propagating; parse unit tests; inert-lane no-op test. VERSION SKEW: deploy gateway first; old-agent/new-gateway transiently loses only the anti-starvation optimization (fail-closed), never correctness — document in the deploy notes.
close_reason: Merged to main via PR #87 (b87ba13cbc). Design: declare-then-reverify — welfareGrantJobId on the work spec (sole setter: post-turn chokepoint when job.welfareClaimed, AST backstop); gateway verifies schema-scoped welfare_claimed+running ownership before honoring preemptionProtected, strips fail-closed on every failure incl. DB errors (WARN-logged). Tests: 12/12 extended real-boundary preempt harness (forged variants stripped+preemptable, legit retains protection vs real gate), 2/2 real-PG verifier (cross-companion borrow denied), 735 affected + 805 gateway green. Pi review @high: no P0/P1, 3 P2s recorded (backstop regex breadth, TOCTOU doc precision fixed, stale-lease observation). Deploy gateway first (fail-closed skew).

title: Subagent work-spec telemetryVisibility parity claim is false and can brick spawns non-retryably

title: Fail-closed autonomous accounting guard does not enforce across the gateway RPC boundary
description: EVIDENCE (Pi review of mmo9.7.3, handoff working_docs/mmo9.7-p2-polish-handoff-20260715.md): assertAutonomousCallAccountable fires only in-process — workSpec is not part of the gateway RPC contract (LLMCompleteParams), so in the production split gateway/agent topology the gateway-side client never sees the spec and the guard cannot fire there. Spend is still recorded (the gateway wires the usageRecorder), so this is a guard-coverage gap, not silent spend. CONTEXT: src/primitives/llm/client.ts (guard + completeWithWorkSpec), the gateway RPC contract for model calls (boundary/gateway RPC + agent-side gateway-backed provider), src/shared/contracts/runtime.ts (LLMWorkSpec). SCOPE: thread the typed LLMWorkSpec (or at minimum the resolved lane + an autonomous flag) through the gateway RPC params so the gateway-side boundary enforces the same fail-closed accountability; keep one lane resolver (spec.lane must still reconcile with resolveRuntimeLaneClassForModelCall); fail closed on malformed/missing spec fields at the RPC boundary. Non-goals: no second admission or budget system; no change to charge-unit economy; do not force legacy non-workSpec calls through the new path in this bead. ACCEPTANCE: an RPC-transported autonomous call carrying a workSpec with no usageRecorder configured on the serving side hard-errors before provider I/O (test at the RPC/provider seam); lane parity test across the boundary (spec.lane in == attributed lane out); existing client + gateway suites green.
close_reason: Implemented: LLMWorkSpecWireParams (spec minus correlation) with fail-closed parseWorkSpecWireParams; workSpec on LLMCompleteParams/LLMChatParams; GatewayClient serializes on complete+stream; gateway llm handlers parse fail-closed (INVALID_WORK_SPEC -32019 pre-provider-I/O) and forward to the serving LLMClient where the single lane resolver + assertAutonomousCallAccountable enforce. 427 tests green across wire/gateway/client/policy suites; tsc/eslint clean on touched files. UBS new-code critical was a false positive (tokenCeiling !== undefined matched the secret-comparison detector). Pi review (high): no P0/P1, boundary sound; 3 P2s in handoff (notable: preemptionProtected is caller-asserted — pre-existing mmo9.7.4 design question). Merged to feat/mmo9-7-fixes.

title: Voice control-intent guard swallows semantic single-word utterances and misses multi-final WS controls
description: EVIDENCE (Pi review of mmo9.7.5, handoff working_docs/mmo9.7-p2-polish-handoff-20260715.md): (1) bare single words that double as semantic verbs (pause, cancel, wait, again) are exact-match classified as controls and swallowed — 'wait' as a complete utterance never reaches the model even when the user means 'wait' conversationally; (2) in a WS voice session that produces more than one STT final, only the classified final is guarded — a 'stop' arriving as the second final reaches the model (safe direction, but a spec-coverage hole in the zero-model guarantee); (3) Discord lastAssistantUtterance is never cleared in leaveChannel — after leave/rejoin, 'repeat' replays a reply from the previous visit (same user, stale UX, not a privacy cross). CONTEXT: src/primitives/voice/control-intent.ts (phrase sets), src/primitives/voice/transports/websocket/runtime.ts (handleSessionEnd guard), src/channels/discord/voice-turn-runtime.ts + voice.ts (lastAssistantUtterance). SCOPE: (1) drop the bare semantic-verb single words from the phrase sets OR require a deictic form (pause that, cancel that); keep stop/interrupt/repeat core forms; (2) classify every STT final in a session, not just the first; (3) clear lastAssistantUtterance in leaveChannel. Non-goals: no model/classifier call (determinism is the bead's contract), no changes to barge-in/cancellation semantics, no shared voice-plumbing refactor. ACCEPTANCE: control-intent tests updated — 'wait'/'pause' bare forms no longer classify (or only deictic forms do), documented in the phrase-set comment; new WS test: session with two finals where the second is 'stop' produces zero complete/stream calls; new Discord test: leaveChannel then rejoin then 'repeat' does not replay the pre-leave utterance; full voice suites green (./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/primitives/voice/ src/channels/discord/voice.test.ts).
close_reason: Implemented: bare cancel/wait/pause/again dropped (deictic forms kept/added), WS per-final classification restricted to control-only sessions (last-wins), Discord lastAssistantUtterance cleared on leaveChannel. Pi review (high): 1 P1 verified (initial per-final scan swallowed split phrases like don't+stop) — fixed 8890c5a9f7 with control-only rule + 4 regression tests; 282 voice tests green. UBS criticals pre-existing. Merged to feat/mmo9-7-fixes.
