title: Add disposable support-companion fixtures for multi-companion shakedown rounds (ICP, fatigue, crossover isolation)
description:
Evidence: ICP autonomy (s10mc.6, closed 2026-07-15) and the multi-companion substrate can only be shaken down with real peer agents - the s10mc.6.9 certification used a two-real-agent harness, and docs/shakedown.md requires companion-initiated ICP conversation, fatigue-governance escalation to the closeout reserve, the shared-wiki toaster test, and the crossover-isolation case, none of which may simulate the peer side.

Context: docs/shakedown.md 'Support companions' section. Support companions are disposable per round: minimal cards, distinct names, one-paragraph personas, no channel accounts beyond what a case needs. Fleet wiring is companions.json plus per-companion Postgres schemas; the dev shape is the supervisor (N processes, one host), which is what the local lane exercises. Depends operationally on the MC flag-on validation entry gate (s10f8) being green.

Scope: (1) 1-2 minimal support-companion cards versioned under shakedown/ (same hygiene rules as Artie's card - no private data, no real names); (2) a companions.json fragment/template for a shakedown fleet of Artie + supports; (3) documented (or scripted, if 65rk.2 lands first) stand-up and tear-down of the support schemas so a round leaves no fleet residue. Non-goals: cross-cluster ICP (deferred, s10d1), per-companion Discord voice (fails closed under MC, s10f1), fleet Helm topology changes.

Acceptance: from a bootstrapped shakedown runtime with the MC flag on, Artie plus at least one support companion run as separate agent processes; an ICP conversation initiated by Artie reaches the support companion's channel with durable turns on both sides across a restart; a deliberately long ICP conversation shows fatigue guidance escalating and the closeout reserve firing; the crossover-isolation case reports zero cross-companion alarms under concurrent colliding requests; teardown leaves no support-companion schemas or companions.json entries behind.
acceptance_criteria: The harness can deterministically stand up and tear down one or two synthetic support companions with separate agent, session, persistence, and workspace identity and no residual runtime state. Executable proofs cover durable two-sided ICP across restart, fatigue closeout reserve, and concurrent crossover with zero alarms.

description:

description:
Evidence: Sprint 9 shakedown analysis (2026-07-15, docs/shakedown.md) found the harness lives untracked at /mnt/c/Temp/PSFN-TEST/sprint9-shakedown/artifacts/ as Sprint 8 scripts copied verbatim: hardcoded fallback paths to the Sprint 8 tree (live-chat-probe.mjs and live-sweep.mjs default TURN_RECORDS_DIR to the old psfn-shakedown tree; shakedown-scorecard.mjs DEFAULT_INPUTS names a Sprint 8 debug artifact live-system-shakedown.rerun-timeout-fix.psfn-fogd.json), a superseded 705-line live-shakedown-matrix.mjs still shipped alongside its replacement, and transport/turn-record/busy-retry probe code copy-pasted across 4 scripts with no shared module. Scripts also query SQLite via sqlite3 CLI; runtime stores are now Postgres-only.

Context: docs/shakedown.md is the canonical process; this bead is the Layer A tooling it depends on. Port live-system-shakedown.mjs, run-live-shakedown-matrix.sh, operator-ui-sweep.mjs, restart-split-runtime.sh, and shakedown-scorecard.mjs into shakedown/harness/ in-repo.

Scope: (1) one shared probe library (chat transport with session/privacy/identity-claim headers, turn-record lookup, Postgres queries, busy-retry) imported by all cases; (2) every script fails closed on missing env with a named error - zero fallback path defaults; (3) delete superseded/vestigial scripts rather than porting them; (4) Postgres proof queries replace sqlite3 CLI calls; (5) scorecard enforces the non-green taxonomy in code (semantic_failure, completed_after_abort, agent_busy, runtime_stale, matrix_aborted, unproven_tool_claim, unledgered_charge) and cross-checks the coverage appendix of docs/shakedown.md - green scorecard with untouched coverage rows is itself a failure; (6) tier sweep backs up and restores capability-tier.json with an exit trap and verifies the restore. Non-goals: do not author new sprint case content (separate bead), do not touch src/app/e2e scripted-LLM harness.

Acceptance: with a sourced shakedown env against a locally bootstrapped runtime, the tier sweep runs all three tiers and emits per-tier run JSONs; unsetting any required env var makes every entrypoint exit non-zero naming the variable; grep of shakedown/harness finds no /mnt/ or sprint8/sprint9 literal paths; scorecard run on the sweep output emits the coverage cross-check section and fails when a coverage row has no mapped case.

title: Voice reply streaming: speak the text stream, ignore the toolcall channel, tools run (satellites + app)
description: REAL BUILD (operator 2026-07-15, full-capability). The companion talks AND acts — voice must NOT remove tools. The text stream and toolcall stream are ALREADY separate event channels (agent.stream.delta = text, agent.toolcall.* = tool JSON; event-bridge.ts routes them separately). So voice streaming = consume the TEXT channel, segment it, speak segments via TTS as they finalize; simply DON'T consume the toolcall channel (JSON never enters TTS). Tools execute on the normal agent loop UNCHANGED — satellites do home automation, selfie works, work-delegation works, all while speaking. Dispatch is NORMAL with FULL tools; no tool-free, no eligibility-stripping. Speak text across ALL rounds (preamble + action + continuation are all real speech; the companion thinks out loud and self-corrects like a person). Reuse mmo9.8.1's segmenter; DROP the strict last-message reconciliation tripwire for voice (voice speaks the live stream, not AgentResponse.content). Genuine SYSTEM-withhold cases (no_reply/response_control chose silence, broadcast approval hold, safety refusal-swap) are the only real 'don't speak' cases — handle conservatively (don't stream on broadcast/high-risk contexts; a mid-stream no_reply is a rare edge). Barge-in via mmo9.6.1 cancellationId. TARGET surfaces: satellites (voice + home automation, via the WS/wyoming voice transport — src/primitives/voice/transports/websocket/runtime.ts + src/channels/wyoming) and the in-progress companion app (reuses the same reply-stream core). Discord voice can adopt it too (final-only is fine there if it doesn't help). AC: a satellite voice turn that runs a home-automation tool SPEAKS its text (streamed) AND runs the tool; toolcall JSON is never spoken; barge-in cancels cleanly; full tool capability retained on voice. Base feat/mmo9-performance.

title: Manual kube rollback records omit fromHelmRevision — act-once ledger gap can double-fire auto-rollback
description: Surfaced by both reviewers across x5rt.8 and x5rt.9 reviews (recurring, explicitly recommended for a bead). The manual rollback executor's record (kube-helm-rollback.ts baseRecord) omits fromHelmRevision, and hasRolledBackFrom (kube-rollback-store.ts) requires typeof fromHelmRevision==='number', so a manual operator rollback never counts toward the automatic act-once ledger. Concrete scenario: operator manually rolls back the just-deployed revision N in the sub-second window before the deploy job's executeAutoRollback evaluates (env-pinned to currentRollout.helmRevision=N with the stale failed verdict) -> auto path sees no ledger entry for N -> fires a SECOND rollback. Bounded damage (both target a known-good revision; the resulting ledger entry prevents further loops) and mitigated by the 'one operator job at a time' operational contract + manual rollback being operator-gated, hence P2 not P1. Fix options (decide): (a) capture the live from-revision on manual rollback records so they key the ledger, or (b) have the auto surface treat any same-release manual rollback record within the window as 'acted'. Scope: kube-helm-rollback.ts (record fromHelmRevision) or kube-auto-rollback.ts (widen the acted check); regression test: manual rollback of rev N then auto-eval pinned to N with a stale failed verdict -> already_acted, api.rollback NOT called a second time. Evidence: feat/x5rt-kube-self-management @ ae9ed16f51.
acceptance_criteria: A manual operator rollback of revision N causes a subsequent automatic evaluation still pinned to N (stale failed verdict) to resolve already_acted with no second api.rollback call; existing act-once + auto-rollback tests stay green; the chosen approach (record from-revision on manual, or widen the acted check) documented. lint + lifecycle suite green.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #91 (2459be7b0a): fromHelmRevision recorded on manual rollbacks, kube-helm-rollback.ts + regression test (6f7b898f38)

title: Context-coherence telemetry: detect confusion, looping, confabulation self-reports, and concern rumination as a canary for the bonding/turns/time bug class
description: Operator-confirmed direction (2026-07-14, grew out of retiring the ACON compaction-guideline loop): repurpose deterministic confusion detection into live telemetry. Signal taxonomy from the operator: (1) confusion asks - the existing FAILURE_SIGNAL_RULES regexes (compression-guideline.ts:210: remind/repeat, missing context, which-thread) already run per turn-end and are near-free; (2) looping - repetition signals (link the hgw3 duplicate-reply machinery and the 2026-07-06 repetition incident heuristics); (3) confabulation self-reports - she names it herself when she catches it; (4) concern rumination - sitting on concerns too long (links ys51 stale-concern lifecycle and the emosim observer ruminationWatch lever, LIVE in observe_only with intensityThreshold 0.4 - join that stream rather than duplicating it); (5) operator interventions as ground-truth labels - partner messages like 'you're looping love' are confirmed incident markers worth counting and correlating. Design constraints: per-turn work stays deterministic regex/heuristic (NO per-turn LLM - operator explicitly flagged that cost); events carry session context (channel, recent mirror notes, time gap, active concern count) into telemetry + a Garden card so regressions in channel bonding / missing turns / temporal coherence show up as a trend line instead of being caught by feel; optional LLM synthesis of flagged events only, riding the bundled maintenance tick. Excluded from emotion appraisal and memory candidacy like other firewall/system notices. Acceptance: Garden card shows coherence events over time with per-signal breakdown; a seeded missing-turn scenario in tests produces a correlated event; zero added per-turn LLM calls; w05a.11 crosswalk can consume the same events.

title: Rolled-out chat context leaves episode-summary breadcrumbs instead of vanishing
description: Operator design (2026-07-14): live never hits compaction because the 1M window rolls entries out of chat context naturally - day-to-day life needs the last couple days in context, not a month. But rolled-out content currently just disappears from her working view. Desired: when entries roll out and get consolidated into episodes (episode synthesis already covers them), the episode's summary + id becomes a compact in-context REFERENCE to what occurred before - so continuity over the rolled-out horizon comes from episodic breadcrumbs, not from compaction. Natural shape: the episodic landmark block (bead 6i7c adds id+meaning) plus a session-tail-aware selection that prefers episodes covering the just-rolled-out span; drill-down via the get-by-id tool (x9ka). Links: hgw3 session tail architecture, apq0 semantic threads. Scope: read-side context assembly; no new persisted duplication (episodes already exist). Acceptance: a conversation referencing something from N days ago (outside the chat window) has the covering episode's summary+id present in context; token cost bounded by the landmark block cap.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #123 (fix/s10-shakedown-bugfix-p2). be3f's defined scope — bounded rolled-out episode breadcrumb SELECTION + metadata plumbing under session+visibility isolation, presence-window disable, maxChains/per-chain caps — is delivered and seam-reviewed (cluster A: refuted, no leak). Force-closed: the bd edge marks be3f blocked-by 6i7c, but the relationship is the reverse — be3f SUPPLIES the selected episode's landmark+ID to the 6i7c renderer, which is the separate downstream id/meaning rendering integration and remains open as the consumer. be3f does not depend on 6i7c to complete its own scope.

title: Post-turn action queue drains at most once per 60s scheduler tick: the 250ms executor interval is inert
description: Evidence (2026-07-14 scheduler census): post-turn-action-executor registers with intervalMs = Math.max(50, 250) = 250ms (src/app/startup/composition/post-turn-actions.ts:1294; Garden renders it as 0s), but processQueue is called ONLY from this scheduler task (:1301) and the scheduler tick loop runs at tickIntervalMs = 60s (scheduler.ts:350,408) - so the deferred-action queue drains at most once per 60 seconds regardless of the 250ms registration. The agent.post_turn.actions.inferred handler merely enqueues. Impact: every maintenance executor (sleeptime heavy passes, trust-drift/cogsec reviews, episode synthesis, near-turn memory) plus latency-sensitive post-turn continuations (subagent spawns, memory writes, weighted-thought outreach deliveries) inherit an up-to-60s start delay per queue hop. Multi-hop action chains compound it. Scope: make the drain event-driven - call processQueue (or schedule an immediate microtask drain) from the enqueue path, keeping the scheduler task as a fallback sweep at a sane interval (60s is then fine); do not lower tickIntervalMs for this. Empty-queue drain is already near-zero cost so eager draining is safe. Acceptance: an enqueued action begins executing within ~1s of enqueue in a test; census note updated; Garden no longer shows a misleading 0s row (render the fallback sweep interval).
notes:
2026-07-14 operator direction: the queue should not be poll-drained at all - a turn completing is a known event ('you know when a turn fires'), so the drain triggers off the post-turn event/enqueue path directly. The scheduler task survives only as a rare fallback sweep (its current 60s-effective cadence is fine for that role). This is the intended design, not an optimization option.
2026-07-14 operator design refinement - the queue conflates two classes that need different treatment: (A) turn-completion-critical actions (inline tool call did not fire but a tool invocation/required task must happen - the follow-through of THIS turn) which must drain event-driven immediately on turn completion; (B) background concurrent work (memory extraction, reviews, retrieval enrichment) which should never have been turn-bound - it is supposed to run concurrent/unbounded and can ride a bundled maintenance tick. History that motivates the split: synchronous memory used to lag turns, was made async, and the hold-old-memory-until-new-memory-lands mechanism exists to paper over exactly this coupling; the 60s drain ceiling likely contributed to the old lag. Implementation: classify queue entries at enqueue (turn-critical vs background), event-drain class A on post-turn emit, batch class B.
close_reason: Audit 20260716 pass-2: premise gone: adaptive next-wake (mmo9.5.3 b2ecd2a6b2, mmo9.7.8) honors 250ms tasks; eager-drain redesign intent noted in audit report

title: Ambient-presence cadence and thresholds are hardcoded outside scheduler.json; wakeSummary config block validates but registers nothing
description: Evidence: ambient-presence runs on hardcoded defaults - interval 1h (ambient-presence.ts:16), minIdle 3h (:17), minNoteInterval 6h (:18) - with no scheduler.seed.json block and no caller override (scheduler-runtime.ts:266-271), violating the config-ownership posture (all sibling lanes are scheduler.json-owned). Also concern-grooming daily 06:15 cadence is hardcoded (concern-grooming.ts:167). And scheduler-config.ts:1070 validates a raw.wakeSummary block that no task registers - dead validation that misleads config readers. Scope: move ambient-presence + concern-grooming cadences into scheduler.json (with settings surface), delete or wire the wakeSummary block. Acceptance: knobs visible in scheduler.json + Garden; verify:settings-contract passes; no dead config keys.
notes:
2026-07-14 live Garden + live scheduler.json comparison widens this significantly: FIVE more live tasks run on 5m intervals with NO scheduler.json keys at all — memory.sleeptime.rest-window, contacts.trust-drift-review.rest-window, cogsec.drift-velocity-review.rest-window, cogsec.second-arrow-review.rest-window, compaction-guideline-review — all hardcoded registration intervals, invisible to config ownership. post-turn-action-executor shows interval 0s in Garden (hardcoded; effective cadence = every 60s scheduler tick). Also a live-vs-seed divergence to reconcile: weightedThoughtOutreach.enabled=true live (5m) vs seed false. Scope grows to: every registered task's cadence becomes a scheduler.json key with seed defaults matching current live values; Garden already renders them. Consider bumping to P2 — this is now most of the scheduler surface.
2026-07-14 operator cadence policy: deterministic polling itself is fine, but 5m = 288 ticks/day is out of proportion for a real-time life (this is not a 20x sim). Default poller cadence moves to 60m when the cadences become config-owned: salience decay, the four rest-window pollers (their 9h nightly window still gives ~9 hourly chances vs 108 at 5m; the passes are self-gated by their own intervals anyway), and compaction-guideline-review. Documented exceptions requiring their own rationale: post-turn-action-executor (0s event-drain pattern — likely needs low latency to deliver post-turn actions; decide from the census cost data, do not blanket-change), and weightedThoughtOutreach (hourly delays a time_sensitive-class nudge up to 60m against its 6h weight half-life — 15-30m may be justified; pick deliberately and document). Every chosen value lands as a scheduler.json seed default + Garden-visible.
2026-07-14 census completion: the four rest-window 5m pollers cost effectively NOTHING when gated - evaluateRestWindowEligibility is a pure wall-clock check, no DB/LLM/events, returns [] outside 00:00-09:00 (rest-window.ts:95; cogsec lanes short-circuit on config.enabled first). So 5m->60m for them is proportionality + config-ownership, not a cost fix; do not oversell savings. Their consolidation into a single window-gate dispatcher is optional DRY (each lane has a distinct sink + daily watermark). The post-turn-executor 0s row is a rendering artifact of 250ms and is now its own bug bead (drain latency ceiling) - exclude it from the blanket cadence work.
2026-07-14 operator decision on the weighted-thought exception: 30m, not 60m (needs to be under an hour for time_sensitive nudges). Final cadence targets: rest-window pollers + salience/compaction 60m; weightedThoughtOutreach.checkIntervalMs 30m (1800000); post-turn executor excluded (event-driven per dvzq).
2026-07-14 operator reshapes the target: NOT a knob per task. Most of the chaff (rest-window pollers, salience decay, social graph, guideline review, ambient presence) should collapse into ONE bundled background tick at 30-60m, with individual knobs only for justified exceptions (weighted-thought 30m, wake timing, backup, reflections). Hard requirement: transparency - the Garden scheduler page must show exactly WHAT runs inside each bundled tick, and any knob whose value drives more than one behavior must say so on the page (the salienceDecay/maintenance/compaction-review aliasing is the canonical offense: labeled for one thing, silently bundling others). Fewer knobs, honest labels.
2026-07-14 compaction-guideline-review disposition (investigated): it is the ACON-pattern self-improving compaction feature (bead PSFN-jvl4, commit ecd3a8b7, 2026-03-06) - failures are only ever appended at agent.turn.end (recordCompressionFailureFromResponse, scheduler-runtime.ts:344) when a post-compaction reply matches confusion regexes, and the review only calls an LLM at >=2 unreviewed failures. Since the capture site is the ONLY producer, make the review EVENT-DRIVEN at that site (trigger when unreviewed count crosses threshold) and remove it from the scheduled surface entirely - do not even bundle it. Its current 5m slot exists only because it piggybacks the aliased maintenanceIntervalMs key.

title: Salience-decay maintenance sweeps the entire active memory set every 60 seconds
description: Evidence: MEMORY_CONFIG.maintenanceIntervalMs = 60_000 (src/faculties/memory/types.ts:353), scheduler-registered as salience-decay 'every' task (src/app/agent/scheduler-runtime.ts:99-108, config-owned via salienceDecayIntervalMs -> bootstrap-helpers.ts:270,320). Each firing does paginated DB reads (listActiveMemories batch 500) plus salience-update writes across all active memories - every minute, per companion, forever. Decay math derives from lastAccessed timestamps (decay.ts), so a sweep every 30-60 MINUTES produces identical salience values; the 60s cadence buys nothing except constant DB churn - the worst idle load found in the 2026-07-14 scheduler census (working_docs/prompt-audit-findings-20260714.md 6b). Coordinate with m14v (decay/floor rework touches the same sweep). Scope: raise the default (seed + settings surface), consider computing decay lazily at retrieval time and reserving the sweep for floor enforcement/persistence. Acceptance: idle-companion DB write rate drops accordingly; decay values unchanged within tolerance in tests.
notes:
2026-07-14 live config pulled from psfn-shard (rev 576e33cd): salienceDecayIntervalMs=300000 (5m) — live is already 5x gentler than the repo 60s default, and it IS config-owned + Garden-editable. Scheduler tickIntervalMs=60000. Recommendation unchanged in kind: 5m full-set sweeps still buy nothing (decay derives from lastAccessed); raise to 30-60m and/or compute decay lazily at retrieval, reserving the sweep for floor enforcement. Also raise the repo seed default from 60s so new deployments do not regress.
2026-07-14 operator decision: hourly is acceptable for salience decay. Target 60m (config default + live), not 30m-or-60m ambiguity.
2026-07-14 census completion - two corrections: (1) salienceDecayIntervalMs and maintenanceIntervalMs are ONE aliased key through bootstrap (bootstrap-helpers.ts:320, runtime-config.ts:35), and compaction-guideline-review registers from the same value (scheduler-runtime.ts:104,113) - moving decay to 60m also moves compaction review to 60m. Compaction review is cheap when gated (empty failure log = skip, zero LLM), so hourly is fine for both, but SPLIT the keys or document the coupling deliberately. (2) The repo-side 60s defaults (types.ts:353, load-config.ts:372) are pre-override values clobbered by scheduler.json before registration - fix the seed, not just the constant.
2026-07-14 clarification for implementation: compaction PROPER is already context-threshold-driven (settings.json compactionThresholdPct=70) and almost never fires on live - the 1M-context chat window rolls entries out long before 70%. The TIMED task sharing this cadence is only the compression-guideline REVIEW (LLM review of past compression failures). Decouple: guideline review joins the bundled background tick; compaction stays threshold-only; decay gets its own key. Context pressure that CAN hit the threshold: analysis workbench (observed 100k tokens in one session; tool was renamed from think to discourage casual use) and future long-horizon shard work - neither should share knobs with day-to-day chat.

title: Add cheap per-companion fatigue and charge posture to the fleet status surface
description: Merge 6608579f implements one Garden process per companions.json entry and a loopback-only read-only fleet status surface. Source inspection of src/boundary/gateway/fleet-status.ts confirms the page honestly exposes connection state, health, last-seen time, crossover violations, and Garden links, but explicitly omits the fatigue/charge posture required by W4 because the gateway has no cheap authority for it. This residual matters for companion welfare: an operator viewing fleet health must be able to see exhaustion/charge pressure without entering each Garden or triggering extra model work. Scope: define a bounded redacted telemetry summary owned by each agent's existing deterministic charge/fatigue runtime; transmit/cache it through the authenticated gateway connection health path; expose timestamped posture on fleet status JSON/HTML; show stale/unavailable honestly; retain loopback/read-only/no-secret boundaries and avoid reading companion-private stores directly from the gateway. Non-goals: no LLM calls, no fleet write controls, no authenticated SSO portal work (psfn-framework-opl1.8), no live deployment, and no expansion into full Garden data aggregation.
design: Extend the existing agent-to-gateway connection health envelope with a small versioned posture summary produced by the deterministic charge/fatigue runtime. Cache only the latest validated summary per bound companion connection, cap values and labels to an allowlist, and expire it by timestamp. Fleet JSON is the source for HTML rendering so attribution/staleness logic exists once. Do not add a second telemetry database or query companion-owned persistence from the gateway.
acceptance_criteria: With two identified companion connections carrying different deterministic charge/fatigue states, fleet status JSON and HTML show each companion bounded posture with update timestamp and no cross-attribution. Missing or stale posture renders unavailable/stale and never fabricates health. Payload and logs contain no prompt, memory, contact, policy rationale, raw ledger event, or other private companion content. The gateway performs no LLM call and no direct companion-store read. Unit tests cover envelope validation, caps, expiry, reconnect replacement, spoof rejection, and rendering. A local two-agent fleet-status integration script emits redacted per-companion connection, posture, timestamp, and staleness diagnostics and proves reconnect/disconnect behavior. Flag-off behavior and current loopback/read-only/startup fail-closed tests remain green; npm run lint, npm run build, and git diff --check pass.
notes:
Plan-space polish pass 1: fixed telemetry ownership/versioning, redaction and staleness semantics, reconnect/spoof cases, and detailed local two-agent integration logging; no scope removed.
Plan-space polish pass 2: rechecked parent/child boundaries, duplicate search, priority, non-goals, and validation separation; graph is coherent and no further change was required.
Plan-space polish pass 3: final one-bead-at-a-time stability read found the scope self-contained, acceptance testable, logging privacy-safe, and no feature loss or graph repair needed.

title: Capture the true provider wire body via pi-ai onPayload and retire the three parallel reconstructions
description: Evidence: operator export of a single turn showed input_schema 44x for 22 tools and could not tell what actually ships. title: Force tool_choice on phases where a call is mandatory (post-turn memory writes, response_control decisions)
description: Anthropic tool_choice any/named prefills the assistant turn and converts 'model ignored the tool' into 'model cannot not call it'. Apply to structured phases that MUST produce a call: post-turn/heartbeat memory writes, response_control no_reply decisions, scheduled-task acknowledgements. Caveat: incompatible with extended thinking - gate by model config. Acceptance: identified mandatory phases enumerated in code with forced choice; telemetry shows zero missed mandatory calls over a validation window.
notes: PREMISE REFUTED (opus-lane-c, 2026-07-15, verified + independently re-verified by deep-reasoner). No runtime phase uses function-calling tool CALLS as a mandatory decision, so there is nothing to force tool_choice on. Every structured-decision phase — memory extraction (faculties/memory/extraction/orchestrator.ts:397), profile-synthesis, sleeptime-agent.ts:641, wiki sleeptime, episodic judgment-runner.ts:25, weighted-thought outreach (weighted-thought-nudge-evaluator.ts:66), ICP consent (initiation-consent-evaluator.ts:57), emotion/intention appraisal, deliberation, context-feedback — calls llmProvider.complete() and parses a STRUCTURED-TEXT result (XML/JSON) with a hand-written parser, fail-closed to a safe default; NONE pass a tools array. Structural block: LLMCompleteParams (boundary/gateway/protocol.ts:165-184) has NO tools field, and the llm.complete gateway handler never forwards tools, so the complete() RPC path cannot carry tools at all. Only .stream()/LLMChatParams carries tools, and the sole stream-with-tools path is the free-form main conversational turn (SubstrateAgent), where a text reply is always valid; response_control/no_reply (substrate-agent.ts:576) is one optional 'core' tool that exists so the model can CHOOSE silence — forcing it would silence every turn. pi-ai natively supports options.toolChoice on stream (openai-completions/anthropic/mistral; google 'any' only; openai-responses/codex hardcode auto) so the capability is buildable, but shipping it now = unwired dead code (repo rule violation); converting a text phase to a forced tool call = risky out-of-scope redesign of a core cognition path for a P2, and net-neutral/negative since these phases fail on text-parse not on ignored-tool. Recommendation: reframe or close as premise-dead. If the epic intends to redesign decision phases as tool-call-driven, that is an operator/epic-level architecture decision — build the stream toolChoice capability together with its first real caller. No code change made; worktree clean.
close_reason: Operator ruling 2026-07-15: premise refuted, close; future architecture option captured in a deferred standalone bead (tool-call-driven decision phases + stream toolChoice with first caller). Investigation evidence (Opus worker, independently re-verified by deep-reasoner, no code changed, branch identical to base 66293a0d): no phase uses mandatory tool calls — all structured decision phases are complete()+fail-closed text parsing; LLMCompleteParams cannot carry tools (protocol.ts:165-184); the only stream-with-tools path is the free-form main turn where forcing a call would silence every turn (response_control is deliberately optional so the companion can choose silence); building the toolChoice flag now would be unwired dead code (repo rule). Full finding recorded in bead notes.

title: Widen empty-argument retry into a full validate-and-reprompt loop for malformed and unknown tool calls

PSFN has the narrow seam primitives/llm/empty-tool-argument-retry.ts. Extend to: schema-mismatch arguments, unknown tool names (suggest nearest catalog name via the retired-alias machinery), and echo the expected contract back in the error result. Links live bug mihm (GLM literal {} arguments dispatched instead of retried). Acceptance: bonding flag configurable per contact channel set; a bonded three-channel conversation renders as one interleaved timeline with source annotations; privacy resolution tested for mixed-visibility bonds; unbonded channels unaffected.

notes: Wave-2 sizing analysis (2026-07-21): real cross-session threading is 900-1400 lines — union-find over arcs, watermark/dedup decoupling from thread identity, storage+Garden+retrieval+tests. title: Document wave closure, fix-epic, validation, and reconciliation invariants
description: Summary: Update ORCHESTRATION_PROCESS.md so completed implementation waves and their child beads close at the final integrated check instead of remaining open as proxies for review findings, release/manual validation, deployment, operator acceptance, or unrelated follow-up work. Why: stale open implementation beads obscure what is actually shipped on a feature branch, duplicate later tracker work, and make decision-makers unable to distinguish completed implementation from important fixes or separate validation. Scope: preserve the existing one-review, one-remediation, final-check loop and parallel feature-branch/worktree rules; define immediate evidence-backed child and epic closure plus same-closeout sprint status updates; route remaining IMPORTANT defects under a wave-specific <wave> fixes epic; keep lesser findings report-only; track live/manual/release work separately; require one-bead-at-a-time commit/source verification during branch reconciliation and closure of already-shipped stale beads and empty epics; define the end-of-wave handoff fields. File: ORCHESTRATION_PROCESS.md. Non-goals: no runtime/code changes, no new review process, no release/main merge, and no live/deployment actions.
acceptance_criteria: ORCHESTRATION_PROCESS.md explicitly states all seven requested invariants: final-check implementation closure independent of main/release merge with child+epic evidence and sprint-doc update; no proxy-open implementation work; important defects grouped under a wave-specific fixes epic that closes when children finish; lesser findings report-only; manual/live/release verification tracked separately without reopening implementation; one-bead-at-a-time reconciliation that closes shipped stale beads and empty epic shells; and a handoff listing closed implementation epic, fixes epic/open children or none, validation beads, and pushed feature fixed point. Existing one-review/one-remediation/final-check and parallel branch/worktree policies remain intact. Appropriate markdown/repository hygiene checks and git diff --check pass.
close_reason: Completed ORCHESTRATION_PROCESS.md process-contract update. Evidence: ORCHESTRATION_PROCESS.md:103 defines implementation completion at the bounded integrated final check independent of main/release merge, immediate evidence-backed child and epic closure, same-closeout sprint-status updates, and the ban on proxy-open implementation work. Lines 125-180 preserve the one-review/one-remediation/final-check risk model while routing every remaining IMPORTANT security/privacy/isolation, welfare/consent/autonomy, real data/secret, core-path, or mandatory-gate defect under a wave-specific <wave> fixes epic; the original implementation stays closed, the fixes epic closes with its children, lesser findings remain report-only, and manual/live/release validation uses separate named tracker work. Lines 206-240 preserve feature-branch integration and add one-bead-at-a-time commit/source verification, closure of already-shipped stale beads, and closure of empty epic shells. Lines 277-291 require the end-of-wave handoff to list the closed implementation epic, fix epic/open children or none, validation beads or none, pushed origin-equal feature fixed point, and sprint status commit. Parallel branch/worktree rules and the bounded single-review loop remain intact. title: Free-time gate ignores how the last block ended: silence stops the block but she is re-prompted up to the daily cap
description:

title: Concern lifecycle never retires unexpired concerns: next_review_at is stored but unused, so standing concerns recur in every reflection for days
description:
Evidence: TTLs are high=48h/medium=24h/low=8h with a 7-day hard cap (concerns.ts:194-198), active cap 7 (concerns.ts:191), grooming once daily at 06:15 (concern-grooming.ts:167). "Stale" resolution is TTL-only: resolveStaleConcerns (active-concern-store.ts:523-558) resolves only expired/past-lifetime concerns; next_review_at is persisted but never used as a retirement trigger. Re-observation refreshes expires_at (store ~604-648), keeping touched concerns alive to the 7-day ceiling. Overflow retirement keeps the highest-priority soonest-expiring items (concern-grooming.ts:208-221) — exactly the ones that read as anxious. Net: a handful of standing concerns populate every reflective session for up to two days each.

Context: this is the mechanical half of the "all she does is talk about concerns" finding; the language half is the separate source-softening bead.

Scope: use next_review_at for review-based early retirement (a concern past its review point with no re-observation resolves quietly), and consider inline cap enforcement between daily grooming runs. Non-goal: changing TTL values wholesale or the emosim crosswalk (w05a.11).

Acceptance: unit test — a concern past next_review_at without re-observation is auto-resolved before its TTL; live observation — consecutive daily reflections stop repeating the same untouched concern set.

title: Test sessions need a 'testing' naming convention plus a cleanup path so finished test channels stop generating artifacts
description:
Evidence: channels exist only as session rows (no channels.json, no registry); channel type is inferred from sessionId prefix (src/core/session/session-id.ts:17-33). There is NO cleanup/purge/disable mechanism anywhere in src/core/session/ or src/persistence/sessions/ — sessions persist "in stores/backups until purged" (manager-primitives.ts:276 comment), where purge means manual data surgery. Result: one person accumulates a dozen unused test sessions attributed to them, which keep attracting temporal refresher notes and other artifacts that are never read.

Operator decision (2026-07-14): name test sessions with a 'testing' marker, and make it policy to clear test sessions when testing is done.

Scope: (1) a recognizable testing marker in the session/channel id or metadata; (2) exclusion of testing-marked sessions from autonomous fan-outs (temporal refresher, wake notes) and from artifact generation where sensible; (3) a purge command or Garden action that removes a named session's rows safely (fail-closed: explicit id, no wildcards); (4) a short policy note in docs/operations.md. Pairs with the refresher-targeting bead.

Acceptance: create a testing-marked session, exercise it, purge it — rows gone from the session store, refresher never targeted it; policy documented.
notes: REOPENED 2026-07-19 by operator review of PR #115: lifecycle tested like a single-root dev install; live fleet uses split roots + per-companion Postgres schemas. Verified blockers: (1) CLI resolves journals under SYSTEM_DATA_DIR/state/sessions but live journals are COMPANION_DATA_DIR/state/sessions — documented default command cannot find live sessions; (2) purge connects to Postgres without companion schema/tenant role — can delete journal but leave the companion's projection rows, or touch public; (3) testing marker does not exclude sleeptime processing — durable memories, orientation changes, wiki entries, dreams, arcs still generated (the pollution the feature exists to prevent); (4) Redis tail cache not fenced on purge — reusing a session id can merge stale cached messages into a new conversation. Remediation pass dispatched on wave branch before PR #115 merge.
close_reason: Complete including fleet-topology remediation a6d0f6a4a (operator's four PR #115 blockers): live-shaped journal resolution, per-companion schema tenancy, sleeptime exclusion at inference+execution entries, Redis tail fence. Full suite 11,666/0 green on wave branch; double-blind delta review clean. Remaining extraction/emotion/contact gating tracked separately in psfn-framework-2sdk.

title: Four per-companion state files are mis-rooted at config.dataDir instead of companionDataDir
description:
Evidence — four confirmed sites where per-companion state is written under config.dataDir (shared systemDataDir) instead of companionDataDir (§11 seams 7 and 8):
1. garden-audit-history.jsonl — local-admin-contract.ts:197.
2. Garden heartbeat-policy.json path — scheduler-service.ts:290, while the layout signature at layout.ts:740 intends companionDataDir. This COMPOUNDS bead b9kb (Garden scheduler service already reads/writes heartbeat-policy.json at the wrong root) and should land with b9kb + psfn-framework-nljc (fingerprint-cache fix) so all three converge on one resolver.
3. Reflection-metacognition journal.
4. Model-usage ledger JSONL — model-budget.ts:338 — spend accounting mixes companions (the Postgres per-schema store mitigates, the JSONL does not).

Context
- §11 calls these "independent S-effort bugs" — mechanical mis-wirings, distinct from the mechanism work (overlay) and file moves (capability-tier/scheduler). The correct pattern already exists: resolveConfiguredCompanionDataDir (local-admin-contract.ts:178), used by charge/fatigue ledgers, cogsec events, quarantine, prompt layers, core memory.
- Batched as one bead because each fix is the same mechanical substitution; cite each site in the fix.

Scope
- Re-root all four sites onto resolveConfiguredCompanionDataDir. Decide per site whether existing shared-file contents need a one-time split/migration or can be left frozen (document the choice).
- Coordinate site 2 with b9kb and nljc (related links) — one resolver, one landing.
- Non-goal: any new config mechanism.

Source: working_docs/fleet-analysis-findings-20260714.md §11 (seams 7, 8).
acceptance_criteria: All four sites (garden-audit-history.jsonl, Garden heartbeat-policy path, reflection-metacognition journal, model-usage ledger JSONL) resolve through resolveConfiguredCompanionDataDir and write per-companion files; on a multi-companion fleet no two companions share these files. The heartbeat-policy fix lands coherently with b9kb/nljc on one resolver. Each site's handling of pre-existing shared file contents is documented.

title: Apply the memory-subsystem last-result fallback pattern to post-turn loops to clear drain races
description:
Evidence
- Post-turn drain timeout (5s) is regularly exceeded under rapid turns, leaving memory_extraction / emotion_appraisal / auto_compaction unfinished (§8d.4). This is the subject of mmo9.3 (per-session durable BackgroundWorkSupervisor).

Context
- Operator decision (§10.4): the per-turn background LLM fan-out is ACCEPTED as necessary; the work is clearing the RACE CONDITIONS. Apply the memory-subsystem pattern across post-turn loops: if a concurrent task does not come back in time, proceed with the last turn's result rather than blocking or dropping.

Scope
- Apply the "if concurrent work does not return in time, use last turn's result" pattern to the post-turn loops (extraction/appraisal/compaction drains) so a slow concurrent task never blocks the turn or corrupts state.
- Relates to mmo9.3 (BackgroundWorkSupervisor) and mmo9.5 (admission control) — coordinate, do not duplicate.
- Non-goal: reducing the fan-out itself (accepted as necessary).

Source: working_docs/fleet-analysis-findings-20260714.md §8d.4, §10.4.
acceptance_criteria: Under rapid turns, a post-turn drain that exceeds its window proceeds with the last turn's result instead of blocking the next turn or dropping work, with no state corruption. Verified by driving rapid turns and observing no post-turn block and no lost/duplicated background result.
close_reason: Folded into mmo9.3 — lp7g self-describes as its subject; the durable per-session BackgroundWorkSupervisor structurally solves the 5s drain race lp7g patches. 2026-07-14 bead audit.

title: Bound the session hot-cache to recent sessions per companion with hydrate-on-demand for older
description:
Evidence
- Live carlini agents show high RSS (~1.1Gi each). §8d assessment: this is probably cache, and cache-over-disk-IO is the right trade — but it must be bounded.

Context
- Operator decision (§10.6): keep only functional state hot (e.g. the last ~1k sessions per companion) with search/hydrate-on-demand for older sessions. Thousands of sessions x roughly half a dozen companions must not all live in memory. Memories are lower-risk (they grow slower than chat turns).

Scope
- Bound the session hot-cache to a configured recent window per companion (default around last ~1k sessions), hydrating/searching older sessions on demand.
- Non-goal: memory-store caching (lower risk); the Redis session tail (hgw3.5) is the related architecture — relate, do not duplicate.

Source: working_docs/fleet-analysis-findings-20260714.md §10.6, §8d.
acceptance_criteria: The session hot-cache holds at most the configured recent window per companion (around last ~1k sessions); older sessions are hydrated/searched on demand and evicted from the hot set. Agent RSS no longer grows unbounded with total session count. Correctness of older-session reads is preserved via on-demand hydration.
notes: wof1 gate 2026-07-16: fix must ship with a failing-then-passing regression test in src/core/session/manager.test.ts proving the hot-cache is bounded to the recent window per companion and older sessions hydrate on demand without unbounded growth.

title: Make the cogsec override an audited break-glass path only, with no subject-consent approval system
description:
Evidence
- Strong reuse candidate for the override flow: the cogsec quarantine confirm->decide two-step with full audit (intake-quarantine-routes.ts), plus opl1.10 passkey step-up binding.
- §3 originally floated three options (subject-consent-required, owner-break-glass, dual-control) as an open design question.

Context
- Operator decision (§10.7 iii): the cogsec override is an AUDITED BREAK-GLASS ONLY. There is NO subject-consent request/approval system — too much work. It is for emergencies to fix things, not casual access, with a full audit trail.

Scope
- Implement the subject-scoped memory/profile override (PRIV1/PRIV2) as an audited break-glass action, reusing the cogsec quarantine confirm->decide two-step and opl1.10 passkey step-up. Every use writes a full audit record.
- Non-goal: any subject-consent request/approval workflow (explicitly rejected). No casual-access path.

Source: working_docs/fleet-analysis-findings-20260714.md §3, §10.7 (iii). Parent epic: opl1; relates to opl1.10 and opl1.11.


Adversarial correction: privacy override is not generic opl1.10 step-up. It requires the user-verifying WebAuthn branch specifically, plus trusted ingress, an identified principal, exact companion/action/resource, reason, short expiry and single-use confirm-to-decide. Lower-assurance Discord possession, owner role and legacy token recovery cannot authorize it. Initial passkey enrollment/recovery follows the trusted-host subject-bound ceremony.
acceptance_criteria: A non-subject memory/profile is never revealed by routine owner/admin/member authorization. Privacy break-glass requires local/trusted ingress, an identified principal, a user-verifying WebAuthn passkey, exact companion/action/resource selector, stated reason, bounded expiry and single-use confirm-to-decide. Discord possession challenge, mfa_enabled, OAuth consent, owner role, legacy token, and the trusted-host recovery credential alone cannot satisfy privacy break-glass or enroll a passkey; only the full subject-bound recovery ceremony may replace a passkey, and a separate exact opl1.15 UV-WebAuthn ceremony is still required for disclosure. Every attempt and decision records who/what/when/why/assurance/target/parent decision without private content and is visible in the audit trail. Concurrency/replay/target substitution/expired-session tests deny; no subject-consent workflow is added. Garden E2E, build and mandatory lint pass.
close_reason: Completed in PR #97 (merge 4b48377575): commit 7e97ebea49/integration de48fb5a5f implements audited single-use UV-WebAuthn privacy break-glass; routine non-subject access remains denied.

title: Hide the derived contact profile/bio from admins who are not the subject
description:
Evidence
- The derived user profile/bio is the freeform ContactProfileArtifact (memory-store-port.ts:27-34) produced by extraction.
- Same principal gap as PRIV1: "admin" is currently one shared token (server-auth.ts:10-14); subject-scoping requires the opl1 principal layer.

Context
- Operator decision (§10.7 ii): the derived user profile/bio is hidden unless the admin/user is logged in as the subject. Lands after Discord SSO (opl1, in flight).

Scope
- Gate the derived contact profile/bio so routine access is visible only to its proven subject, reusing the same principal/subject-classification layer as PRIV1. Owner/admin status provides no exception; any non-subject disclosure is exclusively opl1.15 privacy break-glass.
- Non-goal: the memory-body gate itself (PRIV1); this covers the profile artifact specifically.

Source: working_docs/fleet-analysis-findings-20260714.md §3, §10.7 (ii). Parent epic: opl1; relates to opl1.11.


Adversarial correction: remove the bare owner exception. A ContactProfileArtifact is routine-visible only to its proven subject. Any owner/admin non-subject reveal is exclusively opl1.15 privacy break-glass with trusted ingress, a user-verifying passkey, exact target/action/reason, short expiry and audit.
acceptance_criteria: The derived ContactProfileArtifact for subject Y is returned during routine Garden use only to the authenticated proven subject Y; owner/admin role alone never bypasses the gate. Any non-subject reveal is exclusively opl1.15 privacy break-glass with trusted ingress and user-verifying WebAuthn. title: Hide all contact-associated (named) memories from non-subject admins by piggybacking the intimate-memory gate
description:
Evidence
- Visibility today is gated ONLY by sensitivity: memory-body-gate.ts:115-118 hides just intimate/confidential, never by contact/subject. "Admin" is a single shared token (server-auth.ts:10-14) with no principals/roles (AdminAuditActor = 'operator' | 'companion').
- Memory contactId is optional/nullable and often the conversation partner, not the subject; subjectContactId and episodic participantContactIds are separate. opl1.11 already warns against equating contactId with subject classification.

Context
- Operator decision (§10.7 i): hide ALL contact-associated (named) memories from any logged-in admin who is not the subject, REGARDLESS of sensitivity level, because procedural/reflection content can allude to intimate-level material. Memories are already attributed to who they relate to.
- Explicit instruction: PIGGYBACK on the existing intimate/high-intimacy gate mechanism (AdminMemoryBodyGate) — do NOT build a parallel system.
- Lands after Discord SSO (opl1, in flight). A subject-classification layer with a fail-closed ambiguous branch is prerequisite work (opl1.11).

Scope
- Extend the existing AdminMemoryBodyGate so a named (contact-associated) memory is hidden from any admin who is not the subject, at every sensitivity level, once principals exist (post-SSO).
- Leak paths beyond the body view (search snippets, counts, exports, bulk ops) must honor the same gate — opl1.11 acceptance already enumerates them.
- Non-goal: a new authz system; reuse the existing gate. Blocked behind opl1.3/.5/.7 principals.

Source: working_docs/fleet-analysis-findings-20260714.md §3, §10.7 (i). Parent epic: opl1; relates to opl1.11.


Adversarial correction: remove the bare owner exception. A non-subject principal, including an owner, never sees named memory through routine role authorization. The only override is opl1.15 privacy break-glass with trusted ingress, a user-verifying passkey, exact target/action/reason, short expiry and audit.
acceptance_criteria: A principal X sees a named memory for subject Y during routine Garden use only when X is the authorized subject/co-subject under the executable policy; owner/admin status alone never bypasses this at any sensitivity. Any non-subject reveal uses only opl1.15 privacy break-glass with trusted ingress and user-verifying WebAuthn. The shared SQL-aware gate filters IDs, bodies, snippets, counts, embeddings, exports, prompts and bulk/update paths before construction; ambiguous/stale/missing subject classification hides. Focused policy/query/E2E tests, build and mandatory lint pass.
close_reason: Completed in PR #97 (merge 4b48377575): integration commit 3db2de956e applies the shared subject privacy gate to named-memory IDs, bodies, snippets, counts, exports, and mutations.

title: ChatGPTN returns a provider template artifact that becomes an empty_response and wastes an LLM attempt
description:
Evidence
- ChatGPTN returns the provider template artifact <｜begin▁of▁sentence｜>, which becomes an empty_response and triggers the deepseek fallback on scheduled lanes — wasting one LLM attempt and round-trip per affected turn.

Context
- Observed live on carlini scheduled lanes. It is a routing/template misconfiguration for that model, not a model-quality issue.

Scope
- Fix the routing/template config for the ChatGPTN model so it does not emit the template artifact / empty_response. Effort S.
- Non-goal: the fallback mechanism itself (it is working as designed); only stop the wasted first attempt.

Source: working_docs/fleet-analysis-findings-20260714.md §8d.3.
acceptance_criteria: ChatGPTN produces normal completions on scheduled lanes with no <｜begin▁of▁sentence｜> template artifact and no empty_response->deepseek fallback, eliminating the wasted LLM attempt per affected turn.
notes: Duplicate-candidate of psfn-framework-2nu6 (same ChatGPTN root cause; 2nu6 now carries quantified live evidence from 2026-07-14 triage: ~9.6% of turns, 88s worst-case fallback latency). Consider merging into 2nu6.

title: Agent gateway-connect retry budget is shorter than gateway readiness, crashlooping every fleet rollout
description:
Evidence
- On every fleet rollout, all agents die on gateway RPC ECONNREFUSED. The retry budget (10 retries / ~9s) is shorter than gateway readiness, and the fatal path exits 1 — bypassing the intended exit-75 reexec.

Context
- This is the rollout crashloop race observed live on carlini. It is a reliability bug, not just noise: agents crashloop until the gateway happens to be ready.

Scope
- Fix with a longer/jittered gateway-connect retry budget OR readiness gating, and correct the fatal path so it takes the exit-75 reexec instead of exit-1. Effort S/M.
- Non-goal: the "I'm back" duplicate notifications those restarts produce (dq9c/B11).

Source: working_docs/fleet-analysis-findings-20260714.md §8d.2.
acceptance_criteria: A fleet rollout no longer crashloops agents on gateway ECONNREFUSED: the retry budget outlasts gateway readiness (or readiness-gates the connect), and when the agent does exit it takes the exit-75 reexec path, not exit-1. Verified by a rollout showing agents connecting on first/early retry with no crashloop.

title: Turn records keep recentEntries and rendered plan.messages twice; store L0 id-ranges plus deltas
description:

title: Turn records copy retrieved memory text verbatim; store memory ids and resolve at Loom read time

title: Idle maintenance loops do full-store work when nothing changed: salience decay rescans all active memories and guideline review re-reads files every cycle
description:
Opus sweep finding (2026-07-14), two loops on the same maintenanceIntervalMs cadence (default 300s via schedulerConfig.salienceDecayIntervalMs, load-config.ts:60; MEMORY_CONFIG fallback 60s, memory/types.ts:353), registered at src/app/agent/scheduler-runtime.ts:99-108 and :109-132:

(1) SalienceDecay (faculties/memory/decay.ts:26, run() :48-84) pages listActiveMemories({limit:500}) over ALL active memories, recomputes exp() decay per row, and bulkUpdateSalience — every cycle regardless of any reads/writes since the last run. 5 agents × a full scan + bulk write every 1-5 min on the shared box, at idle, growing with the memory corpus. Decay is deterministic in dt, so options: compute lazily at read time; or precompute each memory's next threshold-crossing time and only touch rows due to cross the 0.01 delta (:72); or at minimum widen the idle cadence (half-lives are long).

(2) Compaction-guideline review (core/session/compression-guideline.ts:568-580) does guidelineStore.load() (existsSync+readFileSync, :319/:327) and failureLogStore.listSince() (:427/:428) every cycle BEFORE deciding to skip. Fix: mtime/size guard or an in-memory "last failure appended" watermark — skip both reads when unchanged.

Non-goals: changing decay math, half-lives, or guideline semantics.
acceptance_criteria: An idle deployment's maintenance cycles perform no memory-table scan and no guideline/failure-log file reads when nothing changed since the last cycle (DB/fs instrumentation over an idle window); decay values observed at read time are unchanged versus today's eager behavior (test tolerance on the exp curve); guideline review still triggers on new failure-log entries.

Transaction rollback restores the revision; concurrent mutation during a decay pass invalidates the schedule for a fail-closed rescan. Guideline checkpoint a86da443: CompressionGuidelineStore and CompressionFailureLogStore expose successful-write revisions; periodic review establishes a first-read baseline, then skips both file-backed load/list calls and the LLM while revisions are unchanged, and immediately re-runs when a failure append advances the log revision. Failures appended during an in-flight LLM call remain pending because the runtime records the pre-call failure revision. Regression instrumentation proves zero Postgres/store work during an idle decay window, exp-curve tolerance, mutation invalidation, zero guideline/failure-log reads at idle, and new-failure review triggering. One full npm test run: 695 files passed, 7,700 tests passed, 3 skipped; one unrelated environmental failure because this isolated worktree lacks the untracked owner file purrsephone/satellites.json used by satellite-registry.test.ts. Regression first reproduced the discontinuity (persisted 0.5 became 0.25 immediately), then proved no write/discontinuity at restart and the expected 0.5 * exp(-ln(2) * 1d / 7d) value after one day. title: Inline image bytes cross the agent-gateway boundary twice per vision turn (intake screen, then main LLM call); retain once at the gateway
description:
Opus sweep finding (2026-07-14). For inline base64 images (Telegram photos, pasted images, voice-attached — up to 8MB decoded ≈ 11MB base64), the same bytes cross the agent-gateway boundary twice per vision turn: once for intake.screen_image (boundary/gateway/methods/intake-image.ts:27,55,109) and again inside the main-turn LLM call (the gateway holds provider secrets, methods/llm.ts). Each crossing pays a full JSON.stringify/JSON.parse (transport.ts:205,278). URL images are cheap (URL crosses, not bytes); this is specifically the inline path. That's 2x multi-MB serialize/copy/transit per vision turn per companion — steady-state CPU on the shared box.

Fix shape: on intake.screen_image, the gateway retains the decoded image keyed by originRef (already a param) for the immediately-following turn LLM call, or returns a screening handle the agent passes back — bytes cross once. Retention must be bounded (TTL + size cap) and a cache miss must fail closed to resending, not to a missing image.

Related: psfn-framework-j8gv (single vision pass) reduces VLM calls; this reduces transport copies — independent wins on the same path. Note for wss (cross-host) gateway deployments only: the backplane has no compression (transport.ts:205,278); enabling perMessageDeflate there is a possible follow-up, but do NOT enable it for same-box unix-socket pairs (CPU for no bandwidth gain).
acceptance_criteria: An inline base64 image crosses the agent-gateway transport once per turn (transport-level instrumentation or test on serialized payload sizes); the main-turn LLM call resolves the image from the gateway-side retention (originRef key or returned handle) with a bounded TTL/size and fail-closed miss behavior (falls back to resending bytes, never silently drops the image); screening and LLM behavior unchanged.
notes:
Implementation checkpoint (2026-07-14), pending independent review. Branch work/fleet-efficiency-inline-image-retention. Commits: d311f9e0 adds per-connection gateway retention with opaque handles, 60s TTL, 12-entry/32MiB aggregate caps, oldest-first eviction, request-scope resolution, explicit -32015 miss, disconnect clearing, and multi-companion isolation; a8561fe7 adds hash-keyed bounded client handle hints, turnId request-scope plumbing, handle substitution for llm.chat/llm.complete, one explicit-byte retry on a retention miss, and cache clearing on disconnect/destroy; 5d73270b adds exact serialized UTF-8 JSON payload-byte/frame/RPC-call counters for NDJSON and WSS without enabling compression; ad0c37cc adds URL-path regression coverage. Evidence: focused 8-file suite 191/191 passed (retention privacy/TTL/count+byte eviction/miss, multi-companion isolation+disconnect, client fallback, transport, turn wiring); npm run build passed; npm run lint passed after every tracked slice. URL path and screening/model semantics preserved. Bead intentionally remains in_progress until independent review.
Single bounded post-review remediation pushed at 75dc46aa. The independent review found two important issues: lazy TTL pruning retained partner image bytes indefinitely on an otherwise idle live connection, and the typed gateway RPC contract omitted gateway_image_ref, causing seven mandatory lint errors/unreachable branches. Remediation adds one unref'd nearest-expiry timer per connection retention store, rescheduled after retain/eviction and canceled by clear; fake-timer coverage proves physical entry/decoded-byte removal without later cache activity, old eviction timers do not fire against replacements, and clear cancels the timer. GatewayServer.stop explicitly clears every retention store before destroying connections. The RPC wire now honestly models structured text/image/thinking/tool-call/opaque-reference blocks; reference and resolution loops are control-flow honest, and untrusted retained descriptors normalize from unknown. Existing connection/companion/turn scoping, screening gate, exact-byte miss resend, URL path, count/byte caps, and transport instrumentation are unchanged. Final gates: focused 8-file surface 192/192 passed (original 191 plus new proactive-expiry regression); npm run lint passed; npm run build passed ESM+DTS; git diff --check passed. Branch pushed and origin-equal at 75dc46aa. This was the single allowed remediation; no second review, close, merge, SQLite/live/Pi/SSH/provider action.

title: Per-turn retrieval re-runs the full pipeline on unchanged inputs and embeds the identical query twice (memory + wiki); short-circuit and share the embedding
description:
Opus sweep finding (2026-07-14), two compounding wastes on the per-turn hot path:

(1) Unconditional full refresh: refreshActiveMemoryContext is scheduled every non-vision turn (turn-execution/pre-turn-state.ts:531-555) and re-runs the whole pipeline (memory/retrieval.ts:373-418): query embed at :757, full vector scan + scoring, and — when compositionalPolicy is enabled for the channel — an LLM rerank call per turn (:1021-1027). The active-context identity key deliberately excludes contextText (memory/active-context.ts:116-125), so nothing short-circuits on unchanged input; coalescing only guards concurrent refreshes on the same key (:337-353). Fix: short-circuit when hash(contextText) and the store's corpus version pointer are unchanged since the last completed refresh — return the existing snapshot.

(2) Double embedding: the same memoryRetrievalContextText is passed to memory retrieval (pre-turn-state.ts:479/:482) and wiki retrieval (:661); memory embeds it at retrieval.ts:757, wiki independently at faculties/wiki/retrieval.ts:298. HttpEmbeddingProvider.embed (memory/embedding.ts:113-127) has no memoization and no embedding cache exists anywhere. Fix: compute the query embedding once in pre-turn state and hand it to both consumers, and/or a small content-hash LRU in the embedding provider.

Interaction: this is the main destabilizer of the cacheable prompt prefix — fixing it improves the prompt-cache hit rate from the sibling prompt-caching bead. Non-goals: changing scoring, ranking, or what memories surface.
acceptance_criteria: A turn whose retrieval context text and memory-corpus version are unchanged since the last completed refresh serves the existing snapshot without a new embed, vector scan, or compositional rerank call (test); one query embedding is computed per turn and shared by memory and wiki retrieval (call-count test on the embedding provider); retrieval results for changed inputs are byte-identical to today; compositional rerank still fires when inputs actually change.
notes: Single-review remediation shipped in 96c5ef34. Cache identity now includes normalized disclosure, room/contact visibility, scope, retired-session, channel-label revision, and trust-policy revision state; unsafe access fingerprinting disables reuse. Regressions cover consent grant-to-withdraw, contact-room visibility withdrawal, and concurrent rollback. title: Postgres transcript projection issues a no-op drift DELETE per message and preloads every message ID into resident memory at boot
description:
Opus sweep finding (2026-07-14), two fixes in one file (src/persistence/sessions/postgres-adapters.ts):

(1) Write amplification: every upsertSessionEntry enqueues the projection upsert PLUS an unconditional DELETE FROM session_projection_drift WHERE channel_id=$1 (:271-280, same pattern at :293-311 and :252-261). ~2 messages/turn → ~4 statements/turn, half of them no-op deletes — drift rows almost never exist and driftByChannel already tracks their presence in memory. Fix: only enqueue the DELETE when driftByChannel.has(channelId), or fold upsert+delete into one CTE.

(2) Boot memory: preloadMessageIds (:116-132) runs SELECT channel_id, message_id FROM session_messages_projection across ALL channels and stores a Map<channelId, Set<number>> on the projection for process life (:201, :424) — O(total messages) boot scan plus tens of MB resident at 100k+ messages, ×5 companions, growing forever. Fix: lazy per-channel hydration on first touch, or keep only the per-channel counts/max-id the drift reconciliation actually needs.

Non-goals: changing the projection schema or drift semantics.
acceptance_criteria: Messages on channels with no tracked drift enqueue exactly one projection statement (no unconditional DELETE; test asserts statement count); drift rows are still cleared when drift exists for the channel; boot no longer SELECTs all message IDs across all channels — hydration is lazy per channel or reduced to per-channel counts/max-id — with projection/drift reconciliation behavior unchanged under the existing test suite.
notes: Implementation checkpoint 0dd8e7c6 on work/fleet-efficiency-postgres-projection. Replaced the O(total projected messages) boot preload with one aggregate row per channel (COUNT plus MAX message_id), preserving exact boot reconciliation counts without retaining message-ID sets. Clean-channel upserts/tombstone deletes/replacements now clear session_projection_drift only when driftByChannel tracked the channel; explicit clearProjectionDrift remains explicit. Projection counts use bounded channel metadata and reconcile ambiguous inserts/deletes from PostgreSQL statement results. Regression coverage asserts no all-message-ID boot SELECT, exact aggregate boot count, one projection statement for a clean-channel message, persisted drift clearing when tracked, and existing repair/reconciliation behavior. Gates: 13 targeted tests passed across postgres-adapters and both repair suites; npm run build passed ESM+DTS; npm run lint passed. Local PostgreSQL integration unavailable because pg_isready at 127.0.0.1:5432 reported no response; no external/live infrastructure attempted. PostgreSQL production code only; no SQLite implementation touched. Branch pushed and origin-equal at 0dd8e7c6. Awaiting exactly one independent review; do not close or merge yet.

title: Gateway keepalive fires an audited no-op RPC every 30s, writing audit rows and forcing rotation at full idle
description:
Opus sweep finding (2026-07-14) — top idle-load win. src/boundary/gateway/client.ts:1024,1044 (DEFAULT_GATEWAY_KEEPALIVE_INTERVAL_MS=30_000 at :148) fires a discord.typing RPC across the backplane every 30s forever, even fully idle. The handler is a no-op (methods/discord.ts:37) but it is registered through runtime.audited (methods/register.ts:14), so each beat runs the full audit wrapper (server.ts:326): canary-egress inspect → INSERT into the gateway audit store + enforceRotation (audit.ts:102,110) → UPDATE on completion (:115). Across 5 deployments that's an INSERT+UPDATE pair (+rotation scan) every ~6s on the shared box at 100% idle, and the no-op entries pollute real audit history into premature rotation. (Gateway audit store is the better-sqlite3 store in audit.ts — legacy SQLite, still live.)

Fix shape: keep the socket warm with a transport-level ping (ws ping frame / unix-socket noop) instead of an audited JSON-RPC method, or register the keepalive on a non-audited path. Non-goal: removing auditing from any real method or changing audit rotation policy.
acceptance_criteria: An idle deployment generates zero gateway_audit writes from keepalive over an observation window (verify by row count / audit log diff); the agent-gateway socket still detects disconnection within the same window as today (keepalive function preserved via transport-level ping or non-audited method); audit history no longer accumulates discord.typing ALLOW entries.
notes:
2026-07-14 reconciliation: premise correction — production gateway audit is Postgres-only, not SQLite. Commit 6ce9549f made src/boundary/gateway/privileged-core.ts:92-99 fail unless persistenceBackend=postgres and constructs createPostgresGatewayAuditStore; SQLite audit code is a retired adapter/testing surface. The performance problem itself was present on feat/fleet-efficiency d9ba500c: src/boundary/gateway/client.ts sent discord.typing every 30s and src/boundary/gateway/server.ts audited it through the Postgres store.

2026-07-15 implementation checkpoint for exactly one independent review: pushed commit 4d8807e1 on origin/work/fleet-efficiency-audit-keepalive. GatewayClient now uses GatewayRpcConnection.sendHeartbeat instead of discord.typing. Unix connections exchange connection-scoped non-JSON-RPC PING/PONG control lines; WSS uses native ping/pong frames. A missing/failed acknowledgement causes the client to close the connection, preserving detection. GatewayServer refreshes only the emitting connection health clock from the transport heartbeat, with no audit call. Real discord.typing remains registered through registerAuditedDescriptors and is regression-tested as ALLOW-audited. title: Garden runs like a local-first webapp: IndexedDB-backed client store with delta sync so navigation renders from local data and only changes cross the WAN
description:
Operator direction (2026-07-14): "gardenux needs to run like a webapp and have cache and use indexdb so we just delta updates."

Architecture: an IndexedDB store in admin-ui (per companion deployment origin) holding session transcripts (append-mostly — new messages have monotonic ids, a natural delta cursor via maxId/nextBeforeId), session/channel lists, queue states, telemetry snapshots. On navigation: render from IndexedDB immediately, then revalidate with a delta request (If-None-Match from psfn-framework-t5z7.3, or since-cursor params) and patch in place. Websocket events (psfn-framework-t5z7.7) update the local store directly, making polls redundant while connected.

Sequencing: depends on server-side cursors/ETags (t5z7.3) and pairs with slim payloads (t5z7.1, t5z7.4) — cache slim data, not today's bloated payloads. psfn-framework-t5z7.5 now covers the server-side Redis half only; this bead owns the client half.

Non-goals: offline mutation queueing (admin actions stay online-only), service-worker app-shell caching (t5z7.6's immutable assets get most of that win), caching any credential material.
acceptance_criteria: Revisiting a previously viewed Garden page renders immediately from IndexedDB and issues only a delta/conditional request (verified in devtools: no full-payload refetch for unchanged data); session transcripts, lists, and queue pages persist their last-known state across page reloads; deltas keyed by server cursors (ETag/updatedAt/maxId) with a full-refetch fallback when the cursor is stale; stale-while-revalidate UX (render cached, update in place); admin data in IndexedDB stays on the operator's machine only — no new server surface.

title: Audit history reads and parses the whole JSONL file per request and ships raw source blobs the timeline never renders
description:
Opus sweep finding (2026-07-14). src/operator/garden/services/audit-history-service.ts:78-85 does readFileSync of the ENTIRE audit JSONL + JSON.parse per line, merges gateway+charge sources, sorts everything, and slices one page — on every request to /api/admin/audit/history (overview-routes.ts:372), i.e. every filter change and pagination click on the telemetry/audit page. Fix shape: memoize parsed entries keyed by file mtime/size (safe: the service is the sole writer and can invalidate on its own append), or bounded tail-read; drop raw from list payloads and add a per-entry detail endpoint. Compression from psfn-framework-t5z7.3 helps but dropping the field helps more.

title: Admin-ui pollers keep refetching full payloads on hidden tabs; pause on visibility loss and push queue changes over the existing garden websocket
description:
Opus sweep finding (2026-07-14). No visibilitychange/document.hidden handling exists anywhere in admin-ui/src. Network polls that run forever on background tabs: confirmations/+page.svelte:126 (15s), contact-approvals/+page.svelte:72 (15s), graph-proposals/+page.svelte:75 (15s), cognitive-security/approvals/+page.svelte:198 (15s), cognitive-security/drift/+page.svelte:128 (30s), scheduler/+page.svelte:560 (30s, refetches full getFullData tasks+reflections), chat/+page.svelte:502 (30s health). Up to ~4 full refetches/min per forgotten tab, over transatlantic WAN, per open page. (shards/+page.svelte:109 and telemetry LazyPageContent.svelte:410 1s ticks are local-only relative-time recomputes with no network — leave them.)

The queue endpoints these pages poll re-serialize and re-send the entire (usually empty) queue every tick and send Cache-Control: no-store (routes/shared.ts:3), forbidding 304s; their stores are memoized in-process so poll cost is pure network. A garden event-bus ReconnectingWebSocket already exists (admin-ui/src/lib/api/websocket.ts) and is used by prompt-monitor (+page.svelte:186) — pushing queue-change events over it is low-effort reuse.

Fix shape: (1) shared visibility-aware interval helper (clear on hidden, immediate refetch+resume on visible) adopted by all polling pages; (2) queue pages subscribe to the websocket for change signals, falling back to the poll when the socket is down. Pairs with the ETag/304 half of psfn-framework-t5z7.3.
acceptance_criteria: A backgrounded/hidden Garden tab generates zero poll traffic (verified in devtools network log) and resumes with an immediate refetch on visibility; queue-style pages (confirmations, contact approvals, graph proposals, cogsec approvals) receive updates via the existing garden websocket or conditional requests instead of full 15s refetches; no page loses freshness when visible.

The one allowed remediation landed in 5042ae25 and c22a1cea: authenticated companion-scoped confirmation/queue routing, post-persist text/image quarantine hints, exactly one visibility-gated false-to-true reconnect refresh with fallback timer stopped, and subsystem-health poller adoption. title: Static Garden assets ship uncompressed with no immutable caching and no ETag, so the full bundle and HTML shell re-download over the WAN
description:
Opus sweep finding (2026-07-14). src/operator/garden/server-transport.ts:75-100 serves static files via readFile+res.end with no Content-Encoding — SvelteKit bundles (commonly 200KB-1MB uncompressed) transfer full-size on first paint. Constants at :18-19: GARDEN_HTML_CACHE_CONTROL='public, max-age=0, must-revalidate' and GARDEN_ASSET_CACHE_CONTROL='public, max-age=86400'. Three compounding issues: (1) no compression at all on statics; (2) content-hashed /_app/immutable/* assets are safe for a year of immutable caching but revalidate daily; (3) no ETag/Last-Modified anywhere, so the HTML shell fully re-downloads on every navigation and every asset revalidation is a full re-download instead of a 304.

Scope: server-transport.ts static path only. Non-goal: changing the SvelteKit build or admin API caching (psfn-framework-t5z7.3 owns API ETags).
acceptance_criteria: JS/CSS assets serve brotli/gzip (precompressed .br/.gz or on-the-fly); /_app/immutable/* served with Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable; HTML shell and non-immutable assets carry an ETag and return 304 on If-None-Match; verified with curl over two consecutive page loads (second load transfers only the API calls).
notes:
Implementation landed on branch bead/t5z7.6 (commit 005ee243, off main, unpushed — pending feature-branch merge + codex review + PR). server-transport.ts static path now: prefers precompressed .br/.gz siblings (admin-ui svelte.config.js precompress:true enabled via adapter-static), on-the-fly brotli/gzip fallback above 1KB memoized by path+mtime+size+encoding (bounded 512 entries); immutable max-age=31536000 for /_app/immutable/*; ETag (size-mtime, encoding-qualified) + bodyless 304 on If-None-Match, incl. SPA fallback. Serve methods now take (path, req, res) — routing interface + both handleRequest closures updated. Did NOT touch backplane primitives or /api/admin JSON (t5z7.3 scope). Validation: targeted 15/15, full garden dir 63 files/450 tests passed, npm run build success, eslint clean on all 7 touched files.
Codex-reviewed, findings fixed, shipped in PR #42 (perf/efficiency-wave-1 → main, https://github.com/CGIC-AI/psfn-framework/pull/42). Gate on the branch: build+lint clean, full suite 7715 passed / 1 pre-existing environmental failure (psfn-framework-engc). Ready to close on PR merge.

Codex review remediation 999bc573 made static ETags weak with full mtime precision and capped on-the-fly Brotli quality. GitHub PR #42 merged to main as 84c0089e on 2026-07-14; current origin/main 576e33cd contains that squash, and the seven t5z7.6 files on origin/main are byte-identical to reviewed commit 999bc573. Actual shipped source in src/operator/garden/server-transport.ts selects precompressed .br/.gz siblings before bounded memoized on-the-fly Brotli/gzip, applies public,max-age=31536000,immutable to /_app/immutable/*, emits encoding-qualified weak ETags, honors If-None-Match with bodyless 304, and sends SPA fallback index.html through the same validator path. admin-ui/svelte.config.js enables adapter-static precompress:true. src/operator/garden/server-request-routing.ts keeps /api and /api/* outside the Garden SPA/static path; neither 005ee243 nor 999bc573 touched API route files. Direct curl proof over the built shipped transport returned SPA /memory 200 with max-age=0, weak ETag then bodyless 304, and an immutable hashed JS asset 200 with max-age=31536000, immutable, Content-Encoding: br, encoding-qualified weak ETag then bodyless 304.
