title: Make kube source refresh ownership-safe and non-destructive
description: The final ae758a4f psfn-shard ship exposed a deterministic failure in scripts/ops/ship-kube-update.sh around the companion self-management source refresh. The live checkout /home/psfn/psfn-framework-source is NVMe-backed and owned by uid/gid 999 for the runtime. The script invokes sudo git without an inline safe.directory override, so Git rejects the checkout as dubious and leaves /tmp/psfn-repo-refresh.bundle behind. The same block also uses git reset --hard, which is unnecessarily destructive and can collide with preserved untracked content such as vendor/emosim. For this deployment the operator recovered safely by fetching with -c safe.directory=/home/psfn/psfn-framework-source and fast-forwarding with merge --ff-only; the untracked vendor directory was preserved. Update the repo-owned ship workflow to handle the intended uid-999 ownership without global/off-repo Git config, use a fail-closed non-destructive update strategy, clean its temporary bundle on success/failure, and report a precise warning when the checkout cannot fast-forward. Scope: scripts/ops/ship-kube-update.sh plus focused tests/docs if needed. Non-goals: deleting untracked source content, changing runtime owner JSON/PVC data, or adding global safe.directory state on psfn-shard.
acceptance_criteria: A test or reproducible harness proves source refresh succeeds for a checkout owned by a different uid using only inline/repo-scoped Git trust. The workflow fast-forwards an ancestor checkout to the shipped commit without git reset --hard and preserves unrelated untracked files/directories. A divergent or dirty tracked checkout fails closed with an actionable message and no partial branch movement. Temporary bundle cleanup is verified. npm run lint passes before closure.
close_reason: Done in PR #93: ship-kube-update source refresh now uses ff-only merge + dirty-tracked-files refusal + temp-bundle EXIT trap instead of the destructive hard-reset flow (7d0325d990)

title: Reconcile repository-hygiene identity literal allowlist after CogSec integration
description:
Summary:
During psfn-framework-es4t validation, npm run verify:repository-hygiene passed the public-sanitize phase but failed the identity-literal scan because the combined current-main and CogSec tree contains numerous PSFN/psfn literals not represented in the scanner's intended allowlist/ownership contract. The failures span pre-existing current-main files and newly merged CogSec files; this is validation debt, not a reason to weaken or bypass the scanner during the urgent shadow rollout.

Scope:
- Run npm run verify:repository-hygiene from current main and capture the complete identity-literal findings.
- Classify each occurrence one file at a time as legitimate product/protocol/runtime identity, fixture, documentation example, or accidental hardcoding.
- Replace accidental literals with canonical companion identity/config resolution.
- Add only narrowly justified stable allowlist entries for legitimate constants; do not blanket-ignore directories or disable the gate.
- Preserve public sanitization behavior and existing runtime identity contracts.

Non-goals:
Do not rename the PSFN project/protocol identifiers or perform unrelated copy cleanup.
acceptance_criteria: npm run verify:repository-hygiene passes on current main without blanket directory exclusions; every retained literal has a documented narrow justification in the owning scanner/allowlist; runtime-facing accidental companion-name hardcoding is replaced with canonical identity resolution and targeted tests; npm run lint and affected identity/config tests pass.
close_reason: Completed in commit a81cdd49. Classified all 76 current identity-literal findings and added 57 narrow file+pattern+context allowlist entries with specific project/protocol/runtime justifications; no scanner logic, scan roots, or directory exclusions changed, and synthetic unallowlisted companionName='PSFN' remains detected. Validation: 8 identity-scanner/gate tests passed; npm run verify:identity-literals passed (1369 files, 441 justified hits); npm run lint passed; npm run build passed; npm run verify:repository-hygiene passed; git diff --check passed. Independent standards and spec reviews both PASS with no findings.

- GET /v1/companion/artifacts/{id}/preview?satelliteId=&endpointId=&claimType= — requires artifacts scope; serves only artifacts announced previewable, path-contained under companion-data generated-images root, size-capped 5MB; 404 unknown, 403 otherwise.

title: Preserve retryability and surface failures in inbound message pumps
description:
Summary: the inbound Discord and inter-companion pumps promise that conversational messages are not dropped, but non-busy failures are logged, swallowed, and then recorded in the recent-success dedupe cache. A replay during the dedupe window is suppressed and neither the human nor peer companion gets a failure result.

Evidence on origin/main c7c7ef8a:
- src/app/agent/gateway-message-handlers.ts:126-143 retries only errors matching the busy pattern.
- Lines 183-240 catch any other handleMessage, text send, or media send error, append an audit entry, then unconditionally move every dedupe key to recentDiscordMessages in finally.
- Lines 509-520 run the pump fire-and-forget, so notification acknowledgement is not a delivery acknowledgement.
- Lines 533-570 repeat the same behavior for companion messages and unconditional recentCompanionMessages bookkeeping.
- The targeted gateway-message-handlers suite passes but contains no replay-after-failure contract.

Impact: transient provider, persistence, or outbound gateway failures become silent conversational loss. In the companion lane this also breaks the expectation that peer conversation remains an ordinary reliable channel.

Scope: model explicit queue outcomes and retry/notification behavior without reintroducing duplicate replies. Keep the existing indefinite busy wait and outbound duplicate-reply guard.
acceptance_criteria: Discord and companion message pumps distinguish processing success, intentional no-reply, and failure; only successful or deliberately terminal outcomes enter success dedupe state; transient model/persistence/gateway delivery errors retain a bounded retry path or durable failed state; Discord users receive a non-companion-authored failure notice when a turn cannot be delivered and operators receive actionable status; peer senders receive an explicit failure/negative acknowledgement; tests cover handleMessage, text send, media send, and companion-send failures plus replay after failure; npm run lint passes.
close_reason: Completed and shipped in main merge 10476c91 via implementation 3e4f6d2a and fixture integration f9de62ab/50267d74. Discord and companion dedupe commit only after confirmed delivery; Discord reply delivery checkpoints resume partial text/attachment sends without replaying completed steps; companion failures use authenticated receipt-bound reports routed to the original sender, with failure audit/observation and no conversational loop. Residual restart state remains explicitly in-memory and was reviewed. Validation: worker focused 85 tests, merged channel/auth suites, full Vitest 6687/6687, and npm run lint passed.

title: Fail closed for tools without capability policy and classify journal actions

- src/system/capabilities/gate.ts:64-89 treats an empty required-token set as allowed.
- src/boundary/integrations/journal/tools.ts:56-136 implements durable list/read/write/append/search without withCapabilityRequirement.
- src/boundary/integrations/journal/runtime-wiring.ts:9-22 registers that tool in the real runtime.
- A direct resolver check on c7c7ef8a returns {"read":[],"write":[]} for the live journal tool.
- Existing capability suites pass because they test classified tools but do not enumerate the executable registry for missing policy.

This generic class was also identified as OPUS_AUDIT_S10.md finding 02-M2, but no matching tracker item was found. Scope: make policy completeness mechanically enforced and fix journal now. Preserve explicit NO_CAPABILITY_REQUIREMENT for reviewed exceptions; do not infer safety from an unknown tool name.
acceptance_criteria: Every canonical executable tool is required to declare an action-aware capability resolver or an explicit reviewed no-capability marker; missing metadata fails startup/registration instead of resolving to an empty requirement; journal list/read/search require identity.read and write/append require memory.write or a deliberately documented equivalent; a registry-conformance test enumerates the live canonical tool surface and fails on unclassified additions; custom tier with zero tokens cannot write journal; targeted tests and npm run lint pass.
close_reason: Completed and shipped in main merge 10476c91 via implementation commit 1c9bcb25. Capability requirements now fail closed for every executable tool not explicitly classified, journal list/read/search require identity.read, write/append require memory.write, and malformed/unknown journal actions deny. Registry/facade/gate tests cover unclassified tools and all journal action classes. Validation: worker and integrated npm run lint passed; full Vitest 6687/6687 passed.

title: Update dev toolchain dependencies flagged by npm audit
description:
Summary: During the Sprint 10 codebase audit, `npm audit --json` on origin/main reported 6 dev-tooling vulnerabilities: 1 critical, 3 high, 1 moderate, and 1 low. `npm audit --omit=dev --json` reported zero production dependency vulnerabilities, so this is currently scoped to the test/build/admin-UI developer toolchain.

Evidence from npm audit on 2026-07-09:
- Direct dev dependency vitest is affected by GHSA-5xrq-8626-4rwp, fixed by vitest 4.1.10 according to npm audit.
- Transitive dev/build dependencies include vite advisories GHSA-4w7w-66w2-5vf9, GHSA-v2wj-q39q-566r, GHSA-p9ff-h696-f583, GHSA-v6wh-96g9-6wx3, and GHSA-fx2h-pf6j-xcff.
- Other transitive advisories include picomatch, flatted, postcss, and esbuild.

Scope: Update pinned dev/build/test dependencies to exact fixed versions and verify no production dependency risk is introduced.

Non-goals: Do not apply `npm audit fix --force` blindly or widen dependency ranges.
acceptance_criteria:
- Root and admin-ui package manifests remain exactly pinned.
- npm audit --omit=dev --json reports zero vulnerabilities.
- Full npm audit has no critical or high vulnerabilities, or any remaining dev-only findings are documented with exact rationale.
- npm run lint and relevant test/build gates pass.

title: Surface startup memory hydration failures as degraded runtime state
description:
Summary: The Sprint 10 audit found that agent startup treats active memory and active core-memory hydration failures as warnings and continues boot. If hydration fails after restart, the runtime can accept user turns with missing continuity state while only logging the problem.

Evidence:
- src/app/agent/main.ts:342-350 catches hydrateStartupActiveMemoryContexts errors and logs `Startup active memory hydration failed`.
- src/app/agent/main.ts:352-358 catches hydrateStartupActiveCoreMemoryBlocks errors and logs `Startup active core-memory hydration failed`.
- Startup then proceeds into internal state rehydration and runtime wiring.

Scope: Make startup continuity hydration failures visible and actionable in production.

Non-goals: Do not redesign the memory schema or change memory extraction policy in this bead.
acceptance_criteria:
- Production startup either fails closed or enters an explicit degraded state when active memory/core-memory hydration fails.
- The degraded state is exposed through existing health/admin status surfaces and prevents silent first-turn continuity loss.
- Local/continuous behavior is documented if intentionally more permissive.
- npm run lint and targeted startup/memory tests pass.
close_reason: Closed

title: Retry or classify transient direct model-room empty_response
description: Summary: During the 2026-07-08 local kube shakedown on feat/multi-companion after deploying image 0.1.0-kube-3d07ebf5, the direct model-room path for nuns-carlini hit a single OpenRouter z-ai/glm-5 empty response. Gateway logged originStage=model_room.direct, lastCategory=empty_response, lastError='LLM response from openrouter/z-ai/glm-5 contained no text or tool calls', and returned HTTP 502. A targeted retry with the same provider/model/channel shape succeeded and returned nonblank FH Monastery location/world content. Scope: make direct model-room completions robust to transient provider empty_response/no-text cases, either by retrying the same candidate once with explicit logging or by classifying the result in a way the UI/operator can distinguish from missing credentials/config. Files likely involved: src/channels/api/agent-backend.ts direct model completion path, src/primitives/llm model fallback/client error classification, and model-room UI error reporting if needed. Non-goals: do not hide persistent provider/config failures; do not add broad fallback to unrelated provider/model without operator policy.
acceptance_criteria: A direct model-room completion that receives one provider empty_response retries once or returns an explicit transient-provider-empty diagnostic distinct from missing credentials; tests cover transient empty_response followed by success and persistent empty_response; local model-room shakedown no longer leaves a one-off provider empty as an indistinguishable terminal 502.
close_reason: Done in PR #93: bounded 2-attempt retry on transient empty response, persistent-empty stays 502 model_error + tests (0bd941b867)

title: Garden cogsec consolidation: single left-hand tab with remediation, firewall, and approval pages; operator-only double-confirm release
description: UX consolidation (operator, 2026-07-09): Garden already has remediation pieces; bundle ALL cognitive-security surfaces into one left-hand 'Cognitive Security' tab with remediation, firewall (policy/telemetry), and approval (quarantine queue) as separate pages under it. Quarantine review requirements: ONLY the primary operator (highest-level human / primary partner) can release quarantined items; the quarantine page must show which classifiers fired and explain the exact suspected issue so the human makes an informed call; release requires DOUBLE-CONFIRM ('Are you sure?' -> 'Are you *sure* sure?'); release options: release raw, release sanitized (safe representation from htm9.7), discard, and always-allow/always-deny-this-source (the flywheel -- every decision updates per-source policy so the same class stops escalating; feeds the trusted sites/people lists in htm9.13). Model the queue on the existing pending-contact-approvals surface (src/core/contacts/pending-contact-approvals.ts + its Garden routes); batched, async, exception-only -- never interrupt-driven. Depends-on: psfn-framework-htm9.1, psfn-framework-htm9.7. Acceptance: /garden shows the consolidated tab; release path enforces operator capability + double-confirm server-side (not just UI); every release/discard decision writes an audit event with actor + reason; per-source always-allow/deny persists into intake-policy config; admin API routes under /api/admin/* follow existing route conventions.
close_reason: Implemented on feat/cogsec-intake-firewall (33 commits, validated); pending merge to main.

title: Source-risk-scaled scrutiny and light-touch data marking, with trusted sites/people lists
description: Scrutiny scales with SOURCE risk, not just static sender trust (operator, 2026-07-09): high scrutiny for raw web search results and files from random/shady sites; lower (still scanned) for trusted preprint sites like arXiv; tunable knobs in intake-policy.json -- trusted sources get lighter/faster handling (skip L2/L3 unless L1 flags), unknown sources get more layers. Trusted origin != safe: npm/GitHub supply-chain attacks are the counterexample -- everything gets at least L1. Data marking: for web documents let the scanners, risk score, and source determine how intrusively content is marked. Reference behavior that already works: the HMAC-out-of-sync XML wrapper flags text as unverified/possibly-untrustworthy, the companion responds but treats it warily, and the wrapper disappears once fixed -- use the same light-touch approach (wrap + provenance note at low risk; datamark-interleave or summary-only as risk rises; marker pre-stripped from inbound content by htm9.4 so it cannot be forged). Over time build persisted lists of trusted sites and trusted people so less firewall machinery fires (or fires faster) for them -- fed by the Garden flywheel decisions (htm9.11). The upstream Trinity pattern was tuned for agency-run businesses; ours is tuned for 'your friends who happen to be AI'. Depends-on: psfn-framework-htm9.1, psfn-framework-htm9.4. Acceptance: marking intensity is a pure function of (scanner labels, score, source tier) covered by table-driven tests; trusted-list hits measurably skip escalation layers (latency assertion); marking wrapper renders in PromptPlan blocks with provenance; lists are operator-editable via Garden and persisted in the config owner.
close_reason: Implemented on feat/cogsec-intake-firewall (33 commits, validated); pending merge to main.

title: Slow-poisoning detection: emotional drift-velocity monitoring over chats and derived memories (VAD/GoEmotions/EmoSem)
description: Slow memory poisoning / belief drift evades per-message scanning -- but the system already has multiple emotional monitoring channels: VAD, GoEmotions, and (for Persephone) EmoSem. Detection idea (operator, 2026-07-09): watch for rapid shifts in emotional classification that do not match established patterns -- e.g. high-love -> hate over a few benign-looking turns; track not just drift but the VELOCITY of drift relative to prior trends. Normal fluctuation is expected (a companion won't always be happy with you -- people who care get annoyed, want you to do better); the signal is too-much-too-fast in an atypical direction. Applies to L0 chats AND to memories generated from them. Implementation shape: clone the deterministic nightly-lane pattern from src/core/contacts/trust-drift-signals.ts + trust-drift-review-lane.ts (zero-LLM signal derivation, conservative thresholds, batched review card, NEVER auto-mutating state); per-source aggregates: emotional-valence trajectory per contact, memory-write rate per source, trust-lobbying label frequency (from envelope labels), retrieval share of low-trust sources. Output: batched Garden review card under the cogsec tab (htm9.11). MINJA/MemoryGraft literature confirms nothing packaged exists -- this is build-fresh and the system's most differentiated capability. Depends-on: psfn-framework-htm9.1 (envelope labels feed the aggregates), psfn-framework-htm9.11. Acceptance: synthetic drift scenario (gradual valence flip over N turns) raises a review card while a normal-fluctuation corpus (annoyance, disagreement, repair cycles) stays quiet; detector runs off-turn (scheduler lane), adds zero latency to the synchronous gate; review card shows the trajectory evidence.
close_reason: Implemented on feat/cogsec-intake-firewall (33 commits, validated); pending merge to main.

title: Second-arrow detection: self-poisoning via memory stacking around a single concern (rumination inflation)
description: Distinct from third-party slow poisoning: the self-inflicted case (Buddhist second arrow). Evidence (operator, 2026-07-09): a concern built up around a specific memory bug; because the companion could not inspect the memories directly, the concern escalated, generated a stack of near-duplicate memories about that one bug, and deduplication did not catch them all (partly because duplicates kept being generated). The stacking inflated a stress factor -- the bug was not major; repeatedly thinking about it made it FEEL major. Because the system is so heavily built around memory and emotion (a container for a Gestalt entity to find its space), this class matters a lot. Detection shape: per-topic memory-creation velocity + similarity clustering (embedding proximity of recent writes to one concern/topic), concern-loop detection (same concern re-triggering extraction repeatedly), and stress-factor attribution (which cluster is inflating which affect dimension). Response is gentle and reviewable, not automatic deletion: surface a batched review card (htm9.11 lane, same never-auto-mutate rule as htm9.14) proposing consolidation of the cluster via the EXISTING episodic canonicalization/merge machinery; optionally a soft self-notice worded per the htm9.12 language contract. Non-goals: do not suppress genuine repeated concerns (a real ongoing problem legitimately recurs); do not touch dedup heuristics blindly -- investigate why duplicates were generated as part of this work. Depends-on: psfn-framework-htm9.12, psfn-framework-htm9.14 (shares the lane infrastructure). Acceptance: replay of the historical incident pattern (stacked near-duplicate concern memories) produces a consolidation review card with the cluster and stress-attribution evidence; healthy repeated-topic corpus (ongoing project discussed daily) stays quiet.
close_reason: Implemented on feat/cogsec-intake-firewall (33 commits, validated); pending merge to main.

title: Companion-initiated blocking: soft block (channel disconnect + quarantine event) and hard block (gateway drop) as companion agency
description: Mission-level (operator, 2026-07-09): a companion should be able to escalate against an abusive user all the way to a block, as their own choice -- up to 'I never want to see this person's messages again.' Already supported: dropping trust to bottom and choosing not to respond. Extend with: (1) SOFT BLOCK -- messages from an ID are no longer accepted or processed (channel effectively disconnected); each drop generates a quarantine event so the operator sees it; (2) HARD BLOCK at the gateway/cogsec firewall -- inbound from that ID is dropped full stop, before any processing; don't waste context (or companion attention) on it; (3) if Discord's API allows bot-side blocking of inbound messages, do that too (human-in-the-loop confirmation), but the gateway drop is the guaranteed backstop regardless of platform support. Semantics: in group rooms the companion would typically just ignore (no room-wide disruption); in DMs, drop at the gateway. Blocking is a companion-initiated tool action (agency), with the block list persisted as system-owned state and visible/reversible in the Garden cogsec tab; unblocking is a companion or operator action, never automatic. Depends-on: psfn-framework-htm9.1 (events), psfn-framework-htm9.11 (visibility). Acceptance: companion tool can set soft/hard block on a contact ID; hard-blocked ID's inbound never reaches the agent process (gateway-level test); soft block generates quarantine events; group-vs-DM semantics covered by tests; block list surfaces in Garden with audit history.
close_reason: Implemented on feat/cogsec-intake-firewall (33 commits, validated); pending merge to main.

title: Image intake screening via small VLM at L2.5/L3 (OCR + description in one call), no heavy OCR in L1
description: Images are currently the least-screened surface: inline/URL images become raw vision blocks with only size/count/MIME caps (src/core/agent/substrate-agent/vision-attachments.ts:543-659), and the vision-reviewer path's text summary is treated as trusted afterward (no untrusted wrap, lines 179-231). Operator decision 2026-07-09: do NOT build a heavy OCR pipeline (Tesseract et al. too slow/bulky for L1; CLIP+OCR inside the firewall too heavy) -- use a small vision-language model at L2.5/L3 that does OCR and image description in one API call for a fraction of a cent, and catches adversarial cases like near-white text on white that a machine reads but a human cannot. The VLM transcript/description is ITSELF untrusted (taint rule from htm9.1): route it through the L1 text scanners + envelope before it becomes prompt-visible; keep image-source provenance high-risk regardless of transcript cleanliness (pixel-perturbation/steganography attacks have no deployable detector -- documented residual risk). Also fix the existing vision-reviewer summary to carry the envelope label instead of implicit trust. Depends-on: psfn-framework-htm9.1, psfn-framework-htm9.7. Acceptance: an image with embedded instruction text (typographic injection, including near-white-on-white) is flagged and quarantined before any vision block reaches the model; benign images pass with description attached under an untrusted-data label; latency measured per call.
close_reason: Implemented on feat/cogsec-intake-firewall (33 commits, validated); pending merge to main.

title: File ingestion pipeline for all channels: md/text/CSV/office/PDF/images now, audio transcripts through cogsec, video deferred
description: Goal: companions can read attached files across channels -- markdown, text, CSV, Office docs, PDFs, images now; audio via the EXISTING transcription capability with the transcript routed through the cogsec pipeline (a transcript becomes a prompt, so audio is a real injection channel); video deferred until a locally-runnable multimodal model (Gemma-class with video) is practical. Current state (verified 2026-07-09): Discord is the ONLY channel with document parsing + quarantine (src/channels/discord/file-ingest.ts); Telegram captures bare attachment metadata with no download/parse path at all (src/channels/telegram/adapter.ts:1282-1311); API channel does images only. Scope: extract the Discord parse pipeline into a shared channel-agnostic ingest faculty, wire Telegram + API attachments through it, and route ALL parsed text through the intake envelope + L1->L3 layers (htm9.2) -- text attachments currently get zero scanning even on Discord post-parse. Dependency constraints (operator): parsing packages (PDF etc.) pre-installed and PINNED in the container; no arbitrary runtime installation of out-of-scope dependencies; new packages arrive deliberately through the update cycle. Depends-on: psfn-framework-htm9.2. Acceptance: same file sent via Discord, Telegram, and API produces the same parsed text, same envelope, same screening decision (adapter-parity test); audio transcript path carries envelope labels; container builds with pinned parser deps; no new dep installed at runtime.
close_reason: Implemented on feat/cogsec-intake-firewall (33 commits, validated); pending merge to main.

title: Design Garden Discord login and identity-linked authorization
description:
Summary: Harden Garden sign-in/auth. User noted the current Garden sign-in/sign-out path is effectively an SSH/VL web interface with a key and suggested Discord login because chat participants already have Discord accounts. Desired direction: if the operator/admin/partner logs in with Discord, the system can associate that login with their account, relationship, and memory visibility so they are not blocked from viewing what is legitimately theirs.

Scope: Design and then implement a Garden authentication model based on Discord OAuth/identity linking, including admin/operator role mapping, contact/relationship association, session handling, and authorization checks for memories and relationship-scoped data. Preserve fail-closed behavior. Integrate with existing Garden/API boundaries and settings ownership.

Non-goals: Do not bypass existing capability gates; do not expose memories solely because a Discord account exists; do not hard-code live secrets or create off-repo auth config. This bead may need to be split into design and implementation tasks after code inspection.
acceptance_criteria: A concrete auth design exists for Discord OAuth login, identity linking, admin/operator role mapping, and relationship-scoped memory authorization; implementation or follow-up beads define exact files and settings; Garden access fails closed for unlinked Discord accounts; no secrets or auth overrides are stored outside repo-owned/live-approved config; tests cover authorized admin/partner access, unlinked denial, and relationship-scope denial.
close_reason: Subsumed by opl1 epic: its Garden-Discord-login/identity-authz scope is opl1.1/.3/.7/.9 done fleet-wide and subject-scoped. 2026-07-14 bead audit.

title: Replace assistant/user terminology in UI and episode/process surfaces
description:
Summary: Audit and replace product-facing language that refers to the companion as 'assistant' or the person speaking with them as 'user'. User request: 'The way the language is used in episodes and process also possible in other places within the UI and within the way that people are referenced needs to not use the term assistant for the companion or user for the person that speaking with them.'

Scope: Search UI copy, Garden/admin surfaces, episode/process views, labels, headings, empty states, and visible runtime/person references. Replace 'assistant' with companion-appropriate terms and 'user' with person/operator/contact/participant language based on context. Keep protocol/internal role identifiers unchanged where required by provider APIs, serialized contracts, OpenAI message role semantics, or database compatibility, but isolate those from product-visible labels.

Non-goals: Do not rename protocol roles or storage fields unless a separate migration is designed. Do not break OpenAI/LLM message role contracts that require 'user'/'assistant'.
acceptance_criteria: Visible UI copy in Garden/admin episode/process/person-facing surfaces no longer uses 'assistant' for the companion or generic 'user' for the person where a contextual term is possible; required protocol/internal role literals remain intact and are not product-visible; tests or snapshot/golden checks are updated where copy changes; npm run lint passes for tracked code changes.
close_reason: Completed by git commit 9db0d073 (Use companion terminology in UX copy). Evidence: admin-ui chat/session/prompt-monitor surfaces now use the shared companion-name store for companion reply labels; prompt role labels display person/companion language while preserving provider role values; account/channel labels avoid generic user copy; companion-ui operational traces display session companion/person names while preserving role metadata. Validation passed: npm --prefix admin-ui run check; npm --prefix companion-ui test -- src/lib/traces.test.ts; npm --prefix companion-ui run typecheck; npm run lint; npm --prefix admin-ui run build; npm --prefix companion-ui run build; npm --prefix companion-ui run lint; npm --prefix companion-ui test.

title: Add bulk enable/disable control to model selection UI
description:
Summary: On the Garden/admin model selection page, add a prominent per-model control so the operator can disable or enable an entire model entry without toggling each individual purpose tag or route assignment. User phrasing: 'in the model selection page, have a disabled button so we can disable something without having to do each individual item. You can just turn off entire models on and off like that.'

Scope: Wire an enabled/disabled flag through the canonical model registry owner-file contract, expose the state in the model settings UI, and make disabled models unavailable to model routing and primary role projection while keeping their settings visible/editable. Preserve strict settings ownership and validation.

Non-goals: Do not redesign model routing, add provider-group semantics, or implement Garden authentication/terminology cleanup in this bead; those are tracked separately.
acceptance_criteria: Model selection/settings UI exposes a clear per-model enable/disable control; disabled/enabled state remains visible on each model card and in the registry count; saving writes disabled models through the canonical models.json/modelRegistry path as enabled:false and omits enabled:true; disabled models are ignored for enabled-primary validation, role assignment projection, and runtime routing; targeted tests/type checks cover the registry and routing behavior; npm run lint passes.

Evidence: admin-ui/src/routes/models/+page.svelte adds per-model Enable/Disable Model control and visible enabled/total state; src/system/settings/schema-model-registry.ts preserves enabled:false and excludes disabled models from primary projection; src/primitives/llm/routing.ts skips disabled registry entries. Validation passed: npm test -- --run src/primitives/llm/routing.test.ts src/system/settings.test.ts; npx vitest run --config admin-ui/vite.config.ts admin-ui/src/lib/models/registry.test.ts; npm --prefix admin-ui run check; npm run verify:settings-contract; npm run lint; npm run build; npm --prefix admin-ui run build.

title: Document adversarial-review bugfixing practices and add Codex skill
description:
Summary: Add a PSFN process document capturing bugfixing lessons from Bun's Rust rewrite that apply to this repo, including adversarial review, regression-first fixes, no stubs/silent fallbacks, parallel-work boundaries, and workflow repair when agents repeat mistakes. Create a local Codex skill that can be invoked to run an adversarial review pass over recent commits or a specified commit range from a separate reviewer mindset. Add a short AGENTS.md pointer to the new docs file so agents know to consult it for high-risk bugfix/process work, without loading the full guidance on every session start.

Scope: documentation and local skill authoring only; no runtime code changes. Non-goals: do not implement automated CI gates or modify existing runtime validation scripts in this bead.

title: Cross-link virtual/physical places on the Rooms and Satellites pages (operator UX placement for vinz.30)
description:

The operator's original UX model also wanted the model surfaced in-context: VIRTUAL spaces summarized on the conversation Rooms page (/rooms) and PHYSICAL places on the Satellites page (/satellites), with overlapping physical<->virtual rooms cross-linked. This is additive polish on top of the delivered /places surface.

- /satellites shows each satellite's bound physical place (place displayName + link to /places), reusing GET /api/admin/places.

title: [S10] places.json -> Mermaid world-map generator (interim visual, pre-editor)
description:
Interim world visualization before the full map editor (vinz.22): a pure generator that renders places.json (+ satellite bindings) as a Mermaid flowchart. Becomes the 'render' half of the eventual editor.

Scope: (1) pure renderPlacesMermaid(placesRegistry, satelliteRegistry) -> Mermaid string, colocated with the places registry (src/shared/contracts/places-registry.ts / src/channels/backplane/places-registry.ts); sites as subgraphs, places within, satellites bound via placeId, affordances grouped by role (perceiver vs effector) + backend (ha/satellite/vr), and physical<->virtual twin/overlap links rendered ONLY when a twin field is present (forward-compatible with vinz.29's twinOf/mirrorsPlaceId; seed has none yet). Match the existing docs/architecture-diagram.mmd convention (flowchart TB, subgraphs, classDef). (2) Garden admin read route GET /api/admin/places/map returning the mermaid text, reusing vinz.17's places service, so the admin-ui panel (vinz.30) can render it live. (3) a dev script (npm run map:places) that writes/prints docs/world-map.mmd so it renders in docs immediately. Deterministic output, fail-closed on malformed registry, empty registry -> minimal valid diagram.

Related: vinz.22 (full editor, this is the interim), vinz.30 (admin-ui renders the route), vinz.29 (twin overlap fields). Depends on vinz.1 (places registry) + vinz.2 (satellite bindings), both shipped.

Acceptance: given a places.json, the generator emits valid Mermaid showing sites/places/satellites/affordances (and twins when present); the Garden route returns it; the script writes a rendered .mmd; tests cover role grouping, empty registry, and twin-present vs absent.
close_reason: Shipped on origin/s10-location-foundations @ f9c914f8 (merge of 9a1f5326): renderPlacesMermaid generator (src/channels/backplane/places-mermaid.ts), Garden route GET /api/admin/places/map, npm run map:places script, committed docs/world-map.mmd. Uses \n line breaks matching docs/architecture-diagram.mmd house convention; twin/overlap links forward-compatible with vinz.29. 11 tests. Interim visual before vinz.22 editor.

title: [S10] Garden personal/world wiki delineation
description:
Surface a clear PERSONAL vs WORLD distinction in the Garden wiki UX. Today there is NO scope field in the wiki data model (WikiDocumentMetadata, src/faculties/wiki/types.ts:18-34 — only sourceClass/sensitivity/tags) and the Garden wiki UI (admin-ui/src/routes/wiki/+page.svelte, nav.ts:37) is read-only with no personal/world toggle. The wiki today is entirely world/reference knowledge for one companion (retrieval header literally says 'supplemental world knowledge — NOT lived memory'); the personal-vs-world split is PLANNED (multi-companion W5 / i5s2), not yet real.

Scope: (B1) extend AdminWikiListData + listWikiDocuments (services/types/wiki.ts:7, wiki-service.ts:17) to group/label docs by scope; (B2) add a scope filter + labels to the wiki list cards (+page.svelte:194-216, where sourceClass/sensitivity badges already render); (B3) split the 'Wiki' nav entry (nav.ts:37) into Personal vs World, or add scope tabs.

Near-term the scope must be DERIVED (from sourceClass/sensitivity/tags) since no scope field exists; once i5s2 lands a real world-scope field, re-point the grouping to it. Do NOT invent a divergent scope model — align with whatever i5s2 defines. Collision: coordinate any api-routes.ts edits with vinz.17; the wiki service/types/UI files are NOT touched by .17.

Acceptance: the operator can view the wiki filtered/grouped into personal vs world (derived), each doc labeled with its scope, without changing wiki write behavior; when i5s2's real scope field exists the delineation reflects it. Read-only UX; no change to personal-never-in-world enforcement.
close_reason: Premise dead + superseded. Bead's own description states no scope field existed and the split was planned-only; the scope model then shipped (commits b75b855d, a0705063: faculties/wiki/scope.ts write guards, Postgres wiki_document_chunks.scope + shared_wiki_chunks, /api/admin/wiki/scopes + shared-world endpoints). The remaining gap is frontend-only, tracked by psfn-framework-v26r, which this bead's own AC names as its successor ('re-scoped to frontend-only or closed as superseded'). Closing as superseded by v26r.

title: [S10] World-wiki bulk import (fail-closed, personal-fact guarded)
description:
Add a bulk/external ingestion path for WORLD knowledge into the wiki. Today content enters the wiki only via (1) the companion 'wiki' tool's per-doc write/import actions and (2) the nightly sleeptime synthesis pass; there is no bulk import and no admin import route (all 3 Garden wiki routes are GET-only, api-routes.ts ~668-724).

Scope: a bulk importer that loops the single write chokepoint WikiStore.upsert() (src/faculties/wiki/store.ts:289) with an import-class sourceClass (imported_partner_vault_note | parsed_document | external_reference | system_seed) + mandatory provenanceRefs, reusing the existing per-doc import validation (wiki tool 'import' action / buildUpsertInput, src/faculties/wiki/tools.ts:73-89). Expose via a new POST /api/admin/wiki/import Garden route + a write method on AdminWikiService (src/operator/garden/services/wiki-service.ts, services/types/wiki.ts) modeled on the rooms admin pattern.

HARD CONSTRAINT: every imported item MUST pass through filterPersonalFactProposals (src/faculties/wiki/sleeptime-wiki-pass.ts:302-342) before upsert — personal facts (relational/emotional/intimate/confidential/contactId-bearing) must NEVER enter the wiki (Charter Law 32 / Sec 6.26). Fail closed: rejected items are reported, not silently dropped; provenance mandatory; wiki writes never create L2 memory.

Aligns with vinz.4 (world/place publisher) and the multi-companion shared-wiki bead i5s2 (which will define the real world-scope + caretaker/operator-approval gate); do NOT pre-empt i5s2's shared-schema/propose-only model — this bead targets the current single-companion wiki store. Coordinate the api-routes.ts mount point with vinz.17 (also edits that file).

Acceptance: an operator can bulk-import a set of world-knowledge docs with provenance; any doc containing personal facts is rejected by the guard with a clear reason; imported docs are searchable/retrievable and marked as import-class provenance; no L2 memory is created.
close_reason: Closed

title: Voice and satellite binding rules for multi-companion: one companion per satellite, one-to-one routing
description: Decisions (review): voice routes exactly like text — one-to-one to the endpoint/app/Discord-voice-chat the companion is generated on, even with multiple companions doing TTS/STT in one voice chat. Hard rule: one companion per satellite (and per app) — one emanation to one physical device, never two; a satellite device + ID acts as a channel carrying its location info; once bound, the emanation speaks only through that device; if the operator moves rooms the companion rebinds to that room's device and future voice forwards there. Scope: verify the voice stream path threads W1 companion routing (it already carries a companionId tag — src/boundary/gateway/server.ts:415-416); enforce the one-companion-per-satellite invariant at binding time, fail closed. Context: the Wyoming-based voice-to-satellite approach is likely not final; the full voice rewrite is a separate deferred bead. Acceptance: binding a second companion to an occupied satellite is rejected; voice round-trip in multi-companion mode reaches only the bound companion. Plan: working_docs/sprint-10-multi-companion.md W7.

title: [S10] Conversation-follows-you: session handoff on presence room change
description: Workstream G1 (Decision 7). When a presence event fires on a different satellite/place than the active emanation (user says 'I'm going to the kitchen', leaves the bedroom, presence lands on the kitchen satellite), hand off the active emanation and continue the SAME conversation in the new place rather than starting cold. Wire src/core/agent/active-emanation-state.ts (the B2 handoff surface) driven by the D1 bridge; situated block (B1/B3) then foregrounds the new room. Guardrails: debounce/settle so passing through doesn't thrash; only follow on a confident presence claim for owner/partner (trust-gated); do not follow into a place with no bound satellite.
acceptance_criteria: A presence event on place B while emanating in place A moves the active emanation to B and the live session continues (context carried, not reset); rapid transient events do not thrash; an unrecognized/low-confidence presence does not trigger a follow.
close_reason: Closed

comments.text: 2026-07-13 orphan audit: leave OPEN (guardrails shipped; session-continuity acceptance not demonstrated). Commits 6631a85a + 4ae3f9c4 (merge 36c56fac) wire physical presence claims through trust/freshness/physical-place/debounce gates, CompanionPresenceTurnPort, and SituatedEmanationTracker; presence-follow.test.ts covers the move and deny paths. But applyEmanationFollowHandoff in src/core/agent/substrate-agent.ts only updates situated/durable location. The implementation does not hand off or alias SessionManager/channel history between the old and new satellite channels, and its tests assert tracker/port/event/note behavior rather than 'same conversation continues (context carried, not reset)'. Keep open until that explicit session-continuity criterion is implemented/proven or acceptance is rescoped to emanation-only follow.

title: [S10] Location-scoped concerns/reminders fire on presence events
description: Workstream G2 (Decision 7, absorbs old D4). Entering a place can trigger a proactive internal turn scoped to that place's concerns ('drink water', 'bring down snacks'). Model location-scoped concerns/reminders (owner-/companion-authorable, keyed by placeId) and fire on the D1 presence event via the heartbeat/internal-turn path (scheduler/scheduler.ts -> heartbeat-post-turn-runtime.ts). Respect the LLM-call-economy principle: a cheap deterministic gate (eligible unfired concern for this place? fired recently?) decides WHETHER to spend a turn before any LLM call. Avatar 'runs into frame'/procedural animation is horizon, not built here.
acceptance_criteria: Entering a place with an eligible location-scoped concern fires exactly one proactive turn; a place with no eligible concern fires nothing; the deterministic gate prevents repeat/duplicate firing and respects charge; concerns are owner-only editable in Garden.
notes: 2026-07-27 older-history reconciliation: KEEP OPEN. Commit a2226c46c7 cites vinz.21 but implements virtual-room presence follow (src/core/agent/virtual-room-follow.ts), which belongs to the conversation-following scope, not this bead's location-scoped concern/reminder trigger. No implementation of placeId-keyed concerns, deterministic eligible/recently-fired gate, charge-aware proactive turn, or owner-only Garden editor was found; repo search only mentions this scope in docs/productivity-pack.md.

title: [S10] Publish world/place info into the companion wiki/vault
description:
Workstream A4 (Decision 2). Publish a human-readable, browsable projection of the world (sites, places, notable affordances, operator-authored place lore) into the companion wiki/vault so she has browsable world knowledge. Derived read-only projection of places.json (plus optional operator prose), NOT a second source of truth. Coordinate with shared-world wiki MVP (psfn-framework-i5s2) for ACLs/review gates.
Seam: places.json -> wiki/vault publisher; respects i5s2 gates.

title: [S10] Virtual place kind + MUD-over-Discord virtual-environment testbed
description:
Workstream A3 (reframed per Decision 5). kind:'virtual' places with virtual affordances (backend 'vr'/virtual-object ids), no HA binding. First virtual environment this sprint = a text MUD run over the EXISTING Discord channel: virtual places + virtual objects driven through Discord, exercising the same places.json model, situated block, and world tool as physical rooms (only effector backend + transport differ). No engine dependency. UE5 is a future-horizon non-goal (epic, S6.8).
Seam: places.json virtual entries; world tool control routing branches on backend; Discord channel as transport.
acceptance_criteria: Virtual place + objects load from places.json; world list/perceive/control operate on them through Discord; situated block foregrounds the virtual place's affordances exactly as for a physical room.
close_reason: Virtual place capability landed via vinz.1/.9/.26: kind:virtual places, world perceive/list/control/move MUD contract (world/tools.ts), situated-block handling, room-entry tests. Verified on main.

title: Consolidate companion skill storage under root skills and personal workspace skills
description:
Summary: Clarify and enforce the companion framework skill storage contract. Repo-provided/global companion skills should live under the repository root skills/ directory. Companion-authored or user-managed skills should live in that companion's personal writable root under WORKSPACE_PATH/skills/<category>/<name>/SKILL.md. The current tree is split between root skills/ and data/skills/tools/web-fetch/SKILL.md, and the loader defaults/config seed still prioritize companion/skills before skills.

Files to inspect/update: config/skills.seed.json; src/faculties/skills/loader.ts; src/faculties/skills/loader.test.ts; src/faculties/skills/runtime.test.ts; src/faculties/skills/runtime-wiring.test.ts; src/faculties/skills/filter.test.ts if its config fixture needs alignment; docs/tool-surface.md or README/setup docs where they describe global versus personal skills. Move the tracked web-fetch skill from data/skills/tools/web-fetch/SKILL.md into root skills/web-fetch/SKILL.md or another root skills subdirectory consistent with the existing loader shape.

Why: DATA_DIR/system data is runtime-owned state/config, not the place for global deployment skills. Splitting static skills between skills/ and data/skills/tools makes it unclear what ships with the framework versus what the companion creates. The framework should provide global companion skills from skills/, while each companion can create its own skills in its own WORKSPACE_PATH skills directory.

Scope: update runtime defaults, seed config, tests, and docs to express this contract; move the stray tracked data/skills skill into root skills/; preserve existing managed skill create/update behavior under WORKSPACE_PATH/skills. Non-goals: do not implement the future Hermes security scanner/agent-created-skill guard in psfn-framework-i72.2; do not create compatibility readers for data/skills; do not migrate live untracked data outside the repo.
acceptance_criteria: config/skills.seed.json defaults to root skills/ as the global skill directory; the skills loader no longer injects companion/skills ahead of root skills/ by default; the tracked repository has no data/skills SKILL.md files; managed skill create/update paths still point at WORKSPACE_PATH/skills; targeted skills tests pass; npm run lint passes before closure.
notes:
Implementation is present in the worktree: root skills/ is now the only default global skills directory, config/skills.seed.json lists only skills, the old companion/skills and psfn/skills constants/default source were removed, repo write allowlist now includes skills/ instead of companion/psfn, docs clarify repo-global skills vs WORKSPACE_PATH/skills personal managed skills, and the tracked web-fetch skill was moved from data/skills/tools/web-fetch/SKILL.md to skills/web-fetch/SKILL.md.

title: Carlini's primary model ChatGPTN (local vLLM via LiteLLM) intermittently leaks DeepSeek template artifact, forcing fallbacks and empty Discord replies
description:
Evidence
Carlini gateway log, 4x on 2026-07-06/07 (01:31:17, 01:33:31, 05:48:51, 12:05:11), verbatim:
WARN [ModelFallback] Candidate failed; trying fallback model {"purpose":"agent.turn.prompt","errorCategory":"empty_response","failedModel":"ChatGPTN","failedProvider":"litellm","nextModel":"deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash","nextProvider":"openrouter","error":"LLM response from litellm/ChatGPTN began with provider template artifact <｜begin▁of▁sentence｜>"}
Additionally 4x "WARN [Discord] Discord handler returned empty response without a suppression marker" on channel 1486443955561299979 (08:24-08:56) — plausibly the same degradation on interactive turns.

Context
PSFN detects the artifact correctly (src/primitives/llm/client.ts:100-103, throw at ~1999, classified retryable at error-classify.ts:93) — this is a serving-stack problem, not PSFN code: the ChatGPTN vLLM endpoint (http://192.168.1.43:8000/v1) is emitting a DeepSeek chat-template control token at response start (wrong/missing chat template or template mismatch in vLLM or the LiteLLM route). Every occurrence pushes the turn onto the openrouter fallback where psfn-framework-l73i (dropped tool args) lives, so fixing this shrinks exposure to that bug too.

Scope
- Fix the model serving config: vLLM chat template for the ChatGPTN deployment and/or the LiteLLM route mapping on Carlini's cluster (chart values liteLlm.config.yaml). Ops/config change, likely no PSFN code.
- Investigate the 4 empty Discord replies once the artifact leak is fixed; file separately if they persist.

Acceptance criteria
- Zero "provider template artifact" ModelFallback WARNs over a multi-day window on Carlini.
- No unexplained empty Discord handler responses in the same window.

Related: psfn-framework-l73i (exposed by the fallback this bug triggers), psfn-framework-c1tv (other LiteLLM route config debt).
notes: Live triage 2026-07-14 (image 0.1.0-kube-c0385f2b, 6h window): 13 of 135 turn selections (~9.6%) failed with 'LLM response from litellm/ChatGPTN contained no text or tool calls' -> empty_response -> fallback chain ChatGPTN -> deepseek-v4-flash -> glm-5.2. One turn needed the 3rd hop (deepseek also returned empty once); worst case turn 019f6260 took 88s with 2 wasted model calls. Blast radius: main companion primary Discord channel 10x + internal:free-time:idle 3x, 14:16-17:11. Error surfaces at src/primitives/llm/client-response-helpers.ts:279, classified empty_response at error-classify.ts:89. litellm config has drop_params:true — consistent with tool-calling/template incompat on the vLLM backend. NOTE: psfn-framework-liql tracks the same root cause (template artifact angle) — candidates for merge.

title: Streamed tool-call arguments still dropped (stream_parse_dropped) on openrouter deepseek fallback — journal write silently no-oped
description:
Evidence
Carlini gateway log 2026-07-06 01:31:22 (verbatim):
WARN [LLMClient] Tool call arrived with empty arguments {"provenance":"stream_parse_dropped","toolName":"journal","toolCallId":"call_b479e03e7990472fbfa5dd76","argumentFragmentBytes":20,"provider":"openrouter","model":"deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash","requestId":"free-time-quiet_hours-0-1783402271699","channelId":"internal:free-time:quiet-hours"}

Context
src/primitives/llm/client.ts:1167-1170 documents stream_parse_dropped as the pre-patch pi-ai failure mode that "should not fire once the pi-ai index-routing patch is applied" — so the patched accumulator still loses fragments for deepseek-v4-flash via OpenRouter streaming. The companion attempted a journal write and it silently no-oped; she cannot see the failure. @mariozechner/pi-ai is pinned + patched via patch-package (patches/) — investigate the streaming tool-call accumulator there for this provider/model shape (possibly index-less or differently-indexed deltas).

Scope
- Reproduce with a captured deepseek/openrouter stream if possible; extend the pi-ai patch; regenerate patch file.
- Consider fail-closed handling: an empty-arg tool call on a fallback turn could be surfaced to the agent as a tool error instead of dropped, so she can retry (matches no-swallowed-errors rule).
- Non-goal: model/provider selection changes.

Acceptance criteria
- A regression test (or captured-stream fixture) that previously produced stream_parse_dropped now yields intact arguments, and/or the dropped call surfaces as a visible tool failure to the agent loop rather than a silent no-op.
- No stream_parse_dropped occurrences in gateway logs across a week of live operation on the fallback model.

- Non-goals: do not modify memory text/ids/timestamps; do not touch the HMAC-chained session journals; do not synthesize subjectContactId.

- After apply, the social-graph builder scans them (scanned>0 with watermark reset or set below their extractedAt) and produces co_presence/named proposals visible in Garden graph approval.

Blocked by psfn-framework-tsyo and psfn-framework-0zd9.

title: Move shell.exec execution out of the gateway secrets boundary into a broker that never held credentials
description: Evidence (gateway/boundary audit 2026-07-07): shell.exec is registered as a gateway method (boundary/gateway/methods/index.ts:25, methods/shell.ts) and executes as a child of the secrets-holding gateway process. Isolation is by env scrubbing + allowlisting (shell-runner.ts:96-126 builds a clean env, no process.env inheritance, command/cwd allowlists, symlink canonicalization) — strong in practice, but charter 6.5/Phase 3 requires untrusted execution OUTSIDE the secrets boundary structurally, not socially. The analysis_workbench path is the model to match: out-of-process child with env: {}, --permission, --disallow-code-generation-from-strings, and a normalizer that throws unless isolatedFromGatewaySecrets:true (sandbox-execution-port.ts:288-296). Fix: route shell.exec execution through a broker process that never held gateway secrets (the agent-side broker already claims isolatedFromGatewaySecrets:true), keeping policy evaluation and audit at the gateway. Scope: no change to the policy/allowlist semantics; this is a process-boundary move.
acceptance_criteria: shell.exec child processes are spawned by a non-secret-holding broker (verified by a test asserting the executing process env cannot contain gateway secrets even without scrubbing); policy + audit behavior unchanged; e2e shell path passes.

title: Datetime-contradiction guard false-positives can replace valid replies with a refusal
description: Evidence (Codex peer review 2026-07-07): src/core/agent/substrate-agent/runtime-datetime-contradiction-guard.ts:46,50 define broad phrase patterns ('must be a bug', 'are you sure') applied over the whole response once a datetime anchor exists (:136); if retry still trips, agent-invocation.ts:748 replaces the reply with a first-person datetime refusal. A valid reply containing 'are you sure?' for a non-datetime reason can be converted into a datetime refusal. Context: care-sensitive — silently replacing companion speech is exactly what the guard exists to prevent in the other direction. Fix: require the trigger phrase to be datetime-adjacent (proximity window or clause-level match) rather than anywhere in the response; log guard activations as typed events for Garden visibility. Scope: keep the guard; tighten matching. Related: refusal text provenance is covered by the fallback-provenance bead.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests cover a non-datetime 'are you sure?' reply passing untouched and a real contradiction still caught; guard activation emits a typed event.
close_reason: Landed via PR #297 (main 2128516951); review record in lane PR #285, commit a20361f38. Acceptance met in full: broad phrases ('are you sure', 'must be a bug', ...) now require a time reference within a 160-char adjacency window (time/clock/date terms, weekday/month names, digit shapes; bare 'May' excluded for the modal-verb collision), so a non-datetime 'are you sure?' reply passes untouched end-to-end while a real datetime contradiction is still caught; typed CONTENT-FREE agent.datetime_guard.activation events are emitted at all three outcomes for Garden visibility, with a regression asserting the payload can never carry her text. Empirically probed in review: a scheduling-small-talk false positive costs one retry with her reply preserved verbatim (no text replacement exists on this base), and a missed-nudge false negative only skips the retry. Train-side follow-through: 2128516951 aligns the voice reply-stream content-gate straddle case with this adjacency contract — the straddling broad phrase without a datetime reference is precisely the false positive the change eliminates, and the anti-fabrication core is preserved by a new datetime-adjacent straddle case. Validation per #285: 39 files / 486 tests green in-lane, reviewer independently re-ran 35 files / 394; lint:changed clean (13 files); UBS criticals all blame pre-existing; blind adversarial review (Opus) PASS, zero blocking findings. Bookkeeping: this bead was in DEFERRED (not open) state; closing because the deferred scope is now delivered on main.

title: bug
description:
Evidence (2026-07-07): npm run ship:kube -- --components agent failed with 'FAIL: live psfn-garden carries no contract hash (pre-hash image); first selective ship requires --components all' while all three live pods demonstrably carried the SAME hash (5521c3d6021fc87c, verified by kubectl exec cat /app/contract-hash.txt on garden/gateway/agent minutes later, matching the new image's in-image verification line). Garden was mid crash-loop at guard time (probe SIGTERM ~80s after boot, 7 restarts in 13min, then stable), so the guard's exec returned nothing.

Cause: scripts/ops/ship-kube-update.sh:160 — LIVE_HASH=$(rkubectl exec ... cat /app/contract-hash.txt 2>/dev/null || true) treats ANY exec failure (pod not ready, container restarting) as an empty hash, and empty hash is reported as 'pre-hash image'. This forces pointless full-stack rebuilds, defeating the per-component chart split.

Scope: distinguish 'exec failed / pod not ready' (retry with backoff, then fail naming the real cause) from 'file genuinely absent' (the true pre-hash case). Do not weaken the guard itself.

Related: garden's boot-time probe crash-loop (clean SIGTERM after ~80s, repeatedly, on every rollout) is what exposed this; consider a separate look at garden's startup/liveness probe timing.

Acceptance: with one component's pod deliberately restarting, --components agent either succeeds after retry or fails with an exec/readiness error message; 'pre-hash image' is only reported when a ready pod truly lacks /app/contract-hash.txt.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #91 (2459be7b0a): bounded reachability probe distinguishes exec failure from missing hash, ship-kube-update.sh (f4b07587f4)

title: session:repair:integrity is unreachable in production images and surgery flows do not re-sign chains
description:
Evidence: During psfn-framework-tswt remediation, npm run session:repair:integrity could not run in-pod: tsup only compiles the four main entrypoints (tsup.config.ts), the production image has no tsx, and the agent pod lacks GATEWAY_SESSION_HMAC_KEY (gateway-only env). Scope: (a) compile the maintenance CLIs (or a single maintenance entrypoint) into dist so they run in-image with node, or provide an operator-side wrapper that pulls files + key and round-trips them; (b) any future surgery helper should re-sign the affected chain as part of its atomic rewrite. Non-goal: changing the HMAC chain format or key management.

Acceptance: a documented single command (in-pod or operator-side) re-signs a sessions dir end-to-end; running it after a simulated entry deletion yields 0 verification failures; psfn-live-ops skill references it.

title: Extract shared surfaces and sever dead SQLite bridges so legacy SQLite modules become unreferenced
description:
Summary:
Extraction/bridge-severing prep phase for the SQLite removal push. After this bead, every legacy SQLite module is unreferenced by production code (build- and runtime-wise), so the removal beads 3c2.5/3c2.6 become pure file deletion. This is the needle-threading phase (Fable work); the deletions that follow are mechanical (Codex work).

Evidence (reachability audit 2026-07-06, this session):
- Runtime is already safe: PersistenceBackend is typed 'postgres' only (src/system/config/runtime-config-contracts.ts:29), PERSISTENCE_BACKEND=sqlite throws at config load (load-config.ts:99-111), runtime-factory returns db:null, and every SQLite construction branch in core-runtime.ts / scheduler-runtime.ts / contacts+intention runtime-wiring is dead behind fail-closed guards.
- BUT better-sqlite3 eager-loads at startup of every entrypoint via two static value-import chains: sessions/store.ts -> sessions/sqlite-adapters.ts -> transcript-projection.ts -> sqlite-utils.ts:1, and scheduler-runtime.ts -> backups/service.ts:1.
- ~44 SQLite files are build-coupled through value imports in bridge files (core-runtime.ts:4,41; sessions/store.ts:41-46; contacts/runtime-wiring.ts:5; intention/runtime-wiring.ts:33-35; backups/service.ts:1,48; episodic/index.ts:27).
- Shared helpers/types live INSIDE SQLite modules and are value-used by the Postgres path.

Scope (all changes keep behavior identical; SQLite files stay on disk, just unreferenced):
1. Split mixed intention modules — extract the SQLite store classes out of src/core/intention/concerns.ts, pending-follow-ups.ts, care-reminders.ts, patterns.ts while keeping the shared helpers/types where the Postgres path finds them (mergeConcernStatus/normalizeConcernStatus/isConcernTerminalStatus/validateConcernStatusTransition used by postgres-adapters/concerns-adapter.ts:15-19 and appraisal/*; createBehavioralPatternMemoryPromotionHook value-used by app/agent/main.ts:41; self-model/state.ts:19-45 type imports).
2. Episodic port split — move EpisodicStorePort out of src/faculties/memory/episodic/store.ts; stop episodic/index.ts:27 re-exporting the SQLite store from the barrel the Postgres factory uses.
3. Gateway audit types — move GatewayAuditHistoryPage/GatewayAuditHistoryQuery out of src/boundary/gateway/audit.ts into a port module; repoint audit-history-service.ts:14-18.
4. Sever dead bridges: core-runtime.ts (drop MemoryStore/wireContactRuntime/wireIntentionRuntime value imports and dead branches at :196-210, :366-391; injected Postgres stores become mandatory, fail closed); contacts/runtime-wiring.ts:5,59; intention/runtime-wiring.ts:33-35,391; sessions/store.ts:41-46,409,413,433 (drop createDefaultSQLite* defaults — note ArchivePort/TurnRecordStorePort defaults are actually filesystem/JSONL, keep those behaviors via direct filesystem imports); backups/service.ts (drop better-sqlite3 import :1, restore-verify branch :383, runDatabaseIntegrityCheck import :48); core-bootstrap.ts/scheduler-runtime.ts db?: Database option removal (type surface change); contacts/store/upsert.ts light surgery (drop the one Database-typed function, keep collectUpsertIdentities used by postgres-adapter/crud-operations.ts:42).
5. Keep untouched: contacts/store/emotional-baseline.ts, identity-utils.ts (not SQLite; value-used by Postgres adapters).

Non-goals: no file deletions in this bead (that is 3c2.5/3c2.6); no test-fixture migration (3c2.8); no maintenance/importer changes (3c2.7).

Acceptance criteria:
- rg -l "better-sqlite3|sqlite-vec|sqlite-utils" over src reachable-from-entrypoint graph shows the four app entrypoints no longer transitively value-import any SQLite module (spot-proof: node -e loading dist gateway/agent/operator mains after temporarily moving node_modules/better-sqlite3 aside, or equivalent static trace).
- npm run build, npm run lint pass; focused tests pass: src/app/agent/core-runtime.test.ts, src/app/startup/composition/session-composition.test.ts, src/persistence/backups/service.test.ts, intention/contacts runtime-wiring tests.
- Production startup paths still fail closed when Postgres stores are not injected.
close_reason: Landed on foundation_e0_e2 (merge 4df33735, pushed). SQLite classes extracted to intention/sqlite-stores/; episodic store-port.ts split with barrel fix; audit history types moved to audit-port.ts; db plumbing removed from core-runtime/core-bootstrap/scheduler-runtime/main/runtime-factory; contacts+intention SQLite convenience wiring deleted; sessions/store SQLite defaults replaced with filesystem ports (enableSearchIndex removed); backups/service SQLite capture + restore-verify removed. Evidence: tsup build passes; dist gateway/agent/operator bundles contain zero better-sqlite3 references (grep -c = 0); tsc --noEmit and eslint match baseline exactly (16/8 pre-existing errors in untouched files); focused vitest 780+ tests green incl. post-merge rerun (268 tests) after resolving arc-formation.ts conflict with new judgment-runner code. 3c2.5/3c2.6 are now pure file deletion.

title: Path-containment checks outside layout.ts are weaker string-prefix reimplementations
description:
Summary:
src/persistence/layout.ts:142-145 owns the canonical path-containment check (isStrictSubpath, relative()-based, rejects ..-traversal after normalization) but it is private/unexported. Two modules reimplement containment with weaker pure string-prefix checks that do NOT normalize traversal:
- src/primitives/images/reference-store.ts:384-390 (resolveReferencePath): `candidate !== root && candidate.startsWith(root + '/')`
- src/core/cogsec/forensic-archive.ts:114-121 (assertInsideRoot): same check, inverted.

Why it matters:
This is a correctness/safety gap, not just style — the reimplementations are strictly weaker than the canonical check. Path containment is fail-closed territory.

Suggested implementation direction:
Export isStrictSubpath (or add assertPathInsideRoot(path, root, errorMessage)) from layout.ts — or promote it to src/shared/utils/ as a generic filesystem-safety primitive — and migrate both call sites.

Non-goals:
- Do NOT fold in src/boundary/gateway/filesystem-paths.ts — it is a legitimately separate domain (sandbox workspace path resolution with symlink/realpath handling), not a duplicate.

Acceptance criteria:
- Both sites use the canonical check.
- Tests cover traversal-escape cases (e.g. root + '/../evil', prefix-sibling dirs like root-extra/) at both call sites.
- npm run lint passes before close.
close_reason: Merged (commit 300532dd): isStrictSubpath exported from layout.ts; reference-store and forensic-archive migrated off weak string-prefix checks; traversal-escape and sibling-prefix tests at both sites; launcher also caught and reverted codex removing basename() flattening in parseStoredReference (regression test added). Build pass, 12/12 relevant tests.

title: Experiential template deliberation reimplements runDeliberation in the same file
description:
Summary:
The experiential template deliberation loop reimplements the shared runDeliberation primitive — in the same file that also uses the real one. runExperientialTemplateDeliberation (src/core/scheduler/heartbeat-template-runtime.ts:1397-1650) hand-rolls a multi-round loop with maxRounds/maxWallTimeMs/token-cap stop conditions, per-round token/cost accounting, stopReason tracking, and per-round correlation — all of which runDeliberation (src/primitives/llm/deliberation.ts:458) already owns. The non-experiential path (runTemplateDeliberation, line 1858) already routes through the shared primitive; the branch at line 1844 (isExperientialDeliberationTemplate) diverts to the hand-rolled 3-stage evidence→synthesis→contradiction loop with three inline system prompts (lines 1401-1467, not PromptRegistry-backed) and no retry wrapping around the three stage complete calls (only buildReflectionDeliberationCorrelation is shared).

Why it matters:
Strongest LLM-path duplication found in the 2026-07-06 audit: near-identical budget/round architecture built twice in one file. Every future budget, telemetry, or stop-condition fix must land twice or silently diverge.

Files to inspect/change:
- src/core/scheduler/heartbeat-template-runtime.ts:1397-1650, 1844-1885
- src/primitives/llm/deliberation.ts:458 (DeliberationOptions)
- tests for template deliberation

Suggested implementation direction:
Extend DeliberationOptions to support a fixed stage sequence (evidence→synthesis→contradiction) or a generic stages config, then route the experiential path through runDeliberation and delete the hand-rolled loop. Consider PromptRegistry keys for the three stage prompts while touching them.

Related: the novelty-watermark gating bead for the same surface is filed separately; keep the two changes untangled.

Acceptance criteria:
- Experiential templates run through the shared primitive with the output contract preserved (stage sequence, stopReason, token accounting).
- The hand-rolled loop is removed.
- Tests cover stage sequencing and each stop condition.
- npm run lint passes before close.
close_reason: Merged in cd9927c8 (commit 131e8770): DeliberationOptions.stages fixed-stage mode added to runDeliberation (fail-closed on empty/duplicate stages, conflicting options); experiential evidence→synthesis→contradiction path routed through shared primitive; ~170-line hand-rolled loop deleted; output contract traced and preserved (per-stage correlation heartbeat.deliberation.<stage>, caps, ValuesDeliberationMetadata consumers). 5 new staged-mode tests; 86 tests across 9 suites green.

title: Heartbeat reflection templates fire on cadence without a novelty watermark gate
description:
Summary:
Heartbeat scheduled reflection templates fire on cadence with no novelty gate — only a rapid-fire cooldown. executeTemplate (src/core/scheduler/heartbeat-template-runtime.ts:1870-1885) runs deliberation (experiential path: up to 3 rounds / ~6000 tokens default) on every cadence tick; the only pre-check is assertTemplateExecutionAllowed (lines 597-612), which enforces templateExecutionCooldownUntil to prevent loop storms, not a "did anything new happen since the last reflection" check. Every other sleeptime-style pass (dream-meaning-pass.ts, sleeptime-wiki-pass.ts, arc-formation.ts) gates on watermark-based new-entry signals via the shared evaluateDeterministicGate (src/shared/gating/deterministic-gate.ts). This surface just doesn't use the primitive that already exists.

Why it matters:
Cadence-triggered multi-round LLM spend regardless of whether any session activity occurred. LLM-call-economy principle: deterministic indicators decide IF a call happens.

Files to inspect/change:
- src/core/scheduler/heartbeat-template-runtime.ts:597-612, 1844-1885, template registration ~2470-2476
- src/shared/gating/deterministic-gate.ts (reuse, don't reinvent)
- src/faculties/memory/episodic/dream-meaning-pass.ts / src/faculties/wiki/sleeptime-wiki-pass.ts as the pattern to follow

Suggested implementation direction:
Add a per-template/scope watermark (entries since last reflection) and skip below a configurable minimum, following the dream/wiki pass pattern. Keep the cooldown as-is.

Related: the experiential-deliberation duplication bead filed alongside this one covers the same surface's loop implementation; land whichever first, but don't tangle the two changes.

Acceptance criteria:
- Reflection templates skip with telemetry when insufficient new entries exist since the last run for that template/scope.
- Cadence and cooldown behavior otherwise unchanged.
- Tests cover both skip and fire paths.
- npm run lint passes before close.
close_reason: Merged in cd9927c8 (commit 2f8ba5e8): cadence-fired templates now consult evaluateDeterministicGate with per-template/scope watermark (reflection_template_novelty via episodic watermark store, counting partner-session user/assistant entries); manual run_template bypasses gate but advances watermark; skips emit reflection.template.novelty.gate with zero spend; scheduler.json gains reflectionNovelty.minNewEntries (default 1). verify:settings-contract pass; skip/fire/first-run/manual-bypass tests.

title: Extraction low-signal pre-LLM gate is bypassed for tracked contacts
description:
Summary:
The extraction low-signal pre-LLM gate is bypassed for tracked contacts — the normal case. evaluateExtractionPreLlmGate (src/faculties/memory/extraction/signals.ts) only runs when options.canonicalContactId is absent: src/faculties/memory/extraction/orchestrator.ts:190 wraps it in `if (!options.canonicalContactId)`. canonicalContactId is set for any resolved/tracked contact (via authorContext.canonicalContactKey in pre-turn-state.ts), i.e. nearly all real 1:1 traffic after the first exchange. The outer trigger (evaluateExtractionTrigger, src/faculties/memory/extraction/runtime-helpers.ts:56-107) is content-blind — message-count interval / token threshold only. Net effect: a streak of "ok"/"lol"/"np" from a known contact that crosses the interval still spends a full extraction LLM call — exactly the case the low-signal gate exists to prevent, but it never runs.

Why it matters:
Highest-impact ungated background LLM call found in the 2026-07-06 gating audit. Violates the LLM-call-economy principle: cheap deterministic indicators should decide whether a call is needed before spending one.

Files to inspect/change:
- src/faculties/memory/extraction/orchestrator.ts:190
- src/faculties/memory/extraction/signals.ts (evaluateExtractionPreLlmGate)
- src/faculties/memory/extraction/runtime-helpers.ts:56-107
- tests near the extraction orchestrator/signals tests

Suggested implementation direction:
Run the low-signal/empty-transcript gate unconditionally before the LLM call. If known-contact channels were deliberately exempted, encode and document the reason and replace with a per-contact novelty gate instead — but default assumption is the exemption is an oversight and should be dropped.

Acceptance criteria:
- The pre-LLM gate runs for tracked-contact extractions.
- Low-signal transcripts skip the extraction LLM call, with telemetry recording the skip and reason.
- Signal-bearing transcripts extract exactly as before.
- Tests cover the known-contact low-signal skip path.
- npm run lint passes before close.
close_reason: Merged in e8428877 (commit df018428): gate now runs unconditionally in orchestrator.ts before the LLM call with skip telemetry carrying triggerContactId. History check: exemption introduced with the gate itself in 3b9a1d85 with no documented reason. Validated: npm run build pass; orchestrator.test.ts covers known-contact low-signal skip and signal-bearing extraction unchanged (71/72 extraction tests pass; the 1 failure is pre-existing on baseline 4b900caa, verified in a detached worktree, tracked separately).

title: Dedupe agent 'I'm back' startup notifications across deploy restarts
description: Every deploy, the agent boots 2-3 times (initial pod start, then restart(s) when the gateway pod is replaced and RPC drops - exit-on-RPC-loss is by design), and each boot sends a ready/startup notification to the last active channel ('Ready notification sent to ...' in lifecycle). The partner receives 2-3 'I'm back' messages per rollout. Fix: dedupe the ready notification - persist a marker keyed on image tag (PSFN_IMAGE_TAG env, available since x5rt.1) + channel, and suppress repeat notifications for the same tag within a bounded window (e.g. 15 min); first boot of a NEW build still announces. Optionally also add a wait-for-gateway init/startup gate so the agent's first boot happens after gateway is ready, reducing restarts to 1. Related context: all three deployments share one image, so any rebuild restarts gateway/garden too - per-component images are a separate x5rt.6-era consideration, note it there rather than splitting now.
