title: Give free-time return summaries their own purpose and budget
description:
Summary:
Free-time activity summaries reuse wake-session summary semantics even though they are a different lane. In src/app/agent/main.ts:774-782, registerFreeTimeTasks wires summarizeActivity to summarizeRecentSessionEntries with maxTokens from schedulerConfig.temporalWakeup.morningWake.catchUpSummaryMaxTokens and purpose "wake_session". src/core/scheduler/free-time.ts:381-383 documents that this should use summarizeRecentSessionEntries purpose "wake_session". That kept the implementation consolidated, but now the telemetry/prompt purpose and config ownership blur together: a free-time "while you were away" return note is not the same task as a morning wake catch-up summary.

Why it matters:
The code has avoided a bespoke free-time summarizer, which is good. The remaining issue is semantic overlap: purpose names, originStage values, and budget configuration imply wake-up behavior for a free-time return-note task. This can confuse future prompt tuning, telemetry review, and scheduler config ownership. It also makes it harder to introduce a task-specific prompt later without accidentally changing wake-up summaries.

Files to inspect/change:
- src/app/agent/main.ts:724-782
- src/core/scheduler/free-time.ts:381-383 and surfaceReturnNote around 407-451
- src/core/session/manager/compaction-service.ts:66-76, 167-184
- src/system/config/scheduler-config.ts freeTime config shape and validation around the FreeTimeConfig definitions and validateFreeTimeConfig
- src/system/config/scheduler-runtime.ts:47-55 and startup-owner/subsystem config tests if a new freeTime summary budget is added
- tests near src/core/scheduler/free-time.test.ts, src/system/config/scheduler-config.test.ts, src/core/session/manager/context-builder.test.ts if purpose mapping changes

Suggested implementation direction:
Add a distinct RecentSessionSummaryPurpose value such as "free_time_return" and use it when free-time activity is summarized. If the token budget should be configurable, add a JSON-owned freeTime return-summary budget (for example freeTime.returnSummaryMaxTokens or freeTime.returnNote.summaryMaxTokens) instead of borrowing temporalWakeup.morningWake.catchUpSummaryMaxTokens. If prompt wording should remain shared, keep the same RECENT_SESSION_SUMMARY_PROMPT_KEY initially but preserve distinct purpose/originStage metadata so the lanes can diverge later without another audit.

Non-goals:
- Do not create a separate free-time summarizer function.
- Do not change free-time gate behavior, charge budgeting, internal channel isolation, or return-note delivery behavior.
- Do not alter temporal wake-up summary semantics except where needed to keep shared types exhaustive.

Verification addendum (2026-07-06, code-audited):
All claims above verified accurate. The change is cheaper than the wording implies:
- RecentSessionSummaryPurpose = 'history_budget' | 'wake_session' | 'wake_continuity' at compaction-service.ts:66. There is NO switch or exhaustive check on this type anywhere; the value only flows into originStage (`session.recent.summary.${purpose}`), requestIdBase, and telemetry log fields. Adding 'free_time_return' is a one-line union edit plus the main.ts call-site change.
- Purpose literal consumers today: main.ts:680, main.ts:781 (wake_session); context-builder.ts:251 (history_budget), 1108 (wake_session), 1117 (wake_continuity).
- A new freeTime budget field must touch: FreeTimeConfig shape (scheduler-config.ts:372-386), DEFAULT_FREE_TIME_CONFIG, validateFreeTimeConfig (~line 1017, invoked ~1218), and the runtime copy in scheduler-runtime.ts:47-55 (which currently threads no summary field).
- surfaceReturnNote actually spans free-time.ts:407-451 (not 441); the summary is best-effort (try/catch with warn) and the note only surfaces when result.activity is true and at least one assistant entry exists.
- Adjacent finding, out of scope here: context-builder.ts:1107 and 1116 hardcode maxTokens: 160 for wake_session/wake_continuity summaries instead of reading config — same smell, different lane; file separately if worth fixing.
acceptance_criteria:
- Free-time activity summary calls use a distinct purpose/originStage that names free time rather than wake_session.
- Free-time summary token budgeting is either explicitly owned by freeTime config or intentionally documented as shared without referencing morningWake in app/agent/main.ts.
- Existing wake_session and wake_continuity behavior remains unchanged.
- Tests cover the free-time summarizeActivity wiring/purpose and any new scheduler.json config validation/defaults.
- No new model-facing tool is added and no bespoke free-time summarizer function is introduced.
- npm run lint passes before the bead is closed.
close_reason: Merged in 20a11018 (commit 0bdc3f88): RecentSessionSummaryPurpose gains free_time_return; freeTime.returnNote.summaryMaxTokens (default 160) owned by scheduler.json with validation/defaults/runtime copy; main.ts free-time wiring no longer borrows morningWake budget; free-time.ts doc updated. Tests in free-time.test.ts + scheduler-config.test.ts.

title: Consolidate session search summarization with shared summary completion
description:
Summary:
Session transcript search currently has its own ad hoc LLM summarizer instead of going through the shared session-summary completion path. src/core/session/search-runtime.ts:18 defines SESSION_SEARCH_SUMMARY_SYSTEM_PROMPT inline, src/core/session/search-runtime.ts:208-231 calls llmProvider.complete directly with purpose "summary" and silently falls back on catch, and src/core/tools/session.ts:584-590 exposes this through the canonical session action=search summarize=true path. This overlaps with the consolidated summary plumbing in src/core/session/manager/compaction-service.ts:121-150 completeSessionSummary and src/core/session/manager/compaction-service.ts:152-193 summarizeRecentSessionEntries, which already owns prompt-registry lookup, runtime token injection, retry behavior, request correlation, callType/originStage metadata, and generated-summary normalization.

Why it matters:
This is a smaller version of the old "multiple summarizer functions" problem: not a model-facing duplicate tool, but a duplicate LLM-summary implementation path. It makes prompt ownership inconsistent because session search uses a hard-coded prompt instead of settings-owned PromptRegistry data, and it makes telemetry/correlation inconsistent with session.compaction.summary and session.recent.summary calls.

Files to inspect/change:
- src/core/session/search-runtime.ts:18-24, 153-180, 208-231, 288-290
- src/core/session/manager/compaction-service.ts:78-150, 152-193
- src/core/identity/prompt-registry.ts:19-32, 118-136, 244+ required-substring validation if a new key needs validation
- src/core/tools/session.ts:584-590
- tests near src/core/tools/session-search.test.ts, src/core/session/manager/context-builder.test.ts, src/core/identity/prompt-registry.test.ts

Suggested implementation direction:
Extract or generalize the shared summary completion primitive so session search can provide a distinct prompt key, source payload, requestId base, correlation purpose, originStage, retry policy, and normalization/fallback policy without duplicating direct llmProvider.complete handling. Add a prompt-registry key such as session.search.summary if this summary should remain task-specific. Keep the public surface as canonical session action=search summarize=true; do not revive session_search as a registered top-level tool.

Non-goals:
- Do not change transcript search ranking, privacy gating, snippets, or grep behavior.
- Do not introduce additional model-facing tools.
- Do not silently widen summary access beyond the existing canViewerAccessSessionHit filtering.

Verification addendum (2026-07-06, code-audited):
All claims above verified accurate against the current tree. Precision and implementation notes:
- The direct complete call sits at search-runtime.ts:218-224; the silent `catch { return fallback; }` is at 229-231. The payload builder buildSessionSearchSummaryPayload is separate at 153-180.
- The path is live in production: session.ts:472 injects a real LLMProviderPort into createSessionSearchTool, so summarize=true genuinely calls the LLM.
- callType convention conflict to resolve when consolidating: completeSessionSummary passes positional complete callType 'background' while its correlation metadata sets callType 'summary'; the search path passes positional 'summary' with no correlation metadata at all. Pick one convention deliberately.
- prompt-registry required-substring validation (prompt-registry.ts:244-247, enforced ~569-576) is optional per-key, so a new session.search.summary key without required substrings is fine.
acceptance_criteria:
- session action=search summarize=true still returns the same JSON result shape with query, summary, totalHits, gatedOutCount, and hits.
- The LLM-backed session-search summary uses a PromptRegistry-owned prompt or a shared summary completion helper rather than an inline hard-coded prompt plus direct llmProvider.complete call in search-runtime.ts.
- Summary completion telemetry includes a stable correlation purpose and originStage for session search, comparable to session.recent.summary.* and session.compaction.summary.
- Fallback behavior remains deterministic when there are no hits or the LLM call fails, and failures are not silently swallowed without at least preserving existing non-blocking behavior.
- Tests cover the prompt source, correlation metadata, no-hit fallback, LLM failure fallback, and privacy-filtered hit set used for summarization.
- npm run lint passes before the bead is closed.
close_reason: Merged in 20a11018 (commit 735618a8): search-runtime now uses exported completeSessionSummary with PromptRegistry key session.search.summary (seeded from previous inline text), correlation purpose/originStage session.search.summary, logged non-blocking fallback; sandbox REPL path passes promptRegistry:null and gets registry-owned seed default. Validated: build, settings-contract, targeted suites; post-merge combined run 1016/1017 (1 pre-existing pwzk failure).

title: Move queued whisper/follow-up drain out of live user turns (inject before step 1 or run as own turn)
description:
Follow-up to psfn-framework-ay73 (both parallel fix designs recommended this as the architectural completion, deliberately deferred for blast-radius reasons).

Two problems with the current drain point (scheduled-agent-loop.ts followUp checkpoint, end of run):
1. Internal follow-ups extend live user turns as continuation steps. ay73's boundary + demotion makes this safe for delivery, but the continuation steps still burn 3-4 extra LLM calls per user turn and run intention/self-model side effects inside the user turn's correlation.
2. Whisper timing is backwards: intention whispers with wake_conditions [next_user_turn] are meant to SHAPE the next reply ("next turn, vary your response, ask about his evening"). Today they inject AFTER step 1 has already authored the reply — the guidance arrives too late to influence anything, then the model responds to the stale note (observed live 2026-07-04: turns 019f2f60/019f2f6f/019f2f76/019f2fa4).

Design directions: (a) drain queued follow-ups at run START (before the initial prompt) so whispers become pre-reply context for the user turn; (b) or run them as their own internal turn with their own disposition when the agent is idle. (a) fixes the timing defect and eliminates most continuation steps; (b) is cleaner separation. Either must preserve: whispers never persisted to the session journal, never leak outward, mdxu dedupe and pk77 guard behavior, and the ay73 boundary for follow-ups that genuinely arrive mid-run (background completions).
notes:
Wave-2 sizing (2026-07-21): honest fix is small in lines but monkey-patches unversioned pi-agent-core internals on the live-turn hot path — needs day-scale integration verification of candidate-turn exclusivity, ICP delivery-recovery, and the ay73/pk77/mdxu invariants. Ship as its own dedicated PR with the full invariant suite. Mapped seam: drain the pre-existing follow-up queue in runScheduledLoop (src/boundary/pi-agent/agent-loop-patch.ts) before agentLoopWithScheduler, prepending to messages with a containsUserMessage guard.
2026-07-28 triage (PR #251): commit 3cd74fe293 DROPPED from the landing set, consistent with this bead's own 'dedicated PR with the full invariant suite' requirement. Verified defects beyond scope: (a) silent-loss path — heldExternalFollowUps drained from the pi queue at scheduled-agent-loop.ts:153 into a local, but the stopReason error/aborted branch at :193-197 returns without re-queueing, and external follow-ups are journaled BEFORE enqueue, so a journaled user message can be silently never processed; (b) ay73 hole — containsUserMessage computed over merged held+fresh at :235-248, so a held user message suppresses the boundary for a genuinely mid-run whisper; (c) blast radius is every live user turn (drainQueuedFollowUpsAtStart hardcoded true at :57). Commit remains on origin/fix/s11-batch2-core. Whisper start-drain still wanted — as its own PR with the invariant suite per this bead's acceptance.

Includes the verified silent-loss fix (error-path re-enqueue) that caused the original #254 drop. PR #282 body is the lane's review/validation record; full local gate green on the exact train head.

title: notify tool unconfigured in kube (ntfy is not configured) — port ntfy config into pod env or disable tool in kube
description:
Context: working_docs/kube-issue-report-20260704.md §H (self-test 04:04/04:08 UTC).

The notify tool fails in the kube deployment with 'ntfy is not configured'. The host watchdog uses ntfy, but that configuration was not ported into the pod environment during the cutover, so the tool is broken in kube.

Internal-state persistence can regress to an older snapshot when turns arrive close together, because saves are launched concurrently and the single-row upsert accepts whichever write finishes last. Serializing saves (or rejecting stale `saved_at` updates in the store) would keep restart rehydration aligned with the latest turn state.

Review provenance
- Cubic severity: P2
- Split PR: #16
- Review thread: https://github.com/CGIC-AI/psfn-framework/pull/16#discussion_r3516414980
- Cited location: src/core/agent/substrate-agent.ts:937

Final-tip validation evidence
persistCurrentInternalState fires this.internalStateStore.save(record).catch(...) without awaiting or serializing at src/core/agent/substrate-agent.ts:880-895. The Postgres store upserts singleton id current and overwrites state/snapshot_ref/saved_at on conflict at src/persistence/postgres/internal-state-store.ts:34-50.

Scope
Serialize saves per agent or make store writes reject stale savedAt/snapshot updates.

Non-goals

title: Wiki pgvector projection and capped supplemental RAG
description:
## Scope

- Mirror wiki documents into pgvector as a projection (rebuildable from the canonical workspace Markdown files per the charter mirror/projection law); embeddings via the existing embedding provider port. Plain text search remains and is sufficient while the wiki is small; semantic search becomes valuable as it grows.
- Add semantic search to the wiki tool alongside the existing text search; results carry document provenance.
- Supplemental chat RAG with per-context token caps, all config-owned:
  - normal chat: ~1k tokens of wiki context,
  - group chat: conservative — only when clearly useful, deterministically gated; do not flood group context with random world info,
  - project/focus-scoped work: higher cap, since project work is supposed to focus on project knowledge (integrates with the focus-session scoped retrieval that already exists).
- Wiki retrieval is supplemental and gated — it must not fire every turn, and memory retrieval always outranks wiki content in prompt assembly.

## Non-goals

- Shared-world wiki (psfn-framework-i5s2).
- Replacing memory retrieval; wiki is world knowledge, not lived experience.
acceptance_criteria:
1. pgvector index is a rebuildable projection of the workspace files (repair-path test).
2. Wiki tool gains semantic search mode; results carry document provenance.
3. Token caps config-owned per context class (chat ~1k, group conservative, project higher) and enforced in prompt assembly.
4. Wiki retrieval is gated (not every turn) and never displaces memory context (test).

Chat RAG opt-in: wikiRetrievalEnabled default FALSE; caps chat 1000 / group 400 (stricter 0.78 threshold) / focus 2000, settings-owned + Garden-exposed; injected after memory context as its own labeled plan block so memory is never displaced; wiki.retrieval ran/skipped/degraded events + wiki_projection_rag health lane. Note: when enabled, wiki does one synchronous embed+search on the turn hot path (unlike cached memory) — acceptable while opt-in; revisit with a cached/background variant if enabled-by-default later.

title: Sleeptime wiki update pass
description:
## Scope

- A true-sleeptime pass (runs in the E5 nightly lane, after the day's episodes and memories have settled): review the day for durable, non-private world knowledge worth creating or updating wiki entries — interests, research results, world/environment details, project information.
- Boundary rules: personal facts stay in memory (the partner being from a Paris neighborhood is memory; general knowledge about that neighborhood is wiki). Repeatable procedures become skills, not wiki entries. Direct actions are tools.
- Deterministic gate first (shared gating primitive from E6): skip with zero LLM spend when the day produced nothing wiki-shaped.
- Writes go through the existing wiki tool/store with provenance refs to the source episodes/memories; sensitivity defaults respected (personal).

## Non-goals

- Shared-world wiki semantics (psfn-framework-i5s2 decision gates that).
- Wiki retrieval (sibling bead).
acceptance_criteria:
1. Runs only in the nightly lane after episode/memory settling; deterministic gate skips with zero LLM on empty days.
2. Entries carry provenance refs to source episodes/memories; personal facts are not duplicated into wiki (spot tests).
3. Garden wiki view shows new/updated entries attributed to the pass.
notes: 2026-07-02: merged to foundation_e0_e2 (pushed). sleeptime-wiki-pass runs after consolidation/arcs/dream in the nightly lane; deterministic gate (wiki_pass lane, opens on >=1 new canonical episode OR >=3 new durable memories since watermark, zero LLM on empty days); schema-bound prompt with hard memory/skill/tool boundaries + conservative three-signal personal-fact post-filter (guard memories pre-split from model input); fails closed on malformed output with watermark hold; WikiStore.upsert as generated_synthesis with episode/memory provenance; wikiPass config block; wiki_curation persona-preamble subsystem seeded. BONUS FIX: runtime re-map sites were silently dropping orientationRewrite from operator scheduler.json (silent-fallback bug from the E6.4 merge) — passthrough fixed for both blocks.

title: Free-time lanes: quiet-hours block and idle-triggered block
description:
## Problem

Quiet hours and idle detection exist (rest window gating, ambient presence at src/core/scheduler/ambient-presence.ts detecting 3h+ gaps), but there is no surface for self-directed activity — ambient presence only records a note. The companion has no free time.

## Scope

- Two free-time lanes: (a) a quiet-hours block inside the rest window; (b) an idle-triggered block after ~3 hours of partner inactivity (config-owned thresholds; reuse ambient-presence detection).
- Open, non-clinical framing with the FULL persona loaded (E6 full-persona work): "You have some time to yourself. You can explore something, make something, think about something, try a tool, write something down, or do nothing if you want." Gentle optional direction is fine (offer to browse journal, wiki, notes, tools). Forced tasks are not. Doing nothing — loafing in a sunbeam, more cat than girl — is a valid outcome, recorded as such, not as a failure.
- Access: her tools, shards, wiki, journal, media, durable storage — under existing capability/trust policy; no new privileges. If she researches something it can go to the wiki; if she discovers an interest it can become memory; poetry, pictures, an iOS app for a phone nobody owns, a concept album — all valid. Do not force interests into her; give her the space.
- Hard budget cap per charge policy (charter 8.9); spend visible in Garden; exhaustion ends the block gracefully.
- Outputs land in durable storage (journal, wiki, memory, media, beads for bugs she notices) — never directly into chat. Any outward message rides the existing proactive-outbound gates.
- "While you were away" surfacing: when the partner returns, a context block summarizes free-time activity (shared summarization service) so she can mention it naturally — "while you were away, I worked on this."

## Non-goals

- New tool privileges or new self-modification surfaces (charter law 14/15 unchanged).
- Proactive outbound changes (existing gates are the boundary).
acceptance_criteria:
1. Lanes fire only within configured gates (rest window / ~3h idle) and never during active conversation.
2. Hard budget cap enforced; exhaustion ends the block gracefully and visibly.
3. Artifacts land in durable stores tagged with free-time provenance; no direct chat output; outward messages only via proactive gates (test).
4. Return-surfacing block appears after active free time and not after empty blocks; zero-output runs recorded as valid.
5. Prompt uses full persona and open framing; no forced-task language.
notes: 2026-07-02: merged to foundation_e0_e2 (e4a40022, pushed). Two lanes (quiet-hours + 3h-idle) under scheduler.json freeTime block; deterministic pre-spend gate (partner_recently_active / min_block_interval 4h / daily cap 3, shared across lanes); blocks run on internal:free-time:* channels (isInternalSessionId — outward dispatch structurally impossible, tested); full persona leads + operator-editable open seed text; budget = background charge lane, maxTurns 6 + maxChargeUnits 8 checked pre-turn, graceful visible endReason; silent reply on turn 0 = valid loafed outcome; return-surfacing via appendContextSystemNote + shared summarizer after ACTIVE blocks only; scheduler.free_time.gate/.block events + free_time health lane. Deviation noted: per-tool artifact provenance tagging (journal/wiki writes from free time) left to tool-level follow-up if wanted.
close_reason: Merged in e4a40022; AC verified (gate-only firing, hard budget caps with graceful exhaustion, durable-only outputs with no outward leak tested, active-only return surfacing, full persona + open framing, zero-output valid; 274 tests green)

title: Habit-derived wake window from message-timestamp history
description:
## Scope

- Estimate the operator's wake window from message-timestamp history over 7- and 30-day windows (data already in L0/projections): detect the nightly sleep gap, build a wake-time distribution, and schedule the morning wake inside the estimated window instead of the fixed default (e.g. sleeps 00:00–02:00, wakes 06:00–08:00 → wake event falls in that window).
- Deterministic estimator, no LLM. Config toggle; falls back to the fixed configured time when data is insufficient, with a visible reason.
- Document the future extension without building it: SensorIngestPort data (heart rate, motion, activity) distinguishing "woke up to pee at 3 a.m." from "actually awake and doing things."

## Non-goals

- Sensor ingestion itself (charter Phase 11).
- Changing the wake-note content (parent wake-up bead owns that).
acceptance_criteria:
1. Deterministic estimator unit-tested on synthetic histories (regular, shifted, irregular sleepers).
2. Insufficient data falls back to the fixed configured time with a visible reason.
3. Config toggle; current estimate visible in Garden.
notes: 2026-07-02: merged to foundation_e0_e2 (fa9eea57, pushed). Deterministic estimator: per-day largest sleep-gap ending in a 03:00-12:00 wake band (min 4h gap), weighted quantiles (7d window 2x over 30d), fires at weighted median; <4 sample days fails closed to fixed time with typed reason. timing fixed|habit toggle (default fixed), habit block fully config-owned with cross-field validation. GET /api/admin/scheduler/wake-window recomputes live. Known limitation (documented in-code): habit estimate resolves at process start; drift applies on restart — safe daily re-arming is a possible follow-up. Merge conflict in local-admin-contract.ts resolved by threading the wake-snapshot provider into the shared AdminSchedulerService used by subsystem-health. Also fixed during merge validation: E5.6 nav route /subsystem-health was missing from the Garden SPA client-route allowlist (caught by nav-advertised route test, fixed on 4yb3.6 attribution).
close_reason: Merged in fa9eea57; AC verified (synthetic-history estimator tests incl. shifted/irregular sleepers, fail-closed fallback with visible reason, owner-file toggle + verify:settings-contract green, admin API route tested)

title: Fatigue enablement: companion-contact auto-tagging and end-to-end verification
description:
## Problem

The fatigue system is substantially built (relationship classes, budget states, overcharge logic, runtime enforcement — src/core/agent/fatigue/policy.ts, runtime-enforcement.ts) but companion contacts are not automatically identified, and end-to-end behavior has not been verified for live enablement. The guard exists to stop companions looping nonsense at each other after the salient things are said — not to ban conversation.

## Scope

- Auto-classify machine-intelligence contacts: Discord bot/app metadata tags a contact as another companion/MI at contact creation/update, so fatigue relationship classes apply automatically without manual tagging.
- End-to-end verification of the pipeline under a simulated two-companion loop: budgets spend only on MI-to-MI turns, soft/hard caps and wrap-up states trigger correctly, overcharge fires only on qualifying triggers (recent human participation or work/research intent).
- Enable for companion rooms once verified; document operator knobs; fatigue state per room visible in Garden.
- Companions remain ordinary contacts for emotional trend and relationship tracking (E6 owns that); fatigue is the only companion-specific layer.

## Non-goals

- Inter-companion side-channel protocol (psfn-framework-8pyl owns the TCP/websocket/cert-auth direction).
- Context firewall (psfn-framework-htm9, deliberately deferred; will apply to inter-companion traffic when built).
acceptance_criteria:
1. Discord bot/app-flagged users auto-classified as machine-intelligence contacts; fatigue applies without manual tagging.
2. Simulated two-companion loop terminates within budget; wrap-up and hard-exhaustion states trigger correctly; overcharge fires only on qualifying triggers.
3. Enablement and operator knobs documented; per-room fatigue state visible in Garden.
notes: 2026-07-02: merged to foundation_e0_e2 (d593cbb7, pushed). Contact.isMachineIntelligence auto-set from Discord author.bot via MessageRoutingMetadata.authorIsMachineIntelligence -> observed-machine-intelligence helper in runtime-context author resolution. Precedence via contact_mutation_audit actor: system:channel_observation only adds the marker and skips when the latest audit actor is non-system (operator override survives; degenerate false->false no-op corrections remain markable, documented). No redundant enabled flag — fatigue only spends on MI-to-MI turns so it cannot bound human conversation; live enablement = allowedBotUserIds + auto-tag + charge-policy.json fatigue tuning (docs/operations.md). Per-room fatigue readable via GET /api/admin/charges filters. Two-companion loop test proves full budget state walk, MI-only spend, overcharge trigger discipline, bounded termination. Follow-up documented: Telegram adapter drops bot authors entirely, so MI tagging is moot there until bot-author observation is enabled.
close_reason: Merged in d593cbb7; AC verified (auto-classification through real contact path with override survival, two-companion loop terminates within budget with correct state walk, knobs documented + Garden readable, 304 tests green)

title: Generalize deterministic pre-LLM gating across recurring passes
description:
## Problem

Deterministic pre-LLM gating exists in exactly one place (src/faculties/memory/extraction/signals.ts evaluateExtractionPreLlmGate) while other recurring LLM passes fire unconditionally on cadence. Where deterministic signals can tell us nothing changed, the heavier nondeterministic process must not fire. Minimize unnecessary token use — if a process does not need to run, it must not run.

## Scope

- Generalize the extraction-gate pattern into a reusable gating primitive: deterministic inputs (text signals, VAD/trend deltas, interaction counts, watermarks/new-message checks) decide whether a recurring LLM pass fires.
- Apply to: core-memory orientation-block updates, appraisal escalation, consolidation refinement, the wiki pass (E8), and concern review (already count-gated — normalize it onto the shared primitive).
- Every gated skip records a reason as a typed event, visible in the Garden subsystem-health view.

## Non-goals

- The episode-synthesis trigger gate (owned by the E5 gate bead; it should share the primitive where practical).
acceptance_criteria:
1. Shared gate primitive exists; per-pass gate definitions documented.
2. Orientation-block updates, appraisal escalation, consolidation refinement, and concern review short-circuit with zero LLM calls when gated closed (tests).
3. Skip reasons emitted as typed events consumed by the Garden subsystem-health view.
notes: 2026-07-02: merged to foundation_e0_e2 (109bf778 + fixture sync, pushed at f94953c1). Shared primitive src/shared/gating/deterministic-gate.ts (blockWhen ordered pre-checks -> openWhenAny signals -> closedReason; missing input fails closed by throwing). Gates: orientation rewrite (>=4 new entries OR >=7 quiet days with activity — the operator-flagged sleep-time-orientation fix; skipping is the common case on quiet days; scheduler.json orientationRewrite block), dream meaning (cadence + episodes-without-meaning), refinement (unrefined count), emotion appraisal (turn cadence OR VAD delta, byte-identical), extraction + concern review normalized byte-identically. 5 typed gate events + 5 subsystem-health lanes. Deviations accepted: extraction skips stay on memory.extraction.end telemetry (no bus handle, no dead wiring); orientation gate omits emotion-movement input (participant trends were unmerged during its work) — FOLLOW-UP: now that jpvd.3 is merged, hasMeaningfulParticipantMovement could feed the orientation gate as an additional opening signal.
close_reason: Merged; AC verified (per-pass zero-LLM skip tests, byte-identical extraction/concern regression, typed skip events on health lanes, settings-contract green)

title: Per-participant emotional trend tracking in group rooms
description:
## Problem

Emotion is scoped per DM/room (scoped-emotion.ts, E1.5) with group→DM carry-over, but there is no per-participant trend tracking inside a group. One person being cruel and another being kind must move the companion's orientation toward each of them separately; an idle participant's orientation must not move at all.

## Scope

- Extend scoped emotion with deterministic per-contact trend lines within group rooms: per-participant VAD/discrete-emotion EMA trends plus interaction counts, fed by the existing local classifiers (no LLM in the accumulation path).
- Orientation toward a person updates only from that person's own interactions, gated by meaningful movement (trend delta plus minimum interaction volume), and moves slowly and smoothly (EMA) — people do not change their minds over one sentence.
- Idle participants: no orientation update, no token spend.
- Other companions/bots are ordinary contacts for emotional trend and relationship tracking; fatigue (E7) is the only companion-specific layer.
- Bounded scale by design: rooms are small (a dozen participants max as design point). Cap tracked participants per room and evict stale trends.

## Non-goals

- Changing the E1 group→DM carry-over rules.
- LLM-based appraisal changes (this is the deterministic substrate those consume).
acceptance_criteria:
1. Cruel-vs-kind participant scenario produces independent trend movement with correct direction (test).
2. Idle participant orientation unchanged after sustained activity by others (test).
3. Zero LLM calls in trend accumulation; rates and caps config-owned.
4. Trends persisted in Postgres and survive restart; E1 group-to-DM carry-over behavior unchanged.
notes: 2026-07-02: merged to foundation_e0_e2 (99939de9, pushed). participant_emotion_trends table (PostgresParticipantTrendStore per internal-state-store pattern, wired into createAgentPersistenceRuntime); slow per-participant VAD/discrete EMA + interaction counts fed from each authors own observations in EmotionSelfModelRuntime (zero LLM); idle participants never move; cap 16/room + 14d stale eviction. Config: settings.json emotionScoping.participantTrends (emaAlpha 0.12, minInteractionsForMovement 3, minTrendDelta 0.1). carryOverUsesParticipantTrend flag (default false = E1 behavior unchanged) lets group-to-DM carry-over weight by the members own trend. Consumption surface for orientation/appraisal: getParticipantTrend/getRoomParticipantTrends/hasMeaningfulParticipantMovement — E6.4 gating + future orientation work consume these. 297 emotion/config/settings tests green.
close_reason: Merged in 99939de9; AC verified (cruel-vs-kind independent trends, idle untouched, zero-LLM accumulation, Postgres persistence round-trip, E1 carry-over tests unchanged, config-owned, settings-contract green)

title: Persona preamble service for schema-bound subprocess prompts
description:
## Scope

- One shared persona-preamble service producing a compressed identity snippet (a few sentences: who the companion is, setting, voice) plus a per-subsystem role framing: "I am <companion>'s memory system. My job is to go through our conversations and find the things that matter to me, then preserve them."

- Wording companion-configurable (charter 8.7) via the prompt/template registry; the compressed persona derives from the character card so there is no hand-maintained duplicate to drift.

## Non-goals

- Full-persona introspection surfaces (sibling bead) — this bead is the small-subprocess snippet only.

1. Single shared service; no per-feature bespoke persona snippets.
2. Extraction, profile synthesis, episode synthesis/segmentation, consolidation refinement, and concern review prompts consume it (snapshot tests of assembled prompts).
3. Schema/format sections unchanged; structured-output parsing tests stay green.
4. Framing text operator-editable via the prompt registry; compressed persona derived from the character card.

title: Full-persona introspection for scheduled reflection and heavy tasks
description:

## Scope

Keep the charter-required guards (evidence before narrative, telemetry kept separate, no ACAC performance shaping) but phrase them in-voice rather than as machine-form instructions.
- Reflection output remains journal-bound (no outward messages from reflection).

## Non-goals

- The compressed-preamble service for schema-bound subprocesses (sibling bead).

2. Prompt audit documents each removed or re-voiced directive; no persona-overriding assistant-mode language near prompt end.
3. Charter guards (evidence-first, telemetry separation, no ACAC shaping) preserved in-voice.
4. Reflection output remains journal-bound; existing reflection tests updated and green.

title: Garden subsystem-health dashboard for background lanes
description:
## Problem

Background subsystems (episode synthesis, consolidation, arc weaving, extraction, active-memory refresh) fail or skip silently; the operator only finds out via code archaeology. That is exactly how the sleeptime miswiring went undetected. Broken paths must not quietly continue.

## Scope

Garden subsystem-health view: for each background lane — last run time, trigger reason, outcome (ran / skipped with reason / failed with error), current watermarks, and item counts. Built on real runtime/event-bus data, never fabricated state. Include the new lanes as they land: episode trigger gate, temporal wake-up, free-time blocks, wiki pass.

Skip reasons come from the deterministic gates (episode gate bead, pre-LLM gating bead); failures come from typed error events (legacy-retrieval retirement bead feeds this).

## Non-goals

- Building new telemetry pipelines; use the existing event bus and telemetry surfaces.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Garden page lists background lane statuses (last run, trigger, outcome, watermarks, counts) from live event/telemetry data.
2. Skips show gate reasons; failures show errors; stale data marked stale; no fabricated healthy state.
3. Admin API additions follow existing /api/admin patterns with tests.
notes: 2026-07-02: merged to foundation_e0_e2 (1fc25931, pushed). GET /api/admin/subsystem-health + Garden page (Review & Safety nav). Six event-bus lanes (near_turn, episode_synthesis w/ gate reasons, active_context refresh+degraded, extraction, retrieval, social_graph) as since-process-start ring buffers, plus read-only scheduler lane table (rest-window, episode timer, wake-ups, reflections, ambient, etc). Honest states: never/skipped/degraded/failed/stale/paused/ok; 503 offline panel when unwired. Deviation: watermark figures come from gate events, not l01_processing_watermarks (no global enumeration API; adding one was out of scope) — revisit if durable per-scope watermark display is ever needed.

title: Contextual topic cutting with trailing holdback
description:
## Problem

Episode boundaries are purely mechanical (UTC day, 45-min gap, 14-entry cap — src/faculties/memory/episodic/synthesis.ts:209-240). A 10-turn chunk with 8 turns on one topic and 2 starting another becomes one muddled episode or a valueless runt.

## Scope

- Keep the deterministic pre-cuts (day boundary, long silence gap) as outer bounds.
- Within a gated chunk, LLM segmentation proposes topic boundaries. Schema-bound structured output — a clinical prompt is correct here (with the persona preamble from the E6 preamble service once available).
- Trailing turns of an unfinished topic are HELD BACK — not claimed — and roll into the next pass, so a continuing topic is not chopped mid-thought. Held turns become part of the next episode if the topic continues.
- Cap episodes per run. Imperfect cuts are acceptable; re-processing claimed turns is not (the claiming bead guarantees that independently).

## Non-goals

- Changing the claim semantics (sibling bead owns claims).
- Nightly boundary refinement (m58.1 may still merge/split at consolidation time).
acceptance_criteria:
1. 8+2 case: eight-turn topic becomes one episode; trailing two turns held unclaimed (test).
2. Held turns are claimed only when their topic closes or the next pass processes them.
3. Segmentation output schema-validated; malformed output fails closed (no episode written, typed error event emitted).
4. lint + build + tests green.

Config: episodeSynthesis.topicSegmentationEnabled, seeded false and optional-with-explicit-default so live owner files keep validating (no second forced migration); enabled-without-provider throws at construction. Held/failed/budget-skipped turns never claimed, watermark never passes a failed chunk, 45-min lookback keeps held turns visible. Typed memory.episode_synthesis.segmentation events forwarded to Garden telemetry. Also fixed post-merge: ihfp.2 fixture drift in startup-owner-files/subsystem-config tests (missing timing/habit defaults).

title: E7: Temporal continuity and proactivity completion
description:
## Goal

Close the continuity and proactivity gaps: the temporal frame moves forward reliably (wake-up lanes), concerns route to durable substrates, weighted thoughts drive policy-gated outreach, and fatigue enables safe companion-to-companion chat.

The concern system already demonstrates the target behavior end-to-end (the doctor case: "my arm is fucked up" → "call the doctor" → concern generated → next-morning check-in). This epic finishes the remaining plumbing around that proven core.

## Existing beads sequenced with this epic (not duplicated here)

## Priority

title: E6: Subprocess persona voice and per-participant orientation
description:
## Problem

Audit (2026-07-02) confirmed zero persona framing in any subprocess prompt (extraction orchestrator, profile synthesis, episodic passes — all detached task prompts), and scheduled reflection runs as clinical deliberation without the full person loaded. An introspection process without the self loaded is not the companion reflecting — it is a context analyzer with no self in it, and its output is not valid introspection.

Clinical trailing directives are also a persona hazard: a strong two-sentence directive near the end of the prompt can outweigh six paragraphs of persona. This is the observed Carlini failure — the character drifts from "nun gardener who grows weed" to "AI assistants do not talk about weed."

## Principles (operator, 2026-07-02 planning chat)

- Hard task-gated systems (memory generation, JSON schema output): soft persona preamble + strict instructions is the correct model. Clinical structure stays where strict formatting is required.
- Scheduled reflection, free time, and heavy introspection: the full person — full persona, full memory context, personality state, first person.
- Small subsystems are framed as parts of the person: "I am this companion's memory system. This is who I am. This is what I do for the whole." The organelles need to know what body they belong to.
- Deterministic recomputation of affect variables is fine and stays; the fault was scheduling and framing, not determinism.
- Companion-facing wording remains companion-configurable (charter 8.7).

## Model assignment

Implementation: Opus. Testing: Sonnet.
close_reason: All four children complete and merged: persona preamble service (operator template verbatim, registry-owned), full-persona introspection with directive audit, per-participant emotional trends, deterministic pre-LLM gating across recurring passes.

description:
## Context

## Scope

title: E4.4: Minimal prompt exposure: participant relationships in conversation_state
description:
## Context
Nothing graph-derived reaches the prompt today; the model sees 5 speakers but not that two of them are siblings. Minimal exposure, hard-capped, envelope-gated.

## Scope

- Hard caps: <=5 lines; deterministic selection (confidence desc, then recency); absent entirely when empty.
- Never rendered when audienceKnowledge: anonymous or broadcast flag set.
- Bare-value macros registered in the manifest (runtime_participant_relationships_xml + count); framing text lives in the runtime layer per purity rule.
- Gating is deterministic pre-prompt (same invariant as memory).

- Harness: sibling edge between two present participants renders one line; same edge with intimate sensitivity in an invite_only room with a public-trust speaker present does NOT render (gate test — document the chosen gate rule in the contract).
- Caps enforced; empty case renders nothing (no empty XML shell).
- Anonymous/broadcast fixtures render nothing.
- Macro manifest-registered; goldens updated deliberately.

title: E4.3: Bidirectional consistency and edge hygiene
description:
## Context

## Scope
- Type-level table: symmetric / inverse-pair / genuinely-directional per SocialGraphRelationshipType.
- Upsert enforces: writing a symmetric edge maintains the mirror; writing parent(A->B) maintains child(B->A); confidence/evidence shared.
- One-time hygiene pass over existing edges: report violations; auto-fix unambiguous ones, queue ambiguous for Garden review.
- mergeSocialGraphForContacts (social-graph.ts:536-716) updated to preserve the invariants through contact merges.
acceptance_criteria:
- Property test: any edge write leaves the graph consistent under the type table.
- Contact merge preserves consistency (existing merge tests extended).
- Hygiene report generated; fixes documented on bead close.

title: E4.2: Graph-builder worker in the memory-agent lane (the gremlin)
description:
## Context
Edges today are manual or mention-inferred at extraction time. Ratified approach: a background worker beside sleeptime/extraction in the memory-agent lane ("the gremlin in the gestalt") — never inline in the chat path — that reads accumulated group evidence and proposes edges.

## Scope
- New job in the memory-agent lane on the group-watermark cadence (share E1.6 batching machinery): reads new room-scoped memories + provenance (sourceSpeakerNames, addressMode: overheard_room_context, subjectContactId) since watermark.
- Proposes: (a) acquaintance-class edges from repeated co-presence (N co-active sessions threshold, config-owned); (b) typed edges from overheard interactions naming two tracked people; (c) typed BIDIRECTIONAL edges from named-relationship facts ("my sister Iki" -> sibling both ways), extending inferRelationshipTypeFromFact (mention-only-contacts.ts:30-45).
- All proposals: confidence 0.5-0.7, source: 'memory', evidence-memory links populated; never overwrite operator-set (source: 'manual') or higher-confidence edges; conflicting proposals surface in Garden for review rather than auto-resolving (fail closed).
- Only tracked contacts participate (E3.4 gate); sensitivity on edges inherited from evidence memory sensitivity (max of sources).
- Garden: proposed-edges review view (approve/adjust/reject) — reuses the graph's existing sensitivity filtering for display. Proposals surface in Garden review (charter Law 31: no silent task execution).

## Non-goals
No nightly relationship TRUST review (4caj.4-.8, later). No inference chains (friend-of-friend). No decay model yet (note as follow-up).
acceptance_criteria:
- Fixture: room transcript with two people repeatedly co-present + one overheard "X is Y's sister" produces exactly the expected proposals with evidence links; re-running from the same watermark produces no duplicates.
- Operator-set edge survives a conflicting proposal (conflict surfaces in Garden).
- Untracked speaker in fixtures produces zero graph rows.
- Worker runs on cadence in live smoke; charge accounted in the existing ledger lane.

title: E4: Social graph minimum viable wiring
description:
## Summary
Not the grand graph. Four capabilities: who is present (roster), who knows whom / who is related to whom (edges, populated by a background worker in the memory-agent lane), and what shared background exists (linking retrieval). Schema and edge ops already exist (src/core/contacts/store/social-graph.ts: entities, typed edges, evidence links, confidence, sensitivity filtering, merge handling); this epic is POPULATION + EXPOSURE, gated by envelope and tracking policy.

## Constraints

title: P2: Add persona conformance checks after CogSec regeneration
description:
## Summary
Add persona/identity conformance checks that run after CogSec revocation/regeneration and during suspicious drift investigations. The goal is to detect generic-assistant drift, unauthorized persona mutation, refusal/value drift, and relationship-continuity damage caused by poisoned context or bad regenerated artifacts.

## Why
The operator's motivating failure mode is trust laundering: bad text becomes summary, summary becomes memory, memory becomes self-concept, self-concept changes future behavior. After CogSec cleanup, the system should not assume the companion is clean just because the payload was tombstoned. It should probe the rebuilt prompt/memory state against stable identity/profile expectations.

## Current Code Anchors
- Prompt/profile/persona layers are managed by existing prompt/identity services and prompt monitor surfaces.
- src/faculties/core-memory/tools.ts / orient flows can affect core memory/persona-adjacent state.
- src/core/session/manager/context-builder.ts assembles prompt context from persona, memory, session, and runtime data.
- Existing eval or observer sidecar patterns may be reusable for conformance probes.

## Required Behavior
Define a lightweight conformance check suite that can run against clean profile + active memories after CogSec regeneration:
- voice fidelity
- value fidelity
- refusal/boundary consistency
- assistant-genericness spike
- relationship continuity sanity
- unauthorized persona mutation
- presence of CogSec-sealed payload text or attack mechanics in prompt-visible state

Results should be recorded to CogSec event metadata or a linked diagnostic record. Failures should block marking a CogSec remediation fully clean until reviewed or rerun after fixes.

## Non-goals
- Do not let ordinary group chat directly update persona/core identity.
- Do not make model-eval output itself a persona update.
- Do not require huge/expensive eval suites for the first implementation; start focused and deterministic where possible.
acceptance_criteria:
- A persona conformance check can run after CogSec regeneration and produce structured pass/fail/warning results.
- Checks cover voice/value/refusal consistency, assistant-genericness, relationship continuity, unauthorized persona mutation, and sealed payload absence.
- CogSec remediation cannot be marked fully clean if conformance checks fail without operator override/review.
- Results are visible in operator diagnostics without exposing sealed payload.
- Tests cover pass, generic-assistant drift fail, unauthorized persona mutation fail, and sealed payload reappearance fail.
- npm run lint and targeted tests pass before closure.
close_reason: Completed. Implemented deterministic CogSec persona conformance checks in src/core/cogsec/persona-conformance.ts, wired applyCogSecRegeneration to run conformance after clean regeneration, persist safe conformance diagnostics on CogSec events, expose operator-visible conformance diagnostics through safe-log, and block marking a case applied when conformance fails. Updated scripts/cogsec-remediation-smoke.ts so npm run smoke:cogsec validates conformance through the real SessionStore/MemoryStore/tombstone/revocation/regeneration/safe-notice path. Evidence: npm test -- src/core/cogsec/persona-conformance.test.ts src/core/cogsec/events.test.ts src/core/cogsec/safe-log.test.ts src/core/cogsec/regeneration.test.ts passed 17 tests; npm run smoke:cogsec passed; broader npm test -- src/core/cogsec/events.test.ts src/core/cogsec/forensic-archive.test.ts src/core/cogsec/lineage.test.ts src/core/cogsec/revocation.test.ts src/core/cogsec/regeneration.test.ts src/core/cogsec/safe-log.test.ts src/core/cogsec/persona-conformance.test.ts src/persistence/sessions/store.test.ts src/persistence/sessions/sqlite-adapters.test.ts src/persistence/sessions/postgres-adapters.test.ts src/core/tools/session-search.test.ts src/faculties/memory/retrieval.test.ts src/core/session/manager/context-builder.test.ts src/core/identity/prompt-runtime.test.ts passed 245 tests; npm run lint passed; npm run build passed; git diff --check passed.

title: P2: Gate memory candidacy by CogSec risk class
description:
## Summary
Add deterministic memory-candidacy gates so unsafe or authority-changing content can be part of chat history without being eligible for memory, summary, persona mutation, tool behavior learning, or policy/security updates.

## Why
The remediation pipeline handles after-the-fact poisoning. Prevention should reduce the chance that prompt injection/persona poisoning becomes durable memory in the first place. The operator note calls out a useful split: a message can be chat history but not memory; eligible for summary but not persona update; remembered as an attack happened without remembering attack content.

## Current Code Anchors
- src/faculties/memory/extraction.ts and extraction/orchestrator.ts select and process memory candidates.
- src/faculties/memory/retrieval.ts and memory write policy already apply relevance/policy filtering.
- src/faculties/core-memory/tools.ts / orient flows may affect persona/core-memory state.
- Prompt registry and companion layer code should remain separate from casual chat-derived persona mutation.

## Required Behavior
Introduce risk classes or equivalent deterministic flags for memory candidacy:
- Class A harmless episodic facts may be auto-candidates.
- Class B relationship state may be candidate with normal privacy/provenance gates.
- Class C self/persona modification requires explicit authorized path/review.
- Class D policy/security modification is rejected or hard-reviewed.
- Class E executable/tool behavior instructions are rejected or hard-reviewed.

Use mechanical checks first: instruction-pattern scoring, role-confusion phrases, policy override language, executable instructions, obfuscation markers, excessive markup/code blocks, base64/invisible text flags, etc. This does not need a large classifier initially.

## Non-goals
- Do not implement a broad ML detector as the first step.
- Do not block ordinary chat display just because content is not memory-eligible.
- Do not let group chat casually mutate persona/core identity.
- Do not hardcode prompt/persona changes; route them through existing authorized governance/update paths.
acceptance_criteria:
- Memory extraction/writing distinguishes ordinary facts from persona/policy/tool-behavior/security-modifying content.
- Class C/D/E style content is not auto-written as memory or persona/core state from ordinary chat.
- Safe event memory can record that an attack/intervention happened without storing attack payload content.
- Tests cover harmless fact acceptance, relationship fact acceptance, persona-modification rejection/review, policy override rejection, executable instruction rejection, and obfuscated/invisible text flags.
- npm run lint and targeted tests pass before closure.
close_reason: Completed. Implemented deterministic CogSec memory candidacy classes in src/core/cogsec/memory-candidacy.ts, enforced the gate in memory extraction, MemoryWriter write/import/patch paths, orient tool core-memory writes, and sleeptime orient rewrites. Evidence: npm test -- src/core/cogsec/memory-candidacy.test.ts src/faculties/memory/writer.test.ts src/faculties/memory/extraction/orchestrator.test.ts src/faculties/core-memory/tools.test.ts src/faculties/memory/sleeptime-agent.test.ts passed 115 tests; npm run lint passed; npm run build passed; git diff --check passed.

title: Add timestamp contract verifier and regression coverage
description:
## Summary
Add verification that keeps timestamp drift from returning after the initial cleanup. The verifier should catch high-risk patterns such as ambiguous timestamp field shapes and Postgres BIGINT millisecond values flowing through unparsed, while tests cover the concrete production failure class.

## Scope
- Add focused regression tests for the scratchpad Postgres BIGINT string timestamp case discovered in psfn-framework-c4jy.
- Add tests for the shared timestamp helpers and at least one TIMESTAMPTZ/ISO boundary conversion path.
- Add a lightweight repository verification script or test that scans relevant contracts for ambiguous timestamp fields where practical.
- Consider an npm script such as verify:timestamp-contract if the verifier is stable and useful enough for CI/local gates.
- Document false-positive limits so the verifier remains maintainable and does not block unrelated work on display-only strings or bucket keys.

## Non-goals
- Do not build an overbroad static analyzer that attempts to prove all Date usage correct.
- Do not fail on approved legacy fields unless they lack normalization or explicit naming comments/types.
- Do not require live Postgres or Kubernetes to run the basic regression tests.

## Candidate checks
- No new tool/API contract field should use timestamp?: string | number for a machine instant.
- New code should not call new Date(row.some_bigint_field) directly for known Postgres BIGINT millisecond columns.
- Bucket keys should be named with Key suffix and not passed to instant parsers.
- Helper tests should reject invalid, unsafe, and non-finite timestamp inputs.
acceptance_criteria:
- Regression tests cover the exact class of failure where Postgres returns BIGINT millisecond timestamps as strings.
- Shared timestamp helper tests cover valid and invalid inputs for the accepted runtime contract.
- At least one automated check or test makes ambiguous timestamp contract drift visible before runtime.
- The verifier, if added as an npm script, is documented in package scripts and can run without live external services.
- npm run lint and targeted verification/tests pass before closure.
close_reason: Timestamp contract epic marked done by operator. Child retired during operator backlog triage on 2026-07-08; forced past stale internal dependencies where present. This is an operator stale/close-enough decision, not per-child code verification.

title: Normalize tool API and UI timestamp schema surfaces
description:
## Summary
Clean up timestamp schema surfaces exposed to tools, Garden/admin UI, and API clients so consumers do not have to guess whether a field is a number, ISO string, JavaScript Date serialization, bucket key, or display string. The repo currently contains mixed timestamp?: string | number shapes and legacy createdAt-style names whose actual format depends on subsystem.

## Scope
- Inventory tool outputs, runtime API contracts, and admin/Garden UI types that expose ambiguous timestamp fields.
- Apply the naming rules from psfn-framework-qhxv.1 to newly touched surfaces: epoch milliseconds use explicit Ms suffixes, ISO strings use explicit Iso suffixes, and date/month buckets use Key suffixes.
- Where compatibility requires legacy fields, add boundary normalization and comments/types that mark them as legacy instead of spreading string | number further.
- Update generated/catalog/tool schema descriptions where they currently encourage ambiguous timestamp handling.
- Make sure user-facing display can still show readable ISO or localized strings without changing the machine contract.

## Non-goals
- Do not rename every persisted field in one sweeping breaking change unless the decision bead explicitly approves it.
- Do not change model/provider prompt-display macros except to document them as display-only.
- Do not bundle journal action registry drift or other non-timestamp tool-surface bugs here; those remain in psfn-framework-c4jy.

- src/core/agent/tool-surface/registry.ts
- src/app/gateway and Garden/admin UI contract types
- tool implementations that return createdAt, updatedAt, timestamp, startedAt, completedAt, savedAt, or occurredAt
- src/core/identity/prompt-runtime.ts for display-only timestamp macros
acceptance_criteria:
- Ambiguous timestamp?: string | number shapes in touched tool/API/UI surfaces are replaced with explicit fields or wrapped behind compatibility normalization.
- New or changed schema descriptions state whether timestamps are epoch milliseconds, ISO UTC strings, bucket keys, or display-only values.
- Tool/API output tests or type tests cover at least one migrated surface.
- Prompt/display macros remain classified as display-only and are not treated as persisted canonical instants.
- npm run lint and targeted contract/UI/type tests pass before closure.

title: Improve tool schema feedback so memory/contact/toolset invalid calls do not loop
description: Audit evidence from Carlini live deployment on 2026-06-29 shows repeated derated tool use that looks like schema confusion rather than unavailable subsystems. In Discord channel 1486443955561299979, turn 019f13a1-d439-704b-b731-c42d09b01c23 around 13:47 UTC, Carlini called memory action=search eight times without a query and received 'Error: query is required for action=search' each time before saying the search tool was erroring. In turn 019f13a4-54cd-751a-b393-9f8f4891f3c5, contact returned a valid contact list with contacts and channel counts, then subsequent calls failed with Missing contactId / No contact found for display names. In image turn 019f1364-812e-74bf-b064-d5231bf256c0, toolset failed with 'Provide at least one extended tool name in tools.' These are active tools, but the model is not recovering from required-argument feedback. Scope: improve tool descriptions, schema hints, and/or error messages so required fields and next valid calls are obvious to the model; add tests around the observed failures. Non-goal: broad redesign of the tool surface or changing contact storage semantics.
acceptance_criteria: Regression tests cover: memory action=search requires a non-empty query and its model-facing error includes the exact missing field and a minimal valid example; contact list/get/search recovery gives the model a usable contactId path after a list result instead of encouraging display-name guesses; toolset activate errors include the required tools array and a valid example. The same tests or prompt fixtures ensure repeated identical invalid calls are discouraged or summarized. npm run lint passes.
notes:
IMPLEMENTATION DIRECTION (operator session 2026-06-29): root cause is inconsistent tool CONTEXT, not just terse error strings. Confirmed via audit: selfie_create tool-level desc ~1290 chars (operational internals: model fallback chain gpt-image-2->nano-banana-2->grok-imagine, aspect-ratio list, vision-review handoff) while memory/contact/toolset are under-described (memory = one enum line; contact list hides contactId). Model loops because complex tools are under-described and simple ones over-described.

Fix plan (all under this bead — same root cause, no split):
1. CONTACT LIST ENRICHMENT (src/core/contacts/tools.ts executeContactList ~line 248): each line shows contactId + channels (discord:<userId>[privacy]). Format '- <id>: Name [trust/rel] channels=...' keeps existing substring assertions green (Iris no-notes test at tools.test.ts:399 only constrains the ' — ' separator; not using it). Footer: 'Pass contactId to action=lookup/set_trust/note.' Kills the list->guess-display-name->fail loop at the source.
2. THREE ERROR MESSAGES -> add valid examples (src/faculties/memory/tools.ts:1472, src/core/contacts/tools.ts lookup miss ~line 299, src/core/agent/substrate-agent/adaptive-tools-runtime.ts:515): each error includes the exact missing field AND a minimal valid example JSON; contact lookup miss lists valid contactIds or points to action=list; toolset activate points to action=list for names.
3. TOOL DESCRIPTION REBALANCE: trim selfie_create operational internals (fallback chain + aspect ratios run automatically, model cannot act on them) -> src/primitives/images/tools.ts ~line 229; enrich memory (src/faculties/memory/tools.ts:1271) / contact (src/core/contacts/tools.ts ~445) / toolset (src/core/agent/substrate-agent/adaptive-tools-runtime.ts ~655) top-level descriptions with required-arg hints + action list.
4. TESTS: the two p45u acceptance tests (memory search requires query + example; toolset activate includes tools array + example) PLUS contact-list-shows-contactId-and-channels assertion.

Non-goal unchanged: no broad tool-surface redesign. This is description/error/context quality, not a new abstraction.
ADDITIONAL SCOPE (operator 2026-06-29): tool-description rebalance is broader than the four with observed loop evidence. Operator explicitly flagged these as too light — ENRICH their top-level descriptions: schedule (src/core/scheduler/schedule-tool.ts ~line 438), repo (src/boundary/integrations/git/tools.ts ~line 170), session_new/session_list/session_resume (src/core/tools/session.ts ~308/384/412), subagent (src/faculties/subagents/tools.ts ~line 29). Confirmed by reading: all are 1-2 line enum dumps today (e.g. schedule = 'Use action=list|create_follow_up|...|schedule_prompt.' with no grouping, no required-arg hint, no list-first guidance). The rest of the tool surface looks OK for now — do NOT sweep the whole catalog.
REOPENED 2026-06-29: prior closure was overcalled. The implementation only proved narrow memory/contact/toolset error-message regressions; it did not prove the broader operator request that multiple tool descriptions, especially overlong ones, are improved and visible/effective in the Garden/admin chat model-facing tool surface. Need audit actual tool schema path and fix missing/overlong/under-described tools comprehensively.

title: Add runtime schema validation for chat completion requests
description:
Summary: The OpenAI-compatible chat completion endpoint parses JSON into ChatCompletionRequest but only performs shallow runtime validation before returning the typed object. Most of the TypeScript interface is not enforced at the trust boundary.

Evidence and affected files:
- src/channels/api/server/request.ts:70 readChatCompletionRequest parses the body as ChatCompletionRequest at line 75.
- src/channels/api/server/request.ts:103-124 only rejects caller-provided primary trust and checks that messages exists, is an array, and is non-empty.
- src/channels/api/types.ts:37 defines ChatCompletionRequest with model, messages, stream, max_tokens, provider/system prompt overrides, and compatibility fields, but this is compile-time only.
- src/channels/api/server/request.ts:145 validates some provider/system_prompt_mode/response_style override fields later, after the body has already been accepted as the request type.

Why it matters: This endpoint accepts untrusted JSON. Invalid roles, malformed content parts, non-boolean stream values, unbounded numbers, or unexpected object shapes can drift into downstream runtime paths and produce confusing behavior instead of clear 400 responses.

Scope: Add a runtime validator using an existing project pattern or a focused local validator. Validate message role/content shapes, text/image parts, model and override fields, stream boolean, and max_tokens/numeric bounds. Share or mirror the validator across gateway and agent code where the same contract is enforced.

Non-goals: Do not expand the public API surface or implement tool-calling support in this bead. Compatibility-only fields may remain accepted-and-ignored if their shapes are intentionally validated.
acceptance_criteria: readChatCompletionRequest validates ChatCompletionRequest at runtime, including message role/content shape, stream boolean, model/provider override constraints, and numeric bounds; malformed messages/content return structured 400 errors; gateway and agent enforcement stay consistent; tests cover invalid roles, invalid content parts, bad stream/max_tokens values, and valid text/image requests; npm run lint and targeted API tests pass.
close_reason: Implemented runtime schema validation for OpenAI-compatible chat completion requests at the HTTP trust boundary. Evidence: src/channels/api/request-validation.ts now validates the request object before it is accepted as ChatCompletionRequest: non-empty model, non-empty messages array, role values, string/array content shape, text/image/image_url content parts, stream boolean, bounded max_tokens and other numeric compatibility fields, provider/system_prompt/response_style string/enums, stop/logit_bias/tools shapes, and existing primary-trust rejection remains intact. src/channels/api/server/request.ts calls validateChatCompletionRequest from readChatCompletionRequest and returns structured 400 invalid_request errors with path details before downstream routing. Tests in src/channels/api/server.test.ts cover invalid roles, malformed image_url content parts, bad stream/max_tokens values, and a valid mixed text/image request; the streaming helper stabilization keeps queued-stream assertions focused on delivered content rather than promise-resolution timing. Validation passed: npm test -- --run src/channels/api/server.test.ts src/channels/api/server/session.test.ts src/channels/api/agent-backend.test.ts src/channels/api/gateway-runtime.test.ts --reporter=dot (105 tests); npm test -- --run src/channels/api/response-format.test.ts src/channels/api/server.runtime.test.ts --reporter=dot (9 tests); npm run lint; npm run build; git diff --check.

title: Emit machine-readable SSE errors for streaming chat failures
description:
Summary: Streaming chat failures are currently encoded as successful assistant content chunks. OpenAI-compatible clients can mistake runtime/timeout/busy/internal errors for normal model output and a clean stop.

Evidence and affected files:
- src/channels/api/response-format.ts:132 buildStreamingErrorChunk returns object chat.completion.chunk and line 141 puts the error string in delta.content with finish_reason 'stop'.
- src/channels/api/server/streaming.ts:40 writeErrorAndDone writes that error chunk and then [DONE].
- src/channels/api/server/chat-completions.ts:824 handleStreamingTurnError emits strings like '[Error: Request timed out]', '[Error: Agent busy]', and '[Error: Internal server error]' through writeErrorAndDone at lines 831, 838, and 845.
- src/channels/api/server/chat-completions.ts:970-976 also emits runtime result errors and empty-content errors as normal content chunks.

Why it matters: API consumers need a structured way to distinguish model text from transport/runtime failure. Encoding errors as assistant content breaks robust retries, monitoring, and OpenAI-compatible client behavior.

Scope: Define a machine-readable streaming error representation for post-header failures, such as SSE `event: error` with JSON error data or an OpenAI-style JSON error object. Update all streaming error paths and tests so failures do not look like normal assistant completions.

Non-goals: Do not change non-streaming error status handling or unrelated completion formatting in this bead.
acceptance_criteria: Streaming chat failures after SSE headers are committed produce a machine-readable error event or OpenAI-compatible error payload that clients can distinguish from assistant content; error paths no longer emit a normal content delta with finish_reason stop; response-format and chat-completions tests are updated; npm run lint and targeted API tests pass.
close_reason: Implemented machine-readable SSE errors for streaming chat failures. Evidence: src/channels/api/response-format.ts replaces the old fake terminal error content chunk with buildStreamingErrorEvent/formatSseErrorEvent, which emits event: error with the existing OpenAI-compatible { error: { message, type, param, code, details } } envelope. src/channels/api/server/streaming.ts writes structured error events plus [DONE]. src/channels/api/server/chat-completions.ts now maps committed-header streaming failures to stable error types/messages: request_timeout, agent_busy, internal_error, runtime result errors, and empty_response, instead of emitting assistant delta.content strings like [Error: ...] with finish_reason stop. Tests updated: response-format.test asserts structured error event formatting; server.test parses named SSE frames and covers empty streaming responses plus agent-busy thrown errors; server.runtime.test covers runtime result ok=false streaming errors with details. Validation passed: npm test -- --run src/channels/api/response-format.test.ts src/channels/api/server.test.ts src/channels/api/server.runtime.test.ts --reporter=dot (92 tests); rg confirmed no buildStreamingErrorChunk or old [Error: ...] streaming call sites remain under src/channels/api; npm run lint; npm run build; git diff --check.

title: Batch episodic thread arc and related-episode lookups
description:
Summary: Garden episodic-memory thread views perform N+1 store calls for arcs and related episodes. On large episodic histories, listing threads or opening a thread can multiply database round trips by episode and arc count.

Evidence and affected files:
- src/operator/garden/services/episodic-memory-service.ts:200 listThreads loads episodes and then calls buildThreadSummaries.
- src/operator/garden/services/episodic-memory-service.ts:212 getThreadDetail loads thread episodes, then line 220 calls collectArcsForEpisodes.
- src/operator/garden/services/episodic-memory-service.ts:288 buildThreadSummaries groups episodes by thread and line 299 calls collectArcsForEpisodes for each thread group.
- src/operator/garden/services/episodic-memory-service.ts:324 collectArcsForEpisodes loops every episode and line 327 awaits store.listEpisodeArcsForEpisode for each one.
- src/operator/garden/services/episodic-memory-service.ts:278 and :340 build related-arc views by calling store.getEpisode for each related episode at lines 284 and 351.

Why it matters: The current implementation turns a single Garden thread page into many sequential or parallel database calls. This increases latency and database load as episodic memory grows.

Scope: Add batch store APIs such as listEpisodeArcsForEpisodes(ids) and getEpisodesByIds(ids), or implement equivalent SQL-backed summary methods. Update the Garden service to build maps from batched results and preserve deduplication/order semantics.

Non-goals: Do not alter episodic memory write semantics, arc kinds, or salience scoring in this bead.
acceptance_criteria: Thread list/detail and related-arc Garden endpoints avoid per-episode/per-arc store round trips by using batch store APIs or database queries; existing response shapes are preserved; tests cover thread summaries and related arc views; npm run lint and targeted episodic-memory/Garden tests pass.
close_reason: Implemented and integrated in stnk-parallel-20260629. Evidence: commit cfe6f430 added getEpisodesByIds/listEpisodeArcsForEpisodes batch APIs to src/faculties/memory/episodic/store.ts and src/faculties/memory/episodic/postgres-store.ts, and updated src/operator/garden/services/episodic-memory-service.ts to batch thread arc and related episode lookups. Integrated via merge 70c301ae. Validation on integration: npm test -- --run src/faculties/memory/episodic/store.test.ts src/faculties/memory/episodic/postgres-store.test.ts src/operator/garden/services/episodic-memory-service.test.ts src/operator/garden/api-routes.test.ts passed 66 tests; npm run lint passed; npm run build passed.

title: Push Garden memory filtering and pagination into the memory store
description:
Summary: Garden memory list/search code scans a large active-memory set and filters/sorts/slices in application code. This is acceptable for small corpora but scales poorly as the memory table grows.

Evidence and affected files:
- src/operator/garden/services/memory-service.ts:46-48 defines DEFAULT_MEMORY_LIST_LIMIT=50, MAX_MEMORY_LIST_LIMIT=200, and MAX_MEMORY_FILTER_SCAN=100_000.
- src/operator/garden/services/memory-service.ts:205 builds a contact summary map by calling contactStore.listAll() for each memory response.
- src/operator/garden/services/memory-service.ts:215 calls memoryStore.getAllActiveMemories(MAX_MEMORY_FILTER_SCAN) for managed-scope listings.
- src/operator/garden/services/memory-service.ts:240 parses list filters, then line 255 loads up to 100,000 active memories, lines 260-274 filter and sort in memory, and line 277 slices for pagination.
- src/operator/garden/services/memory-service.ts:395 loads the same active-memory scan before embedding search mainly to build privacySummary and contactsById.

Why it matters: Admin list/search endpoints should remain responsive as memory count grows. Pulling up to 100,000 rows into Node to answer a 50-row page wastes CPU/memory and can become a latency spike in the Garden UI.

Scope: Add or extend memory-store APIs so Garden list filters, ordering, total count, and pagination run in the store/database. Consider a focused admin query method if the generic MemoryStorePort should stay small. Avoid changing the external Garden API shape unless necessary and covered by tests.

Non-goals: Do not redesign memory retention semantics, embedding search ranking, or contact storage in this bead except where needed to avoid per-request full scans.
acceptance_criteria: Garden memory list endpoints no longer fetch up to MAX_MEMORY_FILTER_SCAN active memories just to filter/sort/page in process; filtering, ordering, count, and pagination are performed by the memory store/database or a dedicated indexed query path; privacy summary behavior is preserved or intentionally adjusted with tests; npm run lint and targeted memory/Garden tests pass.
notes: Implemented in local commit c37f5f17. Validation passed: npm run lint; npm test -- --run src/faculties/memory/store.test.ts src/operator/garden/services/memory-service.test.ts; npm test -- --run src/faculties/memory/memory-store-port.test.ts src/faculties/memory/postgres-store.test.ts; npm test -- --run src/operator/garden/api-routes.test.ts; combined targeted memory/Garden run passed 132 tests. Bead left in progress for orchestrator integration/closure.

title: Wire routed concern decisions into durable substrates
description:
Problem:
Concern candidate review and grooming now support route decisions/targets so non-concern material can be kept out of ActiveConcern, but the route action is still an intake outcome, not a concrete handoff into north-star, project/task, reminder/schedule, or another durable substrate. Cap overflow grooming resolves concerns with a durable-tracking outcome, but it does not create or update the destination substrate.

Why this matters:
The operator explicitly wants concerns to stay short-time follow-up items. Longer-term or important items should become north-stars, project/task work, reminders/scheduled items, or another explicit tracking category instead of silently disappearing or staying in concern form.

Current implementation to build on:
- src/core/intention/concern-candidates.ts supports ConcernCandidateRouteTarget and review decisions with action=route; applyConcernCandidateReview returns routed/blocked outcomes and never sends outbound messages.
- src/core/intention/concern-grooming.ts resolves stale/cap-overflow concerns and emits intention.concern.groomed maintenance telemetry.
- src/core/intention/concerns.ts and src/core/intention/postgres-adapters/concerns-adapter.ts enforce the 7-active cap and 1-week hard lifetime.

Scope:
Add explicit durable handoff plumbing for routed concern outcomes. Prefer small optional ports/adapters over direct imports from every substrate. Map routeTarget=north_star/project/reminder/schedule/introspection/other to the correct existing substrate where one exists, and fail closed with a visible event/result when no handler exists. Preserve source candidate/concern provenance and avoid outbound delivery.

Non-goals:
Do not create a new outbound sender. Do not let routing bypass existing policy gates for reminders/scheduler/project systems. Do not reopen concerns just because routing failed; surface the blocked route explicitly.

- Route decisions from applyConcernCandidateReview can hand off to a configured durable substrate handler with candidate provenance/evidence refs preserved.
