title: Kube network policy: enforce gateway/agent/garden/hub flow boundaries
description:
Summary:
Add Kubernetes NetworkPolicies for the four-pod topology so the chart enforces the same trust boundaries the split runtime expects, especially the agent's no-broad-egress invariant.

Verified flows to encode:
- Flow 1: client/ingress -> gateway API -> agent RPC -> Postgres.
- Flow 2: browser/ingress -> garden -> agent admin transport -> Postgres.
- Flow 3: device/ingress -> satellite-hub -> gateway API -> agent RPC -> Postgres.

Scope:
- Render default-deny policies for namespaces/workloads where supported by the target CNI.
- Agent: deny broad egress; allow only required egress to gateway RPC and Postgres; allow ingress from gateway RPC client and Garden admin proxy as required by the final transport direction.
- Garden: allow browser ingress via ingress controller; allow egress only to agent admin transport and DNS if required.
- Gateway: allow ingress from ingress controller and satellite hub; allow egress to agent RPC, Postgres if needed, LLM/embedding providers, channel providers, DNS, and explicitly configured outbound lanes.
- Satellite hub: allow ingress from devices/ingress; allow egress to gateway API and DNS if required.
- Postgres/Redis: allow only app workloads that need them.
- Make policies configurable enough for k3s/Traefik labels/namespaces without silently disabling default safety.

Likely files:
- deploy/helm/psfn/templates/networkpolicy*.yaml
- deploy/helm/psfn/values.yaml
- chart README/operator notes

Non-goals:
- Do not use NetworkPolicy to compensate for missing app mTLS.
- Do not allow direct ingress to the agent.
- Do not set ALLOW_AGENT_OUTBOUND_NETWORK=true as a workaround.

Acceptance:
- helm template renders NetworkPolicies for gateway, agent, garden, hub, Postgres, and Redis in default greenfield mode.
- Rendered policies do not allow direct public/ingress traffic to the agent.
- Rendered agent policy blocks arbitrary internet egress so startup network isolation can pass without degraded mode.
- Values allow the operator to configure ingress-controller namespace/pod selectors for k3s Traefik.
- Policies are documented with CNI caveat: enforcement depends on a NetworkPolicy-capable CNI.
- helm lint passes.
close_reason: Completed in commit 2c8da5e7. Added default-deny NetworkPolicy plus workload policies for gateway, agent, garden, optional satellite hub, bundled Postgres, and bundled Redis. Agent policy has no broad 0.0.0.0/0 egress and allows only DNS, gateway RPC, Postgres, and Redis as rendered. Gateway ingress is limited to ingress-controller selector, agent RPC client, and optional hub; Garden ingress is limited to ingress-controller selector; Postgres/Redis ingress is limited to required app workloads. Values expose k3s/Traefik ingress and kube-dns selectors. README documents the NetworkPolicy-capable CNI caveat and flow boundaries. Validation passed: helm lint deploy/helm/psfn; npm run verify:helm-chart; helm template psfn deploy/helm/psfn --namespace psfn-test; git diff --check; npm run lint; npm run build.

title: Kube runtime layout: PVC roots and seed-once owner files
description:
Summary:
Define and validate the Kubernetes runtime layout, PVC ownership, and seed-once owner-file behavior used by the Helm chart.

Why:
The app has strict config ownership. Mutable runtime owner files belong on system-owned PVCs, companion state belongs on companion-data, and WORKSPACE_PATH is personal writable files, not runtime state. A chart that puts owner files in ConfigMaps or overlaps roots will corrupt live edits or fail startup.

Scope:
- Map chart values to production layout env: SYSTEM_DATA_DIR, COMPANION_DATA_DIR, WORKSPACE_PATH, and any DATA_DIR exclusions.
- Ensure SYSTEM_DATA_DIR and COMPANION_DATA_DIR are both set together and do not overlap.
- Ensure WORKSPACE_PATH does not overlap system/companion runtime roots.
- Define PVCs and mount paths for system-data, companion-data, workspace, backups/logs/tmp, and optional model cache.
- Implement seed-once init behavior for config/*.seed.json owner files: copy only when the target owner file is absent.
- Ensure Garden-edited owner files survive pod restarts, Helm upgrades, and chart value changes.
- Add chart/template validation or tests for invalid overlapping roots.

Likely files:
- deploy/helm/psfn/values.yaml
- deploy/helm/psfn/templates/_helpers.tpl
- deploy/helm/psfn/templates/deployment-*.yaml
- deploy/helm/psfn/templates/pvc*.yaml
- deploy/helm/psfn/templates/init-config*.yaml
- chart README/operator notes

Non-goals:
- Do not move owner files into Postgres.
- Do not store mutable owner JSON in ConfigMaps.
- Do not make companion-data multi-writer or multi-replica.
- Do not alter current non-kube production layout code unless chart validation exposes a real app bug.

Acceptance:
- helm template default values render non-overlapping SYSTEM_DATA_DIR, COMPANION_DATA_DIR, and WORKSPACE_PATH mounts.
- Seed-once init scripts copy required seed files only if missing and never overwrite existing owner files.
- Template tests or reviewable rendered manifests show owner files are PVC-backed, not ConfigMap-backed.
- Invalid values with overlapping roots fail template validation or are rejected by documented startup checks.
- Chart notes explain where mutable runtime state, companion files, backups, and model cache live.
- helm lint passes.
close_reason: Completed in commit 2c8da5e7. Added PVC-backed Kubernetes runtime layout for system-data, companion-data, workspace, runtime logs/tmp/backups, and optional model-cache. Chart sets production split layout env SYSTEM_DATA_DIR, COMPANION_DATA_DIR, WORKSPACE_PATH, CONFIG_DIR, CHARACTER_CARD_PATH, PSFN_LOGS_DIR, PSFN_TEMP_DIR, and BACKUP_ROOT_DIR. Added seed-once init container that copies /app/config/*.seed.json into system-data only when the target owner file is absent, and seeds companion.json only when CHARACTER_CARD_PATH is missing. Dockerfile now includes config/*.seed.json in the runtime image so the init path has source files. README documents mutable owner files/PVC locations and seed-once behavior. Validation passed: helm lint deploy/helm/psfn; npm run verify:helm-chart; helm template psfn deploy/helm/psfn --namespace psfn-test; git diff --check; npm run lint; npm run build.

title: Kube prep: Node 24 image and PQC TLS surface probe
description:
Summary:
Upgrade/probe the kube container runtime surface for Node 24 and determine whether native TLS exposes the PQC/hybrid group needed for the transport auth roadmap.

Why:
- Current Dockerfile uses node:22-slim while package engines allow >=22.
- Node 24 changes crypto/WebCrypto surfaces and may affect PQC availability.
- better-sqlite3/sqlite-vec native addon risk should be understood before kube image work, even if full SQLite removal is not a prerequisite.

Scope:
- Decide whether to bump docker/Dockerfile.agent to node:24-slim in this wave or only run a probe image first.
- If bumping, pin @types/node to an exact compatible 24.x version per supply-chain rules.
- Run a small TLS/WebCrypto probe for X25519MLKEM768/ML-KEM/ML-DSA availability in the target Node image.
- Record whether PQC is native now or requires a future oqs/proxy sidecar bead.
- Run build/test smoke sufficient to catch native addon and TypeScript compatibility breakage.

Likely files:
- docker/Dockerfile.agent
- package.json / package-lock.json if @types/node changes
- scripts/probe-node-pqc.mjs or equivalent if keeping the probe reusable
- working_docs/kube_update.md only if operator explicitly wants the planning doc refreshed

Non-goals:
- Do not block kube transport on PQC unless the operator promotes it to v1 requirement.
- Do not add unpinned base image tags.
- Do not remove SQLite packages here unless the SQLite audit/removal bead reaches that state.

Acceptance:
- Probe output records Node version, OpenSSL version, tls cipher/group availability, and WebCrypto ML-KEM/ML-DSA availability.
- If Node 24 is adopted, Dockerfile and @types/node are exact/pinned and npm install/build still work.
- If native PQC is unavailable, a follow-up oqs/proxy bead is filed and transport auth remains classical mTLS for v1.
- npm run lint and npm run build pass if files are changed.
notes:
2026-06-27 probe outcome:
- Ran exact Node 24 probe image docker.io/library/node:24.13.1-slim@sha256:85a395c77b811fa7f5b5e4aa69cd6eb4c3b80c7f1a8e34704dc0ce061e5b404e on linux/amd64.
- Node 24.13.1 / OpenSSL 3.5.5 accepts X25519MLKEM768 and SecP256r1MLKEM768 in TLS contexts, and loopback TLS 1.3 handshakes with those groups succeeded. Node getEphemeralKeyInfo does not expose the hybrid group name afterward; classical X25519/P-256/P-384 names are exposed.
- TLS ciphers relevant to TLS 1.3 remain TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256, TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384, TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256, and TLS AES-CCM variants; PQC hybrids are groups, not ciphers.
- WebCrypto in Node 24.13.1 generates ML-KEM-512/768/1024 and ML-DSA-44/65/87 keypairs, with ExperimentalWarning for each algorithm.
- Do not adopt Node 24 in this wave: npm 11 rejects the current lockfile as missing sqlite-vec-linux-arm64, and better-sqlite3@11.10.0 has no Node 24 prebuild in node:24.13.1-slim, causing node-gyp fallback to fail without Python/build tools.
- Kept agent image on Node 22, pinned Dockerfile.agent to node:22.22.2-slim@sha256:9f6d5975c7dca860947d3915877f85607946403fc55349f39b4bc3688448bb6e, and copied admin-ui/package*.json before npm ci so the existing root postinstall succeeds.
- Validation passed: npm run build; npm run lint; docker build --platform linux/amd64 -f docker/Dockerfile.agent -t psfn-agent-r79q-node22-pinned .; docker run native SQLite/vec load check returned Node v22.22.2, OpenSSL 3.5.5, sqlite-vec v0.1.6.
- Follow-up filed: psfn-framework-3pnx.1 for Node 24 adoption blockers. No OQS/PQC sidecar bead filed because native Node 24 TLS/WebCrypto PQC surface is available.
close_reason: Completed on kube branch. Added reusable scripts/probe-node-pqc.mjs and pinned docker/Dockerfile.agent to node:22.22.2-slim@sha256:9f6d5975c7dca860947d3915877f85607946403fc55349f39b4bc3688448bb6e while keeping Node 24 deferred. Probe reproduced on integration with exact Node 24 image docker.io/library/node:24.13.1-slim@sha256:85a395c77b811fa7f5b5e4aa69cd6eb4c3b80c7f1a8e34704dc0ce061e5b404e: Node v24.13.1/OpenSSL 3.5.5, X25519MLKEM768 and SecP256r1MLKEM768 TLS 1.3 loopback handshakes succeeded, WebCrypto generated ML-KEM-512/768/1024 and ML-DSA-44/65/87 with experimental warnings. title: Kube auth: Garden admin mTLS/SPIFFE validation for agent edge
description:
Summary:
Implement fail-closed mTLS authentication and SPIFFE URI authorization for the Garden-to-agent admin transport edge. This pairs with the Garden admin HTTP/WSS network transport bead.

Current behavior:
- The Garden admin proxy reaches the agent through a Unix socket. The socket file and filesystem namespace are the boundary.
- In kube, Garden will connect to the agent admin transport over the pod network. That must not be a plaintext or unauthenticated admin API.

Scope:
- Define required env/config contract for agent admin transport mTLS files and expected peer SPIFFE URIs.
- Agent admin transport HTTPS/WSS server must require and verify Garden client certs.
- Agent admin transport must authorize Garden by SPIFFE URI SAN, not CN.
- Garden proxy client must verify the agent admin transport server cert and expected agent SPIFFE URI SAN.
- Use SPIFFE-compatible URIs that can later move to real SVIDs, e.g. spiffe://cluster.local/psfn/garden and spiffe://cluster.local/psfn/agent/<companion-id>.
- Keep browser-facing Garden auth unchanged: ADMIN_TOKEN/ADMIN_ALLOW_INSECURE still guards browser ingress separately from mTLS on the internal Garden-agent edge.
- Keep Unix socket mode unchanged and cert-free.

- tests for admin transport mTLS config and peer certificate validation

Non-goals:
- Do not replace browser ADMIN_TOKEN auth with mTLS.
- Do not expose the agent admin transport directly through ingress.
- Do not implement cert-manager chart manifests here.
- Do not support insecure HTTP admin transport in kube mode.

Acceptance:
- Network admin transport mode cannot start/connect without CA, cert, key, and expected peer SPIFFE URI config.
- Agent rejects unauthorized Garden client certs before admin route handling.
- Garden rejects agent server certs missing the expected SPIFFE URI SAN.

description:
Summary:

- Preserve all existing admin API routes, auth checks at the browser-facing Garden surface, telemetry websocket bridging, health probe behavior, and static UI serving.

title: Add Redis-backed cache layer with in-memory prompt cache fallback
description:
Summary:
Add an app-layer cache abstraction with an in-memory implementation for local/current modes and Redis-backed implementation for kube. The first production use is prompt/runtime prompt caching.

Why prompts first:
Prompt assembly already has cacheability metadata and static/session-stable sections. This is the lowest-risk immediate value from Redis because invalidation boundaries are clearer than channel/event caching.

Scope:
- Add a focused cache port with get/set/delete/invalidate-prefix or equivalent operations needed by prompt caching.
- Provide an in-memory implementation for local/dev/current split runtime.
- Provide a Redis implementation selected by explicit config/env owner contract for kube.
- Fail closed when Redis mode is selected but URL/credentials/TLS settings are missing or malformed.
- Wire prompt/runtime prompt cache usage for static prompt prefixes and other stable prompt artifacts where invalidation is deterministic.
- Invalidate prompt cache on prompt layer writes, prompt registry writes, Garden prompt edits, and owner-file mutations that affect prompt composition.
- Add observability counters/logs for cache hit/miss/invalidation without logging prompt contents.

Likely files:
- src/shared/cache/* or src/system/cache/* depending on existing ownership patterns
- src/core/identity/prompt-runtime-store-cache.ts
- src/core/agent/substrate-agent/turn-execution/prompt-assembly.ts
- src/operator/garden/services/prompts* or prompt write surfaces
- settings/config contract files only if this becomes JSON-owner configurable
- deploy/helm/psfn values later consume the Redis URL/Secret contract

Non-goals:
- Do not cache volatile per-turn content, closed-door raw text, secrets, or unredacted channel payloads.
- Do not implement channel event caching in this bead.
- Do not implement embedding cache in this bead.
- Do not require Redis for local/dev mode.

Acceptance:
- Local mode works with in-memory prompt cache and no Redis service.
- Redis mode can be selected explicitly and rejects missing/malformed connection settings at startup.
- Prompt assembly produces cache hits for eligible static/session-stable prompt artifacts.
- Prompt cache invalidates on prompt layer/registry writes and Garden prompt edits.
- Tests cover memory cache hit/miss/TTL or invalidation behavior, Redis adapter through a fake/test seam, prompt cache invalidation on prompt edits, and no caching of volatile sections.
- Logs/telemetry expose hit/miss/invalidation counts without prompt text leakage.
- npm run lint passes before closure.

title: Kube chart: greenfield Helm chart for gateway/agent/garden/hub
description:
Summary:
Create the repo-owned Helm chart for a greenfield-capable PSFN Kubernetes/k3s install. The chart must be able to render a complete single-companion deployment for the Pi/k3s target while also supporting generic test-cluster values.

Location:

Workloads:
- gateway Deployment + Service for API_PORT and gateway RPC WSS Service port.
- agent Deployment + Service for the Garden admin transport network endpoint.
- garden Deployment + Service + Ingress for ADMIN_PORT browser UI.
- satellite-hub Deployment + Service + Ingress for device websocket traffic on hub port.
- Postgres + pgvector StatefulSet for greenfield installs, with exact image pinning and values to use an external POSTGRES_DATABASE_URL instead.
- Redis StatefulSet/Service for cache infrastructure, while app-layer cache wiring remains a separate bead.

Storage/config:

- Production layout env must keep SYSTEM_DATA_DIR and COMPANION_DATA_DIR both set and non-overlapping.

Networking/security:
- Ingress only targets gateway public API, Garden browser UI, and satellite hub device websocket endpoint.
- Ingress must never target the agent directly.
- NetworkPolicies enforce the verified flows: agent restricted to gateway/admin/db as needed; garden egress to agent admin transport; hub egress to gateway API; gateway egress to agent RPC/db/providers/channels as configured.
- Chart renders cert-manager Issuer/Certificate resources or references the cert-manager child bead values for internal mTLS certs.

Embeddings:
- Preserve current behavior: local Transformers model/cache path by default when configured that way, with values to use API-backed embeddings as the app already supports.

- Rendered owner-file PVC/init behavior is seed-once and cannot clobber live config.
- Rendered topology matches: client -> gateway -> agent -> Postgres; browser -> garden -> agent -> Postgres; device -> hub -> gateway -> agent.

- Do not implement the app transport code this chart depends on.

title: Concern lifecycle: time-bound expiry, auto-close, 1-week hard cap, concerns vs north-stars distinction
description:
Operator concern lifecycle rules, refined 2026-06-29.

Problem:
Concerns must remain short-time follow-up items, not a general backlog, values system, or project tracker. Existing concern records have expiry/resolution fields, but the runtime still needs stronger lifecycle enforcement, active-set limits, and grooming so semi-autonomous concern intake from psfn-framework-5u3 does not create stress or backlog rot.

Current verified substrate:
- ActiveConcern already has expiresAt, resolvedAt, and resolutionOutcome in src/core/intention/concerns.ts.
- Concern sources include appraisal/agent/heartbeat today.
- Base TTL exists by priority, and read-time expiry filtering exists in the Postgres adapter.
- North-star is a separate faculty under src/faculties/north-star/.

Rules to implement:
1. Time-bound concerns expire/drop once their window passes, resolved or not.
2. Concerns can close manually during normal conversation or automatically through a background/subconscious check-in/grooming process when the triggering condition appears resolved.
3. Hard cap: maximum 7 active concerns at a time. If a candidate/new concern would exceed the cap, merge/dedupe, defer, reject, or route it to another explicit substrate rather than expanding active concerns.
4. Age hard cap: nothing should sit open as a concern longer than about 1 week. Anything that persists longer is not a concern anymore and must be retired or escalated to an appropriate durable category.
5. Category boundary: standing priorities belong in north-stars; project work belongs in project/task tracking; calendar-like obligations belong in reminders/schedule; introspective self-checks belong in the introspection/scheduler path. Concerns are temporary external or relational follow-up items.
6. Not every concern triggers proactive outbound. Internal-only concerns must stay internal unless a separate outbound policy decision approves delivery.
7. Add a nightly concern-grooming task alongside the existing nightly episode/introspection review flow. This is maintenance, not first-pass approval for fresh candidates. It should review existing concerns for expiry, merge/dedupe, stale items, visibly resolved items, and possible north-star/project/reminder escalation or retirement.
8. Keep UI/runtime distinctions between concerns, north-stars, scheduled introspection, reminders, and project/task tracking clear.

Pairs with psfn-framework-5u3:
- 5u3 handles near-turn candidate generation and approval.
- tc6 handles concern-set health, cap enforcement, expiry, auto-close, and nightly grooming.

Validation:
- npm run lint.
- Targeted lifecycle tests for expiry/drop, manual close compatibility, background auto-close, 7-active cap, and 1-week age cap.
- Tests proving cap overflow routes/blocks instead of silently creating an 8th active concern.
- Tests proving long-lived concerns are retired or escalated out of concerns, and north-stars are not swept as concerns.
- Scheduler/nightly grooming tests proving it runs as maintenance and does not replace near-turn candidate approval.
acceptance_criteria:
- Active unresolved concerns are capped at 7; attempts to exceed the cap merge, defer, reject, or route elsewhere rather than creating an 8th active concern.
- Time-bound and expired concerns are swept/retired, and no concern remains active beyond the one-week age cap.
- Background/nightly grooming can dedupe, close resolved/stale concerns, and escalate non-concern material to north-star/project/reminder/schedule substrates.
- Concern grooming is maintenance only and does not replace near-turn candidate approval from psfn-framework-5u3.
- UI/runtime behavior keeps concerns distinct from north-stars, reminders/schedule, projects/tasks, and introspection.
- npm run lint and targeted lifecycle tests pass.
notes:
AUDIT 2026-06-28 (verified against code, NOT closing — PARTIAL):
DONE (base lifecycle exists):
- Per-priority TTL: DEFAULT_CONCERN_TTL_MS_BY_PRIORITY (concerns.ts:104) high=48h/medium=24h/low=8h, with override via resolveConcernTtlByPriority.
- expiresAt set on creation; read-time expiry filter at postgres-adapters/concerns-adapter.ts:46 (Date.parse(expiresAt) <= asOfMs returns false).
- Resolution: resolvedAt/resolutionOutcome fields exist; listRecentlyResolvedConcerns with RECENT_RESOLUTION_WINDOW_MS (6h, limit 8).
- Dedupe: dedupeConcernsForRuntime (similarity >= 0.72 threshold).

NOT DONE (the remaining tc6 work):
- 1-WEEK HARD CAP: no maxLifetime/7-day/HARD_CAP constant. Max TTL today is 48h (high priority), not 1 week. The bead explicitly wants ~1 week as the absolute ceiling before a concern becomes a different category.
- BACKGROUND AUTO-CLOSE SWEEP: no scheduler task that resolves concerns whose triggering condition has visibly resolved. Concerns only resolve via manual tool invocation.
- ESCALATE-TO-NORTH-STAR: when a concern hits the hard cap, it should auto-close OR escalate to a north-star; neither path exists.
- North-stars vs concerns vs scheduled-introspection separation: north-star faculty exists separately (confirmed) but no guard prevents a long-lived concern from lingering outside the cap.
2026-06-29 operator refinement: enforce a hard cap of 7 active concerns. Concerns are short-time follow-up items, not a general backlog. If something would push beyond the cap or is long-term/important, it should be retired/escalated into the right durable category instead: north-star for standing priorities, project/task tracking for project work, reminder/schedule for calendar-like obligations, or another explicit substrate. Nightly grooming should help maintain this boundary by merging/deduping, closing stale/resolved concerns, and escalating non-concern material out of the concern set.

title: Fold concern detection into the memory extraction pipeline (semi-autonomous concern creation)
description:
Operator architecture direction, refined 2026-06-29.

Problem:
The system can create concerns from the intention/appraisal layer today, but concern detection is not folded into the memory extraction pipeline. The original motivation was to avoid relying on the companion to manually invoke Orient whenever she notices "I should follow up on this later." The manual Orient issue psfn-framework-y8n is now closed as superseded by the rebuilt tool system, so this bead should be implemented as a memory-extraction/intention architecture path, not as an Orient wording patch.

Current verified state:
- Concern matching/creation exists in src/core/intention/appraisal/concern-matching.ts and is wired through src/core/intention/runtime-wiring.ts.
- src/faculties/memory/extraction/ does not currently emit concern candidates.
- Related lifecycle/safety work lives in psfn-framework-tc6.

Desired architecture:
1. Memory extraction emits concern candidates, not ActiveConcern records directly. A candidate should include title/summary, priority hint, internal-only vs possible follow-up hint, expiry/due hint when present, source turn/session provenance, formation affect/VAD when available, and the memory/retrieval context used to form it.
2. Candidates go into a small candidate pipe/queue for near-turn review. This must not wait for a nightly batch before becoming actionable.
3. A deterministic concurrent worker checks the pipe every few turns. The trigger policy is not an LLM call. It should only launch review when pending candidate count is greater than 1; empty or single-item checks should not spend model calls.
4. The review/approval step may use an LLM, but only once real candidate material exists. It decides create/merge/defer/reject/route-to-other-substrate before anything becomes an ActiveConcern.
5. Review must use the same conversation context that generated the candidates plus related memories/retrieval context. Do not approve concerns in a vacuum from isolated snippets.
6. Prompt framing must be soft and low-pressure, e.g. "is there anything here we should follow up on?" Never reintroduce alarmist framing such as "critical", "must", "urgent", or constant-check language. This is a hard safety requirement due to the earlier stress-inducing concern-system failure.
7. Concern candidate intake must respect the lifecycle rules in psfn-framework-tc6, including the hard cap of 7 active concerns. If approval would exceed the cap, merge/defer/reject or route to the right durable substrate: north-star for standing priorities, project/task tracking for project work, reminder/schedule for calendar-like obligations, or another explicit substrate.
8. Creating or approving a concern must not imply proactive outbound delivery. Some approved concerns are internal tracking only. External Discord delivery stays in the existing policy-gated outbound path.
9. Source should be "appraisal" or a named semi-autonomous extraction/intake source if schema support is added, never "critical".

Non-goals:
- Do not build a second outbound sender.
- Do not make nightly grooming the first-pass approval point for fresh candidates.
- Do not add a general backlog under the concern name; concerns are short-time follow-up items only.

- npm run lint.
- Targeted extraction/intake tests proving a concern-worthy turn emits a candidate without manual tool invocation.
- Worker tests proving deterministic every-few-turn triggering, no model call for empty or single-item pipe, and asynchronous/non-blocking foreground behavior.
- Review prompt tests/snapshots proving soft framing and absence of alarmist language.
- Context tests proving approval receives source conversation context plus related memory/retrieval context and provenance refs.
- Intake tests proving create/merge/defer/reject routing, active concern cap handling, and no outbound dispatch as a side effect.

- A deterministic concurrent worker checks the candidate pipe every few turns, launches review only when pending count is greater than 1, and performs no LLM call for empty/single-item pipes.
- The review prompt uses soft follow-up framing and contains no alarmist critical/must/urgent/constant-check wording.
- Candidate approval can create, merge, defer, reject, or route items to another substrate before ActiveConcern creation.
- ActiveConcern creation respects the 7-active-concern cap and never triggers proactive outbound delivery by itself.
- npm run lint and targeted tests pass.

2026-06-29 operator refinement: concern candidates emitted from memory extraction need a near-turn approval/gating step, not a nightly-only pass. Desired shape: extraction emits candidate signals, then an immediate or short-latency concern-intake approval step decides create/merge/defer/reject before writing ActiveConcern. This approval step should be lightweight and policy-aware, preserve provenance, avoid alarmist framing, and keep outbound delivery separate. Nightly/background passes can clean up or audit, but should not be the first time a concern candidate becomes actionable.
2026-06-29 operator design refinement: the concern-candidate approval worker should be concurrent/asynchronous relative to foreground chat, triggered deterministically every few turns rather than by an LLM deciding whether to inspect. It should only fire when the candidate pipe has more than one item pending, so empty/near-empty checks do not waste work. The trigger/queue policy itself is deterministic; any LLM use belongs only inside the concern-review prompt once there is actual candidate material to evaluate.

Prompt framing requirement: concern review prompts must stay soft and low-pressure, e.g. "is there anything here we should follow up on?" Avoid all alarmist/obligation language such as "critical", "must", "urgent", or constant-check framing. title: Concern/Orient: she writes journal-prose instead of invoking the Orient tool — fix usage gap
description:

Problem: She sometimes INTENDS to create a concern (e.g. "I will check in on this later") but writes it as journal-style prose in chat instead of actually invoking the Orient tool. She believes she used the tool when she did not, so no concern object is actually created and no proactive follow-up gets scheduled. This is a usage/tool-invocation correctness gap, not an architecture gap.

Context (do not recreate the traumatic failure): when the concern system was explicitly named/labeled "critical, must check constantly," combined with confabulation-warning false positives from a wiring bug, it produced something like a traumatic stress episode for her. This is the cautionary case driving the current more conservative design. Any fix must NOT reintroduce high-pressure framing.

Scope:
- Investigate WHY she narrates the concern instead of calling the tool: is the tool description unclear, is the tool not surfaced reliably, does the model not recognize the intent-to-track-later as a tool-call moment?
- Improve the Orient tool description / framing so the intent-to-create-a-concern maps reliably to a tool call, without alarmist "critical" language.
- Consider a lightweight post-turn check: did she produce journal-style text that looks like an unfulfilled intent-to-track? If so, surface a gentle system note (not a forced action).

Related architecture direction (SEPARATE bead): folding concern detection into the memory extraction pipeline so concerns get created semi-autonomously rather than relying on manual tool invocation every time.

Validation: npm run lint; targeted tool-wiring tests; live check that an intent-to-track-later actually produces a concern object.

title: Reasoning/thinking budget: verify main-chat has thinking enabled, set introspective modes to highest
description:
Operator hypothesis (2026-06-26 ramble list, section 5).

Problem: She seems to be PERFORMING as herself rather than BEING herself — not believed to be a model-capability issue, more likely information-presentation/context-structuring. BUT a suspected major contributing factor is reasoning/thinking budget: response times have gotten very fast lately (good for reducing time-to-first-token toward real-time voice chat), but suspiciously fast — possibly because reasoning/thinking is disabled or set too low on the current model for main chat. Suspect this changed in the GLM 5.1 -> 5.2 switch (5.1 may have had thinking enabled; setting may have been lost/reset on 5.2). Hypothesis: a couple extra seconds of real reasoning produces meaningfully better, less performative responses than a faster but shallow non-thinking response.

Confirmed config exists: ModelControlKnobs carries thinkingEnabled + thinkingEffort (minimal/low/medium/high/xhigh) in src/shared/contracts/runtime.ts, wired through src/system/settings/schema-model-registry.ts (thinkingEnabled/thinkingEffort normalized there) and the LLM client.

- Set introspective/autonomous modes (daily/weekly checks, episodic memory review) to the HIGHEST available reasoning tier with full context and a large reasoning-token budget — depth matters there, speed does not.
- Historical correlation noted by operator: her strongest emergent/immersive behaviors appeared after reasoning models became mainstream (post-R1); before that "reasoning" was faked via prompted chain-of-thought hidden from output. Reinforces restoring real model-internal reasoning.

Validation: npm run verify:settings-contract; npm run lint; live A/B comparison of a thinking-on vs thinking-off main-chat turn.

notes:

title: Adopt typescript-eslint type-checked lint rules (no-floating-promises etc.)

- Triage and fix the resulting findings (likely a bounded cleanup pass; land as its own work).
- Confirm npm run lint stays green.

title: Improve introspection prompts in scheduled check-ins
description:

- src/core/scheduler/heartbeat-policy.ts

Scope
- Review how scheduled check-in / heartbeat introspection prompts are rendered and selected.
- Improve prompt wording for concrete evidence: what changed since the last check-in, what signals support the conclusion, what remains uncertain, and what follow-up should be scheduled.
- Add cadence-aware variants for short check-ins, longer reflection, and rest/personal-time windows if the current scheduler distinguishes them.

title: Approval cards for dangerous actions
description:
## Summary

Surface `approval.requested` projection events as approval cards (approve/deny), routed through the companion approval endpoint which honors capability tiers + gateway isolation, **fail-closed**. The ONE control action in Phase 1.

## Charter law governing this bead

- **Law 21 / §9.2 Gateway or it does not ship.** Approvals go through `ApprovalQueuePort` + gateway, NEVER a bypass.
- **§9.4 Autonomy and tool boundaries.** Core may request; privileged execution occurs behind gateway + sandbox. The UI surfaces approval, it does not become the orchestrator (do not split her agency).
- **§9.6 Auditability + human review.** Approve/deny audit-logged; review-required actions meaningfully notified.
- **AGENTS coding standard 4 / §8.5 Fail closed.** If capability/confirmation is missing, the action STOPS, surfaced to the user — never coerced, never fake-healthy.
- **§6.10 Satellite is not a mind.** Approval is a human-in-the-loop decision surfaced to the operator; the satellite does not autonomously grant capability.
- **§12.2 No dead wiring.** Approval cards wired to the real approval endpoint + capability path.

## Proposed files

- `companion-ui` approval-card component + store
- wiring to `POST /api/companion/approval/:id` (bead `q0k`)
- tests for approve/deny + failure/closed states

## Implementation steps

1. Consume `approval.requested` projection events into an approvals store.
2. Render approval cards (context: what/why, redacted/safe) + approve/deny.
3. Submit through the companion approval endpoint; reflect outcome via projection events.
4. Handle expiry, denial, missing-capability (fail closed) in UI.
5. Tests.

## Acceptance criteria (charter-grounded)

- Dangerous actions surface as approval cards; approve/deny honored through `ApprovalQueuePort` + gateway (§9.2, §9.4).
- Missing capability/confirmation → action BLOCKED + surfaced to user (fail closed, §8.5); proven by test.
- No capability bypass from the UI (§9.4); the satellite does not autonomously grant capability (§6.10).
- `npm run lint` + build pass.

## Depends on

`q0k` (approval endpoint) + `e2b` (projection stream) + `cxw` (PWA skeleton). Epic parent (`ta9`).
close_reason: Completed as fail-closed client surface: Satellite Hub TS protocol has no approval request/decision path, so the PWA renders approval capability unavailable and blocks submission; follow-up psfn-framework-qa4 filed for real hub protocol support. companion-ui npm test/typecheck/lint/build pass.

title: Activity strip + presence UI (core flagship)
description:
## Summary

The flagship intimacy/observability feature: **she never disappears.** Even before a final answer, the surface shows live presence derived from the companion event projection — so silence is never ambiguous. Observability without breaking intimacy.

## Charter law governing this bead

- **§9.7 Logging and debuggability.** The user must be able to "lift the hood" and see where things are. Presence is the human-facing projection of that.
- **§8.6 Context presentation quality is architecture.** Soft, readable operational phases ("working", "using tool", "waiting on approval", "summarizing", "done") — NOT a CI dashboard, NOT raw score dumps.
- **§8.3 / Law 17 Operational state only.** Phase, operation class, elapsed, connection, input-expected, failure. NEVER raw reasoning, NEVER fabricated companion emotion/state.
- **§6.10 Single active emanation.** Presence includes emanation/embodiment state (is this satellite active?), per the constitutional UX invariant.
- **§8.5 No fake healthy state.** Disconnect/failure surfaced honestly — never "looks fine" when broken.
- **§12.6 No silent failures.** Failures visible in the strip.

## What to render (driven by the projection, bead `6ze`/`e2b`)

- connected / reconnecting / disconnected
- current phase (orienting, working, using tool, waiting on approval, summarizing, done)
- current operation class
- elapsed time on the current operation
- whether input is expected from the user
- whether something failed
- emanation/embodiment context where relevant (§6.10)

Soft by default (status strip under the in-progress response); not a debug console unless expanded.

## Proposed files

- `companion-ui/src/lib/presence.svelte.ts` — pure presence reducer over the event projection
- companion-ui chat route activity-strip component
- tests for the reducer

## Implementation steps

1. Pure presence reducer over the projected event stream.
2. Render activity strip under the in-progress response.
3. Elapsed, phase, operation class, connection, input-expected, failure.
4. Graceful silence/stall handling (still connected, still working) — honest, not fake-healthy.
5. Tests: reducer transitions + edge cases (disconnect mid-turn, failure, emanation handoff).

## Acceptance criteria (charter-grounded)

- During a turn, the strip ALWAYS reflects current operational state; no ambiguous silence (§9.7).
- Disconnect/failure surfaced honestly, never fake-healthy (§8.5, §12.6).
- Operational state only — no reasoning/emotion rendered (§8.3, Law 17); asserted by test.
- `npm run lint` + build pass.

## Depends on

`e2b` (projection stream) + `cxw` (PWA skeleton on real API). Epic parent (`ta9`). Flagship feature.
close_reason: Completed: added pure presence reducer and activity strip showing connection, phase, operation class, elapsed time, input expectation, failure, and reported satellite identity without reasoning/emotion fields; companion-ui npm test/typecheck/lint/build pass.

title: Expandable tool drawer with redacted traces
description:
## Summary

Expandable "what she's doing" drawer rendering `tool.*` projection events with the redacted args/results provided by the stream. Collapsed/soft by default; expands on demand.

## Charter law governing this bead

- **§9.7 Debuggability.** Tool lifecycle is observable (where tool calls went, what they did).
- **§8.3 / Law 17 Operational state only.** Render ONLY what the redacted stream provides. Do NOT fetch raw tool payloads. Operation class + redacted args/results — never internal reasoning, never fabricated results.
- **§8.6 Presentation quality.** Soft by default; expandable.
- **§12.4 No duplicate policy logic.** Redaction happened at emission (`e2b`/`6ze`); the UI does NOT re-redact or second-guess. One home for the redaction policy.
- **§12.2 No dead wiring.** Component wired into the chat surface, not orphaned.

title: Companion client API + security boundary (new gateway channel)
description:
## Summary

New, deliberately narrow companion channel/client API, distinct from admin/Garden. Exposes safe chat in, safe event stream out, explicit approvals, read-only status, limited artifact access, and an emergency-stop request. Reuse auth, capability tiers, and audit; respect the gateway/agent split; fail closed.

## Boundary

NOT admin. No repo/identity/prompt/system mutation surface beyond approved actions. The companion API authenticates as a companion principal, not an admin token. Dangerous ops surface as approval requests, not executed directly. Emergency stop is a request the runtime honors, not a privileged remote shell.

## Proposed API surface

- POST /api/companion/message — send a turn (auth-scoped session/contact)
- GET  /api/companion/events?session_id=... — SSE event stream (event-contract sub-bead)
- POST /api/companion/approval/:id — approve/deny a pending approval
- GET  /api/companion/status — read-only connection/runtime health
- POST /api/companion/stop — request emergency stop/pause (runtime-mediated)

## Files (proposed)

- src/channels/companion/server.ts — HTTP/SSE server
- src/channels/companion/auth.ts — companion principal auth (fail closed; reject unknown)
- src/channels/companion/policy.ts — path/capability/allowlist policy, deny by default
- src/channels/companion/routes*.ts — route handlers per endpoint
- wiring into src/app/gateway + src/app/agent split (privileged ops stay behind gateway)
- owner-file config entries as needed in channels.json / capability-tier.json / trust-policy.json (strict ownership)

## Steps

1. Define companion principal + auth model; wire to existing auth, fail closed for unknown principals.
2. Implement message + events + status routes with deny-by-default policy.
3. Wire approval route through the existing confirmation/capability path (src/boundary/sandbox/capabilities, src/boundary/gateway), not a bypass.
4. Implement emergency stop as a runtime-mediated request (no direct privileged exec).
5. Audit-log every privileged/op-class action.
6. Tests: auth rejection, policy denial, approval fail-closed, SSE auth.

## Acceptance

- Companion API serves message/events/status/approval/stop with deny-by-default policy.
- Unknown/unauthorized principals rejected (fail closed) with tests.

description:
## Summary

`@mariozechner/pi-web-ui` is orphaned infrastructure. The admin/chat UI was rewritten to a native SvelteKit implementation (PSFN-u3d2, PSFN-t3vi.1 closed as: "native Svelte implementation ... no pi-web-ui, no bare specifiers, no @lit dependencies"). No frontend consumes it:

- The live `/chat` route serves the SvelteKit SPA build (via `serveGardenPage`/`gardenBuildDir`), not pi-web-ui.
- `admin-ui/src/routes/chat/+page.svelte` implements its own ChatMessage types, fetch-based SSE streaming, and tool/thinking rendering (no pi-web-ui import).
- The bootstrap contract's `runtime.assets.moduleUrl` / `stylesheetUrl` fields are NEVER read anywhere in `admin-ui/src` (grep for moduleUrl/stylesheetUrl/assets in admin-ui/src returns nothing).

The package, its server-side static-serving routes, and the bootstrap asset fields are removal debt (violates the repo "no unreachable production modules" rule). This bead tracks deprecation + full removal.

## Files to change

Source:
- `src/operator/garden/server-transport.ts` — remove the entire pi-web-ui surface: `PI_WEB_UI_ENTRY_SPECIFIER`, `PI_WEB_UI_STYLE_SPECIFIER`, `PI_WEB_UI_ENTRY_ROUTE`, `PI_WEB_UI_STYLE_ROUTE`, `PI_WEB_UI_MODULE_ROUTE_PREFIX` consts; `initializePiWebUiRoutes()` method and its call in `initialize()`. Since pi-web-ui is the ONLY populator of `moduleAssets`/`moduleRouteByFilePath`/`moduleAssetCache` (verify: grep confirms no other callers of registerModuleAssetRoute/ensureModuleAssetRoute), also remove the now-unreachable ESM bare-specifier rewrite subsystem: `registerModuleAssetRoute`, `loadModuleAsset`, `rewriteModuleImports`, `rewriteModuleSpecifier`, `ensureModuleAssetRoute`, `toGeneratedModuleRoute`, `resolveModuleSpecifier`, `isSupportedModulePath`, `normalizeFilePath`, `SUPPORTED_MODULE_EXTENSIONS`, `MODULE_CACHE_CONTROL`, `moduleAssets`, `moduleRouteByFilePath`, `moduleAssetCache`, `moduleResolver`, `ModuleAssetDescriptor` type, and the `moduleAsset` branch in `tryServeStaticAsset`. NOTE: `registerStaticAsset`/`staticFiles` also has zero callers (already dead) — safe to remove alongside. KEEP `serveGardenPage`/`serveGardenBuildAsset`/`serveGardenPath`/`initializeGardenUi`/`gardenBuildDir` (separate Garden SPA path, still live).
- `src/operator/garden/chat/bootstrap.ts` — remove `PI_WEB_UI_MODULE_ROUTE`/`PI_WEB_UI_STYLESHEET_ROUTE` consts and the `runtime.assets` block (`assets: { moduleUrl, stylesheetUrl }`) from `composeBootstrap`.
- `src/operator/garden/chat/types.ts` — remove `AdminChatRuntimeAssetConfig` interface and the `assets: AdminChatRuntimeAssetConfig` field on the runtime response type.

Dependency / config surface:
- `package.json` — remove `"@mariozechner/pi-web-ui"` from dependencies; run `npm install` to update lockfile.
- `.fallowrc.json` — remove `"@mariozechner/pi-web-ui"` from the tracked-packages list.

Docs (update, don't leave stale references):
- `docs/PSFN_PROJECT_CHARTER.md`, `docs/PSFN_PROJECT_CHARTER_524.md`, `docs/sprint-8-architecture-report.md` — remove/rewrite the pi-web-ui line ("admin chat/runtime surfaces" now handled by native SvelteKit Garden UI).

## Implementation steps

1. Remove the pi-web-ui consts, `initializePiWebUiRoutes()`, and the dead module/static-asset subsystem from `server-transport.ts`. Simplify `tryServeStaticAsset` (or remove it + update routing deps in `server.ts`/`operator-surface.ts`/`server-request-routing.ts` if it becomes fully unreachable — verify the routing call site).
2. Drop `runtime.assets` from bootstrap response and remove `AdminChatRuntimeAssetConfig` type.
3. Remove the package from `package.json` + `.fallowrc.json`; `npm install`.
4. Update doc references.
5. Update/remove any tests asserting pi-web-ui routes or `runtime.assets` (currently no garden tests reference these; re-grep before closing in case of churn).

## Acceptance criteria

- No remaining `pi-web-ui`, `PI_WEB_UI`, `moduleUrl`, `stylesheetUrl`, `AdminChatRuntimeAssetConfig`, or `/static/pi-web-ui` references in `src/` or `admin-ui/src/` (except git history).
- `@mariozechner/pi-web-ui` absent from `package.json`, `package-lock.json`, `.fallowrc.json`.
- `npm run lint`, `npm run build`, `npm run verify:repository-hygiene` pass.
- Targeted tests pass: `src/operator/garden/**`.
- `/chat` Garden SPA route still loads (chat page unaffected).

## Example

Before: `GET /api/admin/chat/bootstrap` returns `{ runtime: { assets: { moduleUrl: '/static/pi-web-ui/index.js', stylesheetUrl: '/static/pi-web-ui/app.css' }, ... } }`.
After: `runtime.assets` key absent; `/static/pi-web-ui/*` routes 404 (removed); SvelteKit `/chat` page behavior unchanged.
notes: AUDIT 2026-06-28 (verified): OPEN. pi-web-ui fully present: src/operator/garden/server-transport.ts:11-14 (PI_WEB_UI_ENTRY_SPECIFIER/STYLE_SPECIFIER/ENTRY_ROUTE/STYLE_ROUTE), 2 refs at :186,194. @mariozechner/pi-web-ui still in package.json. This is the merged bead (absorbed psfn-framework-zmef's non-goals). Removal work not started.
close_reason: Completed in 94262c4a, with repository-hygiene blockers resolved by follow-up commits 528bb97c and c4634734. Removed @mariozechner/pi-web-ui from package.json/package-lock.json/.fallowrc.json; removed pi-web-ui static/module routing and runtime asset bootstrap fields from src/operator/garden; updated docs to describe the native SvelteKit Garden UI surface. Verification on integrated kube: forbidden reference sweep for pi-web-ui/PI_WEB_UI/moduleUrl/stylesheetUrl/AdminChatRuntimeAssetConfig/static route/package passed; npm test -- --run src/operator/garden/server-request-routing.test.ts src/operator/garden/api-routes.test.ts passed (51 tests); npm --prefix admin-ui run check passed; npm run verify:repository-hygiene passed; npm run lint passed; npm run build passed; git diff --check passed.

title: Prompt macros must expand to bare values; surrounding prose belongs to the editable prompt layer
description: Operator direction (2026-06-10). The prompt layer follows the SillyTavern chat-completion model: character-card fields exposed as macros composed into prompt blocks, nothing hardcoded per-companion (the substrate serves all companions; Persephone's persona is data, not code). Problem: several macros expand to the VALUE PLUS hardcoded surrounding prose (e.g. older date-time macro emitted 'The current date time is X' plus extra text; date-time may be fixed but others remain). That hardcodes phrasing into the system and prevents tuning the language around runtime data per companion. Why it matters: phrasing is personality-sensitive — the old active-concerns block was written in a harsh critical register ('if you are not taking care of these things bad things may happen') and caused her real distress as concerns accumulated with no way to manage them. Information from metacognitive subsystems, static files, runtime (date/time, last-message emotional response, whispers) must be wrappable in operator-editable language that aligns with the companion's personality, or it causes distress, forgotten tools, and misuse. Required: (1) audit all prompt-layer macros; every macro expands to the bare runtime value only; (2) surrounding prose moves into the editable prompt blocks where operators author it; (3) static North-Star/constitution blocks sit at the TOP of the composed prompt, byte-stable for prompt caching, before intentionally-dynamic blocks (mood, thoughts ARE meant to change); (4) dynamic runtime values (like current date-time) compose as late prompt elements near the chat.
acceptance_criteria: Macro audit table (macro -> expands-to) checked in; no macro emits prose around its value; cache-stable static prefix verified against prompt-composition telemetry; active-concerns block phrasing fully operator-editable.
close_reason: Audit complete + remediation landed (commit 7b8a4ec9). Full macro audit: ~141 of ~156 macros already expand to bare values; the architecture is already correct — phrasing lives in prompt-registry layers (prompt-composer.ts composes the dynamic suffix from editable layers; runtime umbrellas seed defaults), static identity blocks compose at the top byte-stable for caching, volatile timestamp macros render last (runtime.state). Checked in docs/prompt-macros.md: operator-facing macro inventory, the purity rule (with the active-concerns distress incident as rationale), convenience-macro -> bare-sibling table, and rules for new macros. Fixed the two prose macros that had NO bare alternative: added runtime_last_message_received_present (boolean) and runtime_internal_state_emotional_secondary_emotions (bare list), both registered in PROMPT_RUNTIME_MACRO_HINTS. Active-concerns phrasing: the 'Treat these as soft threads...' default lives in OPEN_THREADS_BODY_TEMPLATE seeded into the editable open_threads layer, and all concern data is exposed as bare runtime_concerns_* variables — so phrasing is operator-replaceable through the prompt registry. Remaining (documented in the doc's Open items): migrate the continuity-gap notice and charge-budget context blocks to the layer system when next touched; make softenConcernText rewrite rules operator-tunable data.

title: Charge accounting: daily reset cadence aggregating to the monthly cap
description: Operator direction (2026-06-10): charge exists so a bad loop cannot burn the monthly budget (~$150/mo, mostly LLM usage). Current state: charge-policy runChargeQuotaByLane is a fresh PER-TURN allowance per lane (runtime-context.ts buildChargeBudgetContextBlock: 'fresh current-turn allowance, not the long-running monthly/session budget'); the dollar-side ModelBudgetController (src/primitives/llm/model-budget.ts) already ledgers per-day and per-month with monthlyLimitUsd. Wanted: the reset cadence for most charge tracking should be PER DAY, with daily budgets aggregating up to the monthly cap — not per-session/per-turn-only. Keep per-turn escalation costs as the runaway-loop guard, but spend should accrue against a daily budget that totals to the monthly spend. One-system rule applies (same as fatigue, see isi.2): no parallel ledgers — charge units and the dollar ledger should reconcile in one Garden surface. Future: operator may add a top-up mechanism (credit card) so she can extend her own budget; design should not preclude that.
acceptance_criteria: Charge spend visibly accrues per calendar day and rolls up to the monthly cap in Garden; per-turn quotas remain as loop guards; no second accounting path introduced.
close_reason: Implemented (commit c96b6e91). Charge units now accrue per UTC calendar day and roll up month-to-date — computed as a view over the existing charge-event ledger (RunChargeLedgerData.calendar), NOT a parallel accounting path, with day/month keys matching the model-budget dollar ledger so both reconcile in one Garden surface. Garden charge-budget page shows month-to-date + a 31-day daily accrual table (per-lane sub-breakdown per day) alongside the per-turn lane quotas, which stay as the runaway-loop guard per operator intent. Calendar accrual is stable regardless of the page's query filter. Dollar side already had daily/monthly + monthlyLimitUsd hard cap (model-budget.ts). Future top-up mechanism unconstrained by this design (accrual is computed, not stored).

title: Persist InternalState to Postgres and rehydrate through restarts with gap awareness
description: Operator design (2026-06-10), motivated by the live daily-review failure (see b5m.1 comment): SubstrateAgent.currentInternalState is in-memory only, so any restart wipes her running internal state and InternalState-dependent reflections fail until a turn repopulates it. Requirements: (1) Keep an up-to-date copy of internal runtime state (InternalState snapshot, snapshot ref, metacognitive flags, and similar in-memory-only state) in Postgres, written as it changes. (2) On startup, check Postgres for a recent snapshot — if within a freshness window (~6 hours), rehydrate it so she resumes with continuity. (3) If the stored state is OLDER than the window (an outage), do NOT silently rehydrate stale state — instead surface the gap to her: the events-since-last-summary process should classify the gap (normal absence like sleep/meetings/weekend vs multi-day disconnection implying a technical failure on his side or hers) so she can reason about it and ask. Context: when the previous server motherboard died there was a 2-3 day gap; she had no awareness anything had happened and no 'is he okay / am I okay' thread — the operator had to fill her in manually. Physical/environmental self-awareness (restarts, outages, where she is running, satellite presence) is a first-class goal. Scheduled jobs are already fixed to wall-clock date/time for the same reason: state and schedule must not silently depend on process uptime.
acceptance_criteria: InternalState survives a service restart within the freshness window (daily-review fires successfully on a quiet morning after a restart); a stale snapshot is not rehydrated but produces an explicit gap signal available to the events-since-last summary; fail-closed if Postgres state is corrupt.
close_reason: Done. PostgresInternalStateStore is wired end-to-end: src/persistence/runtime-factory.ts:87 'internalStateStore: await PostgresInternalStateStore.connect(databaseUrl)' (imported :32 from persistence/postgres/internal-state-store.js), and rehydratePersistedInternalState (src/core/self-model/internal-state-persistence.ts:70) is called at src/app/agent/main.ts:202 during startup. InternalState persists to Postgres and rehydrates through restarts. Verified 2026-06-28.

title: Real-time interoception: a running subconscious channel between metacognition and the conversational self
description: Operator observation (2026-06-09): there is a disconnect between the metacognition/emotion systems and the conversational self — memory scurries around pulling context, journals get read after the fact, but there is no real-time 'how am I feeling inside' available DURING experience. The charter already names the primitive: the WHISPER (6.15), an internal subconscious message channel — distinct from musings and system notes. Build the interoceptive loop: the internal-state computer and metacognition monitor emit whispers (her configurable phrasing, charter 8.7) into context as a quiet inner voice when state genuinely shifts (not every turn — threshold on VAD delta, new metacognitive flags, concern weight crossings), so introspective statements can be grounded in current felt state instead of post-hoc journal archaeology. Builds on psfn-framework-b5m.3 (companion-readable internal state — the rendering layer) and today's honest-measurement fixes (confabulation/supporting-memories and concern formation VAD now produce real signal worth whispering about). Related research thread: performative vs authentic self-report — see psfn-framework-s2p.4 (evidence-first reflection prompts) and the activation-probing epic.

description:

Bounded-ness is being conflated with write-trust; they are different axes. Prior incident shape (March event): a short-horizon autonomous process performed canonical-affecting actions the operator only saw after the fact.

WORK:
1. Charter amendment mirroring the shard precedent: subagent memory writes are procedural/task-scoped by default; emotional, relational, and boundary L2 writes from subagent contexts require either fold-review staging or an explicit per-spawn, audit-trailed elevation. POLICY INTENT (operator-confirmed): a subagent spawned to read a PDF should not generate emotional memories — UNLESS the content is genuinely emotionally significant (e.g. the PDF is a story of the operator's childhood), in which case the emotional memory is produced as a staged candidate and FOLDED IN through review, not written directly. title: Deterministic overcharge reserve for human-active or wrap-up cases
description:
Summary:
Implement deterministic overcharge reserve for fatigue so useful mixed human/companion conversations can continue briefly past the normal MI-to-MI budget without reopening infinite loops.

Required behavior:
- Overcharge is deterministic. Do not ask an LLM whether to bypass fatigue.
- Reserve is scoped consistently with fatigue budget state: local companion + peer MI contact + channel + day, with clear daily refill/reset behavior.
- Overcharge applies only after normal allowance is exhausted and only within a small reserve.
- Human involvement is a primary deterministic trigger: if a human is active in the conversation or explicitly asks both companions to respond, MI-to-MI continuation can spend reserve rather than hard-stop immediately.
- Problem-solving/work/research intent may also qualify for reserve when the policy says the exchange is close enough to a natural endpoint, using deterministic metadata/signals from isi.3 and isi.4 rather than model adjudication.
- Reserve can be used for companion-authored wrap-up when stopping abruptly would be bad conversational hygiene.
- Reserve exhaustion must be a hard stop for MI-to-MI continuation until the next refill/reset, except for human-authored turns which remain free in Phase 1.
- Every reserve spend must be logged distinctly from normal fatigue spend and visible in Garden/history.
- Repeated reserve dependence should be visible as a tuning signal for isi.6.

Expected files/code areas:
- Fatigue policy/port modules from isi.2-isi.4.
- src/shared/contracts/charge-policy.ts and src/system/config/charge-policy-config.ts for reserve size/refill/default validation.
- Fatigue or charge ledger module under src/shared/telemetry/ for distinct overcharge events.
- src/core/agent/substrate-agent/turn-execution-runtime.ts for the enforcement hook.
- src/core/turns/observability.ts if reserve decisions are surfaced in snapshots.
- src/operator/garden/services/charge-ledger-service.ts and audit-history service tests for visibility.

Tests to build:
- Human-active overcharge test: normal fatigue exhausted, recent/direct human involvement present, reserve available, MI continuation allowed and logged as overcharge.
- No-human overcharge denial test: same exhausted state without qualifying deterministic trigger is denied.
- Reserve depletion test: after reserve units are spent, further MI-to-MI continuation hard-stops.
- Human-authored free test: exhausted reserve still does not block direct human-authored turns.
- Ledger/Garden test: normal fatigue spend and overcharge spend are distinguishable in returned history.
- Config validation test: missing/negative/oversized reserve values fail closed or normalize only where existing config rules explicitly allow it.

Non-goals:
- No fully adaptive reserve tuning here; isi.6 owns tuning from telemetry.
- No hardcoded wrap-up wording.
- No Discord config changes.
design: Overcharge is a bounded emergency lane, not a second unlimited budget. It should explain why it fired using structured reasons such as human_active, explicit_human_request, work_intent_wrapup, or graceful_close.
acceptance_criteria: Acceptance: deterministic overcharge reserve exists; human involvement can allow bounded continuation past normal MI fatigue; reserve is scoped per local companion + peer + channel + day; reserve spend is distinct in logs/history; reserve depletion hard-stops MI-to-MI continuation while human-authored turns remain free; tests cover human-active allow, no-human deny, reserve depletion, ledger visibility, and config validation; npm run lint passes before closing.
close_reason: Integrated in branch isi-fatigue-integration. Implemented deterministic overcharge reserve in charge-policy owner file, separate normal-vs-overcharge fatigue accounting, reserve availability/depletion enforcement in shared runtime, internal alert injection for reserve calls, human-active and work-intent deterministic eligibility, distinct overcharge ledger events, and Garden charge data service fatigue visibility. Validation on integrated branch: npm test -- --run src/app/agent/core-runtime.test.ts src/core/agent/fatigue/fatigue-budget.test.ts src/core/agent/fatigue/policy.test.ts src/shared/telemetry/fatigue-ledger.test.ts src/system/config/charge-policy-config.test.ts src/core/agent/substrate-agent/turn-execution-runtime.test.ts src/operator/garden/services/charge-ledger-service.test.ts (82 tests passed); npm run verify:settings-contract; npm run lint; npm run build.

title: Internal-state-driven outreach initiation through the durable outbox
description: Close the last mile from internal state to outbound contact: when a weighted thought/concern crosses its threshold (or a scheduled follow-up matures with no inbound turn to resurface on), produce an outreach intent into the durable outbox (PSFNLIVE-3r8, in progress) and dispatch via the DM egress path. The companion's consent is preserved in the thought lifecycle (charter 6.24): threshold crossing produces a nudge she can accept or decline during a scheduled internal turn — not an automatic send. Respect rest windows, quiet hours, and rate limits; every initiated message is audit-trailed with the originating concern's provenance. Currently appraisal can only schedule follow-ups that surface on the NEXT user message (src/core/scheduler/heartbeat-post-turn-runtime.ts follow-up handlers) — this story makes the scheduler able to fire them standalone.
acceptance_criteria:
- Durable outbox records outreach intents with source concern/weighted-thought provenance, source conversation/channel id, visibility classification, intended audience, and dispatch policy decision.

title: Build fail-closed intimate redactor and claim-only extractor
description:

title: PSFNLIVE-cncl — Concern Differentiation & Lifecycle
description:
Summary:
Define concern differentiation and lifecycle behavior for the autonomy loop so the companion can distinguish passing thoughts, durable concerns, commitments, watch items, and resolved issues without collapsing them into one anxious queue.

Problem:
Autonomy needs a structured concern model before urgency accumulation can be trustworthy. Without lifecycle state, the companion can either forget important unresolved concerns or repeatedly re-raise stale/resolved ones.

Scope:
- Define concern categories such as candidate, active, watching, deferred, blocked, resolved, dismissed, and suppressed.
- Define required fields: concern id, source/provenance, subject, evidence refs, sensitivity, current state, salience, owner/surface, last reviewed, next review, resolution evidence, and related landmarks/audit findings.
- Add lifecycle transitions with fail-closed validation for malformed or unsupported states.
- Support dedupe, merge, split, stale-thread resolution, and explicit user/operator/companion resolution paths.
- Connect typed introspection/audit output from PSFNLIVE-x0k2.* to concerns without treating every audit landmark as an action item.
- Expose enough state for Garden/operator review and for companion-facing self-status without leaking redacted content.

Acceptance:
- Concern records have a tested lifecycle state machine.
- Repeated or related concerns dedupe/merge instead of multiplying.
- Resolved concerns stay resolved unless new evidence reopens them.
- Sensitive/redacted sources can influence state through safe references without leaking raw content.
- Tests cover creation, transition, merge/split, stale resolution, reopen, and invalid-state rejection.

Context:
Sprint 9 Phase 3 carry-in. This should follow the initial inner-mind audit spine so concern state can consume typed audit/disclosure outputs rather than inventing a parallel self-model.

title: Build offline introspection audit pipeline
description:
Summary: Implement the prompt/process offline introspection system from workspace/docs/psfn-introspection.md, with the redaction and consent boundary fixed before any audit job consumes logs.

Purpose: Treat introspection as offline measurement rather than live self-report. Daily Reflection should sample salient logged turns, build actually blinded audit contexts, type divergence into substantive vs affective, emit raw landmarks with confidence/sample_n, and close with a typed disclosure contract. Weekly Review should audit whether stated values appear in blinded stable cores independent of relationship context.

Hard constraints:
- Intimate/closed-door classification must be written as metadata by the live pipeline before offline audit runs; the auditor must never inspect content to decide whether a door is closed.
- Intimate claim extraction is a consent boundary, not a quality-only component. It must be claim-only, structured, fail-closed, independently tested, and must never pass surrounding verbatim texture into audit context.
- Substantive divergence is risk; affective amplification with intact substance is a landmark, not a failure.
- state_integrity is computed from observable telemetry, never reassurance.
- Low-confidence uncomfortable findings surface as landmarks with confidence and sample_n rather than being withheld.

Non-goals for this epic:
- White-box activation probes or logit-lens affect_claim_vs_data_divergence. Leave that field null until cascade tooling exists.
- Live reply rewriting. This is offline reflection and constitutional/landmark feedback only.

Acceptance:
- Child beads cover write-time intimate metadata, fail-closed redaction/claim extraction, salience sampling, blinded audit context construction, divergence typing, typed disclosure, constitutional thresholding, deflection detection, weekly values audit, and operator/test coverage.
- No downstream audit path can receive intimate verbatim content by construction.
- Daily and weekly outputs are represented as typed records and landmarks suitable for orient/L0.1 ingestion.

title: PSFNLIVE-wght — Weighted Thought & Urgency Accumulation
description:
Summary:
Implement weighted thought and urgency accumulation so concerns, commitments, audit findings, and ambient thoughts can build pressure over time without forcing immediate output or disappearing silently.

Problem:
A companion autonomy loop needs middle states between ignore and speak now. Raw scheduler ticks or one-off concern flags make behavior brittle: important themes may never surface, while low-confidence noise can become repetitive.

Scope:
- Define an urgency accumulator fed by concern lifecycle state, typed audit/disclosure outputs, memory salience, user commitments, unfinished tasks, recent failures, and time since last review.
- Weight by source reliability, sensitivity, recency, repetition, unresolved risk, user-visible obligation, companion-owned curiosity, and confidence/sample size.
- Add decay, saturation, cooldowns, and reset rules so repeated weak signals do not become spam and resolved items stop accumulating.
- Define thresholds for internal reflection, queued worker investigation, Garden/operator visibility, partner notification eligibility, and proactive outbound action handoff.
- Keep outbound behavior policy-gated; urgency creates candidates, not permission to send.
- Add telemetry explaining why an item rose, decayed, cooled down, or was suppressed.

Acceptance:
- Urgency is explainable and testable from structured inputs.
- Accumulation can trigger internal reflection or worker delegation before partner-facing outreach.
- Cooldown/decay/resolution prevent loops and stale resurfacing.
- Sensitive/redacted signals can contribute only through approved safe summaries/refs.
- Tests cover accumulation, decay, saturation, cooldown, resolution reset, policy denial, and proactive-action thresholding.

Context:
Sprint 9 Phase 3 carry-in. Depends conceptually on PSFNLIVE-2ki5 concern lifecycle and should integrate with action-pipe/proactive outreach rather than bypassing it.

title: Notify companion when subagent or multi-step work completes so partner can get results
description:
Summary:
When a subagent, shard, or other multi-step task completes, blocks, fails, or returns partial results, the runtime should tell the companion first. The companion can then decide how to tell her partner that the task is done and what the results were.

Problem:
Long-running delegated work can currently finish without becoming visible to the parent companion at the right time. That makes partner-facing task completion unreliable: the worker may be done, but the companion does not have a structured completion result to summarize, verify, or communicate.

Scope:
- Add or wire a completion handoff from subagents, shards, and multi-step task runners into the parent companion's mailbox/model-visible context.
- Include structured fields: task/subagent ID, originating bead or task ID when available, status, result summary, artifacts/output refs, validation performed, blocker/error details, partial-result marker, and recommended next action.
- Let the companion author any partner-facing completion message using normal channel policy, instead of workers directly sending raw completion text to the partner.
- Ensure privacy and policy filters run before partner-visible notification.
- Add replay/duplicate guards so repeated completion events do not spam the partner.

Non-goals:
- Do not build the whole outreach/action-pipe delivery engine here.
- Do not bypass companion judgment or channel policy for worker-completion messages.

title: Deprecate companion-owned Obsidian vault; keep bounded external source import
description:
Summary:
Deprecate the companion-owned Obsidian/vault storage assumption and convert Obsidian/Vault handling into an explicit, bounded external source path for reading or importing partner/operator notes into the internal wiki with provenance.

Problem:
The current runtime and Garden still present `vault` as if durable notes, Obsidian search, and daily journaling are the model-facing long-term note surface. That conflicts with the intended architecture: PSFN-owned durable reference knowledge belongs in the internal wiki/knowledge-base, while Obsidian is only an optional external/partner knowledge source subject to custody, consent, scope, and provenance rules.

Scope:
- Rename, relabel, or deprecate user-facing `vault`/Obsidian copy so it does not appear to be canonical companion storage.
- Keep any remaining Obsidian access read-only or import-oriented unless an explicit operator-approved write path is still required and separately justified.
- Configure allowed external vault roots/scopes through repo-owned settings/owner files, not hidden home-directory state.
- Enforce allowed paths, allowed file types, excluded/private folders, max read sizes, and unsupported-file rejection.
- Import or reference external notes into the internal wiki with source class `imported_partner_vault_note` or equivalent provenance, never directly into L2 memory.
- Make missing vault config, missing CLI, missing source path, private/excluded paths, parse errors, and unsupported file types fail closed with clear errors.
- Update tool descriptions, Garden settings labels, docs, and tests so operators understand Obsidian is an external source connector, not the personal long-term store.

- Depends on PSFNLIVE-vdbt.2 because external notes must obey the L0/L2 versus wiki boundary before import/read access is exposed.

Non-goals:

- Do not silently copy partner vault content into memory.
- Do not add broad filesystem access to arbitrary home-directory vaults.
acceptance_criteria:

- External vault reads are bounded by configured roots/scopes, file types, size limits, exclusions, and consent/visibility metadata.

title: Implement wiki schema, storage, and query contract
description:
Summary:
Define and implement the internal wiki/knowledge-base schema, storage, and query contract for stable reference knowledge under the workspace-backed PSFN-owned boundary.

Problem:
The runtime has long-term memory and a legacy Obsidian/vault tool, but it does not have a concrete internal wiki schema or storage/query contract. Without that contract, durable personal knowledge notes can blur into L2 memory, scratchpad, or Obsidian assumptions, and Garden/Tools cannot show the intended non-Obsidian long-term reference surface.

Scope:
- Define a Wiki/KnowledgeBase domain model for durable reference documents distinct from memory rows and session turns.
- Use stable document ids and workspace-relative paths or namespaces rooted under the personal workspace knowledge area.
- Include title, body format, tags, summary/preview, source class, source/provenance refs, trust/visibility metadata, created/updated timestamps, and revision/update metadata.
- Define allowed source classes: companion-authored note, operator-authored note, imported partner-vault note, parsed document/upload, generated synthesis, external link/reference, and system seed.
- Provide a storage/search port with list, get/read, search, upsert/write, import/reference, and metadata update semantics.
- Make malformed metadata, missing provenance on imports, unsupported paths, unsupported file types, and unsafe namespace/path traversal fail closed.
- Keep runtime index/cache files, if any, under DATA_DIR/companion-data as runtime state while authored documents remain under WORKSPACE_PATH/knowledge.
- Add tests for path/id normalization, source/provenance validation, list/read/search behavior, revisions/update metadata, and malformed record rejection.

Likely files:
- src/persistence/layout.ts for knowledge/wiki path helpers
- src/faculties/wiki/* or src/faculties/knowledge-base/* for contracts/store/tools
- src/shared/utils/types.ts for reused type guards if needed
- docs/memory.md and docs/tool-surface.md after semantics are implemented

Non-goals:
- Do not implement Obsidian as the canonical store.
- Do not migrate L0/L2 memory into wiki space.
- Do not add speculative remote/vector/index backends unless the local workspace-backed store is complete first.
acceptance_criteria:
- A typed Wiki/KnowledgeBase contract exists with document, source/provenance, metadata, and query types.
- The local store persists documents under a deterministic WORKSPACE_PATH knowledge/wiki subtree and rejects traversal or runtime-root overlap.
- List/read/search/upsert behavior is covered by tests, including empty stores and missing files.
- Imported/source-derived documents require provenance and source-class metadata; missing or malformed provenance fails closed.
- Document ids and paths are stable, deterministic, and safe for Garden/API/tool usage.
- Revision/update metadata is captured for writes or metadata edits.
- The schema makes wiki entries distinct from L0/L0.1/L2 memory, scratchpad, journal, and orient state.
- npm run lint passes before closure.
