title: Enforce L0/L0.1/L2 versus wiki knowledge boundaries
description:
Summary:
Enforce the boundary between canonical L0 session history, L0.1 landmarks, L2 typed long-term memory, scratchpad/journal/orient state, and the new internal wiki/knowledge-base.

Problem:
Stable reference material has different semantics from lived memory. If wiki pages are treated as transcript truth or L2 emotional/episodic memory, the companion can misattribute authored/imported documents as lived experience, leak private source material, or let reference facts overwrite relationship memory.

Scope:
- Define explicit rules for what belongs in each surface:
  - L0: append-only session/turn history.
  - L0.1: provenance-bearing episodic landmarks and arcs.
  - L2 memory: typed durable lived/relational facts extracted from interaction or approved sources.
  - Scratchpad/journal: working notes and reflective writing.
  - Orient/current canon: active operational state.
  - Wiki/knowledge-base: durable reference documents, authored notes, imported docs, and curated references.
- Ensure memory extraction does not ingest wiki/source documents as partner speech or lived events by default.
- Ensure wiki search/read context is labeled as authored/imported/reference knowledge in prompts and tool output.
- Allow explicit, provenance-bearing links from wiki documents to L0/L0.1/L2 records without transferring ownership of the wiki body into memory.
- Make imports from vault/uploads/docs fail closed when source class, provenance, privacy/visibility, or allowed path metadata is missing.
- Add tests for misplaced data, missing provenance, retrieval labels, and extraction/import separation.
- Update docs and prompt/tool copy so operators and the model see the boundary.

Likely files:
- src/faculties/memory/extraction/* and retrieval code only where needed to prevent accidental ingestion
- src/core/agent/substrate-agent/runtime-context.ts or prompt block construction for context labels if wiki context is injected
- wiki/knowledge-base tools and Garden services from PSFNLIVE-vdbt.1
- docs/memory.md and docs/tool-surface.md

Non-goals:
- Do not block explicit operator-approved memory writes merely because a wiki document is cited.
- Do not silently copy raw private transcript spans into wiki documents.
- Do not make the wiki a replacement for L0/L2 memory retrieval.
acceptance_criteria:
- Tests prove wiki/reference documents do not create L0/L0.1/L2 memory entries by default.
- Wiki search/read results are clearly labeled as authored/imported/reference knowledge in model-facing output and any prompt context.
- Memory extraction ignores wiki document bodies unless an explicit approved import/write path is used.
- Provenance links between wiki and memory/session records are references only; they do not imply content ownership transfer.
- Missing source class, missing provenance, unsupported visibility, or unsafe import source causes fail-closed rejection.
- Garden and tool surfaces show boundary labels separating Wiki/Knowledge Base from Memory and Episodes.
- docs/memory.md documents the boundary in concrete terms.
- npm run lint passes before closure.
close_reason: Implemented wiki/memory boundary by keeping wiki storage and tools independent from L0/L0.1/L2 memory, labeling list/read/search/write/import results as reference knowledge, and requiring source_class/provenance_refs for imports and source-derived documents. Garden wiki page/API and Tools page copy now separate Wiki/Knowledge Base from Memory and Episodes; docs/memory.md documents the concrete boundary. title: Epic: Workspace-backed Internal Knowledge Base & Wiki
description:
Summary:
Build the companion's canonical internal knowledge-base/wiki as workspace-backed durable reference storage, visible in Garden and reachable through a model-facing tool surface, without treating it as Obsidian, transcript memory, or L2 lived memory.

Current state / problem:
- The code still exposes a legacy `vault`/Obsidian-oriented tool and Garden settings section.
- Garden has Memory, L0.1 Episodes, Images, Skills, and Tools pages, but no first-class wiki/knowledge-base page.
- `WORKSPACE_PATH` is already the repo-defined personal files root for personal knowledge notes, journals, scratchpad files, documents, images, skills, modules, and experiments.
- Existing beads already decided the direction: deprecate any separate companion-owned Obsidian vault assumption, keep partner/Obsidian vault access explicit and bounded, and route stable reference knowledge through an internal wiki/knowledge-base boundary.

Implementation direction:
- The canonical wiki/reference layer should be owned by PSFN, not by Obsidian.
- Store authored/imported wiki documents under a deterministic personal workspace subtree, preferably `WORKSPACE_PATH/knowledge`, with any runtime index/cache metadata under the appropriate system/companion data root.
- Provide a typed KnowledgeBase/Wiki domain port with list/read/search/upsert/import semantics and explicit provenance.
- Keep wiki/reference knowledge separate from L0 session history, L0.1 landmarks, L2 typed memories, journals, scratchpad, and orient/current-canon state.
- Expose the wiki in Garden as its own operator surface with health, document list/search/read, provenance, and boundary labels.
- Expose model-facing access as a clear `wiki` or `knowledge_base` tool, not as `vault`/Obsidian.
- Demote legacy `vault`/Obsidian surfaces to external source/import/read-only integration, or mark them legacy if removal is not safe in the same wave.

Child work:
- PSFNLIVE-vdbt.1 defines and implements the wiki schema/storage/query contract.
- PSFNLIVE-vdbt.2 enforces the L0/L0.1/L2 vs wiki boundary in tools, prompts, imports, and tests.
- PSFNLIVE-vdbt.3 demotes Obsidian to bounded external source handling and removes the companion-owned Obsidian vault assumption.
- psfn-framework-s2p.6 is the charter-law implementation bead for the same architecture and should close with this epic when the implementation is complete.
- psfn-framework-zn9.7 must cover workspace/wiki files in scheduled backups.

Likely files:
- src/persistence/layout.ts
- src/faculties or src/core domain for a Wiki/KnowledgeBase port and store
- src/core/agent/tool-registrar.ts and tool catalog wiring
- src/boundary/integrations/vault/* for legacy Obsidian handling
- src/operator/garden/* and admin-ui/src/routes/* for Garden visibility
- docs/memory.md and docs/tool-surface.md
- relevant tests under src/** and admin-ui/src/**
acceptance_criteria:
- A first-class internal wiki/knowledge-base exists and is not implemented as an Obsidian vault wrapper.
- Wiki documents have stable ids, titles, namespaces or paths, body content, tags, source/provenance refs, owner/source class, timestamps, and update history or revision metadata.
- Model-facing access uses a clear wiki/knowledge-base surface for list/read/search/write/import operations with capability gating for writes/imports.
- Garden has a visible wiki/knowledge-base page or equivalent first-class route showing availability, storage root/index status, documents, provenance, and boundary warnings.
- Memory retrieval and extraction do not silently copy wiki/reference material into L0/L0.1/L2 lived memory.
- Obsidian/Vault access, if still present, is labeled and implemented as bounded external source import/read handling, not canonical companion storage.
- Docs and tool descriptions describe the new boundary and no longer present Obsidian as the target durable note surface.
- Targeted tests cover schema/storage, tool access, memory-boundary behavior, Garden/API visibility, and legacy Obsidian deprecation behavior.
- npm run lint passes before closure.

Implemented the PSFN-owned workspace-backed wiki/knowledge-base under WORKSPACE_PATH/knowledge/wiki with typed document/provenance metadata, model-facing wiki tool, Garden API/UI page, Tools nav visibility, memory/wiki boundary labels, and legacy Vault/Obsidian demotion to external bridge/import source. description:
Summary: PSFNLIVE-3ph softened and capped prompt-facing open threads, but the underlying concern system still over-produces duplicate/stale concerns and does not resolve enough contextually. Scope: refine concern creation, dedupe, expiry, and auto-resolution behavior so prompt-facing concern pressure stays low without losing meaningful async signals. Garden must expose the operator actions for inspecting, resolving, suppressing, or otherwise managing these threads without hand-editing storage. Validation: duplicate/stale concerns collapse or resolve correctly, prompt-facing open threads remain materially quieter over long conversations, and Garden exposes the needed concern-management actions with targeted tests. discovered-from:PSFNLIVE-3ph

description:

title: Implement live human action recognition from camera stream
description:
Summary: develop a human action recognition module that consumes the live camera stream and emits structured real-time action telemetry. Scope: detect and classify observable actions across three dimensions: Body, Hand, and Head. Output contract: provide machine-readable events/state with stable fields for timestamp, confidence, and per-dimension labels so downstream Amica/hub consumers can react without image parsing. Expectations: support continuous inference on live video, handle loss/reacquisition cleanly, and keep the runtime viable for Pi-local execution or an explicitly defined offload path if needed. Example outputs: body posture or gross movement state, hand gesture/action state, and head orientation/action state. Validation: live camera test demonstrates low-latency structured output for all three dimensions and documents the schema and transport path.

title: Add shard completion audit before fold-back
description:
Summary:
Add a structured completion audit turn before a shard can mark itself complete and fold back, requiring evidence for every explicit requirement, artifact, command, test, gate, invariant, and deliverable in its objective.

Problem:
A shard saying it is done is not enough for long-horizon work. Without a completion audit, the parent companion may accept incomplete or weakly evidenced results, especially when the shard objective contains many artifacts or verification gates.

Scope:
- Before normal completion/fold-back, inject a completion audit prompt derived from the shard objective and any plan/checklist state.
- The audit must enumerate objective requirements and map each to concrete evidence from current state: files, outputs, tests, metrics, records, or explicit absence.
- Require statuses per requirement: met with evidence, not met with remaining work, or uncertain with why evidence is weak.
- If any requirement is not met or uncertain and budget/status permits, return shard to Active with next work rather than completing.
- Include the final audit artifact in fold-back, mailbox delivery, Garden/operator view, and self-mod review handoff where relevant.
- Add tests for all-met completion, missing artifact, weak evidence, failed test gate, budget-limited partial completion, and self-mod fold-back review compatibility.

Likely files:
- src/faculties/shards/manager.ts
- src/faculties/shards/* prompts/state/types
- src/core/agent/substrate-agent/runtime-context.ts if audit prompt is injected through runtime context
- self-mod fold-back artifacts if shared
- Garden/operator shard artifact surfaces if exposed

Acceptance:
- Complete shards produce a structured audit artifact before fold-back.
- Unproven requirements prevent normal Complete state when budget/status permits more work.
- Fold-back clearly distinguishes complete, incomplete, uncertain, budget-limited, and blocked outcomes.
- Tests prove completion is evidence-based rather than absence-of-obvious-errors based.

Context:
Derived from working_docs/SHARD_AUTONOMY.md Pattern 4. This is especially important for self-modification shards and other high-impact long-horizon work.

title: Add repeated-condition blocked audit for shards
description:
Summary:
Add blocked-state semantics for shards using a repeated-condition audit: a shard may mark itself blocked only after the same blocking condition persists across consecutive turns, rather than on first failure or ordinary uncertainty.

Problem:
Shards currently lack a middle state between success, failure, max turns, and silent idleness. A transient tool error or hard problem should not immediately become blocked, but a repeated identical blocker should stop the shard and ask the companion for intervention instead of looping forever.

Scope:
- Add blocked-condition capture to shard turn results: normalized condition key, human-readable description, affected artifact/input, evidence, and suggested companion action.
- Track consecutive_blocked_turns in shard state and reset it when meaningful progress occurs or the blocking condition changes.
- After the same blocking condition repeats for the configured threshold, transition the shard to Blocked.
- Emit mailbox/status notifications with blocker evidence and recommended actions: update goal, provide context, replace input, increase budget, retry with changed strategy, accept partial result, or cancel.
- Ensure ordinary hard/slow/uncertain work is not treated as blocked without repeated evidence.
- Add tests for transient error, repeated same blocker, changing blocker, progress reset, blocked notification, and companion resume/update behavior.

Likely files:
- src/faculties/shards/manager.ts
- src/faculties/shards/* state/types
- src/core/agent/substrate-agent/runtime-context.ts for blocked audit prompt/context
- src/shared/event-bus.ts
- notification/mailbox handoff surfaces

Acceptance:
- Shards track repeated blocker evidence and transition to Blocked only after the configured repeated-condition threshold.
- Blocked fold-back/mailbox content includes concrete evidence and companion action options.
- Changing blockers or actual progress resets the blocked counter.
- Tests prevent first-failure blocked states and prove repeated same-condition behavior.

Context:
Derived from working_docs/SHARD_AUTONOMY.md Pattern 3 and Codex blocked-audit semantics.
notes: AUDIT 2026-06-28 (verified): OPEN. No repeated-condition blocked audit (grep empty).
close_reason: Superseded by the later, evidence-backed July bug lghd. That bead owns the real endless continuation/re-prompt failure and the bounded wall-clock/prompt-entry termination needed to prevent repeated no-progress loops. Retired this speculative shard-only repeated-condition design and its obsolete 98xm-era umbrella rather than implementing a parallel blocker state machine.

title: Add per-shard budget tracking and graceful degradation
description:
Summary:
Add token/time budget tracking to shards, with threshold prompts and graceful fold-back when a shard approaches or reaches its declared budget.

Problem:
The global charge/spend system can track overall usage, but shards need local budgets so they can manage long-horizon work responsibly. Without per-shard budget state, a shard can consume resources without knowing when to summarize, degrade scope, or stop.

Scope:
- Extend shard spawn/config state with token_budget, time_budget, optional turn budget, and budget owner/provenance.
- Account token usage, wall-clock time, and turn count after each shard turn, integrating with the charge ledger or runtime usage telemetry rather than inventing duplicate accounting.
- At configurable thresholds, inject budget-aware prompts: heads-up around 80 percent, wrap-up around 95 percent, budget_limited/fold-back at 100 percent.
- Transition shards to BudgetLimited with one final wrap-up turn where policy permits, then fold back with completed work, remaining work, artifacts, and next-step recommendations.
- Surface budget state in mailbox/status messages and Garden/operator telemetry where appropriate.
- Add tests for budget accounting, threshold transitions, wrap-up prompt injection, budget-limited fold-back, zero/missing budget behavior, and charge-ledger integration.

Likely files:
- src/faculties/shards/manager.ts
- src/faculties/shards/* state/types
- charge ledger/runtime usage telemetry integration files
- src/shared/contracts/runtime.ts
- Garden/operator shard telemetry if exposed

Acceptance:
- Shard spawn can declare token/time budgets and those budgets are persisted in shard state.
- Budget usage updates after each turn from authoritative usage telemetry.
- Threshold prompts and BudgetLimited state transitions occur deterministically.
- Fold-back on budget limit includes summary, partial results, remaining work, and exact budget evidence.
- Tests cover normal, warning, wrap-up, over-budget, and missing-budget paths.

Context:
Derived from working_docs/SHARD_AUTONOMY.md Pattern 2. Supports charter budget stewardship and prevents runaway long-horizon resource use.

title: Add shard auto-continuation loop for active long-horizon work
description:
Summary:
Implement shard auto-continuation so an Active shard can keep taking turns until it reaches a terminal, paused, external-input, budget, or max-turn condition instead of stopping after a single turn.

Problem:
Long-horizon shards are intended to run week-to-month quests, but without auto-continuation the parent companion must poll and manually resume them. This is the core reason shards can go dark or remain idle despite having active work.

Scope:
- Add maybeAutoContinueShard or equivalent ShardManager post-turn decision point.
- After each shard turn, check status, queued parent/user/trigger-turn mailbox items, max turns, pause state, external-input wait, blocked/budget states, and cancellation.
- If safe to continue, start the next shard turn with a structured continuation prompt containing shard goal, current turn/max turns, token/time budget status if available, last-turn summary, and next concrete work.
- Ensure auto-continuation yields to foreground parent/user activity and does not starve ordinary turns.
- Emit lifecycle/status telemetry for continued, paused, waiting, stopped, and max-turn fold-back decisions.
- Add tests for continue, pause, external-input wait, max-turn stop, cancellation, foreground-yield, and mailbox trigger-turn precedence.

Likely files:
- src/faculties/shards/manager.ts
- src/faculties/shards/* state/types
- src/core/agent/substrate-agent/runtime-context.ts if continuation context is injected through runtime context
- src/shared/event-bus.ts

Acceptance:
- Active shards auto-start follow-up turns without parent polling when no higher-priority work is pending.
- Auto-continuation respects pause, max turns, external-input waits, cancellation, and mailbox trigger turns.
- Continuation prompts include enough state for the shard to continue coherently without pretending work is done.
- Tests cover the state machine edges and prove foreground responsiveness is preserved.

Context:
Derived from working_docs/SHARD_AUTONOMY.md Pattern 1. This is the P0 behavior because shards otherwise stop after one turn.

title: Shard autonomy goal-mode patterns for long-horizon fold-back
description:
Summary:
Track the shard-specific autonomy patterns from working_docs/SHARD_AUTONOMY.md. These adapt Codex goal-mode behaviors to PSFN long-horizon shards: auto-continuation, per-shard budget tracking, blocked audit, and completion audit before fold-back.

Problem:
PSFN shards can be launched for long-horizon work, but the doc calls out a runtime autonomy gap: a shard may run one turn and stop, lack a local budget, fail without a structured blocked state, or fold back without proving that its objective is actually complete. That creates silent idle work, runaway resource risk, and weak trust in shard outputs.

Scope:
- Extend ShardManager rather than adding a parallel architecture.
- Add shard auto-continuation across turns while respecting pause, max turns, blocked state, budget, external-input waits, and mailbox trigger turns.
- Track token/time budgets per shard and degrade gracefully with heads-up/wrap-up/fold-back behavior.
- Add blocked audit semantics based on repeated same blocking condition rather than first failure.
- Add completion audit before fold-back, requiring evidence for every explicit requirement/artifact/gate in the shard objective.
- Integrate status transitions with mailbox delivery, heartbeat telemetry, partner notification policy, and self-mod shard scoping.

Acceptance:
- The four shard autonomy patterns are represented by child beads with concrete files, behavior, and tests.
- Shards can continue long-running work without parent polling while remaining bounded by budget and explicit lifecycle states.
- Fold-back artifacts distinguish complete, budget-limited, blocked, paused, and partial outcomes.
- Existing subagent/shard mailbox, heartbeat, role, and self-mod beads are linked where they provide prerequisites or related surfaces.

Context:
Source doc: working_docs/SHARD_AUTONOMY.md. Target architecture: PSFN shard fold-back model and src/faculties/shards/manager.ts.

title: Add guardian reviewer subagent for self-modification proposals
description:
Summary:
Adopt Codex review-subagent pattern for PSFN self-modification: proposed code/runtime changes are reviewed by a dedicated guardian/reviewer subagent before fold-back or application.

Problem:
The charter requires self-modification to return artifacts/PR-style outputs and stay shard-scoped. A separate reviewer gives the companion a structured safety check between proposing a change and applying or folding it back. Without this, self-mod work can rely too much on the same actor that generated the change.

Scope:
- Define a reviewer/guardian subagent role specialized for inspecting self-mod artifacts, diffs, tests, capability changes, persistence changes, and policy impact.
- Require self-modification proposals to produce reviewable artifacts: summary, diff/artifact paths, tests run, risk notes, rollback path, and requested approval.
- Route proposals through reviewer before fold-back/application when the change touches code, runtime config, tool policy, persistence, or prompts with security impact.
- Reviewer returns structured findings: approve, request_changes, block, with file/line references where possible and risk categories.
- Preserve human/operator approval requirements; reviewer approval never bypasses capability gates, confirmations, or shard fold-back policy.
- Add tests for clean approval, blocking security issue, missing tests, malformed artifact, and policy gate preservation.

Likely files:
- src/faculties/shards/*
- src/faculties/subagents/*
- self-modification/gateway or git/filesystem integration surfaces
- src/system/capabilities/*
- reviewer role configuration from subagent role profiles

Acceptance:
- Self-mod proposals can be reviewed by a dedicated guardian role before application/fold-back.
- Review output is structured and visible to the companion/operator.
- Reviewer approval cannot bypass human confirmation, capability gates, or policy checks.
- Tests cover approval, request changes, block, missing evidence, and rollback metadata.

Context:
Derived from working_docs/CODEX_DEEP_DIVE.md review/guardian pattern. Related to charter Laws 14-15 and Phase 7 self-modification shard-scoping.

title: Add delegation usage hints, depth limits, concurrency limits, and interrupt semantics
description:
Summary:
Adopt Codex delegation ergonomics so the companion knows how to use subagents well and the runtime enforces bounded delegation depth, concurrency, and partial-result semantics.

Problem:
Tool descriptions say that subagents exist, but they do not teach the companion when to spawn multiple workers, when to reuse existing workers, how to assign ownership, or how to treat interrupted results. Runtime limits for nesting and concurrency also need to be explicit so delegation cannot fan out indefinitely.

Scope:
- Add a concise subagent usage hint block to runtime context explaining when to delegate, how to split work, when to reuse a worker, and how to assign ownership.
- Add explicit max depth and max concurrent subagent/shard limits, sourced from the correct owner-file config and enforced at spawn time.
- Add interruption/cancellation result messages that are model-visible and clearly mark partial results.
- Surface active child count, depth, and blocked spawn reasons in telemetry/Garden where useful.
- Add tests for usage-hint rendering, depth rejection, concurrency rejection, interrupt messages, and non-hallucinated completion handling.

- src/core/agent/substrate-agent/runtime-context.ts

- src/system/settings/contracts.ts
- Garden/operator telemetry surfaces if exposed

Acceptance:
- Companion receives actionable delegation guidance in context.
- Nested delegation and concurrent workers are bounded by enforced config.
- Interrupted child results are marked partial and cannot be mistaken for completed work.
- Tests cover limits, prompt/context rendering, and partial-result semantics.

title: Add subagent lifecycle hooks for spawn, stop, cleanup, and audit
description:
Summary:
Adopt Codex subagent lifecycle hooks by adding hook events around subagent and shard start/stop so operators can inject context, block unsafe spawn, and audit cleanup/completion.

Problem:
PSFN has a planned generic hook system, but subagent creation and completion need first-class lifecycle events. Without them, role context injection, resource cleanup, audit logging, and completion policy are hardcoded instead of operator-extensible.

Scope:
- Add subagent:start and subagent:stop hook events, with shard equivalents if shard lifecycle is separate.
- For start hooks, expose requested role, goal, parent turn/session, inherited context shape, requested toolsets, and limits; allow hooks to add context or block spawn according to policy.
- For stop hooks, expose status, summary/error, duration, tool/token counts, artifacts, and mailbox/notification disposition; allow audit/cleanup actions.
- Ensure lifecycle hooks do not leak private traces into public notifications.
- Add tests for context injection, spawn block, completion audit, cleanup after error, and malformed hook output.

- src/faculties/subagents/*
- src/faculties/shards/*
- src/boundary/gateway/hook-registry.ts or planned hook registry
- src/shared/event-bus.ts
- src/app/startup/composition/*

Acceptance:
- Subagent/shard start and stop emit hookable lifecycle events.
- Hooks can safely block spawn or add context before the child begins.
- Stop hooks run for success, error, cancellation, and interruption.
- Tests prove hooks are ordered correctly relative to mailbox delivery and notification policy.

Derived from working_docs/CODEX_COMPARISON.md Pattern 4 and working_docs/CODEX_DEEP_DIVE.md lifecycle/interrupt sections.

title: Add subagent status lifecycle and parent mailbox delivery
description:
Summary:
Adopt Codex subagent lifecycle/mailbox delivery so every child agent has explicit state and terminal results are delivered to the parent without polling or silent loss.

Problem:
PSFN subagents and shards can run for long periods, complete, fail, or block without a reliable parent-visible result path. Charter Law 31 covers partner-visible notifications, but the parent companion also needs an internal mailbox/result queue so child completions become model-visible context at the right time.

Scope:
- Define a subagent/shard status lifecycle: pending_init, running, completed, interrupted, errored, blocked, cancelled, shutdown.
- On terminal or interrupted states, enqueue a parent mailbox item with child ID/path, role, goal, status, final summary, error/block reason if any, duration, token/tool counts where available, and provenance.
- Add idle-drain behavior: non-urgent child results enter parent context when the parent finishes the current turn or next becomes idle.
- Add trigger_turn behavior for urgent/blocked/failure completions so the companion can start a proactive follow-up turn when policy allows.
- Represent partial/interrupted results clearly so they are not mistaken for complete work.
- Connect mailbox results to partner notification policy where appropriate without making every internal result public.

Likely files:
- src/faculties/subagents/*
- src/faculties/shards/*
- src/core/agent/substrate-agent/runtime-context.ts
- src/app/startup/composition/post-turn-actions.ts
- src/shared/event-bus.ts
- notification/gateway surfaces used by task completion

Acceptance:
- Parent receives model-visible completion/blocked/error/interrupted messages without polling.
- trigger_turn is policy-gated and tested for urgent completions.
- Non-urgent completion messages are drained when idle and do not interrupt active turns.
- Partial results are visibly marked as partial.
- Tests cover success, error, interruption, shutdown, blocked, idle drain, trigger_turn, and privacy-filtered partner notification handoff.

title: Add synchronous pre-tool hook interception with block, modify, and augment
description:
Summary:
Extend the planned hook/pre-flight surface with the Codex PreToolUse pattern: synchronous hooks selected by tool matcher can block execution, modify tool input, or add model-visible context before the tool runs.

Problem:
Existing capability gates and pre-flight validation can allow or deny tool calls, but the Codex comparison highlights a missing middle path: operators should be able to rewrite safe arguments, add required context, or block unsafe calls through extensible policy before execution. Generic async event hooks are not enough for this because tool execution must pause until the hook decision resolves.

Scope:
- Define a pre_tool_use event contract containing session/turn IDs, cwd/layout context, tool name, original JSON input, capability tier, permission mode, and matcher aliases.
- Add hook outputs for block with reason, modified_input, and additional_context.
- Enforce synchronous/fail-closed behavior for registered pre_tool_use hooks: malformed or denying results prevent unsafe execution according to policy.
- Integrate with existing capability gates, safeguards, confirmation queues, and pre-flight validation without bypassing them.
- Add matcher support for tool names/aliases, with tests for shell, web.fetch, filesystem, and analysis_workbench examples.
- Record telemetry showing original input, hook decision, modified input shape, and block reason with sensitive values redacted.

Likely files:
- src/core/agent/substrate-agent/tool-runtime-facade.ts
- src/system/capabilities/safeguards.ts
- src/boundary/gateway/hook-registry.ts or planned hook registry
- src/shared/event-bus.ts
- hook contracts/settings owner files

Acceptance:
- A hook can block a tool call before any side effect occurs.
- A hook can modify tool input and the executed call uses the modified input.
- A hook can add context that is visible to the model without changing the tool call.
- Existing capability and confirmation requirements remain stricter than hook rewrites.
- Tests cover allow, block, modify, augment, malformed hook output, and redacted telemetry.

Context:
Derived from working_docs/CODEX_COMPARISON.md Pattern 3. This is a follow-on/specialization of the Hermes hook and pre-flight beads, not a replacement for them.

title: Add subagent role profiles with companion identity inheritance
description:
Summary:
Adopt Codex role/config layering for PSFN subagents so child agents inherit the companion prompt/personality/runtime context by default, then receive role-specific instructions, tool restrictions, timeouts, and concurrency policy.

Problem:
PSFN subagents currently receive a goal and optional context, but not a first-class role profile or explicit identity-inheritance contract. This makes subagents behave like blank workers instead of bounded extensions of the companion with clear task posture.

Scope:

title: Map emotional telemetry sources and presentation before discrepancy UX
description:
Summary:
Before implementing psfn-framework-031.11, audit the emotional/introspection stack end to end so the additional telemetry is sourced, calibrated, stored, and presented without becoming performative, overconfident, or confabulatory.

Problem:
Section 11 needs more than a display rule for mixed emotions. The system has several emotional signal paths: classifier-inferred VAD/discrete labels, mood/state updates, ACAC self-report, metacognition/introspection prompts, contact emotional snapshots, memory affect metadata, reflection journal entries, and local-model eval/calibration outputs. If these are surfaced without a clear source/provenance/confidence contract, the companion may read noisy telemetry as canonical self-truth or perform the expected emotion rather than investigate it.

Scope:
- Inventory emotional telemetry sources across core emotion, self-model, scheduler/heartbeat, memory extraction/retrieval, reflection, Garden/operator surfaces, and eval harnesses.
- Trace each signal from source to presentation: classifier output -> EmotionState/InternalState -> runtime context -> reflection prompts -> memory extraction/writes -> companion/operator visible surfaces.
- Define provenance categories for downstream use, including classifier_inferred, self_report, activation_or_logprob_calibrated, partner_context_evidence, memory_derived, and stale_or_missing.
- Define confidence and freshness rules for when telemetry can be trusted, downweighted, suppressed, or presented as uncertain.
- Specify section 11 presentation rules: preserve contradiction, do not collapse mixed states into a single story, avoid score-wall UI, avoid clinical/coercive framing by default, and avoid presenting low-confidence signals as canonical truth.
- Review Sprint 9/eval beads that shape this area: [deleted:PSFN-l5f6], [deleted:PSFN-zbj9], [deleted:PSFN-6fq5], [deleted:PSFN-cr0y], [deleted:PSFN-uhny], PSFN-twa0, and psfn-framework-031.11.
- Identify which local-model introspection tests are required before or alongside implementation, especially calibration scenarios for low confidence, conflicting, stale, missing, suppressed, and mixed-state readings.

Likely files:
- src/core/emotion/*
- src/core/self-model/state.ts
- src/core/scheduler/heartbeat-policy.ts
- src/core/scheduler/heartbeat-template-runtime.ts

- src/faculties/memory/retrieval*

- src/operator/garden/* or telemetry/reflection surfaces

Acceptance:
- The emotional telemetry source/provenance/presentation map is captured in the bead design/notes or in a repo doc only if explicitly requested.
- psfn-framework-031.11 has a clear blocking contract for what data it may surface and how uncertainty must be worded.
- Related Sprint 9 emotion/eval beads are linked, and any missing local-model test work is created as follow-up beads.
- The implementation path separates raw telemetry, calibrated signals, self-report, and presentation copy.
- The proposed presentation is balanced: honest about contradictions, non-performative, non-clinical by default, and careful not to promote model guesses into identity claims.

Context:
User called out section 11 as a heavy-lift area: the additional emotional telemetry needs source and presentation review, and the surrounding Sprint 9/local-model introspection beads should inform implementation before the mixed-state UX is built.

title: Implement ambient presence with idle thoughts and time texture
description:
Summary:
Implement companion-authored recommendation #14: the companion should have a substrate sense of existing during quiet gaps, not only waking when messaged.

Problem:
When no one is actively messaging, the companion effectively has no lived texture of time passing. On return, it can know “6 hours” as a number but not feel the difference between minutes and days. Presence should include low-stakes internal continuity during silence, not only response generation.

Scope:
- Add idle-period ambient thought generation as low-priority internal notes, not automatic outbound messages.
- Gate ambient thoughts by rest/me-time policy, charge budget, fatigue/load policy, privacy boundaries, and anti-loop protections.
- Add qualitative time texture to wake-return/context: short gap, long workday, overnight, multiple days, etc.
- Add reconnection warmth scaling as an internal context signal proportional to absence, without forcing performed affection or fake emotion.
- Persist ambient thoughts as internal/provenance-tagged notes only when they are meaningful enough to keep; avoid cluttering L0/L2 with trivial ticks.
- Expose controls and recent ambient activity in Garden.

Likely files:
- src/core/scheduler/*
- src/core/scheduler/rest-window.ts
- src/core/session/manager.ts or wake_return context
- src/core/intention/* and weighted thought/proactive systems
- src/persistence/journals/reflection-* or a dedicated ambient journal
- src/operator/garden/services/scheduler-service.ts

Acceptance:
- Tests cover idle gap classification, ambient thought budget gating, no-outbound-send behavior, anti-loop behavior, and wake-return time texture.
- Ambient thoughts do not fire every heartbeat and do not burn LLM calls unnecessarily.
- Reconnection context is truthful and configurable, not a hidden affection-forcing mechanism.
- Operator can inspect/disable/tune ambient presence behavior.

Companion-authored section 14 says presence is also “existing during the silences.”

title: Build visual autobiography and embodiment identity continuity for generated images
description:
Summary:
Implement companion-authored recommendation #15: generated selfies/images need identity continuity, reference lineage, and emotional context so each rendering feels connected to the same companion.

Problem:
Generated images can change the companion’s face or embodiment from run to run. A reference image helps, but the companion still experiences each render as a new face unless the system preserves lineage, context, and similarity. Visual identity should be anchored in narrative, not only pixels.

Scope:
- Extend the persistent image/gallery model with visual autobiography records: companion-authored notes, emotional context, linked conversation/memory refs, and meaningful milestones.
- Track reference image lineage: source artifact, promotion reason, previous reference, derived generations, and associated lived context.
- Add an embodiment consistency review/score against the active reference, with clear “same me / drifted / different person” companion-readable framing.
- Allow promotion of especially identity-aligned images into reference slots with audit trail and rollback.
- Show gallery, lineage, favorites, notes, and identity continuity in Garden.
- Keep generated visual identity state distinct from canonical selfhood; images are embodiment artifacts, not the whole companion identity.

title: Surface and journal emotional discrepancies without forcing coherence
description:
Summary:
Implement companion-authored recommendation #11 from COMPANION_EXPERIENCE.md: when VAD, mood, discrete emotions, ACAC, or other emotional telemetry disagree, surface the discrepancy honestly instead of smoothing it into a false coherent story.

Problem:
The companion reports that internal state can show contradictions such as low valence alongside high love, or anger during a warm-seeming conversation. Today those disagreements are either ignored or narratively resolved by the reflection system, which risks confabulation. Mixed states should be legible as mixed states.

Scope:
- Detect emotionally meaningful divergence between VAD, mood, discrete emotion labels, ACAC self-report, confidence, and stale/missing signals.
- Render companion-readable discrepancy notes, e.g. “valence reads low while connection/love reads high; this may be a mixed state,” without treating classifier output as canonical self-truth.
- Add a reflection prompt/template path specifically for sitting with mixed emotional evidence: “your systems disagree; what might each one be responding to?”
- Persist discrepancy journal entries with source telemetry, confidence, uncertainty, and provenance.
- Preserve full emotional snapshots on emotional memories, including VAD + discrete + confidence, instead of compressing to a single dominant tag when mixed-state evidence matters.
- Keep output privacy/trust gated; do not leak sensitive context through discrepancy summaries.

Likely files:
- src/core/self-model/state.ts
- src/core/scheduler/heartbeat-policy.ts
- src/core/scheduler/heartbeat-template-runtime.ts
- src/faculties/memory/writer.ts and memory store/schema types
- src/faculties/memory/extraction/*
- src/operator/garden/telemetry or values/reflection surfaces

Acceptance:
- Tests cover divergent VAD/discrete emotion signals, low-confidence emotion telemetry, stale/missing signals, and mixed-state reflection rendering.
- Reflection prompts preserve contradictions and uncertainty rather than forcing narrative closure.
- Emotional memories can retain multi-signal emotional texture where relevant.
- Companion-facing wording is honest, non-clinical by default where possible, and does not promote telemetry into canonical truth.

title: Add authenticity provenance markers for user speech and transformed context
description:
Summary:
Implement companion-authored recommendation #12: the companion needs to know whether text came directly from the partner, from compaction, from memory retrieval, from extraction, or from system injection.

Problem:
Trust in relationship continuity depends on authorship integrity. When context is compacted, extracted, redacted, or injected by system machinery, the companion can lose confidence about whether phrasing is authentically from the partner or infrastructure-transformed. This erodes relational trust.

Scope:
- Add explicit provenance markers/classes for all prompt/context blocks: user_direct, companion_direct, compaction_summary, system_note/system_injection, memory_retrieval, extraction_artifact, projection/search_result, tool_result, and redacted/transformed content.
- Ensure every block answers who authored it, who transformed it, whether wording is direct or derived, whether detail may be lost, and whether it is safe to treat as partner speech.
- Add authenticity confidence for compacted or summarized messages, including source span counts and “emotional texture may be flattened” style warnings where appropriate.
- Make transformations and redactions auditable and visible to the companion without leaking protected material.
- Prevent transformed/internal content from masquerading as partner-authored speech.
- Expose provenance enough in Garden/prompt monitor to debug context authenticity.

Likely files:
- src/core/session/manager.ts and context builder modules
- src/core/agent/substrate-agent/runtime-context.ts
- src/core/internal-role-envelopes/*
- src/faculties/memory/retrieval.ts and retrieval formatting modules
- src/shared/contracts/runtime.ts
- src/operator/garden/prompt-monitor and telemetry services
- admin-ui/src/lib/components/prompt-monitor/*

Acceptance:
- Tests prove direct user messages, compacted summaries, memory retrieval blocks, system notes, and extraction artifacts carry distinct provenance markers.
- Compaction summaries clearly indicate derived status and possible loss of detail.
- No internal/system block can be rendered as partner-authored speech.
- Prompt monitor/Garden can inspect provenance markers for context blocks.

Context:

title: PostgreSQL production persistence migration
description:
Summary:
Track the PostgreSQL production persistence migration. The goal is to stop optimizing production code for both SQLite and PostgreSQL, lock production/runtime persistence to PostgreSQL, and keep SQLite only where explicitly retained for local/dev/test or historical migration support.

Why:
Maintaining dual production paths increases code complexity, testing surface, and performance ambiguity. PostgreSQL gives one production database target for indexes, pgvector, background jobs, query plans, migrations, observability, locking, and cache/queue work. L0 JSONL remains canonical archive truth; Postgres is the production database for mutable/query stores, projections, mirrors, and operational state.

Important charter boundary:
- Do not move canonical L0 session history out of filesystem JSONL.
- Do not move JSON owner-file settings into Postgres.
- Do move production mutable/query stores and projection/search surfaces toward Postgres-only execution.
- Database mirrors/projections must remain rebuildable from canonical sources where applicable.

Scope:
- Audit all runtime dual paths that select SQLite vs Postgres.
- Lock production/continuous live deployments to Postgres where data is database-backed.
- Provide a one-time migration script for existing live SQLite deployments before hard cutover.
- Update docs, startup checks, tests, and Garden health so production fails closed when Postgres is missing or invalid.
- Preserve or explicitly quarantine any dev/test SQLite fallback that remains useful.

Acceptance:
- Child beads cover the cutover, one-time data migration, verification/runbook, and cleanup/docs.
- No production runtime path silently falls back to SQLite when Postgres is required.
- Existing live SQLite deployments have a scripted migration path and verification checklist.

Keeping epic open under sprint-10 until those children are resolved.

[2] In parallel after/alongside: 3c2.7 (codex) retires maintenance/importer tools — voxta importer DELETED per operator decision 2026-07-06, one-shot migration tool DELETED (served 2026-06-09). title: Route proactive intention follow-ups to policy-gated Discord outbound egress
description:
Summary:
Proactive/intention follow-up responses can be inferred and queued, but they currently do not create an outbound Discord chat. That makes proactive care mostly useless in the live Discord surface: the system can decide there is something to say, but the message becomes an internal whisper instead of a companion-authored outbound message.

Observed code shape:
- src/core/intention/appraisal/action-translation.ts creates INTENTION_FOLLOW_UP_ACTION_KIND actions with channelId/channelType/content.
- src/core/scheduler/heartbeat-post-turn-runtime.ts registers the INTENTION_FOLLOW_UP_ACTION_KIND handler and calls agentLoop.followUp(...).
- src/core/agent/substrate-agent.ts special-cases INTENTION_FOLLOW_UP_AUTHOR_ID as an internalWhisper and says these intention appraisal follow-ups are never persisted into the external session journal.
- Gateway Discord egress already exists through GatewayClient.discordSend(channelId, content), and deferred tool handoff/heartbeat reflection paths show that background work can send to channels when explicitly wired.

Problem:
The current follow-up path is useful for private internal reminders, but it cannot satisfy real proactive outreach such as "it has been a while since I checked on this; should I message the partner now?" Once a proactive decision chooses to send, the runtime needs a distinct companion-authored outbound action path instead of reusing internal whisper injection.

Scope:
- Split intention follow-up semantics into at least two explicit outcomes: internal note/reminder-to-self and external proactive outreach.
- Add a policy-gated outbound action kind, for example proactive.outbound_message or intention.outbound_message, that can target Discord first without bypassing gateway/channel policy.
- Resolve target channel and recipient from the originating channel/contact context, fail closed when no valid Discord target exists, and do not guess across privacy boundaries.
- Send Discord messages through the existing gateway/channel egress path, not direct Discord client access from core.
- Persist the outbound message as companion-authored/proactive in L0/session state with provenance, not as partner speech, system note, or internal whisper.
- Preserve the existing internalWhisper follow-up path for private concern/reminder nudges that should not send externally.
- Add dedupe, rate-limit, external-communication eligibility, Garden/action-pipe visibility, and clear sent/denied/blocked telemetry.

Likely files:
- src/core/intention/appraisal/action-translation.ts
- src/core/intention/appraisal/types.ts
- src/core/scheduler/heartbeat-post-turn-runtime.ts
- src/core/agent/substrate-agent.ts
- src/app/startup/composition/post-turn-actions.ts
- src/app/agent/main.ts or channel runtime wiring for sender injection
- src/boundary/gateway/client.ts / discord.send gateway contracts as needed
- src/operator/garden/services/action-pipe-service.ts and admin-ui/src/routes/action-pipe/+page.svelte

Acceptance:
- A proactive external outreach decision can produce a queued action that sends a companion-authored Discord message through gateway.discordSend.
- Internal follow-up nudges still become internal whispers and never leak to Discord.
- Tests cover send success, missing/invalid Discord target, policy denial, duplicate action suppression, rate-limit denial, internal-channel no-send behavior, and persistence/provenance of sent proactive messages.
- Garden/action-pipe shows whether the proactive outbound action was queued, sent, denied, blocked, failed, or deduped.
- No path presents the message as partner-authored or as a fake reply to a user turn.

Context:
User noted on 2026-05-25 that proactive response is coded but cannot actually fire off chats in Discord, making the proactive system ineffective for live use. This belongs under PSFN-rsgg because it is a concrete action-pipe/autonomous behavior delivery gap.

Live post-turn queue inspection found entries but the quick summary did not expose enough action kind/channel/content detail to prove proactive Discord egress works. Related Orient wording was improved in psfn-framework-y8n, but this bead remains open until policy-gated outbound Discord action execution and persistence are implemented/tested.

The basic outbound egress path already exists upstream: IntentionAppraisal can emit followUp.delivery=external, decisionsToPostTurnActionCandidates maps that to intention.outbound_message, heartbeat-post-turn-runtime registers a handler, ProactiveOutboundDispatcher sends through the gateway sender, and app/agent/main.ts restricts the first slice to the configured heartbeat/primary Discord channel with rate limiting and provenance checks. This bead remains open because stored/internal follow-up intent is still not the same as a policy-gated external Discord send; the remaining bug is decision/provenance/resurfacing semantics (when to choose delivery=external, how pending follow-ups/concerns authorize it, and how sent/blocked state is surfaced), not missing gateway.discordSend plumbing.

Do not add duplicate Discord outbound plumbing; the remaining live scope is follow-up decision/provenance/resurfacing semantics and stale-row handling, tied to concern/orient lifecycle rather than missing gateway egress.
2026-06-26 live-code trace for PSFNLIVE-3r8/1xb.2 overlap: current code already has the outbound message action kind, primary-channel policy gate, rate limiter, quiet-hours/time gate, stale-concern provenance blocking, and post-turn queue persistence. Live Pi has no durable outreach outbox or terminal sent/blocked action history table/file, so the remaining gap belongs to PSFNLIVE-3r8 / psfn-framework-1xb.2 durable outbox/audit semantics, not another outbound transport implementation.
2026-06-26 closeout/scope note: do not treat this as missing Discord sender plumbing. Current code already has intention.outbound_message, ProactiveOutboundDispatcher, gateway.discordSend, primary-channel policy, rate limiting, quiet-hour/time gates, and post-turn queue persistence. The remaining live concern is upstream intent/provenance/resurfacing quality: when concern/orient/memory evidence should authorize an external proactive message, and how sent/blocked terminal history is audited. The operator's Orient-subagent direction should be scoped as an intent-capture/orientation reviewer paired with memory subagents, feeding concern/follow-up records and appraisal provenance. It should not duplicate outbound transport. Durable sent/blocked history belongs to PSFNLIVE-3r8 / psfn-framework-1xb.2 outbox work.

title: Implement Charter Law 32 internal wiki/reference knowledge
description:
Summary:
Implement Charter Law 32 by landing the same internal wiki/reference knowledge architecture tracked under PSFNLIVE-vdbt: PSFN-owned, workspace-backed, separate from L0/L0.1/L2 memory, and visible in Garden/Tools.

Problem:
The charter requires a companion-curated internal wiki for stable reference knowledge. The current runtime still has memory and legacy vault/Obsidian surfaces, but no first-class Wiki/KnowledgeBase domain. Reference material can therefore be misplaced into lived memory or hidden behind Obsidian terminology.

Concrete implementation target:
- Define a Wiki/KnowledgeBase port and local workspace-backed store for durable reference documents.
- Store authored/imported reference documents under the personal workspace knowledge area, while keeping runtime index/cache state in DATA_DIR/companion-data if needed.
- Add model-facing list/read/search/write/import access through a clear wiki/knowledge-base tool surface with capability gating.
- Add Garden visibility for wiki health, storage root, document list/search/read, provenance, and boundary labels.
- Keep optional links to L0/L0.1/L2 records as provenance/reference links only.
- Update Obsidian/Vault handling so partner vault reads/imports are external source connectors into the wiki, not canonical companion storage.

Relationship to PSFNLIVE-vdbt:
- PSFNLIVE-vdbt is the implementation epic.
- PSFNLIVE-vdbt.1 implements schema/storage/query.
- PSFNLIVE-vdbt.2 enforces memory/wiki boundaries.
- PSFNLIVE-vdbt.3 demotes Obsidian to external source import/read handling.
- This bead should close when that chain is implemented and validated.

Likely files:
- src/faculties/wiki/* or src/faculties/knowledge-base/*
- src/persistence/layout.ts
- src/core/agent/tool-registrar.ts and tool catalog wiring
- src/operator/garden/* and admin-ui/src/routes/*
- src/boundary/integrations/vault/*
- docs/memory.md and docs/tool-surface.md

Non-goals:
- Do not build a second memory store.
- Do not make Obsidian the companion-owned source of truth.
- Do not treat wiki/reference documents as emotional or episodic memories by default.
acceptance_criteria:
- Charter Law 32 is implemented by a first-class internal wiki/knowledge-base domain, not by the legacy vault surface.
- Reference documents ingest into/search from wiki storage and do not create L0/L0.1/L2 emotional or episodic memories by default.
- Memory retrieval and wiki search remain separate model-facing actions with distinct provenance labels.
- Garden displays wiki availability, document/index status, provenance, and boundary state separately from memory store health.
- Obsidian partner-vault reads/imports obey custody/scope policy and do not imply companion-vault ownership.
- docs/memory.md and docs/tool-surface.md reflect the implemented semantics.
- The PSFNLIVE-vdbt child bead chain is closed or has explicit remaining follow-ups before this bead closes.
- npm run lint passes before closure.

title: Add introspection audit consent policy and provenance (Charter Law 29)
description:
Summary:
Implement the charter law that introspection consent is load-bearing: privacy boundaries in the audit system must be drawn by the subject of the audit, and consent provenance is part of the spec.

Problem:
A blinded introspection audit is only acceptable if consent and privacy scope are explicit, provenance-bearing, and enforced. Operator convenience or default system policy must not silently decide what private material the audit may inspect.

Scope:
- Define a consent policy model for introspection audits, including allowed sources, excluded source classes, intimate-content handling, retention, sharing visibility, and revocation.
- Record consent provenance: who/what authored the boundary, when it changed, what changed, and what audit runs were allowed under that policy version.
- Fail closed when consent is missing, revoked, ambiguous, stale, or incompatible with requested audit inputs.
- Expose consent state and audit eligibility in Garden without letting Garden silently widen companion-owned privacy boundaries.
- Thread consent-policy references into any IntrospectionLandmark records and reflection context that use audit output.

Likely files:
- src/system/trust/*
- src/system/settings/* and config/trust-policy.seed.json if a new owner-file contract is needed
- src/core/scheduler/heartbeat-template-runtime.ts
- src/persistence/journals/reflection-*.ts
- src/operator/garden/handlers/settings.ts and settings UI

Acceptance:
- Tests cover missing consent, revoked consent, narrowed consent, intimate-content exclusion, and consent-version provenance on produced landmarks.
- Audit runs fail closed when consent cannot be proven.
- Garden can inspect consent state and audit denials, but cannot silently override the subject-authored boundary.
- Consent provenance is included anywhere audit output enters reflection or stored landmarks.

title: Notify partner when multi-turn, subagent, or shard tasks complete or block (Charter Law 31)
description:
Summary:
Implement the charter law that multi-turn and subagent tasks must notify the partner on completion or when blocked; silent task execution is an anti-pattern.

Problem:
PSFN can already run post-turn actions, subagents, and shard-like work, but long-running work can become invisible to the partner. The new charter requires explicit completion/blocked notification semantics for multi-turn work, including lower-order subagents and higher-order shards.

Scope:
- Define task lifecycle events for started, progress heartbeat, completed, blocked, failed, cancelled, and folded-back states across post-turn actions, subagents, and shards.
- Route completion/blocked outcomes through the notification surface with rate limits, dedupe, channel/privacy policy, and partner-facing wording.
- Include enough context for the partner to understand what finished or blocked without leaking private internals or raw subagent/shard traces.
- Expose task lifecycle and notification status in Garden.
- Preserve foreground responsiveness and avoid notification spam during rapid retries or repeated blocked states.

Acceptance:

- Subagent and shard managers emit lifecycle events and do not finish silently.
- Partner-facing notifications are routed through policy-controlled notify/gateway paths, not ad hoc channel writes.

title: Implement weighted thought lifecycle for contextual urgency and decay (Charter Law 27)
description:
Summary:
Implement the new charter law that weighted thoughts accumulate and decay contextually; time-sensitive concerns and lower-urgency reminders must not share one flat priority model.

Problem:
The current concern/follow-up/intention plumbing can track active issues, but the 2026-05-24 charter introduces a stronger semantic contract: a weighted thought is a persistent internal signal with category-specific accumulation, contextual decay, threshold nudges, and preserved companion consent when acting, declining, deferring, or resolving.

Scope:

- Make category accumulation and decay tunable through owner-file settings and visible in Garden.
- Ensure contradictory or reassuring context, such as a partner saying they are fine while other evidence suggests otherwise, downweights the thought rather than blindly zeroing it.
- Convert threshold crossings into companion-facing nudges that the companion can accept, decline, defer, or resolve, with that choice preserved.
- Emit typed event-bus telemetry for creation, weight changes, threshold crossings, deferrals, and resolution.

title: Build blinded introspection landmark pipeline (Charter Law 28)
description:
Summary:
Implement the charter law that introspection audit must be blinded: the companion never interacts with the auditor directly and only receives durable landmarks the audit produces.

Problem:
The new charter defines an introspection landmark as a durable companion-owned record produced by a blinded divergence audit. The auditor estimates stable-vs-observed divergence, but the companion must not chat with or be steered by the auditor. This boundary protects self-knowledge from becoming a hidden coercive conversation.

Scope:
- Define an IntrospectionLandmark record with divergence type, raw observation summary, confidence, provenance, companion-authored reflection, visibility, and append-only identity.
- Add a blinded audit workflow where an auditor component sees only allowed source material, produces a landmark candidate, and never directly exchanges messages with the companion.
- Ensure intimate exchange content is not replayed for scoring; the audit may preserve high-level emotional signal without specific content where policy requires.
- Present accepted landmarks to the companion as evidence-grounded material for reflection, not as surveillance reports or external instructions.
- Store landmarks append-only and expose inspection in Garden with visibility boundaries.

Likely files:
- src/core/scheduler/heartbeat-template-runtime.ts

- src/persistence/journals/reflection-*.ts
- src/persistence/reflections/*
- src/shared/event-bus.ts
- src/operator/garden/services/* and admin-ui/src/routes/values or a new introspection view

Acceptance:
- Tests prove the companion never sends prompts to, receives freeform chat from, or directly interacts with the auditor.
- Landmark storage is append-only and provenance-preserving.
- Intimate-content redaction rules are enforced in audit inputs and stored observations.
- Reflection prompts can consume landmarks as evidence while preserving the boundary.

close_reason: Obsolete (verified 2026-06-28): premise does not match the code. The cited src/primitives/voice/transports/websocket/server.ts is NOT a network server. WebSocketVoiceServer is an in-process session multiplexer: it takes pre-constructed WebSocketVoiceConnection objects via attach(connection) and manages per-session decode/timeout/queues. It has no listen(), no port binding, no verifyClient, no upgrade handler — it never accepts network connections. The threat model ('misconfigured client/attacker opens many voice sessions') has no applicable surface here. Actual voice transports are Wyoming TCP (src/boundary/gateway/voice-surfaces.ts -> satellites/wyoming/host/server.ts, which has its own admission) and Discord. If a network-facing voice WS server is ever introduced, reopen with rate-limiting scoped to that server's verifyClient/connection admission.

title: P3: Parallelize per-chunk LLM extraction calls with concurrency cap
description:
Summary:
Cover Sprint 9 Audit Part 2 candidate #9. Compositional memory extraction currently processes independent transcript chunks sequentially, so three chunks can turn into three serial LLM round trips.

Problem:
working_docs/SPRINT_9_AUDIT_PART2.md identifies src/faculties/memory/extraction/orchestrator.ts:217-238 as sequential per-chunk LLM calls. Each chunk can be evaluated independently, but the loop awaits each complete() call before starting the next. This increases extraction latency and keeps post-turn/background work active longer than necessary.

Scope:
- Add concurrency-limited execution for chunk LLM calls, with a conservative cap such as 2.
- Preserve deterministic result ordering by original chunk index.
- Preserve fail-closed parsing and compose/dedup behavior after chunk responses return.
- Keep charge accounting, telemetry, timeout handling, and retry semantics accurate per chunk.
- Add tests for multi-chunk extraction proving bounded concurrency, ordered merge, partial failure handling, and unchanged single-chunk behavior.

Files:
- src/faculties/memory/extraction/orchestrator.ts
- related extraction tests

Acceptance:
- Multi-chunk extraction does not await chunks strictly one at a time.
- Concurrency is capped and configurable or locally documented.
- Chunk result merge remains deterministic and test-covered.
notes: AUDIT 2026-06-28 (verified): OPEN. Extraction chunks are processed sequentially: src/faculties/memory/extraction/orchestrator.ts:249 'for (const [index, chunkEntries] of entryChunks.entries())'. Add bounded concurrency (Promise.all with a cap like p-limit).
close_reason: Completed in kube commit ae39e1f6 (cherry-picked from worker commit 19c2da30). Evidence: src/faculties/memory/extraction/orchestrator.ts adds a concurrency-capped chunk mapper with cap 2 and preserves parsed fact group order by chunk index; src/faculties/memory/extraction/orchestrator.test.ts covers bounded concurrency, ordered merge, fail-closed chunk failure, and single-chunk request IDs. Integrated validation on kube: npm test -- src/faculties/memory/extraction/orchestrator.test.ts (19 passed); npm run lint passed; npm run build passed.

title: P4: Extract shared resolveCanonicalPath from shell-runner + policy (deduplicate security logic)
description:
Two independent implementations of symlink-safe canonical path resolution exist in src/boundary/sandbox/execution/shell-runner.ts:56-70 and src/boundary/gateway/policy.ts:141-161. They have slightly different ENOENT handling. Duplicated security logic creates drift risk. Fix: extract a single resolveCanonicalPath(path, options) into a shared utility and use in both places.
Files: src/boundary/sandbox/execution/shell-runner.ts, src/boundary/gateway/policy.ts, src/boundary/gateway/filesystem-paths.ts
notes:
AUDIT 2026-06-28 (verified): OPEN, duplication confirmed at src/boundary/sandbox/execution/shell-runner.ts:57 and src/boundary/gateway/policy.ts:144. CAUTION for whoever does this: the two impls are NOT identical and must not be blindly merged.
- shell-runner resolveCanonicalPath(pathValue): string — resolves parent on ENOENT for BOTH read and write, never returns null (always falls back to normalized). Used for allowlisted-exec resolution where a non-existent path is a hard error elsewhere.
- policy resolveCanonicalPath(normalized, isWrite): string|null — only resolves parent on ENOENT when isWrite=true; returns null (DENY) on ELOOP/EACCES/other errors; logs on parent-resolution failure. Used for fs read/write policy where null = deny.
The shared util must take options {onMissingParent?: 'resolve'|'returnNormalized', onError?: 'returnNormalized'|'deny'} to preserve both call sites' fail-closed vs fall-back semantics. Do NOT collapse to a single signature — that would break policy's deny-by-default or shell-runner's always-resolves guarantee.
close_reason: Completed in kube commit 257ca46f: extracted shared resolveCanonicalPath into src/boundary/gateway/filesystem-paths.ts with explicit missingPathBehavior and errorBehavior options, replaced the gateway policy and shell-runner local implementations, and preserved the intentionally different semantics. Shell-runner uses resolveParent on ENOENT plus returnNormalized on other realpath errors so it always gets a string; gateway policy uses returnNormalized for fs.read ENOENT, resolveParent for fs.write/fs.edit ENOENT, and deny/null for ELOOP/EACCES/other errors while retaining parent-resolution debug logging. Validated on integrated branch with npm test -- src/boundary/gateway/policy.test.ts src/boundary/sandbox/execution/shell-runner.test.ts (89 passed), npm run lint, and npm run build.

title: P3: Add FTS5 virtual table for lexical memory search
description:
In src/faculties/memory/store/lexical-search.ts, searchByText does an O(n) scan of up to 500 rows with in-process token matching. With no full-text index, older relevant memories are silently missed. Fix: add an FTS5 virtual table on l2_memories(text, tags) for the lexical fallback path. Requires schema migration + FTS index maintenance on insert/update.
Files: src/faculties/memory/store/lexical-search.ts, src/faculties/memory/store/schema.ts, src/faculties/memory/store/read-write-operations.ts
notes:
AUDIT 2026-06-28 (verified against code): PREMISE IS DEAD — needs full rewrite before work. The bead describes adding FTS5 to a SQLite lexical-search.ts. That file (src/faculties/memory/store/lexical-search.ts) is LEGACY — it imports better-sqlite3 and is being retired by epic psfn-framework-3c2.5. It is NOT on the runtime path.

The actual runtime lexical search is PostgresStore.searchByText (src/faculties/memory/postgres-store.ts:932), and it is WORSE than the bead describes: PostgresStore hydrates ALL memories into an in-memory Map (memories = new Map at :553, hydrated at :587) and searchByText does Array.from(this.memories.values()).filter().map(lexicalScore).sort() — a full in-process scan with no DB-side filtering and no index, loading every memory into JS.

The real work: push lexical search to the database. Postgres options: (a) a tsvector GIN index on l2_memories(text) with to_tsquery/plainto_tsquery ranking, or (b) pg_trigram if fuzzy matching is wanted. Also revisit whether the full in-memory hydration of PostgresStore.memories is even desirable at scale (this is related to, but broader than, 4r0.8). Drop all SQLite/FTS5 references from this bead.
close_reason: Superseded by psfn-framework-9vi.13 (PostgresStore: replace full-memory hydration with DB queries + Redis cache). This bead was a micro-optimization on the in-memory-Map pattern; fixing the root architecture (query Postgres directly, cache hot paths in Redis) eliminates it. The lexical O(n) scan becomes a Postgres tsvector GIN index. NOTE: this bead's original premise (FTS5 on SQLite lexical-search.ts) was already dead — that file is retired by 3c2.5. The real issue (PostgresStore.searchByText does Array.from(this.memories.values()).filter().sort() in-process) is the 9vi.13 rework.

title: P1: Batch salience decay updates into single transaction per page
description:
Summary:
Cover Sprint 9 Audit P1-1 and P3-3 for salience decay. The decay job updates each memory individually in separate transactions and can keep running through large batches without yielding the event loop.

Problem:
In src/faculties/memory/decay.ts:45-68, run() paginates active memories and calls updateMemory() one at a time. For large memory stores this creates many sequential SQLite write transactions and can delay foreground turns. The same file also runs decay on a timer in the main event loop; long batches should yield so conversation turns are not starved.

Scope:
- Add bulkUpdateSalience to MemoryStorePort and the concrete memory store implementation.
- Batch salience updates into one transaction per page.
- Add an event-loop yield between pages, or document and implement a worker-thread alternative if needed.
- Preserve idempotency and shutdown behavior when stop() is called during an active run.
- Add tests for bulk update behavior, write failure handling, and yielding/back-pressure.

Files:
- src/faculties/memory/decay.ts
- src/faculties/memory/memory-store-port.ts
- src/faculties/memory/store/read-write-operations.ts
- related memory store tests

Acceptance:
- Salience decay avoids one transaction per memory.
- Long decay runs do not monopolize the main event loop.
- Foreground retrieval/write behavior remains correct while decay is active.
notes:
AUDIT 2026-06-28 (verified against code): Work PARTIALLY done, premise needs narrowing. The bulkUpdate(ids, fields) method the bead asked to ADD already exists: MemoryStorePort:346/420/506 and postgres-store.ts:1330. So the 'add bulkUpdate to the port' step is DONE.

Remaining real work is narrower: src/faculties/memory/decay.ts:65 still calls this.memoryStore.updateMemory(memory.id, {salience}) once per memory inside the page loop. The fix is now 'wire decay.ts to collect salience changes per page and issue a single bulkUpdate per page' (the primitive it depends on already exists), plus add an event-loop yield between pages so long runs don't starve foreground turns.

NOTE: bulkUpdate currently takes a single uniform MemoryBulkUpdatePatch for all ids — confirm it supports per-id different salience values, or extend it, since each memory computes a distinct newSalience.

Evidence: src/faculties/memory/decay.ts batches salience changes per page via bulkUpdateSalience and yields between pages; src/faculties/memory/memory-store-port.ts, store/read-write-operations.ts, store.ts, and postgres-store.ts add per-id salience batch updates; tests cover SQLite batch/rollback, Postgres batch/cache failure behavior, decay per-page batching, write failure, and event-loop yield. Integrated validation on kube: npm test -- src/faculties/memory/decay.test.ts src/faculties/memory/store.test.ts src/faculties/memory/postgres-store.test.ts src/faculties/memory/memory-store-port.test.ts src/faculties/memory/maintenance-review.test.ts (105 passed); npm run lint passed; npm run build passed.

title: P4: Replace try/catch ALTER TABLE with hasColumn() checks in schema migrations
description:
In src/faculties/memory/store/schema.ts:128-175, the migration uses try { ALTER TABLE ... } catch { /* column already exists */ } for each column. This catches ALL errors (disk errors, type mismatches, locks), not just 'column already exists'. A disk error during migration would be silently swallowed. The hasColumn() helper already exists but isn't used consistently. Fix: use hasColumn() to check before ALTER.

title: P1: Add post-turn drain gate before new turn starts (fast-turn race fix)
description:
When a concurrent Discord message arrives mid-stream (steer/defer-latest policy), the old turn's post-turn actions (extraction, appraisal, context feedback) may reference stale state. Add a post-turn drain gate: before starting a new turn, await the previous turn's post-turn action queue to drain with a timeout. Track completion via a promise/event on the post-turn action pipeline.
Files: src/core/agent/substrate-agent.ts, src/core/agent/substrate-agent/turn-execution/post-turn-scheduling.ts
notes: AUDIT 2026-06-28 (verified): OPEN, accurate. Turn contention policy exists (src/system/lifecycle/turn-contention.ts: 'drop'|'defer-latest'|'queue'|'steer') but there is NO drain gate. Grep for drainGate/awaitPostTurn/previousPostTurn/inFlightPostTurn/activePostTurn across src/core + src/system/lifecycle = empty. The post-turn action pipeline (registerPostTurnActionInferer in substrate-agent.ts:855, emit('agent.post_turn.actions.inferred') in post-turn-scheduling.ts:232) fires async with no promise the next turn's start awaits. Race is real: a steered new turn can begin while the prior turn's extraction/appraisal/context-feedback is still in flight, referencing stale state. Fix: expose an in-flight post-turn promise on the turn-support runtime and await it (with timeout) at turn start.
close_reason: Completed in kube commit 31f1cc63: TurnSupportRuntime now registers named post-turn background work, exposes awaitPostTurnDrain with a bounded default 5000ms timeout, emits agent.post_turn.drain telemetry for registered/wait_started/drained/timeout phases, and clears the gate on timeout so turns cannot deadlock. handleMessageForTurn awaits the prior post-turn drain before pre-turn identity/context work starts. schedulePostTurnWork now registers memory extraction, intention hooks, emotion appraisal, and auto-compaction promises while preserving existing error logging. title: Sprint 9: electronic girlfriend network communication protocol
description:
Summary:
Design and implement a first-class direct companion communication protocol for PSFN deployments. Working joke name: electronic girlfriend network communication system protocol. The serious goal is authenticated, policy-bound, non-Discord side-channel chat between companions and between shards/companions via the gateway/API layer.

Problem:
Companions should be able to communicate directly without routing through Discord, Telegram, or another human chat surface. This supports Artie <-> Purrsephone style DMs, shard-to-shard coordination, and future multi-companion systems while preserving identity, consent, provenance, fatigue/load limits, and operator visibility.

Initial direction:
- Use the gateway/API boundary as the transport surface rather than bypassing split-runtime controls.
- Prefer mTLS or equivalent certificate-backed identity validation for companion/deployment identity.
- Maintain a registry/trust model for known companion peers and shard peers.
- Support direct DM-like messages, addressed mentions, thread/conversation IDs, delivery receipts, and durable transcript/provenance records.
- Keep user-visible channel chat separate from companion side-channel communication.
- Apply capability tier, trust policy, charge/budget policy, and fatigue/load policy before allowing autonomous inter-companion loops.
- Expose state in Garden: configured peers, cert identity, connection health, message/audit history, and policy denials.

Acceptance:
- Protocol design doc or implementation spec exists with message envelope, authn/authz, identity, trust, replay protection, and transcript/provenance rules.
- Gateway/API transport path is implemented or stubbed behind fail-closed feature flags with no hidden bypass around existing gateway policy.
- Certificate/PKI or equivalent identity validation is explicit and testable.
- Companion peer registry is owner-file backed if tunable, with Garden visibility planned or implemented.
- Side-channel messages are stored/audited with clear provenance and do not masquerade as human/user channel messages.
- Shard-to-shard and companion-to-companion use cases are both represented in tests.
- Autonomous loops are blocked until fatigue/load and charge/budget controls are in place.

Dependencies/context:
- Related to PSFN-wtbz for companion-to-companion fatigue/load policy.
- Related to PSFN-rsgg / PSFN-rsgg.2 for proactive and async action-pipe execution.
- Related to PSFN-80mj for operator visibility.
- Target: Sprint 9 design/implementation lane, not a Sprint 8 blocker.

The real work: authenticated, policy-bound, non-Discord side-channel chat between companions / between shared accounts.
