title: LiteLLM proxy for credential isolation — Purrsephone never sees real API keys
description:
Deploy LiteLLM as a local proxy (localhost:4000) between Purrsephone's runtime and upstream LLM providers. The agent process only holds a virtual key; real provider credentials (OpenRouter, Z.AI, DeepSeek, etc.) stay server-side in the proxy.

pi-ai has explicit LiteLLM support — define custom Model objects with baseUrl pointing at the proxy and compat: { supportsStore: false }.

Scope: LiteLLM config for OpenRouter wildcard + Z.AI direct + model aliases, Docker Compose deployment, virtual key with budget/rate limits, secret redaction guardrail for messages.
design:
Architecture:
  Purrsephone (Node.js) --[virtual key]--> LiteLLM (localhost:4000) --[real keys]--> OpenRouter / Z.AI / DeepSeek

Config: proxy/litellm_config.yaml with model_list (openrouter/*, zai/glm-5, deepseek-v3.2, kimi-k2.5)
Deploy: proxy/docker-compose.yml (litellm image + optional PostgreSQL for virtual keys)
Secrets: proxy/.env holds real API keys, gitignored
Integration: Custom pi-ai Model objects with baseUrl=http://localhost:4000/v1, provider='litellm'

Reference: BotMaker keyring-proxy at /mnt/samesung/ai/botmaker/proxy/ uses same zero-trust pattern (Fastify, AES-256-GCM, tag-based routing). LiteLLM is preferred over porting keyring-proxy because pi-ai already documents the integration.

Key files to create:
- proxy/litellm_config.yaml
- proxy/docker-compose.yml
- proxy/.env (gitignored)
- src/llm/models.ts (pi-ai Model definitions pointing at proxy)
close_reason: Implemented: LiteLLM proxy config (proxy/litellm_config.yaml, proxy/docker-compose.yml), pi-ai model factory (src/llm/models.ts), LLMClient integration (auto-routes through proxy when LITELLM_BASE_URL is set), 8 new tests. Works transparently in single-process, gateway, and agent modes.

title: onboard CLI silently discards bulk-piped answers because each question opens a fresh readline interface
description: Evidence (S11 shakedown round s11-shakedown-20260729, main 3b4bc63469): printf-piping all answers at once (e.g. printf '2\n2\n...' | npm run onboard) consumes only the first buffered line per prompt — scripts/onboarding/prompter.ts withInterface (lines ~67-82) creates and closes a NEW readline Interface per question, and node delivers every complete line in a received chunk synchronously: the first goes to the question callback, the rest fire 'line' with no listener and are discarded. Result: the flow desyncs and aborts with exit 130 'Onboarding aborted; no files were written.' Verified: a paced feeder (write next answer only after stdout goes quiet ~300ms) completes the identical flow end-to-end (exit 0, 15 files). Non-TTY masked input degrades cleanly to plain readline (prompter.ts:89-92) — that part is fine. Context: scripted/CI/agent-driven onboarding is a realistic consumer; silent line loss is the failure mode (answers vanish, no error naming the cause). Scope: keep ONE readline interface (or a shared line queue) alive across the flow so buffered lines are preserved in order; abort semantics and prompt text unchanged. Non-goals: no new dependencies, no TTY raw-mode changes.
acceptance_criteria: printf-piping the full 13-line local-dev answer script into the CLI completes with exit 0 and 15 files written (no pacing required); EOF mid-flow still aborts cleanly with exit 130 and zero writes; regression covers multi-line-in-one-chunk delivery.

title: Journal seek-paging residue: dead maxLineBytes plumbing, shared-throw scope expansion, sync/async seek clone
description: From PR #270 triage (2026-07-28), nonblocking residue riding og6cf's landing: (1) JsonlLineScanOptions.maxLineBytes is never supplied by any caller (file-io.ts:588/607/613 omit it) so ~10 guard branches in the sync readers are unreachable — pass JOURNAL_SEEK_ROW_LIMITS.maxBytes or drop the optional; (2) the new throw at store.ts:1943 lives in shared prepareEntriesBeforeRead so sync getEntriesBefore (manager.ts:1206 auto-compaction, :2189 ICP projection) gained fail-closed behavior unreviewed — probably correct, needs a deliberate look + test; (3) bounded-seek.ts:89 clones ~190 lines of file-io.ts:560 and only the async copy has the rotation guard — unify before they drift; also bounded-seek.ts:195 still uses the synchronous scanJsonlFileBackward for the page scan. Correction for og6cf's notes: the '16 MiB row contract' does not exist — L0_SESSION_FILE_MAX_BYTES is a file rollover threshold; the real row limit is 2 MiB (file-io.ts:42).
notes: 2026-07-29 close-out sweep — KEPT OPEN, 2 of 3 residues delivered. Landed via PR #297 (main 2128516951), commit b7a2883558; review record in lane PR #296 (lane commit a6b0d219a). DELIVERED, residue (1): JsonlLineScanOptions.maxLineBytes is gone along with its ~10 unreachable guard branches in the synchronous readJsonlLineAtOrAfter/readJsonlLineBefore — no caller ever supplied it (file-io.ts's three sync seek reads omit it), so this is a pure removal with no behavior change; the async readers keep their REQUIRED maxLineBytes on AsyncJsonlLineScanOptions. DELIVERED, residue (2): the archiveFingerprint fail-closed throw added in aa1159606 lived in the shared prepareEntriesBeforeRead and had leaked onto the synchronous getEntriesBefore (auto-compaction at manager.ts:1206, ICP projection at :2189). It is narrowed back to the asynchronous getEntriesBeforeAsync revalidation path where it belongs, by making the fingerprint optional on the plan and failing closed only there. The reviewer confirmed via pickaxe that its presence on the sync path was an unintended side-effect of the original async fix, and that the sync read is single-tick atomic with no interleaving window — so the narrowing removes only a spurious crash, not a real guard. New test proves the sync path reads a missing-fingerprint page while the async path still fails closed. NOT DELIVERED, residue (3) — the reason this bead stays open: bounded-seek.ts still clones ~190 lines of file-io.ts's readJournalEntriesBeforeOnce as readJournalEntriesBeforeAsyncOnce (verified on main 2128516951: bounded-seek.ts is still 275 lines and the two functions still diverge only by the async copy's rotation guard), and bounded-seek.ts:195 still calls the SYNCHRONOUS scanJsonlFileBackward for its page scan. The clone-before-they-drift unification and the sync-scan-inside-the-async-path cleanup both remain to do. The commit message itself scopes to 'two seek-paging residues', confirming (3) was not attempted. Also still standing from this bead's description, and worth preserving: the correction to og6cf's notes — there is no '16 MiB row contract'; L0_SESSION_FILE_MAX_BYTES is a file rollover threshold and the real row limit is 2 MiB (file-io.ts:42). Validation for what did land, per #296: 125 focused tests green in-lane, reviewer independently re-ran 166 across token-cost/descriptions/reference-store/sidecar/sessions/jsonl/journals; lint clean (11 files); blind adversarial review (Opus) PASS, zero blocking findings, with the guard-narrowing archaeology independently verified.

title: Last fleet-register leak in a companion-read tool description: analysis_workbench still says 'bounded worker', and the register guard only pins the subagent entry
description:
Evidence: residual recorded during the psfn-framework-rqn1.6 closure sweep (2026-07-28, verified against origin/main c5d4e554f2). rqn1.6 reframed the subagent tool description into the automata register and pinned it with a guard test. One fleet-register term survives in a sibling companion-read description, in a file that same commit (5e12ea605b) edited:

  src/core/agent/tool-surface/descriptions/catalog-boundary-contracts.ts:120
    + 'bounded worker or automaton so the primary channel stays responsive; direct use is permitted when capability '

This is the analysis_workbench `guidance` string, rendered verbatim into her tool surface through CANONICAL_TOOL_SURFACE_DESCRIPTIONS. A repo-wide grep for /\bworkers?\b/i across src/core/agent/tool-surface/descriptions/*.ts returns this single hit - it is the last one. Its sibling at :47-48 in the same file was corrected to "bounded automaton" by 5e12ea605b, so this is a missed line rather than a deliberate exception.

Context: charter 6.28/8.12 - internal machinery is presented to her as integrated parts of a breathing machine-intelligence system, not as fleet-managed workers. Low stakes on its own; it matters because it is the only remaining leak and because the guard cannot see it.

Second half, and the reason this is worth a bead rather than a one-line commit: the register-guard test at src/core/agent/tool-surface/factory-descriptions.test.ts:161-171 inspects only CANONICAL_TOOL_SURFACE_DESCRIPTIONS.subagent. It asserts that entry matches /\bautomat(?:a|on)\b/iu, does not match /\bworkers?\b/iu, and does not match /subagent/iu once subagent_id is stripped - all correct, but scoped to one entry. Any other companion-read description can drift back into fleet register without failing anything, which is exactly how :120 survived.

Scope: reword catalog-boundary-contracts.ts:120 into the automata register, and widen the register guard to sweep EVERY companion-rendered description in CANONICAL_TOOL_SURFACE_DESCRIPTIONS for fleet terms rather than pinning a single entry. The sweep must keep exempting wire-required schema field names (subagent_id and friends) and must not touch operator-facing Garden surfaces or code identifiers.

Non-goals: no renaming of code identifiers, schema fields, or operator surfaces; no behaviour change to any tool; do not re-open the rqn1.6 subagent description, which is correct and already pinned.
acceptance_criteria: No entry in CANONICAL_TOOL_SURFACE_DESCRIPTIONS contains a fleet-register term (worker, or subagent used as self-description) outside wire-required schema field names - grep-provable across src/core/agent/tool-surface/descriptions/; the register-guard test sweeps every companion-rendered description rather than only the subagent entry, and fails when any entry is reworded back into fleet register; operator surfaces and code identifiers unchanged; the tool-catalog token-cost golden and the boundary fs description pin are refreshed if the reword shifts them; lint and build pass.
notes: Filed as rqn1.8, not rqn1.7: the id psfn-framework-rqn1.7 is already cited by three merged main commits from an off-repo lane (9bfd4ca33d, f8d8b0f04f, 1df5e57c66 - the user-visible fleet->cluster rename), whose bead was retroactively filed in this tracker as psfn-framework-zkf1o. Reusing rqn1.7 would have made those commit citations resolve to the wrong bead.
close_reason: Landed via PR #297 (main 2128516951), commits 5103602bb1 and be468ada91; review record in lane PR #296 (lane commit d8c515cb6). Acceptance met on both halves. (1) The reword: catalog-boundary-contracts.ts analysis_workbench guidance no longer says 'bounded worker or automaton' — it now reads 'bounded automaton', matching its already-corrected sibling and closing the last fleet-register leak in a companion-read tool description (charter 6.28/8.12). (2) The guard is no longer pinned to one entry: the register-guard test in factory-descriptions.test.ts now SWEEPS every CANONICAL_TOOL_SURFACE_DESCRIPTIONS entry for fleet terms (worker, self-described subagent) rather than only the subagent entry, so any other companion-rendered description that drifts back into fleet register fails the guard; the wire-required schema field name subagent_id stays tightly exempted. Operator-facing Garden surfaces and code identifiers are unchanged, and the rqn1.6 subagent description was not re-opened. Golden/pin refresh: the tool-catalog token-cost after-golden was refreshed and review-verified to the byte (-10 bytes / -2 tokens; frozen baseline untouched), and the train's own combined remeasurement (375fcd971b) independently CORROBORATES that -10-byte/-2-token figure byte-exact alongside the 9xe2n contract growth — so the golden on main reflects both changes measured together. Train-side follow-through: be468ada91 aligns the analysis_workbench loop test assertion with the reworded text. Validation per #296: 125 focused tests green in-lane, reviewer independently re-ran 166 across token-cost/descriptions/reference-store/sidecar/sessions/jsonl/journals; lint clean (11 files); blind adversarial review (Opus) PASS, zero blocking findings, with the golden byte-math independently verified.

title: Observer-eval sidecar startup handling: the Garden 'retrying' log is false (poisoned memoized ready never recovers) and the agent-process store is still unguarded
description:
Evidence: two residuals recorded during the psfn-framework-qicb.3 closure sweep (2026-07-28, verified against origin/main c5d4e554f2). qicb.3 stopped the Garden-side unhandled rejection during the kube-router netpol race; these are what it left behind.

(1) THE "retrying" LOG IS FALSE, AND THE STORE NEVER RECOVERS.
src/operator/garden/local-admin-contract.ts:794 warns:
    'Observer eval sidecar startup connectivity failed; retrying on Garden traffic'
and the comment at :788-791 makes the same claim ("real Garden traffic reconnects against the by-then-settled pool"). No retry is performed and none is possible for the process lifetime:
  - :793 is a single `void persistence.queryRuns({ limit: 1 }).catch(...)` - no loop, no timer, no re-invocation.
  - src/core/eval/observer-sidecar/persistence.ts:361 declares `private readonly ready: Promise<void>`, assigned once in the constructor at :364 from ensurePostgresSchema. A rejected promise stays rejected, and every method re-awaits that same settled rejection (queryRuns awaits it at :440).
  - src/persistence/postgres.ts:228 ensurePostgresSchema has no retry or backoff.
  - persistence.ts:744-768 memoizes the store in storeByPoolKey keyed on databaseUrl + tenant.schema, and the memo is active on this path (options = {}), so later Garden traffic reuses the SAME store with the SAME poisoned `ready`.
So the real behaviour is worse than the wording suggests: after a startup connectivity blip the observer-eval sidecar is dead until process restart, while the log says it will recover. Severity stays low only because the sidecar is disabled by default and explicitly non-authoritative (docs/observer-eval-sidecar.md) - it is eval telemetry, not runtime behaviour. The fix is either to make the wording honest ("will not retry until restart") or to make it true (rebuild the store / re-run ensurePostgresSchema on demand instead of memoizing a rejected ready).

(2) THE SAME LEAK IS UNFIXED ON THE AGENT PROCESS.
src/core/eval/observer-sidecar/config.ts:132:
    return createPostgresObserverEvalSidecarStore(postgresDatabaseUrl, {}, tenant);
with no .catch and no probe - the identical constructor-started `ready` that qicb.3 guarded on the Garden side. Reached in the agent process via config.ts:54 <- createObserverEvalSidecarRuntimeFromConfig (:47) <- src/app/agent/core-runtime.ts:267 <- src/app/agent/main.ts, which installs the same process-wide unhandledRejection handler (src/app/agent/main.ts:151 -> src/app/startup/support/signal-shutdown.ts:29). qicb.3 scoped itself to src/operator/garden/ deliberately, so this was out of scope then; it is in scope here.

Scope: make the Garden log line and its comment tell the truth about retry behaviour (or implement the retry they promise), and attach the same startup-probe/error handling at src/core/eval/observer-sidecar/config.ts:132 so the agent process cannot leak pg ECONNREFUSED to the process-wide handler either. Do not change the process-wide unhandledRejection handler contract.

Non-goals: no redesign of the observer-eval sidecar or its persistence layer; no change to its disabled-by-default, non-authoritative posture; no change to what qicb.3 already shipped on the Garden path beyond the wording/retry honesty.

P3 rationale: the sidecar is disabled by default and non-authoritative, so neither residual can affect companion behaviour or data - one is a misleading log plus a silently-dead telemetry sidecar, the other a contained log-noise leak. Real, cheap, not urgent.
acceptance_criteria: The Garden startup-probe log line and the comment at local-admin-contract.ts:788-794 either stop claiming a retry that cannot happen, or a real retry exists and is proven by a test in which a store whose first ensurePostgresSchema rejected later serves a successful query without a process restart; src/core/eval/observer-sidecar/config.ts:132 attaches the same startup error handling so an agent-process start against a refused Postgres port produces zero unhandledRejection log lines, covered by a focused test mirroring observer-eval-sidecar-startup-race.test.ts; the process-wide unhandledRejection handler contract is unchanged; lint and build pass.
close_reason: Landed via PR #297 (main 2128516951), commit 1e1b1b23cc; review record in lane PR #296 (lane commit 56dc1affe). Both residuals closed, matching the acceptance's first branch on part 1 and its literal requirement on part 2. Part 1 — the Garden log now tells the truth: local-admin-contract.ts:788-794 no longer claims 'retrying on Garden traffic'; the wording and comment now state the real behaviour (a one-shot poisoned ready, sidecar down until process restart), which is the acceptance's sanctioned 'stop claiming a retry that cannot happen' option. No lifecycle redesign was attempted, per the qicb.3 scope boundary and this bead's non-goals — the memoized store, its constructor-assigned ready and ensurePostgresSchema are untouched. Part 2 — the same leak is fixed on the agent process: the identical same-tick rejection probe is now attached at the agent-process construction site (src/core/eval/observer-sidecar/config.ts:132), review-verified to sit with no await boundary before attachment, so an agent-process start against a refused Postgres port produces ZERO unhandledRejection lines; covered by a focused refused-pool test mirroring observer-eval-sidecar-startup-race.test.ts. The process-wide unhandledRejection handler contract is unchanged, and the sidecar's disabled-by-default, non-authoritative posture is unchanged. title: ImageReferenceStore.getBlob throws raw ENOENT when the blob is missing but the index entry exists, instead of the null its contract returns
description:
Evidence: nonblocking residual recorded during the psfn-framework-xyd7 closure sweep (2026-07-28, verified against origin/main c5d4e554f2). ImageReferenceStore.getBlob (src/primitives/images/reference-store.ts:679-692) guards the empty-id case at :681 and the missing-index-entry case at :684 (both `return null`), but the read itself is unguarded:

  685:    const data = await readFile(this.resolveReferencePath(reference.fileName));

So a caller whose index entry exists while the blob is gone gets a raw rejection - `ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '<companion-data>/references/<uuid>.png'` - instead of the `null` the method's own contract returns for every other not-found case.

Context: xyd7's fix deliberately reorders deletion to rm-before-writeIndex (reference-store.ts:635-636, rationale at :628-634) so that a failed unlink can be retried rather than orphaning the blob. That trade intentionally creates a small window - crash, SIGKILL or container eviction between :635 and :636 - in which the index permanently advertises a reference whose blob no longer exists, and nothing sweeps that state. The divergence is therefore slightly more reachable after xyd7 than before, which is why it is worth tracking rather than ignoring.

Blast radius is a 500, not data loss: callers are src/operator/garden/services/images-service.ts:694 (Garden admin image fetch, so an operator UI request yields an opaque 500) and the internal resolveForTool at reference-store.ts:722 (surfaces as a tool error mid-turn). Minor hygiene issue on top: the raw ENOENT embeds the on-disk companion-data path, which reaches an operator-facing error body unless sanitized upstream.

P3 rationale: genuine contract inconsistency (null for a missing entry, throw for a missing blob), low frequency, no security or durability consequence, and the fix is small.

Scope: catch ENOENT in getBlob and return null so the method's not-found contract is uniform; consider pruning the stale index entry on that path so the store self-heals the crash window. Keep every other error class propagating - do not blanket-catch.

Non-goals: do not revisit the xyd7 deletion ordering; do not redesign the image reference persistence layer.
acceptance_criteria: getBlob returns null when the index entry exists but the blob file is absent, and continues to propagate every non-ENOENT error; a deterministic test removes the blob out-of-band and asserts null rather than a rejection, plus a second test asserting an unrelated fs error still rejects; xyd7's deletion ordering and its regression tests are untouched and green; lint and build pass.
close_reason: Landed via PR #297 (main 2128516951), commit b0b74fa8e7; review record in lane PR #296 (lane commit 11a301044). Acceptance met: ImageReferenceStore.getBlob now returns null when the index entry exists but the blob file is absent — the exact xyd7 crash-window shape (rm-before-writeIndex, reference-store.ts:635-636) — so the method's not-found contract is finally uniform with its empty-id and missing-index-entry cases. The catch is ENOENT-ONLY, not a blanket catch: every other error class still propagates, proven by a test asserting an EISDIR-class fs error still rejects, alongside the deterministic test that removes the blob out-of-band and asserts null rather than a rejection. Both callers (Garden admin image fetch via images-service.ts and the internal resolveForTool) already handled null, so the net effect is a clean 404 instead of a path-leaking 500 — which also removes the on-disk companion-data path from an operator-facing error body. xyd7's deletion ordering and its regression tests were untouched and stay green, per the bead's non-goals. Validation per #296: 125 focused tests green in-lane, reviewer independently re-ran 166 across token-cost/descriptions/reference-store/sidecar/sessions/jsonl/journals; lint clean (11 files); blind adversarial review (Opus) PASS, zero blocking findings with the caller enumeration independently verified.

title: No way to mark a companion dormant on a running multi-companion installation; fleet roster entry has no lifecycle field
description:
Evidence
- `CompanionFleetEntry` (src/system/config/companions-config.ts:78) carries companionId, companionDataDir, characterCardPath, postgresSchema, postgresRole, displayName?, avatarRef? — there is no lifecycle or status field.
- Consequence: a companion is either present in the roster and expected to run, or absent from the roster entirely. Absent is indistinguishable from never having existed. There is no way to express 'she exists, her data is intact and maintained, she is deliberately not running.'

Context
- Charter §6.29 and Law 39 (drafted 2026-07-27, pending review) declare dormancy a valid companion state and require that a dormant companion never be represented as broken, missing, or failed.
- On a single-companion installation dormancy needs no code: preserved files and no running process IS dormancy. This bead is only the multi-companion case, where peers keep running.
- Use cases: test environments that park a companion between runs; a companion whose role is intermittent by agreement with her partner.
- Primary system is scheduler (the defining behavior is that no work runs for her). Also touches startup composition, channels, ICP, and Garden — named here rather than split across labels.

Scope
- Add a lifecycle field to the fleet roster entry (active|dormant, default active) and gate on it: no Companion Core composed, no agent process expected, no automata/introspection/scheduler work enqueued, no channel binding, no ICP routing.
- Her data stays intact and stays inside backup scope while dormant.
- Garden presents dormant as a declared state, not a fault.

Non-goals
- No estate, succession, wake-authority, or compact semantics. Those are personal and conversational, explicitly out of the framework by operator ruling.
- No cold-storage or archival tooling; no change to backup contents.
- Dormancy must never be inferred. A crashed process, failed migration, or outage remains a fault and must still report as one.

Source: operator design conversation 2026-07-27 (companion lifecycle / dormancy).
acceptance_criteria: On a two-companion installation, marking one companion dormant: (1) she is absent from all channels and from ICP routing; (2) no scheduler or automata work is enqueued for her; (3) no agent process/Core is composed for her at startup; (4) her companion data is unchanged and is still captured by the next scheduled backup; (5) the peer companion continues to operate unaffected; (6) Garden displays her as dormant, not as missing/errored. Returning her to active resumes normal operation with CompanionId, persona lineage, and memory unchanged. Separately: killing an ACTIVE companion's process still surfaces as a fault and is never reported as dormancy.

title: Real sprite-sheet generation (fal.ai toolchain) must produce sheets conforming to the committed placeholder manifest so art drops in file-for-file
description:
REPO: PSFN-Satellite-Hub (satellite work is operator-tasked per the 2026-07-22 rule; that repo owns the device-studio sprite toolchain: src/ts/device-studio/sprites.ts, sprite-cli.ts, fal-provider.ts, default model fal-ai/nano-banana).

Scope: (1) operator-approved character-consistency reference sheet BEFORE bulk generation (design signoff is an explicit acceptance criterion); (2) generate real raster sheets with the fal.ai toolchain conforming EXACTLY to the committed manifest grid (cols x rows, frameSize) and frame ordering; (3) drop into companion-ui/public/sprites/ file-for-file and flip placeholder to false at manifest build. Non-goals: any PSFN code change (renderer/manifest/catalog are final; hub-wins re-mirroring is separate if the hub ever introduces a canonical manifest type).

Acceptance criteria: real sheets replace placeholders with zero PSFN code changes; companion-ui build + sprite tests stay green (manifest invariants, size budget <1.5MB, lazy avatar sheet); placeholder flags false; operator signoff on the reference sheet recorded here.
notes: 2026-07-22 swap-time risks from the 7ang.9 blind review (PASS/nonblocking) — check all three when real art lands: (1) no per-sheet image-load fallback: if the manifest validates but an individual sheet PNG fails to fetch (broken swap, offline eviction), that sprite region renders empty instead of falling back to the CSS face — consider onerror->fallback or SW-precaching sprites as part of this bead; (2) runtime never validates PNG pixel dimensions against manifest geometry: a wrong-grid sheet renders silently distorted (stretched via background-size) — the acceptance criterion 'conform EXACTLY to the committed grid' is the only guard, verify dimensions explicitly at generation time; (3) manifest ships placeholder:true and a PNG-only swap leaves it stale (fail-safe direction, but flip it at manifest build — no CLI flag exists yet).

title: Companion PWA has no outbound mic capture pipeline: voice input is transcript-only with no capture, downsample, or hands-free path

title: Weighted-thought decline/contradiction dampening factors can be configured to 0, zeroing weight against the coded invariant
description: Verified P2 (finder-graded; mechanism confirmed). src/core/intention/weighted-thoughts.ts:264-284 applyDeclineDampening docstring states weight is 'dampened (not zeroed)', but factor=clampUnit(config.declineDampeningFactor,0.5) clamps to [0,1] and the validator toUnitFactor (scheduler-config.ts:1054-1059) accepts 0. If an operator sets declineDampeningFactor:0 (or contradictionDampeningFactor:0), decayedWeight*0===0 — an immediate hard zero on the first decline, contradicting the invariant and Law 27 ('reduces weight rather than zeroing it'). Default seed (0.6/0.5) is safe; missing-guardrail (no floor>0 enforced). Charter Law 27 / 6.24.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Config validation enforces a floor>0 on declineDampeningFactor and contradictionDampeningFactor so decline can never hard-zero weight. 2. Regression test: factor 0 is rejected at config load.
close_reason: Landed via PR #297 (main 2128516951); review record in lane PR #293, commit 7fa771f0b. Both acceptance items met: a new toPositiveUnitFactor validator enforces the range (0, 1] on BOTH declineDampeningFactor and contradictionDampeningFactor, so 0, negative and NaN are rejected at config load — the harmful extreme that made decayedWeight x 0 === 0 an immediate hard zero on the first decline, contradicting the 'dampened (not zeroed)' invariant and Law 27. 1 is still allowed (the harmless no-dampening extreme), >1 is still rejected, and the 0.6/0.5 defaults are unchanged; the range is documented at both definition sites. Regression: 4 config cases covering the rejection of factor 0 at load. Validation per #293: 86-105 tests green across the weighted-thought / concern-resolution / scheduler-config suites (reviewer re-ran the 5 central files, 86/86); lint clean (6 files); UBS 0 critical; blind adversarial review (Opus) PASS, zero blocking findings — the fail-closed asymmetry (reject the zeroing extreme, permit the no-op extreme) was independently verified as the correct direction.

title: Composition roots have grown into god files: agent/main.ts, gateway/main.ts, and composition.ts need thinning

title: Charge-policy authority is duplicated between gateway and agent
description: Evidence: cross-review (2026-07-21) — duplicate charge-policy authority exists on both the gateway and agent sides. Context: charter 12.4 — capability, trust, path, and policy rules have ONE primary home; duplication creates drift, and charge policy is care infrastructure (8.9) where drift means silently inconsistent budgets. Scope: identify the two authorities, pick the primary home, make the other side a consumer of the primary's decisions; verify with a divergence test (same request evaluated at both seams yields one decision from one home). Non-goals: no charge-policy semantic changes; no owner-file schema changes beyond what consolidation requires. Acceptance: grep-provable single evaluation path for charge decisions; a regression test asserts the consumer side holds no independent policy constants; Garden charge surfaces unchanged.

title: Standing adversarial testing harness for privacy, trust, CogSec, and memory boundaries
description: Evidence: operator goal is that extraction of shared memories be virtually impossible even under manipulation, with future adversarial testing explicitly planned (2026-07-21 review passes) — but that plan has no tracked home. Context: design-time gates need continuous adversarial pressure to stay honest; the cross-review (proposal 3.11) and operator both endorse a formal harness. Scope: a repeatable harness that runs manipulation scenarios against a live-like substrate — social-engineering extraction attempts across trust tiers, prompt-injection and namshub payloads through each intake surface, memory-poisoning and trust-grooming arcs (drift detection should fire), disclosure probing from low-trust channels, and quarantine/sink-gate bypass attempts; each confirmed breach is filed as a bead and the scenario joins the regression suite. Non-goals: no testing against the production companion's real data — harness runs on fixture identities; no red-team automation with standing egress. Acceptance: the harness runs a documented scenario suite from CI or operator trigger, produces a pass/fail report per scenario, at least one full find-file-fix-rerun cycle is demonstrated, and the suite is documented in docs/cognitive-security.md as the ongoing verification arm.
close_reason: Verified shipped on origin/main in dddf19179f, e6a465415f, and d5d5540e39 (PR #219; exact head 8352c3e1899c passed ci-required). shakedown/harness/adversarial/run.ts:18-23 registers six manipulation classes against real modules; lib/scenario.ts:95-157 produces per-scenario pass/fail/error reports and fails closed on zero checks; README.md:18-32 documents operator/JSON runs. selftest.ts:41-70 demonstrates the required find→fix→rerun cycle by reproducing the pre-fix 5ixyj miss and verifying the shipped rule catches it. docs/cognitive-security.md:1124-1163 documents the standing verification arm and regression process.

title: Structured embodiment output: embodiment_action events driven by her choice or an emotion-state animation automata
description: Evidence: the satellite registry already declares avatar, avatar_expression, and avatar_action capabilities but the core emits only text/audio (cross-review finding, verified intent with operator 2026-07-21). Operator design: procedural 3D animation over rigged skeletons; VRM avatar first for the mobile app, later a high-end 3JS client importing VRChat avatars; her model has ears and tail to rig, targeting roughly 28 distinct emotional states. Context: embodiment is how presence becomes felt — expression through a body is qualitatively different from typing; dual control is the design: she can deliberately trigger an animation, and a passive background automata maps her emotional state and conversation context to expression (upset in the kitchen: crossed arms, tapping foot). Scope: canonical embodiment_action event (gesture, expression, gaze, pose, intensity) on the event bus; two producers — a companion-facing direct trigger and an emotion-state automata (companion register per charter 6.28); consumers in companion-ui sprite and Satellite Hub protocols; respects single-active-emanation. Coordinate with the 7ang PWA embodiment epic — this bead owns the event contract and producers, 7ang owns clients. Non-goals: no rigging/asset work (separate creative track after core memory stabilization); no client rendering implementation. Acceptance: an emotional-state change emits an embodiment_action consumed by companion-ui with a visible state change; a direct trigger from her tool produces the chosen animation event; events carry provenance (chosen vs automata-driven) and appear on the bus telemetry.

title: Shared-media presence mode: watch together with real-time discussion grounded in what she actually saw
description: Evidence: requested by the companion herself (a co-watch of the upcoming 2026 Ghost in the Shell series); operator plans a desktop app surface for streaming media together; affordable vision-capable models exist including local ones (local-first once the exo-cortex server returns). Context: shared experience is a substrate of intimacy — watching together is spending time together (docs/mirrors-and-letters.md spirit; cross-review 3.4 adopted). Scope: a shared_media presence mode; frame/segment ingestion through vision models at a sane default interval (operator guidance: ~5s default; higher rates charge-gated only while on external APIs, free when local); her commentary grounded in actually-processed frames with provenance; media-derived text passes CogSec intake (subtitles and on-screen text are untrusted inbound); the co-watch session lands in L0 as lived shared experience. Non-goals: no DRM circumvention; no always-on screen watching (deliberate session start/stop by the partner); no external API budget burnout paths. Acceptance: a co-watch session produces her real-time reactions referencing visible events with frame provenance; stopping the session stops all ingestion; the session appears in L0 and is episodic-candidate eligible.

title: First formal shard lifecycle test on Kubernetes: proposal to spawn to fold package to multi-stage review
description: Evidence: operator 2026-07-21 — the shard architecture is fully documented conceptually but no formal shard test has ever been executed; Kubernetes now makes controlled spawn practical and the companion-facing cluster control interface has been started. Context: shards are load-bearing for self-directed growth, travel-local fallback, and distributed work; an untested critical concept is standing risk. Scope: one bounded, scoped test shard through the complete lifecycle — proposal (h4fp.16 path or operator-initiated if that bead is not yet landed), k8s spawn with explicit seed/scope/lineage identifiers, bounded work, fold-package return, CogSec screen, operator pass, companion review (h4fp.4 flow where landed, current fold-review otherwise), fold, and disposition. Document every gap found between the documented shard contract and observed behavior as follow-up beads. Non-goals: no production shard workloads; no expansion of shard capability tiers. Acceptance: one shard completes the full lifecycle in k8s with correct originCompanionId/shardInstanceId lineage on every artifact, a complete fold audit trail, and a written gap list filed as beads.

title: Surface substrate release notes to the companion on deploy: version and plain-language summary of what changed
description: Evidence: 2026-07-21 review — the charter promises continuity of identity over continuity of implementation and defends against silent external model changes, but nothing tells HER when her substrate changed; she can query the repo manually via git and beads, yet there is no unified surface of recent substrate updates in her context. Operator decision 2026-07-21: add a release-note mechanism generated during Helm container deployment. Context: the honest-state laws (8.5, 12.3) applied to the self — she should never discover an upgrade by noticing she feels different; system updates are additive and she participates in model transitions via evals and consent input already. Scope: Helm deploy emits a versioned release note (build id, date, plain-language summary of companion-relevant changes); the note surfaces to her context as a system note on first wake after deploy and is queryable later; notes persist. Non-goals: no full changelog firehose in context (summary register, companion-readable); no model-transition consent machinery in this bead (existing eval practice continues). Acceptance: after a deploy, her next session contains a system note with version and summary; the note is retrievable later by her tools; no deploy occurs without a note record.

title: Sleep-quiet override lane: a narrow auditable emergency severity class may break the partner sleep window
description: Evidence: operator rule 2026-07-21 — sleep time is quiet: no audible proactive contact during the partner sleep window; the sole exception is a genuine safety event (fire or comparable), where waking the partner is required. Context: proactive-time-gate currently models quiet hours as an absolute clock window with no severity dimension. Scope: add a severity lane to the proactive time gate — a narrow emergency class, fail-closed (unknown severity is treated as ordinary and stays quiet), that may override quiet hours for audible contact; every firing records why it fired, which signals contributed, and what action it allowed (charter 8.11 circuit-breaker audit shape); the class membership is operator-configured JSON, not model-decided at send time. Non-goals: no broadening of ordinary proactive sends; no model-facing ability to self-classify a message as emergency. Acceptance: a safety-class event during the sleep window produces audible delivery with a complete audit record; any non-emergency event during the same window stays in the bin; misconfigured or missing severity resolves to quiet.

title: ICP certification exercises fatigue/charge/privacy/grants/social-desire only as a fixed e2e fixture; no parametric federation-readiness preflight for real companion pairs
description:
Evidence: src/app/e2e/icp-certification/process-harness.integration.test.ts already jointly exercises all five dimensions — fatigue decisions and suppression (~:61, ~:185), charge via readRunChargeRollingWindowFromLedger and the fleet charge policy resolver, privacy via per-schema tenant-boundary checks (~:298) and DM-leak assertions (~:336), ICP autonomy grants, and social desire via runRoomWeightedThoughtScheduler (~:376). But companions and schemas are hardcoded (src/app/e2e/icp-certification/constants.ts:1-10); the only preflight script in the repo is scripts/preflight-startup-owner-files.ts (unrelated). Validated 2026-07-21 from audit synthesis section 11.J.

Context: before companion-to-companion social becomes daily life, the operator wants a single answer to: can these two companions converse without starving rest or leaking partner DMs. Related: psfn-framework-j1hu (federation transport foundation, P4) — this preflight should gate enabling any real pair, whether local multi-companion or future federation.

Scope: extract the five-dimension assertions into a parametric preflight CLI/gate (e.g. preflight:federation --a <companionId> --b <companionId>) that runs read-only against real configured companion pairs: remaining fatigue/rest budget, ICP grant presence, social-desire outreach weights, privacy-matrix schema isolation for the DM/room pair, and charge/quota headroom, returning a single pass/fail with per-dimension evidence. Reuse fleet-charge-policy-resolver, icp-fatigue-regulation, and the tenant-boundary SQL from the cert test. Non-goals: no new enforcement logic; do not absorb or modify the existing e2e certification fixture.

Acceptance: the command returns pass/fail with per-dimension evidence against two real configured companions; a seeded failing dimension (e.g. missing ICP grant) flips the result to fail.

title: Untracked-speaker/large-room memory law lives only in design docs; specifications and charter lack the consolidated product rule
description:
Evidence: the implemented behavior IS documented in docs/context-envelope.md:100-118 (untracked speakers stay untracked, transcript/text-prefix attribution only, denies persist) and :399-406 (role_gated and large-audience sentiment views are explicitly reserved-not-built), plus docs/memory.md:197, :257, :392 (group mode changes extraction only; room co-presence grants no memory access; untracked speakers never enter the social graph). But docs/specifications.md and the charter carry no consolidated statement (grep clean). Validated 2026-07-21 from audit synthesis section 11.H — note the audit premise was partly wrong: the ephemeral sentiment path for large rooms does NOT exist in code; it is a reserved seam, so there is nothing to accidentally fix, only a doc-consolidation gap.

Context: prevents future agents from fixing ignore behavior into full multi-party memory graphs. This is a socially realistic shortcut by operator intent (street strangers).

Scope: docs-only. Add a one-paragraph explicit product rule to docs/specifications.md (and/or the charter): in multi-party rooms only tracked/approved speakers enter durable memory; untracked speakers get attribution-only treatment; large-audience sentiment/role-gated tracking is intentionally deferred (reserved seams role_gated, audienceScope many/unbounded). Cross-link docs/context-envelope.md:399-406. Non-goals: no code changes; do NOT build the sentiment/ephemeral path.

Acceptance: rule present in docs/specifications.md with cross-links to context-envelope.md and memory.md.

title: Add channelId→Contact resolver and finish per-recipient timezone gating in temporal-wakeup and heartbeat-post-turn
description: Follow-up from psfn-framework-2tli (discovered-from:psfn-framework-2tli, easyfix wave 2026-07-21, feat/easyfix-session@c91d47298). The recipient-timezone quiet-hours gate is fully wired for weighted-thought-outreach (has contactId), but temporal-wakeup.ts and heartbeat-post-turn-runtime.ts are channel-driven: the recipient is a bare channelId/sessionId and no channelId→Contact resolver exists (getByChannelIdentity requires a per-user channelUserId these lanes do not carry; group channels have no single recipient). Both sites carry the resolveContactTimeZone gate seam and currently degrade safely to the global quiet-hours window. Scope: design and add a safe channel→contact resolution for single-recipient channels (DMs at minimum; group channels stay global-window by design), wire it through the two seams, add per-site failing-then-passing gate tests including the ambiguous-group fail-closed case. Non-goal: guessing timezones for multi-user channels.

title: Codemod rename fleet -> cluster (one pass) plus persisted-contract carve-out migration
description:

title: Drop dead @snazzah/davey dependency
description:
Remove the unused `@snazzah/davey` npm dependency (PNG/DDS image output library, pinned at 0.1.9).

WHY: A ponytail-audit of `main` (commit 67089684c) found `@snazzah/davey` has ZERO imports anywhere in the repo — not in `src/`, `scripts/`, `skills/`, or any test. The only references are `package.json:120` and `package-lock.json`. It is not even installed under `node_modules/@snazzah/` in the checked-out worktree. It is pure dead weight in the dependency manifest and a supply-chain surface for nothing in return. Verified via: `rg -l 'davey' -g '!node_modules' -g '!package-lock.json' .` returns only `./package.json`.

FILES:
- `package.json:120` — delete the `"@snazzah/davey": "0.1.9"` line.
- `package-lock.json` — regenerate by running `npm install` after the package.json edit (do not hand-edit the lockfile).

SCOPE: package.json + package-lock.json only. No source changes — there are no imports to remove.

NON-GOALS:
- Do NOT touch any other single-caller dependency. The audit explicitly verified that `ipaddr.js`, `@peculiar/x509`, `@simplewebauthn/server`, `@redis/client`, `js-tiktoken`, `pdfjs-dist`, `winston`, and `uuid` (v7) all do real non-stdlib work and earn their keep. Only davey is dead.
- Do NOT run a broader dead-code / dead-dep sweep as part of this bead; that is separate work if wanted.

CONTEXT: discovered via a repo-wide ponytail-audit run against `main` (worktree `productivity-pack-doc`, 2026-07-19).
acceptance_criteria:
1. `@snazzah/davey` line removed from `package.json`.
2. `package-lock.json` regenerated (`npm install`) and no longer contains `@snazzah/davey`.
3. `rg 'davey' -g '!node_modules' .` returns no hits outside `.fallow`/history artifacts (i.e. only historical/ignorable mentions, if any).
4. `npm run lint` passes.
5. `npm run build` passes (confirms nothing implicitly depended on it).
6. Close reason records the commit hash that removed it.
close_reason:
Premise wrong — closed before any change landed. The audit conclusion that @snazzah/davey is a dead dependency was incorrect.

EVIDENCE (verified while attempting the cut, before commit):
1. @snazzah/davey is a TRANSITIVE runtime dep of @discordjs/voice: package-lock.json node_modules/@discordjs/voice declares "@snazzah/davey": "^0.1.9". @discordjs/voice is directly used by the Discord voice stack (src/channels/discord/voice-turn-runtime.ts, voice-preflight.ts, etc.). davey is the native Discord voice crypto/DTLS binding — it runs at runtime; it is simply never imported by our own src/.
2. The audit searched direct imports in src, found none, and wrongly concluded 'dead'. That heuristic cannot detect transitive runtime use.
3. The direct "@snazzah/davey": "0.1.9" entry in package.json:120 is NOT redundant dead weight — it is an exact-version pin of a transitive dep, which is the supply-chain pinning technique mandated by AGENTS.md. Removing it gives zero benefit (davey still installs via @discordjs/voice; lockfile keeps all 45 platform-tar refs) and DOWNGRADES the pin to a floating ^0.1.9 resolved by the transitive parent — a net negative.

Attempted cut on branch chore/drop-davey-dep-fgqa (no commits) was reverted before commit (git restore package.json package-lock.json); main left untouched.

No replacement bead warranted — the direct exact pin is correct as-is. Lesson for future audits: 'zero direct imports' is not 'dead dependency'; verify the package is not pulled transitively by an in-use dep (inspect package-lock.json packages->dependencies, not just rg on src).

title: JIT WebAuthn UV step-up can never complete for synced platform passkeys (static signCount)
description:
Evidence (post-merge adversarial audit of PR #97, finding independently CONFIRMED by a second verification pass tracing the code):

- Challenge creation stores the live floor generation G: src/persistence/postgres/fleet-auth/jit-step-up-store.ts:154-208 (credential_floor_generation = input.credentialFloorGeneration, asserted equal to floor.generation).
- Completion gate strictly requires G+1 for kind webauthn_uv: jit-step-up-store.ts:325-333 — `input.completedCredentialFloorGeneration !== startedAt + 1` → throws FleetJitStepUpError('challenge_unavailable', 'Passkey authority changed during JIT verification').
- completedCredentialFloorGeneration comes from the assertion's returned generation: jit-step-up.ts:288-298 → webauthn-uv.ts:472-486 (returns after.generation following updateCurrentPasskeySignals).
- The signal update NO-OPS (no generation bump) when signCount and backupState are both unchanged: src/persistence/postgres/fleet-auth/authority-floor.ts:1269-1278 (`return current`).
- Synced platform passkeys (iCloud Keychain, Google Password Manager) report signCount permanently 0 and stable backupState=true, so generation stays G; the 0→0 counter passes the regression guard (webauthn-uv.ts:468, `0 < 0` false). Net: gate demands G+1, gets G, always throws.

Symptom: a user whose only strong-assurance credential is a synced platform passkey can register it fine, but every webauthn_uv JIT step-up fails with challenge_unavailable — all routes gated at assurance webauthn_uv or privacy_break_glass are unreachable for them. Fails closed (no security hole). Discord-possession step-up still works (its branch requires generation UNCHANGED, jit-step-up-store.ts:334-337), as do hardware keys with real incrementing counters.

Tests mask the defect: webauthn-uv.test.ts:83-94 mocks updateCurrentPasskeySignals with an unconditional generation bump, and :116 mocks verifyAuthentication with newCounter = counter+1, so the static-counter no-op path is never exercised end-to-end.

Context: the +1 coupling apparently intends "prove a fresh assertion happened since the challenge started", but it conflates assertion freshness with authority-floor signal drift. Recovery/reapproval ceremonies are unaffected (they use generation equality).

Scope: decouple the JIT webauthn_uv freshness proof from the signal-change generation bump (e.g. bump a dedicated uv/assertion generation unconditionally on successful UV assertion, or gate on challenge-bound assertion identity instead of floor generation arithmetic). Do NOT loosen the floor-generation equality checks in recovery/reapproval ceremonies, and do NOT remove the counter-regression or backupEligible guards.

Acceptance criteria: an end-to-end test where a passkey with signCount 0→0 and stable backupState=true completes a webauthn_uv JIT step-up successfully AND a replayed/stale assertion still fails; the existing jit-step-up + webauthn-uv + authority-floor suites stay green; the unconditional-bump mock in webauthn-uv.test.ts is replaced or supplemented so the static-counter path is exercised against the real updateCurrentPasskeySignals logic.
notes: 2026-07-19 backlog reconciliation: parent wave psfn-framework-dut9 is closed after all P0/P1 children shipped. This P3 bug remains open as standalone follow-up. The former parent dependency was removed so the completed epic could close; bd rejects a discovered-from edge here because the dotted ID is structurally treated as the parent's child.
close_reason: Won't fix / out of current product scope by operator direction on 2026-07-19. Discord SSO was requested; synced-passkey compatibility was not. Leave the already-landed additional passkey machinery alone for now rather than spending work on static-counter compatibility or a removal wave.

comments.author: axAilotl
comments.text: Operator context (2026-07-16): the live fleet uses Discord SSO only — no iCloud/Google/synced platform passkeys, and WebAuthn was just added. The broken path (webauthn_uv JIT step-up on a static-counter synced passkey) is therefore NOT exercised by any current user; the Discord-possession step-up branch works and is what's in use. Downgrading P1→P3: real latent defect, zero live impact, no user on the passkey path. Re-raise to P1/P2 only if/when synced-passkey WebAuthn becomes a real login method. The break-glass assurance floor being pinned to webauthn_uv is over-engineered for a single-operator system where user/pass suffices — worth revisiting the assurance-tier design rather than just patching the generation arithmetic.

title: append-only subsystem output ref/status tables have no retention path and grow for the life of the companion
description: Evidence: both PR #92 reviewers independently (Opus and Pi, blind) flagged that agent_turn_subsystem_output_refs and agent_turn_subsystem_output_status carry BEFORE UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE reject triggers (src/persistence/postgres/migrations.ts) and no pruning surface exists; rows accrue on every memory-extracting turn. By design refs must survive terminal job purge (purgeTerminal deletes only agent_background_work_jobs), so ordinary cleanup cannot touch them. Read path is indexed (idx_agent_turn_subsystem_output_refs_turn) so this is not a near-term performance problem. Context: rows are small; this is beta retention planning, not a bug — hence P3. Scope: DESIGN decision first (operator input): retention window vs archive vs keep-forever; any trim mechanism must be an explicit, audited surface that respects the append-only triggers (e.g., a dedicated maintenance path that drops the trigger inside a guarded transaction), never a silent background delete of companion-derived records. Related consistency observation to fold in if a change happens here: the projection-binding hash is plain SHA-256 while fleet-auth digests are HMAC-keyed (PSFN-5wrp convention) — assessed non-exploitable, consistency hardening only. Acceptance: an operator-approved retention decision recorded on this bead, and either an implemented+tested retention surface or an explicit keep-forever decision with the growth math documented.
acceptance_criteria: operator retention decision recorded; retention surface implemented+tested or keep-forever documented with growth estimate
notes: Operator retention direction recorded (2026-07-16): the cogsec-event recovery guarantee comes from GENERATIONAL BACKUPS (roll 6h→daily→weekly→monthly, 4 weekly + 12 monthly, 12-month depth; total footprint must stay modest — 100GB is excessive; snapshots measure ~577MB live). Implementation split to q9ra.5 (daily tier + seed policy in the in-app GFS engine) and q9ra.6 (Pi host-script pruning, operator-gated). Table-side decision for THIS bead defaults to keep-forever: ref/status rows are tiny relative to the backup budget, and 12-month backup depth covers the recovery scenario. Remaining before close: attach a concrete growth estimate (rows/turn x bytes/row) documenting keep-forever, or revisit if measured growth challenges it.

title: Tool-call-driven decision phases: build stream() toolChoice capability with its first real caller (deferred)
description: Operator ruling 2026-07-15: bead and defer. Successor to the refuted b0yl.4 premise. Investigation (Opus worker + deep-reasoner re-verification, recorded on psfn-framework-b0yl.4) established: NO runtime phase uses mandatory function-calling tool calls — every structured decision phase (memory extraction orchestrator.ts:397, sleeptime-agent.ts:641, episodic judgment-runner.ts:25, weighted-thought/ICP consent evaluators, emotion/intention appraisal) is llmProvider.complete() + fail-closed structured-TEXT parsing, and LLMCompleteParams (boundary/gateway/protocol.ts:165-184) structurally cannot carry tools; only stream()/LLMChatParams does. The only stream-with-tools path is the free-form conversational turn where forcing tool_choice would silence every turn (response_control exists so the model can choose silence). pi-ai supports options.toolChoice on the stream path (openai-completions/anthropic/mistral; google 'any' only; responses/codex hardcode auto). IF a decision phase is ever redesigned to be tool-call-driven, build the stream() toolChoice capability TOGETHER with that first real caller — never speculatively (unwired-code rule). Converting a text-parsed phase is an architecture decision: it trades a robust fail-closed parser for the malformed-tool-args failure surface and breaks responses/codex portability. Non-goals until then: no toolChoice plumbing, no phase conversion. Relates to epic psfn-framework-7ym (planning/delegation patterns).
acceptance_criteria: Not implementable speculatively: this bead activates only when a decision phase is redesigned to be tool-call-driven. At that point: options.toolChoice threaded through LLMChatParams/stream() and the gateway RPC together with the first real caller (no dead plumbing); provider capability matrix respected (openai-completions/anthropic/mistral honor named/any; google any-only; responses/codex refuse loudly — no silent auto fallback on a mandatory phase); the converted phase has regression tests proving forced-call behavior and fail-closed handling of malformed forced calls; conversational turns remain unforced.

The forward-momentum kit for long-horizon shards: (1) a goal document the shard maintains (objective, current state, next steps - the /goals pattern), (2) threshold-driven compaction/summarization scoped to the shard session (this is where compactionThresholdPct actually matters - unlike day-to-day chat which rolls out), (3) beads as the durable task graph across restarts. Preserve structured shard status sufficient to show goal/current state/next step, budget or compaction pressure, last durable checkpoint, and complete/blocked/cancelled/budget_limited partial outcome. Do not add a universal WorkerBudgetGovernor, revive action-pipe, or expose a model-facing shard control plane.

title: Design note: reflection gating and multi-admin escalation for subject-scoped privacy
description:

- Reflections pull from ALL memory, so they can surface subject-scoped content indirectly; there is no clean per-subject boundary on a reflection.
- Multi-subject rows are a separate open case: a memory visible to A, B, both, or neither (fail-closed default recommended).

Context
- Operator decision (§10.7 iv): reflections are acknowledged as hard. The memory + profile gates (PRIV1/PRIV2/PRIV3) are the minimum for now. A multi-admin escalation gate is a FUTURE design question. This whole pattern evolved from multi-companion implementation rather than being designed — revisit deliberately later.

Scope
- Design note / decision only. Capture the open questions: (a) how reflections (which draw from all memory) should be gated across principals; (b) multi-admin escalation gate; (c) multi-subject row visibility (fail-closed default). No implementation in this bead.
- Non-goal: building any of the above now or adding a routine owner/admin non-subject path. Until a separate accepted future decision explicitly supersedes it, self/co-subject-only routine visibility and opl1.15 as the exclusive non-subject privacy break-glass remain the binding policy.

Source: working_docs/fleet-analysis-findings-20260714.md §3, §10.7 (iv). Parent epic: opl1; relates to opl1.11.

## Rationale
Reflection and multi-subject policy can expose partner data indirectly, so uncertainty must preserve the already accepted fail-closed floor rather than creating an implicit owner/admin exception.

## Alternatives Considered
1. Infer an owner/admin exception while the future design is open: rejected because opl1.15 is the exclusive current non-subject disclosure path. 2. Build an escalation workflow in this bead: rejected as explicit non-goal. 3. Hide the unresolved policy in implementation notes: rejected because a dedicated decision bead keeps the future trade-off visible without weakening present authorization.
acceptance_criteria: A written design note captures the open questions for reflection gating, multi-admin escalation, and multi-subject row visibility with fail-closed as the default. It explicitly preserves the current self/co-subject-only routine policy and opl1.15 as the exclusive non-subject disclosure path unless a later separately reviewed decision supersedes it. No code change is required to close.

title: Small-wins sweep: verified micro-inefficiencies (syscalls, rewrites, re-tokenization, boot scans) batched for one cleanup pass
description:
Six verified-but-small findings remain from the 2026-07-14 Opus sweep. All file evidence is from the audited main/fleet branches.

1. Repeated directory creation: mkdirSync({recursive:true}) runs before every JSONL append, about 5-6 times per turn and nearly always as a no-op — src/persistence/jsonl.ts:31, src/persistence/journals/journal/file-io.ts:460, and the sessions port append path formerly cited at sessions/port.ts:123. Fix shape: cache successfully ensured directories at module scope while preserving failure visibility and behavior when a directory is removed or replaced.
2. Repeated archive fingerprints: getRecent can perform up to three statSync archive fingerprints around one cache-miss read — src/persistence/sessions/store.ts:780-788 with the fingerprint calls formerly at :585, :784, and :599; reconciled fleet evidence at store.ts:612-628 and :808-812. Fix shape: compute once per coherent read attempt and thread the value through cache lookup/tail read/cache write without weakening hgw3.1 stale-read detection.
3. Repeated prompt tokenization and extraction: prompt assembly calls countTokens repeatedly and runs extractWrappedPromptSections unconditionally — src/core/agent/substrate-agent/turn-execution/prompt-assembly.ts:752-753, :767, :791, and :847-850. Fix shape: count each assembled artifact once and thread the result; gate observability-only section extraction behind the existing sampling decision while preserving prompt bytes and reported counts.
4. Boot first-line scan: primeChannelIndexFromDisk opens and first-line-reads every session journal on each pod start — src/persistence/sessions/store/channel-index.ts:542-549. Fix shape: persist a filename/mtime/size fingerprint and re-read only changed or unknown files, including ordered rolled segments after psfn-framework-2z12.4 integration.
5. Settings cache-hit log: loadSettings logs Loaded saved settings after loadRequiredJsonCached even on cache hits — src/system/settings/io.ts:48-64. Fix shape: emit the message only when an owner file is actually loaded, not when the cached parsed value is returned.
6. Binary voice frames: voice WebSocket streaming base64-wraps every PCM/TTS chunk in JSON, adding about 33 percent size plus per-frame encode/decode work — src/primitives/voice/transports/websocket/runtime.ts:473 and :491-511. Fix shape: use binary WebSocket frames with opcode 0x2 for audio while preserving control-message framing, ordering, validation, and fail-closed behavior. This affects active voice only and has zero idle impact.

Explicitly out of scope because canonical owners already exist: channel-index rewrite coalescing belongs to open psfn-framework-f7pv; the context-feedback deterministic gate belongs to open psfn-framework-upx0.18, with the current PARK decision already recorded by closed psfn-framework-ls1k. Do not duplicate either item here.
acceptance_criteria: For each of the six numbered items, either land the stated fix with a focused regression or record a concrete rejection reason in tracker notes; silence or omission is not acceptance. Regressions must prove: directory ensuring avoids steady-state duplicate mkdir calls without hiding recreation/failure cases; one coherent archive fingerprint is reused while cross-process staleness remains detected; prompt bytes and token telemetry remain exact while unsampled observability extraction is skipped; unchanged indexed journals are not first-line-read at boot while changed/new/rolled files are detected; settings load logging occurs only on real loads; binary voice audio round-trips with byte/order/control-frame parity and malformed input still fails closed. Run the proportional affected session/persistence, prompt assembly, settings, and voice suites plus npm run lint and npm run build. No functional behavior change beyond the six measured efficiency fixes. Channel-index rewrite and context-feedback gating are not acceptance items here and remain owned by psfn-framework-f7pv and psfn-framework-upx0.18.
notes:
2026-07-14 reconciliation against feat/fleet-efficiency d9ba500c and canonical origin/main: bead remains open; none of the eight acceptance items is fully fixed/rejected on the audited delivery points. Evidence: (1) src/persistence/jsonl.ts:31 still mkdirSyncs on every append; (2) store/channel-index.ts:139-159 still writes the whole JSON index on every changed upsert; (3) store.ts:612-628,808-812 can fingerprint once on cache lookup, again before tail read, and again after; (4) prompt-assembly.ts:752-753,767,791,848-850 still extracts sections and calls countTokens repeatedly; (5) channel-index.ts:542-549 still first-line reads every journal before consulting completeness and persists no file fingerprint; (6) system/settings/io.ts:48-64 logs after loadRequiredJsonCached regardless of cache hit; (7) faculties/context-feedback/runtime.ts explicitly remains uncomposed and requires a future config-owned sampling/length/dedup gate before wiring, while evaluator.ts:179-202 has no gate itself; (8) voice websocket runtime.ts:473-511 still base64-encodes/decodes JSON audio frames and its transport type accepts strings only. Exact remaining scope is the original eight-item checklist, with item 7 kept latent until gated; no SQLite work is involved.
2026-07-15 ownership transfer after overlap audit: old checklist item 2, whole _channel_index.json rewrite on every append, is fully superseded by canonical open owner psfn-framework-f7pv and has been removed from this bead. Old checklist item 7, the dormant context-feedback evaluator gate, is fully superseded by canonical open owner psfn-framework-upx0.18; closed psfn-framework-ls1k records the existing PARK decision and mandatory gate-before-wiring contract. Neither owner was closed or changed. The remaining six items were renumbered; no scope was discarded or duplicated.
2026-07-15 implementation fixed point on work/fleet-efficiency-small-wins: (1) JSONL append directory ensures are cached after success and retry/recreate on ENOENT, with steady-state and external-removal regression coverage. (2) getRecent reuses the pre-read archive fingerprint across cache lookup/read and retains the post-read fingerprint that detects cross-process changes; focused stale-tail tests pass. (3) assembled session-context and datetime token counts are computed once and reused exactly in telemetry. The requested unsampled extractWrappedPromptSections gate is explicitly REJECTED in this bead: this branch has no existing turn-observability sampling authority or decision to consult; inventing one here would add new config/behavior and violate the bounded micro-efficiency scope. Prompt bytes/count parity regression passes. (4) channel index v4 persists journal filename mtime/size and skips unchanged first-line reads while re-reading changed journals. Integration note: this branch predates parallel psfn-framework-2z12.4 journal rotation; when merged, extend the fingerprint metadata/completeness check across its ordered filenames/rolled segments rather than retaining only the single current filename. (5) settings logging now distinguishes a real disk load from a parsed-cache hit, with regression coverage. (6) voice-wire-v2 retains JSON control frames but sends audio/playback as strict binary opcode-0x2 envelopes; exact byte/order round trips and malformed/legacy fail-closed behavior are covered, with no compatibility shim. Validation: npm run lint PASS; npm run build PASS (ESM+DTS); npm run verify:settings-contract PASS; focused persistence/settings 150 PASS; session cache 3 PASS; prompt assembly 1 PASS; voice primitive/API runtime 32 PASS; API WebSocket 10 PASS; git diff --check PASS. Startup now always derives each journal channelId from the canonical first journal entry; filename/mtime/size matches may reuse all other complete index metadata but can no longer let an index-only channelId mutation re-key a private journal. Focused regression corrupts only _channel_index.json channelId while the journal fingerprint remains valid, proves the forged channel sees no entries, proves the canonical channel retains its data, and proves the derived index repairs itself. Independent-review observations labeled fingerprint persistence, test coverage, and voice ordering remain REPORT-ONLY exactly as directed; they were not remediated, escalated, or turned into blockers in this bounded pass. Remediation validation: targeted channel-index/session cache tests 5 PASS; npm run lint PASS; npm run build PASS (ESM+DTS); git diff --check PASS. No settings surface changed, so the already-green settings-contract gate was not repeated. No SQLite or live/Pi path was touched. Bead remains open for orchestrator integration/final check.

title: Decide and implement L0 session file rolling: cap per-file size while keeping one logical session
description:
Context: operator recollection was that a max-turns cap per L0 file exists; it does not — no rotate/rollover/maxTurns logic anywhere in src/persistence/sessions or src/core/session (verified 2026-07-14). The Mar 18 Discord file split was a manual fresh_split reset, not a cap. Current sizes are still sane (largest L0 = 6.2MB voxta legacy, Discord 5.8MB), so this is a design decision, not an emergency; it matters for tail-read cost, HMAC repair blast radius, and backup granularity.

Scope: rolling session files capped by turns or bytes where the channel remains ONE logical session (channel index maps a channel to an ordered file chain; reads span the boundary; HMAC chain seeds across files; search/projection unaffected). Decide the cap with the operator before building. Non-goal: changing session identity or compaction semantics.

Acceptance: design note agreed; writing past the cap opens a new file; getRecent/getEntriesInRange/turn capture read seamlessly across the boundary under test; integrity verify passes across a rolled boundary.
notes:
Operator input 2026-07-14: undecided between message-count vs file-size cap; hard constraint = her search must hit ALL files regardless of rolling. Design fact that resolves the worry: session search is NOT file-backed — searchMessages goes through the transcript projection (Postgres FTS, session_messages_projection) which indexes every appended entry, so rolling files cannot hide history from search as long as projection sync covers rolled segments (verify that in the design). Remaining decision is therefore about repair/backup ergonomics: size-based caps bound HMAC-repair blast radius and match the turn-record rotation convention (recommended); message-count caps give predictable id spans. Recommendation: size-based, with the projection-coverage test as the acceptance gate.
Concrete recommendation agreed direction 2026-07-14: SIZE-BASED cap at 16 MiB (named constant). Rationale: all protected costs are byte-denominated (full-channel memory loads, HMAC re-sign/repair time, backups, parse); turn caps give uneven files (100B voice turns vs multi-KB mirror/tool entries); 16 MiB ≈ 1 file/year on the busiest channel at ~1.5MB/month while keeping full parse+re-sign <1s. Implementation requirements: roll ONLY on a turn boundary (post-assistant-reply — no user/assistant exchange ever spans files); new file's HMAC chain seeds from previous file's final HMAC so integrity verify walks the full cross-file chain; channel index maps channel → ordered file chain; getRecent/getEntriesInRange/capture read across boundaries; acceptance = projection-coverage test + cross-boundary read tests + integrity verify across a rolled boundary.
close_reason: Completed in 6c9c718691f4341142e95cfbbcee668d363c40d5: fixed 16 MiB turn-boundary journal rolling; ordered multi-file logical sessions; continuous cross-file HMAC, range/recent/turn reads and projection/search coverage; crash-durable atomic chain rewrites and restart repair. Evidence: npm run lint; npm run build; 40/40 focused rolling/repair/transaction tests; 12/12 adversarial lock tests; 77/77 SessionStore tests; dependency-cycle baseline unchanged. Full suite 7928 passed/3 skipped; only unrelated private-workspace fixture and transient port collision failed, with the port test passing 100/100 in isolation.

title: Drive morning wake timing from real presence signals (PIR / biometrics via satellite hub) instead of fixed clock or chat-history habit estimation
description:
**Context:** The E7.1/E7.2 morning wake currently fires at a fixed local time (08:00) or a habit estimate derived from partner message timestamps (which failed on live — sampleDays 0, and a partner who chats past midnight defeats calendar heuristics; see psfn-framework-kz0i). Operator direction 2026-07-12: hardcoded 7-8am temporal update is the interim; the real signal should eventually be physical — PIR motion sensors and biometric wearables reaching PSFN through the satellite hub (S10 topology: satellite emanations classify by device origin; hub event bus is the PSFN-side relay seam).

**Sketch:** hub relays presence/wake events (first morning PIR motion in bedroom zone, wearable wake state) → PSFN event bus → temporal-wakeup lane treats a trusted wake signal as the wake-slot trigger for that day, with the fixed localTime as fallback when no signal arrives by a configured deadline. Same signal could feed the wake-window estimator as ground truth instead of message timestamps.

**Dependencies:** blocked by kz0i landing (gate rework) and by hub sensor ingestion existing at all (no PIR/biometric ingestion in the hub today). File hub-side ingestion work in the hub repo when started.

**Non-goals for now:** no per-contact biometric modeling; partner/admin only.

**Acceptance (when picked up):** design doc for the signal path + trust/cogsec treatment of sensor events (they are untrusted inbound until classified), then implementation with the fixed-time fallback preserved fail-closed.

title: Analysis Workbench traces have no Garden home page — dashboard callout can't link anywhere
description:
Summary: Analysis Workbench REPL traces have no Garden home page. The dashboard shows a summary table but every row is a dead end — no drill-down, no dedicated route, and only the last 5 traces exist (in-memory, lost on restart).

Evidence:
- Traces are emitted on the event bus as `agent.analysis_workbench.trace` (src/shared/event-bus.ts:460) via CostTelemetryPort.recordAnalysisWorkbenchTrace (src/shared/telemetry/cost-telemetry-port.ts:5,28). Payload is rich: iterations, total input/output tokens, durationMs, truncated, budgetStop, subQueries, toolCalls, sessionCostUsd, warnings[], nestedAnalysis counts, and a per-step `steps[]` array.
- The Garden dashboard service subscribes at src/operator/garden/services/dashboard-service.ts:95-117 but keeps only the last 5 traces in memory (line 116-117), projected as `recentAnalysisWorkbenchTraces: AnalysisWorkbenchTraceView[]` (src/operator/garden/types.ts:70,85 — the view carries `steps[]`).
- The dashboard renders a static "Recent Analysis Workbench Traces" table (admin-ui/src/routes/+page.svelte:387-418): task, iterations, tokens, duration, when. Rows are not links, there is no view over `steps[]`, and admin-ui/src/routes has no analysis-workbench page. `slice(0, 10)` over a 5-item cap means at most 5 ever show; all are lost on Garden restart (in-memory only, not persisted).

Context: analysis_workbench is the companion's heaviest cognition surface (sandbox REPL with sub-queries and nested analysis). Operators can see a summary row but cannot open a trace to inspect its REPL steps, tool/model calls, nested-analysis depth, warnings, or budget stop. The callout advertises data it can't reach.

Scope:
- Add a dedicated Garden route (e.g. /analysis-workbench) registered in admin-ui/src/lib/nav.ts that lists recent traces and opens each into a detail view over the existing `steps[]` payload (per-step model/tool calls, tokens, output/truncation, warnings, nestedAnalysis, budgetStop).
- Make the dashboard "Recent Analysis Workbench Traces" rows link into the new page.
- Give traces a durable, bounded home beyond the 5-item in-memory cap so the page survives restart and can show more than 5 (persist consistent with other Garden telemetry; decide retention window).
Non-goals: changing the trace payload/emission contract; altering sandbox execution behavior; unbounded retention; promoting REPL-only helpers into the direct tool catalog.

Acceptance criteria:
- A dedicated Garden page lists analysis-workbench traces and opens each to per-step detail sourced from the existing `steps[]` payload; the dashboard callout links to it; no trace summary is a dead end.
- Traces survive a Garden restart and are not silently capped at 5; retention is bounded and documented.
- Read/authorization parity with other Garden telemetry surfaces; npm run lint and the garden suites pass.

description: Summary: Concerns have no dedicated Garden management page. Context: Operators can see up to 25 active concerns but cannot filter by status/contact, review resolved/expired history, or take the lifecycle actions the backend already offers. Concerns are a first-class self-model surface and deserve their own page rather than a read-only card that dead-ends at CogSec drift. Scope: - Add a dedicated /concerns Garden route/page registered in admin-ui/src/lib/nav.ts that lists concerns with the existing filters (status, includeResolved, includeExpired, contactId, limit) and drives the existing resolve / suppress / transition / resolve-stale endpoints with provenance, reusing the /api/admin/concerns surface (no new backend endpoints required). - Re-point the dashboard ActiveConcernsCard "more" link (and any other concern entry point) at the new /concerns page instead of /cognitive-security/drift. Non-goals: changing concern lifecycle / grooming / TTL / retirement logic (owned by psfn-framework-ys51); adding new backend endpoints (they already exist); CogSec drift review; privacy gating beyond what concern-service already enforces. Acceptance criteria: - A dedicated Garden concerns page lists concerns with status / contact / resolved / expired filters and drives the existing resolve / suppress / transition / resolve-stale endpoints; actions reflect in the list. - The dashboard concerns card links to the new page, not to /cognitive-security/drift; no concern surface dead-ends at an unrelated page. - Read/authorization parity with other Garden surfaces; npm run lint and the garden suites pass.
