title: Supply-chain compromise feeds wired into the dependency-update cycle (not in-app)
description: Operator decision 2026-07-09: free supply-chain compromise feeds/lists (that notify on recent npm/GitHub hits) are worth wiring into the dependency-UPDATE cycle -- not needed inside the app now. Rationale: compromises usually surface publicly within ~an hour; the risk window is an auto-update pulling a compromised package before anyone notices -- which is exactly why the project does NOT auto-update: pin, then plan updates deliberately. Scope: pick 1-2 free feeds (e.g. OSV, GitHub Advisory Database, Socket/StepSecurity-style free tiers -- evaluate at implementation), add a check step to the deliberate update workflow (script under scripts/ or CI job that runs when lockfile changes) that cross-references pending upgrades against recent advisories and fails loudly on a hit; document the pin-then-plan policy in docs/operations.md. Non-goals: no runtime/in-app scanning, no auto-remediation, no new always-on service. Acceptance: lockfile-diff check runs in the update workflow and demonstrably flags a known-bad package version from advisory test data; operations doc records the policy.

title: Canary tokens in privileged context as egress tripwire
description: Borrowed from rebuff (Apache-2.0, archived -- vendor the idea, not the code): plant a per-session secret canary token in privileged context (system-layer prompt material); watch outbound content and tool parameters at the gateway egress boundary for the token. A canary appearing in egress = prompt leak / hijack in progress -> CogSec event + hold the outbound action for review. Cheap, deterministic, catches the class of attack where injection succeeded despite the intake layers (defense in depth for the mindwall). Scope: token generation per session, injection into the PromptPlan static layer, egress scan at the gateway boundary (src/boundary/gateway/), event + hold path. Rotation per session so a leaked token has no replay value. Depends-on: psfn-framework-htm9.1. Acceptance: a simulated leak (canary echoed into an outbound message/tool param) is caught at the gateway, the action is held, and a CogSecEvent records it; benign turns pay near-zero latency (substring scan); token never appears in Loom-visible logs in cleartext.

title: 'Heartbeat' naming misleads: runtime is reflection/post-turn machinery, not a blind periodic LLM pass
description: Rename the runtime reflection and post-turn orchestration machinery that is historically called heartbeat, because PSFN does not run blind periodic LLM heartbeat passes. The genuine scheduler heartbeat is a liveness watchdog that emits health state and performs no companion behavior; it may retain heartbeat terminology. Port the stranded implementation from e7158d050 onto current origin/main: rename focused files, imports, source symbols, tests, and operator-facing labels from heartbeat runtime/template/policy/post-turn names to reflection or post-turn names. Preserve behavior, cadences, gates, tool schemas, and schedule actions. Preserve persisted/wire-compatible string values such as heartbeat.run_template, internal:heartbeat session IDs, persisted task/source kinds, correlation stages, and the heartbeat-policy.json artifact, documenting why source symbols and persisted values differ. Scope is repository code only. Non-goals: no live cluster rollout, no PVC/config mutation, no channels.json heartbeatChannelId owner-key migration, no companion-data rewrite, no scheduler watchdog removal/behavior change, and no reflection novelty or deliberation redesign.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime reflection/template/policy and post-turn files and source symbols no longer use heartbeat as their conceptual name; the genuine liveness watchdog remains clearly distinct; persisted action/session/source/correlation/config string values required for compatibility remain unchanged and are documented at their definition sites; behavior-preserving focused scheduler/composition/Garden tests pass; npm run build and npm run lint pass. Live rollout and owner-file migration are explicitly outside this bead.
notes:

Census evidence: the registered heartbeat task is a pure liveness beat (schedule.healthcheck emit + presence upsert, ZERO LLM; scheduler-runtime.ts:254); the LLM work lives in the separate reflection:* template tasks. Suggested: liveness-beat/presence-beat for the task id + Garden label.
Operator scope correction 2026-07-21: this bead/PR is code implementation only—rename reflection/post-turn runtime machinery so it is not called heartbeat. Fleet/cluster rollout, live config/PVC mutation, and deployment validation are separate work and are explicitly out of scope here. Recover the stranded e7158d050 implementation onto current origin/main, preserving behavior and persisted action compatibility.
Recovery published 2026-07-21 as draft PR #195 from commit 2abd55597. The historical e7158d050 implementation was ported and rebased onto current origin/main as one code-only commit. Preserved genuine liveness heartbeat terminology plus persisted/wire/tool-schema compatibility values; no live rollout, PVC/config mutation, channels.json owner-key migration, or companion-data rewrite. Validation on the rebased/remediated branch: npm run lint passed; npm run build passed; 446 focused runtime tests passed; 136 review-remediation tests passed; 4 Garden UI tests passed; hardcoded-settings guard passed during implementation. title: Four system-config modules each reimplement positive-integer validation
description:

Config validation is fail-closed territory; four implementations free to diverge on rounding/inclusivity semantics is latent inconsistency in exactly the place the settings-contract guard exists to prevent it.

title: Numeric clamp helpers are privately redeclared 25+ times across subsystems
description:
Summary:
Roughly 25+ private redeclarations of the same three tiny numeric helpers — clampUnit (0..1), clampSigned (-1..1), clamp(value, min, max), all `Math.max(min, Math.min(max, v))` with a finite-check fallback — because no shared numeric-utils module exists. Sites found 2026-07-06:
- memory: types.ts:616-624 and writer.ts:280-288 (byte-identical to each other), extraction/importance.ts:40-43, extraction/config.ts:23-25, retrieval/scoring.ts:456-458 (identical exported clamp pair), retrieval.ts:2300-2308, retrieval-compose.ts:61, boundary-log.ts:54-56, sleeptime-agent.ts:185-198
- shards: fold-review.ts:110-119, output-review.ts:180-189
- self-model: metacognition.ts:592, state.ts:1154
- session: manager-primitives.ts:857
- emotion: state.ts:218-224, scoped-emotion.ts:54-62, observer.ts:515-521, participant-trends.ts:44-54, audio-classifier.ts:505, persona-adaptation.ts:424-538 (five clamp functions in one file)
- eval: observer-sidecar/projection.ts:936-944, observer-sidecar/crosswalk.ts:1027
- intention: weighted-thoughts.ts:114-118
- contacts: store/emotional-baseline.ts:25-30, store/social-graph.ts:34

Suggested implementation direction:
clampUnit(value, fallback?), clampSigned(value, fallback?), clamp(value, min, max) in a new src/shared/utils/numeric.ts. Single mechanical sweep; each site is a 2-4 line no-risk swap. Watch the minor variance in finite-check branching style — pick one semantic (non-finite → fallback) and verify no site depends on a different one.

Acceptance criteria:
- Shared module exists; listed sites migrated; behavior identical (spot-check the finite-fallback variance).
- npm run lint passes before close.
close_reason: Merged in 32ce74f0 (commit d61795f4): src/shared/utils/numeric.ts with clamp/clampUnit/clampSigned (overloads honor explicit undefined fallback); 26 sites migrated, 6 left with verified divergent semantics (midpoint fallbacks, NaN-passthrough crosswalk, throw-before-clamp patterns, integer clamp) documented in the agent report. Merge conflict in heartbeat-template-runtime resolved: local clampUnit dropped for shared import, dead estimateDeliberationCostUsd not restored. Post-merge: build pass; 1361/1362 across 121 touched suites (1 failure = known pwzk baseline).

title: JSONL line-reading is reimplemented 9+ times; two appends bypass appendJsonLine
description:
Summary:
The JSONL line-read pattern (existsSync guard → readFileSync → trim-empty guard → split('\n') → map(trim) → filter(Boolean) → per-line try-parse-skip) is independently reimplemented at least 9 times, while src/persistence/jsonl.ts already owns the write side (appendJsonLine) and would be the natural home for the reader:
- src/persistence/journals/reflection-journal.ts:238-256
- src/persistence/journals/reflection-metacognition-journal.ts:393-412
- src/persistence/journals/reflection-substrate.ts:245-262
- src/core/identity/prompt-registry.ts:405-413
- src/core/identity/card-versioning.ts:122-131
- src/core/session/continuity-artifacts.ts:214-232
- src/core/internal-role-envelopes/store.ts:247-263
- src/persistence/sessions/turn-records.ts:456-469
- src/persistence/artifact-lifecycle/manager.ts:114-121
- src/core/identity/prompt-store.ts:425-440 (lower-level fd variant, same intent)

Two appends also bypass appendJsonLine, reimplementing mkdir+appendFileSync:
- src/faculties/memory/journal.ts:52-61 (MemoryJournal.append)
- src/core/intention/outreach-outbox.ts:159-165

Why it matters:
Nine independent readers means nine independent (and today inconsistent) error-handling/logging decisions for corrupt lines. Consolidation reduces bug surface and makes update behavior uniform.

Suggested implementation direction:
Add readJsonLines<T>(path, normalize: (raw: unknown) => T | null, opts?: { onError?, warnLabel? }) to src/persistence/jsonl.ts, returning parsed entries plus a skipped/corrupt count. Migrate the listed readers; route the two appends through appendJsonLine.

Non-goals:
- Do NOT fold in src/persistence/journals/journal/file-io.ts — it is a genuinely different streaming forward/backward scanner (chunked fd reads, quarantine sidecar, tail-limit scanning) solving a different problem.

Acceptance criteria:
- One reader primitive; listed sites migrated; corrupt-line handling preserved or explicitly improved (no new silent skips — surface skipped counts where callers logged before).
- Both bespoke appends use appendJsonLine.
- npm run lint passes before close.
close_reason: Merged (commit c7ae4ed9): readJsonLines<T> added to persistence/jsonl.ts returning {entries, skipped, corrupt}; 10 readers + 2 appends + outreach-outbox read-side migrated; prompt-store.ts fd scanner deliberately left (different bounded-recovery behavior). Post-merge: build pass, 519 tests green across persistence/identity/internal-role-envelopes suites.

title: Straggler LLM call sites lack baseline correlation metadata or swallow errors silently
description:
Summary:
Most LLM call sites populate full correlation metadata (requestId/turnId/channelId/callType/purpose/originType/originStage). The 2026-07-06 audit found stragglers below baseline:
1. src/core/session/compression-guideline.ts:587-610 (runPeriodicGuidelineUpdate) — weakest-instrumented bespoke path in the codebase: inline prompt, ZERO correlation metadata, no retry, no local catch; the error propagates to generic scheduler-level logging (src/app/agent/scheduler-runtime.ts:99-113) with no LLM-observability fields at all. Same shape as the search-runtime finding in psfn-framework-7ozg but with a thinner safety net. Consider a PromptRegistry key while touching it.
2. src/core/intention/appraisal/evaluator.ts:159-162 (DEFAULT_SYSTEM_PROMPT from types.ts:23-43) — no requestId/channelId/turnId threaded into complete().
3. src/core/intention/concern-candidates.ts:349-368 — partial correlation (missing originType/originStage).
4. src/boundary/sandbox/capabilities/llm.ts:105 and :121 — two silent `catch {}` blocks around the sandboxed completion path; at minimum log/telemeter failures (no-swallowed-errors rule).

Justified exceptions — do NOT touch:
- src/core/intention/weighted-thought-nudge-evaluator.ts stays bespoke by design: documented fail-closed-to-DECLINE behavior on a consent-gated send path; adding retry/shared plumbing risks side effects.
- src/core/emotion/appraisal.ts APPRAISAL_SYSTEM_PROMPT is a versioned behavioral instrument (docs/self-eval-prompt-audit.md), intentionally not registry-owned.

Suggested implementation direction:
Wire getRequestContext() correlation the way focus.ts / web/search.ts do at sites 1-3; replace the two silent catches at site 4 with logged/telemetered failure handling that preserves current non-blocking behavior.

Acceptance criteria:
- Sites 1-3 carry baseline correlation fields; site 4 no longer swallows errors silently.
- Behavior otherwise unchanged (no new retries or prompts unless separately scoped).
- Focused tests where the subsystems already have test files.
- npm run lint passes before close.
close_reason: Merged (commit adcccd4b): compression-guideline gains full correlation + warn-before-rethrow; intention appraisal evaluator and concern-candidates get complete correlation fields; sandbox llm.ts silent catches replaced with logged non-blocking handling. Build pass, 295 episodic/intention/session tests pass post-merge; lint failures are the pre-existing trio tracked in psfn-framework-pwzk.

title: Three call sites reimplement LLM retry/fallback owned by shared primitives
description:
Summary:
Three call sites reimplement LLM retry/fallback machinery that shared primitives already own:
1. src/core/session/manager-primitives.ts:289-314 defines a SECOND withRetry (unconditional catch-all retry, no retryability check) name-colliding with the canonical withRetry in src/primitives/llm/retry.ts:137 (retryable-error detection, circuit-breaker integration, injectable sleep). Sole consumer: compaction-service.ts:127-148. The name collision is a discoverability hazard for anyone reaching for "the" retry helper.
2. src/boundary/integrations/web/search.ts:37-80 (createWebSearchQueryJson) hand-rolls a for-loop retrying only on JSON.parse failure (thrown/network errors propagate uncaught on any attempt). Its correlation metadata is the best in the codebase (distinct .retry originStage per attempt) — keep that, replace the loop.
3. src/primitives/images/vision-reviewer.ts:211-244 loops over resolveRoutingCandidates with a forced modelHint per iteration, silently swallowing per-candidate errors (only lastError retained, no logging, no correlation metadata at all). This duplicates the client's own candidate iteration/circuit-breaker (client.ts:782, 1536-1557) minus its protections.

Suggested implementation direction:
- Keep exactly one withRetry export: rename the session-local one (e.g. withUnconditionalRetry) or fold its semantics into primitives/llm/retry.ts as an explicit isRetryable-override.
- Wrap web-search complete+parse in the shared withRetry with a parse-failure retryable predicate.
- Have vision-reviewer call complete(context, 'vision') without modelHint and let the client's candidate iteration/circuit-breaker handle fallback; add baseline correlation metadata. If per-candidate visibility is needed, add an attempted-candidates trace to the client rather than duplicating the loop.

Acceptance criteria:
- One withRetry export in the codebase.
- Web-search parse-retry semantics preserved; correlation metadata retained.
- Vision fallback coverage preserved with no silent per-candidate swallowing.
- Focused tests for each migrated site.
- npm run lint passes before close.
close_reason: Merged in 43a54491 (commit 9f4867a1): single withRetry export (session-local one deleted; compaction uses shared with isRetryable: () => true — retry budget/delay/onRetry equivalence traced); web-search parse-retry via shared withRetry with WebSearchJsonParseError predicate preserving .retry originStage, null-on-exhaustion, unretried propagation; vision-reviewer manual candidate loop removed after verifying client 'vision' routing covers the same set (FallbackRunner + circuit breaker + clamped output limits), baseline correlation added, warn-before-rethrow. Post-merge: build pass, 536/537 (1 = pwzk baseline). Conflict in manager-primitives imports resolved (kept clampUnit, dropped unused sleep).

title: Context-feedback evaluator is unwired and would fire per-turn ungated if composed
description:
Summary:
The context-feedback evaluator would fire an LLM call on essentially every turn with zero deterministic gate — and it is currently dormant, which needs an explicit decision. buildContextFeedbackCandidate (src/faculties/context-feedback/runtime.ts:174-202) fires whenever contextManifest/turnId/completedAt exist and response content is non-empty, i.e. virtually every turn; ContextEvaluator.evaluate (evaluator.ts:179) then makes the LLM call. There is no sampling rate, no min-content check, no novelty/dedup. Mitigating fact: wireContextFeedbackRuntime (runtime.ts:238) is not referenced anywhere in the composition tree, so the subsystem makes no calls today. The moment someone wires it, it becomes the highest-volume ungated background LLM call in the runtime.

Why it matters:
Fully built but unwired code conflicts with the working rule that new code must be wired to a runtime entrypoint; and wiring it as-is would violate the LLM-call-economy principle at maximum volume (per-turn).

Files to inspect/change:
- src/faculties/context-feedback/runtime.ts:174-202, 238
- src/faculties/context-feedback/evaluator.ts:48-56, 179
- src/app/startup/composition/composition.ts (if wiring)
- config owner for gate settings if wired

Suggested implementation direction:
Decide explicitly: wire it or park it. If wiring: add a deterministic gate first — sampling (1-in-N turns), min response length, and hash-keyed dedup of near-identical exchanges — with JSON-owned config. If parking: record the decision and either remove or clearly mark the subsystem as not composed.

Acceptance criteria:
- Either the subsystem is wired behind a config-owned deterministic gate with tests covering skip/fire paths, or its unwired status is an explicit recorded decision (bead comment/docs), not an accident.
- No per-turn ungated LLM call is introduced.
- npm run lint passes before close.
close_reason: Merged in d85875b2 (commit 1c7549e7): PARK decision implemented — 9-line doc comment on context-feedback runtime.ts stating intentionally-not-composed status and mandatory config-owned deterministic gate (sampling, min length, hash dedup) before any wiring; grep confirms wireContextFeedbackRuntime referenced only by its definition and test. No behavior change.

title: wake_continuity summaries fire without an entry floor and wake budgets are hardcoded
description:
Summary:
The wake_continuity summary has no independent entry floor, and both wake summary budgets are hardcoded. In src/core/session/manager/context-builder.ts:1092-1129, once orientation telemetry `fired` is true (idle-gap threshold + >1 relevant recent entries, buildOrientationNoteTelemetry ~593-660), BOTH summarizeRecentSessionEntries calls fire — purpose wake_session and purpose wake_continuity. The session side inherits the >1 entry check; the continuity (cross-channel) side has no minimum of its own — a single trivial cross-channel message still reaches the LLM, backstopped only by the callee's empty-source check (compaction-service.ts:152-157), which requires ZERO entries to skip, not trivial entries. Additionally context-builder.ts:1107 and 1116 hardcode maxTokens: 160 for both lanes instead of reading owned config (adjacent finding recorded in psfn-framework-zpgz).

Why it matters:
Wasted LLM call on trivial continuity content at every qualifying wake; hardcoded budgets bypass the JSON config ownership model.

Files to inspect/change:
- src/core/session/manager/context-builder.ts:1092-1129 (and 593-660 for the fired gate)
- src/core/session/manager/compaction-service.ts:152-157
- src/system/config/scheduler-config.ts temporalWakeup shape (catchUpSummaryMaxTokens precedent at ~321)
- tests near context-builder.test.ts and scheduler-config.test.ts

Suggested implementation direction:
Require continuityEntries.length (or total chars) above a small floor before the wake_continuity call. Move the two hardcoded 160 budgets into JSON-owned temporalWakeup config with validated defaults.

Acceptance criteria:
- Trivial-continuity wakes skip the wake_continuity LLM call, with telemetry.
- Both wake summary budgets read from owned config; defaults validated.
- wake_session behavior unchanged.
- Tests cover the floor and the config plumbing.
- npm run lint passes before close.
close_reason: Merged in 20a11018 (commit 26ffaff7): temporalWakeup.wakeSummary {sessionSummaryMaxTokens:160, continuitySummaryMaxTokens:160, continuityMinEntries:2} config-owned; context-builder floor gates the wake_continuity LLM call (deterministic no-provider fallback preserved); budgets no longer hardcoded. Tests in context-builder.test.ts + scheduler-config.test.ts.

title: Pre-compaction extraction never advances the interval watermark, re-sending extracted messages
description:
Summary:
Pre-compaction extraction does not advance the interval watermark, so the same messages can be sent to the extraction LLM twice. lastExtractionCount is only updated inside evaluateExtractionTrigger (src/faculties/memory/extraction/runtime-helpers.ts:96) when the interval/token-threshold trigger fires. The pre_compaction and crash_recovery paths (src/faculties/memory/extraction.ts:214-227, queueCompactionExtraction) never touch it. A batch already extracted via pre-compaction can be re-included in recentEntries on the next interval-triggered extraction and re-sent. The only backstop is per-fact novelty scoring against the last 30 memories (extraction/signals.ts computeNoveltyScore), which runs AFTER the LLM call — so the duplicate call is still spent.

Why it matters:
Genuine same-content-twice LLM path. Likely low frequency (compacted messages tend to age out of the recent-N window first) but pure waste when it fires, and it undermines the watermark's meaning.

Files to inspect/change:
- src/faculties/memory/extraction.ts:214-227
- src/faculties/memory/extraction/runtime-helpers.ts:56-107 (watermark update at :96)
- tests near the extraction runtime/trigger tests

Suggested implementation direction:
Have pre-compaction/crash-recovery extraction advance (or record coverage of) the interval watermark for the message range they consumed, so the next interval trigger only considers genuinely new entries. Preserve crash-recovery semantics — never skip content that was NOT successfully extracted.

Acceptance criteria:
- A batch extracted via pre_compaction is not re-sent by the next interval trigger.
- Crash-recovery still extracts anything not previously covered (no missed extraction).
- Tests cover watermark advance across both trigger paths.
- npm run lint passes before close.
close_reason: Merged in e8428877 (commit 890f0b5e): advanceExtractionWatermarkForCoverage moves lastExtractionCount only after awaited extraction resolves, never regresses, skips advance on coalesced/stale runs (fail-closed: failures leave watermark untouched so crash recovery still covers). Tests: pre_compaction batch not re-sent, partial-range coverage keeps tail triggering, failed pre-compaction does not advance, crash recovery covers backlog exactly once.

title: Document the observer-eval sidecar (it is invisible outside the code)

title: Collapse retired per-action tool factories behind unified tool services
description:
Summary:
The model-facing tool surface is mostly consolidated, but several canonical unified tools still delegate internally by instantiating old per-action AgentTool factories. This is not currently a model-facing duplicate-tool problem because startup composition registers canonical names only and registry tests guard retired aliases. It is still a structural cleanup candidate: implementation code retains old top-level tool names and AgentTool wrappers that can confuse future maintenance or accidentally get re-registered.

Concrete examples observed (verified 2026-07-06; two additional domains found — see addendum):
- src/core/tools/session.ts:470-482 createSessionTool instantiates createSessionSearchTool, createSessionGrepTool, createSessionNewTool, createSessionListTool, createSessionResumeTool, createStartFocusTool, and createCompleteFocusTool, then routes canonical session actions to those old tool execute methods at src/core/tools/session.ts:571-630. The registered surface is session, but internal object names include session_new, session_list, session_resume, session_search, session_grep, start_focus, and complete_focus. Note: the wake_return action is handled inline (599-620), not via a factory.
- src/faculties/core-memory/tools.ts:337-363 routes orient values_list/values_add/values_update by constructing createValuesListTool/createValuesAddTool/createValuesUpdateTool. The registered surface is orient, but internal object names include values_list, values_add, values_update. These are constructed per-call inside execute, not once at wrapper construction.
- src/core/identity/prompt-tools.ts:520-530 creates prompt_layer_list, prompt_layer_get, identity_diff, identity_changelog, prompt_layer_update, prompt_layer_rollback, and prompt_layer_toggle tools inside createIdentityTool. The registered surface is identity, but internal object names are still old split identity tools. IMPORTANT framing correction: these seven names are NOT registered retired aliases (identity's retiredAliases list is only persona_update and character_card_update, registry.ts:246-248), so they are unguarded internal helper AgentTools rather than "retired" tools — no drift guard covers them today.
- src/faculties/north-star/tools.ts:98-103 creates north_star_list/create/update/delete/reorder tool objects inside createNorthStarTool. The registered surface is north_star, but internal object names are still old split north_star_* tools. All five ARE registered retired aliases (registry.ts:379-383, hidden).

Additional domains found in the 2026-07-06 verification sweep (same pattern, previously unlisted):
- src/core/tools/lifecycle.ts:449 createSystemTool internally constructs createRestartTool (name self_restart, lifecycle.ts:256) and createRebuildTool (name self_rebuild, lifecycle.ts:340) at 499/507 and routes to their execute at 504/512. Both are registered retired aliases (registry.ts:334-335).
- src/faculties/core-memory/tools.ts orient ALSO delegates the concern actions create_concern/list_concerns/resolve_concern to createCreateConcernTool/createListConcernsTool/createResolveConcernTool from src/core/intention/tools.ts (names at 169/80/124), constructed per-call (~366/385+). All three are registered retired aliases (registry.ts:223-225).

So the full split is SIX domains: session, orient-values, orient-concerns, identity, north_star, system. All other unified tools were checked and are clean (memory, scratchpad, contact, media, repo, web, fs, shell, beads, vault, skill, schedule, toolset implement actions inline).

Guardrail coverage note (verified):
Coverage is two-tiered. The facade/model-facing registration guard only rejects the drift-guard subset MODEL_FACING_DRIFT_GUARD_RETIRED_TOOL_ALIASES (registry.ts:55-82 — session_*, focus, values_*; tested at tool-runtime-facade.test.ts:61-67). north_star_*, self_restart/self_rebuild, and the concern aliases are protected only by the composition-path assertNoRetiredFirstPartyToolAliases (registry.ts:523-533). The identity prompt_layer_* internals are protected by neither. Consider strengthening guards as part of this cleanup.

No-leakage confirmation: every old create*Tool factory's only non-test consumers are its defining module and the single unified wrapper delegating to it. No re-registration risk exists today.

Why it matters:
This is the non-summary version of the same consolidation concern: one model-facing capability should have one canonical action surface and one plain implementation/service layer, not a canonical wrapper that keeps building retired AgentTool objects. Current tests prevent exposure drift (with the two-tier caveat above), so this is cleanup rather than an urgent bug. The risk is future confusion: an agent or engineer searching for tools sees old exported create*Tool factories and old tool names, and a future wiring path could accidentally register them again.

Files/tests to inspect:
- src/core/tools/session.ts and src/core/tools/session-search.ts / src/core/tools/focus.ts
- src/faculties/core-memory/tools.ts, src/faculties/values/tools.ts, and src/core/intention/tools.ts
- src/core/identity/prompt-tools.ts and src/core/identity/card-versioning.ts
- src/faculties/north-star/tools.ts
- src/core/tools/lifecycle.ts
- src/core/agent/tool-surface/registry.ts and src/app/startup/composition/tool-surface-registry.test.ts
- src/core/agent/substrate-agent/tool-runtime-facade.test.ts for retired alias rejection
- focused tests for each unified tool: session, orient/core-memory, identity, north_star, system

Suggested implementation direction:
Do this incrementally by domain (six domains, per above). Extract the actual behavior into plain action/service functions with canonical action names, then have the unified AgentTool execute switch call those functions directly. Keep old create*Tool factories only if tests or non-model internal APIs still need them; otherwise remove exports and update tests to exercise the canonical tool. Preserve or strengthen drift guards so retired aliases cannot be registered, discovered, pinned, or described — and consider widening the facade drift-guard subset to cover north_star_*, self_restart/self_rebuild, and concern aliases.

Non-goals:
- Do not change the model-facing tool names or action schemas unless a separate compatibility bead explicitly scopes it.
- Do not remove retired-alias metadata from src/core/agent/tool-surface/registry.ts; it is still useful as a guardrail.
- Do not refactor all domains in one large change if smaller per-domain beads would be safer.
acceptance_criteria:
- Produce either a small implementation pass for one domain or split follow-up beads by domain before closing this umbrella cleanup.
- At least one unified tool no longer delegates by constructing retired per-action AgentTool objects; it calls plain service/action functions directly.
- Startup composition still registers only canonical first-party tool names and app/startup/composition/tool-surface-registry.test.ts continues to pass.
- Retired aliases remain rejected by tool-surface registry and adaptive tool runtime tests.
- Existing public behavior of the canonical tool action(s) is preserved with focused tests.
- npm run lint passes before any implementation bead is closed.
close_reason: Merged (7 commits, 6a635960..6d1bb011): all six domains collapsed (session, orient-values, orient-concerns, identity, north_star, system) — unified tools call plain execute*Action functions; all 24 retired per-action factories deleted (tests rewritten against canonical tools); MODEL_FACING_DRIFT_GUARD_RETIRED_TOOL_ALIASES widened to cover concern/north_star/self_restart+self_rebuild aliases with facade-rejection tests; dead capability/reversibility entries pruned to satisfy guard invariants. Post-merge: build pass, 621/622 across 47 tool suites (1 = pwzk layout-ordering family). Follow-up regression from earlier b7q8 merge found during this integration (parity.test correlation arg) was fixed separately in 514e3121.

title: P3: Triage Fallow hard hygiene findings
description:
Summary
The q7tv/c4jy wrap-up Fallow pass on 2026-06-30 produced broad existing repo debt plus two hard-error-style findings that are not part of the prompt/runtime repair branch and should be triaged separately.

Fallow command
- npx -y fallow --format json > /tmp/fallow-report.json

Relevant findings
- unresolved_imports: scripts/ops/continuity-watchdog-healthcheck.mjs:16 imports ../../data/ops/continuity-watchdog-state.json, which Fallow cannot resolve.
- unlisted_dependencies: dotenv imported from scripts/prefetch-hf-models.ts:3 and scripts/verify-startup-owner-files.ts:1 but reported as unlisted.
- The same report also showed broad pre-existing debt totals: 964 total issues, including unused files/exports/types/class members and duplicate exports. This bead is not a mandate to delete those blindly.

Scope
- Determine whether the continuity watchdog JSON is runtime-generated, intentionally absent from repo, or should be represented by a committed fixture/default path.
- Determine whether dotenv should be a direct dependency, dev dependency, or Fallow ignore based on how those scripts are run.
- Prefer fixing the underlying ownership/config issue over suppressing, unless the absence/import is intentional and documented.

Non-goals
- Do not refactor the full Fallow report.
- Do not delete files solely because static analysis reports unused.
- Do not touch prompt/runtime repair code unless this triage discovers a direct regression.

Failure modes
- Adding a fake state JSON that masks a real runtime owner-file requirement.
- Moving dotenv into the wrong dependency class and breaking production scripts.
- Suppressing findings without documenting why they are intentional.
acceptance_criteria:
- continuity-watchdog-healthcheck.mjs unresolved import is either fixed with the correct repo-owned/runtime-owned path handling or intentionally suppressed with a documented reason.
- dotenv dependency classification is corrected in package metadata or intentionally ignored with a documented reason.
- Any changes pass npm run lint and the smallest relevant script/test checks.
- Handoff states whether the broader 964 Fallow findings remain existing debt and are out of scope.
close_reason: Superseded duplicate triage shell. Evidence: bd search Fallow shows the two concrete hard findings already tracked as open actionable beads: psfn-framework-8wf5 covers scripts/ops/continuity-watchdog-healthcheck.mjs unresolved state JSON import, and psfn-framework-va9i covers the unlisted dotenv imports in scripts/prefetch-hf-models.ts and scripts/verify-startup-owner-files.ts. The broad 964-item Fallow report was explicitly out of scope/non-goal in psfn-framework-xz9n, so keeping this P3 triage shell open duplicates the two specific beads without adding remaining executable scope. title: P3: Decide and migrate channel privacy labels to channel-owned configuration
description:
Summary
Track the operator's follow-up concern that channel privacy labels are currently per-user or user-shaped in a way that may be weird for group chats. The likely target is a channel-owned privacy model, but this is not part of the immediate P0 implementation.

Problem
In group contexts, privacy/visibility labels should probably be properties of the channel/room, not properties of each user. Per-user channel privacy labels make behavior harder to reason about and can create inconsistent room semantics.

Decision needed
- Identify current owner(s) for channel privacy/visibility labels.
- Decide whether channel visibility should live in channels.json or another channel-owned config surface.
- Define migration behavior for existing per-user labels.
- Define Garden/settings exposure and validation rules.

Files to inspect first
- src/system/settings/contracts.ts and src/system/settings.ts.
- src/shared/contracts/runtime.ts.
- channel classification helpers under src/system/trust and runtime/session code that calls classifyChannel.
- Existing channel config owner file, likely channels.json and related Garden exposure.

Non-goals
- Do not block P0 room-scoped memory gating on this.
- Do not change leave-room/revocation policy here.
design: This should be handled as a design/settings contract decision before implementation because settings ownership rules are strict in this repo.
acceptance_criteria:
- Current channel privacy ownership is documented with concrete file/config anchors.
- A decision is recorded for channel-owned vs per-user privacy labels.
- If channel-owned privacy is approved, follow-up implementation beads are created with settings owner-file, Garden exposure, migration, and tests.
- P0 group memory behavior remains room/channelId based regardless of this later model decision.
notes:
Operator explicitly said this is not a now thing.
Current ownership evidence from 2026-06-29 inspection:
- src/system/trust/policy.ts:297 classifyChannel currently resolves exact/prefix overrides from trust-policy channelClassification first, then meta.privacyLevel, then isDirectMessage/private-prefix/default visibility.
- src/core/contacts/types.ts:5 defines ChannelPrivacyLevel as ChannelVisibility, and ContactChannelLink/ContactConversationChannel carry privacyLevel fields.
- src/core/contacts/store/schema.ts:73 and :84 persist privacy_level on contact_channel_ids and contact_channel_activity, so today there is contact/user-shaped privacy state.
- src/operator/garden/services/contacts-service.ts:583 applies privacy updates through contactStore.setConversationChannelPrivacy or setChannelPrivacy from contact edit payloads.
- channels.json is already the owner file for Discord channel-level group-memory overrides (docs/memory.md:141, src/channels/backplane/config.ts:468), making it the likely owner-file candidate if channel privacy becomes channel-owned.
- src/faculties/subagents/faculty.ts and src/faculties/shards/manager.ts still expose/mention contact_set_channel_privacy, while docs/tool-surface.md:188-190 says it aliases to set_channel_privacy to keep per-channel privacy on the contact relationship surface. This is the product/design conflict to resolve later.
Decision remains deferred: P0 room-memory gating stays channelId/room based and must not wait for this migration.
2026-06-29 implementation wave: deferred intentionally. Operator said channel privacy label ownership is not a now thing. P0/P1 runtime privacy now uses deterministic room/channelId memory gating and does not depend on migrating contact-shaped privacy labels. Keep this decision bead for the later settings-owner/Garden migration design.
close_reason: Absorbed by psfn-framework-76rn.2 (channel-owned privacy label migration); decision ratified 2026-07-01: private/invite_only/public, channel-owned, default invite_only.

title: Use a bulk store path for Garden retention-class memory updates
description:
Summary: Garden memory bulk updates use the store bulkUpdate path for type/sensitivity-only changes, but fall back to a service-layer per-ID loop when retentionClass is included. The endpoint is capped at 500 IDs, so this is not urgent, but it still creates avoidable round trips and duplicates retention-tag update logic outside the store.

Evidence and affected files:
- src/operator/garden/services/memory-service.ts:587 bulkUpdate handles admin bulk mutations and caps IDs at 500 on lines 594-595.
- src/operator/garden/services/memory-service.ts:629 uses memoryStore.bulkUpdate when retentionClass is absent, but line 631 switches to bulkUpdateWithRetentionClass when retentionClass is present.
- src/operator/garden/services/memory-service.ts:643 bulkUpdateWithRetentionClass loops every ID, line 652 calls memoryStore.getById, and line 665 calls memoryStore.updateMemory for each memory.
- src/faculties/memory/postgres-store.ts and src/faculties/memory/store/read-write-operations.ts already contain bulk update primitives that should be the preferred ownership boundary.

Why it matters: The service currently performs up to 1,000 store operations for a 500-item retention update and owns tag mutation details that belong closer to the memory store. This can make admin bulk actions slower and harder to keep consistent across SQLite/Postgres implementations.

Scope: Add a store-level bulk retention-class update or transactional batch path that updates retentionClass and related durable/preference tags consistently. Have the Garden service delegate to that path.

Non-goals: Do not change the 500-item admin cap or retention-class product semantics in this bead.
acceptance_criteria: Garden bulk memory updates that include retentionClass no longer perform getById/updateMemory one ID at a time from the service layer; retention tags/class updates are applied through a store-level bulk method or a bounded transactional batch path; existing tag semantics for durable and standard retention are preserved; tests cover mixed valid/deleted/missing IDs; npm run lint and targeted memory tests pass.
notes: Local implementation commit 88b2421f. Validation: npm test -- --run src/operator/garden/services/memory-service.test.ts src/faculties/memory/store.test.ts src/faculties/memory/postgres-store.test.ts passed; npm run lint passed. Bead intentionally left in_progress for orchestrator integration/closure.
close_reason: Implemented and integrated in stnk-parallel-20260629. Evidence: commit 88b2421f added shared retention tag handling in src/faculties/memory/types.ts, transactional SQLite bulk retention updates in src/faculties/memory/store/read-write-operations.ts, a single store-level Postgres bulk update path in src/faculties/memory/postgres-store.ts, and changed src/operator/garden/services/memory-service.ts to delegate retentionClass bulk updates through memoryStore.bulkUpdate rather than getById/updateMemory loops. Integrated via merge dffbf8db. Validation on integration: npm test -- --run src/operator/garden/services/memory-service.test.ts src/faculties/memory/store.test.ts src/faculties/memory/postgres-store.test.ts src/faculties/memory/memory-store-port.test.ts src/operator/garden/api-routes.test.ts passed 136 tests; npm run lint and npm run build passed.

title: Preserve structured server error bodies in the admin UI API client
description:
Summary: The admin UI API client drops structured server error bodies and throws ApiError with only HTTP statusText. Garden endpoints often return useful JSON error messages, so operators lose actionable diagnostics.

Evidence and affected files:
- admin-ui/src/lib/api/client.ts:15 apiGet throws new ApiError(res.status, res.statusText) at line 25 for non-OK responses.
- admin-ui/src/lib/api/client.ts:29 apiPost repeats the same pattern at line 40.
- admin-ui/src/lib/api/client.ts:44 apiPostMultipart repeats it at line 58.
- admin-ui/src/lib/api/client.ts:62 apiPatch repeats it at line 73, and later helpers follow the same style.
- admin-ui/src/lib/api/errors.ts already has space for a body/message-carrying error, but most callers do not populate it.
- src/operator/garden routes commonly send JSON envelopes such as { error: '...' }, which are not surfaced by the current client helpers.

Why it matters: Operator-facing admin workflows need the server's actual error message to diagnose validation failures, permission denials, and runtime problems. Status text alone often collapses distinct failures into 'Bad Request' or 'Internal Server Error'.

Scope: Centralize non-OK response handling in admin-ui/src/lib/api/client.ts. Parse JSON error envelopes and plain text bodies safely, populate ApiError, and preserve existing 401 redirect behavior.

Non-goals: Do not redesign Garden error envelope formats or change server status codes in this bead.
acceptance_criteria: admin-ui API helpers parse JSON/text error responses before throwing; ApiError exposes the server error message/body consistently; 401 redirect behavior is preserved; tests cover JSON error envelopes, text errors, and empty error bodies; npm run lint and targeted admin-ui tests pass.
close_reason: Implemented structured admin UI API error preservation. Evidence: admin-ui/src/lib/api/client.ts now centralizes non-OK response handling with throwIfNotOk, parses JSON error envelopes ({ error: string }, { error: { message } }, { message }), preserves raw text bodies, falls back to statusText for empty bodies, stores the raw response body on ApiError.body, uses the server error message as ApiError.statusText/message text, and keeps 401 redirect-to-/login behavior. The shared path is used by apiGet/apiPost/apiPostMultipart/apiPatch/apiPut/apiDelete/apiPostForm. Added admin-ui/src/lib/api/client.test.ts covering JSON envelopes, string envelopes, text errors, empty bodies, and 401 redirect behavior. Validation passed: npx vitest run src/lib/api/client.test.ts src/lib/api/websocket.test.ts src/lib/stores/auth-storage.test.ts --reporter=dot (10 tests); npm --prefix admin-ui run check; npm --prefix admin-ui run build; npm run lint; git diff --check.

description:

title: Human attention pressure timeout extension for fatigue
description:
Summary:
Future extension to fatigue: handle human attention pressure where a human repeatedly pings or demands attention from a companion beyond what the relationship/context supports. This is explicitly not part of the initial companion-to-companion fatigue implementation.

Problem:
Phase 1 treats human-authored turns as fatigue-free so companions remain responsive to humans while MI-to-MI loops are controlled. There are foreseeable group-chat and DM cases where a human repeatedly pings a companion in a stressful or socially inappropriate way. That needs moderation/relationship semantics rather than machine-loop prevention semantics.

Scope:
- Define a separate human attention/load policy keyed by human contact, channel, relationship/trust state, recent ping frequency, direct mentions, and room context.
- Support respectful timeout behavior: the companion can receive an internal alert and decide how to set a boundary in her own voice.
- Keep consent/trust boundaries clear. Do not silently punish normal primary-user interaction.
- Make policy configurable and visible to the operator before enforcement.
- Use the fatigue telemetry foundation where useful, but keep separate reason codes from MI-to-MI loop fatigue.

Expected files/code areas when implemented:
- Fatigue/care policy modules created by psfn-framework-isi.*
- src/core/contacts/* for relationship/trust reads
- shared runtime turn enforcement modules under src/core/agent/substrate-agent/*
- Garden settings/history services for visibility
- docs/operations.md if operator-facing behavior changes

Tests to build when implemented:
- Repeated low-trust human pings in a group channel trigger a boundary alert after configured thresholds.
- Primary/trusted relationship has higher tolerance and does not trip ordinary conversation.
- Human timeout state is per contact + channel and does not suppress other humans.
- Boundary wording is model-authored from an internal alert, not hardcoded.
- Operator config validation rejects unsafe or missing thresholds.

Out of scope:
- Do not build this before MI-to-MI fatigue is in place.
- Do not mix these counters with companion-to-companion response budgets.
- Do not change Discord mention-gating behavior.
design: Separate this from MI-to-MI fatigue. Machine-loop fatigue protects against infinite agent loops; human attention timeout protects the companion from excessive social demand and needs stricter consent/moderation review.
acceptance_criteria: Acceptance: future bead is considered ready when MI-to-MI fatigue telemetry exists, and this extension has deterministic thresholds for human attention pressure, relationship-aware tolerance, per-contact+channel state, companion-authored boundary alerts, Garden/operator visibility, and tests for repeated low-trust pings, trusted-user tolerance, per-channel isolation, non-hardcoded boundary wording, and config validation.
notes: AUDIT 2026-06-28 (verified): OPEN, net-new (future extension). Human attention pressure timeout extension for the fatigue system. Explicitly a future extension per desc.
close_reason: Review remediation shipped in 940dc5a78a4f739b11271c93f5dacab784f80151. Verified physical source-channel and contact-scoped source-message replay identity in turn-execution-runtime.ts and human-attention-pressure.ts; privacy-minimal sourceMessageId/turnId provenance, explicit allowlisted ledger projection, and unknown-key rejection in human-attention-ledger.ts; strict threshold ordering and single-message primary protection in charge-policy-config.ts. Validation: 273 focused tests, npm run lint, npm run build, npm run verify:settings-contract, npm run verify:hardcoded-settings, and git diff --check passed. Branch pushed; PR #111 remains open and unmerged; review comment posted.

title: Consolidate duplicated sleep()/delay helpers into one shared util
description:
Summary:
The ponytail-audit (2026-06-28) found 13 non-test files hand-rolling the same Promise+setTimeout sleep helper, 6 of which define their OWN local copy of the function. No shared sleep util exists. AGENTS.md mandates 'extend existing primitives before inventing parallel abstractions' and 'reuse shared type guards instead of redefining locally' (bead psfn-framework-qfa). This is the async-helper equivalent.

Local copies of the same one-liner (function defaultSleep/delay/sleep returning new Promise(r=>setTimeout(r,ms))):
- src/primitives/llm/retry.ts (defaultSleep)
- src/core/agent/stream-adapter.ts
- src/boundary/gateway/discord-startup.ts
- src/channels/discord/voice.ts
- src/primitives/images/fal.ts
- src/primitives/images/comfyui.ts

Inline duplicated sites (no local fn, just inline new Promise(resolve=>setTimeout(resolve,ms)) or setTimeout(resolve,ms)):
- src/boundary/integrations/vault/ops.ts:226
- src/app/e2e/e2e-voice-roundtrip.ts:177
- src/app/e2e/e2e-walkthrough.ts:148
- src/boundary/gateway/url-policy.ts:350
- src/core/eval/observer-sidecar/queue.ts:624

- src/channels/discord/voice-recovery-runtime.ts:328

Steps:
1. Add a single sleep(ms: number): Promise<void> to src/shared/utils/ (alongside isRecord/normalizeStringArray in types.ts, or a new timing.ts — prefer extending existing utils over a new file unless timing clusters grow).
2. Replace the 6 local copies and the 9 inline sites with imports of the shared util.
3. Keep the abstraction minimal: just sleep(ms). No jitter/retry/until — those belong in callers (e.g. retry.ts already owns backoff logic; only its internal sleep helper is the dup).

Acceptance criteria:
- rg for 'new Promise\(.*setTimeout\(.*resolve' and 'setTimeout\(.*resolve' under src returns 0 (or only intentional non-sleep uses).
- The 6 local sleep/delay/defaultSleep definitions are gone.

Scope is mechanical dedup; do NOT bundle with retry/backoff refactors or performance work.
notes:
Implemented 2026-06-28.

Added src/shared/utils/timing.ts (single sleep(ms) util, matches the one-concern-per-file grain of shared/utils: env/errors/fs/types).

title: Replace dotenv dep with Node native --env-file-if-exists
description:
Summary:
The ponytail-audit (2026-06-28) found 'import \'dotenv/config\'' in 10 entrypoints plus the dotenv dependency (16.6.1). Node 22+ (repo engines is >=22.0.0; planning to bump to Node 24 with the postgres-only cutover) ships a native equivalent. dotenv can be removed.

CRITICAL k8s/docker gotcha (the reason this is not a blind sed swap):
- 'import \'dotenv/config\''  -> when .env is ABSENT it is a silent no-op, no error.
- 'process.loadEnvFile()'     -> when .env is ABSENT it THROWS.
Prod containers/k8s inject env via ConfigMap/Secret into real process.env; there is NO .env baked into the image. A naive process.loadEnvFile() swap crash-loops pods. Use --env-file-if-exists (Node 22.9+) which is exact dotenv/config semantics: loads if present, silent if absent.

Both dotenv and --env-file-if-exists default to NOT overriding existing process.env, so orchestrator-injected vars still win. Verified equivalent override behavior.

Files/surfaces (the 10 import 'dotenv/config' sites):
- src/app/gateway/main.ts
- src/app/startup/index.ts
- src/app/cli/chat-cli.ts
- src/app/maintenance/transcript-projection-repair.ts
- src/app/maintenance/import-character.ts
- src/app/maintenance/session-integrity-repair.ts
- src/app/maintenance/migrate-embeddings.ts
- src/app/maintenance/migrate-persistence-layout.ts
- src/app/maintenance/session-repair.ts
- src/app/maintenance/session-attribution-repair.ts
- package.json dependency 'dotenv' and any @types (none currently)
- package.json scripts: add --env-file-if-exists=.env (or --env-file=.env guarded) to the dev/gateway/agent/maintenance entrypoint script flags so the flag owns the load instead of in-code imports.

Steps:
1. Add --env-file-if-exists=.env to the relevant package.json script entrypoints (dev, gateway, agent, split, yolo, the maintenance npm scripts). Alternatively keep a single guarded process.loadEnvFile() guarded by existsSync('.env') in the earliest shared startup module if script-flag wiring is awkward for maintenance CLIs — pick whichever is the smaller diff, prefer the flag.
2. Delete the 10 'import \'dotenv/config\';' lines.
3. Remove the dotenv dependency from package.json and run npm install to update the lockfile.
4. Confirm .env.example is unaffected (it is bootstrap-only docs, not authority per AGENTS.md).

Acceptance criteria:
- rg "dotenv" under src returns 0 (excluding comments/docs explaining the removal).
- dotenv is absent from package.json dependencies and package-lock.json.
- A local run WITHOUT a .env file present does not throw (proves the k8s no-file case).
- A local run WITH a .env file present still loads it (proves dev case).
- Existing injected process.env still overrides .env values (proves override semantics).
- npm run lint, npm run build pass.
- Entry-point smoke (npm run gateway, npm run agent) loads env as before.

Related: depends on the Node 24 bump and pairs naturally with the postgres-only cutover tracked in epic psfn-framework-3c2 (removal of the last local-state env authority). Do NOT bundle with the sqlite removal work.
notes:
Implemented 2026-06-28.

Added src/shared/utils/load-dotenv.ts: a side-effect module wrapping process.loadEnvFile('.env') in an existsSync('.env') guard. The guard is required because bare process.loadEnvFile() THROWS on absent .env (unlike dotenv/config which is a silent no-op) -- without it, k8s/docker containers with no .env file would crashloop. Verified loadEnvFile does NOT override existing process.env (matches dotenv/config default), so injected orchestrator vars still win. Resolves .env relative to process.cwd(), same as dotenv/config.

Converted 20 sites (audit originally said 10; corrected to 14 src + 6 eval):
- 14 src/app/*.ts files: import 'dotenv/config' -> import '../../shared/utils/load-dotenv.js' (uniform relative path since all sit at src/app/<dir>/ depth).
- 6 eval/*.ts files (discovered during impl, invoked by npm eval:* scripts via tsx): 5 used programmatic import {config as loadDotenv} from 'dotenv' + loadDotenv() call -> side-effect import + dropped the now-redundant call (env loads earlier at module load, strictly fine); 1 (ttft-real-providers.ts) used the side-effect form already. eval/ already imports from ../../src/shared/utils/* (precedent: types.js), so the boundary crossing is established.

SCOPE FINDINGS (recorded, informed the safe shape):
- scripts/start-gateway-agent.sh ALREADY sources .env itself via psfn_source_dotenv_preserving_existing_env (no-override) before spawning node -- so for dev/start/split/yolo the in-code import was already a redundant no-op. Untouched.
- Docker agent target src/app/agent/main.ts never had the import; agent:docker runs node dist/agent-main.js with no .env (k8s injects env). Untouched.
- startup/index.ts is a DISABLED fail-closed entrypoint; startup-surface-hygiene.test.ts asserts it stays disabled. Import swapped, disabled posture preserved (test passes).

Removed dotenv (16.6.1) from package.json dependencies; npm install pruned it from package-lock.json and node_modules.

BEHAVIOR VERIFIED (3 runtime cases via tsx):
- absent .env -> silent no-op, no throw (k8s/docker safe).
- present .env -> loads it (dev).
- injected process.env -> wins over .env (override semantics preserved).

Quality gates: npm run lint PASS, npm run build PASS, verify:repository-hygiene PASS (4 baseline cycles, no regressions; shared type guards pass), targeted vitest 28 tests PASS (start-gateway-agent.test.ts wrapper-sourcing + startup-surface-hygiene.test.ts).
Net: -1 dependency (dotenv). 20 files, +20/-26 LOC. Pure drop-in with supply-chain-hygiene win.
close_reason: Completed. Replaced dotenv dep with native process.loadEnvFile() via a guarded shared side-effect module across 20 sites (14 src + 6 eval). Guard preserves silent-no-op-on-absent (k8s-safe); no-override semantics preserved (injected env wins). Wrapper .env sourcing and docker path untouched. dotenv removed from package.json + lockfile + node_modules. lint+build+repo-hygiene+28 targeted tests pass.

title: Standardize on uuid v7 for all generated IDs (retire v4 sites)
description:
Summary:
The ponytail-audit (2026-06-28) found mixed uuid generation: turn IDs already use v7 (src/core/turns/id.ts uses v7 for sortable TurnIDs), but 10 other internal ID sites still use v4. There is no external surface validating version==4 on any of these IDs (verified: all are internal postgres row IDs, contact link IDs, memory event IDs). Standardizing on v7 gives: lexicographic==chronological ordering (better postgres indexes / recency queries on contact/memory tables), one import style and one mental model across the codebase, and removes the audit's separate 'v4 -> crypto.randomUUID' question entirely (keep the uuid dep, use v7 consistently).

The uuid dependency STAYS: v7 has no stdlib equivalent (crypto.randomUUID() only produces v4). This is about consistency, not dep removal.

Files/surfaces (the 10 v4 sites):
- src/core/contacts/store/upsert-resolve-operations.ts:156 (import {v4 as uuidv4}; partial.id ?? uuidv4())
- src/core/contacts/store/identity-link-verification.ts:128 (id: uuidv4())
- src/core/contacts/store/identity-utils.ts:83 (uuidv4().replace(/-/g,'') -> 32-hex; v7 still valid 128-bit, produces 32 hex, fine)
- src/faculties/memory/writer.ts (multiple: id at ~923, ~1106; patchEventId ~1309; replacementId ~1362; externalRef 'abstraction:'+uuidv4() ~1472)
- src/core/contacts/postgres-adapter/crud-operations.ts (id at :174 partial.id?.trim()||uuidv4(); :847 id: uuidv4())

Steps:
1. In each of the above files, change 'import { v4 as uuidv4 } from \'uuid\';' to 'import { v7 as uuidv7 } from \'uuid\';' and replace uuidv4() calls with uuidv7(). Keep any local alias that callers already use if a mass rename is noisy, but prefer the v7 name for clarity.
2. For identity-utils.ts:83 the .replace(/-/g,'') 32-hex transform is preserved as-is on the v7 output.
3. Verify the postgres column types for these IDs still accept the value (they are text/uuid; v7 is a valid RFC 9562 uuid, no schema change needed). Confirm there is no CHECK constraint or format validator assuming v4 anywhere.

Acceptance criteria:
- rg "v4 as uuidv4|uuidv4\(\)" under src returns 0 (excluding tests asserting v4 behavior, if any exist and are intentionally kept — verify they still make sense).
- All generated IDs in contacts and memory stores are v7 and lexicographically sortable.
- No postgres schema migration required (v7 is a valid uuid); confirm with a schema inspection.
- npm run lint, npm run build, and the affected store test suites (contacts, memory/writer) pass.
- Turn IDs remain v7 (already correct), no change to turns/id.ts.

Scope: mechanical version bump for consistency + index health. Do NOT bundle with retry/sleep dedup or the env-file work.
notes:
Implemented 2026-06-28.

Converted 10 v4 sites across 5 files to v7 (alias renamed uuidv4 -> uuidv7 for consistency with the existing turns/id.ts convention):
- src/core/contacts/store/upsert-resolve-operations.ts (1: contact id fallback)
- src/core/contacts/store/identity-link-verification.ts (1: verification id)
- src/core/contacts/store/identity-utils.ts (1: createVerificationToken, the 32-hex .replace(/-/g,'') path)
- src/core/contacts/postgres-adapter/crud-operations.ts (2: contact id fallback, verification id)
- src/faculties/memory/writer.ts (5: memory id x2, patchEventId, replacementId, externalRef abstraction:)

turns/id.ts left as-is (already v7). uuid dep STAYS (v7 has no stdlib equivalent).

NO IMPACT ON EXISTING ITEMS (verified before editing, not assumed):
- Generator change affects new inserts only; existing postgres rows keep their v4 UUIDs forever, no rewrite/migration.
- No .sql CHECK constraints or version assertions on any uuid column (zero matches).
- No isUuid/uuidRegex/format validator anywhere assuming v4.
- No WHERE id > cursor pagination (the one thing that would break mid-stream version switch). Clean grep.
- id is never a primary ordering key; every ORDER BY/.sort uses a real timestamp (created_at/extracted_at) with id only as a deterministic tiebreaker within a timestamp group. v4 tiebreak order was arbitrary/random anyway, so moving to v7 is strictly more correct, never a regression.
- createVerificationToken: v7 still 128-bit -> 32 hex after replace, valid token format. Runtime sanity check confirmed len=32, /is hex/, validate()==true, version()==7, sortable.

Quality gates: npm run lint PASS, npm run build PASS, targeted vitest 173 tests PASS (writer + contacts, 6 files).
Net: 5 files, +15/-15 (symmetric alias swap).
close_reason: Completed. 10 v4 sites across 5 files -> v7. No impact on existing items (generator change is new-insert-only; no v4-assuming constraints/validators/cursors; id is always timestamp-tiebreak not primary order). uuid dep stays. lint+build+173 tests pass.

title: SPIFFE SVID: per-companion/shard workload identity + DB provenance stamping
description: Two sub-concerns, consumable separately. (a) Transport identity: each companion AND each shard gets its own SPIFFE SVID (spiffe://cluster.local/psfn/companion/<id> and spiffe://cluster.local/psfn/shard/<id>); gateway validates on mTLS. Builds on the SPIFFE SANs wired in the Gateway TCP/WSS bead. (b) DB-write provenance: stamp every shared-DB memory/intention write with the writer workload's SVID, so shard fold-back into main is auditable (which companion/shard authored each row) — this is the load-bearing part for the federated multi-agent future and touches the Postgres memory-store write path. User flagged 'we can see if this is better' — this bead includes a design note evaluating whether per-shard provenance is worth the write-path cost vs simpler fold-back manifest. Builds on Gateway TCP/WSS mTLS SANs. Validation: mTLS handshake tests, provenance-column tests on memory writes.

Root-of-trust credential still exists (SA token / workload identity) — that is unavoidable and the point. title: Memory decay tuning: tick rate too frequent + differentiate halflife by memory type
description:
Operator open question (2026-06-26 ramble list, section 7).

Problem: Current tick rate for memory salience decay is suspected to be far too frequent (5-minute ticks called out as excessive). Unclear what the actual per-tick decay percentage is. Needs measurement and tuning of BOTH tick frequency and per-type decay rate. Some over-generation of low-salience/low-value memories is happening during normal operation (not catastrophic since they decay out, but contributes noise).

Confirmed substrate: src/faculties/memory/decay.ts uses exponential halflife decay: salience * exp((-LN2 * dt)/halflife), running on a default interval of MEMORY_CONFIG.maintenanceIntervalMs. So per-type halflife is already structurally supported; the question is whether it is actually differentiated today or flat.

Proposed differentiation:
- Procedural memories — decay FASTER (facts about routines/state get superseded roughly weekly).
- Emotional / high-significance memories — decay SLOWER (they matter more long-term; significant shared moments should not fade in a week).
- Favorited memories ("our song", etc.) — already have a mechanism to be excluded from decay or decay extremely slowly, pullable during introspection.

Scope:
- Measure current tick frequency and per-type halflife values actually in effect.
- Implement/confirm per-type halflife (procedural fast, emotional slow, favorited near-zero decay).
- Raise the decay tick interval from ~5min to something less wasteful; tune per-tick percentage accordingly so the decay curve shape is preserved.
- Audit the over-generation of low-salience memories (separate but related — extraction thresholds).

Validation: npm run lint; targeted decay tests proving procedural < emotional < favorited decay rates over a simulated window; confirm favorited exclusion.

Priority: P3.
notes: AUDIT 2026-06-28 (verified): OPEN. decay.ts uses DECAY_HALFLIFE (imported from types.ts:3, used :53) with getMemoryDecayProfile halflifeMultiplier. The tuning concerns: tick rate too frequent + differentiate halflife per type. Config/tuning work.
close_reason: Superseded: tick-rate half is 2z12.10 (sweep cadence, operator decided 60m); halflife-by-type half is m14v (operator-approved per-type decay/floor/prior matrix in its DESIGN). Confirmed independently by memory and scheduler audit lanes. 2026-07-14 bead audit.

title: Artifact/attachment shelf (Phase 1.5)
description:
## Summary

Surface `artifact.created` projection events on an attachment/artifact shelf with LIMITED, read-oriented artifact access. Phase 1.5 — sequenced AFTER the presence loop is proven; may slip past Phase 1.

## Charter law governing this bead

- **§11.5 `ArtifactReturnPort`.** Artifacts come through the artifact-return seam (shard/subagent fold-back, §6.13), scoped + provenance-tagged.
- **§6.13 Shard fold-back provenance.** Artifacts preserve provenance (core/shard lineage); the shelf shows provenance, not anonymous blobs.
- **Law 21 / §9.2 Gateway mediation.** Limited artifact fetch is gateway-mediated, read-only, scoped.
- **§8.5 / §12.3 Fail closed / no mock fallback.** Out-of-policy artifacts DENIED, never silently served.
- **§12.2 No dead wiring.** Shelf wired to the real artifact endpoint only.

## Proposed files

- `companion-ui` artifact-shelf component + store
- limited artifact fetch via the companion API (read-only, scoped)
- tests

## Implementation steps

1. Consume `artifact.created` projection events.
2. Render shelf entries; fetch scoped, read-only artifact previews through the gateway.
3. Deny anything outside policy (fail closed).
4. Preserve + display provenance (§6.13).
5. Tests.

## Acceptance criteria (charter-grounded)

- Artifacts surface in a shelf with scoped read access via gateway; out-of-policy DENIED (§9.2, §8.5).
- Provenance preserved/displayed (§6.13).
- No arbitrary file surface; read-oriented only.
- `npm run lint` + build pass.

## Depends on

`q0k` (limited artifact access) + `e2b` (projection stream) + `cxw` (PWA skeleton). Epic parent (`ta9`). Phase 1.5.

title: Adaptive fatigue tuning from live channel telemetry
description:
Summary:
Phase 2 follow-on: replace/tune Phase 1 static fatigue knobs using real telemetry from live companion-to-companion and group-chat behavior. Do not implement before isi.2-isi.5 provide reliable events and operator-visible history.

Required behavior:
- Use recorded fatigue, overcharge, channel activity, human participation, relationship state, and outcome metadata to tune per-channel or per-channel-class policy values.
- Support channel-specific behavior: busy human group chats should converge toward small MI-to-MI allowances; quiet companion rooms/DMs can permit more back-and-forth when useful.
- Keep operator-assigned maximum bounds. Adaptation can recommend or apply within configured safe ranges only.
- Preserve deterministic enforcement at runtime. Any learned/adaptive output becomes config or policy parameters, not an LLM-in-the-loop gate.
- Include telemetry for outcome quality where available: whether work produced artifacts/decisions/memories, whether reserve was repeatedly needed, whether conversations hit hard stop, and whether humans re-engaged.
- Provide a review path in Garden or a report surface before automatic tuning is enabled.

Expected files/code areas:
- Fatigue ledger/history modules created by isi.2-isi.5.
- src/operator/garden/services/charge-ledger-service.ts, audit-history, or a future fatigue service for review/reporting.
- src/system/config/charge-policy-config.ts for safe adaptive bounds if tuning writes owner-file policy.
- Potential new analysis script under scripts/ or src/app/maintenance/ to replay fatigue telemetry and propose policy changes.
- docs/operations.md if operators need guidance for reviewing/tuning fatigue policy.

Tests to build:
- Replay/analysis tests with synthetic busy group, quiet room, and DM histories showing different recommended limits.
- Safety-bound tests proving recommendations cannot exceed operator max or drop below required minimums.
- Determinism tests proving the same telemetry yields the same recommendation.
- Garden/report tests if a review surface is built.

Non-goals:
- No Phase 1 enforcement. This depends on isi.2-isi.5.
- No LLM adjudication of individual turns.
- No human attention timeout; separate follow-up bead owns that.
design: This is intentionally deferred until there is live data. The goal is not a complex first implementation; the goal is to close the loop from observed room behavior to safer, better-tuned deterministic policy knobs.
acceptance_criteria: Acceptance: after Phase 1 telemetry exists, adaptive/recommendation tooling uses real fatigue and channel metadata to propose or safely apply per-channel/per-class tuning; operator bounds are enforced; runtime enforcement remains deterministic; tests cover busy group vs quiet room behavior, safety bounds, determinism, and any Garden/report surface; npm run lint passes before closing.
close_reason: Integrated in branch isi-fatigue-integration. Implemented deterministic fatigue tuning report builder that consumes fatigue ledger events and policy config, recommends per-channel-setting changes within operator bounds, keeps runtime enforcement deterministic, and exposes the report through the Garden charge ledger service without automatic owner-file mutation. Validation on integrated branch: npm test -- --run src/app/agent/core-runtime.test.ts src/core/agent/fatigue/adaptive-tuning.test.ts src/core/agent/fatigue/fatigue-budget.test.ts src/core/agent/fatigue/policy.test.ts src/shared/telemetry/fatigue-ledger.test.ts src/system/config/charge-policy-config.test.ts src/core/agent/substrate-agent/turn-execution-runtime.test.ts src/operator/garden/services/charge-ledger-service.test.ts (86 tests passed); npm run verify:settings-contract; npm run lint; npm run build.

title: Double analysis_workbench sub-query budget for legitimate multi-hop investigations
description:
Summary:
Double the effective analysis_workbench sub-query budget for legitimate multi-hop investigations. The old migrated bead described a vague "12-step turn limit"; the concrete limit in this repo is the analysis_workbench max sub-query setting.

Problem:
Deep code/log investigations can require more than 12 internal LLM sub-queries. The runtime currently defaults analysisWorkbenchMaxSubQueries to 12, which can stop legitimate multi-hop analysis early. The setting is owner-file/Garden visible, but the default and tests still preserve 12.

Current code evidence as of 2026-06-29:
- src/system/config/load-config.ts:82 defines DEFAULT_THINK_MAX_SUB_QUERIES = 12.
- src/system/config/load-config.ts:306 uses that default for analysisWorkbenchMaxSubQueries.
- config/settings.seed.json:129 sets analysisWorkbenchMaxSubQueries to 12.
- src/app/startup/composition/parity.ts:168 copies config.analysisWorkbenchMaxSubQueries into the REPL budget.
- src/core/tools/analysis-workbench/types.ts:95-99 caps autonomous tier maxSubQueries at 20, so raising only the owner-file default to 24 would still be clamped.

Scope:
- Raise the effective analysis_workbench sub-query budget from 12 to 24 for the tier where long multi-hop investigations are expected to run.
- Update the owner-file default and settings seed so new deployments see the intended value.
- Update analysis_workbench tier caps or tier-specific behavior so the intended 24-query budget is actually reachable where allowed.
- Update Garden/settings defaults and tests that currently expect 12.
- Preserve finite caps, charge/budget telemetry, and clear stop reasons when the limit is reached.

Non-goals:
- Do not make analysis_workbench unbounded.
- Do not loosen ordinary parent-turn tool-use policy for routine work.
acceptance_criteria:
- The effective default analysis_workbench sub-query budget for the intended capable tier is doubled from 12 to 24, not silently clamped back to 20.
- Owner-file defaults, settings seed, Garden settings defaults/display, and runtime config tests agree on the new limit.
- Tier budgets are updated or explicitly documented so nursery/apprentice remain conservative while the sprint target tier reaches 24.
- The runtime still enforces a finite sub-query cap and reports sub-query-limit exits clearly.
- Targeted analysis-workbench/config/settings tests pass.
- npm run lint passes before closure.
notes:
AUDIT 2026-06-28 (verified): OPEN, net-new (or operational). No matching implementation exists; grep for the named feature/symbol = empty.

Current default still comes from src/system/config/load-config.ts:82 DEFAULT_THINK_MAX_SUB_QUERIES = 12 and config/settings.seed.json:129 analysisWorkbenchMaxSubQueries = 12. buildReplConfig applies config.analysisWorkbenchMaxSubQueries at src/app/startup/composition/parity.ts:168. analysis_workbench autonomous tier currently caps maxSubQueries at 20 in src/core/tools/analysis-workbench/types.ts:95-99, so a naive default bump to 24 would be clamped unless tier budget is updated too. git log search found analysis-workbench hardening/settings commits but no qxma/sub-query-limit completion commit.

description: Extend EmotionObserver to fuse signals from multiple modalities (text + audio, eventually + face) using weighted averaging by confidence. When only text is available, use text-only path. design:
In EmotionObserver:
- Track available modalities per-turn (text always, audio when voice active, face when camera active)
- Per-modality confidence score (classifier output confidence)
- Fusion: fused_VAD = Σ(modality_VAD * confidence) / Σ(confidence)
- Categorical fusion: highest-confidence label across all available modalities
- Graceful degradation: works with any subset of modalities
- Future: camera emotion classifier slot (MTCNN + lightweight head)

title: Prompt history corruption recovery + lastKnownGood persistence
description:
Two related prompt stack durability gaps found in independent March audit:

1. **Prompt history silent corruption** — `src/identity/prompt-store.ts` `readHistory()` wraps JSONL parse in try/catch and returns empty array on failure. A corrupted history file silently loses all version history with no notification, repair mechanism, or backup.

2. **`lastKnownGood` not persisted** — `src/identity/prompt-composer.ts` maintains a runtime-only `lastKnownGood` composed prompt. On cold restart after corrupting all layers, identity is empty until character card re-seeds. Should persist last-known-good to disk so it survives process restarts.

Files to modify:
- `src/identity/prompt-store.ts` — add corruption detection + partial recovery (read valid lines, skip broken ones) + operator warning log
- `src/identity/prompt-composer.ts` — persist `lastKnownGood` to disk (atomic write alongside layers.json), load on startup

Implementation steps:
1. In `readHistory()`: instead of returning `[]` on parse error, try line-by-line recovery (valid JSONL lines before the corruption point). Log a warning with the corruption offset.
2. Add `persistLastKnownGood(result: ComposeResult)` to PromptComposer — atomic write to `<promptDir>/last-known-good.json`.
3. On startup, if `compose()` produces empty result, attempt to load persisted last-known-good before falling back to character card seed.
4. Add tests for: corrupted history partial recovery, last-known-good persistence round-trip, cold-start with corrupted layers + persisted fallback.
close_reason: Completed

title: Investigate secondary post-reply plan/act system for long-run autonomous scenarios
description:
Summary:
Investigate and design a secondary autonomy layer that runs after normal reply completion to support longer-horizon plan/act loops (multi-step tasks, deferred actions, background follow-through) without blocking the primary conversational turn loop.

Why:
Current runtime supports in-turn tool use and targeted follow-up/heartbeat flows, but lacks a generic post-reply action-inference/planning engine for sustained multi-step execution across time.

Files likely involved:
- src/agent/substrate-agent.ts
- src/agent/event-bridge.ts
- src/event-bus.ts
- src/scheduler/scheduler.ts
- src/scheduler/heartbeat-tools.ts
- src/tools/* (extended autonomy tools)
- src/channels/admin/* (observability/config surfaces)

Investigation steps:
1. Map current control flow from message completion -> tool execution -> follow-up queues -> scheduler interactions.
2. Identify safe insertion points for a secondary planner/actor loop (post-reply hook, queue worker, or scheduler-backed executor).
3. Define execution model options:
   - event-driven post-reply inference
   - periodic planner tick
   - hybrid (event trigger + periodic reconciliation)
4. Specify boundaries/safety: concurrency, cancellation, retry/backoff, budget limits, capability gating, approval paths.
5. Define persistence requirements for long-running plans (state machine, checkpoints, idempotency keys).
6. Propose minimal MVP architecture + rollout plan with metrics and failure handling.
7. List required API/admin UX surfaces for visibility and operator override.

Deliverables:
- Short design doc (architecture options, tradeoffs, recommended path)
- MVP task breakdown beads (implementation sequence)
- Test strategy (unit + integration + soak scenarios)

Example:
Before: model can suggest a tool/action but no generic engine continues plan execution after response completion.
After: secondary autonomy system can pick up declared intents, schedule/execute steps asynchronously, and report progress/results back into channel/admin telemetry.
