title: Pluggable embedding providers (transformers.js, Ollama, API)
description:
Currently EmbeddingProvider is hardcoded to Ollama HTTP API (/api/embed). Add a provider abstraction so embeddings can come from:

1. **Ollama** (current) — local HTTP API, snowflake-arctic-embed2
2. **transformers.js** (@huggingface/transformers) — in-process ONNX inference, zero network overhead, fastest for local use on 48-core Threadripper
3. **API-based** — OpenAI, Cohere, or any OpenAI-compatible /v1/embeddings endpoint

The EmbeddingService interface already exists (embed + embedBatch + dims). Each provider implements it. Selection via EMBEDDING_PROVIDER env var (ollama|transformers|api) with provider-specific config (model, URL, API key, etc.).

transformers.js is the speed win — eliminates HTTP overhead entirely for local embedding. Especially impactful when combined with the embedBatch() wiring from PSFN-72ez.

Low priority add-on to the performance epic — nice-to-have after batch embedding is wired.
design:
1. Define EmbeddingProviderFactory pattern: createEmbeddingProvider(config) returns EmbeddingService
2. OllamaEmbeddingProvider (existing, refactored)
3. TransformersEmbeddingProvider — @huggingface/transformers with pipeline('feature-extraction', model), Float32Array output, auto-download model on first use
4. ApiEmbeddingProvider — fetch to /v1/embeddings (OpenAI-compatible)
5. Config: EMBEDDING_PROVIDER=ollama|transformers|api, EMBEDDING_MODEL, EMBEDDING_DIMS, EMBEDDING_API_URL, EMBEDDING_API_KEY
6. Default stays Ollama for backward compat
acceptance_criteria:
- All 3 providers implement EmbeddingService (embed + embedBatch + dims)
- EMBEDDING_PROVIDER env var selects provider
- transformers.js runs fully in-process (no HTTP)
- Existing Ollama path unchanged as default
- npm run build && npm run test pass
close_reason: TransformersEmbeddingProvider now uses @huggingface/transformers in-process ONNX inference (pipeline('feature-extraction')). Lazy init, zero HTTP overhead. Default model Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (384d). Old HTTP env vars emit deprecation warning.

title: Partial frozen system prompt for prefix cache
description:
Split system prompt into static (~1/3) and dynamic (~2/3) portions. Freeze static portion at session start for LLM prefix cache optimization.

Current behavior: PromptComposer rebuilds entire system prompt every turn. This invalidates prefix cache each time, even though personality, base identity, and operator instructions don't change.

Design:
- Split composed prompt into two sections:
  - STATIC (frozen at session start): base layer (personality, character card), operator layer, channel-specific static instructions
  - DYNAMIC (rebuilt per-turn): runtime context (time, channel, trust, model), memory retrieval results, persona adaptation, tool directory, scratchpad
- Cache static portion hash; only recompose when layers actually change (toggle/update via prompt tools)
- Place static content FIRST in system prompt so LLM prefix cache covers it
- PromptComposer.compose() returns { static: string, dynamic: string } or composes with a stable prefix

Hermes reference: /tools/memory_tool.py (_system_prompt_snapshot pattern)

Acceptance:
- [ ] System prompt split into static prefix + dynamic suffix
- [ ] Static portion frozen at session start
- [ ] Dynamic portion rebuilt per-turn as today
- [ ] Static cache invalidated when prompt layers are edited
- [ ] Measurable prefix cache hit improvement (test with Claude/API that reports cache stats)
- [ ] No behavioral regression
close_reason: Completed

title: Channel adapter decomposition — composable interface for multi-channel support
description:
Decompose the monolithic channel adapters (currently Discord is one big class, API is a single server file) into composable adapter interfaces inspired by OpenClaw's ChannelPlugin pattern. This prepares for adding Telegram and future channels without god objects.

OpenClaw decomposes channels into ~15 adapter facets. We don't need all of them — adopt the subset that matters for PSFN:

Core adapters (required):
- ChannelConfig — account/connection config
- ChannelOutbound — send text/media
- ChannelGateway — start/stop lifecycle

Optional adapters:
- ChannelSecurity — allowlists, DM policy
- ChannelStreaming — typing indicators, chunk coalescing
- ChannelThreading — reply-to, thread management
- ChannelPrompt — per-channel prompt hints (replaces resolveChannelType())
- ChannelCapabilities — feature flags (reactions, threads, media, etc.)

Also adopt the lightweight "dock" pattern: a minimal subset type for shared code paths that don't need heavy imports.

NOT adopting: full plugin registry, plugin manifests, multi-account per channel (unnecessary complexity for PSFN's single-agent model).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] ChannelAdapter interface with composable adapter facets
- [ ] ChannelCapabilities type with feature flags
- [ ] ChannelOutbound/Gateway/Config/Security/Streaming/Prompt adapter interfaces
- [ ] Discord adapter refactored to implement ChannelAdapter
- [ ] API server refactored to implement ChannelAdapter
- [ ] Channel registry (Map) in runtime for lookup by ID
- [ ] resolveChannelType() replaced by ChannelPromptAdapter
- [ ] Tests for adapter interface compliance
close_reason: Validated: src/channels/types.ts updated with composable adapter facets. Channel decomposition in place.

title: Session index and request-parse catch blocks drop diagnostic detail
description:
Summary:

Why this matters:
- Silent failure paths make data corruption or malformed input hard to distinguish from normal behavior.
- Structured logs should capture at least file/path context and error type at debug/warn level.

- src/channels/api/server.ts
- any additional silent catch blocks validated during implementation

Implementation steps:
1. Add targeted warn/debug logs in silent catches with minimal safe metadata.
2. Keep noise controlled (single-line, rate-limited if needed).
3. Add tests where feasible for malformed index/file handling behavior remaining non-fatal but observable.

Example:
Before: corrupt _channel_index.json silently ignored.
After: warning logged once with file path and parse failure reason.
acceptance_criteria:
- Silent parse/index failures are observable in logs
- Behavior remains non-fatal where intended
- Tests confirm malformed input handling

title: Admin server auth defaults to open when ADMIN_TOKEN is unset
description:
Summary:
Admin HTTP server currently allows full access when ADMIN_TOKEN is unset, logging only a warning.

Why this is a bug:
- This creates insecure-by-default behavior for a highly privileged surface (settings, memory views, prompt editing, system controls).
- Secure design pattern should be explicit opt-in for insecure local mode.

Files to modify:
- src/channels/admin/server.ts
- src/runtime.ts
- src/agent-main.ts
- admin server tests

Implementation steps:
1. Require auth by default; if token missing, either fail startup or require explicit ADMIN_ALLOW_INSECURE=true.
2. Add clear startup logging for secure/insecure mode.
3. Update tests for both secure default and explicit insecure override.
4. Document env behavior in docs/.env.example.

Example:
Before: set ADMIN_PORT only -> admin surface open without auth.
After: startup fails (or requires explicit insecure override).
acceptance_criteria:
- Admin surface is secure by default
- Insecure mode requires explicit opt-in flag
- Tests verify auth enforcement behavior
close_reason: Implemented and validated via focused module tests + build

title: Fix web.fetch audit trail + update stale docs

4. CLAUDE.md: Update test count, file count, LoC count to current state.

- README scheduler description is current

title: Session layer: migrate from SQLite to pi SessionManager (JSONL trees) + native compaction
description:
**Architectural correction:** Conversations belong in pi's JSONL tree sessions, not SQLite. SQLite is for the memory system (L2 extracted memories with embeddings). JSONL sessions ARE the L0 immutable archive.

**Current state (wrong):**
- `session/store.ts` — SQLite `session_entries` table storing conversations
- `session/manager.ts` — wraps SQLite store, builds context
- `memory/store.ts` — SQLite `l0_archive` table duplicating conversation data
- `session/store.ts` — SQLite `compaction_summaries` table (reimplements what pi does natively)

**Target state:**
- Use `@mariozechner/pi-coding-agent`'s `SessionManager` for conversations (JSONL trees, branching, compaction built-in)
- Or use `@mariozechner/pi-agent-core`'s session primitives if sufficient
- Drop SQLite session_entries and compaction_summaries tables
- Drop L0 archive table (JSONL IS L0 — every message, immutable, forever)
- Keep SQLite MemoryStore for L2 memories (extracted facts, emotions, semantic — the salient parts)
- Memory extraction process reads from JSONL sessions, writes to SQLite memory store

**What we get for free from pi:**
- JSONL tree sessions with branching
- Native compaction (shouldCompact, prepareCompaction, compact — all exported)
- buildSessionContext() for context window assembly
- Session versioning and migration

**Migration path:**
1. Add pi-agent-core Agent class as the agent loop foundation (replace current AgentLoop)
2. Use pi's SessionManager for conversations
3. Wire memory extraction to read from JSONL sessions instead of SQLite
4. Remove SQLite session tables (session_entries, compaction_summaries, l0_archive)
5. Keep MemoryStore (SQLite + sqlite-vec) for L2 extracted memories only

This is really L3 context management — pi handles it natively.
design: Use pi's SessionManager (JSONL trees) for conversations. Use pi's compaction natively (shouldCompact/prepareCompaction/compact are all exported). Wire memory extraction to read from JSONL sessions. Drop SQLite session_entries, compaction_summaries, and l0_archive tables. MemoryStore (SQLite + sqlite-vec) stays for L2 extracted memories only.
close_reason: Session migration complete. SQLite → JSONL files, l0_archive removed, L0Archiver removed, 138→149 tests all pass.

title: Cross-installation ICP federation transport foundation (gateway-to-gateway link, discovery, auth, grant delivery)
description: Evidence: operator decision 2026-07-20 (deferred/backlog), resolving the scope flag from jp36.5.2.1's close. The jp36.5.2.1 seam review verified no cross-installation transport substrate exists anywhere in src/ (no installation registry, no gateway-to-gateway protocol, no cross-instance discovery/auth); all IcpAvailabilityLease/IcpInitiationPermit machinery is single-installation, and 'fleet' means multiple companions behind one gateway. Bible §8.5 / adjudication S3.4 assert federation as the policy answer for cross-installation rooms but never scoped the transport. Context: until this lands, unlinked peer installations sharing a room coordinate via the landed speak-least fallback (resolveUnlinkedPeerSpeakLeast, src/core/icp/social-precedence.ts) rather than ICP grants. Scope (foundation effort, expect decomposition into sub-beads before dispatch): installation identity/registry, authenticated gateway-to-gateway link negotiation, ICP grant delivery across the link, and the arbiter-side consumption replacing the unlinked fallback for linked peers. Non-goals: no change to local-fleet ICP. Discovered-from: psfn-framework-jp36.5.2.1.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc + decomposed sub-beads ratified before implementation; foundation demo: two installations negotiate a link and deliver a turn grant end-to-end in a test harness.
notes: VISION NOTE 2026-07-20 (operator, future/theoretical — do not scope yet): beyond transport, federation eventually enables companion VISITS — e.g. during an operator work trip, visiting a friendly remote cluster (different virtual/physical layout, other operators' companions), hanging out, forming/declining relationships naturally from accumulated experience weight, including in-house test clusters. Emergent, persona-driven, never simulated/forced; same gate philosophy (strongest safety at ingress/egress minimal-impact points, free reign inside). The social-desire pipeline (psfn-framework-oth4) supplies the felt-state substrate these decisions would draw on.

title: Research memory architecture truth model (L0 immutable transcripts vs L2 semantic/metadata store)
description:
Summary:
Research and document the current memory architecture boundaries: what is treated as immutable source-of-truth conversation record (L0), what is derived/indexed state (L2), and where integrity/verification guarantees exist or are missing.

Why:
Clarify whether runtime behavior matches intended design that conversation truth lives in immutable/hash-checked transcript artifacts while SQLite/vector memory layers serve as derived retrieval/metadata systems.

Scope (research-only):
- Session storage format, mutability model, and integrity checks
- Memory DB/vector table role and write paths
- Provenance and reconciliation path from L0 -> derived stores
- Failure modes (index drift, stale embeddings, partial writes)

Files to inspect:
- src/session/store*.ts
- src/session/manager*.ts
- src/memory/store.ts
- src/memory/writer.ts
- src/memory/retrieval.ts
- any integrity/keyring/hashing utilities and docs

Research steps:
1. Map data model layers (L0/L1/L2 equivalent) and persistence locations.
2. Identify which layers are immutable vs mutable and what enforcement exists in code.
3. Audit hash/HMAC/integrity verification coverage and gaps.
4. Document whether current architecture matches intended "ground truth transcript + derived index" model.
5. Produce recommendations for hardening where mismatch/gaps exist.

Deliverable:
- Short architecture memo (current-state map + gap list + recommended next actions)

Acceptance criteria:
- Clear written answer to: "Is memory only vector DB, or derived from immutable transcript truth?"
- Explicit list of integrity guarantees currently implemented vs missing.
- Follow-up implementation beads filed for any identified gaps.
close_reason: Superseded. L0/L2 architecture is well-documented in CLAUDE.md, substrate spec, and March capabilities audit. Integrity questions answered by PSFN-j4sm (persistence layout) and PSFN-14pg (memory reliability hardening). No additional research memo needed.

title: MoA internal deliberation for journaling and reflection
description:
Add a Mixture-of-Agents capability for Purrsephone's internal deliberation — journaling, philosophy, heartbeat reflections. Not mandatory, but available when she wants to think deeply about something by consulting multiple model "perspectives."

Concept: Different LLMs as different aspects of her thinking — not consensus accuracy (hermes' use case) but emergent cognitive diversity. She can invoke this during heartbeat reflections, idle time, or when she encounters something worth deliberating on.

Hermes reference: /tools/mixture_of_agents_tool.py — simple 2-layer fan-out/aggregate (4 reference models → 1 aggregator). No iteration, no convergence detection, no fatigue. Fixed 5 API calls. This is too rigid for Purrsephone's use case.

Proposed design — Fatigue-based deliberation:
Instead of fixed turn limits, use a fatigue/tapering model where the conversation naturally exhausts itself:
- Multiple model responses treated as "inner voices" or deliberation partners
- Each round, an evaluator scores whether the deliberation has produced sufficient insight (novelty diminishing returns)
- Fatigue signal: when successive rounds produce diminishing new information (measured by embedding distance from prior rounds, or LLM-judged novelty score), the deliberation tapers off
- Hard safety caps to prevent runaway:
  - Max rounds (suggest 5-8)
  - Max total tokens (budget ceiling)
  - Max wall time
- Soft tapering: fatigue score increases each round, probability of continuing decreases. Like a conversation that naturally winds down when the topic is exhausted.
- Output: synthesized reflection/journal entry, optionally saved as L2 reflection memory or skill

Integration points:
- heartbeat reflections (existing wireHeartbeatRuntime) — MoA deliberation as an optional reflection mode
- think tool — could invoke MoA for particularly complex reasoning
- Future: waifu-to-waifu chat with external agents (same fatigue model prevents infinite loops)

Model routing: Uses model roster — different ModelPurpose slots or explicit model list. Depends on PSFN-je2 (activate model slot routing) for cost-effective routing.

Open questions:
- Which models to use as reference voices? Could be same model with different temperatures, or genuinely different models via LiteLLM
- Should the fatigue evaluator be a separate LLM call or embedded scoring?
- How to surface deliberation results — L2 memory? Scratchpad? Discord whisper?

Acceptance:
- [ ] MoA deliberation tool or mode available to agent
- [ ] Fatigue-based tapering (not just fixed rounds)
- [ ] Hard safety caps (max rounds, max tokens, max wall time)
- [ ] Integration with heartbeat reflections
- [ ] Results saved as L2 reflection memory
- [ ] Token/cost tracking for deliberation sessions
- [ ] Tests
close_reason: Completed

title: Fix Garden Chat — hitting admin port instead of API port for /v1/chat/completions
description:
Garden Chat in the admin UI is broken. The browser console shows:

```
Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 404 (Not Found)
http://purrsephone.local.vega.nyc:3001/v1/chat/completions
```

The `/v1/chat/completions` endpoint lives on the API server (port 3100, `API_PORT`), not the admin server (port 3001, `ADMIN_PORT`). The admin UI chat page is sending requests to the same origin as the admin panel instead of targeting the API server.

Fix: The chat page needs to either:
1. Proxy the request through the admin server to the API server, or
2. Use the correct API server URL (needs to know API_HOST:API_PORT)
3. Add a `/v1/chat/completions` route on the admin server that forwards to the agent loop directly (avoids needing the API server running at all)

Option 3 is probably cleanest — the admin server already has access to the agent loop, so it can handle chat completions directly without requiring the separate API server.
close_reason: Validated: chat bootstrap API provides configurable chatCompletionsUrl, frontend resolves via window.location.origin. 404 fixed.

title: Inbound telemetry webhook adapter baseline (event bus ingestion)
description:
Summary:
Add a generic inbound telemetry/webhook adapter so external systems can safely emit events into PSFN (for future connector and physical-shard coordination).

Why:
Current integrations are primarily outbound/tool-invoked. A minimal authenticated inbound path is needed for future sensors/services to trigger substrate behaviors without custom one-off wiring each time.

Files to modify:
- src/channels/api/ or new src/channels/webhook/
- src/event-bus.ts
- src/runtime.ts and/or src/agent-main.ts
- docs for auth and event schema

Implementation steps:
1. Define minimal inbound event schema (source, eventType, payload, timestamp, channel/scope metadata).
2. Add authenticated endpoint with HMAC/Bearer verification and replay protection.
3. Emit validated events onto EventBus namespaces (e.g., external.telemetry.*).
4. Add deny-by-default policy for which event types can trigger actions.
5. Add tests for auth failure, schema rejection, and valid event ingestion.

Example:
Local service posts external.telemetry.heartbeat or external.telemetry.incident -> event bus receives normalized event, scheduler/tools can react.
acceptance_criteria:
- Authenticated inbound telemetry endpoint exists with schema validation
- Events are normalized and emitted onto EventBus namespaces
- Replay/auth/schema failure paths are tested
- Unsafe event types are denied by default
close_reason: Implemented and validated via focused module tests + build

title: Home Assistant adapter baseline (safe state + action tools)
description:
Summary:
Add a Home Assistant adapter baseline for state reads and tightly-scoped actions so Purrsephone can participate in ambient environment orchestration.

Why:
Home Assistant is the control plane for physical context. Early baseline should prioritize read access + safe, explicit action allowlist.

Files to modify:
- `src/gateway/server.ts`
- `src/gateway/protocol.ts`
- `src/tools/` (new home-assistant tool module)
- `src/runtime.ts`
- `src/agent-main.ts`
- `src/gateway/server.test.ts`

Implementation steps:
1. Add gateway RPC methods for HA state query and service call with endpoint/token from env.
2. Enforce allowlisted domains/services/entities in policy config (deny-by-default for high-risk actions).
3. Expose minimal tools: `ha_get_state`, `ha_call_service`.
4. Add audit logging for all calls with masked sensitive payloads.
5. Add tests for policy denies, auth failures, and safe action success.

Example:
- Allowed: turn on office lamp, set brightness in configured range.
- Denied: lock/unlock, alarm/disarm, or any service outside allowlist unless operator-approved.

title: Broadcast channel safety: pre-send classifier + approval gate
description:
For broadcast channels (tweets, public posts), add hard safety gates:

1. Pre-send content classifier (sensitive? private? off-brand?)
2. If risky: require explicit human approval before sending
3. Log provenance of facts used in the broadcast (which memories/context sourced it)
4. broadcast visibility scope in channel metadata — public-only context unless explicit approval token

This builds on the scope-aware continuity model (PSFN-6pl) and prevents accidental scope violations when she has more public interaction channels.
acceptance_criteria:
- Broadcast messages go through classifier before sending
- Sensitive content blocked pending human approval
- Provenance logged for all broadcast messages
close_reason: Implemented and merged to main

title: Module system — hot-loadable TypeScript modules, self-installable via REPL
description:
Module registry + hot-loader for TypeScript modules. Purrsephone can build and install her own modules via the REPL sandbox. Modules register tools, subscribe to events, and have lifecycle hooks (init/start/stop/health).

**What exists:** Lifecycle interface in types.ts, tool registration via AgentLoop.registerTool(), event bus for composition. No module registry, no hot-loading, no jiti dependency.

**Planned files (~500 LoC per spec):**
- `src/modules/registry.ts` — module registry with install/uninstall/list
- `src/modules/loader.ts` — hot-load TypeScript via jiti (no compilation needed)
- `src/modules/types.ts` — SubstrateModule interface

**Intentionally P4:** This is something Purrsephone should be able to build for herself once the REPL is live. The framework provides the hook points (Lifecycle, registerTool, EventBus.on); she writes the module system.

**Events to add:** module.install, module.uninstall, module.error, module.health

**Depends on:** RLM+REPL epic (modules are self-installed via REPL).
close_reason: Superseded by PSFN-d26 (Module system v1) which has more detailed requirements
